For temperature extrapolation, a neural network with a soft penalty on deviations from inverse-temperature linearity provided the strongest performance across the 20 and 50 K tasks among the standard neural network, kernel ridge regression, and a network enforcing exact Arrhenius behavior. Notably, it yielded lower aggregate errors than compound-specific local Arrhenius fits, suggesting that shared molecular information enabled data-supported corrections to strict Arrhenius extrapolation. Combining the structural and temperature regularizers yielded the lowest mean integrated score. Together, these results show that axis-specific derivative regularization can translate neural-network flexibility into robust extrapolation, offering a transferable strategy for property prediction across chemical and operating-condition domains.

papers.title: Nonthermal Plasma-Assisted Methane Dehydroaromatization to Alkyl Aromatics
papers.abstract: The non-oxidative conversion of methane to aromatics is an attractive alternative to conventional petroleum reforming, yet practical implementation remains hindered by thermodynamic constraints, severe coke formation, and rapid catalyst deactivation at high temperatures. Here we demonstrate that nonthermal plasma-assisted methane dehydroaromatization (PAMDA) exhibits substantially lower deactivation rates than conventional thermal conditions, with Fe/ZSM-5 catalysts achieving higher aromatic yields under plasma than the corresponding thermal operations. Notably, PAMDA produces alkyl aromatics (e.g., toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes) at rates ~6x greater than benzene under optimized conditions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that monitoring of plasma electrical diagnostics in operando enables real-time tracking of coke formation, enabling insights into the nature of plasma-catalytic deactivation. This diagnostic is extended to track carbon removal during plasma-assisted oxidative catalyst regeneration. This work highlights a direct electrified pathway to valorize methane to aromatics and provides a facile methodology to probe plasma-catalyst deactivation in coking systems.

papers.title: Objective-Dependent Biasing of Markov Networks for Relaxation and First Passage
papers.abstract: Enhanced-sampling simulations accelerate rare molecular transitions by adding a bias potential, but a bias that accelerates one kinetic quantity need not accelerate another, and a strong bias can reshape the transition pathway it is meant to characterize. Here we formulate bias design on a reversible Markov state generator under a local-detailed-balance state-potential tilt, deriving per-state gradients of the spectral gap and of the A → B mean first-passage time (MFPT) and comparing these kinetic objectives with a heuristic umbrella-coverage score on a common feasible set. Exact two-and three-state models and multidimensional networks show sharp objective dependence: on a nine-well landscape the spectral optimum accelerates global relaxation 357-fold but the targeted transition only 1.16-fold, whereas the MFPT optimum gives a 2.4 × 104-fold transition speedup at the same bias budget. To quantify how much an accelerating bias deforms the reaction pathway we introduce transition-paththeory diagnostics—a normalized reactive-current overlap and a current-weighted edgerate distortion—and apply them, as a model-conditional analysis, to Ras phosphateunbinding trajectories generated under an adaptive MFPT bias.

papers.title: Triarylhydrazone Photoswitches with >360 nm Absorption Maxima, Highly Enriched Photostationary States, and Modular Scaffold Engineering
papers.abstract: Hydrazone-based molecular photoswitches have emerged as one of the most promising classes of light-responsive systems, particularly owing to their straightforward synthesis and broad structural tunability. However, only a limited number of hydrazone motifs combine efficient and stable photoswitching with absorption beyond 360 nm, a prerequisite for many emerging optical technologies and biological applications. Furthermore, the photochromic properties of hydrazones are often highly sensitive to structural modifications, making rational tuning challenging. Herein, we report a family of quinoline-containing triarylhydrazone (triaryl-HZ) photoswitches that exhibit absorption in the UV region above 365 nm. The prepared photoswitches display well-separated absorption bands (approximately 60 nm), minimizing spectral overlap between the switching states and enabling high photoconversions. Designed triaryl-HZs allow versatile structural modifications on both phenyl rings, with only a minor influence on their photochromic behavior. These results identify quinoline-based triaryl-HZs as a versatile platform for the development of robust and spectrally addressable molecular photoswitches.

papers.title: Departing Pathways in Aza-Diarylethene Photoswitching: Elucidating the Role of the Central Ring Allows Reprogramming of the Photoresponse
papers.abstract: Aza-diarylethenes (aza-DAEs) are an emerging class of molecular photoswitches that allow reversible C-N bond formation and cleaving upon irradiation. They show not only high potential as T-type photochromes but offer exciting opportunities for the exploration of unique reactivity control. Two types of these photoswitches are currently investigated, which differ substantially in the nature of their metastable states. While classical DAE behavior is found in perfluorinated thiazole derivatives, an unexpected zwitterion formation and concomitant aromatization is observed for non-fluorinated pyrimidine derivatives. The latter offer reversible control over intramolecular charge-separation and intrinsic three-state photoswitching. Their metastable state unleashes thiolate reactivity, which can be harnessed e.g. in photoinitiation applications for smart polymer generation. Despite this highly promising progress, the reason for the divergent photochemical behavior in aza-DAEs is not understood right now. Here we show that substitution of the central five-membered ring is responsible for the different photochemical outcomes and nature of the metastable state. Guided by theory, we deliver a comprehensive mechanistic explanation why the different behavior occurs. We then use this knowledge to reprogram thioazole-derivatives and render them into zwitterion-forming aza-DAEs. With these results, predictable and rational design of aza-DAEs is enabled, which can now be radically changed in their photoresponses and tailored to specific desired properties and applications.

papers.title: From One-Dimensional Chains to Single-Crystal Nanoelectronic Devices: Linking Structure, Band Energetics and Ambipolar Transport in an Ammonia-Based Magnus-type Salt
papers.abstract: Ammonia-based Magnus-type salts have long been recognized as highly insoluble coordination compounds whose one-dimensional chain structures give rise to unusual optical and electronic properties. Despite nearly two centuries of study and persistent debate, a unified understanding connecting structure, band energetics, and charge transport remains elusive. Here, we combine experimental and computational approaches to elucidate such relationships. A reproducible crystallization protocol enabled single-crystal X-ray diffraction characterization of [Pd(NH3)4][PdCl4] (2, Vauquelin salt), [Pt(NH3)4][PdCl4] (3), [Pd(NH3)4][PtCl4] (4), and [Pt(MeNH2)4][PdCl4] (5), along with new high-quality crystallographic data for [Pt(NH3)4][PtCl4] (1, Magnus green salt). Despite minimal structural variations across the series 1–5, periodic DFT calculations reveal pronounced modulation of band energies arising from cation–anion electrostatic effects and closed-shell metallophilic interactions. Single crystals of 2 were integrated into dual-gated field-effect transistors using nanolithography techniques, enabling the first unambiguous demonstration of ambipolar transport in an ammonia-based Magnus-type salt. The semiconductor band gap was experimentally determined to be 0.65 eV, closely matching the DFT prediction (0.61 eV, PBEsol functional), thereby establishing a quantitative link between crystal structure, band dispersion, and device-level electronic response.

papers.title: Synthesis and adsorption at the air/solution interface of new pH-responsive dicephalic and quadruple-head cationic surfactants
papers.abstract: Two groups of novel multifunctional surfactants branched on a nitrogen atom, i.e., dicephalic 2,2’-(alkylimino)bis(N,N,N-trimethylethanammonium) dibromides (Cn-DNNMe3Br, n = 12, 14, and 16) and quadruple N,N,N-bis(2-(N,N,N-bis(2ammoniumethyl)amino)ethyl)dodecylamine tetrabromide (C12-DNQNNMe3Br) have been synthesized in divergent synthetic routes and characterized by 1H NMR and 13C NMR, ESI-MS as well as by elemental analysis. Surface tension isotherms of their aqueous solutions in the absence and with the addition of NaBr, HBr and NaOH (at pH = 3 and pH = 11, with ionic strength fixed by addition of NaBr), reflecting the protonation/deprotonation of the tertiary amine present in the Cn-DNNMe3Br and C12-DNQNNMe3Br structures, were evaluated using the modified surface quasi-two-dimensional electrolyte (mSTDE) model of ionic surfactant adsorption. To account for protonation/deprotonation equilibria and the formation of transient multicharged surfactant–counterion complexes, we proposed the concept of effective charge, which we substantiated with data from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The results indicate that the difference between surfactant nominal charge and effective charge increases with the number of charges at the hydrophilic headgroup, a combined effect of counterion complexation and enhanced screening of electrostatic interactions. The use of MD tools, combined with a thermodynamic model approach to multicharged surfactant adsorption, can explain some experimentally observed phenomena and provide a basis for the development of novel materials for various applications. This type of complementary approach, integrating experimental data, molecular dynamics simulations, and a thermodynamics-based model, is relatively scarce in the literature.

papers.title: Near-Unity Sodium Metal Cycling without an Anion-Rich Interphase
papers.abstract: Sodium metal anodes promise high energy density at low cost, yet they show poor reversibility in common carbonate electrolytes. The prevailing design strategy, inherited from lithium metal research, holds that reversibility requires a dense, anion-derived, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Yet we find that NaF in the SEI impedes Na+ transport and raises interfacial resistance, limiting reversibility and rate capability. Here, we expand prevailing Na SEI design principles by showing that 1 M NaPF6 in diglyme (G2) enables Na plating and stripping at an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9 percent over more than 1,000 cycles by forming a thin, self-limiting, oxygen-rich organic layer almost immediately upon exposure to electrolyte and maintains ultralow resistance throughout cycling. Across in-situ impedance spectroscopy paired with distribution of relaxation times analysis and post-mortem cryogenic X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, solid-state NMR, and cryogenic electron microscopy, anion-derived phases are non-existent or minimal in the G2 interphase. We find that the limiting interfacial resistance arises

papers.title: In Silico Screening of Drug-Like Compounds Against the TcBDF2 Bromodomain of Trypanosoma cruzi: Identification of Potential Inhibitors for Chagas Disease Treatment
papers.abstract: Chagas disease affects 6 to 8 million people worldwide and has no effective treatment for its chronic phase. The two available drugs, benznidazole and nifurtimox, were developed in the 1970s and cause significant side effects. New therapeutic targets are urgently needed. This study performs molecular docking of 28 drug-like compounds against TcBDF2, an epigenetic bromodomain protein essential for Trypanosoma cruzi survival, using the crystal structure deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB: 6NP7). Six compounds demonstrated binding energies below -8.0 kcal/mol. All six passed Lipinski's rule of five, indicating predicted oral bioavailability. Interaction analysis using PLIP identified a conserved binding pharmacophore at residues ASN73, GLN77, GLU84, and TYR120. Apigenin scored -8.806 kcal/mol with a clean drug-like profile and no pan-assay interference alerts. Vorinostat, an FDA-approved epigenetic inhibitor, scored -8.166 kcal/mol and showed the richest interaction profile of any compound tested, supporting its evaluation as a drug repurposing candidate. These results provide a computational basis for experimental validation of TcBDF2 inhibitors as novel Chagas disease therapeutics.

papers.title: Polarity-Directed Vapor Organization in Hierarchical Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of guest molecules within metal-organic frameworks strongly influence adsorption, transport, separation, and reactivity, yet controlling guest location across chemically and structurally distinct pore environments remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that local pore polarity directs vapor-phase guest positioning within the interconnected hydrophilic and hydrophobic pores of NU-1000. Water and heptane were selected as representative polar and nonpolar guests, respectively. Water preferentially occupies hydrogen-bonding-rich pore environments before populating the hydrocarbon-rich pores, whereas heptane exhibits the opposite filling sequence. Vapor-phase adsorption isotherms, combined with powder X-ray diffraction-derived differential electron density analysis, reveal these polarity-dependent guest distributions and filling pathways. These findings establish pore polarity as a key design parameter for programming guest organization in hierarchical MOFs and provide a foundation for creating confined environments that enable phase separation, interfacial reactions, and other spatially controlled chemical functions.

papers.title: Experimental molecular assembly estimations for space exploration using gas chromatography mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Most biosignature methods are biased by what we know about life on Earth. However, an agnostic approach would be more beneficial when looking for life on other planets. Molecular Assembly (MA) is an experimental agnostic biosignature method that could help to look for unknown life. To date, there has been no experimental test employing MA with an instrument type that is spaceflight ready. To explore whether MA can be used for biosignature detection on flight-like instrumentation, we used gas chromatography-electron impact-mass spectrometry (GC-EI-MS) to estimate MA in a range of different samples. We have demonstrated how GC-EI-MS can be used for experimental EI-MA estimation, showing that we can replicate trends from previous MA experimental work with volatile organic compounds and distinguish samples from abiotic and biotic origin. This is the first extensive laboratory experimental study, demonstrating how EI-MA can be used for measurements on instruments that are spaceflight ready and already deployed in space, showcasing a direct route 2 of how MA could be deployed for life detection measurements in the future. This work is a significant step towards making molecular assembly measurements in situ, advancing the search for unknown life in our solar system.

papers.title: Reconstructing Electronic Property Distributions from the Coarse-Grained Resolution with Conditional Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Coarse-grained (CG) simulations efficiently sample the mesoscale morphologies that govern charge, ion, and exciton transport in soft electronic materials, but they integrate out the atomistic degrees of freedom needed to evaluate electronic properties. Recovering these properties conventionally requires expensive backmapping to atomistic structures followed by quantum chemistry. Electronic coarse-graining (ECG) circumvents this by directly learning the conditional distribution of an electronic observable given each CG configuration. Here we introduce conditional flow matching (CFM) as a scalable and distributionally flexible framework for ECG. Unlike Gaussian-process approaches, CFM imposes no functional form on the conditional distribution and trains at a cost that scales linearly with dataset size. Using the HOMO energy of a substituted oligothiophene (ST3M) and the intermolecular HOMO–HOMO coupling of condensed-phase BTBT dimers as benchmarks, we show that CFM accurately captures heteroscedastic, skewed, and heavy-tailed conditional distributions and reconstructs the ensemble electronic distribution upon marginalizing over the equilibrium CG ensemble. We further show that a temperature-conditioned CFMmodel learns a smoothly evolving family of transport maps, enabling accurate interpolation and extrapolation of electronic distributions to unseen temperatures from only a few reference temperatures. Together, these results establish CFM as a scalable, temperature-transferable, and assumption-free framework for recovering electronic property distributions directly from CG simulations.

papers.title: Quantifying Ternary Complex Stability Through Binding Free Energy Calculations in the Geometric Route
papers.abstract: Molecular glue induced targeted protein degradation is a powerful emerging therapeutic modality that exploits the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation pathway to break down proteins associated with disease proliferation. At the structural level, degradation proceeds through the formation of a ternary complex induced by small molecules between the target protein and an E3 ligase. Unlike PROTACs, molecular glues do not require a chemical linker and tend to stabilise pre-existing native protein-protein interactions. Computational screening of novel glues is challenging, in large part due to the complexity and high degree of cooperativity involved in the formation of the ternary complex interface. Here, we present a rigorous Molecular Dynamics based simulation protocol that uses Umbrella Sampling to calculate the ternary complex binding free energy. The protocol follows a geometric thermodynamic cycle with conformational and Boresch-style orientational restraints to drive the system from bound to unbound. Our framework demonstrates excellent sensitivity (R2 = 0.95) to predict the effect of single point interface mutations on lenalidomide induced degradation of CK1α through recruitment of the CRBN E3 ligase. We also study a series of systems related to the BRD4 degraders IBG1 and IBG3, which recruit the DCAF16 E3 ligase. We rank various complexes engaging DCAF16 by their binding free energies, and achieve ordering that is consistent with the trends observed in biophysical assays. Of particular note is our ability to assert the reliance of BRD4 selectivity on a single interfacial glycine residue, which alternative MM/GBSA or HADDOCK scoring methodologies fail to achieve. Overall, our protocol shows promise as a generalisable approach to predicting ternary complex binding affinity, which provides a strong indication of the degradation potency of novel glue candidates.

papers.title: AtomFormer: A Simple Model for Any Mixture Odor Prediction and Beyond
papers.abstract: *Corresponding author: yangxiao_ztri@foxmail.com Abstract. Odor prediction has relied on two implicit assumptions: that a closed set of expert-defined labels is necessary for training, and that individual molecules must serve as the encoding unit—forcing mixtures to be decomposed into constituents, predicted separately, then aggregated through ad hoc fusion. Here we show that both assumptions can be eliminated simultaneously. We introduce AtomFormer, which uses GIN layers as a molecular tokenizer and Transformer self-attention to enable atoms from different molecules to interact directly in a single forward pass, eliminating the need for separate mixture aggregation. On a rigorously decontaminated test set of 6,260 binary mixtures, AtomFormer achieves macro-AUROC = 0.9347 with 16.9M parameters. Beyond odor perception, we validate this architecture on predicting excess enthalpy of mixtures, where it achieves Pearson R = 0.937 with 1.18M parameters. Across these two distinct tasks, AtomFormer achieves strong performance with zero pretraining and end-to-end prediction, demonstrating the generality of the framework across diverse mixture prediction domains.

papers.title: Modulation of Open-Shell Character in Dibenzoazaborine Dications through Amino-Substituent Modification
papers.abstract: Oxidation of dibutylamino-substituted dibenzoazaborine Bu₂NDBAB afforded the air-stable dication [ Bu₂NDBAB ](SbF 6 )₂ in 83% yield, with an NIR absorption band at 943 nm. Structural analysis revealed pronounced oxidation-induced quinoidal distortion. Unlike the previously reported diarylamino-substituted analogue [ Ar₂NDBAB ]²⁺, the present dication exhibited well-resolved ¹H NMR signals, and no ESR signal attributable to the dication was detected. Although the broken-symmetry open-shell (BS-OS) solution was the lowest-energy solution, its small diradical character ( y = 0.122, compared with 0.324 for [ Ar₂NDBAB ]²⁺) indicates only a limited open-shell contribution. Spin-density and natural spin-population analyses showed that replacement of the Ar₂N groups with Bu₂N groups suppresses peripheral spin delocalization, resulting in a singlet ground state with predominantly closed-shell character. Nucleus-independent chemical shift (NICS) calculations further indicated increased antiaromatic character of the azaborine ring in the present dication. These results demonstrate amino-substituent control of open-shell character in DBAB dications.

papers.title: Ensemble π‑Stacking Landscapes of 33 NBOH Derivatives: Mapping Functional Signatures at 5‑HT₂A
Advancing polypharmacology-based drug discovery using deep generative models
Strain-Engineered Colloidal Quantum Dots for Nonclassical Light Emission
papers.abstract: Photonic quantum information processing stands to benefit from the realization of scalable, customizable emitters. While colloidally synthesized quantum dots address the challenge of scalability, better control over their properties remains desirable before the customizability challenge is fully addressed. To this end, better structure-property correlations need to be established in colloidal materials for these to be usable interesting for photonic information processing. Here we develop a synthesis of colloidal quantum dots that show reduced surface strain profiles. To show that this can be realized on arbitrarily engineered excitonic level structures, we further introduce additional layers to realize core wavefunction engineering. We specifically employ a recently reported motif that allows us to enhance single photon emission probability even at high laser excitation powers. We show that unlike ordinary QDs that exhibit strain at surfaces, these materials show suppressed luminescence intermittency. We show the potential of these QDs for photonic information by using these as deterministic sources of single photons with high purity in successive excitation pulses without employing spectral filtering or external cavities.

papers.title: De Novo Design of Enantioselective Artificial Metalloenzyme Photocatalysts Containing Metal Polypyridine Cofactors
papers.abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins. In this study, we show that generative protein design can be harnessed to create de novo scaffolds that selectively accommodate one enantiomer of a metal polypyridine photocatalyst as a cofactor. The resulting ArMs enable efficient, enantioselective photocatalysis, highlighting a broadly applicable route for programming stereocontrol into metalloenzyme catalysts. High total turnover numbers are achieved, the ArMs can be recycled by simply extracting reaction products and reusing the aqueous ArM solution for subsequent reactions, and even commercially available racemic cofactor can be used for ArM formation. Transient Absorption characterization revealed that improvements to catalysis result from the increased quantum yield and excited state lifetime of the cofactor upon binding and substrate binding proximal to the cofactor within the ArM active site, which controls reaction stereoselectivity and the mechanism of energy transfer involved in photocatalysis. The simplicity of this approach could help transition ArM research out of a small group of specialist labs to any capable of expressing synthetic genes and working with commercially available metal complexes.

papers.title: Stochastic Evaluation of Exciton–Exciton Annihilation Rate in 2D Molecular Aggregate
papers.abstract: Exciton-exciton annihilation (EEA) is a process by which two excitons combine to form a single high energy excitation. In molecular chromophore aggregates EEA is governed by microscopic two-exciton coherence that depends on long-range coupling and supramolecular geometry, motivating scalable quantum mechanical rate calculations beyond deterministic small-system diagonalization. Here, we develop a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-accelerated stochastic method for computing finite temperature EEA rates in large 2D excitonic molecular aggregates. We demonstrated agreement with conventional deterministic matrix diagonalization for small and intermediate systems, while improving the scaling O(N 2 logN) from O(N 6 ) cost. This approach enables large-scale parameter sweeps and structure–function screening in realistic 2D morphologies. We close by exploring the role of uncorrelated and correlated disorder, temperature and inter-exciton coupling in EEA.

papers.title: Disruption of Lipid Sorting and Endosomal Transport in Cyclodextrin-mediated Cytotoxicity
papers.abstract: Cyclodextrins (CDs) are widely used as pharmaceutical excipients, yet their systemic use is constrained by cytotoxic effects that remain incompletely understood. While β-cyclodextrins are commonly associated with cholesterol extraction, it remains unclear whether this mechanism alone explains their biological activity. Here, we investigate the effects of native and modified CDs in human renal proximal tubule cells using complementary imaging, flow cytometry, and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Distinct, host-dependent responses were observed. α-Cyclodextrin induced rapid membrane disruption at elevated concentrations, whereas methylated β-cyclodextrin (Meβ-CD) produced a progressive phenotype characterized by increased membrane permeability, impaired lipid internalization, and reduced cell proliferation under sub-lethal conditions. Despite these differences, both Meβ-CD and γ-cyclodextrin enhanced cholesterol internalization without evidence of immediate depletion, indicating modulation of endogenous transport processes. In contrast, Meβ-CD selectively disrupted membrane lipid uptake and altered extracellular lipid composition, yielding vesicle fractions enriched in cholesterol esters and ceramides but depleted in phosphoinositides. These findings support a model in which cyclodextrins perturb phosphoinositide-dependent lipid trafficking pathways, providing a mechanistic link between altered lipid distribution and cytotoxic response, and informing the design of safer CD-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Making messy biophysical measurements computable: an open layer that standardizes and quality-checks bioactivity data, validated against expert curators
papers.abstract: Background. Machine-learning models for proteins increasingly train on large, pooled collections of laboratory measurements-binding affinities such as IC50, Ki, Kd and EC50 (numbers that describe how tightly a molecule binds its target), togetherwith biophysical readouts from techniques such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), bio-layer interferometry (BLI) and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). These measurements arrive in different units, from different assay formats, fitted with different models, and at different levels of quality. Pooling them without care injects substantial noise. The per-record quality flags that some databases attach are incomplete, and they do not travel with the data once records from several sources are combined. What has been missing is an open, model-agnostic layer that turns raw measurements into records a downstream pipeline can consume directly: unit-normalized, quality-checked, and carrying their own uncertainty and provenance. What we built. biophys_interop is an open Python toolkit and data schema. It maps any supportedmeasurement to a single canonical record spanning 24 measurement types (modalities), converts units to a common standard, and runs a registry of 72 deterministic, method-aware quality-control (QC) rules. Every rule cites a reason from the measurement literature, recommends a concrete action, and returns a simple pass / warn / fail flag together with a calibrated uncertainty. The library is small and has few dependencies. We are deliberate about what our validation does and does not cover: two broadly applicable affinity rules (a plausible-value-range rule and an exact-duplicate rule) are tested at scale against an independent curator’s labels; the remaining method-specific biophysical rules are offered as a literaturegrounded, executable registry-useful and auditable, but not claimed as validated here, because no public database publishes the per-record ground-truth flags that would be needed to score them. Results. Using ChEMBL’s own data_validity_comment and potential_duplicate annotations as an independent ground truth, transparent rules on the standardized record reproduce two of ChEMBL’s three curator flag families on 175,387 held-out records across 30 human targets, with no trained model (value-range rule: Matthews correlation coefficient [MCC] 0.61; duplicate rule: MCC 0.65). The thresholds transfer cleanly to a completely separate set of targets (train on 15, test on 15 disjoint targets; 88,443 held-out records; MCC 0.73 and 0.64). Going beyond the curator, the layer flags 929 internally inconsistent records that ChEMBL did not flag, and a comparison against the independent BindingDB database exposes 38 disagreements of 100-fold or more, 89% of them unmarked by either database. A domain expert who checked a 24-record sample against the primary literature confirmed 16 of 24 (67%) as genuine data errors, including 11 of 12 cross-database conflicts. We reproduce the known cross-assay noise regime reported by Landrum and Riniker, and show that a comparability gate based on assay metadata more than halves the median disagreement between records (0.51-> 0.21 log units). Finally, feeding the calibrated signal into a downstreammutation-effect (ΔΔG) predictor gave no reliable improvement; we report this negative result in full. The toolkit, the rule registry, the cleaned datasets, and one-command reproduction scripts are released openly. Conclusions. Once heterogeneous public measurements share one representation, simple transparent rules can catch data problems-matching expert curators at scale on the rule families we tested, and catching errors those curators missed. The result is a reusable, auditable data layer for protein machine learning, rather than a new predictive model. Keywords: bioactivity data; data curation; quality control; ChEMBL; BindingDB; data standardization; FAIR data; machine learning; interoperability; reproducibility

papers.title: Potential for off-grid flexible production of sustainable aviation fuel in Australia
papers.abstract: offers a pathway to decarbonise the aviation sector, but off-grid systems face fundamental challenges from the intermittency of solar and wind resources. This paper develops an optimisation framework for off-grid e-SAF production integrating solar and wind generation, battery storage, proton exchange membrane electrolysis, direct air capture (DAC), and SAF synthesis. The Fischer–Tropsch (FT) and Methanol-to-Jet (MtJ) pathways are evaluated under rigid operation and then under flexible operation using a network flow model that optimises component capacities to minimise the levelized cost of production (LCOP). Process integration reduces DAC thermal demand by 77%, enabling 57–77% of DAC heat to be supplied internally. Under rigid operation, LCOP is 21.5–22.4 AUD/kg (2025), dominated by capital expenditure for renewable overcapacity and storage. Flexible operation reduces LCOP by approximately 50% to 10.2–10.6 AUD/kg, with MtJ exhibiting superior operational flexibility due to liquid methanol storage that decouples upstream electrolysis from downstream synthesis. Spatial analysis across Australia identifies Albany, Leigh Creek, and Barcaldine as the most cost-effective sites (LCOP 10.2–11.1 AUD/kg), with high-quality co-located solar and wind resources being the key determinant of economic viability. Both pathways achieve net-negative greenhouse gas emissions (–122 and–94 gCO2e/MJ for FT and MtJ, respectively) when electricity carbon intensity falls below 0.1 kg CO2e/kWh. These findings demonstrate that flexible operation, process integration, and strategic site selection can enable off-grid e-SAF production to approach cost parity with conventional aviation fuels.

papers.title: Preparation and Soil Degradation Behavior of Additive-Free Chitosan Films for Biodegradable Food Packaging
papers.abstract: Chitosan is a renewable, biodegradable, and intrinsically antimicrobial alternative to petroleumbased packaging, but most chitosan films contain plasticizers or cross-linkers that complicate foodcontact safety and end-of-life disposal. Here, additive-free films were prepared from chitosan, water, and near-stoichiometric acetic acid. A 128 cP grade at 2.0% (w/v) provided the best castability. Single-step drying (55 ℃/6 h) and two-step drying (55 ℃/6 h followed by 120 ℃/0.5 h) were compared. The second step reduced residual chitosan–acetate-associated mass loss and produced a stiffer film (elongation at break, 11.9 ± 1.4%; elastic modulus, 351.7 ± 56.4 MPa) than the more extensible single-step film (43.2 ± 2.8%; 251.1 ± 19.1 MPa). Both films were water-insoluble, enzymatically degradable, and lost 17.7–21.9% of their dry mass after 28 days in lysozymecontaining buffer. A non-destructive transparent-pot soil assay allowed one specimen to span airexposed, enclosed-air, and soil-contact zones. Both films disintegrated completely within 60 days only in direct soil contact, whereas the air-exposed and enclosed-air regions remained intact for 180 days. This within-specimen design directly visualized soil-contact-driven degradation without specimen retrieval. In a preliminary apple-wrapping trial, the film reduced browning and dehydration relative to unwrapped controls. Drying protocol therefore provides an additive-free route to mechanically distinct chitosan films for flexible or semi-rigid packaging applications. Keywords: Chitosan film; biodegradable packaging; drying protocol; soil biodegradation 1. Introduction Petroleum-derived plastic packaging is one of the most persistent forms of environmental pollution, with several hundred million tons of plastic produced annually and only a small fraction recovered through recycling or composting [1,2]. Food packaging accounts for a large share of this waste stream, and its short service life relative to the multi-decade persistence of conventional polyolefins in the environment has intensified the search for biodegradable alternatives derived from renewable resources [3,32]. Among the biopolymers considered for this purpose, chitosan is one of the most extensively studied because it is abundant, non-toxic, film-forming, and intrinsically antimicrobial [4,5,7,25]. Cast chitosan films are transparent, provide a useful oxygen barrier, and have been explored as edible coatings and stand-alone packaging materials for fruit, meat, and bakery products [6,8,9,10].

papers.title: Electromigration allowing deviations from electroneutrality: Formation of solitons
papers.abstract: The electroneutrality condition, or electroneutrality assumption, states that positively and negatively charged ions in an electrolyte solution balance each other, such that the total net electrical charge is zero. There is, however, an exception: the diffuse layer of the electrical double layer when the wall surface carries a fixed electric charge. This situation is common in capillary electrophoresis, where it gives rise to electroosmotic flow, and is also important at the surfaces of colloidal particles, in porous media, in membranes, and in biological ion channels. This paper describes a further mechanism for generating space charge and, consequently, deviation from electroneutrality. The charge is generated by applying an external driving potential across a separation channel filled with plugs of electrolyte solutions at different concentrations. The phenomenon was investigated using a mathematical model based on the Poisson and Nernst–Planck equations. One-dimensional simulations of sodium chloride solutions demonstrated the dependence of the magnitude and polarity of the generated charge on the applied voltage. The model was subsequently extended to a twodimensional axisymmetric geometry and coupled with the Navier–Stokes equations to account for liquid flow. Simulations of Alizarin Red S solutions showed that the space-charge cloud can detach from the concentration boundary. It is “sucked out” from the concentration boundary, moves ahead of it, and forms a localized soliton structure through the interaction of Coulombic forces and hydrodynamic flow. Experimental observations in a polydimethylsiloxane microfluidic channel confirmed the predicted shape and movement of the concentration boundary. These results demonstrate that externally driven electromigration can produce mobile regions of space charge and local deviations from electroneutrality.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Photo-Induced Bond Dissociation of A NPIM Derivative: A Case Study on Quantum Spin-Manipulation for Efficient Uncaging
papers.abstract: Photolabile protecting groups (PPGs) are indispensable tools for spatiotemporally controlled release of reactive functional groups. Recently, we proposed a quantum spin-manipulation (QSM-1) strategy that employs triplet ground-state cations to render ion-pair recombination spin-forbidden, thereby enhancing the uncaging quantum yield. In this study, the photodissociation mechanism of a 2-(4-nitrophenyl)-1H-indole-3-ylmethyl (NPIM) photocage bearing a benzoate leaving group was investigated to evaluate the effectiveness of a triplet excited-state-mediated QSM pathway (QSM-2). Spectroscopic analyses revealed that the excited state of NPIM possesses a relatively small singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔEST = 5.3 kcal mol–1), enabling efficient intersystem crossing (ISC) from the intramolecular charge-transfer singlet excited state to the triplet excited state. Oxygen-quenching experiments demonstrated that photodissociation proceeds predominantly from the triplet excited state. Time-resolved absorption spectroscopy identified the singlet excited state (τ = 1.6 ns), triplet excited state (τ = 2.3 μs), and NPIM radical intermediate (τ = 1.5 ms). In situ infrared analysis directly detected benzoic acid, an oxidized NPIM product, and CO2 generated from the benzoyl radical, supporting a homolytic bond-cleavage mechanism. Ultrafast time-resolved infrared spectroscopy of the NPIM chromophore revealed formation of a twisted intramolecular charge-transfer state that promotes ISC by reducing ΔEST. Density functional theory calculations further indicate that C–O bond homolysis from the triplet excited state is energetically feasible and is driven by relief of excited-state antiaromaticity. These results establish that uncaging of NPIM derivatives proceeds through triplet-state homolysis and demonstrate the validity of the QSM-2 strategy for designing efficient photochemical release systems.

papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of an Anthocyanin-Sensitized TiO2 Solar Cell
papers.abstract: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using natural organic photo-sensitizers offer a cost-effective, eco-friendly alternative to conventional silicon photovoltaics. In this study, an organic DSSC was fabricated using unpurified raspberry anthocyanin extract (predominantly cyanidin-3-O-sophoroside and cyanidin-3-glucoside) deposited onto a nanocrystalline titanium dioxide (TiO2) thin film with an iodide/triiodide redox electrolyte shuttle. Under halogen light illumination, the cell yielded an overall energy conversion efficiency of 0.00235%, consistent with the hypothesis of < 1% efficiency. Characterization across eight color filters showed the highest percentage of short-circuit current under yellow (69.6%) and orange (68.8%) filters, due to the incandescent source’s thermal emission spectrum as modeled by Wien’s approximation of Planck’s law. Furthermore, photon flux measurements revealed that short-circuit current scales linearly with incident illuminance due to photon-limited electron injection, whereas open-circuit voltage exhibits a weak logarithmic relation. Limitations on overall conversion efficiency were identified as semiconductor film thickness (45 µm), source heat dissipation, and competitive surface binding by non-photoactive impurities.

papers.title: Aggregation of porous organic cryptophane cages and xenon-aggregate interactions in aqueous media: Implications for host-guest chemistry and hyperpolarized 129Xe NMR biosensing
papers.abstract: Molecular self-assembly and aggregation are ubiquitous phenomena in supramolecular and host-guest chemistry, particularly in aqueous media. Aggregation of host molecules affects guest binding and spectroscopic properties of the system. Porous organic cryptophane (Cry) cages are the gold standard for xenon capture in hyperpolarized 129 Xe NMR biosensors (XBS). Despite the Cry structure being hydrophobic and aromatic, both of which promote aggregation, the XBS field has so far mostly considered monomeric (isolated) Xe@cage systems where two-site Xe exchange occurs only between the cage and the solvent environments. With this in mind, I have performed large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of water-soluble Cry cages and free Xe atoms in aqueous conditions to study Cry aggregation and Xe-aggregate interactions at the molecular level. The simulations predict aggregation that depends strongly on the number of hydrophilic groups on the cages, with cages having fewer such groups aggregating more. Aromatic π-π interactions between the cages are found to play an important role in the aggregation. Analysis of Xe interactions with the largest observed Cry aggregate revealed hitherto unreported solvent-exposed and buried Xe binding sites with Xe residence times of more than a hundred nanoseconds. These findings suggest that aggregation of cryptophanes and other porous organic cages should be considered in their host-guest chemistry and applications. In particular, the validity of the commonly assumed two-site Xe exchange model in the XBS field should be carefully assessed in the presence of aggregation.

papers.title: Leveraging the collective knowledge of fragmented multimodal datasets by aligning representations
papers.abstract: Chemists often use different formats and modalities to describe the same polymers (e.g., PSMILES, BigSMILES, systematic names), molecules (e.g., SMILES, 1H NMR, IR), and materials (e.g., MOFid, pXRD, crystal structures). This fragmentation makes it challenging to leverage all available data using classical machine learning approaches. To address this, we developed ChemFuse, a contrastive learning-based approach to align fragmented data representations into a shared embedding space. ChemFuse’s aligned embeddings allow us to combine data from multiple sources to improve downstream predictive models by increasing the amount and diversity of the training data. The model performance improves by 44.7% for polymers (aligning PSMILES and BigSMILES), 44.7% for molecules (aligning SMILES and 1H NMR), and 44.6% for MOFs (aligning

papers.title: First-principles analysis of the metal-free H2 dissociation mechanism by semiquinone radicals in mitochondrial Complex I and III
papers.abstract: Although molecular hydrogen (H2) ameliorates a wide range of pathological conditions, how animal cells, which lack the metal hydrogenases that dissociate the nonpolar, exceptionally strong H–H bond, activate H2 has remained unresolved. Using first-principles calculations (unrestricted B3LYP-D3BJ/def2-SVP/CPCM) on active-site clusters of the Complex I Q-chamber (PDB 7QSK) and the Complex III Qo site (PDB 1PP9), we examined whether semiquinone can dissociate H2 in the buried, low-dielectric enzyme interior. At both sites the anionic semiquinone Q•- had no pathway for cleaving H–H, and only the neutral QH•, protonated by nearby residues, opened a homolytic hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) pathway with a well-defined transition state and a bound product. The spin density on the transferring hydrogen shifts continuously from nearly 0 in the reactant to +0.99 for free H•, confirming at the electronic level a true homolytic HAT, neither proton nor hydride transfer. The reaction energies (+23 to +30 kcal/mol) agree with a bond-dissociation-free-energy (BDFE) comparison showing QH• to be a spin-allowed hydrogenatom abstractor about 30 kcal/mol superior to superoxide, and thus central to the reaction. However, this reactive QH• arises only under hyper-reductive pressure, where quinone-pool overreduction and a high membrane potential coincide to occupy and protonate the buried semiquinone site; H2 dissociation is therefore established only when this hyper-reductive-pressure reaction-site environment is present, as a necessary condition. Because H2 has among the strongest σ bonds, the barrier is high and sharp, and quantum tunnelling is required for the reaction to proceed at body temperature. Crossover-temperature analysis places Complex I (316.9 K) on the tunnelling-dominated side and Complex III (255 K) on the thermal side, so the two sites straddle body temperature, with a predicted primary kinetic isotope effect of kH/kD ≈ 6–7. The Marcus inverted region we previously observed in solution is an experimental fingerprint of this tunnelling. Together, these results reframe H2 medicine from classical antioxidant scavenging to a quantum-tunnelling-assisted, reductive-pressure-conditioned conditional hydrogenase activity, and position it within quantum biology.

papers.title: Atroposelective Pd(0)-Catalyzed Direct Intermolecular C–H Arylation of Thiazole N-Oxides Provides Access to Heterobiaryls
papers.abstract: Despite the importance of heteroaryl atropisomers in medicinal chemistry and catalysis, straightforward access to these motifs via direct enantioselective C-H heteroaryl-aryl coupling remains challenging. We report an enantioselective Pd(0)-catalyzed arylation at the C4 position of thiazole N -oxides forging the critical atropochiral axis. A designer point- and axially chiral monodentate phosphine is instrumental to enable high reactivities along with a tight stereocontrol. A broad combination of substrates is coupled in high enantioselectivities, including two different heteroarenes. The enantioenriched thiazole N -oxides are amenable to derivatizations around the substituents contributing to stability of the chiral axis, including a reduction of the N -oxide moiety without racemization.

papers.title: Samarium-Driven Vacancy Engineering in CeO2/Ru(0001) Inverse Catalysts
papers.abstract: Ceria-based inverse catalysts derive their functionality from Ce 3+ –oxygen vacancy chemistry, yet strategies to deliberately control vacancy formation and distribution at metal–oxide interfaces remain limited. Here, we demonstrate that aliovalent samarium doping provides a direct and tunable route to vacancy engineering in the prototypical CeO 2 /Ru(0001) inverse catalyst. Using real-time, nanometerresolved low-energy electron microscopy in combination with low-energy electron micro-diffraction, Xray absorption spectroscopy in photoemission electron microscopy, and density functional theory, we directly correlate lattice structure, oxidation state, and vacancy formation under reducing conditions. Sm incorporation generates extrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are accompanied by Ce 3+ formation, which induces a pronounced lattice expansion that in turn fosters the formation of additional intrinsic oxygen vacancies, substantially enhancing reducibility and stabilizing reduced ceria phases relative to undoped CeO 2 . The doped system exhibits accelerated reduction kinetics, ordered intrinsic vacancy formation, and modified phase-transition behavior. By establishing how aliovalent dopants govern the vacancy landscape and redox response in inverse ceria catalysts, this work provides atomic-level mechanistic insight and concrete design principles for engineering reducible oxides at metal–oxide interfaces with tailored redox properties.

papers.title: Efficiency and Accessibility Are Not Enough: Chemical-Validity Filtering in High-Throughput Screening of Organic Photovoltaic Materials
papers.abstract: Descriptor-based screening for organic photovoltaics ranks molecules on computed properties such as frontier-orbital energies and synthetic accessibility, but such descriptors do not test whether a highly ranked molecule is a chemically sensible material. We screened 17,458 molecules from the PubChemQC database using PCESAScore—Scharber-model efficiency minus the RDKit synthetic-accessibility score—and examined what the metric actually returns. Seven molecules cross the viability threshold, but three are not organic semiconductors (molecular oxygen, a magnesium carbonate salt, a quinhydrone cocrystal) and three more carry reactive groups (two azides, one nitroso). A transparent chemicalvalidity filter and a reactive-group screen reduce the viable set from seven to four to a single stable candidate. The top-ranked molecule, an azidotriazine, reaches a 36.1% nominal efficiency—above the Scharber model’s single-junction ceiling—from a 0.91 eV gap, and carries a 9.26 D dipole and a negative computed reorganization energy: signatures of an unusable material, not a lead. Across the dataset, heteroatom composition correlates only weakly with orbital energies (|r| ≤ 0.34), so no simple design rule holds. Descriptor-based materials screens require an explicit chemical-validity and stability gate; the gap between the pre-and post-gate viable sets is a result in itself.

papers.title: Photoswitchable Carbon Nanohoops with Light-Controlled Fullerene Recognition and Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: Cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) are among the most versatile carbon nanohoops for fullerene recognition. However, their structural, electronic, and host-guest properties are fixed by molecular composition. Here, we introduce a different concept by incorporation of a diarylethene (DAE) photoswitch into the CPP framework, thereby transforming a static carbon nanohoop into a light-responsive supramolecular host. DFT calculations reveal that photoisomerization of the incorporated DAE unit reversibly expands the nanohoop cavity by approximately 1 Å, enabling light-controlled switching of fullerene selectivity among C 60 , C 70 , and C 84 . Beyond structural changes, photoisomerization also reorganizes the electronic structure and excited-state properties of the host-guest complexes. Ring closure introduces a previously inaccessible DAE-centered charge-transfer (CT) state in addition to the conventional CPP-to-fullerene CT pathway. Although this new CT state is strongly stabilized in polar media, electron-transfer kinetics indicate that rapid charge recombination limits its population, whereas the conventional CT state remains long-lived. These findings demonstrate that incorporation of a DAE photoswitch enables reversible control over cavity size, guest selectivity, exciton localization, and electron-transfer dynamics, yielding adaptive, stimuli-responsive carbon nanohoops with broad potential in photoactive materials.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Genomic Prediction, High-Throughput Phenotyping and Climate-Adaptive Breeding In Maize and Rice: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: Climate change is intensifying abiotic stresses such as drought and heat, posing significant threats to global food security and the productivity of staple crops including maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.). Conventional breeding approaches are often constrained by the complex genetic architecture of stress-adaptive traits and lengthy breeding cycles, highlighting the need for more efficient, data-driven strategies. This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for genomic prediction, high-throughput phenotyping (HTP), and climate-adaptive breeding in maize and rice. We discuss the applications of machine learning architectures, including multilayer perceptron (MLP), convolutional neural networks (CNN), random forest (RF), deep neural networks (DNN), gradient boosting methods, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), in improving genomic selection and capturing complex genotype–environment interactions. The review further explores the integration of AI with HTP technologies, including autonomous robotic platforms, drones, hyperspectral imaging, and LiDAR, to enable rapid, accurate, and non-destructive phenotypic assessment. In addition, we examine the role of AI-driven predictive models in identifying stress-responsive genes, improving trait prediction, and accelerating the development of climate-resilient crop varieties. Current challenges, including data heterogeneity, computational demands, model interpretability, and biological validation, are also discussed alongside emerging solutions such as multi-view learning, transfer learning, and intelligent precision design breeding. Overall, the convergence of AI, ML, multi-omics, and advanced phenotyping technologies represents a transformative framework for next-generation crop improvement, offering new opportunities to accelerate sustainable breeding programs and strengthen global food security under changing climatic conditions.

papers.title: Dual-Responsive Organic Sensor for Hydroxyl Radical and Hypochlorite: A Synthetic Approach to Cellular Monitoring
papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) mediate essential cellular processes; immune defense, redox signaling, and apoptosis; yet their overproduction drives oxidative stress implicated in cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, cancer, and diabetes. Because individual ROS species differ fundamentally in reactivity, half-life, and biological target, accurate diagnosis of oxidative pathology requires tools capable of discriminating between specific species rather than detecting global oxidative burden. Hydroxyl radical (•OH) and hypochlorite (ClO−) represent an especially challenging pairing: •OH is one of the most potent and non-selective oxidants, reacting at near-diffusion-controlled rates with numerous biomolecules, while ClO− is an abundant immune effector whose dysregulation drives inflammatory pathology. Despite their cooccurrence in oxidative stress contexts, limited small-molecule fluorescent probes have demonstrated selective, mechanistically orthogonal responses to both species within a single low-molecular-weight scaffold in live cells. Here we report PHVN, a coumarin–phenothiazine conjugate bearing a vinyl ester linker, rationally designed to exploit the distinct chemistries of these two oxidants: selective oxidation of the phenothiazine sulfur to a sulfoxide by ClO− disrupts intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and produces a ratiometric blue-shifted emission (610 → 480 nm), while radical addition of •OH across the electron-rich vinyl alkene causes concentration-dependent fluorescence quenching. PHVN exhibits a hypochlorite detection limit of 13.5 nM with a response time under 20 seconds, a hydroxyl radical detection limit of 36.7 μM, and excellent photostability with no visible decay under continuous excitation for an hour. The probe shows negligible cross-reactivity toward a broad panel of competing ROS, biologically relevant metal ions, and endogenous thiols. Critically, PHVN readily permeates live mouse bone marrow cells without appreciable cytotoxicity and reports concentration-dependent, spectrally distinct responses to exogenous ClO− and •OH by flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy, establishing its potential for intracellular ROS monitoring under biologically relevant conditions.

papers.title: Planck Blackbody Radiation and Its Free Electron Model in Potential Box
papers.abstract: Regarding the essential issue of the oscillator in Planck's blackbody thermal radiation, the free electron model (FEM) in potential box has been proposed. The results of nonlinear curve fitting have shown that FEM can describe the intensity distribution of the blackbody thermal radiation and their peak wavelength relationship ( λ m T =2945 mm‧K) is basically consistent to Wien displacement law, which indicates that Planck's thermal radiation originates from the transition of electrons in the high-energy level to the low-energy level in the model.

papers.title: Efficient and Accurate Ligand Strain Calculations in Solution with the AIMNet2 Neural Network Potential
papers.abstract: Conformational strain, the energy a ligand pays to adopt its bound conformation, contributes to binding affinity but is routinely misestimated. The standard estimate references a single gasphase energy minimum, which ignores solvent and mishandles charged ligands, whose intramolecular electrostatics collapse in vacuo into compact minima that deflate the unbound reference and inflate the apparent strain. We introduce AIMNet2-CPCM, a neural network potential trained to B97-3c energies and forces in a conductor-like continuum solvent (CPCM) that treats neutral and charged species on the same footing. Because inference is GPU-batched, it makes a solvated global-minimum search, and with it a solvation- and charge-aware strain calculation, practical across an entire structure-based screening library. Across ~8K PDB ligands the solvated strain has a median of 4.0 kcal/mol and rises with net charge; the trend is well determined through net charge -2, while the -3 and -4 polyanions that dominate the high-strain tail, where continuum solvation is least reliable, are reported as upper bounds. A classical force field follows the neutral strains but overstates the charged ones, because, like any gas-phase method, it collapses the charged unbound minimum that solvent screening keeps open. The strain values show no dependence on crystal resolution and accumulate across many small torsional changes rather than one large rotation. Profiling at this scale further shows that the same ligand strains very differently across the targets that bind it, so AIMNet2-CPCM not only brings solvationand charge-aware strain to screening scale but recasts ligand conformational strain as a property of the specific bound pose rather than a transferable molecular descriptor.

papers.title: SurfPro2: a relational database, curation workflow and repository of surfactant physicochemical data
papers.abstract: Access to diverse, well-curated experimental data remains a major challenge in chemistry, underpinning applications ranging from machine learning (ML) and molecular discovery to data-driven scientific understanding. While several repositories provide chemical structures, biological activities and reaction data, comprehensive and maintainable databases of surfactant physicochemical properties remain limited. Here, we present SurfPro2, a relational database, curation workflow and repository of surfactant physicochemical data. SurfPro2 combines manually curated source data, a transparent processing pipeline and explicit provenance tracking to create a reproducible and queryable resource for surfactant science. The database contains 6898 measurements describing 1624 compounds from 328 literature sources, including critical micelle concentration (CMC), air-water surface tension at CMC (γ CMC ), surfactant efficiency (C 20 ), surface pressure at CMC (Π CMC ), minimum molecular area (A min ) and maximum surface excess concentration (Γ max ). Measurements span temperatures from 5 to 65 °C and nine experimental methods. In this article, we describe the construction of SurfPro2 and demonstrate how its relational design enables analysis of temperature dependent behaviour, measurement uncertainty and reproducible extraction of ML-ready datasets. SurfPro2 provides a pipeline linking data curation to dataset generation under a FAIR framework, forming a template for long-term maintenance, reuse and aggregation of surfactant property data.

papers.title: Shear viscosity of liquid Pb–Bi: a near-degenerate alloy test of the static Rice–Allnatt description
papers.abstract: The Bretonnet–Silbert (BS) pseudopotential, with linearised Weeks–Chandler–Andersen (LWCA) perturbation theory and Rice–Allnatt (RA) transport theory, is a static, pairwise route to the magnitude of the shear viscosity of liquid sp metals. We use the miscible Pb–Bi alloy as a composition-axis test of this static description, over 21 compositions (xBi = 0–1) within 500–1200K, benchmarked against the Assael and Guzachev measurements. Because Pb and Bi have nearly equal hard-sphere diameters (σBi/σPb = 0.983), the alloy is near-degenerate: mixing adds cross correlations and a composition degree of freedom. The temperature-gradient deficit found for the pure metals, a calculated |dη/dT | too small by about a factor of two over the physical single-phase window (900–1200K) and up to a factor of three once the sub-liquidus formal extrapolations are included, is not relaxed along this composition axis, so within this framework the single-component approximation does not by itself supply the missing slope. The binary three-pair RA sum collapses onto the effective single-component route to within 0.27%, and a eutectic Ornstein–Zernike calculation with a Malijevský–Lab́ık bridge narrows the deficit by only a few percent. The soft-tail fraction ηs/η = 0.53–0.58, a common fixed-cutoff diagnostic, is nearly composition-independent. The pipeline captures the order of magnitude and the monotonic composition background of η(xBi) but does not reproduce the experimental non-monotonicity, which the source attributes to a metastable melt microheterogeneity outside the equilibrium closures tested here. Because the near-degeneracy makes the binary structural corrections intrinsically small, the test bounds the single-component approximation for this chemically similar pair rather than for alloys in general. It adds composition-axis evidence to the prior interpretation that the missing temperature dependence is consistent with a dynamic contribution beyond the static description.

papers.title: Mapping the Polymer-to-Ceramic Design Space: A Retrieval-Augmented Meta-Analysis of Preceramic Polymer Architecture and Microstructural Evolution
papers.abstract: Polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) offer a molecular-to-microstructure design pathway unavailable through powder processing, yet the quantitative relationships between preceramic polymer architecture and ceramic properties remain scattered across four decades of literature spanning polymer chemistry and ceramic science journals. Here we present a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assisted meta-analysis of the PDC field. A domain-specific natural language processing pipeline was deployed against a curated, multi-tier corpus of 949 peer-reviewed publications to extract structured descriptors across eleven categories covering the full polymerto-ceramic transformation pathway, from backbone architecture and molecular weight through pyrolysis conditions to phase composition and mechanical properties. Extraction accuracy was validated against expert annotation on a 30-paper pilot set (89% phrase recall, < 2% false extraction). The analysis reveals stark reporting asymmetries within the 772-paper PDC tier: microstructural phase (87% of papers) and pyrolysis conditions (77%) are well documented, while elemental composition (34%) and molecular weight (16%) are systematically omitted. No paper reports crosslink density as a number with physical units. We map the dominant polymer families through their pyrolysis transformations to SiOC, SiC, and SiCN phases, quantify consensus processing windows (median pyrolysis temperature of 1200 °C; median ceramic yields of 75 wt%), and identify contradictions the literature has not resolved, including the effect of heating rate on yield. Notably, the corpus is too sparse in linear-precursor data (n = 20) to test even the foundational hypothesis that backbone architecture controls ceramic yield (Mann-Whitney p = 0.26; 80% power only for yield differences ≥ 10 wt%). Cross-tier comparison with conventional ceramics localizes where PDCs reach property parity and where gaps persist. The resulting descriptor landscape provides a quantitative foundation for standardized reporting and for machine-learning-driven design of preceramic polymers.

papers.title: Revisiting the Vibrational Force Field of Matrix-Isolated
papers.abstract: The 17-e anion, [Fe(CO) 4 ] - , was first characterised in 1981 by Breeze et al 1 . We subsequently challenged their interpretation 2 , suggesting that they had produced [Fe(CO) 3 ] - . In the light of new calculations here, we withdraw that view. We confirm that has the structure (as previously reported) and we have calculated the following, new, energy-factored force constants: k 1 = 1437.2 k 2 = 1456.2 k 11 = 48.6 k 12 = 47.7 where k 1 refers to the three chemically identical equatorial CO groups and k 2 refers to the sole axial CO group ( k 11 and k 12 are the CO,CO interaction constants). This force field is significantly different from that originally proposed.

papers.title: BraggCalculator
papers.abstract: Powder diffraction maps an atomic structure to an experimentally familiar fingerprint. Simulating that fingerprint is therefore a routine step in phase identification, structure screening, refinement, and machinelearning workflows. BraggCalculator is a Python package that simulates ideal, monochromatic powder X-ray and neutron diffraction from periodic crystals. It accepts CIF files and structures from pymatgen or the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE), and returns indexed reflections, powder lines, or broadened profiles in scattering angle or momentum transfer. A NumPy backend provides a lightweight CPU path, while an optional PyTorch backend supports automatic differentiation and accelerator execution. Install the released package from PyPI with: `python -m pip install braggcalculator`. Source code, documentation, examples, and the reproducibility material for this paper are available at: https://github.com/FrederikLizakJohansen/BraggCalculator

papers.title: Rhamnolipid Biosurfactant for All-Green-Solvent-Processed Perovskite Solar Modules
papers.abstract: Physical properties and toxicity of solvents remain barriers to scalable manufacturing of perovskite solar modules. In blade coating of thin films, solution viscosity and surface tension govern meniscus stability and wet-film quality. However, conventional green solvents for perovskite deposition, such as dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), exhibit high viscosity and surface tension, hindering large-area film formation. Here, we report a bio-derived rhamnolipid (RL) surfactant with dual functionality: it reduces solution surface tension to improve coating uniformity; it also interacts with DMSO to facilitate its removal during air quenching and thermal annealing. This regulates perovskite crystallization kinetics and passivates interfacial defects, enabling compact less-defective largearea perovskite films. As a result, we report 10.23 cm2 perovskite solar minimodules which achieve power conversion efficiency of 20.8% and retain up to 73.3% of initial efficiency after 940 h of maximum power point tracking. The biosurfactant strategy contributes towards scalable and environmentally responsible manufacturing of perovskite solar modules.

papers.title: Porous Organic Cages: CC1 as a Blueprint for Molecular Design, Structure–Property Relationships, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Porous materials such as inorganic porous materials, hybrid nanoparticles, metalorganic frameworks, porous organic polymers, metal organic polyhedral, and porous organic cages have attracted significant attention due to their diverse applications in gas storage, molecular separation, sensing and catalysis. Among them, porous organic cages (POCs) have emerged as an important class of discrete porous materials that combine permanent intrinsic cavities, solution processability, structural tunability, and diverse functional properties. Among the various cage architectures reported to date, CC1 represents one of the earliest and most influential systems, providing fundamental insights into the molecular design, assembly, porosity, and functional behavior of porous organic cages. Beyond its role as an individual cage structure, CC1 has served as a conceptual platform for understanding the relationships between molecular architectures, crystal packing, pore accessibility, and material performance that underpin the broader development of the POC field. This review examines CC1 as a blueprint for the design and evolution of porous organic cages. We discuss the synthetic strategies and dynamic covalent chemistry that enable cage formation, the structural features governing intrinsic and extrinsic porosity, and the characterization methods used to elucidate cage architecture and solid-state behavior. Particular emphasis is placed on the design principles derived from CC1 that have guided the development of subsequent generations of cages with enhanced stability, functionality, and performance. The roles of CC1 and related cages in gas storage and separation, molecular recognition, sensing, catalysis, membrane technologies, and porous liquids are critically evaluated, highlighting how molecular-level modifications influence macroscopic properties. Furthermore, we compare CC1 with representative advanced cage systems to identify emerging trends in pore engineering, functionalization, and application-driven design. Current challenges, including scalability, structural robustness, processability, and industrial implementation, are discussed alongside recent advances in computational screening, datadriven materials discovery, and machine-learning-assisted cage design. By positioning CC1 within the broader context of porous organic cage research, this review provides a framework for understanding the evolution of the field and offers perspectives for the rational development of next-generation porous molecular materials.

papers.title: Total Synthesis of Piperhancin B and Isofutoquinol
papers.abstract: We report the first total synthesis of piperhancin B, a natural neolignan exhibiting promising nitric oxide production inhibitory activity. Remarkably, this natural product possesses a highly strained housane structure, which constitutes a huge synthetic challenge. Our synthesis is inspired by the biogenetic hypothesis for this natural product, and involves a key [2+2]-cycloaddition promoted by a photosensitizer. The precursor of this biomimetic step is obtained via an organometallic addition between an alkenyl lithium fragment and a quinone monoacetal, allowing to assemble both propylbenzene units. The power of this approach lies in the possibility of slightly modifying the organometallic fragment in order to reach different structures. This way, the total synthesis of isofutoquinol A was also achieved, and this work paves the way to the synthesis and evaluation of other analogues.

papers.title: Continuous UV-Spectroscopic Interrogation of Enzymes Processing Phosphorylated Intermediates Through Modular Reaction Networks
papers.abstract: Phosphorylated intermediates are ubiquitous across primary and secondary metabolism, yet continuous and versatile assay systems for the interrogation of the enzymes that use them are underdeveloped. To address this gap, we developed a system for P hosphate detection by S ucrose phosphorolysis, I somerization and oxidation, the PSI (or Ψ) module. In contrast to existing assays, Ψ provides a continuous UV-based read-out at neutral pH in different buffer systems and can readily be incorporated into longer reaction sequences to assay a variety of different enzymes of interest. We herein describe the development of Ψ and demonstrate the utility of an optimized variant for the interrogation of prenyltransferases, isomerases, and kinases.

papers.title: Photochemical Induction of Trion-based Polaritons in Quasi-1D Inorganic Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Strong coupling between optical cavity modes and excitons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) has attracted considerable interest due to its potential applications in nanophotonics and nonlinear optical technologies. Owing to their high refractive index, TMD systems sustain optical cavity modes that strongly couple with excitons to form exciton-polaritons. However, trion-based polaritonic states under ambient conditions without external cavities remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the photochemical induction and stabilization of exciton-trion-polaritons (ETPs) in multiwalled WS2 nanotubes (NTs) through the combined effects of nanotube diameter, light excitation, and chemical hole scavenging. Large WS2 NTs (~100 nm, NTs-I) support internal cavity modes and pronounced exciton-polariton (EP) coupling, under strong-light excitation, which promotes trion formation due to the intrinsic n-type character of WS2. Potassium iodide (KI) suppresses electron-hole recombination and stabilizes trion populations through efficient hole scavenging. Consequently, distinct low-, medium-, and high-energy trion-polariton branches emerge. Control experiments using neutral-density filters, KCl, solar irradiation, and core-shell WS2@WSe2 NTs confirm the trion-mediated origin and tunability of the observed states. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals prolonged excitedstate dynamics and stabilized trion-related features in KI solution. Complementary quantum mechanical modeling, finite-difference time-domain simulations, and machine-learning-assisted analysis successfully reproduce the experimental optical response and confirm hybridization between cavity photons, excitons, and trions, with Rabi splitting reaching ~140 meV. These findings establish WS2 NTs as a versatile roomtemperature platform for tunable trion-polaritonic phenomena and open pathways for polaritonic applications in photocatalysis and renewable energy technologies.

papers.title: Which state are you converging? A spin audit of sample-based quantum diagonalization benchmarks on iron–sulfur clusters
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD/QSCI) selects determinant subspaces from quantum-circuit samples for classical diagonalization; its iron–sulfur demonstrations anchor utility-scale quantum-chemistry claims, and a recent critique disputes them at matched subspace dimension. Both sides benchmark on energy-based diagnostics, not spin identity. We introduce a rotation-invariant spin audit: exact determinant-space ⟨S²⟩, invariant S²-Gram spectra over quasi-degenerate manifolds, and higher spin moments (⟨S⁴⟩ through ⟨S⁸⟩) that bound the spin-sector decomposition, and apply it to the public [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] benchmarks, IBM's shipped qiskit-addon-sqd pipeline, and IBM's published hardware data. No audited execution returned the named singlet at competitive energy; for published states unavailable to direct audit, the energy-only records do not establish singlet identity. Classical selected-CI growth converges to a spin-contaminated attractor (⟨S²⟩ ≈ 4.7 on [2Fe-2S]); samples drawn from it preserve the contamination; spin-inversion completion permits spin symmetry without producing it; and the released [2Fe-2S] hardware samples yield no energy advantage over the uniform-random control. A scalar mean does not identify these states: two audited arms share ⟨S²⟩ ≈ 2.00, one a triplet eigenstate (Var(S²) = 3×10⁻⁶), the other a 2:1 singlet–quintet mixture whose triplet weight its third moment bounds below 10⁻⁴. At the largest published dimension (5.625×10⁷ determinants, reconstructed here from the released support), the numerically stable lowest root lies 170 mHa below the published energy at ⟨S²⟩ = 1.3711 (stable under an 18.6-fold residual tightening to 1.1% of the 0.285 mHa gap), with Var(S²) = 6.9 and first two moments excluding any decomposition confined to S ≤ 2. Near-singlet character survives only as a non-stationary superposition: selection does not commute with S². Energy-only SQD benchmarks therefore do not establish convergence to the named target state; we propose measured spin moments as a mandatory benchmark output, with spin control active rather than passive.

papers.title: Fluorescent Dyes in Image-Guided Surgery: Chemical Properties, Targeting, and Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Fluorescence-guided surgery (FGS) has emerged as a transformative intraoperative modality that enables real-time, optical visualization of target tissues to improve surgical precision and oncological outcomes. This review examines the chemical properties, targeting mechanisms, and clinical applications of fluorescent dyes currently used or under investigation in FGS. Currently, the two most clinically established agents, indocyanine green (ICG), a cyanine-based NIR fluorophore, and 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA), a porphyrin precursor using tumor-selective metabolic accumulation, are discussed alongside emerging fluorophore classes including xanthenes, BODIPYs, and oxazines, which offer superior photostability and spectral tunability. Targeting strategies are reviewed across three paradigms: passive accumulation via the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, active receptor-mediated targeting through antibody-dye conjugates such as cetuximab-IRDye800CW, and activatable probes that remain optically silent until triggered by tumor-specific enzymatic or pH conditions. Clinical applications in tumor margin detection, sentinel lymph node mapping, and vascular imaging are evaluated with reference to key clinical trials and regulatory milestones. Finally, future directions including NIR-II fluorophores, multimodal imaging agents, stimuli-responsive nanoprobes, and AI-assisted image interpretation are discussed.

papers.title: Coumarin acrylamide as a fluorescence switch-on monomer to assay kinetics of radical polymerizations and for bioimaging
papers.abstract: Radical polymerizations are among the most widely used polymer synthesis methods and have become versatile reactions for modifying living cells with bioorthogonal macromolecules and creating artificial cells.
