The simulations further suggest that trajectories reaching the conical-intersection region preferentially evolve toward planar or twisted geometries in the ground-state. Twisted conformations become more populated during the nonequilibrium dynamics in solution. These findings provide molecular-level insight into nucleobase photodynamics in the condensed phase and demonstrate the potential of the present framework for simulating excited-state dynamics in complex biological environments.

papers.title: Soft-templated carbon models elucidate the anomalous increase of capacitance in nanopores
papers.abstract: Supercapacitors are energy storage devices characterized by fast charging capabilities. The discovery of enhanced capacitance in nanoporous carbons radically challenged the understanding of their charging mechanism, sparkling the development of in situ characterization methods and computational modeling techniques. However, the microscopic origin of this effect remains debated: The importance of pore size on the capacitance put forward in the seminal study was recently questioned in a work focusing on the carbon disorder. Here we close this debate by reconciling these apparently conflicting perspectives. We demonstrate that, at fixed disorder, capacitance does indeed increase with decreasing pore size. Our conclusions are enabled by molecular dynamics simulations methodological advances, that overcome long-standing limitations and yield quantitative agreement with electrochemical measurements. By bridging the gap between earlier observations and recent interpretations, our study provides a unified framework for understanding capacitance in nanoporous materials and offers guidelines for the design of nextgeneration supercapacitors.

papers.title: Model of the Henrys: Eyring, Frank, and the Foundations for Predicting Transport Coefficients
papers.abstract: Henry Eyring’s absolute rate theory provides a microscopic picture of liquid transport based on molecular jumps, while Henry Frank’s free volume theory relates entropy changes to an effective cage volume in condensed phases. In this work, we integrate these two frameworks to obtain the Model of the Henrys (MotH), a unified description of transport phenomena based on the (re)movement of molecules within a system. Starting from Eyring’s viscosity expression, we replace vaporization energies by residual energies, and express the free volume via Frank’s entropy–free-volume relation using residual entropy. The resulting model contains a small set of molecule-specific parameters. We demonstrate that viscosity, self-diffusion coefficient, and thermal conductivity of alkanes, alcohols, carbon dioxide, and water can be described in good agreement with experimental and molecular dynamics data over wide temperature and pressure ranges. Here, the ability to describe transport properties of hydrogen bonding or polar molecules with strong intermolecular interactions like alcohols and water is a novel theoretical and practical contribution. Analysis of the fitted parameters confirms Frank’s original idea that free volume is primarily controlled by molecular size, whereas activation energies are strongly family-dependent, with associating fluids showing high activation energy. Furthermore, we show that MotH provides a theoretical foundation for empirical entropy scaling relations. Finally, we show that activation energy, free-volume, and entropy-scaling models are complementary rather than competing concepts.

papers.title: When Do Models Win? A Learning Curve Benchmark for Molecular Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes
papers.abstract: In many molecular property prediction tasks, such as drug discovery and OLED material design, labeled data are often limited to only tens to thousands of samples due to high experimental costs. Despite the rapid development of machine learning models, it remains unclear which model classes are most effective under such low-data regimes and how their performance evolves with increasing data. In this work, we present a comprehensive learning curve benchmark of molecular property prediction across a broad model suite spanning traditional machine learning, graph neural networks (GNNs), transformer-based molecular language models, SE(3)-equivariant 3D networks, descriptor-based hybrids, multi-task learning variants, and multimodal graph–sequence fusion baselines. We systematically vary the training data size from 50 to 3,000 samples and evaluate on the QM9, ESOL, Lipophilicity, and BACE datasets using scaffold splits with repeated trials for statistical robustness. Our analysis reveals four principal patterns: (1) regime-dependent model optimality — deep learning models dominate continuous physicochemical property prediction (ESOL, Lipophilicity), while kernel-based methods such as Gaussian Process Regression remain superior for bioactivity prediction (BACE) across most of the tested range, with clear crossover points emerging between traditional and deep learning approaches; (2) target-dependent benefit of 3D inductive bias — on QM9 an equivariant 3D network trained on DFT-optimized geometries performs strongly on LUMO and the HOMO–LUMO gap but struggles on HOMO despite these exact geometries, isolating a representational mismatch rather than a geometry-quality limitation; on Lipophilicity and BACE, single-conformer ETKDG inputs yield essentially flat learning curves, where weak conformer geometry and the conformer-insensitivity of these endpoints cannot be fully disentangled — though both readings point to a mismatch between single-geometry 3D models and conformer-insensitive targets; (3) non-monotonic pretraining benefit — the advantage of modern transformer and 3D foundation models (ChemBERTa-2, MoLFormer-XL, SELFormer, Uni-Mol-PT) over GNNs and fingerprints is most pronounced at intermediate training sizes on most tasks (and at the smallest on bioactivity), and neither parameter count nor pretraining-corpus size predicts downstream accuracy (the compact ChemBERTa-2 outperforms the far larger MoLFormer and SELFormer on ESOL and Lipophilicity); and (4) model selection over model averaging — in a controlled post-hoc analysis, even oracle ensembles that select their members by test-set error barely improve on the best single model in the lowest-data regime (at most +1.2% at N=50, and negative on ESOL), indicating that the dominant lever under data scarcity is choosing the right single model rather than combining several. Our findings provide actionable guidelines for model selection under data scarcity and highlight learning curve analysis as a principled tool for understanding model behavior across the property–scale plane. Scientific Contribution: This study establishes a comprehensive learning curve benchmark for molecular property prediction in low-data regimes, systematically comparing a broad suite of model families—including traditional machine learning, graph neural networks, transformer-based molecular language models, SE(3)-equivariant 3D networks, descriptor-based hybrids, multi-task learning variants, and multimodal graph–sequence fusion baselines—across four datasets spanning physicochemical, quantum mechanical, and biological activity properties. We identify regime- and target-dependent model optimality and crossover points between traditional machine learning and deep learning methods, quantify the target-dependent benefit and conformer-fidelity limits of 3D equivariant networks, and provide actionable, data-scale-aware guidelines for model selection in low-data molecular property prediction.

papers.title: Quantification of contaminants and proton exchange in garnet phase powders and their impact on Li+ transport in hybrid electrolytes
papers.abstract: Garnet-phase Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12 (LLZO) is a promising solid-state electrolyte in lithium metal batteries but suffers from contaminant formation upon exposure to ambient conditions. We use a suite of analytical methods to quantify this contamination and the resulting protonation of LLZO’s crystal structure, and their removal via heat treatment under argon. We quantify contaminant removal in 3 unique temperature regimes, one where LiOH is removed at lower temperatures (<350 o C) and two where Li 2 CO 3 is removed at intermediate (350-550 o C) and high (>550 o C) temperatures. Removal of LiOH and Li 2 CO 3 in the intermediate regime proceeds through a mechanism involving beneficial H + /Li + exchange with the LLZO lattice, whereas high temperature Li 2 CO 3 removal proceeds through the thermal decomposition mechanism of Li 2 CO 3 to evolve CO 2 and deposit solid Li 2 O. Through these quantification methods, we show that most, but not all, contaminants are removed upon heating to 800 ˚C, with 97% of the Li 2 CO 3 and 85% of the LiOH present in the as-given materials being removed. We show that heat treatment in a stagnant atmosphere is less effective than treatment under active gas flow. Relithiation of the LLZO lattice is also found to improve Li + transport across the LLZO particle interface when immersed in a Li + -bearing organic electrolyte, and the protonation of LLZO contributes more to slowing interfacial Li + transport than the presence of interfacial contaminants.

papers.title: Integrating Ion Mobility–Resolved Tandem Mass Spectrometry and Microcrystal Electron Diffraction for Structural Elucidation
DeepChem-DEL: Leveraging Chemical Foundation Models to Improve DNA-Encoded Library Modeling
papers.abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) allow screening of extremely large chemical spaces by tagging compounds with DNA barcodes. As these datasets grow in scale and complexity, machine learning has become essential for signal denoising and binder identification. In parallel, chemical foundation models pretrained on large molecular corpora have advanced the broader cheminformatics landscape by learning transferable molecular representations. However, existing tools for DEL machine learning remain fragmented, which limits systematic construction of modeling pipelines and prevents the easy integration of chemical foundation models into DEL workflows alongside classical approaches. To address these challenges in DEL modeling, we introduce DeepChem-DEL, an open-source suite of reproducible machine learning workflows for DEL modeling built on the DeepChem ecosystem. DeepChem-DEL integrates (i) a configurable denoising pipeline with (ii) modular DeepChem workflows for enrichment prediction, hit identification, and benchmarking across diverse model classes, including chemical foundation models enabled through extensions to the open-source ChemBERTa-3 framework. We evaluate DeepChem-DEL on the KinDEL and BELKA datasets, reproducing key baselines and enabling direct comparison across model classes. Our experiments demonstrate that leveraging chemical foundation models yields performance competitive with, and in several cases exceeding, previously explored approaches such as graph convolutional networks and random forest models. Together, these results establish DeepChem-DEL as a scalable and extensible platform for DEL machine learning, while highlighting the potential of chemical foundation models to advance DEL-based hit discovery.

papers.title: Portico: a program for the asymptotic classification of transition-state normal modes
papers.abstract: We present Portico (Projection Onto Roto-Translational Internal COordinates), a program for the automated classification of transition-state normal modes according to their asymptotic product character. In molecular dissociation and fragmentation, some modes that appear vibrational at the transition state evolve into rotations or translations of the product fragments. Their correct identification is essential in kinetic and statistical models that treat vibrational and roto-translational degrees of freedom separately, but current assignments often rely on visual inspection or systemspecific criteria. Portico constructs a redundant coordinate basis combining the internal vibrations of the product fragments with rigid-body translational and rotational displacement vectors evaluated at the transition-state geometry. The transition-state normal modes are expressed in this mixed basis, and their roto-translational character is quantified by a scalar weight,Ω𝑖. The imaginary-frequency mode is treated separately as the reaction coordinate, whereas the real-frequency modes are ranked according to their Ω𝑖 values. The method applies to channels yielding atomic, linear, and nonlinear fragments and does not require propagation toward the asymptotic product region. Portico thus provides an objective and transferable tool for automated reaction analysis and statistical models of molecular fragmentation.

papers.title: Hybrid QM/ML approaches for the prediction of regioselectivity in Minisci C–H functionalisation reactions
papers.abstract: Regioselectivity models are of key importance to the implementation of C–H functionalisations in synthetic route planning. In structure- and fragment-based drug discovery (SBDD/FBDD), ligand-target affinity is enhanced by elaborating weak hits into potent leads along vectors dictated by the protein structure. Consequently, the ability to functionalise a heterocyclic hit in a site-selective, and atom-economic manner could enable rapid exploration of structure-activity relationships (SAR). Designed to support this process, machine learning (ML) models for C–H regioselectivity prediction often report impressive accuracy, but progress in the development of these models, as well as their deployability, can be hindered by inaccessible or partially disclosed data, misaligned validation objectives, or an incomplete understanding of their domain of applicability. Herein, we present a quantum mechanics/machine learning (QM/ML) approach to predict the regioselectivity of Minisci reactions derived from carefully curated and publicly available data. We analyse and quantify data biases before validating our models, alongside relevant baselines, on a new, unique, FBDD-inspired experimental test set performed with high-throughput experimentation (HTE). We demonstrate superior accuracy on this experimental set compared to previous and baseline approaches, and offer a realistic perspective on their prospective performance. To support future development, we made our model and HTE dataset freely available at github.com/samgeoesp/minisci_regio.

papers.title: Generator-Collector enhanced Square Wave Voltammetry for Acetaminophen detection
papers.abstract: Alan O’Riordan Precision Electrochemistry Nanosensor Group Tyndall National Institute, University College Cork Cork, Ireland 0000-0002-7554-1536 While generator-collector (GC) electrochemistry using traditional electrochemistry methods, such as cyclic voltammetry, has been employed to enhance the detection of a number of analytes, little work has been done on coupling this phenomena with pulsed techniques. These techniques, such as square wave voltammetry (SWV), have been shown to enhance the detection capabilities of sensors, when employed without the use of GC mode. In this work, the effects of enabling GC mode on an interdigitated electrode array coupled with SWV are presented. Subsequently sensor surfaces were modified, via electroplating of gold, to further enhance the performance. The effect of varying key operational parameters for SWV, such as frequency and amplitude, as well as the applied potential bias to optimise GC mode were also studied. This sensor was subsequently utilised for the detection of acetaminophen in buffered samples, demonstrating the signalenhancing effects of GC SWV.

papers.title: Absolute, fast, accurate and easy-to-use method for determining the injected samples volumes in capillary electrophoresis and related methods using an injection tracer
papers.abstract: In this study, a simple, rapid, and reliable methodology was developed for measuring the injected sample volume in capillary electrophoresis and related techniques. The method does not require a calibration curve, nor knowledge of sample viscosity, injection pressure, or time. It is applicable under both significant and weak electroosmotic flow and is compatible with single or sequential injections. The principle of the method is straightforward: a band of neutral molecules is injected before the sample, which has been previously spiked with the same molecule. Classical mechanics allow the absolute calculation of the injected band volume, and the area of this band is simply compared with that of the neutral molecule peak to determine the injected volume of the unknown sample. Experimental validation demonstrated excellent agreement with volumes calculated from Poiseuille’s law. The method was further validated by performing sequential injections of multiple samples, demonstrating high precision across all injections.

papers.title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library via Ir-Catalysed Atroposelective C–H Arylation and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
papers.abstract: Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variant of Buchwald-type ligands are empowering ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step-intense synthetic approaches restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tuneable family of atrop-chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three-step assembly protocol exploits first a CpX-IrIII-catalysed atroposelective C–H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provides a diverse library of chiral air-stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was showcased with a challenging enantioselective gold-catalysed cycloisomerization and a palladium-catalysed asymmetric phenol dearomatization process. In both transformations, one member of the reported ligand family displayed excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er.

papers.title: Well-Defined Magnesium Complexes Enabled Hydroborative Cleavage of Monomeric and Polymeric Substrates
papers.abstract: In this work, we synthesized β-diketiminate (NacNac)-supported magnesium complex (DippNacNaciPrMg.THF) (DippNacNac = (2,6-iPr2C6H3)NC(Me)C-(H)C(Me)N(2,6-iPr2C6H3)) (Mg-1) and amidinate-based magnesium complex PhC(NtBu)2MgiPr.THF (Mg-2) and investigated their catalytic performance in the hydroborative reduction of ester, carbonate, and lactide carbonyl functionalities in both monomeric and polymeric substrates. Among the two catalysts, Mg-1 exhibited superior efficiency over Mg-2 in the HBpin-mediated reduction of carbonyl-containing monomers. The catalytic methodology was subsequently extended to the hydroborative depolymerization of carbonyl-containing polymers, including polyesters and polycarbonates. Notably, this represents the first report of NacNac- and amidinate-supported magnesium complexes being employed as catalysts for the hydroborative depolymerization of polyester and polycarbonate materials. Furthermore, the gram-scale depolymerization of polycaprolactone (PCL) was successfully demonstrated, highlighting the potential for future scale-up. A borylated reaction intermediate was also isolated and structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, providing valuable mechanistic insight. Overall, this study demonstrates the significant potential of magnesium-based main-group catalysts as sustainable and efficient systems for the hydroborative depolymerization of carbonyl-containing polymeric materials.

papers.title: Intranasal Delivery of Molecularly Engineered Nanoparticles for Temporal and Multi-Target Alzheimer's Therapy
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is driven by a self-reinforcing cycle of amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregation, cerebral hypoxia, and chronic neuroinflammation, which severely limits the efficacy of single-target interventions. Here, we develop a molecularly engineered temporal therapeutic strategy that achieves multi-target treatment of AD by integrating rapid photothermal Aβ disaggregation and hypoxia reversal with long-term oxygen-mediated immune remodeling. Through methoxyl-position engineering of a triphenylamine donor core, we identified a NIR-II para-substituted photothermal agent (NDA-DpMT) with the most red-shifted absorption at 984 nm and the highest photothermal conversion efficiency, reaching 73% in the aggregated state. NDA-DpMT was co-encapsulated with an oxygen-carrying perfluorocarbon (PFC) into GM1/TAT-modified human serum albumin nanoparticles (TGAP NPs) for nasal delivery. Under NIR irradiation, TGAP NPs rapidly disaggregate Aβ aggregates and inhibit Aβ aggregation in vitro. Photothermally responsive oxygen release relieved the hypoxic condition of microglia, reduced intracellular oxidative stress, and promoted the transition from M1 to M2 type macrophages. In AD mouse models, this temporal combinatorial therapy significantly reduces Aβ burden, normalizes hypoxia-inducible factor-α (HIF-α) expression levels from 33.2% to 3.4%, and remodels the neuroinflammatory microenvironment over days to weeks. The ratio of activated microglia polarized to the M2 anti-inflammatory phenotype increased by 27.4%, accompanied by the downregulated expression of TNF-α and IL-6. The treatment significantly improved neuronal ultrastructure and effectively restored learning and memory functions. This work establishes a molecularly optimized, time-programmed multi-target therapeutic paradigm that disrupts the pathological vicious cycle of AD, representing a promising translational strategy for effective AD treatment.

papers.title: Synthesis of oxime, lactone, and lactam derivatives from 29-hydroxyfriedelan-3-one and their cytotoxic activity against breast cancer and leukemia cells
papers.abstract: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide, with breast cancer and leukemia among the most prevalent types. Some chemotherapy options are becoming obsolete due to multidrug-resistant cells and new tumor initiation mechanisms. We aimed to investigate semisynthetic natural products as potential scaffolds for novel antitumoral agents. Eleven derivatives (2-12) were synthesized from 29-hydroxyfriedelan-3-one (1), an abundant friedelane-type triterpene isolated from Cheiloclinium cognatum aerial parts extracts. Nine products presented oxime, lactone or lactam moieties on C-3. The reaction yields ranged from 18 to 87%. Their cytotoxic activity against breast cancer and leukemia (MDA-MB-231 and K-562, respectively) cells were assessed. Compounds 6, 7, 10, and 12 were more potent (IC50 = 32-63 µM) against these cell lines than 1 (IC50 = 58-80 µM). All derivatives showed low cytotoxicity towards the non-cancerous WI-26 VA4 cells. Eight compounds fitted at least two drug-like empirical rules. Self-organizing map analysis showed that properties related to intermolecular interactions were most strongly associated with biological activities. These results open perspectives for the investigation of new friedelane triterpenes as potential anticancer agents with higher cytotoxic potency and optimized physicochemical properties.

papers.title: Computationally Guided Donor-Engineering of Azahelicenes Towards High-Performance Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.abstract: Developing circularly polarized luminescent (CPL) organic emitters that simultaneously exhibit high emission efficiency and strong chiroptical activity remain a significant challenge. Herein, we report a computationally guided design strategy for donor-functionalized azahelicenes with enhanced CPL performance. By evaluating transition dipole moment parameters and predicted glum values, representative azahelicene candidates were identified, synthesized, and systematically investigated. Single-crystal analysis revealed that donor functionalization and structural locking play crucial roles in modulating helical geometry, molecular rigidity, and intermolecular packing. In solution, these azahelicenes exhibited efficient fluorescence and pronounced chiroptical responses, with |gabs| and |glum| values reaching the 10-2 level. TD-DFT calculations further elucidated the relationship between molecular structure, transition dipole orientation, and CPL activity. Moreover, one azahelicene derivative AzaICz-1 displayed reversible pH-responsive luminescence and chiroptical switching, accompanied by red-shifted emission spectra and slightly reduced g values after protonation. This work provides valuable insights into the rational design of high-performance and stimuli-responsive chiral luminescent azahelicenes.

papers.title: Model Population Analysis to Optimize Near-Infrared-Based Screening of Deoxynivalenol in Wheat
papers.abstract: The widespread contamination of wheat with deoxynivalenol (DON) necessitates rapid, non-destructive screening methods. Although near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy offers a promising cost-effective solution, indirect detection via Fusarium-induced sample compositional changes often suffers from high model variance and overfitting. This study systematically evaluated the impact of seven methodological factors, namely dataset selection, dataset balancing, sample grinding, toxin type, sample weighting, spectral preprocessing, and variable selection, using model population analysis (MPA) to assess the performance of partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) sub-models for classifying wheat samples as compliant or non-compliant with the European Commission (EC) limit of 1000 μg/kg DON. By using repeated random splits with a stratification constraint across the seven methodological factors, 12,800 PLS-DA sub-models were generated. To study the effects of each factor, a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was employed. The results indicated that model performance was highly influenced by all methodological factors, with the toxin type and dataset balancing showing the greatest impacts on the F1-score and True Positive Rate (TPR), respectively. The optimal pipeline achieved an estimated F1-score of 0.74 ± 0.01 and a TPR of 0.84 ± 0.01 by utilizing Austrian-only wheat samples, intact kernels, standard normal variate (SNV) preprocessing, and downsampling for data balancing, without variable selection. Notably, samples labelling based on total DON (tDON, sum of DON and its acetylated and modified forms) improved classification performance, indicating that there might be a stronger correlation with Fusarium-induced sample compositional changes with tDON than with DON. Furthermore, applying an observation-weighting approach to highly uncertain samples mitigated the propagation of reference analytical error, significantly reducing false negative misclassifications near the regulatory threshold. Overall, our results provide a rigorously validated framework for optimizing complex chemometric pipelines, establishing a robust NIR methodology for challenging application such as indirect non-destructive screening of DON in wheat.

papers.title: Unraveling the Role of Macrocyclic Backbone in Cu–N–C Molecular Catalysts for Electrocatalytic CO2-to-CH4 Reduction
papers.abstract: Cu–N–C molecular catalysts with well-defined Cu–N4 sites show strong potential for CO2-to-CH4 production, yet the role of the macrocyclic backbone remains unclear. Herein, we compare two representative Cu–N–C molecular catalysts, copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) and copper tetraphenylporphyrin (CuPr), to clarify how the macrocyclic backbone influences CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis. When supported on conductive carbon and integrated into gas-diffusion electrodes, CuPc markedly outperforms CuPr, achieving a CH4 Faradaic efficiency of 79.5%, a high partial current density of -575 mA cm-2, a mass activity of 19,166.7 A g-1, and stable operation for over 80 h at -150 mA cm-2. Characterization results suggest that the Pcmacrocyclic backbone modulates the electronic structure of the Cu center and interfacial charge-transfer behavior, possibly through its extended π-conjugated Pc-ring and bridge-N environment. Theoretical calculations reveal a favorable CH4-forming pathway on the CuPc/C model, with a lower free-energy barrier for the potential-determining step than that reported for CuPr, suggesting facilitated CH4 formation. These findings indicate that the macrocyclic backbone can regulate reaction pathways and intermediate adsorption energetics, providing mechanistic insight and design guidance for molecular catalysts for CO2-to-CH4 electroreduction.

papers.title: Navigating Compositional Space in Palladium Hydride: Benchmarking Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Palladium plays a crucial role in advancing the hydrogen economy, serving in applications such as hydrogen purification, sensing, catalysis, and conversion. While machine learning approaches have shown great promise to accelerate first-principles calculations, it is currently unclear if they are accurate enough to contribute to the design of Pd-based membranes and catalyst materials. The core challenge lies in navigating the vast compositional space in non-stoichiometric Pd-hydride phases. To address this challenge, we develop a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) for palladium hydride using an on-the-fly active learning approach. This method efficiently samples diverse atomic configurations across a wide range of hydrogen concentrations. The trained MLIP is validated against experimental data, demonstrating prediction of thermo-mechanical and chemical properties with density functional theory (DFT)-level accuracy. Additionally, its transferability and performance are compared against existing semi-empirical methods. The heat of mixing for Pd-H is found to be negative with the trained MLIP, whereas it is positive valued for the EAM potential available in literature. Consequently, our MLIP yields a more realistic phase diagram with the -phase hydrogen concentration being closer to the experimental one.

papers.title: Elucidating the Dynamic Behavior of Surfactants: A Chemical Language Model Perspective
papers.abstract: The practical utility of a surfactant is determined not only by its equilibrium behavior but also by how quickly it takes effect. Dynamic surface tension (DST)—the time evolution of the surface tension driven by surfactant adsorption onto a freshly formed interface—controls foaming, emulsification, and rapid wetting. Existing techniques for measuring DST are labor-intensive and unsuited for high-throughput screening, hindering surfactant discovery. Here we introduce the first machine-learning framework for predicting DST, providing a valuable complement to experimental approaches. Trained on a purpose-built, curated database of 979 DST series for 233 surfactants, the domain-specific chemical language model reproduces DST with a mean absolute error of 6.5 mN m –1 and predicts the characteristic half-time of the surface-tension relaxation with a coefficient of determination of 0.78. A hybrid aleatoric–epistemic uncertainty quantification explicitly delineates the applicability domain and, by discarding high-variance predictions, lowers the mean absolute error to 5.6 mN m –1 . Finally, a game-theoretic (Shapley) attribution shows that the model autonomously recovers fragment-level rules that are consistent with colloid-chemical knowledge. Our framework, combining physics-informed training, rigorous uncertainty estimation, and game-theoretic interpretability, offers a general strategy for tackling time-dependent interfacial phenomena. The curated database, the trained model, and an interactive online predictor are released publicly.

papers.title: Stereospecific Engagement of a Methyl-Sensitive ECL2 Anchor Site in 5-HT₂A by α-Substituted NBOH Derivatives
Wearable electrofluidic biosensing system for real-time quantitation and adaptive stratification of fluctuating trace sweat antibodies
papers.abstract: However, sweat antibody detection remains particularly challenging because antibody concentrations are substantially lower than those of common sweat markers such as cortisol and glucose. By integrating ultra-sensitive interfacial capacitive sensing with ultra-fast AC electrothermal target enrichment, we develop detachable monolithic biosensors for sweat antibodies, which are based on antigen probe functionalized flexible electrode arrays. A wearable biosensing system, incorporating a pressure-regulated PDMS sweat-collection patch and a wristwatch-style microcapacitance detector, is further constructed to enable real-time quantitation of ultra-trace antibodies in sweat. SARS-CoV-2 N protein antibody and Hepatitis B surface antibody in sweat are tested with a limit of 10-6 ng/mL, a linear range of 10-5~10-1 ng/mL, and a responding time of 30 s. In response to the fluctuations of sweat biomarker levels, adaptive stratification algorithms are implemented by leveraging the sensor’s high dynamic range through machine learning. Validated on 25 volunteers with a stratification balanced accuracy exceeding 0.74, this system provides a versatile wearable platform capable of quantifying and stratifying a broader range of highly fluctuating, low-abundance sweat biomarkers.

papers.title: Computational prediction of Y-doped Cd2Sb2O7 as a competitive Sb-based n-type Transparent Conducting Oxide
papers.abstract: Transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) with diverse band alignments are essential for next-generation optoelec- tronic devices, where precise energy level matching and carrier type control are critical for efficient performance. In this work, we computationally predict that Y-doped Cd2Sb2O7 is a promising new n-type TCO candidate. Using hybrid density functional theory (DFT), we show that Y substitution introduces resonant donor states high above the conduction band minima, leading to high mobility and high electron conductivity while maintaining optical transparency in the visible range. This study reinforces the potential of Sb(V)-based oxides for expanding the functional landscape of TCO materials, and emphasizes the value of full defect chemistry prediction in computational design of new optoelectronic materials.

papers.title: CensorADMET: Controllable Constraint-Satisficing Regression for Censored ADMET Data
papers.abstract: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) measurements are often reported only as upper or lower bounds because an assay does not resolve activity beyond its tested concentration range. These inequality­labelled observations contain useful directional information, yet dropping them loses signal and threshold substitution changes the regression target. Interval likelihoods retain the information but provide no direct control over the extent to which censored observations influence exact­value fitting. We introduce CensorADMET, which minimises an exact­label objective with an exact­only prediction anchor while targeting a prespecified aggregate probability­deficit budget for censored intervals. Across ChEMBL 36 inhibition cohorts evaluated under chemical and assay­provenance shifts, the primary anchored satisficing setting reduced one­sided bound violations by 0.15–0.29 with a median exact­label MAE cost of at most 0.04 p­units. Plain Tobit interval likelihood achieved larger violation reduc­ tions but larger MAE costs; concentration­space AFT provided a competitive fixed operating point but no tunable deficit target. The same trade­off was observed under simultaneous assay­and­ scaffold shift and was directionally consistent in an exploratory cohort of solubility, clearance, and half­life measurements. CensorADMET therefore allows practitioners to specify and audit a model­implied censor­consistency target rather than accept the operating point induced by an unweighted interval likelihood or indirectly selected loss weight. Scientific Contribution. CensorADMET introduces a constrained censored­regression objective whose user­specified aggregate probability­deficit budget parametrises a targeted accuracy–con­ sistency operating point. It evaluates this budget­targeted control across natural censoring and chemical and assay­provenance shifts, separating bound consistency from exact­value accuracy, uncertainty calibration, and hidden­value recovery.

papers.title: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
papers.abstract: Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable non-invasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results elucidate the wavelength-dependent 2 reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

papers.title: DFG Project Report: Surface-Compartmentalized Micelles by Stereocomplex-Driven Self-Assembly
papers.abstract: Surface-compartmentalized micelles (patchy or Janus-type) show an outstanding interfacial activity, making them highly attractive for various applications. In this project alternative routes to surface-compartmentalized micelles were developed based on crystallization- (CDSA) and stereocomplex-driven self-assembly (SCDSA) of polylactide (PLA)-based block copolymers. SCDSA of diblock copolymers bearing enantiomeric poly( L -lactide)/poly( D -lactide) blocks and highly incompatible corona-forming blocks (polystyrene (PS) and poly( tert -butyl methacrylate) (P t BMA)) was introduced as facile method to prepare uniform spherical micelles with a semicrystalline stereocomplex (SC) core, formed by the enantiomeric PLA blocks, and a shamrock-like microphase-separated PS/P t BMA corona. The patchy micelles showed a significantly higher interfacial activity compared to micelles with a homogenous PS corona and were also successfully employed in the stabilization of emulsions and as compatibilizers in strongly incompatible PS/P t BMA blends. The excellent performance of patchy micelles is attributed to their adaptive corona that enables selective swelling/collapse of the respective miscible/immiscible patches at the emulsion or blend interface. However, with SCDSA other morphologies (cylinders, platelets) could not be realized. Co-crystallization-driven self-assembly (CCDSA) of PS- b -P L LA- b -P t BMA (SLT) triblock terpolymers with the corresponding P L LA homopolymer gave for the first time access to platelet-like micelles, featuring a non-concentric, nanometre-sized, stripe-patterned corona. Depending on the length of the employed P L LA homopolymer either twisted patchy platelet or defined pyramidal structures composed of stacked patchy platelets can be produced. Interestingly, the neat SLT assembled to Janus micelles with an amorphous P L LA core, attributed to the strongly hindered crystallization of the P L LA middle block. The interfacial activity of the patchy platelets is significantly higher compared to spherical patchy micelles, and they proved effective in stabilizing emulsions. Finally, CDSA and SCDSA were combined to selectively load the P L LA patches within patchy worm-like micelles formed by a double-crystalline PS- b -PE- b -P L LA (PE = polyethylene) triblock terpolymer. When CDSA is conducted in THF only the PE middle block crystallized and worm-like micelles with a crystalline PE core and an amorphous, patchy PS/P L LA corona were formed. Subsequently, the P L LA patches were selectively loaded via stereocomplexation with an enantiomeric P D LA homopolymer, yielding micelles with P L LA/P D LA SC domains in the corona showing a significantly increased size. This project revealed the excellent potential of stereoregular PLA-based block copolymers for the preparation of surface-compartmentalized micelles of varying shape and tailored corona functionalities utilizing SCDSA and CCDSA.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Pavement as an Ecosystem Technology: A Retrofit Pathway to Negative-Carbon Road Systems
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic pavement — road and airfield surfaces incorporating titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) — targets the diffuse, use-phase, mobile-source emissions that constitute the majority of transportation’s greenhouse-gas footprint. We report independent laboratory and field results for the first commercially scalable retrofit photocatalytic system, which integrates photo-reactive TiO 2 into established pavement-preservation carriers (PlusTi™). Under ambient ultraviolet excitation, TiO 2 drives a non-selective redox cascade — an “artificial photosynthesis” — that mineralizes vehicle-borne CO 2 to durable bicarbonate and oxidizes NO x , VOCs, and tire/brake-wear microplastics. Verified performance includes a 41–61% reduction in CO 2 concentration at fieldspecification dose (>1,000 t CO 2 removed per lane-mile per year), ~60% NO x reduction, 94.8–99.6% microplastic particle-size reduction, and measurable urban-heat-island mitigation. We frame the treated road network as an ecosystem technology (ecotech): a distributed atmospheric-processing surface that performs ecosystem services at urban scale using only ambient solar energy, no machinery, and no land displacement. A companion contribution is methodological — an expansion of lifecycle carbon-accounting boundaries beyond the industry’s cradle-to-gate (A1–A3) convention to a cradle-to-grave framework with a use-phase (Scope 3, Category 11) removal module, supported by published ISO-compliant EPDs and a Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) protocol now in peer review.

papers.title: A curated list of material properties for 30 photovoltaic absorbers
papers.abstract: I present a highly commented list of eight material properties for 28 experimentally synthesized and 10 computationally modeled photovoltaic absorbers (30 distinct materials). These properties are used to evaluate the recently proposed Γ PV figure of merit of these 30 photovoltaic materials in a separate study (DOI:10.48550/arXiv.2404.14732). α and σ are parameters describing the spectral average and spectral dispersion of the absorption coefficient spectrum, τ is the non-radiative carrier recombination lifetime, µ is the carrier mobility, n is the dark carrier concentration, ϵ is the static dielectric constant, m is the density-of-states (DOS) effective mass, and E g is the band gap. The results can be reproduced on https://github.com/DTU-Nanolab-materials-discovery/PV-figure-of-merit.

papers.title: ORGANOSILICA NANOPARTICLE FORMATION FROM HYDROPHILIC SILANES
papers.abstract: The surface properties and morphology of organosilica nanoparticles dictate their ef icacy in biomedical applications, yet synthesizing stable particles from hydrophilic precursors remains highly challenging. This study investigates the impact of precursor hydrophilicity on nanoparticle formation, cooperative self-assembly, and inal morphology using three distinct organosilanes: (3aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES), N-(3-triethoxysilylpropyl)-4,5-dihydroimidazole (TESPDHI), and 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane (MPTMS). Single-step co-condensation of APTES with tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) yielded either aggregated particles or macroscopic gels due to rapid, unmatched hydrolysis rates (observed via in situ 1H NMR) and charge neutralization. Conversely, a multi-step acidic pre-hydrolysis method controlled monomer hydrolysis and facilitated charge-matching interactions with anionic surfactants, yielding highly mesoporous nanoparticles. Furthermore, the introduction of glycol-based co-solvents and subtle temperature increases shifted the nanoparticle morphology from hollow spheres to ordered mesoporous structures. While TESPDHI demonstrated a similar formation pathway in luenced by solvent-mediated π-π interactions, MPTMS displayed unique behavior due to electrostatic repulsion between mercapto and silanol groups. These indings provide critical pathways for controlling the structural properties of organosilica nanoparticles synthesized from hydrophilic precursors.

papers.title: AIE-Active Azahelicenes with High-Performance Circularly Polarized Luminescence for Lipid Droplet Visualization
papers.abstract: While helicene derivatives have been widely recognized for their promise in advanced photonic technologies, their bioimaging applications are relatively unexplored. Herein, we report a three-step synthesis of aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-active azahelicenes, Aza[7]T, Aza[7]TM, and Aza[7]TOM, by combining a nitrogen-containing helical framework with triphenylamine derivatives. These molecules display red to deep-red emission and intense chiroptical responses, with dissymmetry factors reaching the 10-2 level. Among the series, Aza[7]TOM exhibited excellent lipid-droplet (LD) targeting specificity (Pearson’s colocalization coefficients R2 > 0.98), low cytotoxicity, high imaging brightness, and wash-free staining ability in living HeLa cells. Structure illumination microscopy super-resolution imaging further revealed well-defined intracellular LDs with sharp boundaries. Notably, Aza[7]TOM could also sense the maturation state of LDs, making it a valuable probe for studying LD dynamics and biogenesis.

papers.title: Modeling Glass-Transition Temperatures with an Emphasis on Pharmaceutical Compounds
papers.abstract: The glass-transition temperature (Tg) marks the transition of an amorphous material from a rigid glassy state to a more mobile rubbery or supercooled-liquid state. Tg indicates molecular mobility, crystallization tendency, and physical stability in amorphous materials. For drug molecules, Tg may indicate their bioavailability. Experimental determination of Tg is often limited by crystallization, thermal degradation, or the inability to isolate stable amorphous phases; computational predictions are valuable for prioritizing compounds and multicomponent formulations before extensive experimental screening. This review examines computational approaches for predicting Tg across organic amorphous materials, with emphasis on pharmaceutical compounds and formulations. Lastly, we outline future directions for improving computational methodology for Tg prediction.

papers.title: Grammar for Chemically Auditable MOF Adsorption Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine learning is now routinely used to screen metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), but the object seen by a model is not the crystal itself. Instead, it is a representation: a selected set of geometric, topological, chemical, or learned descriptors that determines which structural evidence can influence prediction, ranking, and candidate selection. Here, we develop a representationcentric audit for MOF adsorption machine learning using a large ARC–MOF-derived cohort with matched CO2 and CH4 uptake targets. Six descriptor regimes—compact geometry, full geometry, topology only, compact geometry plus topology, full geometry plus topology, and redundancy-reduced geometry—are compared across linear, local, tree-ensemble, boosting, and shallow neural-network baselines under repeated data-split and random-seed settings. Descriptor family explains 17.5% of the variation in target-mean-normalised RMSE, close to the 21.2% contribution of model choice, while model and descriptor rankings are only moderately stable across benchmark contexts, with mean Kendall’s τ values of 0.629 and 0.604, respectively. The effect is most consequential at the screening stage: defensible changes in representation can alter the shortlists of top-ranked MOFs even when average prediction errors remain similar. Full geometry plus topology, combined with a random-forest model, provides the strongest default configuration in this audit, although the value of topological information is conditional rather than universal. We therefore propose a descriptor grammar for chemically auditable MOF discovery: state what evidence the model sees, quantify descriptor sensitivity, test ranking and shortlist stability, and distinguish representation-stable conclusions from representation-fragile candidate claims before promoting elite, anomalous, or rule-breaking materials.

papers.title: Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Prognosticating Lithium-Ion Battery Degradation: A Mixture of Experts Approach
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for lithium-ion batteries is critical for ensuring reliability and safety in energy storage systems. This paper introduces a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that synergistically combines bidirectional gated recurrent units with multi-head attention mechanisms and MLP-Mixer modules within a mixture of experts framework. The proposed model effectively captures complex temporal dependencies and degradation patterns from battery capacity time series data. Extensive experimental evaluation on NASA and CALCE public datasets demonstrates the superior performance of our approach, achieving relative errors of 0.005 and 0.0019 respectively, substantially outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The hybrid architecture provides robust RUL predictions while maintaining computational efficiency, offering significant improvements for battery health monitoring and prognostic applications.

papers.title: Poxvirus F13L homodimer-interface targeted by BoltzGen cyclic-minipeptides and permeable mutants
papers.abstract: Hundreds of Boltzgen cyclic-minipeptide-conformer candidates of different sizes targeted the vaccinia poxvirus F13L homodimer-interface (F13Lmin) in a Tecovirimat-binding manner. However, only low affinity candidates < 6-mer predicted membrane-permeabilities for intracellularly targeting F13L. Therefore, a 9-mer cyclic-minipeptide parent-template predicting top-affinity but low-permeability, was computationally mutated to explore thousands of derived amino acid sequences to search for highpermeabilities. The strategy resulted in high-permeability mutant-candidates conserving their cyclization, high-affinities and similar F13L targeting-sites. Because their many contacts to F13L amino acids, candidates may best adapt to Tecovirimat resistant mutations. Additionally, cyclic-minipeptides provide easy chemical synthesis and high environmental and endoprotease stability. Therefore, membrane-permeable cyclic-candidates may be instrumental to computational-guide further developments toward Tecovirimat-resistant alternative drugs. Because of targeting F13L highly-conserved sequences, some of these candidates may predict interferences to other poxviruses.

papers.title: From Hydrothermal Vents to Ocean Worlds: the Prebiotic Chemistry of Ketene
papers.abstract: Living systems are sustained far from equilibrium by continuous, enzyme-mediated turnover of chemical fuels. How comparable chemistry could begin without evolved catalysts, and against the thermodynamic cost of assembling complex molecules in water, remains unresolved. Here we show that ketene (CH2=C=O) and its nitrogen analogue ketenimine, generated abiotically at hydrothermal vents and confined within amphiphile membranes, act as chemical engines transducing geochemical energy into life's building blocks. Using ab initio nanoreactor molecular dynamics, we find the confined cumulenes react with water and in situ hydroxyl radicals to assemble amino acid, sugar and amide precursors, including intermediates of the formose reaction and reductive citric acid cycle, via exergonic radical pathways. Under anhydrous conditions they instead collapse into unfunctionalized C6-C12 hydrocarbon scaffolds, a dead-end aliphatic endpoint consistent with the long-chain organics reported in Martian mudstone by the Curiosity rover. We read this divergence as two planetary trajectories: persistent water sustained the proto-metabolic cycle on early Earth, whereas Mars's desiccation arrested it in an unreactive hydrocarbon state. For Europa, whose tidally heated subsurface ocean preserves aqueous conditions, the chemistry remains viable, yielding four independent, spectroscopically testable signatures distinguishing active aqueous proto-metabolism from cryogenic chemostasis. The framework recasts the onset of dynamic kinetic stability, and hence habitability, as a consequence of confined aqueous disequilibrium.

papers.title: Data-Driven Multi-Objective Analysis of Activity–Poisoning resistance Trade-Offs in Complex Multimetallic Electrocatalysts for Glucose Oxidation
papers.abstract: The discovery of efficient and durable multimetallic nanoparticle electrocatalysts requires effective navigation of vast compositional spaces. However, systematically exploring these spaces while balancing competing performance objectives remains challenging. Here, we present a closed-loop experimental framework for medium-throughput screening and multi-objective analysis of trade-offs between activity and poisoning resistance for the electrochemical glucose oxidation reaction (GOR). The framework couples electrochemical nanoparticle synthesis, performance evaluation, material characterization, and machine learning to systematically explore the six-element Au–Ir–Pt–Pd–Rh–Ru composition space. Nanoparticles with controlled compositions were synthesized via our recently developed electrodeposition approach and evaluated with respect to their activity and poisoning resistance for the GOR under alkaline conditions. The experimental data were used to train Gaussian process regression (GPR) models of activity and poisoning resistance. The resulting models reveal distinct activity and poisoning resistance landscapes, highlighting a trade-off between the two objectives. Highly active compositions are localized near the Au–Pt bimetallic edge with minor contributions from Ir, Pd, Rh, and Ru. In contrast, the most poisoning resistant compositions were found toward the center of the composition space with contributions from Rh and Pd up to 20 at%. Model interpretation via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) confirms Au and Pt as the primary contributors to both activity and poisoning resistance, while Rh and Pd provide additional contributions to poisoning resistance. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable, data-driven strategy for the discovery of complex multimetallic electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Reconfigurable Peptide Nanostructures via Sequence and Solvent Tuning
papers.abstract: Peptide self-assembly in aqueous media is dominated by hydrophobic collapse and backbone hydrogen bonding, further stabilized by side-chain-specific interactions such as cation-π, aromatic stacking, and electrostatics. However, under non-aqueous and low-water conditions, reduced contributions from the hydrophobic effect allow a rebalancing of intermolecular interactions. This opens up alternative assembly configurations, including ones suited to dry-state and solvent-responsive peptide materials. Here, we investigate how solvent environment (methanol vs water) and peptide sequence collectively impact supramolecular organization. We use a series of amphiphilic octapeptides with the general sequence (XEXK)2 where X represents hydrophobic amino acids with distinct side-chain properties (Phe, Trp, Ile, or Leu). In water, (FEFK)2, (IEIK)2 and (WEWK)2 formed the expected β-sheet-rich bilayer nanofiber assemblies, whereas (LELK)2 remained largely disordered. In methanol (MeOH), while (FEFK)2, and (IEIK)2 retained similar structures, solvent-dependent structural reconfiguration was observed for (WEWK)2 with a shift toward side-chain directed assembly, resulting in morphological transitions from one-dimensional nanofibers in water to extended two-dimensional nanosheets in MeOH. Comparison of molecular dynamics simulations in water and MeOH suggests significant reorganization of intermolecular interactions stabilized by H-bonding and electrostatic interactions, and presenting Trp residues toward solvent interface. In the dry state, these MeOH- assembled (WEWK)2 nanosheets could be transformed into nanofibers in the solid state, upon exposure to high relative humidity (RH) (or upon solvation in liquid water). These findings establish the internal conformational entropy and steric of amino acid side chains regulate the dynamicity, structural adaptability, and solvent-driven reconfiguration of peptide bilayer assemblies. This provides a framework for engineering adaptive, reconfigurable solid state peptide materials beyond aqueous self-assembly.

papers.title: Dynamic solid-liquid equilibrium controls propylene electrochemical epoxidation on silver-based catalysts
papers.abstract: Although silver-based catalysts are the benchmark for thermocatalytic epoxidation of propylene, they are considered as subpar compared to Pd-based catalysts for the electrocatalytic epoxidation of propylene. Recent reports have challenged this view, demonstrating that heterogeneous and homogeneous Ag-based catalysts can reach similar faradaic efficiency (FE) exceeding 60% when paired with azole-based ligands. The mechanistic origin for this comparable activity remains unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that both heterogeneous and homogeneous Ag-based catalysts form a similar active catalyst under operating epoxidation conditions. Using electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM) combined with postmortem structural characterizations, we show that the onset for propylene epoxidation is concomitant with the oxidation of Ag+ and the formation of AgO that acts as the true active catalyst. Constructing experimental Pourbaix diagrams for bare silver and silver with two azole-based ligands, 1,2,3-triazole (Tz) and pyrazole (Pz), we show that these ligands profoundly modify the onset for AgO crystallization, and thus the onset for propylene epoxidation. In detail, Tz is found to decrease the onset potential for AgO formation and to enable enhanced FE of 73%. Combining in-situ surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (SEIRAS) with EQCM, we further demonstrate that the enhanced selectivity originates from the anodic decomposition of Tz that forms an hydrophobic layer preventing water oxidation. This finding reframes catalyst and electrolyte design for electrocatalytic epoxidation, suggesting that anodically formed hydrophobic coatings are essential for achieving enhanced FE.

papers.title: Soft Nano/Microgels Observed in situ at Fluid Interfaces:Recent Progress and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: In this invited focus review, recent progress in understanding the interfacial behaviors of soft nano/micro hydrogels (hereafter referred to as microgels) is reviewed, with particular emphasis on research done by the authors’ group. Unlike rigid polymeric particles, soft microgels display unique interfacial behaviors at air/water and oil/water interfaces. Beginning from our finding of the unusual drying behavior of aqueous dispersions of poly(N-isopropyl acrylamide) (pNIPAm)-based microgels, we have systematically investigated single microgel deformation at interfaces, the compression behavior of interfacial microgel arrays, and the more complex self-organization processes during the drying of sessile droplets. Furthermore, our group has also found that well-defined nanocomposite microgels can be used to create unique soft materials that have not been achieved using conventional microgels. Finally, future perspectives on this topic will be discussed based on our findings and viewpoint.

papers.title: Late-Stage C4-Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
Size-Dependent Properties of Metal-Organic Framework Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Size-dependent phenomena appear across materials science, from quantum-confined semiconductor nanocrystals to size-tunable catalytic metals. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), a compositionally diverse class of porous coordination materials composed of metal nodes and organic linkers, are no exception. Despite the long-standing view of MOFs as bulk crystalline solids defined by their periodic lattice, a growing body of evidence demonstrates that MOF properties such as optical behavior, electronic structure, phase transition, mechanical flexibility, and adsorption characteristics depend markedly on particle size. Here, we report recent findings on size-dependent phenomena of MOF nanoparticles and emerging evidence that their metal-ligand bonds become more labile at smaller dimensions, offering a unifying explanation for the diverse size effects observed across this class of materials.

papers.title: Features of the Gibbs Equation (∆G = ∆H - T∆S) Applied to Solvation, Vaporization, and Complexation Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: The Gibbs equation (∆ G = ∆ H – T ∆ S ) remains a cornerstone of chemical thermodynamics. Yet the scope and origins of the widely observed correlations between the enthalpies (∆ H ) and entropies (∆ S ), or Gibbs energies (∆ G ) and enthalpies, have long been debated. This study systematically analyzes over 4,500 experimental thermodynamic values at 298.15 K to establish quantitative principles governing the ∆ G vs. ∆ H relationship across solvation, vaporization, and molecular complexation processes. By classifying systems according to hydrogen-bonding capabilities, we demonstrate that non-associated solute–solvent pairs universally follow a baseline linear correlation (the Barclay–Butler line). Systematic deviations from this baseline are quantitatively attributed to distinct physical contributions: conformational flexibility in long-chain aliphatics (hindered internal rotation), a constant entropic penalty per directional hydrogen bond, and predominantly entropic solvophobic effects in associated solvents. Through thermodynamic transformations, these solvation/vaporization rules are extended to yield a universal linear ∆ G –∆ H relationship with an invariant slope of 0.660 for both solution- and gas-phase molecular complexation, encompassing hydrogen bonding, charge transfer, and dispersion interactions. The framework is successfully applied to α -cyclodextrin host–guest systems, where it can be used as a diagnostic tool for detecting anomalous or non-inclusion binding modes and for deeper analysis of the complexation mechanism. Ultimately, this work transforms the Gibbs equation into a predictive instrument, enabling accurate estimation of enthalpies from single-temperature Gibbs energy measurements and providing a unified, mechanism-independent foundation for analyzing intermolecular interactions in systems of varying complexity.

papers.title: High-speed photoresponse of CVD-grown lateral TMD heterostructures
papers.abstract: Although chemical vapor deposition (CVD) enables wafer-scale fabrication of transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) photodetectors, CVD-grown devices are often limited by high defect densities and are generally considered significantly slower than devices based on exfoliated materials. Here, we demonstrate that the extrinsic response time of CVD-grown TMD photodetectors can be substantially reduced by built-in electric fields arising from p-n junctions but also asymmetric Schottky barriers in monolayer lateral heterostructures. In particular, the heterostructure devices exhibit response times improved by 1.5-2 orders of magnitude compared to devices based on a single TMD material. With that, the fastest devices achieve bandwidths exceeding 230 MHz, corresponding to fall times on the order of 1 ns.

papers.title: Improved Aromatic Finkelstein Reactions for the Synthesis of Iodinated BODIPYs
papers.abstract: Iodinated 4,4-difluoro-4-bora-3a,4a-diaza- s -indacenes (BODIPYs) are valuable synthetic intermediates for the formation of functionalised fluorophores, as they enable downstream nucleophilic aromatic substitution (S N Ar) and metal-catalysed cross-coupling reactions. However, there are limited synthetic routes available for the synthesis of such iodinated BODIPYs, particularly for the selective introduction of iodine at the 1, 3, 5 and 7-positions. Herein, we present an improved route to iodinated BODIPYs, based on an aromatic Finkelstein reaction, in which bromo-substituted BODIPYs are transformed into their corresponding iodoanalogues. Our optimised reaction conditions, excess NaI in refluxing acetone for 1.5 hours, allowed for the formation of 3,5-diiodo-8-aryl-BODIPYs in high yields (90-95%). Furthermore, we show that the aromatic Finkelstein reactions of bromo-substituted BODIPYs with NaI show high regioselectivity for the 1, 3, 5 and 7-positions, with the 2, 6-positions being unreactive, across a range of substrates. This allows for the efficient formation of both mono-iodo and mixed bromo/iodo-substituted BODIPYs, through the preferential substitution of bromines at the 1, 3, 5 and 7-positions. We anticipate that this operationally simple, high yielding and highly regioselective pathway for the synthesis of iodo-BODIPYs will be impactful in the further development of functionalised BODIPY platforms.

papers.title: Investigating the Stacking Diversity in 2D COFs: Implications for Structural and Elastic Properties
papers.abstract: 2D covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are layered organic materials that often adopt multiple stacking configurations or exhibit disordered stacking motifs. The stacking type is known to have a significant influence on their properties. However, only a single averaged experimental structure is typically reported from powder X-ray diffraction analysis, and computational COF databases likewise consider only one stacking configuration for downstream property screening. Here, we investigate a subset of 132 2D structures from the CURATED-COFs database through a density functional theory based workflow that systematically screens different stacking patterns. We show that energetically, typically multiple configurations are thermally accessible at typical solvothermal synthesis temperatures and the experimentally averaged structures may misrepresent the true local stacking environment, leading to inaccurate property predictions. We demonstrate the impact of stacking for relevant properties, including porosity, linear elasticity, and exfoliability, and provide structural rationalization for the observed property variations across stacking configurations. These results highlight the stacking configuration as an underexplored design variable for property-targeted COF development, while also indicating possible pitfalls in computational screening workflows and experimental structure interpretation.

papers.title: Alkene Isomerization and Carbonyl Reduction of α,β-Unsaturated Carbonyls with Ketoreductase
papers.abstract: The amino acid-to-enzyme, part-to-whole transition leads to the emergence of enzymatic complexity and diversity. The conventional convergent, heuristic enzymology approach typically classifies enzymes into defined catalytic categories for the predictive identification of enzymes through sequence and conformation homology, thus countering the very essence of emergence. The emphasis on inner core conformational domains for catalysis translates to the tightly confined perspective of discrete domain enzymology. Herein, we report a divergent, emergent enzymology approach, disregard of enzyme classification for the expansive identification of enzymes into the hidden, unchartered categories, thus in compliance with the very essence of emergence. The emphasis on inner-to-outer potential conformational domains for catalysis translates to the broadly open perspective of continuum domain enzymology. In particular, herein, with α,β-unsaturated carbonyls, alkene isomerization as one extra catalytic modality has been identified along with the native carbonyl reduction catalytic modality for ketoreductase, with each effected within disjoint conformational domains. Further, the native carbonyl reduction catalytic modality has empowered the achievement of exquisite flip-flop R-enantioselectivity and Senantioselectivity. The mechanistically disjoint divergence of conformational domains and catalytic modalities within a single enzyme architecture, as showcased herein, epitomizes the very essence of emergence and promises an enormous discovery space for enzymatic complexity and diversity.

papers.title: Persistent Homology using Nets: Topologically Informed Machine Learning Descriptors of Framework Materials
papers.abstract: Topological nets define the connectivity in framework materials, influencing their pore structure and mechanical properties. In this work, we investigate the importance of incorporating this information into machine learning models for gas adsorption prediction. To this end, we develop a novel representation, persistent homology using nets (PHuN), which computes topological features directly from the framework net via persistent homology. We show that PHuN leads to a computationally efficient representation that captures important topological information. We apply this representation to predict gas adsorption properties and demonstrate its ability to produce accurate predictions, especially when combined with other commonly used geometric and chemical descriptors. Further, to gain interpretable insights, we perform an ablation study combined with an analysis of feature importance to evaluate the contribution of different sets of descriptors and inspect how topological, geometrical, and chemical descriptors affect model performance.

papers.title: Operating Conditions Redefine MOF Design: Interpretable Windows Expose Cross-Process Conflict and Pressure-Driven Rank Reversal
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening identifies which metal–organic framework (MOF) ranks highest under one set of conditions, but not whether its design logic survives another operating regime. Here, we discover compact descriptor windows across 278,407 ARC-MOF structures while jointly optimizing elite enrichment, support, and topology diversity. Five process scores resolve into compatible and antagonistic blocs rather than a universal hierarchy. Natural-gas and landfill-gas purification align closely (Spearman 𝜌 = 0.949; top-decile Jaccard 54.37%), whereas post-combustion CO2 capture and methane storage oppose one another (𝜌 = −0.812; Jaccard 0.15%). Only 84 structures (0.030% of the database) remain top-decile performers across all five processes. Pressure likewise preserves or reverses candidate identity: single-gas CO2 rankings are conserved from 0.015 to 0.15 bar (𝜌 = 0.947) but invert across 0.4–16 bar (𝜌 = −0.395), with 27.5% of low-pressure elites entering the high-pressure bottom decile. Sign reversals in pore size, accessible surface area, and occupiable volume connect both scales to an affinity-to-capacity transition. Process-specific rule cards distinguish broad explanatory regions from narrow high-purity shortlists, and Pareto selection prevents enrichment through topology collapse. This framework converts database screening from a list of winners into auditable, operating-condition-specific design guidance.

papers.title: Single-GPU ML/MM Metadynamics Captures Enzyme-Bound Carbohydrate Puckering
papers.abstract: Machine-learning/MM simulations promise QM/MM-like conformational sampling at molecular-dynamics cost, but practical proof-of-concept examples for enzyme-bound carbohydrates remain scarce. Here, we evaluate a MACE/AMBER well-tempered metadynamics protocol for the -1 mannoside in GH125 α-mannosidase against a previously reported QM/MM conformational reference. Despite the deliberately approximate mechanical-embedding implementation, the workflow captures the dominant enzyme-imposed puckering trend on single-GPU resources, establishing a rapid route for conformational prescreening of carbohydrate-active enzymes.

papers.title: Lewis Acid-Mediated Defluorination of Fluorinated Diluents in Battery Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Fluorinated diluents have been widely adopted in lithium metal batteries in recent years and represent one of the most successful strategies for stabilizing the electrode-electrolyte interphase. Because these molecules interact only weakly with alkali metal ions and are largely excluded from the primary solvation shell, they are generally considered chemically inert. Here, however, we show that incorporating fluorinated diluents into sodium metal electrolytes unexpectedly triggers severe sodium corrosion, revealing a striking contrast between lithium and sodium systems. This behavior motivated a systematic investigation of the underlying reaction mechanism, suggesting that fluorinated diluents may not be as chemically inert as previously assumed. We propose that PF5, generated from NaPF6, catalyzes the defluorination of fluorinated diluents in the presence of sodium metal, producing NaF and carbonaceous decomposition products. Extending this study across different salts, fluorinated diluents, and alkali metals further reveals that this behavior is broadly observed across diverse electrolyte chemistries and alkali metal systems. Beyond explaining this unexpected reactivity of fluorinated diluents, we leverage these mechanistic insights to establish a new strategy for controlled in situ NaF formation that stabilizes the interphase. By tuning the diluent structure and concentration, we regulate the extent of this reaction to promote beneficial NaF formation, enabling stable anode-free sodium metal batteries cycling for over 800 cycles.

papers.title: Dynamics of liquid-liquid phase-separated microdroplets
papers.abstract: Synthetic mimics of biological condensates serve as a versatile platform for understanding the dynamics of liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) and the functional biomolecules encapsulated within the condensed microenvironment. In recent years, owing to their exceptional partitioning capabilities and material properties, these LLPS microdroplets have been widely studied for supporting complex functions, including self-assembly, catalysis, growth, division, motility, cargo transport, and pore formation, thereby demonstrating potential to develop ‘life-like’, evolvable synthetic systems. Furthermore, the heterogeneous and secluded microenvironment of these droplets enables them to regulate biomolecular functions in a spatiotemporal manner. Despite this, there is limited understanding of the dynamical aspects of LLPS microdroplets and their internal microenvironment, particularly from an experimental perspective. In this review, we highlight the complex dynamical aspects of the internal microenvironment of LLPS droplets and how it impacts the dynamics of encapsulated biomolecules and their functions. Furthermore, we also provide a perspective on how these dynamical features can be exploited to design ‘life-like’ protocells.

papers.title: A Hidden Deactivation Pathway of the Long-Lived MLCT State in Fe(HMTI)(CN)2 Revealed by Multireference Calculations
papers.abstract: Iron complexes are attractive earth-abundant alternatives to noble-metal photosensitizers, yet their metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) lifetimes are limited by fast nonradiative decay through low-lying metal-centered (MC) states. Fe(HMTI)(CN) 2 exhibits one of the longest excited-state lifetimes reported to date for iron complexes. Its fused-ring macrocyclic ligand HMTI was designed to suppress Fe–ligand bond elongation, thereby blocking relaxation through MC states and giving rise to a long-lived MLCT state. Nevertheless, the observed lifetime of 1.25 ns is shorter than expected from the idealy “nested” arrangement of the potential energy curves proposed previously, in which relaxation was considered only along the Fe–ligand distances. Here, DFT and multireference calculations that take all degrees of freedom into account reveal a previously unrecognized relaxation pathway through a T 1 /S 0 minimum-energy crossing point (MECP), in which one of the two diimine moieties of HMTI is deformed while the Fe–ligand distances remain essentially unchanged. This asymmetric deformation of the HMTI skeleton localizes the dπ orbital that is otherwise delocalized over the macrocycle, destabilizing the S 0 state more strongly than T 1 , so that the S 0 /T 1 gap narrows rapidly toward the MECP. These results identify a nonradiative deactivation channel from the T 1 state, which has 3 MLCT (d xz ->π*) character, to the ground state, consistent with the nanosecond MLCT lifetime observed experimentally. Our findings indicate that rigidifying the Fe–ligand bonds alone is not sufficient: suppressing asymmetric macrocycle deformation—and the accompanying modulation of the π/π* levels and dπ mixing—offers a complementary design strategy toward iron complexes with even longer-lived MLCT states.

papers.title: Single-and Multi-bead Coarse-grained Form Factors for SAXS Calculations
papers.abstract: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is widely used to study proteins in solution, but atomistic scattering calculations are computationally demanding for large systems and many-body simulations. We develop two coarse-grained, polynomial form factor models for proteins: a one-bead-per-residue amino acid model and a Martini bead-based model. We systematically derive the form factors using the single-bead approximation with rotamer-library averaging to incorporate amino acid conformational variability. The models are evaluated against atomistic calculations, existing coarse-grained form factors, and experimental SAXS data from the Small Angle Scattering Biological Data Bank, SASBDB. Compared with a two-bead residue model, the amino acid bead model shows improved agreement to atomic scattering model, achieving nearatomistic accuracy. The Martini bead form factors perform comparably, or better, to existing Martini form factors. Comparisons with experimental SAXS profiles show that both models achieve similar agreement when hydration-shell contributions are included. These results demonstrate that systematically parameterised coarse-grained form factors provide accurate and efficient SAXS calculations, supporting their use in large-scale biomolecular modelling and simulation-based SAXS analysis. Coarse-graining also enables scattering calculations for highly dense interacting systems.

papers.title: Pose-coupled native-interaction weighting in kinase ensemble docking: EGFR enrichment and CDK2 transfer
papers.abstract: Background. Ensemble docking can assign a high neural score to a ligand without showing whether the selected receptor-specific pose recovers interactions observed in target holo structures. We tested whether explicit recovery of target-native interactions adds early-ranking information to GNINA when both signals are evaluated for the same pose. Methods. Syndesis docked the EGFR DUD-E benchmark against four ATP-site holo structures, rescored the top Uni-Dock pose from each receptor with GNINA, and encoded interactions with ProLIF.
