A technical challenge is that ff19SB introduces residue-specific backbone dihedral energy correction maps (CMAPs), which required new support in GROMACS for residue-aware force-field preprocessing and topology generation. Unlike older force fields such as CHARMM27, in which CMAPs are parameterized using only atom types, ff19SB extends this scheme with additional amino-acid typing. Here, we describe how we ported and validated the Amber ff14SB and ff19SB force fields for use with GROMACS as AMBER14SB and AMBER19SB, respectively. The ported force fields reproduce the Amber reference topologies exactly, with per-interaction energies matching to within the single-precision floating-point limit (< 10 −7 kJ/mol). To achieve this level of consistency between Amber and GROMACS, we resolved discrepancies in their handling of fundamental constants, parameter precision, and improper-dihedral atom ordering logic. In long unrestrained ubiquitin simulations, the converted ff19SB reproduces the conformational free-energy profile obtained with the native Amber implementation. This work provides the first official port of an Amber force field to GROMACS in more than a decade, improving feature parity between the two simulation packages. We provide a reproducible porting and validation procedure that can be used for modified variants and future versions of Amber force fields.

papers.title: Electrocatalytic Hydrodeoxygenation of Aldehydes Enabled by Pd@CNTstabilized Pickering Emulsions
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrodeoxygenation (ECHDO) has the potential to produce high-value chemicals from aromatic aldehydes using water as a hydrogen source. However, the efficiency of this approach is limited by the low solubility of aromatic aldehydes in aqueous electrolytes, by electrical losses in organic electrolytes, and by generally low Faradaic efficiency and complex product separation. In addition, recent reports have revealed that aldehyde electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) predominantly yields alcohols, while their subsequent electrocatalytic hydrodeoxygenation remains a major challenge, limiting overall C–O bond cleavage. Here, we report the ECHDO of aromatic aldehydes using a Pd@CNTs catalyst located at the interface of a Pickering emulsion system. Our approach leverages the triphasic nature of the Pickering emulsion to create an effective environment for complex catalytic processes, enabling selective ECHDO of various aromatic aldehydes to valuable tolyl derivatives with up to >99% yield and ~62% Faradaic efficiency (FE). Mechanistic investigations confirm that the reaction is of electrocatalytic nature, and that the sequential ECH-ECHDO pathway proceeds through transient alcohol intermediates in our system. This strategy may thus provide alternative solutions to the ECHDO of biomass-derived aromatic aldehydes including lignin-derived aromatic aldehydes encountered in biorefineries and fine chemical synthesis.

papers.title: An Autonomous Passive MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
papers.abstract: Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ 2 -OH)[( E )-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kg MOF −1 day −1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating uniquely fully autonomous multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RH avg = 12.4 %, T avg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (I avg = 496 W m −2 ) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day −1 (185 mL kg MOF −1 day −1 ). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RH avg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

papers.title: Metal-and Additive-Free Transfer Hydrogenation of Nitrones to Hydroxylamine Derivatives with PhSiH3
papers.abstract: Hydroxylamine derivatives are essential structural motifs in numerous pharmaceuticals, bioactive compounds, and synthetic intermediates. Despite significant advances, the reduction of nitrones remains challenging owing to their inherent 1,3-dipolar character and limited efficient metal-free protocols. Therefore, this study reports a practical metal-and additive-free transfer hydrogenation of nitrones, employing a readily available PhSiH3 serving as the hydrogen donor. The findings demonstrated the effective conversion of a wide range of ketone-and aldehyde-derived nitrones into their corresponding hydroxylamine derivatives in good to excellent yields with remarkable chemoselectivity under mild conditions. The reaction is readily scalable and demonstrates broad functional group tolerance, accommodating bromo, chloro, fluoro, trifluoromethyl, thioether, thiophene, and furan substituents. Hence, the proposed operationally simple protocol provides a practical and sustainable strategy, facilitating the synthesis of structurally diverse

papers.title: Rapid, energy-lean sonochemical synthesis of metal-free polybenzoxazine bifunctional photocatalyst for H2O2 production and furfuryl alcohol oxidation
papers.abstract: The development of scalable, selective, and durable photocatalysts remains a major challenge in artificial photosynthesis. Herein, we introduce a new class of metal-free polybenzoxazine frameworks synthesized through an unconventional template- and surfactant-free emulsion sonochemical strategy, enabling systematic elucidation of the structure–property relationships governing photocatalytic activity. This green, energy-efficient process affords gram-scale quantities within an hour, circumventing the substantial energetic demands typically associated with the synthesis of architecturally complex porous photocatalysts. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the benzoxazine-rich framework selectively drives the visible-light-mediated twoelectron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR), facilitating efficient H2O2 production from water and molecular oxygen under ambient conditions. Among this series, P-mtt exhibits the highest activity, achieving an H2O2 evolution rate of 1250 μmol g-1 h-1 and accumulating 6.4 mM H2O2 after 24 h of continuous irradiation while retaining excellent structural and photochemical stability. P-mtt further demonstrates efficient photon utilization, delivering an apparent quantum yield of 12% at 420 nm and a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.48%. Notably, its performance translates to practical conditions, enabling efficient H2O2 production directly from unpurified seawater. Combined ultrafast spectroscopic measurements and theoretical simulations indicate that sub-nanosecond localization of photogenerated electrons from both free-carrier and excitonic states at catalytic reaction centers facilitates efficient charge utilization and selective 2e- ORR. Beyond H2O2 photosynthesis, P-mtt exhibits remarkable bifunctionality by simultaneously driving the Achmatowicz oxidation of furfuryl alcohol to a value-added pyranone intermediate through a decoupled energy-transfer pathway, while continuously producing H2O2. By integrating scalable low-energy synthesis, high photocatalytic efficiency, and dual-function catalytic selectivity, P-mtt represents a promising polymeric platform for decentralized H2O2 production and sustainable solar-driven chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Breaking Enantiopurity Paradigm: A Chiral Catalyst That Requires Enantioimpurity for Enantioselectivity
papers.abstract: Asymmetric catalysis traditionally relies on enantiopure ligands to achieve high enantioselectivity. However, nonlinear effects (NLEs) can enable scalemic catalysts to match or even surpass their enantiopure counterparts. Here, we report an unprecedented phenomenon in zinc-catalyzed alkylation of benzaldehyde using 3,3'-diiodo-BINOL ligand: the enantiopure ligand yields a racemic product, while scalemic versions generate significant enantioselectivity (up to 60% ee). This challenges the paradigm that enantiopure ligands are inherently superior. Mechanistic studies reveal multiple active catalytic species in equilibrium, with distinct enantioselectivities dependent on ligand enantiopurity, catalyst loading, and temperature. Kinetic analyses and VTNA studies confirm non-constant catalyst orders, suggesting higher-order aggregates (e.g., trimers) alongside dimers. This work demonstrates how scalemic ligands can outperform enantiopure ones, offering a new perspective on chiral amplification and practical advantages in catalytic design.

papers.title: Linking wind-power fluctuation to degradation of PEM water electrolyzer
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is highly attractive for renewable-powered hydrogen production, yet its degradation under realistic wind-power fluctuations remains insufficiently understood. In this study, a durability assessment framework was established by replaying a real annual wind-power profile at different acceleration factors, combined with electrochemical diagnostics, post-mortem characterization, and degradation extrapolation. The results show that faster replay of power fluctuations leads to more pronounced performance degradation under dynamic operation, while the degradation remains less severe than that during steady electrolysis at high current density. Nyquist and distribution of relaxation times analyses reveal that the degradation is dominated by the increase in charge-transfer resistance. Post-mortem characterization further reveals distinct degradation pathways: high-current steady operation induces stronger Ir redistribution and dissolution-migration behavior, whereas rapid fluctuation promotes surface reconstruction toward Ir3+-rich states. Based on these findings, a two-stage degradation model was established to estimate the annual degradation under the original wind-power profile, yielding an overall prediction error of only 0.6%. These results provide a quantitative framework for understanding and predicting electrolyzer durability under wind-coupled operation.

papers.title: Ageing mechanisms and regeneration of an LMFP/NMC blended cathode
papers.abstract: Ageing and recycling studies are essential to assess the durability and circularity of emerging commercial battery chemistries. Here, the ageing mechanisms of a commercial lithium-ion cells containing an LMFP/NMC blended cathode are investigated after dynamic and calendar ageing. The dynamically aged cell exhibits a 52% loss of its initial capacity after 700 cycles. While no significant capacity fading is observed after 18 months of calendar ageing. Postmortem characterization combined with electrochemical analysis reveals that capacity fade arises from both loss of active material (LAM) and loss of lithium inventory (LLI). Incremental capacity analysis shows the progressive fading of all redox contributions, while the disappearance of NMC-related electrochemical activity and thermal signature points to severe degradation of the layered oxide component. Structural and morphological analyses confirm lattice parameter changes, crystallite size reduction, particle cracking, and partial deterioration of the cathode surface. ICP-MS further reveals cathode–anode cross-talk, with dissolved Mn, Ni, and Nb species detected on the graphite anode after ageing. Finally, solvent-free relithiation is applied to regenerate the aged LMFP/NMC blend. The LMFP phase is efficiently relithiated and its electrochemical activity is largely restored, whereas the NMC component remains structurally damaged despite partial relithiation. These findings highlight both the potential and the limitations of direct regeneration strategies for blended commercial cathodes, showing that the performance benefits of cathode blending come with new challenges for recycling processes.

papers.title: Smolyak Hierarchy-Inspired Protocol (SHIP): Hierarchical Exploration of Sparse-Reward Spaces with GFlowNets
papers.abstract: Generative modelling is a useful methodology for large-scale combinatorial problems involving many possible candidates. Such problems typically suffer from exponential scaling in complexity as the size of the system being studied is increased, and this impedes search space exploration and discovery. This work explores the parallel between the problem of generating high-value samples from a high-dimensional distribution and choosing a sparse set of grid points for high-dimensional integration using the Smolyak hierarchy. The proposed method, called Smolyak Hierarchy-Inspired Protocol (SHIP), is a Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet) based framework in which high-value higher-dimensional samples are generated by extending up from high-value lower-dimensional samples sequentially and iteratively. This protocol is tested on a model problem of approximating path-integral solutions to open quantum dynamics using Small Matrix Path Integral for reward evaluation. We show that the capacity of this approach to circumvent problems related to poor reward connectivity is drastically improved when action space representation is updated based on interpretable features identified in solutions at intermediate steps. These results serve to motivate the implementation of this protocol more broadly for other generative problems in physical and chemical systems.

papers.title: Phosphoestamer Sequence Controls Capture/Release
papers.abstract: While the synthesis of sequence-defined polymers is becoming established, the next frontier is sequence-determined function. Sequenced-defined oligo/polyphosphoesters (phosphoestamers) of dodecane diol (C12) and hexa(ethylene glycol) (HEG) show sequence-dependent and salt-responsive self-assembly profiles which arise from electrostatic interactions of their phosphate backbones. In this work, we used 24mer sequence isomers, C1212-HEG12 and (C12-HEG)12, to investigate the mutual interaction of phosphoestamer sequence and resulting self-assembly with the phosphate-selective anion-binding capability of a bisindolylpyrrole fluorescent probe. Our results show that the probe coordinates phosphates within phosphoestamers, and that phosphate recognition can be modulated by controlling local environment through monomer sequence and self-assembly. Further to this, we measured salt-triggered structural changes, producing a system capable of capture-and-release of the probe via competitive anion binding. This research creates new opportunities to use phosphoestamers in downstream applications, such as drug delivery and diagnostics.

papers.title: Harnessing phosphine oxides interactions with HF and HBF4 to enable the hydrofluorination of alkynes
papers.abstract: Synthetic methodologies for the metal-free fluorofunctionalisation of alkynes to give hydrofluorination products still remain scarce. In this paper, we report on detailed studies on the interaction between the phosphine oxides R 3 P=O (R = Cy, Ph, Morph) and hydrogen fluoride. The hydrogen fluoride adducts R 3 P=O-HF form with gaseous BF 3 a tetrafluoroborate salt. The characterisation methods of fluorine-specific interactions of HF with the oxides include NMR and IR spectrsocopy, X-Ray crystallography, TGA measurements and 18 O isotopic labeling studies. The tetrafluoroborate salt [Cy 3 POH][BF 4 ] was applied to allow for a simple and metal-free hydrofluorination of alkynes. The conversion into fluoroalkenes or gem-difluoroalkanes at room temperature can be controlled by variation of the temperature or by addition of the Lewis-acid BF 3 ⋅OEt 2 .

papers.title: Towards unified catalyst discovery through transferable composition–activity relationships
papers.abstract: Multinary materials provide vast compositional flexibility for optimizing electrocatalytic reactions, yet systematic exploration of their composition space is challenging. Density functional theory (DFT)-derived models, thin-film materials libraries for high-throughput characterization, and nanoparticle-based electrochemical screening provide complementary routes for catalyst discovery. However, it has to be shown that composition–activity trends obtained from these different approaches are transferable, which would allow their combination into a unified approach. Here, we evaluate the transferability of composition–activity relationships across these experimental and theoretical approaches, using the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in the quaternary system Ir–Pd–Pt–Ru as a model case. Three complementary datasets, consisting of ORR data from DFT-derived theoretical activities, thin-film materials libraries, and electrodeposited nanoparticles, were used to independently construct continuous composition–activity landscapes using Gaussian Process Regression. To enable direct cross-platform comparison despite differences in electrochemical techniques, absolute activity metrics and sample density across the quaternary system, the data were converted into rank-normalized activity landscapes. It is shown that, regardless of their differences, all three approaches consistently identify Pd-rich compositions with moderate Pt incorporation and low Ru/Ir content as high-activity regions. While the detailed shapes of the obtained activity landscapes differ between the approaches, the dominant compositional trends are consistent. These results demonstrate that the composition–activity trends are transferable across theory-based, thin-film, and nanoparticle catalyst screening platforms, providing the basis for a general strategy of accelerated catalyst discovery combining different datasets.

papers.title: Expanding Metal Complex Enzyme Inhibitor Discovery Through High-Throughput Virtual Screening
papers.abstract: Transition metal complexes occupy regions of three-dimensional chemical space that organic scaffolds cannot easily reach, yet their use in target-based drug discovery has been held back by the absence of structurally diverse, readily available screening libraries. We addressed this by curating MOSAIC ( M etal c o mplex library for S tructure- Ai ded I n silico s c reening), a first collection of 16,901 neutral, drug-like metal complexes assembled directly from experimentally determined geometries deposited in the Cambridge Structural Database. Docking this library against the allosteric site of the oncology target MAT2A (methionine adenosyltransferase 2A) with MetalDock returned the copper complex Cu1-Complex , from which we designed the diamagnetic zinc analogue Zn1-Complex for detailed study. A combination of nanoDSF, ligand-observed and competition NMR, HDX-MS, site-directed mutagenesis and molecular dynamics placed Zn1-Complex in the allosteric pocket and showed that it engages the site differently from the established inhibitor Pf-9366 , while functionally inhibiting the enzyme. Together, these results establish MOSAIC as a validated, generalisable platform for target-based metal complex discovery as the first scalable strategy for systematically exploiting metal complexes against any well-defined binding site.

papers.title: Post mortem insights into swollen LiFePO4 batteries: reversible degradation and suitability for direct recycling
papers.abstract: Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries are increasingly deployed in electric vehicles, raising concerns regarding the management of prematurely retired cells, particularly those affected by swelling. In this work, a comprehensive post mortem investigation of a swollen LFP prismatic cell is conducted to elucidate the degradation mechanisms associated with swelling and to assess the feasibility of cathode regeneration. A multiscale characterization combining electrochemical testing, gas and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction, Mössbauer spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, X-ray fluorescence, and FTIR spectroscopy is employed. The results reveal advanced electrolyte degradation, gas generation, and electrolyte dry-out, leading to strong spatial heterogeneity in lithium distribution across the cathode, while the olivine structure of LFP remains preserved. Despite significant lithium inventory loss and local ageing effects, no evident irreversible structural damage of the active material is observed as the olivine structure remains preserved. A mild aqueous regeneration process based on lithium reinsertion using ascorbic acid successfully restores the cathode material at the 100 g scale, yielding electrochemical performance comparable to that of the pristine LFP. These findings suggest that cell swelling is largely associated with electrolyte-related phenomena and does not preclude efficient direct regeneration of LFP cathodes, supporting the relevance of direct recycling strategies for swollen lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: One pot synthesis of carbon dots derived from d-glucose monohydrate: Comprehensive investigation on optical properties and luminescent mechanism
papers.abstract: The best optical properties of N-CDs from D-glucose monohydrate and urea have been synthesized. The use of D-glucose monohydrate as a carbon source and urea as a nitrogen source offers many benefits, including low cost, easy availability, high quantum yield, and high carbon content. The effects of various urea masses on the surfaces of CDs and N-CDs were evaluated. The blue fluorescence of N-CDs A is the highest intensity with average lifetime of 4.18 ns. UV Vis spectra show absorption at 255 nm due to π→π* transitions in C=C bonds and at 326 nm attributed to n→π* transitions in carbonyl groups. The Tauc plot calculation yielded a lowest band gap energy of 3.84 eV (N-CDs A). N-CDs A increases the homogeneity of particle distribution and reduces agglomeration with particle size of 4.46 nm from TEM analysis. The investigation revealed that the incorporation of nitrogen into carbon dots enhances optical properties and electronic structure, as well as producing more uniform particles.

papers.title: Photoluminescent and photoconductive BaZrS3 films grown at device-compatible temperatures from stable sulfide precursors
papers.abstract: Chalcogenide perovskites (CPs) are attractive earth-abundant, non-toxic light absorbers. BaZrS3 is a prominent candidate in the CP family due to its 1.7-2.0 eV band gap, which aligns well with a top absorber in Si-based tandem solar cells. The main bottleneck in CP photovoltaics lies in the thin-film crystallization. So far, CP thin films have been crystallized either at device-incompatible temperatures above 900 °C or under high sulfur pressures at lower temperatures, which yields suboptimal optoelectronic properties due to S interstitial defects (Si). To overcome kinetic barriers at moderate temperatures without the need for excess sulfur, we use a stable, amorphous sulfide precursor film that readily crystallizes during post-annealing under S-poor conditions. We report a synthesis route at 600 °C that is robust towards oxygen contamination and still produces BaZrS3 thin films with some of the narrowest x-ray diffraction peaks reported so far, indicating high crystallinity. Importantly, the films exhibit photoconductivity, a bandgap-aligned photoluminescence peak, and intragrain carrier mobility of 70 cm2V-1s-1. Oxygen segregates into nano-voids at grain boundaries, preserving high-quality intra-grain transport pathways. Our results demonstrate that BaZrS3 can achieve promising optoelectronic quality at processing temperatures compatible with tandem solar cell integration, shifting the primary challenge towards grain-boundary passivation.

papers.title: Ultrasensitive Polymeric Fluorescent Nanothermometers Based on Environment-Sensitive DCM-Like Dyes: Decoupling Aggregation, Polarity, and Viscosity Contributions
papers.abstract: Temperature measurements at the nanoscale are essential for understanding physiological and pathological processes. Here, we report fluorescent polymeric nanothermometers (FPTSs) based on thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) endfunctionalized with environment-sensitive DCM-like fluorophores, which self-assemble into well-defined nanoparticles in aqueous media. Two closely related probes, DCMC and DCMQ, exhibiting similar solvatochromic behavior but opposite aggregation tendencies (aggregation-caused quenching, ACQ, vs aggregation-induced emission, AIE), are used to screen the respective contributions of aggregation, polarity, and microviscosity in the temperature-dependent fluorescence response. Upon heating, the LCST-driven collapse of PNIPAM triggers nanoscale reorganization of the polymeric assemblies, leading to a local environment of reduced polarity and increased microviscosity. This results in a fluorescence enhancement accompanied by a spectral blue shift, enabling both intensityand ratiometric-based temperature sensing. The systems display high sensitivity, including in the physiological temperature range. In particular, the DCMC-based nanothermometer combines a large Stokes shift with near-infrared emission, highlighting its potential for bioimaging applications.

papers.title: Assembly-by-Elimination of 3D Nanoarchitectures with Designed Interstitials and Interweaves
papers.abstract: The realization of metamaterials with tailored functional responses requires three-dimensional (3D) architectures that combine low packing fractions with complex topology. Such metastructures can enhance strength-to-weight ratios, accommodate large deformations, manipulate light and enable efficient transport and actuation under 3D confinement. However, extending topology-driven design from the macroscale to the nanoscale remains challenging due to limitations in 3D nanofabrication. Although self-assembly offers a path to realizing 3D organizations, it typically favors densely packed, high-symmetry structures, making it difficult to achieve intricate, low-density architectures with complex connectivity. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Assembly-By-Elimination (ABEL), a strategy for designing periodic topologically complex low-packing-fraction 3D nanoscale metastructures. ABEL begins by assembling a fully interconnected, high-packing-fraction template lattice, followed by programmable removal of selected structural elements, yielding a targeted metastructure. We experimentally demonstrate the ABEL strategy using, as a 3D template, a body-centered-cubic DNA lattice composed of DNA cubic frames with a sequence-specific set of bonds. After assembly, addressable elimination of bonds sculpts the template into an open metastructure by disconnecting prescribed individual frames or sublattices, thus realizing low-density nanoscale organizations and interpenetrating networks. We then investigate the Young’s modulus of created metastructures, and show that it scales approximately linearly with bond density, directly linking nanoscale architecture to mechanical response. By combining designed 3D lattice templates with addressable elimination of bonds and structural elements, ABEL provides a route to realizing complex architectures with prescribed nanoscale topology.

papers.title: Tuning hydrogel mechanics through synergistic metal–ligand coordination and chemical fueling
papers.abstract: Chemically fueled anhydride formation offers a powerful strategy to create polymer networks with transient mechanical reinforcement. In this work, metallo-supramolecular hydrogels were developed with two independent crosslinking mechanisms, metal-ligand coordination and transient anhydride formation, yielding materials capable of intrinsic self-healing and temporally controllable properties. Bis(pyridin-2-ylmethyl)amine (DPA) units were incorporated into polymers as ligands. The coordination strength of the resulting persistent dynamic cross-links is tunable by varying both the metal ion (Fe 2+ or Ni 2+ ) and nature of the ligands through substitution with chloro or methoxy groups. Carboxylic acid repeat units provide fuel-driven transient anhydride formation on treatment with carbodiimides. The resulting transient cross-links can be tuned by changing the carboxylic acid structure, affecting the lifetime of the transient state and its stiffness. Lap-shear-inspired healing tests show that the materials achieve more than 90% healing under fueled conditions within 15 h. Notably, the fuel-driven process accelerates healing resulting from the persistent dynamic metal-ligand coordination. This work demonstrates a versatile platform for soft materials with programmable mechanics and autonomous self-healing.

papers.title: Programming Rotational Register to Prescribe Crystal Polymorphism
papers.abstract: Crystal polymorphism underlies many of the distinct properties of condensed matter, yet for atoms and molecules, polymorphs are typically selected by thermodynamics and kinetics rather than by design. Programming crystal polymorphism is particularly challenging for structures that share identical bond connectivity but differ only in the relative orientation of neighboring building blocks. Although programmable self-assembly can prescribe which building blocks bind, it does not directly encode how they are oriented once bonded. Here, we introduce the rotational register, the relative torsional orientation between bonded building blocks, as an independent bond descriptor that complements programmable valence and connectivity. Progressive symmetry breaking of the sequence-programmed DNA pattern at the vertices of DNA tetrahedra provides increasingly precise control over the rotational register, enabling the selective assembly of tetrahedrally coordinated crystal polymorphs: type-II clathrate, cubic diamond, and hexagonal diamond. Cubic and hexagonal diamond differ only in the rotational register encoded at a single vertex type, yet this local rule controls polymorphism while preserving identical bond connectivity. The programmed polymorphs are validated by small-angle X-ray scattering, electron tomography, 2 and both Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, reprogramming the rotational register enables reversible transformation between cubic and hexagonal diamond. These results establish rotational register as a programmable bond descriptor, complementing programmable connectivity with explicit control over the orientation of bonded building blocks.

papers.title: Experimental and Simulation Study of Foliar Nanofertilizers through Cellulose-nanofibril Templating
papers.abstract: Despite the higher absorption efficiency of foliar fertilizers compared to soil fertilizers, the risk of fertilizer loss remains. Additionally, traditional foliar fertilizers tend to form large, irregular particles on leaves, hindering plant absorption. This study investigated the effects of three types of cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs), negatively charged CNF (TCNF), unmodified CNF, and positively charged CNF (GCNF), as functional additives in foliar fertilizer formulations. It is observed that incorporating 0.4 wt.% CNFs (CNF, TCNF, and GCNF) increased the suspension viscosity. All CNFs reduced the KNO3 average particle size from the microscale to the nanoscale, 2 with 0.4 wt.% CNF lowering it from 4.26 ± 1.81 μm to 0.12 ± 0.13 μm. Classical molecular dynamics simulations identified that the cellulose surface provides multiple nucleation sites, resulting in more and smaller fertilizer nanoparticles. Moreover, CNFs increased the adhesion rate of fertilizer suspensions. This retention trend became more evident with charged CNFs, increasing adhesion rate from 57.05 ± 2.98% to nearly 70%. The KNO3/GCNF treatment increased tomato yield by 125% compared with the water control. These findings demonstrate that CNFs provide a simple, effective strategy for developing additive-based fast-acting nanofertilizers, addressing the inherent challenges of conventional foliar fertilizers.

papers.title: Mechanistic Determinants of Passive Permeation in Binary Lipid Membranes from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Passive permeation is a fundamental determinant of pharmacokinetics. The models that simulate permeation pathways and predict their energetic requirements need to account for the complexity of biological membranes. However, the impact of lipid bilayer composition on the thermodynamics of the passive permeation process is not yet fully understood. This study systematically evaluates how specific lipid types influence the free energy profiles through binary lipid bilayers for six xenobiotics with structural diversity: amantadine, diclofenac, metoprolol, pindolol, ranitidine, and scopolamine. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted using MemCross, an all-atom MD protocol based on the Accelerated Weight Histogram (AWH) method, for five binary lipid mixtures. The bilayer models combined 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-snglycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) with cholesterol (CHOL), 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3phosphoethanolamine (POPE), 1,2-diarachidonoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DAPC), or sphingomyelin (SM) to represent the lipid diversity of human plasma cell membranes. Our results demonstrate the lipid features that significantly modulate the free energy landscapes. We show that permeation is governed jointly by lipid composition and the intrinsic molecular properties of the permeants. We identify the mechanistic descriptors that drive the permeation process, explaining how they collectively contribute to passive permeation outcomes. Based on this knowledge, multivariate models were established, identifying key descriptors that can be obtained from rapid unbiased MD simulations.

papers.title: 3D Printing of Metal–Organic Polyhedra: From Porous Molecules to Spatially Programmed Porous Architectures
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing of microporous materials remains challenging due to the intrinsic processing limitations of extended porous frameworks, which often require binders or complex inks. Herein, we report the first 3D printing of metal–organic polyhedra (MOPs). Our approach exploits the ability of MOP solutions to self-gelate in response to chemical stimuli, forming gels composed exclusively of porous molecular units. These gels can be processed via direct ink writing (DIW) to produce dimensionally stable, hierarchically porous 3D architectures with preserved porosity and with retained porosity and, in some cases, increased accessible surface area relative to the pristine solids. Building on this, the simplicity of our strategy enables dual-MOP printing, combining complementary chemical functionalities in a single object while maintaining structural integrity and hierarchical porosity. We also demonstrate spatially controlled multi-material printing through sequential deposition of different MOP-based inks, enabling Janus structures and multilayered aerogels. This work establishes MOPs as processable porous building blocks for additive manufacturing, providing a versatile platform for producing multifunctional porous materials with programmable architecture and 3D-resolved composition.

papers.title: Foldamers with Two Distinct Helical Motifs Controlled by Solvent
papers.abstract: Abiotic foldamers that switch between distinct, well-defined geometries are rare. Here, we report a structurally simple series of oligomers with alternating ortho -phenylene and 2,3-pyrazinylene repeat units. Deconvolution of variable-temperature ¹H NMR spectra, with the help of ab initio chemical shift predictions, shows that the oligomers favor a compact, arene-stacked helix in chloroform but a structurally distinct extended helix in acetone. The longest oligomer investigated, a heptamer, exhibits nearly perfect solvent-switching behavior at low temperature, effectively doubling its length in acetone compared to chloroform. X-ray crystallography confirms that the hybrid backbone is capable of both folding motifs. While arene–arene stacking drives folding in chloroform, non-classical intramolecular C-H···N hydrogen bonds appear to stabilize the alternate conformers in acetone. Both geometries are enthalpically favored in their respective solvents, highlighting how a balance of weak, competing interactions can be harnessed to achieve large-scale geometry changes in synthetic foldamers.

papers.title: Highly stable microporous water for energy absorption
papers.abstract: Water has poor compressibility. However, introducing hydrophobic porosity into water can make it highly compressible, as water molecules can be squeezed into the hydrophobic pores under pressure. This offers an exciting opportunity to use water to absorb mechanical shock. One straightforward approach to deliver this concept of microporous water is to disperse hydrophobic porous particles in water. However, using highly porous metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) in water poses a stability challenge: whether MOF particles can form a uniform suspension and remain stable over time without degradation. Herein, we propose a strategy that not only addresses stability concerns but also enhances the energy absorption of MOF intrusion under mechanical impact: shielding the MOF crystal with a mesoporous silica shell. The silica shell provides the long-term chemical and physical stability of the MOF particle, and its mesopores also allow external water to enter the MOF pores under pressure, albeit requiring higher mechanical input. Given the nature of the coating method, we envision it can be deployed across many different MOF materials and is a scalable approach to making stable microporous water for energy absorption.

papers.title: Water transport in MOF monoliths under pressure
papers.abstract: Pressurised intrusion into hydrophobic metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is of considerable interest for energy absorption and fluid transport applications, yet the transport mechanisms in monolithic architectures remain poorly understood. Here, in-situ synchrotron radiographic imaging and powder diffraction have been employed to reveal the mechanism of pressurised water intrusion in ZIF-8 monoliths, through simultaneous visualisation of water transport and monitoring evolution in the crystal structure. The mechanism is dependent on the compactness of the monolith, with denser monoliths exhibiting a distinct edge-to-centre intrusion mechanism, whereas loosely packed monoliths display spatially uniform intrusion across the entire crosssection. Dimensions of the monolith sample also influence the intrusion pressure and extrusion kinetics by altering the transport path length for guest water molecules. These findings provide the first direct experimental evidence of pressure-driven water transport in MOF monoliths and reveal the mechanisms responsible for water intrusion in monoliths with varying dimensions and compacities. Moreover, this is the first study to report simultaneous synchrotron diffraction and imaging at elevated pressures, facilitated by the development of a novel high-pressure sample environment that allows in-situ measurements and has broad potential utility in combined imaging and diffraction studies at elevated pressures.

papers.title: PDB Manipulation Suite (PDBMS): A browser-based toolkit for PDB file manipulation, molecule building and biophysical analysis, easily extendable via reasoning models
papers.abstract: We present here the PDB Manipulation Suite (PDBMS, https://pdbms.altervista.org/ ), a modular hub of web apps and platforms designed for the seamless creation, edition, and analysis of biomolecular coordinate files, all online and client-side i.e. without any user files even passing by any server. The suite is organized into specialized sub-platforms: (i) PDBMS-tools for rapid structure analysis and editing, supporting residue renumbering, sequence extraction, B-factor hacking, CIF/PDB conversion, basic calculations such as distances or solvent accessibility, and various means for mapping data; (ii) Web-PackMol for the assembly of complex molecular systems; and (iii) Web-MDA and the Conformational Ensemble Inspector for the deep analysis and inspection of single structures as well as ensembles coming from molecular dynamics trajectories, BioEmu predictions of conformational landscapes, docking poses, NMR models, etc., all assisted by a novel form of AI copilot that we introduce here. The various tools at the PDBMS facilitate inference of structural details, dynamics, and interactions across molecules and across time or ensemble indexes; others aid in the visualization of various kinds of data including AlphaFold 3 confidence scores and outputs from modern NMR spectroscopy pipelines. Since the source code for all tools at the PDBMS is inherently open and was developed largely with AI reasoning models at Google’s AI Studio, it is extremely easy to modify or add new functionalities at will. We demonstrate this by providing customized tools to assist the editing and visualization of outputs from NMR-specific software like NMRtist and Sparky; and we also demonstrate how the AI agent built into the Web-MDA app can provide new functionalities on request including modification of the app’s own GUI. By providing a “zero-footprint” environment available out of the box with no installs, no downloads, no registration, and trivially clonable code for custom local modifications and reuse, we hope the PDBMS will facilitate work in structural bioinformaticians, structural biology and molecular modeling online but preserving absolute data confidentiality, extreme portability across devices and operating systems, and maximal flexibility. We also hope these tools and ideas for in-software AI use will inspire others to develop further smart, client-only scientific software.

papers.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Regio- and Enantioselective Hydroamination of Allenes: Direct Access to α-Tertiary Chiral Allylic Amines
papers.abstract: We disclose a highly regio- and enantioselective Ir(I)-catalyzed hydroamination of 1,1-disubstituted allenes, providing a broadly applicable access to α-tertiary chiral allylic amines, very relevant structural motifs that are mostly inaccessible through other enantioselective strategies. The method employs an a-aminopyridine as nucleophile, and displays a broad substrate scope, accommodating both aryl- and alkyl-substituted allenes. Removal of the pyridine moiety of the products yields synthetically challenging primary allylic amines bearing α-tetrasubstituted stereocenters. Notably, addition of i -PrOH after completion of the hydroamination enables an in situ transfer hydrogenation of the generated alkene to deliver the corresponding a-tertiary saturated amines with equally high selectivities. The use of trisubstituted allenes in the hydroamination protocol is also feasible, affording in this case a-secondary allylic amines, also with high selectivities. Finally, experimental and computational mechanistic studies support a hydrometalation/C–N bond-forming sequence as the preferred reaction pathway, with the C-N reductive elimination step identified as enantio- and TOF-determining.

papers.title: Self-Assembly Drives Rare-Earth Separations in a Family of M4L4 Cages
papers.abstract: Rare-earth elements are indispensable to high-tech applications, making efficient rare-earth separations increasingly essential. An emerging approach to these challenging separations is the self-assembly of lanthanide-based supramolecular cages. In this study, we establish design principles for self-assembly-driven rare-earth separations by investigating four ligands with distinct substituents (termed L -Cbz, L -alkene, L -propyl, and L -benzyl). We found that these ligands react with rare-earth metals to yield M 4 L 4 cages, M 2 L 2 complexes, or no self-assembly products, depending on the identity of the metal. Single crystal X-ray diffraction shows that Dy 4 ( L -benzyl) 4 cages adopt a tetrahedral geometry, while pure L -Cbz precipitates from La 2 ( L -Cbz) 2 solution, suggesting that M 2 L 2 is an unstable intermediate. Our results indicate that the bulk and flexibility of the ligand substituents modulates these cage-formation thresholds, providing design rules for L -based rare-earth separations. In a simple separation procedure, we found that L -Cbz exhibits outstanding separation factors (SF) for mixtures involving early lanthanides, achieving SF values of 639 for an La/Dy mixture, 835 for a Nd/Lu mixture, and 1767 for an La/Lu mixture. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) measurements reveal that inter-ligand interaction, ligand-arm flexibility, and M–N bond lengths collectively govern M 4 L 4 cage formation, providing practical guidelines for designing ligands for self-assembly-based rare-earth separations.

papers.title: Self-centring structural damping with MOF-based compressible liquids
papers.abstract: Introducing hydrophobic cavities to water makes a compressible liquid that can absorb mechanical energy. Herein, we present a self-centring, energy-absorbing damping technology based on this material concept and demonstrate its potential in seismic protection. We used a water-based compressible liquid that absorbs mechanical energy via water intrusion into hydrophobic metal-organic frameworks under pressure and recovers its volume when the pressure is removed, enabling reversible energy dissipation. We conducted a systematic study, from a novel mechanical design to ensure the damper works under both compression and tension, to mechanical testing of the damper, both standalone and within a metallic frame structure, and numerical simulation of the damper in protecting a pile-supported wharf against representative earthquake motions. We demonstrated that such a compressible liquid damper can effectively limit structural deformation, reduce mechanical strain, and eliminate residual deformation after the loading event. Such advantages over traditional dampers are underpinned by the intrinsic nature of compressible liquids, including a substantial bulk modulus before intrusion occurs, which enhances initial structural stiffness; reversibility that offers selfcentring; and energy dissipation that reduces the energy transmitted to the structure. Moreover, the damping performance is highly tunable, simply by using different porous materials and liquids, without changing the damper design. Altogether, this work offers the prospect of compressible liquid dampers for vibration damping, with potential applications in various civil and mechanical engineering fields.

papers.title: Saturated Organic Poly-ionomer Films Match Proteins as Surprising Electronic Conductors
papers.abstract: We demonstrate efficient long-range electronic transport through ultrathin (<100 nm) multilayers of highly charged, non-conjugated polyionomers (PIs), a class of organic materials fundamentally distinct from conventional organic semiconductors. Layer-by-layer assembled films of poly(allylamine hydrochloride) (PAH) on poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) stacks exhibit nearly temperature-independent conductance between 80 and 300 K and weak thickness dependence. Impedance spectroscopy and time-dependent electrical measurements establish that transport is electronic rather than ionic, while the absence of charge accumulation during UV photoelectron spectroscopy and Kelvin probe measurements indicates efficient charge dissipation throughout the films. The transport efficiency of the PI films is comparable to, and, for thicker films, exceeds, that of electron-conducting protein films. The reproducible experimental results are incompatible with quantum tunneling or thermally activated hopping, pointing to an unconventional transport regime. We hypothesize that electrostatic and structural disorder within the highly charged polymer network generates a manifold of broad, spatially distributed localized electronic states connected by percolation-like tunneling pathways, with electronic polarization facilitating long-range transport. Our results show charge-rich PIs as a platform for electron transport in soft matter and suggest that collective electrostatic interactions may enable long-range charge transport in the absence of molecular conjugation or band formation.

papers.title: MolecuAR: A Multilingual WebAR Molecular Visualization Tool Connected to PubChem for Chemical Education
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional molecular representation is important in chemistry education, yet preparing interactive augmented-reality resources can require specialized authoring and molecule-specific assets. MolecuAR is an open, mobile-first WebAR educational software prototype that combines multilingual name resolution, PubChem-connected structure retrieval, browser-based ball-and-stick rendering, an expandable property panel, and a human-in-the-loop development process involving ChatGPT 5.6. Repository and release records were used to distinguish documented implementation from unsupported claims about development speed or learning effectiveness. An initial audit of release v1.0.1 identified missing imports that prevented the detailed information panel and front/rear camera control from operating. These integration faults were corrected in v1.1.0. Targeted follow-up testing on a mobile device confirmed that the information panel expands and retrieves PubChem-derived properties and that the camera control switches between front- and rear-facing modes. Representative multilingual, name, and CID queries and structure loading remained functional. The software is openly available through GitHub Pages and archived on Zenodo. Cross-device performance, hand-tracking robustness, and learning outcomes have not yet been evaluated systematically. MolecuAR therefore provides a traceable proof-of-concept for database-connected, AI-assisted educational software development while preserving human responsibility for chemistry, pedagogy, testing, and scientific claims.

papers.title: Spin–Phonon Coupling in Molecular Qubits and Organosuperelasticity in Molecular Crystals: A Review
papers.abstract: Molecular symmetry, rooted in group theory, provides a unifying language that connects the spatial arrangement of atoms to the electronic, magnetic, and mechanical behaviour of matter. This review examines two arenas in which symmetry-based reasoning has proven especially powerful. First, in molecular electron-spin qubits, group-theoretical selection rules identify the vibrational modes most strongly coupled to electron-spin states and thereby govern spin–phonon coupling, spin–lattice relaxation, and coherence; the [Fe4S4]+ cluster family and a series of tetragonal transition-metal complexes serve as illustrative cases. Second, in molecular crystals, a single symmetry element can dictate the direction and reversibility of large mechanical deformations, a phenomenon termed organosuperelasticity. Across both arenas, controlling symmetry offers a rational route to controlling function.

papers.title: Digital Analytical Twins: A Specimen-Centric Architecture for Self-Driving Analytical Laboratories
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories increasingly combine robotic handling, automated instruments, workflow orchestration, machine learning, digital twins and autonomous experiment planners. In this literature the central question is usually framed as: which experiment should be performed next? For analytical science, microscopy and surface analysis, an equally fundamental question is often left implicit: what is the persistent digital object on which those experiments are performed? Analytical instruments rarely measure an abstract material; they measure specific regions of heterogeneous physical specimens, often through different coordinate systems, fields of view, contrast mechanisms, sampling depths and spatial resolutions. Without a persistent specimen-level representation, an autonomous analytical laboratory cannot reliably know whether a feature observed by optical microscopy is the same feature later interrogated by SEM, EDS, XPS, SIMS or AFM. This paper introduces the Digital Analytical Twin (DAT) as a specimen-centric computational object for autonomous analytical science. A DAT is not merely an image archive or laboratory record. It is a structured, persistent representation of a physical specimen that encodes specimen identity, geometry, coordinate systems, fiducial references, regions of interest, analytical observations, multimodal layers, provenance, uncertainty and temporal integrity. We argue that the DAT is the missing specimen layer between instrument digital twins and experimental planners. Instrument twins model what an instrument can do and how it may fail; planners decide what should be attempted; the DAT represents the physical specimen as an analytical object, enabling instruments and planners to act coherently on the same material across sessions and modalities. The architecture is discussed in the context of correlative microscopy and surface analysis, including optical microscopy, SEM, EDS, XPS, SIMS and AFM. We define a staged taxonomy ranging from DAT-1, concerned with spatial identity and cross-instrument registration, to DAT-3 and DAT-4, in which Bayesian state estimates, predicted spectra and intervention responses support closed-loop experimental planning. We also discuss practical enabling layers: multimodal fiducial markers, non-invasive extraction of spatial information from instrument video outputs, interoperable markup languages such as DATML, and crypto-graphic timestamping of analytical records. The central claim is that an instrument observes a specimen, but an autonomous analytical laboratory reasons about a Digital Analytical Twin.

papers.title: Compensated ferrimagnetism above 600 K in a metal-organic framework
papers.abstract: Compensated ferrimagnets combine long-range magnetic order with small stray magnetic fields, but realizing such behavior over broad temperature ranges in chemically designable materials remains challenging. Recently, radical-bridged pyrazine frameworks were shown to support ferrimagnetism well above room temperature. Here we demonstrate that this concept can be extended to substantially higher magnetic energy scales in Mo(pyrazine) 3 , a three-dimensional molecular framework adopting a ReO 3 -related topology. Antiferromagnetic coupling between the sublattices gives rise to a nearly compensated ferrimagnetic state that persists to at least 625 K (352 °C), with a small net moment maintained over a broad temperature range rather than emerging only at a specific compensation temperature. Spectroscopic, magnetic, and computational analyses attribute this behavior to exceptionally strong radical-mediated exchange involving the diffuse 4d orbitals of Mo(III), which sustains a persistently compensated ferrimagnetic state to at least 625 K. These results establish Mo(pyrazine) 3 as a benchmark high-temperature molecular ferrimagnet and demonstrate that chemically designable molecular frameworks can unite exceptionally high-temperature magnetic order with intrinsic broad-temperature compensation.

papers.title: Capturing Activity Trends in Metal-Organic Framework Catalysis using Minimal Active Site Models
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offer immense potential as catalysts owing to their modular and tunable structures, yet their vast combinatorial design space makes discovery challenging. Although realistic models of MOF active sites are effective for detailed mechanistic studies, their complexity and system-specific nature hinder transferable, predictive catalyst design. Here, we demonstrate that activity trends in MOF catalysis can be captured using representative minimal active site models comprising small transition metal complexes, significantly reducing computational cost. Using MOF-catalyzed CO oxidation as a model reaction, we derive linear free energy scaling relationships from these minimal models that map catalytic activity onto two easily computable descriptor variables. These descriptors enable rapid prediction and comparison of realistic active sites across diverse MOF families while uncovering the intrinsic limitations of conventional catalyst tuning strategies. Our framework rationalizes the exceptional activity of experimentally reported catalysts, highlights the role of cooperative neighboring metal centers in breaking the existing scaling constraints, and identifies candidate materials with even higher predicted activities. The present approach lays a robust foundation and a starting point for establishing a powerful framework for predicting and optimizing active sites in crystalline and glassy MOFs for a wide range of chemical transformations.

papers.title: Mechanochemical C‑Terminal Activation of Peptides: Solvent‑Minimal Thiocarboxylation with Suppressed Epimerization
papers.abstract: A solvent‑minimal mechanochemical approach enables one‑step peptide C‑terminal thiocarboxylation with efficient suppression of epimerization. The method affords peptide thiocarboxylic acids from diverse substrates, including epimerization‑prone dipeptides, while significantly reducing material input, demonstrating a sustainable strategy for peptide C‑terminal activation.

papers.title: Bimodal Learning from Imperfect NMR Data (BLIND): A chemistry-ignorant model for autonomous structure elucidation from NMR
papers.abstract: Automatically inferring molecular structure from analytical measurements is a key step toward closing the loop in autonomous chemical research. Yet it remains challenging, because structurally relevant information is distributed across multiple channels, affected by experimental imperfections, and often insufficient to uniquely define a molecular structure. Here, we present BLIND (Bimodal Learning from Imperfect NMR Data), a bimodal transformer that translates 1H and/or 13C NMR data into molecular structures without any chemical priors, such as molecular formula, elemental composition, or possible fragments. Unlike previous approaches, BLIND is trained exclusively on more than 5.5 million experimental spectra extracted from the chemical literature, learning from the inherent heterogeneity of real-world NMR data. Under fully unconstrained, chemistry-ignorant conditions, BLIND correctly infers the molecular structure, including stereochemistry, in more than half of the chemically diverse test cases and otherwise narrows the solution to only a few plausible candidates. On an independent expert-curated dataset acquired under controlled experimental conditions, the prediction accuracy exceeds 80%. BLIND handles various molecular sizes and structural complexity (up to 130 non-hydrogen atoms) and generalizes across a broad chemical space, including compounds with less common elements, multiple stereocentres, and multiple chemical species. These findings demonstrate that experimental data are a valuable source of structural information that should not be blindly replaced by idealized simulated datasets. Trained directly on such data, BLIND enables end-to-end structure elucidation from routine NMR measurements, allowing inferred structures to be fed back into real-time synthetic decisions in autonomous chemical research.

papers.title: Reactive Molecular Dynamics of Hydrogen Evolution at Charged Interfaces Using Machine Learning Potentials
papers.abstract: Understanding electrochemical reaction mechanisms requires atomistic simulations that simultaneously capture charged interfaces, explicit solvent, and long-time dynamics, which remain beyond the reach of conventional ab initio molecular dynamics. Here, we develop an equivariant machine learning interatomic potential trained on density functional theory data for electrochemically activated MoS2/water interfaces under charged conditions. The resulting model reproduces first-principles energetics with an error of 7 meV/atom, while enabling nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations of systems containing hundreds of atoms. The simulations reveal that hydrogen evolution is strongly governed by surface hydrogen coverage, with higher coverages promoting faster H2 formation while preserving the interfacial water structure. Mechanistic analysis identifies the Heyrovsky-like pathway as the dominant hydrogen evolution mechanism, whereas Tafel recombination contributes only at high coverages. The emergence of sustained hydrogen evolution, stable interfacial populations, and coverage-dependent reaction pathways demonstrates that electrochemically informed MLIPs can reproduce chemically meaningful reactive dynamics at charged interfaces over nanosecond time scales.

papers.title: Effects of laser beam irradiation on displacement of microparticles at an air–wet gel interface
papers.abstract: Optical trapping based on radiation pressure has enabled advanced manipulation of microparticles. Previous studies have primarily focused on Gaussian-beam optical trapping of nanoparticles using tightly focused laser beams. In such systems, high-intensity pulsed lasers with short temporal widths are commonly employed and have been extensively used to investigate photothermal and photobleaching effects at the subcellular scale. However, the effects of moderate-intensity continuous-wave lasers (tens of mW), which are widely used in recent applications, remain insufficiently explored, particularly regarding photothermal-induced mechanical forces. In this study, I investigate the displacement behavior of microparticles induced by a millimeter-scale laser beam spot. Two types of particles (BaSOand TiO ) were examined under and outside the irradia 4 2tion region of a 20 mW, 450 nm laser beam. Clear particle displacement occurred in water droplets and on wet gelatin gel surfaces at the millimeter scale. The observed motion is attributed to a combination of radiation pressure, optical gradient forces, photothermal convection, and evaporation-induced flow. Comparison of experimental conditions suggeststhatphotothermal fluid flow isthe dominant mechanism governing particlemobilityunderwetconditions,particularlyatgelinterfaceswherethermal transport effects are enhanced.These results demonstrate that low-power, broad-area laser beams similar to laser pointers can induce measurable microscale mass transport at liquid–solid interfaces, highlighting potential implications for interface manipulation and laser safety in biological environments.

papers.title: Integrating ToxCast/ToxRefDB Data with Quantitative Adverse Outcome Pathway for Risk Assessment of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) pose complex, multi-mechanistic health risks that are difficult to evaluate using conventional in vitro or in vivo approaches alone. Here, we developed a quantitative adverse outcome pathway (qAOP) model integrating ToxCast and ToxRefDB data to enable mechanism-based, high-throughput risk assessment of EDCs. Molecular initiating events (MIEs) for 40 representative EDCs were prioritized from ToxCast bioassay data and mapped onto the AOP wiki database, yielding six integrated AOP networks comprising 22 MIEs, 167 key events, and 40 adverse outcomes (AOs) spanning organ- and gender-specific endpoints. Chemical–MIE potencies were quantified using Toxicological Priority Index (ToxPi) scores derived from ToxCast AC50 values, while MIE–AO probabilistic relationships were weighted using the PageRank algorithm applied to AOP network topology. Matrix multiplication of these two probabilistic layers generated integrated toxicity scores predicting EDC–AO associations. Model performance was validated against in vivo ToxRefDB data using machine learning-based receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, achieving AUC values of 0.86 and 0.73 for hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity, respectively. This data-driven qAOP framework provides a mechanistically transparent alternative to black-box QSAR models, bridges in vitro and in vivo toxicological evidence, and offers a scalable, animal-free strategy for prioritizing and screening emerging EDCs and structural analogues within Integrated Approaches to Testing and Assessment (IATA) frameworks.

papers.title: Phonon Spectra Reveal How Selective Fluorination Enhances Hole Transport in Benzodithiophenes (BDT)
papers.abstract: Selective fluorination is one of the most widely used chemical modifications for improving hole mobility in donor-type organic semiconductors. It is commonly assumed that the benefits arise from isolated geometric or electronic descriptors, such as a planar backbone, a shift of frontier orbitals, a tighter π-stack, or a larger transfer integral, without exploring how these changes propagate through the hierarchical length scales. Here, we map the full phonon spectrum of fluorinated and non-fluorinated benzodithiophene (BDT) trimers using inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and project the phonon density of states (PDOS) and participation ratio (PR) onto individual backbone subunits to identify, atom-by-atom, how selective F-for-H substitution changes the molecular structure and function. For anti configurations, F-substitution stiffens the inter-ring modes at 680 cm−1, which is correlated with improved planarization, delocalization through the dihedral, and reduction of electron-phonon coupling by 40–73%. Fluorination also reduces intramolecular electron–phonon coupling in syn configurations by 10×, through completely different phonon modes which localize the coupling to in-plane deformation modes at 580 cm−1 and dihedral twisting modes at 773 cm−1. Hole mobility calculations using transient localization theory show that BDT-F anti-isomer outperforms the syn-isomer at nearly identical π-stacking distances, and the computed mobilities agree well with experiment. These results provide insights into how selective fluorine substitutions affect electrostatic and dynamic performance across molecular to materials length scales.

papers.title: Convenient Implementation of Rung-3.5 Density Functionals in Standard Gaussian-Basis Codes
papers.abstract: Developing more broadly accurate density functional approximations can be accomplished not only by new parameterizations with existing ingredients, but also by using new ingredients encoding new physics, such as rung-3.5 energy densities that allow a better balance of static correlation and electron delocalization and also allow an explicit treatment of static correlation. Here we introduce a convenient implementation of rung-3.5 energy densities as ingredients for new density functionals. With this implementation, overlap-projected rung-3.5 functionals can be implemented in any code that uses Gaussian basis functions by computing a set of auxiliary basis functions with the same form as Gaussian basis functions but having modified orbital exponents. We illustrate the method with M11po, an overlap-projected rung-3.5 functional based on the broadly accurate M11plus density functional. M11po gives performance approaching that of the harder-to-implement M11plus functional, and it is freely available as an extension to the PySCF electronic structure package.

papers.title: Deep-AGAPE: An Open-source Web-Based Machine Learning Tool for Predicting G-Quadruplex Ligand Stabilization
papers.abstract: The identification of biologically active molecules within a vast chemical space remains a major challenge in drug discovery. In this context, G-quadruplexes (G4s), non-canonical nucleic acid structures involved in gene regulation and cancer-related processes, have emerged as promising therapeutic targets. However, experimental screening of G4-binding ligands is costly and timeconsuming, highlighting the need for efficient computational approaches. Building on the first version of the tool, in this work, we present Deep-AGAPE an open-source machine learning framework designed to predict the stabilization potential of small molecules toward G-quadruplex structures. The pipeline integrates data curation from G4LDB, in-house datasets and literature sources, molecular descriptor calculation using Mordred, an open-source cheminformatics tool, and supervised learning models trained on experimentally derived activity labels based on FRET melting assays. Compared with the previous AGAPE version, Deep-AGAPE incorporates a fully reproducible preprocessing workflow, including feature selection, imputation, and normalization, followed by model training and evaluation using stratified cross-validation. Unlike the original AGAPE framework, Deep-AGAPE removes the need for proprietary software and computationally expensive quantum chemical descriptors. Descriptor-based models consistently outperformed transformer-derived molecular representations, with the optimized XGBoost and Deep Neural Network models achieving independent test F1-scores of 0.848 and 0.810, respectively. To facilitate accessibility, the model is deployed through an interactive web platform that allows users to input molecules via SMILES, file upload, or molecular drawing, and obtain predictions along with confidence scores.

papers.title: Metal-Organic Cages to functionalize CNTs: higher dispersibility and phase-transport
papers.abstract: Multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) have potential for a range of industrial applications. However, their utility is constrained by challenges related to processing and dispersibility due to their tendency to aggregate in solvents, especially polar ones. This study describes the use of a metal-organic cage (MOC) to non-covalently functionalize and disperse MWCNTs in both water and polar organic solvents. The MOC interacts with the CNTs through stacking interactions, displaying a clear preference for thinner tubes. An understanding of the functionalization of the CNTs was obtained through calorimetric, microscopic and spectroscopic techniques. The counterion-responsive solubility behavior of the MOCs provided a means to transport CNTs between liquid phases. The resulting MOC-bound CNTs exhibit improved dispersibility, enhancing their processability while preserving the intrinsic properties associated with the sp2 carbon framework. Importantly, the cages can be removed, allowing the material to revert to its pristine state. This work thus introduces a reversible, non-covalent strategy for CNT functionalization based on coordination cages, offering a route to CNT processing within and across liquid phases.

papers.title: Coherent Pulsed Dynamic Nuclear Polarization with Endogenous Metal-Ions
papers.abstract: Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) can overcome the intrinsically low sensitivity of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and enables structural characterization of a wide range of materials. In inorganic solids, DNP can be achieved by introducing paramagnetic metal ions as endogenous polarizing centers. However, DNP enhancements obtained with metal ions are typically an order of magnitude lower than those achieved with organic radicals because of the intrinsic properties of high-spin metal-ion electron systems. Here, we present the first experimental demonstration of coherent pulsed endogenous metal-ion DNP using frequency-swept chirped microwave excitation at W-band (94GHz). Experiments on Mn 2+ and Gd 3+ -doped Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO) show that the integrated solid effect (ISE) improves DNP efficiency by up to an order of magnitude compared with the conventional single-frequency solid effect (SE). Furthermore, ISE outperforms the adiabatic solid effect (ASE) for systems with broad electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra, in contrast to the behavior observed for narrow-line organic radicals. Frequency-swept excitation is highly robust and maintains near-optimal performance over wide microwave-frequency and magnetic-field ranges. We further demonstrate that adiabatic microwave pulses can selectively excite the satellite transitions of high-spin electron systems, increasing the population difference of the central transition and thereby providing an additional mechanism for enhancing DNP efficiency. These results establish coherent frequency-swept pulsed DNP as an effective strategy for overcoming the limitations of endogenous metal-ion polarizing and pave the way for highly sensitive NMR studies of inorganic materials.

papers.title: Creatine as an Organocatalyst for the Synthesis of 2,3-Dihydroquinazolin-4(1H)-one Derivatives via Multi-component Reactions at Room Temperature
papers.abstract: Creatine's potential as an organocatalyst for organic synthesis is demonstrated specifically for the preparation of 2,3-dihydroquinazolin-4(1H)-one derivatives. Use of a multi-component sequence involving aldehydes, isatoic anhydride, and ammonium acetate efficiently leads to the desired products at rt (25-30 °C) using an “on water” approach. Creatine’s functional groups promote key hydrogen bonding and proton transfer, perhaps permitting it to be used as a natural Brønsted acid catalyst.

papers.title: A Cross-Species Comparison of Excitation Energy Transfer in Red-Lineage Photosystem I
papers.abstract: The Photosystem I supercomplex (PSI) is a central component of photosynthesis in plants and algae. Its antenna subunits absorb the light energy and transfer it through an interconnected pigment network to the reaction center (RC), where it is stored as chemical energy. Although the excitation energy transfer (EET) processes in photosystems have been well characterized for individual organisms, evolutionary variation and inconsistent modeling settings have obscured cross-species comparisons, and it remains unclear which common structural features sustain EET efficiency. To address this, we combined kinetic modeling and rate theories to simulate EET processes in multiple red-lineage PSIs, each consisting of hundreds of chlorophylls, using the same set of experiment-derived parameters. We performed network analysis to probe how their EET processes respond to structural variation across distinct species. The exciton becomes increasingly delocalized as it approaches the core region of the PSIs, creating a strong exciton-energy gradient (EEG) that funnels it to the RC. However, the EEG is effective only over a limited distance range from the RC, encompassing small PSIs almost entirely but not the larger ones. In large PSIs, the pigments farther from the RC are weakly coupled, thereby hampering EET. Large PSIs, therefore, adopt strategies to maintain the efficiency of long-range EET alongside the EEG effect, such as variations in pigment identity in the peripheral region of the antenna. Such effects also broaden the energy range of light absorption. By comparing red-lineage PSIs on an equal footing, we present a general simulation framework to understand the response of EET to structural rearrangements in the pigment network.

papers.title: The Human ADME Score: A Quantitative Metric of Drug-likeness for Orally Administered Compounds
papers.abstract: Quantitative assessment of ADME-related drug-likeness remains challenging as small-molecule drug discovery expands into larger and more complex chemical space. We hypothesized that drug-likeness for orally administered compounds is best quantified at the level of functional absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties rather than by simple molecular descriptors or clinical pharmacokinetic outcomes alone. Using diverse nonclinical (n = 32,307) and clinical (n = 588) compound datasets containing 123,909 ADME measurements, we developed the human ADME Score, a continuous multiparametric score ranging from 0 to 1. The score integrates aqueous solubility, passive cellular permeability, free hepatocyte intrinsic clearance, P-gp apical efflux ratio, and fraction unbound in plasma. The ADME Score distinguished nonclinical from clinical compounds (median 0.47 vs. 0.67), was higher among clinical compounds with oral bioavailability >50% (median 0.70; 83% with scores >0.5), and differentiated compounds across chemotypes, projects, and drug targets. It was broadly consistent with classical druggability guidelines (median 0.59 vs. 0.37 for Lipinski’s rule of 5) and moderately correlated with QED, while providing a continuous functional readout. Overall, the ADME Score provides a practical framework for quantifying ADME-related drug-likeness across diverse chemical spaces, chemotypes, and modalities. Graphical abstract ADME Score illustrated using apixaban, a factor Xa inhibitor and anticoagulant. This approach enables continuous quantification of drug-likeness, allowing interpretation across relevant chemical spaces and chemotypes.

papers.title: A physical aid to site-selective modification of a peptide: targeting of single residues for conjugation, stapling, and labeling with a nanopore and mechanical positioning
papers.abstract: A physical device to aid post-synthetic modification of specific single residues in a peptide at the single molecule level is proposed; it is similar to a structure that was recently proposed for peptide synthesis without side-chain protection (doi: 10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-gsw8x-v5). An electrolytic cell with cis and trans chambers bridged by a nanopore is combined with a mechanical positioning system in which peptides with a homopeptide header or header and trailer are anchored to a platform at one or both ends. A peptide can be moved electrophoretically through the pore with an applied voltage and positioned electromechanically by moving the platform(s) in sub-nm steps with piezo-electric sensors and actuators. A specific residue can be targeted for shielding inside the pore and movement thereafter into trans for targeted protection before it is exposed to reactants (catalyst, linker, conjugate) for modification. Peptides can be modified at the free N- or C- end (single platform) or at arbitrary internal positions (single or dual platform) by cyclization (including overlapping and nested cycles), stapling, linking, or conjugation with a desired cargo for drug delivery/tracking while allowing for diffusion effects. Modification procedures are outlined in theory and illustrated with examples. In many cases successful modification can be detected from the blockade current level in the pore. The results of coarse-grained probabilistic computational simulations showing target, catalyst, and conjugate converging in space, a pre-condition for target-conjugate binding while diffusing in trans, are presented; they suggest that with a trans chamber height of 1 micron-1 mm, the molar catalyst/conjugate-to-target ratio required for convergence in under a minute with probability 1 is 103-106. Although this appears excessive virtually all of the former can be recovered and recycled. The method may be implemented in parallel with an array of pores in a synthetic membrane; with a pore separation of 20 nm on a 2 cm × 2 cm chip, the theoretical maximum yield is ~1.6 picomoles, the actual yield can be estimated from the blockade current. In its present form the proposed system does not scale to the bulk level so its potential use is limited to research and preclinical studies.

papers.title: ReactiveLJ: A Coordination-Dependent Lennard-Jones-Based Potential for Reversible Bonding in Coarse-Grained Simulations
papers.abstract: Associative polymer networks are cross-linked by reversible bonds whose continual formation, dissociation, and exchange rearrange network topology and thereby govern viscoelastic and transport properties.
