papers.abstract: The integration of single-atom catalysts into metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offers a promising strategy for coupling molecular catalytic sites with photoactive architectures. While previous studies have focused primarily on the identity and coordination environment of single-atom sites, the role of their spatial placement within photocatalytic MOFs remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate how site-specific placement of linker-bound nickel single atoms significantly influences the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution efficiency in MIL-125(Ti)-NH2. Using a post-synthetic Schiff-base strategy, we construct half-Salen coordination motifs that direct Ni(II) incorporation into distinct spatial environments within the framework. Spectroscopic and porosity analyses reveal that salicylaldehydederived sites are preferentially formed within the internal pore network, whereas bulkier aldehydes predominantly modify external surfaces. Despite exhibiting lower degrees of functionalization and lower Ni loading, internally positioned Ni(II) sites deliver the highest photocatalytic activity, reaching 11.2 mmol g-1 h-1 under visible-light irradiation and outperform all other materials in the series. Notably,

papers.title: Half-edge graphs, Lewis Formulas, and Electron Pushing
papers.abstract: Lewis structures are frequently used to display the electronic structure of molecules. Chemical reaction mechanisms, on the other hand, are commonly visualized by means of “curved arrows” that denote the movement of electron pairs or single unpaired electrons. Here we adapt the concept of half-edge graphs to provide a unified mathematical framework that encompasses Lewis structures and “arrow-pushing”. The formalism is used to show that any given atom-to-atom map for a balanced reaction can be explained by a sequence of electron-pushing operations. We then introduce simpler graph-like ACSet data structures, called electron-feature graphs. Comparing the corresponding categories, we observe that electron-feature graphs form a quotient of half-edge graphs that in essence “anonymizes” the electrons. We argue that electron-feature graphs are the appropriate level of description for studies into decomposing reaction rules into mechanistic sequences of electron pushes.

papers.title: How the Oxidation State Drives Bonding Properties in CeIII and CeIV Tris(amidinate) Complexes
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis and characterization of a pair of homoleptic cerium tris(amidinate) complexes, [Ce III {PhC(N t Bu) 2 } 3 ] and [Ce IV {PhC(N t Bu) 2 } 3 ][Al(OC 4 F 9 ) 4 ], containing cerium in both its trivalent (Ce III ) and tetravalent (Ce IV ) oxidation states. To the best of our knowledge, these represent the first examples of a lanthanide-amidinate system where both trivalent and tetravalent complexes have been isolated and structurally characterized in such a congruent ligand coordination. With electronic structure and bond analysis, we demonstrate that while the metal-ligand bonding in both species is dominated by interactions involving Ce 5d valence orbitals, there is a measurable participation of the 4f orbitals specifically within the Ce IV homolog. Ce L 3 -edge high-energy resolution X-ray absorption near edge structure (HR-XANES) and valence band resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (VB-RIXS) are employed to evaluate the bonding properties and are complemented with quantum chemical calculations based on density-functional theory (DFT). Crucially, the high-resolution nature of these spectroscopic techniques, coupled with theoretical modelling, enables a quantitative deconvolution of the bonding interaction directly from the experimental data. This approach allows us to partition the individual contributions of both the 4f and 5d electrons to the metal-ligand interaction. Our findings highlight the increased role of 4f electron density in stabilizing high-valent lanthanide complexes, due to improved energetic and spatial overlap between nitrogen donor lone pairs and the Ce IV acceptor manifold.

papers.title: Unlocking the potential of Glycosidase-Cleavable AgroDrug Conjugates for Sustainable Agriculture
papers.abstract: The Crop protection industry is currently locked in a race to discover the next generation of efficacious, safe and disruptive modalities. Towards this endeavour, Agrodrug conjugates (AgDCs) offer many unique opportunities to tune the properties of active agrodrugs via meticulous selection of their distinct components. Herein, we present the first study on the utilization of cleavable conjugates for agricultural applications. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the potential of AgDCs for use in crop protection and establishes this modality as an innovative addition to the toolbox for optimizing bio-active crop protection modalities.

papers.title: Structure and Stability Prediction of Binary and Ternary Molecular Mixed Crystals Using Ensemble Free Energies
papers.abstract: Mixed crystals provide a route to tune the properties of molecular solids through continuous changes in composition. However, predicting their stability is challenging because it requires determining both substitution energies and configurational entropy across large configuration spaces. Here, we combine crystal structure prediction, force field lattice energy calculations, and ∆-machine-learning energy corrections with a scaled partition-function approach to assess structure prediction and evaluate binary and ternary mixed crystals of anthracene (ANT), acridine (ACR), and phenazine (PNZ). The composition-dependent ensemble free energy (∆G ensemble ) was estimated without exhaustive enumeration of all configurations from representative ensembles of substituted supercell models of mixed crystals. Crystal structure prediction reproduces the known polymorphs as the lowest energy structures and the mixed crystal modelling approach reproduces the main experimental binary trends: ACR incorporation into ANT and the α and β polymorphs of PNZ, ANT incorporation into ACR form II, and the formation of a PNZ β-type phase. Furthermore, we predict additional thermodynamically stable compositions, including PNZ incorporation into ACR form IX, and ternary crystals based on ACR forms II, VI and VII. Stable three-component regions arise from binary trends, with ACR mediating between both ANT and PNZ. These results demonstrate a practical framework for predicting the structure, thermodynamic stability and composition limits of molecular mixed crystals.

papers.title: Atomically Defined Photoswitchable Hybrid Nanostructures Built from Functionalized Norbornadienes and Cobalt Oxide Nanoislands on Au(111)
papers.abstract: Organic photoswitches on surfaces enable the construction of interfaces that can store solar energy (molecular solar thermal systems, MOST) or change their functional properties in response to light (photoresponsive interfaces). However, many photoswitches show significantly altered photoresponsive behavior when anchored to metallic surfaces. To enable knowledge-based design of light-sensitive interfaces from prefabricated building blocks, it is essential to electronically decouple the light-sensitive unit from the rest of the system, for example by anchoring it to oxide islands that spatially separate the molecule from the catalytic active metal surface. In this work, we investigate the photoswitching behavior of a norbornadiene-based photoswitch, 2-cyano-3-(4-carboxyphenyl)norbornadiene (CNBD), anchored via a carboxylate linker to atomically defined CoO nanoislands on Au(111). Using infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRAS) and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), we investigate the adsorption and photoconversion behavior of these hybrid systems. CNBD selectively adsorbs on the CoO islands and forms self-organized monolayers (SAMs). Time-resolved photochemical IRAS shows that the activation barrier for the thermal back-conversion of anchored CNBD on the ultrathin CoO islands is comparable to that on thick oxide layers and of the free (non-anchored) molecule. This finding shows that a single Co-O bilayer is sufficient to decouple the CNBD from the underlying catalytically active Au(111). These findings pave the way for the knowledge-based design of photoswitchable nanostructures with atomic precision and predictable light sensitivity.

papers.title: The Golden Path to Brightness: Unlocking Room-Temperature Rare Earth Luminescence with Phosphinocarboxylate-based RE/Au Complexes
papers.abstract: Rare earth/transition metal (RE/TM) complexes offer unique opportunities to combine complementary electronic properties within a single molecular framework but remain challenging to access because of the distinct coordination preferences of both metal classes. Herein, we report the first phosphinocarboxylate-based strategy for the selective assembly of heterobimetallic RE/TM complexes. Guided by the hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) concept, 2-(diphenylphosphino)benzoate ligand enables sequential, site-selective coordination of hard rare earth ions and soft Au(I) centres, affording air-stable RE/Au complexes through a modular synthetic approach. The monometallic rare earth clusters display remarkable coordination flexibility and serve as predefined synthons for subsequent Au(I) incorporation. Photophysical investigations reveal that selective Au(I) coordination fundamentally enhances the luminescence properties while preserving the characteristic emission signatures of the individual rare earth ions. Most notably, Au(I) shifts efficient rare earth-centred luminescence from cryogenic to ambient temperatures and markedly enhances ligand-centred phosphorescence in the yttrium analogue. The enhanced emission is consistent with increased structural rigidity, stronger spin–orbit coupling induced by the heavy Au(I) centre, and more efficient ligand-to-metal energy transfer, with the Au-phosphinocarboxylate fragment acting as a metal–organic chromophore. These findings establish phosphinocarboxylates as a versatile ligand platform for the rational design of photoactive heterobimetallic RE/TM complexes.

papers.title: Fundamentals of Electrochemical Energy Storage: Theory and Practice
papers.abstract: The rechargeable alkali-ion battery has emerged as a transformative technology, revolutionizing portable energy storage in a wide range of applications, from small electronic devices to large electric vehicles. In this review, we combine modern theoretical and computational methods with an examination of electrochemical properties for lithium and post lithium-ion batteries. From fundamental thermodynamics and kinetics to computational techniques for materials design, we examine frameworks for deriving relationships for key battery properties such as voltage and capacity. We also explore the complexities of ion migration processes, including hopping mechanisms between lattice sites, and extend our focus to the broader field of electrochemical properties, including conductivity, redox potentials and interfacial properties. Finally, we outline perspectives on the outstanding challenges and promising opportunities in the theory and computation of rechargeable battery materials, paving the way for future advances in energy storage technology.

papers.title: Wise Co-Solvent Selection for Modulating Bromide Solvation and Improving the Efficiency of Flowless Zn-Br2 Batteries
papers.abstract: Flowless aqueous Zn-Br2 batteries (ZBBs) are attractive for safe, low-cost stationary energy storage, yet remain limited by bromine-related self-discharge and a rate-dependent efficiency trade-off: coulombic efficiency (CE) often increases at high current density, whereas energy efficiency (EE) decreases due to polarization. Here, we apply co-solvent engineering to tune water–bromide solvation in 0.5M ZnBr2 electrolytes and rationally balance CE and EE. Ethylene glycol (EG) and 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME) produce complementary electrochemical responses: EG improves high-rate EE by modifying the water hydrogen-bond network, while DME enhances CE through stronger perturbation of bromide-ions solvation. Guided by this mechanistic distinction, 2-methoxyethanol (ME) was selected as a bifunctional co-solvent. Raman spectroscopy, 1H NMR, and 81Br NMR reveal that ME simultaneously restructures the hydrogen-bond network and bromide-ions solvation environment, thereby optimizing both EE and CE. With only 5 vol% ME, ZBB cells operated with 200 mAh g-1 cathodes deliver CE >97% at 5 A g-1 (25C) and EE >87.5% at 1 A g-1 (5C), outperforming pristine ZnBr2, EG-, and DME-containing electrolytes in overall CE–EE balance. Under 5 A g-1 (25C) cycling, ME-based cells maintain >96% CE and 80-85% EE for 2400 cycles, highlighting molecular co-solvent design as a powerful route toward durable high-rate ZBBs.

papers.title: Photocyclization of 3DPA2FBN Yielding Core-Edge Fused Donor-Acceptor Cyanoarene Photocatalysts
papers.abstract: Donor-acceptor cyanoarenes are widely employed as photocatalysts, yet their photostability and degradation pathways remain critical areas of investigation. Herein we report that commercially available 3DPA2FBN, upon irradiation with blue light at room temperature, undergoes photocyclization events with extrusion of HF, generating structures in which the electron-deficient cyanoarene core is fused to the diphenylamine-derived electron-rich periphery. A mono- and a bis-cyclization product are obtained in regioselective fashion, along with a metastable precursor of the latter. These products were successfully isolated and fully characterized. Moreover, the two photostable photocyclized products were evaluated across various photocatalytic benchmarks. Our findings provide key insights into chemical evolution of cyanoarene photocatalysts, demonstrating that degradation pathways can generate new, catalytically competent molecular species.

papers.title: Light-Gated Targeting of DNA Replication Foci in Cancer Cells
papers.abstract: DNA three-way junctions (3WJs) are transient non-canonical DNA structures linked to replication stress, genome instability and cancer, but their controlled recognition remains rare and has not yet been demonstrated in cells. Here we report the first light-gated system for dynamic 3WJ recognition, operating both in vitro and in cellulo. Using solid-phase peptide synthesis protocols, we engineered an oligocationic FeII peptide helicate in which the 3WJ-binding core is masked by a photolabile linker and a folded-back polyglutamate caging module. Initial screening identified E12 as the minimal sequence required to suppress 3WJ binding. Fluorescence, UV-vis, CD, MALDI-MS and HPLC-MS confirmed peptide helicate formation, ΛΛ chirality, efficient photocleavage and generation of the uncaged system upon irradiation. Competitive EDTA assays showed that the uncaged FeII peptide helicate is kinetically inert toward ligand exchange in aqueous medium. Fluorescence titrations and EMSA assays showed that the caged peptide helicate does not bind 3WJ or canonical duplex DNA, whereas light activation restores selective 3WJ recognition. In eGFP-PCNA HeLa cells, the caged probe showed poor retention and no localization at replication foci, while ex-situ and in-cell irradiation restored nuclear accumulation and PCNA colocalization. This work establishes for the first time light as an external trigger to control DNA junction recognition in cells and expands peptide helicates as modular supramolecular scaffolds for chemical biology.

papers.title: Chemical Shift Prediction Beyond the Electronic Structure Limit
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a critical tool for developing pharmaceuticals, studying proteins, and identifying natural products. However, many diagnostic chemical shift variations remain too small to be interpreted by computational methods, making costly multidimensional NMR analyses unavoidable. Here, we show that existing shift prediction methods have reached the electronic structure limit but that the resulting accuracy plateau can be overcome by explicitly modeling rovibrational effects and solute-solvent interactions. Our approach is greatly accelerated by a newly developed family of equivariant neural networks, MagNET, and increases frontier prediction accuracy significantly. In more routine cases, where only implicit solvation is needed, MagNET reduces the cost of high-quality predictions from hours to seconds. These models were trained on a new dataset we release representing the largest collection of computed shieldings ever assembled, encompassing millions of diverse solutes and solvated poses. Our study establishes the machine-learning-accelerated modeling of electronic structure, rovibrational, and solvent effects as a physically grounded path towards chemical accuracy and automated, shift-only structural elucidation.

papers.title: Unlocking the activities of polyglutamylation enzymes in brain tubulin with top-down mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Microtubules, essential components of the cytoskeleton, are formed from a− and b−tubulin heterodimers which are organized in a cylindrical fashion, like a barrel. The C-terminal tubulin tails remain exposed on the outside of the MT, where they can be highly modified by post-translational modifications (PTMs), including glutamylation, which modulates the interaction of tubulin with other proteins. The addition and extension of polyglutamate chains are regulated by tubulin tyrosine ligase-like (TTLL) enzymes. In mice, TTLL7 is primarily responsible for the addition of the first glutamate residue, and TTLL1 acts as an extender, adding more glutamates to form a polyglutamate chain. By analyzing tubulin from wild-type, TTLL1-KO, TTLL7-KO, and double-KO mouse brains using top-down mass spectrometry (TD-MS), we demonstrate the distinct and non-redundant enzymatic specificities of TTLL1 and TTLL7: TTLL1 exclusively modifies a−tubulin, while TTLL7 targets b−tubulin. Deletion of each enzyme leads to the selective loss of polyglutamylation in the corresponding tubulin, with no compensation by other TTLLs. In total, we identified 47 proteoforms, with up to 5 glutamylations, verified by targeted MS/MS fragmentation. Despite challenges posed by the high sequence homology and acidic C-terminal tails of tubulins, our automated TD-MS pipeline enables rapid proteoform identification in complex samples. This approach provides, for the first time, a comprehensive snapshot of the glutamylation status of intact tubulins, paving the way for quantitative studies of the tubulin code. Our method, adaptable to other enzymes, reveals critical enzymatic roles in microtubule regulation and highlights the utility of TD MS for studying challenging protein targets.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Techno-Economic-Environmental Assessment for the recovery of Ce, La, Pr, Nd, and Y from U.S Based Ore Concentrates
papers.abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are essential for advanced energy technologies, electrified transportation, modern electronics, and strategic defense systems. Although the United States possesses substantial domestic REE resources, the nation currently lacks sufficient downstream processing infrastructure and remains highly dependent on foreign supply chains for refined REE products. Re establishing domestic REE processing capacity has therefore become a strategic priority, but doing so requires the development of processing routes that are both economically viable and environmentally responsible. Establishing transparent baseline processing systems is consequently necessary for evaluating future technologies and identifying the primary drivers of process performance. Unlike many previous REE techno-economic studies that rely on simplified blackbox process representations, this work develops rigorous equilibrium-based process models capable of explicitly resolving precipitation, dissolution, gas evolution, and stagewise solvent extraction behavior. Integrated process flowsheets and complete solvent extraction separation trains were designed for bastnaesite, monazite, and xenotime concentrates representative of major U.S. ore systems to produce high-purity rare earth oxide (REO) products. Using these integrated flowsheets, comprehensive techno-economic and environmental assessments were performed for two production capacities corresponding to 150 and 1000 ton/yr REO throughput. Capital expenditures (CAPEX), operating expenditures (OPEX), and levelized costs of production (LCOP) were quantified for each processing route, together with gate-to-gate life cycle assessment metrics and evaluations of environmental compliance using EPA-inspired effluent guidelines. The analysis demonstrates that solvent extraction complexity is a dominant factor governing both the economic viability and environmental footprint of conventional REE processing systems. This work establishes a transparent and reproducible baseline framework for conventional domestic REE processing that can support future comparisons with alternative separation technologies, recycling systems, and process optimization strategies.

papers.title: Green Chemistry, Circular Economy, and Artificial Intelligence: Towards Sustainable and Regenerative Industrial Systems in Algeria
papers.abstract: Green chemistry, formalized in the mid-1990s, provides a design framework for reducing or eliminating hazardous substances, minimizing waste, and improving the overall sustainability of chemical products and processes. In parallel, the circular economy has emerged as a systems-level paradigm that seeks to retain the value of materials, components, and products for as long as possible through reuse, repair, remanufacturing, recycling, and regeneration. More recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a major enabling layer for both domains by supporting molecular discovery, reaction prediction, process optimization, autonomous experimentation, and the intelligent management of circular material flows. This review examines the converging roles of green chemistry, circular economy, and AI in the transition toward sustainable and regenerative industrial systems. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances in foundation models for chemistry, self-driving laboratories, digital twins, Green AI, AI-assisted catalyst discovery, and digital product passports. We also discuss the relevance of these developments for resource-intensive and environmentally sensitive contexts, including the Algerian industrial landscape and its coastal zones, while avoiding unsupported quantitative claims. Finally, we address major challenges related to data quality, model bias, reproducibility, scalability, governance, and the carbon footprint of AI. Taken together, the evidence suggests that the convergence of these three fields can accelerate safer chemistry, circular manufacturing, and industrial decarbonization, provided that technological innovation is coupled with robust environmental assessment and responsible implementation.

papers.title: Reaction-programmed hydrogel formation via base-triggered conversion of a peptide progelator
papers.abstract: Short peptides are promising building blocks for supramolecular soft materials yet controlling when and where hydrogelation occurs remains challenging. Here, we report a reactionprogrammed strategy for peptide hydrogel formation based on a biphasic progelator system. A Fmoc-protected heterochiral tripeptide is confined to an organic phase and activated by baseinduced deprotection, generating the free gelator. The resulting change in polarity drives phase transfer into an aqueous buffer, where self-assembly yields a fibrillar hydrogel network. Gelation kinetics, morphology, and mechanical properties are governed by the amount of base, which regulates peptide generation, local pH, and interfacial mass transport. Compared to conventional bulk pH triggers, this approach enables spatiotemporal control over assembly and produces distinct 2 supramolecular architectures. These results establish chemical activation coupled to phase-transfer as a design principle for programming peptide-based soft materials.

papers.title: A Stable Ruthenium(CAAC-5) Olefin Metathesis Catalyst for Bioconjugation
papers.abstract: Olefin metathesis is a powerful transformation for carbon–carbon bond formation, yet its application in biological settings is challenged by the instability of most ruthenium catalysts in aqueous media. Herein, we report a stable Ru(CAAC-5) olefin metathesis catalyst bearing a functional handle for bioconjugation. The resulting hybrid catalyst catalyzes ring-closing metathesis (RCM) and displays extended lifetimes in aqueous media. Functionalized CAAC-5 ligands bearing a protected aniline linker were prepared via enamine alkylation and coordinated to ruthenium to afford the corresponding Ru(CAAC-5) complex. In a benchmark RCM reaction under biologically relevant conditions, the ruthenium complex exhibits enhanced catalytic robustness and reaches turnover numbers of up to 600. Deprotection of an amine-functionalized handle enables the bioconjugation to proteins and peptides. Using this platform, the catalyst was anchored to biomolecules through supramolecular anchoring to human carbonic anhydrase II (hCA II), click conjugation to peptides (SS01), and covalent attachment to ubiquitin (Ubi). To the best of our knowledge, this aniline-functionalized Ru(CAAC-5) complex is the first CAAC-bearing metathesis catalyst amenable to bioconjugation, while retaining the prolonged catalytic activity characteristic of CAAC-based systems in aqueous media.

papers.title: Catalytic Uncaging of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner Ring-Expansion
papers.abstract: Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload—a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof-of-concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled the tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.

papers.title: Rational Design of Neuro-Mitoxantrone Derivatives as Dual LRRK2/APP Inhibitors for Parkinson's Disease: Structural Modification, Alternative Strategy Assessment, and Medicinal Chemistry Rationale
papers.abstract: Background: Mitoxantrone hydrochloride (CAS 65271-80-9), an anthracenedione antineoplastic agent, has been identified as a dual inhibitor of the LRRK2-APP neurotoxic feed-forward cascade implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD) neurodegeneration. However, its direct clinical translation is precluded by irreversible cardiotoxicity, non-selective cytotoxicity, and negligible blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration. Objective: To propose and evaluate novel Neuro-Mitoxantrone Derivative (NMD) series through rational medicinal chemistry, addressing all three pharmacological liabilities concurrently while preserving dual LRRK2/APP inhibitory activity. Methods: Four structural modification strategies were designed and evaluated: (I) 1,4-dihydroxy → 1,4-dimethoxy/difluoro substitution to ablate cardiotoxicity; (II) core de-planarisation via tetrahydrogenation, aza-ring bioisostere, or spirocyclic fusion to eliminate DNA intercalation; (III) CNS optimisation via piperazine-CF3/CN cyclisation, LAT1-targeted prodrug conjugation, or macrocyclic constraint; and (IV) asymmetric LRRK2 hinge-anchor pharmacophore to decouple dual-target binding. Five structural design series (Figures 1–7) were generated and assessed against published precedent. Results: All three core modifications are supported by published literature and clinical/preclinical precedent. Modification I is validated by Pixantrone (EMA-approved, 2012). Modification II is validated by canonical DNA intercalation SAR requiring molecular planarity. Modification III is validated by established CNS drug design (piperazine CNS scaffold prevalence; LAT1 prodrug studies; macrocyclic LRRK2 inhibitor programme). A key theoretical conflict between Modification II and APP mRNA 5'-UTR IRE binding was identified and resolved through Strategy A (aza-ring) and Strategy B (LAT1 prodrug). The macrocyclic design (Strategy D) represents the greatest structural departure from the parent mitoxantrone scaffold. Conclusion: NMD compounds represent a structurally rational, literature-supported series of anthracenedione derivatives with potential for oral neuroprotective therapy in Parkinson's disease. Synthesis, in vitro LRRK2 kinase assay, APP mRNA suppression, and rodent BBB penetration studies are proposed as the immediate validation pipeline.

papers.title: An Ultrathin Water-Retentive TiO2 Interfacial Layer for Enhanced Low-Humidity PEMFC Operation
papers.abstract: Operating proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) under low relative humidity (RH) is attractive because it simplifies the balance-of-plant by relaxing external humidification and reduces the risk of electrode flooding; its central drawback is that insufficient membrane hydration raises ohmic resistance and accelerates degradation. Incorporating hydrophilic additives into the microporous layer (MPL) is a widely used strategy to retain water and address this low-RH penalty, yet the loading-dependent transport limits and associated mass-transport trade-offs at higher humidity remain poorly quantified. Here, we engineer an ultrathin water-retentive interfacial layer onto the pre-existing MPL of commercial gas diffusion layers (GDLs) by ultrasonically spraying hydrophilic titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticles at controlled TiO2 mass loadings (0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20 and 0.30 mg/cm2). Physical characterization shows the loading-dependent trends: increasing TiO2 content monotonically decreases the surface contact angle, while excessive loading thickens and occludes the MPL, increases transport and electrical penalties, and establishes a maximum viable loading of 0.10 mg/cm2. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) across humidities reveals a strict operational trade-off: at 30% RH, the optimal 0.05 mg/cm2 loading retains hydration, reducing the high-frequency resistance by ∼38mΩcm2 relative to the unmodified baseline and enhancing peak power; conversely, at 100% RH the same hydrophilic layer imposes a mass-transport penalty due to liquid-water accumulation. These results explicitly map the structural and electrochemical boundaries of hydrophilic MPL modification and provide practical design guidance for TiO2-modified MPLs in PEMFCs.

Inquiry-Driven Jupyter Notebooks for Analyzing Time-Resolved Thermodynamic Data in the Physical Chemistry Laboratory
papers.abstract: The increasing importance of data-driven workflows across chemistry has created a need to integrate computational and cyberinfrastructure skills throughout the undergraduate curriculum. Physical chemistry laboratories provide a particularly effective environment for this integration because of their emphasis on mathematical modeling, quantitative interpretation, and analysis of experimentally measured data. Described here is a set of inquiry-driven Jupyter notebook modules designed for the analysis of time-resolved thermodynamic data collected from two classic physical chemistry experiments: the Clément–Desormes determination of the heat capacity ratio of gases and freezing point depression measurements for molar mass determination. Implemented within the Google Colaboratory environment and deployable on ChemCompute, the notebooks combine interactive visualization, data filtering, smoothing, numerical differentiation, and computational analysis with experimentally acquired datasets. Interactive plotting features, including adjustable slider bars and dynamically updated visualizations, allow students to explore how computational analysis choices influence interpretation of noisy thermodynamic measurements. The modules were scaffolded to emphasize conceptual understanding and inquiry-driven exploration of scientific workflows rather than programming syntax alone. Students modified partially completed functions, explored parameter-dependent behavior, and interpreted dynamically updated plots while developing skills in data slicing, filtering, visualization, and computational analysis. In the heat capacity ratio module, students additionally connect experimentally measured thermodynamic behavior with statistical thermodynamic calculations performed using Psi4. These modules provide a flexible framework for integrating interactive scientific computing and computational thinking into the undergraduate physical chemistry laboratory while reinforcing core thermodynamic concepts through analysis of dynamical experimental data.

papers.title: Coordination-Dependent Effects of Non-Monovalent Cations on Fatty Acid Bilayers
papers.abstract: Fatty acid vesicles are promising models for early protocells but are destabilized by multivalent metal ions required for prebiotic chemistry. Here, we systematically investigate the effects of Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , Mn 2+ , Cu 2+ , and Fe 3+ on fatty acid bilayers using a combination of experimental and computational approaches. We find that membrane responses are strongly ion-specific and governed by interactions with the carboxylate interface. Ca 2+ induces rapid bilayer disruption through direct coordination, whereas Mg 2+ primarily reduces colloidal stability, promoting vesicle aggregation through solvent-separated interactions. Mn 2+ exhibits intermediate behavior, inducing membrane heterogeneity and localized structural changes. Importantly, we show that metal ion speciation critically modulates these effects: complexation and precipitation reduce the availability of free ions, while coordinating ligands such as bicine can increase metal ion solubility and thereby alter ion–membrane interactions. Together, these results establish a mechanistic link between ion coordination, solution chemistry, and membrane stability, providing new insight into the physicochemical constraints governing protocell viability under highly heterogeneous and thus more prebiotically-relevant conditions.

papers.title: Measuring the Membrane Protein-Bound Lipidome
papers.abstract: Lipids play diverse physiological roles in energy storage, signaling, and cell structure. Another less appreciated role is as allosteric modulators of membrane proteins. However, it is challenging to determine the identify and affinity of lipids interacting with a given membrane protein target. In this review, we discuss analytical advances in using lipidomics to profile lipids bound to specific membrane proteins, which we will refer to as protein-lipid interactomics. We will consider the challenges of solubilizing and isolating the membrane protein while retaining relevant lipid interactions, focusing on detergents and lipid nanoparticles made with polymer, peptide, and protein scaffolds. We will also discuss aspects of overall experiment design, including basic identification, quantitative experiments, progressive delipidation, and lipid exchange to probe the strength of lipid interactions. Finally, we conclude with key questions, current analytical challenges, and proposed future directions for this emerging field.

papers.title: PoreForge: Unified Inverse Design of Nanoporous Materials for Electrochemical Energy Storage and Environmental Catalysis
papers.abstract: Nanoporous materials govern the performance of electrochemical energystorage and environmental-catalysis systems, yet their design remains locked in a slow trialand-error loop because pore geometry, surface chemistry, and operating conditions span a vast joint space that molecular-dynamics and density-functional-theory simulators can sample only sparsely. We propose PoreForge, a unified AI-driven inverse-design framework that targets three chemistry applications within a single model: lithium-sulfur battery separators that suppress polysulphide shuttling, beta-FeOOH photo-Fenton catalysts that coproduce hydrogen and degrade pollutants, and graphene nanochannels for low-energy desalination. PoreForge encodes each material into a canonical pore representation that fuses a completed 3D point cloud, a surface-chemistry graph, and an operating-condition vector. A contrastive Chamfer-distance geometry-completion backbone densifies sparse structural probes into this shared representation, a multi-task mixture-of-experts predictor estimates application-specific performance from the same embedding, and a reinforcement-learning policy performs inverse design by editing the canonical representation to match a target performance vector under a learned adversarial prior that enforces structural plausibility. A domain-adversarial term enables cross-application transfer so that knowledge from the data-rich lithium-sulfur dataset accelerates design on the data-sparse photo-Fenton and desalination tasks. We curate three chemistry datasets, LSB-Sep, PFenton, and GraphDesal, and show that PoreForge matches or exceeds the MD/DFT oracle on every headline metric while consuming only about 3 percent of its wall-clock time, attaining 821 mAh/g capacity at 0.048 percent per cycle decay on lithium-sulfur, 1.92 mmol/g/h hydrogen with 97.1 percent dye degradation on photo-Fenton, and 27.6 L/m2/h flux with 99.8 percent salt rejection on desalination.

papers.title: Operando observation of immobilized carbonic anhydrase for CO2 conversion
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis with immobilized enzymes is pivotal for continuous and sustainable industrial bioprocesses. However, the relationship between enzyme dispersion on solid supports and catalytic activity is not well described. Here, we investigate the immobilization of Persephonella marina carbonic anhydrase (PmCA) on multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), combining confocal fluorescence microscopy and high-resolution electron microscopy to correlate enzyme surface loading with CO2 hydration activity. A dual fluorescence labeling strategy enables operando visualization of enzyme location and function, revealing that catalytic activity on the carrier exhibits two distinct regimes: (i) a stochastic regime at low enzyme loadings where activity shows high variability with monolayer coverage yielding the highest perenzyme activity, and (ii) a saturation regime at higher loadings where activity converges on a loading-independent value, attributed to crowding effects. This integrated approach reveals spatiotemporally resolved structure-function relationships for a heterogeneous biocatalyst, establishing a basis for understanding and engineering of advanced enzyme-based catalytic materials.

papers.title: Establishing Quantitative Electrolyte-Solid Electrolyte Interphase Relationships in Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: Despite the high energy density of lithium metal batteries (LMBs), lithium loss driven by electrolyte decomposition at the highly reductive lithium metal anode to form the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) remains a critical challenge. Recent studies have established the correlation between an anion derived, inorganic SEI and interfacial stability, motivating electrolyte design strategies which promote preferential anion reduction at the lithium metal anode. Current electrolyte design strategies emphasize the importance of an anion-dominated Li+ solvation structure to promote this inorganic-rich SEI, yet there is a lack of quantitative evidence linking SEI composition with the strength of Li+-anion and Li+-solvent interactions in the electrolyte. Here, we systematically study a series of ether-based solvents with varied dielectric constants in order to connect variation in solvation structure to anion content in the SEI. LiF titration provides a quantitative assessment of the fraction of SEI products derived from anion reduction and demonstrates that an anion-dominated Li+ solvation structure, characterized with nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and Raman spectroscopy, does not necessarily correlate to anion-selective SEI formation. Instead, both an anion-dominated solvation structure and reductively stable solvent are necessary to achieve high anion selectivity. Based on this finding, we develop a descriptor-based model informed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations of both Li+ solvation ability and 2 solvent reductive stability to screen for solvent candidates which enable high anion selectivity. This model aligns with existing examples of ether-based Li metal electrolytes and helped to identify an electrolyte formulation of tert-butyl methyl ether and tert-amyl methyl ether to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.3 %. By demonstrating that both an anion-dominated solvation structure and a reductively stable solvent are necessary to enable high anion selectivity during SEI formation, this work identifies a key solvent design rule for high-performance electrolytes for lithium metal batteries.

papers.title: Electron Activated Dissociation Technique for Middle-Down Mass Spectrometric Analysis of Disulphide Bonds and Free Thiols: Application in Characterising Monoclonal Antibody Biotherapeutic Fragments
papers.abstract: Disulphide bonds contribute to the conformational structure of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and are therefore vital for their stability, biological function and safety. However, the biopharmaceutical manufacturing process can influence these bonds, potentially leading to the formation of free thiols, scrambled configurations, or degradation products, which may negatively impact quality and safety. Current analytical strategies for characterising disulphide bonds and free thiols in mAbs are predominantly based on labelled and label-free bottom-up mass spectrometry approaches. However, these methods are often time-consuming and may generate unwanted artefacts such as disulphide bond scrambled products. As a result, middle-down and top-down mass spectrometry methods are being explored as alternative approaches. However, their broader application remains limited by challenges in achieving sufficient MS/MS fragmentation for reliable characterisation of protein modifications and disulphide linkages. In this study, we evaluated an electron-activated dissociation (EAD) on the Sciex ZenoTOF 7600+ system for middle-down characterisation of intra- and interchain DSB and free thiols in mAbs. The EAD fragmentation generated diagnostic fragment ion patterns that can confirm intra-chain disulphide linkages on the subunits. This approach was applied to assess domain-specific free thiol on the NISTmAb Fc/2 subunit, as well as disulphide-scrambled products generated from mild reduction. Additionally, the method was effective in characterising fragments from antibody degradation. Overall, this EAD-based approach provides a rapid alternative for antibody product characterisation across different stages of the production process.

papers.title: Predicting Thermodynamic Solubility of Drugs in Fasted State Simulated Intestinal Fluid (FaSSIF) Using Multitask Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic solubility of drug candidates in simulated intestinal fluid, particularly Fasted State Simulated Intestinal Fluid (FaSSIF), is a key predictor of oral bioavailability and therefore critical for drug discovery. However, predictive models for FaSSIF solubility remain underdeveloped, in part due to data scarcity. This study demonstrates that using relevant auxiliary datasets substantially improves solubility predictions of deep learning models. Directed message passing neural networks (Chemprop) are trained with auxiliary chemical property data, and several deep learning strategies such as multitask learning, pre-training, and cascade workflows are explored. Models are benchmarked on internal (821 compounds) and public (117 compounds) datasets of FaSSIF solubility using random and cluster splits. The results show that multitask models with kinetic solubility, solubility in other solvents, and logD achieve overall the best performance across datasets, and adding pKa data further improves prediction for the internal dataset. Task weighting and descriptor augmentation are also investigated. Curated public datasets and data splits are provided to support future benchmarking.

papers.title: Effects of Chemically Activated L-Nucleotides on Nonenzymatic RNA Copying
papers.abstract: It has long been known that L-nucleotides inhibit the nonenzymatic copying of D-RNA templates, suggesting that nucleotide homochirality must have been attained before the emergence of RNA replication and the Origin of Life. Recent advances in nonenzymatic RNA copying, including the use of 2-aminoimidazole–activated monomers, and the elucidation of a reaction mechanism involving 2-aminoimidazolium-bridged dinucleotides, have inspired us to revisit the effects of L-nucleotides on the copying of D-RNA. We find that 2-AI-activated D- and L-nucleotides form heterochiral bridged dinucleotides at a slightly faster rate than homochiral bridged dinucleotides. 2-AI-bridged homochiral L/L dinucleotides bind with a lower affinity to D-RNA primer-template complexes and lead to much slower D-RNA primer extension than D/D bridged dinucleotides. Heterochiral bridged dinucleotides bind surprisingly well to D-RNA primer-template complexes but react slowly, leading to competitive inhibition. X-ray crystallography reveals that L-nucleotides bind to the template by standard base pairing, but that the reactive phosphate is not in a productive orientation for phosphodiester bond formation. Even more strikingly, an L-nucleotide at the 3′ end of a D-RNA primer is a chain terminator. X-ray crystallography shows that the 3′-hydroxyl of the terminal L-nucleotide faces away from the phosphate of the incoming reactive substrate, explaining the failure of continued primer extension. We also show that L-nucleotides can be incorporated in a D-RNA stem-loop via loop-closing ligation, removing them from the replicating pool. Together, our results provide a kinetic and structural framework for understanding why a high level, if not complete, homochirality is required for nonenzymatic RNA replication.

papers.title: Vacancy-Regulated Dual Single-Atom COF/g-C3N4 S-Scheme Heterostructures for Selective Multi-Carbon Product Formation via Solar-Driven Artificial Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: The photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into multi-carbon (C₂+) fuels provides a sustainable route for carbon utilization but is often limited by poor charge separation, inefficient CO2 activation, and sluggish carbon–carbon coupling. Herein, a vacancy-regulated Fe–Cu dual single-atom covalent organic framework/graphitic carbon nitride (COF/g-C3N4) S-scheme heterostructure was rationally designed and synthesized to enhance solar-driven artificial photosynthesis. Nitrogen-vacancy engineering generated abundant defect sites that improved visible-light harvesting and CO2 adsorption, while atomically dispersed Fe–Cu dual sites embedded within the COF promoted efficient CO2 activation and stabilized key *CO intermediates for C–C coupling. The intimate COF/g-C3N4 interface established an S-scheme heterojunction that facilitated directional charge transfer while preserving strong redox potentials. Comprehensive characterization using XRD, FESEM, TEM, HAADF-STEM, XPS, XANES/EXAFS, EPR, Raman spectroscopy, UV–Vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, photoluminescence spectroscopy, BET analysis, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and transient photocurrent measurements confirmed the successful formation of nitrogen vacancies, atomic Fe–Cu dispersion, and strong interfacial electronic coupling. The optimized heterostructure exhibited enhanced visible-light absorption with a narrowed band gap of approximately 2.18 eV, a 3.2-fold increase in photocurrent density, 61% lower charge-transfer resistance, and a 4.5-fold longer photoluminescence lifetime than pristine g-C3N4, indicating substantially improved charge separation. Under simulated AM 1.5G solar irradiation, the optimized catalyst achieved a total CO2 reduction rate of ≈820 μmol g-1 h-1, with a C₂+ product selectivity of 83.6%, producing ethylene, ethanol, and acetate as the dominant products while maintaining over 93% of its initial activity after ten consecutive cycles. Density functional theory calculations revealed that nitrogen vacancies redistributed the electronic structure, Fe–Cu dual single-atom sites reduced the activation barrier for *CO dimerization, and the S-scheme interface promoted efficient charge migration, collectively accelerating carbon–carbon bond formation. This work demonstrates that integrating vacancy engineering, dual single-atom catalysis, and S-scheme heterojunction construction provides an effective strategy for highly selective solar-driven CO2 conversion and offers new design principles for next-generation photocatalysts for artificial photosynthesis and renewable solar-fuel production.

papers.title: A Computational Study of Gemcitabine Encapsulation in CC3 Porous Organic Cage: Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, Binding Free Energy, and Structure-Activity Relationship Analysis
papers.abstract: Gemcitabine, a first-line nucleoside analogue chemotherapy drug, is rapidly inactivated in plasma by cytidine deaminase (CDA), severely limiting its therapeutic efficacy. Porous organic cages (POCs) have emerged as promising drug delivery vehicles due to their discrete, soluble architecture and tunable cavities. Here, we report a comprehensive computational structure-activity relationship (SAR) study of gemcitabine encapsulation across five CC3-based cage variants using molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and MM-PBSA binding free energy analysis. AutoDock Vina blind docking yielded exclusively endohedral binding (20/20 poses, best ΔG = −5.7 kcal/mol) for pristine CC3. Three independent 200 ns GROMACS MD simulations of pristine CC3 at 300 K reveal stochastic encapsulation-release dynamics consistent with μM-affinity binding (ΔGbind = −13.44 ± 0.41 kcal/mol). A systematic SAR campaign across four additional cage variants establishes critical design rules: N-methyl endo-functionalization (CC3-methyl) eliminates encapsulation by reducing cavity volume; aromatic fluorination (CC3-F12) provides marginal electrostatic improvement but insufficient kinetic stabilization; exo-phenyl functionalization (CC3-exo-phenyl) blocks drug entry entirely; while lowering simulation temperature to 280 K achieves complete, reproducible endohedral encapsulation across all three independent replicas (100% endohedral, mean 2.25 ± 0.25 Å, no exit events in 200 ns each). Probability distribution analysis confirms the transformation from a broad bimodal distribution at 300 K (mean 9.4 Å, 46% endohedral) to a sharp unimodal peak at 280 K (mean 2.25 Å, 100% endohedral). Framework breathing analysis reveals that CC3 is more rigid at 280 K (Rg std = 0.07–0.08 Å) than at 300 K (Rg std = 0.17 Å), consistent with thermally-stabilized encapsulation. These results establish a robust multi-scale computational framework to guide the rational design of porous organic cages for targeted drug delivery applications.

papers.title: Enhancing Grignard reactions via anion borrowing in deep eutectic /organic biphasic media
papers.abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. When assessing nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules, it has been shown that improved performance can be achieved using deep eutectic solvents (DESs). In this case, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i -PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results show an increased preference for the Grignard reaction over the formation of by-products originating from a β-H transfer from the isopropyl group with the DES/THF media. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the reaction of a neutral Grignard in bulk THF kinetically favours the β-H transfer, the chlorine enrichment originating from the DES is shown to make the two reactions kinetically more equivalent, and to drastically favor the thermodynamic preference for the Grignard product, a result of increased intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This result is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these non-conventional solvents.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and In Silico Evaluation of Antidepressants as Novel MexB Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: Background: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa poses a critical therapeutic challenge, primarily mediated by overexpression of the MexAB-OprM efflux pump system. Classical efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) such as PABÉTAN and NMP show promising in vitro activity but remain clinically intractable due to severe cytotoxicity. Drug repositioning offers an expedited pathway to identify safer alternatives through FDA-approved psychoactive molecules. Methods: A targeted library of 48 FDA-approved antidepressants was subjected to rigid molecular docking against the hydrophobic binding pocket of MexB (PDB: 2V50) using AutoDock Vina (v1.2.7). Benchmarking against reference EPIs (PABÉTAN ΔG = −9.53 kcal/mol; NMP ΔG = −9.48 kcal/mol) validated method selectivity. The top three candidates underwent comprehensive 2D/3D interaction analysis and in silico ADMET profiling via pkCSM. Results: Vilazodone (an FDA-approved 5-HT reuptake inhibitor and 5-HT1a partial agonist) emerged as the lead candidate with exceptional binding affinity (ΔG = −10.94 kcal/mol), surpassing reference inhibitors by 1.41 kcal/mol and 1.46 kcal/mol respectively. Structural analysis revealed optimized aromatic core anchoring through π-π stacking interactions with Phe178, Phe610, and Phe628, complemented by a unique dual hydrogen-bonding network with Gly675 and Asn676. Critically, Vilazodone avoids the unfavorable electrostatic repulsion with Lys134 observed in PABÉTAN. In silico ADMET profiling demonstrated high human intestinal absorption (92.77%), robust P-glycoprotein inhibition capacity, and a pharmacokinetic profile superior to reference EPIs. Conclusion: This study establishes Vilazodone as a highly promising lead compound for targeting the MexB efflux mechanism in P. aeruginosa. The convergence of superior binding thermodynamics, favorable structural interactions, documented FDA safety profile, and validated P-gp inhibition properties positions Vilazodone as a significant advance over conventional EPIs. These in silico findings warrant immediate experimental validation through in vitro synergy assays and bacterial accumulation studies.

papers.title: Physics-guided modelling of temperature-dependent electrical conductivity of functional oxides
papers.abstract: Functional oxide materials are widely employed across a range of electronic applications, where electrical conductivity and its temperature dependence serve as key screening metrics for material suitability. Across these applications, experimental characterisation remains resource-intensive and time-consuming. As a result, machine learning approaches have recently emerged as a digital alternative to accelerate materials discovery processes. However, datadriven approaches are typically restricted by the lack of a comprehensive experimentally-sourced database, with existing models trained on simulated density-functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we compiled an experimental database of over 7,000 temperature-dependent electrical conductivity samples for oxides, primarily extracted from commercial materials databases and peer-reviewed literature. We benchmark MODNet, a state-of-the-art general purpose composition-based machine learning baseline, against TriCondNet (a three-specialist conductivity network), a novel physics-guided neural network (PGNN) architecture developed to capture temperature-dependent electrical conductivity behaviour of metallic and semiconducting oxides. Our results demonstrate that TriCondNet outperforms baseline models on standard error metrics while adhering to the physical models for temperature–conductivity dependence. We then applied our top-performing model to an extensive composition list, screening candidates for two different application-specific case studies: dielectric and thermoelectric materials. Candidates were ranked based on their required conductivity relevant to the case study and associated uncertainty estimates. The resulting top ranked candidates matched materials already recognised as leading dielectrics and thermoelectrics, confirming that the workflow recovers established high-performers and establishing TriCondNet as a reliable basis for identifying new candidates through composition interpolation across known oxide families.

papers.title: Immobilized Thiol Catalysts for Native Chemical Ligation in Flow
papers.abstract: Native chemical ligation (NCL) is a well-established research tool, used to access long and complex peptides that cannot be efficiently synthesized by other means such as linear solidphase peptide synthesis (SPPS). However, its broader application beyond the research laboratory scale is limited due to limitations such as high dilution, slow reaction kinetics and challenges associated with using homogeneous thiol catalysts, including poor compatibility with desulfurization methods and difficult removal in subsequent chromatographic purification. In this study we report a continuous-flow NCL platform enabled by the development of a novel immobilized version of the aromatic thiol catalyst 4-mercaptophenylacetic acid (MPAA). This strategy employs shelf-stable peptide hydrazides that are activated in situ to acyl pyrazoles and subsequently converted to reactive thioesters in flow by the immobilized catalyst, thereby facilitating ligation with cysteine-containing peptides. The platform is directly compatible with inline desulfurization and supports high throughput synthesis of complex, structurally diverse and therapeutically relevant peptides up to 84 amino acids in length. This work establishes immobilized aryl thiols as a viable catalyst for NCL in continuous flow, identifies involved key challenges and provides foundation for its prospects towards industrial peptide manufacturing.

papers.title: Efficient Bayesian Optimization of Separation Chemistry in the Scarce-Data Regime Using Kinetic Reaction Networks
papers.abstract: Chemical process optimization is a critical and challenging task relevant to a broad range of industrial applications. Bayesian optimization (BO) has emerged as a powerful framework for navigating complex solution spaces, often with substantially greater efficiency than conventional experimental design approaches. While BO is commonly implemented using domain-agnostic Gaussian processes, its performance can potentially be further improved by incorporating domain knowledge. In this work, we propose a model-based BO framework that combines data-driven kinetic reaction networks with the pointwise optimal parameter sets (POPS) approach for improving uncertainty quantification. We apply this framework to the optimization of liquid-liquid uranium extraction using two monoamide ligands, N,N -dihexyloctanamide (DHOA) and N,N -di(2-ethylhexyl)-isobutyramide (DEHiBA). We evaluate the performance of the kinetic-model-based BO framework relative to a traditional Gaussian process counterpart, with particular emphasis on the scarce-data regime. We find that the kinetic reaction networks provide consistent and reliable predictions and that the POPS approach yields well-calibrated uncertainty estimates that can be effectively leveraged to guide the Bayesian optimization process. These features improve optimization efficiency, particularly in the scarce-data regime. Additional performance gains are obtained by regularizing the kinetic reaction networks using quantum mechanical calculations.

papers.title: Heat or Speed? Decoupling Thermal and Motion Contributions to Er3+ Upconversion
papers.abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) can be used as nanoscale motion sensors exploiting motion-induced changes in luminescence intensity ratios (LIRs). In addition, UCNPs are well established as powerful luminescent probes for LIR-based thermal sensing. This work investigates aspects of angular motion and temperature and elucidates mechanisms of cross-coupling with the goal of designing decoupling strategies, including dual-readout schemes for orthogonal sensing. To this end, Er 3+ /Yb 3+ -codoped NaGdF 4 UCNPs were systematically investigated, confirming that the green-to-red LIR of the Er 3+ emission is affected by stirring, allowing for motion sensing, however, only under known thermal conditions. Conversely, the population and depopulation kinetics of the Er 3+ ion’s 4 F 9/2 → 4 I 15/2 transition show stirring dependence that is unaffected by temperature, with relative angular motion sensitivities (S r rpm ) of up to ca. 3% per 100 rpm. In parallel, the commonly applied green-to-green LIR using the Er 3+ ion’s 2 H 11/2 → 4 I 15/2 and 4 S 3/2 → 4 I 15/2 transitions for thermal sensing is found to be more robust than the green-to-red LIR under varying stirring conditions. For this to hold true, it is crucial to eliminate any contribution of the 2 H 9/2 → 4 I 13/2 transition at 558 nm, being affected by motion. Overall, we here unveil the underlaying mechanism of stirring-dependent Er 3+ upconversion and propose a strategy to decouple thermal and motion contributions, thereby opening new avenues toward dual sensors and nanotechnologies with potential relevance for, e.g., biomedical or microfluidic applications.

papers.title: Light-Driven Control of Polar Order in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric nematic (NF) liquid crystals are polar fluids that combine long-range orientational order with spontaneous macroscopic polarization and exceptionally large dielectric permittivity. While these properties make NF materials attractive for responsive soft devices, incorporating additional functionality remains challenging because polar order is highly sensitive to molecular mismatch. Here we introduce a molecular design strategy that enables optical control of NF materials using azobenzene-based mesogens structurally matched to the archetypal NF compound DIO. Two derivatives are themselves ferroelectric nematogens, demonstrating that photoisomerizable mesogens can intrinsically sustain and modulate NF polar order, with large and reversible light-induced changes in polarization and dielectric permittivity. The same structural matching principle also enables non-NF azobenzenes to co-assemble with DIO at concentrations up to 20 wt% while preserving ferroelectric nematic order. In selected blends, light irradiation shifts the transition between ferroelectric nematic and antiferroelectric smectic order, reversibly switching the material between high- and low-permittivity states. Together, light and temperature provide complementary handles to navigate this phase landscape of competing ferroelectric and antiferroelectric order. These results provide a molecular design strategy for programming collective polar order in ferroelectric nematic fluids using light-responsive mesogens.

papers.title: CatGo: Bridging CLI Coding Agents with Interactive Structure and Workflow Management for Computational Chemistry
papers.abstract: Computational chemistry is increasingly limited not by individual calculations but by the manual effort of assembling, parameterizing, executing, and monitoring multi-step workflows across heterogeneous engines and computing environments; existing frameworks ease provenance and job management yet remain code-centric, limiting accessibility. Here we present CatGo, an AI-native computational chemistry workbench operable directly by large-language-model (LLM) coding agents through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface. Beyond a workflow engine, CatGo provides an interactive three-dimensional structure builder with atom-level editing, adsorption-site and adsorbate-placement tools, an integrated terminal for direct HPC access, and a bidirectionally synchronized visual editor, all sharing a single state so that human users and agents operate on the same structures and workflows. Researchers state objectives in natural language; agents then construct, validate, execute, and monitor directed-acyclic-graph workflows across VASP, CP2K, ORCA, LAMMPS, and machinelearning interatomic potentials, aided by compact graph-state serialization and batch mutations that cut LLM tool-calling overhead. We demonstrate an end-to-end Pt(111) oxygen-reduction workflow generated from a single natural-language instruction, establishing CatGo as a reproducible, agentdrivable workbench for computational chemistry.

papers.title: Comparing outdoor and accelerated weathering of polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene – predicting the degradation of microplastics in the environment
papers.abstract: Accelerated weathering becomes increasingly popular in microplastic research to produce defined, environmentally relevant reference particles and determine their degradation kinetics. To predict the persistence of environmental microplastics, models must be developed that correlate real-life with accelerated weathering. Therefore, we compare long-term accelerated and outdoor weathering studies using amorphous polystyrene, semi-crystalline low-density polyethylene and polypropylene particles. While mechanical stress was similar in all experiments, temperature and irradiance varied outdoors. In all cases, the particles weather due to photooxidation inducing chain scissions, polar functional groups and crosslinks. Macroscopically, particles degrade in three stages: surface abrasion, fragmentation and particle aggregation. By introducing a time-dependent acceleration factor composed of the Schwarzschild and Arrhenius laws, we derived a model with two parameters - the material-specific activation energy E A and the Schwarzschild coefficient p. While p was around 0.5 suggesting decreasing photon efficiency with increasing flux for all probed polymers, E A varied between 10 kJ/mol (PS) and 26 kJ/mol (LDPE, PP). Due to the E A differences, identical accelerated weathering durations correspond to markedly different outdoor timescales depending on polymer type and formulation. Using publicly available weather data, the model captures seasonal and regional variations more accurately than common models using average temperatures or constant acceleration factors. Synopsis: The characteristics of commodity plastics like PS, PE and PP weathered in natural environments can be predicted by parameterizing the irradiance and temperature from accelerated weathering studies.

papers.title: Weathering of microplastic creates nanometre-sized surface-near cavities – A 129Xe NMR spectroscopic study
papers.abstract: Microplastic (MP) particles undergo simultaneous structural and morphological transformations during weathering. These processes are expected to generate surface features across multiple length scales, ranging from micrometere-sized cracks and fractures to nanometre scale roughness and surface-near cavities. In particular, the latter strongly influences the adsorption, and thus the transport, of environmental contaminants. However, the characterisation of these surface features is severely hampered by the low overall surface areas of typical MP particles. Here, we demonstrate that a multiscale characterisation approach combining scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), krypton physisorption and hyperpolarised 129 Xe NMR spectroscopy allows to identify the complex surface morphology induced by environmental weathering. Therefore, an important gap for understanding the development of MP particle surface evolution and the uptake of environmental pollutants can be closed. For different batches of artificially weathered polystyrene (PS) microplastic particles, this approach allowed to determine the micrometre scale surface damage, the resulting nanoscale topographical features and the trends for the specific adsorptive surface area during weathering The hyperpolarised 129 Xe NMR spectra enabled to identify the corresponding surface near confined structures and small cavities. The NMR spectroscopic analysis was based on reference materials with well-defined pore sizes that provide a calibration of the 129 Xe chemical shifts using the Terskikh model, thereby providing a cavity size-to-chemical-shift relation. These findings highlight the importance of microporous surface domains as potential adsorption sites for ions and small organic molecules, including environmentally relevant toxic compounds. The results illustrate the use of hyperpolarised 129 Xe NMR spectroscopy as a powerful tool for investigating weathering-induced nanostructural changes in microplastics. The implications for contaminant uptake and transport are generally relevant of MP in environmental systems.

papers.title: SurfKit: Multi-property surfactant prediction combining experimental data and molecular dynamics simulations
Extending the Python RESP Framework for Extra Point Charge Fitting
papers.abstract: The Restrained Electrostatic Potential (RESP) method is widely used to derive electrostatic parameters for Newtonian-based models. However, conventional nuclei centered charge models can struggle to reproduce anisotropic features such as halogen σ-holes and electron lone-pair regions. Herein, an extension is presented of the Psi4-compatible Python resp implementation of Alenaizan et al. that enables partial atomic charge fitting to user-defined extra point sites represented as massless dummy particles. This reengineering introduces an INI-based configuration layer, a revised driver.py that propagates extra point sites through grid/ESP handling, and an updated espfit.py engine that continues to support multi-conformer fitting, and an updated extras.py that includes functions for adding extra point centers to the fitting. Also introduced into the code are functions for computing RMSE and RRMSE metrics, along with support for the recently developed van der Waals radii by Charry and Tkatchenko. Several examples are provided that demonstrate Stage 1 and Stage 2 fitting involving single conformation, multiple conformations as well as the generation and use of multiple orientations. The resulting workflow is transparent, reproducible, and enables the development of both nuclei-centered and off-centered electrostatic models for molecular mechanics-based simulations.

papers.title: Integrating GC-MS with Computational Toxicology for Pesticide Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Pesticide risk assessment separates analytical detection from toxicological evaluation, leaving a practical gap: regulatory-compliant residue levels reveal nothing about the biological hazard of detected compounds, and computational toxicology models are rarely validated against real environmental measurements. This study presents an integrated framework combining GC-MS residue quantification with QSAR-based toxicity prediction, using Mordred molecular descriptors and Random Forest and Gradient Boosting classifiers, deployed as an open-source web API for real-time risk assessment. The framework is demonstrated on three composite cassava samples from a smallholder production system, in which seven pesticides spanning organochlorines, organophosphates, and pyrethroids were detected at 0.40% to 2.20% of Maximum Residue Limits. Toxicity prediction returned uniformly non-mutagenic and non-carcinogenic classifications across all compounds. Concordance with literature classifications was 57.1% (4 of 7 compounds) for both Ames mutagenicity and carcinogenicity. The carcinogenicity mismatches were concentrated in organochlorines specifically (dieldrin, endosulfan II, and methoxychlor, three of the four detected organochlorines, all documented as carcinogenic in the literature but predicted non-carcinogenic), consistent with bioaccumulation and endocrine-disruption mechanisms that extend beyond features captured by topological and constitutional molecular descriptors. The mutagenicity mismatches, by contrast, were not organochlorine-specific (endosulfan II, parathion, and dimethoate), indicating the descriptor-based limitation is mechanism- and endpoint-dependent rather than a general organochlorine blind spot. Integrated risk scoring identified three compounds warranting medium-priority monitoring despite full regulatory compliance, demonstrating that toxicity-weighted assessment differentiates hazard profiles that concentration-based screening cannot. The framework's modular architecture, separating analytical input, descriptor calculation, toxicity prediction, and risk integration, supports extension to additional crops, chemical classes, and toxicological endpoints. All components are openly available. Because several compounds examined in the field-sample evaluation are represented in the training data available for descriptor-based QSAR, a graph neural network was additionally trained on identical data splits and evaluated, alongside the descriptor-based classifiers, against a deliberately constructed, genuinely held-out probe set of 22 organochlorine pesticides. Neither the descriptor-based classifiers nor the graph neural network reliably generalise to this compound class, indicating the under-prediction problem reflects limitations in training labels and mechanism coverage rather than molecular feature representation alone.

papers.title: The Oil Well as the Mine of the Future: Towards In-situ Coproduction of Critical Minerals and Hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: The global demand for critical minerals and materials (CMM) is rapidly outpacing conventional supply chains. This Perspective presents a paradigm shift by demonstrating that mature U.S. sedimentary basins are not merely depleting fuel reservoirs but are vast, accessible repositories of mineral wealth. By integrating in-situ mining (ISM) chemistries into existing oil and gas infrastructure, we can leverage billions of dollars in sunk capital to address modern supply chain bottlenecks while simultaneously enhancing energy recovery. Our analysis of thirteen U.S. hydrocarbon reservoirs identifies fifteen critical elements, including titanium, vanadium, nickel, cobalt, etc., ubiquitous within the sedimentary matrix. We highlight that 1% enhanced recovery rate of hydrocarbon from the existing reservoirs and 1% recovery rate of CMM from 5% of these accessible formation volumes could yield over 530 million barrels of oil, 6 Tcf natural gas, and 500 million metric tons of CMM, providing scale context for the potential energy and material significance of sedimentary co-production. Future research should focus on optimizing selective lixiviants that maintain reservoir integrity while maximizing yields of CMM and hydrocarbons within a closed-loop system. Redefining the earth as a reactor offers a pragmatic and low-footprint pathway to secure national industrial competitiveness and advance technological leadership.

papers.title: Computing Nucleation Rates from Confined Equilibria: The Critical Cluster Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Nucleation is a fundamental step in the formation of new materials, with nucleation rates governing phase-transition pathways and outcomes that influence material properties across chemistry, physics, and biology. Nevertheless, extracting nucleation rates remains challenging: experiments are limited by the microscopic length scales involved, while molecular simulations are hindered by the rare-event nature of nucleation and the large system sizes required to sample low-supersaturation regimes typical of experiments and industrial processing. Here, we build on the established thermodynamic correspondence between stable clusters in small, closed systems and critical clusters in open systems, and develop a multicomponent extension, the Critical Cluster Equivalence Principle, that transforms this correspondence into a practical workflow for calculating nucleation rates. We employ this equivalence to determine solvent-mediated NaCl crystal nucleation driving forces and rates over a wide range of supersaturations (S NaCl ∈ [1.5, 4]), and further validate the framework by benchmarking against curvature-corrected homogeneous nucleation rates for argon vapour condensation. This has been achieved using a small number of brute-force, finite-size simulations in which cluster-size statistics and monomer-exchange dynamics in the steady-state map directly onto critical clusters in macroscopic systems. By combining this multicomponent correspondence with the computational approach developed here, the current investigation has obtained nucleation rates in excellent agreement with experiments and enhanced sampling simulations. This approach provides a unified and generalizable tool for predicting nucleation rates with minimal computational effort, enabling routine application across a wide range of material systems.

papers.title: Topology-Based Lattice Engineering in DNA Nanomaterials
papers.abstract: In this study, we establish the topological adaptability and structural resilience of periodic soft matter entanglements using the DNA tensegrity triangle, a foundational motif in structural DNA nanotechnology, as a model system. Motivated by the Reidemeister moves, which consist of three local moves on knot or link diagrams, we systematically slide the strand termini relative to junction crossings to yield 47 unique biomolecular structures. With this method, we identify three major results: (1) a “poke crossover” between unlinked helices with inter- locking nicks that drastically increases lattice rigidity, alters lattice geometry, and provides a convenient metal cation binding site; (2) a new class of four-arm junction, the semi-junction, which is held together by a single rotatable bond and features globally relaxed torsional strain and novel crystal packing; and (3) a facile topological inversion between left- and right-handed tertiary structures enabled by the rotational freedom of the semi-junction, demonstrating how local flexibility at a single connection can reorganize global molecular chirality without disrupting the underlying architecture.
