Applied to the hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions, the corrected framework reveals that small Tafel slopes are indicative of a reversible Volmer step with low surface coverage, irrespective of reaction path and adsorption type, while mechanistic discrimination only emerges at high Tafel slopes. Experimentally, we observe Tafel slopes of 140mV dec−1-190mV dec−1 on polycrystalline Pt in alkaline media, values not captured by the classical framework but naturally described by the corrected one. Furthermore, by providing a continuous analytical solution that spans from these interaction-dominated asymptotes down to the rigorous 0mV dec−1 reversible limit, our framework eliminates the need to heuristically define Tafel regions.

papers.title: Reactive Atomistic Simulations of Doping-Driven Co-Aggregation in P3HT:F4TCNQ
papers.abstract: The performance of doped organic semiconductors (OSCs) is governed by a strong coupling between the doping equilibrium and the film morphology, yet capturing both simultaneously in a single atomistic model has remained difficult. Here we use the Reactive Monte Carlo Molecular Dynamics (RMCMD) method to study poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) doped with 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-7,7,8,8-tetracyanoquinodimethane (F4TCNQ), a prototypical OSC-dopant pair, and show that dopant aggregation and doping efficiency are mutually determined. We find that ionization converts a pre-aggregated dopant cluster into a mixed P3HT:F4TCNQ ”co-aggregate” whose extent is set by the reaction free energy; as dopants ionize, Coulomb repulsion drives them apart and pulls in ionized P3HT so that higher doping efficiency and greater OSC-dopant mixing are self-reinforcing. Introducing explicit solvent, we observe ionization-driven P3HT:F4TCNQ co-aggregation and displacement of solvent from the dopant coordination shell, consistent with experimentally reported poor solubility of ionized P3HT:F4TCNQ complexes. We also observe a higher doping efficiency in the more polar solvent acetonitrile than in chlorobenzene.

papers.title: Conversion-Resolved Kinetics of ABS Thermolysis Using Differential Coats-Redfern and Friedman Analysis
papers.abstract: Acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) is an important engineering plastic in electrical, electronic, automotive, consumer-product, and additive-manufacturing applications. However, its pyrolytic recycling requires reliable kinetic interpretation beyond global thermogravimetric descriptors. In this study, non-isothermal thermolysis of ABS was investigated at 15, 20, and 25 °C·min-1 using differential Coats-Redfern and Friedman isoconversional analyzes with rate-parity and conversion-variant compensation checks. Because conversion-averaged Ea can mask local deviations for isoconversional mechanistic model selection, root mean square error (RMSE) of Ea was used as the primary metric for comparing d-CR and Friedman activation-energies. Under the combined criteria, the L2 random-scission model showed the smallest RMSE of Ea and acceptable rate-parity (R2parity = 0.98938) and compensation behavior (R2compensation = 0.99597), and was therefore selected as the most plausible approximate model. The conversion-averaged Friedman activation energy was 171.12 kJ·mol-1, and the mean pre-exponential factor reconstructed with L2 at 25 C·min-1 was 3.86 × 1020 s-1. These results demonstrate that the d-CR-Friedman framework provides a practical conversion-resolved strategy for interpreting ABS thermolysis beyond classical CR linearity and global kinetic-parameter extraction.

papers.title: Intrinsic Irreducible-Cartesian Tensor Carrier for Equivariant Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Equivariant interatomic potentials use compact angular irreps, while many observables and long-range sources are Cartesian tensors. We introduce the intrinsic irreducible-Cartesian tensor carrier (ICTC), which builds harmonic polynomial bases and intertwiners in Cartesian algebra while storing features directly in compact 2l+1 carriers. A degree-wise orthogonal bridge lets supported MACE checkpoints run in ICTC coordinates with 10000-step double-precision energy/force agreement, and fused ICTC tensor products remove the high-degree Cartesian-3j bottleneck. With matched MACE training protocols, ICTC trains faster on revised MD17, liquid water, and a Materials Project trajectory subset; learning-rate controls identify a finite-width update-scale effect inside the same irreducible function space. The carriers also define deployable Cartesian source coordinates for production molecular dynamics, covering electrostatic multipoles and an l=2 anisotropic polarizability for eigensolver-free many-body dispersion.

papers.title: Enhancing the robustness of rhodium single-atom catalysts for styrene hydroformylation through carbon nitride doping
papers.abstract: Rh single-atom catalysts (SACs) have recently attracted significant attention as highly active heterogeneous catalysts for the hydroformylation of olefins. Despite the potential of these systems to become an alternative to the commercial and highly efficient homogeneous Rh and Co catalysts, leaching, an important drawback of SACs, still needs to be addressed. In this study, we have developed a series of Rh SACs supported on heteroatom (P or/and B)-doped carbon nitride for the hydroformylation of styrene and investigated the effects of heteroatom-doping on the catalytic performance. The developed Rh SACs selectively promoted the reaction and exhibited superior durability against Rh leaching to a dopant-free counterpart catalyst.

papers.title: Cross-exposure transferability and failure boundaries of self-supervised DNN denoising for AR-HAXPES depth profiling
papers.abstract: Laboratory-source angle-resolved hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (AR-HAXPES) is photon-starved atthespatialresolution required formapping,wheretheframe averaging needed to recover a clean depth profile at every position drives total acquisition time into a prohibitive regime. Self-supervised neural denoising offers an alternative to acquisition-time scaling, and a recent companion study 1 has systematically benchmarked its performance against alternative strategies; however, its operational envelope across exposures, its cross-exposure transferability, and its failure modes in the photon-starved regime remain uncharacterised. Here we evaluate self-supervised denoising atthe smallestpossibletargetwindow across three exposures spanning a 25-fold range of per-frame photon flux on a model C / Al 2 O 3 / TiO 2 / Si multilayer. We identify an empirical directional rule for cross-exposure denoiser deployment — train S/N ≥ inference S/N —, characterise the failure boundary in the photon-starved regime where upstream denoiser collapse propagates into constraint-saturated inversion solutions, and locate the asymptotic reach of alltested denoising strategies (frame averaging, Self-DNN, Cross-DNN) relative to a methodological floor set by the reproducibility of the reference. Within the success region of this rule, cross-exposure transfer enables up to a 48-fold equivalent acquisition-time reduction on the depth-RMSE axis (14-fold on the Wasserstein-1 interface- localization axis) at the most photon-starved 4.8 s/frame condition. These results frame self- supervised AR-HAXPES denoising as a characterisable engineering operation with quantifiable failure boundaries and recovery routes, rather than as an empirical post-processing recipe.

papers.title: Asymmetric Pulse Electrodeposition of High-Index Faceted Gold Nanostructures for 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation
papers.abstract: This work reports the electrodeposition of high-index faceted gold particles resembling rhombic hexecontahedrons in choline chloride urea deep eutectic solvent through the application of asymmetric potential pulses. Potential pulses alternated between cathodic potentials ranging from -0.20 V to -0.25 V vs. Ag/AgCl and an anodic limit of 0.35 V vs. Ag/AgCl near the gold dissolution onset. While the cathodic pulse duration was fixed at 0.5 s, the anodic pulse duration varied from 0.5 s to 2.5 s to study its influence on crystal growth. Symmetric pulses produced poorly defined structures, whereas longer anodic pulses induced tetrahexahedral and truncated bipyramidal nanostructures. Further increasing the reduction overpotential induced a shape transition to rhombic hexecontahedral morphologies, attributed to the ligand effect of urea. Blank cyclic voltammograms in NaOH solution and Pb underpotential deposition measurements on pulse-deposited gold indicated the formation of structures enclosing [n(110) × (111)] facets. The electrocatalytic performance of the pulse deposited nanostructures towards 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation was tested, showing strong activity for partial aldehyde oxidation and moderate activity for the oxidation of the alcohol moiety. This study demonstrates that asymmetric pulse electrodeposition offers a promising approach to tailoring surface geometries and highlights the role of deep eutectic solvents in shaping crystal structures.

papers.title: Immobilized Thiol Catalyst for Native Chemical Ligation in Flow
papers.abstract: Native chemical ligation (NCL) is a well-established research tool, used to access long and complex peptides that cannot be efficiently synthesized by other means such as linear solidphase peptide synthesis (SPPS). However, its broader application beyond the research laboratory scale is limited due to limitations such as high dilution, slow reaction kinetics and challenges associated with using homogeneous thiol catalysts, including poor compatibility with desulfurization methods and difficult removal in subsequent chromatographic purification. In this study we report a continuous-flow NCL platform enabled by the development of a novel immobilized version of the aromatic thiol catalyst 4-mercaptophenylacetic acid (MPAA). This strategy employs shelf-stable peptide hydrazides that are activated in situ to acyl pyrazoles and subsequently converted to reactive thioesters in flow by the immobilized catalyst, thereby facilitating ligation with cysteine-containing peptides. The platform is directly compatible with inline desulfurization and supports high throughput synthesis of complex, structurally diverse and therapeutically relevant peptides up to 84 amino acids in length. This work establishes immobilized aryl thiols as a viable catalyst for NCL in continuous flow, identifies involved key challenges and provides foundation for its prospects towards industrial peptide manufacturing.

papers.title: Crystal symmetry engineering of one-dimensional helical perovskites for integrated circularly polarized light detection and bulk photovoltaic effect
papers.abstract: Crystal symmetry engineering through chiral organic cation design enables the integration of circularly polarized light (CPL) detection and the bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in solution-processed low-dimensional chiral perovskites. One-dimensional (1D) helical lead-halide perovskites are promising candidates for this integration because their helical inorganic framework intrinsically gives rise to chiral electronic structures; however, most solution-processed helical thin films crystallize in a chiral but nonpolar space group ( P 2 1 2 1 2 1 ), preventing the emergence of BPVE. Here we show that rational 4-substituent engineering of chiral naphthylethylamine (NEA) cations drives a controlled symmetry reduction from P 2 1 2 1 2 1 to the chiral–polar space group P 2 1 , without perturbing the strongly distorted helical inorganic framework. This substituent-induced symmetry lowering converts previously nonpolar helical films into polar ones, simultaneously activating BPVE while preserving the pronounced chiroptical response. The resulting chiral–polar thin films exhibit highly selective CPL detection with large extinction ratios, together with a clear zero-bias photocurrent and a finite photovoltage under solar illumination arising from BPVE. These results establish crystal symmetry engineering through organic cation design as a molecular design principle for multifunctional chiral perovskite optoelectronics.

papers.title: Metal-Induced Single-Chain Folding of Unstructured Synthetic Macromolecules into Precise Tertiary Structures
papers.abstract: The folding of discrete, sequence-defined macromolecules into precise tertiary structures underlies function in biology 1,2 . Nevertheless, despite significant advances in sequence-defined polymer synthesis 3-7 , analogous folding of synthetic macromolecules into cavity-bearing tertiary structures driven by sidechain interactions has not been achieved 8-10 . We introduce a general metal-directed strategy for macromolecular folding that addresses this limitation. First, a discrete 2.6 kDa macromolecule bearing an unstructured backbone and four bis-pyridyl pendants is folded around two Pd(II) centers to afford a unique, knedel-like globular object whose precise chain conformation provides a single sterically accessible portal to a low-symmetry internal cavity capable of molecular recognition, as demonstrated using anionic small molecule guests. Then, analogous metal-directed folding of macromolecules with different sequences based on the order of four monomers generates isomeric folded structures that, when bound to the same anionic guests, display distinct spectroscopic fingerprints arising from sequence-specific host-guest interactions. Altogether, this work achieves a longstanding goal of bioinspired folding of sequence-defined synthetic macromolecules, opening new avenues for encoding structure and function within a single macromolecular strand.

papers.title: The Syntax of Matter: Synthesis Planning as the Foundation of Generative Chemistry
papers.abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have improved benchmark performance for chemical property prediction, yet reliable transfer to new chemical domains remains limited. A contributing factor is that many models treat molecules primarily as static graphs, ignoring the causal logic of how they are constructed. This review surveys multistep synthesis planning (2020-2026) and argues that the field is undergoing a fundamental transition: from an Era of Navigability (2018-2023), focused on the computational feasibility of finding any route through combinatorial search space, to an Era of Validity (2024-Present), focused on the chemical correctness of those routes. We organize the literature around two dominant paradigms, search-based planning and direct sequence generation, and analyze how their design choices relate to different notions of validity. To resolve the ambiguity of current "solvability" metric, which frequently exceeds 99% by measuring only topological connectivity, we introduce a formalized Hierarchy of Chemical Validity (Solv-N). This framework distinguishes between syntactic (Solv-0) and topological (Solv-1) success, which are largely solved, and the higher-order constraints of selectivity (Solv-2) and executability (Solv-3), which remain open challenges. We critically examine how legacy benchmarks and inflated virtual inventories obscure this distinction, and we conclude with a roadmap for synthesis-aware foundation models evaluated under explicit Tier 2-3 constraints.

papers.title: History-Aware Text Representations for Polymer Property Prediction from Literature-Derived Records
papers.abstract: Macroscopic polymer properties are shaped not only by repeat-unit chemistry but also by how polymers are synthesized, processed and formulated. Yet most polymer machine-learning pipelines rely on structure-only encoders that reduce each material to a repeat-unit representation. Here we introduce Holistic History-aware Text (HHT), a framework that represents polymer composition, synthesis routes and processing conditions as natural-language descriptions, embeds them with a frozen pretrained large language model (LLM), and predicts properties using a lightweight regression head. By retaining experimental history, HHT distinguishes polymer samples that share the same monomer chemistry but differ in synthesis or processing history, and accommodates complex formulations for which canonical repeat-unit SMILES are unavailable. Using this representation, we curated 9,415 records from more than 1,000 papers spanning six polymer properties. We further identify pronounced article-level clustering in these literature-mined datasets and introduce a baseline to quantify its effect. HHT outperforms structure-only encoders for all six properties and surpasses the article-level baseline for five, with only a marginal difference for ultimate tensile strength. Overall, HHT provides a practical framework for history-aware polymer property prediction, extending structure–processing–property learning to heterogeneous literature-derived records that cannot be captured by repeat-unit chemistry alone.

papers.title: A fully-polarizable KS-DFT/AMOEBA embedding scheme for plane wave basis sets through the MiMiC framework
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a fully-polarizable QM/MM embedding scheme for plane-wave basis sets implemented in the MiMiC framework. In this scheme, the QM subsystem is treated with Kohn--Sham DFT, while the environment is modeled through the AMOEBA polarizable force field, as implemented in Tinker-HP. We investigate its propensity for the electron spill-out problem, compare it with the more widespread electrostatic embedding QM/MM, and showcase its potential by calculating the dipole moment of an acetone molecule solvated in different solvents. Even though restricted to single-point calculations, the presented implementation is the first step towards an efficient fully-polarizable QM/MM embedding scheme for molecular dynamics simulations targeting modern high-performance computing facilities.

papers.title: Functionalization and Mechanical Properties of Poly(lactide-cyclohexadiene oxide) Block Copolymers
papers.abstract: A series of lactide (LA) and cyclohexadiene oxide (CHDO) multiblock copolymers was synthesized using a redox switchable complex, (salfen)Zr(OiPr)2 (salfen = N,N’-bis(2,4-di-tert-butylphenoxy)-1,1’-ferrocenediimine), with LA being polymerized by the reduced state, while CHDO was polymerized by the oxidized state of the catalyst. Diblock (PCHDO-PLA) and triblock (PLA-PCHDO-PLA and PCHDO-PLA-PCHDO) copolymers were prepared, and all the copolymers were post-functionalized using a thiol-ene click reaction. Dynamic mechanical analysis showed that both triblock copolymers have a better elasticity than the diblock copolymer, and all the functionalized copolymers have a better elasticity than the corresponding non-functionalized copolymers.

papers.title: Raven: agentic AI for materials discovery enabled by post-trained chemistry LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language model agents can connect scientific text, molecular generation, simulation, and laboratory planning, but their use in materials discovery is limited by weak reproducibility, hidden intermediate state, and scarce domain-specific quantum-chemical data. Here we introduce Raven, a state-aware multi-agent framework for materials discovery powered by QuantumChem-200K, a corpus of more than 214,000 organic molecules annotated with photoinitiator-relevant properties including two-photon absorption cross sections and singlet–triplet intersystem-crossing energies. Raven combines replayable state-graph orchestration with QuantaMind, a Qwen-2.5-32B model fine-tuned on QuantumChem-200K for molecular property prediction and screening. A frozen QuantaMind forward model verifies candidates generated by an inverse model, and GRPO post-training uses this verifier as a reward signal to align generation with target property constraints. In a two-photon-polymerization photoresin campaign, Raven generated, filtered, verified, and ranked candidate resins, connecting auditable agent reasoning to experimentally testable materials.

papers.title: Magnetic Structure Model of Hydrogen Molecule and Its Verification Method
papers.abstract: Magnetic structural model of hydrogen molecule, the opposite magnetic poles of two Bohr’s hydrogen atoms attract to form hydrogen molecule, is proposed in this article, which is completely consistent with the experimental results that “the electrons in the hydrogen molecule can have no momentum about the axis of symmetry”. According to the model, various structural parameters of hydrogen molecule are calculated quantitatively, in which, the minimum value of the total energy is -31.95851eV, the distance between two atomic nuclei is 0.74120Å, the distance between two circular orbitals is 0.37869Å, the kinetic energy of the two electrons is 24.22485eV, repulsive energy between two electrons is 12.16298 eV, and magnetic attraction energy between two hydrogen atoms is -7.73367eV. This model can be experimentally verified through the following method: preparing hydrogen molecule crystals at ultra-low temperatures, and using neutron diffraction to determine the distance between two atomic nuclei in the crystal, and using X-ray diffraction to determine the distance between two circular orbitals (the distance between the centers of the two regions with the highest electron density). If the measured results are same or similar to the calculated values, it can further prove that the magnetic structure model of the hydrogen molecule is correct and the nature of covalent bond attraction is magnetic force. Keywords: Hydrogen Molecular; Magnetic Structure; Covalent Bond; Bohr’s model

papers.title: Diradical vs zwitterion – Controlling π-spin polarization in donor-acceptor heterotriangulene dimers
papers.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) with open-shell electronic structures have attracted increasing interest due to their potential applications in molecular electronics, spintronics and quantum technologies. However, controlling π-spin polarization and magnetic interactions in PAH-based diradicals remains a significant challenge. We present a spin-orbital detuning strategy to modulate magnetic couplings and enable reversible spin states (diradical-zwitterionic) switching. Using first-principles calculations, we investigated donor-acceptor heterotriangulene dimers (DA-HTDs) with various electron-donating and -withdrawing groups in gas phase and solvents of varying polarity. We reveal a linear correlation between monomer spin-orbital mismatch and antiferromagnetic (AFM) couplings, predicting record-high values up to −586 meV. Beyond a critical spin-orbital energy difference of 2.43 eV, π-spin polarization collapses, resulting in a zwitterionic diamagnetic ground state. Solvent polarity provides an external handle to control this phase transition, with the trihydrotriangulene-trioxotriangulene (TRIH-TOT) dimer remaining a diradical in non-polar but becoming zwitterionic in polar solvents. This behavior can facilitate solution synthesis of the diradicals from ionic monomers, and long-term storage as a diamagnetic state. These findings establish practical design rules for engineering spin states and solvent-responsive organic magnetic materials.

papers.title: More selective Grignard reactions via anion borrowing in deep eutectic /organic biphasic media
papers.abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. When assessing nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules, it has been shown that improved performance can be achieved using deep eutectic solvents (DESs). In this case, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i -PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results show an increased preference for the Grignard reaction over the formation of by-products originating from a β-H transfer from the isopropyl group with the DES/THF media. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the reaction of a neutral Grignard in bulk THF kinetically favours the β-H transfer, the chlorine enrichment originating from the DES is shown to make the two reactions kinetically more equivalent, and to drastically favor the thermodynamic preference for the Grignard product, a result of increased intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This result is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these non-conventional solvents.

papers.title: Solitarius: An Agentic Architecture for Computer-aided Molecular Inverse Design
papers.abstract: Applying generative molecular design requires both chemical knowledge to turn a scientific aim into a computable objective and technical skill to configure and run the workflow that pursues it. Here, we present Solitarius , an architecture for automated computer-aided molecular discovery. It leverages agentic large language models (LLMs) for planning and configuring molecular generation workflows while delegating the underlying operations (e.g., model training, generating chemical structures, and optimisation) to a dedicated molecular generative AI platform. Solitarius further guides the LLM agents to use this platform as a human expert would, selecting appropriate procedures for a given objective and executing them accordingly. We first test whether LLM agents alone, without this guidance, are capable of reliably running the generative chemistry workflow, which exposes a gap in their ability to manage multi-step procedures. Equipped with both key generative algorithms and guidance, first, we apply Solitarius to the design of singlet-fission chromophores that satisfy the desired excited-state energetic criteria. We then use Solitarius to expand an organocatalyst dataset into sparsely populated regions of its property space. Across these examples, we demonstrate how Solitarius interprets scientific intent from plain-language goals, formulates scoring logic that reflects the desired objective, and iteratively executes molecular-generation workflows until the desired objectives are met. In the singlet-fission design example, Solitarius revises the planned design workflow as the search strategy evolves with the new results, shifting from open-ended de novo generation to structure-guided exploration using filters to avoid rediscovery and focus on the vicinity of the input molecules. For dataset expansion, Solitarius independently analyses the dataset to identify sparse regions. It then formulates an approach to populate them while preserving key catalytic structural motifs.

papers.title: Analytical nuclear gradients for the CC2 method using pair-natural orbitals based on localized virtual molecular orbitals for ground states
papers.abstract: Analytical nuclear energy gradients are indispensable for geometry optimizations and potential-energy-surface explorations, yet their development for pair-natural-orbital (PNO)-based methods remains limited. In this work, we present the analytical nuclear gradient theory for the ground-state PNO-based second-order approximate coupled cluster (CC2) model using localized virtual molecular orbitals (LVMOs). The gradient theory is formulated within the Lagrangian framework as an extension of our previously developed LVMO-based PNO-MP2 analytical gradient theory. Although the use of LVMOs requires additional localization constraints in the Lagrangian, orthonormal LVMOs simplify the coupled-perturbed equations and energy gradient expressions, and these advantages are exploited in the PNO-CC2 analytical gradient formulation. The implementation is extended to the spin-component-scaled (SCS) variant. To facilitate the development and implementation, we extended our previously developed automated symbolic derivation framework, which systematically generates the derivative expressions for gradient calculations. Benchmark calculations on phenylalkane chains demonstrate favorable scaling of the analytical gradient evaluation. Gradients vary smoothly along a bond-dissociation coordinate of a ketene derivative, indicating that PNO orbital truncation does not introduce noticeable artifacts. Geometry optimizations of difluorodiene reproduce the characteristic elongation of electron-rich bonds observed for the CC2 theory relative to the MP2 theory. Applications to intermolecular complexes show that the PNO-CC2 framework provides optimized structures and binding energies comparable to those from the PNO-MP2 framework. Single-point gradient calculations for realistic molecular systems of around one hundred atoms demonstrate applicability of the implementation. This work establishes the analytical gradient formulation for ground-state PNO-CC2 theory and provides a foundation for future extensions to excited states.

papers.title: A neural-network approach to probing correlations within multimass velocity-map imaging data sets: beyond covariance mapping
papers.abstract: Covariance mapping has proved to be a powerful approach to extracting correlations between particle momenta from velocity-map imaging data sets, providing detailed insights into a wide range of chemical dynamics in the high-count-rate experimental regime where coincidence approaches fail. Despite its strengths, covariance mapping is susceptible to noise in the data set, and is only able to identify twobody and three-body correlations, with higher-order correlations requiring the use of more complex cumulance methods. Here, we show that a neural network can learn event-specific particle correlations from multimass velocity-map imaging data sets recorded under high-count-rate conditions. We develop a conditional point-process model that learns detector-plane correlated ion distributions directly from the data set, and evaluate the performance of the model using two different evaluation metrics. When used to extract two-body correlations between Coulomb explosion products of SO2, the method returns a result in excellent agreement with that obtained using conventional recoil-frame covariance mapping, with performance metrics indicating statistically significant event-specific conditioning even in a regime characterised by noisy and highly similar events. The model is easily extended to enable determination of higher-order correlations, which we demonstrate using a simulated data set for the five-body breakup of (E)-1-bromo-1-chloro-2-fluoroethene. Our results indicate that conditional point process learning offers a promising alternative to covariance and cumulance analysis for use in analysing data from a wide variety of chemical dynamics experiments.

papers.title: BEAD: a Human-in-the-Loop Agentic Framework for Explainable and Prospective Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: A critical bottleneck in AI-driven drug discovery is the inability to integrate traditional medicinal chemistry intuition, which frequently results in uninterpretable or chemically implausible molecular outputs. Here, we present BEAD (Bridging the gap between Experiment- and Artificial intelligence-based Drug design), a human-in-the-loop agentic framework for explainable drug design. BEAD places medicinal chemists in the decision-making loop to explore and optimize new scaffolds or molecules. Retrospective studies on MAT2A, PKMYT1, and IL-17A demonstrate that BEAD enables successful cross-target scaffold hopping and scaffold-constrained molecular generation via conversational interactions. Prospectively, we deployed BEAD in a real-world drug discovery targeting PRMT5. A two-stage pipeline was executed from cross-target scaffold hopping-based hit discovery to scaffold-constrained lead optimization. By synthesizing only nine molecules, we successfully identified CRP-276. Crucially, CRP-276 achieved in vivo anti-tumor efficacy equivalent to the clinical reference MRTX1719, alongside superior target selectivity and improved ADMET profiles. Ultimately, this work represents a successful implementation of a powerful human-AI collaborative system, enabling efficient, interpretable and empirically grounded drug design.

papers.title: Polyanion-Based Compounds for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
papers.abstract: Rechargeable magnesium metal batteries represent a compelling post-lithium energy storage technology owing to the abundance of terrestrial magnesium reserves, their current cost-effectiveness and intrinsically higher safety relative to lithium systems, coupled with their capacity to deliver high volumetric energy density. However, this promise and beyond remains constrained by the stringent requirement that rapid and reversible Mg 2+ transport can be achieved in concert with electrochemical and thermodynamic stability across both electrodes and electrolytes. Within this context, polyanion compounds, such as phosphates, silicates, and borates, have emerged as a pedagogically rich and technologically versatile class of materials. Polyanion-based compounds offer high redox voltages, exceptional thermal and chemical robustness, and a plethora of crystallographic chemistries that permit rational tuning of Mg 2+ migration pathways. This Review surveys polyanion-based positive electrodes and solid electrolytes for rechargeable magnesium batteries, with emphasis on computational prediction, mechanistic elucidation, synthetic methodology, advanced structural and spectroscopic characterisation, and the prospects for all- solid-state magnesium batteries capable of operating under high‑temperature conditions.

papers.title: Asymmetric Alkene Isomerization Approach to C4-Substituted Piperidines
papers.abstract: Chiral C4-substituted piperidines are prominent motifs in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and alkaloid natural products, yet broadly applicable strategies for their asymmetric synthesis and diversification remain underdeveloped. Here we report a catalytic enantioselective alkene-isomerization platform that converts readily accessible C4-substituted tetrahydropyridines into enantioenriched cyclic enamines and enamides. In this Rh-catalyzed process, positional migration of the alkene simultaneously establishes the C4 stereogenic center and generates a polarized enamine or enamide handle for downstream functionalization. The method accommodates diverse C4 substituents, including primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl groups as well as aryl, heteroaryl, alkenyl, alkynyl, ester, carboxylic acid, and fluorinated motifs, delivering products in high yields and enantioselectivities. The resulting chiral enamines and enamides are versatile linchpins for the synthesis of 2,4-, 3,4-, and 2,3,4-substituted piperidines, bicyclic and polycyclic nitrogen heterocycles, medium-ring azepines, and acyclic stereodefined amide derivatives through regio- and stereoselective functionalization, cycloaddition, ring-expansion, and deconstructive transformations. Mechanistic studies support a Rh(I)-catalyzed and nitrogen lone pair-assisted hydride-transfer pathway. In this mechanism, enantioinduction originates from formation of a chiral catalyst–substrate complex, while the rate-limiting step involves rotation of the piperidine ring around the Rh(I)–C(allylic) bond. Overall, this work establishes asymmetric alkene isomerization of cyclic allylamines as a direct and modular entry to stereochemically rich C4-substituted piperidine architectures.

papers.title: Intrinsic Irreducible-Cartesian Tensor Carrier for Equivariant Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Equivariant interatomic potentials need compact angular features, while many physical observables and long-range sources are Cartesian tensors. We introduce the intrinsic irreducible-Cartesian tensor carrier (ICTC), which builds harmonic polynomial bases and intertwiners in Cartesian algebra but stores features and contraction legs directly in the irreducible 2l+1-dimensional carrier, avoiding the ambient 3^l tensor layout. A degree-wise orthogonal bridge maps ICTC to the real-spherical convention of MACE, so supported pretrained checkpoints run in ICTC coordinates and reproduce energies and forces to floating-point tolerance over 10,000-step double-precision trajectories. Fused ICTC tensor products remove the high-degree Cartesian-3j bottleneck and remain competitive with optimized spherical kernels, while matched benchmarks show faster convergence on revised MD17, liquid water, and a Materials Project trajectory subset. The same carriers emit Cartesian long-range sources, from electrostatic multipoles to a degree-2 rank-two polarizability for eigensolver-free anisotropic many-body dispersion (MBD), deployed in a production molecular-dynamics engine.

papers.title: Nanoscale Strain-Engineering Controls Hydrogen Reactivity in Nanoparticle Catalysts
authors: Jessi E. S. van der Hoeven
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle catalysts empower clean and energy-efficient chemical production, with their performance traditionally tuned through particle size, composition, and support interactions. Lattice strain has emerged as an additional handle to control catalytic reactivity, yet its experimental implementation in thermal catalysis has remained limited due to the lack of robust, strain-controlled materials. Here, we demonstrate the power of strain-engineering in nanoparticle catalysts for thermally-driven hydrogenation catalysis combining experiment and theory. Using a model system of Pt-shell Au 1-x Cu x -core nanoparticles, we systematically tune surface lattice strain from −3.5% compressive to +2.1% tensile. Catalytic evaluation in the hydrogen–deuterium exchange reaction reveals a direct relationship between lattice strain and hydrogen reactivity. Increasing tensile strain enhances the HD exchange reaction rate by a factor 6 through more facile hydrogen displacement at the nanoparticle surface. Our results establish lattice strain as a powerful and experimentally accessible design parameter for performance control of nanoparticle catalysts in thermal catalysis.

papers.title: Optimizing the Thermoelectric Performance of the Earth-Abundant Layered Phosphide BaCuP through Defect Engineering
papers.abstract: Thermoelectric materials offer a direct route for converting waste heat into electricity, but the discovery of efficient, sustainable, and non-toxic compounds remains a major challenge. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric potential of the layered 1-1-1 phosphide BaCuP using a combination of hybrid density functional theory, defect calculations, Boltzmann carrier transport theory, and machine-learning assisted lattice thermal conductivity simulations. The electronic structure reveals a small indirect band gap of 0.19 eV and strongly anisotropic valence-band dispersion, arising from Cu–P derived states, which favours in-plane hole transport. Defect calculations show that BaCuP is intrinsically strongly p-type due to the very low formation energy of copper vacancies under Cu-poor conditions, yielding high hole concentrations. We further assess K and La doping as routes to tune the carrier concentration, and find that La doping is particularly promising because it slightly reduces the intrinsic hole concentration toward the optimum range for thermoelectric performance. To accurately describe phonon transport, we train a machine-learning interatomic potential and use homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, which captures higher-order anharmonic effects beyond conventional third-order approaches. BaCuP is predicted to exhibit a lower lattice thermal conductivity relative to CaCuP due to the heavier Ba. Combining the electronic and thermal transport properties, we predict a peak directionally averaged figure of merit zT of about 0.65 at 800 K in La-doped BaCuP, with in-plane values approaching 1 but hindered by the out-of-plane direction. Additional reductions in lattice thermal conductivity through heavy nanostructuring could further increase the average zT beyond 0.8, highlighting BaCuP as a promising phosphide thermoelectric.

papers.title: Zinc-Air Micro-batteries in Tear Fluid for Contact Lens Electronics
papers.abstract: Contact lenses are emerging as a promising platform for wearable electronics, but the design and scaling of power sources remain important considerations due to constraints in size, biocompatibility, and limits on thermal dissipation. Herein, we investigate the use of zinc-air microbatteries operating in tear fluid for the first time, using form factors relevant to contact lens electronics. A three-slab heat transfer model is used to estimate allowable power dissipation based on the temperature rise at the lens-sclera interface. The model indicates that allowable device power is governed by heat transfer to ambient air and into the eye interior, providing a design rule for limiting thermal dissipation. Experimentally, single stack devices with cathode/anode dimensions ranging from 200 × 200 µm 2 to 2000 × 2000 µm 2 were clean-room fabricated and characterized in simulated human tear fluid. We measure open-circuit voltages of approximately 1.0 V and areal power densities between 0.02 and 0.06 mW/cm 2 , within the limits of safe operation at the corneal surface. We find considerable variability in the maximum power density across batteries with different lateral dimensions, suggesting that factors arising from the fabrication conditions limit the discharge rate. In total, these results provide conservative thermal design criteria for evaluating allowable power dissipation near the ocular surface, and support zinc-air microbatteries as a contact lens-relevant power source.

papers.title: TEMPO+-catalyzed electrochemical α-oxyamination of β-ketoester through an outer-sphere electron transfer: kinetics, mechanism and green chemistry
papers.abstract: We report an electrocatalytic synthesis for α-oxyamination of β-ketoesters employing TEMPO+ as an electrocatalyst, while TEMPO served as a substrate in a three-electrode system consisting of a platinum mesh electrode as the working electrode in a mild reaction condition of only 0.5 V vs Ag/Ag+ in NH4PF6 supporting electrolyte and acetonitrile solvent without the addition of any base. Seventeen diverse examples have been provided, and most of the syntheses were accomplished with more than 80% isolated yield in just 45 min. Massive 1.31 and 1.56 V overpotentials lowering (equivalent to 30.2 and 36.0 kcal/mol energy) have been observed for the activation of the α-CH proton of a model β-ketoester and for a β-ketoester having an electron-withdrawing group (-CF3), respectively, through the electrocatalytic reaction developed herein. Employing spectroelectrochemistry, pseudo-1st-order rate constants were determined by varying solvents and electrolytes. The yields of the reactions were found to be correlated with rate constants. Moreover, higher diffusion coefficients of TEMPO/TEMPO+ in different solvents and higher ion conductances of electrolytes in the same solvent resulted in higher yields/rate constants. Based on cyclic voltammetry, spectroelectrochemistry and kinetic isotope effect studies, an outer-sphere one-electron transfer mechanism has been proposed, wherein TEMPO+ oxidized β-ketoester through one electron transfer to generate a radical cation, which thereafter lost a H+ to generate a radical species. After that, the radical species coupled with TEMPO to complete the synthesis of α-oxyaminated β-ketoester. As a synthesis application, α-oxyaminated product was converted to quinoxaline using 1,2-benzenediamine.

papers.title: A modular skill and orchestration framework for traceable agentic computational chemistry
papers.abstract: Large-language-model agents can now operate the software of computational chemistry, but how their science compares with the answers human experts produced remains untested. Here we present AI Computational Chemist (AICC), a modular skill framework that equips general-purpose agents for computational research: tool-agnostic scientific knowledge, per-code operational skills and orchestration procedures over a machine-readable control plane. We compared an autonomous GPT-5.5 agent, a reference-informed follow-up and the authors’ published computational-content extracts on real referees’ requests from Nature Communications papers, under a fixed document-level rubric executed by two LLM evaluators. The autonomous agent received mean scores of 64.8 and 65.5 of 100, against 72.6 and 54.7 for the published extracts; after one round of human follow-up steering, the same agent scored 69.8 and 72.2. The relative ranking is evaluator-dependent and strongly influenced by differences in documentation completeness. Agent reports scored consistently well on execution reporting and transparency; their principal weaknesses were interpreting reviewer intent and selecting an adequate computational scale.

papers.title: Antibacterial Activity of Metal-Free Bipyridines: Vinylpyridine versus Methyl Substituents
papers.abstract: In this work, we report that incorporating a vinylpyridine arm into 4,4′-dimethyl-2,2′-bipyridine ( L1 ) significantly enhances antibacterial potency against both Gram-positive ( B. subtilis , S. epidermidis , S. aureus ) and Gram-negative ( S. enterica , E. coli ) pathogens. The metal-free vinylpyridine-bipyridine ligand ( L2 ) demonstrates excellent activity with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) values as low as 7 μg mL -1 (for S. epidermidis ), with favorable biocompatibility and negligible cytotoxicity toward human cells up to 200 µg/mL. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and molecular mechanics – Poisson Boltzmann surface area (MM–PBSA) free-energy calculations against two protein targets: 2w6o (for E. coli ) and 3hsb (for B. subtilis ) reveal that the planar π-extended vinylpyridine arm of L2 enables van der Waals, π–alkyl, and hydrogen-bonding interactions with bacterial protein targets. Among the two targets, the 3hsb binding pocket, characterized by aromatic and polar residues, affords the most stable L2 −3hsb complex, with a binding free energy of −16.2 kcal mol -1 . The homoleptic iron(II)-polypyridyl complexes ( MC1 and MC2 ) substantially reduce the antibacterial activity of corresponding free ligands ( L1 and L2 ), highlighting that metal coordination can suppress the intrinsic antibacterial activity of the parent scaffolds. Contrary to the commonly reported enhancement of antibacterial activity upon metal complexation, present results suggest that careful structural tuning or functionalization of polypyridine ligands can afford antibacterial activity under metal-free conditions.

papers.title: Atomically precise metal nanoclusters in nitrate-to-ammonia electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Driven by the growing need for sustainable ammonia production and effective nitrate remediation, the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has emerged as a promising technology. This process enables the conversion of nitrate pollutants into ammonia under mild operating conditions, offering a greener alternative to the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch route. However, the complex multi-electron and multi-proton transfer pathways involved in NO3RR require catalysts capable of precisely regulating intermediate adsorption, activation, and transformation. Atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs), with their well-defined atomic structures, tunable electronic properties, and identifiable active sites, have recently attracted considerable attention as model catalysts for elucidating structure–activity relationships. This review discusses the fundamental aspects of NO3RR, including key intermediates and reaction mechanisms, and summarizes recent advances in the use of atomically precise metal NCs for nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. The catalytic performances of mono-, bi-, and trimetallic NCs are systematically compared, highlighting the roles of active-site engineering, ligand modulation, heterometal incorporation, and cluster assembly in regulating activity and selectivity. The review concludes by discussing the key challenges that remain in this field and highlighting future research directions toward the development of NC-based electrocatalysts with enhanced activity, selectivity, and long-term stability for sustainable ammonia production.

papers.title: Proteomics as an Emerging Tool for Understanding Biotransformation and Toxicological Impacts of Contaminants
papers.abstract: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics is rapidly advancing, becoming fast, affordable, and increasingly accessible to environmental scientists. This perspective outlines how proteomics can illuminate biotransformation processes and sublethal organism-level effects, and highlights future opportunities enabled by emerging technologies. Our goal is to give a concise overview on realistic expectations of current capabilities while inspiring scientists to adapt and develop novel proteomic approaches addressing fundamental questions in contaminant science.

papers.title: Metagenomics and Machine Learning for Per-and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS): A Review of Convergent Approaches, 2020–2025
papers.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, mobile, and toxic contaminants whose carbon–fluorine bonds resist conventional remediation. Two computational-experimental fields have grown rapidly and begun to converge on the problem: environmental metagenomics, which characterizes the microbial communities and enzymes capable of transforming fluorinated compounds, and machine learning (ML), which predicts PFAS toxicity, environmental fate, biodegradation potential, and enzyme function. This review synthesizes 97 works published between 2020 and 2025, identified through a structured search of OpenAlex, PubMed, and arXiv and thematically coded by relevance. We find that the strict intersection—studies that jointly apply metagenomic and ML methods to PFAS—remains small (19 works) but is expanding faster than either feeder literature, driven by defluorinating-enzyme discovery, protein structure prediction (notably AlphaFold2-guided analysis of reductive dehalogenases), ML-guided design of synthetic microbial communities, and multi-omics integration. We organize the field into microbial degradation discovery, defluorination enzymology, community profiling, ML-based toxicity/fate/occurrence prediction, and integrative pipelines; summarize the dominant ML methods; and identify the principal barriers to progress: scarce and heterogeneous labeled data, incomplete functional annotation of fluorine-active enzymes, limited external validation, and the gap between in-silico prediction and experimental confirmation. We conclude that metagenomics and ML are complementary rather than competing tools, and that closing the design–build–test loop between genome-resolved discovery and predictive modeling is the field’s most promising near-term direction.

papers.title: RESEARCH ARTICLE Fast Isotopic [18F]Fluoride Exchange in Iminosulfur Oxydifluorides and Triflimidoyl Fluorides: A novel approach for [18F]tagging of primary amine-derived precursors
papers.abstract: Direct incorporation of fluorine-18 into primary amine- derived molecules remains a major challenge in radiochemistry. Current strategies largely rely on multistep conjugation of electrophilic prosthetic groups, limiting automation and generating significant waste. Herein, we report a general and ultrafast 19 F- 18 F isotopic exchange on iminosulfur oxydifluorides and triflimidoyl fluorides, two Sulfur-Fluorine exchange (SuFEx) derived motifs readily accessible from primary amines. The reaction proceeds within seconds and tolerates a broad range of functionalities. Additionally, the method was successfully automated on commercial modules, and radiolabelled molecules were isolated through simple cartridge purification, with high molar activity, further highlighting the potential of this methodology for streamlined and more sustainable radiotracer production. Finally, we carried out chemical and biological stability studies showing that [ 18 F]iminosulfur oxydifluorides resist in vivo metabolism and can be employed as radiolabelled synthons for PET imaging.

papers.title: A Novel Approach for Monitoring The Spatial Distribution and Quantitative Analysis of Micronutrients in Plant Tissues Using Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry Imaging
papers.abstract: Quantitative imaging of plant tissues by laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) is hindered by the lack of matrix-matched calibration standards. Established approaches, such as gelatine or homogenized tissue blocks, do not replicate plant matrices accurately. Here, we introduce a nano-dispenser-based calibration strategy that deposits nanolitre volumes of elemental standards directly onto paraffin-embedded grain sections, exploiting the low endogenous metal content of the endosperm to generate in situ calibration curves. Calibration performance for Mg, Mn, Cu, Zn and Mo was assessed using LA-ICP-MS imaging and Iolite data processing. The method demonstrated excellent linearity (R2 > 0.98), reproducibility across multiple grains, and sub-ppm limits of detection. Comparative analysis with in-house homogenized blocks and NIST wheat reference material confirmed superior accuracy and reproducibility of the nano-dispenser approach. As a proof-of-concept we have applied the method for the quantitative imaging of metals in a whole barley grain section and the results show excellent agreement with published data obtained by conventional liquid-mode ICP MS. The technique reported here provides a robust, scalable solution for quantitative metallomics studies of plants tissues, enabling improved assessment of nutrient distribution and supporting the development of standardised protocols for LA-ICP-MS Imaging

papers.title: Spin Magnetoreception Through Redox-Active Residues and Nucleotides
papers.abstract: The radical pair mechanism explains how low-intensity magnetic fields influence the coherent singlet–triplet interconversion of spin-correlated radical pairs formed by electron transfer in photoredox-active biological chromophores. Although this mechanism has primarily been studied in the context of avian magnetoreception, electron-transfer processes in other biological systems should, in principle, also be magnetosensitive. Here, we determine the maximum magnetic field e!ect (MFE) on radical pairs formed by residues within proteins, and by nucleobases within genetic material, to be similar to those formed by flavin-based complexes in cryptochrome. We calculate the contribution of Zeeman and hyperfine couplings to the overall spin Hamiltonian in each donor and acceptor species, and find the optimal reaction rates by solving the Liouvillespace master equation for propagation of spins. We present the MARY (Magnetically Altered Reaction Yield) curves for each radical pair, revealing that the highest magnetosensitivity consistently occurs in the 0.2–0.6 mT range. Variations in the earth’s magnetic field itself can alter the forward reaction rates in these radical pairs by 1-3%, biasing redox reactions to favor triplet product formation. We provide an open-source program, MagnetoSimmer, for screening biological electron transfer reactions for vulnerability to environmental magnetic fields. Our work suggests that magnetosensitivity is an intrinsic property of redox reactions in proteins and genes.

papers.title: MARS-RNA: An Automated Pipeline for Correlating RNA Molecular Dynamics Trajectories with Chemical Probing Data
papers.abstract: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules fold into complex, highly dynamic three-dimensional conformational structures that govern their biological activities. Chemical probing methods, such as SHAPE (selective 2’-hydroxyl acylation analyzed by primer extension), provide structural insights in the form of one-dimensional (1D) nucleotide reactivity profiles. However, mapping these one-dimensional profiles back to the underlying dynamic structures remains a key challenge, as traditional analyses rely on a static view based on three-dimensional (3D) high-resolution structures from X-ray crystallography or NMR, rather than accounting for the dynamic nature of the system. In this Application Note, we introduce MARS-RNA (MD Analysis for Reactivity and Structure), an automated pipeline that extracts and integrates multi-scale structural and geometric features from RNA Molecular Dynamics (MD) trajectories, combining them with secondary (2D) and 3D annotations from X3DNA-DSSR to identify features that correlate with experimental reactivity. MARS-RNA processes raw GROMACS trajectories, performs frame-by-frame structural annotation, calculates spatial centroids and physical distance fluctuations, computes Pearson/Spearman correlation coefficients against SHAPE data, and pre-processes results for machine learning pipelines. We show its value on the RNA 3′-UTR (PDB ID: 1AUD, chain A), by highlighting several single correlation with SHAPE reactivity.

papers.title: Excited state dynamics of an air-stable low-spin carbene manganese(III) dual charge transfer chromophore
papers.abstract: We report synthesis, structure and properties of a N-heterocyclic carbene pyridine manganese(III) complex featuring a low-spin ground state. The complex exhibits excellent stability under ambient conditions in the solid state and even dissolved in water. The low-spin ground state is characterized by a large zerofield splitting according to temperature-dependent magnetic susceptbility measurements. Spectroscopic and quantum chemical studies demonstrate that multiple electronic transitions of distinct character are concentrated within a broad absorption band in the visible spectral region. Excitation at various energies across this absorption band and observation of the excited state evolution by ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy deliver excited-state lifetimes on the picosecond timescale. The short excited state lifetimes are attributed to rapid relaxation to the ground state via distorted excited states. These findings offer new insight into the photophysics of manganese(III) complexes and lay a foundation for the development of photoactive manganese(III)-based chromophores.

papers.title: Systematic Investigation of Reaction Parameters and Purification Strategies for DNA-Polymer Conjugates
papers.abstract: DNA-polymer conjugates are an emerging class of biohybrid materials with applications in therapeutics and biosensing, yet quantitative guidelines for optimizing conjugation conversion and purification remain unreported. Here, we systematically investigate the parameters governing the NHS ester-amine coupling of single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) to synthetic polymers and the subsequent purification of these DNA-polymer conjugates. Aqueous-phase size exclusion chromatography was identified as the most reliable method to assess conjugation conversion and purification efficacy. Using this approach, we found increases in concentration, pH, and the ratio of polymer to ssDNA consistently improved conjugation conversion, while increasing the molar mass of either starting material decreased conversion. Subtle differences in ssDNA sequence were also found to affect conjugation efficiency. In both low-throughput chromatographic and high-throughput spin column purification settings, anion exchange achieved higher purity than all other techniques, though with reduced material recovery. Together, these findings provide a practical framework for reproducible coupling of chemically diverse macromolecules, with broad implications for the development of oligonucleotide therapeutics and biosensors.

papers.title: Spin-Resolved Dielectric Bath Embedding Theory for Metallic Surfaces
papers.abstract: We introduce spin-resolved dielectric bath embedding theory (SR-DBET), which incorporates a physics-informed embedding potential to describe attractive and repulsive interactions, a charge dielectric bath to capture charge polarization, and a spin dielectric bath to account for spin density fluctuations. We demonstrate the accuracy of SR-DBET through adsorption energy calculations on Cu surfaces. This embedding scheme is essential for extending embedded correlated wavefunction theory to spin-polarized quantum systems.

papers.title: VPT2 Meets MLPs: IR and Raman Spectroscopy of Eight Molecules, Including 74-Atom Cholesterol, Using MACE-OFF and MACE-MDP
papers.abstract: Vibrational second order perturbation theory is a widely used method to perform post-harmonic calculations of vibrational energies and infrared (IR) and Raman spectroscopy. We recently reported an application of this approach for vibrational energies using Fortran and Python software with machine-learned potentials, with an application to 21-atom aspirin. Here we report extensions and applications to perform the calculations of IR and Raman spectroscopy. Applications are made to six molecules, with up to 31 atoms, considered in a recent paper by Kapil and co-workers using MACE-based software for the MLP (MACE-OFF) and dipole moment/polarizability (MACE-MDP) to perform double-harmonic calculations of IR and Raman spectra. Large differences are seen between those and the VPT2 spectra for XH-stretch fundamentals, and comparisons with experimental IR spectra show significant improvement of the VPT2 spectra over the double-harmonic calculations. The extendability of the new software is demonstrated for 74-atom cholesterol using MACE software. The strength and weakness of the VPT2 approach is shown for the IR spectrum of the formic acid dimer, using our PIP potential and dipole moment surface.

papers.title: A Wearable Multimodal Platform for Monitoring Plant Heat Stress via Leaf VOCs and Relative Humidity
papers.abstract: Heat stress limits plant productivity by disrupting transpiration, altering leaf microclimate, and activating metabolic pathways that increase volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions. VOC signatures, combined with leaf-level relative humidity (RH), provide early indicators of plant stress, but conventional analytical methods are costly, bulky, and unsuitable for continuous in situ monitoring. Here, a low-cost multimodal sensing platform based on laser-induced graphene (LIG) is reported for real-time, on-leaf detection of methanol, acetic acid, and RH under ambient conditions. The platform integrates Pt-modified LIG electrodes with PtNP/ZnONR@ZIF-8 for methanol, PtNP/ZnONR@ZIF-8/Sn3O4 for acetic acid and GO:PDMAA for RH sensing. After optimization, the sensors respectively achieved sensitivities of −75.83 Ω/log(ppm), −1.63 Ω/ppm, and −4,776.01 Ω/%RH with detection limits of 0.382 ppm, 0.318 ppm, and 1.53 %RH and more than 97% signal retention over 26 days. On-leaf measurements over 2 weeks showed methanol increasing from ~0.3–13.8 ppm to ~13.5–59.0 ppm, acetic acid from ~6.6–14.8 ppm to ~23.3–60.6 ppm, and RH decreasing from ~72.2–86.3% to ~52.5–65.1% under heat stress. These coupled chemical and microclimate changes provide direct, dynamic stress readouts during plant monitoring. By moving beyond single-analyte measurements, the proposed multimodal approach enables early stress detection, data-driven crop management, and next-generation precision agriculture applications.

papers.title: The effect of Pt concentration on lean methane oxidation over Pd-Pt/CeO2 catalysts depends on ceria faceting
papers.abstract: Pd:Pt/CeO 2 catalysts supported on shape-controlled CeO 2 nanorods and nanocubes were investigated for lean methane oxidation to determine how Pt substitution and support morphology affect activity, stability, water inhibition, and redox behavior. Nanocube-supported catalysts showed higher methane oxidation activity than nanorod-supported catalysts despite their lower surface area, indicating that intrinsic redox properties and noble metal–CeO 2 interactions are more important than total surface area. Pt substitution improved performance in a morphology-dependent manner, with the best-performing composition shifting from 1:1 Pd:Pt for nanorods to 6:1 Pd:Pt for nanocubes. Water strongly inhibited all catalysts, increasing the apparent activation barriers; however, Pt addition made the H 2 O reaction orders less negative, suggesting improved tolerance toward water-derived surface species. HRTEM, HAADF-STEM, and in situ NAP-XPS indicate that deactivation is not mainly caused by support morphology loss, extensive noble-metal sintering, or carbon deposition. Instead, CH 4 -TPR and NAP-XPS suggest that deactivation is linked to reversible changes in Pd, Pt, and Ce oxidation states, surface hydroxylation, and the accessibility of interfacial oxygen species. Overall, the best performance results from balancing highly active PdO x –CeO 2 sites with the stabilizing and water-tolerance effects introduced by Pt.

papers.title: Ruthenium-Catalyzed N-Dealkylation of Aromatic Amines
papers.abstract: In industrial organic chemistry, amines and N-alkylamines represent crucial intermediates. Conversely, N-methyl amines are undesirable byproducts of recycling processes of polyamides or polyurethanes that involve methanolysis or hydrogenolysis steps. Therefore, there is growing interest in creating novel and effective synthesis techniques for the elimination of alkyl groups in these compounds. Therefore, we report an efficient Ndealkylation system of secondary and tertiary aromatic amines using ruthenium-based Shvo-type catalysts. Notably, this novel methodology avoids the use of stoichiometric oxidants of established methods such as peroxides or molecular oxygen and enables a new synthetic pathway for the synthesis of secondary and primary amines with good to excellent selectivity.

papers.title: CACHE Challenge #4: Targeting the TKB Domain of the E3 ligase CBLB, an Immuno-Oncology Target
papers.abstract: The Critical Assessments of Computational Hit-finding Experiments (CACHE) are prospective benchmarking exercises where small molecule ligands predicted for a nominated protein of interest are procured and tested experimentally. In CACHE #4, 23 participating teams each selected up to 100 compounds designed to bind the E3 ligase CBLB, an immuno-oncology target. The organizers released the first public structure of CBLB in complex with a known ligand at the outset of the challenge to enable the discovery of chemically novel molecules. Out of the 1,688 compounds collectively predicted, ten compounds from nine participants showed some sign of activity (primary hits), but only two were convincingly confirmed (validated hits) across multiple biophysical binding assays and in subsequent analogs, and only one of them was chemically novel. The apparent difficulty of finding novel CBLB ligands, previously reflected by the chemical similarity of inhibitors from the patent literature, suggests that potent CBLB hit molecules were either rare in the screened commercial libraries, or that computational methods may have struggled to retrieve presumably present but weak ligands, or that the conformational dynamics of the binding site was not sufficiently accounted for. The successful method was strikingly atypical. Selection from a chemical binding similarity classifier followed by a Random Forest binding affinity predictor trained on inhibitors from the patent literature were refined using a diffusion-model binding pose predictor. The road to an ML-driven breakthrough in computational hit-finding can take unexpected turns. Which of these turns reveal novel horizons and which are mere distractions will best be investigated and answered collectively. The discovery in CACHE #4 of a novel series of CBLB ligands is not a trivial achievement and may inform medicinal chemistry efforts towards clinical candidates that complement immune checkpoint inhibition to elicit antitumor immune response in cancer patients.

papers.title: Single-Molecule Fluorescence Reveals Catalytic Heterogeneity and Active Species in Copper Nanocatalyzed Click Reactions
papers.abstract: The copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) is a cornerstone of click chemistry and has been widely employed in many applications. However, its mechanism with heterogeneous catalysts remains incompletely understood. Catalytic reactions mediated by metal nanoparticles may occur on the nanoparticle surface via a heterogeneous catalysis pathway and/or through metal ion leaching that leads to a homogeneous reaction pathway. In this work, we developed a novel fluorogenic CuAAC reaction based on a naphthalimide probe that enables single-molecule visualization using total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy. This approach allows direct observation of catalytic turnover events on individual copper nanoparticles (Cu NPs) with high spatial and temporal resolution. Analysis of single-molecule trajectories revealed catalytic heterogeneity and provided kinetic insights, both inaccessible in ensemble measurements. The reaction kinetics followed a Langmuir–Hinshelwood model with noncompetitive adsorption, indicating that the azide and alkyne substrates occupy distinct active sites on the nanoparticle surface. Comparison between single-molecule and ensemble rates suggested that both heterogeneous and homogeneous reaction pathways contribute to the Cu NP-catalyzed reactions. These findings elucidate structure–activity relationships and mechanistic pathways in Cu NP-catalyzed CuAAC, offering guidance for the rational design of improved heterogeneous click catalysts.

papers.title: Programming Electrocatalytic Alkene Epoxidation via Potentiodynamic Control of Surface Oxygen
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic alkene epoxidation offers an attractive route to epoxides using water as an oxygen source at near ambient conditions, but direct electrochemical strategies often suffer from low selectivity and limited catalytic activity. Here, we demonstrate that programmable electrochemical operation can accelerate hexene epoxidation on gold by controlling the time-dependent coverage of surface oxygen. Oscillating the applied potential between -0.6 and 1.1 V Fc/Fc+ at frequencies from 10 -3 to 10 -1 Hz, increased the rate of electrochemical hexene epoxidation on gold by up to 20x relative to potentiostatic operation. In the absence of potential oscillation at steady state, the Au surface was primarily saturated with oxygen adsorbates derived from electrochemical water oxidation. Although these adsorbates are required for epoxidation, excessive surface oxygen coverage limits productive hexene interaction with the surface. Potentiodynamic operation lowered the time-averaged oxygen coverage to sub monolayer values, increasing the availability of sites for hexene and accelerated the macroscopic rate of epoxidation. This dynamically programmed surface state accelerated epoxide formation without compromising selectivity, with Faradaic efficiencies reaching approximately 20% at 0.5 M hexene. Hydrodynamic measurements further showed that epoxidation is coupled to interfacial transport, indicating that near surface hexene availability influenced the observed rate in addition to surface oxygen dynamics. Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that dynamic electrochemical operation can program surface coverages to enhance electrocatalytic alkene epoxidation by more than an order of magnitude without sacrificing Faradaic efficiency.

papers.title: Infrared analysis suitable for high-throughput detection of keratin film formation from sheep wool material
papers.abstract: Sheep wool represents an abundant and underutilized bioresource, primarily composed of keratin, with significant potential for the development of sustainable biomaterials. In this study, the formation of keratin films from wool was investigated using a combination of mechanical processing and ATR-FTIR-spectroscopy. A total of 585 ATR spectra were collected from raw wool sheets, dry-pressed and wet-pressed samples, among these 74 spectra were identified visually by colour and hardness as films. The results show that mechanical treatment, particularly in the presence of moisture, promotes keratin reorganization and film formation. ATR analysis identified characteristic amide bands and structural changes toward β-sheet rich conformations associated with film stability. Collected data was used to train Random Forest machine learning models, yielding high accuracy range from 0.95 to 0.97, with Cohen’s κ values between 0.74 and 0.84. Current results demonstrate infrared analysis potential as a complementary tool for automated analysis of keratin film formation in complex materials.

papers.title: Systematic Benchmarking Dataset Generation for Graphical Model Reaction Templates
papers.abstract: Computational kinetic modeling relies on accurate transition-state geometries and activation barriers. While machine learning models trained on ab initio data have shown promise for transition-state search and barrier prediction, they often struggle to generalize to out-ofdomain reactions due to biases and uneven coverage of reaction space in existing datasets. To address this challenge, we introduce a dataset of 12,030 actual reactions (ARs) derived from 452 model reactions (MRs), which are sampled from an extensive, heuristic-free, graph-based reaction template database. The dataset includes DFT-optimized transition-state geometries and thermochemistries and is designed to improve model transferability by systematically expanding chemically relevant reaction space around shared reactive cores. We also provide an automated workflow to generate this dataset, enabling broader use and extension by the community. Finally, we benchmark MR activation barriers as surrogates for AR barriers and present a case study demonstrating that AR augmentation improves machine-learning performance, highlighting the value of structured reaction-space expansion for kinetic modeling.

papers.title: Switching Reactivity with Light: C–P Bonding Controls Singlet Oxygen Generation and Reactivity in DHP–CPD Photoswitches
papers.abstract: The dimethyldihydropyrene photochromic system is a 14π-electronic framework that switches to a lessaromatic non-planar system with visible light. In this work we unravel a neutral phosphorus heteroatom-appended dimethyldihydropyrene (DHP) photoswitchable system which acts as a self-sensitizer, enabling precise, wavelength-selective control over singlet oxygen capture with dual reactivity. The attachment of the phosphorus directly to the DHP scaffold allowed red light (640 nm) to selectively generate a phosphinate intermediate (DHP-2), while green light (525 nm) triggers further transformation into an endoperoxide. The dual reactivity can thus be selected easily by the choice of the appropriate wavelength of light. The formation of the photoproducts also displayed dependence on the DHP-1 concentration. Thus, this work establishes a unified approach to engineering singlet oxygen generation, wavelength-selective fixation, and the release of singlet oxygen within a single molecular scaffold.

papers.title: A Machine Learning QSAR Model for Predicting hTERT Telomerase Inhibitor Potency: ChEMBL Dataset Curation, Algorithm Benchmarking, and Prospective Application to Natural and Synthetic Anticancer Compounds
papers.abstract: Human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) is reactivated in approximately 85–90% of human cancers, establishing it as one of the most broadly expressed oncological drug targets; yet no quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) model trained on curated experimental bioactivity data has been reported specifically for hTERT inhibitor potency prediction. Here, we curate a target-wide hTERT IC50 dataset from ChEMBL (CHEMBL2916; 616 unique compounds, pIC50 range 4.03–8.34) and benchmark five regression algorithms across three molecular feature representations: Morgan circular fingerprints (ECFP4), RDKit physicochemical descriptors, and their union, for predicting hTERT inhibitory potency. An XGBoost model trained on the combined feature set was selected as the best-performing architecture (cross-validated R2 = 0.549± 0.081) and validated through nested cross-validation (R2 = 0.508± 0.070), an independent held-out test set (R2 = 0.533; RMSE = 0.507 log units), and a y-scrambling permutation test (p = 0.020), confirming a genuine and statistically significant structure-activity relationship. Permutation-importance analysis revealed that potency is driven predominantly by lipophilic and polarizable surface-area descriptors (SlogP VSA10, PEOE VSA10, SMR VSA7), consistent with the hydrophobic character of the hTERT thumb-domain binding pocket. The model was applied prospectively to six structurally diverse inhibitors spanning four compound classes: BIBR1532, zidovudine (AZT), raltitrexed, allicin, EGCG, and quercetin, with applicability-domain analysis based on maximum Tanimoto similarity to the training set. Among in-domain compounds, quercetin (pIC50 = 5.74) and zidovudine (5.12) achieved the most balanced profiles of predicted potency and drug-likeness. Physicochemical profiling using QED scores and Lipinski/Veber criteria identified BIBR1532 as the most developable compound (QED = 0.688; zero Lipinski violations), whereas EGCG ranked lowest (QED = 0.212; two Lipinski violations). Jointly interpreting predicted potency, applicability-domain status, and physicochemical developability reveals that raw potency rankings alone are misleading for this target, and that an integrated computational framework is necessary for reliable inhibitor prioritization. These findings provide the first validated QSAR baseline for hTERT and complement physics-based docking and molecular dynamics analyses of these compounds reported in a companion study.

papers.title: Inverse theoretical spectroscopy via Monte Carlo sampling: From spectra to ensembles of molecular structures
papers.abstract: A molecule’s structure determines its spectroscopic properties, and vice versa, molecular spectra are indispensable for elucidating its three-dimensional structure. Here, we present a Monte Carlo sampling scheme for generating an ensemble of molecular structures that is compatible with an ensemble of spectra around a given reference spectrum. By analyzing this spectrally-constrained ensemble, we can determine which structural changes are compatible with the given reference spectrum. By constraining the spectrum only in selected windows, a more fine-grained analysis of selected spectral features becomes possible. We explore our spectral Monte Carlo sampling method for the dye molecule DFHBI, considering its electronic excitation spectrum. We find that the conformational space of molecular structures with similar spectra is vast, and we identify high-energy distorted structures whose spectra closely match that of the ground-state structure. Our method provides a novel, ensemble-based perspective on the inverse mapping from spectra to molecular structures.

papers.title: β-Stereoselective Glycosylation without Acyl Participation: Evaluation of β-(1→2)-Linked Disaccharide Donors and Their Application to Glycoarray Design for Antibody Characterization
papers.abstract: β-(1→2)-Glucans constitute a relatively rare and substantially underexplored class of polysaccharides.
