Of particular interest is the macrocyclic β-(1→2)-glucan from Brucella (CβG), which regarded as a promising diagnostic marker of brucellosis. However, the development of CβG-based diagnostic system requires careful consideration of potential interference from short β-(1→2)-linked gluco-oligosaccharides present in various bacterial commensals and pathogens. To address this challenge, we performed the stereoselective synthesis of a representative series of trisaccharide antigens bearing di-β-(1→2)-glucoside motifs. Several strategies for β-selective insertion of the di-β-(1→2)-glucoside block were evaluated, including approaches employing picolylated and silylated donors as well as donors lacking stereodirecting groups at C-2. Optimal results were achieved using nonparticipating thioglycoside donors activated by a FeCl 3 /TCCA promoter system in acetonitrile. The method proved to be widely applicable to a range of monosaccharide acceptors, affording the target trisaccharides with excellent β-selectivity. The applicability of prepared oligosaccharides for profiling carbohydrate specificity of antibodies was demonstrated by large-scale screening of human donor sera.

papers.title: GNN-ωPBE: Range-Separation Parameters Learned from Three-Dimensional Structures
papers.abstract: Range-separated hybrid (RSH) functionals improve density functional theory (DFT) modeling of organic semiconducting molecules by reducing self-interaction and delocalization errors, but their accuracy depends critically on the range-separation parameter (ω). Although our previously developed ML-ωPBE functional generates moleculespecific ω values from topology-based descriptors, its applicability is limited for flexible molecules with rich conformational diversity. We introduce GNN-ωPBE, a machine learned RSH functional that generates geometry-specific ω values directly from atomic numbers and three-dimensional (3D) atomic coordinates. Built on a graph neural network (GNN) representation, GNN-ωPBE encodes interatomic interactions through internal coordinates and distinguishes different conformers of the same molecule, enabling it to capture geometry-dependent variations inaccessible to topology-based molecular descriptors. Trained on a conformer-resolved dataset, GNN-ωPBE reproduces benchmark OT-ωPBE with a mean absolute error (MAE) of approximately 0.00760 a−1 0 . Our study advances machine learned density functional development from molecule-specific to geometry-specific modeling of conformational effects in electronic structures.

papers.title: Early Detection and Recovery of SCF Convergence Failures in Automated Quantum Chemistry Workflows via Time-Series Learning
papers.abstract: Self-consistent field (SCF) convergence failures represent a major bottleneck in high-throughput workflows, particularly for open-shell systems and material discovery. To address this challenge, we introduce an autonomous pipeline that treats the electronic structure descriptors from early spin-unrestricted SCF iterations as a time-series problem. Using statistical descriptors extracted from only ten iterations, a lightweight gradient-boosted classifier accurately predicts convergence failures. The model achieves 94.8% accuracy on 55,000 doublet anionic QM9 test molecules after being trained on only 10,000 examples. We then couple this early-warning predictor with restart-based level-shifting interventions derived from Bayesian Optimization of the α- and β-shifting parameters. Across six diverse SCF test sets, our pipeline successfully rescued 53.9% of inherently difficult-to-converge molecules while maintaining a 96.3% convergence rate for easy cases, reducing the total number of iterations across the 1200 calculations by 248,355 steps. Overall, this proof-of-concept demonstrates that treating early SCF iterations as a time-series problem provides a data-efficient active-monitoring layer, which can be paired with various remedies to fine-tune convergence parameters and enable more autonomous, large-scale electronic structure workflows.

papers.title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metals Ordering in Multivariate Metal-Organic Frameworks
Understanding and Reporting PFAS Exposure: Wide-scope Retrospective Suspect Screening of High-resolution Mass Spectrometry Data from Exposomics Studies
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) comprise thousands of persistent and structurally diverse chemicals that contribute to chronic human exposure. Yet, routine biomonitoring targets only a limited set of regulated legacy compounds, underestimating overall exposure. We present a retrospective, wide-scope suspect screening analysis framework to extract PFAS information from archived LC–HRMS exposomics datasets. A curated list of 1,666 PFAS, filtered for reversed-phase LC compatibility and enriched with structural descriptors, predicted retention indices, and MS$ fragments, was used to reprocess two human biomonitoring studies involving firefighter serum pools and population-based plasma samples. Candidate features were prioritized using precursor accuracy, isotopic patterns, and MS2 similarity, followed by spectral quality filtering and retention time-index regression models based on isotopically labeled standards, reinforcing identification confidence. The reanalysis recovered up to 80% of previously reported PFAS while revealing overlooked high-confidence carboxylic, sulfonic, and sulfonamidoacetic acid homologs, and >30 tentative PFAS series, encompassing isomeric clusters (alcohols and ethers) and structurally distinct subclasses (alkylpyrimidine PFAS). The reanalysis framework also revealed shared homolog patterns across exposure contexts. By framing PFAS chemical space and providing a reusable repository of confirmed and tentative structures, this framework reinterprets HRMS biobanked data, improving PFAS pattern assessment.

papers.title: Molecular Motion-Activated Spin-Vibronic Coupling: A Pre-Twisting Design Strategy for Efficient Pure Organic Room Temperature Phosphorescence
papers.abstract: Suppressing molecular motion in the solid state has long been regarded as a golden key for achieving efficient room temperature phosphorescence (RTP), as it minimizes the rates of nonradiative decay and external quenching. Here we demonstrate a counterintuitive principle: specific solid-state molecular motion can serve as a productive driving force for efficient intersystem crossing (ISC) and thereby enhance RTP. Ortho -substituted benzoic acids were employed as model compounds to evaluate the significance of molecular motion in regulating RTP. It is verified that twisting of the carboxylic acid group can activate spin vibronic coupling (SVC)—a second-order coupling mechanism in which vibronic coupling and spin–orbit coupling operate simultaneously—to facilitate ISC and yield more efficient and ultralong RTP. A five-state model was established to elucidate the ISC process and an effective pre-twisting molecular design strategy was proposed for the rational development of high-performance RTP materials. This work reshapes the understanding of molecular motion in the solid state from a universally detrimental factor to a tunable mechanistic lever for triplet harvesting.

papers.title: A Multitask Graph Neural Network Framework for AMES Mutagenicity Prediction
papers.abstract: The long, complex, and costly process of drug development makes early, reliable toxicity assessment a central challenge in pharmaceutical research. Accurately predicting drug-induced toxicity and mutagenicity is crucial for guiding decision-making and reducing late-stage attrition. Deep learning approaches can predict the results of the Ames mutagenicity test, a standard screening method; however, most existing models rely on molecular descriptors that limit structural representation, lack interpretability, and do not account for Ames results of individual bacterial strains. Graph neural networks (GNNs) are chemically intuitive and overcome these limitations. This work presents a deep learning, multitask GNN model for predicting Ames mutagenicity. The proposed approach outperforms existing models, including those from the Ames/QSAR International Challenge. Furthermore, the model is highly interpretable. Explainability analysis of atom-level contributions reveal that the model is capable of learning known structural alerts associated with mutagenicity, along with additional molecular patterns and three-dimensional structural properties. Importantly, these insights are captured in a strain-specific manner, highlighting the value of a multitask approach. Finally, the model is able to identify previously unreported molecular substructures potentially associated with mutagenicity, supporting its utility in drug design and development.

papers.title: Spin Manifolds in the [Fe4S4(SCH3)4]2− Cluster from Localized Active Space State Interaction Singles and Pair-Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Iron–sulfur clusters play central roles in biological photosynthesis, respiration and catalysis. The [Fe4S4(SCH3)4] 2− cluster possesses a dense manifold of low-lying electronic states arising from strong magnetic interactions among the Fe centers, making its electronic structure challenging to describe theoretically. Previous multireference studies have generally optimized excited states individually, while neglecting the interactions among low-lying states. In this work, we investigate the low-lying electronic states of [Fe4S4(SCH3)4]2− using localized active space state interaction singles (LASSIS) combined with pair-density functional theory (PDFT). By treating all states within a common model-space Hamiltonian, LASSIS generates a single set of orthogonal low-lying states. The resulting spin-state energies organize into distinct manifolds. The same overall pattern is obtained for active spaces ranging from 22 electrons in 20 orbitals to 54 electrons in 36 orbitals. To enable these calculations, we also implement GPU acceleration for the most computationally demanding components of the LASSIS workflow.

papers.title: Reprogrammed cobalt–hydride reactivity enables enantioselective alkene hydrosulfenation
papers.abstract: Catalytic enantioselective functionalization of unactivated alkenes is a central strategy for building saturated, three-dimensional molecules, yet accessing aliphatic C(sp3)–S stereocenters remains difficult. Sulfenic acids (RSOH) offer a direct entry to hydrosulfenation products, but their rapid background consumption typically outcompetes addition to ordinary alkenes. Here we report a dual cobalt-cycle strategy that reprograms Co–H reactivity to enable enantioselective hydrosulfenation. Instead of canonical metal–hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) to the alkene, Co–H transfers H• to a sulfinyl radical generated from a succinimide-based sulfinamide, assembling RSOH in situ. The resulting oxidized cobalt species undergoes catalyst metamorphosis and serves as a chiral Lewis-acidic platform that promotes outer-sphere, polar C–S bond formation to furnish sulfur-stereogenic sulfoxides with up to 92% ee across diverse alkene classes. Gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization, and stereoretentive conversion to sulfoximines demonstrate practicality.

papers.title: A Modular and Removable Radical Relay Platform for Remote Side-Chain C–H Editing of Amino Acids
papers.abstract: Site-selective functionalization of inert side-chain C(sp3)–H bonds in amino acids and peptides remains a longstanding challenge owing to the high bond dissociation energies and similar reactivity profiles of multiple aliphatic C–H sites. Herein, we report a modular and removable nitrogen-radical relay strategy for remote side-chain C(sp3)–H functionalization of amino acids. Readily accessible N-acyloxy amide modules are installed through the amino acid carboxyl group and serve as precursors to nitrogen-centered radicals. Under visible-light photoredox conditions, single-electron reduction triggers N–O bond fragmentation to generate nitrogen-centered radicals, which undergo selective intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to activate remote aliphatic C–H bonds and enable subsequent heteroarylation. The directing module can be readily removed under mild conditions, affording synthetically versatile amino acid derivatives. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and applicability to amino acids, peptides, heteroarenes, and complex molecular frameworks. Mechanistic studies indicate that site selectivity is governed primarily by the geometric requirements of the 1,5-HAT process rather than by the thermodynamic stability of the resulting carbon-centered radicals. This work establishes a general platform for remote C–H editing and the synthesis of structurally diverse non-natural amino acids.

papers.title: Dynamic vacancy redistribution shifts Pd nanoparticle coalescence from orientation-gated to defect-enabled on reduced CeO2(110)
papers.abstract: Sintering deactivates supported catalysts, yet how mobile support defects couple to crystallographic transport anisotropy during nanoparticle coalescence remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a ternary Ce–O–Pd machine-learning interatomic potential (Ce–O–Pd MLIP) by fine-tuning a pre-trained large atomic model and validate it against density functional theory (DFT) calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations resolve early-stage coarsening of Pd 62 /Pd 287 nanoparticle pairs on CeO 2–x (110) and reveal direction-selective coalescence: [11̅0]-aligned pairs exhibit higher probabilities and shorter onset times than [001]-aligned pairs. CI-NEB calculations identify complementary transport anisotropies, with Pd adatom diffusion favored along [11̅0] and oxygen-vacancy migration favored along [001], enabling dynamic defect redistribution within the interparticle region. Statistical trajectory analysis shows that increasing the interparticle oxygen-vacancy fraction from 10% to 30% raises coalescence probability and accelerates bridge and neck nucleation, including along the kinetically less favorable [001] alignment. Time-resolved metrics further show that transient low-coordinated bridge-Pd intermediates precede complete particle merging. These results show that dynamic vacancy redistribution couples with anisotropic metal transport to shift nanoparticle coalescence from orientation-gated to defect-enabled, and identify interparticle vacancy enrichment and effective connectivity as kinetic descriptors for defect-mediated structural evolution and stability of oxide-supported nanoparticles.

papers.title: Grounding LLM Reasoning with Digital Modeling for Autonomous Chemical Discovery
papers.abstract: The application of large language models (LLMs) to scientific research has raised growing expectations for autonomous discovery. Although LLMs are capable of scientific reasoning, literature investigation and hypothesis generation, they lack feedback under physical constraints and therefore cannot reliably distinguish effective designs from plausible but invalid hypotheses or hallucinations. Here we develop an agentic system for autonomous covalent organic framework (COF) discovery that builds a closed feedback loop between LLM reasoning and domain-specific digital model (DDM) verification. Using COFid, a structured representation developed in this work to convert COFs into language-compatible scientific objects, the LLM agent identifies Xe/Kr separation as a target problem, designs workflows for LLM-DDM interactions, evolves hypotheses from literature and computational feedback, and retains effective design rules while discarding invalid assumptions. As a proof of concept, the autonomous campaign screened 150 COF candidates and converged toward compact aryl–triazine frameworks with Xe/Kr selectivities exceeding those of previously reported COFs. The discovered design principles reveal that effective Xe/Kr discrimination arises from pore-field matching, where confined yet accessible pore environments amplify the differential stabilization of Xe over Kr. This work establishes an LLM–DDM feedback-loop paradigm for autonomous materials discovery, enabling physics-grounded, interpretable, and evolutionary design of complex reticular materials.

papers.title: Electroosmotic Flow in Fractal Tree Networks with Spatially Varying Surface Charge
papers.abstract: Electroosmotic transport through branching microchannel networks plays a central role in numerous charged biological porous media, membranes, and microscale physiological systems, yet existing optimization theories are largely restricted to uniformly charged channel walls. In practical devices, however, surface charge often varies spatially because of chemical functionalization, embedded electrodes, adsorption of ionic species, or intentional surface patterning, significantly altering electroosmotic transport. In the present work, we develop a generalized analytical framework for electroosmotic flow of Newtonian fluids in fractal tree-like circular microchannel networks with generation-dependent wall zeta potential. Without invoking the Debye–Hückel slip approximation, the governing electrokinetic equations are solved by incorporating finite electrical double-layer effects through the Poisson–Boltzmann equation. Closed-form expressions for the electroosmotic flow rate and hydraulic resistance of individual channels are derived and subsequently extended to self-similar branching networks under fixed total volume and fixed total wetted surface-area constraints. The influence of branching geometry, channel length ratio, branching number, network depth, and average wall zeta-potential ratio on the normalized electroosmotic conductance is systematically investigated. The analysis reveals the existence of a unique optimal branching architecture that maximizes electroosmotic transport efficiency. Under volume-constrained conditions, the generalized scaling law for the optimal radius ratio is obtained as β∗ = α−1/4 N−1/2, whereas under surface-area constraint the corresponding relation becomes β∗ = α−1/3 N−2/3. Additional scaling relations governing channel length, applied electric potential, mean velocity, volumetric flow rate, and hierarchical evolution of surface area and volume are also established. The present model reduces exactly to previously reported electroosmotic scaling laws for uniformly charged channels as limiting cases, thereby validating the formulation while substantially extending existing optimization theory to electroosmotic networks with spatially varying surface charge. The derived scaling laws provide fundamental design principles for high-performance electroosmotic microfluidic devices, artificial vascular systems, lab-on-a-chip platforms, and electrokinetically driven transport networks.

papers.title: Catalytic C-F Bond Activation of Allylic Fluorides by Lewis or Brönsted Acid : A Real Synthesis Tool of Natural Products and Diversity Molecular Architectures
Reticularized Silver Nanoclusters: From Luminescence to Sensing
papers.abstract: Silver nanoclusters (Ag NCs) occupy a rare chemical space where atomic precision, quantum-confined electronic structures, and rich excited-state behavior converge, yet their practical utility is often limited by structural fragility, environmental sensitivity, and weak processability. Reticularization offers a powerful solution by transforming discrete Ag NCs into crystalline extended architectures in which cluster cores, protective ligands, bridging linkers, and pore environments operate as an integrated functional lattice. This Review examines reticularized Ag NCs, or Ag nanocluster metal–organic frameworks (Ag NCMOFs), as an emerging class of programmable optical and sensing materials. We discuss how Ag cluster nuclearity, ligand-shell chemistry, linker electronics, framework dimensionality, topology, and confinement collectively dictate stability, intercluster communication, charge-transfer pathways, and luminescence. Particular attention is devoted to the photophysical consequences of reticular assembly, including framework-rigidified emission, cluster–linker excited states, triplet-state activation, ratiometric fluorescence–phosphorescence, guest-modulated color changes, circularly polarized luminescence, and optical memory. We then highlight sensing platforms in which crystalline Ag-cluster frameworks translate oxygen diffusion, volatile-organic-compound uptake, explosive recognition, metal-ion binding, antibiotic interaction, amino-acid recognition, and water-induced lattice transformation into optical or Raman-readable outputs. Beyond sensing, we survey emerging roles in catalysis, electrocatalysis, photonics, electronics, antimicrobial interfaces, and molecular diagnostics. By connecting atomic structure to framework-level function, this Review presents Ag NCMOFs not as simple assemblies of emissive clusters, but as reticularized quantum materials in which periodic order converts fragile molecular emitters into robust, adaptive, and information-rich functional solids.

papers.title: Exact concentration regions for stimulus-switched competitive binding under finite depletion
papers.abstract: The reported C/B composition of a published pH-programmed coordination cage provides a stringent test for transferring binary binding constants into a competitive mixture. At pH 7.5, the observed C/B ratio requires Keff B (7.5) < 6.38885 M−1, but the entire quoted marginal rectangle for the transferred B affinities lies above this bound under the same-site model and fixed reported pKa. This tension motivates a bounded inverse calculation for finite-depletion competitive binding. Starting from the established one-site equilibrium model, target odds factor as OaOb = S∆, separating the controlled-free-concentration selectivity swing from finite-depletion effects. For two guests with one total fixed, monotonicity converts independent fidelity and occupancy requirements into explicit one-sided concentration thresholds whose intersection is the complete admissible interval. A pairwise endpoint bound gives a necessary consistency test for observed ratios in mixtures containing additional same-site competitors. The construction is extended to two independently variable totals through exact boundary curves parameterized by free-host concentration, without assuming convexity or a one-interval topology. In the Cullen system, the binary C/B projection shows that finite depletion changes a 95% decision, while a full acid/C/B map independently underpredicts middle-pH C dominance under transferred constants. A second application to a pH-responsive naphthotube shows the high-selectivity-margin regime: depletion changes the maximin by only 0.23 percentage points and the 95% window remains broad. The method provides model-conditional concentration windows, concentration-region maps and parameter-transfer consistency tests.

papers.title: Comparative Preclinical Evaluation and Toxicological Study on a Human Skin Model of Biocompatible Hydrophilic Polymer Prodrugs for Subcutaneous Anticancer Delivery
papers.abstract: Subcutaneous (SC) administration is attracting increasing interest as an alternative to intravenous (IV) delivery due to its numerous clinical and practical advantages. However, the SC administration of vesicant and irritant anticancer drugs remains precluded by their severe local toxicity. To overcome this limitation, the concept of water-soluble polymer prodrugs has recently emerged as a promising strategy. Herein, to fully exploit this potential and make a significant step forward clinical translation, we investigated water-soluble polymer prodrugs based on paclitaxel and a library of clinically relevant hydrophilic polymers, including: polyacrylamide (PAAm), poly[oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate] (POEGMA300 and POEGMA950), poly[N-(2-hydroxypropyl)methacrylamide] (PHPMA) and poly(2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC). Through a comprehensive preclinical evaluation encompassing physicochemical characterization, in vitro studies, in vivo efficacy and safety assessments, and ex vivo toxicological evaluation in living human skin biopsies, we established detailed structure–property relationships governing SC performance. Varying the polymer backbone enabled broad modulation of key parameters, including injectable doses (100–700 mg.kg-1 in Ptx), plasma drug release kinetics (3–35% released after 24 h), cytotoxicity (IC50 = 10–105 nM in MCF-7 cells), and pharmacokinetic behavior (bioavailability = 10–79%). Importantly, polymer prodrugs based on PAAm, POEGMA300, POEGMA950, and PHPMA achieved antitumor efficacy in mice comparable to Taxol administered IV at 15 mg.kg-1 and outperformed the commercial formulation at 60 mg.kg-1 owing to their three-fold higher maximum tolerated doses. Remarkably, all polymer prodrugs exhibited excellent local tolerability in both murine and human skin models. Overall, this study provides, to our knowledge, the first comprehensive framework linking polymer structure to biological performance for the SC delivery of irritant and vesicant anticancer agents, as well as the first assessment in human skin, thereby offering valuable design guidelines and paving the way toward clinical translation.

papers.title: A shared expression to predict monomer consumption in itaconate – acrylate radical copolymerizations developed with symbolic regression
papers.abstract: Copolymerizations of two or more monomers are important, because they allow for tailoring the polymer properties by the selection of monomers and by the amount of each monomer in the product. While tailoring of the copolymer composition is relatively easy using reactivity ratios, the prediction of the copolymerization rate requires the knowledge of a detailed kinetic model. Knowledge of the associated kinetic coefficients for the particular comonomer choice is limited. Data-driven methods are promising to avoid the complex experimental determination of all kinetic coefficients, which becomes particularly important with the introduction of new monomers in the context of circular processes. Using shared expressions developed with symbolic regression, a single, interpretable model capturing the copolymerization rates across various itaconates and acrylates is developed and presented. As an example, copolymerizations of bio-based itaconic acid esters with acrylates with a mean absolute relative error of 0.07 considered.

papers.title: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training datasets and have limited physical transparency. We reveal a physics-based linear correlation mapping complex coverage-dependent adsorption energies directly to trivially computable gas-phase pairwise interactions that are evaluated via Mie potentials. This correlation is governed by bond order conservation: as surface-adsorbate interactions weaken under crowding, adsorbate-adsorbate interactions strengthen. This correlation generalizes across diverse crystal facets, surface tensions, and distinct single- and multi-component adsorption classes (e.g., dissociative S*, N*+O*, and non-dissociative CO*). The predictive utility of gas-phase pairwise interactions is directly validated against experimental calorimetry. Ultimately, these gas-phase pairwise interactions are a transformative descriptor for lateral interactions on surfaces. The generalizability and physical interpretability of this descriptor will engender a new paradigm for modeling catalyst structures and kinetics under in situ conditions.

papers.title: Direct detection of reactive intermediates in photocatalytic water splitting with small carbon species on TiO2(100)
papers.abstract: Direct detection of elusive intermediates is crucial for deciphering the mechanisms of photocatalytic reactions at semiconductor interfaces. Time-of-flight mass spectrometry under ultrahigh vacuum conditions in conjunction with ultraviolet laser irradiation is employed to investigate photocatalytic water (D 2 O) splitting and its coupling with methyl iodide (CH 3 I) fragments on TiO 2 (100). Direct detection of elusive intermediates, such as D, OD, and OOD species, unequivocally provides experimental evidence for the elementary steps of photocatalytic water splitting under ultrahigh vacuum conditions. In the presence of CH 3 I, additional pathways emerge leading to methane (CH 3 D) and methanol (CH 3 OD) formation via reactions between photogenerated water and methyl iodide fragments. Temperature-dependent measurements indicate that photocatalytic water splitting proceeds most efficiently at room temperature, whereas density functional theory calculations elucidate the underlying mechanisms that govern the surface reactions. These results reveal molecular-level pathways of light-driven reactivity and provide a framework for controlling selective photocatalytic transformations at semiconductor interfaces.

papers.title: Selectivity Maps for Electrochemical Ethylene Oxidation to Ethylene Oxide and Ethylene Glycol
papers.abstract: Electrochemical ethylene oxidation can produce ethylene oxide and ethylene glycol, but selectivity is limited by competition with the oxygen evolution reaction and overoxidation. At the same time, the mechanistic literature is fragmented across oxo-, peroxo-, and hydroxyl-mediated pathways, creating ambiguity and hindering systematic improvement. Using density functional theory (DFT) and scaling relations, we build a unified descriptor-based framework comparing the three pathways across fcc metals, metal(II) oxides, and rutile-structured oxides. The oxygen binding strength is found to control ethylene activation via oxo and peroxo species, while a carbon-based descriptor describes the hydroxyl pathway and product binding defines an overoxidation limit. The resulting selectivity maps identify the catalyst properties required for each route, rationalize the high performance of individual catalysts such as oxidized Pd, and provide transferable guidelines for designing selective alkene oxidation catalysts.

papers.title: Employing “FAST Water” to Accelerate Self-Assembly
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations are a powerful tool for elucidating the molecular mechanisms of supramolecular self-assembly, but the long timescales of aggregation often make all-atom simulations computationally challenging. Here, we evaluate the recently developed TIP3P-FAST water model as a simple strategy to accelerate self-assembly simulations in aqueous solution. TIP3P-FAST employs mass repartitioning and rescaling within a water molecule, increasing molecular mobility without altering the underlying potential energy surface. We investigate three representative self-assembling systems with distinct aggregation mechanisms and resulting morphologies: L-phenylalanine tripeptide (FFF), methylsubstituted ureido-pyrimidinone (UPy), and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Simulations of isolated solutes reveal around three-fold increase in diffusion coefficients in TIP3P-FAST water compared to conventional TIP3P water, while solvent-accessible surface areas, radial distribution functions, hydrogenbond numbers, and interaction energies remain unchanged. Self-assembly simulations initiated from dispersed monomers show markedly accelerated aggregation kinetics in FAST water, as evidenced by a faster decrease in solvent-accessible surface area and in the number of clusters. For UPy, enhanced dynamics facilitate more efficient structural reorganization, yielding assemblies with structural characteristics comparable to, or even more ordered than, those obtained in TIP3P water. These results demonstrate that TIP3P-FAST substantially reduces the computational cost of atomistic self-assembly simulations while preserving equilibrium structural and thermodynamic properties, providing a practical route for studying complex supramolecular systems.

papers.title: Machine-learning Assisted Raman Spectroscopy for Prediction of Oenological Parameters in Red and White Wines
papers.abstract: Rapid and reliable quantification of oenological parameters is essential for quality control and process optimisation in winemaking. In this study, we investigate the potential of Raman spectroscopy combined with machine learning regression models as a non-destructive approach for the simultaneous prediction of multiple oenological parameters in both red and white wines. Spectra from 50 white and 50 red wines were acquired at two excitation wavelengths, 785 and 1064 nm for white wines, and exclusively at 1064 nm for red wines due to strong fluorescence interference from anthocyanins and other pigmented phenolic compounds. Multiple regression algorithms were evaluated, including linear models, kernel-based methods, tree-based ensembles, and unsupervised feature extraction techniques, such as independent component analysis (ICA) and principal component analysis (PCA). The performance of the models was assessed against reference measurements using standard error and goodness-of-fit metrics, and the overfit was quantified through two new metrics derived from the comparison between training and validation errors and their standard deviation. The results show that model suitability is parameter-dependent, with ICA followed by linear regression outperforming other approaches across most parameters and wine matrices. For white wines, 9 parameters were successfully predicted with errors comparable to the uncertainty of the reference measurements. For red wines, an accurate prediction was achieved for ethanol, glycerol, and extract. This study demonstrates the potential of machine learning-assisted 1 Raman spectroscopy for robust multi-parameter wine analysis, offering a fast, non-destructive alternative to conventional methods suitable for routine oenological monitoring.

papers.title: Nanostructured Hydrogel Surface Functionalization Controls C2C12 Myoblast Adhesion and Differentiation
papers.abstract: Cell culture platforms benefit from chemical cues that recapitulate key aspects of the native biological environment. However, substantial challenges remain in designing scaffolds that also control the spatial organization of these cues. This is particularly difficult at gel interfaces, where functional groups must be presented within the outermost few nanometers to efficiently direct processes such as cell adhesion and spreading, but where nano- to microscale heterogeneities in synthetic hydrogel structure can obscure intended patterns. Here, we show that highly structured functional molecular layers, covalently transferred to polyacrylamide (PAAm), create hydrogel interfaces with defined surface chemistries, including amine, carboxylate, and zwitterionic groups, that regulate adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation of C2C12 murine myoblasts on hydrogels ranging from 10 to 90 kPa in stiffness. Functionalization with charged headgroup chemistries within this nanometer-thick interfacial layer increases cell density by 2–6-fold and average cell area by 50–100% relative to unfunctionalized PAAm, while increasing the abundance of extended triangular and rectangular cell morphologies by 5–30-fold. Upon differentiation, amine-functionalized 10 kPa surfaces exhibit geometric mean cell densities 24-fold higher than unfunctionalized surfaces, as well as ~2-fold higher median numbers of nuclei per multinucleate structure.

papers.title: DNA mimic helical foldamers with up to 100 units: synthesis and recognition of a multiprotein complex
papers.abstract: DNA mimic foldamers (DMFOs) are helically folded aromatic oligoamides bearing negatively charged side chains that mimic the shape and charge distribution of double-stranded B-DNA. DNA mimicry typically entails the regular alternation of two different aromatic amino acid monomers, M and Q. Here, we introduce a new synthetic approach of (MQ)n oligomers on solid phase that enabled the production of sequences as long as a 100mer, weighing 35 kDa, formally equivalent to a 50-base pair DNA duplex, or equivalent in molecular weight to a 300amino acid protein. The approach takes advantage of dimeric Fmoc-MQ-OH as elementary building blocks. Three such macromonomers were synthesized using Q and M units bearing different side chains. Solid phase synthesis protocols were validated in all three series. Helix handedness was shown to be determined by a single chiral residue. The purified long oligomers were analyzed by reversed phase high-performance liquid chromatography, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for their purity, identity, and helix-handedness bias. Clusters of foldamers forming in the presence of Ca2+ could be visualized by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), validating their dimensions.

papers.title: Process-Informed Co-Optimization of Liquid Air Energy Storage and Data Centers under Off-Design Thermodynamic Operation
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of AI data centers (DCs) is intensifying stress on power systems and exposing operators to volatile electricity markets. This work develops a process-informed co-optimization framework that integrates liquid air energy storage (LAES) with DC operation. Unlike blackbox storage models, the proposed formulation captures LAES thermodynamics through charging start-up dynamics and off-design discharge behavior, linking process efficiency with dispatch decisions. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer program with a robust extension for joint participation in energy and reserve markets. Results across CAISO, PJM, and ERCOT show that LAES–DC integration reduces operating costs by 9%–48% in energy markets and up to 55% when reserve services are included. The analysis reveals that optimal operation is governed not only by price signals but also by maintaining LAES near efficient thermodynamic regimes, with DC workload flexibility shaping demand to support process performance.

papers.title: Hierarchical iDDA-DIA coupled to polarity‑switching MS1 scan samples expands annotation and quantification depth in untargeted metabolomics
papers.abstract: Untargeted LC–HRMS studies face a fundamental trade‑off between MS/MS coverage, MS sampling density, and total analysis time, particularly in large‑scale metabolomics and exposomics projects. To overcome these limitations and enhance both chemical coverage and method reproducibility, we introduce a two‑stage acquisition strategy that decouples fragmentation acquisition from routine sample analysis. In Stage 1, deep fragmentation information is captured through iterative data‑dependent acquisition (iDDA) combined with data‑independent acquisition (DIA) on pooled quality control (QC) samples, performed in one polarity at a time across complementary chromatographic modes (ZIC‑HILIC for hydrophilic and C18 for hydrophobic compounds). In Stage 2, all study samples, QCs, and blanks are acquired in rapid polarity‑switching MS full‑scan mode, maximizing scan cycle and chromatographic sampling without sacrificing polarity coverage.

papers.title: From binding to bonding: DOSY-NMR to detect covalent ligand-lectin interactions
papers.abstract: Covalent ligands are increasingly exploited in drug discovery yet validating covalent adduct formation typically relies on mass spectrometry and X‑ray crystallography—methods that become resource‑intensive and impractical when extended to the parallel evaluation of multiple ligands. Here we establish a solution‑state NMR workflow for the direct detection and screening of reversible covalent ligands, using the lectin domain BC2L‑C‑Nt from Burkholderia cenocepacia and a series of salicylaldehyde‑functionalized glycomimetics as a proof‑of‑concept system. These ligands were previously confirmed to form covalent adducts with Lys108 by mass spectrometry, allowing us to assess the ability of the workflow to detect and differentiate covalent engagement. At the core of the approach is 1 H Diffusion‑Ordered Spectroscopy (DOSY‑NMR), applied here to distinguish free ligands, non‑covalent complexes, and covalent adducts based solely on their diffusion coefficients. DOSY measurements on aldehyde‑bearing ligands revealed new species consistent with protein‑bound complexes, confirming covalent bond formation under near‑physiological conditions. Comparison with the native non‑covalent ligand (H‑type 1 trisaccharide) demonstrated the ability of DOSY to discriminate covalent complexes from high‑affinity, fast‑exchange non‑covalent interactions, while negative controls lacking either the electrophilic warhead or the fucose recognition motif confirmed the structural requirements for covalent binding. Orthogonal validation was obtained through 1 H– 13 C HSQC and 13 C DOSY experiments using isotopically labelled ligands, which provided molecular‑level confirmation of covalent adduct formation. Together, these results position DOSY‑NMR as a rapid, direct, and experimentally accessible method for distinguishing covalent from non‑covalent binding modes, bothin reversible and irreversible covalent ligand systems, becoming a complement technique when evaluating covalent compounds.

papers.title: 𝑴𝑪𝑪𝑷𝒆𝒓𝒇𝒐𝒓𝒎𝒂𝒏𝒄𝒆: Towards unbiased selection of machine learning classification models – Case studies on environmental QSAR endpoints
papers.abstract: Industrialization and human activities have led to the accumulation of a wide array of organic chemicals in the environment, most of which exert significant toxic effects. This warrants the quick and efficient filling of toxicity data gaps for developing safer alternatives, which is often not possible by trial-and-error experimentation. Therefore, researchers have developed multiple in silico-based machine learning models to predict the toxicity of these chemicals towards various environmental endpoints. However, there exist some practical challenges in the unbiased selection of machine learning models among similar competing models. The present study proposes three novel metrics that account for model robustness, generalizability, and overall model performance (𝑀𝐶𝐶𝑅𝑜𝑏𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑛𝑒𝑠𝑠, 𝑀𝐶𝐶𝐺𝑒𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑧𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦, and 𝑀𝐶𝐶𝑃𝑒𝑟𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒) that can be used quantitatively for an unbiased identification of the best classification-based model. Three different binary classification environmental fate and toxicity datasets (small, comparatively large, and medium-sized) were considered to evaluate the potential of these metrics. Each dataset was randomly split into a modeling and an independent test set. The modeling set was further split into training and validation sets three times using rational and random splitting approaches. A total of 72 machine learning models were trained, crossvalidated, and evaluated on the validation sets. The proposed metrics were computed for each model. Models possessing the highest 𝑀𝐶𝐶𝑃𝑒𝑟𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 value and acceptable values of 𝑀𝐶𝐶𝑅𝑜𝑏𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑛𝑒𝑠𝑠 and 𝑀𝐶𝐶𝐺𝑒𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑧𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦 were selected as the best ones. We also analyzed some of the failed cases based on the threshold values that we propose. The best models, when subjected to independent test set predictions, generate better predictions than most of the models in the same train-validation split. Therefore, this work provides simple guidance for an unbiased selection of classification-based machine learning models that are expected to generate reliable external predictions.

papers.title: Playing to Learn: MS Cards, an Educational Card Game for Teaching Mass Spectrometry Instrumentation
papers.abstract: Teaching mass spectrometry presents a significant pedagogical challenge due to its multidisciplinary nature and the complexity of the instrumentation. In an effort to make mass spectrometry learning more engaging and enjoyable for students, a card game has been developed. This novel educational game, called MS Cards, is designed to enable students to describe the different components of mass spectrometers and how they work. By matching specific cards, learners actively discover and logically interconnect instrument configurations with their inherent properties, target molecule types, and acquisition modes. The MS card game was iteratively tested and evaluated across different educational contexts at two universities. The students were invited to evaluate the card game approach through a questionnaire. Analysis of the students’ feedback suggests a high percentage of approval for the game as a pedagogical, guiding, and motivating tool.

papers.title: Activity and selectivity descriptors for ethylene glycol electrooxidation from first-principle scaling relations
papers.abstract: The electrooxidation of ethylene glycol emerged as a co-electrolysis anode reaction with the potential of valorizing PET-waste into industrially attractive chemicals such as glycolic acid. Although the focus on the reaction is increasing steadily in recent years, systematic means for catalyst developments are still lacking. Herein, we present a Sabatier volcano for ethylene glycole electrooxidation towards glycolic acid from a density functional theory-based limiting-potential analysis of late transition metal catalysts. A simple two-dimensional descriptor analysis rationalizes the enhanced activity of Pt and Pd compared to Au, as well as a reason for the latter’s near perfect selectivity towards glycolic acid. Furthermore, it provides target values for oxygen and carbon-affinity descriptors for ideal catalysts, where low oxygen affinity is beneficial to avoid surface oxidation at reaction conditions, while a high carbon affinity is beneficial for the initial activation and general smoothing of the free energy landscape of the reaction. Finally, we show that alloys are capable of linearly interpolating the single metals on the activity map, allowing the fine-tuning of the descriptors, if surface disalloying can be avoided.

papers.title: Temperature-and pressure-dependent water stabilization of CO dimerization on Cu(100)
papers.abstract: The electrochemical CO(2) reduction reaction offers a pathway to producing fuels and high-value chemicals from waste CO2 using renewable electricity. Among known catalysts, only copper in aqueous electrolytes enables the formation of C2+ products with high activity. The process of the C-C coupling is believed to be limited by the dimerization of two adsorbed *CO to form a *OC-CO* intermediate. Experimental strategies to improve selectivity toward C2+ products have recently focused on increasing temperature and pressure in the system, but the origins of these effects remain poorly understood. In this work, the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the *OC-CO* dimer at the electrochemical interface of Cu(100) has been investigated, as a function of temperature and pressure using machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on DFT data. Extended molecular dynamics simulations with an explicit aqueous interface show that increased water density stabilizes the *OC-CO* intermediate through increased hydrogen bonding between interfacial water and the dimer. In contrast, temperature has no direct effect on the CO–CO association barrier, but instead indirectly influences reactivity by destabilizing *CO adsorption. Introducing a potassium cation leads to a large reduction in the interface work function, but only minor changes were observed in the energetics of the dimer formation. No correlation between cation-dimer distance and energetics is observed, suggesting a limited role of local field effects. These results identify hydrogen bonding as the key factor governing the stabilization of the *OC-CO* intermediate under experimental conditions. This work demonstrates how machine-learning interatomic potentials can facilitate systematic analysis of dynamic interfaces, and can be a powerful tool in theoretical exploration of electrolyte effects on reaction intermediates across extended time and length scales.

papers.title: Dynamic Piezoelectric Charge Engineering of Dual Single-Atom COF/g-C3N4 S-Scheme Heterostructures for Efficient Artificial Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: Artificial photosynthesis offers a sustainable route for converting solar energy into chemical fuels while simultaneously addressing the challenges of anthropogenic CO2 emissions and global energy demand. Nevertheless, the practical implementation of photocatalytic CO2 reduction and hydrogen evolution is hindered by limited visible-light absorption, rapid recombination of photogenerated charge carriers, and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. In this work, a dual single-atom Fe–Co catalyst anchored on a covalent organic framework (COF)/graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) S-scheme heterostructure was successfully developed through a rational dynamic piezoelectric charge engineering strategy. The intimate coupling between COF and g-C3N4 established an efficient S-scheme heterojunction, while atomically dispersed Fe–N4 and Co–N4 active sites provided abundant catalytic centers for CO2 activation and proton reduction. Under simultaneous simulated AM 1.5G solar irradiation and ultrasonic mechanical stimulation, dynamic piezoelectric polarization generated an additional internal electric field that reinforced interfacial charge separation and promoted directional carrier migration toward the isolated Fe–Co active sites. Comprehensive structural characterization, including XRD, XPS, aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM, XANES, and EXAFS, confirmed the successful formation of a highly crystalline heterostructure with uniformly dispersed Fe and Co single atoms and the absence of metal aggregation. The optimized Fe–Co SAC/COF/g-C3N4 photocatalyst achieved a CO evolution rate of 756 μmol g-1 h-1 and a H2 evolution rate of 3145 μmol g-1 h-1, representing approximately 13-fold and 11-fold enhancements, respectively, over pristine g-C3N4. The catalyst further exhibited a maximum apparent quantum efficiency of 16.8% at 420 nm, a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 2.6%, and retained more than 94% of its initial photocatalytic activity after ten consecutive reaction cycles. Density functional theory calculations revealed pronounced interfacial charge redistribution, enhanced electronic states near the Fermi level, stronger CO2 adsorption (−0.86 eV), and substantially reduced Gibbs free-energy barriers for *COOH formation (0.36 eV) and hydrogen adsorption (0.18 eV), confirming accelerated multielectron transfer kinetics. The synergistic integration of dynamic piezoelectric polarization, S-scheme charge transfer, and dual single-atom catalysis provides an effective strategy for maximizing solar-to-chemical energy conversion and offers a promising platform for the design of next-generation photocatalysts for efficient artificial photosynthesis and sustainable solar fuel production.

papers.title: Synthesis, Redox Properties and Magneto-Optical Activity of a Homologous Set of Metallo-5,5-Dimethylisocorrole Complexes
papers.abstract: A homologous set of 5,5-dimethyl-10,15-bis(pentafluorophenyl)-isocorrole (5-DMIC) complexes supporting NiII, PdII, PtII, or ZnII metal centers have been prepared and characterized. These complexes are readily accessible via modular synthetic routes and can be purified and obtained in moderate to good yields. Single crystal X-ray di@raction studies carried out for the Ni[5-DMIC], Pd[5-DMIC], and Pt[5-DMIC] complexes reveal M–N bond distances ranging from 1.84–1.99 Å across the series along with minimal metal displacement from the N4 plane, ranging from 0.014 Å for Ni[5-DMIC] to ~0.046 Å for the heavier isocorrole homologues. Accordingly, M[5-DMIC] complexes are highly planar with metal centers that are tightly coordinated in square planar geometry within the tetrapyrrole core. Electrochemical studies revealed a periodic trend in the reduction potentials with Pt[5-DMIC] being the most easily reduced (Ered = –0.84 V vs. Fc/Fc+). Additionally, the metalloisocorroles display strong absorbance in the UV-visible and near-infrared (NIR) regions, with Ni[5-DMIC], Pd[5-DMIC], and Zn[5-DMIC] exhibiting NIR bands centered around 900 nm, while Pt[5-DMIC] absorbance extends nearly to 1050 nm and into the NIR-II window. Given the unique, long-wavelength spectral characteristics, the M[5-DMIC] complexes were evaluated as NIR magneto-optical materials via magnetic circular dichroism (MCD), marking the first such study for isocorrole complexes. In contrast to the behavior of higher-symmetry D4h metalloporphyrins, the low-symmetry, non-aromatic isocorrole framework lacks a proper rotation axis required to support Faraday A-terms, resulting in the magneto-optical response being governed entirely by Faraday B-terms. Notably, Zn[5-DMIC] exhibits a sign reversal of the B -term in the Soret-like region, which may be attributed to di@ering frontier orbital contributions for this complex. Collectively, these results establish metalloisocorroles as structurally distinctive, low symmetry redoxactive, NIR-absorbing platforms with varied magneto-optical activity that are well positioned for various photophysical applications and detailed interrogation.

papers.title: Tall oil pitch as a graphite feedstock: direct conversion of a biomass-derived by-product into bulk graphite
papers.abstract: Tall oil pitch (TOP), a high-boiling by-product obtained from crude tall oil refining in the kraft pulping process, was converted into bulk graphite through catalyst-free thermal treatment. This result demonstrates that a biomass-derived industrial residue can serve directly as a feedstock for graphite. Without catalysts or prior purification, thermal treatment of TOP produced bulk graphite, as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction. The results indicate that graphite can be generated from multicomponent resin-derived residues through simple thermal processing. This work expands the range of candidate feedstocks for graphite production to include industrial by-products from biomass refining and suggests a route for upgrading TOP into a higher-value carbon material.

papers.title: Obtaining Dynamics of Supported Metal Nanoparticles using Cost-effective Training of Machine Learning Force Fields
papers.abstract: Metal–support interactions (MSI) play a critical role in heterogeneous catalysis by influencing catalyst stability and reactivity. A long-term objective is to model catalytic systems in simulated experiments, to obtain atomistic insights into MSI under reaction conditions. Achieving this goal requires extensive modelling of large atomistic systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFF’s) enable simulations at these scales by providing orders of magnitude speedups compared to density functional theory (DFT). However, effective fine-tuning of MLFFs requires smart sampling of the configurational space of supported nanoparticle systems. Notably, the chemically relevant interfacial region constitutes only a small fraction of the total atoms, highlighting the need for cost-effective training strategies. Here, we demonstrate two such strategies using Co/TiO2 as a model system: cross-polymorph training and reducing support slab layers. The latter lowers the number of electrons in each training structure, significantly reducing computational cost, which scales roughly cubically with electrons. Combining both strategies produced an accurate MLFF capable of revealing a novel minimum-energy configuration for a Co nanoparticle on TiO2 anatase. The presented strategies are applicable to all metal oxide-supported metal nanoparticle systems and enable the development of MLFFs capable of probing MSI at the atomistic scale.

papers.title: Varying Mechanisms Dominate Formate Formation in Electrochemical CO2 Reduction on Cu, Au and Pb: A Constant Potential DFT-based Microkinetic Analysis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) offers a route to convert renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals while closing the anthropogenic carbon cycle. However, the technology remains immature and is limited by low selectivity and energy efficiency. These challenges are less severe for the two-electron products, carbon monoxide and formate, making them attractive targets. Formate is of particular interest due to its potential as an energy carrier and its relatively high market value. Yet its formation mechanism remains debated, hindering rational catalyst design. Here, we combine grand canonical DFT, a hybrid explicit-implicit solvent model and microkinetic simulations to elucidate the formate formation mechanism on Cu, Au and Pb, and show that distinct pathways dominate on each metal. On Cu, the formation of formate proceeds via O-down chemisorption of CO2 followed by protonation. In contrast, Au exhibits negligible activity, arising from a mechanism where adsorbed hydrogen atoms combine with incoming CO2 species. Finally, Pb facilitates a direct outer sphere-like process from physisorbed CO2 to formate, with high activity, which we attribute to its diffuse p-like states near the Fermi level, a feature shared by other formate-selective post-transition-metal catalysts. The variation of mechanisms for formate production likely underlie the difficulty of identifying universal activity descriptors for eCO2R and suggest that catalyst design might necessitate mechanism specific descriptors.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Acyl Anion Equivalents from Carboxylic Acids via Acylsulfonylhydrazides: A Practical Organocatalytic Umpolung
papers.abstract: The development of mild and practical acyl anion equivalents remains a cornerstone challenge in modern organic synthesis, as traditional umpolung strategies often rely on moisture-sensitive reagents, strong bases, or specialized N-heterocyclic carbene catalysts. Here we report that readily available N,N-acylsulfonylhydrazides serve as efficient acyl anion surrogates under operationally simple organocatalytic conditions. Using DMAP as a nucleophilic catalyst, these stable hydrazide precursors readily provide acylation products of a wide range of carbon electrophiles, including aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, activated ketones, olefins, and imines. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations and HRMS analysis, reveal an unconventional pathway wherein DMAP adds to the acyldiazene intermediate, triggering nitrogen extrusion and generating a zwitterionic nucleophile. This dual role of DMAP in enhancing both the stability and nucleophilicity of the reactive species circumvents the hydroxycarbene rearrangement pathway, offering a practical and scalable alternative to existing acyl anion methodologies.

papers.title: Approach-Region Commitment and Environmental Friction
papers.abstract: The commitment of a reacting system to productive barrier crossing depends on how strongly the environment dissipates energy into the approach-region coordinate, rather than oscillatory recrossing. This dissipation is quantified by a single dimensionless damping ratio, χ0 = Γeff/(2Ω0), where Ω0 is the precursor-well approach frequency and Γeff is the total projected friction. Using three independent estimator routes calibrated to spectroscopic linewidths (Route A), solvent longitudinal relaxation times (Route B), and DFT electronic friction coefficients (Route C), χ0 is computed here for nine canonical systems, constituting an Approach-Region Commitment (ARC) Atlas, spanning gas-phase unimolecular reactions, liquid-phase electron transfer and proton-coupled electron transfer, surface heterogeneous catalysis, and solid-state ion transport. Gas-phase systems are deeply underdamped (χ0 ∼ 10−3–10−2), providing a dynamical interpretation of the excess-energy requirements of RRKM unimolecular kinetics through the approach-region commitment probability rather than through transition-state recrossing alone. Selected condensed-phase systems approach or enter the near-critical window χ0 ∈ [0.8, 1.3] (K-promoted metal surfaces; fast-solvent ET near the upper window flank), while viscous solvents and poisoned surfaces fall into the overdamped regime. The results are not obtained by fitting χ0 to reaction outcomes: Γeff and Ω0 are taken from independently measured, computed, or explicitly bracketed physical observables in each case. The progression from gas to liquid to surface corresponds to a severalorder-of-magnitude span in χ0, revealing that solvent choice, surface promotion, and phase selection each shift χ0 in a predictable direction relative to the exceptional-point stability boundary at χ0 = 1.

papers.title: Photon Partitioning in Reconfigurable Visible-Light Flow Reactors for Simultaneous Photochemical and Photocatalytic Degradation
papers.abstract: Simultaneous photochemical and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants under visible light presents a fundamental reactor design challenge because both pathways compete for the same incident photon flux. Photons absorbed directly by the pollutant drive non-catalytic photolysis, whereas photons absorbed by the photocatalyst generate reactive species responsible for heterogeneous photocatalysis. Maximizing one pathway can therefore reduce the photon availability for the other, making it difficult to design reactors that efficiently exploit both processes. Here, we present a reconfigurable visible-light photoflow reactor that enables systematic investigation of this photon competition through adjustable optical path length, interchangeable open-channel (OC) and tubular-channel (TC) geometries, and direct measurement of light transmission using transparent reactor windows. Methylene blue degradation was employed as a model reaction with immobilized metal-free graphitic carbon nitride (g-C₃N₄) as the photocatalyst. Empirical optimization revealed that the OC geometry provided superior noncatalytic degradation compared with batch operation, whereas the TC geometry enhanced slurry photocatalysis through higher flow velocity and improved catalyst suspension and illumination. Thin optical paths suffered from reduced photon utilization as degradation progressed and the solution became increasingly transparent. Immobilizing g-C₃N₄ as a coating eliminated catalyst recovery while enabling investigation of catalyst placement. A back-coated catalyst configuration outperformed front-coated designs by allowing long-wavelength photons to drive photolysis within the solution before shorter-wavelength photons activated the catalyst, thereby minimizing scattering losses and improving overall photon utilization. The optimized back-coated reactor increased the apparent degradation rate constant by 2.3-fold compared with the non-cataltic batch reactor, maintained stable performance over five consecutive cycles, and achieved 97% methylene blue removal in continuous single-pass operation without catalyst separation. These results demonstrate that controlling photon partitioning through reactor geometry and catalyst placement enables simultaneous optimization of catalytic and non-catalytic degradation pathways, providing a general strategy for the design of efficient visible-light photochemical flow reactors.

papers.title: SabreSDN: A Complex-Valued 1D U-Net for Denoising SABRE-Hyperpolarized NMR Spectra at Low Concentration
papers.abstract: Signal Amplification By Reversible Exchange (SABRE) can enhance nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) signals by several thousand-fold through para-hydrogen-derived hyperpolarization. However, at low substrate concentrations (50~$\mu$M and below), the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) remains insufficient for reliable spectral analysis, particularly in time-resolved measurements where signal averaging is precluded by the finite hyperpolarization lifetime. Traditional denoising methods such as exponential windowing and Cadzow filtering rely on manually tuned parameters and fail to preserve fine spectral features. We introduce SabreSDN (SABRE Signal Denoising Network), a complex-valued 1D U-Net that operates directly on complex NMR spectra (8192~points, real and imaginary channels). The network incorporates four key architectural components: (1)~complex convolutions (CConv1d) that encode the absorption--dispersion Hilbert-transform relationship as a structural prior, halving parameter count relative to unconstrained real-valued convolutions; (2)~CBAM1d attention modules that jointly model channel-wise and frequency-axis feature importance; (3)~a MultiScaleBlock bottleneck with parallel dilated convolutions (dilation~1,~4,~8) to simultaneously capture narrow singlets, $J$-coupled multiplets, and broad spectral features; and (4)~gated skip connections that selectively suppress noisy encoder features during decoding. Training uses a three-component composite loss that allocates $4\times$ higher weight to peak-containing regions ($\sim$2.4\% of spectral points) together with frequency-domain amplitude matching and baseline smoothness regularization. Trained on 50~$\mu$M SABRE-hyperpolarized $^{19}$F NMR data (20,000 noisy--clean pairs, 80/20 train/val split across 50~epochs), the model reduces validation loss from 0.162 to 0.024. Denoised spectra show clear recovery of $J$-coupling multiplet fine structure with minimal baseline distortion. With 7.71~million parameters and $\sim$2~ms GPU inference per spectrum, SabreSDN is practical for integration into existing SABRE NMR acquisition pipelines. Code and model weights are available at \url{ https://github.com/kimariyb/SABRE-Denoise }.

papers.title: Machine Learning Reveals Transport-Controlled Performance from a Curated Dataset of Hydrovoltaic Devices
papers.abstract: Hydrovoltaic devices provide an intriguing route for harvesting electricity from water- 14 mediated transport processes, but quantitative comparison across reported systems remains 15

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking with a Proper Approximate Density Functional: Exact Ground-State Energy as a Close Lower Bound on the Computed Energy
papers.abstract: In the widely-used Kohn-Sham density functional theory for the many-electron ground state, only the density functional for the exchange-correlation energy is approximated. While the exact density functional minimizes at the exact ground-state energy for any system, widely used approximations can at best describe normally correlated ground states. A “proper” approximation for a given problem is defined as one that well describes relevant normally correlated states. Strong correlation, present in many quantum materials, can arise due to abnormally high degeneracy of the Kohn-Sham occupied and unoccupied one-electron energies near the Fermi level. In such situations, the approximate functional may lower its energy by spontaneously breaking symmetries that the ground-state density shares with the many-electron Hamiltonian, reducing the degeneracies that lead to strong correlation. Here the Levy constrained search is invoked to argue that the total energy of a proper functional with maximal spontaneous symmetry breaking is bounded from below by the exact total energy, and that the bound may be close to the extent that the abnormal degeneracies are removed and the broken-symmetry density expresses a single dominant slow time-dependent density fluctuation of the strongly-correlated ground-state wavefunction. This is a consequence of a minimum principle, and it may not hold in non-variational but more accurate approaches to normal correlation such as coupled cluster theory. Since the correlation energy of any one-electron state is zero, a widely proper approximate functional should be nearly or exactly self-interaction free, and progress toward a proper self-interaction correction is reviewed here. The time-centered physical interpretation of symmetry breaking is also discussed.

papers.title: Rapid Evaluation of Glassy Carbon Electrode Surface with Machine Vision
papers.abstract: Automation of electrochemical methods is crucial to achieve high-throughput experimentation (HTE) and self-driving laboratories (SDLs) for accelerating chemistry and materials engineering on pressing research challenges. Obtaining reproducible and reliable electrochemical results requires frequent monitoring of the experimental apparatus, particularly the surface condition of the electrodes. Here, a rapid surface evaluation method that combines optical macro imaging with machine learning (ML) is investigated. We demonstrated that the degradation of a glassy-carbon (GC) electrode can be quantified using only an optical image. This approach enables easily automatable, non-intrusive, and rapid monitoring of electrode health without significantly increasing the complexity of the experimental setup, while also providing spatially resolved insights into degradation.

papers.title: Competing Substrate and Free-Surface Effects on Ion Transport in Ultrathin Polymer Electrolyte Films
Automated Classification and Representation of sp2–sp2 Atropisomers in the MolBar Identifier
papers.abstract: Atropisomerism, a form of chirality arising from restricted rotation around single bonds, holds significant pharmacological importance. Yet, the automated identification and representation of atropisomerism in molecular databases and cheminformatics tools remain limited. Identifying bonds that lead to stable atropisomers typically involves labor-intensive experiments or costly quantum chemical scans. In this work, we present an extension of the molecule identifier MolBar that automatically classi- fies each sp 2 –sp 2 bond in a three-dimensional molecular structure as either rapidly convertible or configurationally stable (rotational barrier ≥ 20 kcal/mol), specifying the absolute configuration for the latter. Our methodology uses two distinct classifiers, a physically motivated classifier for steric hindrance and a message-passing graph neural network for electronic effects. Integrated into MolBar, this module enables unsupervised, largescale annotation of atropisomeric bonds along with their absolute configurations. This advancement facilitates the representation of atropisomerism in databases and supports atropisomerism-aware machine learning in drug discovery. A new version of MolBar (1.2.0) is available on the Python Package Index (PyPI) and can be installed using the pip command: pip install molbar.

papers.title: Sea spray aerosol as a newly identified source of atmospheric gas-phase perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids
papers.abstract: Perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) are persistent environmental contaminants found throughout different ecosystems, including the global oceans. Many of these compounds are bio-accumulative and toxic. Previous studies have shown that sea spray aerosol (SSA), formed by wave breaking and subsequent bubble bursting, is enriched in PFCAs and provides a means for their condensed-phase transport from the oceans to the atmosphere. This has been considered as a main pathway for PFCA distribution to even remote regions of the Arctic and Antarctic, impacting human and ecosystem health far away from sources. Here we present novel evidence that PFCAs transported into the atmosphere via SSA may subsequently partition to the gas phase. This previously unconsidered process may cause particle-only measurements and models to underestimate the total atmospheric PFCA burden associated with SSA emissions. Our field observations from the Eastern North Atlantic Ocean and laboratory studies using a high-resolution time-of-flight chemical ionisation mass spectrometer (HR-ToF-CIMS) reveal that the amount of gaseous PFCAs released from SSA may exceed particle-phase concentrations and depends primarily on the low pH of SSA particles, a result of the concentration of ocean water components in the particles upon formation and drying. To date, this mechanism has not been considered in estimates of oceanic PFCA emissions, indicating an underestimation of this source also for PFCA deposition. We encourage future studies to perform a systematic analysis of gas-phase PFCA emissions from SSA during different seasons and locations, both in field and controlled laboratory settings to constrain this newly identified source of gas-phase PFCAs.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Insight into Species Competition in Electrochemical Upgrading of Bio-oil
papers.abstract: Bio-oil derived from lignocellulosic biomass represents a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels as an energy source and chemical feedstock. Fast pyrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass yields a rich mixture of oxygenated organic species with low energy density and low stability, which can be electrochemically upgraded to increase energy density and stability and produce value- added chemicals. Here, we focus on electrocatalytic hydrotreatment of furfural (FF) and 4-propylphenol (4-PP), two constituents of raw bio-oil. In a binary mixture, the presence of FF has been shown to inhibit the reduction of 4-PP. The underlying mechanisms of these competing reactions are probed using density functional theory (DFT) and experimental electrochemical deposition techniques. The binding energies of FF and 4-PP, as well as their respective reduction products and associated reaction thermodynamics, are examined comparatively on multiple facets of single-crystal platinum and ruthenium catalysts. FF is shown to bind competitively compared to 4-PP, particularly on Pt(111) and Ru(0001), and hydrogenation products such as tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (THFA) and 4-propylcyclohexanol (4-PCOL) were found to bind less strongly to the surfaces than the reactants. FF reduction side products, including dimers furoin (FUI) and hydrofuroin (HF), were also found to bind competitively with 4-PP. No thermodynamic barriers were observed for FF hydrogenation to THFA, whereas 4-PCOL formation is favored on Pt facets, and propylcyclohexane (PC) formation is favored on Ru. The presence of barriers to 4-PP hydrogenation indicates that FF hydrogenation is thermodynamically favored on Pt and Ru. Further, limiting potential calculations suggests that the FF reduction pathways are generally favorable around 0 V vs. RHE. In contrast, the 4-PP reduction pathways require a more cathodic bias, achieved at potentials less than -0.1 V vs. RHE. Adsorption behavior of FF-derived reduction products on polycrystalline Pt is experimentally validated using a Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM). Such experiments yield estimates of aqueous-phase free energies of adsorption, which are correlated with the gas phase for comparison with computational results. Overall, the DFT model results suggest that the observed inhibition of 4-PP by FF is due to competitive adsorption and favorable FF reaction thermodynamics.

papers.title: Enhancing Electronic Conductivity and Solvent Accessible Porosity via Oxidative Deinsertion in a Vanadium Catecholate Framework
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) that combine high electronic conductivity with porosity remain rare because the structural features that promote charge transport often compromise porosity. Here, we report a redox-active three dimensional vanadium catecholate framework, [(CH 3 ) 2 NH 2 ] 2.5 V(HOTP) (HOTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaoxidotriphenylene), an anionic MOF that is charge-balanced with [(CH 3 ) 2 NH 2 ] + occupying the pores. Controlled topotactic oxidation using thianthrenium hexafluorophosphate enables the stepwise deinsertion of these charge-balancing cations, yielding five distinct oxidized phases. Spectroscopic analyses reveal that both the vanadium centers and HOTP linkers participate in the oxidation process, generating mixed-valence structures with Robin–Day class II/III delocalization across both metal and ligand components. Progressive oxidation and cation removal produce a dramatic enhancement in charge transport, culminating in an increase in electronic conductivity of nearly five orders of magnitude from ~10 –6 S cm –1 in the unoxidized phase to 0.4(2) S cm –1 in the most oxidized phase, accompanied by near complete removal of the cation from the pores. These results are a rare example of a porous framework in which electronic conductivity increases concomitantly with pore-vacating cation deinsertion, providing a strategy for reconciling electronic conductivity and pore accessibility in MOFs.

papers.title: Growth of Methylobacterium extorquens strains PA1 and AM1 on La3+ Inorganic-Organic-Hybrid Nanoparticles Containing the Metallophores Rhodopetrobactin B and Methylolanthanin
papers.abstract: Lanthanides (Ln) are not only essential for modern technologies but have also been shown to be involved in bacterial C1 metabolism. Methylotrophic bacteria use these elements in the active sites of lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase enzymes. To acquire these poorly soluble elements from their environment bacteria use metallophores and dedicated membrane proteins. While soluble Ln-sources such as chlorides are most often added in a laboratory setting, it is unrealistic that bacteria encounter such these more bioavailable Ln sources in nature where these elements are part of complex soil matrixes and minerals. Here, we present the synthesis and characterization of inorganic-organic hybrid nanoparticles (IOH-NP) that contain both La 3+ as well as the natively produced chelators rhodopetrobactin B (RPB B) and methylolanthanin (MLL). The obtained [La(OH) 2 ][RPB B] and [La(OH) 2 ][MLL] IOH-NP were characterized by means of scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), infrared spectroscopy and elemental analysis. This revealed that they were indeed nanometer sized and the [La(OH) 2 ][ MLL] IOH-NP slightly smaller than their RPB B counterpart. IOH-NPs were supplied as the sole Ln source to two strains of Methylobacterium extorquens, PA1 and AM1. We demonstrate for the first time that IOH-NPs can exert a beneficial effect on bacterial growth, with [La(OH) 2 ][MLL] nanoparticles outperforming both [La(OH) 2 ][RPB B] nanoparticles and LaCl 3 . Whereas IOH-NP are typically investigated as antimicrobial agents against antibiotic-resistant pathogens, they are rarely employed as a means of supporting bacterial growth. Our findings have broader implications for the cultivation of Ln-dependent bacteria: nanoparticle-based supplementation allows systematic control over Ln availability and the preparation of well-defined stoichiometric formulations for studying methylotrophy, a potential advantage over the often poorly characterized Ln species present in conventional bacterial growth media.

papers.title: Photosensitized Synthesis of 1,2-Iminosulfides via β-Fragmentation of Bifunctional Oxime Reagents
papers.abstract: The regioselective photochemical 1,2-iminothiolation of olefins was achieved via the photosensitized activation of bifunctional oxime ester reagents. Central to the design of the oxime ester reagents was an ethylene linker that facilitates the rapid synthesis of reagents via a 1,4-conjugate addition pathway and ensures that the steric and electronic properties of the thiol substituent do not impede photoactivation via triplet-triplet energy transfer catalysis. Upon photochemical activation of the oxime ester reagents, N,O-homolysis, de-carboxylation and de-ethenylation simultaneously generates both a thiyl and an iminyl radical that sequentially react with olefinic reagents.
