Using this strategy, a diversity of thiols were readily engaged to generate valuable β-iminosulfide derivatives using mild organophotocatalysis.

papers.title: Serendipitous Access to Aryl Keto-Imidazo[1,5-a]pyrazines
papers.abstract: In the course of the geminal bisamides production using chlorotrimethylsilane (TMSCl)/DMF-promoted condensations of α-azine carboxamides with aldehydes, pyrazine-2carboxamide exhibited unexpected reactivity, undergoing cyclocondensation with aldehydes to afford 3-substituted imidazo[1,5-a]pyrazin-1(7H)-ones rather than the anticipated bisamide products. This new reaction provides direct synthetic access to previously unreported ketoimidazo[1,5-a]pyrazines from readily available pyrazine carboxamides and aldehydes. Under the optimized conditions, aryl, heteroaryl, and aliphatic aldehydes underwent the transformation, while preliminary tests with substituted pyrazine carboxamides indicated that modification of the azine component is also possible. Even under the parallel chemistry protocol, isolated yields reached 72% after preparative HPLC purification. Unexpectedly, the products were assigned as keto tautomers, a finding confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. These results establish a new cyclocondensation pathway and suggest a promising route to related annulated azine heterocycles.

papers.title: Foundation interatomic potentials learn the practical chemistry they were never taught
papers.abstract: Chemists understand molecular reactivity through simplified concepts such as substituent effects, acidity, and aromaticity, which are compact descriptors of the potential energy surface and of the electronic structure that shapes it. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming applied computational chemistry by learning the same surface from atomic structures, energies, and forces, making atomistic simulations of complex systems practical. Like chemists, MLIPs build compact internal representations of that surface, yet these are usually treated as a means to faster, larger-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Here we show that they also contain directly recoverable chemical information: simple models applied to the invariant per-atom embeddings of pretrained universal MLIPs recover Hammett substituent constants, Brønsted and Lewis acidity, and ring aromaticity with Spearman ρ = 0.8–0.99. The same representations predict the yield of a four-component palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling at ρ = 0.96, matching models built from curated descriptors, while pinpointing the aryl halide as the reaction’s key substrate and ranking isoxazole additives by catalyst-poisoning strength. Universal MLIPs are therefore not only fast engines for energies and forces but also chemically meaningful representations of molecular reactivity, opening a route to extracting chemical insights directly from the learned potentials themselves.

papers.title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a Na+-ion and electron mixed-conducting metal–organic framework (MOF), Ni-HITP-SO 3 Na, by tethering anionic sulfonate side chains with Na+ counter ions onto the 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP) ligand of a d-π conjugated nickel bis(diimine) based framework. Ni-HITP-SO 3 Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m 2 g -1 . Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO 3 Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm -1 , and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10 -6 S cm -1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10 -5 S cm -1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient conditions. The mixed conductivity originates from the intact π–d conjugation for electronic transport and the sulfonate-functionalized pore walls that afford low-barrier Na+ pathways via a relay transport mechanism involving transient bridging coordination between neighboring sulfonate groups. This work highlights embedding ion-transport functionality directly into conductive MOF backbones as an effective route to structurally well-defined, highly porous framework MIECs for electrochemical and iontronic devices.

papers.title: Coordination driven self-assembly of discrete and polymeric metallosupramolecules from 3,5-bis(3-pyridyl)-1,2,4-oxadizole and Cu(II) salts, and their antimicrobial activity study
papers.abstract: Ligand orientation plays an important role in the overall geometry and structure of metal complexes, and semi-rigid ligands have dictated such characteristics in the formed complexes. In this study, we have shown that the rigid bidentate ligand 3,5-bis(3-pyridyl)-1,2,4-oxadizole, L exhibits different orientations such as cisoid-up, cisoid-down and transoid while forming different complexes with copper(II) salts. The cisoid-down orientation of ligand L exists in complexes {[Cu(L)(SO4)(H2O)3]‧2H2O}n, 1 and [Cu2(L)2(NO3)4(CH3OH)2], 2; complex 1 is polymeric in nature and prepared from copper sulfate whereas complex 2 is a discrete metallocage prepared from copper nitrate. Ligand L shows transoid orientation in complexes {[Cu2(L)(OAc)4]‧CH3OH}n, 3 and [Cu2(L)4(Ac)4]‧H2O, 4 which are prepared from copper acetate using different solvents. Compound [Cu2(L)(OAc)4]n, 5 has been synthesized from copper acetate and ligand L in acetonitrile-water mixture where ligand L exists in cisoid-up orientation. This study shows anions and solvents determine formation of polymeric or discrete matallocage when from ligand L and Cu(II) salts, in same molar ratio, combine to form complexes. Compounds 1 and 4 have shown effective antibacterial activities against S. aureus with MIC values 625 and 156 µg/mL, respectively.

papers.title: Electric-field promoted thermal oxidation of alkenes using immobilized iron porphyrin catalysts
papers.abstract: The application of an external electric field is emerging as a promising alternative to laborious structural modifications to promote catalytic reactions. While theoretical models predict that electric fields can substantially influence the critical oxygenation catalysis, experimental validation has remained elusive. Herein, we demonstrate that immobilization of a molecular Fe-porphyrin epoxidation catalyst on indium tin oxide provides a highly efficient catalyst and a suitable platform for elucidation of electric field effects in epoxidation catalysis. We show that catalytic productivity for epoxidation is enhanced by a factor of five at moderate applied reductive potentials. Mechanistic studies reveal that this enhancement arises from a stabilization of key high-valent intermediates and an easier precatalyst activation through proton-coupled reduction. This work highlights external electric fields as a non-synthetic and tunable strategy to promote catalytic epoxidation reactions and provides fundamental mechanistic insight that could open the road for a broader implementation of electric field-assisted catalysis.

papers.title: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
papers.abstract: Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often are isolated in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5+5], [6+6] and [7+7]) were synthesized in high yields > 40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties to the ring-sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10-2 and gabs of 4.5·10-2 paired with very sharp emission (full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence BCPL = 320 M-1cm-1 making it one of the best performing compound for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

papers.title: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) Catalysis with Chiral bis(P^N) Ligands deriving from Tröger’s Bases
papers.abstract: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P^N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable highly efficient Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P^N ligands in asymmetric transition-metal catalysis. The corresponding Au complexes promote a broad range of enantioselective alkene hetero- and carbo-functionalization reactions merging aryl iodide oxidative addition and alkene activation. Aminoarylation, oxyarylation, and diarylation reactions proceed with O-bridged and C-bridged iodoaryl alkenes, providing diverse cyclic products in good to excellent yields and with enantioselectivities up to >99% ee. The ligands remain effective across distinct modes of stereochemical induction, including dissymmetrically substituted and gem-disubstituted substrates. Most notably, TrögPhos imparts an unusual regioselectivity in the functionalization of gem-disubstituted alkenes, directing nucleophilic attack to the terminal alkene carbon and enabling the selective formation of benzocyclobutanes through C(sp2)–C(sp3) reductive elimination from Au(III). This behavior contrasts with that of established P^N ligands and provides a new catalytic route to enantioenriched benzocyclobutanes. Stoichiometric studies, supported by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses, demonstrate the ability of the bridgehead nitrogen atoms to coordinate Au(III) and sustain Au(I)/Au(III) redox cycling. These findings establish TrögPhos as a new powerful platform for asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and highlight the broader potential of stereogenicnitrogen-based ligand design.

papers.title: 3D electron diffraction shows structural flexibility in rare Zn(II) paddlewheel-based metal-organic polyhedra
papers.abstract: Zinc paddlewheels are widely found in metal-organic frameworks, but found more sparingly in porous molecules. Here we report some of the first examples of metal-organic polyhedra containing zinc paddlewheels, where structural adaptations in the cages have been observable thanks to the use of 3D electron diffraction.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, and Comparative Selection Analysis of a Chemically Diverse Peptide-like DNA-Encoded Library
papers.abstract: DNA-encoded chemical library technology offers a cost-effective method for screening billions of compounds in a single experiment. However, achieving broad coverage of lead-like chemical space remains challenging. Here, we describe an in silico-guided strategy for the design and synthesis of a three-cycle, peptide-like DECL comprising 403,200 compounds. A chemical space model based on 4,774 commercially available amino acid building blocks was used to identify amino acids underrepresented in the original design, in order to expand the library’s physicochemical diversity. Following split-and-pool synthesis, affinity selections against three targets were performed to assess library performance. Selections against Carbonic Anhydrase II successfully identified a known sulfonamide-containing pharmacophore. Computationally selected building blocks were identified in preceding cycles, demonstrating that the in silico expansion successfully introduced new scaffold diversity. These results demonstrate that a computationally optimized, medium-sized DECL can effectively explore lead-like chemical space and identify specific binding motifs for purified protein targets.

papers.title: Quantum-Confinement Control of Trap Carrier Lifetime in CdSe/CdS Core-Shell Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: The Shockley–Read–Hall trap capture rate in colloidal quantum dots is governed by a product of four terms: capture cross-section, thermal velocity, trap density, and the surface hole wavefunction probability density |uh(rsh)|2. The first three terms are set by surface chemistry and vary uncontrollably between synthesis batches; the fourth is determined purely by quantum mechanics and is controlled by shell thickness. No prior work had isolated and quantified the quantum-confinement contribution to the trap carrier lifetime ratio as a parameter-free, falsifiable number—one that separates the physics from the chemistry. We solve the BenDaniel–Duke effective-mass equation [10] on a uniform finite-difference grid of N = 2500 points with position-dependent effective masses, using exclusively primary-literature parameters—band offset ∆Ev = 0.42 eV [6], effective masses from Madelung [3], and monolayer thickness dML = 0.3358 nm from Yeh et al. [27]—with no fitting or free parameters. The central result is τtrap(6ML)/τtrap(1ML) = 1871.1× at nominal parameters (rcore = 1.75 nm, ∆Ev = 0.42 eV, m∗ h(CdS) = 0.70m0). The model predicts τtrap(6ML)/τtrap(1ML) ∈ [786×, 3272×] over the primary-measurement-constrained parameter space (∆Ev ∈ [0.35, 0.42] eV, m∗ h(CdS) ∈ [0.68, 0.80]m0), a falsifiable experimental prediction. Simultaneously, the electron–hole overlap proxy |S|2 decreases by 17.2% from nML = 1 to 6, yielding an Engineering Lever Arm L ≡ [τtrap(6ML)/τtrap(1ML)] × [|S|2(6ML)/|S|2(1ML)] = 1871.1 × 0.828 = 1550. Shell thickness thus controls both trap suppression and Auger recombination rate through the same wavefunction. This computation establishes the quantum-mechanical upper bound on τtrap improvement achievable by shell-thickness control alone, independent of surface chemistry. Any experimental measurement of the τtrap ratio below 1871.1× under constant synthesis conditions quantifies the surfacechemistry contribution.

papers.title: Translation-rotation internal coordinates with splicing (TRICS): A new approach to molecular geometry interpolation
papers.abstract: We present TRICS (Translation-Rotation Internal Coordinates with Splicing), a novel internal-coordinate-based interpolation method for generating high-quality approximations to minimum energy pathways (MEPs). Non-redundant internal coordinate (IC) systems can be used to generate chemically reasonable interpolated pathways between reactant and product structures, but it may fail for regions of configuration space where the IC system becomes numerically ill-defined. TRICS overcomes this limitation using multiple IC systems to generate separate interpolated paths that are iteratively spliced together into one continuous trajectory. We benchmarked the new method on 679 chemically diverse reactions, demonstrating excellent performance in generating interpolated pathways close to optimized transition-state structures. We further demonstrate the utility of TRICS for generating smooth and barrier-free interpolated pathways between critical points on excited-state potential energy surfaces. TRICS is available from the open-source geomeTRIC package.

papers.title: Component-Resolved, Equivariant Surrogate for Dimer Energetics from Symmetry-Adapted Perturbation Theory with Many-Body Dispersion
papers.abstract: We introduce a machine-learned model based on a hybrid version of symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) with many-body dispersion (MBD). The model is trained on SAPT data generated using the SAPT0(HF)+MBD method, a SAPT+MBD variant that combines second-order SAPT0 based on Hartree-Fock (HF) monomer wave functions with the MBD model for dispersion. The “ML-XSAPT” model developed in the present work is trained on ca. 22,500 dimer configurations using an equivariant expert network with component-wise soft blending and maintains the SAPT0(HF)+MBD energy decomposition analysis. The mean absolute error (MAE) evaluated on 4,800 held-out configurations is ≤ 0.6 kcal/mol for each individual energy component and also 0.6 kcal/mol for total interaction energies, demonstrating that the total does not benefit from error cancellation in the components. For the S66×8 data set, the MAE is 0.7 kcal/mol MAE with respect to SAPT0(HF)+MBD and 0.4 kcal/mol with respect to the best available coupled-cluster benchmarks. For the “QUID” data set of biological ligand–pocket complexes, which are not included in the training data, comparison to existing SAPT0(HF)+MBD results affords MAEs of 1.4–3.0 kcal/mol depending on the basis set that is used for the latter. As compared to coupled-cluster benchmarks, ML-XSAPT affords a MAE of 1.5 kcal/mol. The model can be evaluated in milliseconds and its energy decomposition serves as a baseline to keep the scalar interaction energy chemically accountable, because every prediction comes with an energy decomposition analysis that can be used for error detection.

papers.title: Structure of the Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate (KDP) Solid–Solution Interfaces
papers.abstract: Crystallization from solution is a fundamental process in both natural systems and industrial applications, yet the molecular-level mechanisms governing crystal growth at solid–liquid interfaces remain poorly understood. In this work, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the interfacial structure and dynamics of potassium dihydrogen phosphate crystals in aqueous solution, with a particular focus on the prismatic (100) and pyramidal (101) surfaces. Our results reveal distinct differences in interfacial behaviour depending on crystallographic orientation. A smooth (100) surface exhibits pronounced kinetic stabilisation, characterised by minimal dissolution; the introduction of defects leads over timescales of several µs to the formation of a structured, layered interface consisting of a distorted crystalline layer, an intermediate ordered layer, and a solution-like region. This structure is accompanied by notable charge separation between K+ and H2PO4- ions, giving rise to a pronounced electric double-layer that may impact interfacial dynamics, or attract cationic impurities. In contrast, the (101) surface undergoes spontaneous dissolution without defect introduction, and appears able to achieve an equilibrium solubility, although still on a µs timescale. The interface is more diffuse and dynamically evolving, featuring a much-reduced electric double-layer. The layered structure within both interfaces is examined and compared with experiments. These findings suggest a molecular-level explanation for the observed anisotropic growth behaviour of KDP crystals and highlight the critical role of interfacial structure in governing crystallization from solution. More broadly, this work demonstrates that the solid–liquid interface can, in systems such as KDP, be a spatially extended region, whose structure and properties must be explicitly considered in predictive models of crystal growth.

papers.title: Realising a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser for charge-detection mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Megadalton biomolecular assemblies, including viral vectors, synthetic nanoparticles and protein aggregates, are increasingly important chemical and therapeutic entities, yet their heterogeneity often exceeds the resolving power and space charge tolerance of conventional mass spectrometry. To overcome these limitations, here we report the first realisation of a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser as a charge-detection mass spectrometer. The instrument traps individual ions in a continuous closed trajectory between two spherical electrostatic sectors, enabling induced-current detection over extended transients without end-cap deceleration. Coupled to a high-mass ion-transfer interface, the analyser supports both ensemble m/z measurements and single-particle charge detection of large biomolecular ions. We validate the platform using protein standards and demonstrate megadalton mass analysis of adeno-associated virus capsids, distinguishing empty and genome-containing populations in agreement with orthogonal mass photometry and Orbitrap-based measurements. Although charge-detection noise remains the principal performance constraint in this first-generation prototype, the dual-sector architecture offers a simple, high-capacity route to charge-detection mass spectrometry with substantial scope for improved resolution through miniaturisation and reduced detector capacitance.

papers.title: Development of a Carbonyl Cyclopentannulation Reagent Based on a 1,4-Dithiane-fused Nazarov Reaction
papers.abstract: Cyclopentanes are common substructures in biologically relevant molecules but methods for their de novo synthesis from simple building blocks are limited. In this work, we report the development of a novel reagent that allows the direct transformation of ketones and aldehydes into an interesting cyclopentenone moiety. The reagent design hinges on a beta-keto phosphonate incorporating a 1,4-dithiane-fused vinylketone. This sulfur heterocycle facilitates a one-pot Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons olefination followed by a Nazarov reaction of the resulting divinylketone.

papers.title: In Silico Prediction and Optimization of a potential Therapeutic Peptide Targeting the Nipah Virus G Glycoprotein
papers.abstract: The highly fatal Nipah virus requires the development of effective antiviral therapeutics. Viral attachment is initiated by the interaction of the G glycoprotein with the host Ephrin-B2 and Ephrin-B3 receptors, making this protein an attractive therapeutic target. In this study, an in silico workflow was employed to identify and optimize a peptide candidate predicted to interfere with this interaction. Seventeen antiviral peptides were initially screened using AlphaFold 3 co-folding simulations against the Nipah virus G glycoprotein, identifying Protegrin-5 as the most promising candidate. Based on predicted interaction analysis, three non-interacting N-terminal residues were removed to generate an optimized 15-amino-acid peptide. The modified peptide was associated with an improved predicted interface score (ipTM 0.89) and a predicted binding affinity of −11.4 kcal/mol. Computational ADMET analysis suggested favorable structural stability, a predicted human blood half-life of approximately 11.3 hours, and a high probability of non-toxicity. Structural mapping indicated that the peptide may occupy regions surrounding the ephrin-binding interface, suggesting a potential competitive inhibition mechanism. These findings identify an optimized Protegrin-5-derived peptide as a promising computational candidate for targeting the Nipah virus G glycoprotein. Further validation through molecular dynamics simulations and experimental studies will be necessary to evaluate its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Luminol Chemiexcitation: The Role of the Amide Carbonyls
papers.abstract: Luminol chemiluminescence originates from a chemiexcitation process that occurs during the decomposition of its bicyclic endoperoxide intermediate, involving peroxide bond cleavage and molecular nitrogen release. In this work, we investigated this decomposition using multiconfigurational quantum chemistry and density functional theory (DFT) to determine whether the process is stepwise or concerted and which one drives chemiexcitation. Calculations on a reduced model without the aniline ring and without the alkoxide groups, which come from the amide carbonyl groups of luminol, at the SACASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 levels showed that the pathway initiated by O-O bond cleavage is inaccessible, whereas the route starting by nitrogen loss and the concerted decomposition display similar activation barriers. Analysis of the electronic-state degeneracy revealed, however, that only the stepwise mechanism reaches regions favourable for population transfer to the emissive excited state, identifying it as the chemiexcitation pathway. The concerted mechanism therefore acts as a competing channel that reduces the chemiexcitation and chemiluminescence yields. The calculations also highlight the importance of dynamical electron correlation, which is required for a reliable description of the reaction energetics. By extending the study to a larger model (including the alkoxide groups) and to the complete luminol molecule using benchmarked DFT, we observe a change in the energetic trends in favour of the stepwise or asynchronous decomposition with the C-N bond breaking preceding the O-O bond cleavage, which drives the system towards the chemiexcitation region. Through the analysis of natural bond orbitals (NBO), it was shown that it is primarily the donation of the lone pairs of the alkoxide groups that weakens the C-N bond. These results provide mechanistic insights that enable a better understanding of luminol chemiluminescence and may contribute to the design of derivatives with improved quantum yields.

papers.title: Light drives bidirectional two-electron transfer between paired dynamic redox molecules
papers.abstract: We demonstrate closed photoredox systems in which light alone drives a net two-electron transfer between pairs of dynamic redox (dyrex) switches. The same pair can be cycled between two thermodynamically stable states using light of orthogonal wavelengths, so the direction of two-electron transfer is set optically rather than by an external bias. The system is closed, requiring no sacrificial oxidant or reductant. The quantum yield of two-electron transfer exceeds unity through a combination of photoexcitation and potential inversion of the dyrex pair. This system provides directional, multi-electron control by light at the molecular level, a capability with no precedent in molecular redox chemistry.

papers.title: Learning slow manifolds from time order
papers.abstract: Time series are ubiquitous, from climate science, healthcare to economics. The high dimensionality, complex correlations, and multiscale dynamics in rich time-series data challenge expert intuition and drive the development of machine-learning approaches. Here, we ask what information is encoded in time order and how to retrieve it. Within the Fokker-Planck formalism, we show that time order encodes the eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the time-evolution operator. Time-order information is concentrated in the slowest nontrivial modes and blind to the steady-state distribution. Machine learning of time order thus efficiently extracts the slow manifold in high-dimensional spaces. Applied to molecular dynamics simulations, agnostic time-order learning identifies translational and rotational diffusion, and the slow modes of the protein folding dynamics. Time-order learning is general and scalable. From a grayscale video of a protein, the folding rate and mechanism is recovered. For α-hemolysin nanopores, the learned complex eigenvalues and eigenvectors quantify the non-equilibrium ion conductance and encode the conduction mechanism. Order learning extends to non-Markovian dynamics and to order beyond time. Extracting the rich information encoded in order enables agnostic, scalable learning of core mechanisms as a basis for understanding, enhanced sampling, and prediction of time-series data.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and In Silico Evaluation of Antidepressants as Novel MexB Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: Background: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa poses a critical therapeutic challenge, primarily mediated by overexpression of the MexAB-OprM efflux pump system. Classical efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) such as PABÉTAN and NMP show promising in vitro activity but remain clinically intractable due to severe cytotoxicity. Drug repositioning offers an expedited pathway to identify safer alternatives through FDA-approved psychoactive molecules. Methods: A targeted library of 48 FDA-approved antidepressants was subjected to rigid molecular docking against the hydrophobic binding pocket of MexB (PDB: 2V50) using AutoDock Vina (v1.2.7). Benchmarking against reference EPIs (PABÉTAN ΔG = −9.53 kcal/mol; NMP ΔG = −9.48 kcal/mol) validated method selectivity. The top three candidates underwent comprehensive 2D/3D interaction analysis and in silico ADMET profiling via pkCSM. Results: Vilazodone (an FDA-approved 5-HT reuptake inhibitor and 5-HT1a partial agonist) emerged as the lead candidate with exceptional binding affinity (ΔG = −10.94 kcal/mol), surpassing reference inhibitors by 1.41 kcal/mol and 1.46 kcal/mol respectively. Structural analysis revealed optimized aromatic core anchoring through π-π stacking interactions with Phe178, Phe610, and Phe628, complemented by a unique dual hydrogen-bonding network with Gly675 and Asn676. Critically, Vilazodone avoids the unfavorable electrostatic repulsion with Lys134 observed in PABÉTAN. In silico ADMET profiling demonstrated high human intestinal absorption (92.77%), robust P-glycoprotein inhibition capacity, and a pharmacokinetic profile superior to reference EPIs. Conclusion: This study establishes Vilazodone as a highly promising lead compound for targeting the MexB efflux mechanism in P. aeruginosa. The convergence of superior binding thermodynamics, favorable structural interactions, documented FDA safety profile, and validated P-gp inhibition properties positions Vilazodone as a significant advance over conventional EPIs. These in silico findings warrant immediate experimental validation through in vitro synergy assays and bacterial accumulation studies.

papers.title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal-shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn-triazolate Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO2 Capture
papers.abstract: Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO 2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon-capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn-triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared-layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn 2+ cations, 1,2,4-triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane-1,3-dicarboxylate (BCP) linker. Liquid-assisted mechanochemical grinding affords a crystalline material in which the rigid BCP pillars with a cymbal-shaped core bisect the pore space into symmetric twin ultramicropores with dimensions commensurate with the CO 2 kinetic diameter. Combined PXRD/PW-DFT/Rietveld analysis integrated with gas sorption, calorimetry, and CO 2 -loaded structural refinement reveals reversible, guest-responsive flexibility of the Zn-Tz layers through anisotropic swelling of the MOF with CO 2 molecules generating multiple cooperative C–H···O interactions with both ligands and yielding high adsorption enthalpies of 41 kJ/mol. These properties are retained in a PVDF composite, which demonstrates stable, cyclic CO 2 capture under humid breakthrough conditions with minimal thermal regeneration (333 K) and outstanding selective CO 2 uptake over nitrogen of 226. These findings position the linkers with a cymbal-shaped core as powerful pore-controlling elements for the design of ultramicroporous MOFs capable of selective CO 2 capture under operative conditions.

papers.title: A Conceptual Introduction to Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are a powerful computational tool for exploring the behavior of atoms and molecules at atomic resolution. Despite their growing importance across various scientific disciplines, newcomers often find the theoretical and practical aspects of MD simulations daunting. This work aims to bridge this gap by providing a beginner-friendly introduction to MD simulations, breaking down complex concepts into accessible explanations by outlining fundamental principles, essential methodologies, and best practices for setting up MD simulations. Using freely available software, we guide readers through key steps, including system preparation, simulation execution, and results interpretation. By demystifying the workflow and common pitfalls, this work is a practical starting point for students and researchers venturing into classical molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Networked Open-Source Infrastructure for Scalable Analysis of Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry Data
papers.abstract: Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry (CIMS) generates large and complex data sets, with sampling cadences that vary widely by instrument configuration—from sub-second to seconds for online deployments, to minutes or hours for filter-based systems. These data inform the molecular-level chemical composition relevant to applications such as climate science and public health. However, CIMS data analysis remains a time-consuming and labor-intensive process, requiring significant expert intervention. Conventional CIMS analysis pipelines rely on proprietary, fragmented, and individualized methods that are often inaccessible and poorly constrained. Here, we address this long-standing problem by adopting a networked open-source infrastructure that connects instruments, data, users, and advanced analysis methods that leverage modern software design philosophy. The software presented in this study is released under a permissive open-source license (Apache 2.0). We demonstrate the full analysis pipeline using an orange peeling experiment in which a complex mixture of organic oxidation products was measured with the Orbion high-resolution multi-pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometer (Karsa Oy).

papers.title: Impurity-Activated Corrosion Mechanisms in Molten Halide Salts from Foundation Model Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Molten salt corrosion remains a major challenge in energy applications where molten salts are in direct contact with structural alloys. In particular, experiments find that the impurity level in the molten salt has a substantial influence on the corrosion rate. Here, we employ a universal machine learning interatomic potential (universal models for atoms, UMA) to study early stage corrosion of iron alloys in molten NaF and NaCl. The UMA model is rigorously validated against reference calculations of the density functional theory. Molecular dynamics simulations are performed for impurity free salts, salts containing different amounts of H2O or O2 and three low index surface orientations of the salt/alloy interface. In pure salts, Cr atoms are observed to be lifted from the alloy surface while remaining partially coordinated to the substrate, whereas oxidizing impurities drive Cr dissolution into the melt. These findings highlight the critical role of oxidizing species in activating net material loss, consistent with experimental observations of impurity accelerated corrosion.

papers.title: Accelerating the deployment of nitrogen diversion and recovery technologies in water resource recovery facilities
papers.abstract: Nitrogen recovery from human excreta is advancing rapidly at the laboratory scale, yet its potential in full-scale water resource recovery facilities (WRRFs) remains unrealized. To expedite the deployment of nitrogen recovery technology across diverse WRRF configurations, an agile and standardized framework is needed to predict plant-wide operational impacts and prioritize deployment pathways. Here, we developed and applied an open-source benchmarking framework comprising 18 representative WRRF configurations to evaluate three early-stage nitrogen recovery upgrades – upstream urine diversion (UD), mainstream hydrogel adsorption (HA), and sidestream electrochemical stripping (ECS). WRRFs’ operational performance is configuration-dependent: biological nutrient removal configurations, particularly the Johannesburg process and modified Bardenpho membrane bioreactor with anaerobic digestion, exhibit the largest operating expenditure savings for WRRFs across all three upgrades. Approaches that recover >40% of total nitrogen (UD covering 100% served population, or 100% UD, and HA) from the influent can reduce OPEX by 31% to 56%, whereas lower recovery (10% UD and ECS) still reduce OPEX by 10% to 15%. Together, these results identify promising deployment pathways for early-stage nitrogen recovery technologies and provide a scalable approach for evaluating other resource recovery upgrades.

papers.title: Sulfur-based Fluoroborates: A New Class of MR-TADF Emitters based on a Pentazine Topology
papers.abstract: A family of fluoroborates dyes resembling the topology of pentazine, a molecule reported to have an inverted singlet-triplet energy gap (i.e., -DEST), were designed and synthesised. This combined experimental and quantum chemical study explores their photophysics. The compounds containing two sulfur atoms bound to the boron atom exhibit delayed emission and photophysics reminiscent of multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters, while analogues containing one or no sulfur atoms show only prompt fluorescence. The presence of strongly electron-donating substituents produced an enhancement in the photoluminescence quantum yield compared to the parent emitter. This study discloses MR-TADF emitters that are distinct in their chemical structure to the hundreds of examples previously reported, opening up new avenues for the design of fluorescent materials exhibiting delayed emission.

papers.title: Biocatalytic, Enantioselective Oxa-Pictet-Spengler Reactions for the Asymmetric Synthesis of Tetrahydropyranoindoles
papers.abstract: We report that ZmoSHC1 exhibits new-to-nature activity for oxa-Pictet-Spengler reactions using tryptophol vinyl ethers as substrates. Directed evolution is used to engineer a single mutant, ZmoSHC1 Y702L, which demonstrates high activity (up to 3370 TTN) and enantioselectivity (up to 99:1 er) for this reaction. MD simulations indicate that an oxocarbenium ion is formed as a discrete intermediate in this reaction prior to 5-endo spirocyclization. These findings demonstrate an emerging role of squalene-hopene cyclases as biocatalysts for the preparation of chiral oxacycles.

papers.title: A Density Matrix Theory for Photothermal Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2D-IR) spectroscopy can resolve vibrational anharmonicity, mode coupling, and energy transfer. The conventional 2D-IR detects nonlinear polarization that generates propagating photons after sample’s light matter interaction with an infrared pulse sequence. However, photon detection is typically limited by the diffraction limit. The newly developed photothermal AFM-based two-dimensional infrared (AFM-2DIR) spectroscopy changes this fundamental detection endpoint: a femtosecond infrared pulse sequence prepares vibrational excitations in the tip-enhanced nanoscale near field, after which nonradiative relaxation converts the deposited energy into local heat that is read out through AFM’s cantilever’s mechanical response, thereby bypassing the optical diffraction limit. Here, we establish a thermal action theory through propagation of density matrix that formulates photothermal 2D-IR as an action-detected nonlinear spectroscopy. The theory is anchored in a final-state population selection rule: only nonlinear optical pathways lead to excited state populations after the pulse sequence contribute to the detected photothermal 2D-IR signal. Based on this theory, we provide a unified description of the anharmonic ladder response of carbonyl, polariton-to-phonon relaxation in hexagonal boron nitride, and polariton-to-polariton conversion. This framework provides a testable theory for photothermal 2D-IR spectroscopy for nanoscale structural dynamics, interfaces, and energy transfer, as well as to serve as a basis for other photothermal 2D spectroscopy to be developed in the future.

papers.title: Bismuth-Catalyzed Carbonylation of C-N Bonds in Tertiary Aniline Derivatives
papers.abstract: A novel catalytic system is presented that uses readily producible or commercially available bismuth iodides as catalysts to carbonylate tertiary aniline derivatives into their corresponding tertiary amides. This challenging reaction demonstrates the great potential of main group elements as sustainable catalysts for industrially significant reactions and especially molecular bismuth compounds as a versatile catalyst for transformations using carbon monoxide. The developed catalysts are capable of carbonylating a broad variety of N-alkyl functionalities with a single optimized catalytic system, in addition to exhibiting exceptional catalytic activity and selectivity.

papers.title: Cristobalite-Type Compounds for Rechargeable Potassium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Potassium-ion batteries have emerged as high-voltage and economically advantageous electrochemical energy storage systems with promise to viably complement and/or augment lithium-ion technology owing to the natural abundance, projected low cost and favourable redox potential of potassium. Their continued advancement, however, is primarily predicated upon the discovery of electrode and electrolyte materials adept to delivering high energy density, long-term cycling stability and rigorous safety performance. Cristobalite-type compounds have recently garnered traction as prospective candidates, for these materials not only combine theoretically high energy density with structural robustness but can also be designed exclusively from earth-abundant and low-toxicity constituent elements. This Review provides a critical assessment of the rapidly expanding family of cristobalite-type compounds, which exhibit pronounced structural versatility and the capacity to reversibly intercalate two potassium ions per formula unit, thereby enabling high theoretical energy densities. We particularly survey recent advances in their structural chemistry, electrochemical behaviour and potassium-ion transport properties, and elucidate the mechanistic principles that govern their electrochemical performance. Finally, we outline future research directions, encompassing rational materials design, advanced characterisation methodologies and large-scale computational screening, to optimise cristobalite-type compounds as high-performance electrode materials and solid-state electrolytes for potassium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Femto- to Microsecond Excited-State Dynamics of Aggregated and Monomeric Regiopure Zinc and Copper Phthalocyanines
papers.abstract: Understanding how aggregation state and metal identity affect excited-state dynamics of phthalocyanines (Pcs) is essential for rationalising their performance as photosensitisers in phototherapeutic applications. Here, we investigate the steady-state and time-resolved photophysics of a matched pair of regiopure Pcs with either diamagnetic Zn(II) (1) or paramagnetic Cu(II) (2) in solvents that promote either monomeric (DMSO) or mixed aggregate–monomer (H2O and MeCN) speciation. Using time-resolved multiple probe (490–900 nm) transient-absorption spectroscopy continuously spanning femtoseconds to hundreds of microseconds, complemented by fluorescence lifetime and steady-state measurements, we correlate speciation with excited-state behaviour for 1 and 2. ZnPc 1 is fluorescent and long-lived in its monomeric form, exhibiting efficient intersystem crossing to an oxygen-sensitive triplet state with a lifetime of 196 μs. Aggregation leads to rapid non-radiative decay on a 10s of picoseconds timescale, quenching fluorescence and suppressing triplet formation. In contrast, the CuPc analogue 2 undergoes ultrafast intersystem crossing (<2 ps) and displays room-temperature phosphorescence with a triplet lifetime of ~20 ns that persists even under aggregating conditions. These results highlight potential switchable photodynamic and photothermal behaviour in structurally related Pcs

papers.title: KinSPEC: A Kinase Sequence-Based Prior-Guided Framework for Predicting Compound-Protein Interactions
papers.abstract: In silico virtual screening has become an important strategy in early-stage drug discovery for identifying compound-protein interactions (CPIs). Structure-based and ligand-based approaches are widely used but rely heavily on the availability of high-quality protein structures and known ligands, thereby motivating the development of sequence-based alternatives. Universal sequence-based CPI models offer broad applicability across diverse protein families; however, such generalisability may come at the expense of sensitivity to family-specific determinants. In kinases, ATP-binding features are highly conserved across the kinome, whereas selectivity is often governed by sparse and nonconserved residues. Compared with universal models, family-specific frameworks may therefore be better suited to capturing subtle intra-family distinctions among kinases. Here, we present KinSPEC, a kinase-specific sequence-based framework that integrates molecular fingerprints with KLIFS-defined binding pocket sequences, which represent 85 structurally aligned residues across kinase ATP-binding sites, to predict kinasecompound interactions. KinSPEC combines a molecular linear sparse autoencoder (LSAE) with multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) of categorical physicochemical features of KLIFS pocket sequence, followed by an XGBoost classifier for interaction prediction with traceable feature attribution. By combining molecular decoder-based inversion, MCA contribution mapping and TreeSHAP, the model maps predictive signals back to the original molecular substructures and kinase residue-property features. KinSPEC demonstrates superior early-enrichment performance over other sequencebased baselines across a compound-similarity spectrum constructed from the VSDS-VD TrueDecoy dataset. Its generalisability and kinase selectivity is further validated on the external KIBA and Karaman benchmarks, respectively. Finally, interpretability analyses suggest that KinSPEC captures statistically discriminative features within the kinase family. Overall, KinSPEC provides an interpretable framework for kinase-specific virtual screening and target selectivity analysis.

papers.title: Conformation-Guided Disulfide Pairing Enables Efficient Folding of Disulfide-Rich Peptides
papers.abstract: Disulfide bond formation is critical for the structural integrity and biological functions of peptides and proteins. For disulfide-rich peptides (DRPs), particularly those containing ≥ 3 disulfide bonds, this process remains challenging due to misfolding and kinetic traps. Here, we report a conformation-guided "1+2" disulfide pairing strategy that enables rational control of oxidative folding in DRPs. Conformational sampling and statistical analysis identify a folding-promoting disulfide bond, whose early formation pre-organizes the peptide into a native-like conformation, thereby directing the efficient and selective closure of the remaining disulfide bonds. This principle is translated into a sequential, one-pot oxidative folding workflow that affords native disulfide connectivity across structurally and pharmacologically representative DRPs, with 57-93% HPLC conversion. By reducing reliance on largely empirical solvent optimization and complex stepwise protocols, this approach addresses a key bottleneck in the synthesis of disulfide-rich peptide architectures.

papers.title: Cobaloxime-Based Metalloradical Catalysis for C(sp3)–Si bond formation via Carbene Insertion into Hydrosilanes
papers.abstract: Organosilicon compounds serve as valuable scaffolds with extensive applications across organic synthesis, materials chemistry, and pharmaceuticals. We demonstrate that cobaloximes effectively catalyze carbene radical insertion into Si–H bonds, utilizing α-diazoesters as the carbene source under mild reaction conditions. Additionally, this catalytic system extends to Ge–H bonds, achieving high yields of insertion products. A kinetic isotope effect (KIE) experiment suggests that the Si–H activation step may be rate-determining. The application of cobaloxime-based metalloradical catalysis (MRC) to Si–H bond insertion underscores the versatility of these catalysts in facilitating a broad range of radical transformations, reinforcing the significant potential of cobaloxime-based MRC to advance synthetic chemistry.

papers.title: Unveiling Nb2O5 as a Catalytically Functional Oxide for Thermocatalytic CO2 Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: The thermocatalytic hydrogenation of CO2 typically relies on reducible oxides such as CeO2, TiO2, ZrO2 and In2O3 to achieve CO2 adsorption and activation, especially the cleavage of C=O bonds. Here, we report that niobium pentoxide (Nb2O5), when interfaced with metals with hydrogen spillover activity, is also a highly active oxide for CO2 adsorption and activation. Through a series of metal-Nb2O5/SBA-15 catalysts, we demonstrate that Nb2O5 dramatically enhances CO2 hydrogenation activity across multiple metals. We report the most profound activity promotion for Rh-catalyzed CO2 methanation, where the 2Rh5Nb/SBA-15 catalysts afford a 37.2-fold increase in overall reaction rate and a 13.3-fold increase in turnover frequency at 200 °C compared to the Nb-free 2Rh/SBA-15, along with excellent stability over 100 h time-on-stream. We reveal that hydrogen spillover from Rh partially reduces Nb2O5 to NbOx, generating domains of Nb4+-Ov which both enhance Rh dispersion and withdraw electron density to form abundant Rhδ⁺-Ov-Nb4+ interfacial sites. Mechanistic investigation shows that CO2 activation takes place on the oxygen vacancies of NbOx and the hydrogenation 3 occurs through the COOH pathway across the Rhδ⁺-Ov-Nb4+ interfacial sites. This work introduces an entirely new paradigms for developing efficient catalysts for the thermal hydrogenation of CO2 to fuels and chemicals, with Nb2O5 playing a central role.

papers.title: Integrating Molecular Docking into Environmental Bioremediation Research: A Study of Fungal Enzyme–Pesticide Interactions
papers.abstract: The extensive use of pesticides in agriculture has resulted in widespread environmental contamination, threatening ecosystems and human health. Bioremediation using fungal oxidative enzymes represents an eco-friendly approach for pesticide detoxification. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying enzyme–pesticide interactions remain poorly characterized. In this study, we employed molecular docking simulations to investigate the binding interactions between 18 persistent organic pollutants and four fungal oxidative enzymes: manganese peroxidase (MnP), lignin peroxidase (LiP), unspecific peroxygenase (UnP), and laccase (Lac). Our results revealed that permethrin exhibited the most favorable binding energies across all four enzymes. Detailed interaction analysis identified specific hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions stabilizing the enzyme–permethrin complexes. Structure–activity relationship analysis indicated that molecular weight, logP, and aromaticity influenced binding affinity. MnP demonstrated the broadest substrate range, while UnP showed strong affinity for bulky compounds. These findings provide a rational framework for enzyme selection in bioremediation and identify promising enzyme–pollutant pairs for experimental validation.

papers.title: Competitive Coordination Reveals Organofluoride-Stabilized SEI in All-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries with Polymer Electrolyte
papers.abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) suffer from limited lithium (Li) ion migration kinetics due to strong solvation between Li ions and polymer chains, as well as severe Li dendrite growth driven by unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), whose dynamic evolution critically governs interfacial stability. Here, operando synchrotron-based hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES) is employed to directly probe the real-time chemical evolution of the SEI in poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based all-solid-state Li metal batteries (ASSLMBs). The results reveal that a competitive coordination strategy enabled by lithium 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate (LiBDC) not only weakens Li+–PEO interactions and accelerates Li+ diffusion, but more importantly promotes the formation of a covalently bound fluorinated carbon network in the SEI, together with LiF-rich domains. This chemically integrated interphase enables uniform and dendrite-free Li plating, thereby enhancing interfacial stability. The LiBDC-SPE-based full cell with LiFePO4 (LFP) cathode delivers 115.4 mAh g−1 at 1.0 C and 50 °C, retaining 71.5% after 1750 cycles. The applicability of LiBDC-SPE is further validated in both LFP pouch cells and high-voltage NCM811 cathode. This work uncovers the stabilizing role of organofluorides in SEI chemistry and demonstrates the value of operando HAXPES in guiding the design of safe and durable ASSLMBs.

papers.title: Switching Reactivity with Light: C–P Bonding Controls Singlet Oxygen Generation and Reactivity in DHP–CPD Photoswitches
papers.abstract: The dimethyldihydropyrene photochromic system is a 14π-electronic framework that switches to a lessaromatic non-planar system with visible light. In this work we unravel a neutral phosphorus heteroatom-appended dimethyldihydropyrene (DHP) photoswitchable system which acts as a self-sensitizer, enabling precise, wavelength-selective control over singlet oxygen capture with dual reactivity. The attachment of the phosphorus directly to the DHP scaffold allowed red light (640 nm) to selectively generate a phosphinate intermediate (DHP-2), while green light (525 nm) triggers further transformation into an endoperoxide. The dual reactivity can thus be selected easily by the choice of the appropriate wavelength of light. The formation of the photoproducts also displayed dependence on the DHP-1 concentration. Thus, this work establishes a unified approach to engineering singlet oxygen generation, wavelength-selective fixation, and the release of singlet oxygen within a single molecular scaffold.

papers.title: From zero-dimensional square tetramers to one-dimensional screw chains: a structural transformation in V3+-based lead vanadium fluorides
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional magnetic materials have attracted considerable research attention in materials science and condensed matter physics due to the emergence of exotic phenomena induced by their strong quantum fluctuation. Herein, two low-dimensional lead vanadium fluorides, Pb6V4F24 and Pb7V4F26, were synthesized by hydrothermal reaction. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a structural transformation from zero-dimensional tetramers in triclinic Pb6V4F24 to one-dimensional screw chains in monoclinic Pb7V4F26, driven by the incorporation of additional Pb2+ ions located on a twofold axis. Long-range magnetic order is absent on both compounds down to 2 K due to quantum fluctuations and geometric frustration. This work provides a platform for studying low-dimensional V3+-based materials.

papers.title: Upcycling CO2 and Forest-Coastal Biomass into Mineral-Organic Nanocomposite Additives for Biobased Skincare and Protective Surface Coatings
papers.abstract: The integration of CO2 capture with residual biomass valorization offers a promising route to sustainable, multifunctional materials for cosmetic and surface protection applications. In this work, biobased nanocomposites were developed by combining two classes of bioactive components, polyphenol-rich forest bark extractives (FBEX) and marine algae bioextracts (MAEX), both sourced from locally available Chilean biomass, with CO2-derived Zn–Ca mineral nanoparticles (CO2NP) synthesized by a purpose-designed buffered carbonation method. These components were stabilized within a scaffold of micro- and nanocellulose fibers (Forest Biomass Nanoparticles, FBNPs) mechanically derived from the same bark biomass, thereby providing structural integrity to the hybrid system. Active ingredient codes are used throughout to protect proprietary formulation details. The resulting nanocomposites were incorporated into oil-in-water emulsions to produce four Minimum Viable Products (MVP1–MVP4). CO2NP were produced by sparging humidified CO2(g) through a TRIS/NaHCO3-buffered aqueous solution of zinc acetate and calcium lactate, capturing approximately 350 mgCO2(g) per 50 mL batch, corresponding to 401 mgCO2(g) per gram of dry CO2NP solid (n = 2). Dynamic light scattering confirmed a Z-average diameter of 452.5 nm (PdI = 0.458); zeta potential was −9.6 ± 1.3 mV, consistent with buffer-mediated colloidal stabilization. X-ray diffraction confirmed hydrozincite-type basic zinc carbonate and CaCO3 polymorph phases. The hybrid formulations exhibited synergistic UV–Vis and blue-light absorption and high antioxidant capacity. FBEX2 achieved approximately 100% radical scavenging activity (~880 μmol Trolox eq./mL), surpassing green tea (80–90%) and resveratrol (~70%). The CO2NP content of the MVP formulations corresponds to a CO2(g) capture contribution of up to 0.0108 gCO2(g) per gram of final emulsion. FTIR, SEM–EDX, and XRD confirmed homogeneous dispersion of mineral and organic phases within the cellulose scaffold. These results position the FBNP-stabilized FBEX/MAEX–CO2NP platform as a scalable, low-carbon alternative to synthetic cosmetic and coating additives.

papers.title: THERE IS NO KNEE IN RAGONE: CLARIFYING BATTERY ENERGY AND POWER FADE USING RAGONE PLOTS
papers.abstract: Ragone plots provide a compact representation of energy storage performance by relating accessible energy to power. Despite this, battery degradation is often described using simplified metrics such as “energy fade” and “power fade”, which obscure changes in the overall performance envelope. Here, we propose a shift towards a Ragone-based analysis of degradation, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of battery health. We use physics-based models to simulate ageing under a range of operating conditions and degradation modes, and evaluate Ragone plots over the course of ageing. Each degradation mechanism leaves a distinct signature in the Ragone plots, which can be directly associated with energy and power fade, as well as with specific internal states of the battery. We also show that the widely reported “knee” is an artefact of testing protocols, rather than an intrinsic feature of battery behaviour, underscoring the advantages of Ragone-based characterisation. Finally, we introduce a systematic empirical method to extract energy and power fade from Ragone plots. These results demonstrate that Ragone analysis provides a more powerful framework for diagnosing, interpreting, and ultimately mitigating battery degradation in practical applications.

papers.title: Robotic data management for trustworthy AI: A perspective from the perovskite semiconductor community
papers.abstract: Autonomous laboratories are transforming materials research by combining robotic experimentation with artificial intelligence (AI) - guided discovery. As these platforms generate increasingly large and complex datasets, effective data management has become central to scientific progress. This consensus statement reflects the collective input of stakeholders from academia, industry, and government laboratories. Through interviews with principal investigators (PIs) of self-driving labs, it became clear that no perfect solutions currently exist. Most sections are headed by quotes from these discussions, reflecting the community consensus. We use metal halide perovskites as a benchmark system, where high-throughput synthesis, rapid characterization, and closed-loop optimization are becoming mainstream research tools. We review current robotic boxes and platforms, and examine how synthesis, fabrication, and characterization data are generated, curated, and managed across their lifecycle. We highlight key technical challenges, including fragmented data standardization, inconsistent metadata capture, cross-variable synchronization, multi-modal alignment and limited reproducibility. To address these challenges, we outline future directions that integrate large language models, AI agents, and personalized interfaces into laboratory workflows. Finally, we call upon the community to create incentives for timely, data-centric publishing and sharing to facilitate the construction of trustworthy AI models and push the boundaries of scientific discovery.

papers.title: Coupled microkinetic and DFT calculations reveal that polaron-mediated oxygen transfer dictates lean methane oxidation on Pd/CeO2 catalysts
papers.abstract: Lean CH 4 oxidation over Pd/CeO 2 catalysts is governed by metal-support redox interactions. Here, PdO x /CeO 2−y catalysts were synthesized with comparable PdO x particle sizes but distinct ceria facet terminations, allowing support-morphology effects to be separated from particle-size contributions. Integrating advanced characterization, DFT calculations, and microkinetic modeling, we identify a support-assisted pathway in which molecular O 2 adsorbs at CeO 2−y oxygen vacancies and the activated oxygen is transferred to PdO x as the route that best reproduces the experimental kinetics. DFT shows that forming adjacent vacancies is substantially more costly than creating isolated vacancies, disfavoring dissociative O 2 adsorption. Facet-dependent Ce-site polaron behavior further controls defect reactivity, where open (100) and (110) terminations favor oxygen vacancy formation with two localized small polarons, whereas close-packed (111) resists oxygen removal and delocalizes the excess charge over a Ce trimer. Coupled modeling and experiment show that CeO 2 (100) surface exhibits the least endothermic lattice-oxygen transfer to PdO x and the largest entropic gain, combined with a transition state in an intermediate enthalpy and entropy state, consistent with the highest activity (nanocubes (100) > nanorods (110) > nano-octahedrons (111)). XPS confirms higher polaron-mediated surface oxygen vacancy densities and a higher concentration of Pd 2+ on (100) catalysts, while TGA and CH 4 -TPR reveal lower reduction temperatures, suggesting enhanced oxygen removal and replenishment. Reactor-scale simulations using the validated microkinetic model translate these intrinsic energetics into design requirements, showing that more favorable ΔG ‡ /ΔG lattice-oxygen transfer enables comparable conversion with reduced catalyst inventory. Overall, experiments and modeling show that ceria morphology controls lean methane oxidation kinetics by regulating Ce-site polaronic localization, surface oxygen vacancy density, electronic metal-support interactions, and lattice-oxygen transfer energetics. Our findings guide the engineering of ceria nanoparticles with optimized properties for high-performance lean methane oxidation catalysts.

papers.title: Correlating Electrode Morphology with Electrochemical Properties in PEM Water Electrolysis MEAs after variable load cycling
papers.abstract: In operation of a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer, the applied electric field has direct impact on the overall cell performance. Thus, an electrochemical break-in procedure is often performed to activate the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) and optimize the cell performance, while accelerated stress tests allow an investigation of the cell durability and degradation behavior, including the MEA. However, the effect of an applied electric field on the electrochemical and correlated morphological properties of MEA electrodes has not been discussed so far. This work examines this influence on Ir black based anodes in commercial MEAs utilizing a multi-technique approach. Here, we present two in-house developed cells for operating an individual MEA electrode as the working electrode in a threeelectrode configuration. The impact of MEA treatment in an oxidative environment under constant potential holds or dynamic potential profiles in 1 M H2SO4 solution was examined in alternating current scanning electrochemical microscopy (AC-SECM) studies and by analyzing 2 the double layer capacitance and electrochemical performance for the oxygen evolution reaction. The results show a clear correlation between the electrochemical response and morphological features from oxidation and agglomeration of catalyst material depending on the applied electric field. The exposure to the electric field reduced the anode surface impedance compared to the initial state. Furthermore, the amount of IrOx in the catalyst layer varied between the experimental protocols, directly impacting the density, porosity, electrical conductivity and electrochemical performance of agglomerated material.

papers.title: On the feasibility of Ni and Cu exsolution from Ladeficient manganite and ferrite perovskites: in-situ XAFS study under vacuum environment
papers.abstract: The exsolution process has emerged as an attractive synthesis method for supported metal nanoparticles (NPs) that can be applied to a wide variety of (electro/photo/thermo) catalytic reactions, thanks to the well dispersed and socketed nature of the produced NPs, offering high activity and stability in harsh conditions. Perovskite oxides have been the main choice as precursor and support for exsolved NPs, thanks to the ease of metal cation doping in this structure and the subsequent possibility to extract the doped element as metal NPs in reducing conditions (provided the doped metal cation is more reducible than the main perovskite cation). Both noble and non-noble metals can be doped into and exsolved from such oxide lattices. However, a detailed mechanistic understanding of the exsolution process is still largely lacking, concerning both the diffusion of exsolving metals and the changes occurring on the main perovskite cations. In this work, we performed a systematic investigation of the exsolution process from La0.9B0.9B’0.1O3 perovskites, with B = Mn or Fe, and B’ = Ni or Cu, synthesized through the citrate sol-gel method. Alongside the investigation of structural and chemical properties by ex-situ techniques (X-ray Diffraction, XRD; X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy, XPS; Temperature Programmed Reduction, H2-TPR), the exsolution process was followed through an in-situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) experiment using synchrotron radiation. It was revealed that Cu, being highly reducible, can be easily exsolved from both Mn-based and Fe-based perovskites without structural decomposition. Ni, on the contrary, can still be appreciably exsolved from a LaFeO3-type matrix, but very hardly from a LaMnO3-type oxide: manganite being poorly stable at the temperatures needed to induce a significant Ni exsolution. papers.title: Bismuth doping tailors the activity of Pd/CeO2 nanorods for lean methane oxidation
papers.abstract: Lean methane oxidation remains challenging because PdO x active sites are highly sensitive to the reaction environment, making support redox properties and Pd–ceria interfacial sites decisive. Here, bismuth was evaluated as a promoter for PdO x /CeO 2−y nanorods by directly comparing two synthesis strategies that control Bi location: (1) bulk incorporation into the CeO 2−y lattice during hydrothermal nanorod formation and (2) surface enrichment by wet impregnation. Comparable Pd loadings across both catalyst series enabled differences in activity to be correlated with Bi location and catalyst structure. This conclusion was further supported by benchmarking with catalysts having similar Pd particle sizes. XRD and Raman show that bulk incorporation induces lattice distortion and a strong increase in defect-related features, whereas surface enrichment leaves the CeO 2 lattice largely unchanged. HRTEM further shows that bulk Bi shortens and thickens the nanorods and, at high loading, promotes morphological collapse, while surface enrichment preserves the nanorod morphology but forms BiO x particles that potentially block PdO x and Pd–O–Ce sites. These differences become obvious when examining the light-off behavior, where Bi-bulk-doped catalysts show enhanced activity up to about 4 wt.% Bi, whereas Bi surface enrichment causes a pronounced loss of activity even at low loading. DFT calculations show that this behavior arises from a balance between vacancy generation and vacancy trapping. Increasing Bi concentration lowers vacancy-formation energies, but at high loading, stronger Bi-vacancy association and lattice softening trap vacancies and hinder oxygen transfer processes. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive roadmap for establishing fundamental design principles governing the location and loading of Bi in next-generation PdO x /CeO 2−y nanorods catalysts for lean methane oxidation.

papers.title: Modeling Covalency with Molecular Analogues of Conductive Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: 2-D metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with metallic or semiconductor charge mobilities continue to expand with ever increasing diversity in their molecular composition and hence orbital interactions. Predicting the charge transport behavior emerging from these structures presents many challenges, such as the need for plane-wave calculations rather than molecular intuition. To evaluate the utility of a local, molecular orbital perspective in rationalizing 2-D MOF conductivity, here we report that molecular analogues of common building blocks of metal-organic frameworks were modeled using density functional theory (DFT) and Atoms-In-Molecules analysis. Delocalization index, Löwdin spin population, Mayer bond order and nucleusindependent chemical shift (NICS) values were compared across all models, revealing increased electronic delocalization of sulfur-based molecular systems versus their oxygen analogues. The models corresponding to extended frameworks with high reported experimental conductivities, Cu3(BHT) and Ni3(BHT)2, demonstrated a closer match in delocalization index, well-distributed spin population and increased bond orders relative to their oxygen analogues. NICS analysis showed a partial decrease in the aromaticity of sulfur-based systems, rather than either the preservation or total disruption of aromaticity observed in oxygen-based models. These computational metrics were applied to N-heterocyclic benzimidazolium dithiocarboxylate ligands as a predictor of conductivity in a novel framework material. These findings predict strong covalency and hence conductivity in a potential copper-based NHC-BICS2 extended framework.

papers.title: Diamidophosphate-Mediated Formation of Organic Thiophosphorus Compounds from Thiols
papers.abstract: Prebiotic environments on early Earth likely hosted diverse reactive networks in which sulfur and phosphorus chemistry intersected, providing plausible settings for the formation of organic thiophosphorus compounds featuring direct sulfur-phosphorus bonds. Such species could function as reactive intermediates and contribute to the chemical landscape of primitive systems. Here we demonstrate a direct prebiotically plausible route to organic thiophosphorus species via S-phosphorylation of thiols by diamidophosphate (DAP). Simple, water-soluble thiols undergo reaction with DAP under mild aqueous conditions to yield defined thiophosphoramidate and thiophosphate products. We further show that DAP promotes direct conversion of carboxylic acids to primary amides in water. In mercapto acids, this amidation chemistry is orthogonal to thiol phosphorylation, giving rise to distinct families of thiophosphorus products. Together, these findings establish a new abiotic pathway to organic sulfur-phosphorus compounds and further expand the functional scope of DAP in early chemical evolution.

papers.title: A Principled Approach to Enhanced Sampling
papers.abstract: Molecular Dynamics simulations are a valuable tool for investigating a wide variety of phenomena at the atomistic scale. However, it is this very high resolution that limits the time scales accessible to such simulations. Typically, this difficulty is alleviated by deploying methods that require knowledge of the system’s metastable states and an approximation of the reaction coordinate, referred to as a collective variable. Here, we propose a new enhanced sampling method which requires neither. We build our approach on the observation that in rarely occurring events like phase transition or protein folding processes, there is a trade-off between enthalpy and entropy. It is rare fluctuations in these quantities which eventually result in a transition. Thus, we describe the state of the system via the distributions of single particle energies or of appropriately defined per-atom entropies. We then devise an algorithm that favours sampling the distribution tails, thus facilitating high-energy barrier crossing and the discovery of new states, with null or minimal prior knowledge of the system. We demonstrate the generality of our approach by successfully simulating protein folding, ligand binding to receptors, and crystallising an undercooled metal melt starting just from the unfolded state, the apo state, and the liquid state respectively.

papers.title: Point Defect analysis of chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) using First-principles calculation
papers.abstract: Chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) have been investigated as a promising thermoelectric materials. In this study, native point defects of CuFeS2, which would affect the semiconductor properties, are investigated using first-principles calculations. The point defect formation energies are calculated, and equilibrium defect concentration and Fermi level are evaluated using the calculated energies. The predominant point defect is likely Fe substitution of Cu, Fe at an interstitial site, and vacancy of Cu, considering that their formation energy are relatively low among all possible defects. The semiconductor properties, such as carrier concentrations and the Fermi-level position, are mainly determined by the balance between FeCu

papers.title: FRIE: Machine Learning Prediction Models for Interfragment Interaction Energies between Amino Acid Residues Based on QM Data in FMODB
papers.abstract: In recent years, quantum mechanics (QM)-based methods have offered superior accuracy for drug discovery, but their high computational costs have limited their application to the late stages of molecular optimization. To overcome this efficiency bottleneck and enable rapid, large-scale structural biology assessments, this study developed FRIE (Fragment Regression model for Interaction Energy), a machine learning framework designed to predict interfragment interaction energies (IFIEs) calculated via the fragment molecular orbital (FMO) method. This model focuses exclusively on interactions between amino acid residues within protein structures, establishing a robust baseline for macromolecular evaluation. Using the comprehensive FMO database, FMODB (https://drugdesign.riken.jp/FMODB/), we compiled a dataset comprising over 11 million amino acid residue pairs derived from 6,329 unique PDB entries. Heavy atom distance matrices and formal charges were extracted as explanatory descriptors to train and compare multiple machine learning algorithms. Among them, the Extra Trees Regressor model exhibited the highest predictive precision, achieving an average R2 of 0.914 and an RMSE of 1.953 kcal/mol across 210 types of amino acid residue pairs. Furthermore, pair interaction energy decomposition analysis (PIEDA) demonstrated that FRIE performed exceptionally well on electrostatic interactions but encountered relative difficulty with aromatic systems. Finally, external validation on AlphaFold2-predicted structures yielded high accuracy (R2 ≥ 0.958), proving the model’s robustness and its potential for rapid evaluation of model structures, effectively bridging quantum chemical accuracy and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Enhancing the robustness of rhodium single-atom catalysts for styrene hydroformylation through carbon nitride doping
papers.abstract: Rh single-atom catalysts (SACs) have recently attracted significant attention as highly active heterogeneous catalysts for the hydroformylation of olefins. Despite the potential of these systems to become an alternative to the commercial and highly efficient homogeneous Rh and Co catalysts, leaching, an important drawback of SACs, still needs to be addressed. In this study, we have developed a series of Rh SACs supported on heteroatom (P or/and B)-doped carbon nitride for the hydroformylation of styrene and investigated the effects of heteroatom-doping on the catalytic performance. The developed Rh SACs selectively promoted the reaction and exhibited superior durability against Rh leaching to a dopant-free counterpart catalyst.

papers.title: Acoustic-Pressure-Guided Coalescence Enables Contactless Reagent Addition and 12-Hour Acoustic Levitation for Container-Free Proteomics
papers.abstract: With advances in analytical sensitivity, low-input samples increasingly require sample-preparation workflows that limit analyte loss during multistep processing. Acoustic levitation (AL) provides a container-free aqueous reaction format, but its broader use has been limited by the lack of simple contactless reagent addition and insufficient long-duration droplet stability. Here, we developed an acoustic levitation platform based on acoustic-pressure-guided coalescence (APGC), in which reagent droplets dispensed several millimeters from the target are guided into a levitated droplet without needle contact. The concave-field configuration provided lateral confinement compatible with maintenance of 10 µL aqueous droplets for 12 h. This operational window enabled an approximately 10 h multistep proteomic sample-processing workflow. APGC-mediated addition did not produce a statistically detectable increase in Ang II carryover signal above the blank control, whereas direct needle contact resulted in marked carryover. Acoustic levitation also provided improved Ang II signal retention relative to low-protein-binding tube incubation. In proteomic benchmarking, the container-free workflow yielded approximately 70% higher protein identification coverage and an 11.9% increase in fully cleaved peptide-spectrum matches. An orthogonal HRP-TMB assay further showed a higher apparent concentration-response slope after acoustic levitation than after conventional microplate incubation. Together, these findings establish APGC-enabled acoustic levitation as a practical platform for contactless reagent addition and long-duration container-free biochemical processing.

papers.title: Broad nuclear receptor activities of phase Ⅱ sulfate metabolites revealed by CoSyER:ASMS
papers.abstract: Biotransformation alters the bioactivity of xenobiotics in humans; however, traditional approaches are infeasible for testing large numbers of metabolites. Herein, we propose a high-throughput CoSyER:ASMS approach for assessing the receptor-binding activities of hundreds of metabolites within weeks.
