As proof of concept, 139 sulfate metabolites were synthesized from 222 ToxCast chemicals using an optimized one-pot combinatorial synthesis approach. Four nuclear receptors (PPARγ, PXR, ERRγ, and FXR) were further selected for AS-MS analysis to evaluate binding activities of 139 sulfate metabolites and corresponding parent compounds, covering 1,112 binary interactions. Interestingly, sulfate metabolites exhibited broad nuclear receptor binding activities towards PPARγ and PXR, with 29 and 25 ligands detected by AS-MS, respectively. Bioactivities of triclosan sulfate and 1-hydroxypyrene sulfate were validated using synthesized standards and an orthogonal fluorescence assay. By employing CoSyER:ASMS, this study highlights the broad nuclear receptor binding activities of phase II sulfate metabolites.

papers.title: Protodeboronation Enables the Formation of Dimethylsulfonium Cysteine for Controlled One-Pot Peptide and Protein Modification
papers.abstract: The transformation of cysteine residues into more reactive species is a powerful entry point to post-translational protein modification and the synthesis of complex bioactive peptides, yet existing approaches often suffer from limited selectivity and undesired side reactions. Here we report iodomethylboronic acid (IMBA) as a small alkylating agent that selectively converts cysteine residues in peptides and proteins into dimethylsulfonium species via rapid protodeboronation. The resulting S,S-dimethylsulfonium-modified cysteine can be stabilized at low temperature. Subsequent β-elimination furnishes dehydroalanine under mild and biocompatible conditions. Multiple cysteine residues can be simultaneously modified. The overall transformation generates only iodide, boric acid and dimethyl sulfide as byproducts. Full conversion of cysteine is achieved with low equivalents of IMBA reagent, enabling direct downstream diversification of the resulting dehydroalanine with nucleophiles and eliminating the need for conventional two-step workflows.

papers.title: Stereospecific Engagement of a Methyl-Sensitive ECL2 Anchor Site in 5-HT₂A by α-Substituted NBOH Derivatives
Interfacial structure of conjugated polymer photocatalysts with water and scavengers for sacrificial hydrogen evolution
papers.abstract: Conjugated polymers have emerged as competitive photocatalysts for the sustainable production of hydrogen from water. Their synthetic versatility allows for systematic tuning of their opto-electronic properties and polarity to improve visible-light-driven hydrogen production. One challenge in the field is the lack of understanding of interactions of water and reactants on the molecular level with the photocatalyst. Here we probe the molecular structure of different polymer-water interfaces and link structural motifs to trends in catalytic efficiency and wettability. We study two polymers with a fluorene-co-dibenzo[b,d]thiophene sulfone backbone, where one polymer has n-dodecyl sidechains and one bears significantly more hydrophilic ethylene glycol sidechains. Additionally, we study a polymer with a fluorene-co-phenylene backbone and bearing n-dodecyl sidechains. A combination of phase-resolved and conventional sum frequency generation spectroscopy revealed that, despite different conjugated backbones and sidechain structures, the interfacial water structure was qualitatively similar for the probed polymers, where the net ordering was higher in alkaline environments compared to acidic environments. We associate this observation with a pH dependent negative surface charge. The similarity of the water structure at the different polymer surfaces suggests that variations in hydrogen production cannot be solely attributed to polymer-water interactions, but rather to selective interactions with sacrificial electron donors, so called scavengers. Both tested scavengers, triethylamine and ascorbic acid, influenced the interfacial water structure of polymers with n-dodecyl sidechains. Contrary to this, the interfacial structure of the more hydrophilic polymer with ethylene glycol sidechains was unaffected by the scavengers, which likely relates to its higher hydrogen evolution rate. As such, the work provides valuable insights into the interface of these photocatalysts with scavengers. This will be of particular importance when considering value-added oxidations, such as biomass oxidation coupled to hydrogen evolution which will require a balance of accessing protons, water and reductants.

papers.title: 25 Years of Cardiac Ion Channel QSAR: From hERG Dominance to Multi-Channel Modelling
papers.abstract: In 2013 the Comprehensive in vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) initiative proposed multi-channel assessment for proarrhythmic risk evaluation, yet ligand-based predictive modelling has remained largely single-channel. To quantify and explain this mismatch, we survey 146 QSAR and machine learning studies on cardiac ion channels published between 2001 and early 2026. Across this period, 90% of studies target hERG as their sole ion channel endpoint—a proportion reflecting regulatory incentives, data availability, and research inertia rather than scientific necessity. Although public data for Nav1.5 and Cav1.2 were sufficient for modelling years earlier, both channels received only isolated studies until 2022. Since then, multi-channel modelling has expanded substantially, with multiple groups now addressing hERG, Nav1.5, and Cav1.2 jointly. In contrast, two CiPA channels, Kv4.3 and Kir2.1, remain entirely unmodelled due to genuine data scarcity. Closing the remaining gaps will require coordinated data release (or federated learning) for neglected channels, methods suited to data-scarce targets, and standardised benchmarks enabling rigorous progress tracking—none of which individual research groups can establish alone.

papers.title: Chemically Interpretable Explanations for Molecular Property Prediction via Fragment-Level Shapley Values
papers.abstract: Machine learning has emerged as a powerful approach for molecular property prediction and drug discovery. However, the black-box nature of many machine learning models limits their interpretability, trustworthiness, and adoption in interdisciplinary research settings. This is especially the case in molecular machine learning, where explanations of model predictions are used for informed decision-making and downstream tasks. Shapley values, originating from cooperative game theory, provide a principled framework for attributing model predictions to individual input features. However, existing Shapley value-based explanations for molecular machine learning often rely on sampling-based approximations or operate at the level of abstract features, which can reduce attribution stability and limit chemical interpretability and actionability. Here, we introduce a fragment-level Shapley value framework that enables the exact computation of feature contributions at the level of chemically meaningful fragments for molecular property predictions without relying on sampling or feature imputation. By decomposing molecules into fragments, the proposed approach yields actionable explanations that can be directly related to established chemical concepts. We apply the method post hoc to random forest and graph convolutional network models using common molecular representations, including extended-connectivity fingerprints and molecular graphs. The approach is evaluated across three representative property prediction tasks: aqueous solubility, mutagenicity, and antiviral potency. Fragment-level Shapley values reproduce wellestablished chemical trends, identify known toxicophores, and enable guided molecular optimization. In addition, the method provides insights into model learning characteristics and helps delineate the applicability domain, particularly in settings with limited and structurally biased data. Overall, this work demonstrates that adapting Shapley values to chemically meaningful fragments enables interpretable explanations for molecular machine learning models, supporting molecular optimization and model validation.

papers.title: Chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry with double helical inversion
papers.abstract: Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under non-equilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules ( MR ) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers ( SaS ) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double helical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

papers.title: Confinement of the Oxygen Reduction Active Zone in Protonic Ceramic Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalytic reactions in porous mixed-conducting solids enable energy conversion technologies from fuel cells to electrolyzers, yet the interplay between molecular-level rate-determining steps and their macroscopic spatial extent remains poorly understood. Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs), in which the cathodic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) proceeds in H + /O 2− /e − triple-conducting oxides, exemplify this challenge: facile bulk proton diffusion is conventionally assumed to spread the active reaction zone ( L eff ) throughout the entire porous electrode. Here, we transform this understanding by bridging atomic-scale kinetics with macroscopic spatial utilization. By coupling in-situ modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with hydrogen/deuterium isotope-resolved impedance analysis, we identify the vacancy-assisted dissociation of accumulated superoxide (O 2 − ) into active O − species as the molecular-scale rate-determining step. Crucially, integrating these surface kinetics with porous-electrode theory reveals that this O⁻ formation acts as a kinetic sink, consuming protons near the electrolyte interface before they can penetrate the electrode bulk. As a result, the overall ORR reaction is confined to only a 110 nm zone in state-of-the-art PrBa 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 1.5 Fe 0.5 O 5+δ cathodes at 600 °C, leaving ~98% of the porous scaffold electrochemically inert. Overcoming the interfacial proton exchange barrier to expand L eff , rather than solely accelerating surface kinetics, defines a design principle for porous mixed-conducting electrodes.

papers.title: Armstrong's Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM)
papers.abstract: Traditional electron-configuration notation (e.g., 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6) represents multi-electron systems using integer orbital occupations that reflect dominant configurations but do not explicitly encode the multi-configurational nature of correlated electronic states. In wavefunction-based electronic structure theory, the electronic state is expressed as a linear combination of configurations, each assigning integer electron occupations to orbitals and contributing with a finite coefficient. Standard notation typically reflects only the dominant configuration, while the underlying distribution of contributing configurations remains implicit. This work introduces Armstrong’s Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM), a representational framework that replaces fixed integer occupations with bounded intervals derived from the configuration interaction expansion of the electronic wavefunction. For each subshell, AREECM determines minimum and maximum occupation numbers nMin​ and nMax, over a selected configuration support set defined by a cumulative weight threshold. These are normalized by the total electron count Z, yielding fractional bounds PMin=nMinZ, PMax=nMaxZ expressed in the form nl^Z*[PMin, PMax]v where the suffix v encodes the support-selection criterion. AREECM provides a compact representation of configurational variability within standard electronic structure descriptions without modifying underlying quantum mechanical formalism. It encodes the range of subshell occupations implied by the wavefunction while remaining compatible with conventional electron-configuration notation.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Nickel-Catalyzed Heck–Matsuda Reactions: Theoretical Evidence for a Ni(I)/Ni(III) Catalytic Cycle
papers.abstract: Nickel catalysis offers a cost-effective alternative to palladium in cross-coupling, though its role in the Heck--Matsuda (HM) reaction remains poorly defined. Using DFT, we examined Ni(0)/Ni(II) and Ni(I)/Ni(III) catalytic cycles employing pyridine--oxazoline (Pyox) ligands. The open-shell Ni(I)/Ni(III) pathway was found to be both kinetically and thermodynamically favored, featuring an oxidative addition barrier of 24.5 kcal mol -1 and a facile reductive elimination (3.7 kcal mol-1), whereas the singlet cycle exhibited higher barriers (22-35 kcal mol -1 ) for reductive elimination step. Energy span analysis (ESA) reveals that reaction turnover-frequency (TOF) determining states depend strongly on the olefin structure, shifting between oxidative addition, β-hydride and reductive elimination step. The calculated TOF for Ni(I)/Ni(III) systems reach values of 8.03 h-1 bypassing the high reductive-elimination barriers that limit the singlet pathway. For cyclic enols, β-hydride elimination governs selectivity, and is stabilized by Ni-OH interactions. These findings establish Ni(I)-based precatalysts as key to efficient and stereoselective HM reactions under mild conditions, expanding the accessible catalytic space beyond Pd analogues.

papers.title: Revealing Hidden Organic Radicals in Carbon Black-hilled Rubber by Multi-harmonic EPR Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Carbon-black filled rubbers are widely used materials, yet the radical processes occurring within the elastomer matrix, particularly during vulcanization, remain poorly understood. Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy could provide direct insight into these mechanisms by probing unpaired electrons. However, radicals associated with carbon black particles generate a very broad signal, masking the weaker and narrower contribution of the organic radicals from the elastomer phase. By employing multiharmonic EPR detection to selectively observe the organic radicals, this work enables access to these previously hidden radicals and opens new opportunities to investigate vulcanization mechanisms in reinforced rubber materials.

papers.title: Multidimensional Temperature-Accelerated String Method: Sampling Multiple Transition Pathways and Slow Variables
papers.abstract: The finite-temperature string (FTS) method identifies transition pathways between known metastable states in a selected collective-variable (CV) space, thereby reducing computational cost by focusing sampling along the pathway. Biomolecular transitions, however, often involve many slow variables and multiple competing pathways that can affect apparent free-energy barriers and kinetic estimates. Accuracy can, in principle, be improved by including putative slow CVs, ensuring ergodic sampling of other slow variables, and sampling multiple possible pathways; however, achieving this in practice remains challenging. Here, we implement and systematically assess FTS in multidimensional CV spaces, using retrospective replica-exchange acceptance probabilities to diagnose overlap between neighboring biased windows and Multistate Bennett Acceptance Ratio reweighting to recover unbiased free energies. After validation on the Müller-Brown potential, we apply the approach to alanine dipeptide in vacuum and show that the backbone transition free energy is insensitive to the inclusion of additional CVs. In contrast, for phenylalanine dipeptide in vacuum, a two-dimensional FTS in backbone (ϕ, ψ) space undersamples the slow side-chain χ 2 rotamer states. To address this limitation, we introduce a temperature-accelerated string method (TASM), in which the string bias is retained in the reduced backbone space while temperature acceleration enhances sampling of slow variables not explicitly included in the string. TASM improves χ 2 sampling, corrects the apparent free-energy barrier, and gives good agreement between effective Kramers’ rate estimates and direct mean-first-passage-time calculations. Explicit three-dimensional strings that include χ 2 further reveal multiple side-chain rotamer pathways during the backbone transition, with the dominant pathway depending on the transition direction.

papers.title: Characterizing the speciation and oxidation state of SnF2 in model toothpastes by 31P, 117/119Sn and 17O solution and solid-state NMR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Stannous fluoride (SnF2) is widely used in commercial toothpaste products as an anticaries fluoride source, antimicrobial agent, and desensitizer. However, oxidation of stannous ions (Sn2+) to stannic ions (Sn4+) results in lowered efficacy. To better understand the speciation of SnF2 based toothpastes, solution and magic angle spinning (MAS) solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) experiments were performed on solutions containing SnF2 and its common chelator pyrophosphate (PP). The concentration of Sn2+ to Sn4+ can be easily monitored by integration of the 31P solution NMR spectrum of PP solutions. 17O and 119Sn double-resonance NMR experiments were initially performed on 17O-enriched model compound sodium stannate hydrate, Na2Sn(OH)6. Using 119Sn{17O} heteronuclear spin echo (J-resolved) NMR experiments one-bond tin oxygen J-coupling constants were measured to be 140 Hz. The dephasing amplitude enables the 17O enrichment level to be measured, or alternatively, if the enrichment level is known, the number of bonded oxygen atoms can be determined. Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) was applied to enable

papers.title: Can catalytic activity be varied on different Cu sites for HCOO hydrogenation?
papers.abstract: HCOO pathway dominates the production of CH3OH synthesis on Cu catalysts. HCOO hydrogenation is therefore of crucial importance for its kinetic hurdle. It is reported catalytic variation on different Cu facets as their surface Cu atoms are of different coordination number. Cu nanoclusters are constituted by Cu atoms in different coordination number (CN). Therefore, the present work reports catalytic variation of HCOO hydrogenation along different ensemble sites (ES), which is assembled by numbered Cu sites, on Cu16. To identify geometric characteristics of Cu sites that present high HCOO hydrogenation performance, Cu4, Cu8, Cu32 including Cu(111) are sampled in this work. As a result, we found high catalytic performance of reaction for average generalized coordination number of ES greater than 3.9.

papers.title: Pressure-Drop-Mediated Oscillatory Dynamics in Advanced Two-Phase Natural Circulation Systems: A Spectral Analytical Framework
papers.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive linear stability analysis of a two-phase natural circulation loop (TPNCL), focusing on the prediction of instability regimes through analytical modeling. The system under consideration consists of interconnected single-phase and two-phase regions, including the downcomer, horizontal and vertical pipes, heated section, boiling region, riser, inclined pipe, and steam drum. Governing conservation equations of mass, momentum, and energy are derived separately for single-phase and two-phase flow regimes and subsequently linearized around steady-state conditions using small perturbation theory. The perturbation variables are expressed as exponential functions to enable analytical solutions, leading to explicit relations for enthalpy, flow rate, and pressure fluctuations in each segment of the loop. These solutions are integrated to obtain pressure drop expressions, which are combined to form a closed-loop characteristic equation governing system stability. The real and imaginary components of this equation are analyzed by substituting a complex frequency parameter, yielding a quadratic relation in terms of steady superficial velocity. The derived formulation provides clear identification of contributions from frictional, gravitational, and acceleration effects across different regions. Stability criteria are established based on the sign of the real part of the total pressure drop. The analysis enables determination of admissible operating ranges of flow velocity and highlights the role of geometric and thermophysical parameters in driving instability. The proposed analytical framework offers a structured approach for predicting instability thresholds in TPNCL systems and can serve as a foundation for design optimization and validation against experimental data.

papers.title: Smartphone-Based Investigation of First-Order Reaction Kinetics in a Photochromic Spiropyran–Merocyanine System
papers.abstract: Reaction kinetics is a foundational topic in undergraduate curricula. There is continued interest in developing instructional laboratory experiments that enable students to directly visualize reaction progress and to study reaction kinetics quantitatively simultaneously. Here we report photochromic spiropyran as a visually intuitive and quantitative platform for studying reaction kinetics. Upon ultraviolet irradiation, spiropyran (SP) undergoes reversible photo-isomerization to its merocyanine (MC) form, producing distinct color changes. The conversion of MC to SP can be monitored in real time using colorimetric signals from photos collected by smartphones. The photochemical back reaction exhibits first-order kinetic behavior, enabling rate constants to be extracted from time-dependent photos within a single laboratory period. The reaction rates in different solvents were identified and could be enhanced by the green light irradiation. The procedure requires only commercially available reagents, simple light sources, and smartphones, making it accessible for undergraduates’ courses as well as demonstrations for K-12 students. Overall, this spiropyran-based experiment provides a visually engaging and adaptable approach to enhance student understanding of reaction kinetics through photochromism.

papers.title: Can catalytic activity be varied on different Cu sites for HCOO hydrogenation?
papers.abstract: HCOO pathway dominates the production of CH3OH synthesis on Cu catalysts. HCOO hydrogenation is therefore of crucial importance for its kinetic hurdle. It is reported catalytic variation on different Cu facets as their surface Cu atoms are of different coordination number. Cu nanoclusters are constituted by Cu atoms in different coordination number (CN). Therefore, the present work reports catalytic variation of HCOO hydrogenation along different ensemble sites (ES), which is assembled by numbered Cu sites, on Cu16. To identify geometric characteristics of Cu sites that present high HCOO hydrogenation performance, Cu4, Cu8, Cu32 including Cu(111) are sampled in this work. As a result, we found high catalytic performance of reaction for average generalized coordination number of ES greater than 3.9.

papers.title: A Machine Learning QSAR Model for Predicting hTERT Telomerase Inhibitor Potency: ChEMBL Dataset Curation, Algorithm Benchmarking, and Prospective Application to Natural and Synthetic Anticancer Compounds
papers.abstract: Human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) is reactivated in approximately 85–90% of human cancers, establishing it as one of the most broadly expressed oncological drug targets; yet no quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) model trained on curated experimental bioactivity data has been reported specifically for hTERT inhibitor potency prediction. Here, we curate a target-wide hTERT IC50 dataset from ChEMBL (CHEMBL2916; 616 unique compounds, pIC50 range 4.03–8.34) and benchmark five regression algorithms across three molecular feature representations: Morgan circular fingerprints (ECFP4), RDKit physicochemical descriptors, and their union, for predicting hTERT inhibitory potency. An XGBoost model trained on the combined feature set was selected as the best-performing architecture (cross-validated R2 = 0.549± 0.081) and validated through nested cross-validation (R2 = 0.508± 0.070), an independent held-out test set (R2 = 0.533; RMSE = 0.507 log units), and a y-scrambling permutation test (p = 0.020), confirming a genuine and statistically significant structure-activity relationship. Permutation-importance analysis revealed that potency is driven predominantly by lipophilic and polarizable surface-area descriptors (SlogP VSA10, PEOE VSA10, SMR VSA7), consistent with the hydrophobic character of the hTERT thumb-domain binding pocket. The model was applied prospectively to six structurally diverse inhibitors spanning four compound classes: BIBR1532, zidovudine (AZT), raltitrexed, allicin, EGCG, and quercetin, with applicability-domain analysis based on maximum Tanimoto similarity to the training set. Among in-domain compounds, quercetin (pIC50 = 5.74) and zidovudine (5.12) achieved the most balanced profiles of predicted potency and drug-likeness. Physicochemical profiling using QED scores and Lipinski/Veber criteria identified BIBR1532 as the most developable compound (QED = 0.688; zero Lipinski violations), whereas EGCG ranked lowest (QED = 0.212; two Lipinski violations). Jointly interpreting predicted potency, applicability-domain status, and physicochemical developability reveals that raw potency rankings alone are misleading for this target, and that an integrated computational framework is necessary for reliable inhibitor prioritization. These findings provide the first validated QSAR baseline for hTERT and complement physics-based docking and molecular dynamics analyses of these compounds reported in a companion study.

papers.title: Evidencing Fast and Reversible Proton Insertion of a Metastable Bilayered Tungsten Oxide
papers.abstract: Materials that exhibit fast and reversible electrochemical modulation of properties such as electronic conductivity, optical absorption, and volume are of interest for electrochromic, neuromorphic, and actuator switching technologies. Here, we report on the rapid first-order phase transition during proton-insertion coupled electron transfer (PICET) in a metastable bilayered tungsten oxide hydrate (H2W2O7). We utilize quasi-elastic neutron scattering measurements to gain insights into the structural water content and dynamics. We employ operando electrochemical X-ray diffraction and optical microscopy to track changes in structure and color during PICET. X-ray diffraction results reveal that H2W2O7 has a rapid first-order structural transition characterized by the loss of octahedral tilting and the relaxation of geometric distortions within the inorganic layers. Operando stress measurements during electrochemical polarization reveal that the phase transition coincides with rapid mechanical deformation. Optical microscopy shows a reversible two-step color change concurrent with the structural transition, from transparent to blue to gold. These discrete optical regimes correspond to changes in electronic conductivity. Our results show that H2W2O7 is a promising material for electrochemical switching technologies.

papers.title: RMG-Py v4: 17 Years of Open Source Reaction Mechanism Generation
papers.abstract: Kinetic modeling describes reacting chemical systems through networks of elementary reactions and their associated rate parameters. Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG-Py) automates the construction of these networks by simulating reaction fluxes to identify dominant chemical pathways in silico. RMG-Py v4.0.0 marks 17 years of open-source reaction mechanism generation, introducing substantial improvements in performance, usability, and chemical scope. Benchmarks demonstrate higher throughput relative to prior versions alongside streamlined installation via Docker and binary distributions. Key new capabilities include automated library selection, improved species selection algorithms, integration with the Julia-based ReactionMechanismSimulator.jl for simulating arbitrary reactor configurations, and PySIDT-based property estimators. Heterogeneous catalysis support is improved by addition of new adsorbate thermophysical property data, new reaction families, resonance templates of surface-bound species, and uncertainty quantification for parameter sensitivity analysis. The release also extends RMG-Py into new chemistry domains with electrochemical mechanisms for battery and CO2RR applications and an automated fragment-based modeling framework for pyrolysis of large molecules. Together, these advances improve new users’ experience, expand the range of tractable systems, and maintain RMG-Py at the forefront of computational kinetic modeling.

papers.title: The thermodynamic limit of battery degradation predictability is nine orders of magnitude below empirical variance
papers.abstract: Capacity fade in lithium-ion batteries exhibits significant cell-to-cell variance, fundamentally limiting the accuracy of lifetime predictions. Current approaches treat this variance as an intrinsic feature of the electrochemical system and attempt to model it through machine learning. Here, we show that the Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation (TUR)—a universal bound from non-equilibrium statistical mechanics—places a rigorous lower limit on the coefficient of variation (CV) of any macroscopic current, including the capacity fade rate. Applying this framework to 46 commercial LiFePO4/graphite cells cycled under 21 fast-charging protocols from the open-source Severson dataset, we compute the total entropy production per cycle from time-resolved voltage, current, and temperature telemetry. We find the macroscopic TUR bound to be CVmin ≈ 4 × 10−12, approximately nine orders of magnitude below the empirically observed CV ≈ 0.005. This astronomical gap arises from the 1/ √ N suppression of single-ion fluctuations across N ∼ 1022 lithium ions per cycle. Our result demonstrates that virtually all observed battery lifetime variance is thermodynamically avoidable—it originates from manufacturing variability, protocol design, and environmental factors, not from fundamental physical limits.

papers.title: Bismuth-Catalyzed Synthesis of Carbon Nanobelts
papers.abstract: Carbon nanobelts (CNBs) have attracted widespread interest, yet their precise synthesis remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report the efficient synthesis of two novel CNBs, namely (18,12) CNB [30] and (18,15) CNB [33], which represent the sidewall segments of (18,12) and (18,15) carbon nanotubes (CNTs), respectively. The key step involved a bismuth triflate-catalyzed cyclization of ethoxyvinyl-substituted carbon nanorings. The molecular structures were confirmed by HR-MS, NMR spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). Moreover, STM images clearly demonstrate the characteristic double-contour feature of these two CNBs. Density functional theory calculations show that (18,12) CNB [30] exhibits dominant local aromaticity. Photophysically, (18,12) CNB [30] displays a remarkable narrow‑band deep‑blue emission at 430 nm with a full width at half‑maximum of only 6 nm. This work not only expands the synthetic methodologies available for the construction of CNBs but also provides promising templates for the bottom‑up synthesis of chirality‑specific CNTs.

papers.title: Potential‑Driven Tetragonal CuFe2O4 Phase Transition Enables Near‑Complete Nitrate‑to‑Ammonia Conversion with Minimal Nitrite Accumulation
papers.abstract: The development of electrocatalyst for nearly complete electrocatalytic nitrate reduction without accumulating nitrites in the product feed is indispensable for sustainable nitrate contaminated wastewater treatment and carbon-neutral green ammonia production. In this study, CuFe 2 O 4 nanowires could mimic the bifunctional nature of nitrite reductase where Cu act as nitrate adsorption and deoxygenation center while Fe promoted adsorption of H* and the reduction of *NO to NH 2 . We demonstrate the involvement of a hydride‑transfer pathway supported by obtaining four‑electron transfer from rotating‑disk voltammetry and further corroborated by the mechanistic insights obtained from DFT analysis. The faradaic efficiency for ammonia exceeded 95% at all applied potentials, with an ammonia‑to‑nitrite yield‑rate ratio of 13 at −1.1 V vs. Reversible Hydrogen Electrode. The enhanced nitrite reduction was due to the potential dependent cubic to tetragonal phase transition at higher overpotential exposing undercoordinated iron sites promoting H* adsorption and hydrogenation of *NO. The tandem electrocatalysis mechanism led simultaneously to high NH 3 selectivity, suppressing hydrogen evolution reaction and resulting negligible nitrite accumulation. This work establishes a correlation between ammonia selectivity, surface structure and phase of spinel CuFe 2 O 4 and provides crucial mechanistic insights into reaction pathways of NO 3 - /NO 2 - electroreduction

papers.title: Coordination-Enabled Antibiotic Capture and Optical Sensing in Water with a Dual-Function Mesoporous Zirconium Metal-Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) combining high porosity and structural robustness provide unique platforms for the selective capture of pollutants in water. In addition, they can serve as platforms to immobilize luminescent species for sensing applications. Here, we present a strategy to integrate accessible coordinative sites and lanthanide luminescent reporting centers within robust MOFs, enabling simultaneous capture and mechanistic sensing of carboxylate-containing pollutants. The post-synthetic grafting of Eu(III) ions into mesoporous Zr- and Hf-based MIP-206 and microporous MOF-808 frameworks yielded chemically stable, single-site lanthanide centers. Advanced synchrotron techniques, including Eu L3-edge EXAFS and X-ray pair distribution function (xPDF) analysis, reveal that Eu ions are predominantly coordinated to the M6 oxo-clusters, forming isolated surface-bound sites while preserving framework crystallinity and porosity. The resulting materials exhibit strong fluorescence arising from efficient ligand-to-metal energy transfer (antenna effect). When evaluated towards the model antibiotics amoxicillin (AMX) and chloramphenicol (CHL), Zr-MIP-206(Eu) shows selective adsorption and efficient fluorescence quenching, enabling sensitive and linear detection of AMX at low concentrations (< 40 μM). These findings highlight the synergy between cluster accessibility, lanthanide functionalization, and framework stability in Zr-MIP-206(Eu) for effective environmental monitoring in aqueous media.

papers.title: Physicochemical and Structural Determinants of BACE1-Selective Inhibition: An Integrative Modeling Study using A Combined Ligand-and Structure-Based Approach
A Critical Evaluation of Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Organic Synthesis: Activation Modes and Green Metrics
papers.abstract: While domino and cascade reactions are widely celebrated for their step economy and intrinsic bond-forming efficiency, evaluating their true sustainability requires moving beyond a purely molecular perspective to incorporate rigorous Green Chemistry metrics. This review critically reassesses sequential transformations, including ionic, radical, pericyclic, photochemical, transition-metal, and biocatalytic pathways, through a quantitative framework termed the “Molecular–Process Discrepancy”. Rather than providing a traditional descriptive overview, this manuscript integrates quantitative indicators, such as Atom Economy (AE) and Process Mass Intensity (PMI), to evaluate the actual environmental footprint of these reactions. By analyzing recent synthetic applications, this evaluation reveals that theoretical green advantages are frequently negated at scale by specific physicochemical and engineering bottlenecks, most notably the dilution paradox in macroscopic batch systems, interphase mass transfer limitations, and catalyst deactivation. Ultimately, the findings indicate that resolving these scale-up hurdles requires a definitive transition from isolated molecular design to integrated process engineering. Specifically, the integration of continuous-flow microreactor technologies and AI-driven retrosynthesis emerges as a critical pathway to bridge the gap between elegant molecular synthesis and genuinely sustainable chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: IN SITU FORMATION OF ACTIVE METAL COMPLEXES: SERUM ACTIVATION OF PHOTOSENSITISERS FOR PHOTODYNAMIC THERAPY
papers.abstract: Metal complexes are important tools in biomedicine as therapeutic or diagnostic agents. Yet, inside the organism they can get degraded, loosing efficiency and causing unwanted toxicity. Instead, we want to target metal ions from labile metal pools to attempt forming new metal complexes with biological activity in situ. With this we intend to explore new routes to extend the efficiency of metal-based therapeutic agents and reduce possible toxicity linked to degradation under biological environments. Here we demonstrate our approach by using porphyrin ligands that are capable of binding to serum albumin and get activated with the ions carried by the protein. Newly formed metallo-porphyrins are improved photosensitisers (PS) for photodynamic therapy (PDT), and maintain their anticancer properties better than non-metallated PSs under relevant cell growing conditions.

papers.title: FAVES V4: A Production-Deployed Compliance and Liability Screening System for Drug Discovery at 122M-Compound Scale, Aligned to HHS/ONC FAVES and NIST AI 600-1
papers.abstract: FAVES V4 is a compliance and liability screening system for drug discovery, aligned to two complementary federal frameworks: the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services / Office of the National Coordinator FAVES rubric for trustworthy AI in healthcare and life sciences,30 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1),37 which names chemical and biological design tools as a distinct chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) risk class (Section 2.1). The five letters; Fair, Appropriate, Valid, Effective, Safe; are not principles asserted in this paper; they are operational properties demonstrated against published evidence in production, with named action-ID anchors drawn from NIST AI 600-1 throughout Section 4. A single-API screening call returns regulatory status (DEA / FDA / CWC / EPA / EU REACH), structural alerts (1,585 SMARTS across PAINS, Brenk, NIH, ZINC, and 7 ChEMBL sub-catalogs via RDKit FilterCatalog), pharmacokinetic classification (BOILED-Egg), and prior-art disclosure (InChIKey identity resolution against PubChem and a local 122M-compound database), with per-field provenance metadata. The system is deployed in production with both live RDKit computation (~5 ms per molecule) and a precomputed database cache (122,407,635 documents). The five FAVES properties are operationalized through a complete governance bundle: an Intended Use Statement (Appropriate), risk-based component classification mapped to GAMP and CSA (Valid), end-to-end validation protocol with predetermined acceptance criteria (Valid), three-layer audit trail with two non- skippable layers (Safe), and change-control SOP with a worked rollback example (Safe). Validation across five tests against predetermined acceptance criteria; V3 regulatory benchmark, V4 field completeness, BOILED-Egg implementation, prior-art resolution, and external cross-RDKit- version reproducibility; yields 362/362 compounds passing post-fix at the time of submission. The initial 341/342 pre-fix execution identified a single defect; an incorrect cortisol SMILES in the deployed FDA whitelist that omitted the 11β-hydroxyl; which was root-caused, corrected, deployed, and re-validated through the documented change-control SOP. We report both numbers transparently: the defect was surfaced because the validation was honestly scoped to the full 102-compound regulatory benchmark rather than an undersized fixture, and the change-control loop functioning visibly in production is itself a stronger claim than a never-exercised one. To our knowledge, this is the first cheminformatics screening system whose full HHS/ONC- and NIST AI 600-1-aligned governance scaffolding is described in operational detail, with each of the five FAVES properties demonstrated against public evidence. The benchmark dataset, validation reports, and latency measurements are released for reproducibility; the seven NMCP-FAVES governance documents are summarized in Section 4 with NIST action-ID anchors and worked examples, and full operational versions are available from the corresponding author. Keywords: structural alerts, PAINS, BOILED-Egg, controlled substances, regulatory compliance, prior art, drug discovery, cheminformatics, GAMP 5, software validation, autonomous

papers.title: (Hetero)adamantane synthesis: A triple alkylation reaction
papers.abstract: (Hetero)adamantanes containing tetrel bridgeheads (C, Si, and Ge) are important structures in surface and chemical sciences. Syntheses of diamondoid structures generally occur in a linear fashion, often using harsh conditions. These limitations make it difficult to access diverse (hetero)adamantane-based molecules with interchangeable functional groups for broad applications. The discovery of an expedient and convergent methodology for the synthesis of diamondoid scaffolds is described. The convenient synthetic route proceeding via a triple alkylation reaction represents a breakthrough in accessing the adamantane molecular class. Applications of this transformation to diamondoid tripods containing tetrel bridgeheads (C- and Ge-) were explored.

papers.title: From 2D Graphs to Sub-Unit pKa: Nine Iterations to Beat MolGpKa on Both Scaffolds and Sulfonamides
papers.abstract: Accurate pKa prediction for drug-like molecules remains a significant gap between com- mercial tools (Epik ∼0.5 RMSE, MoKa ∼0.4 RMSE) and open-source methods, particularly for sulfonamides and heterocyclic N–H compounds prevalent in medicinal chemistry. We present a systematic nine-iteration ablation converging on a routed ensemble that outperforms MolGpKa on both general scaffolds and sulfonamides simultaneously—the first open-source model to do so. Starting from a 2D molecular graph baseline (v1, SAMPL7 RMSE 3.48), we isolate each variable: global xTB descriptors help scaffolds but not sulfonamides (v2); data augmentation fails (v2-aug); per-atom Mulliken charges help sulfonamides but hurt scaffolds (v3); routing combines both (v4, SAMPL7 2.19). We then identify the architectural gap with MolGpKa: per-atom pKa output targets trained on microscopic data. Per-atom output alone fails with macroscopic labels (v5). Microscopic labels from Uni-pKa improve scaffolds but not sulfonamides (v6). Merging microscopic and macroscopic data with a mixed loss produces the first model with no tradeoff (v7, scaffold 1.31, SAMPL7 1.32). Adding full xTB charge coverage solves sulfonamides (v8, SAMPL7 0.535) but hurts scaffolds. The final routed ensemble (v9) achieves scaffold RMSE 1.255 (R2 0.878) and SAMPL7 RMSE 0.535 (R2 0.948)—beating MolGpKa by 62% on scaffolds and 45% on sulfonamides, with calibrated uncertainty and zero failure rate. All models trained on open data (IUPAC, ChEMBL, Uni-pKa) with open-source tools (xTB, RDKit, Chemprop).

papers.title: Molecular Targets Shape Reasoning Topology: Bidirectional Validation of Chemistry-Inspired Bond Classification for AI Reasoning Chains
papers.abstract: Recent work classified AI reasoning chains using chemistry-inspired bond types, namely covalent (deductive), hydrogen (reflective), and van der Waals (exploratory), showing that structural stability of reasoning predicts training data quality (Direction A). We test the complementary direction: does the molecular target being reasoned about shape the topology of reasoning itself (Direction B)? Across 478 reasoning traces from five ADMET endpoints, we find that it does, with large effect sizes (Cohen's d = 0.94 and 1.75, both p < 10 −9 , surviving Bonferroni correction). We collect chain-of-thought traces from Claude Opus 4.6 performing ADMET property predictions across CYP2D6, CYP3A4, CYP2C9, hERG, and P-gp, using live computational chemistry tools via the Model Context Protocol. A four-signal Semantic Bond Classifier, using sentence embeddings, discourse markers, positional distance, and an energy proxy, classifies reasoning bonds without requiring attention weights from open-source models. Of five pre-registered hypotheses, aggregate reasoning structure does not predict prediction accuracy (H1-H4, all p > 0.12). However, molecular targets strongly determine reasoning topology (H5): CYP2D6 reasoning (2D substructure-driven) shows significantly more covalent bonds than hERG reasoning (3D conformation-dependent), while hERG reasoning shows more van der Waals bonds than CYP2D6. Classifier ablation reveals semantic similarity as the dominant signal (∆ = 13.2 percentage points when removed). These results close a bidirectional loop: chemistry metaphors explain reasoning structure, and chemistry problems shape reasoning structure. The finding that molecular target type determines reasoning topology, with large, interpretable effect sizes, has implications for understanding how AI systems adapt their problem-solving approach to domain-specific demands.

papers.title: NovoExpert-2: State-of-the-Art ADMET Prediction via Gradient-Boosted Trees on MapLight Fingerprints and GIN Embeddings
papers.abstract: We present NovoExpert-2, a dual-method approach to molecular property prediction that achieves state-of-the-art performance on five endpoints of the Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) ADMET benchmark. Our primary model combines MapLight-style fingerprint fea- tures (2,573 dimensions: Morgan ECFP, Avalon, ErG, and RDKit 2D descriptors) with 300- dimensional GIN supervised masking embeddings from the DGL-LifeSci pretrained model zoo, passed to a 5-seed CatBoost classifier/regressor ensemble. We additionally evaluate a Chemprop v2 directed message-passing neural network (D-MPNN) as a secondary method, and for each endpoint report the stronger of the two. Evaluated on all 22 endpoints of the TDC ADMET benchmark using official splits and per-endpoint metrics, NovoExpert-2 exceeds published state- of-the-art on CYP2D6 Veith (AUPRC 0.778 vs. 0.750, +0.028), CYP3A4 Veith (AUPRC 0.916 vs. 0.900, +0.016), CYP3A4 Substrate Carbonmangels (AUROC 0.660 vs. 0.656, +0.0040), Clearance Hepatocyte AZ (Spearman 0.511 vs. 0.487, +0.024), and DILI (AUROC 0.922 vs. 0.916, +0.006). The first four wins use CatBoost+MapLight+GIN; DILI uses Chemprop v2, which exploits end-to-end learned representations that better capture the multi-mechanism drug- induced liver injury phenotype. We additionally present a metric correction for our previously reported NovoExpert-1 CYP2D6 result: prior work measured AUROC (0.864) while the TDC leaderboard uses AUPRC; under the correct metric, NovoExpert-1 would score approximately 0.64 AUPRC on CYP2D6 and would not have beaten SOTA. NovoExpert-2, evaluated with the correct per-endpoint metric throughout, provides a more rigorous basis for leaderboard comparison. All code, trained models, and prediction files are publicly available.

papers.title: Human NEU3 and NEU4 enzymes prefer short polysialic acid substrates
papers.abstract: Regulation of sialic acids is important to many biological processes and involves both biosynthesis and catabolism. The human neuraminidase enzymes (hNEU) regulate many sialosides in human health and disease. Polysialic acid (polySia) is a polyanion of α(2→8) linked sialic acids with roles in nervous, reproductive, and immune systems and is dysregulated in some malignancies and mental disorders. The unique chemical properties of this polymer, which include an enhanced susceptibility to acid-catalyzed hydrolysis, have hampered its study. Herein we describe the first systematic study of hNEU isoenzyme activity towards polySia in vitro. Our experimental design allowed us to study the impact of several factors that may influence polysialic acid degradation including pH, polymer size, and the relative ionic strength of the media. We report that short chains of polySia (oligoSia, degree of polymerization, DP 3-8) were substrates of NEU3 and NEU4 at acidic pH, but not at neutral pH. We were unable to detect hNEU-catalyzed hydrolysis of longer polymers (polySia, DP 10-20) over background hydrolysis. These findings suggest that longer polySia oligomers may be degraded through a neuraminidase-independent mechanism, such as internalization or degradation in endosomes and lysosomes.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Raman Spectroscopy of Nitrate Electroreduction Reveals Dynamic Interfacial Adsorbate Evolution
papers.abstract: Nitrate electroreduction offers a pathway for coupling wastewater remediation with sustainable ammonia production, yet its mechanistic details under operating conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we directly resolve the dynamic evolution of nitrate-derived intermediates at electrified interfaces, addressing a key limitation in understanding dynamic reaction pathways. We employ time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TR-SERS) to monitor the interfacial behavior of NO 3 – and NO 2 – during nitrate reduction on roughened silver electrodes and observe potential-dependent vibrational shifts attributed to systematic changes in adsorption modes under increasingly cathodic potentials. Density functional theory calculations further support the vibrational assignments and provide insight into preferred binding motifs across the applied potential range. By tracking the time evolution of adsorbates, this approach provides insights into the sequence of adsorption and transformation steps on silver. The combined experimental and computational analysis contributes to a molecular-level understanding of nitrate electroreduction and provides a framework for probing dynamic reaction intermediates in nitrogen conversion electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Study of Ions at Surface Nanobubble Interface: Adsorption Without Gas Retention
papers.abstract: Surface nanobubbles are nanoscale gaseous domains anchored at solid–liquid interfaces, notable for their unexpected stability against dissolution. Although they share size and composition with bulk nanobubbles, the mechanisms underlying their persistence at interfaces appear distinct. In this study, we employ molecular dynamics simulations with the polarizable SWM4-NDP water model to examine the role of ions at the nanobubble interface. Our simulations reveal a preferential enrichment of Cl− ions at the interface, while Li+ ions remain fully hydrated and largely excluded. Residence time analysis confirms this asymmetry, showing prolonged interfacial retention for Cl− relative to Li+. Interestingly, the transport of gas molecules across the interface remains largely unaffected by local ion density, and the potential of mean force profiles for nitrogen permeation as well as the orientational structure of interfacial water are nearly unchanged in the presence of ions. Together, these results indicate that while anions can accumulate at the nanobubble interface, their presence does not significantly influence gas transfer processes. This points toward stabilization pathways that extend beyond purely electrostatic effects, highlighting the importance of alternative mechanisms in sustaining surface nanobubbles.

papers.title: Carbothermal Reduction Reaction as a Strategy for Boosting Thermoelectric Performance of Binary Metal Oxides: A Case Study of ZnO Ceramics
papers.abstract: As a powerful concept, grain boundary engineering has been increasingly applied to enhance energy conversion efficiency in thermoelectric (TE) materials through directly modulating electronic and thermal characteristics. However, most efforts so far have focused only on introducing extrinsic defects or impurity phases into the system, without considering the impact of contact properties or the synergistic role of extrinsic and intrinsic defects as critical factors in power conversion. In this work, we provide a holistic discussion on the correlation between intrinsic and extrinsic defects and their effects on the thermoelectric properties of metal oxide materials using the carbothermal reduction (CTR) process. Taking ZnO as a model material, we show that vacancy-assisted migration of Zn interstitials leads to a decrease in the Schottky barrier height at grain boundaries. In addition, the increase in carrier concentration and band gap narrowing caused by carbon doping enhance the power factor up to 246 μW/mK 2 , which is comparable to the excellent values reported for transition metal-doped ZnO compounds. By minimizing the specific contact resistance of the electrode/TE material interface down to 12.7 mΩ cm 2 at a clamping pressure of 20 MPa, the output power of a single-leg module reaches 292 μW and a power density of 2.86 mW/cm 2 at Δ T = 65 K. This is significantly higher, almost by a factor of three, than those of state-of-the-art ZnO based thermoelectric generators. This work demonstrates a cost-effective avenue toward the development of efficient and practical thermoelectric devices.

papers.title: Dispersionless range-separated hybrid meta-GGA functional
papers.abstract: We present a new dispersionless, range-separated hybrid meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) density-functional theory (DFT) approach, dlωB97M, augmented with the D20 as-mod dispersion function (a modification of D20 as [J. Phys. Chem. A, 125:1787, 2021]), resulting in the dlωB97M+D20 as-mod method. The novelty of the new method is the introduction of a multiplicative factor gradually switching off D20 as at intermolecular separations shorter than the van der Waals (vdW) minimum, the region where semilocal density-functional approximations (DFAs) start to recover dispersion interactions. D20 as-mod still accurately approximates the true dispersion energies of most dimers at vdW minima and larger separations. We have tested the performance of dlωB97M+D20 as-mod against a suite of published DFT+D methods across a diverse set of benchmark interaction energies. Our results demonstrate that dlωB97M+D20 as-mod delivers consistently reliable predictions, with accuracy superior to that of the best published DFT+D metods. Since the dlωB97M contribution includes only physical components of interaction energy that a semilocal DFA can recover and D20 as-mod approximates true dispersion energy except at very short separations, dlωB97M+D20 as-mod is more appealing from a physical point of view than most DFT+D approaches. It also allows meaningful energy decomposition analysis as the fraction of dispersion energy recovered by dlωB97M is known. Thus, taking into account its accuracy, dlωB97M+D20 as-mod can be recommended for modeling intermolecular interactions.

papers.title: Engineering Paediatric Formulations: A Systematic Review of Process Systems Methods, Sectoral Gaps, and the PPES Framework
papers.abstract: Background: Children constitute a distinct physiological population, and conventional adult-focused manufacturing approaches are poorly suited to meeting their formulation needs. Process Systems Engineering (PSE) — which encompasses quality-by-design (QbD), process analytical technology (PAT), mechanistic modelling, digital twins, and machine learning (ML) — provides a structured, model-based framework for addressing this challenge across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetics, and hygiene products intended for children. Methods: This study followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines to conduct a systematic review. Five automated bibliographic databases were searched using 110 structured queries across thematic blocks, supplemented by manual searches of Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, Engineering Village, and grey literature sources. Following screening of 5,844 records, 100 studies published between 2000 and 2026 were eligible for inclusion. Results: Pharmaceutical studies accounted for the majority of the included evidence (86 studies), with food/nutrition (9) and cosmetics/skincare (5) considerably underrepresented; hygiene products were completely absent from the literature. The most common research approach was empirical formulation design without a named PSE method (72%), followed by biopharmaceutical modelling (9%), 3D printing (4%), QbD (4%), design of experiments or optimisation (4%), ML/AI (3%), and particle engineering (2%). PAT and digital twin methods were entirely absent. Safety was the most frequently reported primary outcome (52%), followed by acceptability or palatability (19%). Neonates (30%) and infants (21%) dominated by age group; toddlers and school-age children were severely underrepresented (1% each). European studies accounted for 76% of the included evidence. Publication activity accelerated sharply after 2019, accounting for 50% of studies. Egger's test indicated no significant publication bias (p > 0.05). Conclusions: PSE tools and frameworks remain substantially underused in paediatric consumer goods development, particularly outside pharmaceuticals. Advanced PSE methods are largely confined to pharmaceutical dosage form research and are almost entirely absent from food, cosmetics, and hygiene categories. This review introduces the Paediatric Product Engineering Systems (PPES) Framework and identifies five priority research directions for accelerating the cross-sectoral adoption of PSE in paediatric formulation science.

papers.title: Integrating Enhanced Molecular Sampling, RNA-Specific Scoring Functions, and SILCS Technology for Small-Molecule Targeting of RNA
papers.abstract: Increasing knowledge of the wide range of biological functions of ribonucleic acids (RNAs) have made them a critical target in drug development. Accordingly, modifying their function through targeting them with small, drug-like molecules for the development of therapeutic agents is attractive. However, the rational design of RNA-targeting small molecules has been hindered by the intrinsic structural complexity and dynamics of RNAs. Here, we develop an in silico method to facilitate RNA-targeting small molecule discovery that integrates enhanced sampling molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using the classical Drude polarizable force field with the Site Identification by Ligand Competitive Saturation (SILCS) technology. Enhanced sampling MD simulations initiated with apo RNA structures guided by reaction coordinates selected from order parameters identified through machine learning combined with survey data of ligand-bound structures of TAR RNA enable identification druggable RNA conformations. Two custom RNA scoring functions are developed to 1) select RNA conformations with a high probability of containing druggable sites and 2) identification of nucleotides comprising binding sites that are able to participate in interactions with small molecules. Subsequently, selected conformations are subjected to the SILCS method for final selection of potential binding sites. Across three validation RNA systems, our method successfully identifies all experimentally known binding sites for four RNAs with both helical and non-canonical regions. In addition, novel potential binding sites were identified supported by high affinity SILCS FragMaps and docking analysis of FDA-approved ligands. However, only one of two binding sites in the THF riboswitch were identified indicating limitations in the application of the method to RNAs with tertiary contacts. The developed method is anticipated to enable efficient virtual screening and lead optimization for RNA-targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: Learning from SILCS FragMaps: Combining Physics-Based Energies with Artificial Intelligence for Rapid Drug Permeability Prediction
papers.abstract: Prediction of drug passive permeability represents an important component of rational drug design requiring continued development of methods to address this problem. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have long been shown to be of utility for prediction of compound permeability though they are limited by the range of chemical space in the datasets used in the training of the models. To address this, in the present study, the site-identification of ligand competitive saturation (SILCS) methodology is used to calculate free energy profiles for compounds across 3 model lipid bilayers; a POPC-cholesterol bilayer, a bilayer model mimicking PAMPA experiments, and a bilayer modelling the blood brain barrier. We present a rapid workflow generating around 15000 such profiles that accounts for the passive permeation of more than 2500 unique ligands for 3 different membranes. The free energy profiles, which account for all accessible protonation states of the compounds, are then used as features in a collection of AI models. As the physics-based free energy profiles are calculated based on the functional group types in the compounds combined with the SILCS FragMaps calculated for the bilayers, their use potentially improves model transferability by overcoming the limitation of the applicability of the AI models to the chemical space included in the training set assuming the SILCS-based energies are representative of barriers to the compound permeabilities. The resulting models are shown to be competitive with available passive permeability models while additionally offering energetic information on the contribution of functional groups to the permeation barriers that may be used for rational compound optimization. Limitations in the cell-based training data, including the presence of drug transporters, are discussed.

papers.title: Synthesis, Redox Properties and Magneto-Optical Activity of a Homologous Set of Metallo-5,5-Dimethylisocorrole Complexes
papers.abstract: A homologous set of 5,5-dimethyl-10,15-bis(pentafluorophenyl)-isocorrole (5-DMIC) complexes supporting NiII, PdII, PtII, or ZnII metal centers have been prepared and characterized. These complexes are readily accessible via modular synthetic routes and can be purified and obtained in moderate to good yields. Single crystal X-ray di@raction studies carried out for the Ni[5-DMIC], Pd[5-DMIC], and Pt[5-DMIC] complexes reveal M–N bond distances ranging from 1.84–1.99 Å across the series along with minimal metal displacement from the N4 plane, ranging from 0.014 Å for Ni[5-DMIC] to ~0.046 Å for the heavier isocorrole homologues. Accordingly, M[5-DMIC] complexes are highly planar with metal centers that are tightly coordinated in square planar geometry within the tetrapyrrole core. Electrochemical studies revealed a periodic trend in the reduction potentials with Pt[5-DMIC] being the most easily reduced (Ered = –0.84 V vs. Fc/Fc+). Additionally, the metalloisocorroles display strong absorbance in the UV-visible and near-infrared (NIR) regions, with Ni[5-DMIC], Pd[5-DMIC], and Zn[5-DMIC] exhibiting NIR bands centered around 900 nm, while Pt[5-DMIC] absorbance extends nearly to 1050 nm and into the NIR-II window. Given the unique, long-wavelength spectral characteristics, the M[5-DMIC] complexes were evaluated as NIR magneto-optical materials via magnetic circular dichroism (MCD), marking the first such study for isocorrole complexes. In contrast to the behavior of higher-symmetry D4h metalloporphyrins, the low-symmetry, non-aromatic isocorrole framework lacks a proper rotation axis required to support Faraday A-terms, resulting in the magneto-optical response being governed entirely by Faraday B-terms. Notably, Zn[5-DMIC] exhibits a sign reversal of the B -term in the Soret-like region, which may be attributed to di@ering frontier orbital contributions for this complex. Collectively, these results establish metalloisocorroles as structurally distinctive, low symmetry redoxactive, NIR-absorbing platforms with varied magneto-optical activity that are well positioned for various photophysical applications and detailed interrogation.

papers.title: Stereospecific Engagement of a Methyl-Sensitive ECL2 Anchor Site in 5-HT₂A by α-Substituted NBOH Derivatives
FluoFlow as a Family-anchored fragment flow matching for near-infrared fluorophore candidate discovery
papers.abstract: Generative models could accelerate fluorophore discovery, but wavelength conditioning is difficult when red and near-infrared emitters occupy sparse, family-structured regions of chemical space. We introduce FluoFlow, a fragment-tree flow-matching workflow that combines emissionband conditioning with chemically meaningful family-anchor decoding. Across three seeds, unconstrained generation produced strictly monotonic but compressed responses to 450, 550, 650 and 720 nm targets, with a mean 720–450 nm predicted-emission slope of 74.1 ± 16.5 nm. In contrast, BODIPY AP4 relaxed family-anchor decoding generated reproducible 720 nm candidate pools: three 10,000-sample runs gave a mean unique NIR650 hit rate of 54.4%, a mean unique NIR700 hit rate of 29.9%, and a Top24 predicted emission of 726.3 nm. Novelty and synthesis filters retained candidates with moderate nearest-neighbour similarity and Top50 mean synthetic accessibility of 3.72. These dry-lab results support family-anchored flow matching as a constrained discovery workflow; prospective spectral measurements remain required for the final experimental claim.

papers.title: Utility of Acid Co-Product from Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis as a Function of System-scale, Location, and Flexible Operation
papers.abstract: Bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BPMED) produces acid and base from seawater, and is being primarily advanced for base generation, with co-produced acid needing valorization. Acid cost and utility depend on process scale, electricity prices, and industrial context. Colocating BPMED with desalination facilities and operating flexibly can reduce production costs. In this study we investigate BPMED coupled to representative California desalination systems set in different locations and spanning different scales (0.02, 6, and 108 MGD), with their operation scheduled around price signals specific to their local grid. The resulting acid production profiles are evaluated against regional industrial utilization opportunities considering transport distance, local demand, and product quality. Results show that smaller systems exhibit stronger responsiveness to electricity price variability, and seasonal pricing slightly changes production costs, with winter showing higher daily variability and bigger cost increases at larger scales due to greater electricity price volatility. While flexible operations affect acid production paths, practical viability is mainly determined by downstream utilization. Location near industrial users and acid concentration are key factors; early analysis indicates that upgrading acid concentration is required to meet current user needs. Our findings suggest effective desalination-BPMED deployment relies on system performance, operational flexibility, and local product demand.

papers.title: Parallel Evolution of Dirhodium Artificial Metalloenzymes Creates Distinct Reaction Environments for Selective Carbene Transfer
papers.abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) combine the reactivity of transition metal catalysts with the selectivity and evolvability of protein scaffolds. Understanding different mechanisms by which scaffolds can impart selectivity would greatly facilitate ArM design efforts. In this study, we conducted parallel directed evolution prolyl oligopeptidase (POP)-based dirhodium ArMs toward two mechanistically distinct carbene insertion reactions, N-H and Si-H insertion, to study differences in their stereoselectivity and reaction specificity. Starting from a common parent enzyme, iterative mutagenesis and screening yielded variants 6-A and 4-I, which exhibit high activity and enantioselectivity for N-H and Si-H insertion, respectively, along with orthogonal reaction specificity. Structural and computational studies, including molecular dynamics simulations, reveal that directed evolution promotes the emergence of distinct cofactor binding modes within the POP active site, corresponding to a polar environment for N-H insertion and a more hydrophobic environment for Si-H insertion. Mutagenesis experiments validate the functional relevance of these environments and highlight differences in local and long-range interactions governing catalysis. These findings demonstrate that parallel evolution on mechanistically divergent reactions can drive the formation of distinct catalytic microenvironments within a single enzyme scaffold, providing new insights into secondary-sphere engineering and the design of functionally specialized ArMs.

papers.title: Continuous Flow Electrophotochemical Minisci Reaction via Catalytic Benzophenone Regeneration
papers.abstract: The use of benzophenone as a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalyst is limited by catalyst deactivation through ketyl radical dimerization, often requiring stoichiometric loadings. Herein, we report a continuous flow electrophotochemical strategy that enables its catalytic use via in situ regeneration from benzopinacol. This approach relies on a simple single-pass reactor that integrates photochemical activation with electrochemical turnover. Under these conditions, Miniscitype alkylation of pyridines proceeds efficiently using catalytic benzophenone, with performance comparable to conventional photochemical protocols and sustained activity over extended operation. The method shows broad substrate scope and was further extended to Giese-type additions and Paternò-Büchi cycloadditions.

papers.title: Extending Generative Machine Learning for Sustainable Polymer Design: An Integrated Workflow from Generative Models to Bio-Based Candidates
papers.abstract: The discovery of sustainable bio-based polymers is a pressing need, as traditional synthetic polymers derived from fossil fuels pose significant environmental challenges. However, bio-based alternatives often occupy different regions of chemical space and typically lack the mechanical and thermal performance of their synthetic counterparts. In this study, we present a generative machine learning pipeline to design and predict the properties of novel polymers, with current validation on synthetic datasets and future extension to bio-based systems. We utilize a variational autoencoder (VAE) trained on the PI1M dataset to generate over 60,000 new synthetic polymer candidates from learned latent embeddings. These candidates are evaluated using UMAP visualization and neural network-based property predictors. We discuss PolyGPT, an autoregressive extension for token-level control, and outline how property heads and conditioning strategies can guide discovery toward targeted thermal/structural traits. Altogether, our results substantiate the feasibility of a property-aware, generative pipeline that expands polymer libraries and lays the groundwork for inverse design of bio-based candidates.

papers.title: On again, off again: thiol-Michael photoactivated dynamic covalent chemistry
papers.abstract: Light-responsive dynamic covalent chemistry is a powerful tool that can provide spatiotemporal control of dynamic bond exchange when coupled with light as an external stimulus. Despite its promise, there is a need to develop new tools to harness light for controlling dynamic covalent chemistry. Here, we report a new strategy that couples a traditional coumarin photoremovable protecting group with a thiol-Michael dynamic covalent system at the site of photoactivation. This coumarin Michael acceptor undergoes traditional thiol-Michael exchange on the ground state. We show that irradiation of the resulting thiol-Michael adduct photolytically releases the thiol and regenerates the Michael acceptor in a reversible manner over multiple cycles, as confirmed by UV-vis and NMR spectroscopy with in-situ irradiation. This strategy for designing light-responsive dynamic covalent bonds will expand the toolbox for spatiotemporal control of systems including hydrogels and drug delivery platforms.

papers.title: Impact of Chronic Hydration–Dehydration Cycling on Enamel Analog Microhardness and Crack Propagation: An in Vitro Model of Dry Environmental Stress
papers.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the effects of repeated hydration–dehydration cycles on the mechanical integrity of enamel analog materials, focusing on microhardness reduction and crack propagation behavior under simulated dry conditions. Methods: Commercial hydroxyapatitebased enamel analog discs (n = 60; diameter 6 mm, thickness 2 mm; Sigma-Aldrich) were subjected to controlled hydration–dehydration cycles over 14 days. Four groups were established: Control (constant hydration), Mild (1 cycle/day), Moderate (3 cycles/day), and Sustained (6 cycles/day). Dehydration was performed at 37°C and 20% relative humidity, followed by rehydration in artificial saliva. Mechanical properties were assessed via Vickers microhardness testing and nanoindentation mapping. Crack propagation was evaluated using controlled indentation and quantified by optical microscopy and SEM. Results: Microhardness decreased progressively with cycling frequency, with Sustained cycling showing a 28% reduction compared to Control (p < 0.01). Crack propagation length increased significantly in Moderate and Sustained groups, reaching a 2.1-fold increase. SEM analysis revealed microstructural discontinuities and increased porosity in high-frequency cycling conditions. Significance: Hydration–dehydration cycling induces fatigue-like degradation in enamel analogs, significantly compromising mechanical integrity. This model provides a reproducible, ethics-independent framework for studying environmental stress on enamel-like materials.

papers.title: Fluorescent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Chemical Sensing: Design Strategies, Mechanisms, and Analytical Applications
papers.abstract: Fluorescent metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as transformative platforms for chemical sensing, combining ultrahigh porosity, tunable optical properties, and versatile host-guest chemistry to achieve exceptional sensitivity and selectivity. This review synthesizes recent advances (2018-2025, with emphasis on 2021-2025) in the design, synthesis, and application of luminescent MOF sensors for environmental monitoring, biomedical diagnostics, and food safety. Three interconnected themes are examined: (1) design principles governing fluorescence tuning through ligand engineering, metal node selection, and pore architecture optimization; (2) synthesis strategies and composite architectures enhancing stability and sensitivity, including post-synthetic modification, lanthanide functionalization, and MOF-dye hybrids; and (3) sensing mechanisms (photoinduced electron transfer [PET], Forster resonance energy transfer [FRET], and inner filter effects [IFE]) and their translation into analytical applications achieving sub-parts-per-billion detection limits and rapid response times. Representative systems demonstrate exceptional performance: Ag12bpy-NH2 achieves 0.1 ppm oxygen detection in 0.3 s, LCU-109 detects Fe3+ and Cu2+ at 0.0043 and 0.0028 ppm in river 2 water, and Zr-CAU-24 enables 5-min aflatoxin B1 screening in beverages. Despite these advances, persistent challenges, including water stability, photostability quantification, mechanistic standardization, and scalable manufacturing, limit widespread deployment. Critical research gaps are identified, including the need for quantitative structure-property models, long-term operational stability data, and techno-economic analyses. Coordinated interdisciplinary efforts in materials innovation, standardized validation protocols, and device integration are proposed as enabling pathways for MOF sensor translation from laboratory demonstrations to validated analytical tools within 3-5 years.

papers.title: The Key Role of Solvation in Enhancing Electrochemical Promotion of Brønsted Acid Catalysis
papers.abstract: Electrostatic polarization of catalyst-solution interfaces has been demonstrated to modulate the rate of liquid-phase heterogeneous Brønsted acid catalysis by up to five orders of magnitude. Previous studies in acetonitrile establish that maximal rate-potential scaling emerges only in high ionic strength solutions, indicating that rate promotion is highly sensitive to the electrostatic potential profile at the interface. Herein, we examine the role of the solvent on the electrolyte strength sensitivity of polarization-induced promotion of Brønsted acid catalysis. Using carbon paper with Brønsted acid functionalities as a catalyst, we measured liquid-phase 1-methylcyclopentanol dehydration rates in dimethyl carbonate, acetonitrile, and propylene carbonate solvents, with electrolyte concentrations ranging from 1 to 600 mM. In acetonitrile and dimethyl carbonate, the apparent transfer coefficient is less than 1 at all tested electrolyte strengths and decreases with decreasing electrolyte strength, implying that the proton traverses only a fraction of the electrostatic potential drop to form a surface-bound oxonium intermediate prior to rate-limiting C-O bond cleavage. In contrast, in more polar propylene carbonate, the rate-potential scaling returns near-unity apparent transfer coefficients that are insensitive to electrolyte concentration down to 1 mM, implying that the proton traverses the entirety of the electrostatic potential drop to form a putative freely solvated oxonium intermediate prior to rate-limiting C-O bond cleavage, outside the electrochemical double layer. The enhanced solvating power of propylene carbonate serves to increase the intrinsic rate of Brønsted acid catalysis, in the absence of electrostatic forcing, by ~4 orders of magnitude relative to acetonitrile and dimethyl carbonate. These findings highlight that enhanced solvation of protonated intermediates is essential for maximizing the promoting effect of polarization on Brønsted acid catalysis. Furthermore, these findings imply that for strongly polar solvents, catalyst potential plays a central role in Brønsted acid catalytic rates even in low ionic strength media. Together, these results show that solvent selection modulates both the intrinsic reaction rate and sensitivity to catalyst potential, emphasizing the importance of understanding interfacial electrostatic effects in thermochemical reaction systems.

papers.title: All-Photonic Yellow-Red-Blue-Green Orthogonal Photoswitching for Rewritable Four-Color 2D and 3D Displays and Optical Memories
papers.abstract: Light-induced color change is the defining and most fundamental characteristic of a photochromic material.
