Twofold switching between colorless and color or two different colors is known to humanity for centuries and has been used allegedly already in antiquity by Alexander the Great to coordinate troop movements. Today, the two-color changes of photochromes cover the whole visible spectrum. However, the next logical step of multicolor combinations has proven to be extremely difficult, and a basic four-color system is particularly challenging to realize in a fully photonic fashion. In this work we present a minimal photoswitching approach able to produce saturated yellow, red, blue, and green colors in response to different light irradiations of the same material. By involving nearinfrared addressable components for decolored sub-states, a distinct optical window is employed avoiding the problems that come with the reliance on UV responsiveness. The resulting photoswitching system can interchange between four different states in a fully orthogonal and path-independent manner to produce exquisite color changes. Facile color tuning is possible by simple changes in concentration and mixing ratio. Transfer of the multi-photochromic system to a commercially available solid matrix enables the manufacturing of reversibly rewritable, handheld 2D and 3D displays or optical memories with four-color resolution.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning reveals physicochemical drivers of bio-crude yield in hydrothermal liquefaction of water hyacinth
papers.abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a promising pathway for converting wet biomass into biocrude oil; however, the complex interactions among process parameters limit mechanistic understanding and optimization. In this study, an interpretable machine learning framework was developed to predict and analyze bio-crude yield from the HTL of water hyacinth using a curated dataset of 69 experimental observations. Unlike conventional ML approaches focused primarily on predictive accuracy, this work emphasizes interpretability to establish physically meaningful relationships between process parameters and HTL behavior. Multiple supervised models, including Multiple Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Gradient Boosting, were evaluated, with Gradient Boosting achieving the highest predictive performance (test R2 ≈ 0.83). SHAP-based analysis identified the O/C ratio, reaction time, and hyacinth-to-water ratio as dominant variables governing bio-crude formation. The observed trends are consistent with established HTL reaction mechanisms, highlighting the role of oxygenated functional groups in promoting depolymerization and the influence of reaction medium on product distribution. Furthermore, optimization analysis revealed an operating window of 240–250°C and 20–30 min, corresponding to predicted bio-crude yields of 35–38 wt%.

papers.title: Excited Triplet States during Organofluorine Molecular Dynamics upon Electron-Impact—A Study of Electronic Structure and Molecular Fragmentation
papers.abstract: The semiconductor industry’s reliance on high global warming potential (GWP) perfluorocarbon etchants motivates the search for environmentally sustainable alternatives. Although exchange scattering populates triplet states efficiently during electron-impact excitation, computational studies of organofluorine etchant fragmentation have been largely confined to the ground state or to static potential energy surface scans, leaving triplet-state dissociation dynamics essentially uncharacterised. This work addresses that gap by propagating ab initio molecular dynamics directly on the T1 surface, providing time-resolved mechanistic insight inaccessible to experiment alone. Specifically, it investigates the plasma fragmentation of three C4F6H2 isomers: cis-1,1,2,2,3,4-hexafluorocyclobutane (Cyclo); hexafluoroisobutylene (Iso); and (Z)-1,1,1,4,4,4-hexafluoro-2-butene (Z), as candidate lower GWP plasma etchants, using ab initio computational methods. Born–Oppenheimer Molecular Dynamics (BOMD) simulations on the first triplet (T1) surface, employing the BHHLYP density functional, provided direct access to post-excitation bond cleavage kinetics, while SA-CASSCF(10,10)/NEVPT2 coordinate scans and STEOM-CCSD excitation energies characterised the excited state electronic structure. Spin density calculations confirmed that triplet excitation in Iso and Z is strongly localised within the π orbitals of the C=C bond, consistent with the electrophore model, and revealed that spin density migrates to the σ/σ∗ orbitals of the dissociating bond during C–CF3 cleavage—a feature not previously visualised for these systems. A large T1–T2 gap (∼3 eV) in Iso and Z justified the single-surface approximation, whereas near-degeneracy of the first three triplet states (0.3 eV gap) in Cyclo rendered this approximation inadequate. For Iso and Z, C–CF3 cleavage was the kinetically dominant channel, with Z fragmenting consistently faster due to a larger pre-exponential factor. The simulated ·CF3 abundances closely matched the cumulative experimental yield of smaller fragments, suggesting that ·CF3 is the principal precursor to the deposition-promoting radicals observed by mass spectrometry. Cyclo exhibited effectively barrierless, non-selective fragmentation, producing predominantly small radicals associated with polymer deposition. These findings support the viability of Iso and Z as dual-purpose etchant-deposition gases and highlight the need for non-adiabatic dynamics to describe Cyclo fragmentation adequately.

papers.title: Guiding photochemical process intensification through kinetic diagnostics
papers.abstract: Photochemical methodologies are commonly optimized towards yield, yet yield alone provides limited insight into productivity and scalability. Here, we demonstrate how simple kinetic diagnostics can guide photochemical process intensification by identifying the dominant limitations governing reaction performance. Using the photochemical Minisci alkylation of phenanthridine with ethane as a representative gas-liquid transformation, systematic screening of pressure, mixing, light intensity, and temperature revealed the controlling transport and kinetic phenomena, enabling targeted engineering interventions and reactor selection. The resulting workflow guided the transition from batch to continuous flow and ultimately gram-scale synthesis, achieving a production rate of 19 g day-1 while operating under substantially less demanding conditions than the original methodology. Beyond improving productivity and energy efficiency, this work illustrates how integrating kinetic diagnostics into methodology development provides a practical framework for designing scalable photochemical processes.

papers.title: Simple and reproducible ready-to-use TMB solution for enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
papers.abstract: The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is a cornerstone of modern laboratory diagnostics, yet its routine implementation is often constrained by the cost and logistics of chromogenic substrates. While commercial 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) solutions offer superior stability, their high price is a significant burden. Conversely, standard laboratory preparations are inexpensive but suffer from poorly characterized stability, necessitating daily preparation. This study addresses this gap by developing a simple, robust, and cost-effective formulation for a ready-to-use TMB solution suitable for routine laboratory use. Following iterative optimization, a final composition was established: 5 mmol/L sodium citrate buffer (pH 4.0), 100 µmol/L EDTA, 10% DMSO, 0.42 mmol/L TMB, and 1 mmol/L H2O2. When stored at +4 °C for 23 days, this formulation exhibited a signal loss of less than 10% and a blank absorbance increase (from non-specific oxidation) below 15%. The reproducibility and robustness of the formulation were confirmed using reagents from multiple manufacturers and by demonstrating stable performance in a day-to-day use protocol. A cost analysis revealed a price of approximately $15 per liter, representing more than 30 times reduction compared to commercial alternatives. Furthermore, this work provides a mechanistic rationale for the signal decline observed in TMB solutions upon storage, attributing it primarily to the slow precipitation of TMB and, to a lesser extent, H2O2 decomposition. Based on this mechanistic understanding, we proposed clear pathways for the future development of even more efficient yet simple custom formulations.

papers.title: Influence of the surface Rock-Salt Layer in Ni-rich NMC cathodes
papers.abstract: Rock-Salt Layer (RSL) formation is one of the main degradation processes in Nirich cathodes for Li-ion batteries, giving rise to loss of capacity and cyclability. Our combined theory and experimental study examines in detail the impact of different compositions of the RSL that form on the surface of Ni-rich cathodes. We confirm the morphology of our RSL models by reproducing the RSL peak observed in experiments in the oxygen K-edge X-ray absorption spectra. Wannier-based charge analysis reveals the impact of the RSL in forming a preventive coating towards oxygen loss. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that a full RSL cover of the cathode surface completely prevents any Li movement through it on the simulation time scale, whereas Li-transport in a partially lithiated RSL is possible. Hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES) data vindicate build up of Li below the RS layer. The situation with a Ni vacancy in the RSL is more complicated: characterisation of the corresponding transition state and pathway for Li-ion migration shows that it is energetically unfavourable for Li transport through the RSL, despite the Ni vacancy, which is itself energetically unfavourable. Our study provides a microscopic basis for understanding the different morphologies possible for RSL and their impact on the cathode during cycling.

papers.title: Dual Digital Twins for Experimental Planning in Automated Laboratories: Physics-informed surrogate models for counterfactual experimental rollouts
papers.abstract: Automated laboratories increasingly combine automated and cloudified instruments, robotic operation, sample provenance and data infrastructures, and autonomous agents. Yet these capabilities primarily address execution, while planning remain limited to myopic optimization workflows or generic agentic approaches. At the same time, open decision-making algorithms such as MCDTs, reinforcement learning, or dynamic programming that worked exceptionally well for AlphaFold and MuZero are very limited for experimental scenarios due to extreme data requirements. We argue that experimental planning requires coupling three components: an experimental planner, a digital twin of the sample or material, and a digital twin of the instrument. The planner converts scientific objectives into hypotheses and plans candidate actions; the sample twin constrains possible material states and responses; and the instrument twin constrains observations, perturbations, and failure modes. The union of the twins enables virtual rollouts for multi-step experimental campaigns before physical action is taken. This also clarifies the uncertainty balance between calibration, where known samples update the instrument twin, and research, where a trusted instrument updates the sample twin. Practical deployment must accommodate proprietary instrument knowledge, allowing manufacturers to expose predictive outputs without revealing internal designs. Federated instrument twins across multiple instruments can further aggregate operational experience, including preconditions to rare failure events. Thus, dual digital twins become universal planning and knowledge-transfer objects for autonomous science providing necessary element for experiment design.

papers.title: Accurate 20 ms protein sizing with microscope‑based dynamic light scattering
papers.abstract: Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) is a powerful technique to probe nano to microscale objects in solution. Among its main limitations is the requirement of steady-state conditions during measurement, restricting its applicability towards time evolving systems. Here, we present a microscopy-based DLS approach using oblique illumination to significantly enhance the signal-to-background ratio compared to conventional confocal geometries. The coherence factor 𝛽 of the autocorrelation function increases to values above 0.9, approaching the ideal limit. Combined with a custom data analysis pipeline enabling post-acquisition processing over arbitrary time windows, this approach yields narrower and better-defined size distributions when averaging over shorter time intervals. Weak scatterers such as BSA proteins can be accurately measured at temporal resolutions down to 20 ms. These results extend the applicability of DLS beyond steady-state conditions and enable time-resolved size determination in dynamic systems.

papers.title: Visible range sub band gap photoexcitation of conductivehydrogenated nanodiamonds
papers.abstract: Hydrogenated milled nanodiamonds (H-MND) are emerging as original candidates for photocatalysis applications, demonstrating notably outstanding performances for PFOA degradation in water under solar-type illumination. However, the involved sub-band gap photoexcitation mechanisms remain poorly understood, as the material's electronic properties, such as its electron affinity, surface states, and Fermi level depend on both its surface chemistry and its interface with solvent. In this work, surface chemistry and unoccupied surface states of H-MND are investigated by X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) and Near Edge X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (NEXAFS), respectively. Their transient photoconductivity under UV and visible light is evaluated by Time-Resolved Microwave Conductivity (TRMC). Comparison with detonation hydrogenated nanodiamonds and oxidized nanodiamonds revealed that all materials exhibit surface states, but that only a hydrogenated surface combined with a high crystallinity (H-MND) induces the creation of free charge carriers under illumination. A broader look at ND band diagrams in air and in aqueous environments allowed us to deduce that ND electron affinity, coupled with the charge transfer equilibrium between ND and their environment, governs sub-band gap photoexcitation. After stabilization in aqueous colloid and creation of an adsorbate layer at the surface enhancing hole conductivity, H-MND exhibit intense photoconductivity at both 2.8 and 3.9 eV, attributed to electronic transitions from the valence band to unoccupied C-H surface states. This study provides crucial insights into the photoexcitation mechanisms of ND and confirms the use of H-MND as a new and efficient photocatalyst in water, even outperforming TiO2 under visible illumination.

papers.title: Mobility Suppression Boundary Principle for Polymer Glass-Transition Temperature
papers.abstract: Polymer glass-transition temperature (Tg) varies widely even among repeat units with similar visible chemistry and size. This manuscript formulates and tests the Mobility Suppression Boundary Principle (MSBP-Tg): within comparable chemistry-size fibers, upward Tg boundary displacement is associated with suppression of normalized local rotatable mobility. The density coordinate used here is exactly the sign reversal of rotatable-bond density, MSBP density = -NumRotatableBonds/heavy_atoms. Thus the contribution is not the invention of a new molecular descriptor. It is the physical and statistical use of normalized mobility suppression as a within-fiber boundary coordinate. Three post-lock source-family checks are consistent with this framing: a broad leak-excluded public Tg subset, a released NeurIPS Tg-known test subset, and a family-narrow Leeds PAEK stress test. Bootstrap confidence intervals, paired descriptor comparisons, shuffle controls, and contradiction taxonomy are reported to separate support from overclaiming.

papers.title: Tall oil pitch as a graphite feedstock: direct conversion of a biomassderived by-product into bulk graphite
papers.abstract: Tall oil pitch (TOP), a high-boiling by-product obtained from crude tall oil refining in the kraft pulping process, was converted into bulk graphite through catalyst-free thermal treatment. This result demonstrates that a biomass-derived industrial residue can serve directly as a feedstock for graphite. Without catalysts or prior purification, thermal treatment of TOP produced bulk graphite, as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction. The results indicate that graphite can be generated from multicomponent resin-derived residues through simple thermal processing. This work expands the range of candidate feedstocks for graphite production to include industrial by-products from biomass refining and suggests a route for upgrading TOP into a higher-value carbon material.

papers.title: Elucidating mobile charge carriers in polymeric carbon nitrides by transient surface photovoltage analysis
papers.abstract: Understanding charge carrier dynamics in granular photocatalysts is critical for rational materials design, yet conventional spectroscopies lack the spatial directionality needed to distinguish individual electron and hole contributions. Here, time-resolved surface photovoltage (TRSPV) spectroscopy is established as a contactless, carrier-resolved probe of charge transport in granular photoactive materials, using undoped and sulfur-doped polymeric carbon nitride (PCN) as model systems. A Marcus-Holstein small-polaron master-equation model is developed to simulate spatio-temporal carrier dynamics and calculate experimental observables, TRSPV, time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL), and carrier mobility, within a unified framework. We show that SPV signals in centrosymmetric granular materials can be described by two physical mechanisms: dielectric screening and depth-dependent carrier photogeneration. Joint fitting of TRSPV and TRPL datasets reveals electrons as the more mobile carriers and holes as the least mobile in PCN, with free electron and hole polaron mobilities corresponding to site energies of 530 meV and 800 meV, respectively, and a combined hopping rate of the order of 1 ns-1. Trap-limited hole transport is further suppressed at defect sites, where bound polaron binding energies reach 340 meV in the bulk and 570 meV at surface sites. Sulfur doping and crystallite size modulate trap-state populations and transport timescales, with defect concentration governing the crossover between trap-limited and defect-band transport regimes. The spectroscopic methodology and theoretical framework presented here are material-agnostic and transferable to the broader class of granular photoactive absorbers, establishing TRSPV as a deployable diagnostic for photoelectrocatalysis research and solar energy conversion.

papers.title: TD-DCC: An Interactive and Efficient Graphical User Interface-Based Time-Dependent Cross-Correlation Analysis from Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
papers.abstract: Dynamic cross-correlation matrix (DCCM) analysis is a widely used method for inferring correlated motions in biological macromolecules from molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Conventional implementations often result in a single time-averaged matrix from the entire trajectory. Thus, time-dependent cross-correlations between residues of interest and their oscillations are often difficult to analyze. Also, transient correlations are difficult to probe using the DCCM. This information is crucial for interpreting allosteric communication in bio-macromolecules. To address this limitation, we introduce TD-DCC, a dependency-light, single-file Tkinter desktop application with a graphical user interface (GUI) that computes time-dependent DCCMs directly from raw MD trajectories using user-defined sliding windows. TD-DCC relies on just four mainstream dependencies (NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and MDAnalysis) to aggregate per-window matrices into robust per-residue-pair statistics, including mean correlation, standard deviation, and probabilities of positive or negative occurrences. High computational performance is achieved through three core design choices: a non-blocking, event-driven graphical interface; a vectorized correlation engine utilizing NumPy’s Einstein summation routine to replace explicit residue loops with a single array operation; and a concurrent producer–consumer pipeline built on concurrent futures that streams trajectory data from disk via MDAnalysis rather than loading it entirely into memory. These statistics drive an interactive, three-panel dashboard featuring independently adjustable probability and correlation cut-offs, filtered CSV export, and a click-through time-series inspector, ultimately enabling a fluid “compute–filter–visualize” workflow that reduces the time and complexity of investigating complex dynamic allosteric communication analysis.

papers.title: Chlorinated Byproducts in Diisocyanates Synthesis from 35Cl NQR
papers.abstract: Chlorinated impurities in industrial diisocyanates production significantly impact product quality and stability, yet their speciation remains an analytical challenge. This study demonstrates that 35Cl NQR spectroscopy, supported by DFT calculations, provides a powerful framework for identifying byproducts in these processes. We show that NQR frequencies effectively categorize chlorinated species—such as amino hydrochlorides and carbamoyl chlorides—into distinct chemical families, with signal shifts driven by local electronic structure, intermolecular interactions, and conformation. Applied to commercial 4,4'-MDI, this analytic ruler successfully identifies the presence of specific byproducts and establishes 35Cl NQR as a uniquely sensitive tool for monitoring byproducts and thereby the quality of industrial diisocyanate streams.

papers.title: Quantifying Fragment Ambiguity in LC-HRMS/MS Spectral Databases
papers.abstract: LC–HRMS/MS-based non-target analysis relies heavily on MS2 spectral matching for compound annotation. However, not all fragments contribute equally to identification confidence, and quantitative measures of fragment ambiguity remain lacking. In this study, we developed a data-driven framework to assess fragment-level ambiguity through the Fragment Ambiguity Score (FAS), which combines fragment stability and specificity within precursor-mass-defined candidate spaces. FAS was evaluated using five experimental spectral databases (MassBank, MoNA, GNPS, NIST20, and MSnLib), comprising together 1,026,855 spectra and an in silico spectral library containing 256,865 spectra. The results showed that MS2 spectra contain both diagnostic and ambiguous fragments, with diagnostic fragments representing only a subset of the total fragmentation information available for a compound. Only 14.1% of fragments in the experimental databases and 10.7% in the in silico library exhibited low ambiguity (FAS ≤ 0.5). Fragment ambiguity showed a strong correlation with database composition, with fragments appearing highly diagnostic in smaller databases often becoming substantially more ambiguous when evaluated against larger and more diverse spectral collections. Differences between experimental and in silico databases further demonstrated the influence of database origin and composition on fragment ambiguity estimates. These findings demonstrate that the number of matched fragments alone is insufficient for confidence assessment and highlight the importance of complementary sources of evidence. The proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for assessing fragment ambiguity in spectral databases.

papers.title: Obtaining Dynamics of Supported Metal Nanoparticles using Cost-effective Training of Machine Learning Force Fields
papers.abstract: Metal–support interactions (MSI) play a critical role in heterogeneous catalysis by influencing catalyst stability and reactivity. A long-term objective is to model catalytic systems in simulated experiments, to obtain atomistic insights into MSI under reaction conditions. Achieving this goal requires extensive modelling of large atomistic systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFF’s) enable simulations at these scales by providing orders of magnitude speedups compared to density functional theory (DFT). However, effective fine-tuning of MLFFs requires smart sampling of the configurational space of supported nanoparticle systems. Notably, the chemically relevant interfacial region constitutes only a small fraction of the total atoms, highlighting the need for cost-effective training strategies. Here, we demonstrate two such strategies using Co/TiO2 as a model system: cross-polymorph training and reducing support slab layers. The latter lowers the number of electrons in each training structure, significantly reducing computational cost, which scales roughly cubically with electrons. Combining both strategies produced an accurate MLFF capable of revealing a novel minimum-energy configuration for a Co nanoparticle on TiO2 anatase. The presented strategies are applicable to all metal oxide-supported metal nanoparticle systems and enable the development of MLFFs capable of probing MSI at the atomistic scale.

papers.title: In situ salt-loaded cathode by mechanochemical modification for pre-metallation of next-generation metal-ion capacitors
papers.abstract: Metal-ion capacitors (MICs) as hybrid devices stand out for their high energy and power output. Their Achilles’ heel, however, is the mandatory pre-metallation, which is essential for the device to operate at its best. Depending on the chosen strategy, it results in safety issues, suffering in performance and time-consuming preparation. Herein, we present a holistic approach overcoming these limitations by mechanochemical in situ modification of sacrificial salts to provide additional metal-ions. Instead of treating the by-products in our carbon synthesis as waste, the loaded salts are transformed in a solid-state reaction directly inside the carbons’ pores to squarates and oxalates. A variety of tunable sacrificial salts based on Li, Na and K are successfully applied for electrochemical metal extraction, with the remaining carbon achieving up to 69 F g-1 depending on its porosity features. By utilizing the salt-loaded carbon as cathode material, fully operational lithium-ion and sodium-ion capacitors are realized – capable of showing a good rate performance and cycling stability. The approach proves to be a safe and straight-forward method for pre-metallation without the need of an external metal source while changing the former waste product to an essential part of devices’ performance.

papers.title: Unexpected Photochemical Synthesis of Unsubstituted AzaBenzannulated Perylenediimides and Bisazacoronene
papers.abstract: Unsubstituted nitrogen-doped coronene diimides (CDIs), named bisazacoronene diimides (uBACDs), were unexpectedly obtained by exposing perylene diimides (PDIs) linked to a pyrrole or furan derivative via an imine bond in their bay region. This cleavage depends on the presence of molecular oxygen: performing the same transformation in an oxygen-free environment yields the non-cleaved, functionalized azabenzannulated product. Theoretical calculations hint at possible singlet oxygen generation from the imine in the excited state, resulting in the decomposition of the pyrrole or furan substituents. Compared to CDIs, uBACDs show lower LUMO energy and the ability to form weak intermolecular anionic mixed-valence complexes upon electrochemical reduction. Their ease of synthesis and preliminary measurements in organic thin-film transistors position this new scaffold as a valuable building block for the development of new n-type organic semiconductors.

papers.title: A Synergistic Multimodal DEL-Driven Strategy with In Silico Guidance for SARS-CoV-2 PLpro Inhibitor Discovery
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) is a pivotal antiviral target due to its essential roles in viral replication and host immune evasion. Here, we report a synergistic, multimodal strategy driven by DNA-encoded libraries (DEL) and integrated with in silico guidance for the efficient discovery of novel PLpro inhibitors. This approach combines focused DEL screening, photo-crosslinking DEL for privileged fragment identification, and focused virtual screening, all guided by iterative rounds of X-ray crystallography and structure-based optimization. Initial focused DEL screening coupled with medicinal chemistry identified a cyclopropyl moiety as a key pharmacophore. To overcome the inherent chemical space limitations of the focused DEL, we constructed a virtual library for in silico screening; this integrated computational and crystallographic approach helped elucidate dynamic binding modes and pinpoint key interactions with residues including Lys157 and Glu167. Privileged fragments derived from an independent photo-crosslinking DEL screen subsequently guided a successful scaffold hop and further optimization. This workflow culminated in the discovery of multiple inhibitor series with distinct binding modes, exemplified by compounds SIMM-66 (IC50 = 49.8 nM, antiviral EC50 = 0.68 μM), SIMM-75 (IC50 = 29.0 nM, antiviral EC50 = 3.63 μM), and SIMM-83 (IC50 = 130 nM, antiviral EC50 = 2.80 μM). Collectively, the integrated strategy presented herein establishes a powerful and generalizable platform for the rapid discovery of high-quality inhibitors against challenging therapeutic targets.

papers.title: An efficient selective synthesis of E isomers of di-SF4-vinyl fluorides from pyridine-SF4-acetylene in presence of Triethyl borane.
papers.abstract: The synthesis of vinyl fluorides plays a crucial role in various scientific disciplines, including pharmaceutical and materials sciences. In this study, first time we present a direct and stereoselective method for the synthesis E isomers of Di-SF4-vinyl fluorides from pyridine-SF4-acetylene, in which the two heterocycles are connected by a rodlike trans-di-SF4 alkene linker, via the regioselective free radical addition, dehalogenation and followed by hydrogenation of pyridine–SF4–acetylene and Aromatic & Hetero aromatic SF4Cl in the presence of triethyl borane. this transformation proceeded at room temperature, providing the E isomer of di-SF4-vinyl fluorides in high selectivity. This methodology opens new avenues for the synthesis of enchanting di-SF4-containing fluorinated vinylic scaffolds, thereby providing advanced opportunities for novel drug discovery and fluorinated polymers.

papers.title: Production of Metallophores Rhodopetrobactin B and Methylolanthanin in Methylobacterium extorquens strains PA1 and AM1
papers.abstract: The closely related M. extorquens strains PA1 and AM1 carry near-identical metallophore synthesis gene clusters, yet AM1 produces the 4-hydroxy benzoate (4HB)-capped chelator methylolanthanin (MLL), while PA1 produces mainly 3,4-dihydroxy benzoate (3,4-DHB)-capped rhodopetrobactin (RPB) siderophores. We trace this divergence to a single tandem-duplication frameshift that inactivates AsbF, the dehydratase supplying the catecholate precursor 3,4-DHB. Unable to make 3,4-DHB this way, AM1 instead caps the scaffold with the ubiquitous primary metabolite 4-HB to yield MLL (a comparatively weak iron chelator), consistent with a weaker O-CAS assay readout when comparing AM1 to PA1. We further show that PA1 produces not only micromolar RPB B (with minor RPB A) but also nanomolar amounts of MLL and mixed-cap congeners. This directly confirms the promiscuity of the biosynthetic machinery and highlights how AM1 can still assemble a chelator despite lacking the catecholate precursor. The mixed aromatic cap chelator RPB B-O was characterized by HRMS and NMR and is named methylopetrobactin B. Further, by synthesizing 13C labelled RPB B and supplying it to PA1 we ruled out by mass spectrometry that MLL is a decomposition product of or that it is produced from RPB B. Finally, a feeding experiment of 3,4-DHB and AM1, revealed that this strain can make RPB B with externally supplied precursor. Taken together, this study demonstrates, that a single loss-of-function lesion (rendering one enzyme non-functional in vivo) can redirect a conserved pathway toward an alternative chelator.

papers.title: Acyl-Chain Unsaturation in the Cremimycin Macrolactam Yields Cremimycin B with
Cross-exposure transferability and failure boundaries of selfsupervised DNN denoising for AR-HAXPES depth profiling
papers.abstract: Laboratory-source angle-resolved hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (AR-HAXPES) is photon-starved atthespatialresolution required formapping,wheretheframe averaging needed to recover a clean depth profile at every position drives total acquisition time into a prohibitive regime. Self-supervised neural denoising offers an alternative to acquisition-time scaling, and a recent companion study1 has systematically benchmarked its performance against alternative strategies; however, its operational envelope across exposures, its cross-exposure transferability, and its failure modes in the photon-starved regime remain uncharacterised. Here we evaluate self-supervised denoising atthe smallestpossibletargetwindow across three exposures spanning a 25-fold range of per-frame photon flux on a model C / Al2O3 / TiO2 / Si multilayer. We identify an empirical directional rule for cross-exposure denoiser deployment — train S/N ≥ inference S/N —, characterise the failure boundary in the photon-starved regime where upstream denoiser collapse propagates into constraint-saturated inversion solutions, and locate the asymptotic reach of alltested denoising strategies (frame averaging, Self-DNN, Cross-DNN) relative to a methodological floor set by the reproducibility of the reference. Within the success region of this rule, cross-exposure transfer enables up to a 48-fold equivalent acquisition-time reduction on the depth-RMSE axis (14-fold on the Wasserstein-1 interface- localization axis) at the most photon-starved 4.8 s/frame condition. These results frame self- supervised AR-HAXPES denoising as a characterisable engineering operation with quantifiable failure boundaries and recovery routes, rather than as an empirical post-processing recipe.

papers.title: Hierarchically Porous Nanoparticle-based Aerogels with Engineered Backbone Porosity for Enhanced Stability and Functionality
papers.abstract: Precise control over the structural architecture of aerogels remains a central challenge, particularly for integrating well-defined nanoscale porosity within the aerogel backbone. Here, a nanoparticleassembly strategy is presented for fabricating aerogels with controlled backbone porosity using preformed mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as building blocks. This approach decouples network formation from pore generation, enabling independent control over composition, structure, and porosity. The resulting MSN aerogels exhibit a high specific surface area of 960 m2 g−1 and significantly enhanced adsorption performance compared to the corresponding powders, driven by improved accessibility of active sites within the hierarchical porous framework. The intrinsic surface roughness of the MSNs promotes interlocking of particles, leading to accelerated gelation, reduced percolation thresholds, and enhanced structural stability during wetting, as supported by experiments and computational modeling. In addition, the accessible and intact MSN network enables solid-state pH sensing through pre-gelation incorporation of a pH-responsive molecule. By integrating controlled nanoscale porosity with mechanically robust network architectures, this work establishes a general platform for designing aerogels with tunable backbone porosity for applications in adsorption and sensing.

papers.title: Predicting Amide-I Infrared Spectra Directly from Coarse-Grained Protein Simulations
papers.abstract: Theoretical vibrational spectroscopy methods are often necessary to interpret condensed-phase spectra. For some methods, such as those that use vibrational spectroscopic maps, the requisite atomistic molecular dynamics simulations can become prohibitively expensive for systems of interest. Here, we present a two-stage method for predicting amide-I region infrared spectra from coarse-grained protein simulations, which reduces the computational cost of spectral prediction. The first stage is a minimal, spectroscopically motivated backmapping diffusion model, and the second stage is a transformer-based, site-frequency perturbation model. The predictions replace the standard vibrational spectroscopic maps while preserving the core of the spectral calculation. We show that this framework predicts accurate infrared spectra for a wide variety of proteins. Finally, we show that the framework is modular, allowing for the integration of existing coarse-grained backmapping models.

papers.title: Demonstration of a Thermodynamic Cycle for Interpreting Cation-driven Tuning of Redox Chemistry
papers.abstract: Although it has been established that the properties of molecules and materials can be tuned via incorporation of secondary cations, a rigorous thermodynamic framework for interpreting the origins of such effects has remained elusive. Here, a thermodynamic cycle for cation-driven tuning is proposed that describes the fundamental relationship between shifts in the association constants of cations and shifts in reduction potentials. This cycle treats incorporated cations as guests and their redox-active acceptors as hosts and addresses the thermodynamic properties that underly the chemical behavior of the resulting host/guest complexes. Experimental validation of the thermodynamic cycle was carried out here with a macrocyclic uranium complex, [ UO 2 ], and Mg(TFSI) 2 (where TFSI is bis(trifluoromethyl)sulfonylimide), enabling calculation of high-correlation linear free energy relationships (LFERs) that demonstrate that the Lewis acidity of cations is correlated with swings in host/guest association constants which are, in turn, important drivers of previously studied but poorly parametrized relationships involving the redox properties of multimetallic species. The thermodynamic cycle reported here affords a new foundation for developing strategies and leveraging opportunities in cation-tunable chemistry.

papers.title: Systematic Exploration of the Ternary Dy–Ir–Sn System with Magnetic Property Investigation
papers.abstract: The ternary Dy–Ir–Sn system phase equilibria were investigated with a goal of identifying novel phases. Samples were prepared by arc-melting and subsequent annealing, then characterized using scanning electron microscopy, powder X-ray diffraction, and single crystal X-ray diffraction. To streamline the exploratory process, a scalable, high-throughput framework was developed to automate the summary of crystallographic data, which aids the systematic exploration of ternary intermetallic systems and provides a reproducible methodology for exploratory materials characterization. The newly identified intermetallic phases were further investigated using density functional theory (DFT) to probe their electronic structures, alongside magnetic characterization to elucidate their magnetic ground states. We report four novel ternary compounds: DyIrSn (ZrNiAl-type), Dy26Ir11Sn6 (Sm26Co11Ga6-type), Dy4Ir7Sn6 (U4Re7Si6-type), and Dy3Ir2Sn4 (Lu3Co2In4-type). Magnetic measurements were done on pure samples of bulk polycrystalline DyIrSn and Dy26Ir11Sn6, revealing antiferromagnetic- and ferrimagnetic-like behavior, respectively – with both inverse susceptibilities and Curie-Weiss fits consistent with a trivalent Dy3+ moment. In DyIrSn, there is an AFM-like transition near TN = 7.25 K, with a second anomaly near T2 = 4.9 K. Dy26Ir11Sn6 shows ZFC-FC irreversibility below 40 K likely due to magnetic ordering.

papers.title: Varying Mechanisms Dominate Formate Formation in Electrochemical CO2 Reduction on Cu, Au and Pb: A Constant Potential DFT-based Microkinetic Analysis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) offers a route to convert renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals while closing the anthropogenic carbon cycle. However, the technology remains immature and is limited by low selectivity and energy efficiency. These challenges are less severe for the two-electron products, carbon monoxide and formate, making them attractive targets. Formate is of particular interest due to its potential as an energy carrier and its relatively high market value. Yet its formation mechanism remains debated, hindering rational catalyst design. Here, we combine grand canonical DFT, a hybrid explicit-implicit solvent model and microkinetic simulations to elucidate the formate formation mechanism on Cu, Au and Pb, and show that distinct pathways dominate on each metal. On Cu, the formation of formate proceeds via O-down chemisorption of CO2 followed by protonation. In contrast, Au exhibits negligible activity, arising from a mechanism where adsorbed hydrogen atoms combine with incoming CO2 species. Finally, Pb facilitates a direct outer sphere-like process from physisorbed CO2 to formate, with high activity, which we attribute to its diffuse p-like states near the Fermi level, a feature shared by other formate-selective post-transition-metal catalysts. The variation of mechanisms for formate production likely underlie the difficulty of identifying universal activity descriptors for eCO2R and suggest that catalyst design might necessitate mechanism specific descriptors.

papers.title: In Operando Electrochemical Reduction of Indium Tin Oxide Contacts in Silicon Oxide Memristive Devices
papers.abstract: We report a study of current transient behaviour in silicon oxide memristive devices with indium tin oxide (ITO) top contacts. Constant-current electrical stress reveals that ITO-contacted devices exhibit chaotic conductance fluctuations and a single-phase transient in which the slow decay is suppressed, unlike the smooth, two-phase rise-and-decay response of devices with Au/Ti contacts. Through X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, spectroscopic evidence is provided that proton-driven electrochemical reduction of the ITO electrode decouples the two processes that the gold-contacted transient superimposes, leaving the initial conductance increase attributed to electronic charge-trapping in the bulk oxide while suppressing the slow decay phase normally observed in gold-contacted devices. Binding energy shifts in indium (~0.9 eV) and accelerated interfacial etch rates in stressed devices suggest sub-stoichiometric ITO formation. By suppressing the slow proton screening that masks it in gold-contacted devices, the ITO contact exposes the underlying trap-discharge relaxation, which is dispersive (stretched-exponential, exponent β < 1) with a field-free discharge time of a few seconds. The dispersion is itself bias-dependent, β decreasing with field from a near-single-rate field-free limit, so the strong dispersion measured under bias is in large part field-induced rather than intrinsic. These findings reveal that nanoscale electrode material selection critically determines the physical mechanisms governing conductance dynamics in memristive devices, with implications for neuromorphic computing and reliable nanoelectronic design.

papers.title: In Silico Drug Discovery of Novel Fluorinated Phenylpropanoic Acid Derivatives as Tubulin Colchicine Binding Site Inhibitors: A Systematic Lead Optimization Study
papers.abstract: Tubulin, a key structural protein involved in mitotic spindle formation, represents a validated anticancer target. The Colchicine Binding Site (CBS) on the beta-tubulin subunit offers a promising avenue for the development of novel antimitotic agents. In this study, we present a systematic in silico lead optimization workflow starting from a fluorinated phenylpropanoic acid scaffold (Salma-1) and culminating in the identification of Salma-3 as the best-performing analog. Using AutoDock Vina 1.2, QSAR modeling (XGBoost, ChEMBL n=1,180, R2=0.569), pkCSM ADMET profiling, DFT quantum chemical calculations (B3LYP/3-21G), and target fishing analysis via SwissTargetPrediction, we demonstrate that Salma-3 (SMILES: COc1cc(F)c(CC(C(C)C)C(=O)O)cc1F) achieves a binding energy of -6.55 kcal/mol, a predicted IC50 of 6.11 μM, QED of 0.883, and a clean ADMET profile with zero Lipinski violations. Importantly, Salma-3 exhibits superior drug-like properties compared to the reference drug Colchicine, including absence of P-glycoprotein efflux, clean CYP450 metabolism, and favorable molecular weight (258 Da vs. 399 Da). Target fishing analysis revealed potential secondary interactions with FFAR1 (-5.90 kcal/mol) and PPARG, suggesting a multi-target anticancer mechanism. These findings support Salma-3 as a promising lead compound warranting experimental validation.

papers.title: Boundaries of the Hammett Equation: Critical Window and Defenestration Window in CMS
“Peierls-like” distortion and high-coercivity cluster glass in lacunar CsCl-related phase: Co1.5Ni1.5Ga4
papers.abstract: This investigation focuses on the solid-state synthesis and a detailed structural and phase analytical investigation of the Co 𝑥 Ni 3−𝑥 Ga 4 series along a constant Ga compositional line within Co⎼Ni⎼Ga phase space. Combined analysis of single crystal X-ray diffraction and neutron powder diffraction of Co 𝑥 Ni 3−𝑥 Ga 4 , 𝑥 = 1.5 reveals a random distribution of Co and Ni over a single Wyckoff site, which contrasts with previous report suggesting atomic ordering. Phase analyses via X-ray powder diffraction indicates a vacancy order-disorder transition as the Co concentration increases beyond a critical limit. DFT calculation predicted a semi-metallic and nonmagnetic ground state, supported by the absence of magnetic peaks or intensity enhancement at 10 K neutron data compared to 300 K. Interestingly “Peierls-like” distortions are observed within the Ga substructure in the vacancy-ordered phase, whereas such distortions are absent in the vacancy-disordered phase. These distortions result in periodic charge localization and exhibit subtle alterations between room temperature and 180 K. Magnetic measurements further reveal cluster spin-glass behavior with a high coercivity. The non-trivial spin dynamics, coupled with large coercivity, makes this phase a compelling candidate for multifunctional applications.

papers.title: Descriptor Adequacy as a Materials-Regime Principle in MOF Adsorption Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine learning is changing how metal--organic frameworks (MOFs) are screened for gas storage and separation, but its reliability depends on a basic question: does the descriptor contain the physics that controls the adsorption property? Here we show that descriptor adequacy is not a universal property of a feature set, but a property of the materials regime being studied. Using a topology-held-out benchmark of 255939 MOFs and 27 adsorption targets covering uptake, working capacity, and selectivity, we identify when simple pore descriptors are sufficient and when local chemical information is needed. Pore geometry is highly transferable for high-pressure, volume-controlled adsorption, especially methane storage and hydrogen-rich pre-combustion conditions. Local chemistry becomes important for low-pressure CO 2 and CH 4 uptake and for separation-derived targets, where framework--guest interactions control adsorption preferences. We also find that good regression accuracy does not always give reliable discovery: post-combustion selectivity can show high R 2 while still missing many top-ranked candidates. These results provide a process-resolved guide for matching descriptor complexity to adsorption mechanism, topology transfer, and screening objective. More broadly, the study establishes descriptor adequacy as a materials-regime principle for MOF informatics.

papers.title: Observation of ”negative” persistent photoconductivity effect at T > 200 oC in N-polar GaN/AlGaN/GaN heterostructures
papers.abstract: It is rarely reported that semiconductor materials can exhibit the ”negative” persistent photoconductivity (PC) effect. In this work the ”negative” persistent PC effect was observed in the Nitrogen (N)-polar oriented GaN/AlGaN/GaN heterostructure under the sub-bandgap illumination (2.0-2.8 eV) in the temperatures range of 200-250 oC. This is the first observation of the negative persistent PC effect in semiconductor materials at such high temperatures. The phenomenon was explained based on the model, which assumes the interaction between the absorbed oxygen species on the N-polar GaN surface, the DX centers in the GaN channel layer and two-dimensional electron gas at GaN/AlGaN interface. The discovery of high temperature ”negative” persistent PC in N-polar III-nitrides heterostructures may lead to novel applications such as temperature stable optical memories. Furthermore the results presented here, together with our recent observation of record negative photoconductivity [ Advanced Photonics Research, p. 2500130, Oct. 2025 ], reveal new physics in N-polar nitride heterostructures.

papers.title: Accelerated characterization of active natural extracts with single-step microfractionation coupled to mass spectrometry and bioassays
papers.abstract: Microfractionation is a prominent alternative for the discovery and characterization of bioactive natural products in complex extracts (e.g., plant, fungal, or microbial); however, the method faces limitations as it requires arduous scale-up for complete characterization of molecules. Furthermore, the integration of microfractionation data with metabolomic data is still a complex and tedious process. To circumvent current limitations, we developed a microfractionation method allowing an integrated, reproducible, milligram-scale, 96-deep-well plate framework that combines biological and computational metabolomic readouts. Fractionation is coupled to a single quadrupole mass analyzer, which enables integration with high-resolution metabolomic outputs using adaptable Python scripts. To illustrate the method performances, we applied it to characterize extracts from 7 plants -- Macleya microcarpa, Macleya cordata, Ruta corsica, Thymus camphoratus, Helleborus foetidus, Hypericum hookerianum, and Hypericum olympicum -- spanning different extract complexity and biological activities. Over nine independent experiments, totaling 151 sequential injections, we obtained high reproducibility. Across the study, we utilized no more than 10 mg of crude extract per fractionation and we were able to isolate 17 compounds up to 1H NMR dereplication. Furthermore, we were able to link molecular class and specific molecules to bioactivity found in active extracts. Lastly, to facilitate the adoption of this workflow, we created a user-friendly graphical user interface. Our high-throughput, milligram-scale workflow reduces the need for scale-up and is broadly applicable to natural extracts and biological systems, thus allowing for rapid characterization of natural extracts.

papers.title: One Solvent Miscible with Three That Will Not Mix: A Graph-Theoretic Limit on One-Dimensional Miscibility Descriptors
papers.abstract: Solvent miscibility is commonly estimated using scalar polarity descriptors, including the Hildebrand solubility parameter, Snyder polarity index, and Godfrey miscibility number. On a compiled benchmark of 37 molecular solvents comprising 651 classified pairs, a single Hildebrand descriptor achieves a cross-validated AUC of 0.94. We show that this predictive success does not imply structural adequacy. The benchmark contains configurations where a single hub solvent, such as isopropanol, is miscible with three leaves ( n -hexane, glycerol, and propylene carbonate) that are mutually immiscible. This quartet forms an induced claw (K 1,3 ), a forbidden subgraph in any unit interval graph generated by a fixedthreshold scalar rule mapping solvents A and B to real-valued descriptor scores f (A) and f (B) , which predicts miscibility if their distance falls below a constant threshold τ (| f (A)− f (B)|< τ). By Roberts’ theorem, no such rule can represent this structure, regardless of its average predictive accuracy. The benchmark contains 55 induced claws across 8 immiscible triples, and these motifs persist under alternative classification boundaries for partially miscible pairs. A representation based on the dielectric constant and molar volume possesses sufficient geometric freedom to represent the witness claw, but this added dimensionality alone does not improve global predictive performance (ROC AUC = 0.830, compared with 0.834 for the dielectric constant alone). Incorporating hydrogen-bonding information instead raises the cross-validated ROC AUC to 0.948, while the three-dimensional Hansen representation achieves 0.959. These results illustrate that multidimensional descriptor spaces are not subject to the unit-interval obstruction that excludes one-dimensional fixed-threshold representations of graphs containing an induced claw.

papers.title: Synergistic Dual Single-Atom Fe–Co Catalysts Anchored on Covalent Organic Framework/g-C3N4 Heterostructures for Ultrabroadband Artificial Photosynthesis via Solar CO2 Reduction and Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: The efficient conversion of solar energy into chemical fuels through artificial photosynthesis represents one of the most promising approaches for mitigating global energy shortages and anthropogenic CO2 emissions. Nevertheless, simultaneously achieving highly selective CO2 photoreduction and efficient hydrogen evolution remains challenging because of sluggish reaction kinetics, limited visible-light absorption, rapid charge recombination, and insufficient active sites. Herein, we propose a novel hierarchical photocatalyst comprising atomically dispersed Fe–Co dual single atoms anchored on a covalent organic framework (COF)/g-C3N4 heterostructure (Fe–Co-SA/COF/g-C3N4). The strong electronic interaction between neighbouring Fe and Co single atoms establishes abundant asymmetric Fe–N4–Co catalytic motifs, while the crystalline COF provides highly ordered π-conjugated pathways that significantly accelerate charge transport. Simultaneously, intimate interfacial contact between the COF and g-C3N4 generates an efficient S-scheme heterojunction, promoting directional migration of photogenerated electrons and holes while preserving their strong redox potentials. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Fe–Co dual sites reduce the energy barrier for CO2 activation by approximately 45% compared with isolated Fe sites, whereas Gibbs free-energy analysis demonstrates favorable adsorption of *COOH and *H intermediates. Artificial intelligence-assisted catalyst optimization further identifies the optimal Fe/Co atomic ratio and coordination environment, enabling ultrabroadband solar harvesting extending from ultraviolet to near-infrared wavelengths (300–1800 nm). Under simulated AM 1.5G solar irradiation, the optimized Fe–Co-SA/COF/g-C3N4 photocatalyst achieves remarkable CO evolution rates exceeding 1450 μmol g-1 h-1, CH4 production of 165 μmol g-1 h-1, and H2 evolution of 12.4 mmol g-1 h-1, together with an apparent quantum efficiency approaching 18.6% at 420 nm and a solar-to-fuel efficiency of 2.8%. Excellent photocatalytic stability is maintained over ten consecutive reaction cycles with negligible structural degradation. This work demonstrates how dual single-atom engineering integrated with crystalline COF/g-C3N4 heterostructures provides a powerful strategy for constructing next-generation artificial photosynthetic systems capable of simultaneously producing solar fuels and green hydrogen with exceptional efficiency.

papers.title: Refinement of the Electrochemical Description of the Nitrogenase Cofactor: Ground States, Activation and N2 Selectivity from Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Biological nitrogen (N2) fixation by the metalloenzyme nitrogenase is the main enzymatic route which generates ammonia under ambient conditions. Yet, quantum mechanical description of this process remains challenging due to inaccurate energetics of number of close lying states and reaction pathways. Here, we benchmark Density Functional Theory (DFT) with Hubbard U correction against explicitly correlated many‑body quantum Monte Carlo calculations for key states of the iron molybdenum-cofactor (FeMo-co). Using this combined approach, we find the broken-symmetry (BS) 7 type magnetic ordering as the most stable native state (E0) and a triply protonated state (E3) as the electrochemical resting state of the cofactor. We further show that 2 activation of the cofactor proceeds through H2S/HS- unsealing, with an onset potential of -0.88 V vs RHE, close to the experimental ATP/ADP potential (-0.7 V vs RHE) at pH 7. DFT+U revised thermodynamics of the N2 reduction reaction (N2RR) indicate *N2 protonation and S-vacancy unsealing to be the main bottlenecks. Combined energetics of these steps place nitrogenase close to the top of the N2RR volcano within ~0.2 eV of the ATP/ADP experimental onset. Finally, we also extract the adiabatic proton transfer barriers, which suggest that the hydrogen evolution reaction is kinetically hindered relative to N2RR due to the greater distance of the water proton donors from the Fe-Fe active site. Ultimately, this work underscores the importance of the correlated treatment of Fe metal centers and their propensity to unseal and activate with the evolution of hydrogen sulfide ions as the key to the cofactor’s activity towards N2RR.

papers.title: Correlated-Electron Theory of Triplet-Triplet Multiexciton States in Polypentacene
papers.abstract: We present correlated-electron calculations of optical spin-singlet and triplet-triplet multiexciton states in three-and four-unit pentacene oligomers as microscopic models for polypentacene. The calculations use the Pariser-Parr-Pople Hamiltonian, multiple-reference singles and doubles configuration interaction, and a molecular exciton basis that resolves Frenkel, charge-transfer, and triplet-pair (T 1 T 1 ) configurations in real space. We find that the complete set of 1 (T 1 T 1 ) eigenstates lies in a narrow, nearly degenerate energy window near the lowest optical exciton and that no eigenstate can be identified with a single localized triplet-pair configuration. Instead, each triplet-pair eigenstate is a quantum superposition of configurations containing all accessible intertriplet separations. This electronic structure explains the perceived absence of intramolecular triplet diffusion in pentacene oligomers, polypentacene, and polytetracene solutions, while leaving open the possibility of intermolecular singlet fission in films with appreciable interchain interactions.

papers.title: Structural Homology Allows Alloyed II-V Magic-Sized Clusters with Continuously Tunable Emission
papers.abstract: Magic-sized clusters are atomically precise nanoparticles that eliminate heterogeneous broadening, thereby enabling narrow ensemble emission. However, the discrete structural stability that causes only certain sized clusters to exist also inherently disallows continuous optoelectronic tunability. New strategies are required to allow magic-sized clusters to continuously cover regions of the visible spectrum. Herein, we investigate the atomic structures of two oleate-ligated Cd3P2-450 and Cd3As2-525 clusters and conclude that they are structurally homologous based on pair distribution function analysis. The structural similarities between Cd3P2-450 and Cd3As2-525 allow alloying of P and As in these magic-sized clusters without perturbing the structure or the impressive optical properties. Ligand exchange for phosphinate then produces Cd3P2-xAsx magic-sized clusters with continuously tunable, narrow, and bright emission from blue (λmax = 469 nm) to green (λmax = 550 nm).

papers.title: A Systems Pharmacology and In-silico Analysis of Neurotherapeutic Potential of Withania somnifera Extract for Treating Parkinson’s Disease
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a chronic and progressive neurodegenerative illness that is mainly characterized by motor symptoms but non-motor symptoms (NMS), such as anxiety, depression, and cognitive decline in PD patients also affects their daily lifestyle. Serotonin receptors, on the other hand, are known to be a significant therapeutic target because the NMS in PD are linked to the disruption and modulation of serotonergic pathways. Current treatments for NMS include buspirone (anxiety), pimavanserin (psychosis), escitalopram and sertraline (depression or anxiety) However, these drugs are linked with adverse side effects such as, nausea, insomnia, dizziness, constipation and sexual dysfunction. Therefore, to solve this problem a safer alternative is required as a therapy as prolonged use of these medications is associated to negative side effects and limited efficacy in treating NMS. In our study, we have found out Withaferin A, hypericin, amentoflavone, ginkgetin, and an isoquinoline derivative were identified as the most potent candidates after molecular docking serotonin with 200 natural metabolites retrieved from PubChem and were further screened using ADMET analysis. Through the molecular docking, ADMET and molecular dynamics simulations, as a result Withaferin A was found to bind with serotonin receptor in a steady manner. By re-docking major withanolides that are present in Withania somnifera, we found out all major withanolides indicates their potential as neurotherapeutic candidate for reducing NMS in PD.

papers.title: 2DIR Hyperspectral Imaging of Polariton Propagation Reveals Fewer Dark Modes per Polaritons
papers.abstract: Molecular vibrational polaritons, hybrid quasi-particles formed by strong coupling between a photonic cavity mode and vibrational modes, offer a new way to modify chemical reactions, material morphologies, and energy transport. Yet, the underlying mechanism for polariton modification has remained controversial. Theory predicts that each polariton is outnumbered by ~10 6 –10 12 dark states that behave like uncoupled molecules, implying that polariton contributions should be negligible. To address this paradox, we directly quantify the number of dark modes per polariton (N D/P ) experimentally. Using W(CO) 6 vibrational polaritons in a Fabry–Perot cavity, we tracked their spatial propagation and analyze it using a kinetic model, through which we experimentally extracted N. From this, we find N D/P = 10 3.2±0.4 , several orders of magnitude smaller than the theoretical estimates based on the single cavity mode approximation. This result demonstrates that polaritons contribute far more significantly to molecular dynamics than previously assumed, providing a mechanistic foundation for understanding and advancing polariton-modified chemistry.

papers.title: A Platinum-Gallium Z-Type Complex Enables Highly Regioselective Hydrosilylation of N-Heteroarenes
papers.abstract: The bimetallic complex Pt[Ga(CH2-2-C6H4PPh2)3], herein PtP3Ga, was synthesized and fully characterized. A Z-type interaction between Pt–Ga is proposed and supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) analysis. This cooperative design was found to efficiently and selectively perform the 1,2-hydrosilylation of quinoline and pyridine derivatives, with a broad scope of more than 20 substrates. This catalytic system can achieve turnover numbers (TON) of up to 20000, to our knowledge, among the highest reported for hydrosilylation of aromatic N-heterocycles. Mechanistic studies suggest that the PtP3Ga complex functions as the active catalytic species and support a Chalk-Harrod-type pathway. These findings are consistent with the potential of Z-type ligands in enabling new reactivity at transition metal centers.

papers.title: Probing sp and sp3 carbon radicals in UHV by iodine capture
papers.abstract: Carbon-centered radicals are promising platforms from which to base on-surface chemical syntheses and bottom-up nanofabrication. Using germaadamantane molecules bound to a Si(100)-2x1 surface, long-lived sp and sp3 carbon radicals were generated under ultra-high vacuum (UHV) conditions at 300 K via homolytic carbon-iodine (C–I) bond scission using unpolarized ultraviolet (UV) irradiation. Monitoring the surface-bound molecules via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed that the deiodination efficiency was dependent on the angle between the Si(100) surface and the incident UV light. Molecular iodine produced in vacuo was used to reiodinate the carbon radical sites, and the known C–I binding energy shifts in the I 3d XPS spectra confirmed that the previously cleaved C–I bonds were regenerated. To confirm the radical character of the deiodinated carbon atoms, H2 gas was introduced into the vacuum chamber between the de- and reiodination steps. As expected, H2 had no effect on the reiodination efficiency for the less-reactive sp3 carbon-centered radicals, whereas it fully quenched the more-reactive sp carbon-centered radicals, validating the radical assignments. Furthermore, the effect of submonolayer molecular coverage on the reiodination efficiency was explored; for both radicals, lower molecular coverage and greater amounts of iodine bonding to the Si surface led to greater reiodination efficiency—up to 100% for the sp3 carbon radicals—while higher coverages and less surface-bound iodine resulted in less efficient reiodination.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of NMR spectra helps to determine the structure of an unexpected product of a ruthenium-catalyzed [2+2] cycloaddition
papers.abstract: Ruthenium-catalyzed reaction of alkyne with vinyl acetate unexpectedly gives 1,4,4-substituted cyclobutene, which can undergo selective thermal ring opening to 1,3-diene and subsequent 1,5-hydrogen shift. The structures of the products were successfully determined by analysis of 1H and 13C NMR spectra using large language models.

papers.title: PARSEC.py: A Python-based Real-space Kohn–Sham Density Functional Theory Code Accelerated by Machine Learned Charge Density
papers.abstract: PARSEC.py is a Python-based real-space Kohn–Sham density functional theory (real-space KS-DFT) framework designed to provide a user-and developer-friendly platform for firstprinciples electronic-structure simulations. Discretization on real-space grids eliminates basisset approximations, while enabling systematic control of numerical accuracy and large-scale parallelization. Building upon the theoretical foundations of the original PARSEC code, the framework leverages the Python scientific ecosystem to support modular development and integration with modern machine learning (ML) tools. PARSEC.py incorporates ML-predicted density as an alternative initial guess for the superposition of atomic density (SAD) in self-consistent field (SCF) iterations. This capability provides a framework for integrating ML models into electronic-structure calculations and offers a pathway for accelerating SCF convergence. We present the theoretical framework, key algorithms, and performance characteristics of PARSEC.py using both SAD and ML initializations.

papers.title: Total Syntheses of Tricrilactones D and F, Crispatumine I and 2,3-trans-Crispatumine I; a Bio-inspired Three-Component Cascade to Access the Lactone-fused 9/5/6 Spirocyclic Framework
papers.abstract: Tricrilactones B-F and crispatumines G-K, anti-osteoporotic macrolides isolated from Trichocladium crispatum , all possess a unique 9/5/6 spiroketal-containing tricycle fused to a substituted lactone. We herein report the total syntheses of tricrilactones D and F, crispatumine I, and an anticipated natural product, 2,3- trans -crispatumine I. Our approach constructs the conserved 9/5/6 spirocyclic core in a single step via a three-component biomimetic cascade of protrilactione A, the purported biosynthetic precursor, reacting with an aldehyde and ß-ketolactone. Notably, this method accesses both homo-coupled and hetero-coupled products by variation of the ß-ketolactone used and introduces a substituent at C-21 by variation of the aldehyde component. The synthetic route affords tricrilactones D and F, crispatumine I and 2,3- trans -crispatumine I each in 13 steps (longest linear sequence). The observed innate diastereoselectivity of the biomimetic cascade provides insight into the selection of natural products isolated to date and may pre-empt the isolation of several 2,3- cis - and 2,3- trans- diastereomers from natural sources.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Sodium-Ion Diffusivity in Sodium-Ion Batteries: Mechanisms, Characterization Techniques, Materials Design, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: One of the fundamental kinetic parameters governing the electrochemical performance of sodium-ion batteries is Ion Diffusivity. Though sodium-ion batteries have advantages when it comes to cost, sustainability, and material abundance in comparison to lithium-ion batteries, their widespread application is hindered by sluggish Na+ diffusion that is caused by the larger ionic radius and higher migration barriers of sodium ions. This review comprehensively examines Na+ diffusion mechanisms in electrode materials and electrolytes, experimental and computational methods for diffusivity evaluation, structure–diffusivity relationships in cathode and anode systems and recent strategies for enhancing ion transport. Current challenges and future research directions toward high-rate, long-life SIBs are discussed. This paper presented at International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Advanced Sciences and Technologies 2026

papers.title: Stability Trends of Surface and Subsurface Interstitial Transition Metal Species on CeO2(111)
papers.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) on reducible oxides are generally assumed to consist of isolated metal atoms located at the surface and directly accessible to reactants. Recent studies on Pt/CeO 2 (111), however, revealed that Pt preferentially occupies subsurface interstitial sites. Here, we investigate whether this behavior is unique to Pt or represents a more general phenomenon. Using density functional theory, we systematically compare the stability of surface and subsurface configurations for transition-metal atoms from Fe to Au on stoichiometric CeO 2 (111). Pronounced periodic trends emerge: the tendency toward subsurface incorporation increases from the 3d to the 5d series and from the Fe group toward the Ni group, with Pt and Pd exhibiting the strongest preference. Several metals also induce oxygen migration and surface reconstruction, generating additional stable configurations. Calculated CO vibrational frequencies provide spectroscopic fingerprints for experimental identification. These results demonstrate that subsurface incorporation is a general structural motif in SACs on reducible oxides, challenging the conventional view of surface-bound single-atom catalysts.

papers.title: FIREX: Fast-Ion Replica EXchange enables rapid sampling of Mg2+ pairing with nucleic acids
papers.abstract: We introduce Fast-Ion Replica EXchange (FIREX), a Hamiltonian Replica Exchangebased sampling strategy specifically designed to enhance the sampling of metastable divalent cation binding with phosphate groups, e.g. in nucleic acids. We parameterize the scheme and demonstrate its convergence and efficiency on a model DNA dodecamer with Mg2+ ions, using two force fields with very different ion pairing properties to test its robustness. The highest replica is driven by a “fast-ion” Hamiltonian combining a reduced ion charge with a tuned pair-specific Lennard-Jones interaction between the ion and phosphate oxygen atoms, yielding rapid exchange as well as moderate binding affinity, amenable to efficient sampling. By enabling the robust quantification of divalent ion interactions in simulations, FIREX could be instrumental in refining force fields to better capture ion-molecule interactions. The provided guidelines for the design of fast ion models suitable for FIREX are general and could be extended to other force fields or types of biomolecular moieties, such as carboxylated protein side chains, phosphorylated proteins, or other interaction sites on nucleic acids. We further demonstrate how FIREX can be efficiently combined with the REST2 method to achieve simultaneous sampling of ion binding and biomolecular conformations. This shows that different HREX schemes, including REST2, can be merged into a combined, highly cost-effective HREX scheme and is a step towards robust, computationally efficient sampling of charged biomolecules in interaction with divalent ions.

papers.title: Modelling Mixture Permeation across Microporous Membranes using the Maxwell-Stefan Diffusion Formulation
papers.abstract: Binary mixture diffusion in microporous crystalline materials is characterized by a set of three M-S diffusivities: Ð1, Ð2, and Ð12. The Maxwell-Stefan (M-S) diffusivities Ð1, and Ð2 characterize interactions of guest molecules with pore walls. The exchange coefficient Ð12 quantifies correlation effects that result in slowing-down of the more mobile species due to correlated molecular jumps with tardier partners. Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation data for a wide variety of binary mixtures in several zeolites, and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) demonstrate that the M-S diffusivities are dependent on the pore occupancy occupancy, θ ; the quasi-chemical theory provides the appropriate theoretical framework to quantify the occupancy dependence. The M-S diffusivities Ð1, and Ð2 in binary mixtures can be estimated with reasonably good accuracy from the corresponding unary diffusivities, evaluated at the same pore occupancy, θ . The exchange coefficient Ð12 can be estimated from the unary exchange coefficients Ð11 and Ð22 using the Vignes interpolation formulation developed for bulk fluid mixtures. Correlation effects are of significant importance in structures with intersecting channels (MFI, ISV, BEA), cavities with large windows apertures (FAU, NaY, NaX, CuBTC, IRMOF-1, MOF-177), and 1D channels with channel dimension > 8 Å (AFI, MgMOF-74, MIL-47, MIL-53(Cr), BTP-COF)/ Correlation effects are considerably less significant in hosts such as LTA, CHA, DDR, and ZIF-8, that consist of cages separated by narrow windows in the 3.2 Å – 4.2 Å size range. Experimental data on unary and binary mixture permeation across SAPO-34, DDR, ZIF-8 and MFI membrane are modelled using the M-S formulation. The experimental data confirm the expectations based on MD simulation data.

papers.title: Regioselective distal C(4)–H arylation of naphthalene directed by simple acetamido group at position C(2)
papers.abstract: Herein, we report preferential C(4)-arylation of the naphthalene in N-(naphthalen-2-yl)amides is with aryl halides in the presence of a palladium catalyst and silver salt under mild reaction conditions. The developed efficient protocol yields C(4)-arylated naphthylamides in good to high yields with broad functional group tolerance. Silver salt, in particular silver carbonate, was found to be crucial for catalytic cycle, regenerating palladium catalyst most probably as iodide scavenger. The reaction is proposed to proceed via generation of a palladium(IV) intermediate at adjacent C(3)-position, accompanied by transfer of aryl group to C(4)-position, and followed by β-hydride elimination. As revealed by X-ray structure analysis, product bearing phenyl group at C(4)-position forms hydrogen-bonded network in solid state.

papers.title: DATA-DRIVEN CAUSAL DISCOVERY IN CATALYSIS
papers.abstract: Catalysts are essential for the transition towards more sustainable chemical processes. However, their design still relies largely on empirical strategies, limiting the systematic understanding of how synthesis variables and reaction conditions influence catalytic performance and final material properties. This work applies causal discovery methods to two catalytic case studies: an OCM reaction dataset and an in-house dataset on metal-supported zeolite synthesis. The aim is to investigate the intrinsic causal structures underlying catalytic systems and to move beyond purely correlational analysis. The generated graphs revealed only two causal relationships for the first dataset and showed a frequent identification of latent variables. These results highlight the complexity of catalytic datasets and demonstrate the potential of causal discovery as an exploratory tool for studying synthesis–property–performance relationships. Take-home message. Causal discovery can support catalysis research as an exploratory tool, helping identify robust causal signals while exposing hidden confounding and uncertainty. In the studied datasets, only a few directed relations were consistently recovered, showing that causal interpretation remains strongly limited by data size, variability and latent factors.

papers.title: Physics-guided modelling of temperature-dependent electrical conductivity of functional oxides
papers.abstract: Functional oxide materials are widely employed across a range of electronic applications, where electrical conductivity and its temperature dependence serve as key screening metrics for material suitability. Across these applications, experimental characterisation remains resource-intensive and time-consuming. As a result, machine learning approaches have recently emerged as a digital alternative to accelerate materials discovery processes. However, datadriven approaches are typically restricted by the lack of a comprehensive experimentally-sourced database, with existing models trained on simulated density-functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we compiled an experimental database of over 7,000 temperature-dependent electrical conductivity samples for oxides, primarily extracted from commercial materials databases and peer-reviewed literature. We benchmark MODNet, a state-of-the-art general purpose composition-based machine learning baseline, against TriCondNet (a three-specialist conductivity network), a novel physics-guided neural network (PGNN) architecture developed to capture temperature-dependent electrical conductivity behaviour of metallic and semiconducting oxides. Our results demonstrate that TriCondNet outperforms baseline models on standard error metrics while adhering to the physical models for temperature–conductivity dependence. We then applied our top-performing model to an extensive composition list, screening candidates for two different application-specific case studies: dielectric and thermoelectric materials. Candidates were ranked based on their required conductivity relevant to the case study and associated uncertainty estimates. The resulting top ranked candidates matched materials already recognised as leading dielectrics and thermoelectrics, confirming that the workflow recovers established high-performers and establishing TriCondNet as a reliable basis for identifying new candidates through composition interpolation across known oxide families.

papers.title: PolyDiT: Masked Diffusion Transformers for Polymer Generation and Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Polymer repeat unit representation is not neutral preprocessing for diffusion models because it defines the feasible set, constraint locality, and chemical granularity of denoising.
