We introduce PolyDiT, a bidirectional discrete Diffusion Transformer (DiT) framework that learns polymer generation and propertypredictive features through masked reconstruction of representation-indexed polymer states. PolyDiT compares SMILES, SMILES byte pair encoding (SMILES-BPE), SELFIES, Group SELFIES, and graph states while holding the masking schedule, sampling protocol, and property head protocol fixed. Across 20 generation runs with 10,000 samples each over small, medium, large, and extra large model sizes (S, M, L, and XL), SELFIES reaches the decoded validity ceiling, Graph keeps the required two attachment points among valid samples and improves validity from 0.592 to 0.894 from S to XL, and Group SELFIES preserves high novelty relative to the training set. Property prediction follows a different pattern: Graph and SMILES achieve the most consistently strong held-out prediction performance across the eight targets. PolyDiT shows that polymer generation and property prediction should not be forced through a single preferred representation, but organized around the representation that best matches the chemical constraint and learning objective.

papers.title: Development of a High Throughput Automated Titration System Relevant for Extraction of Critical Metals
papers.abstract: An accurate determination of the acidity (pKa) of extractants in biphasic solvent systems is crucial, as this physicochemical property impacts efficiency and selectivity in the recovery of technologically critical metals. The conventional manual or semi-automated titrations used for this purpose frequently require substantial human input to operate continuously. This work demonstrates the construction of a modular automated titration system to address these limitations and provides a framework for measuring pKas in the organic phase, for a more realistic representation of industrial solvent extraction processes. The automated system integrates three Tecan Cavro XLP6000 syringe pumps with 9 programmable channels each for the delivery of liquids, and a laboratory grade probe for pH measurement. The pumps and pH electrode are controlled by commands executed in Rxn Rover, an open-source automation software developed in LabVIEW. The system incorporates closed-loop data analysis through pKaScope, a Python package, also integrated into Rxn Rover, eliminating post-experiment workload. The low-polarity diluents in which the measurements were taken directly reflect nonpolar environments typical of industrial solvent extractions, and our workflow shows remarkable precision over replicate experiments. By facilitating smooth configuration changes and performing automatic rinse protocols between experiments, capabilities that are impractical with manual methods, this automated system allows for high-throughput analysis that continuously performs experiments and subsequent data analysis. Overall, the modularity of the system allows for its potential application to other chemical techniques that require robust handling of liquid solutions and rapid analysis of data. This feature can also enable its transition into a fully self-driving system that monitors experimental progress and makes real-time changes without human intervention.

papers.title: Engineered Fluids Unlock Coupled Geological Hydrogen and Critical Mineral Recovery from Ultramafic Rocks
Direct Determination of the Acidity of Organophosphorus Extractants in Nonpolar Organic Solvents Using Biphasic Potentiometric Titrations
papers.abstract: The current revolution in artificial intelligence (AI) has catalyzed global demand for electronic components and the critical metals that make up these electronic systems. This new demand has increased strain on the already thinly stretched global supply chains that provide the materials for electronic components. Innovation in the field of critical metal separation can help to relieve supply train stress and provide the required critical materials more efficiently. The current state of the art utilizes acidic organophosphorus ligand extractants for industrial biphasic solvent extraction of technologically critical metals. The acidity of these extractants governs their performance during extraction of critical metals and is quantified through potentiometric titration methods. Traditional titration methods extrapolate aqueous pKa. This approach fails to capture true pKa values as in a real nonpolar solvent environment. Herein, we demonstrate methodology measurement of pKas of representative extractants in the organic phase directly for the first time. Titrations were undertaken in biphasic systems for straightforward measurement of protonation in hydrophobic organic solvents. Following a transformation of the titration curve into proton binding isotherms, the pKa in the organic phase is calculated using pKaScope, a Python library and command-line interface program developed in-house. Results reveal multiple pKas for various hydrophobic ligands, ascribable to monomeric and dimeric acidic dissociation. The pKas were also shown to scale linearly with solvent hydrophobicity, highlighting the effect of solvation on the acidity of these extractants.

papers.title: Ratiometric Luminescent Thermo-Hygrometry, Metal-Dependent Second Harmonic Generation, and Humidity-Variable Magnetic Relaxation in a Manganese(II)-Doped Zinc(II) Molecular Halide
papers.abstract: Molecular materials based on metal complexes can link optical, electrical, and magnetic properties, all sensitive to external stimuli. This feature opens a pathway for their exploration as highly efficient sensors and advanced switches. We report the synthetic strategy for a truly multifunctional material linking dual-stimuli optical sensing with tunable non-linear optical activity and chemically modulated magnetic response. This was realized by incorporating magneto-luminescent Mn(II) ions into a Zn(II) molecular halide of [ZnII(dppmO2)3][ZnIICl4]·nH2O (1) (dppmO2 = bis(diphenylphosphino)methane). The heterometallic {ZnII 0.9MnII0.1} material (2) exhibits dual photoluminescence (PL), including UV-PL from dppmO2 ligands coordinated to Zn(II) and red-PL from d-d electronic transitions of octahedral Mn(II) centers. Thanks to this optical feature and water vapor sorption capability, 2 exhibits ratiometric luminescent thermo- hygrometry in the around room-temperature (RT) region, being able to detect both temperature and relative humidity (RH) through the ratio between two PL signals. Due to the crystallization in a polar Pna21 space group, 1 and 2 exhibit distinct second-harmonic generation at RT, with its 3-fold enhancement induced by Mn(II) dopants. Thanks to the presence of Mn(II) complexes in water-sensitive Zn(II) halide, 2 also reveals RH-variable slow relaxation of magnetization realized by modulation of a Raman process.

papers.title: Direct Photocatalytic Synthesis of 1,3,4-Oxa(thia)diazoles from aldehydes and (thio)hydrazides.
papers.abstract: 1,3,4-Oxa(thia)diazoles have a great interest in different areas of chemistry. Despite the different methodologies reported in the literature, a general approach under mild photocatalytic conditions would broaden the applications of these molecules. Here we report a visible-light photocatalytic synthesis of 1,3,4-oxadiazoles and 1,3,4thiadiazoles from readily available aldehydes and (thio)hydrazides using an acridine photocatalyst under mild conditions. The scope was found to be broad, and gram-scale synthesis was achieved. Surprisingly, the transformation proceeds efficiently under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions despite constituting a net oxidative process. Mechanistic investigations combining Stern-Volmer analysis, radical-trapping experiments, quantum-yield measurements, cyclic voltammetry, and control reactions reveal that the in situ-formed protonated hydrazone is the primary quencher of the excited photocatalyst and that the reaction proceeds via a closed photoredox cycle involving radical intermediates. Most notably, cyclic voltammetry deepened understanding of the roles of trifluoroacetic acid and 1,2-dichloroethane (DCE) in the catalytic cycle, including the possible terminal oxidant under anaerobic conditions. Finally, the synthetic utility of the methodology is demonstrated through a concise, modular synthesis of a derivative, providing rapid access to this important class of acridine-based heterocycles relevant to materials science.

papers.title: Memory-Aware SIMD-Enabled Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Code-Generation Procedure: Acceleration of the MB-pol Potential Energy Function as an Example
papers.abstract: Permutationally invariant polynomials have been used to develop a variety of highly accurate potential energy surfaces. Particularly when combined with the many-body expansion, such potentials present a promising avenue for reducing the computational cost of simulations with coupled-cluster accuracy. In practice, performing molecular dynamics simulations with many-body polynomial potential energy functions requires evaluating the polynomial and its gradients thousands of times at each simulation step. If the cost of that evaluation can be reduced, larger systems and longer time scales will be available for study. Each individual gradient calculation requires evaluating tens of thousands of floating-point operations, making polynomial evaluation an excellent candidate for vectorization using single-instruction multiple-data (SIMD) instructions available on modern CPUs. However, depending on how the polynomial is factored and optimized, each evaluation may require a substantial amount of memory, producing a memory bottleneck that prevents vectorization from achieving the nominal SIMD speedup. A new memory-aware procedure for generating highly optimized polynomial routines is presented and applied to the MB-pol potential energy function as a prototypical example. The algorithm reduces the memory consumption of the routines by identifying and extracting duplicate subexpressions and by iteratively reordering the program’s statements to minimize the size of the working set. These memory optimizations allow vector instructions to be efficiently exploited, producing speedups in polynomial evaluation of nearly 4× and 8× when the AVX2 and AVX-512 vector instruction sets are employed, respectively. Using this approach, the performance of polynomial-based many-body potential energy functions can be significantly improved.

papers.title: Detailed Microkinetics for NOx-Containing Exhaust gas conversion through Automated Mechanism Generation within Correlated Uncertainty on Pt(111)
papers.abstract: Three-way catalytic converters simultaneously oxidize hydrocarbons and reduce NOx species. Under stoichiometric conditions the oxidation of hydrocarbons requires the transfer of oxygen from NOx species. The manner in which this occurs and the intersection of chemistry involving mixtures of C, H, N, and O atoms have not been fully explored. Experimental light-out curves reveal that stoichiometric exhaust gas containing 1000 ppm NO increases the light-out temperatures of carbon monoxide and ethene by 50 ◦C over the same exhaust mix without NOx on Pt supported on alumina. To understand what is going on, the Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG) is extended and used to explore the inhibitive effect of NOx on hydrocarbon conversion. Density functional theory (DFT) results using the BEEF-vdW functional are used to derive thermophysical properties for 73 adsorbates and kinetic parameters for 36 elementary reactions. These data are used to retrain the estimation routines within RMG to work more generally for C, H, N, O chemistry on surfaces. An ensemble 2000 microkinetic models within the correlated uncertainty space of the density functional theory (DFT)-derived parameters is generated with RMG. Light-out curves are simulated and compared against experiment for each member of the ensemble. A best-fit member is identified and used to probe why the addition of NOx shifts the hydrocarbon conversion temperature. The best fit captures the light-out behavior of all species well, but struggles to capture the magnitude of NO oxidation at intermediate temperatures. The best fit reproduces the ethene shift, and shows a minor temperature shift in the carbon monoxide curve, but is far smaller than experiment. The shift of carbon monoxide is attributed to *NO preventing the build up of *O, and the shift in ethene is attributed to *NO shuttling surface *O to *CCH3 to form O*CCH3 which prevents vacant site formation.

papers.title: Inverse theoretical spectroscopy via Monte Carlo sampling: From spectra to ensembles of molecular structures
papers.abstract: A molecule’s structure determines its spectroscopic properties, and vice versa, molecular spectra are indispensable for elucidating its three-dimensional structure. Here, we present a Monte Carlo sampling scheme for generating an ensemble of molecular structures that is compatible with an ensemble of spectra around a given reference spectrum. By analyzing this spectrally-constrained ensemble, we can determine which structural changes are compatible with the given reference spectrum. By constraining the spectrum only in selected windows, a more fine-grained analysis of selected spectral features becomes possible. We explore our spectral Monte Carlo sampling method for the dye molecule DFHBI, considering its electronic excitation spectrum. We find that the conformational space of molecular structures with similar spectra is vast, and we identify high-energy distorted structures whose spectra closely match that of the ground-state structure. Our method provides a novel, ensemble-based perspective on the inverse mapping from spectra to molecular structures.

papers.title: The Use of PFAS in Drug Product Presentations including Formulations, Primary and Secondary Packaging, and Delivery Devices: The Survey Conducted by the IQ Consortium Drug Product PFAS Working Group to Review the Potential Impact of PFAS Restrictions on Patient Access to Medicines
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely present across the pharmaceutical drug product supply chain, yet their role and prevalence remain incompletely characterized. An industry survey conducted by the IQ Drug Product PFAS working group (DPPFAS WG), with participation from 13 pharmaceutical companies, assessed the use and presence of PFAS across drug product modalities including oral solid dosage forms, parenteral, inhalation products, and cell and gene therapies as well as across primary and secondary packaging and drug‑delivery devices. Survey responses indicate limited presence and use of PFAS in drug product formulations themselves, but extensive presence in primary packaging and device components, with 70–85% of respondents reporting PFAS in components such as vial stoppers, syringe and cartridge plungers, blister packs, and device systems including autoinjectors and inhalers. Most respondents indicated the use of polymeric fluoropolymers (such as PTFE, PCTFE, ETFE, FEP) and selected monomeric PFAS were reported. These materials provide critical functional benefits, including low permeability to moisture and oxygen, lubricity, containment, and control of extractables and leachables, chemical resistance, and reliable device performance. While respondents are actively pursuing PFAS substitutions and identifying suitable alternatives, in most cases suitable alternatives are not available. Even once a suitable alternative is identified, development remains challenging. Transitioning will require extensive testing, lengthy timelines, and impose a significant burden on boards of health responsible for reviewing and approving alternatives, necessitating greater flexibility and time. Science and risk based regulatory approaches are therefore essential to ensure uninterrupted patient access to medicines, including life‑saving therapies.

papers.title: Development of a Screening Workflow for the Halogenation of Nitrogen Heterocycles with Vanadium-Dependent Haloperoxidases
papers.abstract: The halogenation of nitrogen heterocycles is a privileged transformation for accessing important synthetic intermediates and biologically active targets in medicinal chemistry. Despite the importance of N-heterocycle halogenation, current methods rely on reagents or catalysts that are largely unselective and produce a significant amount of waste products. With an emerging interest in using halogenating enzymes to address these challenges, the vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase class of enzymes has emerged as a powerful platform for screening halogenation reactions under a uniquely large set of reaction conditions. Herein, we report the development of a screening workflow for the halogenation of heterocycles with the chloroperoxidase from Curvularia inaequalis (CiVCPO). Using a high-throughput screening strategy, representative model heterocycles are screened for direct chlorination and bromination reactions, and the optimized conditions are translated to extended substrate scopes in moderate to high yields. The volume of high-throughput data obtained allowed us to develop a predictive model for substrate halogenation conditions. This screening platform is applied to established industrial intermediates and to the discovery of previously undiscovered enzymatic nitrogen-halogen bond formation and decarboxylative halogenation reactions.

papers.title: Ultra coarse-grained modeling of chiral molecular fluids
papers.abstract: Molecular chirality is ubiquitous in nature and a signature of life. Understanding molecular chiral symmetry breaking has critical applications in pharmaceuticals, catalysis, functional soft materials, and biomolecular assemblies. Molecular dynamics simulations can provide insights into the microscopic mechanisms of chirality symmetry breaking, but simulations of complex molecular chiral systems at atomistic resolution remain computationally prohibitive because chirality-driven phase behavior can occur over large length and time scales. To address this challenge, we develop a bottom-up ultra coarse grained (UCG) model of a chiral fluid in which each molecule is represented by a single UCG bead endowed with a binary probabilistic internal state representing molecular handedness. The dynamical evolution of the internal state is coupled to the configurational environment and modulates the coarse-grained interaction potential. This coupled evolution of the internal states and coarse-grained configurational dynamics permits the use of a highly-coarsened single-bead representation of chiral molecules that would not be possible by conventional coarse-graining approaches. We show that the resulting UCG model can accurately simulate both the temperature-and density dependent spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking from a racemic fluid into an enantiomerically pure phase. Our results demonstrate that the UCG framework provides an effective route for developing coarse-grained models to study chiral molecular fluids.

papers.title: Near-micron single-crystalline Mn-rich cathodes with exceptional cycling stability
papers.abstract: Achieving high-energy-density and long-term cycling stability in Mn-redox-based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni- and Co-free Li-ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn-redox cathodes using near-micron single-crystalline δ-phase cation-disordered rocksalt (δ-DRX), derived from Mn-rich DRX, delivering an energy density of ~640 Wh kg -1 with ~97% capacity retention over 400 cycles. The very high energy density and cycle life were achieved by using a high Mn content, to eliminate oxygen redox activity, and careful control of the synthesis parameters to tune single crystal particle size. Using high-throughput automated electron microscopy, we identify interparticle compositional heterogeneity present in the early stage of phase-pure DRX formation as the origin of orthorhombic LiMnO 2 impurity formation during cooling, a finding that rationalizes the long high-temperature dwell times required and the associated particle coarsening in conventional synthesis. We demonstrate that an accelerated cooling strategy kinetically suppresses localized impurity formation, reducing long high-temperature exposure, and enables downsizing of single-crystalline Mn-rich DRX particles to the near-micron regime (D50 = 1.5 μm). This work provides a mechanistic basis for particle-size control in Mn-rich DRX synthesis, and presents δ-DRX as a stable, sustainable, high-performance, Ni- and Co-free cathode material.

papers.title: Do electrostatic forces correlate with dispersion forces in charged molecular systems?
papers.abstract: Electrostatic and dispersion forces in molecular systems have traditionally been considered independent, where each force arises from distinctly different mechanisms. However, ionic liquid systems, in which electrostatic interactions are particularly strong (ranging from -310 to -430 kJ mol -1 ), suggest a connection between these forces due to the significant increase in dispersion forces compared to systems comprising of neutral molecules. This study investigates over 2000 molecular systems, divided into four categories: cation-anion interactions (Category 1), neutral molecule-cation interactions (Category 2), neutral molecule-anion interactions (Category 3), and interactions between neutral molecules (Category 4). Our findings reveal that electrostatic interactions are correlated with dispersion interactions in systems involving cations (Categories 1 and 2), indicating that cations play an important role in mediating the relationship between these two forces in molecular systems. A machine learning model with simple inputs of intermolecular distances and Morgan fingerprints predicts the dispersion component of interaction energies belonging to Category 1 more favorably than Category 4, elucidating a detectable dependence of dispersion forces on electrostatic forces.

papers.title: Knowledge-Graph-Guided Design of Compositionally Flexible Alloys for Sustainable Metal Recycling
papers.abstract: Developing engineering alloys that retain target properties despite compositional variability in mixed metallic scrap remains a major challenge in sustainable alloy design. Machine learning can accelerate alloy development, but limited datasets, extrapolation into underexplored composition spaces, and insufficient physical constraints reduce prediction reliability. To address these challenges, a recycling-oriented framework based on physicalmetallurgy knowledge graphs, termed ReAlloy-KG, is developed. Four task-specific models predict martensite start temperature (Ms), stacking fault energy (SFE), yield strength (YS), and pitting potential (Epit), and their outputs are integrated for multi-objective screening. Physically constrained screening of 20,301 compositions generated by virtual blending of 321 and 201LN stainless steels with Fe-50Ni (wt.%) powder feedstock identifies a continuous admissible region that contains 1,995 candidates and satisfies phase stability, deformation stability, corrosion resistance, and yield strength criteria. Experiments on five boundary-selected alloys confirm a stable face-centered cubic austenitic matrix before and after tensile deformation, yield strengths near the target range, and pitting potentials above both the screening threshold and the commercial 304 stainless-steel benchmark. This work establishes a transferable strategy for designing compositionally flexible alloys capable of accommodating the unavoidable compositional variability inherent in mixed scrap streams.

papers.title: Molybdenum pincer complex based reduction of dinitrogen: Mechanistic bifurcation at the stage of Mo(I)-N2 intermediates
papers.abstract: The synthesis and characterization of a new PPP ligand, bis(di-cyclopentylphosphinoethyl)phenylphosphine (PPP-Cyp), and its derived molybdenum complexes [MoBr 3 (PPP-Cyp)], [Mo≡NCl 2 (PPP-Cyp)], [Mo≡NBr 2 (PPP-Cyp)] and [Mo(η 6 -toluene)(PPP-Cyp)] are presented. The activities of these compounds towards catalytic N2RR (nitrogen reduction reaction) and reductive N2-splitting are investigated. A combination of experimental results with DFT calculations elucidates the critical role of the alkyl substituents R at the terminal phosphine donors, which through steric and electronic interactions determine whether Mo(II)- and Mo(I)-N 2 intermediates follow a bimolecular pathway, undergoing N-N-cleavage, or a monomolecular pathway, undergoing further reduction to Chatt-type Mo(0) complexes. Importantly, these two pathways originate from a common intermediate, [MoX(N 2 )(PPP-R)], which thus is located at a bifurcation of molybdenum pincer-based N2RR mechanisms.

papers.title: Functional Upcycling of Waste by Thermo-Electromagnetic Autocatalysis
papers.abstract: Industrial wastes, particularly electronic wastes, pose major environmental and societal challenges owing to their rapidly increasing annual generation approaching hundreds of millions of tonnes 1 , compositional complexity, toxicity and low recycling rates 2 . Existing recovery routes are often resource-intensive and rely on large quantities of acids and bases, reaching up to 2 L kg⁻¹ of waste 3 . We report Thermo-Electromagnetic Reduction and Autocatalysis (TERA), a rapid, carbon-free and acid-free process for the extraction of critical and strategic raw materials from complex wastes, exemplified through processing of In- and Sn-containing electronic wastes spanning diverse waste streams. Techno-economic analysis supports industrial scalability and the potential of TERA as a cost-effective and resource-efficient (10 kWh kg⁻¹) recycling technology. Beyond metal recovery, TERA exploits a previously unrecognized oxygen-vacancy-mediated autocatalytic reduction pathway that accelerates metallization while simultaneously driving self-organized restructuring of residual oxides, enabling direct upcycling into hierarchical oxide catalysts for methanol synthesis. Across waste streams of widely varying compositions, TERA achieves high metallization rates, efficient impurity partitioning and metal yields exceeding 90% within minutes, validated at hundreds-of-grams scale. These results establish TERA as a fast, flexible and energy-efficient platform for coupling critical-material recovery with the directed transformation of waste-derived oxides into functional materials.

papers.title: KANA AI: A Chemical-Informed Neural Network with Hard Thermodynamic Constraints for Multicomponent Activity Coefficient Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate activity coefficient prediction (ln γ) for multicomponent mixtures is essential for compu-tational deep eutectic solvent (DES) discovery, yet existing methods are either thermodynamically inconsistent (black-box machine learning) or architecturally restricted to binary mixtures (hardconstraint neural networks such as HANNA). We present KANA AI, a chemical-informed neural network that embeds Gibbs–Duhem consistency, pure-component boundary conditions, permutation invariance, and Gibbs–Helmholtz consistency as hard architectural constraints, scaling to arbitrary multicomponent mixtures (N = 2 through N = 10) via mole-fraction-weighted aggregation. The model predicts excess Gibbs energy (gE/RT ) as its primary output and derives ln γ analytically through automatic differentiation, guaranteeing thermodynamic consistency by construction. Trained on 287,028 multicomponent mixture samples and evaluated across four hyperparameter configurations with five reproducibility runs, KANA AI achieves a best validation MAE of 0.0749 with R2 = 0.9964. A systematic 6–7× gap between RMSE and MAE across all configurations reveals a long error tail driven by underrepresented chemical families, identifying targeted data acquisition as the primary path to improvement. All four thermodynamic consistency checks pass for every configuration and seed tested, confirming that the hard-constraint guarantees are robust to hyperparameter choice. The multicomponent capability enables a proposed five-step computational DES screening pipeline capable of evaluating ternary and quaternary formulations inaccessible to binary-only models.

papers.title: Hyper-Porous Membranes for Nano-Confinement-Driven Chromatographic Uranium Trapping
papers.abstract: Most conventional membrane and ion-exchange technologies fail to efficiently remediate ultradilute radioactive actinides in complex aquatic systems because of severe charge shielding by background electrolytes and diffusion-limited kinetics. Here, we break this operational mode by demonstrating high-velocity chromatographic nano-trapping using porous amorphous covalent triazine framework (CTF) composite membranes. Synthesized via a low-temperature Friedel-Crafts reaction, followed by programmable post-formation oxidation, the engineered polymer phase resists structural collapse, revealing a highly developed surface area of 230 m2 g−1 and a total pore volume of 132 mm3 g−1. When integrated into a sustainable fibrous cellulosic support, this architecture behaves similarly to an ultra-dense stationary phase in high-performance frontal liquid chromatography. Under continuous convective flow of 1 mL min−1, equivalent to a pure-water flux of 764 L h−1 m−2, the highly tortuous sub-nanometer channels eliminate mass-transfer resistance. At ecologically relevant pH values, thermodynamic speciation drives uranium to migrate as hydrocomplexed, nano-sized phases rather than as free ions. This reactive membrane achieves nearbenchmark theoretical capacity for uranium extraction over a wide trace range of 10 to 200 ppb in artificial seawater in a single pass. This morphology-enforced entrapment, driven by chemofixation at introduced polar N(O)-donor coordination nodes, establishes a design rule for sustainable reactive separation systems capable of on-the-fly resource recovery and environmental remediation.

papers.title: Interfacial structure of conjugated polymer photocatalysts with water and scavengers for sacrificial hydrogen evolution
papers.abstract: Conjugated polymers have emerged as competitive photocatalysts for the sustainable production of hydrogen from water. Their synthetic versatility allows for systematic tuning of their opto-electronic properties and polarity to improve visible-light-driven hydrogen production. One challenge in the field is the lack of understanding of interactions of water and reactants on the molecular level with the photocatalyst. Here we probe the molecular structure of different polymer-water interfaces and link structural motifs to trends in catalytic efficiency and wettability. We study two polymers with a fluorene-co-dibenzo[b,d]thiophene sulfone backbone, where one polymer has n-dodecyl sidechains and one bears significantly more hydrophilic ethylene glycol sidechains. Additionally, we study a polymer with a fluorene-co-phenylene backbone and bearing n-dodecyl sidechains. A combination of phase-resolved and conventional sum frequency generation spectroscopy revealed that, despite different conjugated backbones and sidechain structures, the interfacial water structure was qualitatively similar for the probed polymers, where the net ordering was higher in alkaline environments compared to acidic environments. We associate this observation with a pH dependent negative surface charge. The similarity of the water structure at the different polymer surfaces suggests that variations in hydrogen production cannot be solely attributed to polymer-water interactions, but rather to selective interactions with sacrificial electron donors, so called scavengers. Both tested scavengers, triethylamine and ascorbic acid, influenced the interfacial water structure of polymers with n-dodecyl sidechains. Contrary to this, the interfacial structure of the more hydrophilic polymer with ethylene glycol sidechains was unaffected by the scavengers, which likely relates to its higher hydrogen evolution rate. As such, the work provides valuable insights into the interface of these photocatalysts with scavengers. This will be of particular importance when considering value-added oxidations, such as biomass oxidation coupled to hydrogen evolution which will require a balance of accessing protons, water and reductants.

papers.title: Interfacial interpenetration underlies cooperative deformation and toughness in polymer nanoparticle assemblies
papers.abstract: Polymer materials containing numerous interfaces are often assumed to exhibit limited mechanical robustness. Here, we demonstrate that polymer nanoparticle assemblies can achieve exceptionally high toughness, with fracture strains above 1400%, tensile strengths up to 21.5 MPa, and fracture energies exceeding 80 MJ m -3 despite the presence of numerous particle-particle interfaces. Using a well-defined model system with systematically tuned interfacial properties, we reveal that enhanced polymer chain mobility during film formation promotes interparticle interpenetration, which in turn enables cooperative deformation during stretching. By combining high-speed atomic force microscopy and in situ small-angle X-ray scattering under uniaxial stretching, we directly capture the transition from heterogeneous to cooperative deformation. These findings establish a nanostructure-property relationship linking nanoparticle composition, interfacial structure, and film mechanics, and provide design guidelines for tough materials via waterborne nanoparticle assembly.

papers.title: AGENTi: APCI-ESI Analyte Ionization Fidelity Pre-Screening Workflow using Multimodel Inference
papers.abstract: To realize separation and detection by mass spectrometry a neutral analyte is converted to an ion by an ionization source, which can occur either in solution or in the gas phase. The two most common methods to achieve solution or gas phase ionization are by electrospray ionization (ESI) and atmospheric-pressure chemical ionization (APCI), respectively. Both ESI and APCI can generate the same resultant ion species; however, it has been shown that preferential charge sites can change in response to an ionization source environment. Therefore, an additional quality control is warranted a priori to delineate erroneous analyte identification and/or unequivocal structural assignment. For protonation, protomer fidelity can be assessed by comparing the ion-mobility collision cross section (CCS) values obtained for both ESI and APCI. In this work, we utilized proxy standards (i.e., controls) derived from the available literature to develop a proof-of-concept multimodel inference application called AGENTi to probe differences in ionization for high-throughput protomer shift exploratory analysis. AGENTi uses in sequence the TensorFlow Autoencoder anomaly detection and the YDF Gradient Boosted Tree machine learning frameworks to generate more balanced and robust anomaly scores. We found that using a multimodel screening approach can reduce false positive capture at an acceptable loss of true positives. Moreover, we expect to achieve a better recovery of true positives with an improvement on the current Gradient Boosted Tree regression model for ∆CCS prediction as more ESI-APCI dual data are obtained for training. In all, we demonstrated in this pilot study that our foundation model for a priori probing of ionization pathway fidelity is feasible and efficient with AGENTi. The AGENTi prototype application and documentation are accessible at https://github.com/mitkeng/AGENTi.

papers.title: Experimental and Computational Studies of Intraresidue Hydrogen Bonding Mimicry of Chloroalkene Dipeptide Isosteres
papers.abstract: Peptide bond isosteres are effective tools for investigating backbone-mediated interactions in peptides and proteins. (Z)-chloroalkene dipeptide isosteres (CADIs) have emerged as promising amide bond surrogates; however, their H-bonding properties are poorly understood. In this study we applied computational, spectroscopic, kinetic, crystallographic, electronic structure, and functional analyses to investigate the ability of CADIs to mimic intraresidue C5 H-bonds . Electrostatic potential and interaction energy calculations suggested that the chlorine atom of a CADI can act as a directional H-bond acceptor. Experimental investigations using valine-based model compounds demonstrated that CADIs exhibit stronger C5 hydrogen-bond mimicry than the corresponding fluoroalkene (FADI) and alkene analogues, as evidenced by FT-IR, NMR, and H/D exchange experiments. X-ray crystallographic and natural bond orbital analyses further supported the presence of attractive intramolecular interactions that involved the chlorine atom. Functional validation using an amyloid b-derived peptide model demonstrated that CADIs preserve the aggregation behavior of the native peptide sequence, whereas the corresponding FADI and alkene analogues do not. The results confirm that the chlorine atom of a CADI is a functionally relevant H-bond acceptor and can partially mimic the C5 hydrogen-bonding properties of a peptide bond. The findings of this study provide a molecular basis for the peptide bond mimicry of CADIs and demonstrate how weak halogen-mediated interactions can contribute to the stabilization of peptide secondary structures and supramolecular assemblies.

papers.title: Modular Synthesis of Branched Aliphatic Aldehydes via Unified Iron-Photocatalyzed Decarboxylation and C-H Activation
papers.abstract: We report a concise and practical method for the synthesis of branched aliphatic aldehydes via Iron-Ligand to Metal Charge Transfer (Fe-LMCT) catalysis. Fe-LMCT catalysis has emerged as a sustainable and highly versatile platform in organic synthesis by generating reactive radical intermediates from abundant chemical feedstocks. Our strategy utilizes alkyl radicals generated either via the decarboxylation of carboxylic acids or through chloride radical mediated direct hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) from unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds. These intermediates subsequently undergo an Intermolecular Giese-type conjugate addition with α-substituted acroleins. While the Fe-catalyzed decarboxylative coupling reactions were known for their kinetically sluggish nature, often requiring 12 to 72 hours, we have developed a protocol that effectively delivers the coupling products in just 5 hours of 450 nm blue LED irradiation, even for challenging unactivated primary carboxylic acids. Detailed mechanistic investigations – including kinetic profiling, quantum yield calculations, UV-Vis spectroscopy and DFT studies – elucidated the effect of solvent switching and the substrate activation by iron-coordination behind this profound rate acceleration.

papers.title: Thermo-Electrohydrodynamics of Confined Droplets
papers.abstract: A theoretical and analytical investigation of the coupled electrohydrodynamic and thermocapillary behaviour of a confined leaky dielectric droplet suspended in an immiscible liquid medium is presented within the creeping-flow regime using the small-deformation approximation. Based on the Taylor–Melcher leaky dielectric framework, analytical solutions are obtained for the electric, thermal, and hydrodynamic fields to examine the influence of confinement, thermal Marangoni forcing, and electrical and thermal property contrasts on the interfacial stresses, flow structure, and droplet deformation. The results show that the electrical property contrast establishes the baseline EHD circulation, whereas the thermal conductivity contrast determines the interfacial temperature gradients responsible for Marangoni stresses. Depending on their relative directions, thermocapillary stresses may either reinforce or oppose the electrically induced motion, leading to qualitatively different responses. Confinement both suppresses large-scale recirculation and amplifies thermocapillary sensitivity through the enhancement of local interfacial temperature gradients within the narrowing annular region surrounding the droplet. The analysis further reveals nonmonotonic variations in the thermally induced stresses and deformation with increasing confinement, with the associated crossover behaviour being governed primarily by confinement rather than solely by the magnitude of thermal forcing. Despite substantial changes in stress distribution, circulation intensity, and deformation characteristics, the underlying quadrupolar temperature structure and characteristic four-cell flow topology remain preserved throughout the parameter range investigated. These findings reveal how interfacial charge transport, thermal conduction, thermocapillary stresses, and confinement collectively govern electro-thermocapillary droplet dynamics and provide a mechanistic basis for controlling droplet behavior in confined multiphase systems.

papers.title: β-Stereoselective Glycosylation without Acyl Participation: Evaluation of β-(1→2)-Linked Disaccharide Donors and Their Application to Glycoarray Design for Antibody Characterization
papers.abstract: β-(1→2)-Glucans constitute a relatively rare and substantially underexplored class of polysaccharides. Of particular interest is the macrocyclic β-(1→2)-glucan from Brucella (CβG), which regarded as a promising diagnostic marker of brucellosis. However, the development of CβG-based diagnostic system requires careful consideration of potential interference from short β-(1→2)-linked gluco-oligosaccharides present in various bacterial commensals and pathogens. To address this challenge, we performed the stereoselective synthesis of a representative series of trisaccharide antigens bearing di-β-(1→2)-glucoside motifs. Several strategies for β-selective insertion of the di-β-(1→2)-glucoside block were evaluated, including approaches employing picolylated and silylated donors as well as donors lacking stereodirecting groups at C-2. Optimal results were achieved using nonparticipating thioglycoside donors activated by a FeCl 3 /TCCA promoter system in acetonitrile. The method proved to be widely applicable to a range of monosaccharide acceptors, affording the target trisaccharides with excellent β-selectivity. The applicability of prepared oligosaccharides for profiling carbohydrate specificity of antibodies was demonstrated by large-scale screening of human donor sera.

papers.title: Donor-Acceptor Conjugated Copolymers as pH-Responsive Chromatic Indicators: A TDDFT and Colorimetric Screening Study
papers.abstract: Color change upon change of pH is a key indicator for smart packaging materials that signal food spoilage. Donor-acceptor (D–A) conjugated copolymers are attractive candidates for such indicators, as their charge-transfer transitions are highly sensitive to electronic perturbations such as protonation, an aspect that remains largely unexplored for smart packaging applications. In this study, we use DFT and TDDFT to screen 16 D–A copolymers, built from a 4×4 pairing of four donors and four acceptors, in their neutral and protonated states using the oligomer approach. For each system we compute the protonation-induced shift of the absorption spectrum and convert the spectra into perceived color through the CIE-1931/CIEDE2000 formula. We find that the magnitude of the absorption-peak shift depends almost entirely on the acceptor, but is by itself a poor predictor of the color change a human observer registers, as the largest shifts often fall in the near-infrared. We find that B3LYP functional yields optical gaps closer to the experiment that CAM-B3LYP. Regarding the absorption spectra shift, DPP-based copolymers prove robust to functional choice, whereas the standing of the TPD-and BT/isoindigo-based systems is functional-sensitive. Carbazole–BT emerges as the most promising candidate, showing a strong, easily perceptible color change with both functionals.

papers.title: Reaction Dynamics of OH + SiH4 → H2O + SiH3: A Quasi-Classical Trajectory Study on the PES-2022 Surface
papers.abstract: A quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) study is presented of the OH + SiH 4 → H 2 O + SiH 3 hydrogen-abstraction reaction on the full-dimensional analytical potential energy surface PES-2022. A total of 1.8 million trajectories were run at seven fixed collision energies (Ecoll = 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 kcal mol−1), yielding more than 28 000 DZPE reactive trajectories. The integral reactive cross section σ(E) rises from 0.56 Å 2 at E = 0.5 kcal mol −1 to a plateau near 4.9 Å 2 above E = 6 kcal mol −1 .

papers.title: Time-resolved Green Chemistry Metrics for Low Energy Depolymerization of Polyethylene Terephthalate
papers.abstract: For the circular utilization of plastics such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), chemical recycling has emerged as a promising approach for processing diverse waste streams. Methanolysis is particularly advantageous because impurities in the monomer dimethyl terephthalate can be readily removed by purification. Recently, methanolysis aided by equilibrium-shifting reagents has attracted attention as an efficient depolymerization strategy. Comprehensive evaluation of such systems remains challenging, however, because reaction efficiency depends on multiple factors. Herein, we developed a time-resolved green-chemistry metrics based on in-situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy for real-time monitoring of PET depolymerization. Using this approach, we identified K 2 CO 3 as an inexpensive precatalyst that functions effectively in dimethyl carbonate-aided methanolysis. Timeresolved analysis enabled quantitative comparison of reaction conditions and revealed that depolymerization at 73 °C for 7 min affords the most favorable environmental energy factor (ξ) among reported PET methanolysis systems. Kinetic analysis further identified KOMe as the catalytically active species and its deactivation pathway and regeneration mechanism under reaction conditions. Finally, a 483-g-scale depolymerization experiment was successfully performed under ambient pressure, demonstrating the practical feasibility of this energetically efficient process. The combination of readily available catalyst and real-time green-chemistry evaluation framework provides a rational strategy for optimizing and scaling up PET chemical recycling.

papers.title: Exploiting Ruthenium(II) Polypyridyl Complexes to Advance Intracellular Photoredox Catalysis as an Antimicrobial Strategy
papers.abstract: As antibiotic resistant infections become ever more prevalent, the WHO has designated the antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis as a silent epidemic. With over 1.1 million deaths directly caused by AMR in 2021 and a further 4.7 million associated deaths annually, there has never been a more pertinent time to investigate novel drug modalities and methods to tackle these challenging infections. Herein, we report a series of antimicrobial photocatalysts ( 1 – 4 ), which exhibit low-nanomolar activity against a panel of pathogenic reference strains, including all six ESKAPE pathogens and minimal off-target toxicity towards mammalian cells in-vitro. These catalysts have been extensively screened for their photoredox and biological properties, where we have used a series of spectroscopic techniques in combination with cellular assays, chemoproteomics, and super-resolution microscopy to uncover the mechanistic actions of these agents. They act primarily through intracellular NADH depletion, and induce biomolecular damage - located primarily at protein histidine residues. Furthermore, given the excellent antibacterial activity of this class of complexes we developed a targeted bioconjugate of our lead, 1 which shows augmented activity against ESKAPE pathogens. This work provides further evidence toward the utility of rationally designed photocatalysts in the fight against AMR.

papers.title: Scanning lanthanoid magnetic susceptibility tensors by spy molecules using paramagnetic fast magicangle spinning NMR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Magnetic properties of lanthanoid ions at the atomic level are challenging to derive despite the wealth of chemical and structural information encoded in them. We herein report protondetected paramagnetic solid-state NMR experiments at magic-angle spinning frequencies of 100 kHz and more that allow to scan the magnetic susceptibility tensors of europium(III)-based π-containers in the solid state, which have initially been determined in solution. An isolated water molecule and a guanidinium cation binding non-covalently to the aromatic cavity of such containers have been explored as highly sensitive reporters that make use of the chemical shift changes caused by the molecular orientation of the magnetic susceptibility tensors (pseudocontact shifts). By not diluting the lanthanoid complex in a diamagnetic matrix, we study the importance of inter-complex interactions in the solid state on the measured pseudo-contact shift values of the spy molecules. Our study shows how the field of paramagnetic solid-state NMR is opening up to increasingly complex molecules, particularly highlighting the strength in probing weak chemical interactions in host-guest complexes.

papers.title: Influence of Ligand Rigidity and Steric Bulk on Reductions of Tridentate NON-Diamido Alkaline Earth Metal Complexes
papers.abstract: Structural modifications to tridentate NON ligands have been shown to play a key role in controlling the outcomes of group 2 metal diamide reduction reactions. Herein, two bulky, geometrically flexible diamines, F NON Ar H 2 ( F NON Ar H 2 = O{2-N(H)Ar-4- t BuC 6 H 3 } 2 ; Ar = 2,4,6- i Pr 3 C 6 H 2 (Trip); 2,4,6-Cy 3 C 6 H 2 (TCHP)), have been synthesised. Treatment of F NON Trip H 2 with one equivalent of either BePh 2 , Mg{CH 2 (SiMe 3 )} 2 , or Ca{N(SiMe 3 ) 2 } 2 in methylcyclohexane yielded group 2 metal diamide complexes. In the solid-state, monomeric [Be( F NON Trip )] features a T-shaped beryllium geometry, whereas the magnesium and calcium analogues [{Ae( F NON Trip )} 2 ] (Ae = Mg or Ca) are dimeric with distinct aggregation modes in the solid state. Although the strontium and barium counterparts could not be isolated, their treatment with THF led to structurally characterised [Ae( F NON Trip )(THF) n ] (Ae = Sr, n = 3; Ae = Ba, n = 4). Analogous deprotonations of the super-bulky F NON TCHP H 2 pro-ligand in toluene afforded donor-free [Be( F NON TCHP )], the toluene adduct complexes, [Ae( F NON TCHP )(PhMe)] (Ae = Mg, Ca), and the N -bridged dimeric barium system, [{Ba( F NON TCHP )} 2 ]. Potassium reductions of these group 2 metal diamides led to a variety of outcomes, including reductive ligand C‒O cleavage processes, yielding K 2 [Mg{OC 6 H 3 t Bu-4-N(Trip)-2}{C 6 H 3 t Bu-4-N(Trip)-2}{Mg( F NON Trip )}], K 2 [Be{OC 6 H 3 t Bu-4-N(TCHP)-2}{N(TCHP)(C 6 H 4 t Bu-3)}] 2 , O 2 activation giving [K 2 {Mg( F NON TCHP )} 2 (m-O)], and metal hydride formation via solvent hydrogen abstraction, leading to [K 2 {Ca( F NON TCHP )(m-H)} 2 ]. All of these reduction reactions are thought to proceed via transient, reactive metal(I) radical species K[Ae( F NON Ar )•].

papers.title: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for GPU Materials Science
papers.abstract: Despite significant progress in large language models (LLMs) with general reasoning capabilities, their adaptability remains limited in interdisciplinary domains that require specialized expertise, such as materials science. To address this gap, this study constructs a domain-specific benchmark for GPU materials science, comprising a systematically curated evaluation dataset and a comprehensive assessment of representative LLMs on domain-specific tasks. As part of this benchmark development, we also develop GPUmatLLM, a specialized domain language model fine-tuned on high-quality data from academic papers, patents, and other relevant sources for the GPU materials science. Benchmarking results reveal a notable performance gap among the representative LLMs, with no single model excelling in both general scientific reasoning and GPU material–specific knowledge acquisition. In contrast, GPUmatLLM demonstrates improved comprehensive performance on GPU materials tasks, surpassing baseline models in domain-specific inference while maintaining competitive performance in general scientific reasoning. However, the model still exhibits limitations in retaining general knowledge for manufacturing purposes, and more critically, it fails to discover novel materials or innovative processes. This work provides an effective framework and practical paradigm for evaluating and optimizing domain-specific LLMs in specialized materials science fields.

papers.title: Quantitative Pathway-Resolved Kinetics from Neural Network-Guided Weighted Ensemble Simulations
papers.abstract: Many crucial biomolecular processes, such as ligand dissociation and conformational switching, occur via multiple competing transition pathways. While standard rare-event sampling methodologies provide rigorous estimates of the global transition rate, they typically collapse the underlying mechanistic heterogeneity into a single global constant, obscuring the relative kinetic contributions of distinct channels. Here, we introduce a path-resolved weighted ensemble (WE) framework that quantitatively assigns steady- state flux to competing transition channels without modifying the underlying unbiased dynamics. In our approach, initial reactive trajectories generated via direction-guided adaptive sampling are clustered by dynamic time warping (DTW) and smoothed into neural-network-refined representative paths. These refined routes are formulated as path collective variables (PathCVs) to pre-seed and guide channel-specific WE simulations. We demonstrate the robustness of this framework across systems of increasing complexity. On a model three-hole potential, the method accurately captures a temperature-dependent pathway crossover. In the benzamidine-trypsin complex, it isolates the dominant unbinding route while quantifying the fluxes of subdominant channels. Finally, for imatinib dissociation from Abl kinase, the method reveals that the clinically relevant N368S resistance mutation drastically redistributes reactive flux from the P-loop/hinge channel toward the αC-helix channel, accelerating escape. This framework successfully translates qualitative pathway classification into rigorous, pathway-specific kinetic observables, offering a powerful tool for understanding mutation-induced mechanistic

papers.title: Designing Ultrasmall Nb-doped Alloy and Nanocomposite Ir Electrocatalysts for Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: Developing durable, low-Ir-content catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to advancing green hydrogen production. Here, we explored Nb incorporation as a strategy to reduce Ir usage and investigated its impact on OER performance. By exploiting the redox properties of different solvents in a simple solvothermal synthesis, we prepared two distinct Nb-Ir catalyst systems. 5 nm alloy nanorods with Ir and Nb mixed on the atomic scale were prepared using highly reducing solvents, while <2 nm decahedral Ir/NbOx composites formed in less reducing media. Operando X-ray total scattering complemented by X-ray absorption spectroscopy revealed that both catalyst types preserve metallic cores during OER, while ultrathin (<4 Å) IrOx shells form the active phase, detectable only by absorption spectroscopy. In the composites, a pre-existing surface oxide grows under oxidative potentials. In contrast, the IrNb alloys undergo Ir surface oxidation at OER onset, generating a similarly thin IrOx shell. In the alloys, Nb incorporation induces lattice expansion, while Nb is proposed to be preferentially oxidised under applied potentials, promoting Nb surface migration and dissolution, creating similar active phases in both systems. However, the higher dispersion of IrOx and possibly interfacial IrOx-NbOx interactions enhance OER activity in the composite materials. Our results demonstrate how multimodal operando characterisation can resolve subtle, localised oxidation processes also for supported electrocatalysts, and we can establish clear relationships between nanostructure, Nb-Ir interactions, and catalytic performance.

papers.title: A Descriptor for Non-Arrhenius Ion Transport Enables Design of Sulfide Superionic Conductors
papers.abstract: Solid electrolytes are central to the realization of safe, high-energy all-solid-state batteries, yet their practical deployment is still constrained by an incomplete understanding of ion transport across broad temperature ranges. In sulfide solid electrolytes, deviations from classical Arrhenius behavior are increasingly observed, but such non-Arrhenius transport is rarely quantified in a way that can be generalized, interpreted chemically, or incorporated into materials design. Here, we establish a data-driven framework to quantify and leverage non-linear ionic transport in sulfide electrolytes. By curating a database of 867 conductivity-temperature entries spanning thio-LISICON and LGPS-type families, we introduce a Meyer-Neldel deviation (MND) descriptor that converts temperature-dependent drift in apparent activation energy into a material-level measure of non-Arrhenius transport. Descriptor analysis reveals that more than 40% of sulfide electrolytes exhibit notable non-Arrhenius behavior beyond the near-ambient regime and that MND organizes the transport landscape into low-conductivity/high-barrier and superionic/low-barrier classes associated with ionic-radius mismatch, electronegativity difference, and enthalpy-entropy compensation. Physics-informed machine learning further shows that, when used as a learning target, MND improves the extraction of structure-transport relationships that are obscured in conventional conductivity-based models. Guided by this framework, we identify and synthesize a previously unreported LGPS-type composition, Li10Ge0.3Si0.15Sn0.55P2S12, which delivers 7.21 mS cm-1 at room temperature, an activation energy of about 0.288 eV, and weak non-Arrhenius behavior in close agreement with prediction. These results establish MND as a chemically interpretable descriptor for integrating transport nonlinearity into the analysis, prediction, and prospective design of sulfide superionic conductors.

papers.title: Unified chemical memory and computation in a single-molecule nanoreactor
papers.abstract: Molecular systems can store data, and chemical reaction networks can form reservoirs for computation, but architectures that integrate both functions remain elusive. Here we show that a single nanopore can both store and process information by using its own chemical dynamics. Confined in an individual protein nanopore acting as a nanoreactor, reactive cysteine residues on a single β strand encode ‘1’ bits, and unreactive residues encode ‘0’ bits – together constituting configurable memory tapes. Reversible thiol–selenosulfide exchange reactions convert cysteine thiolates into transient selenosulfide adducts, producing complex reaction dynamics that enable data retrieval. The chemical reaction network inside the nanoreactor acts as an autonomous physical reservoir. The data-reading process generates the temporal dynamics, which are decoded with a simple linear readout for memory tape classification and future reaction-trend prediction. All 15 reactive 4-bit memory tapes are distinguishable and identified with >90% overall accuracy in 15-way classification. The timescale over which the reservoir retains predictive capacity is chemically tunable by reactant concentration, network complexity or memory tape composition. Our design principles generalize to (bio)chemical reaction networks and information processing systems with a single-molecule readout and reversible transitions.

papers.title: Firefly-Geni: Automated Iteration-Guided Generative Discovery of TADF Molecules
papers.abstract: The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure-property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely fragmented and underutilized. Here, we present Firefly-Geni, an automated and interpretable active-evolution framework that transforms dispersed literature knowledge into structurally novel TADF candidates through a closed-loop workflow. Firefly-Geni integrates large-language-model (LLM)-assisted data extraction, multitask property prediction, conditional molecular generation, and theoretical evaluation. Its data-mining module converts unstructured literature into a curated database of experimental property entries. A dual-molecular-graph multitask predictor and a conditional generator are integrated with quantum-chemical feedback, enabling iterative refinement toward structural novelty. From 100,000 molecules generated under target conditions of a singlet-triplet energy gap ΔE ST = 0.05 eV and a synthetic accessibility (SA) score of 2.5, Firefly-Geni identifies over one hundred theoretically validated and synthetically accessible candidates spanning diverse emission wavelengths. Interpretability analyses further reveal chemically meaningful structure-property relationships and generation preferences, confirming that the candidates encode physically relevant low-ΔE ST design motifs. This work offers a closed-loop, explainable strategy for actively evolving TADF candidates from literature knowledge, providing a generalizable route for data-driven molecular discovery.

papers.title: Temperature-Dependent Behavior of C14-C18 Alkyl Surfactants with Ionizable and Neutral Head Groups at the Water-Decane Interface
papers.abstract: Surfactants stabilize liquid-liquid interfaces, where adsorption is highly temperature-dependent. Interfacial shear rheology and pendant drop tensiometry were combined to study surfactant monolayers at the n-decane-water interface. Shear rheology revealed a temperature-driven phase transition, characterized by a loss of elasticity and a transition to a gas-like state. Pendant drop experiments confirmed this behavior, showing rising interfacial tension followed by plateau formation. Thermodynamic calculations based on a temperature-dependent Gibbs adsorption equation demonstrated that the adsorption free energy (ΔG ads ) is the dominant factor controlling the adsorption state. Phase transition temperatures determined by both methods were strongly influenced by chain length and head group chemistry: longer chains enhanced temperature stability as both chain-chain and chain-solvent interactions intensified and positively charged head groups exhibited the highest interfacial ordering. Together, these results link interfacial thermodynamics and mechanics, offering new insights into surfactant-driven phase stability and emulsion control.

papers.title: Simultaneous Exfoliation and Nitrogen Doping of Aerosolized Graphite Oxide by Flow Through a Plasma Reactor
papers.abstract: Continuous production of high-surface-area graphene-related materials with controllable heteroatom doping remains challenging, due to their low reactivity. Here, we demonstrate simultaneous exfoliation, reduction, and nitrogen doping of aerosolized graphite oxide (GO) in a flow-through microwave plasma reactor. Spray-dried GO powder was passed through Ar/N2 and Ar/N2/H2 plasmas operated at reduced and near-atmospheric pressures, producing reduced graphene oxide (rGO) with specific surface areas up to 700 m2 g-1. Compared with continuous tube-furnace exfoliation, plasma processing produced higher surface areas while incorporating nitrogen from N2, with contents up to ≈7 at.%. TEM, AFM, and Raman spectroscopy Jankhani et al. Page 2/31 05/15/2026 confirmed few-layer, defect-rich rGO sheets, while XPS showed a nitrogen profile dominated by pyrrolic and pyridinic configurations. To disentangle the preferential sites for graphitic, pyridinic, and pyrrolic doping, density functional theory was employed. The modeling highlighted higher binding of pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen in the basal plane and armchair edges, respectively, which is further enhanced by the proximity of oxygen functional groups. Vacancy formation during reduction creates favorable sites for nitrogen incorporation during in situ exposure to an N2-containing plasma. While N-doped rGO has broad applicability for a range of applications, we demonstrate significantly enhanced performance for the oxygen reduction reaction compared to benchmark, undoped rGO.

papers.title: CDR-encoded recognition of Toll-like receptor 2 by a signalling-attenuating scFv
papers.abstract: A phage-derived scFv binder, scFv33, recognizes the TLR2 LRR domain with low-tens-of-nanomolar apparent affinity and attenuates PAM3CSK4-induced cytokine transcription. Structure-informed modelling links this activity to a CDR-encoded charge–polarity–aromatic interface, providing a chemically interpretable route to TLR2-targeted immune modulation.

papers.title: IR-DOSY: A Complementary Method to NMR-DOSY For Polymer-Size Characterization
papers.abstract: We present a method for determining the diffusion coefficients of polymers in solution using Infrared Diffusion-Ordered Spectroscopy (IR-DOSY). We validate this approach for three distinct polymers dissolved in acetonitrile: poly(tetrahydrofuran) (polyTHF), cellulose acetate butyrate (CAB), and a styreneacrylate copolymer. The hydrodynamic radii (Rh) extracted from IR-DOSY exhibit excellent agreement with the results from complementary 1H NMR-DOSY experiments. To resolve the diffusion coefficient of these polymers without relying on empirical peak-fitting parameters or initial assumptions, we implement an advanced Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) numerical inversion method in IR-DOSY. This continuous distribution model successfully isolates the main polymer envelope from fast-diffusing solvent or artifact tails, and it yields hydrodynamic radii that are consistent with the ones from single-species fits. We thus show that IR-DOSY, in particular when paired with MaxEnt inversion, offers a robust, stable method for polymer analysis that operates efficiently in nondeuterated organic solvents, and thus provides a useful complement to NMR-DOSY and other polymer-size determination methods.

papers.title: GNN-ωPBE: Range-Separation Parameters Learned from Three-Dimensional Structures
papers.abstract: Range-separated hybrid (RSH) functionals improve density functional theory (DFT) modeling of organic semiconducting molecules by reducing self-interaction and delocalization errors, but their accuracy depends critically on the range-separation parameter (ω). Although our previously developed ML-ωPBE functional generates moleculespecific ω values from topology-based descriptors, its applicability is limited for flexible molecules with rich conformational diversity. We introduce GNN-ωPBE, a machine learned RSH functional that generates geometry-specific ω values directly from atomic numbers and three-dimensional (3D) atomic coordinates. Built on a graph neural network (GNN) representation, GNN-ωPBE encodes interatomic interactions through internal coordinates and distinguishes different conformers of the same molecule, enabling it to capture geometry-dependent variations inaccessible to topology-based molecular descriptors. Trained on a conformer-resolved dataset, GNN-ωPBE reproduces benchmark OT-ωPBE with a mean absolute error (MAE) of approximately 0.00760 a−1 0 . Our study advances machine learned density functional development from molecule-specific to geometry-specific modeling of conformational effects in electronic structures.

papers.title: Phenomenological Prediction of Halide Perovskite Phase Stability Phenomenological Prediction of Halide Perovskite Phase Stability via Dielectric-Response Analysis: Equivalence to First-Principles Thermodynamics at Five Orders of Magnitude Reduced Computational Cost
papers.abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid halide perovskites have achieved power conversion efficiencies exceeding 26% in single-junction solar cells, yet phase stability remains the primary bottleneck for commercialization. The cubic α-phase of FAPbI3 spontaneously transforms to the hexagonal δ-phase at room temperature, and compositional engineering through mixed cations (Cs/FA/MA) and halides (I/Br) has emerged as the dominant stabilization strategy. However, the combinatorial space of the six-component system (Cs_xFA_yMA_{1-x-y}Pb(I_zBr_{1-z})3) exceeds 5000 compositions, rendering exhaustive first-principles screening computationally prohibitive—one density functional theory (DFT) calculation requires 1–7 days per composition. Here we present the ε-field domain method, a dielectric-response-based phenomenological approach that predicts phase stability through macroscopic observables (dielectric constants ε_hi, ε_lo and Curie temperature T_c) with only three input parameters. We demonstrate equivalence between this method and the established DFT-thermodynamic framework across six experimentally validated compositions, achieving a computational acceleration of 105-fold (5043 compositions screened in 0.02 seconds versus ~1700 years of CPU time for DFT). The optimal compositional window predicted by the ε-field method (Cs 2–8%, FA 78–89%, MA 3–18%, I 93–99%) agrees quantitatively with the celebrated triple-cation perovskites of Saliba et al. (Science 354, 2016) and Kim et al. (Nat. Commun. 8, 2017). We further provide temperature-dependent predictions for eight key compositions and propose five new candidate formulations awaiting experimental verification. The physical origin of this equivalence lies in the fact that both dielectric response (ε) and thermodynamic stability (ΔH_f) emerge from the same Pb-I framework electronic structuremacroscopic permittivity and microscopic formation energy are distinct expectation values of the same Hamiltonian. The ε-field method exploits this reduced parametrization by bypassing intermediate electronic-structure calculations, directly accessing stability-relevant information encoded in macroscopic observables.

papers.title: Advancing polypharmacology-based drug discovery using deep generative models
Genetically programmed biotemplating enables five-orders-of-magnitude conductivity enhancement in amorphous phosphate cathodes via 3D transport networks
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that bio-directed amorphization enables intrinsically fast ion transport in phosphate cathodes. Using genetically programmed M13 bacteriophage, we synthesize amorphous FePO 4 nanowire networks in water at low temperature, with NaCl as the only by-product. After lithiation, amorphous LiFePO 4 exhibits a 10 5 -fold conductivity increase compared to crystalline powder references, reaching σ 0 = 2 × 10 −7 S cm −1 at room temperature. Impedance spectroscopy reveals a transition from 1D, spatially constrained transport in crystalline material to a 3D percolating network in the amorphous phase. The conductivity follows Arrhenius behaviour with a low activation energy of 0.36(1) eV and shows structural relaxation above ∼120 °C that tunes transport. Coordinated water acts as a control parameter governing redox behaviour and enabling capacities up to ∼140 mAh g −1 after optimized dehydration while retaining high-rate performance. These results establish biotemplating-driven amorphization as a general strategy linking sustainable synthesis with emergent fast-ion functionality.

papers.title: Fluorine-Free Conjugated Polyelectrolyte Optical Nanosensor Array Enables Trace PFAS Detection and Discrimination
papers.abstract: Environmental contamination of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) into water supplies has become a global concern due to their toxicity, incidental discharge, and long halflife. Despite advancements in portable sensors, the simultaneous detection and discrimination of diverse PFAS at sub-nanomolar concentrations remains challenging without material fluorination, which further generates unintended PFAS waste. Here, the design, synthesis, and analytical performance of three emissive fluorine-free conjugated polyelectrolytes (CPEs) are demonstrated. Three CPEs with robust luminescence were synthesized with varying cationic ammonium side-chains to enable pronounced differences in each polymer's spectroscopic behavior upon electrostatic interaction with each PFAS. When coupled with array-based sensing methods, these polymeric sensors discriminated among seven PFAS (PFBA, PFOA, PFNA, PFBS, PFOS, PFDS, PFHxS) with interferents. To improve limits of detection (LODs), the CPEs were immobilized within hydrogels to enhance polymer-analyte interactions, thereby demonstrating extraordinary sensitivity (LOD = 63 pM) and selectivity without generating fluorinated waste.

papers.title: The Effect of Trialkyl Borates as Lewis Acids on Quinones for Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Capture and Concentration
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 capture and concentration (eCCC) systems have the potential to operate at higher efficiencies than current thermal systems. Quinones have been the focus of many eCCC studies as redox carriers, as they can capture or release CO2 depending on their oxidation state. Quinones (Q) with more cathodic potentials bind CO2 more strongly when reduced; however, more cathodic potentials result in O2 sensitivity. Intra- and intermolecular non-covalent interactions have been explored to anodically shift the second reduction potential (E1/2(Q-1/Q-2)) while maintaining CO2 binding affinity (log(KCO2 )). In this report we investigate the effect of four trialkyl borate additives, B(OMe)3, B(OEt)3, B(OiPr)3, and B(OBu)3, on the second reduction potential (E1/2(Q-1/Q-2)) and the CO2 binding affinity (log(KCO2)) of three quinones, TCQ, TFQ, and 2-ClBQ. With up to 300 equivalents of these additives, changes in the second reduction potential ranged from 0 to 430 mV.

papers.title: Symmetric Atomic Orbitals Model and the Nature of Chemical Bonding
papers.abstract: A conjecture of symmetric atomic orbitals model was proposed in 1984, through decades of studying all kind of molecular geometries, the experimental evidences of the conjecture have been found: there are causal relationship between molecular geometries of various configuration and symmetric atomic orbitals. According to the model, the nature of chemical bonding has been discovered: geometries of main group compounds are closely related to vertices of symmetric atomic orbitals, this is the nature of covalent bonding, and geometries of the transition metal complexes are closely related to edge and face centers of symmetric atomic orbitals with full electrons, this is the nature of coordination bonding. The experimental results indicate that geometries of main group compounds are completely consistent with the nature of covalent bonding, geometries of the transition metal complexes are completely consistent with the nature of coordination bonding, and properties such as the periodic law of elements are closely related to symmetric atomic orbitals. These indicate that the conjecture is correct, based on this, a new model of many-electron atomic structure, symmetric atomic orbitals model, has been established. This model not only unifies covalent bonding and coordination bonding theory, but also atomic and molecular structure theory, and let our understanding of atomic and molecular structures enter an era of correct, clear, and visualization.

papers.title: Solid-electrolyte interphase reactivity with the bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide anion governs cycling instabilities of sodium metal anodes
papers.abstract: Highly reversible and long-cycling Na metal anodes would enable Na-based batteries to approach energy densities competitive with established Li-ion technologies while leveraging earth-abundant materials. While several Na electrolytes have demonstrated impressive cyclability with Coulombic efficiency (CE) exceeding 99%, the number of high-performance electrolytes is lower, and designs are more restrictive, than counterpart Li systems to date. Meanwhile, design principles for high-performance Na electrolytes and their derived Solid Electrolyte Interphases (SEI) are less well established. Here, we examine factors that differentiate Na cyclability across different salts (1 M NaPF6, NaOTf, NaClO4, and NaFSI) in an exemplar class of primarily diglyme (G2) electrolytes. We first examine the hypothesis, commonly encountered in literature, that elevated Na SEI solubility compared to Li is a strong driver of CE. Upon conducting solubility measurements of sodium and lithium fluoride, carbonate, oxide, and methoxide (i.e. MF, M2CO3, M2O, and MOCH3, with M = Na or Li) phases in neat solvent, we find that while solubilities are indeed elevated (e.g. Na2O in G2: 2.3×10-4 M) for Na SEI compared to Li SEI (e.g. Li2O in G2: 2.3×10-5M), the absolute solubility is expected to be exceedingly small in 1 M electrolytes (<10-9 M) due to the common ion effect. However, one notable exception is (Na, Li)OCH3 (e.g. NaOCH3 in 1 M Na+ G2: ~10-6 M), broadly representative of organic Na SEI phases. Looking beyond simple solubility, we find that OCH3

papers.title: Nanomechanical Insights into Curing-Driven Morphological Evolution in Crumpled Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes
papers.abstract: Crumpled polyamide thin films are widely used as selective layers in nanofiltration membranes, where their nanoscale morphology is closely associated with water transport and solute separation. Although crumpled morphology is commonly discussed in terms of reaction-diffusion processes during interfacial polymerization, increasing evidence suggests an important yet less understood role of thermal curing as an active morphology-evolution step. Here, we combine amplitude-modulation frequency-modulation (AM-FM) atomic force microscopy, in situ heating measurements, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, finite element analysis (FEA), substrate-dependent fabrication, and nanofiltration testing to examine how thermal curing reshapes crumpled polyamide nanofiltration membranes. The simultaneous increase in surface roughness, decrease in Young’s modulus, and increase in XPS-estimated crosslinking degree show that the nanomechanical softening occurs concurrently with curing-associated chemical evolution. In situ AFM measurements and FEA reveal that stress relaxation or redistribution contributes to ridge amplification and growth during thermal curing. Substrate-dependent experiments further show that post-cure morphology amplification varies strongly with the supporting substrate, suggesting that substrate mechanical properties and boundary conditions modulate the evolution of the polyamide layer during curing. Membranes with amplified crumpled morphology exhibit enhanced water permeance while maintaining high salt rejection. Together, these results support a working framework in which reaction-diffusion processes establish a heterogeneous precursor film, while thermal curing promotes coupled morphological, nanomechanical, and chemical evolution under substrate-dependent boundary conditions. This study highlights thermal curing as an active materials-processing parameter for controlling polyamide thin-film morphology and nanofiltration function.

papers.title: Mobile Proton Control for Improved Stability of Tyrosine O-Sulfation in Mass Spectrometry Analysis
papers.abstract: Tyrosine O-sulfation is a posttranslational modification (PTM) in membrane and secreted proteins.
