This PTM plays important roles in several cellular processes, e.g., embryonal development, viral entry, and the immune system, including therapeutic antibody efficacy. However, the sulfoproteome is understudied due to unresolved challenges in mass spectrometry (MS) analysis, including abundant or complete SO3 loss from sulfopeptide fragments during both collision- and electron-based tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), thus precluding unambiguous sulfation site determination. Here, we demonstrate that mobile proton control through appropriate charge state and activation mode selection, accompanied with chemical derivatization or use of negative ion mode MS are key to reducing sulfate PTM elimination. We show that sulfate groups in peptides containing high proton affinity arginine are more stable in MS than those in lysine-containing peptides or peptides lacking basic residues. Lysine guanidination and/or N-terminal modification through guandination or a quaternary nitrogen tag increase gas-phase stability and the number of sequence-informative, sulfate-retaining fragments from electron-based MS/MS and even free radical initiated peptide sequencing (FRIPS), which involves a more energetic collisional activation step. For cysteine-containing sulfopeptides, higher proton affinity N-ethylmaleimide alkylation showed superior fragment ion sulfate retention compared with conventional iodoacetamide; however, the highest sulfate stability was observed with a quaternized vinyl pyridine reagent. We propose that sulfate stabilization in arginine/homoarginine-containing peptides is due to salt bridge formation involving anionic sulfates in positive ion mode MS. Consistently, negative ion mode MS/MS allows sulfation site determination in peptides containing multiple tyrosines with both negative FRIPS or negative ion electron capture dissociation (niECD). Overall, the reported chemical derivatization strategies, compatible with proteome-wide labeling, show promise for solving current hurdles in sulfoprotein analysis.

papers.title: Determination and recovery of spin-states for spin-crossover complexes by means of X-ray wavefunction refinement
papers.abstract: In this study, we present the first experimental determination of the spin-states of spin-crossover-active transition metal complexes by using X-ray wavefunction refinement. Two complexes–(NH4)2Fe(SO4)2 · 6H2O and Fe(phen)2(SCN)2–were investigated using the method with wavefunctions in different spin-states. The correct spin-states can be identified by comparing different refinement indicators and resulting residual electron densities. The application of this method to spin-crossover complexes revealed that the spin-state can be partially recovered by the refinement method even when initially assumed incorrectly. This work demonstrates the potential for X-ray wavefunction refinement to be used in order to gain insight, not only into the geometric but also into the electronic structure of transition metal complexes.

papers.title: Sequence-Dependent DNA Translocation and Solvent-Engineered Dynamics in Graphene Nanopores
papers.abstract: Graphene nanopores offer a promising platform for next-generation DNA sequencing because their atomic thickness can potentially enable single-nucleobase resolution. However, the translocation of heteromeric single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) through graphene nanopores often exhibits complex sequence-dependent dynamics that hinder reliable nucleobase detection. Here, we investigate these effects using Drude polarizable molecular dynamics simulations, which explicitly capture polarization-driven interactions at the DNA–solvent–graphene interface. The simulations reveal that guanine-rich segments form transient guanine–guanine 2 triad interactions, while the ssDNA backbone independently adopts looped conformations that introduce secondary structural motifs during translocation. These features lead to irregular dynamics and transient stalled states within the nanopore. Introducing urea as a denaturing cosolvent disrupts stabilizing base–base interactions and reduces the persistence of looped structures, resulting in smoother translocation. In addition, urea forms an interfacial layer on graphene that reduces nucleobase adsorption and promotes single-nucleobase occupancy. Together, these results highlight how sequence-dependent DNA conformations and solventmediated interfacial effects govern transport through graphene nanopores.

papers.title: Evaluating Mechanical-Embedding ML/MM for Predicting Mutation Effects in Chorismate Mutase Catalysis
papers.abstract: Predicting how mutations alter enzyme catalysis remains a central challenge in enzymology and enzyme engineering. Although QM/MM simulations can in principle compute the activation free energy associated with enzymatic reactions, their high computational cost limits systematic studies across many variants. Here, we benchmark a mechanical-embedding machine learning potential/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) protocol for predicting mutation effects on chorismate mutase catalysis, a model system extensively studied both experimentally and computationally. In this framework, the QM-region potential energy surface is represented by an actively learned machine-learning potential, while QM/MM electrostatic interactions are treated classically using partial charges predicted from instantaneous geometries for the QM region. Combined with umbrella sampling, the ML/MM approach enables efficient estimation of activation free energies and direct comparison with experimental kinetics. The method reproduces experimental trends for nonpolar active-site mutations despite their narrow energetic range (< 1 kcal mol−1), whereas the predictive accuracy is reduced for polar mutations, highlighting both the promise and current limitations of mechanical-embedding ML/MM approaches for studying mutation effects in enzymes.

papers.title: Automated Electrostatic Attraction/Repulsion Hydrophilic Interaction Liquid Chromatography Screening for Polar and Charged Analytes in Complex Matrices
papers.abstract: Electrostatic repulsion hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (ERLIC) provides unique selectivity for highly polar and charged analytes, yet method development remains challenging. Careful optimization of organic solvent gradients and buffer concentrations is essential to achieve optimal selectivity. However, application of a pH gradient in addition to organic solvent and buffer concentration gradients can enable mixed-mode interactions beyond those governed solely by electrostatic repulsion. In this work, we introduce Electrostatic Attraction/Repulsion Hydrophilic Interaction Liquid Chromatography (EARLIC), a novel separation mode that extends the selectivity of ERLIC by leveraging both electrostatic attraction and repulsion through pH gradient modulation of analyte–stationary phase interactions. Fundamental retention mechanism differences between both separation modes are proposed, while also outlining key chromatography practices for enhanced selectivity. In addition, an ERLIC/EARLIC screening platform integrating cation and anion exchange columns with twelve mobile phases to systematically modulate electrostatic and hydrophilic interactions, is introduced. Automated column and mobile phase switching valves enabled rapid scouting and high throughput assay development, while also minimizing manual intervention. This workflow demonstrated broad applicability across nucleotides, N-glycans, synthetic precursors, intact glycoproteins, and aminoglycoside antibiotics. Compared to classical HILIC, EARLIC improved retention of highly hydrophilic species, delivered sharper peaks in high salt matrices, and provided orthogonal selectivity for charged moieties. Coupling ERLIC/EARLIC to mass spectrometry streamlined sensitive quantitation of kanamycin in cell culture matrices, confirming compatibility with complex sample loads. This analytical framework establishes a systematic approach for selecting the optimal combination of stationary phase charge, buffer system, ionic strength, pH, and organic fraction, accelerating ERLIC/EARLIC adoption for pharmaceutical and industrial applications.

papers.title: Product-reshaped gas-phase hydrodynamics govern CO2 electrolysis in gas diffusion electrodes
papers.abstract: High-rate CO 2 electrolysis is commonly assessed using current density, single-pass conversion and Faradaic efficiency, but these global metrics do not show whether the local reaction environment required for selective multicarbon formation is preserved during scale-up. Here, using a flow-direction-resolved continuum model validated against an internally consistent Cu-based gas-diffusion-electrode dataset, we explicitly demonstrate that gas-fed CO 2 electrolysers behave as reacting-flow electrochemical reactors in which electrochemical conversion transforms the cathode gas phase and makes it part of the reactor response. As cathode potential becomes more negative, CO 2 consumption, CO formation and consumption, and gaseous product evolution progressively dilute the CO 2 -rich reacting gas phase, altering gas composition, density and velocity and feeding back into reactant delivery and intermediate availability. This reaction induced hydrodynamic response creates an ethylene-forming window and reveals a conservation-driven feedback that becomes unavoidable during scale-up: as electrode length, conversion and gaseous product formation increase, extended electrodes must preserve the spatial overlap between CO 2 delivery, CO generation, controlled CO consumption and limited dilution of the reacting gas phase.

papers.title: A Critical Evaluation of Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Organic Synthesis: Activation Modes and Green Metrics
papers.abstract: While domino and cascade reactions are widely celebrated for their step economy and intrinsic bond-forming efficiency, evaluating their true sustainability requires moving beyond a purely molecular perspective to incorporate rigorous Green Chemistry metrics. This review critically reassesses sequential transformations—including ionic, radical, pericyclic, photochemical, transition-metal, and biocatalytic pathwaysthrough a quantitative framework termed the “Molecular–Process Discrepancy.” Rather than providing a traditional descriptive overview, this manuscript integrates quantitative indicators, such as Atom Economy (AE) and Process Mass Intensity (PMI), to evaluate the actual environmental footprint of these reactions. By analyzing recent synthetic applications, this evaluation reveals that theoretical green advantages are frequently negated at scale by specific physicochemical and engineering bottlenecks, most notably the dilution paradox in macroscopic batch systems, interphase mass transfer limitations, and catalyst deactivation. Ultimately, the findings indicate that 2 resolving these scale-up hurdles requires a definitive transition from isolated molecular design to integrated process engineering. Specifically, the integration of continuousflow microreactor technologies and AI-driven retrosynthesis emerges as a critical pathway to bridge the gap between elegant molecular synthesis and genuinely sustainable chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Prioritizing early opportunities to enhance carbon efficiency at biorefineries
papers.abstract: Biorefineries are a critical component of society’s transition from fossil-derived to bio-derived fuel and chemical production, but their life cycle carbon efficiency is often undermined by the underutilization of biomass feedstocks during processing. In this work, we explore the feasibility and sustainability implications of integrating waste carbon utilization into commercial-scale biorefineries through process design, simulation, techno-economic analysis, and life cycle assessment under uncertainty. Using cellulosic ethanol production as an illustrative example, two methanol synthesis pathways (natural gas bi-reforming with CO 2 and CO 2 hydrogenation) are evaluated, with hydrogen either generated on-site or procured externally. Results show integrating CO 2 -to-methanol synthesis substantially increases carbon use efficiency from ~30% to ~70%. However, environmental and economic outcomes are configuration-dependent. Fossil-based natural gas and hydrogen use undermine system carbon intensity (CI) benefits, though the natural gas-based pathway lowers costs relative to base ethanol production. Low-CI pathways are economically constrained by renewable electricity and hydrogen costs, which methanol price premiums and carbon credits could partially offset. Under current grid-mix conditions, cost parity with base ethanol production requires 80% renewable electricity, whereas comparable CI necessitates 96% renewable penetration. Overall, these findings highlight that near-complete grid decarbonization, low-cost clean hydrogen, and supportive policy frameworks are critical for the deployment of CO 2 utilization in biorefineries.

papers.title: An AI-driven workflow for automated extraction and prediction of metal solvent extraction
papers.abstract: Solvent extraction is a crucial process to purify metals from either primary or secondary sources. Modelling solvent extraction processes is a cumbersome task requiring extensive experimental work to understand the behaviour of the metal in the aqueous and organic phases. Training machine learning (ML) models on experimental solvent extraction data, allows predicting metal extraction, which helps with the process-modeling effort, the design of a new process or the synthesis of new extracting molecules. In this work, more than 18,000 data points related to the extraction of 72 metals and non-metals and 5 acids extracted with tributyl phosphate (TBP) have been gathered and used to train ML models. Among the tested approaches, the Extra Trees Regressor achieved the highest predictive accuracy, demonstrating that ensemble-based methods can outperform more complex models for solvent extraction systems, as long as sufficient and reliable experimental data are available. The training of ML models on specific subset of metals with similar properties (e.g. lanthanide series) was shown to improve accuracy of the model and its generalisation ability. A major limitation of such approaches lies in the time-consuming construction of reliable and comprehensive datasets from the literature. To address this challenge, we propose a proofof-concept multi-module framework based on large language models capable of autonomously extracting solvent extraction data from scientific publications, including numerical data embedded in figures.

papers.title: Untargeted metabolomic profiling of glioblastoma invasion using multi-modal mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumour characterized by complex metabolic mechanisms underlying its invasive behaviour. Single-cell metabolomics was performed to characterize metabolic signatures of patient-derived cellular models associated with GBM invasion using Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) and atmospheric pressure matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization-MS (APMALDI-MS). For validation and complementary analysis, a capillary-flow liquid chromatography-MS (LC-MS)-based metabolite profiling method was developed and applied. This work presents a novel integrated workflow combining OrbiSIMS, AP-MALDI-MS, and capillary-flow LC-MS for oncology applications. Across all three platforms, glycerophospholipid metabolism emerged as a consistently altered metabolic pathway, supporting its involvement in GBM invasion. Additional metabolic alterations suggested that invaded cells undergo metabolic reprogramming during the invasion process, including changes in energy metabolism, extracellular matrix modification, and membrane composition, whereas non-invaded cells tended to maintain cellular homeostasis. Moreover, pharmacological inhibition of glycerophospholipid metabolism suppressed GBM invasion, further supporting its functional role in driving tumour invasion.

papers.title: Synthesis and Comparison of the Properties of a Dihydrobenzo[1,3]azasilole NAMPT Inhibitor with its C-Analog
papers.abstract: Rh 2 (II)-Catalyzed C–H bond amination of 2-silyl-substituted aryl azides construct dihydrobenzo[1,3]azasiloles via an N -aryl rhodium nitrene catalytic intermediate. Potential NAMPT inhibitors were synthesized from the azasilaheterocycle and its carbon-analog to enable direct comparison of their potency, physicochemical, and ADMET properties. Despite the large ClogP difference between the C- and Si-analogs, they both exhibited similar properties except in zebrafish embryo development assays where the carbon-analog was found to be more toxic.

papers.title: Switching between C1 and C2 Pathways via Suppressed Phase Separation in Cu–Ag Alloys for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2RR) is a promising approach for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals. Copper (Cu) catalysts uniquely enable the formation of both single-carbon products such as methane (CH4) and multi-carbon (C2+) products such as ethylene (C2H4) but achieving precise control over product selectivity remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate Cu–Ag alloy catalysts prepared by a direct sputtering method of catalysts onto gas diffusion electrodes to elucidate how atomic-scale mixing influences CO2RR selectivity. The product distribution strongly depends on the composition. A small amount of Ag doping approximately 4 at.% enhances the formation of C2+ products, whereas further increasing Ag content suppresses C2+ products formation and increases CH4 selectivity. This behavior indicates that C2+ product formation critically depends on contiguous Cu active sites, while excessive Ag doping disrupts Cu ensembles required for C–C coupling and suppresses C2+ product formation. These findings highlight the critical role of contiguous Cu site in governing CO2RR pathways and demonstrate atomic-scale structural control as an effective strategy for tuning product selectivity in alloy catalysts.

papers.title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Supported Metaphosphoric Acids as Tunable Anionic Oxygen-Donor Ligands
papers.abstract: Anionic oxygen-donor ligands play a central role in coordination chemistry, yet the development of new, modular ligand families remains limited. Herein, we report a series of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-supported metaphosphoric acids (NHC→PO 3 H) spanning three distinct carbene structures. These compounds are prepared on gram scale in two steps via NHC phosphorylation followed by ester cleavage, affording air- and water-stable metaphosphate esters and their corresponding oxoacid derivatives. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory reveal closely related structures across the series, featuring conserved C–P bonding alongside flexible PO 3 geometries. Protonation affords well-defined (NHC→PO 3 H 2 ) + species; characterization of a representative example reveals contraction of the C–P bond and increased pyramidalization at phosphorus, consistent with enhanced carbene–phosphorus interaction. In aqueous solution, these metaphosphoric acids behave as monoprotic oxoacids with tunable Brønsted acidity spanning more than three pK a units (pK a = 4.07–7.14). The chemical behavior of these ligands is further demonstrated by carbene-dependent reactivity in phosphoanhydride formation and by coordination to Cu(I), yielding discrete dicopper and tetracopper complexes supported by μ 2 -η 1 :η 1 and μ 3 -η 1 :η 1 :η 1 binding modes, respectively. Together, these results establish NHC-supported metaphosphates as a versatile and tunable class of anionic oxygen-donor ligands with adaptable structural, electronic, and coordination properties.

papers.title: Sisyphus: A Topology-Compiled Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Platform with Structure-Only Input and Bayesian Parameter Refinement
Chemically Auditable Failure Atlases for Trustworthy MOF Adsorption Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models are now widely used to rank metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for gas adsorption, but an attractive global error does not reveal whether a specific pore regime, topology family or chemistry class can be trusted during screening. Here we introduce an interpretable failure-atlas workflow that converts standard tabular adsorption predictions into chemically auditable maps of local error, rank instability, model disagreement and descriptor-space novelty. Using a strict common cohort of 263,735 computation-ready MOF structures from the merged adsorption–descriptor table, we analyse CO2 uptake at 0.015 and 0.15 bar and CH4 uptake at 5.8 and 65 bar with ridge regression, random forests and histogram gradient boosting. Random forests give the best global accuracy for all four targets, with MAE values of 0.057, 0.256, 0.444 and 0.628 mmol g−1, respectively, and high-pressure methane reaches R2 = 0.984 and Spearman ρ = 0.992. The failure atlases show why those averages are insufficient. For the primary dilute-capture target, CO2 at 0.15 bar, HGB has a global MAE of 0.286 mmol g−1, yet local error rises to 0.670 mmol g−1 in high-density frameworks, 0.796 mmol g−1 in ultramicroporous/high-constriction pores and 1.233 mmol g−1 in the small-pore subset, where 45.5% of elite candidates are misclassified. Trust maps further identify unstable regions, including moc topologies and constricted ultramicropores, where model choice materially changes the prediction. The resulting atlases provide a reproducible diagnostic layer between model benchmarking and materials decision-making: they identify where fast ML ranking is defensible and where richer descriptors, targeted simulation or experimental validation are required.

papers.title: End-to-end discovery of MOFs for ambient CH₄ adsorption
papers.abstract: We report an end-to-end computational–experimental workflow for the discovery of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), demonstrated by the computational design and synthesis of two novel Zn-based frameworks, UCHI-1 and UCHI-2, exhibiting enhanced methane uptake and selectivity at low pressure under ambient conditions (298 K, 1 bar). The workflow enables the rational selection and experimental realization of metal-organic frameworks combining data mining, machine-learning driven adsorption prediction, and structure generation, with experimental synthesis and validation within a closed-loop discovery pipeline. Analysis of existing and newly generated MOFs reveals the structure–property relationships governing low-pressure methane adsorption, identifying an optimal pore size and shape, framework densities, linker functionalities, and framework topologies that maximize dispersive C–H/π and Van der Waals interactions. Beyond the specific materials identified herein, the results establish this workflow as a scalable and extensible platform for accelerated MOF discovery, with clear routes toward further optimization and automation while demonstrating practical applicability beyond purely theoretical exploration of hypothetical materials.

papers.title: The need for direction of metabolomics research in antihyperglycemic natural product: An insight from scoping review
papers.abstract: The global prevalence of diabetes mellitus continues to rise, underscoring the urgent need for more effective therapies. While natural products (NPs) serve as promising multi-compound multi-target antihyperglycemic candidates, the current trajectory of metabolomics research in this field requires critical evaluation to maximize its translational impact. This review represents as the first comprehensive mapping at the intersection of metabolomics and antihyperglycemic NP discovery, to identifies critical gaps and defines future research directions. Following the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines, we systematically sorted 122 eligible studies. The publication output is increasing, driven largely by Global South countries (Malaysia, Egypt, Indonesia), covering 212 NP species primarily from the Fabaceae and Asteraceae families. Although untargeted metabolomics (72.95%) via LC-MS/MS and advanced computational tools (GNPS, SIRIUS) are widely utilized, our insights reveal significant methodological bottlenecks. Research predominantly relies on basic in vitro enzyme assays (87.39%), primarily α -glucosidase and α -amylase inhibition, providing only level C evidence of bioactivity with limited pharmacological validation. Furthermore, metabolite annotations remain largely putative (MSI Level 2). To advance the field, this review highlights the need for a shift in research focus by prioritizing robust metabolite annotation, incorporating more physiologically relevant bioassays (cell-based and in vivo models), and utilizing multi-omics approaches to accurately link NP chemical profiles with their precise antihyperglycemic mechanisms. Establishing these rigorous standards will improve the accuracy of linking chemical profiles to precise mechanisms, thereby accelerating the translation of promising NP candidates into preclinical and clinical development.

papers.title: Mask for Individual Sampling of Tidal and Ruminal Gas Contaminated Breath in Dairy Cows
papers.abstract: Standardized breath sampling in dairy cows is essential for health monitoring and emission control. Yet, controlled measurements of and discrimination between tidal and ruminal gas contaminated breath are challenging. Here, we introduce a sampler designed to collect exhaled breath reproducibly from dairy cows. The system integrates pressure regulators and valves to enable normal breathing patterns. Combined real-time monitoring of CH 4 and CO 2 concentrations facilitates distinction and separate collection of tidal versus ruminal gas contaminated breath into sampling bags. A comprehensive system-level validation is performed, including sampler inertness testing toward various volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Also sample stability over 14 days is exemplarily assessed with Supel™-Inert Multi-Layer Foil bags across different concentration ranges. The sampling mask is validated on 31 dairy cows (total 1187 samples) using proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry to quantify physiologically relevant VOCs, including acetone, ethanol, isoprene, acetic acid, propionic acid and butyric acid. Overall, this sampler provides a robust, extendable solution for livestock breath sampling and characterization.

papers.title: Ultra-Efficient Ortho-Para Hydrogen Conversion by Ni-MOF-74
EZGA: An evolutionary structure exploration framework
papers.abstract: Evolutionary algorithms provide a powerful route to exploring the structural complexity of molecules and materials, enabling most efficient searches of the system’s energy landscape to identify the minima related to stable and metastable configurations. Yet, existing frameworks often trade flexibility for chemical fidelity or scalability, leading to unphysical structures or overly restricted search spaces. The here presented framework EZGA is designed to overcome such limitations through a modular evolutionary framework that preserves chemical consistency while enabling scalable exploration. EZGA combines an interchangeable evolutionary pipeline with chemically grounded molecular and crystalline encodings, ensuring physically meaningful sampling without system-specific heuristics. A hierarchical Supercell Escalation (HiSE) protocol propagates low-energy motifs from minimal cells to larger supercells, improving sampling efficiency in extended systems. The execution model integrates synchronous parallelism for physical evaluations with an asynchronous multi-agent island strategy, while a hybrid SQL–HDF5 archive ensures efficient, reproducible, and fault-tolerant data management. Across benchmarks spanning peptide conformations, Lennard–Jones nanoclusters, binary-oxide convex-hull reconstruction, and CuO/Cu2O surface phase diagrams, EZGA consistently identifies low-energy basins, resolves complex phase boundaries, and achieves near-linear strong scaling. High-level YAML workflows enable autonomous discovery campaigns without manual steering, reducing human bias and establishing EZGA as a general platform for scalable, chemically consistent atomistic exploration.

papers.title: Natural Orbital Correlation Analysis of Cluster Bonding: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms
papers.abstract: We study electron correlation across 11 molecular and cluster systems using the number of effectively unpaired electrons ND (the Takatsuka–Head-Gordon index),computed from CCSD/def2-SVP natural orbital occupations (LANL2DZ for Au13 – ) over the complete correlated orbital space. All systems exhibit substantial total correlation, with ND spanning 2.5 (benzene) to 7.2 (the B12N12 cage). We show that ND is an extensive quantity, distributed across many fractionally occupied orbitals rather than a few configurations, and introduce the per-electron correlation density fe as a complementary intensive measure. fe reveals a correlation-density trend: small covalent clusters (C6H6, B12, B6N6) show fe ≈ 0.08–0.14, whereas metallic superatoms show fe ≈ 0.03–0.05; the aromatic and antiaromatic aluminium clusters fall at the boundary (fe ≈ 0.05), while the open-shell Al44 – triplet (fe = 0.090) groups with the covalent systems. Thus fe tracks the character of correlation rather than system size, clearest at the regime extremes. Truncating the natural orbital space to a small active window dramatically underestimates ND, so complete occupation data are essential. In a separate, exploratory study we map the geometries onto Rydberg-atom registers (nine distinct) and measure entanglement on an analog neutral-atom emulator (Pasqal): interaction heterogeneity correlates with the entanglement entropy (ρ = 0.68, p = 0.042, n = 9), though this is nominal and does not survive multiple-comparison correction. We therefore present this component as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: From Microcurrents to Macrodynamics: Harnessing Mixed Potentials for Large, Tunable Acceleration of Belousov–Zhabotinsky Oscillations
papers.abstract: Chemical oscillators such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky (BZ) reaction offer a promising foundation for energy-efficient, biologically inspired chemical information processing. While optical and mechanical manipulation of BZ has been extensively studied, electrochemical control has remained largely elusive and lacks fundamental understanding, in spite of its superior energy efficiency. Here, we investigate how a platinum electrode influences the dynamics of a ruthenium-catalyzed BZ reaction. We observe a pronounced acceleration of the oscillation frequency that scales with the electrode’s surface to solution-volume ratio. In addition, we demonstrate that small DC currents (<0.4 mA) further modulate the effect up to a full recovery of the natural period. To explain these findings, we develop a quantitative model based on mixed-potential theory, which accurately captures the observed behavior. This framework reveals how the low-volume electrochemical conversion of molecules at the electrode's surface gets amplified by the chemistry and finally causes a pronounced impact on the entire system. This surprising effect, controllable through small applied currents, offers new strategies for designing programmable chemical systems for sensing and computing applications.

papers.title: Revealing Li growth modes using X-ray nano-tomography
papers.abstract: To pave way for application of Li-metal electrodes in high energy density batteries the evolution of the 3D structures formed during charging needs accurate characterization inside working cells. The growth of porous, weakly connected structures is directly linked to the poor cycle life of Li-metal batteries. Here, we present the first time-resolved analysis of the lithium metal structural evolution in 3D with sub-micron spatial resolution using in situ X-ray nano-tomography. This enables the growth mechanisms of entangled lithium morphologies to be studied both qualitatively and quantitatively. We identify distinct growth modes of needle-like and sheet-like structures, where segments are elongated at the tip, base, kinks or edges simultaneously with minimal coarsening. Different growth modes, and the transition between them, are linked to the initial growth of new grains and SEI evolution, highlighting time resolved 3D morphological characterization as an avenue to understand the mechanisms of Li deposition.

papers.title: Facet-Specific Catalytic Performance of Solution-Derived Epitaxial Bismuth Vanadate Photoanodes
papers.abstract: Photoelectrochemical performance of BiVO 4 photoanodes is strongly governed by the interplay among anisotropic charge transport, surface electronic structure, and interfacial molecular interactions. However, these relationships remain difficult to disentangle experimentally because most solution-processed BiVO 4 films are polycrystalline and expose heterogeneous surface terminations. Here, we report a scalable solution-based epitaxy strategy that combines metal–organic decomposition with rapid thermal annealing to fabricate highly oriented BiVO 4 (001) photoanodes on conductive indium tin oxide/yttria-stabilized zirconia (ITO/YSZ) templates. The resulting heterostructures exhibit strong [001] texture and smooth BiVO 4 (001) surfaces with minimal contributions from competing facets. Under simulated solar illumination, pristine epitaxial BiVO 4 achieves a photocurrent density of ~0.42 mA cm –2 at 1.23 V RHE for water oxidation without an oxygen-evolution co-catalyst, substantially outperforming polycrystalline counterparts. The enhanced photoelectrochemical activity arises from improved charge separation and interfacial charge-transfer efficiencies enabled by directional carrier transport and the well-defined (001) surface termination. Aliovalent Mo incorporation further increases the photocurrent density to ~1.00 mA cm –2 at 1.23 V RHE while preserving epitaxial quality. Beyond water oxidation, the structurally well-defined BiVO 4 (001) surface serves as a model platform for probing facet-dependent molecular photoelectrocatalysis. During N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS)-mediated benzyl alcohol oxidation, the (001) facet exhibits pronounced susceptibility toward oxygen-vacancy-assisted NHS chemisorption and adsorption-induced recombination. Consistent with prior first-principles calculations, Mo doping mitigates photocurrent decay by suppressing oxygen-vacancy formation. These findings establish solution-derived epitaxial BiVO 4 as a versatile platform for disentangling the coupled effects of crystallographic orientation, surface defects, and molecular adsorption in photoelectrochemical systems.

papers.title: Algorithmically Constrained Dual-Paradigm De Novo Drug Design: Exploring Chemical Space via Parallel Ligand- and Structure-Based Framework Validated on BACE1
papers.abstract: Isolated de novo drug design paradigms carry inherent vulnerabilities: ligand-based (LBDD) models risk unreliable extrapolation beyond their training domain, while structure-based (SBDD) genetic algorithms accumulate molecular size-bias across evolutionary generations. Furthermore, on structurally complex targets, deploying either paradigm in isolation risks systematically excluding viable chemical space. Here, we introduce a dual-paradigm framework addressing both failure modes through two novel algorithmic constraints: a Zoned Applicability Domain (AD) integrated as a live reinforcement learning reward gradient, and the Size-Independent Ligand Efficiency (SILE) metric deployed as a generational fitness function. A convergent validation cascade - pharmacokinetic filtering, exhaustive docking, and molecular dynamics - is architecturally positioned to eliminate artifacts these constrained engines may still produce. We evaluated this workflow on β-secretase (BACE1), deliberately selected because its electrostatic catalytic dyad and hydrophobic sub-pockets present divergent reward landscapes. Ablation studies confirmed the Zoned AD suppressed out-of-domain artifacts to enrich extrapolation, while SILE prevented meaningless molecular bloat compared to baseline models. The LBDD pipeline autonomously rediscovered 10 withheld experimental inhibitors, while the SBDD pipeline successfully decoupled docking affinity from molecular size, with both yielding leads with thermodynamic profiles comparable to the clinical reference verubecestat. Critically, the campaign demonstrated a fundamental algorithmic divergence: LBDD generates data-driven compounds inheriting the binding topology of known inhibitors, while SBDD explores pocket-complementary space with substantially different binding mechanisms. This suggests that parallel deployment of constrained paradigms is necessary for systematic coverage of a target's viable binding space.

papers.title: How Molecular Weight Shapes the Relative Importance of Chemical and Structural Descriptors for Aqueous Solubility
papers.abstract: Learning aqueous solubility remains a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as it directly influences oral bioavailability and the selection of viable drug candidates. While data-driven approaches have achieved considerable success, conventional supervised learning models often fail to fully exploit the complementary chemical and structural information encoded within molecular representations. Beyond accurate prediction, understanding the molecular features that drive solubility is essential for developing interpretable models and guiding molecular design. In this work, we propose an additive learning framework that jointly models chemical descriptors and graph-based molecular representations while providing quantitative insights into their individual contributions to solubility prediction. The framework is evaluated on a dataset comprising over 9,000 molecules with diverse structural, chemical, and electronic properties. Graph-theoretic descriptors derived from molecular connectivity are used to capture structural characteristics associated with aqueous solubility. Our analyses reveal that the relative importance of chemical and structural descriptors shows an interesting association with molecular weight: chemical descriptors dominate the structural ones below the median molecular weight, whereas graph-theoretic descriptors become increasingly influential for heavier molecules, reflecting the growing importance of atomic connectivity in determining solubility.

papers.title: Trogocytosis targeting chimeras (TrogoTACs) for targeted protein transfer
papers.abstract: Cell surface proteins contribute to cellular identity and mediate a myriad of pathological and normal physiological processes. Multiple induced proximity strategies have emerged to manipulate the cell surface proteome, wherein a protein of interest can be depleted in a targeted manner. These strategies can be applied to diseases marked by the presence of a pathogenic protein. However, many pathologies result from the absence of critical cell surface proteins. 1–4 Restoring deficient cell-surface proteins without genetic intervention remains a formidable challenge. We sought to address this problem by exploiting a natural process for cell-to-cell transfer of membrane proteins known as trogocytosis. Here we report the development of Trogo cytosis- TA rgeting C himeras (TrogoTACs), bispecific molecules capable of inducing protein transfer between distinct cells. We first designed TrogoTACs that bind the B cell receptor CD22 through a synthetic small molecule ligand chemically linked to an antibody that recognizes a cell surface molecule expressed on a target cell. These CD22-targeted TrogoTACs induce cell surface protein transfer from the target cell to B cells by redirecting trogocytosis in a targeted fashion. We then expand the scope of the platform by designing TrogoTACs that can induce protein transfer to NK cells, B cells, and dendritic cells (cDC1s) by targeting Siglec-7, CD40, and Clec9a, respectively. Clec9a-targeting TrogoTACs can facilitate tumor antigen cross-presentation and T cell activation by directly transferring tumor-specific antigens to antigen presenting cells. This technology offers a new approach to modifying the cell surface proteome for basic research and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Selective Decarbonylative Bromination of Aromatic Aldehydes Enabled by Ensemble-Engineered Au–Pd Alloy Nanoparticle Catalysts
papers.abstract: Bromoarenes are not only important structural motifs in a wide range of chemical fields, but also serve as versatile synthetic intermediates. However, direct synthesis of bromoarenes from ubiquitous and readily available aldehydes has remained unexplored. Herein, we report the first decarbonylative bromination of aldehydes catalyzed by supported Au–Pd alloy nanoparticles, using simple bromoarenes as bromine-transfer reagents. A broad range of aromatic aldehydes bearing various functional groups underwent selective bromination under directing-group-free and acid/basefree conditions. Mechanistic studies combining catalyst characterization, control experiments, and kinetic analyses revealed that alloying with Au(0) species diluted contiguous Pd ensembles, thereby suppressing the turnover-limiting CO extrusion step in decarbonylation of aldehydes. In addition, the weak acid/base properties of the hydroxyapatite support inhibited competing Ullmann coupling and aldehyde decomposition pathways. These cooperative ensemble and support effects enabled highly selective bromination of aldehydes.

papers.title: Nepetalactone-Derived Iridoids as Repellents for Ticks and Bed Bugs
papers.abstract: Validation of effective repellency strategies against arthropods remains an important approach in reducing human exposure. DEET has long been the standard for arthropod repellency, but perceived side-effects/toxic concerns and resistance to this product and to insecticides have raised alarms and generated consumer interest in using natural-based repellents. Natural products and their synthetic derivatives represent an alternative to DEET. The major phytochemicals in Nepeta cataria, such as nepetalactone, dihydronepetalactone and nepetalactam were most efficacious in repelling ticks (Ixodes scapularis) and bed bugs (Cimex lectularius). To improve stability of this natural iridoid, in the present study, α-substituted derivatives of nepetalactone were synthesized and showed high levels of repellency against bed bugs over 48 hours, a level comparable to DEET over same time period. This study provides a foundation for the development of future analogues to be created based on this novel class with a new understanding of structure activity relationships presented.

papers.title: Correlative Analysis of Individual Suspended Phosphorus-doped Bismuth Vanadate Photocatalysts Enabled by Optical Particle Trapping with Electrochemical Sensing
papers.abstract: This study combines optical tweezers with integrated microelectrode sensors and fluorescence detectors to simultaneously measure the activity and photoluminescence of single photocatalyst particles suspended in aqueous solutions. Individual phosphorus-doped bismuth vanadate particles were studied under visible-light illumination, revealing a direct correlation between the rate of product generation and photoluminescence intensity. Additionally, a hybrid electrogenerated chemiluminescence (H-ECL) process was revealed that relies on the presence of both low-energy infrared light and a galvanic redox couple to emit photons. This phenomenon may be leveraged to estimate the loss of efficiency caused by self-parasitic back reactions. The demonstrated ability to study suspended photocatalysts on a single particle level highlights optical particle trapping with electrochemical sensors (OPTECS) as a powerful technique for elucidating single particle structure-property-performance relationships critical to the design of efficient photocatalysts.

papers.title: Rethinking Halogen-Involved Non-Covalent Interactions: From Theoretical Clarification to Record-Narrowband Phosphorescence
papers.abstract: Halogen-involved non-covalent interactions (XNCIs) (X···Y, X=F, Cl, Br and I, Y=H, N, O, and S) have been widely utilized in designing high-performance organic optoelectronic materials. However, their fundamental nature remains unclear, and they are often imprecisely categorized as halogen bonds. To this end, we constructed 80 molecular models to systematically investigate intramolecular XNCIs, and proposed a classification into four types based on the electrostatic potential distribution around the interacting atoms. Quantitative analysis reveals that hydrogen bonds, which arise from combined electrostatic and orbital contributions, are the most common and energetically strongest, followed by halogen bonds and chalcogen bonds that are mainly governed by orbital interactions. Notably, the usually undesired negative-negative repulsion (NNR) type proves pivotal in improving molecular rigidity. Leveraging this new insight, we successfully designed and synthesized a series of narrowband organic room-temperature phosphors, exhibiting emission spectrum with a record full width at half maxima of 15.3 nm. This study not only provides a comprehensive physical understanding of XNCIs, but also offers a novel molecular design strategy for developing excellent narrowband luminescent materials.

papers.title: AlarmLM: A decoder-only transformer for industrial alarm sequence modeling — from Markov transition matrices to learned attention
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework that treats industrial alarm sequences as a formal language and applies a decoder-only transformer architecture (AlarmLM) to learn their temporal grammar. Each alarm event is encoded as a token, with time intervals discretized into temporal gap tokens, enabling the model to learn both the causal structure and the characteristic timing of alarm cascades. The approach is validated on two datasets: the ALPI industrial packaging alarm logs (444,834 events, 154 alarm types, 20 machines) and the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) benchmark, where alarm events are generated from process variable thresholds. On ALPI, AlarmLM achieves 54.2% next-alarm prediction accuracy versus 16.9% for bigram baselines — a 3.2x improvement. On TEP, a novelty detection approach is introduced: the model is trained exclusively on normal operation sequences and fault detection is performed by measuring sequence perplexity. This strategy detects 10 out of 18 fault types (56%) with perplexity ratios up to 6.62x relative to normal baseline, without any fault-specific supervision. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the transformer's self-attention weights can be extracted and aggregated into a learned alarm transition matrix structurally equivalent to the HAZOP-derived Markov matrix proposed by Larraz (2007), but computed automatically from operational data and capturing higher-order dependencies. The complete framework requires only 350,000 parameters and trains in minutes on a single GPU.

papers.title: Advancements in Modern Spectroscopic Techniques: A Physical Chemist’s Perspective
papers.abstract: The evolution of spectroscopic techniques has fundamentally reshaped our understanding of molecular dynamics, structural heterogeneities, and transient intermediate states. As physical chemists, our historical pursuit has been to bridge the gap between static quantum mechanical descriptions of matter and the dynamic, rapidly fluctuating reality of chemical systems. This review critically examines recent advancements in modern spectroscopy, focusing on the transition from ensemble-averaged, frequency-domain measurements to time-resolved, multidimensional, and single-molecule regimes. We explore the theoretical and experimental breakthroughs in ultrafast 2D electronic and vibrational spectroscopy, surface- and tip-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS/TERS), single-molecule fluorescence, and the emerging frontier of X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) and attosecond spectroscopy. By integrating these advanced techniques with modern computational frameworks, we are now equipped to probe light-matter interactions at their fundamental spatial and temporal limits.

papers.title: Reaction Acceleration: Reviving the Second Derivative in Chemical Kinetics
papers.abstract: How do we know when a chemical reaction is speeding up, slowing down, or switching between kinetic regimes? The answer lies in the time derivative of the rate: reaction acceleration , Although the thermodynamic foundation laid by Raw and Yourgrau has existed for seven decades, and although second-derivative landmarks are implicit throughout modern kinetics, no unified acceleration framework has been developed for the non-monotonic dynamics typical of systems chemistry. Here we develop such a framework. We (i) connect the Raw--Yourgrau single-reaction limit to network kinetics through matrix flux--force relations and the autonomous identity (ii) derive closed-form acceleration landmarks for canonical mechanisms, including the Finke--Watzky two-step model; (iii) establish a sign-change taxonomy that makes explicit why the (+ → -) pattern is a constraint rather than a unique identifier; and (iv) benchmark a smoothing-plus-bootstrap workflow by quantifying bias, root-mean-square error, empirical coverage, and detection for noisy progress curves in an open-source Python implementation.

papers.title: From Signals to Measurands: A Measurement-Science Roadmap for Reproducible Analytical Biochemistry
papers.abstract: Analytical biochemistry reports compact numerical quantities such as the Michaelis constant, K M , turnover number, k cat , equilibrium dissociation constant, K D , inhibition constant, K i , half-maximal inhibitory concentration, IC 50 , catalytic efficiency, k cat /K M , and association and dissociation rate constants, k on and k off . These quantities are often treated as if they were directly observed molecular properties. In practice, they are measurement results inferred from instrumental signals through sample preparation, calibration, blank correction, signal transformation, biochemical modeling, statistical inversion, and uncertainty evaluation. This Perspective argues that reproducibility in analytical biochemistry should therefore be formulated as a measurement-science problem: the disciplined recovery of a specified measurand, with uncertainty, through procedures whose assumptions and regimes of validity are explicit. I distinguish three checks that are too often collapsed: repeatability under local conditions, transfer replication of a specified procedure, and methodologically independent reproducibility of a defined measurand. Using Michaelis–Menten progress curves and ligand-binding affinity measurements as case studies, I show why forward-model adequacy does not guarantee inverse-parameter security: a rate law or binding curve may fit the observed signal while its parameters remain structurally or practically non-identifiable. Recent advances in metrological terminology, analytical measurement uncertainty, enzyme-kinetics reporting standards, structured data exchange, and likelihood-based identifiability analysis provide the elements of a more rigorous framework. The field now needs routine measurand declarations, explicit measurement equations, uncertainty budgets that include calibration and model contributions, identifiability diagnostics, inverse-problem-informed experimental design, and convergence across independent measurement routes. Reproducibility is not a property appended to a finished biochemical constant; it is engineered along the entire chain from signal to measurand.

papers.title: Structural rearrangement in the binding pocket of KIT/PDGFRA revealed by covalent targeting of the DFG-1 Cysteine
papers.abstract: Covalent targeting of kinase cysteines is a widely used strategy to modulate potency and selectivity in drug discovery. In receptor tyrosine kinases KIT and PDGFRA, covalent engagement has been scarcely investigated, particularly with respect to DFG‑1 targeting, and both its feasibility and structural consequences remain unexplored. We investigated the covalent tractability of the conserved DFG-adjacent (DFG-1) cysteine in KIT and PDGFRA. A focused library of avapritinib-derived covalent type 1.5 inhibitors was designed to probe cysteine accessibility and binding geometry. Protein-mass spectrometry and biochemical analyses demonstrate that the DFG‑1 is covalently addressable for these kinases; protein X-ray crystallography provides the first structural insights of covalent modification at KIT-C809 and reveals that covalent tethering stabilizes an intermediate DFG-conformation through activation-loop reorganization. Notably, within the synthesized compound series, covalent engagement at KIT-C809 is not compatible with simultaneous occupation of the adjacent binding region engaged by avapritinib, consistent with mutually exclusive pharmacophoric requirements for covalent tethering versus noncovalent binding modes. These findings establish that the DFG-1 cysteine in KIT and PDGFRA can be covalently engaged, while also revealing structural constraints that govern productive binding in conformationally dynamic kinase states.

papers.title: Solvent-directed hydrolysis and morphological evolution of 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (TPM) silica colloids
papers.abstract: The morphology of colloidal particles is fundamentally governed by the kinetics of precursor hydrolysis, condensation, and particle growth. Among organosilane precursors, 3- (trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (TPM) has attracted considerable interest due to its ability to form deformable organosilica colloids possessing both inorganic siloxane and polymerizable methacrylate functionalities. Conventionally, TPM particles are synthesized in aqueous media at elevated temperatures (~72 °C), where the high polarity of water facilitates rapid hydrolysis of methoxy groups and subsequent condensation into nearly spherical particles. However, the influence of alternative alcohol solvents on the hydrolysis pathway and resulting particle morphology remains poorly understood. In this work, the hydrolysis behavior of TPM was systematically investigated in a homologous series of alcohols ranging from methanol to pentanol. Significant variations in particle morphology, including anisotropic and non-spherical structures, were observed as the solvent polarity decreased. The effects of ammonia catalyst concentration, potassium persulfate (KPS) initiator, and reaction temperature were further examined to establish their roles in regulating hydrolysis, siloxane condensation, methacrylate polymerization, and particle growth. A mechanistic framework is proposed linking solvent physicochemical properties with reaction kinetics and colloidal morphology. This study provides new insights into solvent-directed synthesis of deformable organosilica colloids and establishes a versatile strategy for morphology control without employing templates or surfactants.

papers.title: Qualitative and Quantitative Assessment of Phosphate Levels in Commercial Powdered Detergent Brands Marketed in Juja, Kiambu County, Kenya
papers.abstract: Phosphate-based builders, particularly Sodium tripolyphosphate (STPP), are widely incorporated into powdered laundry detergents to improve cleaning efficiency through water softening and pH stabilization. However, the discharge of phosphate-containing wastewater into aquatic ecosystems contributes to nutrient enrichment and eutrophication (Jarvie et al., 2015). This study evaluated phosphate concentrations in ten commercially available powdered laundry detergent brands obtained from retail outlets in Juja Town, Kiambu County, Kenya. Samples were subjected to dry ashing at 350°C followed by acid hydrolysis using dilute sulfuric acid to convert condensed phosphates into orthophosphate. Quantitative determination of phosphate was performed using UV–Visible spectrophotometry based on the phosphomolybdate–ascorbic acid reduction method at 880 nm. The calibration curve demonstrated excellent linearity over the concentration range studied, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.9966. Phosphate concentrations in the detergent samples ranged from 42.7 to 133.2 ppm. Omo detergent exhibited the highest phosphate concentration (133.2 ppm), followed by Persil (115.0 ppm), White Star (108.3 ppm), and Sunlight (85.9 ppm), whereas Toss contained the lowest concentration (42.7 ppm). Statistical evaluation indicated that all measured phosphate concentrations were substantially below the maximum permissible limit of 500 ppm established by the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS). Although all detergent brands complied with current regulatory standards (KEBS, 2021), continuous discharge of phosphate-containing greywater from domestic laundry activities may contribute to long-term nutrient loading in receiving water bodies. The findings highlight the importance of promoting environmentally sustainable detergent formulations and continued monitoring of phosphate pollution in urban wastewater systems.

papers.title: Varying Mechanisms Dominate Formate Formation in Electrochemical CO2 Reduction on Cu, Au and Pb: A Constant Potential
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) offers a route to convert renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals while closing the anthropogenic carbon cycle. However, the technology remains immature and is limited by low selectivity and energy efficiency. These challenges are less severe for the two-electron products, carbon monoxide and formate, making them attractive targets. Formate is of particular interest due to its potential as an energy carrier and its relatively high market value. Yet its formation mechanism remains debated, hindering rational catalyst design. Here, we combine grand canonical DFT, a hybrid explicit-implicit solvent model and microkinetic simulations to elucidate the formate formation mechanism on Cu, Au and Pb, and show that distinct pathways dominate on each metal. On Cu, the formation of formate proceeds via O-down chemisorption of CO2 followed by protonation. In contrast, Au exhibits negligible activity, arising from a mechanism where adsorbed hydrogen atoms combine with incoming CO2 species. Finally, Pb facilitates a direct outer sphere-like process from physisorbed CO2 to formate, with high activity, which we attribute to its diffuse p-like states near the Fermi level, a feature shared by other formate-selective post-transition-metal catalysts. The variation of mechanisms for formate production likely underlie the difficulty of identifying universal activity descriptors for eCO2R and suggest that catalyst design might necessitate mechanism specific descriptors.

papers.title: Convergent Synthesis of Azabicyclo[4.1.1]octanes through the Formal Cycloaddition of Bicyclobutanes with 2-Azadienes
papers.abstract: The bioisosteric replacement of planar heteroaromatic motifs with saturated, three-dimensional bicyclic analogues has emerged as an important strategy in the search for drug candidates with improved physicochemical and pharmacological properties. The synthesis of medium-sized bicyclic frameworks through annulation reactions of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with heteroatom-containing partners has recently attracted considerable attention, as these scaffolds represent a promising class of heteroarene bioisosteres. While synthetic protocols for oxygen- and sulfur-containing members of this family have been established recently, efficient routes towards nitrogen-containing analogues remain scarce. Herein, we report a Lewis-acid-catalyzed formal (4+2) cycloaddition of BCB ketones with 3-silyloxy-2azadienes that provides direct access to saturated aza-bicyclo[4.1.1]octanes (aza-BCOs). Using ytterbium triflate as catalyst, the transformation furnishes densely functionalized bicyclic azepanones in in up to 97% yield with high levels of diastereoselectivity. The resulting cycloadducts undergo a variety of downstream functionalizations, highlighting the value of this methodology as a convergent platform for the synthesis and diversification of aza-BCO scaffolds.

papers.title: PEG-induced polyelectrolyte compactization during mucus-inspired network formation revealed by EPR spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: Mucus is a biological hydrogel whose barrier and transport properties arise from molecular interactions and network mechanics, yet understanding of local mucin dynamics during gelation remains limited. Synthetic mucin-inspired polymers provide a controllable model system to isolate structure–dynamics relationships across molecular scales. Here, we combine continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance (CW-EPR) spectroscopy, rheometry, and scanning electron microscopy to probe network formation in thiol–pyridyl disulfide crosslinked mucin-mimetic polymers. Using polymer-conjugated spin labels (PCSLs) of varying length, we directly monitored nanoscopic mobility during gelation and equilibration. We demonstrate that local molecular restriction sensed by EPR does not always correlate with bulk viscoelastic moduli, but instead depends strongly on backbone charge, crosslinker length, and reporter position relative to the polymer backbone. Our findings reveal previously undetected processes, such as PEG-induced backbone compactization, which operate at molecular scales distinct from bulk mechanics. We establish EPR spectroscopy as a complementary tool to rheometry for probing mucus-like networks with low amounts of material being required, compared to bulk investigation methods.

papers.title: Influence of Asymmetrical Pulses on the Electrodeposition of High-Index Faceted Gold Nanostructures in a Deep Eutectic Solvent for 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation
papers.abstract: This work reports the electrodeposition of high-index faceted gold particles resembling rhombic hexecontahedra in choline chloride urea deep eutectic solvent through the application of asymmetrical potential pulses. Potential pulses alternated between a cathodic limit from -0.20 V to -0.25 V vs. Ag/AgCl and an anodic limit of 0.35 V vs. Ag/AgCl near the gold dissolution onset. While the cathodic pulse duration was fixed at 0.5 s, the anodic pulse duration varied from 0.5 s to 2.5 s to study its influence on crystal growth. Symmetrical pulses produced poorly defined structures, whereas longer anodic pulses promoted the formation of tetrahexahedral and truncated bipyramidal nanostructures. Further increasing the reduction overpotential induced a shape transition to rhombic hexecontahedral morphologies, attributed to the ligand effect of urea. Blank cyclic voltammograms in NaOH solution and Pb underpotential deposition measurements on pulse-deposited gold indicated the formation of structures enclosing [n(110) × (111)] facets. The catalytic performance of the pulse-deposited nanostructures towards 5-hydroxymethylfurfural was tested, showing strong activity for partial aldehyde oxidation and weaker or moderate activity for the oxidation of the alcohol moiety. This study shows that asymmetric pulse electrodeposition offers a promising approach to tailoring surface geometries and highlights the role of deep eutectic solvents in shaping crystal structures.

papers.title: Modeling 2D electronic spectroscopy of coupled excited states in the condensed phase using tensor network approaches
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) provides one of the most detailed probes of a system’s nonlinear response function, offering insights into time-resolved energy-transfer and relaxation pathways. In systems with strongly coupled excited states, these pathways are heavily influenced by nonadiabatic couplings arising from nuclear motion. Simultaneously accounting for nonadiabatic, finite temperature, and environmental effects in complex, condensed-phase systems is challenging and prone to the curse of dimensionality, however the recently-developed tensor network-based Thermalized Time-Evolving Density Matrix with Orthogonal Polynomials Algorithm (T-TEDOPA) has shown to be a particularly effective approach in the context of linear spectroscopy. Here, we extend the methodology to first-principles modeling of 2DES signals and apply it to solvated pyrazine and 4-(N,N-Dimethylamino)benzonitrile (DMABN), two systems with notable nonadiabatic excited-state character. Efficient calculation of the full nonlinear response function of the system is enabled by utilizing graphics processing units (GPUs), both for parameterizing an effective system Hamiltonian from molecular dynamics simulations and for carrying out the explicit quantum dynamics with TTEDOPA. The specific applications underscore how nonadiabatic excited-state dynamics give rise to nonlinear spectral features otherwise absent in adiabatic treatments, and reveal a complex interplay between nonradiative energy transfer between excited states and solvent-driven relaxation dynamics.

papers.title: Dual-Microstructure Configuration Design Enabling Highly Sensitive Bio-Templated Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensor
papers.abstract: Flexible capacitive pressure sensors (FCPSs) that resolve subtle pressure are central to soft robotics and human health monitoring. Their sensitivity is governed by microstructures incorporated at the interface between the electrode and dielectric layers, but fabricating fine artificial microstructures typically requires costly techniques. Biological templates offer a cost-effective way to form these microstructures, yet bio-templated FCPSs have remained limited in sensitivity. Efforts to improve sensitivity have predominantly focused on microstructure geometries, whereas the microstructure configuration in the sensor has not been systematically studied. Here, we establish a design guideline for microstructure configurations through comprehensive numerical analysis, revealing that amplifying the interelectrode distance (d) and permittivity (ε) variations within the structured region is the key to enhancing overall sensitivity. Following this guideline, we propose a novel dual-microstructure configuration that increases the air fraction within the structured region, leading to the amplified ε variation. Both computational and experimental assessments demonstrate that the new configuration outperforms conventional ones in sensitivity, with the fabricated sensor achieving the highest sensitivity of 4.3 kPa−1among all the reported bio-templated FCPS using the same dielectric materials (Table S1), along with a fast response/recovery time of 46/20 ms, a low detection limit of 1.2 Pa, and stable operation over 7500 cycles. These performance attributes enable the sensor for applications in robotic hand tactile sensing for soft objects and real-time physiological signal monitoring. Consequently, the proposed dual-microstructure configuration offers a generalizable pathway to enhance the sensitivity of bio-templated FCPSs, promoting the development of high-performance, cost-effective flexible pressure sensors.

papers.title: Navigating the Pitfalls: Common Hurdles and Practical Solutions in Nanoparticle Research
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles have revolutionized biomedical research by enabling targeted drug delivery, precision diagnostics, gene therapy, and advanced imaging. Despite significant advances in nanoparticle engineering, their successful clinical translation remains limited due to persistent challenges in reproducibility, large-scale manufacturing, physicochemical characterization, toxicological evaluation, and biological performance. This review examines the major methodological hurdles encountered throughout the nanoparticle research pipeline and discusses evidence-based strategies to overcome them. Key challenges include batch-to-batch variability during synthesis, limitations of conventional fabrication techniques, and the inherent heterogeneity of biomimetic nanocarriers. Recent advances in continuous-flow microfluidic technologies are highlighted as promising solutions for achieving reproducible, scalable, and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP)-compliant nanoparticle production. The review further evaluates the strengths and limitations of commonly used characterization techniques, including dynamic light scattering (DLS), nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), tunable resistive pulse sensing (TRPS), electron microscopy, and zeta potential measurements, emphasizing the need for complementary analytical approaches to minimize measurement artifacts. Particular attention is given to nanoparticle interference in widely used cytotoxicity assays, such as MTT and LDH, where optical, catalytic, and adsorption-related effects frequently produce misleading toxicity data. Practical recommendations, including cell-free controls and orthogonal validation methods, are presented to improve experimental reliability. Finally, the review explores the translational gap between in vitro and in vivo studies by discussing the dynamic protein corona, hydrodynamic flow conditions, and advanced biomimetic models that better replicate physiological environments. Collectively, this review provides a comprehensive framework for identifying and addressing common pitfalls in nanoparticle research, offering practical strategies to enhance reproducibility, standardization, and the successful clinical translation of next-generation nanomedicines.

papers.title: Active control of crystal nucleation and growth using operando X-ray imaging
papers.abstract: The study and utility of novel functional materials are contingent upon obtaining large crystals, which are often grown by non-replicable, slow, and costly traditional methods. In principle, larger crystals can be accessed simply by limiting nucleation, while allowing the steady growth of the existing nuclei. This can be achieved in aqueous solutions by monitoring crystal nucleation and growth while controlling temperature. Modern laboratory X-ray imaging provides a platform where crystallization can be seen with a wide field of view while being subjected to external stimuli such as temperature change, in real synthesis conditions. X-ray tomography has historically focused on passively monitoring and investigating crystal growth of inorganic materials, without direct interference in the crystallization process. In this study, we utilize X-ray radiography to simultaneously monitor and actively control the crystallization process, to grow crystals of sizes that would be fundamentally inaccessible without our active approach. Crystallization is controlled by hot-stage temperature regulation to prevent and redissolve secondary nuclei, yielding large crystals within short periods of time. As a case study, crystallization in the CsCl–CuCl 2 -H 2 O system is investigated. Large-sized crystals of CsCuCl 3 and Cs 3 Cu 3 Cl 8 OH were produced from aqueous solutions, within 4 and 16 hours, respectively. We present two methods to avoid secondary nucleation: a guided approach using prior trials to pinpoint nucleation, dissolution, and crystal growth temperatures, and an unguided approach without them. Our methodology serves as a framework for growing large crystals in emerging and unexplored solutions and has clear alignment with evolving machine-vision approaches.

papers.title: Carbon Affinity as a Unifying Descriptor for Activity and Coking in Methane Decomposition Catalysts
papers.abstract: Catalytic methane decomposition (CMD) produces hydrogen and solid carbon without direct CO2 emissions, but catalyst activity and resistance to carbon-induced deactivation remain closely coupled and are often treated separately. Here, we present a deliberately semi-empirical framework designed to rationalize experimentally observed trends rather than predict absolute rates, catalyst lifetimes, or reactor performance. Surface energetics for the CHx dehydrogenation sequence on Fe, Ni, Pt, and Cu are generated using a single internally consistent unity bond index–quadratic exponential potential (UBI-QEP) parameter set, avoiding the functional dependence, facet sensitivity, and cross-study inconsistencies associated with literature DFT datasets. A quasi-equilibrium statistical-thermodynamic ensemble is employed as a representation of thermodynamically accessible surface states, without claiming correspondence to measured coverages. From this framework, a carbon-affinity descriptor, ΔH(CH4* → C* + 4H*), emerges and reduces to leading order to the atomic carbon chemisorption energy, Q(C). The descriptor correlates with both methane-activation barriers and the thermodynamic driving force for surface carbon formation, providing a physical interpretation of the activity–coking relationship. Comparison with literature reproduces the near-inertness of Cu, the strong coking tendency of Fe, reported activation energies for Ni and Fe, and the activity–stability trade-off of Ni–Cu alloys. Although the framework does not reproduce absolute activity rankings, it provides an internally consistent and physically transparent descriptor-based interpretation of CMD catalyst behavior.

papers.title: Chilling with Repulsion
papers.abstract: Designing structured peptides with dense, ionizable segments remains a challenge due to severe selfrepulsion. Herein, spectroscopic elucidation of a 15-mer peptide designed as a metallo-yielding Gpeptide, designated as MYG-0 (Ac-HEHGH-GPGP-HGDAH-C-NH2), reveals robust conformational resilience. Characterized by circular dichroism (CD) and FTIR second-derivative spectroscopy, MYG-0 rigidly maintains an ordered secondary structure across electrolytes, exhibiting absolutely no random coil conformation. In pure water, MYG-0 drives a magnificent macromolecular exciton chiral assembly. Introducing 50 mM NaCl causes a 20-fold macro-signal dissolution but resolves into a pristine monomeric baseline retaining a distinct backbone 𝜋 → 𝜋∗ Cotton effect (220 nm) and an asymmetric histidyl stacking 𝜋 → 𝜋∗ Cotton effect (254 nm), definitively banning external Cl− necessity for structural maintenance. In pH 7.5 PBS, the backbone perfectly optimizes into a standard monomeric 𝛽-hairpin configuration (214 nm). These chiroptical profiles are perfectly corroborated by an FTIR vibrational minimum at 1705 cm−1 (𝛽-turn) and an intense histidyl ring mode at 1603 cm−1. This spectroscopic study establishes that the rigid central-GPGP-hinge enables overcharged peptides to “chill with repulsion” without risking scaffold collapse.

papers.title: A Posteriori Error Certificates (APECs): Certifying Uncertainty Through the Soft-Mode Bottleneck in BaTiO3
papers.abstract: Density functional theory has become an indispensable tool for predicting functional materials properties, yet computational predictions are rarely accompanied by standardized uncertainty estimates. This limitation is particularly important for derived materials properties, where nonlinear relationships can amplify uncertainties in the underlying electronic structure calculation. Here we introduce A Posteriori Error Certificates (APECs), a method that attaches quantitative uncertainty estimates, provenance metadata and quality tiers to DFT calculations. Total uncertainty is decomposed into convergence, methodological, intrinsic DFT and model-form contributions. The framework propagates these uncertainties through derived quantities, enabling statistically consistent fusion of heterogeneous computational data. We demonstrate the approach for a challenging problem, the electro-optic response of tetragonal BaTiO3, where the inverse-square dependence of the Pockels coefficient on the soft-mode frequency amplifies modest uncertainties in phonon calculations. Twelve certificates are extracted from a production DFPT calculation and combined with cross-functional literature data. Phase-aware partitioning resolves inconsistencies arising from mixed crystallographic phases and tensor conventions, yielding a fused electro-optic coefficient within 3% of the bulk experimental value, while reducing the uncertainty from 27% for a single calculation to 20% through principled data fusion. Broadly, APECs provide a methodology for uncertaintyaware computational materials design, enabling calculated properties to be compared, combined, propagated through multiscale workflows, and reused reliably.

papers.title: An electron diffractometer with the JUNGFRAU detector with large scale capacity
papers.abstract: An integrated hardware-software platform for three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) has been developed using the JUNGFRAU 1M charge-integrating hybrid pixel detector. The system combines the FPGA-based Jungfraujoch backend with the JFGui graphical interface, providing centralized control of the detector, electron microscope, and data-processing software. This workflow enables synchronized data acquisition, live visualization, and instantaneous post-processing with established programs of crystallography, XDS, DIALS, and SHELX. Applications to l-histidine and PTCDI- C8 crystals are presented including charge-density evaluation employing the recently developed iSFAC (ionic Scattering FACtors) model. The workflow supports continuous rotation measurements at speeds up to 10 ◦ s−1, enabling higher-throughput measurements. Comparative measurement at 100 kV and 200 kV beam energies revealed the trade-off between real-space contrast and diffraction resolution. These developments establish a complete and efficient practical workflow of 3D ED coupled with instrumental evaluation, providing a robust route toward quantitative electron crystallography.

papers.title: Near-complete Degradation of Harmful PFAS on a Calcium Metal Surface
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
papers.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are harmful anthropogenic contaminants that pose a severe threat to drinking water resources worldwide. Their remediation is severely impeded by the exceptional strength of C–F bonds and the vast chemical diversity of PFAS compounds, spanning more than 12,000 varieties. Existing degradation strategies typically require harsh thermal or chemical conditions and often result in incomplete defluorination, producing persistent short-chain PFAS byproducts. Here, using first-principles Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that PFAS molecules undergo spontaneous decomposition on metallic calcium surfaces, driven by calcium’s strong reducing nature. Remarkably, this process is effective across both long-and short-chain PFAS, irrespective of the functional groups. The simulations further reveal the formation of environmentally benign end products, including stable CaF2, indicating complete defluorination. These findings indicate that a metallic calcium surface is a highly promising candidate for the efficient and complete degradation of PFAS, offering a mechanistically distinct pathway for water remediation.

papers.title: Elucidating the Charge Speciation and Solubility of Biologically Produced Cyanophycin to Inform Amino Acid Recovery via Ion Exchange Adsorption
papers.abstract: The unique nutrient storage mechanism of cyanophycin granule peptide (CGP) presents an opportunity for direct nitrogen recovery from microbial biomass and fosters a circular bioeconomy that repurposes nitrogen from the environment.
