However, efficient recovery of cyanophycin and its constituent amino acids via ion exchange adsorption is hampered by limited understanding of how polymer composition, charge behavior, and morphology influence solubility and separations. To elucidate these unknowns, we integrate experimental characterization with electrostatic modeling to describe the pH-dependent adsorption behavior of insoluble and lysine-containing soluble cyanophycin variants. Adsorption experiments demonstrated that amino acid recovery efficiencies are strongly governed by electrostatic interactions, with enhanced uptake occurring under conditions of high net polymer charge. Together, these results establish a mechanistic framework that links CGP composition, charge characteristics, and solubility to separation performance, enabling targeted design of ion exchange processes for nitrogen recovery from biologically produced polymers.

papers.title: When Are Two-Dimensional Covalent-Organic Frameworks Good Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries? A Data-Driven Analysis
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium-ion batteries. Despite more than a decade of research, existing heuristics for designing electroactive COFs lack generality and the suitability of these materials as alternatives to conventional inorganic electrode remain poorly resolved. Here, we map structure–electrode–function relationships across 1099 experimentally synthesized 2D COFs from the CoRE COF database by developing a data-driven framework integrating density-functional theory computations with machine learning models and establish atomic-level design rules governing electrode behavior. We uncover that cathode-like character originates from dense, multidentate nitrogen and oxygen rich coordination pockets at pore walls, characteristic of imide cores, acylhydrazones, keto–amine linkages, and π-macrocycles, whereas anode-like behavior is encoded by spatially separated redox sites and open π-rich interlayer galleries that sustain weak, reversible Li+ intercalation. Sequential voltage, capacity, and conductivity-based screening across the database yields 14 anode and 14 cathode candidates. We show that the known chemical space of 2D COFs cannot outperform inorganic electrodes in terms of operating voltages. However, strategic pairing of 2D anode|cathode pairs within an all-organic lithium battery architecture delivers full-cell voltages exceeding 2 V with capacities above 200 mAh/g on both electrodes, surpassing small organic molecules and polymer counterparts. The screening framework presented here is transferable to other metal-ion chemistries and framework families, laying a robust foundation for accelerating next-generation organic electrode discovery.

papers.title: Efficient, Black-Box Estimation of Reaction Paths via Redundant Internal Coordinate Interpolation
papers.abstract: Reaction path interpolation is a fundamental task in computational chemistry, both as a stand-alone estimation of a reaction profile and to provide initial guesses for transition state and minimum-energy path optimization methods. We present an efficient black-box method that generates chemically meaningful paths by linearly interpolating in redundant internal coordinates (RICs) and transforming each image independently to Cartesian coordinates. This embarrassingly parallel formulation enables highly efficient path generation, making the method particularly attractive for high-throughput applications. The central obstacle in this context is the back-transformation from RICs to Cartesian coordinates, which is non-trivial for the large displacements encountered along a reaction path. Implemented in the open-source Python package chemcoord, our approach robustly handles the coordinate transformation, collinearity, bond breaking and formation, and other challenging edge cases. We benchmarked against established path generation methods, namely geodesic, image-dependent pair potential (IDPP), and Z-matrix interpolation, measuring the path integral of the energy along the reaction coordinate. Our method yields paths of higher quality than Z-matrix or IDPP interpolation and of similar quality to geodesic interpolation, while offering substantially lower computational cost.

papers.title: Competing Chemisorption and Physisorption of CO2 in Halide-Functionalized Zirconium MOFs
papers.abstract: By removing formate capping ligands from the zirconium nodes of NU-1000, a version of the metal-organic framework NU-1000 was generated having nodes terminated with hydroxo/aqua ligand pairs. Unexpectedly, this material can adsorb CO2 at low pressure through chemisorption. In-situ DRIFT spectroscopy and computational studies show that CO2 chemisorption proceeds through reaction with hydroxo ligands to form bicarbonate species. We demonstrate that this chemisorption extends to MOF-841 when it bears equivalent nonstructural ligands. Post-synthetic functionalization with second-sphere halide ions suppresses chemisorption through protonation of the hydroxo ligands, while simultaneously enhancing physisorption following the trend chloride > bromide > iodide. These results illustrate the pivotal role of node functionalization in governing CO2 adsorption in Zr-MOFs.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Acyl Anion Equivalents from Carboxylic Acids via Acylsulfonylhydrazides: A Practical Organocatalytic Umpolung
papers.abstract: The development of mild and practical acyl anion equivalents remains a cornerstone challenge in modern organic synthesis, as traditional umpolung strategies often rely on moisture-sensitive reagents, strong bases, or specialized N-heterocyclic carbene catalysts. Here we report that readily available N,N-acylsulfonylhydrazides serve as efficient acyl anion surrogates under operationally simple organocatalytic conditions. Using DMAP as a nucleophilic catalyst, these stable hydrazide precursors readily provide acylation products of a wide range of carbon electrophiles, including aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, activated ketones, olefins, and imines. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations and HRMS analysis, reveal an unconventional pathway wherein DMAP adds to the acyldiazene intermediate, triggering nitrogen extrusion and generating a zwitterionic nucleophile. This dual role of DMAP in enhancing both the stability and nucleophilicity of the reactive species circumvents the hydroxycarbene rearrangement pathway, offering a practical and scalable alternative to existing acyl anion methodologies.

papers.title: Ferrielectric Quasiracemic Crystals Engineered from Enantiopolar Racemates
papers.abstract: Ferrielectrics, materials with partly switchable polarization, enable functional responses such as pyroelectricity and piezoelectricity. However, purely organic examples and general design strategies remain scarce. Here we show that quasiracemates (QR), derived from enantiopolar centrosymmetric racemates, provide a generalizable route to organic ferrielectrics. In these structures, quasi-enantiomers assemble into antiparallel polar ribbons that reveal the hidden polarization of the parent racemate. When one quasi-enantiomer bears acidic protons capable of forming hydrogen bonds, a bistable double-well potential may emerges, enabling ferrielectric switching. Guided by this principle, we design ferrielectric QR composed of N-Ac-R-Val and N-Ac-S-Thr (P21). The crystals display ferrielectricity along with a large pyroelectric coefficient around 4*10^-9 (C/(K*cm^2) and a modest piezoelectric response (d22 around 2.75pm/V). The macroscopic polarization and polar properties are tunable by varying the N-Ac-S-Thr concentration.

papers.title: Catalyst-controlled divergent strain-release amination and skeletal
High pressure synthesis for gold-backboned polymer
An Integrated CREATE Method for Teaching Polymer Synthesis
papers.abstract: Teaching polymer chemistry in the undergraduate and graduate chemistry curricula is important to prepare students for the demands of the modern chemical workforce. Validated and inquiryguided teaching strategies for these topics, however, remain scarce. We implemented an integrated CREATE (Consider, Read, Elucidate the hypothesis, Analyze and interpret data, Think of the next Experiment) approach within a combined junior/senior-undergraduate and first-year graduate Polymer Synthesis course to teach modern polymerization concepts while developing scientific literacy and professional self-confidence. The integrated approach incorporated six CREATE sessions throughout a semester long course that introduced key course content through the analysis of primary literature. Data was gathered over five years (2019-2023), yielding 107 paired survey responses from 136 enrolled students. Using the CREATE method, students demonstrated significant improvements in confidence reading primary literature and large effect sizes across all nine assessed CREATE skills, with the strongest gains in decoding literature, interpreting data, and active reading. Notably, learning outcome improvements were observed across all demographic groups, including education level, gender, and prior research experience, with students having no research experience showing the largest gains. One semester of integrated CREATE exercises produced confidence improvements comparable to two semesters of traditional laboratory research experience. Coding of two open-ended survey questions demonstrated that students perceived the CREATE method to be simultaneously challenging and rewarding. These results demonstrate that the integrated CREATE approach effectively delivers complex content knowledge while significantly enhancing students' learning outcomes, offering a scalable model for advanced chemistry courses.

papers.title: Comparing Symmetry-Adapted Perturbation Theory to Intermolecular Energy Decomposition Analysis Based on Absolutely Localized Molecular Orbitals
papers.abstract: Energy decomposition analysis (EDA) can provide insight into the nature of noncovalent interactions, even though individual energy components are not uniquely defined by quantum mechanics. The present work examines the two titular EDA schemes and elucidates the degree of transferability between their energy components. We first demonstrate that a low-cost, atoms-in-molecules manybody dispersion (MBD) model can effectively replace the conventional, perturbative definition of dispersion in symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT). As compared to high-level ab initio benchmarks, the resulting SAPT + MBD approach affords high accuracy for both small dimer and larger biomolecular fragments taken from ligand–protein complexes. Individual SAPT + MBD energy components exhibit good correlation with those computed using the absolutely localized molecular orbital (ALMO) EDA scheme, the latter of which is built around density functional theory. Quantitative differences between the energy components can be substantial, however, except in the case of electrostatic interactions that are defined in the same manner in both schemes. These conclusions hold across a range of density functionals used in ALMO-EDA calculations, and for different choices of the “dispersionless” functional that is used to isolate the dispersion energy from the target-functional interaction energy in ALMO-EDA calculations. The present work provides calibration plots to translate between SAPT + MBD and ALMO-EDA energy components. For a large data set of biomolecular fragments, SAPT + MBD calculations afford better agreement with ab initio benchmarks as compared to calculations using the state-of-the-art ωB97M-V functional, especially when triple-ζ basis sets are used for SAPT.

papers.title: Prospect to Boost Catalytic Activity of Precious Metals by Adsorption Atop Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: We use first principles calculations and chemical bonding analysis to investigate how the adsorption on topological insulators modifies the chemical properties of thin films of catalytic metals, Pt, Au, and Ag. Topological surface states (TSS) present at the Fermi level and coinciding with the physical termination of the topological insulators are found to interact with the metal monolayers, and themselves become modified by the adhesion, particularly in the case of relatively stronger Pt adhesion. The properties of the monolayers are in turn affected by the interaction with TSS. Specifically, the adsorption strengths of the typical catalytic intermediates exhibit important shifts that can lead to enhanced catalytic reactivity. H is an adsorbate present in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and thermal dehydrogenation, and its adsorption energy is often used as a descriptor of the activity. The bonding to the supported Pt film is slightly weaker than that to the Pt metal, due to TSS involvement. This is expected to place the system closer to the apex of the catalytic volcano for HER than Pt itself. The adsorption of CO on Au and Ag is, in contrast, strengthened by TSS, potentially opening an opportunity to electrochemically reduce CO-a process not achieved by bulk Au or Ag electrodes. We note that all interactions with the TSS play a perturbative role in binding. The metals provide electronic states deep below the Fermi level, facilitating the bonding mechanisms notorious for these adsorbates on the corresponding metals. TSS supply additional bonding and/or antibonding effects that are relatively weak, but likely consequential for catalysis.

papers.title: Machine learning approaches to predicting metal catalyst performance in olefin polymerization
papers.abstract: Olefin polymerization is a cornerstone of the modern chemical industry, and the development of high-performance metal catalysts is essential for controlling polymer microstructure and properties. Traditionally, catalyst optimization has relied on resource-intensive experimental screening. However, the past decade has seen the emergence of machine learning as a transformative tool for identifying non-linear patterns in highdimensional datasets and accelerating catalyst discovery. This review discusses recent efforts in applying supervised, unsupervised, and active learning methods to metal-catalyzed olefin polymerization. We examine the development of molecular descriptors—both manually crafted from density functional theory and learned through graph neural networks—and outline typical workflows for data curation, model selection, and interpretability using tools like Shapley additive explanations. Key applications are highlighted across ethylene and propylene homopolymerization, oligomerization, and copolymerization with polar monomers, demonstrating how machine learning can predict catalytic activity, molecular weight, and selectivity while providing mechanistic insights. Finally, we discuss the current challenges and future opportunities for data-driven catalysis research.

papers.title: Single-Atom Fe–N4 Sites Anchored on Hierarchical COF/g-C3N4 Heterostructures for Ultrabroadband Solar CO2 Photoreduction and Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: The development of efficient photocatalysts capable of simultaneously converting carbon dioxide into valuable carbon-neutral fuels while producing hydrogen remains a major challenge in solar energy conversion. Herein, we report a novel hierarchical Fe–N4/COF/g-C3N4 heterostructure featuring atomically dispersed Fe catalytic centers anchored within a nitrogen-rich covalent organic framework (COF) coupled with exfoliated graphitic carbon nitride nanosheets. The catalyst was synthesized through a sequential in situ COF growth and Fe coordination strategy followed by controlled thermal stabilization, resulting in highly dispersed Fe–N4 active sites and a robust Z-scheme photocatalytic architecture. Structural characterization by XRD, FTIR, XPS, BET, and aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirmed successful formation of crystalline COF domains, intimate COF/g-C3N4 interfacial contact, and isolated Fe–N4 coordination environments. The hierarchical architecture exhibited a high specific surface area of 486 m2 g-1 and strong optical absorption extending from the ultraviolet region into the near-infrared spectrum (400–850 nm). Compared with pristine g-C3N4, the Fe–N4/COF/g-C3N4 heterostructure displayed significantly reduced photoluminescence intensity, enhanced photocurrent response, and lower charge-transfer resistance, indicating highly efficient charge separation and migration. Under simulated AM 1.5G solar irradiation, the optimized photocatalyst achieved CO evolution and H2 production rates of 312 and 1280 μmol g-1 h-1, respectively, which were approximately 7.5 and 9.3 times higher than those of pristine g-C3N4. Furthermore, the catalyst retained over 92% of its initial activity after ten consecutive reaction cycles. The superior photocatalytic performance is attributed to the synergistic integration of atomically dispersed Fe–N4 catalytic centers, hierarchical COF nanochannels, ultrabroadband light harvesting, and direct Z-scheme charge transfer. This work establishes a new strategy for constructing next-generation single-atom photocatalysts for integrated solar fuel generation.

papers.title: Field-Driven Proton Transport in Water Revealed by Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Grotthuss diffusion has been extensively studied, its response to strong electric fields remains difficult to access because simulations must simultaneously describe bond breaking/forming and induced polarization over a sufficiently long time-scale. Here, we develop a reactive and polarizable machine-learning interatomic potential for molecular dynamics simulations of the hydrated excess proton in water. A zero-field PiNet2-ft model first establishes an equilibrium reference for structure and diffusion. We then introduce a finite-field coupling using the AD(OS) model, enabling non-equilibrium molecular dynamics under an applied electric field E. In the linear-response regime (E < 0.04 V/Å), the drift-velocity-derived proton mobility is shown to be in excellent agreement with the equilibrium proton diffusion coefficient. Surprisingly, this linear relation between the drift velocity and the field strength persists up to a strong field of 0.15 V/Å. By analyzing the free-energy landscape of the PT reaction, we show that a new reaction channel is opened at high field strength, which facilitates fast PT. This behavior is further enabled by the distinct response of protonated water system, where the water network shows no comparable dielectric-saturation signature and largely preserves its structural fluctuations and mobility under strong fields.

papers.title: Versatile Multi-Stimuli and Rotatable Sample Environments for In Situ and In Operando High-Temperature Small- and Wide-Angle Scattering Studies at Synchrotron Beamlines
papers.abstract: Driven by the growing demand for in situ and in operando investigations of structural transformations under complex stimuli, we present versatile and compact sample environments developed for synchrotron-based small-angle and wide-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS/WAXS) experiments. The setups combine multi-parameter control, enabling simultaneous control of temperature (up to 1000 °C), gas atmosphere, light irradiation, and nearly 360° sample rotation. These capabilities facilitate real-time monitoring of nanoscale processes, including nanoparticle exsolution in perovskites and phase transitions of confined liquid crystals under UV illumination. The integration of multi-parameter controls within compact and modular cells overcomes significant technical challenges, expanding experimental capabilities at the P62 beamline of PETRA III. Our developments provide a versatile platform for investigating stimuli-responsive materials under realistic conditions, enhancing understanding of structure–property relationships and informing the design of advanced functional materials across catalysis, energy storage, and soft matter physics.

papers.title: A Literature-Derived Dataset and Data-Driven Screening Tool for CO2-to-Methanol Heterogeneous Catalysts
papers.abstract: CO2 hydrogenation to methanol is widely studied as a route to chemical CO2 utilization, but reported catalyst performance is scattered across hundreds of publications using different metal–support combinations, loadings, and operating conditions, making cross-study comparison difficult. We compiled a structured dataset of 1,339 experimental data points from 57 peer-reviewed studies (2015–2023), covering 31 base metals and 45 supports under operating temperatures of 150–400 °C, pressures of 1–150 bar, and H2/CO2 ratios of 1–9.1. Using a subset of 761 complete records, we trained an ordinary-least-squares regression on one-hot encoded catalyst identity (base metal, support) and the three operating variables to screen a 17 base × 27 support full-factorial grid (459 combinations) at fixed reference conditions (250 °C, 30 bar, H2/CO2 = 3). Five-fold cross-validation gives a mean R2 of 0.41 (± 0.24) and a mean absolute error of 3.3 percentage points — a single favorable train/test split can yield R2 as high as 0.84, which we show is not representative of the model's general performance. Only 68 of the 459 screened combinations (15%) correspond to a base–support pair actually present in the source literature; the remaining 391 are model extrapolations to untested compositions. We release the dataset, model code, and an interactive screening dashboard, and report these limitations explicitly so that ranked candidates are used as hypotheses for experimental follow-up rather than as validated performance claims.

papers.title: Bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide anion decomposition initiated by the Solid Electrolyte Interphase
papers.abstract: Lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) is widely regarded as the leading salt for stabilizing lithium metal anodes, owing to the formation of an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and enabling Coulombic efficiencies (CE) >99.5%. Here, we identify sulfur–fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry as a previously unrecognized pathway governing the stability of FSI under cycling and aging conditions. We show that O-nucleophiles abundant at the lithium surface, including Li2O and lithium alkoxides, react with FSI to produce bis(sulfonato)imide derivatives, establishing a self-driven SEI degradation pathway. Through a detailed kinetic and crystallographic study, we isolate critical SuFEx intermediates and identify their chemical fingerprints in SEI layers. We demonstrate that methoxide-substituted FSI anions are particularly detrimental: being soluble and reduced at potentials less cathodic than FSI, they alter the SEI formation mechanism and decrease CE. These findings reframe electrolyte design strategies and suggest that suppressing SuFEx reactivity is essential for achieving sustained CE >99.9%.

papers.title: Stereodivergent Csp3–Csp3 Bond Construction via Lewis base/Iridium Cooperative Catalysis: A Modular Synthesis of Tertiary Fluoride-containing Stereodiads.
papers.abstract: The synthesis of tertiary fluoride-containing stereogenic centers remains a significant challenge. This is challenge is amplified when such units are embedded within vicinal stereocenters arrays, where both absolute and relative stereochemistry must be controlled. Here we disclose a stereodivergent Lewis base–iridium cooperative catalysis method that unites a-fluorinated C1-ammonium enolate and p(allyl)Ir intermediates to construct tertiary fluoride-containing stereodiads. Each catalyst is independently responsible for the configurational outcome of each stereocenter comprising the stereodiad during Csp3–Csp3 bond construction. Noteworthy is the conversion of easily prepared racemic a-fluoro esters to single a-fluoro C1-ammonium enolates via Lewis base catalysis.

papers.title: Do Chemically Modified Oligonucleotide Therapeutics Require Environmental Risk Assessment?
Differential Coats-Redfern Analysis for Thermolysis of Carbon-Relevant Polymers
papers.abstract: Thermolysis of plastic waste is increasingly explored both as an end-of-life route and as a precursor step for producing carbonaceous materials, but most thermogravimetric (TG) data for polymers are collected under single heating rates with limited data resolution and are not optimized for kinetic analysis. In this study, we use the recently developed differential Coats–Redfern (d-CR) framework to extract conversion-resolved kinetic information from open-source TG curves of eight technologically important polymers (PP, PS, PET, PMMA, PC, PA, PUR, PTFE) recorded at 10 °C·min⁻¹. Classical Coats–Redfern (CR) analysis of these single-rate datasets yields curved ln[g(α)/T²] versus 1/T plots and conversion-averaged activation parameters that can misrepresent the underlying degradation behavior. In contrast, d-CR converts the same thermogravimetry into conversion-resolved Eₐ(α) and ln A(α), while rate-parity and conversion-variant compensation tests for an effective mechanistic model selection. The resulting profiles reveal systematic differences in thermolysis energy demand between commodity and engineering polymers and provide a kinetic baseline for assessing whether catalytic routes genuinely reduce process severity in plastic recycling schemes from future works.

papers.title: Assessing cell survival and biosignature preservation of the extremely thermoacidophilic archaeon Acidianus manzaensis after exposure to Mars-like conditions
papers.abstract: Considering the harsh surface conditions on Mars, terrestrial organisms that can survive and remain detectable after exposure to similar conditions provide invaluable models for guiding current and future search-for-life missions. To this end, we evaluated the extremophilic archaeon Acidianus manzaensis grown on ESA01-E Mars analog material as a model organism. We exposed cell-mineral mixtures to one month of desiccation and two weeks of Mars-like conditions in a Mars simulation chamber to evaluate the potential for cell survival after exposure to these conditions. In the search for reliable biomarkers in other planetary environments, such as Mars, molecules that are stable over geological timescales while preserving information indicative of their potential biological origin are crucial. Thiophene-bearing quinones fulfill these requirements, and thiophenes, which are their basic moieties, have been discovered on Mars. Therefore, we analyzed the thiophene-bearing quinone composition of A. manzaensis using mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and discussed potential molecular alterations. Successful re-cultivation after one month of desiccation and two weeks of exposure to Mars-like conditions proved the durability of the organism and its capability for cell recovery after exposure to extreme conditions, paving the way for further investigation.

papers.title: A linear relationship linking the aggregated isotopic moments of a molecular formula to those of its constituent elements
papers.abstract: It has long been recognized that the isotope patterns of unknown analytes provide valuable information that facilitates the determination of their molecular formulas in mass spectrometry experiments. It is primarily the combined abundances of isotopic variants aggregated by the number of nucleons, as well as the associated aggregated masses that have been used for this purpose. However, there is additional information in the higher moments or alternatively in the higher cumulants of the aggregated isotope patterns, which is rarely exploited. This article demonstrates that a transformation can be applied to the aggregated isotopic moments of a molecular formula such that the result can be expressed as a linear combination of the correspondingly transformed isotopic moments of the formula’s constituent elements. This relationship can be used to quickly calculate the aggregated isotopic moments and cumulants of molecular formulas, and it also provides a starting point for more efficiently addressing the inverse problem of determining a molecular formula on the basis of an observed isotope pattern.

papers.title: Accurate Molecular Properties via Bootstrap Embedding
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the utility of back-transformed bootstrap embedding (BE) one- and two-particle density matrices (1 and 2-PDMs) by computing dipole moments and force gradients for several polar systems. The resulting mean absolute error in atomic force gradients at BE2/CCSD is approximately 0.003 a.u./bohr even in most polar and strained environments. We refer to this approach for generating molecular properties as Bootstrap Embedding – Direct Matrices (BE‑DM). This efficient evaluation of dipole moments and atomic force gradients holds significant promise for machine learning applications, where coupled-cluster-level forces can substantially enhance the quality of machine-learned potentials.

papers.title: Catalytic Desymmetrization Unlocks Enantioselective Access to Chiral Triptycene Scaffolds
papers.abstract: Chiral triptycene frameworks with intrinsic three-dimensional rigidity constitute versatile building blocks for asymmetric catalysis and circularly polarized luminescence materials, yet catalytic highly enantioselective routes toward their asymmetric construction remain underexplored. Herein, we report an N -heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed desymmetrizing acylation of triptycenyl diphenols via acylative functionalization with diverse aldehydes, furnishing enantioenriched chiral triptycene derivatives. Mechanistic control experiments unveiled that the initial acylation event serves as the stereo-differentiating step, while the secondary acylation only marginally influences the observed enantioselectivity. Kinetic profiling identifies the formal first-order kinetics with respect to PhCHO, NHC catalyst, while the higher loading of triptycenyl diphenol proved detrimental to the reaction rate. This desymmetrization strategy enables facile access to diversely functionalized chiral triptycene synthons, offering a practical platform for advancing chiral material synthesis and asymmetric catalytic methodology.

papers.title: RETRACTED: Pulsed selectivity programming of photothermal CO2 hydrogenation
papers.abstract: Retracted at the authors' request because a recently discovered experimental artefact renders the conclusions unreliable. Pulsed optical excitation is an emerging strategy to control heterogeneous catalysis beyond steady-state operation. Here, we compare photothermal CO₂ hydrogenation over Ru/SrTiO₃ under 1064 nm pulsed and continuous-wave illumination, without any auxiliary heat source. At identical average intensity, nanosecond pulsed irradiation markedly enhances catalytic activity, affording up to 19-fold higher CO₂ conversion, together with maximum production-rate enhancements of approximately 27-fold for CO and 19-fold for CH₄. Meanwhile, the photon-to-product quantum efficiency improved from 0.03% for continuous-wave to 0.7% for pulsed illumination, representing a 23-fold enhancement. Further, tuning the effective pulse-duration from 161 to 95 ns, at constant pulse energy, reversibly switches the dominant product between CH₄ and CO. Using IR imaging and thermal modeling, we trace the mechanistic origin to both a high peak temperature and the heterogeneous microstructure of the catalyst solid. Overall, we demonstrate that pulsed irradiation accesses an activity-selectivity operational space distinct from continuous heating, and that the temporal structure of light delivery provides a route to dynamically program catalytic performance.

papers.title: Plasticize me sweetly: sugar-based plasticizers for poly(lactic acid)
papers.abstract: Carbohydrates are among the most abundant biopolymers in the world and offer a promising source for the synthesis of value-added chemicals. Galactaric acid is an attractive bio-based building block that has not yet been fully exploited. Currently, regulatory, sustainability, safety-by-design and performance requirements for polymer additives are becoming increasingly strict. As a result, innovation in this field must be accelerated to develop new materials with enhanced properties. With this objective, new sugar-based plasticizers based on galactaric acid have been synthesised. Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) was selected as a brittle, bio-based polymer, to evaluate the ability of these additives to improve its mechanical properties. The best additive led to an increase of the elongation at break up to 260% when compared to the starting PLA. Experimental results have been supported by computational studies and show how small modifications in the molecular structure can influence both the synthesis and the performance of these additives.

papers.title: From Fluorine to Iodine: Halogen Effects on Fluorescein Emission
papers.abstract: Despite the fact that fluorescein probes are widely used in clinical diagnostics, including ophthalmology and gastrointestinal endoscopy, they continue to attract considerable scientific interest across diverse research areas, from fluorescein‑based voltage indicators and fluorogenic cancer biomarkers to modern organic photoredox catalysis. Although the effects of fluorination on fluorescein and the heavy‑atom influence on its emission properties have been examined separately in numerous studies, here we systematically investigate the complete fluorine‑to‑iodine substitution series within a single, structurally unified fluorescein scaffold. In the first part, the work focuses on synthesis of a series of disodium salts differing in substitution on the xanthene core. We then quantify their fluorescent and photochemical properties, including the photodegradation quantum yields, a parameter not previously reported for this dye family. And finally, we construct a FRET‑based dithienylethene-tetrachlorofluorescein photoswitching dyad, characterize its photochromic behaviour, and demonstrate its potential for anti‑counterfeiting applications.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-empowered biochar engineering: From design fundamentals to commercialization
papers.abstract: Engineered biochar is a promising carbon material for sustainable energy and environmental applications, yet its transition from laboratory-scale synthesis to commercial deployment remains constrained. Current developments largely relies on trial-and-error and heuristics-based approaches, making it difficult to establish synthesis-structure-performance relationships and posing reproducibility challenges across scales and locations. Recent years we have witnessed the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to navigate this complex design space. In this Perspective, we describe the landscape of this rapidly evolving field, including engineered biochars’ property prediction, metal/metalloid and organic pollutant adsorption, soil and agronomics, and functional- and catalysis‑based applications. Our critical assessment reveals that, AI methods are predominantly employed for predictive modeling, while experimental validation and data-guided engineered biochar design remain significantly underexplored (<5% of total studies). To address this concerning gap, we propose five actionable directions: (1) automated extraction of published data using large language models (LLMs), (2) analysis of complex multivariable interactions with supervised learning, (3) designing biochar with target properties through active learning, (4) augmenting characterization techniques with deep learning, and (5) automation of biochar production. We highlight methodological frontiers and opportunities for knowledge transfer among biochar technologies. Collectively, these directions outline a holistic AI-driven ecosystem for biochar science, enabling scalable translation from laboratory discovery to industrial deployment.

papers.title: Mineral-controlled heat-stiffening in dynamically crosslinked polymer networks
papers.abstract: Dynamically crosslinked polymer networks are an important class of soft matter increasingly applied in several fields ranging from wearable electronics to biomedical applications in large part due to their useful stimuli-responsive behavior. However, these materials typically soften with increasing temperatures. Here we report a series of dynamically crosslinked mineral-polymer networks that exhibit a rare phenomenon of reversible heat-induced stiffening. Specifically, mineral-polymer networks assembled in water via in situ growth of mineral nanoparticles composed of CaCO3, MnCO3 or CoCO3, display increasing modulus, decreasing dissipation and slower stress relaxation with increasing temperatures to a degree that is strongly correlated with the nature of the in situ grown mineral nanoparticles. Additional evidence suggests that this mineral-controlled heat-stiffening behavior is driven by entropy-dominated thermodynamics associated with internal water rearrangements causing rigidification of the loadbearing mineral-polymer interfaces within the networks. The dynamically crosslinked mineral-polymer nanocomposites presented in this work provide a promising platform for the design and investigation of soft materials with thermo-mechanical properties dominated by entropy rather than enthalpy.

papers.title: Synthesis of C2-SF4-Indoles in presence of Blue LED.
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for fluorinated motifs beyond conventional PFAS-related CF3 and CF2 groups has stimulated interest in sulfur–fluorine-based alternatives. Herein, we report a blue LED-promoted one-pot synthesis of previously unknown Ar-SF4-linked indoles through a radical addition/cyclization sequence using aryl(heteroaryl)-SF4Cl reagents and N-(2-ethynylphenyl)sulfonamides. The method provides efficient access to a variety of pyridyl- and aryl-SF4-containing indoles under mild conditions. Notably, the photochemical protocol proved more effective than the Et3B/O2 conditions previously employed for related SF5 chemistry, highlighting the distinct reactivity of SF4Cl reagents. This work expands the synthetic utility of the SF4 motif and provides access to SF4-linked heteroaromatic architectures of potential interest as next-generation fluorinated molecular scaffolds.

papers.title: MOFEvolve: Literature-Driven Evolution of Experimental MOFs
papers.abstract: The discovery of functional metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) requires computational workflows that can rapidly convert newly reported experimental knowledge into actionable design hypotheses. However, existing MOF discovery pipelines often rely on static structure databases and do not fully utilize the design rationale described in experimental literature. Here, we present MOFEvolve, an automated framework for literature-driven derivative design of experimental MOFs. MOFEvolve collects MOF articles and crystallographic information files, then uses large language models to extract target-property context and MOF-specific component information and to curate parent crystal structures. From these parents, it generates derivative candidates through target-property-guided metal substitution, site-selective metal doping, and linker functionalization, each guided by the target property. The selected transformations are applied directly to curated parent CIFs to produce computation-ready derivative structures. We evaluate MOFEvolve using retrospective derivative-recovery benchmarks based on experimentally realized MOF modifications. The framework recovers 46.2% of temporal cases, where derivatives were reported in later independent publications, and 68.6% of contextual cases, where parent-side design context was available in the same publication, roughly doubling a random-selection baseline in both settings. These results show that literature-derived design information can enrich plausible derivative candidates and provide a scalable route for evolving experimental MOFs into computation-ready derivative structures for materials discovery.

papers.title: Staphylococcus FtsZ interfaces targeted by membrane-permeable BoltzGen cyclic-minipeptides
papers.abstract: BoltzGen, Prodigy, Cyclops and PyMol/Python combinations computationally predicted permeable cyclic-minipeptides targeting intracellular cell-division FtsZ filaments of Staphylococcus aureus, one of the most important antibiotic-resistant Gram-positive bacterial human pathogens. In particular, this work targeted a downsized-FtsZαß dimer-interface model with cyclic-minipeptides. Except rank621, however all predicted cyclic-minipeptide membrane-permeabilities were low, despite their picoMolar affinities tops. Therefore, a novel PyMol/Python script-strategy was successfully developed to generate thousands of mutated rank621-derived sequences to select optimal affinities and permeabilities preserving similar downsized-FtsZαß targets. Permeable cyclic-minipeptides not only predict higher resistance to exoprotease degradation, high conformer stability, and easy chemical synthesis, but also higher resistance to resistant single-mutations. Developed Google-Colab ipynb notebooks and PyMol/Python scripts are included as AdditionalFiles for experimentally-guided additional explorations.

papers.title: Mechanism of C–H Activation/Amination by Paddle-Wheel Diruthenium Catalyst: Multireference Insight and Comparison with Dirhodium
papers.abstract: Highly accurate multireference electronic-structure calculations elucidated the detailed mechanism of paddle-wheel dinuclear Ru-catalyzed C–H activation/amination. The reaction proceeds through a stepwise pathway consisting of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) from the allylic carbon to the nitrene nitrogen, followed by C–N bond formation. Multireference descriptions uncovered significant radical contributions in the nitrenoid intermediate, rationalizing the HAT character of the C–H activation step. They further revealed that the C–N bond formation proceeds through single-electron transfer from the allylic carbon radical into the empty Ru-π∗ orbital. Remarkably, the analogous dirhodium system was also found to follow the same stepwise HAT mechanism rather than the concerted hydride-transfer pathway suggested by previous single-reference density functional theory studies.

papers.title: sorbaMOF DB: An Extensible MOF Adsorption Database Platform with a Case Study on Direct Air Capture of CO2
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into materials discovery is increasingly constrained by the quality and reliability of underlying datasets. This challenge is particularly critical for adsorption in Metal–Organic Frameworks (MOFs), where structural inconsistencies in widely used databases and the choice of force fields and charge models can strongly affect the reliability of predicted adsorption properties. Here, we introduce sorbaMOF DB, a general and extensible reliable MOF adsorption database. As a first implementation, we present a CO2 adsorption dataset under direct air capture (DAC) conditions (400 ppm, 298 K), addressing a key gap in both experimental and computational resources. Starting from a consolidated set of ~240,000 MOF structures, we apply rigorous structural validation to ensure simulation readiness. High-throughput screening is then performed using a MOF–CO2 interaction protocol established through systematic benchmarking of force fields and partial charge schemes against high-quality density functional theory reference calculations. Our results further highlight the role of framework flexibility in improving prediction fidelity and quantify the impact of water adsorption under DAC-relevant conditions. Beyond adsorption database construction, this platform delivers a machine learning framework coupled with SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to extract interpretable structure–property relationships governing DAC performance.

papers.title: Transitioning from glassware to plasticware in an industrial analytical laboratory following a laceration incident : A case study
papers.abstract: Glassware-related lacerations are the most frequent category of injury in chemistry laboratories. Despite this, manual dishwashing, a daily routine step in every analytical laboratory, is virtually absent from safety literature as a distinct risk context. Here, we report a case study from an incident at the quality control laboratory of Saipol (Groupe Avril), a major European oilseed processing company, where a laboratory technician sustained a hand laceration requiring three sutures following the breakage of a glass beaker during post-analytical rinsing. Internally, glass cuts were identified as the most frequent accident type across Groupe Avril laboratories over the past ten years. The technician was wearing laboratory gloves at the time of the incident, revealing the insufficiency of personal protective equipment alone as a risk control strategy. A root cause analysis identified two contributing factors: water accumulation on the outer surface of the beaker reducing grip, and an instinctive catch reflex that forced the technician’s hand against the shattering glass. Following the NIOSH hierarchy of controls, a material substitution program was then implemented. A glassware use inventory (~300 items/week) and a chemical compatibility assessment revealed that over 50% of glass items used mainly for titrimetric applications could be substituted with plastic equivalents (like PETG, PP, and PMP/TPX). Comparative analyses confirmed no measurable analytical interference from the newly introduced PETG vessels. Consequently, the substitution achieved a 30% reduction in glassware usage across the facility for the two past years. This case study provides a transferable framework (inventory, compatibility evaluation, material selection, analytical validation, and implementation) for industrial analytical laboratories seeking to reduce glassware-related injury risk.

papers.title: Flame Spray Pyrolysis Tailored In2O3-ZrO2 Hetero-Contacts for Enhanced Hydrogen Production in DME Steam Reforming
papers.abstract: Dimethyl ether steam reforming (SRD) is a promising route for efficient, on-demand hydrogen generation. In2O3-ZrO2 has proven to be a promising catalyst, when physically mixed with γ-Al2O3 yet its activity relies strongly on the nature and density of oxide-oxide heterointerfaces. Here, we use single- and double-flame spray pyrolysis (S-FSP, DFSP) to tune the hetero-contacts of In2O3-ZrO2 catalysts. Across indium loadings (1-15 wt%), D-FSP consistently outperforms S-FSP, particularly at low reaction temperatures (325-350 °C) relevant for energy-efficient H2 release. The distinct precursor mixing conditions in S-FSP and D-FSP lead to markedly different catalyst architectures, which in turn govern their catalytic performance. While S-FSP predominantly yields solid-solution-type materials with pronounced indium surface enrichment at higher loadings, D-FSP intrinsically promotes the formation of well-defined In2O3-ZrO2 hetero-contacts with a high density of interfacial sites. These interfacial sites enable more efficient conversion of the intermediate methanol in D-FSP catalysts, explaining their superior low-temperature activity and distinct CO2 & H2 selectivity. Overall, our results show that a simple variation of the flame configuration in FSP effectively controls heterocontacts and catalytic pathways, enabling efficient and durable catalysts for hydrogen generation within a circular DMEto-H2 energy storage cycle.

papers.title: High-throughput site scoring of SNAr electrophiles using graph-local xTB/Fukui descriptors
papers.abstract: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (S N Ar) is widely used to functionalize electron-poor aryl and heteroaryl halides, but quantitative prediction of reaction barriers and site selectivity becomes more challenging when several C–X bonds can react. A semiempirical site-scoring equation was developed for the 74-substrate benzyl alcohol/DMSO benchmark reported by Lu–Paci–Leitch. The model uses xTB-derived global reactivity descriptors and atom-condensed Fukui indices evaluated in a graph-local environment around each candidate aromatic C–X bond. The selected equation uses molecular electronegativity and four site-local contrast descriptors, giving a common representation for aryl, heteroaryl and fused heteroaryl scaffolds. Five disjoint stratified folds give held-out RMSE = 3.09 kJ mol -1 , MAE = 2.54 kJ mol -1 and R 2 = 0.861; the all-data refit gives RMSE = 2.69 kJ mol -1 and MAE = 2.18 kJ mol -1 . The equation correctly identifies the experimentally observed major site for all 13 mapped multisite benchmark examples. Application to 40,401 enumerated aryl, heteroaryl and fused heteroaryl halides gives 79,748 C–X site scores. The resulting structure–reactivity maps identify low-barrier electrophiles and multisite substrates with large predicted site gaps. The equation provides a low-cost screening approach for electrophile ranking and site selection within the calibrated aryl-halide domain.

papers.title: Accelerating and Scaling On-Lattice Solid-on-Solid Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations Using an Autoregressive Conditional Variational Autoencoder
papers.abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations are fundamental for modeling atomistic surface morphology evolution, but their inherently sequential execution of atomic steps creates severe computational bottlenecks. This computational burden restricts accessible time-and length scales, making dynamic coupling with continuum solvers, such as Computational Fluid Dynamics, difficult. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces a novel surrogate model based on an autoregressive fully convolutional Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE). As a proof of concept, we demonstrate the acceleration and scaleup of a 1D+1 Solid-on-Solid kMC model. By predicting the structural evolution over large time leaps and conditioning on thermodynamic parameters like temperature, the CVAE accurately captures the statistical surface growth and roughness dynamics across long time scales. The surrogate maintains high predictive fidelity while achieving massive computational speed-ups, bypassing expensive transition rate recalculations during temperature fluctuations, condensing many sequential events into a single forward pass, and demonstrating spatial scalability to significantly larger lattices. This approach provides a great speed-up for kMC simulations, paving the way for efficient multiscale simulation frameworks.

papers.title: Freestanding van der Waals C60 Thin Films
papers.abstract: Freestanding thin films have enabled the study of intrinsic material properties by eliminating substrate-induced constraints, yet their preparation has been limited to covalently bonded or strongly interconnected materials. Molecular solid thin films, stabilized by weak van der Waals (vdW) interactions, remain largely unexplored in freestanding form due to their inherent mechanical instability. Here, we establish a simple sublimation-assisted strategy to fabricate freestanding films of fullerene C60 as a model molecular solid. This approach produces macroscopic films with thicknesses ranging from 200–500 nm and extends to continuous films as thin as 20 nm suspended across tens of micrometers. Spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations confirm that the C60 films retain their structural and chemical integrity and exhibit characteristic electronic properties. Atomic force microscopy deflection measurements demonstrate that these films are mechanically self-supporting, exhibiting a Young’s modulus of ~5.7 GPa despite being stabilized solely by intermolecular vdW interactions. We further show that 20-nm-thick freestanding C60 films can be directly modified through UV- or ozoneinduced intermolecular crosslinking while preserving structural integrity. This work establishes a general route to freestanding molecular solid films, enabling studies of substrate-free materials with tunable structural and chemical functionalities.

papers.title: Noble Gas Aggregation and Dynamics in Molten Alkali Chloride Salts
papers.abstract: Noble gas behavior in molten alkali chloride salts is important for understanding gas retention, transport, and removal in high-temperature molten salt environments. Although previous molecular simulations have examined single-particle properties such as noble gas solubility and diffusion, the thermodynamics of early-stage gas aggregation in molten salts remain less well understood. Here, we develop an ab initio-informed classical molecular dynamics framework for quantifying stepwise noble gas aggregation in molten LiCl and KCl. Salt-specific gas–ion interaction parameters are obtained by combining quantum mechanical gas–ion interaction scans with ab initio molecular dynamics structural benchmarks. The resulting classical models are then used to compute potentials of mean force (PMFs) for two-body, three-body, and four-body association geometries of argon and xenon. Longtimescale simulations are also used to compute diffusion coefficients, providing a complementary dynamical perspective on gas behavior in each salt. The PMFs show that argon exhibits a consistent tendency toward local association in both salts, with stronger stabilization in LiCl. Xenon displays a more salt-dependent response: KCl supports increasingly favorable Xe association across the sampled aggregation geometries, whereas LiCl shows weaker association and larger intermediate barriers. Diffusion coefficients indicate that both gases are more mobile in KCl than in LiCl, with argon diffusing slightly faster than xenon within a given salt. Overall, these results show that noble gas aggregation in molten salts cannot be predicted from gas size or gas–gas attraction alone, but instead depends on the coupling between gas identity and the salt-specific local environment.

papers.title: Linker-Linker Coupling and Charge Storage Drive CO2 Photoreduction in Porphyrinic Zr(IV)-Based Metal–Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing photoactive organic linkers are promising platforms for artificial photosynthesis, yet the nature of the photoactive state in Zr(IV)-based MOFs remains controversial, particularly the proposed involvement of transient Zr(III) centers formed through linker-to-node charge transfer. Here, we elucidate the mechanism of CO 2 -to-formate conversion in MOFs by comparing redox-active PCN-223 with redox-inactive UiO-66-NH 2 . Although both MOFs contain the same Zr 6 -oxo cluster, their linkers differ in redox activity and interchromophore coupling, which allowed us to decouple linker-driven excited-state interactions from cluster-centered contributions to photocatalysis. Using in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance, infrared spectroscopy, and transient optical spectroscopy, we show that the Zr 6 -oxo cluster remains redox-inactive during photocatalysis, ruling out linker-to-node electron transfer as the dominant pathway. Instead, framework assembly in PCN-223 induces strong interporphyrin coupling that promotes exciton delocalization and symmetry-breaking charge separation, generating long-lived linker-centered radical states absent in molecular porphyrins. Triethanolamine selectively scavenges the oxidized porphyrin species, stabilizing the reduced radical and enabling accumulation of photogenerated reducing equivalents within the framework. Remarkably, CO 2 reduction proceeds even after illumination ceases, revealing photocharging behavior in which stored linker-centered charges sustain catalysis in the dark. We further provide direct evidence for transient CO 2 •− species, which is consistent with a proton-coupled electron-transfer pathway inside the MOF pores. Together, these findings show that collective chromophore interactions, rather than metal-node redox chemistry, govern charge separation, charge storage, and catalytic reactivity in photoactive Zr-MOFs.

papers.title: Importance may not be that important: A common misconception in data-driven materials development
papers.abstract: With the growing adoption of machine learning methods in physics, data-driven materials development has emerged as one of the most prominent methodologies in materials research. In data-driven materials development, feature importance is often misused to infer direct relationships between input descriptors and material properties, because importance merely reflects a feature’s contribution to reducing model error, rather than its physical significance. Using an oxidative coupling of methane dataset, we show that regular but irrelevant features can drastically alter importance rankings, leading to misleading conclusions. To address this common issue, we propose and advocate using straightforward correlation analysis between predicted outputs and individual features to achieve more reliable model interpretation and materials prediction. This approach reveals key correlations—both positive and negative—that may be overlooked by importance-based methods alone.

papers.title: Diffusion and transport of hydrogen peroxide across lipid membranes
papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important biological oxidant that can be formed both enzymatically and non-enzymatically, and several enzymatic systems are capable of rapidly decomposing it. During its short lifetime, H 2 O 2 can participate in cell signaling at low concentrations or induce irreparable molecular damage at high concentrations. The diffusion of H 2 O 2 in cells and tissues remains under debate, particularly regarding the role of cellular membranes as barriers to its diffusion and the mechanisms involved in its transport. Diffusion across lipid-only membranes occurs approximately five orders of magnitude more slowly than through an equivalent layer of water and can be influenced by lipid composition, temperature, and membrane fluidizers. This low permeability is attributed to the limited solubility of H 2 O 2 in the hydrophobic core of the lipid bilayer. The permeability of biological membranes to H 2 O 2 is within a similar range, with reported permeability coefficients between 2 × 10 -4 and 3 × 10 -3 cm s -1 . Given the similarity between H 2 O 2 and water, several aquaporins have been found to facilitate H 2 O 2 diffusion across cellular membranes. In humans, aquaporins 3 and 8 are considered the main facilitators of H 2 O 2 transport, while the role of aquaporin 1 remains controversial. Although membrane permeability to H 2 O 2 is relatively low and limits its transmembrane flux, diffusion remains rapid, and only a few cellular systems-most notably peroxiredoxins-can effectively compete with H 2 O 2 efflux. This review provides quantitative information on H 2 O 2 diffusion within cells and across cellular membranes and contrasts these processes with its predominant biochemical reactions.

papers.title: Spatial Heterogeneity of the Fluorine-to-Lithium Ratio as a Descriptor of Battery Failure by Laser-Induced XUV Spectroscopy (LIXS)
papers.abstract: Fluorine-containing phases are closely linked to electrolyte decomposition, interphase formation, and failure processes in Li-ion batteries, yet their spatially resolved analysis in composite cathodes remains difficult. Here, laser-induced XUV spectroscopy (LIXS) was used to map fluorine- and lithium-related emission lines in composite lithium cobalt oxide cathodes (LCO). The study used the fluorine emission line at λ = 12.72 nm and the lithium emission line at λ = 13.42 nm and applied them to pristine, formed, aged, and failed LCO cathodes. A matrix-matched calibration using seven Li metal oxide cathode materials at three fluorine levels showed increasing fluorine-related intensity within each matrix, along with pronounced matrix specificity and dispersion. This indicated that fluorine quantification in composite cathodes is influenced by matrix effects, non-thermal equilibrium plasma behavior, and heterogeneity of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) containing fluorine-bearing phases. In the mapped cathodes, the F/Li intensity ratio provided the most sensitive descriptor of degradation, showing increasing imbalance and greater spatial heterogeneity from pristine to failed electrodes. LIXS is therefore advantageous for comparative mapping of light-element/halogen heterogeneity in battery cathodes, where reliable fluorine quantification across chemically distinct composite materials remains intrinsically difficult.

papers.title: Mechanism of Zwitterionic Photochromism in Aza-Diarylethenes Revealed by Direct Observation of a Closed-Ring Intermediate
papers.abstract: Aza-diarylethenes have emerged as a unique class of photochromic molecules exhibiting reaction pathways that are inaccessible to conventional diarylethenes. In particular, certain azadiarylethenes generate zwitterionic closed-ring photoproducts, giving rise to unusual photochromic behavior. However, the elementary processes responsible for the formation of zwitterionic photoproducts remain unclear, hindering mechanistic understanding of this unusual class of photochromic reactions. Here, we investigate the photochromic reaction mechanism of a benzofuran-fused aza-diarylethene (BF-ADE) using steady-state spectroscopy, thermal kinetic analysis, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, visible-to-near-infrared transient absorption spectroscopy, time-resolved infrared spectroscopy, oxygen-quenching experiments, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Spectroscopic, computational, and crystallographic analyses consistently demonstrate that photoirradiation of BF-ADE ultimately generates a zwitterionic closed-ring isomer, BF-ADE(c-Z), while thermal bleaching proceeds through the neutral closedring isomer, BF-ADE(c). Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy revealed ultrafast excited-state dynamics with a characteristic time constant of 1.6 ps. More importantly, timeresolved infrared spectroscopy provided direct spectroscopic evidence for the formation of the conventional closed-ring intermediate BF-ADE(c) within the first few picoseconds after photoexcitation. Oxygen-quenching experiments combined with DFT calculations further demonstrated that BF-ADE(c-Z) is generated predominantly from BF-ADE(c) on the ground-state potential energy surface rather than through a triplet-mediated pathway. These findings provide a unified mechanistic framework for zwitterionic photochromism in aza-diarylethenes and reveal the pivotal role of a conventional closed-ring intermediate in generating zwitterionic photoproducts.

papers.title: Laser-directed photochemical synthesis of complex DNA microarrays and libraries
papers.abstract: In situ photolithographic synthesis of nucleic acids offers high-throughput capability and versatility across a wide range of canonical and analog nucleic acid chemistries, substrates, and surface functionalization strategies. However, adapting this synthetic approach to new applications involving physically large layouts and dispersed or larger features requires an optical exposure system capable of delivering light with greater flexibility than that offered by digital micromirror device technology. We present a portable, low-cost laser-scanning system that enables large-area nucleic acid synthesis with precise photodeprotection across arbitrarily defined array patterns. The system integrates a 405 nm laser with scanning optical components, a holographic beam shaper, and irradiance control. Using interchangeable lenses allows synthesis areas up to 110 × 110 mm and spot sizes ranging from 100 to 700 µm. Phosphoramidites bearing the SPh-NPPOC photolabile protecting group can be efficiently deblocked in milliseconds with high-intensity laser light, enabling parallel synthesis of arrays of 95mers.

papers.title: Polypyrrole-Polydopamine Composite Conductive Polymers for Electrical Stimulation in Tissue Engineering
papers.abstract: Conductive polymers have emerged as a paramount category of biomaterials within the domains of tissue engineering and regenerative medicine, attributed to their capacity for transmitting electrical signals and facilitating effective interactions with cellular entities. Among this class of materials, polypyrrole (PPy) has been extensively utilized in the development of electroactive scaffolds, systems for cellular stimulation, and bioelectronic interfaces, owing to its advantageous electrical conductivity and commendable biocompatibility. Nevertheless, challenges such as suboptimal surface adhesion, restricted mechanical stability, and inadequate processability have impeded the broader application of this polymer. Recently, polydopamine (PDA), a polymer derived from the biomineralization processes observed in seashells, has been introduced as a viable approach to enhance the efficacy of PPy-based systems, owing to its rich array of functional groups, remarkable adhesion properties, and elevated biocompatibility. The findings indicate that the incorporation of PDA can substantially augment the performance of PPy systems by improving adhesion, amplifying cellular interactions, augmenting structural integrity, and facilitating charge transfer processes. Such enhanced properties have resulted in the widespread utilization of PDA/PPy composites across various applications, including but not limited to the electrical stimulation of cells, neural tissue engineering, bioelectronic systems, wound healing, intelligent drug delivery systems, and biosensors.

papers.title: A Critical Evaluation of Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Organic Synthesis: Activation Modes and Green Metrics
papers.abstract: While domino and cascade reactions are widely celebrated for their step economy and intrinsic bond-forming efficiency, evaluating their true sustainability requires moving beyond a purely molecular perspective to incorporate rigorous Green Chemistry metrics. This review critically reassesses sequential transformations—including ionic, radical, pericyclic, photochemical, transition-metal, and biocatalytic pathwaysthrough a quantitative framework termed the “Molecular–Process Discrepancy.” Rather than providing a traditional descriptive overview, this manuscript integrates quantitative indicators, such as Atom Economy (AE) and Process Mass Intensity (PMI), to evaluate the actual environmental footprint of these reactions. By analyzing recent synthetic applications, this evaluation reveals that theoretical green advantages are frequently negated at scale by specific physicochemical and engineering bottlenecks, most notably the dilution paradox in macroscopic batch systems, interphase mass transfer limitations, and catalyst deactivation. Ultimately, the findings indicate that 2 resolving these scale-up hurdles requires a definitive transition from isolated molecular design to integrated process engineering. Specifically, the integration of continuousflow microreactor technologies and AI-driven retrosynthesis emerges as a critical pathway to bridge the gap between elegant molecular synthesis and genuinely sustainable chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Exploring the Chemical Space with a Foundation Model for Optimizing Drug Discovery in Neglected Diseases, the case of Leishmaniasis
papers.abstract: Applications of AI to the discovery of new treatments could have a large impact on the acceleration of drug discovery for neglected diseases such as Leishmaniasis. Taking advantage of a lead compound derived from a library of 1.8 million molecules screened against Leishmaniasis Infantum and a dataset used for further refining the lead compound potency and metabolic stability, we fine-tuned a foundational model MMELON (Multi-view Molecular Embedding with Late Fusion) to accurately predict these properties with high AUROCs of 0.90 and 0.87 respectively. Indeed, although the lead compound had many promising properties, such as high potency, low host cell toxicity, and excellent in vivo efficacy, high clearance and low bioavailability made it unfit for implementation in a clinical trial. In order to find new molecules with the desired properties, the fine-tuned MMELON was then used to generate new predictions, prospecting the 10,000 molecules from the Enamine library with most similarity to the lead compound. The purpose was to obtain a new diverse set of molecules with high potency and metabolic stability, to further explore clearance and bioavailability. A subset of 59 new compounds were chosen using fine-tuned MMELON predictions and sent for further experimental testing. Overall, 29 hits (49.2%) were correctly predicted to have high potency and 14 hits (23.7%) were correctly predicted to have low metabolic rate. The molecules were also quite distinct from the lead compound DNDI-6993, opening new avenues for the development and implementation of a new treatment for Leishmaniasis.

papers.title: CoSyER: A high-throughput data generation approach for environmental machine learning
papers.abstract: Machine learning holds great promise for chemical hazard assessment, but the lack of large, standardized datasets limits advances. We herein propose Co mbinatorial Sy nthesis for E nvironmental R esearch ( CoSyER ) as a high-throughput data generation approach for environmental machine learning, capable of generating hazard data for hundreds of compounds within weeks. To demonstrate proof of concept, we synthesized ~300 organophosphate ester (OPE) mixture via one-pot combinatorial synthesis. The synthesized chemicals were incubated with liver microsomes to determine their biotransformation rates. Interpretable machine learning revealed that ether and aryl moieties enhance biotransformation via oxidation or hydrolysis. We further assessed the bioactivity of ~300 OPEs toward seven selected human proteins and identified the constitutive androstane receptor (CAR) as a nM-affinity target for OPEs, with Log P as the most important feature for machine learning prediction of binding affinity. This study highlights CoSyER as a high-throughput approach for hazard assessment at the chemical class level to avoid regrettable substitutions.

papers.title: Isobutanol Dehydration to Linear Butenes on Ferrierite: Mechanistic Insights from operando FTIR, Chemometrics and Kinetic Modelling
papers.abstract: The selective dehydration of isobutanol to linear butenes catalyzed by acidic ferrierite (H-FER) has been investigated by operando IR spectroscopy under close batch conditions and along a temperature ramp. The employed apparatus permits to alternatively acquire spectra of both the gas phase composition and the species adsorbed on the H-FER surface, thus providing fundamental insights onto the products formation and the reaction intermediates formed on the catalyst surface. In the gas phase, the high selectivity for linear butenes was confirmed in the first phases of the reaction, followed by a slower isomerization to isobutene and by the formation of heavier compounds due to secondary processes. Detailed MCR-ALS analysis of the adsorbed species’ spectra permitted to also identify and quantify adsorbed 2-butanol and trans-2-butene on the H-FER surface, providing a first indication of the alcohol isomerization as a key step in the reaction mechanism. The proposed mechanism was evaluated by microkinetic modelling of both gas phase and surface concentration profiles, showing that the consecutive isomerization of isobutanol to adsorbed 2-butanol followed by its dehydration to trans-2-butene is more favorable than the one-step dehydration-isomerization of isobutanol. In contrast, the direct dehydration of isobutanol to isobutene was found to be slower over the entire investigated temperature range.

papers.title: High-throughput synthesis and screening of cyclometallated iridium complexes for antibacterial applications
papers.abstract: The discovery of novel antibiotics to address the rise of antimicrobial resistance is an increasingly pressing issue for global health. In recent years transition metal complexes have gained attention as potential antibacterial agents. We herein describe a new methodology to generate hundreds of novel cyclometallated iridium compounds with bidentate Schiff ligands in a high-throughput combinatorial approach, alongside the expansion of an existing approach using bidentate pyridine-triazole ligands, with the aim of finding new metalloantibiotics. Variety in the libraries was introduced by including three cyclometallating phenylpyridine ligands, demonstrating that the synthesis can tolerate both electron rich and electron poor metal scaffolds while using mild and biologically compatible conditions. Screening of the crude reaction mixtures in a Direct-to-Biology approach revealed a number of highly active complexes against Gram-positive bacteria, which was confirmed by re-synthesis and further testing of lead compounds. This approach widens the scope of combinatorial chemistry, enabling rapid exploration of the chemical space involving cyclometallated iridium complexes.

papers.title: Accelerated Stable Structure Prediction of Li-Intercalated Bilayer Graphene Using a Data-Efficient Deep Learning Framework
papers.abstract: Replacing bulk graphite with few-layer graphene is a promising route toward improving both the storage capacity and rate capability of fast-charging Li-ion batteries. As the simplest layered graphene system, bilayer graphene (BLG) provides an ideal model for uncovering the structural origins of these improvements, which in turn requires accurate identification of its thermodynamically stable structures. However, predicting stable Li-intercalated structures requires exhaustive exploration of a vast configurational space using density functional theory (DFT), which rapidly becomes computationally prohibitive for large supercells. Here, we present DESSP, a data-efficient deep learning framework for accelerated stable structure prediction in Liintercalated BLG. DESSP combines a genetic-algorithm-based search pipeline with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) used as a surrogate for DFT, enabling broad yet efficient exploration of the potential energy surface. Representative structures sampled along the search trajectories are then selectively labeled with DFT to train a high-fidelity MLIP, while a distillation-based strategy further improves predictive accuracy. The resulting model achieves near-DFT accuracy, generalizes effectively to larger supercells, and reproduces the thermodynamic convex hull at substantially lower computational cost, providing a scalable framework for studying nanoscale layered electrodes in batteries.

papers.title: Skeletal editing as synthetic tool to prepare benzo[e][1,2,4]triazines from 2aminobenzimidazoles via nitrogen atom insertion
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a one-pot, two-step reaction that converts readily available 2-aminobenzimidazoles into scarcely accessible benzo[e][1,2,4]triazines via nitrogen atom insertion. This sequential transformation includes an electrophilic amination step with bench-stable MSH.HOTf, followed by an oxidation with commercial hypervalent iodine reactant. The developed reaction encompasses a wide array of functional handles that could be exploited for post-modification, thus highlighting the synthetic utility of the present work.

papers.title: Alkylthio aurone fluorophores: a structure–property relationship of emission in solution and in the solid state
papers.abstract: Aurones are a class of fluorescent plant flavonoids representing biocompatible fluorophores with tuneable emission colors. In this work, a series of novel 4'-alkylthio aurones is synthesized and their steady-state and time-resolved emission is studied in solution- and solid state in combination with the single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. In solution, the aurones possess virtually identical cyan fluorescence with similar parameters. In contrast, in the crystalline state, the compounds exhibit remarkably variable fluorescence characterized by complex decays allowing to divide them into three groups with (i) slow, (ii) fast, and (iii) combined slow and fast emission decay. The innovative variational analysis developed in this work reveals that the alkyl substituents alter predominantly the radiationless but not the radiative deactivation rate constant indicating that the solid-state fluorescence arises mostly from the same emitter – the alkylthio aurone monomer localized in the regions of different quenching efficiency. According to the XRD data, the conjugation or lack thereof of the S atom with the π-system of the aurone core correlates directly with the solid-state emission intensity and is governed by the structure of the alkyl substituents. Overall, the obtained results provide new important insights into the structure–property relationship of SSSE aurone fluorophores.

papers.title: OSC700: A GW+BSE Dataset of 700 Organic Semiconductor (OSC) Crystals with an LLM-Assisted Data Extraction Agent
papers.abstract: Key parameters for organic optoelectronic device applications derive from the excited-state properties of molecular crystals. Data scarcity (both experimental and theoretical) limits the ability to train machine learning (ML) models to predict these properties. We present the OSC700 dataset of excited-state properties of 700 crystalline organic semiconductors (OSCs) with up to 1168 atoms in the unit cell, calculated using state-of-the-art many-body perturbation theory within the GW approximation and Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW+BSE). OSC700 contains crystals of compounds comprising C,H,N,O,F,S capable of forming a variety of molecular scaffolds and crystal packing motifs. OSC700 is larger and significantly more diverse than the earlier PAH101 dataset [Scientific Data 12, 679 (2025)]. The data records contain the fundamental gap, quasiparticle band structure, static dielectric constant, first singlet exciton energy (optical gap), first triplet exciton energy, full dielectric function, and optical absorption spectra for light polarized along the three lattice vectors. Because absorption experiments on molecular crystals are rare (as opposed to solution or amorphous phases), we developed an LLM-assisted data extraction agent in order to find and retrieve available optical gap data for the materials in OSC700. The agent was able to find experimental data for 16 materials, which we used to validate the results of our calculations. The OSC700 dataset can be used to train ML models to predict the excited-state properties of crystalline organic semiconductors and find promising materials for optoelectronic device applications.

papers.title: Hetero-interfacial Oxygen superionic conduction for efficient high-temperature CO2 Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) hold enormous potential for the conversion of CO2 into high-value fuels, yet their performance is often limited by insufficient oxygen‑ion conductivity and sluggish CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) kinetics. Herein, we develop a hetero-interface superionic conductor that integrates cross-grain bridging and the space charge effect to boost CO2 electrolysis performance of double perovskite electrodes. Specifically, La4Mn5Si4O22+δ (LMS) with ultra‑fast interstitial oxygen transfer bridges crystallographically misaligned PrBaFe1.6Ni0.4O6-δ (PBFN) grains, thereby effectively mitigating the directional limitation of inter‑layer oxygen transport.
