The lattice strain and space-charge effects at the heterointerface of this hybrid electrode enrich oxygen carriers and reduce oxygen-ion migration barriers, realizing interfacial superionic conduction. As expected, the SOEC equipped with a PBFN-LMS cathode achieves an exceptional current density of 1.61 A cm-2 at 1.5 V (800 °C), outperforming PBFN-GDC and the pristine PBFN cathode. Impressively, a 3 cm2 large-area cell exhibits outstanding stability over 1000 hours without carbon deposition. This work develops a cross-grain bridging strategy that enables superionic transport, thereby realizing efficient and stable CO2 electrolysis.

papers.title: Approach-Region Commitment and Environmental Friction
papers.abstract: The commitment of a reacting system to productive barrier crossing depends on how strongly the environment dissipates energy into the approach-region coordinate, rather than oscillatory recrossing. This dissipation is quantified by a single dimensionless damping ratio, χ0 = Γeff/(2Ω0), where Ω0 is the precursor-well approach frequency and Γeff is the total projected friction. Using three independent estimator routes calibrated to spectroscopic linewidths (Route A), solvent longitudinal relaxation times (Route B), and DFT electronic friction coefficients (Route C), χ0 is computed here for nine canonical systems, constituting an Approach-Region Commitment (ARC) Atlas, spanning gas-phase unimolecular reactions, liquid-phase electron transfer and proton-coupled electron transfer, surface heterogeneous catalysis, and solid-state ion transport. Gas-phase systems are deeply underdamped (χ0 ∼ 10−3–10−2), providing a dynamical interpretation of the excess-energy requirements of RRKM unimolecular kinetics through the approach-region commitment probability rather than through transition-state recrossing alone. Selected condensed-phase systems approach or enter the near-critical window χ0 ∈ [0.8, 1.3] (K-promoted metal surfaces; fast-solvent ET near the upper window flank), while viscous solvents and poisoned surfaces fall into the overdamped regime. The results are not obtained by fitting χ0 to reaction outcomes: Γeff and Ω0 are taken from independently measured, computed, or explicitly bracketed physical observables in each case. The progression from gas to liquid to surface corresponds to a severalorder-of-magnitude span in χ0, revealing that solvent choice, surface promotion, and phase selection each shift χ0 in a predictable direction relative to the exceptional-point stability boundary at χ0 = 1.

papers.title: Recent advances in cis/trans stereoselective polymerizations toward functional materials with tailored properties
papers.abstract: Despite the myriad of stereoselective reactions developed to control the cis/trans (or Z/E) configuration of alkenes, analogous stereocontrol has been slower to emerge in polymerization processes. Following pioneering work in stereoselective coordination–insertion polymerizations, a variety of cis/trans stereoselective processes have recently been reported, enabling the synthesis of well-defined polymeric materials with tunable properties. Importantly, many of these advances have also provided control over additional structural features, including tacticitity, regioselectivity, and higherorder topologies. This Perspective surveys recent developments in the field of cis/trans stereoselective polymerizations, highlighting the mechanistic origins of stereocontrol, innovations in catalyst design, and the expanding diversity of compatible monomers. Finally, the unique challenges and opportunites associated with stereocontrol in polymer synthesis are discussed with an eye toward broadening access to precision polymeric materials with tailored properties

papers.title: Electrochemical Cu-ion Insertion in a Tunnel-Structured V2O5 Polymorph
papers.abstract: The distinctive nonlinear dynamical transitions of “neuromorphic” inorganic materials provide a means to build spiking oscillatory circuits for brain-inspired computing. The metal-insulator transition of β′-Cu x V 2 O 5 is controlled by the Cu stoichiometry. Electrochemical Cu-ion insertion into the empty metastable ζ-V 2 O 5 polymorph utilizing an aqueous electrolyte is demonstrated for the first time. X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy techniques in combination with electron microscopy elucidate electronic and structural evolution as a function of Cu-ion insertion. Such electrochemical insertion provides a lever to tune the Cu stoichiometry of the material and thus the metal-insulator transition.

papers.title: Radiosynthesis and PET/CT evaluation of 18F-labeled and non-steroidal androgen receptor inhibitor, [18F]F -ARi, in a non-castrated model
papers.abstract: Androgen receptor (AR)-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) enables non-invasive quantification of AR expression in androgen driven prostate cancer cases. The clinically investigated tracer 16β-[ 18 F]F-fluorodihydrotestosterone ([ 18 F]F-DHT) is limited by endogenous androgen competition in non-castrated patients, rapid metabolism and restricted bioavailability. To address these limitations, we developed a non-steroidal AR-targeted radiotracer, [ 18 F]F-ARi, derived from the precursor ARi-NH, for AR-targeted PET imaging. Methods: [ 18 F]F-ARi was synthesized via one-pot radiosynthesis. Radiochemical yield, purity, and molar activity were quantified by radio-HPLC, and was confirmed using the cold standard [ 19 F]F-ARi. AR-specific uptake, binding, and kinetics were determined in AR-positive LNCaP and 22R v 1 human prostate cancer cells with competitive blocking by ARi-NH, and AR-negative PC-3 as control. The in vivo PET imaging was evaluated by static PET/CT in 22R v 1 tumor-bearing male mice, followed by ex vivo biodistribution and blocking to assess specificity and clearance. 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-Dglucose ([ 18 F]F-FDG) was used as metabolic reference standard. Results: [ 18 F]F-ARi was obtained in 7.4 ± 0.9 % decay-corrected radiochemical yield and 399% radiochemical purity, and 8.79 GBq/µmol molar activity, and remained stable in human serum up to 4 h. Cell uptake of [ 18 F]F-ARi was 52.5 ± 7.8% in LNCaP and 47.4 ± 14.2% in 22R v 1cells, which was blockable by ARi-NH, with minimal uptake in PC-3 cells. Binding affinity was in the nanomolar range (approximately Kd » 9 nM). In 22R v 1 orthotopic model, [ 18 F]F-ARi showed tumor accumulation that was significantly reduced by in vivo blocking. The biodistribution supported AR-mediated tumor retention, low likelihood of defluorination, and mixed hepatobiliary and renal clearance. Conclusion: [ 18 F]F-ARi is a non-steroidal-based AR PET radiotracer with favorable stability, specificity, and preclinical imaging performance. Our data supports further optimization and translation for next-generation AR imaging in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Computational Design of Two Selective Tyrosine Kinase 2 Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Dysregulated interleukin-12 (IL-12) and interleukin-23 (IL-23) cytokine signaling pathways have been implicated in many inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease, plaque psoriasis, or rheumatoid arthritis. While small molecule or biologic therapies exist to target IL-12 and IL-23, limitations to selectivity or long-term efficacy reflect a need for novel drug candidates. Tyrosine Kinase 2 (TYK2), one of four Janus Kinase enzymes, is involved in intracellular IL-12 and IL-23 signal transduction and has been of recent pharmacological interest. In this study, two potential TYK2 selective inhibitors were developed through bioisosteric replacements and rational design. Computational molecular docking, ADMET screening, and selectivity analysis indicate the two candidates as promising scaffolds towards conditions driven by irregular IL-12 and IL-23 cytokine signaling.

papers.title: Quantum-Guided Binding-Site Engineering of Lanmodulin for Zero-Waste Separation of Critical Rare-Earth Elements
papers.abstract: Rare-earth separation remains energy-intensive and waste-generating, motivating aqueous alternatives for selective lanthanide capture. We report a deterministic computational workflow that couples binding-site engineering of lanmodulin with multireference quantum characterization toward dysprosium prioritization. Four experimentally solved lanmodulin structures were harmonized, residue roles were assigned to preserve the first-shell coordination environment while allowing selected second-sphere and interface positions to mutate, and ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, Rosetta triage, and reduced OpenMM rescreening were used to rank redesigned pockets against dysprosium, neodymium, yttrium, aluminum, and iron. The workflow reduced 66 evaluated mask positions to 3 finalists while retaining rare-earth binding in all cases. The top-ranked Hans-derived pocket showed the strongest local confidence signal, the lowest pocket free-energy proxy, and stable rare-earth coordination, but aluminum and iron capture persisted across all three candidate pockets. The nominated pocket was then advanced to multiconfigurational treatment: compact Dy(III) and Nd(III) coordination clusters were extracted and characterized with CASSCF and CASPT2 using a 4f active space, confirming a physically valid 4f manifold for each metal and a well-converged multireference description. These results deliver a quantum-characterized dysprosium-prioritized lanmodulin pocket and matched Dy/Nd electronic-structure references, and show that competitor suppression remains the main design challenge.

papers.title: Active Space Compression High Fidelity Variational Solvers and Exact Consistency under Quantum Molecular Mechanics Embedding
papers.abstract: This study presents a journal ready quantum molecular simulation paper built around a reproducible workflow that couples active space reduction, variational quantum solvers, and simple QM MM electrostatic embedding for benchmark molecules relevant to chemical and biological modeling. The central challenge addressed is the mismatch between realistic molecular Hamiltonians and near term qubit limits. We hypothesized that disciplined active space compression would preserve energy fidelity while transforming otherwise impractical problems into compact qubit representations. Across H2, CO, and CO2 in STO 3G, the workflow reduced qubit demand from eighteen to six for CO and from twenty eight to six for CO2, while retaining VQE errors of 0.051 and 0.039 kcal per mol. Adapt VQE produced closely matched errors of 0.066 and 0.039 kcal per mol. H2 reached near machine level agreement with exact energy. Under QM MM point charge embedding, VQE reproduced exact energy shifts with mean absolute mismatch below 0.004 kcal per mol and near perfect linear consistency. These results show strong quantum output through qubit efficiency, solver fidelity, and environmental response accuracy, supporting a practical route toward scalable environment aware molecular biosimulation and quantum enabled computational chemistry. The framework strengthens reproducibility through deterministic artifacts and publication ready reporting.

papers.title: Prioritizing early opportunities to enhance carbon efficiency at biorefineries
papers.abstract: Biorefineries are a critical component of society’s transition from fossil-derived to bio-derived fuel and chemical production, but their life cycle carbon efficiency is often undermined by the underutilization of biomass feedstocks during processing. In this work, we explore the feasibility and sustainability implications of integrating waste carbon utilization into commercial-scale biorefineries through process design, simulation, techno-economic analysis, and life cycle assessment under uncertainty. Using cellulosic ethanol production as an illustrative example, two methanol synthesis pathways (natural gas bi-reforming with CO 2 and CO 2 hydrogenation) are evaluated, with hydrogen either generated on-site or procured externally. Results show integrating CO 2 -to-methanol synthesis substantially increases carbon use efficiency from ~30% to ~70%. However, environmental and economic outcomes are configuration-dependent. Fossil-based natural gas and hydrogen use undermine system carbon intensity (CI) benefits, though the natural gas-based pathway lowers costs relative to base ethanol production. Low-CI pathways are economically constrained by renewable electricity and hydrogen costs, which methanol price premiums and carbon credits could partially offset. Under current grid-mix conditions, cost parity with base ethanol production requires 80% renewable electricity, whereas comparable CI necessitates 96% renewable penetration. Overall, these findings highlight that near-complete grid decarbonization, low-cost clean hydrogen, and supportive policy frameworks are critical for the deployment of CO 2 utilization in biorefineries.

papers.title: Photon-Limited Kinetics in g-C3N4 Photocatalytic Flow Reactors: The Role of Reactor Geometry and Catalyst Placement
papers.abstract: The performance of heterogeneous photocatalytic reactors has traditionally been optimized through catalyst development, whereas the role of reactor architecture in controlling photon utilization remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that photocatalytic efficiency is governed not simply by the number of absorbed photons, but by how incident photons are partitioned between bulk absorption, interfacial photocatalysis, and optical losses. To investigate this concept, a modular visible-light flow reactor with adjustable optical thickness was developed using graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) in front-coated, back-coated, and slurry configurations. Methylene blue degradation established a photon-limited reaction regime, where apparent kinetics were controlled by photon transport rather than intrinsic catalytic activity. Although slurry and immobilized catalysts exhibited nearly identical optical attenuation, their photocatalytic performances differed markedly, demonstrating that photon attenuation alone cannot predict reactor performance. The back-coated reactor exhibited the highest thicknessnormalized reaction rate and catalyst productivity by promoting sequential photon utilization, allowing photons to first interact with the reaction solution before reaching the catalyst interface. This photon-partitioning framework was validated under continuous single-pass operation, achieving up to 97% methylene blue conversion. The results establish catalyst placement as an independent reactor-design parameter and provide a general framework for designing scalable photon-limited heterogeneous photocatalytic reactors through photon management rather than catalyst development alone.

papers.title: In Operando Electrochemical Reduction of Indium Tin Oxide Contacts in Silicon Oxide Memristive Devices
papers.abstract: We report a study of current transient behaviour in silicon oxide memristive devices with indium tin oxide (ITO) top contacts. Constant-current electrical stress reveals that ITO-contacted devices exhibit chaotic conductance fluctuations and a single-phase transient in which the slow decay is suppressed, unlike the smooth, two-phase rise-and-decay response of devices with Au/Ti contacts. Through X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, spectroscopic evidence is provided that proton-driven electrochemical reduction of the ITO electrode decouples the two processes that the gold-contacted transient superimposes, leaving the initial conductance increase attributed to bulk oxide changes while suppressing the slow decay phase normally observed in gold-contacted devices. Binding energy shifts in indium (~0.9 eV) and accelerated interfacial etch rates in stressed devices suggest sub-stoichiometric ITO formation. By suppressing the slow proton screening that masks it in gold-contacted devices, the ITO contact exposes the underlying trap-discharge relaxation, which is dispersive (stretched-exponential exponent β = 0.54 ± 0.17) with a field-free discharge time of a few seconds. These findings reveal that nanoscale electrode material selection critically determines the physical mechanisms governing conductance dynamics in memristive devices, with implications for neuromorphic computing and reliable nanoelectronic design.

papers.title: Accelerated Mechanochemical Reaction Discovery and Development via Miniaturized Parallel Milling
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical reaction discovery remains constrained by the low throughput and material demands of conventional milling workflows. Herein, we establish miniaturized parallel milling as a general approach for accelerated mechanochemical reaction discovery and development in a mixer-mill equipment. The platform employs inexpensive polypropylene vial reactors mounted on modular holders and enables the rapid evaluation of solvent-minimized transformations with minimal material consumption. Its generality is demonstrated across diverse reaction classes, including fluorination, amide formation, cross-coupling, heterocycle synthesis, and zero-valent-metal-mediated reactivity. Parallel operation enables reproducible reaction screening, kinetic profiling, and optimization of reaction conditions. As a showcase, a mechanochemical aziridine synthesis was developed from initial discovery to optimization, kinetic analysis, and preliminary scope evaluation within only 3 milling campaigns using unmodified mixer-mill equipment. Together, this workflow provides a practical foundation for high throughput mechanochemistry and accelerates the translation of mechanochemical methods from discovery to application.

papers.title: Seven is optimal: a K5 selection principle for photosynthetic energy transfer
papers.abstract: The Fenna–Matthews–Olson complex transfers excitation energy at ~99% efficiency at physiological temperature—a performance no model derives from first principles. We show that a single combinatorial fact does: the complex has seven chromophores, and seven is the unique integer that decomposes as 5+5−3, allowing two complete pentachoric cells (K₅) to share a triangular face (K₃). This K₃ junction minimises the number of inter-cell coupling edges to four—a combinatorial minimum among all 5+5−k decompositions. Applied to the measured Hamiltonian (Adolphs–Renger, 2006), the optimal decomposition places the shared face at {BChl1, BChl4, BChl6} with an intra/inter coupling ratio of 44.7, the four inter-cell edges being the four weakest in the Hamiltonian. The machinery of the companion paper P21—Ohm's law as the stationary Dirichlet state, the edge dipole as stable carrier, face saturation as the resistance mechanism—places the complex deep in the ohmic regime (40% of face saturation), where transport is governed by a monotone density gradient from antenna to reaction centre with zero saturated faces. The absolute quantum yield (~99%) is shown to be dominated by the ratio of trapping to recombination rates, not by the network topology; the K₅ contribution is the separation ratio, the structural robustness, and the identification of the transport bottleneck as catalytic rather than topological. The PE545 complex (eight chromophores, 5+5−2, K₂ junction) is tested as a falsification: its optimal ratio is 11.3, a factor 3.9× below the FMO, and none of its 280 decompositions matches the FMO value. A dipole-dipole Hamiltonian for LH2 B800 (nine chromophores, 5+5−1, K₁ junction) extends the hierarchy to K₃(44.7) > K₂(11.3) > K₁(4.5), confirmed on three independent biological systems. A final section applies the K₅ topology to the CO₂ fixation step itself: the CO₂ molecule sits at a frustration plateau (four saturated edges, zero complete faces), and the K₃ catalyst with coordinated water reduces the photon budget from three edge-flips to one—a result verified by exhaustive enumeration of all 1024 states. All results are verified by a companion script (137 tests, 0 failures) with no free parameter beyond α* = 1/(4 ln 2) and the electron mass.

papers.title: Structural Order Boosts Spin Polarization and Chiral Enhancement in MOF Catalysts for Oxygen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: The efficiency of Electrochemical Water Splitting can be improved using chiral catalysts and the Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect. The spin polarized currents generated by CISS favour the formation of O 2 in its triplet ground state and lower the overpotential required to drive the Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER). However, systematic studies in classes of closely related materials are lacking. Here, we investigate three pairs of nickel(II) coordination polymers based on 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate ligands with either chiral or achiral alkoxy side chains and three different degrees of crystallinity. The most crystalline materials are authenticated as 2D Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) with a layered structure and hexanickel(II) metallacrown subunits. These noble metal-free compounds serve as efficient catalysts of OER, with current densities that compete with or even largely surpass that of state-of-the-art IrO 2 . All chiral materials show asymmetric spin polarization and improved catalytic activity compared to their achiral counterparts. Crystallinity is found to largely enhance the effect of chirality, although the most crystalline MOF samples retain only ~25% of intact alkoxy groups. Our results establish a correlation between structure, spin polarization, and chiral catalytic enhancement and prove that structural long-range order is more important than the number of chiral centers.

papers.title: RETRACTED: In Silico Humanization and Structural Evaluation of the Fab 4G2 Anti-Hantavirus Antibody Fragment
papers.abstract: Retracted at the author’s request because the report contains fundamental errors that render the results inaccurate. Computational antibody humanization is a widely used strategy to reduce predicted immunogenicity in non-human monoclonal antibodies while preserving structural and antigen-binding properties. In this study, we applied an in silico workflow to the Fab 4G2 anti-hantavirus antibody fragment. The parental variable heavy (VH) and variable light (VL) chain sequences were extracted from the Protein Data Bank (PDB ID: 6Z06) and evaluated for predicted MHC-II-associated immunogenicity using the IEDB MHC-II Binding Prediction Tool. Sequence humanization and framework optimization were performed using the BioPhi/Sapiens platform. Structural modeling of the resulting humanized heterodimer was conducted using AlphaFold 3. Protein–protein docking simulations were then executed on the PatchDock server to evaluate the binding of the humanized Fab against its native target, the pre-fusion Puumala virus Gc glycoprotein ectodomain (isolated from PDB ID: 6Z06). The resulting structural models demonstrated a preserved immunoglobulin fold and yielded multiple candidate docking conformations characterized by favorable shape complementarity and negative Atomic Contact Energy (ACE) values.This provides a computationally predicted structural model for future experimental characterization.

papers.title: Mechanisms of N2 Production from N-doped Graphenes under Temperature-Programmed Desorption Analysis: A Computational Study
papers.abstract: Temperature-programmed desorption experiments have shown the release of N 2 originating from graphitic N atoms in nitrogen-doped graphenes. However, the microscopic mechanism of this desorption remains unclear. In this study, quantum chemical calculations based on density functional theory were employed to explore reaction pathways for the formation and desorption of N 2 . The calculations revealed that N atoms can migrate within the graphene lattice via repeated Stone–Wales type rearrangement involving the exchange of C–N bonds, resulting in association of two N atoms leading to desorption as an N 2 molecule. Natural bond orbital analysis reveals that this process is facilitated by the relative weakness of bonds involving nitrogen in the graphene lattice. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations for the overall reaction kinetics further supported this picture.

papers.title: Shear viscosity of liquid Sb and Bi from pseudopotential theory: the temperature-insensitive soft-tail component
papers.abstract: For liquid-metal viscosity computed with the Bretonnet–Silbert (BS) pseudopotential and Rice–Allnatt transport theory, it is unclear which of the kinetic, hard-core, and soft-tail components controls the temperature dependence. We compute the shear viscosity η ( T ) of liquid Sb and Bi from each melting point to at least 500K above it, using five local-field corrections and the Zahid pseudopotential parameters, and resolve the temperature gradient | dη / dT | into these three components. The soft-tail component ηs accounts for 54–59% of the total viscosity but barely changes with temperature, so the calculated gradient is systematically too weak: η is underestimated at the melting point (−16% for Sb, −32% for Bi) and overestimated at high temperature, crossing the reference data near 1025K (Sb) and 850K (Bi). Because η s is an integral over the pair structure g ( r ), replacing the hardsphere form g HS ( r ) with a modified hypernetted-chain (MHNC) one raises η s by 7–21% but does not recover the gradient; across the hard-sphere and MHNC closures tested here, improving the static pair structure alone leaves the slope deficit largely unchanged, pointing to the Rice–Allnatt decomposition rather than these g ( r ) models. The local-field correction changes η by only 3–4%, an order of magnitude less than the spread induced by the nonunique BS parameters; the sparse ab initio molecular-dynamics data do not contradict this weaker-than-experiment gradient. These results delimit the static, pairwise framework for Sb and Bi and provide a component-resolved benchmark for dynamic or many-body extensions of liquid-metal transport theory.

papers.title: First-Principles Analysis of Protonation-Induced Electronic Effects in Tetrakis(p-aminophenyl)porphyrin (TAPP)
papers.abstract: The optical response of pH-sensitive porphyrins depends critically on where protonation occurs, not merely on the total charge accumulated. Using first-principle linear response theory, we systematically map all symmetry-distinct protonation states of tetrakis(p-aminophenyl)porphyrin (TAPP) from neutral to fully protonated (+6), revealing that peripheral and core protonation produce qualitatively different photophysical outcomes. Peripheral protonation preserves the Soret band character with minor shifts, while core protonation drives conformer convergence, symmetry-breaking Soret splitting, and selective Q-band collapse. Q-band oscillator strength evolves non-monotonically ─ increasing initially through orbital mixing before weakening as charge-transfer character emerges. At intermediate protonation (+4/+5), remaining unprotonated aminophenyl groups act as donors in aminophenyl to macrocycle charge-transfer (CT) excitations, identified through charge-density difference (CDD) analysis. Core protonation additionally widens the singlet-triplet gap relative to peripheral protonation, with implications for intersystem crossing and triplet-state engineering. Together, these results establish protonation topology as a molecular design parameter for controlling absorption, charge transfer, and excited-state properties in pH-responsive porphyrin systems.

papers.title: A Generalized Theory for the Structural and Spatial Mapping of Energy, Entropy, and Free Energy
4CzIPN Photosensitizes the Cobaloxime-catalyzed Light-Driven Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: TADF compounds have found great application as photocatalyst in recent years. Their use as photosensitizers (PS), however, is still limited although they have a huge potential as abundant alternatives for traditional noble metal-based PSs, such as [Ru(bpy) 3 ] 2+ . We herein investigate the TADF compound 4CzIPN as a PS together with the catalyst cobaloxime (Co(dmgH) 2 (py)Cl) in the photochemical hydrogen-evolution reaction (HER). Systematic optimization of the solvent composition, 4CzIPN concentration, catalyst concentration, and sacrificial electron donor identified ammonium ascorbate as the most effective SED under the conditions tested. Under optimized conditions, the system reached a TON of 6451 ± 82 after 20 h irradiation. Stern-Volmer quenching experiments and scalar-relativistic quantum-chemical calculations provided rate constants for the different processes in the photosensitization mechanism, demonstrating that the quenching of the excited singlet state (S 1 ) of 4CzIPN by ammonium ascorbate is by far more dominant than the quenching of its excited triplet state (T 1 ). This work demonstrates that 4CzIPN can sensitize the cobaloxime-catalyzed light-driven HER with ammonium ascorbate as the SED and provides mechanistic insight into the role of singlet- and triplet-state quenching in TADF photosensitization.

papers.title: Triple Catalytic Markovnikov Hydrophosphorylation of Unactivated Olefins via Water-Mediated Radical-Polar Crossover Rearrangement of Phosphinites
papers.abstract: Organophosphoryls play crucial roles in biochemistry, materials and catalysis. The phosphorylation of alkenes offers a diverse handle for obtaining such compounds, but its regioselectivity still faces challenges, especially the Markovnikov hydrophosphorylation of alkenes. Herein, we develop a radical Markovnikov hydrophosphorylation of unactivated alkenes for the first time by a sequential reaction of (bis)homoallylic alcohols, Ph2PCl, and water under visible light-driven triple catalysis. The protocol initiates from a Co-H species-mediated metal-hydride atom transfer, followed by an unprecedented water-mediated radical-polar crossover phosphinite rearrangement. This reaction features mild reaction conditions, excellent regio-/stereoselectivity, and good natural products compatibility. The successful radical deuterophosphonation of olefins by using D2O to replace H2O further demonstrates the synthetic value of the protocol. This protocol not only broadens the new mode of phosphinite rearrangement, but also provides a successful example for the radical activation of water and its three-atom splitting and utilization in organic conversion.

papers.title: Armstrong's Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM)
papers.abstract: Traditional electron-configuration notation (e.g., 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6) represents multi-electron systems using integer orbital occupations that reflect dominant configurations but do not explicitly encode the multi-configurational nature of correlated electronic states. In wavefunction-based electronic structure theory, the electronic state is expressed as a linear combination of configurations, each assigning integer electron occupations to orbitals and contributing with a finite coefficient. Standard notation typically reflects only the dominant configuration, while the underlying distribution of contributing configurations remains implicit. This work introduces Armstrong’s Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM), a representational framework that replaces fixed integer occupations with bounded intervals derived from the configuration interaction expansion of the electronic wavefunction. For each subshell, AREECM determines minimum and maximum occupation numbers nMin​ and nMax, over a selected configuration support set defined by a cumulative weight threshold. These are normalized by the total electron count Z, yielding fractional bounds PMin=nMinZ, PMax=nMaxZ expressed in the form nl^Z*[PMin, PMax]v where the suffix v encodes the support-selection criterion. AREECM provides a compact representation of configurational variability within standard electronic structure descriptions without modifying underlying quantum mechanical formalism. It encodes the range of subshell occupations implied by the wavefunction while remaining compatible with conventional electron-configuration notation.

papers.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of 2,4-Disubstituted Homocubanes as meta-Benzene Bioisosteres
papers.abstract: Rigid polycyclic hydrocarbons are valuable substitutes (bioisosteres) for benzene rings because they often confer improved physicochemical properties upon drug candidates. Disubstituted cubanes are ideally suited as benzene bioisosteres but their broader application is limited by their challenging synthesis, particularly of 1,3-disubstituted cubanes, which mimic meta -benzenes. Furthermore, cubanes are incompatible with many transition-metal-mediated transformations because of their propensity to undergo valence isomerization. Despite their close structural similarity to cubanes, homocubanes have remained largely unexplored as benzene bioisosteres. Unlike the corresponding cubanes, many disubstituted homocubanes are inherently chiral, providing access to stereochemically defined analogues whose configuration may influence binding interactions with chiral biological targets. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of 2,4-disubstituted homocubanes and validate these scaffolds as chiral meta -benzene bioisosteres. A versatile enol triflate intermediate can undergo previously unknown one-pot Suzuki or Sonogashira coupling/[2+2] cycloadditions, enabling rapid access to (hetero)aryl- or alkynyl-substituted homocubanes. Additionally, various other cross-coupling reactions ultimately provide alkyl-, carbonyl-, or heteroatom-substituted derivatives. Homocubane analogues of the anticancer drugs ponatinib and sonidegib were prepared in both enantiomeric forms, which revealed substantial stereochemistry-dependent differences in kinase inhibition and metabolic stability. These results establish homocubanes as accessible and versatile tools for medicinal chemistry as chiral analogues of cubanes and benzenes.

papers.title: P2MAT: A machine learning (ML) driven software for Property Prediction of MATerial
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of melting points for pure molecules remains a significant challenge in predictive chemistry, with implications across various scientific fields, including materials science, drug discovery, and separations chemistry. Traditional methods, such as group contribution (GC) techniques, have shown limited success due to the complex relationship between molecular structure and melting point. In this study, we present a data-driven machine learning (ML) approach to predict the melting points of organic compounds, leveraging both 2D and 3D molecular descriptors. Our dataset comprises 19,811 compounds with 2D features and a subset of 4,568 compounds with additional 3D features. We employed feature selection methods, including pair-wise correlation, Boruta, and principal component analysis, to refine our feature set. Various ML models, including linear regression, ensemble-based regression (Random Forest, gradient- boosted regression, Extreme gradient-boosted regression), support vector regression, and deep learning, were evaluated for their predictive performance. The Extreme Gradient Boosted Regression (XGBR) model demonstrated superior performance with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 27.64 K for 2D features and 31.58 K for combined 2D and 3D features. Outlier detection and removal further improved model accuracy. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis provided insights into feature importance, enhancing model interpretability. Our results indicate that ML models, particularly XGBR, can significantly improve melting point predictions, offering a robust tool for the scientific community. Scientific Contribution: The P2MAT application capable to predict both melting point and boiling point from SMILEs string as inputs. The GUI is simple and easy to load in the system.

papers.title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Autonomous experimentation offers an time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction, by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by human’s chemistry insights, a chemistry-infused bandit was established to reflect the locally quadratic relationships between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit reveals how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near those optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-boxed ones. Incorporating chemistry insights into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework of autonomous investigation advancing the catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

papers.title: Latent mechanism mapping in self-driving molecular electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Multiple experimental parameters can contribute to catalytic activity in complex systems; however, uncovering hidden synergistic contribution among individual species is challenging, if not infeasible experimentally via the conventional one-variable-a-time approach. Deploying a chemistry-informed machine learning model in a self-driving laboratory addresses this challenge by accelerating discovery and providing interpretable mechanism-based explanations for synergistic interactions. Here we report the mapping of latent mechanistic interactions in autonomous electrocatalysis driven by a chemistry-informed reinforcement learning model. The model successfully improves the catalytic activities by more than one order of magnitude for homogenous, molecular electrocatalytic reduction of carbon dioxide. It also elucidates new, unexpected emergent phenomena with mechanistic interpretability in a high-dimensional parameter space. Closed-loop inquiry driven by a chemistry-informed model can simultaneously optimize catalysis performance and maps otherwise hidden mechanisms, advancing our understanding of complex systems.

papers.title: Assessing Environmental Impacts of Multi-Step Synthetic Protocols in Material Sciences at Various Technology Levels
papers.abstract: Environmental awareness is increasing worldwide, driven by alarming developments such as the climate change. Therefore, counteractions to slow down or even reduce these negative impacts have been undertaken. This holds true also in areas such as material sciences. Life cycle assessment (LCA) provides a standardized framework to evaluate environmental impacts. While LCAs are widely used for mature technologies, application in early-stage materials research remains limited despite its high potential for sustainable improvements. This article introduces a broadly applicable formalism referred to as Environmental Synthesis Radar (ESR) to systematically evaluate the environmental impacts of multi-step chemical synthesis protocols. ESR goes beyond the typical consideration of only one particular environmental aspect (e.g. “global warming”), but rather considers 18 midpoint impact categories (MICs), and thus yields a much more holistic and conclusive view. Normalization of the individual impacts to the global annual environmental emissions per capita, i.e., the worldwide annual environmental emissions divided by the world’s population, enables comparability of results across different MICs and facilitates contextualized interpretation. We obtain three important environmental metrics: (i) the per capita annual environmental output Vtotal, a single number for comparison of different materials and contextualized interpretation; (ii) the environmental fingerprint VEF for identification of the most impactful MICs, and (iii) the process radar VPR, which allows identification of environmentally critical synthesis steps and substances. Exemplarily, the ESR formalism is applied to two cathode material classes for use in secondary batteries: an organic material based on tris-(p-methoxy)-phenylamines (TPA) and an inorganic reference based on lithiated nickel-manganese-cobalt oxide (NMC). ESR indicates that the impact of synthesizing 1 kg of these materials is a factor of 3 (TPA) or 18 (NMC) below the global annual environmental emissions per capita, indicating that both are environmentally quite harmful. In both cases, the midpoint impact category (MIC) “Human toxicity – cancer” features the largest environmental burden, which we attribute to the use of environmentally harmful chemicals. On the other hand, the laboratory synthesis of TPA is about one order of magnitude more harmful than the industrial production of NMC. However, the organic synthesis can be improved to similar levels as NMC by considering less harmful synthesis routes and upscaling. Using our results obtained for NMC we estimate the environmental impact of LIB production in 2024 to be ~1% of the global annual environmental emissions. The global energy demand is currently steeply increasing, and to maintain leverage regarding the environmental hasards risk management tools should be implemented at the earliest stages. Assessments such as the ESR formalism we introduced here, combining perspectives from synthetic chemistry and LCA (business chemistry), will become more important. Importantly, ESR can be applied independently of the field of application, the material specifics, and the maturity of the technology. Therefore, it provides an easily accessible and very versatile tool for researchers – academic as well as in industry - to evaluate and improve environmental performance of a material synthesis/production at an early stage when there is still lots of leverage. Importantly, it takes into account the holistic view of 18 MICs.

papers.title: Metal-free Csp2-Csp3 coupling to synthesize benzylic quaternary centers
papers.abstract: Synthesis of benzylic quaternary centres remains challenging. The coupling of malonate pronucleophiles with diaryliodonium electrophiles is a potential solution, but limited in scope. Herein, we describe conditions that use unsymmetrical aryl(TMP)iodonium salts, a sustainable solvent and mild base, which is safer than related methods and less wasteful than metal-mediated reactions.

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis in Complex Reaction Systems: The Role of USTAR in High-Resolution NMR Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) has played an essential role in real-time monitoring of reaction systems. However, accurate quantification of complex reactions remains challenging due to issues such as spectral overlap mainly due to structural similarities between reactants and products, low product concentrations resulting in insufficient sensitivity, and magnetic field inhomogeneity during the reaction. We here report a selective pure shift pulse sequence, named U-STAR, which removes all scalar coupling splitting while selectively extracting target resonances from overlapping signals. U-STAR offers extremely narrow linewidths, close to the limit dictated by the transverse relaxation, and up to an order-of-magnitude increase in sensitivity over conventional single-pulse 1D 1H spectroscopy, enabling accurate spectral quantification even under severe peak overlap. The method requires only a few seconds to acquire a spectrum, rendering it ideally suited for reaction monitoring. It was successfully applied across multiple complex reaction systems, including dynamic kefir fermentation processes, polymerization reactions, and electrochemical oxidation. The results show that the USTAR consistently enables monitoring and quantifying a wide range of dynamic systems with high selectivity, sensitivity, and accuracy. This will greatly expand the capabilities of in situ NMR spectroscopy for investigating complex chemical reactions.

papers.title: Charge Localization is the Key to Designing Wurtzite Ferroelectrics Through Heterovalent Alloying
papers.abstract: Heterovalent alloying is a promising strategy to lower the coercive field of wurtzite ferroelectrics, yet it is often presumed to introduce electronic conductivity. Here, we demonstrate that the insulating character of Al1−xMxN alloys (M is a heterovalent cation) is controlled by charge localization rather than charge compensation by Al vacancies. Hybrid DFT calculations of Al1−xHfxN show that Hf d orbitals hybridize with N(p) orbitals to form deep localized states that both preserve insulation and reduce the polarization switching barrier. This mechanism is indirectly supported by the predicted low switching barrier at x = 0.056, in excellent agreement with experimental reports of ferroelectric switching near ∼6 at.% Hf. The behavior generalizes across group-4 heterovalent cations: the localized state becomes deeper from 5d ≈ 4d → 3d, leading to progressively stronger localization for Hf, Zr, and Ti. In contrast, Mg and Si, which lack d orbitals, produce relatively shallower and more delocalized states that increases electronic leakage. These findings highlight that strict charge neutrality (isovalent alloying) is not required to maintain insulation in ferroelectric nitrides and establish charge localization as the key design principle for heterovalent alloying. They also provide a unifying explanation for the well-known challenges of doping wideand ultrawide-bandgap nitride semiconductors. This insight expands the accessible chemical design space for wurtzite ferroelectrics.

papers.title: Rapid chromatography combined with trapped ion mobility mass spectrometry for analysis of derivatized small molecules
Nonlinear Root-Finding via Integrated Geometric Damping and Post-Step Residual Corrections: Theory, High-Order Convergence, and Applications
papers.abstract: Standard Newton-Raphson iterations frequently fail when applied globally due to catastrophic overshooting, stable limit cycles, or divergence near stationary points where the first derivative vanishes. Traditional globalisation remedies rely on iterative line searches or trust-region subproblems that incur high function-evaluation overhead. This paper presents a closed-form, dual-stage modification that ensures global boundedness while accelerating local convergence. First, a pre-step Geometric-Series Damping Framework utilises a dimensionless, scale-invariant nonlinearity metric t = −F (x)/[xF ′(x)] to truncate excessive step lengths under non-local initialisation without supplementary function calls. Second, a Post-Step Adaptive Residual-Ratio Correction monitors the local error using a normalised index evaluated immediately following a tentative update. For the design parameter p = 2, we prove that this rational adjustment produces a fourth-order local convergence rate (O(e4k−1)) over the baseline prior state xk−1, matching the classical Newton efficiency index (41/4 ≈ 1.4142). Numerical benchmarking across non-convex, transcendental, and ill-conditioned systems confirms that this dual formulation expands complex basins of attraction and guarantees numerical stability relative to existing high-order root-finders.

papers.title: Solubility Profiling of Therapeutic Peptides by Taylor Dispersion Induced Precipitation using Nanoliter Sample Volumes
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides are emerging as an important class of pharmaceutical compounds able to bridge the gap between small molecules and large biologics. Although modern peptide synthesis protocols have significantly increased the throughput of drug discovery, developability assessment remains both material- and labour-intensive, creating a bottleneck in development pipelines. Here we present an automated micro-capillary solubility assay able to quantify peptide solubility using only a few µg of product from a single stock solution of either aqueous or DMSO-solubilized peptide, thereby minimising laborious sample preparation. We demonstrate its utility with two families of therapeutic peptides: dual GLP1/glucagon agonists and Y2 peptide agonists. Beyond solubility assessment, the methodology generates additional data on self-association, stability in ionic solutions and identifies glass-surface binding compounds. Combined, this information allows to identify types of oligomerization behaviour both within and across the peptide families, rationalizing differences in solubility and biophysical properties. This platform therefore represents a valuable novel tool in early screening and characterization.

papers.title: Stability and Thermophysical Properties of Solid and Molten BeF2 via Density Functional Theory and Machine Learning Potentials
papers.abstract: Beryllium fluoride is a key component of molten salt mixtures for next-generation nuclear reactors. Despite its importance, reliable experimental data on its thermophysical and thermochemical properties remain scarce, and predictive modeling is complicated by the slow structural relaxation of its highly viscous melt. Here, we investigate the structural stability and thermophysical behavior of BeF 2 across solid and liquid phases using a combination of density functional theory (DFT) methods and two architectures of machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). For crystalline BeF 2 , we compare polymorph stabilities predicted by density functional theory and MLIPs, highlighting the critical role of dispersion corrections in stabilizing the α-quartz phase at 0 K and the ability of MLIPs trained exclusively on molten state configurations to accurately reproduce the relative stability of various polymorphs. MLIP-based simulations are then extended to molten BeF 2 , whose high viscosity and network-forming character require trajectories on the order of tens of nanoseconds to obtain converged properties. Employing the hybrid PBE0-D3 functional, compared to the semilocal PBE-D3 functional, systematically improves agreement with experimental density, ionic conductivity, and heat capacity for molten BeF 2 . Overall, this work demonstrates the potential of machine learning-driven simulations for predictive modeling of BeF 2 across phases and provides a useful reference point for future studies of complex multicomponent fluoride systems.

papers.title: Environmental fate of carbapenem antibiotics: analytical challenges, transformation product identification, and implications for antimicrobial resistance
papers.abstract: Carbapenems are last-resort antibiotics used to treat severe infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. Despite their clinical importance and documented consumption, they remain largely undetected in environmental monitoring studies. This study investigated whether the lack of detection of carbapenems in environmental studies reflects analytical limitations, rapid degradation, or both. Sensitive LC–MS/MS methods were developed for selected carbapenems and used to assess compound stability under analytical and environmentally relevant conditions. All investigated carbapenems exhibited limited stability, with degradation strongly accelerated by methanol. Under environmentally relevant conditions, parent compounds degraded rapidly in river water, biofilm-containing water, and UV-exposed water, with little difference between treatments. High-resolution LC–MS/MS analysis revealed formation of multiple transformation products (TPs) re-taining an intact β-lactam ring. Meropenem generated five β-lactam-retaining TPs, and faropenem generated four, several of which remained detectable long after disappearance of the parent compounds. These findings help explain the lack of detection of carbapenems in environmental surveys and demonstrate that dis-appearance of parent compounds does not necessarily imply elimination of β-lactam-containing structures. The persistence of β-lactam-retaining TPs suggests that environmental exposure and associated selective pressure may persist after parent carbapenems have degraded, highlighting the need for further investigation of their biological activity and potential role in antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Bridging Bulk and Surface Thermodynamics: A Hybrid Pourbaix Framework for Electrocatalyst Stability
papers.abstract: The long-term durability of electrocatalysts remains a central challenge, particularly for non-precious metal catalysts that often exhibit high activity but suffer from rapid degradation under practical operating conditions. A major degradation pathway is the dissolution of active metal sites as ionic or oxidized species at the surface-electrolyte interface, which remains difficult to capture using conventional computational approaches. Here, we introduce the hybrid Pourbaix diagram as a unified framework that integrates bulk and surface thermodynamics to assess the stability of surface metal atoms against dissolution, the redox behavior of adsorbates under electrochemical conditions, and the ion (de)intercalation from and into the crystal lattice. By combining density functional theory (DFT) calculations of such surface phenomena with experimentally reported bulk thermodynamic data, the hybrid Pourbaix diagram describes pH- and potential-dependent stability across surface-bound and dissolved states. The framework is flexible to incorporate grand-canonical (GC) DFT to account for potential-dependent electronic effects and applicable to different types of systems and reactions. We demonstrate the versatility of this approach through representative case studies including Ti–N–C for nitrate reduction, Fe–N–C for oxygen reduction with potential-induced spin-state transitions, and ⍺-K0.125MnO2 surfaces involving Mn dissolution and K+ deinsertion. The hybrid Pourbaix diagram provides a practical platform for analyzing catalyst stability and activation, guiding the design of durable and active electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Phosphorescent Surface-Anchored-Metal-Organic-Frameworks for Optical Sensing of Oxygen
papers.abstract: Thin metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) films, known as surface-anchored metal-organic frameworks (SURMOFs), offer convenient handling and a variety of new applications due to the direct immobilization of porous crystalline materials on various substrates. In this study, we demonstrate the feasibility of using luminescent SURMOFs for optical sensing of oxygen both in the gas phase and in organic solvents. Luminescent SURMOFs were prepared from indium(III) chloride and platinum(II) tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin on pre-treated transparent substrates, such as rigid glass or flexible poly(ethylene terephthalate). These SURMOFs have an average thickness of ~350 nm and exhibit room-temperature phosphorescence (λmax = 645–676 nm). This phosphorescence is efficiently quenched by molecular oxygen in the gas phase (I0/Iair ~50, Stern-Volmer constant KSV ~4–13 kPa−1). Generally, the sensitivity does not correlate with the morphology (revealed by scanning electron microscopy) or degree of crystallinity (accessed by grazing-incidence wide angle X-ray scattering) of the porous films. Additionally, it has been demonstrated that the SURMOFs exhibit luminescence in toluene, which is quenched by oxygen (I0/Iair ~ 2.5, KSV ~ 0.18 kPa-1). While optical oxygen sensing in organic solvents remains a significant challenge, the presented approach offers a viable solution, provided that future research can mitigate fast SURMOF photodegradation under continuous irradiation.

papers.title: Sustainable transformation of lignin major motifs to designable room temperature phosphorescence materials
papers.abstract: Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have emerged as promising platforms for information encryption owing to their unique afterglow characteristics. However, traditional fossil-based RTP systems are limited by poor sustainability and processability. Constructing biomass-derived RTP (BioRTP) materials which bridge the renewable nature of biomass with the structural versatility of synergistic phosphorescent motifs- represents a synergistic and sustainable strategy. Herein, we develop a two-step sustainable strategy to construct high-performance BioRTP systems. First, classical carbazole-benzophenone-based BioRTP luminogens are efficiently synthesized from lignin β-O-4 motifs via high-yield cascade catalytic reactions. Mechanistic investigations reveal the efficient intersystem crossing and suppressed molecular motion for the prominent RTP emission. Second, BioRTP films with three seconds of afterglow property have been fabricated using nature-based sodium carboxymethyl cellulose as matrix. Systematic investigation proves its stronger confinement effects over conventional petroleum-based polymers due to the dense hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic networks. Benefiting from the intrinsic polarity and hygroscopicity of cellulose, the biofilms present humidity and thermo reversibility, hence providing a multicolor anti-counterfeiting platform. As expected, this integrated biomass-based approach bridges sustainability with structural designability, advancing the high-value utilization of lignin.

papers.title: Disentangling the Roles of Covalent and Noncovalent Forces in Excimer Stabilization
papers.abstract: This work elucidates the physical origins of excimer stabilization in aromatic and raregas systems by jointly analyzing intermolecular noncovalent interactions and electron delocalization. Deformation Density–based Energy Decomposition Analysis (DD-EDA) is extended to excited states within single-reference frameworks, specifically Equation-Of-Motion Coupled Cluster (EOM-CC) and Time Dependent Density Function Theory (TD-DFT), enabling rigorous partitioning of interaction energies into electrostatic, exchange, spin-repulsion, induction, and dispersion contributions. For rare-gas excimers (Ne, Ar, Kr), a systematic assessment of basis set effects was also performed. In these excimers, excitonic coupling leads to a pronounced enhancement of polarization energy, only partially attributable to dispersion. In polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (benzene, naphthalene, anthracene, pyrene), dispersion increases significantly upon excitation and dominates stabilization; however, it alone does not account for the observed binding strength. Instead, DD-EDA reveals a disproportionate increase in intermolecular exchange relative to spin-repulsion, a feature absent in rare-gas systems. Domain-Averaged Fermi Hole and delocalization indexes analyses further uncover the emergence of covalent character. Rare-gas excimers exhibit substantial electron sharing driven by excitonic resonance, whereas aromatic excimers show pronounced interfacial delocalization, in contrast to the weak or negative delocalization in ground-state dimers. Overall, excimer stabilization is shown to arise from a synergistic interplay between enhanced noncovalent interactions and intermolecular electron delocalization, providing a refined framework for understanding excited-state intermolecular bonding.

papers.title: Porphyrin-based molecular wires: From polaron delocalization to phase-coherent single-molecule transport — a Woodward Career Award paper
papers.abstract: Molecular wires are the most fundamental type of single-molecule electronic device and they are the components of organic semiconductors. Porphyrins are excellent building blocks for constructing molecular wires because their small reorganization energies and rich redox activity lead to low barriers for charge transport. This short review summarizes work on three types of porphyrin-based molecular wires: (a) axially coordinated shish-kebab complexes, (b) alkyne-linked chains, and (c) edge-fused nanoribbons. The techniques used to probe wire-like behavior are introduced, including single-molecule conductance measurements, and non-contact ensemble measurements, such as time-resolved microwave/terahertz spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (EPR). Experimental results indicate that edge-fused porphyrin nanoribbons, with lengths in the range 5–10 nm, are the most wire-like molecules yet created by solution-phase organic synthesis. This is evident from their highly delocalized and mobile polarons, high single-molecule conductances and their phase-coherent, wave-like charge transport.

papers.title: An AI-driven workflow for automated extraction and prediction of metal solvent extraction Guillaume Zantea, *
papers.abstract: Solvent extraction is a crucial process to purify metals from either primary or secondary sources. Modelling solvent extraction processes is a cumbersome task requiring extensive experimental work to understand the behaviour of the metal in the aqueous and organic phases. Training machine learning (ML) models on experimental solvent extraction data, allows predicting metal extraction, which helps with the process-modeling effort, the design of a new process or the synthesis of new extracting molecules. In this work, more than 18,000 data points related to the extraction of 72 metals and non-metals and 5 acids extracted with tributyl phosphate (TBP) have been gathered and used to train ML models. Among the tested approaches, the Extra Trees Regressor achieved the highest predictive accuracy, demonstrating that ensemble-based methods can outperform more complex models for solvent extraction systems, as long as sufficient and reliable experimental data are available. The training of ML models on specific subset of metals with similar properties (e.g. lanthanide series) was shown to improve accuracy of the model and its generalisation ability. A major limitation of such approaches lies in the time-consuming construction of reliable and comprehensive datasets from the literature. To address this challenge, we propose a proofof-concept multi-module framework based on large language models capable of autonomously extracting solvent extraction data from scientific publications, including numerical data embedded in figures.

papers.title: Let’s Twist Again! Precise Single-Atom Exchange Enables Selective Control of Molecular Vibrations in Donor-Acceptor Emitters, Enhancing TADF and OLED Performance
papers.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) represents the most promising pathway toward high-efficiency all-organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, conventional donor-acceptor (D-A) emitters are fundamentally limited by a critical design trade-off between minimizing the singlet-triplet energy gap (Δ E ST ) and maintaining strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) to ensure fast reverse intersystem crossing (rISC). This work addresses this limitation by employing precise single-atom exchange to selectively suppress unfavorable molecular vibrations leading to large Δ E ST , while simultaneously inducing vibrationally-assisted SOC enhancement by a moderate heavy-atom effect. By modifying the archetypal DMAC-TRZ scaffold with ortho -halogen substituents, we demonstrate that fluorination ( DMAC-diF-TRZ ) and chlorination ( DMAC-diCl-TRZ ) creates a steric hindrance and effectively "locks" the D-A dihedral angle ( θ DA ) near orthogonality to which the minimal Δ E ST corresponds. While fluorination reduces rISC activation energy ( E a ) by nearly threefold from 115 meV to 34 meV, it simultaneously decreases SOC. In contrast, DMAC-diCl-TRZ exhibits a favorable balance between low E a of 52 meV and a fourfold increased SOC facilitated by molecular vibrations involving chlorine atoms. This combination leads to a 40-fold acceleration of the rISC rate, successfully reducing the delayed fluorescence lifetime from 17.6 µs in the DMAC-TRZ to 1.1 µs in DMAC-diCl-TRZ . These molecular-level improvements translate into enhanced OLED performance, with the DMAC-diCl-TRZ based device reaching a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of 26.6% and a remarkably reduced efficiency roll-off with EQE at 25.5%, at 1000 cd m -1 (only a 4.1% reduction from EQE max ) demonstrating the formidable potential of precise vibronic engineering in next-generation optoelectronics.

papers.title: Untargeted metabolomic profiling of glioblastoma invasion using multi-modal mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumour characterized by complex metabolic mechanisms underlying its invasive behaviour. Single-cell metabolomics was performed to characterize metabolic signatures of patient-derived cellular models associated with GBM invasion using Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) and atmospheric pressure matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization-MS (APMALDI-MS). For validation and complementary analysis, a capillary-flow liquid chromatography-MS (LC-MS)-based metabolite profiling method was developed and applied. This work presents a novel integrated workflow combining OrbiSIMS, AP-MALDI-MS, and capillary-flow LC-MS for oncology applications. Across all three platforms, glycerophospholipid metabolism emerged as a consistently altered metabolic pathway, supporting its involvement in GBM invasion. Additional metabolic alterations suggested that invaded cells undergo metabolic reprogramming during the invasion process, including changes in energy metabolism, extracellular matrix modification, and membrane composition, whereas non-invaded cells tended to maintain cellular homeostasis. Moreover, pharmacological inhibition of glycerophospholipid metabolism suppressed GBM invasion, further supporting its functional role in driving tumour invasion.

papers.title: Ensemble-Based Descriptor Analysis of Flexible Odorants: Conformational Landscapes of Geraniol, Nerol, and Linalool
papers.abstract: Conformational flexibility remains a central challenge in the molecular modeling of odorants, because thermally accessible structures may differ from the potential-energy minima identified in conformational searches. Here, we combine automated conformational exploration, multistructural thermodynamics, and descriptor-based statistical analysis to characterize the conformational ensembles of three flexible acyclic terpenic alcohols: geraniol, nerol, and linalool. The conformational searches identify large numbers of minima for the three systems, but only a subset of these structures contributes substantially to the finite-temperature equilibrium ensemble. In all cases, the Gibbs free-energy minima at 310 K differ from the corresponding potential-energy minima, showing that electronically favored compact conformers can be outcompeted by more extended arrangements through entropy-related contributions. Descriptor–energy correlation analyses further show that thermodynamic stabilization is most consistently associated with global shape descriptors, particularly the radius of gyration, rather than with individual local hydroxyl-mediated contact descriptors. Principal component and clustering analyses reveal that the ensembles are better described as continuous conformational landscapes than as sharply separated structural families. The coupling between molecular extension, global compactness, and shape anisotropy depends on molecular topology, with branched linalool displaying the most heterogeneous organization. These results highlight the limitations of relying only on potential-energy minima and support the use of ensemble-based, descriptor-guided molecular modeling strategies for flexible odorants and related acyclic terpenoids.

papers.title: Supramolecular Polymerization into Pyramidal π-Assemblies Enabling Single-Assembly Level Transistors
papers.abstract: While solution-phase supramolecular polymerization yields diverse organic semiconducting π-architectures, evaluating their intrinsic electronic properties at the single-assembly level in the solid state remains challenging. Here, we report the hierarchical supramolecular polymerization of a tetrabenzoporphyrin derivative into discrete pyramidal π-assemblies in solution and their subsequent integration into single-pyramid field-effect transistors. Kinetic and structural tuning during polymerization yielded macroscopic, easily handleable pyramids (> 50 µm in width) ideal for the device fabrication. Owing to the high dispersibility and structural stability of these pyramids, single-pyramid transistors were successfully fabricated via simple drop-casting and solvent evaporation, enabling the direct elucidation of individual p-type charge transport characteristics. This strategy unveils the intrinsic semiconductor properties of pre-organized supramolecular architectures, opening new avenues in supramolecular electronics.

papers.title: Pathway-Resolved Observable Memory Reveals Hidden Mediation from Sparse Conformational Measurements
papers.abstract: Biomolecular conformational transitions are often monitored through a small number of observables, leading to memory functions due to the fact the underlying dynamics involve many coupled and hidden degrees of freedom. Here we discuss extraction of memory from molecular simulation data with a transfer tensor approach. We then use a hierarchy of models to examine what mechanistic information can be gleaned from the extracted memory. An analytically solvable model that involves coupled harmonic oscillators shows how memory modes encode local and shared hidden-bath couplings in an ideal limit. A nonlinear double-well potential coupled bilinearly to a harmonic bath provides an analytical Zwanzig memory kernel, which we compare with transfer tensors extracted from trajectory data to distinguish physical bath friction from projection-dependent observable memory. With a three-coordinate conformational model, we then show that monitoring multiple observables converts scalar memory analysis into a pathway-resolved description of delayed influence among measured coordinates. Variations in barrier height, bath time scales, observable set, and system-bath coupling patterns indicate that pathway power is more robust than assigning global memory periods to individual hidden modes. A hidden-mediator variant further highlights that pathway-resolved memory can reveal delayed communication produced by unobserved mediators. These results motivate observable-memory analysis as a framework for extracting mechanistic information from sparse experimental or simulation measurements, particularly in allosteric systems where hidden mediation and delayed communication are central to function.

papers.title: Cell-laden chitosan 3D bioprinting with the unmodified biopolymer of structural units glucosamine and N-acetylglucosamine to advance bioactive chitosan-based hydrogel tissue models
papers.abstract: Chitosan (CHI) offers tremendous potential for 3D tissue engineering owing to its bioactivity, biocompatibility and biodegradability. This biopolymer can be positively charged, which allows electrostatically interaction with cell membrane and modulation of biological response in cell/biomaterial tissue models and in vivo. Chitosan is a copolymer of glucosamine (GlcN) and N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc), normally soluble in weakly acidic media which is not compatible for cell survival. This work describes the development of liquid CHI bioinks containing cells and their 3D bioprinting into cell-laden chitosan-based hydrogels. A strategy was pursued to achieve solubilization of unmodified chitosan (of GlcN and GlcNAc units) at pHs ∼7 for good compatibility with cells. To this end, random reacetylation of fully deacetylated chitosan was performed. A series of CHI copolymers of varying degrees of acetylation (DA) and high molar masses was obtained. CHI solubility at physiological conditions and incorporation of cells in liquid bioinks was achieved. The physical-chemistry of solubilization of high molar mass chitosans of varying DAs and the rheological behavior were investigated. The 3D bioprinting of cell-laden chitosan-based hydrogels and corresponding cell culture studies were performed. Hydrogels were constructed due to chitosan ionotropic gelation and/or polyelectrolyte complex formation by conventional microextrusion or coaxial core-shell bioprinting, respectively.

papers.title: Active-site electric field tuning unlocks full decarboxylation chemoselectivity in cytochrome P450 OleT
papers.abstract: Electrostatic effects on enzymatic rate acceleration has been well-documented, yet their role in selectivity control remains poorly understood. Here, using cytochrome P450 OleT as a model system, we demonstrate computationally that the chemoselectivity between fatty acid decarboxylation and β-hydroxylation can be precisely controlled by tuning the active-site electric field. Multiscale calculations reveal the synergistic origins of OleT’s atypical decarboxylase reactivity: the intrinsic active-site electric field, aligned along the Fe → O direction of its active species (Compound I), facilitates decarboxylation, whereas hydrogen bonding to the iron(IV)-hydroxo group destabilizes the competing hydroxylation pathway. Furthermore, oriented electric-field calculations show that strengthening the local field preferentially accelerates decarboxylation, owing to the significantly greater charge redistribution character during the decarboxylation reaction. An additional field of 10 MV/cm is sufficient to create absolute chemoselectivity toward decarboxylation. This work highlights electric fields as versatile “smart reagents” for precise selectivity control in biocatalytic enzymes, and further broadens the application scope of electrostatic catalysis.

papers.title: Ring sliding dynamics of single-and double-threaded cyclodextrin-polyethylene glycol polyrotaxane slide-ring polymers under tension
papers.abstract: Slide-ring materials comprising polyrotaxanes are an emerging class of soft materials composed of mechanically interlocked polymer strands threaded by macrocyclic rings. Double-threaded γ-cyclodextrin-based slide-rings in which two polymer chains are threaded through the same ring give rise to materials with exceptional extensibility and toughness that can overcome the elasticity-toughness trade-off inherent to traditional polymer architectures. However, a fundamental molecular-level understanding of how tension, ring chemistry, and threading geometry govern ring mobility remains lacking. In this work, we employ all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to model the thermodynamics and sliding dynamics of single and pairs of native and permethylated α-and γ-cyclodextrin rings on single-and double-threaded polyethylene glycol (PEG) polyrotaxanes as a function of applied tension. Double-threaded configurations, permethylated rings, and rings with stronger binding energies show consistently lower diffusivities than their single-threaded, native, and weakly bound counterparts. The 3D diffusivity of single-and double-threaded native and permethylated cyclodextrin monomers and dimers monotonically decreases with applied tension due to a reduction in the amplitude of the thermal fluctuations. Similar monotonic trends are generally preserved for 1D diffusivity along the PEG chain contour, but less sterically-constrained single-threaded native cyclodextrins in both the monomer and dimer state can exhibit non-monotonic trends due to the interplay of tension-dependent thermal fluctuation that promote mobility and the presence of backbone dihedral gauche defects that serve as a barrier to ring sliding.

papers.title: Linear Perturbation Assessment of Flow Instability in advanced Two‑Phase Natural Circulation (TPNC)Networks
papers.abstract: This research presents a comprehensive linear analysis of the instability phenomena associated with a Two-Phase Natural Circulation Loop (TPNCL). The TPNCL is characterized by distinct single-phase and two-phase regions, each comprising various segments, including downcomers, heated regions, boiling sections, risers, and steam drums. The study employs a one-dimensional framework to derive the governing equations for mass, energy, and momentum in both phases. By perturbing these equations around steady-state values, we identify the linearized forms that capture the dynamics of disturbances within the system. The analysis reveals the critical role of pressure drops across different segments, leading to the formulation of a characteristic equation for stability assessment. The solutions indicate that the stability of the loop is contingent upon the interplay between the two-phase flow dynamics and the single-phase behavior. Utilizing the Nyquist stability criterion, we explore the implications of complex roots of the characteristic equation, providing insights into potential instability scenarios. This work not only enhances the understanding of TPNCL behavior but also serves as a foundation for future investigations into the design and optimization of natural circulation systems in thermal-hydraulic applications.

papers.title: Switching between C1 and C2 Pathways via Suppressed Phase Separation in Cu–Ag Alloys for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2RR) is a promising approach for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals. Copper (Cu) catalysts uniquely enable the formation of both single-carbon products such as methane (CH4) and multi-carbon (C2+) products such as ethylene (C2H4) but achieving precise control over product selectivity remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate Cu–Ag alloy catalysts prepared by a direct sputtering method of catalysts onto gas diffusion electrodes to elucidate how atomic-scale mixing influences CO2RR selectivity. The product distribution strongly depends on the composition. A small amount of Ag doping approximately 4 at.% enhances the formation of C2+ products, whereas further increasing Ag content suppresses C2+ products formation and increases CH4 selectivity. This behavior indicates that C2+ product formation critically depends on contiguous Cu active sites, while excessive Ag doping disrupts Cu ensembles required for C–C coupling and suppresses C2+ product formation. These findings highlight the critical role of contiguous Cu site in governing CO2RR pathways and demonstrate atomic-scale structural control as an effective strategy for tuning product selectivity in alloy catalysts.

papers.title: Temperature rigidity of Rice–Allnatt viscosity across nine liquid sp metals described by the Bretonnet–Silbert pseudopotential
Study of Repetition in a Chan-Evans-Lam Reaction Dataset using Bayesian Optimisation
papers.abstract: In organic synthesis, the Chan–Evans–Lam (CEL) reaction is a widely used coupling methodology for enabling carbon–heteroatom bond formation. The process incorporates mild reaction conditions, good scope, and is complementary to other (C-N bond forming) efforts. However, CEL processes are notoriously variable, making reproducibility problematic and the identification of optimal/robust conditions a persistent challenge. In recent years, data-driven and machine learning approaches have gained prominence as efficient tools for rapidly identifying optimal and consistent reaction conditions. Generating sufficient data for machinelearning model training typically requires high-throughput experimentation (HTE). Traditionally, in a HTE campaign involving the optimisation of a chemical reaction and the establishment of a substrate scope, each set of identical experimental conditions is run in triplicate. The ‘statistical need’ for the replication of, apparently identical, conditions has not been substantially investigated.
