Given the timedependent nature of these campaigns in industry, and the broader issues of reproducibility in synthesis, there is significant worth in the assessment of the value of repetition. Here, we present an offline simulation framework to investigate replication-aware Bayesian Optimisation of chemical reactions. Our approach employs a heteroscedastic Gaussian Process surrogate model, which has been trained on replicate-level observations, where each individual measurement serves as a separate training point with per-condition noise estimates derived from available replicates. We examine how a limited experimental budget can best be distributed between exploring new reaction conditions and repeating previously tested ones. As an offline benchmark, we use an open-source CEL HTE dataset (≈ 3, 600 unique conditions in triplicate), with two objectives: 1) yield of the desired product and 2) selectivity of the desired product relative to a side-product. Our results show that, for both objectives, no replication strategy provides a statistically significant improvement over pure exploration within the available budget. Pure exploration consistently ranks among the strongest strategies, while aggressive replication (mandatory triplication) is clearly detrimental. These findings challenge the default assumption that replication is necessary when optimising under noisy HTE conditions, with broad significance for HTE and traditional one-experiment-at-a-time campaigns in the pharmaceutical and chemical industries.

papers.title: pH-Driven Actuation of Unmodified DNA Origami Rectangles
papers.abstract: DNA origami is a versatile method for constructing molecular machinery, yet many designs rely on responsive motifs or added components to achieve dynamic behaviour. Here, we show that unmodified DNA origami rectangles – one of the most widely used DNA origami structures – exhibit a reversible transition between planar and tubular states upon pH modulation. We propose that this transformation occurs due to the cooperative mechanical coupling of crossover junctions: no DNA modification, special sequences, or extra motifs are needed. The curling/uncurling response extends to connected rectangles: dimers and nanoribbons curl reversibly below pH 7 to form nanotube architectures. This unexpected conformational flexibility of monolayer DNA with pH provides a simple framework for engineering responsive nanostructures that can be transformed without chemical modification or specific sequence motifs.

papers.title: Microscopic stress in biomembranes: A perspective on key concepts, methods, and applications
papers.abstract: Cell membranes are complex assemblies of lipids, proteins, and sterols whose organization and stability arise from a delicate balance of intra and intermolecular forces, entropic effects, and external stresses. The distribution of forces within these membranes underpins their diverse functions and structural stability. The microscopic stress tensor provides a tool to connect this molecular-level force distribution to a mechanical description of the membrane. It offers a powerful framework for assessing leaflet asymmetry and for guiding molecular dynamics (MD) simulations toward accurate modeling of compositionally asymmetric bilayers. Moreover, the stress tensor bridges particle-based models with continuum mechanics, providing a feasible route for estimating key elastic moduli. Despite its promise, calculating microscopic stress in particle-based systems remains challenging due to the lack of a rigorous definition at the molecular scale. Long-range potentials and many-body interactions further complicate the stress formulation, and as a result, local stress calculations remain relatively underexplored. Existing computational approaches are largely limited to system-averaged stresses, leaving fundamental questions of force distribution and anisotropy unresolved. In this perspective, we summarize the historical development and current status of microscopic stress formulations for particle-based models, clarify major conceptual controversies, and identify methodological limitations of existing tools. Additionally, we present new data illustrating best practices for accurate stress calculation in biomembranes and discuss how force-field coarse-graining influences these outcomes. Finally, we outline emerging applications of microscopic stress analysis in studying lipid chemistry, leaflet asymmetry, small-molecule permeation, and transmembrane protein function.

papers.title: Synergistic Paramagnetic, Piezoelectric, and Chiral Optical Effects in Fe-and Mn-Hybrid Metal Halides
Interfacial Reconstruction via Ionic Liquid Additives Enables Dendrite-Free High-Temperature Lithium-Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: Lithium-metal batteries promise step-change energy density but are limited by dendritic growth and interface degradation when using traditional organic solvent-based electrolytes. These failures arise from Li ion-transport limitations and inhomogeneous local current density, which together drive uneven Li deposition. Here, we show that introducing the ionic liquid N-butyl-N-methylpyrrolidinium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (Pyr14FSI) as an additive into the benchmark carbonate electrolyte LP30 reshapes both solvation and interfacial chemistry. Pyr14FSI promotes anions to be included in the Li+ solvation shell and sustains high ionic conductivity, particularly at elevated temperatures. At the Li anode surface, bulky Pyr14+ cations reorganize the electric double layer, on one hand, influencing the composition of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) to be more inorganic, and on the other hand, maintaining a near-surface cation reservoir, which renders a uniform Li plating. This directly improves the electrochemical performance with a higher Coulombic efficiency and improved cycling stability in both Li//Cu and Li4Ti5O12//Li cells, at both room temperature and 80 °C. These results highlight ionic-liquid additives as a rational design strategy to advance towards safe, dendrite-free lithium-metal batteries.

papers.title: Evaluation of Bio-Based Solvents for Sustainable Extraction of Bioactive Constituents from Sea Buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.)
papers.abstract: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) fruits are a valuable source of bioactive compounds with potential applications in food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic formulations. In this study, the influence of extraction technique and solvent composition on the recovery of bioactive constituents from freeze-dried sea buckthorn fruits was evaluated. Three extraction methods, namely conventional maceration, ultrasound-assisted extraction, and microwave-assisted extraction, were compared using ethanol and selected bio-based solvents: Cyrene™, γvalerolactone, and ethyl lactate, applied either as pure solvents or in ethanol-based binary mixtures. The obtained extracts were assessed in terms of extraction yield, total phenolic content, antioxidant activity, carotenoid content, lipid recovery, microstructural changes of the plant matrix, and preliminary regenerative potential using a scratch assay. The results demonstrated that extraction efficiency was strongly dependent on both the solvent system and extraction technique. Microwave-assisted extraction generally provided the highest recovery of phenolic compounds, whereas ultrasound-assisted extraction offered an effective balance between extraction efficiency and process intensity. Ethanol-rich systems remained the most efficient for phenolic recovery; however, among the tested green solvents, ethyl lactate showed the most promising performance for phenolic and antioxidant extraction. In contrast, γvalerolactone was particularly effective in recovering carotenoids, while ethyl lactate-based systems favored lipid extraction. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed that ultrasound- and microwave-assisted extraction induced substantial disruption of sea buckthorn tissue, facilitating the release of intracellular metabolites. The scratch assay indicated that the Cyrene™ extract did not stimulate fibroblast migration under the applied conditions. Overall, the study demonstrates that bio-based solvent systems, particularly ethanol-ethyl lactate mixtures, represent promising sustainable alternatives for obtaining multifunctional sea buckthorn extracts enriched in hydrophilic and lipophilic bioactives.

papers.title: Predictive Design Principles in Plasma-Catalysis
papers.abstract: Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4-2 Gt CO2 yr -1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Nonthermal plasmas offer a path to decentralized, electrified production by generating vibrationally excited molecules, radicals, and ions without bulk heating of gas. Despite this potential, plasma-catalysis remains difficult to design because plasma excitation, surface reaction energetics, and intermediate removal are treated separately, and activity trends do not transfer across chemistries. This review develops a quantitative framework connecting non-equilibrium excitation, surface binding energetics, co-reactant chemistry, and surface temperature to reaction rates, selectivity, and catalyst stability. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without re-parameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.

papers.title: A Nickel-Olefin Pincer Complex as Catalyst for Aldehyde Hydrogenation under Mild Conditions via a Cooperative Mechanism
papers.abstract: The use of a Ni(0)-olefin pincer complex for the base-free catalytic hydrogenation of aldehydes under mild conditions is reported. Insights from DFT calculations complemented by isotope labeling experiments support an unusual H2 activation mechanism involving metal-ligand cooperation via ligand-to-ligand hydrogen transfer (LLHT) to the olefin moiety. In the case of the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl substrate cinnamaldehyde, the C=C bond is hydrogenated preferentially over the C=O bond, which can be assigned to a slower product-release step for C=O hydrogenation.

papers.title: Nanostructured gold electrodes with optimized properties for improved optical detection of polystyrene nanoparticles in suspension
papers.abstract: The manipulation of the surface properties of a plasmonic substrate is essential for achieving the proximity of an analyte to its surface as prerequisite for surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy. Here we studied the interaction of the five benzene derivatives 4-methylbenzene-1sulfonate, 4-vinylbenzenesulfonate, styrene (ethenylbenzene), polystyrene sulfonate (poly(4-vinylbenzenesulfonic acid)), and polystyrene (poly(1-phenylethylen)) for a plasmonic surface, with the intention to detect nanometer-sized polystyrene particles as nanoplastic model 2 analyte in suspension. Electrochemical roughening of screen-printed gold electrodes yielded cauliflower-like nanostructures that were (i) functionalized with self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) or (ii) polarized by applying static electric fields. We found that SAMs that lead to a positively charged electrode surface increased the signal intensities in SERS spectra of 4methylbenzene-1-sulfonate, 4-vinylbenzenesulfonate, polystyrene sulfonate and polystyrene nanoparticles. The detection of 4-methylbenzene-1-sulfonate and 4-vinylbenzenesulfonate was also enabled by application of a negative electrode potential. The strongest SERS signals of styrene were observed on a non-functionalized and neutrally polarized electrode surface, while the optimum spectral detection of the nanometer-sized polystyrene nanoparticles was attained with a positive potential. By electrokinetic manipulation, spectra of the nanospheres were obtained in suspension at a lowest concentration of 5 mg/L. Although the manipulation of both, the surface functionalization and the applied electric field improved the detection of the mono- and 1,4substituted benzene compounds, the electrosorption enables a more flexible and precise control over the adsorption/desorption process of the nanometer-sized polymer particles and is therefore a promising approach for the optical sensing of nanoplastics.

papers.title: Autonomous Control of Polymer Upcycling with a Self-Driving Laboratory
papers.abstract: Plastic upcycling is fundamentally limited by the vast and poorly understood reaction space associated with complex waste streams. While self-driving laboratories (SDLs) have accelerated reaction optimisation in small-molecule synthesis, their application to end-of-life materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce RoboChem-Up, a self-driving platform designed to autonomously discover and optimize polymer upcycling processes. Unlike prior SDLs focused on material synthesis, RoboChem-Up operates directly on complex polymer substrates and integrates dual inline analytics with Bayesian optimisation to navigate multi-objective landscapes. We demonstrate the platform across two orthogonal upcycling paradigms: (i) polyurethane depolymerisation, where the system identifies conditions for full degradation from complex mixtures, and (ii) polystyrene functionalisation, where it achieves targeted control over the degree of modification while minimizing chain scission. Through these case studies we show that RoboChem-Up is capable of tackling both major paradigms of polymer upcycling, monomer recovery and post-functionalisation. Overall, this work establishes autonomous experimentation as a key enabling technology for circular polymer chemistry and the transition from linear to closed-loop materials design.

papers.title: In situ spectroscopic evaluation of copper corrosion during electroreduction of CO2 amine adducts
papers.abstract: This work experimentally investigated the corrosion of a copper working electrode during the direct electrochemical conversion of captured CO 2 sources under basic conditions. The effect of using ammonium carbamate or dimethyl ammonium dimethyl carbamate as the captured CO 2 source on the observed corrosion was studied using bulk electrolysis (BE) and UV-vis or EPR spectroscopy conducted simultaneously for 24-48 hours over a range of applied voltages and captured CO 2 source concentrations. Over time during BE, a maximum in the absorbance was observed at 650 nm in the UV-vis, along with the formation of a blue color, and the appearance of an S = 1/2 signal detected in a flow spectroelectrochemical EPR system. The spectroelectrochemical experiments enabled the kinetics of the electrode corrosion to be evaluated. A distinct difference in rates was observed for ammonium carbamate versus dimethyl ammonium dimethyl carbamate. Characterization of the copper electrode prior to and post BE by atomic force microscopy, powder X-ray diffraction, and scanning electron microscopy indicated a rough surface that became smooth, with an increase in Cu(II) and oxide formation over time. Combined, these data offer insights towards copper electrode corrosion in the presence of amine-based captured CO 2 sources.

papers.title: Large Magnetic Anisotropy in a Coupled Dinuclear FeII Single-Molecule Magnet
papers.abstract: A series of [Me2indM(μ-Cl)(THF)]2 (M = Zn, Mn, Fe) dimers utilizing a novel bulky indoline ligand (Me2indH = 5-methoxy-2,2-dimethyl-3,3-diphenyl-7-diphenylmethylindoline) were synthesized and magnetically characterized. Analysis of the single crystal structure reveals each of the complexes exhibits distorted tetrahedral geometry about the metal center. Static magnetic measurements of 3-Fe demonstrate ferromagnetic coupling (J = 3.05 cm-1) between the Fe ions and an exceptionally high axial anisotropy (D = -33.8 cm-1). Theoretical investigations reveal that the magnetic anisotropy vectors of the two metal centers are largely coaxial along the metal-metal direction. Dynamic magnetic measurements display out-of-phase behavior indicating that 3-Fe acts as a single-molecule magnet with a Ueff of 43.3(5) cm-1.

papers.title: Mixed thiolate/alkoxide antimony cages for stable reversed-bilayer vesicle self-assembly
papers.abstract: A new two-step synthesis produces moisture-stable antimony and arsenic dithiothreitol cages. Structural analysis reveals that the Sb compounds self-assemble into reversed bilayers, consistent with pnictogen-bonded vesicle formation in organic media. The Sb assemblies more efficiently encapsulate and protect rhodamine B than the arsenic analogue or a topological mimic that lacks pnictogen-bonding capability. This work provides a synthetically accessible tool for partitioning organic media to allow for orthogonal reactivity.

papers.title: Synthesis and Comparison of the Properties of a Dihydrobenzo[1,3]azasilole NAMPT Inhibitor with its C-Analog
papers.abstract: Rh 2 (II)-Catalyzed C–H bond amination of 2-silyl-substituted aryl azides construct dihydrobenzo[1,3]azasiloles via an N -aryl rhodium nitrene catalytic intermediate. Potential NAMPT inhibitors were synthesized from the azasilaheterocycle and its carbon-analog to enable direct comparison of their potency, physicochemical, and ADMET properties. Despite the large ClogP difference between the C- and Si-analogs, they both exhibited similar properties except in zebrafish embryo development assays where the carbon-analog was found to be more toxic.

papers.title: Lifecycle and technoeconomic assessment of Donnan dialysis for lithium brine concentration in direct lithium extraction
papers.abstract: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from brines could help meet the growing demand for lithium needed for the global energy transition. Of the proposed DLE processes, unit operations required for lithium purification and concentration are often the most energy- and emission-intensive stages of DLE. In this work, we develop steadystate simulations of a commercial-scale DLE treatment train alongside a framework for lifecycle and technoeconomic assessment. We also simulate a novel DLE treatment train using a low energy-intensity Donnan dialysis (DD) process for lithium purification and concentration, and we compare the lifecycle impacts (specific energy consumption, embodied energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, and water use) and economics (levelized cost of product, net present value, and internal rate of return) of the conventional and novel process on a kg -1 Li 2 CO 3 product basis under six base case scenarios. We observe a clear trade-off between energy- and emission-reduction benefits of the novel process versus water use and cost. Monte Carlo simulation confirms the robustness of analysis to changes in process parameters. Simulation of a best-case scenario (optimal membrane properties and membrane cost reduction guided by federal targets) projects that the novel process could become energy-, emission-, and costcompetitive against the conventional process, though it would remain inferior in terms of water use. Ultimately, this simulation framework provides a means for DLE researchers spanning material innovation, technology development, and process design to benchmark and quantify process-level impacts of their work.

papers.title: The Transition State as a Symmetry Point in the Morphology of the Electron Density
papers.abstract: We show that the transition state is a structural feature of the electron density, corresponding to a symmetry point in its evolving morphology. This symmetry arises in the directional organization of charge within charge-transfer pathways linking reacting fragments and can be quantified using scale-invariant descriptors derived from the Hessian of the density at bond critical points. The difference in directionalities defines a natural morphological parameter, η , whose evolution tracks the redistribution of density along a reaction coordinate. Within a low-order expansion in , the energy is expressed in terms of a bias, h , and a stiffness, β , that together determine the stationary point of the system. In the symmetric limit ( h ≈ 0), this stationary point occurs at η = 0, corresponding to equal directional organization toward competing centers. When h ≠ 0, the stationary point shifts away from symmetry, reflecting a bias in the density’s reorganization. We demonstrate this behavior in a series of morphologically simple atom-transfer reactions, including oxygen transfer, hydrogen-atom transfer in heme systems, and proton transfer. In the neutral atom-transfer cases, the transition state coincides with the symmetry condition η = 0, while in proton transfer it shifts in accordance with the predicted bias. These results provide a structural interpretation of the transition state in terms of the morphology of the electron density and establish a low-dimensional framework for chemical reactivity in which electrostatic effects act through two distinct channels: variations in electrostatic potential primarily modulate β , while electric fields alter h , particularly in reactions involving charged intermediates.

papers.title: RAGMODEX: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Molecular Design and Explainable AI - Interpretable QSAR and Guided Molecular Design of GLUT-1 Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Most cancer cells fuel accelerated proliferation through aerobic glycolysis, which demands continuous high-rate glucose uptake. Glucose Transporter 1 (GLUT-1), the primary membrane transporter mediating this uptake, is overexpressed across a wide range of solid tumors and represents a tractable target for quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modelling. QSAR-guided inhibitor discovery, 2 however, is systematically compromised by two methodological pitfalls. Bit collision in folded circular fingerprints maps chemically distinct substructures to the same bit position, confounding SHapley Additive exPlanations-based feature attribution. Scaffold-based partitioning retains residual structural proximity between training and test sets, inflating generalization estimates. Here it is shown that RAGMODEX (Retrieval-Augmented Generation for MOlecular DEsign and EXplainable AI), a freely available model-agnostic cheminformatics platform, addresses both limitations and enables guided iterative molecular design driven by the patterns encoded in a trained classifier. On a scaffold-split external test set of 1,351 GLUT-1 bioactivity records from ChEMBL, a Random Forest Classifier trained on Extended Connectivity Fingerprint achieves a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.97, a Matthew’s correlation coefficient of 0.83, and a balanced accuracy of 0.92. Leave-one-UMAP-cluster-out cross-validation reduces the ROC-AUC to 0.71, a 25% relative drop confirming that scaffold-split metrics overestimate prospective performance on structurally isolated chemotypes. Accordingly, RAGMODEX is intended as a tool for local optimization within known chemical space, and its predictive reliability does not extend to scaffold-hopping or de novo discovery outside the training domain. For any generated candidate, the per-bit collision database resolves SHAP attribution to its contributing substructures, and the continuous applicability domain score tracks structural distance from the training set at every optimization step. AD validation against the external test set establishes a statistically significant correlation between AD distance and absolute prediction error (Spearman rho = 0.329, p = 6.6*10-10), and probability calibration deteriorates by approximately one third outside the threshold. Two guided design campaigns starting from GLUT-1-active scaffolds produce putative GLUT-1 inhibitor candidates with predicted activity probabilities above 0.85 and applicability domain scores above 0.40, with optimization trajectories remaining within the validated applicability domain at every step. Because RAGMODEX accepts any scikit-learn-compatible binary classifier, the platform extends directly to other therapeutic targets. All code and trained models are publicly available.

papers.title: Gaussian-Harmonic Core–Tail Carriers: From Heisenberg Saturation to the Molar Scale
papers.abstract: This work proposes an ideal counting structure connecting Fourier-Heisenberg saturation, Gaussian-harmonic coherence, and thermodynamic state countability. It asks under which minimal structural condition a normable, non-point-like wave carrier can become externally countable without being reduced to a classical point particle. Starting from Fourier duality, the Heisenberg bound is read as a statistical RMS saturation condition whose limiting form is the Gaussian wave-packet envelope. Harmonic halfaction binding selects a coherent core within this envelope, while the remaining Gaussian-referenced variance capacity defines a residual tail. The core-tail interface is bounded by the overlap of harmonic action reach and a Chebyshev-Basel variance threshold, yielding a narrow Gaussian boundary layer fixed before any molar count is introduced. To connect internal closure with external thermodynamic countability, the Sackur-Tetrode state-counting form is transformed into reduced-Compton units and represented as a closure-compatible spherical shell. This yields a continuous Compton-multiple positional projection factor 𝑛(𝑁) . Closure requires this projection to enter the independently derived Gaussian boundary layer and to become finite, self-similar, and integer-readable. A Lucas-golden trace rule is therefore introduced to focus the upper probabilistic boundary into the interface. The resulting dimensionless closure count is 𝑁 LC = 6.0011049139 × 10 23 , about 0.35% below the SI value of Avogadro's constant when read as a numerical molar count. The significance of 𝑁 LC is therefore not merely numerical. The model does not identify the immediately countable unit of natural manifestation with a classical point particle, nor with a bare Gaussian state alone, but with a core–tail carrier: a Gaussian-harmonic core closed by half-action binding and a Gaussian-referenced residual tail that makes external reconstruction possible. Internally, 𝑁 LC counts the state increments required to bind such a carrier into a closed spherical representation. Externally, the same count appears as the number of core-referenced tail complements required to reconstruct Gaussian countability at the thermodynamic ensemble level. Thus, within the ideal model, the molar scale appears as the projection count at which core–tail carriers become mutually readable as thermodynamic ensemble units. The result is not presented as a fitted derivation of 𝑁 A , but as a structural account of why a molar-scale count can mediate between microphysical closure and thermodynamic manifestation.

papers.title: Co-solvent enhanced solvation shell lability improves ion transport in Li-ion battery electrolytes
papers.abstract: Electrolytes for extreme fast charging (XFC) of Li-ion batteries must combine high ionic conductivity with favorable Li + transference, yet these transport properties are difficult to improve simultaneously in practical carbonate-based liquids. Here, we investigate a 1.2 M LiPF 6 electrolyte series based on ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and acetonitrile (ACN), in which ACN progressively replaces EMC from 0 to 40 vol%. Experiment and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that increasing ACN content raises conductivity from ∼10 to 23 mS cm −1 , lowers viscosity from 3.5 to 2.2 cP, while MD further predicts a modest increase in the Li+ transference number from 0.37 to 0.42. These transport gains exceed what is expected from viscosity reduction alone: the conductivity–viscosity product increases monotonically, whereas ionicity and ion pair fractions change only weakly. At the molecular level, not only does ACN replace EMC in the Li + first solvation shell, it remarkably shortens the residence time of all solvation shell species, thereby increasing solvation shell lability. Onsager analysis shows that ACN enhances the transport of both Li + and PF − 6 while reducing persistent Li + –PF − 6 correlated motion over transport-relevant times. Solvent-resolved correlations and PF − 6 entry/exit analyses further show that ACN promotes faster solvent exchange during local ion-pair formation and relaxation, shifting transport away from a more vehicular regime and toward a more exchange-mediated one. These results identify dynamic solvent tuning as a transport design principle for XFC-relevant electrolytes.

papers.title: Separating porous solids in water
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a new, greener and safer method of using density to separate porous materials, exploiting the concept of pressurised water intrusion. The idea is simple: external pressure can squeeze liquid molecules into porous materials, increasing their mass density and making them sink in that liquid. By selecting a particular pressure, we can leave one material floating and let the other(s) sink, thereby separating them in a mixture. In principle, this method works for any porous material, and not only for powders but also for monoliths or pellets that contain only interparticle spaces. We demonstrate the application of this principle in the separation of materials with different pore sizes, crystal sizes, and macroscopic configurations, including between structure analogues and the same materials. By controlling the kinetics of the subsequent liquid extrusion process, materials can be collected easily and safely after pressure is removed. We demonstrate that we can use water, the most abundant liquid on Earth, and a widely accessible pressure in the MPa range, to complete the separation in minutes. Relying on fundamental microscopic phenomena combined with macroscale mechanical processes, this study is an excellent example of how engineering and chemistry come together to enable science to solve problems. It has the potential to be developed into high-throughput and industrial-scale separation technologies, which could ensure high phase-purity and material consistency in applications, a driving factor in porous material research for decades.

papers.title: Two-step production of 30 wt% aqueous H2O2 from air and water by solar photocatalysis and downstream concentration
papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is widely needed for chemical synthesis, environmental remediation, and emerging energy technologies, 1-3 yet over 95% of its production relies on the energy-intensive anthraquinone process. 2,4 Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from water and oxygen (or air) offers a green alternative, 5-7 but achieving commercially concentrations (30 wt%, ~9.8 M) remains a grand challenge. 8 Herein, a two-step strategy of continuous-flow photocatalytic H 2 O 2 generation from water and air coupled with subsequent concentration is developed. In the first step, a family of composition-tuned covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts is screened, and the component-optimized catalyst COF-4 delivers the highest activity of 6.16 mmol g -1 h -1 in batch reactor and enables stable production of dilute H 2 O 2 (~1.1 mM) for over 50 hours in a lab-made flow reactor, with a solar-to-chemical conversion (SCC) efficiency of 0.13%, exceeding that of natural photosynthesis (0.1%). The system is further extended to a scaled-up panel reactor (0.25 m 2 ) under natural sunlight, delivering very high H 2 O 2 rate (0.24 mmol h –1 ). The resulting dilute stream is subsequently converted into a crystalline H 2 O 2 -containing solid intermediate using a proprietary solidification protocol, and redissolution affords an aqueous H 2 O 2 solution up to 30 wt%. This work demonstrates that continuous solar H 2 O 2 generation and downstream concentration can be decoupled to produce concentrated H 2 O 2 from water, air and sunlight.

papers.title: RXNMapperv2: updated validation and evaluation on expanded chemical space
papers.abstract: Atom-to-atom mapping (AAM) assigns reactant atoms to product atoms and is fundamental for reaction classification, template extraction, and synthesis planning. RXNMapper derives AAM from the attention of a Transformer model trained by masked language modeling on unmapped reaction SMILES. However, its original model selection relied on USPTO-50K, a validation set later shown to contain erroneous mappings. Here we revisit RXNMapper using a curated validation set of 4’533 reactions from the dataset Pistachio. We retrained ALBERT-based RXNMapper models on USPTOfull and Pistachio and selected the best head, layer, and checkpoint on this new validation set. To improve the comparison of AAM algorithms, we developed an evaluation framework that removes ambiguous reference reactions and compares predictions by reaction graph isomorphism rather than direct string matching, avoiding false negatives from inconsistent formats and symmetry-equivalent mappings. Across the golden dataset, Pistachio, and an internal AstraZeneca medicinal chemistry benchmark, the updated models outperform the original RXNMapper and LocalMapper, while rearrangements remain persistent challenges.

papers.title: Computational Design of a Two-Stage Passive Cold Chain System for Vaccine Storage
papers.abstract: Cold chain failure accounts for approximately 25% of global vaccine wastage, with last-mile distribution in off-grid settings posing the greatest challenge. This paper presents the computational design of a two-stage passive cold chain device targeting the 2–8◦C vaccine storage window. Stage 1 uses endothermic dissolution of a NH4Cl/KNO3/water system at a 3:2.5:10 mass ratio, absorbing 169.2 kJ and pro-ducing an observed temperature drop of −2 ± 1◦C from 25 ◦C. Stage 2 uses a phase change material layer selected through ideal solid-liquid equilibria screening of 528 binary organic pairs. The myristic acid/n-tetradecane eutectic, predicted at 4.99 ◦C with an estimated latent heat of 225 J g−1, is identified as the primary candidate. A preliminary Classical Nucleation Theory model predicts acceptable supercooling behaviour under realistic nucleating conditions. The device is electricity-free and field-reusable.

papers.title: A Literature-Derived Dataset and Data-Driven Screening Tool for CO2-to-Methanol Heterogeneous Catalysts
papers.abstract: CO2 hydrogenation to methanol is widely studied as a route to chemical CO2 utilization, but reported catalyst performance is scattered across hundreds of publications using different metal–support combinations, loadings, and operating conditions, making cross-study comparison difficult. We compiled a structured dataset of 1,339 experimental data points from 57 peer-reviewed studies (2015–2023), covering 31 base metals and 45 supports under operating temperatures of 150–400 °C, pressures of 1–150 bar, and H2/CO2 ratios of 1–9.1. Using a subset of 761 complete records, we trained an ordinary-least-squares regression on one-hot encoded catalyst identity (base metal, support) and the three operating variables to screen a 17 base × 27 support full-factorial grid (459 combinations) at fixed reference conditions (250 °C, 30 bar, H2/CO2 = 3). Five-fold cross-validation gives a mean R2 of 0.41 (± 0.24) and a mean absolute error of 3.3 percentage points — a single favorable train/test split can yield R2 as high as 0.84, which we show is not representative of the model's general performance. Only 68 of the 459 screened combinations (15%) correspond to a base–support pair actually present in the source literature; the remaining 391 are model extrapolations to untested compositions. We release the dataset, model code, and an interactive screening dashboard, and report these limitations explicitly so that ranked candidates are used as hypotheses for experimental follow-up rather than as validated performance claims.

papers.title: How Far Can Machine Learning Guide Catalyst Discovery?
papers.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to guide catalyst discovery, but it remains unclear how much reported performance reflects genuine predictive ability. In this work, the evaluation protocol alone is shown to manufacture or erase apparent success. Using the largest experimental dataset in heterogeneous catalysis, 12,708 measurements across 59 catalysts for the oxidative coupling of methane, we find a stark performance hierarchy: (i) random splitting looks excellent (MAE ≈0.75 %, R2 ≈0.90), (ii) holding out process conditions is harder, and (iii) holding out entire catalyst compositions, the only test that reflects real catalyst discovery, collapses accuracy nearly three-fold (MAE ≈2.1 %, R2 ≈0.32). To probe why, we generate and openly release a noisefree, condition-matched library of 70,400 datapoints across 326 virtual catalysts from a validated microkinetic model. The same gap appears without any measurement noise, so the barrier is intrinsic: predicting across a discrete compositional space sampled by only dozens of catalysts. Two findings point the way forward. Data quality beats quantity, a small curated set of active catalysts rivals a library five to six times larger. Additionally, feature attribution reveals that models lean almost entirely on process conditions while ignoring composition, exposing compositional encoding as the central unsolved problem. Honest evaluation changes the verdict on what machine learning can, and cannot, yet do for catalyst discovery.

papers.title: Functionalized 1,4-Oxathianes – Saturated Six-Membered Heterocycles with Tunable Physicochemical Profile
papers.abstract: Functionalized 1,4-oxathianes were developed as tunable isosteres of saturated six-membered heterocycles, exploiting the accessible oxidation states of sulfur to modulate physicochemical properties within a fixed molecular skeleton. Two structurally distinct series were prepared: 3-monosubstituted derivatives bearing primary amine or carboxylic acid groups, accessed via regioselective electrophilic chlorination of 1,4-oxathiane, and spirocyclic 2,2-disubstituted counterparts with an annulated piperidine or azetidine ring, obtained through α,β-unsaturated sulfoxide formation and intramolecular oxa-Michael cyclization. Most building blocks were prepared in both sulfide and sulfone oxidation states on multigram scale. Basicity (p K a ) and lipophilicity (Log P ) were determined experimentally and compared against tetrahydropyran, 1,4-dioxane, morpholine, and piperidine analogs. The sulfone introduction reduced the amine basicity by 0.4–1.6 p K a units and lipophilicity – by 0.4–0.5 Log P units, while the sulfide moiety increased Log P by 0.45 units relative to 1,4-dioxane. Overall, the 1,4-oxathiane scaffold spanned ca. 0.85 Log P units through oxidation state manipulation. One of the spirocyclic building blocks, 5-oxa-8-thia-2azaspiro[3.5]nonane 8,8-dioxide, closely matched morpholine in both properties, confirming its potential as an isostere. A virtual library based on the presented scaffolds demonstrated their full compliance with drug- and leadlikeness criteria.

papers.title: Beyond Ideal Behaviour: Interpreting Cyclic Voltammetry Peak-to-Peak Separation in Three-Dimensional Redox-Active Polymers
papers.abstract: Charge transport in three-dimensional redox-active polymers (3D-RAPs) is governed by a complex interplay among charge-hopping, interfacial electron transfer, and ionic diffusion, which complicates quantitative analysis. Here, we describe how kinetic considerations can be indirectly assessed by considering the peak-to-peak separation (∆E) in cyclic voltammetry (CV) as a phenomenological yet robust descriptor of the overall charge-transport efficiency. Changes in ∆E under systematically varied electrochemical conditions are rationalized in terms of the multiple conduction processes that contribute to the voltammetric response. This approach overcomes limitations associated with the widely used apparent diffusion coefficient (Dapp), whose extraction from bulk electrochemical techniques often fails to provide a physically consistent description of these systems. Using a conjugated metallo-3D- RAP (Fe-poly), obtained by anodic electropolymerization of an amino-functionalized Fe(II) polypyridyl complex as a model platform, we systematically probe the dependence of the voltammetric response on experimental parameters. We show that ∆E captures the cumulative effects of coupled transport processes and enables meaningful comparison across materials and operating conditions. This framework provides a practical metric for evaluating charge propagation in complex redox-active architectures and establishes guidelines for the design of high-performance functional materials.

papers.title: Photon-Limited Kinetics in g-C3N4 Photocatalytic Flow Reactors: The Role of Reactor Geometry and Catalyst Placement
papers.abstract: The performance of heterogeneous photocatalytic reactors has traditionally been optimized through catalyst development, whereas the role of reactor architecture in controlling photon utilization remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that photocatalytic efficiency is governed not simply by the number of absorbed photons, but by how incident photons are partitioned between bulk absorption, interfacial photocatalysis, and optical losses. To investigate this concept, a modular visible-light flow reactor with adjustable optical thickness was developed using graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) in front-coated, back-coated, and slurry configurations. Methylene blue degradation established a photon-limited reaction regime, where apparent kinetics were controlled by photon transport rather than intrinsic catalytic activity. Although slurry and immobilized catalysts exhibited nearly identical optical attenuation, their photocatalytic performances differed markedly, demonstrating that photon attenuation alone cannot predict reactor performance. The back-coated reactor exhibited the highest thicknessnormalized reaction rate and catalyst productivity by promoting sequential photon utilization, allowing photons to first interact with the reaction solution before reaching the catalyst interface. This photon-partitioning framework was validated under continuous single-pass operation, achieving up to 97% methylene blue conversion. The results establish catalyst placement as an independent reactor-design parameter and provide a general framework for designing scalable photon-limited heterogeneous photocatalytic reactors through photon management rather than catalyst development alone.

papers.title: Practical synthesis of chetomin-type alkaloids
papers.abstract: (+)-Chetomin is a bis-epidithiodiketopiperazine (ETP) alkaloid that disrupts the HIF-1⍺/p300 interaction, a transcriptional switch promoting tumor adaptation and survival. It is the defining member of the chetomin-type family, which includes some of the most complex ETP derivatives known. This class has long resisted chemical synthesis, limiting exploration of its anticancer potential and the development of improved analogs and conjugates. We report a gram-scale synthesis of (+)-chetomin in nine steps and 24% overall yield. The synthesis is enabled by a C–H disulfenylation of triketopiperazines that overcomes intrinsic stereochemical bias in the chetomin framework and installs all requisite sulfur atoms in a single operation. This advance provides concise access to skeletally altered analogs of chetomin with enhanced potency and to the intricate chaetocochins A–C, establishing a practical platform for systematic exploration of structure and function in complex ETP architectures.

papers.title: Chemically Informed Representations Enable Prediction of Amphiphilic Copolymer Solution Behavior
papers.abstract: The high-dimensional design landscape characteristic of synthetic polymers challenges the rational design of functional materials. While machine learning models can enable efficient data-driven navigation of these landscapes, representation strategies that capture ensemble properties unique to synthetic polymers (e.g., dispersities in chain length, composition, and sequence) are critical. Yet, the relative performance of representation strategies applied to limited experimental datasets remains poorly understood. Here, we use an experimentally generated dataset of linear, random, amphiphilic copolymers and benchmark strategies for encoding repeat unit-derived chemical information into polymer-level features, using aqueous solution behavior as a model system. We evaluated representations for predicting polymer compaction, quantified by size-exclusionchromatography-based percent collapse, and aggregation state, classified from dynamic light scattering measurements. For percent collapse, representations that encode repeat unit chemical properties outperformed that encode repeat unit identity alone, with the strongest performance achieved by separately encoding hydrophilic and hydrophobic repeat unit descriptors. Feature sets selected by feature ablation further improved generalization to unseen repeat unit chemistry and identified interpretable physicochemical contributors to compaction, including repeat unit dipoles, steric features, and solvent-accessible surface area. In contrast, aggregation state prediction was challenged by measurement variability and physiochemical descriptors underperformed, supporting that optimal polymer representations are task and dataset dependent. A genetic algorithm pipeline enabled data-driven design of polymers with targeted compaction that outperformed experienced human designers, demonstrating that machine learning-guided search can translate chemically-informed representations into practical design outcomes. Together, this work establishes a strategy for building chemically-informed machine learning models that can extract interpretable design rules and support prospective discovery in experimentally constrained systems.

papers.title: In Operando Electrochemical Reduction of Indium Tin Oxide Contacts in Silicon Oxide Memristive Devices
papers.abstract: with indium tin oxide (ITO) top contacts. Constant-current electrical stress reveals that ITO-contacted devices exhibit chaotic conductance fluctuations and a single-phase transient in which the slow decay is suppressed, unlike the smooth, two-phase rise-and-decay response of devices with Au/Ti contacts. Through X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, spectroscopic evidence is provided that proton-driven electrochemical reduction of the ITO electrode decouples the two processes that the gold-contacted transient superimposes, leaving the initial con- ductance increase attributed to bulk oxide changes while suppressing the slow decay phase normally observed in gold-contacted devices. Binding energy shifts in indium (∼0.9 eV) and accelerated interfacial etch rates in stressed devices suggest sub-stoichiometric ITO formation. By suppressing the slow proton screening that masks it in gold-contacted devices, the ITO contact exposes the underlying trap-discharge relaxation, which is dispersive (stretched-exponential exponent β = 0.54± 0.17) with a field-free discharge time of a few seconds. These findings reveal that nanoscale electrode material selection critically determines the physical mechanisms governing conductance dynamics in memristive devices, with implications for neuromorphic computing and reliable nanoelectronic design.

papers.title: Relativistic Norm-Conserving Pseudopotentials for Rare Earths with Spin-Orbit Coupling
papers.abstract: The treatment of spin-orbit (SO) coupling is an essential ingredient for describing the electronic structure of rare-earth optical and magnetic materials. The relativistic pseudopotential (PP) framework provides a promising strategy because the scalar relativistic (SR) effect and the SO coupling can be accounted for in a unified manner. In this work, we present a complete set of relativistic normconserving small-core pseudopotentials (PPs) for rare-earth elements (La-Lu), explicitly including the SO coupling. These PPs are constructed within the Goedecker, Teter, and Hutter (GTH) formalism using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange-correlation functional. Benchmark calculations on the SO splitting of 4f-orbital levels and ionization energies demonstrate that the developed PPs accurately reproduce all-electron Dirac-Kohn-Sham reference data. Beyond the single-particle picture, the PPs also capture the main feature of the splitting of 4f-multiplets, yielding a mean absolute deviation of about 0.080 eV for energy levels of trivalent lanthanide ions with respect to the all-electron Breit-Pauli results. This work establishes the first complete set of relativistic small-core GTH PPs for the entire lanthanide series and provides a practical computational framework, thus enabling both variational and perturbative treatments of the SO coupling in large-scale condensed-phase simulations.

papers.title: A Diffusion Framework for Geometrically Valid and Practically Viable 3D Molecular Generation
papers.abstract: By operating on full Cartesian geometries, three-dimensional (3D) molecular generative models offer direct control over the spatial arrangements dictating molecular properties. Yet generating structures that are both geometrically valid (reasonable bond lengths and angles, valid valencies, and minimal steric clashes) and practically useful, including charge neutrality and synthetic accessibility, remains challenging. Most existing models primarily target geometric correctness. Here, we present a diffusion-based framework for organic molecule generation that jointly addresses these criteria. The framework combines three complementary components: (i) a dataset construction strategy that includes positive examples, defined as geometrically valid, charge-neutral, and synthetically accessible molecules, together with negative examples containing geometric distortions, disconnected fragments, or non-zero net charges, annotated by scalar scores for distortion, fragment count, net charge, and synthetic accessibility; (ii) conditional training schemes that enable the model to learn both molecular structures and these associated attributes; and (iii) guidance mechanisms that use contrasting attributes during sampling to promote favorable features while suppressing undesirable ones. Across multiple 3D molecular datasets, the framework consistently improves geometric validity, charge neutrality, and synthetic accessibility, advancing 3D molecular generation toward more reliable use in practical organic molecular design.

papers.title: Molecular and Surface W-Sites through 31P-detected and Dynamic Nuclear Polarization Surface Enhanced 183W NMR Spectroscopy across Olefin Metathesis Catalysts
papers.abstract: Supported tungsten catalysts are widely employed in industrial olefin metathesis. However, further optimization of their performance requires detailed insight into the local structure of the active sites. Accessing this information remains challenging due to the limited site resolution and surface sensitivity of conventional spectroscopic techniques. While 183 W solid-state NMR spectroscopy could in principle offer direct information on the tungsten coordination environment, its practical application is severely limited due to intrinsically low sensitivity. Herein, we demonstrate that the 183 W NMR signatures of molecular and supported alkylidene complexes are readily accessible through indirect 31 P detection. Through this strategy, we are able to identify two distinct Lewis-acidic tungsten surface sites on WO x /SiO 2 catalysts and resolve their structural characteristics through their NMR fingerprints. Our results indicate that mainly the tungsten-dioxo subset of the isolated tungsten sites exhibits sufficient coordinative unsaturation to bind small molecules and thereby participate in catalysis. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding the catalytic activity and rational design of supported metathesis catalysts.

papers.title: Ion-Pair Design Rules for Defect Passivation in 2D WS2
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors hold great promise for next-generation optoelectronics owing to their direct band gaps in the monolayer limit and strong light–matter interactions; however, device performance is frequently limited by intrinsic point defects. In monolayer WS2, sulfur vacancies strongly quench optical emission, while existing chemical passivation strategies remain largely empirical. Here, we establish ion-pair interactions as a predictive design principle for lithium-based defect passivation. By systematically comparing coordinating and non-coordinating anions, we demonstrate that weaker Li+–anion interactions increase the effective availability of Li+ for vacancy binding, resulting in pronounced photoluminescence (PL) enhancement. The low-temperature PL measurements provide direct spectroscopic evidence for the suppression of defect-bound excitonic emission, while femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) measurements reveal reduced defect-assisted recombination and prolonged exciton lifetimes after passivation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that strong ion-pair formation counteracts passivation by reintroducing mid-gap states, directly linking ion-pair interaction energies to the experimentally observed photoluminescence trends. Guided by this framework, we predict and experimentally validate lithium bis(pentafluoroethylsulfonyl)imide (Li-BETI) as a new passivation agent that matches or exceeds the performance of Li-TFSI. Together, these results provide rational chemical design rules for defect passivation in 2D semiconductors.

papers.title: GVIM 2.0: A Multi-Agent Research System for Chemistry and Materials Science
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as natural-language interfaces for chemistry and materials research, but their utility in scientific workflows depends on their ability to connect user requests with executable tools, structured data handling, and verifiable outputs. Here, we present GVIM 2.0, a multi-agent research system designed to support computational and informatics workflows in chemistry and materials science. GVIM 2.0 integrates language-model-based task planning with domain-specific Skills, packagebacked computational tools, sandboxed execution, and artifact generation. On a 400-question public benchmark suite spanning ChemBench, MaScQA, and ChemLLMBench, the complete GVIM 2.0 workflow answered 325/400 questions correctly, achieving an accuracy of 81.25%, compared with 285/400 questions and 71.25% accuracy for a same-base API-only baseline. We further evaluated GVIM 2.0 on task-native workflows covering molecular solubility prediction, steel yield-strength prediction, reaction-table extraction, MS/MS spectral retrieval, chemical entity extraction, retrospective BACE inhibitor prioritization, Matbench experimental band-gap modelling, and temporal external validation of BACE1 activity prediction. These workflows generated inspectable outputs, including prediction files, metrics, figures, and reports. The results show that GVIM 2.0 can organize reproducible data-to-result workflows for selected chemistry and materials informatics tasks, providing a practical framework for tool-augmented scientific research assistance.

papers.title: Budget-Constrained Compound Library Prioritization with Risk Awareness and Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Background: The bottleneck addressed here is not access to molecular structures, but the limited number of compounds that can be tested, purchased, reviewed or synthesized first. In many early projects, the immediate question is not whether every molecule can receive a model score, but which small fraction of a large library deserves the next unit of experimental attention. Objective: I formulate this as risk-aware, budget-constrained compound-library compression. Given a molecular library and a testing budget, the task is to return an enriched Top-k candidate set while preserving the uncertainty, applicability-domain and risk evidence needed for human review. Methods: The framework is intentionally conservative in its modeling choices and stricter in its evidence handling. It combines a transparent 2D activity proxy, split-conformal uncertainty intervals, applicability-domain evidence, ADMET and structural alerts, leakage auditing, and auditable Top-k export. I use Morgan fingerprints, RDKit descriptors and a multilayer perceptron as a fast, reviewable baseline because an upstream triage layer should first be scalable, inspectable and difficult to over-interpret. Results: On ChEMBL 36, the model achieved Spearman 0.7674 and EF@1% 2.7331 on internal validation, and Spearman 0.5171 with EF@1% 2.4359 on a temporal holdout. After fold-0 training-overlap control, the scaffold-disjoint BACE subset retained ROC AUC 0.7626 and EF@1% 2.0253. In a strict 100-molecule BACE decision-layer replay, the risk-aware order kept Hit@10 at 0.9000 while exposing risk and uncertainty evidence that pure activity sorting omits. An EGFR/CHEMBL203 label-hidden operational replay supported workflow feasibility but is reported as same-source sensitivity analysis rather than independent external validation. Conclusion: The evidence supports risk-aware library compression as an experimental prioritization layer before existing screening, CADD and wet-lab workflows. The claim is intentionally bounded: retrospective label-hidden replay is separated from truly prospective unknown-activity library use, and externally blinded or prospective validation remains necessary before claiming project-specific hit-rate or cost improvements.

papers.title: Pd-Catalyzed Non-Directed C–H Functionalization with Fluoroalkenyl Linchpins
papers.abstract: Non-directed palladium-catalyzed C–H olefination has emerged as a powerful strategy for the direct diversification of arenes but has relied almost exclusively on olefin coupling partners activated through classical mesomeric effects. Herein, we demonstrate that short perfluoroalkyl-substituted olefins, whose reactivity is governed predominantly by inductive electron withdrawal, constitute a complementary class of electronically activated coupling partners for ligand-enabled non-directed C–H olefination. The reaction provides efficient access to a broad range of fluoroalkenylated arenes and heteroarenes with excellent functional-group tolerance and enables the late-stage functionalization of pharmaceuticals and natural products. Mechanistic investigations combining kinetic isotope effect measurements and DFT calculations reveal a distinct reactivity profile compared with classically mesomerically activated olefins, highlighting the influence of olefin electronics on the elementary steps of the catalytic cycle. Furthermore, the resulting fluoroalkenylated products serve as versatile fluorinated linchpins that can be readily diversified into structurally complex fluorinated molecules, establishing inductively activated olefins as a complementary design principle for non-directed C–H olefination.

papers.title: Charge separation kinetics uncovered by tensor decomposition of two-dimensional electronic spectra
papers.abstract: The mechanism and kinetics of charge separation in the reaction center of Photosystem II is still not sufficiently understood despite the vast experimental and theoretical efforts. The most detailed experimental insight into the light-initiated charge separation can be obtained with two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy. This method, however, generates a large amount of data that are challenging to analyze. Furthermore, signals corresponding to the charge separation process can be of low-intensity and thus difficult to extract from the spectra. In this letter, we simulate a charge separation process on a single pigment pair of the reaction center of Photosystem II and the corresponding two-dimensional spectrum. We introduce a general numerical method based on a singular value decomposition of a tensor to break down the two-dimensional spectrum into decay-associated spectra and kinetic traces without any loss of information. We showcase how can this method be used to monitor the charge separation kinetics.

papers.title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
papers.abstract: Selective CO 2 capture from humid, N 2 -rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO 2 /N 2 discrimination with robustness under realistic operating conditions. Yet, few MOFs unify ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce Zn‑ClTOx, a chlorotriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOF, and its PVDF composite, integrating these attributes within an ultramicroporous framework. Zn‑ClTOx is obtained by a non-toxic, water/ethanol-minimized liquid-assisted grinding and water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. The chloro functionalization leads to the formation of isolated CO 2 -sized cavities and polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, promoting directional C–H···O(CO 2 ) contacts and electrostatic complementarity. The favorable CO 2 binding is reflected by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 43 kJ/mol, while almost completely suppressing N 2 adsorption. At 298 K, Zn‑ClTOx adsorbs 2.89 mmol g -1 CO 2 at 0.15 bar and displays an IAST CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 4074 for a 15/85 mixture, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO 2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a Zn‑ClTOx@PVDF composite for a 15/85 CO 2 /N 2 mixture under dry and humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO 2 /H 2 O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO 2 sorption is favored at relative humidity (RH) of 21%, resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH > 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO 2 -selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

papers.title: Heteroatom-Free Liquid Crystalline Elastomers Prepared by Catalytic Chain Transfer Photopolymerization (CCTP2) of Methacrylate Liquid Crystal Monomers
papers.abstract: Liquid crystalline elastomers (LCEs) are soft, anisotropic materials exhibiting stimuli-responsive properties with potential utility in robotics, optics, and sensing. Historically, LCEs have been prepared via hydrosilylation reactions to form polysilicon materials with either main chain or side-chain liquid crystalline segments. Many recent examinations of LCE utilize more accessible synthetic methods based on photopolymerization of acrylated monomers and compositions that contain heteroatom chain transfer or chain extension agents (e.g., thiols or amines) to enable network formation and alignment control. Here, we report the preparation of heteroatom-free (Si, S, N) LCE composed almost entirely of liquid crystalline precursors via catalytic chain transfer (CCT) photopolymerization. Incorporation of a macrocyclic cobaloxime catalyst (CoBF) into formulations nearly entirely composed of a methacrylate liquid crystal monomer (MeC6M) enables precise tuning of network mechanics and stimuli-responsive behavior through controlled chain transfer. The LCE maintain properties and stimuli-response comparable to LCEs prepared by previously established methods with catalyst loading providing a direct handle over network mechanics and thermomechanical actuation. The exceptionally high LC content afforded by this strategy may be particularly advantageous for dynamic optical application to maximize birefringence and minimize scatter.

papers.title: Lipid Matrix-Dependent Effects of Ceramide Enrichment on Cholesterol-Containing PSM and DLPC Membranes
papers.abstract: Ceramide is a bioactive sphingolipid that can reorganize cholesterol-containing membranes, but how membrane properties change with increasing ceramide content in different lipid matrices remains unclear. Using Martini 3 coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we examine cholesterol-containing PSM and DLPC membranes across a controlled palmitoyl ceramide (PCER) composition series at a single liquid-phase temperature. Increasing PCER fraction generally decreases area per lipid and increases lipid ordering, consistent with membrane condensation. However, the responses differ between matrices. In PSM/CHOL, PCER is accommodated within an already ordered environment, producing only modest membrane stiffening. In DLPC/CHOL, PCER promotes more heterogeneous organization and substantial lateral rearrangement, accompanied by a nonmonotonic mechanical response. PCER enrichment also changes cholesterol positioning and orientation in a matrix-dependent manner. These results show that ceramide-induced condensation does not necessarily produce monotonic membrane stiffening and highlight the importance of the host lipid matrix in determining membrane structure and mechanics.

papers.title: Microhydration of methylated pyrazoles and imidazoles: Robust vibrational resonances in red-shifted water
papers.abstract: Mono- and dihydrates of 11 N-methylated pyrazoles and imidazoles are studied as vacuum-isolated complexes at low temperature by linear infrared spectroscopy to reveal the interplay between the hydrogen-bonded water OH stretching fundamentals and anharmonic resonance partners. The water bending overtones with and without additional stretching motion of a water unit against the diazole are identified as the dominant resonance partners. Methyl substitution at the ring allows to tune the water OH stretch wavenumber through these resonances. A simple nested 2×2 model Hamiltonian in combination with harmonic DFT predictions provides an effective joint description of the anharmonic spectra of all 22 investigated hydrogen-bonded complexes, including resonance-induced intensity redistribution patterns. Future multidimensional anharmonic quantum calculations can test to which extent the proposed empirical model is successful for the right reasons. Model-based blind and thus unbiased predictions for 6 experimentally uncharacterized N-alkylated pyrazoles and imidazoles may allow to quantify the predictive power of the DFT-supported anharmonic model Hamiltonian in a future investigation.

papers.title: One-Pot Installation of N-Heterocyclic Carbenes on Gold Nanoparticles through Counterion-Dependent Mild-Base Activation
papers.abstract: N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-stabilized gold nanoparticles offer exceptional chemical and thermal stability, yet their installation typically requires multistep procedures, strong bases, or strictly inert conditions. We report a practical onepot method that enables high-coverage NHC functionalization of gold nanoparticles using only imidazolium salts and a mild base. Systematic control experiments and spectroscopic analysis support a counterion-dependent mild-base activation pathway in which persistent HCO3 -/CO2 -derived intermediates are not observed under the applied reaction conditions. Instead, data are most consistent with an NHC formation that occurs in proximity to the nanoparticle interface, followed by rapid Au–C bond formation. Optimized reaction conditions give quantitative ligand exchange while suppressing particle ripening, and the method tolerates air, moisture, and a broad range of NHC classes, including benzimidazolium, imidazolinium, and mesoionic precursors. These results provide a general, mild, and scalable strategy for preparing robust NHC-functionalized gold nanomaterials.

papers.title: Recyclable Homogeneous Zinc and Cobalt Complexes in Catalytic Hydrosilylation of Ketones and Amides.
papers.abstract: Homogeneous catalysis has many appealing properties yet are plagued by poor separation profiles between catalysts and products. Thus, heterogeneous catalysts dominate applications in industrial settings. We have developed ‘metalla-GAP’ (GAP = Group-Assisted-Purification) which allows simple recovery and reuse of homogeneous metal catalysts. Zinc and cobalt ‘metalla-GAP’ catalysts exhibit high selectivity for the double hydrosilylation of ketones, with good separability and over five cycles afford moderate product yields.

papers.title: Air-Tolerant Copper Catalysis for C–N Cross-Coupling Reactions: Catalyst Reactivation Enabled by Silane Additives
papers.abstract: The applicability of many transition-metal-catalyzed reactions is limited by sensitivity to air and moisture. Copper-catalyzed aromatic carbon–nitrogen bond formation is a versatile and economical synthetic tool, yet most catalytic systems require an inert atmosphere to prevent catalyst deactivation. Rather than developing new catalysts for individual transformations, we now report a silane-enabled catalyst-reactivation strategy that maintains active Cu(I) species under aerobic conditions by reducing off-cycle Cu(II) species. The protocol obviates the use of a glovebox, Schlenk techniques, or degassed solvents, while enabling a wide variety of copper-catalyzed C–N bond-forming processes—including amination, amidation, sulfonamidation, and N-heterocycle arylation—to proceed efficiently under air without compromising good functional group tolerance and chemoselectivity. This strategy provides a general solution to mitigate catalyst deactivation, substantially enhancing the practicality of copper catalysis.

papers.title: Inorganic Enzymes: Hydration-Coupled Electron Transfer Enables Catalysis
Catalysts Deactivation Models in Propane Dehydrogenation Reaction
papers.abstract: The increased availability of propane associated with the large-scale exploitation of shale gas has stimulated the development of on-purpose propane dehydrogenation (PDH) processes. While Pt-based PDH catalysts are utilized in industry, such catalysts typically suffer from fast deactivation due to coking and sintering. In order to describe catalyst deactivation, a first-order exponential decay using a deactivation constant (kd) is often applied although the use of kd rarely reproduce the actual experimental time-on-stream behavior. Herein, four different deactivation models, including a first-order exponential decay, are evaluated using experimental data from alumina-supported PtGa-based PDH catalysts. Among these models, the stretched exponential decay reproduces best the experimental PDH productivity. This model is then successfully applied across an available library of silica-supported Ptbased catalysts prepared via surface organometallic chemistry, highlighting subtle differences between them and the specific effect of promoters.

papers.title: A Tethered Nitrenium Strategy for Functionalized Morpholines
papers.abstract: We describe an effective strategy for the stereospecific synthesis of functional group-rich morpholines. Our reaction protocol benefits from the remarkable properties of tethered nitreniums and utilizes inexpensive, commercial hypervalent iodine oxidants. This technology is operationally simple and does not require the rigorous exclusion of air or ambient moisture for success.

papers.title: Chemoselective Intermolecular Cross-Benzoin Reactions via Pyridinium-Zwitterion Intermediates
papers.abstract: Despite considerable advances in the well-established benzoin reaction, cross-benzoin reactions remain challenging often due to limited substrate scope, generation of undesired products, and engineered catalysts. Here we outline an entirely new entry path into this useful reaction by demonstrating that hydroxycarbenes (R––OH) can serve as alternative synthons for benzoin reactions. We do so by trapping the hydroxycarbene intermediates to avoid their rapid quantum-mechanical tunneling [1,2]H-shifts to the corresponding aldehydes. By extending the pyridine probe technique, nascent hydroxycarbenes are intercepted to form persistent zwitterionic intermediates. These intermediates subsequently react with a variety of aldehydes, enabling cross-benzoin reactions in high yields and chemoselectivities. We provide the first characterization of hydroxycarbene-derived zwitterionic intermediates, using advanced mass spectrometric analyses and support their formation and reactivity with computational studies. Our findings establish nucleophilic trapping as a practical tool for taming hydroxycarbene reactivity and expanding their synthetic utility.

papers.title: Green Chemistry for the Classroom: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Organic Compounds
papers.abstract: Hydrothermal synthesis (HTS) designates the use of hot liquid water as medium for chemical reactions. The technique is very well established for generating crystalline inorganic materials. Recently it was shown that HTS can also be used to prepare organic compounds, which are all bearing a high content in aromatics and heterocyclics. The technique is environmentally friendly for using solely water as medium, especially in comparison to conventional syntheses of such compounds. Here we present HTS of organic compounds in a fashion that allows for implementing it in the classroom. First, we show how HTS can be used as an example to introduce the timely concepts of green chemistry and sustainable syntheses. Second, we review organic cyclocondensation reactions including reaction equilibrium and enthalpic/entropic driving forces as well as real-life examples of cyclocondensation products, as HTS is especially amenable to cyclocondensations. Third, as liquid high-temperature water is well suited to review the temperature-dependence of certain physicochemical features, we provide interactive plots for exploring these data. Fourth, we develop a classroom friendly HTS of a simple organic colorant, that can be performed simple in kitchen pressure cookers. Fifth, at the hand of this classroom experiment we show how measures for the green-ness of a chemical synthesis, such as the Ecoscale are used.

papers.title: Sequence Dependence of Folding and Self-Assembly of Glycine-X Repeat Peptides on Graphite
Subcritical Hydrothermal Synthesis in a Water-Alcohol Co-solvent of Size-Controlled High-Entropy Spinel Oxide Nanoparticles as Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) composed of more than five transition metal elements are promising noble-metal-free electrocatalysts for sustainable water oxidation. However, the low-temperature synthesis of size-controlled, single-phase, and crystalline HEO nanoparticles remains challenging because multicomponent oxide formation requires simultaneous nucleation and crystallization of multiple metal species with different hydrolysis behaviors. Herein, we report an alcohol-assisted subcritical hydrothermal strategy for synthesizing size-controlled HEO nanoparticles composed of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Zn. By tuning the water–alcohol co-solvent composition, the average particle size decreased from 17.2 to 10.0 nm without significant changes in the overall metal composition. Structural characterizations confirmed that the obtained nanoparticles retained a single-phase spinel oxide structure with homogeneous elemental distribution and similar local coordination environments. The size reduction was considered to be attributed to changes in solvent properties, particularly the lowered dielectric constant of the water–alcohol co-solvent, which promotes rapid nucleation and suppresses particle coarsening. The resulting smaller HEO nanoparticles exhibited enhanced alkaline oxygen evolution reaction activity. The nearly unchanged Tafel slopes indicate that the improved activity mainly originates from an increased number of accessible active sites rather than a change in the reaction mechanism. This work provides a simple solution-based route for nanoscale control of crystalline multicomponent oxide electrocatalysts and offers a sustainable design strategy for noble-metal-free water oxidation catalysts.

papers.title: Distribution of Relaxation Times through the Lens of Distribution Theory
papers.abstract: The distribution of relaxation times (DRT) model is widely used to deconvolve electrochemical impedance spectra into timescale distributions. However, standard DRT formulations assume integrable impedance. This condition is violated by electrochemical systems with blocking boundaries where diffusion or charge accumulation causes the low-frequency response to diverge. We formulate DRT inversion in the space of tempered distributions and derive a distributional Fuoss–Kirkwood boundary-value relation in S ′(R), under explicit analyticity, growth, and boundary-value assumptions on the strip continuation of the impedance. In this setting, the DRT is determined by the strip boundary values of the impedance, with Dirac atoms from simple poles, derivatives of Dirac masses from higher-order poles, and power-law tails from non-integrable low-frequency behavior. This formulation clarifies reported discrepancies for capacitive and diffusive systems by making the boundary-value convention explicit and separating distributional identities from pointwise evaluations. We derive closed-form distributional DRTs for generalized resistor-capacitor (RC) circuits, constant-phase elements, and finite-length diffusion transmission-line models in multiple geometries, and establish relationships between the DRT and the distributions of diffusion and capacitive times.

papers.title: Data-Driven Optimization of the Solid-Solution Ratio of Stannitetype CuxAg2-xZnGeySn1-yS4 photocatalysts Using Machine-Learning with Chemically Similar Out-of-Plane Data
papers.abstract: Optimal solid-solution ratio of stannite-type Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 photocatalysts for sacrificial H 2 evolution under visible light ( λ ≥ 420 nm) was predicted using a machine-learning approach. The Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 plane (hereafter referred to as the "in-plane"), defined as a two-dimensional composition space spanned by x and y , consists of 231 points when x and y are 0.0–2.0 and 0.0–1.0 with 0.1 increments, respectively. H 2 activities at only six data points of ( x, y ) = (0.0, 1.0), (0.5, 1.0), (1.0, 1.0), (1.5, 1.0), (2.0, 1.0), and (2.0, 0.0) within the in-plane that located at the edge of the plane had been previously measured. Prediction mapping using our original machine-learning method designed to address data imbalance and experimental-condition dependence in photocatalyst datasets indicated that the region around ( x, y ) = (0.6, 0.3) was predicted to exhibit the optimal solid-solution ratio with maximal photocatalytic activity. On the basis of the prediction mapping, we experimentally investigated the activities of Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 photocatalysts with various solid-solution ratios. The ratio around ( x =0.8, y =0.6) was found to be optimal, and the highest photocatalytic activity was experimentally confirmed in this central solid-solution region. The optimized photocatalyst responded to 660 nm and the apparent quantum yield (AQY) was 8.2% at 420 nm. It was notable that response to visible light with long wavelength and improvement in the activity of the Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 photocatalyst compared to that of previously developed Ag 2 ZnGeS 4 with a stannite structure were achieved by formation of solid-solution based on the machine-learning prediction.
