Furthermore, we examined the contribution of out-of-plane data to the prediction mapping, where out-of-plane data were defined as data points that were included in the training dataset used to construct the machine-learning model but were not represented by the Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 . The sequential removal of subsets of out-of-plane data from the training data and the sequential regeneration of the predicted activity maps demonstrated that out-of-plane data compositionally similar to Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 played an important role in generating the prediction mapping. Composition-space analyses based on dimensionality-reduction, clustering, and distance analyses further revealed that the out-of-plane data located close to the Cu x Ag 2- x ZnGe y Sn 1- y S 4 compositions contributed significantly to capturing activity trends within the in-plane. These insights suggest that compositionally neighboring data outside the target plane can be effectively leveraged to enable reliable data-driven materials discovery even when data within a specific composition plane are severely limited. This study is expected to promote the development of multi-element functional materials beyond photocatalysts.

papers.title: Light-Accelerated Iridium-Catalysed C-H Borylation
papers.abstract: Here we report a mild light-assisted Iridium-catalysed C-H borylation protocol of organic substrates. We demonstrate that adapting the Ishiyama-Tagaki-Miyaura-Hartwig (ITMH) protocol for C-H borylation to proceed under photochemical conditions imparts a pronounced rate enhancement compared to the established dark reaction. This photochemistry methodology achieves higher yields across a broad range of substrates, and is easily scalable using continuous flow technology.

papers.title: Scalable Low-Energy Molecular Conformer Generation with Quantum Mechanical Accuracy
papers.abstract: Understanding molecular geometry is crucial for biological activity and chemical reactivity; however, computational methods for generating 3D structures are limited by the vast scale of conformational space and the complexities of stereochemistry. We approach this problem with a method that combines a dataset of molecular conformers with generative diffusion models. We introduce ChEMBL3D, containing 280 million molecular geometries for 1.8 million drug-like compounds, optimized using AIMNet2 neural network potentials to a near-quantum mechanical accuracy with implicit solvent effects. This dataset captures organic molecules in various protonation states and stereochemical configurations. We then developed LoQI, a stereochemistry-aware diffusion model trained on ChEMBL3D. Through graph augmentation, LoQI generates molecular structures with targeted stereochemistry, an advance over prior generative methods. The model outperforms traditional approaches, achieving up to tenfold improvements in energy accuracy and effective recovery of optimal conformations. Benchmark tests on macrocycles, flexible molecules, and crystal structures confirm efficient low-energy conformer search.

papers.title: Fano Resonances from Guest-Host Coupling of MOF IVCT and Solvent Vibronic Bands
papers.abstract: Guest-host interactions within metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) attract widespread interest due to the utility of MOFs as gas storage and separation vessels, electrodes, catalysts, and as sensors. New methods for detecting and harnessing guest-host interactions therefore remain intensely studied. Herein, we report a Fano resonance arising from coupling of the IVCT band of a MOF, chromium(1,2,3-triazolate)2 (CrTA2), and vibronic bands of adsorbate molecules. Systematic studies reveal the Fano resonance profile is highly sensitive to the guest and environmental dielectric constants, as well as the MOF particle size and steric bulk of the adsorbate. To demonstrate potential applications in sensing, a diverse range of carbonyl- or sulfoxide-containing adsorbates produce reproducible and marked differences in the observed Fano resonances as detected by rapid and routine spectroscopic methods.

papers.title: Unraveling the Temperature-Dependent Redox Cycle of Chromium Species in Molten Chloride Salt via In-Situ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Molten chloride salt is a widely studied high-temperature electrolyte, with established use in pyrochemical reprocessing and electrorefining, and frequent use as a model system for concentrated solar power and molten salt reactor applications. Chromium (Cr) is a key element in high-temperature structural alloys. However, the temperature-dependent evolution and stability of Cr species in this environment remain insufficiently understood. Cr-redox chemistry in molten chloride salts governs the dissolution, oxidation and transformation of Cr-containing species, with direct implications for corrosion and dealloying of structural alloys as well as broader molten-salt processing applications. In the present study, the chemical stability of CrCl2, CrCl3, and Cr2O3 in LiCl-KCl eutectic molten salt at elevated temperatures was systematically investigated using in-situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy. The results revealed that CrCl3 and Cr2O3 remained chemically stable under the tested conditions, whereas CrCl2 underwent oxidation by impurities to form Cr2O3 at 500 °C, but partially converted back to Cr2+ species upon cooling to room temperature. Additionally, the interaction between chromium and NiCl2 in molten salt was examined, indicating that chromium likely reduced Ni2+ to metallic Ni0, while being oxidized to Cr2+, which subsequently underwent a similar chemical evolution as CrCl2 in the molten salt. These findings unravel a temperature-dependent, impurity-mediated redox cycle of Cr species in molten chloride salt, providing a foundation for understanding and controlling Cr the dissolution, oxidation and transformation, and for developing effective corrosion-mitigation strategies to enhance the stability of high-temperature structural alloys in molten-salt systems.

papers.title: Self-healing and stretchable relaxor-dielectrics with resistance to leakage current path formation
papers.abstract: Self-healing materials allow E-skin to recover from unexpected environmental damage. However, self-healing agents (such as reversible hydrogen bonds and curing capsules) often form leakage current paths when applied as dielectrics, leading to gate insulator breakdown in self-healing transistors. In this work, we demonstrate a self-healing stretchable relaxor-dielectric (SS relaxor-dielectric) with resistance to gate leakage, achieved by directly spin-casting a relaxor-ferroelectric VDF ter-polymer (PVDF-TrFE-CTFE) onto a self-healing elastomer (PDMS-MPU 0.4 -IU 0.6 ) film. The SS relaxor-dielectric ensures self-healing capability and enhances resistance to leakage path formation while simultaneously passivating the trap sites at the channel-insulator interface. As a result, self-healing stretchable thin-film transistor (SS-TFT) fabricated with the SS relaxor-dielectric exhibits stabilized off-current, increased on-current, and reduced hysteresis in their transfer characteristics. The SS-TFT achieves ~80 % of healing efficiency in on-current and maintains electrical properties under 20 % of strain. Furthermore, by introducing self-healing properties to the interconnection between electronic components, unit circuits including logic gates (INV, NAND, NOR) and 2T-0C dynamic random-access memory (2T-0C DRAM) cell are configured without additional processing. This work provides a strategy based on a general spin-coating process that is applicable to a broad range of dielectric materials for self-healing electronics.

papers.title: Water clustering in hydrophobic zeolitic imidazolate frameworks under pressure
papers.abstract: Understanding water in hydrophobic nanoscale environments is central to problems ranging from biological recognition and ion transport to geological fluid confinement and nanofluidic energy absorption. Pressurised intrusion into hydrophobic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provides a well-defined platform to study this behaviour, but the molecular behaviour of water during intrusion and extrusion has remained unresolved. Here, we resolve a sequential filling mechanism of water molecules within the canonical MOF, ZIF-8, using in-situ single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, ab-initio calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations to determine the position, stability, and mobility of different water sites and their relation to the framework structure. Our findings reveal that, whilst water–water interactions are central to the intrusion-extrusion behaviour, the precise chemistry, geometry, and flexibility of the framework control the arrangement, stability, and dynamics of intruded water molecules. This indicates that the behaviour of water in hydrophobic MOFs can be controlled by tuning the pore structure.

papers.title: Synthesis and Gas Adsorption Properties of an Isoreticular Family of Zn–Triazolate MOFs
papers.abstract: Flexible metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are attractive porous materials owing to their ability to undergo structural changes in response to external stimuli, enabling applications in gas storage and molecular separations. Here, we report an isoreticular family of Zn–triazolate MOFs incorporating three-dimensional aliphatic dicarboxylate pillar linkers based on cubane (UNSW-100), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (UNSW-102) and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (UNSW-103). Despite their closely related crystal structures, the three frameworks exhibit markedly different gas adsorption and structural responses. While UNSW-103 remains permanently porous following activation, UNSW-102 displays negligible N2 uptake at 77 K despite its crystallographically accessible pore network, together with an unusual dependence of CO2 adsorption on the activation history. Variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction reveals distinct temperature-dependent structural behaviour across the series, with the bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane analogue undergoing a pronounced low-temperature structural transformation. Complementary in situ synchrotron CO2 powder X-ray diffraction further demonstrates contrasting pressure-dependent structural responses between the cubane and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane analogues. These results establish an expanded family of 3D-linker pillared Zn–triazolate MOFs exhibiting diverse adsorption and structural behaviour and provide a foundation for future investigations into the origins of framework flexibility in this class of materials.

papers.title: From α-helices to Mesoscale Order: Structure–Packing Relationships in Polypeptide block Copolymer Films
papers.abstract: Polypeptide-based block copolymers are promising platforms for creating hierarchical nanostructures because their secondary structures can direct mesoscale self-assembly. This study investigates how polypeptide chain length and thermal annealing govern the hierarchical organization of PEG-b-poly(ε-benzyloxycarbonyl-L-lysine) (PZLL) thin films. Combined FTIR, AFM, AFM-IR, and synchrotron GIWAXS/GISAXS analyses reveal that PZLL segments predominantly form α-helical conformations that assemble into hexagonally packed domains with nearly constant lattice parameters across compositions. Increasing the PZLL degree of polymerization stabilizes the α-helical structure, promotes preferential in-plane orientation of cylindrical domains, and enables the formation of long-range ordered fibrillar morphologies, whereas short PZLL chains partially transform into β-sheet structures during film formation and after high-temperature annealing. These findings establish a direct relationship between secondary structure, orientational ordering, and mesoscale morphology in self-assembled polypeptide block copolymer films.

papers.title: Accelerated Mechanochemical Reaction Discovery and Development via Miniaturized Parallel Milling
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical reaction discovery remains constrained by the low throughput and material demands of conventional milling workflows. Herein, we establish miniaturized parallel milling as a general approach for accelerated mechanochemical reaction discovery and development in a mixer-mill equipment. The platform employs inexpensive polypropylene vial reactors mounted on modular holders and enables the rapid evaluation of solvent-minimized transformations with minimal material consumption. Its generality is demonstrated across diverse reaction classes, including fluorination, amide formation, cross-coupling, heterocycle synthesis, and zero-valent-metal-mediated reactivity. Parallel operation enables reproducible reaction screening, kinetic profiling, and optimization of reaction conditions. As a showcase, a mechanochemical aziridine synthesis was developed from initial discovery to optimization, kinetic analysis, and preliminary scope evaluation within only 3 milling campaigns using unmodified mixer-mill equipment. Together, this workflow provides a practical foundation for high throughput mechanochemistry and accelerates the translation of mechanochemical methods from discovery to application.

papers.title: Catalytic redox-neutral decarboxylative aromatization via transfer dehydrogenation
papers.abstract: Arenes are fundamental structural motifs in organic molecules; therefore, methods for introducing aromatic rings are of broad importance. Traditional approaches that install arenes early followed by postfunctionalization often struggle to achieve diverse substitution patterns, high chemoselectivity, or satisfactory processability. As an alternative, constructing arenes via late-stage aromatization of prearomatic intermediates could offer greater flexibility, improved processability, and orthogonal reactivity, which, however, has been underdeveloped. Particularly, there remain substantial challenges of using saturated cyclohexanes as benzene precursors. Here we report a distinct catalytic strategy that uses carboxylic acids as traceless, multifunctional anchors to achieve chemoselective, redox-neutral aromatization of cyclohexanes via transfer dehydrogenation. This approach provides a rare means to selectively aromatize carboxylated cyclohexanes even in the presence of more reactive cyclohexenes and cyclohexanones. The Ir-catalyzed protocol delivers excellent yields, remarkable chemoselectivity, and broad functional-group compatibility. Combined experimental and computational studies support an unusual mechanism involving sequential dehydrogenation, trans-decarboxylation, β-hydrogen elimination, and further dehydrogenation. The utility of the method is demonstrated in site-selective, modular syntheses of diverse multi-substituted arenes through late-stage aromatization.

papers.title: Dynamic Covalent Polymerization Through Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation
papers.abstract: Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is a ubiquitous phenomenon in living systems wherein membraneless organelles form through the spontaneous compartmentalization of small molecules or biopolymers. Synthetic (supra)molecular systems—including small molecules, oligomers, and polymers—have each been shown to undergo LLPS independently. However, creating synthetic polymeric systems that, like living systems, exhibit constitutional dynamics across multiple length scales—from small molecules to macromolecules—remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report an artificial dynamic polymeric LLPS system constructed from biologically relevant building blocks, such as amino acids and disulfides, in which the constitutional dynamics between small molecules and polymers can be engineered within condensed microenvironments that involve multiple weak yet reversible chemical bonds. Compartmentalization within disordered droplets not only elevates the thermodynamic driving force for disulfide-mediated ring-opening polymerization, but also kinetically activates the dynamics of disulfide bonds, enabling the spontaneous, catalyst-free synthesis of high-molecular-weight poly(disulfide)s (up to 400 KDa) in water. The resulting polymers form thermodynamically stable, self-entangled hydrogels, and upon dehydration they undergo quantitative photochemical depolymerization to regenerate virgin-quality monomers. These findings provide a model for constructing a biological system that integrate LLPS with intrinsic dynamic behavior, and may open new opportunities for supramolecular biomaterials.

papers.title: Catalyst-specialized Chemical Language Model Based on Transformer Variational Autoencoder for Catalyst Design and Discovery
papers.abstract: Catalyst design has increasingly benefited from advances in AI, particularly chemical language models (CLMs). However, catalysts occupy a distinct chemical space characterized by unique elemental compositions and structural complexity, which limits the applicability of standard CLMs, thereby reducing their utility for broad catalyst discovery. Here, we present CatTransVAE, a catalyst-specialized CLMbased on a transformer variational autoencoder (VAE). CatTransVAE is developed through pre-training on general compounds and subsequent fine-tuning on diverse catalyst databases. A new template-guided generation framework is introduced to support controlled catalyst design under structural constraints. CatTransVAE demonstrates promising generative performance across multiple catalyst classes and achieves high task validity in template-guided generation. In addition, the proposed two-level embeddings derived from the transformer and VAE components exhibit competitive predictive performance compared with large-scale CLMs. The practical utility of the framework is demonstrated through a catalyst optimization workflow. These results suggest that CatTransVAE provides a useful catalyst-specialized representation and generation framework for accelerating catalyst design and discovery.

papers.title: Image Based Chemical Identification of Ophthalmic Antibiotics
papers.abstract: Substandard and falsified medicines remain a significant global health challenge, while conventional analytical quality control techniques such as high-performance liquid chromatography and X-ray powder diffraction are often costly, infrastructure-dependent, and unsuitable for resource-limited settings. In this study, we present a low-cost analytical framework based on evaporation-induced deposit imaging combined with machine learning for the identification and quantification of five commercial ophthalmic formulations. Droplets were deposited on glass slides, dried under controlled environmental conditions and imaged. A total of 46 quantitative image features were extracted from each dried deposit, capturing texture, morphology, and intensity variations arising from formulation-specific physicochemical behavior. Distinct evaporation-driven crystallization patterns, including coffee-ring structures, dendritic growth, and spherulitic morphologies, enabled clear visual and statistical discrimination among formulations. Principal component analysis revealed well-separated clusters for all five drugs, with the first three principal components explaining 65.6% of total variance. For quantitative analysis, XGBoost and EfficientNet-B3 models were developed using ciprofloxacin and moxifloxacin standard dilution datasets, achieving strong predictive performance with regression slopes close to unity (0.89–0.95) and high R2 values up to 0.98. Model evaluation further demonstrated robust accuracy using R2, MAE, and MSE metrics, while real-sample validation confirmed effective generalization, albeit with increased prediction error due to matrix complexity. These results serve as a proof-of-concept for the utilization of macroscopic images for chemical information techniques.

papers.title: Bright alkyl quantum defects govern early carbon nanotube pharmacokinetics in mice
papers.abstract: Fluorescent quantum defects in single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are a major advance in nanocarbon research, owing to their bright, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths and versatile conjugation chemistries for biomedical sensing and disease targeting. Here, we introduce an efficient, oxygen-free sonochemical route that generates long-chain alkyl defects, simultaneously shortening nanotubes and producing a bright, homogeneously emissive (6,5) SWCNT ensemble. Among 15 screened surfactants and initiators, the branched-chain Niaproof ® 4, which molecular dynamics simulations show packs more densely and uniformly than linear surfactants, yields a 3.4-fold brightness enhancement and a sharp emission peak near 1108 nm. Single-particle spectroscopy reveals J-aggregate emission redshifts at high defect densities, and fibrinogen titration shows defect chemistry governs protein-driven coating displacement. Using a home-built short-wave infrared imaging system (25 mW cm −2 , 989 nm excitation, 1150 nm longpass collection), we show that these sparse defects (~15.2 μm −1 ) drive different, nonmonotonic pharmacokinetics between Niaproof ® 4– and lipid-PEG–functionalized (6,5) at early time points, converging as protein-corona formation masks the underlying chemistry. Histology localizes the nanotubes within macrophages of mononuclear phagocyte system–associated organs. Intravenous administration (50 μg kg −1 ) shows no acute toxicity and short ~2-day retention, while the Niaproof ® 4 group depletes more myeloid cells after corona formation.

papers.title: Synthesis of Dioxasilepanes via TBAT-Catalyzed Hydroxyl-Directed Hydrosilylation
papers.abstract: Treatment of γ-hydroxyenones with diphenylsilane in the presence of catalytic tetrabutylammonium difluorotriphenylsilicate (TBAT) results in the formation of 7membered ring dioxasilepanes. Diastereoselectivity for the reaction can be high (up to >10:1), favoring formation of the anti-substituted dioxasilepane. Desilylation with tetrabutylammonium fluoride (TBAF) produced the corresponding 1,4-diol products in good yield and selectivity.

papers.title: Optimization of Simultaneous Esterification and Transesterification of Waste Cooking Oil using Biomass-based Bifunctional Catalyst via Taguchi L9 Approach.
papers.abstract: The utilization of biomass-based heterogeneous catalysts in biodiesel production is an ecofriendly and sustainable method. This investigation focuses on assessing the catalytic activity of a biomass-derived catalyst, synthesized from eggshells and orange peel waste. Characterization using techniques such as scanning electron microscopy (SEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), energy dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller/Barret–Joyner-Halenda (BET/BJH) revealed a substantial surface area of 134.562 m 2 /g for the prepared catalyst. The Taguchi methodology facilitated the experimental design, optimizing and modeling of simultaneous esterification and transesterification of waste cooking oil (WCO). Monitoring included waste oil biodiesel (WOB) yield and acid value (AV). Methanol-to-oil molar ratio and time significantly influenced WOB yield, while catalyst loading and temperature notably affected WOB AV. Under optimized conditions (methanol-to-oil ratio 12:1, catalyst loading 1 wt.%, temperature 55°C, reaction time 120 min), a maximum WOB yield of 95.27 wt.% and AV of 0.452 (mg KOH)/g were achieved. The WOB's physicochemical characteristics met the biodiesel standards of ASTM D6751 and EN 14214. Additionally, the catalyst, derived from eggshells and orange peel waste, demonstrated efficacy in both esterification and transesterification of WCO, with the ability to be reused for at least four cycles, yielding substantial WOB.

papers.title: From Random Accuracy to Chemical Generalization: A Benchmark for Dye Optical-Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Machine learning is accelerating the design of functional dyes, but reported errors are often dominated by random train–test splits that mix related chromophores, solvents and literature sources. This makes it unclear whether models can support discovery beyond familiar dyesolvent neighborhoods. Here we ask how optical-property predictors perform when evaluation is made chemically honest. We harmonized Deep4Chem and ChemFluor into deduplicated solution-phase benchmarks for absorption and emission wavelengths, preserving dye, solvent and provenance structure. Classical fingerprint/descriptor models were then tested under random, scaffold-family, Murcko-scaffold, scaffold+solvent and article/provenance splits. Random splits gave apparently excellent mean absolute errors of 12.8 nm for absorption and 18.9 nm for emission. The same benchmark became far harder under scaffold-family testing (39.2 and 46.4 nm) and the scaffold+solvent-stress protocol (50.6 and 59.3 nm). Cross-dataset transfer remained substantially poorer than within-dataset interpolation, while error atlases localized failures in red/NIR regimes, macrocyclic families and solvent-sensitive environments. These results reframe dye-property prediction as a benchmark-metrology problem: useful models must report not only low random-split error, but also scaffold, solvent and dataset-shift robustness.

papers.title: Expanding the Role of Zinc in Redox Chemistry through Cooperative Dioxygen Activation and Hydrogen Atom Abstraction in a Dinuclear Zn–Quinone Platform
papers.abstract: Zinc is widely regarded as redox-inactive, yet how it may directly participate in oxygen chemistry remains unclear. Here, we show how a dinuclear zinc complex bearing a redox-active 20 bis(hydroquinone) ligand can activate O2 and oxidize 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol. The dinuclear scaffold is essential: one Zn site stabilizes superoxide while the second supports ligand oxidation, enabling cooperative O2 reduction inaccessible to mononuclear analogues. The generated superoxo–Zn–semiquinone triad mediates hydrogen atom abstraction from the phenol. Spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, kinetics, and DFT calculations establish the reaction mechanism 25 and support radical rebound to a kinetically trapped Zn2 adduct that channels reactivity toward selective C–C coupling. The branched network allows limited regeneration but also leads to framework degradation, yielding a self-limiting turnover-capable system. These findings expand zinc’s role in redox chemistry and redefine its potential biological relevance.

papers.title: MusicMol: Bidirectional Molecule–Music Translation via Neighborhood-Aligned Generation and Transformer Decoding
papers.abstract: What if a molecule could be heard as a piano melody, and a melody could be used to generate a molecule? We present MusicMol, a bidirectional framework for generative translation between small molecules and symbolic music. In the molecule-to-music direction, a label-free, rule-guided conditional flow-matching generator trained on two million ChEMBL compounds maps each heavy atom to four note parameters—pitch, inter-onset step, duration, and velocity. To make the generated music chemically meaningful, MusicMol aligns molecular similarity neighborhoods with differentiable piano-roll neighborhoods using a kernelized alignment loss that combines softmax KL-divergence with rank preservation, so that structurally similar molecules are mapped to acoustically similar scores. In the music-to-molecule direction, a REMI/BPE encoder–decoder Transformer autoregressively decodes symbolic music into valid SELFIES molecular strings, enabling user-composed or performed music to generate molecular candidates. To support this bidirectional loop, we construct, to our knowledge, the largest molecule–MIDI paired dataset to date, comprising ten million compound–score pairs. On held-out music–molecule pairs, the inverse model achieves high token-level generation accuracy and near-perfect molecular validity. Across 30 molecular activity prediction tasks, the music-derived piano-roll representation outperforms four established molecular encoders spanning SMILES, graph, image, and 3D modalities in frozen linear-probe Spearman correlation, R2, and RMSE, and achieves the lowest local label incoherence index (LII) from k=5 to k=100. Deployed as an interactive platform at the Future Learning Center of Zhejiang University, MusicMol lets users hear molecules in real time and translate music into molecular candidates, providing a perceptual and generative interface between chemistry and music.

papers.title: Real-time chemical reaction monitoring with 25 MHz low-field NMR
papers.abstract: Real-time reaction monitoring with Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is an emerging and increasingly important analytical technique. In this work, we develop and implement software to identify molecules and monitor a chemical reaction in real time using a low-field benchtop NMR operating at 24.35 MHz. The approach was validated using a simple acid-catalyzed elimination reaction, the dehydration of cyclohexanol to cyclohexene, and enabled both qualitative and semi-quantitative assessment of the reaction progress. Automated peak integration and yield calculation were performed at each time step, and the results were benchmarked against a high-field 400 MHz Bruker NMR instrument.

papers.title: Direct visualization of hydroperoxy intermediate in fluorescent protein chromophore maturation in PAmCherry1
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread use of fluorescent proteins in bioimaging, the mechanism of oxidative chromophore maturation to form the tyrosine C 𝛼 =C 𝛽 double bond remains unclear. In the photoactivatable fluorescent protein PAmCherry1, this double bond has not yet been formed prior to photoactivation. Here, serial femtosecond crystallography (SFX) using an X-ray free electron laser (XFEL) enabled us to capture the radiation damage-free structure of non-photoactivated PAmCherry1. This structure displayed a covalently bound hydroperoxy moiety (73% occupancy) at the sp 3 -hybridized C 𝛼 atom of the chromophore tyrosine residue within the imidazolinone ring. Unique hydrogen-bonding networks surrounding the hydroperoxy moiety stabilize this highly reactive chromophore species. Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) supported the coexistence of hydroperoxy and enolate chromophore forms. According to spectroscopic analysis, these species exist in dynamic equilibrium. MS analysis further demonstrated that photoactivation is accompanied by the formation of the mature chromophore containing a C 𝛼 =C 𝛽 double bond together with Kolbe decarboxylation. Time-resolved SFX (TR-SFX) using a femtosecond pump laser further revealed decreasing electron density at 800 ps after photoexcitation, consistent with rapid oxidation and decarboxylation. Collectively, these results support a hydroperoxy intermediate as a key species in oxidative chromophore maturation, which is stabilized in non-photoactivated PAmCherry1.

papers.title: An Ionic Wagner Number Predicts Reaction-Zone Localization in Thick Lithium-Ion Cathodes
papers.abstract: Peukert exponents are widely used to summarize battery rate capability, yet they obscure the transition from nearly uniform intercalation across a porous cathode to strongly nonuniform through-plane current distribution. Here we derive an analytical Wagner-number criterion for this transition from a one-dimensional conduction-kinetics model. The ionic Wagner number governs the spatial current distribution, yielding a closed-form second-moment utilization factor and a mechanistic relation between Peukert response and cathode utilization. In its predictive form, the criterion is evaluated before field-resolved simulation from applied areal current density, cathode thickness, effective ionic conductivity, and the Tafel slope parameter; the specific interfacial area cancels from the mean-field expression. The framework establishes a single-mechanism conduction-Tafel ceiling of 1.5 for the Peukert exponent. Isothermal Doyle-Fuller-Newman simulations of a 75.6 µm NMC811 cathode show nearly uniform utilization through 2C discharge, with 93.5% capacity retention, followed by entry into reaction-zone localization as the predicted Wagner number approaches unity near 3C, where electrolyte depletion drives retention down to 45.5%. Balanced thickness scaling and literature data support the predicted Wagner number as an onset criterion for rate-dependent cathode underutilization.

papers.title: Graph-Transformer for Accurate Transition-State Geometries and Barriers in Large Chemical Reactions
papers.abstract: Despite rapid advances in machine learning for transition state prediction, nearly all existing methods remain restricted to small organic molecules containing only a handful of elements and fewer than 30 atoms. Extending transition state prediction to transition metal-catalyzed reactions remains a major challenge because of their larger size, coordination environments, and complex electronic structures. Here, we introduce GRETS (Generate Refine Energies and Transition States), a graph-transformer framework that jointly predicts transition states and activation barriers directly from reactant and product structures. The model is validated on organic reactions and achieves an average root-mean-square deviation of 0.167 Å for transition state prediction, while over half of the predicted activation barriers lie below an absolute error of 3.1 kcal/mol. The strongest performance of GRETS is shown for transition metal-catalyzed reactions, where it achieves subangstrom transition-state accuracy and activation-barrier predictions with a mean absolute error of 1.1 kcal/mol. GRETS maintains its transferability to previously unseen catalytic systems that involve complexes of Au, Co, Fe, Ir, Mn, Ni, Pd, and Pt. These results represent an important step toward data-driven reaction network discovery and catalyst design for large organometallic reactions.

papers.title: Development of a Multi-Arm Vinyl Sulfone Functionalized Core for “On-demand” Assembly of Radiotheranostic agents
papers.abstract: Although targeted radionuclide therapy (TRT) has become a powerful cancer therapy strategy, the development of new TRT agents often requires extensive optimization of specific chemistry/linker units, chelators and pharmacokinetic modifiers. The lack of broadly applicable modular platforms remains a major barrier to streamline the discovery and optimization of TRT agents. Here, we report a cyanuric acid derived tri-vinyl sulfone core (CA-TVS) as a versatile chemical platform for the ondemand assembly of radiotheranostic agents. The three vinyl sulfone functional groups enable rapid, high-yield Michael addition with diverse functional components including targeting ligands (e.g., small molecules or peptides), radiometal chelators, and/or pharmacokinetic tuning motifs under mild aqueous conditions. As a proof of concept, a prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted bivalent conjugate was assembled from CA-TVS and radiolabeled with the imaging/therapeutic 64/67Cu pair in high radiochemical yield and purity. Compared with monomeric PSMA agents, the bivalent constructs demonstrate markedly enhanced tumor uptake and retention, while maintaining low backgrounds in healthy organs. This favorable distribution also translates into a promising therapeutic efficacy in vivo. The generality of this platform was further demonstrated by constructing agents targeting additional cancer biomarkers. In conclusion, this work establishes CA-TVS as a modular, easy-to-handle, and broadly adaptable core platform for rapid development of TRT agents.

papers.title: The Coupling of Mucin-1 b Subunit with Cellular Membranes is Altered Upon Peptide Binding: Towards the Elucidation of Its Signal Transduction Mechanism.
papers.abstract: The influence of the Mucin-1 (Muc-1) receptor in cancer progression and its bad prognosis makes it a potentially ideal target in pharmacology. However, the mechanism of action and its interaction with the cellular membrane are not fully characterized at a proper atomistic level. In this contribution, using long all-atom molecular dynamic simulation, largely exceeding the µs time-scale, we analyze the interaction of the membrane embedded Muc-1 b subunit with a peptide mimicking the MLuc-1 a interface. Despite showing the stability of the protein/peptide aggregate, which can be exploited for drug delivery, we also show and characterize the long-range structural modification of the transmembrane subunit upon peptide binding. This represents the first modeling of the initial Muc-1 signal transduction determined by the formation of the a/b hetordimer.

papers.title: Machine Learning as a Lens for Breaking Scaling Relations in Heterogeneous Catalysis: Strategies, Evidence, and Limits
papers.abstract: Linear scaling relations and the Sabatier principle impose a fundamental ceiling on the activity of heterogeneous catalysts: because the binding energies of related intermediates are coupled, optimising one weakens another, and the best catalyst sits at a volcano apex rather than beyond it. A fast-growing literature claims that machine learning (ML) can identify catalysts that break these relations. This review asks a deliberately sceptical question: does ML genuinely reveal scaling-relation violations, or are many reported “escapes” modelling artefacts of small DFT datasets and overfitting? We first establish the physics of scaling and BEP relations and their d-band origin1,2, then introduce a critical taxonomy that distinguishes genuine breaking from mere widening of the accessible energy distribution and from circumventing scaling via new site types. We survey the ML toolbox for detecting violations (interpretable models, GNN adsorption-energy predictors and active learning over composition space3–5), and then assess five material strategies (single-atom, high-entropy-alloy, inverse, dual-atom and strained/intermetallic catalysts) against this taxonomy. Our central contribution is to separate genuine physical escape from statistical artefact: high-entropy alloys, for instance, predominantly widen the adsorption-energy distribution rather than break the underlying correlation5,6. We close with best practices for validating ML-identified violations.

papers.title: Rapid monoclonal antibody-based methods for the monitoring of dihydroanatoxins in water samples
papers.abstract: Dihydroanatoxins are emerging contaminants produced by cyanobacteria that proliferate in continental surface waters. Recent studies suggest that the oral toxicity of dihydroanatoxin-a may surpass that of anatoxin‑a, a congener of the same family of homotropane alkaloids. Currently, climate change and anthropogenic contamination of continental water reservoirs contribute to more frequent and extensive cyanobacterial blooms, which release these hazardous secondary metabolites. This underscores the need for sensitive and reliable analytical methods capable of detecting dihydroanatoxins at trace levels. In this study, novel bioconjugates based on dihydroanatoxin-a haptens were synthesized and thoroughly characterized, enabling the generation of a panel of high-affinity monoclonal antibodies. Several antibodies exhibited IC50 values below 1 nM for both dihydroanatoxins, dihydroanatoxin-a and dihydrohomoanatoxin-a. Using these immunoreagents, we developed, for the first time, a highly sensitive monoclonal antibody-based direct competitive ELISA with a limit of detection of 0.016 ng/mL for dihydroanatoxin-a. The optimized immunoassay showed excellent precision and accuracy in a variety of fortified freshwater samples (lake, river, water well, and irrigation pond) across concentrations from 0.5 to 200 ng/mL, with recoveries between 79% and 112%, and coefficients of variation below 20%. Validation using naturally contaminated samples revealed good statistical agreement with a reference chromatographic method. Additionally, a lateral-flow immunochromatographic assay was developed for the on-site analysis of both dihydroanatoxins, providing a visual limit of detection of 3 ng/mL. Overall, the developed immunochemical methods offer rapid, reliable, and cost-effective approaches for monitoring dihydroanatoxins in environmental water samples. Keywords Emergent cyanotoxins; Homotropane alkaloids; Monoclonal antibodies; Rapid Methods; Freshwater Monitoring

papers.title: Induced Structural Disorder Enables High Ionic Conductivity and Capacity in Li2Fe1−xMnxCl4 Cathodes
papers.abstract: The development of high energy density solid-state batteries requires the discovery of ionically conductive cathode active materials which enable the production of electrode composites with high cathode active material loadings. Here, we show that an ionic conductivity of 0.86 mS/cm can be achieved in Li2FeCl4 by increasing the structural disorder via a facile mechanochemical and low temperature annealing procedure. We find that the metastable Fd3̅m Li2FeCl4 phase produced by mechanochemical synthesis undergoes a room temperature structural re-ordering to a Cmmm phase on the scale of months, which lowers the ionic conductivity by 2 orders of magnitude, and raises concerns for the shelf-life of metastable materials. We demonstrate that the structural disorder can be “lockedin” by introducing Mn2+ into the system without significantly impacting the ionic conductivity. We further elucidate the origin of the phase transitions and the role of entropic stabilisation on ionic conductivity though density functional theory modelling and machine-learning force field molecular dynamics calculations. These reveal a 3-dimensional Li+ conduction pathway in the disordered structure, which is not present when the material is ordered. By engineering high conductivity disordered, Fd3̅m, phases of Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4, solid-state batteries containing zero catholyte are demonstrated with high voltage plateaus of 3.7 V and capacities of 115 mAh/gCAM and 90 mAh/gCAM, respectively. Considering the high cathode loadings, we demonstrate that the materials Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4 can be used to produce solid state battery cathodes with higher energy densities that that of the commercial material LiFePO4 with similar cost effectiveness.

papers.title: Formation of an oxyhydroxide reconstruction in the water-CeO2(111) interface
papers.abstract: Dynamic reconstruction of metal oxide surfaces in aqueous environments governs processes across catalysis, energy conversion, and biomedicine. Upon contact with water, these materials often transform into an oxyhydroxide that defines the exposed surface sites. However, atomic-scale structure of oxyhydroxide surfaces remains unclear, limiting prediction of their properties. Here we identify the structure of the oxyhydroxide formed at the water-CeO 2 (111) interface by combining near-ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, infrared absorption spectroscopy, cryogenic non-contact atomic force microscopy, and machine-learning assisted global optimization and density functional theory calculations. We find that cerium oxyhydroxide preferentially orders in a (√3 × √3) unit cell, with multiple configurations coexisting within a narrow energy landscape. Oxyhydroxide adopts a corrugated structure formed through rearrangement of CeO 2 units and is stabilized by a network of hydroxyl groups. These results establish oxyhydroxide formation as a kinetically driven surface reconstruction that emerges only above both critical pressures and temporal thresholds.

papers.title: Activating Interstitial Oxygen Conduction in Sr3V2O8 Palmierite Oxides through Minimal Mo Substitution
papers.abstract: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2- conductivity approximately two orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600°C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2- jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.

papers.title: Integrating multi-assay data for antioxidant discovery
papers.abstract: Molecular functions are often characterized by multiple experimental assays that capture related yet non-equivalent mechanistic aspects of the same phenotype. While these assays collectively provide a richer description, their heterogeneity is often treated as a source of variability or noise, raising the question of whether such measurements can instead be exploited as transferable information for molecular discovery. Antioxidant activity exemplifies this challenge because it is commonly evaluated using multiple mechanistically distinct assays. Here, we present AntioxidantDB, a manually curated database containing 522 standardized activity records of eight endpoints. Using this resource, we develop AntioxidantBERT, which combines pretraining with cross-assay learning to jointly model heterogeneous endpoints. Our model outperforms graph- and sequence-based baseline models, demonstrating that heterogeneous assays contain complementary information that can improve molecular prediction. We further apply the model to screen a curated compound library and experimentally validate a set of highly potent antioxidants. Among them, 2″-O-galloylhyperin exhibited strong antioxidant activity and effectively suppressed oxidation-associated browning in plant tissues, outperforming conventional antioxidant controls. This work shows that fragmented assay measurements describing the same molecular function can be integrated to leverage information often overlooked in conventional strategies, providing a general approach for expanding usable data resources in data-scarce settings.

papers.title: A Diamagnetic Fractional-Valence State in Nb(pyrazine)2Cl2
papers.abstract: Pyrazine-based coordination solids have recently emerged as a versatile platform for realizing high-temperature magnetism, valence switching, and correlated electronic behavior. Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of Nb(pyrazine) 2 Cl 2 , a 4d analog of the antiferromagnet V II (pyrazine) 2 Cl 2 . The combined analysis of crystallographic data, X-ray absorption spectra, magnetism, and electrical conductivity indicates a non-integral Nb valence exceeding a simple Nb II description. Surprisingly, Nb(pyrazine) 2 Cl 2 exhibits complete suppression of local magnetic moments and a fully diamagnetic ground state. Supported by density functional theory calculations, our experimental findings reveal how increasing metal–ligand covalency can drive redox non-innocent coordination frameworks beyond the localized-moment limit, yielding a diamagnetic fractional-valence state that lies near the boundary between localized and itinerant electronic behavior.

papers.title: A Consumer-Grade 3D Printer-Based Platform for Automated Electrochemical Sensor Modification, Characterization and Testing
papers.abstract: In this work, we detail an automated electrical contacting stepper system to enable high-throughput electrochemical testing viz moving from ~10 sensors tested and calibrated/day (manual) to ~200 sensors per day (automated) through low cost modification (~€ 20) of hobbyist 3D printers compatible with commercial potentiostat systems. The demonstrated system enables sequential measurement of 16 sensor chips with six sensors per chip, with reduced operator intervention from ~ 3.7 hrs to < 10 mins. System modifications are outlined to enable adaptation for solid state 4-electrode electrochemical testing at scale, providing a realistic route to robust dataset collection.

papers.title: A Brief Overview of the Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation Coating on Mg and its Alloys
papers.abstract: Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation (PEO) process can produce thick, adherent, hard, and corrosion resistant coating over Mg and its alloys. However, these coatings contain micropores, and cracks which degrade the quality of these coatings. A greater understanding of the coating formation mechanism is paramount to overcome these shortcomings on the coating. By appropriately controlling the processing parameters such as composition of the electrolyte, current density, mode of electricity, particle addition, and pH of the solution can improve the quality of these coatings by a long margin. In addition, it is important to understand how to quantify the properties of these coatings.

papers.title: Cobaloxime Catalyzed Efficient Carbene Insertion into Boron−Hydrogen Bond
papers.abstract: Organoboron compounds are important building blocks in organic synthesis because of their versatility in a wide range of downstream transformations. The carbon–boron bond can be readily converted into alcohols, amines, and other functional groups, while also serving as a valuable handle for the construction of C–C and C–heteroatom bonds. Consequently, organoboron compounds have found widespread applications in medicinal chemistry, materials science, and chemical biology. Although numerous methods for C–B bond formation have been developed, general and efficient synthetic strategies remain highly desirable. Carbene insertion into B–H bonds represent a direct and atom-economical approach to C–B bond construction; however, most reported methods rely heavily on noble-metal catalysts. In contrast, the use of earth-abundant metals for this transformation remains unexplored, and cobalt-catalyzed B–H insertion reactions are particularly rare. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed B–H insertion reaction of borane adducts using diazo compounds as carbene precursors. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope with various borane derivatives and delivers organoboron products in good to excellent yields. The synthetic utility of the method is further demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis and downstream transformations of the products into other valuable boron-containing compounds. Preliminary mechanistic studies support the involvement of a cobalt-associated ylide intermediate in the catalytic cycle.

papers.title: Assemblies of Pt(II) complexes under non-equilibrium conditions for temporal signal processing
papers.abstract: The fabrication of artificial non-equilibrium systems offers an effective pathway toward designing smart, adaptive materials with life-like functions. While supramolecular assemblies of platinum(II) complexes provide excellent luminescence for imaging, sensing and photocatalytic applications, these systems operate under equilibrium and hitherto lack fuel-dependent adaptive features. Herein, we introduce an ATP-fueled nonequilibrium supramolecular assembly of a Pt(II) complex (named Pt-1 ) that integrates dissipative photoluminescence (PL), tailored lifetime, and temporal signal processing. ATP induces the self-assembly of Pt-1 into ordered nanostructures through Pt···Pt interactions and π–π stacking, generating enhanced red luminescence arising from a low-energy metal–metal–to–ligand charge transfer (MMLCT) band. The transient Pt-1·ATP assembly exhibits a long-lived triplet excited state with an absolute PL quantum yield of 13.1%, whereas the disassembled state remains weakly emissive. Notably, enzyme-mediated ATP hydrolysis autonomously regulates the lifetime of the active assembly, establishing a dissipative reaction network that transiently encodes functional information. As a result, the PL response is strictly confined to a programmable time window under non-equilibrium conditions. The input sequence and temporal overlap of fuel inputs encode optical outputs in both intensity and time, transforming static combinational logic into four-dimensional information processing. Finally, by leveraging these transient luminescent states, we established a physical security platform for advanced data encryption and dynamic anticounterfeiting. These findings offer a generalised blueprint for engineering time-programmable optical functions and intelligent information processing capabilities into non-equilibrium soft materials.

papers.title: Expanding Uranyl Peroxide Cluster Chemistry via the Introduction of Superoxide Radicals
papers.abstract: Herein we introduce uranyl peroxide clusters that incorporate superoxide radical anions (O2•-) and provide structural and spectroscopic details for the first two examples of this new class of materials, Rb@U60Ox30 – superoxo and K@U60Ox30 – superoxo (compounds 1 and 2). Single crystal X-ray diffraction results revealed shortened O – O bond lengths at approximately 1.4 Å suggesting O2•- replaces some of the peroxide moieties that are bound to UO22+ cations within each cluster. Spectroscopic characterization of 1 and 2 was done in the solid-state and solution using Raman, infrared, UV-Vis-NIR, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and resonance Raman spectroscopies, which probed the behavior of the uranyl, peroxide, and superoxide moieties. Both clusters break down into smaller uranyl fragments in solution, and this results in cascade reactions where superoxide radicals interact with solution components to form additional reactive oxygen species that were detected using solution state X-band EPR spectroscopy. To provide definitive spectroscopic confirmation of the presence of superoxide radical anions in the solid-state, resonance Raman spectroscopy was performed on single crystals of 1, which revealed peaks corresponding to the ν1 fundamental mode of O2•- as well as superoxide bound to the uranyl cation.

papers.title: Analytically Derived Symmetric VSEPR Geometries from Classical Energy Minimization on a Sphere
papers.abstract: The basic VSEPR molecular geometries are derived by treating electron domains as identical repelling charges constrained to a sphere. In order to minimize the total Coulombic repulsion under the constraint, Lagrange multipliers and the Gram matrix are used to show that the minimum-energy configurations for N = 2, 3, 4 are linear, trigonal planar, and tetrahedral. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this analytical approach is intractable for N > 4 due to the multi-angular nature of higher coordinate systems. This approach serves as an excellent enrichment for upper-level undergraduates in electromagnetism or mathematical chemistry and advanced linear algebra, also providing an intuitive path that motivates the shift from manual analytical derivations to computational and numerical methods.

papers.title: PhytoClip: Multimodal Wearable Sensing and Online Machine Learning for Real-Time Plant Health Monitoring and Early Stress Detection
papers.abstract: Wearable plant sensing systems for simultaneous biochemical and physical monitoring with real-time multimodal data analysis remain limited. Here, we present PhytoClip, a multimodal wearable patch that continuously monitors leaf temperature, humidity, three volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with high selectivity, and microenvironmental light intensity and CO2 concentration. PhytoClip features a bookmark-inspired design for secure attachment to leaves of diverse morphologies, supported by a flexible printed circuit board for data acquisition, wireless communication, and cloud-based monitoring. We develop PhytoSense, an open-source machine learning (ML) framework for sensor importance ranking, multi-stress classification, and early stress detection. The integrated PhytoClip-PhytoSense platform detects and classifies nine biotic and abiotic stresses in tomato plants with 92% accuracy. Notably, P. infestans on tomato was detected within 15.5 h post-inoculation, earlier than quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) (~4 days) and visual phenotyping (~7 days), highlighting the potential of integrating multimodal wearable sensing and online ML for precision agriculture.

papers.title: Pulse-Controlled Electrochemical Reactive Capture of CO2 Using a Molecular Cobalt Electrocatalyst and Amine Sorbent
papers.abstract: Electrochemical reactive capture of CO 2 (e-RCC) propose an energy efficient approach of CO 2 upcycling via CO 2 capture from dilute point source and concurrent electrochemical conversion to value added products. We report that pulsed electrolysis cab be an elegant strategy to mitigate mass transport limitations and catalyst stability in e-RCC process. From our investigation on e-RCC using 5% CO 2 v/v (balance N 2 ) as the input gas and n-butylamine as sorbent in acetonitrile/aqueous electrolyte, we report that application of pulsed anodic potential replenish the depleted CO 2 concentration at the electrode surface and concurrently re-oxidize the active cobalt-catalyst, [Co]0, into its stable [Co] 2+ , which substantially reduce catalyst decomposition and in turn minimizes HER. Under optimized conditions, pulsed electrolysis at Ec = −1.69 V with intermittent anodic potential at −0.64 V vs Fc +/0 delivers a FE(CO) of 66.0 ± 3.4%, compared to 22.3 ± 2.1% under controlled potential electrolysis.

papers.title: Integrated Hydrodynamic-Reactive Computational Framework for Fischer-Tropsch Slurry Bubble Column Reactors
papers.abstract: Fischer-Tropsch slurry bubble column reactors (FT-SBCRs) are a key technology for synthetic fuel production, yet their design and scale-up remain challenging due to the strong coupling between multiphase hydrodynamics and reactive transport. This work presents an integrated computational framework for analyzing FT-SBCR behavior from laboratory to industrial scale. The framework couples a phenomenological hydrodynamic model with a reactor-scale reaction-transport model built on a thermodynamic description of the gas-liquid system based on a rigorous equation of state. Hydrodynamic quantities governing interfacial transport are obtained from the former and passed to the latter, facilitating a more reliable prediction of reactor conversion and thermal behavior without relying on empirical pre assignments for the hydrodynamic state. The framework is validated against published cold-flow gas holdup data across a range of column geometries, and against a reported industrial-scale reactor case. A scale-up analysis indicates that bubble size remains largely scale-invariant (4.1–4.4 mm) while interfacial area declines substantially with increasing reactor diameter, quantifying the mass transfer penalty incurred at commercial scale. Finally, a data-driven surrogate trained on the simulation results is used to accelerate operating-condition design. By combining operating variables with hydrodynamic descriptors, the surrogate identifies a conversion-maximizing regime achieving CO conversion above 85%, suggesting that this combined computational approach can provide directional insights for efficient FT-SBCR design and scale-up strategies.

papers.title: Shear viscosity of liquid Sb and Bi from pseudopotential theory: the temperature-insensitive soft-tail component
How Molecular Weight Shapes the Relative Importance of Chemical and Structural Descriptors for Aqueous Solubility
papers.abstract: Learning aqueous solubility remains a key challenge in drug development for improving oral bioavailability. Traditional data-driven solubility estimations using standard supervised models, however, can often suppress the information embedded in a candidate molecule's chemical and structural properties. In addition to the predictive analyses for solubility, it is also important to investigate the underlying inference associated with the solubility prediction of a potential drug candidate. This paper attempts to learn such properties and further proposes an analytic framework with an additive characterization that provides insights into the differential contributions of chemical and graphical descriptors. The dataset used in this work includes over 9000 molecules with structural, chemical, and electronic properties. Using graph-theoretic attributes derived from molecular graphs, we characterize the structural traits of the molecules associated with aqueous solubility. Our analyses highlight that the relative importance of chemical and structural descriptors shifts systematically with molecular weight: chemical descriptors dominate for molecules below the median weight, whereas graph-theoretic descriptors gain importance above it, reflecting the increased importance of atomic connectivity in heavier molecules.

papers.title: A Niobium-Pyrazine Coordination Framework with Metallic Conductivity
papers.abstract: Conductive Metal–Organic Frameworks (MOFs) based on low-valent heavy transition metals remain largely unexplored despite their potential to support itinerant electronic properties. Herein, we report the Nb(pyz) 2 Cl 2 framework (pyz = pyrazine), the first metallic MOF incorporating an early 4d metal node. Through a combination of electrical conductivity, magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity measurements, we demonstrate that Nb(pyz) 2 Cl 2 exhibits an intrinsic metallic conductivity, with a finite density of states at the Fermi level. These results underscore the potential of heavy transition metals for constructing highly conductive coordination frameworks and provide access to extended crystalline solids containing low-valent 4d metal ions.

papers.title: Inhibition of Oxidative Activity by Photo-induced Surface Hydroxyl Groups in Bismuth Titanium Oxide Photocatalyst Detected by Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging
papers.abstract: The surface structure of semiconductor photocatalysts plays a critical role in the extraction of charge carriers during photocatalytic reactions. However, the surface structures of many photocatalysts are dynamic under catalytic conditions, which makes identifying photo-induced changes and their effect on photocatalytic activity challenging. Herein we use super-resolution, single-molecule fluorescence imaging to map the spatial distribution of catalytically active regions and quantify the changes in activity of those regions for photocatalytic oxidation in bismuth titanium oxide (Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 ) nanoplates. Individual nanoplates varied widely in both activity and stability, reflecting significant heterogeneity among a single synthesis batch of photocatalyst particles. We observed that while the nanoplates are more active around the perimeter of the basal facet, those perimeter regions decrease in activity at the same relative rate as the rest of the basal facet, indicating a spatially uniform degradation mechanism. Through ensemble structural characterization of the nanoplates after irradiation, we identified surface hydroxyl groups as the photo-induced feature. Our results indicate that surface hydroxyl groups introduce hole trap states that increase charge recombination at the surface of the nanoplates leading to the observed decrease in activity. Surprisingly, we identified nanoscale features that do not begin with high activity but exhibit a slower rate of activity loss, leading to regions with greater activity relative to the rest of the basal facet at the end of imaging. Our findings highlight the importance of not only understanding how different nanoscale features influence catalytic activity but also how these features evolve over time, which dictates catalyst stability.

papers.title: Switching between C1 and C2 Pathways via Suppressed Phase Separation in Cu–Ag Alloys for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2RR) is a promising approach for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals. Copper (Cu) catalysts uniquely enable the formation of both single-carbon products such as methane (CH4) and multi-carbon (C2+) products such as ethylene (C2H4) but achieving precise control over product selectivity remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate Cu–Ag alloy catalysts prepared by a direct sputtering method of catalysts onto gas diffusion electrodes to elucidate how atomic-scale mixing influences CO2RR selectivity. The product distribution strongly depends on the composition. A small amount of Ag doping approximately 4 at.% enhances the formation of C2+ products, whereas further increasing Ag content suppresses C2+ products formation and increases CH4 selectivity. This behavior indicates that C2+ product formation critically depends on contiguous Cu active sites, while excessive Ag doping disrupts Cu ensembles required for C–C coupling and suppresses C2+ product formation. These findings highlight the critical role of contiguous Cu site in governing CO2RR pathways and demonstrate atomic-scale structural control as an effective strategy for tuning product selectivity in alloy catalysts.

papers.title: Reaction Telemetry for Wireless Continuous Reaction Profiling
papers.abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved using specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sample withdrawal. Here, we 15 introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach employs light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous thermometric and calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical systems, providing real-time access to reaction dynamics under native operating conditions with 20 sub-second temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, mechanistic investigation, and data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

papers.title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
papers.abstract: We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 + O 2 → H 2 O 2 ) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H 2 O 2 vs H 2 O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O 2 . This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H 2 O 2 selectivity by >1000× in aprotic solvents and improve H 2 O 2 selectivity by ~60× compared to protic solvents. We show the synthetic value of H 2 O 2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via Lewis-acidic TS-1 zeolite that activates H 2 O 2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone with quantitative yield. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation applicable to a broad expanse of organic substrates.

papers.title: Seamless QM/MM simulations via a GROMACS–CP2K interface
papers.abstract: Understanding and controlling chemical reactivity in biological systems requires atomic-level insight into processes that are often inaccessible to experiments. Hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations provide a powerful framework to describe chemical reactions in complex environments, but their practical application remains limited by fragmented software ecosystems, restricted accessibility, and methodological approximations that can compromise accuracy and reproducibility. In particular, many existing QM/MM implementations rely on ad hoc couplings, proprietary software, or truncated treatments of long-range electrostatic interactions. Here, we present a robust and fully periodic QM/MM interface between the open-source molecular dynamics engine GROMACS and the electronic structure theory code CP2K. The implementation enables efficient and reproducible QM/MM molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations with a consistent treatment of long-range electrostatics under periodic boundary conditions. By combining the strengths of two widely used community codes, this interface provides a general and scalable platform for studying

papers.title: Unprecedented Tandem Cyclization on Perlin Aldehyde Towards Stereoselective Synthesis of 1,3-Difunctionalized 2-Deoxy Diindolyl-C-Glycosides
papers.abstract: The stereoselective synthesis of 1,3-difunctionalized deoxy sugars remains a synthetic challenge in organic chemistry, despite of significant advancements in modern synthetic methodologies. Herein, we discovered a mild, efficient, highly regio- and stereoselective, transition-metal-free method for the synthesis of 1,3-difunctionalized deoxy sugars using a tandem cyclization reaction between various Perlin aldehydes and a diverse range of indole derivatives, catalyzed by a catalytic amount of indium trichloride within 1-2 hours. This transformation proceeds under mild reaction conditions despite dense carbohydrate functionality, enabling the regio- and stereoselective synthesis of a wide range of intricate 1,3-functionalized 2-deoxy diindolyl-C-glycosides in excellent yield, paving the way for further exploration of their applications in medicinal chemistry and chemical biology. Concurrently, to rationalize the observed regio- and stereoselectivity of these synthetically challenging molecular scaffolds, we also explored the mechanistic details for this transformation by using DFT studies.

papers.title: Ensemble-Based, Database-Independent Prioritization of Sesquiterpene Lactones by Rule-Based MassQL Analysis
authors: Gabriel da Silva Ferreira de Lima
papers.abstract: RATIONALE Sesquiterpene lactones (STLs) comprise a large and structurally diverse class of plant secondary metabolites with important ecological and pharmacological activities. However, class-level detection of STLs in untargeted LC–MS/MS datasets remains challenging because of extensive structural variability, frequent oxidation and acylation, and limited representation in spectral libraries. We therefore developed a database-independent strategy for STL prioritization based on chemically encoded MassQL rules. METHODS An ensemble-based MassQL framework was constructed using formula-driven precursor envelopes representing STL chemical space, systematic Δmass expansions corresponding to common biosynthetic modifications, and mechanism-informed MS/MS neutral-loss patterns. Multiple independent MassQL compendia were executed in parallel, acting as orthogonal detectors of STL-like fragmentation behavior. Candidate features were prioritized according to the number and diversity of matched rule families rather than by spectral similarity or exact structural matching. RESULTS Application of the framework to GNPS sesquiterpene datasets recovered STL-like spectra through convergence of multiple independent fragmentation rules, including precursor–product mass relationships, dehydration, decarboxylation, and acyl-loss signatures. Analysis of the large-scale MassIVE dataset MSV000087728 identified 36,790 features matching at least one STL-oriented rule set, whereas only 2,430 spectra corresponded to GNPS library annotations. Features exhibiting high levels of multi-rule agreement included representative germacranolides, guaianolides, eudesmanolides, and related STL subclasses. The framework also recovered chemically adjacent lactone-containing terpenoids, illustrating both the breadth and boundaries of the encoded chemical space. CONCLUSIONS The proposed framework enables transparent, scalable, and database-independent prioritization of STL-like features in untargeted metabolomics datasets. By focusing on chemically coherent MS/MS behavior rather than compound identity, the approach expands exploration beyond spectral-library coverage and provides a generalizable strategy for class-level retrieval of structurally diverse natural products. Graphical Abstract (GA) Database-independent strategy for prioritizing sesquiterpene lactones using untargeted LC-MS/MS data based on an ensemble of chemically encoded MassQL rules. Instead of relying on spectral library matching, the framework interrogates fragmentation behavior using formula envelopes, ∆mass expansions, and mechanism-driven neutral losses to rank candidate features based on multi-rule convergence. The result is an evidence-weighted prioritization of STL-like chemical space, where the unit of inference is coherent MS/MS behavior rather than compound identity, facilitating systematic STL surveys even for non-specialists in large untargeted datasets.

papers.title: Inline Capacity Recovery of Vanadium Flow Batteries via Methanol-Mediated Catalytic Rebalancing
papers.abstract: Vanadium flow batteries (VFBs) are promising for grid-scale, long-duration energy storage, but their long-term operation is limited by capacity decay from electrolyte imbalance, especially oxidative valence drift caused by parasitic side reactions. Here, we report an inline capacity recovery strategy based on methanol-mediated catalytic rebalancing during VFB operation. As a compact chemical electron carrier, methanol delivers 6 electrons per molecule upon full oxidation, providing high gravimetric electron density and low materials cost. A methanol-fed Pt/C side-stream reactor was integrated with the VFB posolyte loop to reduce excess VO 2 + and rebalance the electrolyte valence. Spectroscopic analyses confirm quantitative conversion without detectable residual methanol-derived organic species under the testing conditions. An inline recovery was triggered whenever capacity retention decreased to ~95%, repeatedly restoring the capacity to >99% of its initial value during 30 days of continuous operation. This strategy provides a practical route for continuous VFB capacity maintenance and electrolyte lifecycle management.

papers.title: Continuous Light-Driven Pure CO2 Production by Regenerative Non-Aqueous Amine–Photoacid Cycling
papers.abstract: Photochemical CO2 separation offers a low-temperature alternative to conventional thermal CO2 separation, replacing fuel-derived heat with light as the energy input. Although prior photoacid and photobase systems have shown promising light-driven CO2 capture–release behavior, continuous pure-CO2 generation from dilute feeds remains insufficiently developed. Here, we demonstrate light-driven pure-CO2 production from a 15% CO2 feed, reaching 3.2 sccm from 1.2 mL min−1 of circulating sorbent solution in a single lab-scale reactor, equivalent to 4.6 L day−1. In the dimethyl sulfoxide amine–photoacid platform, acidity matching allows each photoacid molecule to undergo repeated excited-state proton transfer, coupling carbamic acidforming CO2 capture to efficient release. The evolved CO2 forms self-generated bubbles without external sweep gas in the reduced-pressure continuous flow photoreactor developed in this work. Techno-economic analysis projects a minimum separation cost of $31.7 tCO2 −1 from 15% CO2 source. These results establish a practical foundation for scalable light-driven carbon capture.

papers.title: Molecular conformation as a determinant of tripeptide self-assembly
papers.abstract: In this work we evaluate whether computed tripeptide conformational ensembles are informative of self-assembly propensity. We focused on previously reported tripeptides (the six C-terminal amidated D/Y/F sequence isomers and FFD) and analyzed their conformational ensembles using all-atom molecular dynamics (AA-MD) simulations and intramolecular sidechain dihedral angles as a collective variable. Using a novel method to numerically characterize the conformational free energy landscapes (FELs) generated from these ensembles, we find a correlation between FEL steepness and a sequence's tendency to self-assemble or remain in solution. In addition, we evaluate and rationalize the impact of water model selection on conformational ensembles in terms of peptide-water interaction strengths. The presented methodology implicitly accounts for amino acid sequence context, which is a major determinant of divergent properties for sequence isomers. It also has a low associated computational cost, making use of single molecule simulations to predict supramolecular assembly outcomes. These features make it an important advancement in the generation of theory-informed design rules for peptide materials.

papers.title: Anomalous Reversal of CO2-Induced Viscosity/Diffusivity Trends in Water: A Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Experimental viscosity data for dilute, water-rich aqueous CO2 are available only up to 449 K, leaving the intermediate-temperature regime relevant to geothermal and CCUS (Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage) applications largely unexplored. Here, equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations were used to compute viscosity, self-diffusion coefficients, and density of CO2–H2O mixtures over 278–900 K and 10–30 MPa using multiple water and CO2 force-field combinations. At 278–443 K, increasing CO2 mole fraction increased viscosity and decreased self-diffusion, consistent with available low-temperature measurements. At 573 K, however, the trend reversed: at xCO2 = 5 mol%, viscosity decreased by about 10% relative to pure water at 25 MPa, whereas the self-diffusion coefficient increased by about 7–8% at 20 MPa. Above 700 K, composition effects became weaker and often comparable to the associated uncertainties. Analyses of number density, CO2 hydration, hydrogen bonding, tetrahedral order, and rotational relaxation show that the reversal behavior originates from the temperature-dependent volumetric and structural response of the water network to CO2 dissolution. The results identify a transport anomaly near 573 K that should be considered in modeling water-rich CO2-bearing fluids.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Furan-to-Pyridazine Skeletal Editing
papers.abstract: Pyridazines are privileged diazine scaffolds in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their synthesis remains hampered by the inherent limitations of conventional condensation methods and recent pyridine-based skeletal editing approaches: poor regioselectivity, narrow substrate scope, and requirement for additional oxidation steps. Herein, we report the visible-light-mediated skeletal editing of furans to pyridazines via formal O-to-NN atom-pair exchange using hydrazine hydrate as the dinitrogen source. This ring expansion operates under metal-free, room-temperature, aerobic conditions and bypasses conventional 1,4-dicarbonyl condensation pathways.
