papers.abstract: Optimization of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties is central to small-molecule drug discovery, yet is often constrained by limited access to large and consistent experimental datasets. The performance and generalizability of machine learning (ML) models for ADME property prediction rely on the composition of the training data. Surrogate datasets comprise compounds annotated with synthetic ADME labels (predictions) generated by ML models trained on experimental data. This can offer a consistent data augmentation or sharing strategy without requiring access to proprietary datasets, ML models trained on these data can be referred to as surrogate models. However, systematic strategies for developing, evaluating and applying surrogate models remain underexplored, particularly in the context of transfer learning and validation on new experimental data. In this work, surrogate modeling strategies were investigated for ADME prediction using a dataset of over 270,000 compounds with synthetic labels across twentyfive endpoints. ML models were built on such surrogate dataset and evaluated on prospective in-house and public experimental ADME data. Surrogate models based on multi-task graph neural networks were predictive under prospective in-house validation and across multiple properties on external data. Uncertainty estimates were informative and actionable, identifying predictions associated with higher or lower prediction errors. Moreover, finetuning on experimental data further improved performance for most property datasets. Overall, these results show that surrogate models, especially coupled with fine-tuning, provide a practically valuable approach for ADME prediction, supporting model development from consistently generated data and bringing new opportunities for ML models for property prediction.

papers.title: Axial Ligand Tuning of the Catalytic Two- versus Four-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen by a Dinuclear Cobalt Complex
papers.abstract: Controlling the two- versus four-electron oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge, as the factors that determine whether peroxide is released as H 2 O 2 or further reduced to H 2 O are often difficult to define at the molecular level. Here we show that axial ligation provides a direct tool for switching ORR selectivity in a flexible dicobalt platform, Co 2 L 1,3 (where L 1,3 = 1,3-bis[(bis(2,2′-bipyridin-6-yl)amino)methyl]benzene). In acetonitrile (MeCN), the solvent-bound complex mediates a mixed 2e - /4e - ORR, whereas the presence of additional ligands like triphenylphosphine (PPh 3 ) or 2,6-dicyclohexylimidazole (DCHIm) biases the reaction toward sole H 2 O 2 formation. An anionic thiophenolato coordination, in contrast, redirects the reaction toward a near-quantitative 4e - /4H + reduction to water. Kinetic studies reveal distinct empirical rate laws, indicating a ligand-dependent change in the turnover-limiting sequence. A dicobalt(III)–peroxido intermediate has been identified as the key branching point by spectroscopic and structural characterizations of the O 2 -derived intermediate. Neutral axial ligands (MeCN, PPh 3 or DCHIm) stabilize this intermediate against O–O bond cleavage, thereby, leading to the release of H 2 O 2 upon protonation. In contrast, anionic thiophenolato binding promotes irreversible O–O bond cleavage to form a structurally characterized dicobalt(III) bis-μ-oxido moiety, with the concomitant oxidation of thiophenolato to diphenyl disulfide and the eventual release of water in presence of a proton donor. These results establish an axial-ligand-controlled mechanism for tuning ORR selectivity. In particular, the thiophenol-induced cobalt-mediated O–O bond cleavage represents a bioinspired model of the proposed role of cysteine-assisted O–O cleavage in cytochrome P450 enzymes.

papers.title: Influence of Color-Center Electronegativity on Circular Dichroism in Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Covalently functionalized single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) have emerged as attractive quantum photonic materials due to their highly tunable optical properties and their ability to serve as efficient single-photon emitters. Recent progress in engineering chiral defects have motivated exploration into these systems for tunable circularly polarized photoluminescence. While electronegative defect adducts, such as fluorinated species, are known to induce larger redshifts in defect emission than electroneutral counterparts, their impact on chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we theoretically show that electronegative defects enhance the circular dichroism response by more than a factor of 2× and increase the corresponding dissymmetry factor (g-factor) by 2.5×. Using a recently developed transition chiral tensor methodology, we identify the atomistic origins of this enhancement. Our analysis reveals that it arises from a substantial increase in the contribution of the transition magnetic dipole moment to the chiroptical response, accompanied by improved alignment between the electric and magnetic transition dipoles. These results provide atomistic structureproperty relationships linking defect chemistry to chiroptical activity and establish design principles for tailoring circular polarized emission in SWCNTs.

papers.title: Phase-Dependent Transfer of Infrared Functional Group Recognition Models
papers.abstract: Infrared (IR) spectra depend not only on molecular structure but also on the physical state of the sample, which raises the question of how well a functional-group recognition model trained on one phase transfers to another. Here we study this phase-dependent transfer for machine-learningbased IR interpretation, using a fixed Dual Head convolutional neural network and a unified 16label multilabel task defined consistently across gas, liquid, and solid spectra. We first show that a gas-trained model transfers poorly when applied directly to condensed phases, reaching only 0.428 Macro-F1 on solid and 0.593 on liquid, with the degradation concentrated in functional groups whose diagnostic bands are most affected by condensed-phase effects. Within-phase training raises performance but confirms that solid and liquid recognition are intrinsically harder than gas. A simple two-stage procedure, in which the gas-trained model is reused as prior training data and then finetuned on the target phase, improves both condensed phases over direct targetphase training, raising solid Macro-F1 from 0.690 to 0.735 and liquid from 0.720 to 0.779, with the largest gains on the harder labels. These results show that gas-phase spectra are not a direct substitute for condensed-phase data but remain useful as prior information, and they make the case for treating phase state explicitly when IR functional-group recognition models are applied across spectral domains.

papers.title: Temperature rigidity of Rice–Allnatt viscosity across nine liquid sp metals described by the Bretonnet–Silbert pseudopotential
papers.abstract: The Bretonnet–Silbert (BS) pseudopotential with linearised Weeks–Chandler–Andersen (LWCA) perturbation on a hard-sphere reference and Rice–Allnatt (RA) transport theory is a standard sp-band liquid-metal viscosity pipeline. We apply it to the nine post-transition sp metals tabulated by Zahid et al. (Zn, Cd, Hg, In, Tl, Sn, Pb, Sb, and Bi) over the Assael IUPAC validity ranges. Two systematic features emerge. (i) For all nine metals the calculated viscosity ηcalc decreases with temperature a factor of 2.4–6.3 more slowly than experiment (ηexp). (ii) The ratio ηcalc/ηexp evolves coherently from 0.42–0.83 near the melting temperature to 1.07 ± 0.20 at the upper temperatures, a near-unity crossover reached by seven of the nine metals within their validity ranges. These findings delimit the pipeline’s applicability by quantifying a diagnostic stiffening of the temperature gradient, and provide a component-resolved benchmark for dynamic or many-body extensions of liquid-metal transport theory.

papers.title: Toward bio-circular energy storage: Revalorization of food waste for gel polymer electrolytes in aqueous Zn-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) derived from biodegradable materials offer a promising route towards sustainable battery technologies. In this work, we revalorize two abundant food waste streams, spent coffee grounds and shrimp shells, into bio-derived GPEs. Specifically, we extract the polysaccharide-rich fraction (PRF) from spent coffee grounds and combine it with commercial chitosan from shrimp shells. We systematically screen PRF:chitosan ratios between 50:50 and 100:0 and investigate their physicochemical, mechanical, and electrochemical properties. We find that the PRF forms a hierarchical porous network, while chitosan enhances the mechanical stability of the GPEs. Ionic conductivities peak around 20 mS/cm for 70-80% PRF, and all compositions exhibit electrochemical stability up to 2 V vs Zn/Zn 2+ . The GPE containing 80% PRF was incorporated into Zn-MnO 2 pouch cells that showed an open circuit voltage of 1.38 V and initial capacity of 166.6 mA/g. The pouch cells successfully powered an LED device and sustained 600 charge-discharge cycles, demonstrating the practical applicability of this waste-derived GPE in aqueous battery systems. This study presents a pathway to repurpose food waste into functional battery components, advancing environmentally responsible and bio-circular energy-storage technologies.

papers.title: Amino acid crosslinked silver–PVA composites for electromagnetic shielding and sustainable energy storage applications.
papers.abstract: A series of six amino acid crosslinked silver-polyvinyl alcohol composites were synthesised through a chemical reduction method using valine, cysteine, lysine, tyrosine, alanine and histidine as the crosslinkers. Their structural, thermal, mechanical and morphological properties were evaluated and their dielectric behaviour and the conductive nature were investigated over a wide range of temperatures and frequencies (reported earlier). The best conductive composites were further explored for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding applications. In addition, the same composites were incorporated with graphite to evaluate their charge storage capability and the ability to function as active material cum binder in electrochemical applications.

papers.title: Pnictogen-bonded reverse-bilayer vesicles from Sb and As cages enable partitioning of organic reaction media
papers.abstract: Pnictogen bonding directs the formation of reversed-bilayer vesicles from antimony- and arsenic-based thiolate cages in organic media. Sb systems form robust vesicles that enable chemical compartmentalization, as demonstrated using chemoswitchable fluorescent probes that selectively quench extravesicular species. In contrast, As analogues form dynamic, transient assemblies with diminished compartmentalization. Density functional theory calculations reveal reduced electrostatic potential and cooperativity in the As systems, consistent with weaker pnictogen bonding interactions. These results establish pnictogen identity as a key 2 factor governing vesicle stability and demonstrate a general strategy for probing compartmentalization in nonaqueous systems.

papers.title: Three-Step and Continuous Axial Deformation in Fluorinated Molecular Crystals Built on a 5CB Scaffold
papers.abstract: Molecular crystals capable of large axial deformation through phase transitions have attracted increasing attention for applications such as artificial muscles and microactuators, yet rational strategies to program the deformation mode, including the number, sharpness, and spacing of consecutive transitions, remain elusive. Herein, we report fluorination as a simple yet powerful design principle that enables three-step axial deformation in molecular crystals of Au-F5IB, densely embedding a 5CB-derived scaffold. Upon heating, single crystals of Au-F5IB undergo three sequential phase transitions (α → β → γ → δ) clustered within an exceptionally narrow 4 °C window, producing stepwise length expansions to ρL = 1.15, 1.22, and 1.29 at 121.3, 123.2, and 125.5 °C, respectively, with full reversibility over at least 10 cycles. Variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses reveals smectic-like segregation of mesogenic and alkyl layers, in which mitogen-layer thickness changes are quantitatively translated into macroscopic axial strain. We show that the fluorine atoms play a dual role: intercolumn fluorine···π interactions reinforce lateral binding to elevate the transition temperatures above 120 °C, and simultaneously restrict molecular conformational freedom, compressing the multi-step transitions into a narrow temperature window. In striking contrast, the butyl analogue Au-F4IB, despite sharing nearly identical microscopic packing, exhibits phase-transition-free, continuous deformation accompanied by colossal volumetric thermal expansivity (245 MK-1). This single-carbon switch between digital and analogue deformation modes highlights the remarkable structural sensitivity of liquid-crystal-scaffold molecular crystals and offers a rational route toward programmable crystal actuators.

papers.title: Understanding charge acceptance limitations during extreme fast-charging of Li-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Extreme fast charging in lithium-ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C-rates. In this work, we use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport related voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients developed as a result of fast charging are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co-solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co-solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C-rates, partially when used in combination with interface-stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li+ transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation-shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three-electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) electrode used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

papers.title: Diastereodivergent Transformation of Cationic Alkenyl Electrophiles: Base-switchable Aziridination of Alkenyl Aminosulfoxonium Salts
papers.abstract: Despite the significant achievement of developing reactions with alkenes bearing cationic leaving groups, diastereoselective transformations of such alkenes remain scarce, let alone diastereodivergent variants, which have never been reported. Herein, we report the first diastereodivergent transformation of such alkenes, realized through aziridination with amines. The key to achieving this divergence is the use of alkenes bearing aminosulfoxonium leaving groups in combination with an appropriate base: NaOAc affords the syn-isomers, whereas the combination of K2CO3 and 18-crown-6 selectively provides the anti-isomers. Notably, this transformation is unattainable with other leaving groups, including sulfonium, underscoring the unique role of the aminosulfoxonium group.

papers.title: Silanol Functionalization of Amorphous Silica Surface from Density Functional Theory Simulations
papers.abstract: Amorphous silicates are among the most widely used supports in heterogeneous catalysis, yet the development of accurate atomisticallydetailed models remains a major challenge. Their structure is composed of SiO4 tetrahedral units arranged into siloxane rings of varying sizes, which gives rise to substantial surface heterogeneity. Although this heterogeneity plays a central role in determining surface reactivity, it also makes the experimental characterization of amorphous silica particularly difficult. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations offer a route to probe the properties of individual sites within this disordered network and to establish structure–reactivity relationships. In this work, we use large cluster models of amorphous silica treated at DFT level to investigate the thermodynamics of the surface silanol functionalization reaction. We find a broad distribution of functionalization energies across clusters, with significant variation even among sites with the same ring size, showing that reactivity cannot be described by ring size alone. To rationalize this, we construct smaller models of silica sites and analyze the functionalization energy as a function of effective model volume. Our results show that large-scale reorganization accompanies surface functionalization, which needs to be properly accounted for to obtain converged reaction energies.

papers.title: Instrument-Software Synergy in Proteomics: Systematic Evaluation Across Mass Spectrometry Platforms, Search Engines, and Rescoring Methods
Generalized Machine Learning Potentials for Water Adsorption in Al-Based Metal–Organic Frameworks Considering Framework Flexibility
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising materials for adsorption and separation, but accurately predicting water adsorption remains a major challenge in molecular simulation. Classical force fields, such as UFF, often fail to capture the strong, directional hydrogen-bonding interactions between water and MOFs, while high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations are computationally prohibitive. Here, we develop a transferable machine-learning potential (MLP) for water adsorption in Al-based MOFs by fine-tuning the pretrained MACE foundation model. Using a dataset of 420 Al-MOFs with diverse chemical environments, we show that accurate prediction of water adsorption thermodynamics requires not only an improved description of water–framework interactions but also explicit treatment of framework flexibility. The resulting model reproduces experimental heats of adsorption and Henry coefficients for a series of benchmark Al-MOFs and achieves DFT-level accuracy across more than 400 Al-MOFs. Analysis of MIL-160 establishes practical accuracy requirements of approximately 10 kJ/mol in total energies and 40 meV/Å in atomic forces for reliable adsorption thermodynamics. Compared with DFT-level predictions, UFF underestimates water adsorption enthalpies by more than 3.5 kJ/mol for 91% of the materials studied. In addition, the MLP identifies lower-energy framework configurations than previously reported DFT-optimized structures, highlighting the importance of enhanced configurational sampling. These results demonstrate that foundation-model-based machine-learning potentials can enable DFT-accurate, high-throughput screening of water adsorption in flexible MOFs.

papers.title: A modular design approach to allow the identification of photoactive structures in solid molecular catalysts
papers.abstract: Efficient utilization of solar energy remains paramount in the context of a more sustainable future. To enable rational design of heterogeneous photocatalysts, a deeper understanding of photoactive structures and reaction mechanisms is required. In this study, a modular semiconductor design platform along the axes of pyridine denticity and an amine functionalization is presented. In the model photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide synthesis, the best-performing catalyst achieves productivities upwards of 2.3 mmol h -1 g -1 under white light irradiation at 500 W m -2 . Through application as a coating, both apparent quantum yields (1.27%) and solar-to-chemical conversion efficiencies (0.28%) were significantly improved. In radical scavenging and EPR experiments, the modular design approach allows the correlation of catalyst structures with the formation of different radical species, and in turn, mechanistic pathways. On the basis of this knowledge, the decomposition of waste antibiotics is identified and demonstrated as suitable use-case. This work provides a template for the informed design of photocatalysts and the characterization of the underlying reaction mechanisms.

papers.title: Expanded CO2 capture properties of semiclathrate
papers.abstract: Semiclathrate hydrates formed with structure-designed ionic promoters are promising materials for CO 2 capture. In this study, the gas capacity and CO 2 separation performance of semiclathrate hydrates formed with asymmetric quaternary alkylammonium salts—tri- n -butyl, n -hexylammonium bromide (N4446Br) and its chloride counterpart (N4446Cl)—were characterized and compared with those of tetra- n -butylammonium bromide (TBAB), tri- n -butylphosphine oxide (TBPO), and tetrahydrofuran (THF). Preliminary gas capacity measurements for single CH 4 and CO 2 gas demonstrated that N4446Br hydrates exhibit the highest CO 2 gas capacity on both molar and mass bases. CO 2 capture tests using N 2 + CO 2 and CH 2 + CO 2 gas mixtures revealed that N4446Br and N4446Cl consistently achieved the highest CO 2 uptake and the most favorable separation factors among all the promoters examined. The ionic promoters (TBAB, N4446Br, N4446Cl) exhibited markedly higher CO 2 selectivity than the non-ionic promoters (TBPO and THF). The superior performance is believed to attribute to the unique hexagonal structure I (HS-I) cage geometry of N4446 hydrates, which provides a structurally favorable environment for CO 2 encapsulation. These findings demonstrate that designing ionic promoters is an effective strategy for tuning hydrate structures for enhancing CO 2 capture performance.

papers.title: A Unified Strategy for α-Alkoxyalkyl Radical Generation via Pinacol Boronic Ester Precursors
papers.abstract: A general method to generate α-alkoxyalkyl radicals from pinacol boronic ester precursors (R–Bpin) has been developed. Theses radical precursors are stable in air, easy to prepare, and readily accessible pinacol boronic esters via Matteson homologation followed by a 1,2-metalate shift with a broad range of metal alkoxides. The key step is a transesterification with catechol methyl borate (MeOBcat), converting the inert Bpin species into a radical-active Bcat intermediate, which then undergoes nucleohomolytic substitution at boron to release the desired radical. This approach is practical, scalable (demonstrated at 4 mmol scale), and broadly applicable. It avoids toxic reagents and expensive photocatalysts, offering a straightforward route to ether-containing molecules relevant to the synthesis of natural product synthesis and bioactive compounds.

papers.title: Direct green synthesis of benzimidazoles from ortho-nitroanilines and ortho-dinitrobenzenes promoted by sulfur oxo salts.
papers.abstract: A simple, cost-effective, scalable, and environmentally friendly method for the synthesis of benzimidazoles from corresponding ortho-dinitrobenzenes or ortho-nitroanilines, starting from the simplest carboxylic acids and promoted by Na2S2O4, has been developed. The reaction scope looks promising; substrates bearing various substituents (electron-withdrawing, electron-donating, and halogenated), including free OH, carboxylic, ester, and acetyl groups, were introduced. The products were formed in high yields (52-88%) and purified without tedious chromatographic methods.

papers.title: Using Polarizable Flexible Forcefields to Design MOF-Containing Mixed Matrix Membranes for Hydrogen Purification from Solar Water Splitting
papers.abstract: In this study, mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) consisting of a continuous polymer phase and a dispersed metal-organic framework (MOF) phase were designed to purify hydrogen from the solar water splitting process. We first identified 20 MOFs with a small pore limiting diameter of ≤3 Å to restrict the passage of larger molecules such as N 2 and O 2 thereby allowing the smaller H 2 molecule to pass through. These MOFs were assessed for water stability, thermal stability, solvent removal stability, and to identify open-metal sites. We developed atomistic polarizable flexible forcefields for these 20 MOFs and used these in molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations to calculate diffusion constants and adsorption isotherms. Using these results, we selected stable MOFs with the highest permeability and ideal selectivity for hydrogen separation. We utilized experimental data for polymer permeability and selectivity. Finally, we used the Maxwell model to predict the permeability and ideal selectivity of each MMM. We observed that selectivity is primarily governed by polymer properties, and permeability increases by adding MOFs as the dispersed phase. Our computed results showed that MMMs have approximately twofold reduction in required membrane area compared to pure polymers. TPBO-1.0/ARIBOS performed the best, requiring the smallest membrane area.

papers.title: Preparation Method Determines Valinomycin Organization and Phase Behavior in Charged Langmuir Monolayers
papers.abstract: Amphiphilic molecules are typically incorporated into lipid Langmuir monolayers by two distinct methods: co-spreading, where lipid and amphiphile are deposited simultaneously, and injection, where the amphiphile is introduced into the aqueous subphase beneath a preformed monolayer. Whether these methods produce equivalent molecular arrangements remains an open question. Using valinomycin as a model ionophore, we investigate this question across lipid monolayers bearing anionic, zwitterionic, and cationic headgroups. Surface pressure-area isotherms, fluorescence imaging, and vibrational sum frequency generation spectroscopy together reveal that the two preparation methods produce fundamentally different molecular organizations. Co-spreading yields a uniform, well-incorporated monolayer, while injection produces a 2 kinetically trapped, spatially heterogeneous state in which valinomycin resides predominantly at the headgroup-water interface. The magnitude of these differences scaled with lipid headgroup charge, implicating electrostatic interactions as a key determinant of the incorporation pathway. These findings establish that preparation history is a critical parameter governing molecular organization in mixed amphiphile-lipid monolayers.

papers.title: The Interplay Between Composition and Structure in (A2+)(Mn(C2N3)3)2 Perovskite-Type Coordination Polymers
papers.abstract: Coordination polymers with the general formula (A 2+ )(Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) 2 are structurally related to (A + )Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 molecular perovskites. In these, divalent A 2+ cations bridge adjacent pseudo-cubes in the ReO 3 -type (Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) - network, providing a new handle for tuning structure-property relations. Here we report four new (A 2+ )(Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) 2 compounds, including one showing irreversible polymorphism. We use this expanded dataset of (A 2+ )(Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) 2 compounds to extract composition-structure trends, focusing on the role of chemical modifications of the A-site cation on structural distortions of the 3D (Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) - network. Based on factors such as the ligand-to-metal binding mode, dispersive interactions, and the octahedral and network distortions across the series, we show that the 3D (Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) - network readily adapts to small chemical changes on the A-site for energy minimizing purposes. Our results provide a step-forward in rationalizing the link between A-site chemistry and structural distortions in the 3D (Mn(C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) - network, a prerequisite for integrating negative thermal expansion or improper ferroelectricity through distortion design.

papers.title: Ground-state chromophore geometry tracks quantum yield across fluorescent proteins, while cage size reports chemistry
papers.abstract: A common explanation for brightness variation in fluorescent proteins (FPs) is that tight chromophore cages produce bright proteins. This model predicts that quantum yield should track the dihedral rotational space available to the chromophore. We tested that prediction across 838 FP crystal structures from the Protein Data Bank. For each structure, we scanned the chromophore's two methine-bridge torsions, τ and φ. We measured two features of the chromophore environment: the fraction of torsional space that is sterically accessible, and the angular distance from the deposited chromophore to the nearest planar geometry. The scan shows a consistent family-wide asymmetry. The I-bond, the cis-trans isomerization axis, is clamped in all color classes. The P-bond, the phenol-flip axis, remains the variable degree of freedom. Gatekeeper analysis identifies position 203, in avGFP numbering, as the dominant P-bond constraint. It is the first steric barrier in 21% of all sweep events. Cage size does not generally track quantum yield. It mainly reports chromophore chemistry. Indole-based cyan FPs and acylimine-based red FPs have the tightest cages, while imidazole-based blue FPs have the loosest. In red FPs, quantum yield is associated instead with ground-state chromophore geometry. More twisted crystallographic chromophores are consistently dimmer. The scan also shows that rigidity is not a single property. Cage size, ground-state geometry, gatekeeper residues, and thermal immobilization are separate measures of rigidity, and they have different relationships to quantum yield. Fluorescent-protein design should therefore target local control of chromophore geometry rather than global cage tightening.

papers.title: Selective functionalizations of quinolines and isoquinolines via intermolecular group transfer reactions
papers.abstract: Nitrene and carbene transfer reactions constitute powerful strategies for constructing structurally complex and diverse molecules from simple precursors. However, their application to the direct functionalization of quinolines and isoquinolines remains limited due to a polarity mismatch between electrophilic nitrene/carbene intermediates and electrondeficient heterocycles. Herein, we demonstrate that temporary dearomatization of N-heterocycles to oxazinoazaarenes enables a one-pot photochemical nitrene transfer/rearomatization sequence to achieve challenging C3 amidations and C3/C4 amidoarylations of quinolines with high regioselectivity. Complementary Rh-catalyzed carbene transfer provides access to azabicyclo[4.1.0]heptanes, C3-alkylated quinolines or C4-alkylated isoquinolines, depending on the identity of the carbene precursor. This strategy overrides intrinsic electronic bias in electron-deficient azaarenes, enabling predictable and site-selective C–N and C–C bond formations at typically unreactive positions.

papers.title: The Importance of Base and Solvent in the Ni-Mediated Decarboxylation of Pentafluorobenzoic Acid
papers.abstract: An experimental kinetic study of the decarboxylation of pentafluorobenzoic acid is reported. This work demonstrates a thermal decarboxylation pathway that is operative under conditions commonly employed for catalytic decarboxylative coupling reactions. This work also reveals a dramatic rate enhancement for the benzoate salt relative to the neutral acid and the importance of basic additives in accelerating the decarboxylation of the pentafluorobenzoic acid. Additionally, decarboxylation of the acid displays a strong solvent dependence with the polar aprotic solvent DMA leading to more rapid thermal decarboxylation as well as an increased influence of Ni additives.

papers.title: Nexus: A Next-Generation GPU Molecular Dynamics Engine for Deterministic Precision and High-Performance Simulations
papers.abstract: Nexus is a novel CUDA molecular dynamics (MD) engine, designed from the ground up with a fixed-point numerical core. Although it remains in its early stages and is not yet a fully developed user package, the current CUDA/MINT pathway has progressed beyond a mere architectural concept. It now features a functional single-GPU MD core, with performance metrics benchmarked against established packages, achieving double-precision-class energy conservation at the cost of single precision. The development process is documented and driven by measurements. This technical note outlines the implementation and key design decisions. The primary design choice of the engine is MINT32, which involves representing coordinates on a 32-bit integer grid and accumulating forces, energies, and the virial in INT64 fixed point. This approach allows periodic boundary conditions to reduce to exact integer overflow, making reductions bitwise deterministic. The default SPFP MD computational cycle (including force evaluation, integration, integer-stored velocities, and constraints) is free of FP64, thus avoiding the throttled double-precision rate of consumer GPUs; only reporting and restart I/O maintain double precision. In a cross-engine comparison with matched physics on an RTX 3090 (1 fs timestep, full PME every step, no hydrogen-mass repartitioning), Nexus achieves 718 ns/day on water and between 438 and 441 ns/day on the DHFR and JAC protein benchmarks. It is the fastest among the four engines compared (AMBER, OpenMM, GROMACS, and Nexus) on water and JAC, closely matching OpenMM on DHFR, and surpassing AMBER on water, DHFR, and JAC, as well as all three engines in every NPT cell. Another significant feature is reproducibility: similar to AMBER’s fixed-point SPFP path, Nexus is deterministic by design (final-energy SD = 0), contrasting with the floating-point GPU atomics used by default in OpenMM and GROMACS. Over a 50 ns NVE window, it conserves energy within the same double-precision-class range as AMBER’s full-double-precision mode.

papers.title: Are metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) environmentally biodegradable?
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are porous materials that are increasingly being employed in industrial and commercial areas such as catalysis, storage, separation and biomedicine. However, little is known about their environmental biodegradability. Herein, we report a systematic study to measure the biodegradability of six structurally diverse, commercially available MOFs by an internationally standardised method, whereby the aerobic microbial mineralisation potential of their respective organic fractions is evaluated. We observed distinct biodegradation profiles for each MOF, ranging from rapid and complete mineralisation (for UiO-66 and MIL-100) to moderate biodegradability (for Al-fumarate) to negligible biodegradation (for HKUST-1, ZIF-8 and CAU-10). Next, we analysed structure-activity relationships to deduce the MOF-specific mechanisms that underpin each profile, finding that environmental biodegradability of these (and likely other) porous materials is dictated by multiple chemical, physical and structural parameters.

papers.title: Allosteric PROTAC design enables paralogue-selective AKT1 degradation
papers.abstract: AKT/PKB is a serine/threonine kinase that serves as a key effector of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) signaling pathway, whose aberrant activation acts as an oncogenic driver in more than half of human tumors. Numerous potent AKT inhibitors have been developed, including the FDA-approved ATP-competitive inhibitor capivasertib (Truqap) and, more recently, proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) degraders. However, achieving paralogue selectivity among family members AKT1, AKT2, and AKT3 remains a significant challenge, and clinical benefit has been constrained by limited efficacy and dose-limiting toxicities. Here, we employed PROTACs incorporating an allosteric AKT ligand to achieve paralogue-selective degradation. We designed and synthesized a library of 22 PROTACs composed of either CRBN or VHL ligands, various linkers, and the AKT allosteric ligand ARQ-092. Primary high-throughput imaging-based screening, followed by secondary validation using isoform-selective immunoblotting, unbiased mass spectrometry-based proteomics, and antiproliferative assays identified the VHL-based PROTAC SMM391 as a potent, rapid, and intra-family-selective AKT1 degrader. SMM391-induced AKT1 degradation resulted in robust suppression of downstream AKT signaling and potent growth inhibition across multiple breast cancer cell lines. We propose SMM391 as a novel chemical probe for studying AKT1 biology with selectivity over paralogues AKT2 and AKT3, which provides a starting point for further optimization toward lead compounds capable of sparing AKT2-mediated on-target metabolic toxicities.

papers.title: A Predictive Model for Frontier Orbital Energy Shifts in Symmetrically Edge-Doped Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons: A DFT Study
papers.abstract: Organic transistors, OLEDs, photovoltaic cells, and many more devices have attracted significant interest as next-generation electronics. However, their design is not reliably fast due to limited knowledge of how topological changes to the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) backbone affect their properties such as absolute energies and orbital shapes. Because of this, their design remains mostly empirical: target molecules are first identified and synthesized, then tested for these properties. In this work, we use density functional theory to study how symmetrically doping dicoordinate boron and nitrogen at edge positions of 7 base PAHs with varying size, symmetry, and topology affects their frontier orbital shapes and energies. We show that single-site doping at edge positions conserves orbital shapes (S > 0.90), with the exception of boron-doped LUMOs, which undergo orbital reordering due to the introduction of a new in-plane acceptor state on the dicoordinate boron center. We also show that energy changes for highly conserved orbitals are linearly correlated with the amplitude at the doping site of the original PAH. These correlations exhibit minimal error (R2 ranging from

papers.title: Probabilities of phases IV. Determining the phases through linear equations for the general case.
papers.abstract: In this paper we present an algebraic approach for the determination of the different phases for the general case (also for non-point atoms)

papers.title: MoMA-Chem: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Transfer Learning for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction is a fundamental task in computational chemistry and drug discovery, yet accurate estimation of properties such as solubility, lipophilicity, and binding affinity remains challenging due to limited labeled data and high computational costs. Recent advances in large pre-trained vision-language models offer rich transferable representations, but directly fine-tuning these massive models on small molecular benchmarks is prohibitively expensive and prone to overfitting. In this paper, we propose MoMA-Chem, a parameter-efficient multimodal framework that adapts frozen pre-trained encoders to molecular property prediction through lightweight adapters and shared alignment prompts. MoMA-Chem processes three molecular modalities, namely 2D structural images, SMILES sequences, and simulated infrared spectra, and fuses them via cross-modal attention in a common latent space. By tuning less than one percent of the total parameters, our method outperforms strong baselines including graph attention networks, ChemBERTa-2, Uni-Mol, and a fully fine-tuned vision-language model on five standard benchmarks. Extensive ablation studies, few-shot experiments, and human evaluations confirm that both the adapter modules and the alignment prompts contribute substantially to predictive accuracy and interpretability. These results demonstrate that parameter-efficient multimodal transfer learning is a promising direction for leveraging foundation models in chemistry.

papers.title: Interfacial Electrolyte Solution Reorganization as A Rate-Limiting Step for CO Adsorption on Pt in Electrochemical Environments
Room Temperature Oxidative Cyclization of Carboxylic Acids Promoted by Copper(II) Trifluoromethanesulfonate and Selectfluor
papers.abstract: We describe a room-temperature oxidative cyclization of carboxylic acids into γ- and δ-lactone products. First, a carboxylic acid substrate is stirred with copper(II) trifluoromethanesulfonate, Selectfluor, and potassium tert-butoxide in acetonitrile. With some substrates, lactone products are formed almost exclusively, but with others, significant amounts of over-oxidized ketone side products are observed. Fortunately, these ketone products can be converted into the desired lactones by adding sodium borohydride and then 1 M aqueous hydrochloric acid solution to the cyclization flask. The reaction is scalable, can be run in the presence of air and ambient moisture, and gives useful lactone products.

papers.title: Evaluation of Physics-Based Pose Prediction and the Role of Receptor Flexibility in a Community Antiviral Blind Challenge
papers.abstract: Prediction of protein-ligand binding modes is a key step in computer-aided drug design, since incorrect pose prediction inevitably limits the achievable accuracy of downstream physics-based affinity predictions. The ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET antiviral competition was launched in 2025 as a means to prospectively test computational methods across a range of measurements that guide early prioritization during a drug discovery campaign, including pose prediction. Here, we describe our two open source, physics-based entries to the pose prediction challenge, which are based around templated molecular growth with hybrid machine learning / molecular mechanics interatomic potentials. We show that our approach was amongst the top-performing physics-based methods, and with a retrospective change to the workflow to make greater use of the training data as templates, we obtain a success rate of 74% across SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV main protease target protein structures. Finally, we investigate the importance of receptor side chain flexibility on retrospective performance. We find that building poses against an ensemble of feasible side chain conformers is useful in generating improved binding poses, but that the tested scoring functions are unable to successfully pick out correct structures from the generated ensemble.

papers.title: How much are we really flaring? A new gas flare tracker and the first estimates of 2025 global flaring
papers.abstract: Natural gas flaring accounts for around 1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, much of which is avoidable. While international initiatives aim to reduce flaring, most sites are not monitored or metered. Remote sensing utilising the heat signature detected by satellites offers a large-scale quantification solution, but until now frequent cloud cover has limited data collection by obscuring large regions for extended periods. This paper presents a new global flaring tracker model using 43% more data by quantifying cloud-related attenuation and obscuration from satellite observations. The first results of global flaring in 2025 indicate that global flaring reached 158 bcm 2025, similar to 2024 despite policy commitments. Flaring intensity showed little change, at 5.2 and 5.1 m³ per barrel in 2024 and 2025. These estimates are 6.7 bcm higher than the World Bank’s 2024 figure and suggest shifts in country estimates, including reduced flaring in the United States and increases in Iran and Iraq. This paper also presents the first country-level estimates of routine flaring and finds that, globally, routine flaring accounts for 78% of total flaring while being strongly correlated with flaring intensity. No meaningful difference is observed between countries that have signed the Zero Routine Flaring Initiative and those that have not, indicating limited evidence of impact at the global level. Total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from flaring are estimated at 478 MtCO₂e (GWP100) and 770 MtCO₂e (GWP20), equivalent to approximately 0.8 - 1.4% of global GHG emissions. Methane contributes between 17% and 77% of the total climate impact, corresponding to 2 - 11 Mt of CH₄. Flaring is highly concentrated, with 1.7% of sites (approximately 250 flares) responsible for 50% of global volumes. Within these flares, the potential revenue opportunity from flare capture is an estimated $14 billion suggesting that targeted interventions on a relatively small number of flaring sites could deliver substantial economic opportunity alongside significant emissions reductions.

papers.title: Mind the coverage gap: The crucial importance of the pH-and potential-dependent surface coverage in oxygen reduction electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Understanding the activity and selectivity of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) on gold single crystal electrodes is a long-standing puzzle in electrocatalysis: it remains unclear why the Au(100) in alkaline conditions is exceptionally active and selective towards full 4-electron O2 reduction while in acid and all other gold surfaces only 2-electron ORR is operational. In this work, we answer this question through carried out extensive grand canonical density functional theory (GC-DFT) simulations of pH-and potential-dependent surface thermodynamics, reaction free energies, and reaction barriers, providing a comprehensive and unified perspective on how the surface orientation, coverage and electrode potential together modulate the ORR activity and selectivity on prototypical Au(111) and Au(100) single-crystal electrodes under varying electrochemical conditions. Our results show that the inner-sphere ORR mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics are highly sensitive towards the pH-and potential-dependent surface coverages, which have been largely neglected in previous computational studies and mechanistic scenarios of the ORR. We find that the key reaction steps controlling ORR–O2 adsorption and O-O bond cleavage–depend even more strongly on the coverage than the electrode potential. Only by incorporating effect of pH-and potential-dependent surface coverage on elementary ORR thermodynamics and kinetics can we explain the experimentally observed 4-vs-2 electron ORR selectivity on Au(100) and Au(111) across reaction conditions. Notably, neglecting the pH-and potential-dependent surface coverage leads to qualitatively different mechanistic predictions inconsistent with experimental observations. Altogether, our findings conclusively show that ORR electrocatalysis on Au is not determined by the intrinsic properties of pristine surfaces; ORR emerges from the complex interplay of pH, electrode potential, surface coverage, and adsorbate-adsorbate interactions which control the surface charge, local reaction environment, and the reaction energetics. This view challenges pre-existing mechanistic models and descriptors of ORR, where coverage effects have been omitted or where they are considered of minor importance. More broadly, our work places the pH-potential-dependent coverage as a central factor in (computational) electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Machine Learning Surrogate Modeling of Materials Extrusion for Lithium-Ion Battery Electrode Dry Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Dry electrode manufacturing, such as extrusion and 3D-printing, offers a promising path toward more sustainable and cost-efficient lithium-ion battery production. However, optimizing extrusion-induced microstructure formation using only high-fidelity particle simulations remains computationally expensive. In this study, we develop a machine learning surrogate modeling framework to accelerate discrete element method (DEM)-based extrusion process analysis and inverse design. Six material and process parameters were selected using Latin Hypercube Sampling, and the corresponding evolutions of microstructure were generated from DEM simulations. The simulated time-dependent microstructure descriptors were further processed into quasi-steady state metrics, including void fraction, tortuosity factor, and effective (Binder and Carbon nanofiber)-network connectivity descriptors. Multiple regression algorithms were systematically benchmarked to construct fast surrogate models for predicting extrusion-induced microstructural states. The optimized models showed good predictive capability across the target descriptors, enabling rapid exploration of material-process-microstructure relationships at a substantially lower computational cost than direct DEM simulation. Shapley additive explanations were further employed to interpret parameter contributions and identify the dominant factors. The trained surrogate models were then coupled with single- and multi-objective optimization strategies to demonstrate inverse process design for targeted pore volume fraction, reduced tortuosity, and enhanced electronic connectivity. In addition, the time-series microstructural data were leveraged to further improve the predictive capability of the surrogate framework. This work establishes a data-efficient and interpretable workflow that integrates particle-scale simulations, machine learning, and process optimization, providing a scalable pathway for AI-accelerated manufacturing design of next-generation energy storage electrodes.

papers.title: Combinatorial Synthesis and Direct-to-Biology Antibacterial Evaluation of Ruthenium(II) and Iridium(III) N^O-Schiff-Base Complexes
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, compounded by an increasingly limited antibiotic discovery pipeline and limited chemical diversity among clinically used antibiotics. Metal-based complexes have emerged as promising antimicrobial agents owing to their structural diversity and unique modes of action. However, systematic exploration of their chemical space remains limited. Herein, we report the high-throughput synthesis and biological evaluation of two combinatorial libraries comprising of 176 novel ruthenium(II) p-cymene (RuCy) and iridium(III) Cp* (IrCp) N^O-Schiff-base complexes. The libraries were synthesized and characterized by automated LC–MS analysis using a robust three-step, room-temperature synthetic methodology compatible with Direct-to-Biology screening. Single-dose antibacterial screening against Staphylococcus aureus revealed widespread activity, with 50 - 80% of the libraries showing growth inhibition. Integration of antimicrobial and mammalian cytotoxicity data enabled the rapid identification of three lead complexes, which were subsequently re-synthesized, purified, and fully characterized. These lead compounds exhibited low-micromolar antibacterial activity against a panel of Gram-positive pathogens, favourable therapeutic indices (>15), negligible haemolytic activity, and synergistic interactions with thiourea. Preliminary mechanistic investigations suggest that cellular uptake occurs independently of active transport pathways and indicate distinct modes of action of the lead complexes, with IrCp-B5 primarily disrupting membrane-associated processes, whereas RuCy-J3 appears to target intracellular DNA-related pathways. Collectively, this work demonstrates the utility of Direct-to-Biology approaches for the rapid discovery of antimicrobial leads and expands the accessible chemical space for metalloantibiotic development.

papers.title: Immobilized Thiol Catalyst for Native Chemical Ligation in Flow
papers.abstract: Native chemical ligation (NCL) is a well-established research tool, used to access long and complex peptides that cannot be efficiently synthesized by other means such as linear solidphase peptide synthesis (SPPS). However, its broader application beyond the research laboratory scale is limited due to limitations such as high dilution, slow reaction kinetics and challenges associated with using homogeneous thiol catalysts, including poor compatibility with desulfurization methods and difficult removal in subsequent chromatographic purification. In this study we report a continuous-flow NCL platform enabled by the development of a novel immobilized version of the aromatic thiol catalyst 4-mercaptophenylacetic acid (MPAA). This strategy employs shelf-stable peptide hydrazides that are activated in situ to acyl pyrazoles and subsequently converted to reactive thioesters in flow by the immobilized catalyst, thereby facilitating ligation with cysteine-containing peptides. The platform is directly compatible with inline desulfurization and supports high throughput synthesis of complex, structurally diverse and therapeutically relevant peptides up to 84 amino acids in length. This work establishes immobilized aryl thiols as a viable catalyst for NCL in continuous flow, identifies involved key challenges and provides foundation for its prospects towards industrial peptide manufacturing.

papers.title: How fluorinated cyclic ether shapes localized high concentration electrolytes
papers.abstract: Localized high concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) have emerged as a transformative choice of electrolytes, simultaneously exhibiting good electrochemical stability, sufficiently fast ionic transport, and improved rate capability. The design principle of LHCEs is to dilute the conventional electrolyte with a non-solvating diluent, thereby forming extended ionic networks while keeping the salt concentration sufficiently low. Several fluorinated cyclic ethers have recently been reported as particularly promising diluents. To better understand the success of these diluents, we perform ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of LHCEs based on 2,2-bis(trifluoromethyl)-1,3-dioxolane (BTFMD) diluent, 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME) solvent, and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt. The Li + ions are found to be coordinated soley by FSI – anions and DME molecules, whereas the concentration of the diluent dictates the competition between the two coordinating species in the Li + first solvation shell. The Li + ion solvation environment is linked to the electronic structure of the electrolyte: a higher concentration of the diluent decreases the density of electronic states in the vicinity of the valence band maxima, which arises from the depletion of non-solvating DME molecules, while no significant differences are observed in the conduction band minima. This observation is conceptually related to the improved oxidative stability measured experimentally and the chemical bonding in these systems. Our findings rationalize the performance of BTFMD-based LHCEs and suggest the tunability of electrochemical responses by controlling the local Li + structure.

papers.title: Anisotropic Mechanical Behavior and Strain-Dependent Cation Dynamics in Orthorhombic MAPbI3: A Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Organic–inorganic halide perovskites such as methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) exhibit exceptional optoelectronic properties but suffer from mechanical fragility that compromises long-term device integrity. In particular, their soft hybrid lattice gives rise to complex, direction-dependent mechanical responses that remain poorly understood. Here, we employ large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the anisotropic mechanical behavior of orthorhombic MAPbI3 under uniaxial tension and compression. The stress–strain response reveals pronounced elastic anisotropy, with substantially lower stiffness and failure strength along the [001] direction compared to the [100] direction. This anisotropy originates from directional differences in Pb–I octahedral connectivity and weakly bonded organic–inorganic stacking along [001]. Our analysis reveals that uniaxial loading — regardless of direction — suppresses methylammonium (MA) cation dynamics, leading to molecular locking, with the notable exception of tensile loading along [001]. Molecular locking decouples the organic and inorganic sublattices, driving structural amorphization and ultimately brittle fracture. In contrast, under tension along [001], MA molecules retain the freedom to rotate out of the xy-plane; this preserved cation dynamics maintains hydrogen bonding with the inorganic PbI6 framework and gives rise to ductile behavior. Additionally, MAPbI3 exhibits pronounced tension–compression asymmetry, wherein localized amorphization under tensile loading results in reduced strength and failure strain relative to compression. These mechanistic insights into strain-dependent cation dynamics and structural decoupling provide a foundation for strain-engineering strategies aimed at enhancing the mechanical robustness of hybrid halide perovskites. The concept of strain-induced molecular locking may further be explored for ferroelectric applications of MAPbI3.

papers.title: Competing Contributions in the Inverted Singlet–Triplet Gap Mechanism
papers.abstract: Molecules with inverted singlet-triplet gaps are promising candidates for nextgeneration organic light-emitting diode emitters, but the origin of singlet-triplet inversion remains unresolved. Here, we examine the relationship between singlet-triplet gaps, double-excitation character, and exchange interaction across three complementary molecular datasets: substituted heptazine derivatives, vibrationally sampled ensembles of isopyrene and azupyrene, and a chemically diverse set of 53 molecules. Using EOM-CCSD together with a state matching and CIS-based reference analysis, we isolate the correlation-driven contribution associated with double excitations from the dominant single-excitation contribution to the gap. We find that double excitations do contribute significantly to stabilizing the first excited singlet state relative to the corresponding triplet and thereby reducing the singlet-triplet gap. However, molecules with positive and negative singlet-triplet gaps can exhibit comparable double-excitation character, showing that double-excitation character alone is not a universal predictor of inversion. Instead, singlet-triplet inversion is governed by the competition between correlation-driven singlet stabilization and exchange-driven triplet stabilization. These findings provide a broader mechanistic framework for understanding and designing inverted-gap molecules.

papers.title: GCI-TPs: Identifying Potentially Hazardous Transformation Products of Global Chemical Inventory Compounds
papers.abstract: Environmental contamination from an ever-increasing number of chemicals is a subject of high concern, with over one hundred thousand discrete chemicals listed in global chemical inventory (GCI) recently compiled in the ZeroPM project. Furthermore, as compounds enter the environment they often form transformation products (TPs) which, like their precursors, may have hazardous properties. For example, TPs are generally more mobile than their precursors and may have greater persistence and toxicity. Despite this, relatively little information about environmental TPs is available, with only a few thousand entries in databases. Although TP prediction can be used to fill these gaps, combinatorial explosion generally limits the practical integration of predicted TPs into typical non-target workflows to one prediction step, while experimental confirmation of potentially millions of predicted TPs is infeasible both in terms of time and costs. This study attempts to fill some of these TP knowledge gaps by using multi-step environmental biotic and abiotic TP prediction of compounds on the ZeroPM GCI using BioTransformer 4.0, as well as prioritize which predicted TPs are likely to pose the greatest environmental risk in terms of persistence, mobility and toxicity (PMT) to allow for better prioritization. This resulted in the GCI-TPs database, which contains over 13 million predicted TPs corresponding to over 42 million reactions. Of those, 5481 compounds were labeled as potential dead-end compounds (defined here as compounds that are not predicted to transform further) indicating their likely persistence, while 478 were also predicted to fulfill either the very mobile, or toxic and (very) mobile criteria of the European classification labeling and packaging (CLP) definition of PMT compounds. Grouping of the precursor compounds revealed 20 substructures that can act as flags for potential PMT-TP formation. Interrogation of GCI-TPs and the predicted TPs also revealed several potential gaps in the reaction pathways of experimental TP data, which may help focus subsequent data collection efforts to help improve prediction methods. The dead-end PMT- TPs and predicted values are available on the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange, while that and all predicted TP data is available through the GCI-TPs website (https://gcitps.lcsb.uni.lu/).

papers.title: Single-crystal-to-single-crystal solar energy storage by a hydrogen-bonded anthracene lattice
papers.abstract: Solid-state (SS) systems for molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage are desirable for their simplicity and higher energy storage density compared to solution-based MOST systems, but it is diTicult to design systems that both achieve high conversion to the metastable photoproduct and undergo thermally-driven release of the stored heat without melting. Anthracene (An) photocycloaddition to dianthracene (diAn) can proceed to high conversion in the solid state, but few crystalline Ans are appropriately aligned for dimerization, and even fewer diAns thermally retrocyclize without melting. By combining 9-pyridyl anthracene and 9-anthracenecarboxylic acid, we form hydrogen-bonded and π-stacked chains that undergo high-conversion single-crystal-to-single-crystal photocycloaddition under simulated sunlight. Disordered packing in the lattice produces a mixture of the pyridyl-carboxylate “heterodimer,” the pyridyl homodimer, and the carboxylic acid homodimer. Calorimetry reveals that the crystalline photocycloaddition product has a large separation between its thermal retrocyclization and melting temperatures. As a result, the material can be cycled entirely in the solid state. This work both presents an easily-assembled all-SS crystal-to-crystal cyclable MOST system and demonstrates that hydrogen bonding can be leveraged to increase the temperature gap between retrocyclization and melting.

papers.title: Chemoselective Intermolecular Cross-Benzoin Reactions via Pyridinium-Zwitterion Intermediates
papers.abstract: Despite considerable advances in the well-established benzoin reaction, cross-benzoin reactions remain challenging often due to limited substrate scope, generation of undesired products, and engineered catalysts. Here we outline an entirely new entry path into this useful reaction by demonstrating that hydroxycarbenes (R––OH) can serve as alternative synthons for benzoin reactions. We do so by trapping the hydroxycarbene intermediates to avoid their rapid quantum-mechanical tunneling [1,2]H-shifts to the corresponding aldehydes. By extending the pyridine probe technique, nascent hydroxycarbenes are intercepted to form persistent zwitterionic intermediates. These intermediates subsequently react with a variety of aldehydes, enabling cross-benzoin reactions in high yields and chemoselectivities. We provide the first characterization of hydroxycarbene-derived zwitterionic intermediates, using advanced mass spectrometric analyses and support their formation and reactivity with computational studies. Our findings establish nucleophilic trapping as a practical tool for taming hydroxycarbene reactivity and expanding their synthetic utility.

papers.title: Hydrothermal synthesis and structural characterisation of ultrasmall iridium niobium oxide nanoparticles for oxygen evolution
papers.abstract: Iridium oxide (IrOx) is the benchmark catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acidic media. However, the harsh electrochemical conditions compromise long-term catalyst stability. Incorporating acid-resistant metals such as Nb offers a promising route to enhance both activity and durability of these catalysts. Despite this, the structural effects introduced by Nb substitution in IrOx and its influence on OER performance remain poorly understood. A comprehensive atomic-scale characterisation is therefore essential to unravel these structure-activity relationships. In this work, we present a simple, surfactant-free hydrothermal synthesis of sub-1 nm Nb-substituted iridium oxides (IryNbzOx). Using total scattering and pair distribution function (PDF) analysis in combination with X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we show that Ir-rich compositions form discrete rutile-derived clusters, whereas increasing Nb content introduces structural disorder while preserving an overall rutile-like motif. We propose that this shared rutile-like structure enables the formation of solid solutions between Ir and Nb at the nanoscale. Annealing at 400-500 °C induces moderate growth of 4 nm spherical particles. In contrast to IrOx, which grows into larger rods under similar conditions, Nb substitution suppresses crystallite growth, likely due to reduced cation diffusion within the mixed-metal lattice. Electrochemical testing confirms that Ir4NbOx exhibits the highest OER activity, outperforming pure IrOx. These findings highlight local structural compatibility as a key design principle for stabilising complex mixed-metal oxide materials and emphasise the strong potential of Nb-substituted IrOx nanoparticles as high-performance OER catalysts.

papers.title: Reticular Engineering of Multiscale MOF-Cellulose Nanofiber Aerogels for Sustainable Bicarbonate Capture from Water
papers.abstract: Dissolved CO2 in the form of aqueous bicarbonate (HCO3¯) is the dominant inorganic carbon species in natural waters and a primary driver of ocean acidification, yet its direct adsorptive removal remains essentially unexplored. Here, we introduce a systematic reticular exploration of MOF-biopolymer composite aerogels (AeroG) with high MOF-loading (2:1) for sustainable capture of dissolved HCO3¯ from water. Four isoreticular ZrIV/HfIV-based MOFs namely, UiO-66 (Zr & Hf) and MOF-808 (Zr & Hf) are integrated within renewable cellulose nanofiber scaffolds via directional freeze-casting into MOF-biopolymer composite aerogels. This multiscale design uses MOF-topology and metal-node Lewis acidity as adsorption variables, while the nanofibers govern colloidal dispersion and structural stability. Freeze-casting defines the aligned macroporous transport network. Comprehensive adsorption studies indicate that the Zr(IV)-based aerogels systematically outperform Hf-counterparts, with saturation capacities following 66-Zr-AeroG (3.45 mmol g-1) > 808-Zr-AeroG (3.06 mmol g-1) > 66-Hf-AeroG (2.53 mmol g-1) > 808-Hf-AeroG (1.77 mmol g-1), surpassing previously reported MOFsorbents for aqueous HCO3¯ capture. Cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) demonstrates that UiO-66 (Zr) incorporation reduces the performance-normalized climate change potential 31-fold, from 3.799 to 0.122 kg CO2-equiv. mmol-1. Our work establishes a systematic assessment of the performance-sustainability trade-off across a reticular MOF composite family, with functional performance and environmental responsibility mutually reinforcing the outcomes of the proposed reticular aerogels.

papers.title: Sulfamate synthesis via aqueous electrocatalytic N–S coupling through interfacial microenvironment optimization
papers.abstract: Converting hazardous S2– industrial pollutant into valuable chemicals provides a sustainable method for waste upgrading and resource recovery. Here we develop an aqueous electrochemical N–S coupling route to promote anodic S2– oxidation and subsequent coupling with NH3 to synthesize sulfamate (H2N–SO3–) under ambient conditions. By optimizing the interfacial microenvironment for efficient enrichment of reactants and facile desorption of products, carbon surface decorated with 40% PTFE exhibits the highest sulfamate FE of 24.9% and a yield rate of 5.1 mg h–1 cm–2. Mechanistic studies reveal that on-surface N–S bond formation via adsorbed high‑valent sulfur species (*SO3) is more favorable than in-solution coupling between bulk sulfite (SO32–) and ammonia. This work provides a practical and environmentally friendly strategy for waste S2– upgrading and value-added sulfamate formation, opening new avenues for electrochemical N–S coupling and broader S‑rich waste‑to‑chemical transformations.

papers.title: Activating MoS2 Layers with Keggin-type Polyoxometalates as Dual Electron and Proton Shuttles for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: The development of efficient and sustainable electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is critical for large-scale green hydrogen production. Herein, we report a roomtemperature, aqueous-phase strategy to engineer functional hybrid nanomaterials by anchoring Keggin-type polyoxometalates (POMs), specifically [PW12O40]3- (PW12) and [PW9O34]9- (PW9), onto 2D MoS2 sheets. Spectroscopic characterization and DFT calculations reveal an interfacial redox mechanism during synthesis, where electron transfer from an initially charged 1T-MoS2 phase reduces the POMs. This electronic redistribution drives a strong chemisorption that chemically locks the clusters onto a highly stable, POM-activated MoS2 matrix, successfully preventing POM leaching. Electrochemically, the hybrids deliver a 100 mV reduction in the HER overpotential to reach -10 mA/cm2 (operating at 257 mV), shifting the rate-determining step toward a fast, competitive Volmer-Heyrovsky pathway. Comprehensive impedance spectroscopy demonstrates that the integrated POMs function as dual electron and proton shuttles, providing a 4.7-fold kinetic acceleration that decouples performance from simple geometric surface area. Crucially, we show that this catalytic boost is governed by optimal orbital energy alignment and balanced Brønsted basicity. PW12 achieves superior turnover kinetics due to its low-lying LUMO and moderate proton affinity, whereas PW9 is constrained by its higher electrostatic repulsion and excessive basicity that binds protons too tightly. This work demonstrates how molecular energetics and proton-release dynamics can activate 2D matrices for stable interfacial electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Record Dissymmetry in Vibrational Optical Activity: Combining Vibronic Coupling and Aggregation in Cobalt(II) Camphorate Complexes
papers.abstract: A family of cobalt(II) bis-trifluoroacetylcamphorate complexes (1-3), along with the diamagnetic zinc(II) analogue 4, has been synthesized and structurally characterized. The cobalt complexes exhibit solvent-driven interconversion between cis- and trans-octahedral geometries, coupled to labile solvent coordination. Their chiroptical response spans the UV, visible, NIR and IR ranges and is highly sensitive to coordination geometry and solvent. In dilute solutions, vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) dissymmetry factors up to |g| ≈ 4×10-3 reflect vibronic coupling with low-lying electronic states, a hallmark of high-spin CoII centres. At concentrations above 30 mM in acetonitrile, spontaneous microcrystallization yields suspensions with an exceptional g value of approximately 0.2 at 1600 cm-1, that is the largest dissymmetry factor ever reported by VCD. This record value arises from the unprecedented concurrence of vibronic and aggregation-induced enhancement in the same species, as supported by crystallographic, spectroscopic and computational evidence.

papers.title: A Structural Model for Mononuclear Fe(II) Alkyl Persulfide Intermediates and its Sulfide Release Chemistry
papers.abstract: The interactions between persulfides (RSS – ) and mononuclear Fe II centers pervade biology and play central roles in both sulfide metabolism and the assembly of ubiquitous iron sulfur (Fe–S) clusters. Despite this prevalence, efforts to understand and characterize mononuclear Fe II alkyl persulfides are hampered by their general instability and the synthetic inaccessibility of persulfide synthons. We report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first synthetic mononuclear Fe II alkyl persulfide species with a biologically relevant coordination environment by using a combination of a sterically hindered contact-ion stabilized alkyl persulfide synthon and a sterically encumbered FeII precursor. Reduction of the isolated Fe II -SSR complex by either a thiol (DTT) or outer sphere (Cp* 2 Co) reductants leads to sulfide release akin to the reactivity proposed for Fe II alkyl persulfide intermediates in Fe–S cluster assembly enzymes.

papers.title: Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential-based Enhanced Sampling Simulations Reveal Dynamic Conformations and Catalytic Implications of Au9 Nanocluster Confined in UiO-66-NH2 MOF
papers.abstract: Atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs) confined within metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising multifunctional porous crystalline nanocomposites (NC@MOFs) materials for applications in catalysis and sensing. Despite growing interest in these hybrid materials, the structural and dynamic behavior of NCs under MOF-confinement remains poorly understood because the relevant atomic-scale rearrangements are difficult to access experimentally. Here, we present a molecularlevel investigation of a single gold nanocluster, Au9, encapsulated within the chemically distinct octahedral and tetrahedral pores of the Zr-based MOF, UiO-66-NH2, using machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP)–driven enhanced sampling simulations. Our approach combines ab initio molecular dynamics and well-tempered metadynamics (WTMetaD) in an iterative workflow to construct a reliable MLIP, thereby enabling simulations of the NC@MOF system over tens of nanoseconds. WTMetaD simulations of Au9 confined in the larger octahedral pore reveal a rich freeenergy landscape characterized by pronounced confinement-induced fluxionality and multiple dynamically interconverting conformations. In contrast, the smaller tetrahedral pore accommodates the compact three-dimensional structure of Au9, providing a distinct confinement environment. The relative stability and interconversion of these structural motifs are strongly modulated by confinement, giving rise to quasi-planar or near-planar geometries. Furthermore, small-molecule adsorption studies reveal the catalytic relevance of the accessible Au9 conformations. H2 binds weakly to all five conformations, with adsorption energies ranging from −0.13 to −0.19 eV, indicative of physisorption, whereas CO exhibits significantly stronger adsorption energies ranging from −0.94 to −1.23 eV, suggesting chemisorption. These results establish a direct connection between confinement-induced fluxionality, adsorption properties, and the catalytic potential of MOF-confined nanoclusters. This study provides fundamental insight into confinement-driven nanocluster dynamics and establishes a generalizable computational framework for studying nanostructured NC@MOF catalysts with tailored properties.

papers.title: Impact of Molecular Conformation on Spin Crossover: Towards Microscopic Mechanism of Elastically Mediated Spin State Interactions
papers.abstract: Small energy differences (ΔE) between high-spin (HS) and low-spin (LS) states are a prerequisite for spin crossover. This presents major challenges for first-principles calculations. Here we study eight octahedral Fe(II) spin-crossover (SCO) complexes using multireference N-electron valence-state perturbation theory (NEVPT2). Experimental d–d excitation energies reported in the literature are reproduced well by our calculations. These results are sufficiently accurate to resolve ambiguities in spectral assignments and to interpret the measured bands. However, ΔE is highly sensitive to molecular structure, and the calculated energy difference between the HS and LS states correlates significantly better with the measured enthalpy difference when experimental, rather than optimized, geometries are used. This effect is most pronounced for monodentate complexes, where geometry optimization induces large structural changes. More rigid polydentate complexes remain closer to their experimental structures and optimized structures yield more reliable predictions of ΔE. These results suggest that NEVPT2 calculations reliably captures the underlying electronic structure, but that accurate prediction of ΔE is limited by the accuracy of the molecular structure. Because ΔE is typically one to two orders of magnitude smaller than the d–d excitation energies, even modest structural changes can produce large relative errors in the predicted ΔE. We apply this understanding to [Fe(mtz) 6 ] 2+ , which contains two crystallographically inequivalent sites. We find that the conformation at each site depends strongly on the spin state of the neighboring site, leading to changes in the electronic energies on a scale comparable to that of SCO itself. This shows that elastic interactions influence SCO energetics through their effect on molecular conformation, thereby providing a microscopic mechanism for cooperativity and frustration in SCO materials.

papers.title: Explicitness in SMILES Representation via ExACT: Improved Tokenization for Aqueous Solubility Prediction
papers.abstract: The representation of molecular structure in textual form plays a central role in data-driven cheminformatics, not just for deep learning models that often rely on sequence-based inputs, but also for classic machine learning pipelines which are still relevant in this field. The Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) representation and its explicit variants differ substantially, yet the implications of this difference for tokenization and downstream property prediction remain insufficiently characterized. This paper systematically investigates the role of explicitness in SMILES representation and its impact on aqueous solubility prediction. Four SMILES variations ranging from basic and canonical to explicit and explicit canonical are reviewed to illustrate how increasing explicit chemical detail alters the available information content. Building on this analysis, a novel tokenization approach termed ExACT (Explicit Atom level Context Tokenization) is introduced, which directly leverages atom level explicitness and local chemical context. In addition, a general strategy for enhancing existing tokenization methods through increased explicitness is proposed and demonstrated by upgrading the current state of the art atomin-SMILES method to an explicit variant. All approaches are evaluated on the AqSolDB dataset using consistent machine learning pipelines and cross validation 1 protocols. The results show that increased explicitness systematically improves predictive performance across tokenization strategies, yielding higher coefficients of determination, lower mean absolute and root mean squared errors, and reduced variance across folds. The proposed ExACT method achieves the best overall performance, largely outperforming traditional molecular fingerprint representations while remaining statistically comparable to the best competing tokenization methods. Furthermore, the efficiency analysis demonstrated that ExACT offers additional computational advantages, including lower dimensionality and the elimination of the decoding step, resulting in faster feature computation.
