These findings demonstrate that explicit SMILES representations encode chemically meaningful information that can be effectively exploited through context-aware tokenization, providing an interpretable and computationally efficient alternative representation for molecular property prediction. Scientific contribution This work investigates the role of explicitness in SMILES and its impact on aqueous solubility prediction, proposes a novel ExACT tokenization method and a general strategy for enhancing existing tokenization methods through increased explicitness.

papers.title: Chemical modification as a tool in nonaqueous enzymology
papers.abstract: Nonaqueous solvents have been widely regarded as incompatible media with enzymes. Nevertheless, there is now an extensive body of literature on nonaqueous activity of enzymes in living systems as well as tools of chemistry and biology enhancing the compatibility of enzymatic processes in nonaqueous environments. Likewise, a series of chemical modification development campaigns have demonstrated the power of nonaqueous approaches, offering a unique opportunity in a broad array of fields spanning chemical biology, enzyme engineering, food science, nanoscience, and sustainable chemistry. In this opinion, we discuss the current state of such nonaqueous chemical modification strategies by highlighting recent reports.

papers.title: Stable and Efficient Flexible Semi-Transparent Organic Photovoltaic Modules with Indium Tin Oxide Top Electrode
papers.abstract: Transparent top conductive electrodes are pivotal for semi-transparent organic photovoltaics (ST-OPVs) as it dictates internal light-field distribution, interfacial charge-collection kinetics, and the ultimate environmental robustness of the device. Indium tin oxide (ITO) is the most attractive top electrode for ST-OPVs due to its excellent balance among conductivity, transparency and stability. However, integrating ITO top electrode via magnetron sputtering leads to catastrophic plasma damage to fragile organic active layer in OPVs. Herein, we report a universal interface architecture by introducing a discontinuous metal nano-islands charge-injection buffer layer, enabling damage-free ITO sputtering. In the architecture of ST-OPVs, this metal-hole transport layer (M-HTL) combination acts not only as a kinetic scavenger to quench high-energy species but also as an interfacial dipole that eliminates the Schottky barrier for hole extraction. This strategy yields a record light utilization efficiency of 5.08% among ST-OPVs using non-Ag semitransparent top electrode and enables the scalable fabrication of flexible sub-modules with an active area exceeding 340 cm2 and a power conversion efficiency of 10.26%. Furthermore, the unencapsulated devices demonstrate one order-of-magnitude enhancement in operational lifetime compared to the Ag-based counterparts, while the encapsulated flexible sub-modules tolerate severe thermal and moisture stress for over 3700 hours with almost no performance change. This approach provides a generalized solution for integrating industrial ITO processing with high performance organic and hybrid optoelectronics, accelerating commercialization of power generating smart windows.

papers.title: Absorption correction for plate samples in transmission Xray powder diffraction: improved reliability of atomic displacement parameters
papers.abstract: Absorption in transmission X-ray powder diffraction introduces angular-dependent intensity distortions that can bias refined structural parameters. We present an analytical absorption correction for flat plate samples, derived from the geometry and applicable to both point and area detectors. The correction separates into a scale term and an angular-dependent component; while the former is absorbed by the refinement scale factor, the latter affects relative intensities and biases parameters such as atomic displacement parameters (ADPs). Using CeO2, we show that neglecting absorption leads to systematic variation of ADPs with optical thickness, which is removed by applying the correction. Plate geometry further allows independent determination of optical thickness, enabling absorption to be treated as a physically constrained correction and improving refinement reliability.

papers.title: Large Language Models in Drug Discovery and Development: Multimodal Applications, Translational Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as knowledge-integration, hypothesisgeneration, molecular-representation, clinical-workflow, and documentation-support systems across drug discovery and development. This review adopts a full-pipeline perspective, spanning target identification, molecular generation, virtual screening, ADMET and toxicity assessment, clinical-trial optimization, pharmacology support, pharmacovigilance, regulatory documentation, and emerging agentic workflows. To avoid a simple accumulation of application scenarios, the article organizes the literature around a central analytical thread: how different LLM paradigms create different levels of pharmaceutical value, evidence maturity, validation burden, and translational risk. We distinguish biomedical text LLMs, molecular language models, protein and omics language models, multimodal molecular systems, retrieval-augmented generation systems, and tool-augmented or agentic workflows. For each paradigm and pipeline stage, we separate workflow efficiency, hypothesis generation, candidate prioritization, and validated drug-discovery outcomes. Current evidence shows that LLMs can improve literaturescale synthesis, interface design, molecular ideation, patient–trial matching, pharmacovigilance triage, and structured evidence organization. However, many claims remain based on benchmark evaluation, retrospective analysis, prototype workflows, or case demonstrations rather than prospective experimental or clinical validation. Major limitations include hallucination, data leakage, benchmark saturation, training–test similarity, weak out-of-distribution performance, insufficient wet-lab confirmation, limited route-feasibility analysis, uncertain patentability, model drift, privacy risks, and incomplete auditability. This review therefore proposes an evidencereadiness framework that classifies applications from proof-of-concept to benchmark validation, retrospective external validation, prospective workflow testing, controlled deployment, and regulatory-grade use. By linking application scope, model paradigm, evidence maturity, and risk-aware validation requirements, the article clarifies where LLMs are practically useful today, where claims remain preliminary, and what technical, experimental, clinical, and governance advances are required before LLM outputs can support high-consequence pharmaceutical decision-making.

papers.title: When Does Framework Topology Matter Beyond Pore Metrics in MOF Adsorption Prediction?
papers.abstract: MOF chemists often evaluate frameworks through two complementary languages: familiar pore metrics and framework topology. In adsorption screening, however, fast predictive models usually describe a structure mainly by density, surface area, pore apertures, cavity sizes and void fractions. This raises a practical question: after these pore metrics are known, does topology still add useful information? Here, we compare topology-only, geometry-only and topology+geometry descriptors for methane and carbon dioxide uptake across low-and high-pressure conditions. Compact geometry is the essential first baseline and almost saturates high-pressure methane prediction; adding topology changes the HGB reference model R2 only from 0.974 to 0.977. Topology is therefore not a universal shortcut and cannot replace pore metrics. Its value is selective and becomes clearer when pore access, confinement and network connectivity influence adsorption, increasing R2 from 0.673 to 0.734 for methane at 5.8 bar, from 0.678 to 0.732 for carbon dioxide at 0.15 bar and from 0.463 to 0.536 for carbon dioxide at 0.015 bar. Matched-geometry comparisons, residual diagnostics, net-specific maps and carbon dioxide shortlist analyses show that topology can change which frameworks are selected even when scalar pore descriptors look similar. The conclusion is a practical design rule for MOF screening: pore metrics should be the first lens, but topology becomes a useful complementary descriptor when adsorption depends on how pore space is connected, not only on how much pore space is present.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Small-Molecule Chemical Discovery: From Chemical Language Representation to Closed-Loop Experimental Validation
papers.abstract: Small molecules are not only structural entities but also chemical language objects that can be represented as strings, graphs, three-dimensional conformers, reaction equations, spectra, laboratory records, and natural-language descriptions. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have created a new interface for small-molecule discovery by connecting these heterogeneous representations through sequence modeling, multimodal alignment, tool use, and iterative experimental feedback. This review synthesizes LLM-driven small-molecule discovery from chemical language representation to molecular generation, property-oriented optimization, synthesis-aware design, retrosynthesis planning, and closed-loop validation. Compared with broad surveys of AI in chemistry and drug-centered reviews, this article treats small molecules as general design objects across pharmaceuticals, catalysts, energy molecules, fluorescent probes, agrochemicals, green solvents, and functional organic materials. We further position molecular language models as one branch of scientific world models, in which genes, proteins, reactions, and small molecules are represented as language-like objects that encode biological and chemical regularities. We review molecular representations, datasets, benchmarks, evaluation metrics, model architectures, multimodal systems, and tool-augmented LLM agents. Finally, we discuss autonomous laboratories, experimental feedback loops, chemical hallucination, synthesizability constraints, benchmark standardization, safety, and human–AI collaboration. We argue that the next stage of molecular discovery should move beyond validity-centered generation toward experimentally reliable, synthesis-aware, and feedback-driven chemical design.

papers.title: Discovery of Sphaeriaurantins as Rapid-Acting Antiplasmodials with Dual Activity in Blood and Liver Stages
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of resistance in the malaria-causing protozoan Plasmodium falciparum has heightened the demand for treatments with novel modes of action. Having evolved to produce a myriad of structurally diverse natural products (NPs) as defenses against soil-dwelling parasites including protozoa, Actinomycetota strains are a promising source for the discovery of NPs as antiplasmodial drug leads. Herein, the selective inhibition of P. falciparum is reported for five distinct NP families from Actinomycetota, including an unprecedented family of glycosylated type II polyketides termed sphaeriaurantins (SPAs). The structures of SPAs were established through the combination of MS and NMR spectroscopic data analysis, derivatization and comparison of the deoxyhexose moieties to authentic standards, and quantum chemical calculations, including 1 H and 13 C NMR chemical shifts and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) spectra. The three isolated SPA congeners reveal that the characteristic pseudodimeric structure of the SPA family of NPs, likely introduced at a late stage of the SPA biosynthesis, is highly relevant for the observed low nanomolar activity. SPA A exhibits a rapid killing profile, with activities across all intraerythrocytic stages, and potent liver stage efficacy, as well as a low propensity for resistance development. Taken together, these results suggest a mode of action that most likely is distinct from the existing antimalarials, supporting SPA A as a promising antimalarial drug lead for further development.

papers.title: Metal-Free Hydroboration of CO2 at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron-Appended Nitrenium Catalysts
papers.abstract: The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) into value-added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal-free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report a robust boron-tethered N-heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalyst for the hydroboration of CO2 under ambient conditions. The developed protocol works under very mild conditions (room temperature and 1 bar CO2 pressure) with a low catalyst loading of 1 mol%. The borane reductant governs the chemoselectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH3·SMe2) drives rapid and highly selective complete reduction to the methoxide-level products. In contrast, the use of 9-borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9-BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal-level (CH2(OBBN)2) and completely reduced methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. The catalytic platform exhibits excellent overall turnover numbers (TON). Ultimately, this work establishes a highly sustainable, metal-free methodology for the tunable reduction of CO2 to methanol equivalents, further highlighting the versatility of main-group catalysis.

papers.title: CReM update: a faster, more compact, and more flexible framework for chemically reasonable mutations
papers.abstract: CReM is a context-based molecular structure generation framework that produces chemically reasonable structures by exchanging fragments observed in equivalent local environments. Here, we present an updated CReM version that improves scalability, speed, and flexibility while preserving backward compatibility. The new implementation introduces intramolecular cyclization and partial ring replacement, going beyond classical matched molecular pair replacements and enabling more flexible exploration of cyclic and macrocyclic chemical space. A normalized database schema reduces storage redundancy, supports multiple named fragment sets in a single database, and enables property-aware fragment filtering. Database generation is accelerated through parallel processing and merging, and a Python API was implemented for programmatic workflows. Replacement of the previous reaction-based assembly backend with an RDKit molzip-based procedure further improves structure generation speed. Benchmarks using ChEMBL36 and SureChEMBL fragment databases demonstrate reduced database size, faster database construction and structure generation, and controllable synthetic accessibility through context radius and fragment database composition. Scientific contribution This work extends the CReM structure generation framework by addressing several limitations of the original approach, particularly in the generation of ring systems. The proposed expansion improves both database construction and structure generation speed, while also optimizing database storage. These advances enable the use of substantially larger fragment databases, thereby allowing broader coverage of chemical space than was previously feasible. In addition, the framework provides greater flexibility in molecular structure generation while preserving indirect control over the synthetic accessibility of the generated compounds.

papers.title: Correlative Operando X-Ray Imaging and Diffraction Revealing Mechanical Failure Pathways in Lithium Metal Sulfide-Based All-Solid-State Batteries
papers.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) employing sulfide solid electrolytes and lithium metal anodes offer a promising pathway toward high energy density and enhanced safety. However, their practical deployment remains limited by strongly coupled electro-chemo-mechanical instabilities at both cathode and anode interfaces, which evolve across multiple length scales and remain insufficiently understood under realistic operating conditions. Here, we present a comprehensive multimodal operando characterization approach combining X-ray computed tomography (XCT), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and stack pressure monitoring to elucidate the dynamic degradation mechanisms in LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) | Li6PS5Cl (LPSC) | Li cells. By directly correlating particle-level morphological evolution with latticescale structural and strain dynamics, this methodology enables a unified, multiscale description of interfacial failure processes. Operando XCT and XRD jointly reveal reversible volume changes of ~6 % in NCM811 particles during (de-)lithiation. Spatially resolved operando XRD further uncovers pronounced heterogeneity in lithiation fronts and depth-dependent electrochemical activity across the cathode thickness. In parallel, a partial release of interfacial microstrain is identified at the NCM811|LPSC interface, associated with oxidative decomposition of LPSC solid electrolyte. At the LPSC|Li interface, operando XCT directly visualizes, at moderate current density (0.45 mA cm-2) but high areal capacity (4.17 mAh cm-2), crack initiation and propagation within the solid electrolyte, driven by the lithium plating-induced stress, followed by lithium infiltration, and progressive interfacial contact loss. These processes ultimately lead to mechanical disconnection and the emergence of short-circuiting at higher current densities. Notably, these mechanically induced degradation phenomena exhibit partial reversibility during lithium stripping. This multimodal operando framework provides critical insight into degradation pathways and establishes design principles for mechanically robust sulfide-based ASSBs.

papers.title: Green Synthesis, Characterization, and Catalytic Exploration of Citrus Juice and Urea-Derived Carbon Dots for Bicyclic Heterocyclic Construction. Asif Raza a#, Huma Basheer a#,Imran A Khan a*,
papers.abstract: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have emerged as a promising class of sustainable carbon-based nanomaterials owing to their tunable optical properties, low toxicity, facile synthesis, and broad application potential. In the present study, nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots (N-CQDs) were synthesized through a rapid and environmentally benign microwave-assisted approach using renewable biomass-derived precursors, including Citrus limon (lemon), Spondias mombin (hog plum), Averrhoa carambola (star fruit), and Cymbopogon citratus (lemongrass). Urea and thiourea were employed as nitrogen and sulfur–nitrogen doping agents to enhance surface functionality and modify the electronic properties of the resulting nanomaterials. The synthesized CQDs were characterized using UVVisible spectroscopy, fluorescence analysis, thin-layer chromatography, and complementary physicochemical techniques to evaluate precursor transformation and nanomaterial formation. UV–Visible spectroscopic studies revealed characteristic absorption features associated with π→π* and n→π* electronic transitions, confirming successful carbonization and formation of conjugated carbon domains. Fluorescence investigations demonstrated precursor-dependent emission behavior, with citric acid-derived CQDs exhibiting intense cyan-blue fluorescence, while star fruit- and lemongrass-derived systems displayed green-shifted emissions, highlighting the influence of precursor composition and heteroatom incorporation on optical properties. The study further emphasizes the potential of biomass-derived N-CQDs as sustainable multifunctional nanomaterials and explores their prospective relevance in green catalytic and synthetic chemistry applications, particularly in the context of condensation-driven bicyclic heterocyclic construction. Overall, this work demonstrates an efficient strategy for transforming renewable biomass resources into functional carbon nanomaterials while advancing the integration of green chemistry, nanotechnology, and sustainable materials design.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Bayesian Optimization Strategies for Multilayer Radiation Shield Design Using
papers.abstract: Efficient radiation shield optimization requires identifying high-performing tradeoffs between neutron attenuation, gamma attenuation, and total shield thickness while minimizing the number of expensive simulation evaluations. This work compares three Gaussian-process-based multi-objective Bayesian optimization strategies for the design of five-layer radiation shields using a Geant4 Monte Carlo transport model. The models evaluated were MOO, FULLYBAYESIANMOO, and SAASBO, each implemented using Meta’s Ax optimization framework. Each campaign used the same 500 Sobol initialization trials and was run for 96 hours over a mixed categorical–continuous design space consisting of 40 candidate materials and variable layer thicknesses. MOO produced the largest number of evaluations, completing 1,398 trials, but only 2% of its generated trials were retained on the pooled Pareto front. FULLYBAYESIANMOO completed 123 trials and provided improved solution quality with broader Paretofront coverage than SAASBO, but at substantially higher computational cost. SAASBO completed only 97 trials yet produced the most efficient Pareto-front improvement, with 64% of generated trials contributing to the pooled Pareto front and the lowest generational distance among the three methods. These findings demonstrate that higher optimization throughput does not necessarily translate to better design quality, while highly efficient convergence may come at the expense of full-front coverage. For computationally expensive radiation shielding problems, the results support a staged workflow in which MOO is first used for broad, low-cost exploration of the design space, followed by targeted SAASBO optimization to refine high-quality regions of the Pareto front.

papers.title: Impact of Mesoporous SBA-15 Morphology on the Performance of Mixed-Matrix Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) Membranes in Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) Ultrafiltration
papers.abstract: This study explores the impact of varying morphologies of mesoporous silica SBA-15 on the performance and structure of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) ultrafiltration (UF) membranes. SBA-15 was synthesized in rod, plate, and spherical shapes and incorporated into PAN membranes at optimal concentrations. Attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared analysis (ATRFTIR) confirmed the successful integration of mesoporous silica SBA-15 on membrane surfaces. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed that rod-shaped SBA-15 membranes had a rougher surface than plate and spherical ones, while field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed a finger-like porous structure in all membranes. Membranes with 0.5 wt.% SBA-15, regardless of shape, exhibited enhanced hydrophilicity and performance. Rod-shaped SBA-15 increased pure water flux (PWF) by 44%, plate-shaped by 27%, and spherical-shaped by 15%. The rod-shaped SBA-15 membranes achieved the highest permeate water flux (238.2 L/m2) and BSA flux (142.2 L/m2) due to their superior hydrophilicity, porosity. Although BSA rejection remained stable, the addition of mesoporous silica SBA-15 significantly enhanced the anti-fouling properties of membranes. Membrane resistance decreased by 25% with rod-shaped SBA-15, 15% with plateshaped SBA-15, and 14% with spherical-shaped SBA-15 compared to pristine membranes. This study illuminates the pivotal role of SBA-15 morphology in enhancing the permeability, and fouling resistance of PAN membranes.

papers.title: Detecting and isolating flare plumes from upstream oil and gas sites using aircraft sampling
papers.abstract: Aircraft flights have been used in multiple studies to attempt to isolate and measure the compositions of flare plumes. In this work, flare plumes from oil and gas facilities in the Permian Basin of west Texas were simulated, in combination with other plumes from the facilities, to predict concentrations along typical aircraft flight paths. Multiple types of flight paths were simulated. Aircraft spirals around sites with active flares, which transected flare plumes approximately 1000 m downwind of the flare encountered intersecting simulated plumes from multiple sources on the oil and gas sites, making unambiguous sampling of flare plumes very difficult under most conditions. Aircraft flight paths that followed flare plume centerlines toward active flares were typically able to isolate simulated flare plumes, but only within a few hundred meters of the flare and only if the flare plume centerline closely matched the flight path. Predicted concentration ratios in the simulations were qualitatively consistent with observed data from aircraft flights for the simulated facilities. These results demonstrate the need for very careful interpretation of flare combustion efficiencies derived from data collected by instrumented aircraft flying downwind of oil and gas sites.

papers.title: Generative AI and Structure-Based Workflow for the De Novo Design and Optimization of DprE1 Inhibitor Candidates
Red-Light Tomographic Volumetric 3D Printing in Seconds for Fabrication of Colorless Structures
papers.abstract: Non-pulsed red light photopolymerization is attractive for volumetric additive manufacturing because longer wavelengths can improve light penetration, lower scattering, and reduce photodamage compared with ultra-violet or blue irradiation. In this work, we utilized methylene blue and triethanolamine as a sacrificial type II photoinitiating system for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel printing with a custom-made red-light tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing system. With the optimized formulation, PEGDA hydrogel structures were printed by red light within 30 s. The resulting constructs were colorless, extractable, and contained fully formed internal channels. This work establishes a type II photochemistry system as a promising route for extending tomographic volumetric 3D printing toward lower-energy visible-light irradiation and rapid fabrication of colorless hydrogel constructs.

papers.title: Negative Charge Activation of Surface H₂O Molecules as a Proposed Trigger for Evaporation and Phase Transition
papers.abstract: Evaporating water is known to carry a net negative charge 1 , yet the microscopic trigger that initiates the detachment of individual H₂O molecules from the liquid interface remains debated. While prior studies have addressed charge separation via ion diffusion at the phase front 1 or external-field-induced polarization 2 , these approaches treat charge as a consequence of — or an external input to — the phase transition, rather than as its trigger. Here, we propose that when charge is redistributed at the hydrogen-bonding sites of interfacial H₂O molecules — specifically at the hydrogen atoms connecting to the oxygen atoms of sub-interfacial H₂O molecules below — by any external influence, the resulting negative charge activation generates Coulombic repulsion sufficient to sever the hydrogen bond and expel the molecule into the gas phase. To test this hypothesis, we conducted four experiments: (i) container opening geometry, (ii) a modified gold-leaf electroscope, (iii) closed-circuit bottle configurations, and (iv) applied low voltage (0.10–0.20 V). The gold-leaf electroscope experiment confirmed net charge transfer during phase transition; the closed-circuit copper wire experiment showed that charge dissipation suppressed evaporation by ~22%; and the low-voltage experiment showed that evaporation progressively increased (+0.067% → +0.317%) with stepwise voltage increase (0.10 → 0.20 V). These results indicate that charge redistribution at the hydrogen-bonding sites of interfacial H₂O molecules is a factor influencing evaporation, with implications for evaporation-driven energy harvesting.

papers.title: Performance-Based Evolution of Near-Infrared Serotonin Nanosensors from DNA-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Libraries
papers.abstract: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5HT) is an important neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of mood, appetite, and sleep, and its dysregulation has been associated with disorders such as depression and Parkinson’s disease. Selective molecular tools that can distinguish 5HT from neurochemicals, are essential for advancing both neurochemistry and disease-related research. However, conventional analytical methods are labor-intensive and sometimes suffer from poor discrimination among closely related neurotransmitters. In this study, we developed near-infrared fluorescence 5HT nanosensor based on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) using a performance-based systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment of carbon nanotube (pSELEC) strategy. Unlike conventional affinity-focused selection, this approach prioritized fluorescence modulation as the screening output and combined high-throughput microarray printing, automated fluorescence imaging to evaluate more than 10 6 ssDNA-SWCNT configurations. After characterizing the enriched DNA 2 candidates, Seq6 was selected as finalist scaffold and underwent post-selection engineering such as covalent modification with quencher dye and co-wrapping with dummy DNA. A methylene blue-conjugated Seq6 produced an “turn-off” fluorescence response to 5HT together with an opposite-direction response to dopamine, providing improved discrimination between the two analytes. These results demonstrate that pSELEC is a useful strategy for developing sensitive and selective near-Infrared nanosensors for real-time neurotransmitter sensing.

papers.title: Cooperative Herringbone Hinging and Columnar Shifts in Perovskite-related Coordination Polymers
papers.abstract: Casting a material’s structure into structural degrees of freedom (DOFs), elementary structural features that govern the material’s response to external stimuli, is a powerful concept for rationalizing material responsiveness. Elevating this concept into a materials design strategy requires both the discovery of new DOFs and a clear understanding of how their interplay generates emergent properties. In this work we expand the family of perovskite-related ( A 2+ )( B 2+ (C 2 N 3 ) 3 ) 2 coordination polymers by introducing phosphonium-based divalent A 2+ cations and we show how the cooperative interaction between DOFs leads to biaxial negative thermal expansion (NTE). The materials contain two key DOFs. One DOF originates from the geometric arrangement of the A 2+ cations within the 3D (( BX 3 ) 2 ) 2- ReO 3 -type network. The second DOF arises from translational columnar shifts. These two DOFs act cooperatively so that columnar shifts induce herringbone-type hinging of the A 2+ cations and, overall, causing biaxial NTE. The strength and character of this cooperativity are highly sensitive to subtle modifications of the A 2+ cation such as rigidification through the introduction of a double bond. The results provide a compelling blueprint for engineering material responsiveness through the deliberate design of cooperative structural DOFs.

papers.title: Polyoxotungstate Loaded Carboxymethyl Chitosan Composites with Anticancer Activity: A Mix and Match Approach
papers.abstract: Novel cancer treatments are in high demand, and a wider range of low-cost and easily accessible inorganic compounds along the lines of cisplatin is required. This work proposes polyoxotungstates (POT) and POT-carboxymethyl chitosan (CMC) formulations as anticancer drug candidates and addresses the widely unknown influence of POT nuclearity on anticancer activity. Treating cells with WO 4 2- as a reference achieved statistically similar results to the Keggin-type [PW 12 O 40 ] 3− and lacunary [PW 9 O 34 ] 9− , in regard to their tungsten-normalized IC 50 values. The IC 50 values for each are estimated with a global fit to be 5,470 ± 580 μM tungsten were calculated for cancerous PC-3 cells and 6,040 ± 480 μM tungsten for reference MRC-5 cells. The Preyssler-type POT, [NaP 5 W 30 O 110 ] 14− {NaP 5 W 30 } afforded lower IC 50 values, requiring just. 1.2 mM tungsten (40 μM {NaP 5 W 30 }) for PC-3 cells and 210 μM tungsten (8 μM {NaP 5 W 30 }) for MRC-5 cells. The uptake of tungsten by PC-3 cells, as determined by ICP-MS analysis, is ca. 21 times higher for cells treated with {NaP 5 W 30 } than for Na 2 WO 4 . {NaP 5 W 30 } is also combined with CMC as a drug carrier to enhance the activity, selectivity, and stability of the POT. Nanoparticles could be prepared directly in cell culture media with only slight swelling, affording sizes between 90 and 240 nm, according to DLS. The respective nanoparticles (IC 50 value of 16 μM {NaP 5 W 30 }), as well as a mechanical mixture of {NaP 5 W 30 } with CMC (ca. 2 μM {NaP 5 W 30 }), significantly improved the cytotoxicity towards PC-3 cells compared to pristine {NaP 5 W 30 }. On the other hand, the nanoparticles only slightly increased the toxicity towards the non-cancerous MRC-5 cells (IC 50 of 9 μM {NaP 5 W 30 }) and favorably reduced the toxicity with the mixture (18 μM {NaP 5 W 30 }). This renders the easily accessible mechanical mixture of CMC with {NaP 5 W 30 } or other optional POTs, as opposed to the nanoparticles themselves, a promising starting platform for tests on other cancer cell lines and optimization into effective anticancer agents.

papers.title: Lightweight Domain-Specific LLM for Optical
papers.abstract: The design of optical materials relies on highly specialized knowledge, which creates a major bottleneck for data-driven scientific discovery in the optical material domain. Large language models open new possibilities for scientific research, but general-purpose models struggle with the domainspecific physical logic and terminology. More importantly, no standardized evaluation benchmark exists to systematically assess how well LLMs perform on optical materials tasks. To fill this gap, we first construct two evaluation benchmarks, Optic_Choice and Optic_QA, designed specifically for the optical materials domain. We build a high-quality instruction-tuning dataset of 23,225 question-answer pairs through an automated multi-stage pipeline from a curated corpus of papers and textbook. We then develop OptiMatLLM, a 7-billion-parameter LLM fine-tuned LLM on this corpus. Evaluation results show that OptiMatLLM achieves top performance on our optical benchmarks, reaching 0.79 accuracy on Optic_Choice, while also performing competitively on broader scientific tests such as CMHChem, ChemBench, and MaScQA. The model retains strong general capabilities as well, scoring 0.91 on the GSM8K mathematical reasoning benchmark. We further provide a systematic comparison of multiple leading models on these benchmarks, establishing a reference for future work. All benchmarks, dataset, and model are publicly released to support further research on LLMs for optical and optoelectronic materials design.

papers.title: Bidirectional Plant-Microneedle Responses to Guide Biomaterial Design
papers.abstract: Designing biomaterials compatible with plants and specific payloads enables new technologies for precision agriculture, including targeted and efficient agrochemical delivery. However, broader implementation requires a systematic understanding of the complex interactions among payloads, biomaterial properties, and plant responses to establish foundational design principles that support a sustained biotic–abiotic interface. Using microneedles made of different polymers and microstructures, this study investigates plant–biomaterial interactions to develop effective compound delivery strategies. Biodegradation studies show that microneedle biomaterials impart distinct mechanical strength, hydrophilicity, and surface charge, which influence the release profiles of bioactive cargo. Transcriptomic analyses following microneedle injection reveal mostly universal, but some variable acute responses related to immunity and metabolism, depending on inherent biomaterial properties. Despite these responses, microneedle treatments caused minimal effects on plant growth, chlorophyll content, stomatal conductance, and quantum efficiency of photosystem II. Finally, we demonstrate how biomaterial properties influence the delivery of agrochemicals with distinct chemical and functional characteristics, using hydrophilic plant growth regulator gibberellic acid (GA3) and hydrophobic herbicide pelargonic acid (PA), into tomato and lettuce, supporting the broad applicability of technology. These findings establish principles for engineering plant-biomaterial interfaces to accommodate payloads with diverse characteristics while ensuring plant safety.

papers.title: Synthesis, Evaluation, and Context for Applications of SF5-Containing [1.1.1]Bicyclopentane and [2]Staffane "Hybrid Bioisosteres"
papers.abstract: Bioisosteric replacements are conventionally applied as single-variable changes to a parent molecule during drug discovery campaigns. Herein, we evaluate hybrid bioisosteric replacements as strategic combinations of multiple substitutions that counterbalance the physicochemical consequences of incorporating single bioisosteres individually. For instance, while aryl-CF 3 –> aryl-SF 5 replacement is often associated with increased lipophilicity and metabolic stability, pairing this change with a second bioisostere can conceivably offset an undesired increase in LogD, while preserving other favorable properties. In this context, we validate SF 5 -substituted [1.1.1]bicyclopentanes (SF 5 –BCPs) and SF 5 –[ 2 ]staffanes (SF 5 –BCP–BCPs) as hybrid bioisostere motifs that have not been field-tested due to lack of access to versatile building blocks. We address a key synthetic limitation by developing scalable routes to carboxylic acid-containing intermediates that facilitate incorporation of these motifs into drug-like molecules via carbonyl group manipulations. These advances enable 1) a crystallographic study that contextualizes structural features of these motifs relative to other fluorinated rings, 2) synthesis of structurally diverse pharmaceutical and agrochemical derivatives, and 3) systematic evaluation of single (SF 5 –Ph –> SF 5 –BCP) and multi-component "hybrid" bioisosteric replacements (CF 3 –Ph –> SF 5 –BCP and CF 3 –Ph–Ph –> SF 5 –BCP–BCP) on physicochemical properties through in vitro ADME profiling. Finally, we investigate the chemical stability profile of these novel SF 5 –[ 2 ]staffanes, establish an extensive suite of building blocks, and demonstrate their compatibility with the most frequently used reactions in medicinal chemistry. Together, the results of this extensive study position SF 5 –BCPs and SF 5 –[ 2 ]staffanes as practical hybrid bioisosteres for tuning molecular properties in drug discovery.

papers.title: Pnictogen-bonded reverse-bilayer vesicles from Sb and As cages enable partitioning of organic reaction media
papers.abstract: Pnictogen bonding directs the formation of reversed-bilayer vesicles from antimony- and arsenic-based thiolate cages in organic media. Sb systems form robust vesicles that enable chemical compartmentalization, as demonstrated using chemoswitchable fluorescent probes that selectively quench extravesicular species. In contrast, As analogues form dynamic, transient assemblies with diminished compartmentalization. Density functional theory calculations reveal reduced electrostatic potential and cooperativity in the As systems, consistent with weaker pnictogen bonding interactions. These results establish pnictogen identity as a key 2 factor governing vesicle stability and demonstrate a general strategy for probing compartmentalization in nonaqueous systems.

papers.title: When Chirality Collides: Pathway Complexity to Emergent Supramolecular Asymmetry in Peptide Assemblies
papers.abstract: Controlling supramolecular chirality during the non-covalent synthesis of peptide assemblies is critical for designing biomaterials with programmable mechanical and bioactive properties. However, most helical peptide assemblies formed via supramolecular polymerization rely solely on amino acid point chirality, precluding emergent phenomena such as the majority-rules effect, where modest enantiomeric excess (ee) drives nonlinear asymmetric amplification. While this effect is well established in non-peptidic systems, it remains largely absent in peptides. Here, we introduce a non-covalent synthesis strategy in which peptide point chirality interacts with the dynamic helical chirality of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) during supramolecular polymerization in water. Combined spectroscopic, scattering, microscopy, and computational analyses reveal two distinct regimes. In pH-induced homopolymerization, geometric incompatibility between chiral TPE propeller stacking and the twisted β-sheet hydrogen-bonding network produces a frustrated energy landscape with two polymorphs: kinetically trapped helical nanofibers and thermodynamically favored helical nano-springs, each with distinct helicity. Replacing protons with sodium or calcium ions modulates electrostatic interactions, steering polymorph selection toward nanofibers. In copolymerization with different ratios of enantiomers, the same chirality interplay perturbs β-sheet organization of l/d peptides and reduces the mismatch penalty of opposite enantiomers to ~1–2 kJ mol-1. This enables heterochiral copolymerization and generates a pronounced majority-rules effect, where ~50% ee dictates global helicity, a phenomenon previously absent in peptide systems.

papers.title: Three-Step and Continuous Axial Deformation in Fluorinated Molecular Crystals Built on a 5CB Scaffold
papers.abstract: Molecular crystals capable of large axial deformation through phase transitions have attracted increasing attention for applications such as artificial muscles and microactuators, yet rational strategies to program the deformation mode, including the number, sharpness, and spacing of consecutive transitions, remain elusive. Herein, we report fluorination as a simple yet powerful design principle that enables three-step axial deformation in molecular crystals of Au-F5IB, densely embedding a 5CB-derived scaffold. Upon heating, single crystals of Au-F5IB undergo three sequential phase transitions (α → β → γ → δ) clustered within an exceptionally narrow 4 °C window, producing stepwise length expansions to ρL = 1.15, 1.22, and 1.29 at 121.3, 123.2, and 125.5 °C, respectively, with full reversibility over at least 10 cycles. Variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses reveals smectic-like segregation of mesogenic and alkyl layers, in which mitogen-layer thickness changes are quantitatively translated into macroscopic axial strain. We show that the fluorine atoms play a dual role: intercolumn fluorine···π interactions reinforce lateral binding to elevate the transition temperatures above 120 °C, and simultaneously restrict molecular conformational freedom, compressing the multi-step transitions into a narrow temperature window. In striking contrast, the butyl analogue Au-F4IB, despite sharing nearly identical microscopic packing, exhibits phase-transition-free, continuous deformation accompanied by colossal volumetric thermal expansivity (245 MK-1). This single-carbon switch between digital and analogue deformation modes highlights the remarkable structural sensitivity of liquid-crystal-scaffold molecular crystals and offers a rational route toward programmable crystal actuators.

papers.title: Low partial pressure of oxygen. Thermodynamics and efficient control method.
papers.abstract: To control the partial pressure of oxygen below the level of real oxygen leakage, oxygen-containing molecules such as CO 2 , CO, H 2 O etc.(oxygen buffer) can be used. Consequently, the oxygen activity (i.e. the effective partial pressure of oxygen) below the oxygen buffer concentration is mainly defined by the thermodynamic equilibrium between the gas molecules. In practice, accessible oxygen activities are defined by leakage values and gas buffer concentrations. And vice versa accessible oxygen activities can be used to quantify the leakage and oxygen buffer concentration. This paper presents and compares the analysis of oxygen leakage in several gas systems with analyses performed using in situ freezing of impurities and coulometric titration.

papers.title: ZeoAgent: Autonomous Design of Zeolite Frameworks through Pore-Topology-Guided Generation and Evaluation
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents are emerging as a promising approach to assist and accelerate materials design and discovery. For zeolites, an important class of crystalline porous materials, this paradigm could address a long-standing challenge in framework discovery: the lack of rational strategies for coordinating framework generation with property objectives. Yet building such an autonomous agent system for zeolites remains challenging, as performance is governed by periodic pore topology and strict framework connectivity constraints. This requires the agent to jointly reason over pore architectures and generate valid frameworks. Here we present ZeoAgent, a zeolite-specific system that converts natural-language objectives into computational operations for zeolite structure analysis, property prediction as well as framework design. ZeoAgent uses a point-cloud representation of pore architecture to learn from existing zeolite frameworks and guide the generation of framework candidates, which are then evaluated against the design objective within the same loop. We demonstrate ZeoAgent in representative design tasks, including the design of frameworks with prescribed structural constraints, enhanced diffusion performance, and pore dimensions suited for CO₂/CH₄ separation. This work establishes a route for goal-directed zeolite design, showing how AI agents can be adapted to periodic porous materials governed by constrained pore topology.

papers.title: Parallel Procedures for Efficient Construction of Potential Energy Surfaces Based on Multireference Methods
papers.abstract: The exploration of potential energy surfaces (PESs) is central to the understanding of ground- and excited-state reactions. The construction of potential energy surfaces with multireference methods are usually done sequentially, meaning the calculation usually starts from one geometry, and the molecular orbitals and configuration interaction coefficients are carried over to a successive geometry close to the previous geometry, and so on, ensuring fast and reliable convergence to the desired solution. While this likely yields smooth, reasonable PESs, it is slow because each calculation must wait for the previous one to finish. When multiple processors are available, multiple geometries could in principle be computed in parallel, given an appropriate initial guess. In this work, we devise a set of procedures that balance the reliability of sequential calculations with the efficiency of parallel computing to various degrees. We demonstrate their usefulness in constructing ground-state PESs of Cr 2 , Cu 2 , Mg 2 , and O 3 with complete active space self-consistent field and second-order n -electron valence state perturbation theory, and we make recommendations on procedures that maximize the parallelization of PES construction without sacrificing quality. We expect our approach to serve as an important pointer in maximizing the efficiency of PES construction.

papers.title: Enhanced Carbon dioxide Hydrogenation to Methanol and Methane via Dysprosium–Nickel Co-Doped Alumina Catalysts in a Packed Bed Reactor
papers.abstract: This study investigates the catalytic conversion of carbon dioxide (CO2) into valuable products such as methane and methanol using dysprosium (Dy)–nickel (Ni) co-doped alumina catalysts in a packed bed reactor. The increasing concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere and its contribution to climate change necessitate the development of sustainable technologies for its utilization. In this work, Dy is introduced as a promoter to enhance surface basicity and CO2 adsorption, while Ni provides active sites for hydrogenation reactions. Catalysts with varying Dy loadings (10–25 wt%) were synthesized and systematically characterized using techniques such as FTIR, XPS, XRD, BET, SEM, and EDX to evaluate their structural, chemical, and morphological properties. Characterization results confirm the successful incorporation of Dy as Dy3+ species and reveal that increasing Dy loading enhances CO2 adsorption but gradually reduces surface area due to pore coverage and agglomeration. SEM and EDX analyses demonstrate that moderate Dy loading maintains good dispersion and accessibility of active sites, while excessive loading leads to surface densification and limited mass transfer. Among the studied compositions, 20 wt% Dy exhibits the most favorable balance between adsorption and catalytic activity. Reactor studies, including gas chromatography (FID), mass spectrometry, and refractometric analysis, confirm the formation of methane and methanol as major products. CO2 conversion efficiencies reach up to 80% under optimized conditions, while methanol conversion ranges from 55% to 65%, depending on operating parameters. The results indicate that product selectivity is strongly influenced by catalyst structure and process conditions, with moderate Dy loading favoring methanol formation and higher loading promoting methane production. Overall, this study establishes a clear structure–property–performance relationship for Dy–Ni/alumina catalysts and highlights the importance of optimizing promoter concentration and reactor conditions. The findings provide valuable insights for designing efficient catalysts for CO2 utilization and contribute to the development of sustainable energy and carbon management technologies.

papers.title: DNA Foundation Models for Molecular Biology: From Genomic Sequence Understanding to Function Prediction and Biological Design
papers.abstract: Molecular biology is increasingly shaped by the ability to read, model, and manipulate biological sequences at scale. While protein and RNA sequences have motivated mature branches of biological language modeling, genomic DNA remains a particularly challenging substrate because it encodes coding regions, non-coding regulatory elements, long-range dependencies, evolutionary constraints, population variation, and disease-associated mutations within a single symbolic sequence. This review examines genomic language models and DNA foundation models from a DNA-centered perspective. We first clarify the conceptual boundary between DNA, RNA, and protein language modeling and report the literature-search and model-selection strategy used for this review. We then summarize key methodological dimensions, including tokenization, pretraining objectives, Transformer architectures, long-context alternatives, state space models, reverse-complement-aware inductive biases, training data coverage, and compute cost. Representative systems, including DNABERT, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer, HyenaDNA, Caduceus, GPN, megaDNA, Evo, Evo 2, Borzoi, and AlphaGenome, are compared through a taxonomy that separates self-supervised genomic language models, evolution-aware models, generative genome models, supervised sequence-to-function DNA foundation models, and broader functional genomics predictors. Rather than treating model scale or benchmark accuracy as sufficient evidence of biological utility, we emphasize biological validity, benchmark leakage, homology overlap, species and population bias, interpretability, experimental validation, responsible design, and clinical translation. This framing provides a critical foundation for evaluating how DNA foundation models can support regulatory genomics, variant effect prediction, genome annotation, cross-species transfer, and biologically grounded sequence design.

papers.title: Alkyl Chain Length-Dependent Anticandidal Activity of Dicephalic Cationic Surfactants Branched on Carbon Atom: Computer-Assisted Fluorescence Analysis of Antibiofilm, Antiadhesive and Oxidative Stress Effects
papers.abstract: Candida biofilms associated with medical devices represent a major clinical challenge due to their high resistance to conventional antifungal therapies. In this study, we investigated the structure–activity relationship of a homologous series of dicephalic cationic surfactants branched on carbon atom (Cn-DCNMe3Br, n= 10, 12, 14), with a focus on the effect of alkyl chain length on antifungal, antibiofilm, and cytotoxic properties. Planktonic susceptibility assays revealed a non-linear “cut-off” effect, with the C12 homologue exhibiting maximal fungicidal efficacy across the tested strains (C. albicans, C. glabrata, C. krusei, and C. tropicalis). In contrast, adhesion and biofilm-related assays demonstrated that the less hydrophobic C10 homologue showed superior performance in inhibiting initial cell attachment and disrupting mature biofilms. These findings highlight the critical role of early-stage surface interactions in determining overall antibiofilm efficacy. Mechanistically, the activity of these amphiphiles appears to be strongly associated with their ability to modulate cell–surface interactions, likely through a combination of physicochemical effects, including surface adsorption, alteration of wettability, and electrostatic interactions with microbial cell envelopes. While oxidative stress was observed as a secondary effect, it is not considered the primary determinant of antifungal activity. Crucially, biocompatibility assessment based on hemolysis assays demonstrated a clear chain-length-dependent toxicity profile. While C10 and C12 exhibited concentration-dependent hemolytic activity above 0.5 mM, the C14 derivative showed negligible hemolysis across the tested concentration range (up to 5 mM). These findings underscore the importance of fine-tuning alkyl chain length to balance antimicrobial efficacy, anti-adhesive performance, and host cytotoxicity, positioning this novel class of dicephalic surfactants as promising candidates for surface-functionalization strategies aimed at preventing device-associated infections.

papers.title: Tetraethylammonium Cations Enable C2+ Product Formation in Acidic CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Cation effect is essential to obtain selectivity towards carbon dioxide (CO2) reduction reaction (CO2RR) over the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media. Selectivity towards CO2RR has been largely attributed to the coordination between alkali cations and CO2-derived intermediates. Here, we provide a different perspective by demonstrating that tetraethylammonium (Et4N+), a weakly coordinating cation, can also effectively suppress the HER in acidic media, favoring CO2RR on both Ag and Cu electrodes. The generation of both C1 and C2+ products on Cu indicates that the direct participation of alkali cations as co-catalyst is not a prerequisite for CO2 activation or C-C coupling. We find that CO2RR is independent of the bulk pH in the presence of 1 M Et4N+, as evidenced by similar selectivity across acidic, neutral, and alkaline media. In addition, rigorous impurities control reveals that millimolar-levels of triethylammonium chloride (Et3NHCl) substantially promote HER on Cu catalyst, hence calling for rigorous impurity control. Overall, this work demonstrates that weakly coordinating cations can promote CO2RR across a broad range of pH, indicating that a catalytic role of alkali metal cations is not necessary for CO2RR. Graphical Abstract CO2 reduction with weakly coordinating cations: The weakly coordinating organic cation tetraethylammonium (Et4N+) efficiently suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction, favoring CO2RR on Ag and Cu electrodes. This demonstrates that the direct participation or catalytic role of alkali metal cations is not a prerequisite for CO2 activation or C-C coupling.

papers.title: BackMapNet: A Lightweight Non-Equivariant Framework for Generalised Protein Backmapping
papers.abstract: Coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics enables the simulation of large biomolecular systems over extended timescales, but recovering atomistic detail from CG representations remains a significant challenge. Here, we present BackMapNet, a generalised and computationally e!cient framework for protein backmapping. The method adopts a staged reconstruction strategy for backbone and side-chain prediction. To enhance structural accuracy and physical realism, BackMapNet integrates geometric priors and Ramachandran-guided refinement to constrain backbone torsion angles. The model was trained on molecular dynamics trajectories from twelve structurally diverse proteins. Without retraining, BackMapNet was evaluated on previously unseen proteins. Across these systems, the model consistently achieved sub-Å accuracy, with overall protein RMSDs remaining below 0.85 Å for all test cases. Ramachandran-based refinement reduced torsional outliers while preserving coordinate fidelity. Benchmarking against established methods demonstrates that BackMapNet achieves competitive performance. These results indicate that accurate and transferable protein backmapping can be achieved with lightweight, non-equivariant architectures, provided that appropriate geometric priors and staged reconstruction strategies are employed.

papers.title: ModernMolBERT: A Compact SELFIES Encoder for Molecular Representation Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce ModernMolBERT, an encoder-only transformer model for small-molecule representation learning. ModernMolBERT adapts the ModernBERT architecture to molecular language modelling and pairs it with a SELFIES-aware Atom Pair Encoding (APE) tokeniser. Both released variants (small and base) are pre-trained with masked language modelling on approximately 2.4M unique SELFIES strings from ChEMBL 36 and evaluated as frozen molecular embedders on 25 binary classification benchmarks. ModernMolBERT-base attains a mean ROC-AUC of 77.9 (reported on a 0 to 100 scale), competitive with a strong fingerprint baseline and improving on comparable pre-trained string encoders by roughly five points. ModernMolBERT provides a compact, reproducible, open-source foundation for SELFIES-based molecular representation learning; we release the model weights, the APE tokeniser, and training code.

papers.title: Transmembrane Water Transport by Self-Assembled Metal-Organic Cages can be Controlled by Guest Binding
papers.abstract: Biology makes use of specialised proteins, the Aquaporins, to facilitate rapid water transport across cell membranes whilst strictly excluding salt, enabling maintenance of homeostasis. Whilst attempts have been made to use these properties in water purification and desalination, issues with stability, scalability, and cost have restricted their impact. Recent attention has focussed on building artificial water channels, typically formed from folded or selfassembled polymers. Herein, we disclose the first metal-organic cage which enables water transport in liposomes, and showcase how host-guest chemistry enables control of water flux. We find that a self-assembled pseudo-octahedral Pd6L12 cage acts as a stable and eXective transmembrane channel for water flow at high rates (up to 1.4 × 108 water molecules per second per channel, in the range of natural Aquaporins), whilst strictly excluding the transport of salt. We show that the properties that make metal-organic cages so fascinating in solution – namely their host-guest chemistry – are maintained, but transformed, in the membrane environment. We demonstrate that addition of molecules that bind to the metal-organic cage modulates the rate of water transport across the membrane. Further, rather than blockage being driven by a simple relationship with aXinity or size, instead a complex interplay of membrane partition propensity and binding constant dictate the ability of guest molecules to impede water flow. Our work begins to unpick the rules determining how metal-organic cages can be used as next generation artificial water channels, with novel properties.

papers.title: To Greater Twist: A Kinetically Biased π-Radical Cascade
papers.abstract: π-Radical cascades of open-shell graphene fragments—exemplified by phenalenyl and related systems—are emerging as a versatile synthetic tool for constructing complex polycyclic aromatic frameworks. While previous investigations showed that the reaction outcome can be reduced to a single possibility in both intra- and intermolecular settings, the findings of this study uncover a broader dimension of control. In a scenario with several competing pathways involving di- and trisubstituted phenalenyl derivatives, the cascade is kinetically steered toward a single, more distorted peropyrene product, a counterintuitive outcome enabled by an intrinsic mechanistic bias.

papers.title: Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Molecular Dynamics to Investigate Sequence Dependent Fluorescence in Single Stranded DNA
papers.abstract: The intensity of a photon released from cyanine dye on a labeled oligonucleotide is heavily influenced by the adjacent sequence. This phenomenon could have profound effects in biotechnologies that rely on fluorescently labeled DNA based materials such as PCR, DNA-PAINT, and FISH. For instance, the selection of a DNA probe could result in a lower Signal-to-Noise ratio necessitating further data processing procedures. Currently, π- π stacking between the cyanine dye and the terminal nucleotide is the leading theory to explain this sequence dependent fluorescence. This stabilization minimizes the rotational isomerization of the cyanine dye, increasing the rate of photonic emissions. However, how this occurs in single stranded DNA with minimal secondary structure formation is not well understood. In this work, we use eXplainable Artifical Intelligence (XAI) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) to explore the potential mechanism of the phenomenon in addition to investigating some fundamental questions in biological data science.

papers.title: Overcoming Barriers for Ilmenite Reduction to TiFe through Defect Engineering
papers.abstract: Ilmenite, TiFeO 3 , is an earth-abundant mineral commonly used as a feedstock for TiO 2 , Ti, and Fe via reduction. One reduction product currently being explored is TiFe, an intermetallic compound capable of reversible, near-ambient hydrogen storage. Here, we use first-principles calculations coupled with CALPHAD thermodynamic modeling to evaluate how the kinetics and thermodynamics of point defects and impurities may hinder or facilitate this reduction process. We find that certain impurities within ilmenite can lower the thermodynamic barrier to reduction, including elements such as Mn and Si that are commonly found in the naturally occurring mineral. Elements like Cr, Mn, and V, which considerably decrease the reduction barrier, also offer benefits for the hydrogen storage properties of TiFe, making them valuable at both ends of the reaction. Based on thermodynamic analysis, we find Co and Mn to be particularly promising, because they are fully soluble for Fe in the ilmenite lattice and will not form secondary oxide phases. Additionally, we find that the choice of reduction agent (e.g., {Ca,Mg}H 2 , {Ca,Mg}Cl 2 , {Ca,Mg}F 2 , or {Ca,Mg} metal) affects the favorability of reduction. Native oxygen vacancies have high formation energies; however, the substitutional species H O and F O have much lower energies under H-rich and F-rich conditions, indicating that oxygen removal will be enhanced with H-or F-based reduction agents. Furthermore, diffusion pathways for V O and anion substitutional species are likely to be activated at elevated temperatures typical of reduction, meaning that they can move into and out of the ilmenite lattice readily. Our results provide valuable guidance for engineering ilmenite to facilitate its direct reduction to TiFe, while also offering general insights into how unintentional impurities in reduction flows may contribute to high-value product materials.

papers.title: Unaccounted Impact of Diffuse Capacitance on Electrochemical Reduction of Carbon Dioxide
papers.abstract: The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) relies on precise control of the catalyst and electrolyte environment so that an electric field from the Helmholtz-layer acts on reaction intermediates. Despite established benchmarking protocols, achieving reproducible performance remains difficult even for planar Cu under nominally identical conditions. We show that planar Cu operated at a fixed potential exhibits systematic variation in CO2RR activity and selectivity with counter-electrode potential. This observation is attributed to a previously unaccounted-for effect of diffuse (Gouy-Chapman) capacitance on CO2RR. While the electrolyte composition determines the Helmholtz-layer capacitance, the counter-electrode potential governs the diffuse capacitance. Increasing the counter-electrode potential increases diffuse capacitance, leading to cation crowding near the outer Helmholtz layer, thereby enhancing the overall electric-field contributions. We performed cathodically controlled CO2RR at a fixed working electrode potential of −1.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl, where the intrinsic Helmholtz-layer capacitance remains invariant at ~7.5 µF, while the total double-layer capacitance increases from ~80 to ~153 µF as the counter-electrode potential increased from 4.86 V to 7.76 V vs. Ag/AgCl. This increase reflects enhanced charge storage within the electrolyte beyond the compact layer, rather than changes at the Cu surface, as evidenced by the rise in total interfacial charge density (σdl) from ~1.0 to ~1.8 C m-2 between counter-electrode potential increases from 4.86 to 7.76 V while the Helmholtz-layer charge density (σhelm) remains constant at ~0.1 C m-2. Increasing diffuse capacitance increases C2/C1 from ~0.47 to ~0.91, decreases current density from ~35 mA to ~22 mA, and overall CO2RR efficiency from ~64% to ~47%, which is consistent with the previous reported effect of field enhancement. The corresponding increase in total interfacial electric field from ~3.0 × 109 to ~4.1 × 109 V m-1 further supports this interpretation. Our findings provide direct evidence of the impact of the diffuse-layer on CO2RR and its potential effect on scaling reactors from lab-scale to commercial zero-gap configurations.

papers.title: Reduced Concentration Quenching of Multi-Resonant Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitter Incorporating Pillar[5]arene Macrocycle
papers.abstract: The development of multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters, which simultaneously exhibit narrowband emission, suppressed concentration quenching, and rapid reverse intersystem crossing (RISC), remains a challenge. Here, an MRTADF emitter incorporating pillar[5]arene to suppress aggregation is reported. The “butterfly” shaped emitter BN-APOPV is constructed by tethering pillar[5]arene to a tCzBN MR-TADF skeleton and employing an aryl bridge for connection. Intramolecular energy transfer and TADF type CzAcSF host materials are used to harvest excitons and accelerate RISC. BNAPOPV exhibits sky-blue emission (lPL of 491 nm) with a full-width at half-maximum of 33 nm and a RISC rate constant (kRISC) of 1.37 × 106 s−1 in a 1 wt% doped CzAcSF film. As the doping concentration is increased from 1 to 5 wt%, the photoluminescence quantum yield increases from 76 to 86%. Solution-processed organic light-emitting diodes prepared with BN-APOPV exhibited almost the same maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmax) of 9% at doping concentrations ranging from 1 to 5 wt%. In contrast, the device doped with the emitter BN-AOPV (prepared without pillar[5]arene) suffers from severe aggregation-caused quenching with EQEmax decreasing from 7.0 to 2.7% as the doping concentration increases from 1 to 5 wt%.

papers.title: Automated flow synthesis of native, engineered, and de novo-designed functional luciferases
papers.abstract: Luciferases are widely used bioluminescent reporters, yet access to these enzymes has historically relied on recombinant expression. Here, we show that automated fast-flow peptide synthesis (AFPS) enables the rapid production of functional luciferases spanning native, engineered, and de novo-designed scaffolds. Using AFPS, we synthesized Gaussia luciferase (GLuc, 18.1 kDa, 168 amino acids), picALuc (13 kDa, 120 amino acids), and LuxSit-i (13.8 kDa, 120 amino acids), representing a natural disulfide-rich luciferase, an engineered luciferase, and a de novo-designed luciferase, respectively. Synthetic GLuc was purified, oxidatively folded, and recovered as a monomeric, enzymatically active enzyme with biophysical properties comparable to its recombinant counterpart. picALuc likewise required oxidative folding, whereas LuxSit-i, which lacks cysteine residues, was folded by denaturant removal using size-exclusion chromatography. Biochemical and biophysical analyses confirmed the structural integrity and activity of the three synthetic enzymes. Notably, LuxSit-i represents, to our knowledge, the first total chemical synthesis of a fully de novo-designed enzyme. These three luciferases collectively span natural, engineered, and computationally designed enzyme architectures, which represents an approximately 14% expansion of the known repertoire of fully synthetic enzymes produced by solid-phase peptide synthesis. These studies establish the first examples of fully synthetic luciferases produced by solid-phase peptide synthesis that retain native-like enzymatic activity. Together, these findings demonstrate AFPS as a general platform for accessing functional enzymes across evolutionary and design spaces alike. We anticipate that this platform will enable the development of next-generation luciferases through noncanonical residue incorporation, site-specific modification, and mirror-image variants.

papers.title: Metal-Dependent Control of Methoxy Retention versus Cleavage in Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Lignin-Derived Aromatics
papers.abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation of lignin-derived aromatics provides a sustainable route for biomass upgrading, yet controlling the competition between methoxy retention and C-O bond cleavage remains a central challenge. Here, we establish a metal-dependent selectivity framework for guaiacol hydrogenation by systematically comparing carbon-supported noble metal catalysts (Rh, Pt, Ru, and Pd) under identical electrochemical conditions. While Ru and Pd exhibit negligible activity, Rh and Pt show comparable overall proton utilization but fundamentally different reaction pathways. Under representative acidic conditions, Rh gives high guaiacol conversion with predominant methoxy retention, producing 2-methoxycyclohexanone and 2methoxycyclohexanol as the major products, whereas Pt favors demethoxylation, yielding cyclohexanone and cyclohexanol. This pathway contrast persists across variations in applied potential, temperature, electrolyte pH, and substrate structure, indicating that it originates from intrinsic metal-adsorbate interactions rather than reaction conditions alone. Density functional theory calculations suggest that stronger adsorption, enhanced charge transfer, and increased orbital hybridization on Pt stabilize hydrogen-assisted intermediates and lower the calculated barriers for C-O bond activation, whereas weaker interactions on Rh are consistent with methoxyretaining hydrogenation pathways. These findings support adsorption-controlled bond activation as a key descriptor governing selectivity and provide a general design principle for tuning reaction pathways in electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin-derived aromatics.

papers.title: Approach-Region Dynamics and Rate Turnover in Thermally Activated Barrier Crossing
papers.abstract: Chemical reaction dynamics has a well-developed thermodynamic description of barrier crossing, but a less operational account of the dynamical conditions governing whether a reactive trajectory commits productively or recrosses. This work shows that as a reactive coordinate approaches a transition state through a stable precursor basin, this behavior is organized by a dimensionless damping ratio, χ0 = Γeff/(2Ω0), where Ω0 is the precursor-well frequency and Γeff is the total projected dissipation. Below χ0 = 1 approach dynamics are oscillatory and recrossing-prone; above it monotonic but increasingly sluggish; at χ0 = 1 the approach coordinate reaches an exceptional point and monotonic commitment is fastest. Established descriptions of barrier crossing in electron transfer, proton-coupled electron transfer, and heterogeneous surface reactivity yield locally equivalent precursor-well damped-generator dynamics despite distinct microscopic origins. Three calibrated estimator routes connect χ0 to spectroscopic linewidths, solvent longitudinal relaxation times, and electronic friction coefficients, each with explicit validity bounds. Worked examples illustrate solvent-dependent turnover in TEMPO electron transfer and promoter-dependent N2 activation on Fe surfaces. The approach-dynamics descriptor complements thermodynamic rate theory by quantifying when barrier crossing is limited by recrossing, overdamped sluggishness, or near-critical commitment.

papers.title: Excitation-Wavelength Dependent Electron-Phonon Coupling in Photoinduced Charge-Transfer Titanocenes in Solution
papers.abstract: Metallocene dihalides with single active sites are an industry standard polymerization catalyst. Despite a high potential for visible-light absorption, these compounds remain underutilized in light-driven redox reactions. A primary bottleneck is the presence of ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) excited states that are dissociative in character and possess ultrashort lifetimes. Here, we show the unusual role that the photoexcitation wavelength plays in the excited-state relaxation of organic titanocene chloride compounds by direct observation of long-lived, coherent Brillouin oscillations in acetonitrile solution. A pronounced six-to-eleven gigahertz coherent longitudinal acoustic phonon of the solvent bath observed across the probe window in the case of 266-nm LMCT electronic excitation shows that energy dissipated in the form of heat can travel in wavelike motion of coordinated solvent molecules. The results call for a new photophysical blueprint to describe energy dissipation and electron-phonon coupling in photoinduced charge transfer complexes in solution.

papers.title: Understanding charge acceptance limitations during extreme fast-charging of Li-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Extreme fast charging in lithium-ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C-rates. In this work, we use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport related voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients developed as a result of fast charging are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co-solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co-solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C-rates, partially when used in combination with interface-stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li+ transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation-shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three-electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) electrode used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

papers.title: A Supramolecular Transition Underlies the Pathogenic Threshold in Polyglutamine Disease
papers.abstract: Polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases are neurodegenerative disorders caused by CAG repeat expansions and are characterized by a clinical pathogenic threshold typically observed between 35 and 39 glutamine residues. While this threshold is well established from genetic and clinical studies, its molecular and thermodynamic origin remains unclear. Here, we performed all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and transcriptome analysis to investigate polyQ assemblies spanning the pathological transition region. Potential of mean force (PMF) analysis revealed a pronounced stabilization transition at Q/S 18 (corresponding to Q39), where the free-energy landscape became markedly more favorable than that of shorter polyQ assemblies. This stabilization point coincides with the clinically observed pathogenic threshold. Within the transition region (Q/S 14–18, corresponding to Q31–Q39), we further identified an odd-even effect in intermolecular interaction energies and hydrogen-bonding retention, with odd Q/S values (15 and 17) exhibiting enhanced stability relative to their even-numbered counterparts. RNA-sequecing analysis of polyQ-expressing cells independently revealed that clusters of gene expression profiles depend on their spatial location. These findings support the hypothesis that the pathogenic threshold of polyQ diseases reflects a supramolecular stabilization transition and provide a molecular framework linking assembly energetics to disease onset.

papers.title: ChemAdapter: Chemistry-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Molecular Image Understanding
papers.abstract: Pre-trained vision models have achieved remarkable success on natural image tasks, yet their application to chemistry-specific visual understanding remains challenging due to the significant domain gap between natural images and chemical molecular imagery. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as Adapter modules and LoRA offer a promising solution by updating only a small fraction of parameters, but existing approaches do not exploit the structural priors inherent in chemical molecules, including atom-bond topology, functional group patterns, and stereochemical constraints. In this paper, we propose ChemAdapter, a chemistry-aware parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework for molecular image understanding. ChemAdapter introduces three novel components: a chemistry-aware Adapter module with a learnable functional group dictionary that injects local atomic patterns as prior embeddings into the bottleneck representation, a multi-task sharing mechanism that enables knowledge transfer across molecular structure recognition, chemical image classification, and material property prediction, and a topology-aware attention reweighting module that leverages molecular graph adjacency to emphasize chemically bonded regions. We evaluate ChemAdapter on three chemistry benchmarks including MoleculeNet, QM9, and Materials Project.
