ChemAdapter consistently outperforms existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods and Full Fine-tuning while using less than one percent of trainable parameters, demonstrating that chemistry-specific inductive biases effectively bridge the domain gap and improve molecular image understanding.

papers.title: High-throughput photoiniferter polymerization for the synthesis of ultrahigh molecular weight polymer adhesives
papers.abstract: Despite the long-standing recognition that ultrahigh molecular weight (UHMW) polymers give rise to chain-length-derived emergent material properties, the synthesis of functional UHMW polymers remains synthetically challenging due to oxygen-mediated radical quenching and chain growth limitations in conventional polymerization methodologies. In this study, we introduce an enzyme-deoxygenated photoiniferter polymerization (Enz-PI) that eliminates oxygen sensitivity from photoiniferter polymerization by incorporating a glucose oxidase-mediated in situ oxygenscavenging pathway. Enz-PI allows controlled synthesis of UHMW polymers with low dispersity without using specialized deoxygenation techniques, while maintaining enzyme stability. The mild, oxygen-tolerant conditions also facilitate high-throughput polymerization in low-volume formats, enabling the creation of a chemically diverse UHMW binary copolymer library. The adhesion performance characterization of these UHMW copolymers reveals compositiondependent and synergistic adhesion behaviors, highlighting the interplay between interfacial interactions and bulk energy dissipation in UHMW polymer adhesion. This work offers a framework for oxygen-tolerant access to UHMW polymers and rapid discovery of functional polymer adhesives.

papers.title: Donor-Linker-Driven Electronic Modulation of Metal-Cluster Nodes in MNC-COF for Highly Efficient and Selective Bifunctional Electroreduction of NO3- and CO2
papers.abstract: Metal nanocluster-based covalent organic frameworks (MNC-COFs) represent a fundamentally distinct class of crystalline extended porous materials that combine atomically precise metal active sites with structurally programmable organic architectures. Despite their promise for electrocatalysis, the integration of noble-metal nanoclusters into pristine COF frameworks to achieve precise electronic modulation of catalytic centers remains largely unexplored. Meanwhile, Electrochemical nitrate reduction (eNO3-RR) and CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) represent promising, parallel pathways for sustainable energy conversion and environmental remediation. Herein, we report the first bifunctional trinuclear silver nanocluster-based pristine two-dimensional COF, AgNCNPh, in which Ag3 cluster nodes are embedded within a π-conjugated imine-linked framework along with high surface area and 1D porous channel, enabling strong framework-cluster, electronic coupling and tunable catalytic reactivity. The catalyst exhibits excellent bifunctional electrocatalytic performance, achieving ~77% Faradaic efficiency along with 603 μg h-1 production rate of NH3 from nitrate reduction and ~96% Faradaic efficiency for CO generation during CO2 reduction. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that framework-induced electronic modulation optimizes intermediate adsorption and promotes electron transfer into antibonding orbitals, facilitating N-O and C-O bond activation followed by dissociation. This work establishes noble-metal nanocluster COFs as a promising platform for electronically tunable and selective small-molecule electroreduction.

papers.title: Shell-Thickness Dependence of Hot Electron Transfer in CdSe/ZnS Quantum Dots and Fullerene Derivative Hybrid Systems
papers.abstract: The utilization of hot electrons surpasses the Shockley-Queisser limit, and fundamental understanding of hot electrons provides design principles for photo-energy conversion materials. Although the effect of donor-acceptor distance on electron transfer from the lowest excitonic state in quantum dots (QDs) to the acceptor has been studied (cold electron transfer), that of hot electron transfer still remains unclear. In this study, we hybridized CdSe/ZnS QDs with different shell thicknesses and a fullerene derivative (PCBA) and investigated the effect of shell thickness on electron transfer. Both cold and hot electron transfer showed shell-thickness dependence, however the degree of change in the rate constant was smaller for hot electron transfer than for cold electron transfer. The trends were derived from the electronic coupling constant due to the effective delocalization of the wavefunction of QDs in the higher excited state. This study contributes to the understanding of and ability to utilize hot electrons in QDs.

papers.title: In-depth impurity profiling of therapeutic oligonucleotides by heartcut two-dimensional ion pairing liquid chromatography featuring UV-absorbance and mass spectrometry detection in both dimensions
papers.abstract: Quantitative impurity profiling of therapeutic oligonucleotides (ONs) by liquid chromatography (LC) commonly employs UV-absorbance detection for resolved impurities, while impurities co-eluting with the full-length product (FLP) are assessed by mass spectrometry (MS) detection. However, quantification by MS may introduce bias, compromising accurate purity determination. Twodimensional LC (2DLC) can potentially overcome these constraints, but conventional heart-cutting 2DLC is limited by the constrained volume per transferred fraction (typically 40-80 µL) and does not allow MS detection for the first LC dimension (1D), complicating the identification and quantification low-level impurities. Here, we present a novel heart-cut 2DLC-UV-MS method that couples ion-pairing reversed-phase LC (IP-RPLC) to orthogonal ion-pairing hydrophilic interaction LC (IP-HILIC) using flow-splitting and stationary-phase-assisted modulation. This setup, here referred to as Flow-split Orthogonal Characterization of Unresolved Species (FOCUS), enables transfer of relatively large fractions (≥ 100 µL) from 1D as well as UV-absorbance and MS detection of the separations achieved in both LC dimensions. Modulation conditions were studied and optimized to overcome mobile-phase incompatibilities between the LC dimensions and achieve efficient and sensitive IP-HILIC-UV-MS analysis of heart-cuts from IP-RPLC. The new 2DLC procedure was evaluated using antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) and small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics, demonstrating that potential impurities co-eluting with the respective main drugs in IP-RPLC were resolved by IP-HILIC. The 2DLC approach also revealed potential underestimation of impurity levels by 2.2-4.0% when quantifying impurities using one-dimensional LC-UV-MS only. The 2DLC setup provides a promising, alternative strategy for impurity quantification, exhibiting less reliance on complex calibration approaches.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it is an unintentional duplicate of another preprint ( 10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-n40j7/v2 ).

papers.title: Green Chemistry for the Classroom: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Organic Compounds
papers.abstract: Hydrothermal synthesis (HTS) designates the use of hot liquid water as medium for chemical reactions. The technique is very well established for generating crystalline inorganic materials. Recently it was shown that HTS can also be used to prepare organic compounds, which are all bearing a high content in aromatics and heterocyclics. The technique is environmentally friendly for using solely water as medium, especially in comparison to conventional syntheses of such compounds. Here we present HTS of organic compounds in a fashion that allows for implementing it in the classroom. First, we show how HTS can be used as an example to introduce the timely concepts of green chemistry and sustainable syntheses. Second, we review organic cyclocondensation reactions including reaction equilibrium and enthalpic/entropic driving forces as well as real-life examples of cyclocondensation products, as HTS is especially amenable to cyclocondensations. Third, as liquid high-temperature water is well suited to review the temperature-dependence of certain physicochemical features, we provide interactive plots for exploring these data. Fourth, we develop a classroom friendly HTS of a simple organic colorant, that can be performed simple in kitchen pressure cookers. Fifth, at the hand of this classroom experiment we show how measures for the green-ness of a chemical synthesis, such as the Ecoscale are used.

papers.title: Beyond Targets: Benefits of a Multi-Assessment Approach in Determining Chemical Water Quality for Water Reuse
papers.abstract: The multitude of organic micropollutants (OMPs) in treated wastewater (TWW) represents a significant challenge for water reuse. This study aimed to evaluate water quality using a combination of target analysis, effect-based methods (EBMs), and nontarget screening (NTS) to demonstrate the benefits of a comprehensive chemical risk assessment of TWW and to assess its reuse potential. OMPs were analysed in a pilot plant treating municipal wastewater, using a combination of ozonation, advanced oxidation with hydrogen peroxide, ceramic membrane filtration, and granular activated carbon. Target analysis showed that the treatment effectively removed OMPs, but negative removal was observed after activated carbon, likely due to desorption. After activated carbon, benzotriazole, caffeine, carbamazepine, diuron, fipronil, imidacloprid, linuron, MCPA, O-desmethylvenlafaxine, sulfamethoxazole, and venlafaxine had risk quotients >0.1, with fipronil consistently exceeding 1 and MCPA exceeding its drinking water guideline value. In vitro EBMs, covering oxidative stress, xenobiotic metabolism, cytotoxicity, estrogenicity, and thyroid disruption, detected effects in secondary TWW. EBMs revealed the ceramic membrane treatment’s ability to remove oxidative stress. Based on effect-based trigger values for surface and drinking water, risks for estrogenicity were only absent after the full treatment train. NTS showed that 26–37% of features were removed, driven by oxidative treatments, while membrane filtration and activated carbon effectively removed features introduced by the oxidative treatment. Hence, this study suggests that TWW reuse without advanced treatment is not recommended. The multiassessment approach applied here allowed more nuanced conclusions on water safety, underscoring its added benefit for water quality assessment for water reuse.

papers.title: An efficient neural network architecture for molecular vibrational states: from rigid molecules to molecular complexes
papers.abstract: Accurately solving the nuclear Schrödinger equation for molecular complexes exhibiting noncovalent interactions remains a challenge due to the exponential scaling of basis sets and the presence of strongly anharmonic, large-amplitude motions. Recently, we proposed a neural network (NN) method to tackle high-dimensional vibrational problems and successfully applied it to C 3 H 8 in full dimensionality; however, applying the method to molecular complexes has been hindered by difficulties in representing delocalized wave functions across multiple minima. In this work, we present a substantially improved NN-based methodology that overcomes these limitations through two key developments: (i) a novel NN architecture specifically designed to capture the asymptotic behavior and delocalization characteristics of weakly bound complexes, and (ii) an efficient training protocol that optimizes the variance of local energies. We demonstrate that this approach achieves sub‑cm -1 accuracy for the vibrational ground and excited states of CH 4 with substantially fewer parameters than the previous method requires. Crucially, for the prototypical water dimer (H 2 O) 2 , the new method successfully computes both ground state and intramolecular excited states with ~ 1 cm -1 accuracy using ~6,000 NN parameters. This work establishes a robust and scalable framework for performing full-dimensional, fully coupled vibrational calculations on molecular complexes, paving the way for accurate spectroscopic predictions of systems previously deemed intractable.

papers.title: Photocontrolled Supramolecular Gels in Deep Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: An adaptable strategy for developing light-responsive eutectogels with intrinsic mechanical modulation is introduced. This was achieved through the controlled supramolecular assembly between an amphiphile and a customized azobenzene photoswitch, which displays high solubility in water-free eutectic media. Molecular and mesoscopic characterization provided a detailed understanding of the heterotypic interactions between the photoswitch and the amphiphile, as well as their respective one-dimensional assemblies. UV irradiation induces E→Z isomerization of the azobenzene trigger, enabling efficient transduction of molecular photoisomerization into assembly contraction and the loss of the solid-like character. Under visible light, the system forms robust gels supported by extended architectures that are not affected by solvent evaporation or long-term storage. Photo-induced gel–sol transitions are fully reversible and can be cycled repeatedly with marginal loss of structural and mechanical recovery. As such, this work introduces a versatile approach for the next generation of light-responsive gels based on eutectic systems.

papers.title: Leveraging synergistic regional aromaticity for balanced spectral bathochromism and narrowband emission towards highly efficient and stable green OLEDs
papers.abstract: Balancing bathochromic shift and narrowband emission remains a long-standing bottleneck for multiple resonance (MR) emitters, especially for indolocarbazole (ICz)-based systems with limited spectral tunability. Herein, the study proposes a synergistic regional aromaticity (SRA) strategy that harmonically integrates localized and delocalized aromaticity to address this trade-off, enabling the construction of high-performance green-emitting ICz derivatives. The target molecules are constructed by fusing two naphthalene-like segments onto the ICz core via antiaromatic hexatomic junctions; such fusion mode not only preserves the inherent MR effect of the central ICz matrix for narrow spectral features, but also extends π-conjugation via peripheral naphthalene units to realize effective emission red-shift. Besides, central-anchored steric hindrance effectively suppresses intermolecular interactions, as confirmed by X-ray crystallography. The two SRA-engineered emitters achieve emissive maxima of 505-520 nm with full-width at half-maximum of 20-22 nm in solution state. The organic light-emitting diode (OLED) devices based on above emitters display slightly broadened emission spectra relative to their photoluminescence, while simultaneously achieving external quantum efficiency (EQE) as high as 30.1%. Moreover, both devices exhibit exceptional operational LT90 (time to 90% of the initial luminance) of 4,150 and 5,245 h at 1,000 cd m−2, respectively, representing top-tier stability among narrowband green OLEDs with EQE >20%.

papers.title: The Tetrahedron Speaks: A Holistic Benchmark for DFT in Tetrahedral Framework
papers.abstract: For nearly three decades, benchmarking density functional theory (DFT) functionals for zeolites and other tetrahedral frameworks has relied almost exclusively on average Si-O bond lengths. This practice assumes that accurate reproduction of bond lengths implies correct overall framework geometry. In this work, it is demonstrated that this assumption can be systematically misleading due to error cancellation: local overestimations and underestimations may cancel when averaged, producing apparently accurate mean values while the framework remains globally distorted. A new benchmarking paradigm is introduced based on two framework‑independent metrics: the tetrahedron‑normalized volume (Vᴛᴏ₄) and the tetrahedron‑normalized surface area (Sᴛᴏ₄). These metrics are calculated directly from the geometry of each TO₄ tetrahedron using the Cayley‑Menger determinant for volume and Heron's formula for surface area. Twenty‑six DFT functionals-spanning LDA, GGA, and meta‑GGA approximations with and without dispersion corrections-were benchmarked against high‑precision experimental data for α‑quartz at 13 K. The results reveal a striking pattern. The m‑GGA‑M06‑L functional ranks first in bond‑length accuracy (-0.75%) but twenty‑third in tetrahedron volume (-3.43%) and twentieth in tetrahedron surface area (-1.96%)-a dramatic ranking inversion that demonstrates error cancellation. LDA functionals show excellent bond‑length errors (0.50‑0.68%) but large volume underestimations (11‑13%) and density overestimations (12‑15%), a signature of overbinding that bond‑length averages fail to capture. The Pearson correlation between bond‑length error and tetrahedron volume error is remarkably weak (r = 0.31, R² = 0.10), indicating that 90% of the variance in volumetric accuracy is not explained by bond‑length benchmarks. A self‑consistency check using |ΔV- ΔS| successfully differentiates isotropic errors (LDA: |ΔV-ΔS| < 0.15%) from anisotropic errors (M06‑L: |ΔV-ΔS| = 1.47%). Notably, Vᴛᴏ₄ and Sᴛᴏ₄ capture distortions that bond‑length averages inherently miss and are transferable to any tetrahedral material, including zeolites, metal‑organic frameworks, germanates, and phosphates. It is therefore proposed that tetrahedron‑normalized volume and surface area be adopted as complementary metrics to traditional bond‑length and angle analyses in future DFT benchmarking studies of zeolites and other tetrahedral frameworks.

papers.title: Experimental and DFT insights into phase-dependent performance of NiIn1-xSnx (x=0.5 and 0.8) intermetallic catalysts for acetylene hydrogenation
papers.abstract: Intermetallic catalysts offer a unique platform for the hydrogenation reaction of acetylene, as their well-defined crystal structures and precise stoichiometry enable atomic-level control over active-site composition, geometry, and electronic structure. In ternary intermetallics, the addition of a third element in varying amounts can alter the crystal structure, thereby changing the stable crystal facet(s) and, consequently, the active-site electronic structure, demonstrating an intriguing strategy to boost product selectivity. The site-specific substitution of Sn in NiIn 1- x Sn x ( x =0.5, 0.8) exhibits two distinct phases belonging to hexagonal ( x =0.5) and orthorhombic ( x =0.8) crystal systems. Density Functional Theory calculations show that (0001) and (010) facets of hexagonal and orthorhombic phases, respectively, are the most stable. Catalytic performance for the acetylene hydrogenation reaction confirms that the hexagonal NiIn 0.5 Sn 0.5 is more catalytically active and selective towards ethylene than the orthorhombic NiIn 0.2 Sn 0.8 . The Nudged Elastic Band calculations reveal a significant difference in the kinetics of the conversion reactions, making the hexagonal phase more selective than the orthorhombic phase. Thus, this study combines both experimental and theoretical approaches to understand the superior catalytic performance of the hexagonal phase over the orthorhombic phase, which mainly originates from differences in the atomic arrangement of the most stable surface, which significantly influences the reaction kinetics of acetylene hydrogenation.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing via Biomedical Knowledge Graph Embedding
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing is the identification of new therapeutic applications for existing or investigational drugs [1]. We implemented a large-scale biocomputational knowledge graph (KG) integrating four public databases: ChEMBL, Open Targets, STRING, and STITCH, yielding 973,266 triples across 189,233 nodes. We train and compare three knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models (TransE, RotatE, ComplEx) and two graph neural networks (GraphSAGE, GAT) on a drug-protein-gene-disease prediction assignment. One key finding is that KGE with ranking loss substantially outperforms GNNs for drug repurposing despite GNNs achieving higher AUC, showcasing that commonly used selection metrics do not necessarily translate to real world drug-repurposing performance. RotatE achieves the best ranking performance (MRR: 0.1995,

papers.title: Drastically reducing the cost of the XsTD-DFT family of methods using a minimal auxiliary basis set (ηXsTD-DFT) to efficiently treat ultra large systems
papers.abstract: To have the most efficient simplified quantum chemistry method to compute excited states and response properties for all-atom quantum mechanical (AQM) methodologies, this contribution introduces the ηXsTD-DFT family of methods for which the exact integral simplified time-dependent density functional theory (XsTD-DFT) is adapted considering the resolution of identity (RI) approximation with a minimal auxiliary basis set. This auxiliary set is composed of 1s orbitals with the square of the atomic chemical hardness η scaled by a global factor θ as parameters into the exponent. This approximation allows a drastic reduction of the computational cost. The θ in the ηXsTD-DFT was globally fitted to reproduce reference excitation energies and oscillator strengths for the 17 first molecules of the XsTD-DFT benchmark set. The method was then tested for the entire set of 77 molecules. For B3LYP, the ηXsTDA scheme only deviates on average by only 0.12 eV with respect to TDA, similarly to the TDA-ris scheme. Surprisingly, MADs with respect to TDA are slightly lower than those for the XsTDA method. For this set, on average, the ηXsTD-DFT is 147 times faster than TDA, outperforming both TDA-ris (32x) and XsTDA (82x) schemes. These results highlight the computational efficiency and robustness of the ηXsTD-DFT and suitability for applications in AQM methodologies. To showcase the performances of the method, three increasingly-large systems were selected: a mixed donor/acceptor ligand Pd(II) double cage (395 atoms), photoactive yellow protein (PYP, 1931 atoms), and bacteriorhodopsin (bR, 3835 atoms). In all cases, striking comparisons with respect to experiment were obtained. For bR, the largest system of this study, oneand two-photon absorption spectra were computed in only 2h25min on a desktop computer using ∼500GB of RAM. The ηXsTD-DFT shows also excellent performance to compute core-valence excitations well reproducing the oxygen K-edge NEXAFS spectrum of collagen. A spin-flip version was also implemented and tested for 9 diradicals and a large µ-hydroxo-bridged dimers of corrole tape Ga(III) complexes derivative.

papers.title: A Dual–mode Sorption Model for Selective Ion Partitioning in Ligand-Functionalized Polymer Membranes
papers.abstract: Ion-selective ligand-functionalized polymer membranes (LFPMs) are promising materials for critical mineral (CM) industrial wastewater refining, but the effect of ligand identity on LFPM selectivity remains poorly described. We developed a dual–mode sorption (DMS) model for cation partitioning to quantitatively describe how ligand identity modulates cation selective partitioning in LFPMs. In this study, we trained a machine learning model to interpolate a sparse aqueous ion–ligand affinity (∆G Ion-Ligand ) literature dataset. We then parameterized LFPM-specific DMS models, modeling (1) hydrated free volume cation absorption a priori using the pore model with ion solvation and (2) cation adsorption at ligand sites with a competitive Langmuir model. We correlate Langmuir-type equilibrium coefficients with ∆G Ion-Ligand using linear free energy relationships. Once parameterized, the DMS model accurately predicts experimental partitioning selectivity for most cation pairs. Ultimately, this study elucidates connections between ∆G Ion-Ligand and LFPM selectivity to accelerate systematic LFPM design efforts for CM wastewater refining.

papers.title: New BODIPY-Based Fluorescent Probes with Selective Sensing of Salts
papers.abstract: This study presents novel BODIPY-based probes for the selective detection of lithium, sodium, and magnesium hexafluorophosphate or antimonate salts, in the presence of other salts. Small cations bind to fluorines of dimethylamino-styryl BODIPY and its monobiotinylated hemicucurbit[8]uril macrocycle derivative causing change in probe electronic properties and conformation as evidenced by DFT calculations. Upon binding with target salts, the probes display a distinct visible color shift from blue to pink and fluorescence emission. These combined responses facilitate both rapid "naked-eye" recognition and fluorescence detection, demonstrating the potential of this macrocyclefunctionalized scaffold for practical electrolyte sensing applications.

papers.title: Biotin[6]uril-zinc tetraphenylporphyrin conjugate: a chiral multiporphyrin receptor with size-recognition properties
papers.abstract: A chiral multiporphyrin receptor was prepared by covalent attachment of six zinc tetraphenylporphyrin units to a biotin[6]uril sulfoxide scaffold through flexible amide-linked side chains. In non-coordinating solvents, the conjugate adopts a propeller-like, C3-symmetric conformation in which three π–π-stacked porphyrin pairs are arranged helically around the chiral macrocyclic core, producing a strong exciton-coupled circular dichroism (CD) response in the Soret region. Addition of methanol as a zinc-coordinating co-solvent disrupts porphyrinporphyrin interactions, sharpens the Soret absorption band, and reversibly quenches the CD signal. Binding studies showed that the receptor forms strong complexes with nitrogen-donor ligands, fullerenes, and hemicucurbituril macrocycles, with affinity governed primarily by the guest size and geometry. The highest affinities were observed for guests of approximately 7–8 Å, consistent with sandwich-type binding between adjacent porphyrin units. Although the receptor preferentially binds C70 over C60, it shows no significant enantiodiscrimination toward the chiral guests studied. Overall, this system represents a conformationally adaptive multiporphyrin receptor with reversible solvent- and guest-dependent UV-Vis and CD responses suitable for sensing coordinative and shape-complementary analytes in sub-micromolar concentration range.

papers.title: Second-Layer Cu Composition Governs ORR Activity on Pt–Cu(111) under Steady-State *OH Coverage
papers.abstract: The performance of Pt-based oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts is governed not only by adsorption energetics but also by the thermodynamic accessibility of near-surface structures and the resulting adsorbate coverage. Here, we combine a density-functional-theory-trained cluster expansion model with semi-grand-canonical and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to resolve the structure–activity relationship on Pt–Cu(111) surfaces for ORR. Equilibrium sampling within the bulk Pt 3 Cu chemical potential window identifies Pt-terminated near-surface phases in which the second-layer Cu composition controls the distribution of local subsurface environments that govern the *OH adsorption energy. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations further show that this subsurface composition controls the steady-state *OH coverage and the resulting specific activity, with a maximum activity of approximately 27.1 times that of Pt/C near the chemical potential difference of 0.41 eV, where the second layer contains 50% Cu. In contrast, in-plane disorder at fixed layer-resolved composition produces only modest activity changes, indicating that it acts primarily by reshaping the distribution of local adsorption environments. These results identify second-layer composition as the primary factor governing ORR activity and provide a transferable framework for linking thermodynamically accessible Pt-skin alloy surfaces under steady-state *OH coverage and activity.

papers.title: Riding toward Selectivity: Optimization of Covalent 7-Azaindole-Based BMX Kinase Inhibitors
papers.abstract: The tyrosine kinase expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (TEC) family comprises five non-receptor tyrosine kinases – BTK, ITK, BMX, TXK, and TEC – with key roles in immune signalling. Although BTK and ITK have been extensively studied, selective inhibitors for TEC, TXK, and BMX remain scarce. Recently, we identified 7-azaindole-based covalent BMX inhibitors with potent inhibitory activity and robust cellular target engagement but limited selectivity across TEC family members, especially BTK. Here, we describe a new generation of BMX inhibitors designed to exploit subtle structural differences between BMX and BTK by incorporating diverse N-acylamino substituents at the azaindole 5-position or variations at the linker and warhead. Our compounds display subnanomolar BMX potency and improved selectivity over BTK and other TEC kinases. Key compound 11i showed strong cellular target engagement, good in vitro metabolic stability, a favourable kinome profile, and rapid covalent inactivation kinetics, positioning it among the best BMX chemical probes currently available.

papers.title: Visible-light cobalt-catalysed synthesis of aroyl amides from arylazo sulfones.
papers.abstract: A strategy combining the unique properties of arylazo sulfones as dyedauxiliary group-bearing substrates for arylation reactions and Co2(CO)8 as a catalyst in carbonylation processes was used to prepare aromatic amides. This versatile method was utilized to create a library of aroyl amides with good to excellent yields.

papers.title: A Formal (4+3) Strain-Release Annulation of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes Enables Access to Azabicyclo[4.1.1]octanes
papers.abstract: Strain-release cycloaddition chemistry of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) has emerged as a powerful platform for the construction of saturated bridged frameworks. Despite remarkable advances in formal (2+2), (3+2), and (4+2) annulation reactions, higher-order annulation manifolds of BCBs remain under explored. Herein, we report the first formal (4+3) strain-release annulation of BCBs with indole-derived Michael acceptors, enabling rapid access to azabicyclo[4.1.1]octane-fused indoles. The transformation proceeds under mild base- mediated conditions through a strain-release ring-opening/cyclization sequence and delivers 37 examples in up to 91% yield with uniformly excellent diastereoselectivity. The method exhibits broad substrate scope and tolerates a wide range of functional groups. Synthetic elaborations highlight the utility of the resulting polycyclic scaffolds, while mechanistic experiments and density functional theory calculations provide insight into the reaction mechanism and pathway selectivity. More broadly, this work establishes a previously unknown higher-order annulation mode in BCB with indole-derived precursors and expands the structural space accessible through strain-release reactivity.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Mapping of Copolymerization Curves and Reactivity Ratios via Gradient Flow Polymerization, Inline ATR-FTIR, and Lasso Regression
NMR and Ultrafast Spectroscopic and Mass Spectrometry Characterisation of a Carotenoid Isolated from Methylorubrum extorquens strains PA1 and AM1
papers.abstract: Methylorubrum species are prominent members of the plant phyllosphere, where they are exposed to fluctuating environmental conditions, including intense ultraviolet (UV) radiation. To mitigate such stressors, these bacteria commonly synthesise carotenoids as an oxidative protection. In this study, we investigated the carotenoid production of two closely related methylotrophic strai ns, Methylorubrum extorquens PA1 and AM1 (short PA1 & AM1), with a particular focus on the influence of iron availability. We identified and comprehensively structurally characterised the main carotenoid produced by both strains by using ultraviolet–visible (UV– Vis ) spectroscopy, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) with collision-induced dissociation (CID), ion mobility–mass spectrometry (IM–MS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and ultrafast transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy. We show that both strains produce, unaffected by the iron availability, the same carotenoid, identified as 4-[2-O-11Z-octadecenoyl-β-D-glucopyranosyl]-4,4′-diapo-Ψ,Ψ-carotene-4,4′-dioate. However, the iron availability strongly influenced the carotenoid production making it a tuneable parameter for boosting bacterial carotenogenis in biotechnological settings.

papers.title: Pathway-Resolved Hierarchical Self-Assembly of Biomimetic Double-Walled Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Self-assembly, the spontaneous organization of molecular components into ordered structures without external intervention, offers a powerful route to complex nanomaterials, yet the molecular-level pathways, particularly under non-equilibrium conditions, remain poorly understood. We track in real time the formation of double-walled nanotubes (DWNTs) from the amphiphilic cyanine dye C8S3, a synthetic analogue of light-harvesting chlorosomes in green sulfur bacteria. Combining microfluidic control with two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy, cryogenic transmission electron microscopy, and polarization-resolved single-object microscopy, we identify transient intermediates at both structural and excitonic levels. The results show that the outer nanotube structures first, while the inner nanotube follows with a delay, ultimately giving rise to electronically coupled coaxial architectures. While principal excitonic and morphological features emerge within minutes of self-assembly, axial elongation and orientational refinement proceed over tens of hours in a nucleation–elongation fashion. Notably, suppressing local concentration gradients through more efficient mixing abolishes DWNT formation, establishing spatial heterogeneity as a key design parameter for hierarchical self-assembly. These findings provide a framework for controlling biomimetic light-harvesting nanomaterials, with implications for directing structural outcomes in advanced materials engineering.

papers.title: Exploring the polarization performance of the polysulfide redox couple in a reference electrode-equipped single electrolyte flow cell
papers.abstract: Flow batteries that employ polysulfide species are often limited by their sluggish redox reaction kinetics. While a number of catalyst/electrode options have been explored to lower activation overpotentials, progress has been challenged by the need to disentangle electrode losses from full cell performance as well as by the breadth of electrode, electrolyte, and operation conditions pursued. Here, we systematically characterize electrode performance for the polysulfide redox reaction as a function of electrode material (carbon, nickel, and nickel-sulfide) and temperature (~25 to 70 °C) using a reference electrode-equipped single-electrolyte flow cell with a set electrolyte composition. Our results highlight asymmetry in the polysulfide redox couple, where the different electrodes perform similarly for the faster oxidation, but distinguish themselves for the slower reduction. Furthermore, elevated temperature benefits both reduction and oxidation rates of polysulfide, with the greatest improvements observed for reductive overpotentials. Nickel(-sulfide) electrodes are found to have superior catalytic performance to carbon-based electrodes, while the efficacy of different carbon electrodes appears to depend on their electrochemically-active surface area and surface chemistry. Our reference-electrode based investigations, complemented with full cell polarization and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, collectively show that the nickel(-sulfide) electrodes are susceptible to sulfidization over time (especially at elevated temperature) positively influencing their catalytic behavior, but negatively affecting cell resistance and mechanical integrity. In contrast, flow cells employing carbon electrodes maintain their kinetic and ohmic characteristics throughout the investigation. Overall, the presented methods are particularly effective for assessing the combined roles of electrode and temperature on kinetically-hindered redox flow cells.

papers.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go? - Leveraging an Overlooked Feature of Click-to-Release Chemistry for Affinity Labeling
papers.abstract: Click-to-release (C2R) chemistry is widely used for controlled payload liberation, yet the chemical reactivity of its transient intermediates has remained largely unexplored. Here we show that an intermediate formed during the reaction of trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-appended protein-targeting ligands with release tetrazines (rTzs), previously regarded as a byproduct rapidly quenched by water, can be viewed from a different perspective and exploited as an electrophile for ligand-directed covalent protein labeling. The bioorthogonally generated dihydropyridazine methide (DHP-methide) enables affinity-directed protein labeling that predominantly results in capture at surface-exposed histidine residues proximal to the site of electrophile generation, revealing a histidine-biased covalent modification pathway. Incorporation of functional handles into the rTz platform enables modular reporter installation via orthogonal bioorthogonal reactions. A fluorogenic leaving group design further allows direct optical reporting of the electrophile-generating elimination event, enabling real-time monitoring of DHP-methide formation during the labeling process. Selective labeling is retained in complex protein mixtures and in spiked lysate experiments and can be translated to a cellular context, as demonstrated by confocal imaging of surface-expressed targets following post-labeling fluorophore installation. These findings reframe a mechanistic intermediate of click-to-release chemistry as a functional electrophile for ligand-directed protein modification and establish a previously unrecognized bioorthogonally gated strategy for affinity labeling.

papers.title: Electrophilic Bicyclobutane Synthons
papers.abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) have emerged as versatile synthetic building blocks for the construction of multifunctionalized cyclobutanes and complex polycyclic frameworks at the core of modern medicinal chemistry. 1,3-Disubstituted BCBs are particularly useful to access highly functionalized building blocks, but access to these substrates is often limited by synthetic methodologies requiring long multi-step sequences. Late-stage modification of the BCB core constitutes an alternative strategy to access chemical diversity. However, this has been limited to the reaction of BCBs as nucleophiles with electrophilic partners. Herein, we report on the design, synthesis, and application of novel hypervalent iodine(III) reagents bearing a BCB motif acting as powerful BCB cation synthons. This unprecedented example of a thermally stable hypervalent iodine reagent bearing a carbon substituent linked to three alkyl groups enabled the first late-stage functionalization of the BCB core with sulfur- and carbon-centered nucleophiles, constituting a fundamentally different disconnection to access these key building blocks.

papers.title: Impact of Mesoporous SBA-15 Morphology on the Performance of Mixed-Matrix Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) Membranes in Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) Ultrafiltration
papers.abstract: This study explores the impact of varying morphologies of mesoporous silica SBA-15 on the performance and structure of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) ultrafiltration (UF) membranes. SBA-15 was synthesized in rod, plate, and spherical shapes and incorporated into PAN membranes at optimal concentrations. Attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared analysis (ATRFTIR) confirmed the successful integration of mesoporous silica SBA-15 on membrane surfaces. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed that rod-shaped SBA-15 membranes had a rougher surface than plate and spherical ones, while field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed a finger-like porous structure in all membranes. Membranes with 0.5 wt.% SBA-15, regardless of shape, exhibited enhanced hydrophilicity and performance. Rod-shaped SBA-15 increased pure water flux (PWF) by 44%, plate-shaped by 27%, and spherical-shaped by 15%. The rod-shaped SBA-15 membranes achieved the highest permeate water flux (238.2 L/m2) and BSA flux (142.2 L/m2) due to their superior hydrophilicity, porosity. Although BSA rejection remained stable, the addition of mesoporous silica SBA-15 significantly enhanced the anti-fouling properties of membranes. Membrane resistance decreased by 25% with rod-shaped SBA-15, 15% with plateshaped SBA-15, and 14% with spherical-shaped SBA-15 compared to pristine membranes. This study illuminates the pivotal role of SBA-15 morphology in enhancing the permeability, and fouling resistance of PAN membranes.

papers.title: Advanced Numerical and Deep Learning Modeling of Two-Phase Natural Circulation Loops
papers.abstract: Natural circulation loops (NCLs) play a crucial role in passive heat removal systems used in high-pressure thermal–hydraulic applications such as nuclear reactor safety systems and advanced chemical process equipment. In these systems, fluid motion is sustained solely by density gradients induced by heat addition and phase change, eliminating the need for mechanical pumps and external power input. Accurate prediction of mass flow rate, phase distribution, and system stability under such conditions remains a challenging task due to the highly coupled, non-linear interaction between thermodynamics and fluid dynamics. This study presents a comprehensive hybrid framework for the steady-state analysis of a high-pressure two-phase natural circulation loop operating at 155 bar. First, a detailed physics-based numerical model is developed using energy conservation, steam quality evaluation, homogeneous flow modeling, and buoyancy-driven momentum balance. The governing equations are solved using a successive substitution iterative scheme with numerical under-relaxation to ensure convergence and stability. The numerical solver successfully predicts the equilibrium mass flow rate and vapor quality, providing physically consistent convergence behavior and serving as a high-fidelity reference solution. Building upon the numerical framework, the study introduces a data-driven surrogate modeling approach based on a deep residual neural network (ResNet). The neural network is trained on datasets generated from the validated numerical solver and is explicitly designed to preserve the physical structure of the momentum balance through residual learning. The ResNet demonstrates excellent predictive accuracy, achieving mass flow predictions with over 99.9% agreement and negligible physics residuals. The proposed hybrid methodology effectively combines the transparency and robustness of physics-based modeling with the computational efficiency of deep learning. This approach enables real-time prediction and monitoring of natural circulation systems while retaining strong physical

papers.title: PyFluent: Bridging Open-Source Python Automation with Proprietary Liquid Handling for AI-Driven Laboratories
papers.abstract: Liquid-handling automation is increasingly central to high-throughput experimentation, closed-loop optimization, and AI-assisted laboratory workflows. Although commercial liquid-handling platforms provide robust hardware capabilities, integration with modern scripting environments, reproducible software practices, and adaptive experimental pipelines often remain limited by proprietary control ecosystems. We present PyFluent, a Python-native interoperability layer for the Tecan Fluent platform that bridges vendor-mediated hardware control with open, scriptable laboratory automation workflows. Rather than replacing FluentControl, PyFluent provides structured interfaces that expose Fluent execution pathways through reusable Python APIs while preserving compatibility with the vendor software stack. PyFluent is organized as a three-layer architecture consisting of a user-facing scripting layer, an execution engine, and the underlying proprietary Fluent control environment. The framework supports two complementary user surfaces: a Fluent-specific direct API pathway that preserves access to Fluent-native command semantics, and a PyLabRobot-compatible backend that enables higher-level, hardware-agnostic workflow development. Both pathways converge through a shared execution controller before dispatch through the FluentControl .NET interface. The execution engine includes XML command generation, optional state tracking, simulation support, and structured command routing designed to improve protocol development, testing, and integration with external software systems. We characterize the dispatch boundary of the Fluent control interface, showing that flexible-channel-arm (FCA) operations can be issued directly through the command channel while multi-channel-arm (MCA) and gripper operations are routed through a vendor-subroutine bridge, and we implement a hybrid execution model that exposes both behind a uniform Python API. Representative workflows including serial dilution, plate-to-plate transfer, and reagent addition, are composed in Python and validated in FluentControl’s simulation environment before hardware execution. PyFluent also supports simulation-first development, enabling protocol validation without requiring active hardware access during early workflow design. By exposing each Fluent operation as a discrete, callable method — usable from notebooks, optimization loops, and tool-calling AI agents — and pairing it with a simulation mode that runs before any hardware is engaged, PyFluent lets autonomous systems generate, validate, and execute protocols within a single Python session. More broadly, it shows how commercial laboratory hardware can become a programmable component of self-driving laboratories rather than an isolated endpoint, without sacrificing vendor-supported execution pathways.

papers.title: Seasonal and spatial BVOC emission variability from native Atlantic Forest trees under contrasting anthropogenic influences in Southeast Brazil
papers.abstract: Biogenic volatile organic compound (BVOC) emissions from vegetation are major precursors of ozone (O₃) and secondary organic aerosols (SOAs), yet their behavior in tropical megacities remains poorly understood. We quantified BVOC emissions from four native Atlantic Forest tree species: Alchornea sidifolia (AS), Casearia sylvestris (CS), Guarea macrophylla (GM), and Machaerium nyctitans (MN), sampled during dry and rainy seasons in two forest remnants of the Metropolitan Area of São Paulo with contrasting anthropogenic influence: Matão-IAG (higher) and RMG (lower). Using dynamic enclosure sampling and TD-GC-MS analysis, we measured emission rates (ERs) and estimated O₃ formation potential (OFP) and SOA potential (SOAP). Species identity was the main factor shaping emission patterns, with sesquiterpenes (SQTs) dominating under all conditions. Four emission strategies emerged. CS showed a high and seasonally variable profile, with the highest ERs, OFP, and SOAP, peaking at RMG during the dry season (11.85, 23.24, and 213.30 µg gDM⁻¹ h⁻¹). AS exhibited moderate and compositionally stable emissions (ER 0.81 to 0.98 µg gDM⁻¹ h⁻¹). GM had moderate and compositionally variable emissions (ER 0.98 to 1.66 µg gDM⁻¹ h⁻¹). MN presented low and compositionally heterogeneous emissions, with a dry-season spike at RMG (ER 2.91 µg gDM⁻¹ h⁻¹). Compound-level analysis revealed potential biomarkers: ledene was associated with the dry season, while 2-ethylhexyl salicylate and β-linalool were linked to urban stress. These findings improve the spatiotemporal characterization of BVOCs in the Atlantic Forest and offer an evidence-based framework for sustainable urban forestry in tropical megacities.

papers.title: Nucleophilic Substitution at Difluoro-Carbene Complexes of the Coinage Metals
papers.abstract: Carbene functionalization through direct substitution at the carbene center is well established for Fischer-type carbene complexes of early transition metals but remains exceedingly rare for carbene complexes of late transition metals. Here, we report a general strategy for carbene functionalization at coinage metals based on nucleophilic substitution of difluorocarbene complexes. Persistent LnAu(I)=CF2+ complexes undergo efficient fluorine-to-nitrogen and fluorine-to-oxygen substitution with nucleophiles, providing direct access to fluoro-amino- and fluoro-oxy-carbene complexes. The methodology is also applicable to transient Au(I) difluorocarbenes and extends to Cu(I) and Ag(I) systems, enabling carbene functionalization across the coinage-metal series. Access to a family of closely related group 11 carbenes (10 examples) enables direct comparison of their structure and bonding. Spectroscopic and computational studies reveal that fluorine-to-nitrogen substitution profoundly impacts the electronic structure of the carbene complex, affording species best described as metallated fluoro-iminium ions. Density functional theory supports a highly exergonic additionelimination mechanism driven by Si–F bond formation and identifies metal-to-carbene π-backdonation as the key factor governing the stability of difluorocarbene intermediates, following the trend Au > Cu > Ag. These findings establish nucleophilic substitution as a versatile platform for carbene functionalization and carbene-to-carbene interconversion at coinage metals.

papers.title: Two-Electron Reduction of B–N Lewis Pair Fused Dipyridyl Anthracene Using Alkali Metals
papers.abstract: Boron–nitrogen (BN) incorporation offers a versatile approach to modulate the electronic structure of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons by combining electron-deficient and electron-rich elements within a single π-framework. In this work, we examine the two-electron reduction of a BN-fused dipyridylanthracene (BDPA, 1 ), providing access to a family of alkali-metal dianion salts, M 2 -1 2– (M = Li, Na, K, and Rb). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals cation-dependent ion-pairing motifs, with solvent-separated ion products for Li and K and contact ion products seen for Na and Rb. Computational analysis shows that product stabilization is governed by partial charge transfer from the reduced BDPA core to the metal centers. Structural analysis further reveals substantial bond-length reorganization and increased curvature of the π-framework upon reduction, consistent with the emergence of quinoidal electronic delocalization. This transformation is accompanied by a pronounced redistribution of aromaticity, involving a loss of aromatic character of the pyridyl groups and the central anthracene ring, and an enhancement of aromaticity in the terminal rings, as supported by HOMA and NICS analyses. A comparison of the electronic structure of the dianion 1 2– with those of isoelectronic dianionic all-carbon ( M1 2– ) and neutral BN-fused N,N-dihydrophenazine ( M2 ) analogs demonstrates much more profound quinoidal character of 1 2– , signifying how the dearomatization and delocalization of charge is effectively supported by ‘B–N for C–C’ substitution. Together, these results demonstrate that two-electron reduction can be exploited to trigger dramatic changes in charge distribution and aromaticity, which directly impact the structural and spectroscopic properties of B–N Lewis pair functionalized PAHs.

papers.title: A solid-state Hull Cell for mapping current-density-dependent lithium deposition
papers.abstract: Lithium (Li) deposition in anode-free solid-state batteries is highly sensitive to current density, yet systematic investigation of current-dependent plating behaviour remains experimentally challenging because conventional cell architectures require large numbers of independent experiments to explore relevant operating conditions. Here we introduce the first solid-state implementation of the classical Hull Cell concept, enabling spatially resolved investigation of Li deposition along a continuous current-density gradient within a single galvanostatic experiment. A trapezoidal Li6.5La3Zr1.5Ta0.5O12 (LLZTO) solid electrolyte generates an approximately one-order-of-magnitude variation in local current density through a continuously varying interelectrode distance. Combining finite-element modelling, electrochemical measurements, plasma focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry, we correlate local current density with Li deposition morphology under different external stack pressure conditions. We show that Li deposition is governed by a coupled electro-chemo-mechanical response rather than by current density alone. Low stack pressures promote current collector (CC) delamination and highly localised Li accumulation, whereas intermediate pressures enable deposition morphologies that directly reflect the imposed current gradient. Higher pressures improve deposition uniformity but introduce distinct mechanically driven failure modes, revealing a finite operating window for stable anode-free cycling. Furthermore, Li initially propagates through the columnar microstructure of the sputtered copper (Cu) CC before accumulating at the Cu|LLZTO interface during prolonged plating, demonstrating that CC microstructure strongly influences Li transport pathways. Our solid-state Hull Cell provides a practical framework for the rational design of operating conditions and CC architecture in anode-free solid-state batteries and offers a highthroughput route toward systematic investigation of failure mechanisms under realistic electrochemical driving forces.

papers.title: Moisture instability in sodium-ion battery cathodes defines storage and closed-loop recycling conditions
papers.abstract: Alluaudite-type sodium iron sulfate, Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3, is a promising low-cost 3.8V cathode material for mass-production sodium-ion batteries. However, its deployment has been constrained by its hygroscopic nature, which complicates manufacturing and storage. Here, we resolve the hydration behaviour of Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3 as a function of water vapour pressure (PH2O) and temperature, identifying the hydration boundary and deliquescence threshold that separate anhydrous, hydrated, and aqueous phase regimes. These boundaries define the stable storage window in which anhydrous Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3 remains stable over extended timescales. Our results further show that Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3 hydration proceeds via discrete crystalline phase transitions rather than continuous degradation, establishing moisture instability as a thermodynamically governed property. By leveraging this behaviour, we demonstrate a method for closed-loop aqueous-based recycling of degraded NFS. This process achieves high recovery (~96.82wt.%) of Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3 with electrochemical performance equivalent to the pristine material across 200 cycles. Life-cycle and technoeconomic assessments indicate recycled Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3 exhibits substantially reduced environmental impact and cost relative to virgin NFS and established battery cathodes, including lead-acid, LiFePO4 (LFP), and Ni-Co-Mn layered oxide (NCM622). These results position Na2.5Fe1.75(SO4)3 as a low-impact, economically favourable cathode material and recast its moisture sensitivity not as a limitation, but as an enabling feature for circular design and aqueous reprocessing of next-generation battery cathode materials.

papers.title: Low-Pressure Hydrogenation of Enoates and Carbonyl Compounds with a Bifunctional Copper(I)/NHC Catalyst
papers.abstract: Reductive transformations with copper(I) hydride complexes driven by dihydrogen (H2) as stoichiometric reducing agent typically suffer from limited scope and practicability due to strongly basic conditions and high H2 pressure required. In this work, we show that catalytic hydrogenations of α,β-unsaturated esters and carbonyl compounds are realized by a copper(I) complex constructed from a bifunctional N-heterocyclic carbene complex bearing a 2-iminopyridine subunit. The highly active catalyst allows for practical catalytic hydrogenations at low H2 pressure, in standard laboratory glassware, reaching balloon pressure. The protocol displays high chemoselectivity as functional groups such as halides, nitro groups, amides and heterocycles are tolerated. Mechanistic experiments including isotope labelling studies are consistent with a proximity-induced proton transfer step facilitated by the bifunctional catalyst.

papers.title: Role of sodium acetate anhydrate in the nucleation of the sodium acetate trihydrate phase-change material
papers.abstract: Sodium acetate trihydrate (SAT) is a widely used phase-change material for thermal energy storage, but its tendency to supercool requires the use of nucleating agents to ensure reliable crystallization during operation. Upon heating, SAT undergoes peritectic decomposition to form a liquid phase and sodium acetate anhydrate (SAA). In this study, the role of SAA in the nucleation of SAT was investigated in detail. Two forms of SAA were compared: SAA-1, obtained by peritectic decomposition of SAT, and SAA-2, produced by thermal dehydration of SAT. Consistent with previous findings, SAA-1 was found to be inactive as a nucleating agent. Surprisingly, SAA-2 promoted reproducible crystallization of SAT over multiple heating–cooling cycles. The nucleation activity of SAA-2 gradually decreased during thermal cycling and was lost rapidly at elevated temperatures. Structural characterization with X-ray diffraction revealed that both SAA materials consist predominantly of the same polymorphs and they also displayed very similar Raman spectra. In contrast, pronounced differences in crystal morphology were observed in optical microscopy. SAA-1 forms large, well-faceted lath-shaped crystals, whereas SAA-2 consists of smaller, irregular crystallites with a high density of surface defects. These results indicate that SAT nucleation is controlled by the crystal morphology and surface structure of SAA, and that dissolution–recrystallization processes gradually convert the active SAA-2 into SAA-1 during thermal cycling, thereby eliminating its ability to nucleate SAT. More generally, the findings demonstrate that the performance of nucleating agents can be governed by the evolution and “healing” of their surface structures during operation, an aspect that should be considered in the design of durable phase-change materials for thermal energy storage.

papers.title: Leveraging the Stochastic Nature of Solid-State Nanopore Sensing for Random Number Generation: A Step Towards Cybersecurity Engineering
authors: Y. M. Nuwan D. Y. Bandara
papers.abstract: Unpredictability and entropy are key factors governing the success of cryptographic security, and true random numbers play a pivotal role in this space. While software-driven random numbers are easy and efficient to generate, their deterministic nature creates a vulnerability that could compromise the gate, barring entry to a sensitive system. Here, we propose using measurement randomness arising from physical and chemical aspects of transport (Layer 1), hardware characteristics (Layer 2), event features and extraction (Layer 3; facilitated by the HyperXtract 2.0), and cryptographic whitening via the secure hash algorithm (SHA-256; Layer 4) to create a high-entropy TRNG system. We demonstrate a host of unique experimental conditions (e.g., electrolyte chemistry, applied voltage, analyte type, transport direction, temperature, and amplifier type) across these four layers to generate ~480,000 256-bit long keys with 100% uniqueness in a Pearson-correlation-based statistical entropy harvesting method and most other methods reporting >99.9% unique keys in most instances. Furthermore, the randomness of these keys was evaluated using the NIST SP800-22b statistical test suite and yielded a success rate of ~99% at a 1% significance level. This study thus showcases the utility of solid-state nanopore sensing for generating high-entropy TRNGs and the potential as a robust, non-deterministic source for nextgeneration cybersecurity engineering.

papers.title: Mechanochemistry unlocks CaCO₃ for organic synthesis and for ¹³C labelling
papers.abstract: Calcium carbonate is an abundant form of inorganic carbon, but its poor solubility and lattice stability have prevented its use as a C1 feedstock in organic synthesis. Here, we show that mechanochemical activation provides a solid-state route to CaCO 3 -derived CO 2 under mild, solvent-free conditions, bypassing the need for calcination or dissolution. This intrinsic CO 2 -releasing reactivity can be coupled directly to epoxide carboxylation, enabling cyclic carbonate synthesis from structurally diverse and functionally rich substrates. The solid nature of the carbonate source provides reagent-defined control over CO 2 delivery, a feature that becomes particularly valuable in carbon isotope labelling. We further show that Ca 13 CO 3 can be used as a stoichiometrically dosed source of labelled CO 2 , enabling isotopeeconomical access to 13 C-labelled cyclic carbonates. More broadly, these findings establish stable inorganic carbonates as practical, reagent-defined C1 reservoirs for organic synthesis.

papers.title: Contact-Free Mechanical Mapping of 3D Microprinted Hydrogels using FLIM
papers.abstract: Mechanical characterization of 3D printed hydrogel microstructures typically relies on invasive, contact-based methods that are challenging to perform in aqueous environments. Here, we present a fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM)-based approach that exploits the intrinsic autofluorescence of two-photon 3D laser-printed hydrogel microstructures to enable label- and contact-free mechanical mapping. Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-based micropillar arrays are fabricated with systematically varied laser doses to modulate the degree of network crosslinking, thereby tuning the material stiffness. FLIM measurements reveal a monotonic increase in the intensity-averaged autofluorescence lifetime with increasing laser dose, reflecting a concomitant increase in stiffness. To quantify the mechanical properties of the 3D printed microstructures in aqueous media, we develop a buoyancy-corrected nanoindentation protocol. The resulting reduced moduli exhibit the same trend and show strong agreement with the fluorescence lifetime measurements. In addition, the autofluorescence signal of the micropillars proved highly sensitive to changes in the hydration state. Thus, these results demonstrate that FLIM is a powerful, non-invasive tool for high-resolution mechanical mapping of soft materials, particularly in conditions where other more conventional methodologies are challenging.

papers.title: Triple Helical Assembly of Atomically Precise Silver Cluster Assembled Material: A p-type Semiconductor
papers.abstract: The construction of helical architectures from achiral building blocks remains a fundamental challenge in supramolecular and materials chemistry. We report the first triple-helical clusterassembled material constructed entirely from achiral components via covalent coordination. Thiolprotected Ag12 nanoclusters are linked by rigid 4,4′-bipyridine ligands to form a three-dimensional framework with a unique triple-helical topology. Structural analysis shows that the helicity arises 2 solely from the spatial arrangement of cluster nodes and linkers, without chiral precursors or templates. The material exhibits p-type semiconducting behavior with a conductivity of ~10-6 S/ cm and hole mobility of ~1.7 cm2 /Vs, highlighting its potential for electronic and optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Galvanostatic Electric-Field-Directed Growth of Oriented ZIF-L Membranes on Non-Conductive Porous Supports
papers.abstract: Controlling crystallographic orientation and interfacial continuity is essential for translating anisotropic MOF nanochannels into predictable membrane transport, yet remains challenging as membrane architecture is largely determined during growth. Electric-field-assisted growth offers a route to actively regulate membrane formation in situ, but has been difficult to implement on non-conductive porous supports. Here, we report a rapid, aqueous, room-temperature galvanostatic growth method, termed electric-field-directed galvanostatic growth and evolution (EDGE), that enables preferentially oriented ZIF-L membrane growth on non-conductive anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) without pre-seeding or thermal activation. By electrically coupling insulating AAO to conductive carbon paper, constant-current operation regulates the evolving interfacial growth conditions and yields membranes with pronounced preferred b-axis orientation. Time-resolved analysis reveals a three-stage evolution of nucleation, orientation, and densification, while a homoepitaxial ZIF-L/ZIF-L sealing step improves intercrystalline continuity without disrupting the preferred orientation. Ion-transport measurements validate the structural consequences of alignment and sealing, showing enhanced directional transport and high conductance. This work extends electrochemical MOF deposition to non-conductive porous supports and provides a controlled route to oriented MOF membranes.

papers.title: JAX-Powered Differentiable Pairwise Relaxation for Fast Geometric Screening of Chiral Carbon Nanotubes, with companion python code.
papers.abstract: This paper presents an easy-to-follow JAX implementation of a pairwise model for unbound (π) electron behaviour in chiral carbon nanotubes. The model uses Minkowskisoftened electrostatic potential together with per-electron orientation (quaternions) and temporal phase, the complete force field is expressed as a single scalar energy function. Automatic differentiation returns exact gradients, enabling fast geometry-driven screening on a laptop. A full open-source Python implementation (Foundry → Engine → Observer pipeline) is provided at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20703585 under GPLv3. Model skeletons and electrons are specified in CML and can be machine generated and human edited. On a 240-electron (12, 4) nanotube the relaxation converges in seconds, and an applied axial field reliably collapses the magnetically phase-locked state in a geometry-dependent manner. Pairwise interactions capture most of what matters for many screening questions, and modern differentiable tools like JAX make building this kind of thing straightforward. The companion code is deliberately minimal and readable. Modern gradient descent solvers like Adam also include a momentum term that mimics damped particle dynamics while converging to a ground state.

papers.title: Field-Aware Energy-Conditioned Message Passing Neural Networks for Absorber-Centred Modelling of X-ray Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Message-passing graph neural networks have emerged as a powerful framework for machine learning in chemistry, owing to their ability to represent molecules and materials as graphs and to learn complex structure–property relationships directly from atomic environments. By iteratively exchanging information between neighbouring atoms, these models capture both local chemical interactions and longer-range structural correlations, enabling accurate prediction of a wide range of molecular and materials properties. Herein, we introduce an absorber-centred graph neural network framework for X-ray spectroscopy that can employ either invariant or E(3)-equivariant message passing, allowing the influence of geometric symmetries on predictive performance to be systematically assessed. Atomic environments are constructed relative to the absorbing atom, providing a physically motivated representation of the local coordination environment. To couple structure and spectroscopy, we incorporate an energy-conditioned attention mechanism that dynamically weights atomic contributions as a function of photon energy, enabling the model to learn energy-dependent structure–spectrum relationships across the absorption edge. An optional field-aware extension further incorporates local charge and spin information, allowing electronic structure effects to contribute directly to the learned representation. The resulting framework yields accurate and transferable predictions across diverse chemical environments and establishes a flexible, symmetry-aware, and energy-resolved approach to machine-learned X-ray spectroscopy.

papers.title: A Charge-Consistent Long-Range Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Compatible with Quantum Linear System Algorithms
papers.abstract: Charge equilibration in machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can be formulated as a linear-system problem, making it a promising target for quantum linear-system algorithms (QLSAs). Accurate charge equilibration is also essential for describing non-covalent interactions and long-range charge transfer. However, conventional electronegativity equalization schemes can retain spurious fractional charges between neutral fragments at large-separations. Here, we incorporate atom-condensed Kohn–Sham density functional theory approximated to second order (ACKS2) into a long-range equivariant neural-network MLIP. Across benchmark systems, the ACKS2based model improves energy and force predictions while reducing atomic-charge errors. At a molecule–metal interface, ACKS2 restores molecular fragments to near-neutral charge states upon separation while preserving local charge redistribution near adsorption. Replacing the classical ACKS2 solver with the Harrow–Hassidim–Lloyd algorithm during inference further demonstrates compatibility with quantum linear-system solvers. These results indicate that ACKS2 provides a promising framework for chargeaware MLIPs and highlight a potential pathway toward atomistic simulations based on QLSAs.

papers.title: Curvature-Driven Facet Divergence from a Single Binary Frumkin Isotherm: A Unified Model for Surfactant-Directed Gold Nanorod Growth
papers.abstract: The mechanism by which a cationic surfactant bilayer directs anisotropic gold nanoparticle growth has remained debated for two decades. We present a binary Frumkin adsorption model in which competitive CTA+/Br- adsorption, coupled with curvature-dependent bilayer blocking and independent Ag+ underpotential deposition (UPD), quantitatively reproduces benchmark anisotropic growth across four surfactants—CTAB, CTAC, BDAC mixed, and NaOL mixed—with aspect-ratio (AR) deviation, using surfactant-specific physical inputs (halide identity, CMC, headgroup geometry) and a minimal set of physically constrained parameters. The model requires no empirical SIDE/END rate factors: facet divergence emerges automatically from the curvature dependence of the Frumkin isotherm, and rod/bipyramid differentiation arises from step-edge percolation physics alone. A Helfrich geometric bilayer shield replaces earlier empirical blocking functions, providing a physical Boltzmann factor for bilayer bending free energy. The deposition rate prefactor unifies all four surfactants from three independently measurable quantities (halide ligand efficiency, CMC-scaled micelle transport capacity, and headgroup binding obstruction), reducing effective fitting degrees of freedom to two (the anchor and the Omega interaction matrix, SI §2.3, S6). The model makes three falsifiable predictions: (i) a V-shaped AR response to [Ag+] with an anti-blocking regime below 0.005 mM, (ii) a kinetic AR peak reaching 8.6 before decaying to the final value—directly observable by in situ time-resolved measurements—and (iii) spontaneous bipyramid emergence from the rod growth equations without a dedicated twin channel. A seed-concentration scaling law () collapses all rod morphologies across all surfactants. All predictions are experimentally accessible to routine lab synthesis.

papers.title: Adaptive Source-Task Expert Routing for Supervised Molecular Pretraining in Low-Data Electrochemical Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical molecular property prediction is a low-data setting in which the downstream labels are scarce, the chemical space can be structurally heterogeneous, and the value of a source-domain representation is strongly conditional on the target task. This manuscript develops a systematic source-task view of supervised molecular pretraining and extends it into an adaptive source-routing framework. QM9 quantumchemical properties are used as supervised source tasks, including HOMO, LUMO, HOMO-LUMO gap, and u0; additional source-library experiments further include dipole moment and polarizability. These source-task-specific GINE encoders are transferred to two downstream electrochemical settings, OxPot oxidation-potential prediction and RedDB reaction-energy-related prediction, under random and scaffold splits and multiple low-data budgets. The first part of the study shows that source-task pretraining is useful but not universal. OxPot tends to benefit from frontier-orbital-related source tasks, whereas RedDB exhibits a more mixed source preference. Negative or negligible transfer occurs under some data sizes and split settings, indicating that fixed source selection is insufficient. The second part introduces AdaSGP-GINE, an adaptive source-gated pretraining framework that treats supervised source-task encoders as an expandable expert library. A sample-level gate assigns source weights, sourcespecific adapters refine transferred representations, and weighted fusion produces the downstream prediction representation. Source-weight analyses, RedDB source ablations, and 4-source versus 6-source expansion experiments support the interpretation that AdaSGP provides taskdependent routing and source-library diagnosis rather than a universal best model. A release package containing cached results, figure data, plotting scripts, audit summaries, and reproducibility documentation was also organized to support transparent downstream use.

papers.title: Decoding the Interplay between Charge Mediated and Hydrophobic Interactions in Poly Electrolytes to Unravel Complex Coacervation
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensate formation or coacervation has come to the fore as an extremely attractive research area over the past few years, as these condensates have been conjectured to be the most primitive sort of protocells. One of the most studied coacervation process is the complex coacervation between polyelectrolytes and oppositely charged small molecules. Among these structures, a very well tested system is the poly-L-Lysine/Adenosine Tri Phosphate (pLL/ATP) coacervate. To understand the condensation process, one needs to unravel the forces which dictate the behaviour of pLL dispersed in water at various temperatures and for various monomer charge fractions which are positively charged. Unlike most simulations which have been performed for biologically relevant proteins, here we have used an included solvent Monte Carlo approach on 10-bead flexible strands as the model pLL molecules, where each bead stands for 3 lysine monomers. We have shown that at high pH, when the positive charges are largely neutralized due to deprotonation of the amine groups in the lysine monomers, the strands show a clear tendency to form bundles of rigid and vertically elongated pLL molecules driven by intermolecular attractions caused by hydrophobic repulsion from the aqueous medium. On switching off the hydrophobic interaction, we see no bundle formation and the screened coulomb repulsions dominate pushing the strands away from each other, underscoring the essential role of hydrophobic interaction in pLL structuration. We see a similar tendency to move away from each other by keeping the charges fixed at high reduced temperatures as well. These results agree nicely with experimental observations of the different phases of pLL, in particular the formation of fibrils at high pH and room temperature. The present study thus breaks new ground by using a simple model involving the interplay of coulomb and hydrophobic interaction to achieve the observed conformations of pLL subjected to various conditions, without considering specific molecular conformations, and opens the way to develop a predictive model of pLL/ATP coacervation.

papers.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly of Antibody Design: A Roadmap for Integrating Co-folding with Absolute Binding Free Energy Calculations
papers.abstract: Computational antibody design offers an appealing alternative to experimental affinity maturation. Mutations, insertions, and deletions frequently induce substantial conformational rearrangements in antibodies, whereas many Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) applications are restricted to relatively small changes between structurally similar molecules. Here, we introduce Tango for biologics, an implicit-solvent absolute binding free energy (ABFE) framework that enables whole-protein alchemical transformations between antibody variants without requiring shared scaffolds or structural similarity. Tango was evaluated on three benchmark antibody–antigen series, using both crystallographic and co-folded structures. On crystal inputs, Tango recovered experimental rank ordering of binding free energies with Spearman correlations (ρ) ranging from 0.39 in charged, polar environments to 0.75 in hydrophobic interfaces. A predictive signal was obtained from high-quality co-folded structures, yielding ρ ranging from 0.43 to 0.58. Further, Tango achieved robust lead prioritization across all benchmark systems, with normalized discounted cumulative gains of 0.60–0.83. Co-folding failures were primarily driven by inaccurate antigen placement rather than monomer folding, even for complexes represented in co-folding training sets. Refinements to co-folding methods partially rescued difficult benchmark systems, enabling the generation of simulation-ready complexes. Together, these results define the conditions under which AI-derived structures are sufficient for rigorous affinity prediction, when only lead prioritization remains reliable, and when current co-folding approaches fail prospectively.

papers.title: Predictive Engineering of Molecular Expression in Polar Multicomponent Matrices: Beyond the Linear Volatility Paradigm in Olfactory Chemistry
papers.abstract: Traditional models of aroma compound volatility, such as Jean Carles's "pyramid" paradigm [1], rely exclusively on the boiling point (Tb) and molecular weight (M) of pure substances. These linear models fail to predict the actual evaporation kinetics of volatile compounds from polar aqueous-alcoholic matrices. This work introduces a method to transition from static forecasting to a dynamic expression system framework based on an empirical similarity criterion: the dimensionless Expression Index (Iex). By replacing computationally heavy quantumchemical parameters with accessible structural markers — the octanol–water partition coefficient (logP), Tb and M — a robust engineering descriptor for evaporation kinetics has been developed. The model was verified against a compound library including custom alkyl thymyl ethers, monoterpenes, and polar aromatic alcohols. The thermodynamic paradox of non-linear expression in olfactory chemistry is mathematically substantiated, demonstrating that heavy (M ≥ 200 g/mol), sterically shielded hydrophobic molecules exhibit top-note evaporation kinetics. This directly refutes the long-standing dogma of a linear dependence of volatility on molecular mass.
