Implementing this approach shifts the design of multicomponent systems from empirical raw-material statics to fluid-phase solution thermodynamics.

papers.title: Electron transfer occurs with multiple rates in strongly coupled sys­tems: An atomistic simulation of the Creutz–Taube ion in solution
papers.abstract: Electron transfer between strongly coupled redox centers has posed several challenges for decades, including the relative time scales of spectroscopic measurements and the electron transfer event itself and the interplay of a mixed-valent solute and its solvation shell regarding the degree of electronic (de-)localisation. Using multi-scale atomistic simulations of the most prominent example of a strongly coupled mixed-valent transition metal complex, the Creutz–Taube ion, (𝜇–pyrazine) [Ru(NH 3 ) 5 ] 2 5+ , we provide an independent perspective on the roles that intramolecular vibrations and solvent motion play on its electronic structure and electron transfer events. To analyze the explicitly solvated system in atomistic detail, we developed a new methodology that yields a spectrum of electron transfer rates as a Fourier transform of the cross-correlation function of the spin populations at the redox centers. Surprisingly, the analysis reveals that multiple electron transfer mechanisms are operative, and that solute vibrations and solvent reorganization act independently to affect electron transfer. The methodology presented herein is general and transferrable to other electron transfer systems.

papers.title: OPENING THE LOOP: COMPOSABLE WORKFLOWS FOR SELF-DRIVING LABORATORIES VIA MULTI-AGENT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING
papers.abstract: Laboratories are open-ended action spaces in which researchers compose experimental workflows from a large set of available procedures, adapting the sequence on a per-sample basis to balance information gain against cost. Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) have demonstrated early success coupling machine learning with automated experimental platforms, but typically operate within fixed closed-loop action sequences that do not replicate the composable, goal-directed nature of real research workflows. Here, a multi-agent framework is introduced that extends this open-ended experimental action space to the SDL. The framework pairs an active learning agent with a reinforcement learning agent capable of dynamically routing samples through a rich set of available experimental procedures. The resulting system exhibits several behaviors absent from conventional SDLs, including dynamic composition of per-sample workflows, the ability to scrap unpromising samples mid workflow, continual learning in which later optimization campaigns benefit from earlier workflow discoveries, and recognition that some experiments are only conditionally informative. The method is evaluated in analytically defined virtual environments designed to isolate three regimes: a single informative surrogate, two complementary surrogates, and four partially informative surrogates whose combined cost exceeds a direct device measurement. Across these benchmarks, the RL-SDL reaches target device performance at lower average cost than a fixed-workflow Bayesian optimization baseline while learning to suppress uninformative measurements and preserve device testing for samples with high expected value or high calibration utility. This work identifies open-ended action spaces as the next frontier in SDL generalization and provides a framework for autonomous experimental design in which the experimental workflow itself becomes a learned output of the optimization.

papers.title: Thermal Activation under Electrochemical Conditions: CO and N2 Bond Dissociation on Co(B5)
papers.abstract: In aqueous electrocatalytic environments, the protonation of stable *CO and *N2 to *COH/*CHO and *NNH is fundamentally challenged by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). In this context, direct dissociation of these molecules offers an alternative pathway, forming reactive *C or *N fragments that can be reduced further if surface bonding is not too strong. However, the strong C≡O and N≡N bonds make dissociation challenging under ambient electrochemical conditions, and the extent to which solvent, local field, and electrolyte ions can promote bond dissociation remains unclear. In this work, we quantify these dissociation path at a Co(B5) step site using density functional theory, implicit-solvent calculations, and explicit-solvent enhanced sampling with a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). Implicitsolvent calculations reveal only weak sensitivity to dielectric constant, dipole moment and solvent radius, with barrier variations typically within ≤ 0.1 eV. In contrast, the local H-bonding network in explicit-solvent simulations lowers the dissociation barrier by ∼ 0.3 eV relative to vacuum by stabilising the dissociating atoms. Across different solvents and aqueous solutes, the barrier correlates qualitatively with hydrogen-bond donor strength, pKa, and the local H-coordination number near the transition-state region. Interfacial cations (Li+ and Cs+) modify the work function but do not significantly change the dissociation barrier compared with pure water, suggesting that solvent-mediated interactions dominate under the studied conditions.

papers.title: Metal-Dependent Thermodynamics of Histidine-Mediated Protein Immobilization Revealed by Quantum Chemical Calculations
papers.abstract: Metal-affinity interactions with proteins are widely used in site-directed enzyme immobilization, yet the thermodynamic factors governing metal-dependent binding remain poorly understood. Here, we combine quantum-mechanical calculations with experimental binding data to analyze imidazole coordination to Ni2+, Co2+, Zn2+ and Fe3+ chelated by IDA-and NTA-functionalized supports. Our quantum calculations reveal that Ni2+, and Co2+ show progressively more favorable coordination-shell formation and immobilization free energies as the number of coordinated imidazoles increases, with Ni2+ consistently more favorable than Co2+. On the other hand, Zn2+ exhibits a distinct preference for two-imidazole coordination, whereas Fe3+ is strongly modulated by hydrolysis, which substantially reduces its effective immobilization strength under neutral-pH conditions. These trends are qualitatively consistent with the experimental affinity order determined in the present work: Ni2+ > Zn2+ > Co2+ > Fe3+. To further connect theory and experiment, we define an apparent binding free energy based on mixed two-and three-imidazole coordination states that qualitatively reproduces the experimentally observed relative affinities. Moreover, QTAIM energy decomposition analysis further shows that the Fe-Imidazole interaction is intrinsically the strongest metal-imidazole interaction, although Fe3+ exhibits the lowest apparent affinity because of competition with hydrolytic species. This behavior fully explains the elution experiments, in which Fe3+-based systems exhibit stronger post-binding retention than the corresponding divalent metal complexes. Overall, the results show that metal-dependent enzyme immobilization can be rationalized by the combined effects of coordination preference, chelator environment, first-shell thermodynamics, and hydrolytic speciation, thereby providing a thermodynamic basis for designing improved metal-affinity supports.

papers.title: Structure-factor-based reweighting of molecular dynamics ensembles for atomic displacement modelling in X-ray diffraction
papers.abstract: Atomic motion in single-crystal X-ray diffraction is conventionally described by isotropic or anisotropic displacement parameters, which approximate the underlying probability density of atomic displacements using analytical functions. In this work, an alternative framework is presented in which atomic motion is represented directly by a weighted ensemble of molecular geometries. Instead of refining displacement parameters, experimental diffraction data are interpreted through ensemble-averaged structure factors calculated from individual static structural realizations. Possible ensembles were generated by molecular dynamics simulations using the GFN2-xTB method. For each frame, static structure factors were calculated at the B3LYP/def2-SVP level of theory. The contribution of individual frames to the experimental diffraction pattern was determined by optimizing individual weights assigned to the structures of the ensemble. The weighting formalism was originally derived within a maximum-entropy framework; however, for the systems investigated, the optimal solutions were obtained without requiring explicit entropy regularization. The resulting weights therefore provide a direct refinement of the ensemble against the diffraction data while retaining the full configurational diversity sampled by the molecular dynamics simulation. The resulting ensemble-averaged structure factors can subsequently be reinterpreted within the framework of Hirshfeld Atom Refinement, enabling a direct comparison between the ensemble representation and conventional crystallographic models. The concept is demonstrated using a 100 K dataset of oxalic acid dihydrate. Furthermore, the approach is applied to 2-mercaptopyridone system previously reported to exhibit anharmonic atomic motion. Because molecular dynamics simulations naturally account for correlated motion, libration, dynamical disorder and anharmonic effects, these phenomena are incorporated without introducing explicit displacement models. The study demonstrates that experimental diffraction data can be interpreted through a physically motivated ensemble representation of atomic motion, while also highlighting that the completeness and quality of the underlying ensemble constitute the fundamental limitation of the approach.

papers.title: AI‐Accelerated Design and Modeling of Organic Electrochemical Energy Materials: From Redox‐Active Molecules to Polymer Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Organic electrochemical energy materials (OEEMs) offer a vast design space for rechargeable batteries, redox‐flow batteries, supercapacitors, and mixed ionic–electronic devices, yet their performance depends on tightly coupled thermal, redox, transport, mechanical, morphological, and interfacial properties that can rarely be optimized independently. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the computational design and modeling of these materials, tracing the field’s shift from small redox‐active molecules towards polymeric electrolytes and electrodes. We cover digital representations and data sources, data‐driven property prediction, machine‐learning interatomic potentials, generative molecular and polymer design, and largelanguage‐model‐assisted (agentic) workflows. It is written for researchers entering the area from either direction, whether computational chemists curious about AI, or machine learning (ML) researchers new to electrochemical materials. Rather than an exhaustive survey, we give a selective snapshot of fast‐moving literature, using representative examples to draw out practical, transferable lessons, and we provide a concise checklist of best practices to help newcomers evaluate and report their own work before publication. We close with our perspective on where the field is heading, together with the persistent challenges of experimental data quality, validation, polymer representation, reproducibility, and modeling integration.

papers.title: High-throughput fabrication of helical microswimmers through micromolding and membrane-assisted release
papers.abstract: Two-photon polymerization (2PP)-based 3D printing enables the fabrication of highly complex structures, including structures that are of interest in microrobotics, such as helical microswimmers. However, the direct fabrication of structures entails long fabrication times, a limited choice of materials, and poor scalability. Although micromolding has been proposed previously, as it promises high-throughput microfabrication, approaches to date have either utilized a single-use mold, which again limits scalability, or they have thus far not shown the efficient molding and release of closed-loop geometries. Here, we present a versatile and scalable micromolding and release strategy for the rapid fabrication of 3D helical microswimmers. By integrating a membrane-assisted mold design, the developed platform enables repeated reuse of PDMS molds while expanding material compatibility. Hybrid inorganic-organic materials (polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS)) and hydrogel biomaterials (alginate (Alg) and gelatin (Gel)) based microswimmers were successfully micromolded by using the introduced method through photocrosslinking and ionic crosslinking strategies. The former allows the realization of hard SiO2 microstructures. Large arrays of 3D helical microswimmers were fabricated within 30 min, compared with the tens of hours typically required for 2PP printing. In addition, a thin-film-assisted lift-off approach was developed for efficient harvesting of molded microswimmers. The fabricated hydrogel microswimmers exhibited favorable biocompatibility. After magnetic functionalization, the microswimmers achieved controlled locomotion under external magnetic fields. This work establishes a scalable and material-flexible platform for high-throughput helical microswimmer fabrication.

papers.title: Unlocking Catalytic Power of Fluxional Non-Heme Copper Center
papers.abstract: Metal centers in enzymes are typically considered to operate within well-defined coordination geometries; however, emerging evidence suggests that dynamic metal behavior could also play a functional role. Herein, we report a structure-informed density functional theory-assisted design of artificial non-heme metalloenzymes that harness controlled metal fluxionality to enhance catalytic performance. Using the cupin scaffold, second-coordination sphere engineering enables dynamic interconversion between two copper coordination modes, CuA and CuB, as directly visualized by atomic-resolution crystallography and supported by electron spin resonance spectroscopy. Catalytic and structural analyses identified CuA as a productive species, whereas access to CuB facilitated product release, thereby mitigating product inhibition. This dynamic mechanism was applied to the hetero-Diels–Alder reaction, affording high yields and enantioselectivities in aqueous media. These findings establish metal fluxionality as a programmable design parameter and introduce a new strategy for controlling reactivity through dynamic metal centers in protein scaffolds.

papers.title: Oridonin Penetrates the Blood-Tumor Barrier to Enable Targeted PROTAC Therapy of Glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most lethal brain tumor, characterized by pathological transformation of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) into the blood-tumor barrier (BTB). Nucleolin (NCL), an oncoprotein aberrantly expressed in GBM cells that shuttles between the nucleus, cytoplasm, and cell membrane, has been reported to be transferred to the surface of brain endothelial cells via extracellular vesicles (EVs), driving BTB formation and representing a potential gateway for GBM-targeted therapy. Here, we demonstrate that oridonin (Ori), a natural NCL ligand, selectively crosses the BTB by engaging GBM EV-derived NCL on the BTB endothelium, enabling GBM-specific targeting. We previously showed that Ori, when incorporated into PROTACs, recruits the E3 ligase MDM2 via employing NCL as a molecular bridge, triggering proteasomal degradation of target proteins. Building on these findings, we developed NCL-bridged PROTACs targeting the oncogenic VEGFR2 by conjugating Ori with Cediranib. Structure-activity relationship studies identified Ori-Ced-2 as the most potent VEGFR2 degrader. Mechanistic investigations revealed that Ori-Ced-2 recruits the NCL-MDM2 complex to VEGFR2, promoting its proteasomal degradation. Ori-Ced-2 exhibits anti-tumor activity in orthotopic GBM models with minimal toxicity to normal tissues. Collectively, our findings establish Ori as a BTB-penetrating and GBM-targeting moiety and demonstrate Ori-based PROTACs as a promising strategy for GBM therapy.

papers.title: Archaeoglobus fulgidus CbiXS is a promiscuous chelatase with a broad substrate scope
papers.abstract: Organisms biosynthesize square planar metal tetrapyrrole cofactors containing Mg, Fe, Co, and Ni using chelatase enzymes, which selectively insert the correct metal into a specific organic ligand. Archaeoglobus fulgidus CbiX S has been proposed to be an “ancestral” chelatase enzyme; in this work we have evaluated its substrate scope to ascertain whether this enzyme is a promising starting point for synthetic chelatase design. Size-exclusion chromatography revealed that CbiX S is a tetramer in solution regardless of the metalation state of the enzyme, in contrast to the dimeric structure of the nickel chelatase CfbA. Reaction conditions that minimize enzyme-free metal insertion into tetrapyrroles were determined, which revealed that many of the in vitro activity assays reported in the literature for chelatase enzymes may be plagued by non-enzymatic metal insertion. Under these conditions that minimize uncatalyzed metal insertion, CbiX S was observed to catalyze metal insertion for six different combinations of metal and tetrapyrrole. Based upon the turnover numbers of these reactions, CbiX S is most effective at catalyzing metal insertion for reactants similar to its native substrates: cobalt and sirohydrochlorin. Kinetic analysis for reactions with varying substrate concentrations revealed that CbiX S may be substrate-inhibited for non-native substrates. In addition, the kinetic data identifies metal–ligand bond formation as the rate-limiting step of the enzyme. Due to its broad substrate scope, CbiX S is an encouraging starting point for synthetic chelatase design that could yield non-natural metal tetrapyrroles for use in the biotechnology sector.

papers.title: Role of Vitamin C in Lowering Stress Hormone Levels in Diabetic Patients: A Nine-Day Human Clinical Observation
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetes mellitus drives chronic HPA axis overactivation, elevating cortisol and worsening glycaemic control. Hyperglycaemia simultaneously depletes vitamin C through competitive transporter inhibition, accelerated oxidative consumption, and enhanced renal excretion. Objective: To assess the dose-dependent effect of oral vitamin C supplementation on serum cortisol, blood glucose, and malondialdehyde (MDA) in a Type 2 diabetic patient. Methods: A nine-day single-subject observational study (31 Jan – 9 Feb 2026). A middle-aged female T2DM patient received 0 mg/day (T0), 250 mg/day (T1), and 500 mg/day (T2) oral vitamin C. Cortisol measured by ECLIA; glucose by automated fluoride-plasma method; MDA by TBARS at 532 nm. Results: Cortisol normalised from 239 ng/mL (HIGH) to 9.4 mg/dL (T1) and 7.2 mg/dL (T2). Blood glucose fell 20.2% overall (352.9 → 281.6 mg/dL). MDA declined 15.8% from T1 (0.76) to T2 (0.64 nmol/mL). Conclusion: Oral vitamin C produced dose-dependent normalization of cortisol, progressive glycaemic improvement, and suppression of lipid peroxidation — consistent with its role as a stress-modulating molecule at the intersection of the HPA axis, glucose metabolism, and antioxidant defence.

papers.title: Ion Transport Enhancement in Charge-Regulating Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding how charge regulation influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of ion selfdiffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this non-monotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by up to an order of magnitude for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism, which provides an additional pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerates ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ionconducting hydrogels and suggest new strategies for membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.

papers.title: A comparative optoelectronic study of double carbonyl/amine multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters fused with different aromatic cores
papers.abstract: Carbonyl/nitrogen-doped polycyclic aromatic frameworks have emerged as an important subclass of multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters. While many studies have explored substituent decoration about a central MR-TADF core such as DiKTa, as well as the effect of fusing the DiKTa core with different aromatic moieties, the influence of a central fused aromatic core remains unexplored. In this work, we address this knowledge gap by fusing two DiKTa units with different aromatic cores, namely carbazole, naphthalene, and toluene, to afford DiKTa-Cz-DiKTa, DiKTa-Nap-DiKTa, and DiKTa-Tol-DiKTa, respectively. Through a systematic comparison, we elucidate how the nature of the central aromatic unit governs the electronic structure, excited-state energetics, and photophysical characteristics of DiKTa-based MR-TADF emitters. Compared to the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum of the parent emitter, DiKTa (λPL = 451 nm) in toluene, DiKTa-Tol-DiKTa (λPL = 457 nm), DiKTa-Cz-DiKTa (λPL = 479 nm) and DiKTa-Nap-DiKTa (λPL = 494 nm) are all red-shifted. Carbazole fusion results in a broadened emission profile (FWHM = 42 nm), whereas naphthalene fusion leads to significantly narrowed emission

papers.title: Diversity-Oriented Two-step Annulative π-Extension Enables Access to Structurally Complex Nanographenes
papers.abstract: The development of general strategy for accessing structurally diverse nanographenes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) remains a central challenge in synthetic chemistry. Although annulative π-extension (APEX) enables the direct construction of fused aromatic systems from unfunctionalized PAHs, its structural scope has been largely constrained by the limited diversity of applicable π-extending reagents. Herein, we report on a diversity-oriented two-step APEX strategy that overcomes this limitation through the use of structurally diverse naphthalene-based aryltrimethylsilanes in Pd/o-chloranil-catalyzed C–H arylation, followed by oxidative cyclodehydrogenation. This approach enables the introduction of sterically congested polyaryl motifs and provides access to nanographenes with eight to ten fused rings and diverse ring-fusion patterns. Notably, a negatively curved nanographene containing five-, six-, and seven-membered rings was synthesized and fully characterized by X-ray crystallography, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations, highlighting the capability of this approach to access challenging nanographene architectures. This work establishes a general platform for diversity-oriented APEX synthesis, thereby redefining the scope and synthetic potential of APEX chemistry.

papers.title: Design and Development of Polysulfone/Clay Anion Exchange Membranes for Electrolysis
papers.abstract: The shift to sustainable hydrogen production has increased interest in electrolysis technologies that can use cheaper materials and rely less on critical raw resources. Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) has emerged as a promising method. It combines the benefits of alkaline operation with the compact design and high-current-density potential of membrane-based systems. However, the widespread use of AEMWE is still limited by the lack of membranes that can provide high hydroxide ion conductivity, mechanical strength, dimensional stability and long-term resistance in alkaline conditions. In this context, polysulfone (PSU) materials have gained attention because of their excellent thermal stability, mechanical strength, and ability to form membrane structures. This study looks at pristine PSU, clay-reinforced PSU nanocomposites, quaternized polysulfone (qPSU) and chloromethylated polysulfone (CMPSU) as relevant material systems for anion exchange membranes. It emphasises how chemical treatment and inorganic fillers affect membrane structure and key performance factors such as hydroxide ion transport, water absorption, swelling behaviour, mechanical strength and durability in alkaline conditions. Pristine PSU provides a stable structure but does not conduct ions well, while qPSU and CMPSU add ionic groups that improve anion transport. Clay-based PSU nanocomposites also help reinforce the membrane and control its microstructure, impacting both transport behaviour and stability. Understanding these material types is crucial for determining the relationships between structure and properties, guiding the development of effective PSU-based membranes for AEM water electrolysis.

papers.title: Standard addition-guided correction of charcoal-stripped serum noncommutability in 13C isotope-dilution LC-MS/MS quantification of endogenous serum folates
papers.abstract: Charcoal-stripped serum (CSS) is widely used as a surrogate blank matrix for LC-MS/MS quantification of endogenous serum analytes when true analyte-free serum is unavailable. However, the commutability of CSS with native serum is often assumed rather than experimentally verified. In this study, endogenous serum folate vitamers were used as a clinically relevant model system to evaluate whether CSS-based calibration remains commutable with native serum under 13C isotope-dilution LC-MS/MS conditions and to develop a practical correction approach when noncommutability is present. A rapid LC-MS/MS assay was developed for 5methyltetrahydrofolate (5-mTHF), folic acid (FA), and folinic acid. The assay achieved LODs of 0.009 ng/mL for 5-mTHF and folinic acid and 0.0375 ng/mL for FA, with LOQs of 0.059 ng/mL for 5-mTHF and folinic acid and 0.117 ng/mL for FA, linearity from 0.059 to 60 ng/mL (R2 > 0.995), recoveries of 93% to 96%, and intra-day and inter-day imprecision below 15%. Post-extraction spiking and pooled-serum standard addition showed analyte-dependent and batch-dependent noncommutability between CSS and native serum. Standard-addition slope comparison revealed matrix factors of 1.005 to 1.611 for 5-mTHF, 0.607 to 1.000 for FA, and 0.902 to 1.008 for folinic acid, corresponding to ion enhancement for 5-mTHF, ion suppression for FA, and minimal matrix bias for folinic acid. A pooled-serum, batch-specific matrix-factor correction reduced validation bias for 5-mTHF and FA to within the commonly accepted ±15% criterion. When applied to 66 pediatric clinical serum samples, matrix-factor correction changed classification relative to selected reference decision limits in 10 of 35 patients for 5-mTHF and 5 of 35 patients for FA. Exploratory LC-MS/MS analysis further indicated the presence of co-eluting lipid-related compounds in native serum extracts, supporting residual matrix composition as a plausible contributor to the observed bias. These findings demonstrate that CSS-based calibration can produce clinically relevant matrix-dependent bias in endogenous LC-MS/MS assays despite 13C internal-standard correction. Pooled-serum standard addition provides a regulatory-compatible and sample-sparing approach to quantify and correct this bias without requiring standard addition in every clinical specimen.

papers.title: Can the photoinduced electron transfer in GluER photoenzymes occur through a triplet state?
papers.abstract: Flavin-dependent ’ene’-reductases (ERED) do not naturally rely on light to function. However, EREDs can be repurposed as photoredox catalysts. How light-driven charge transfer (CT) leads to subsequent chemistry remains unclear, particularly regarding the spin dependency of the CT process. Here we computationally investigate whether the CT process is through an intersystem crossing (ISC). We considered four ERED variants and conducted multiscale multireference minimum-energy crossing point (MECP) calculations based on compressed-state multistate pair-density functional theory. We located MECPs between the singlet and triplet manifolds originating from the π → π ∗ excitation on the flavin. The triplet biradical retains π → π ∗ character, which according to El-Sayed’s rule implies that ISC is not kinetically favored. None of the variants show much CT character in the triplet state, suggesting that the pathway to produce the CT state is not likely to be spin dependent and is likely through internal conversion.

papers.title: Homoleptic uranium arenocenes: A new class of actinide sandwich compounds
papers.abstract: Metal-arene sandwich complexes are foundational to organometallic chemistry, yet analogous compounds of the f-elements remain rare, especially for the actinides. This scarcity has limited efforts to understand how this iconic metal-arene bonding motif changes when extended to actinide elements, where metal-carbon bonding, charge transfer, and ligand redox behaviour may depart from established d-block patterns. Here we report the first homoleptic tris(arenide) arenocenes of the felements, together with a related heteroleptic uranium arenocene, establishing a new class of actinide sandwich compounds supported by formally dianionic arene ligands. Crystallographic, spectroscopic, magnetic, X-ray absorption, and multireference computational analyses support their formulation as tetravalent uranium centres engaged in appreciable arene-to-uranium π-bonding interactions across varying coordination modes. The overall metal contribution to bonding decreases as the arene πsystem expands, while 5f-orbital participation becomes more pronounced in complexes bearing larger arene ligands. Direct comparison with the structurally related d-block complex [Hf(η4-C10H8)3]2− reveals greater orbital participation in the uranium system, providing comparative measure for 5f engagement in metal-arene interactions and establishing a new platform for investigating actinide valence orbital contributions to bonding.

papers.title: Excited state QM/MM simulations of far red fluorescent proteins show diverging electronic and physical structure correlated with red shifts
papers.abstract: Fluorescence is a powerful tool in molecular biology and biotechnology to detect and probe molecules and chemical reactions. Far-red fluorescent proteins (~600 nm emission) are of particular interest because they enable deep-tissue and whole-body imaging with minimal background interference. However, designing near-IR RFPs remains a particular challenge due to the unclear relationship between protein structure, function, and emissive behavior. Large Stokes shifts and near-IR (~650 nm emission) are often associated with substantially lowered brightness and fluorescence quantum yields (FQYs), which is not ideal for imaging applications. Our work focuses on unraveling key structural and electronic determinants responsible for specific red-shifts for protein constructs with the red MYG chromophore, specifically to find features necessary for large red shifts and their relationship to eventual FQY. We applied both classical molecular dynamics and state-averaged α-complete active space self-consistent field (SA-α-CASSCF (4,5), α = 0.64) quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM), validated with CASPT2, to uncover detailed structure/wavelength relationships for the series TagRFP, mKate, and Tag675RFP, which vary in emission wavelength from 580-675 nm and in FQY from 8-48%. We find that in addition to hydrogen bonding interactions and water organization, the chromophore’s ability to access pretwisted conformations can alter the overall distribution of emission energies and shift emission further into the red, which also has the effect of lowering FQY. We additionally find that specific changes in orbital character can be responsible for varying levels of π conjugation on the excited state, shifting wavelengths accordingly. This work opens an avenue for the design of far-red proteins by combining control of chromophore planarity, rigidity, and excited state character.

papers.title: Tailoring Liquid Crystalline Self-Assembly and Photophysical Properties of Unsymmetrical Fluorenones via Polar Terminal Groups
papers.abstract: In this work a series of novel unsymmetrical fluorenone derivatives bearing various head groups (H, Br, NO 2 , NH 2 , CN) was synthesized and investigated with respect to their mesomorphicand photophysical properties. Depending on the headgroup SmA, N or SmC phases with phase widths of up to 145 K were observed, except for the NH 2 -substituted derivative. All mesomorphic derivatives exhibited bright yellow to orange fluorescence in the solid state and solution with quantum yields of up to 35 %. Notably, the nitrile derivative showed thermally induced color and emission color shift from yellow to orange, which was not reversible upon cooling to room temperature. These results revealed that the mesomorphic- and photophysical properties of the examined fluorenone derivates are strongly dependent on the headgroup and in the latter case can be significantly influenced by the presence and nature of solvent or temperature.

papers.title: Controlled Growth and Tailorable Functionalization of Two-Dimensional Supramolecular Films
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) supramolecular materials have gained increasing attention due to their intrinsic dynamic and adaptive features, yet intractable growth process and functionalization severely impede their further advances. Here, we report a reaction-mediated modular and interfacial self-assembly strategy that enables both controlled growth and tailorable functionalization of layer-stacked 2D supramolecular films. The self-assembling monomers are generated in situ from water-soluble trishydrazide and boronic acid-containing aldehydes through the formation of hydrazone bonds. Directed by hydrophobic interactions, these hydrazone-based monomers self-assemble at hydrophilichydrophobic interfaces, giving rise to 2D supramolecular polymers (2DSPs) stabilized by in-plane hydrogen bonding between boronic acid groups. Over time, free-standing supramolecular films comprising multilayer 2DSPs are formed, with their growth rate dictated by the kinetics of hydrazone formation. Moreover, films with varying thickness can be grown on diverse substrates, producing tunable structural colors. Importantly, because of the modularity of our self-assembly system, various chemical moieties can be readily incorporated into the films by using different aldehyde-decorated modules, enabling the resultant films with tailorable chemical functionalities without perturbing the self-assembly behavior. Furthermore, by virtue of a sequential growth of distinct functional layers, supramolecular films with layer-resolved chemical properties are created. Such a reaction-mediated modular and interfacial self-assembly strategy may boost the development of sophisticated 2D supramolecular materials with defined dimensions and enhanced functionalities.

papers.title: Universal Solid Support Compatibility with Amino-Modified Oligonucleotide Synthesis
papers.abstract: Amino-functionalized nucleic acids constitute a fundamental class of chemical handles with widespread utility in chemical biology, biotechnology, and studies of the origins of life. Here, we report an efficient, simple and automated methodology for the installation of 3′-amino modifications in DNA and RNA. Our approach utilizes commercially available UnyLinker solid support, which is converted into a mixed N-hydroxysuccinimide carbonate, allowing robust coupling with both nucleosidic and non-nucleosidic amines. Subsequent oligonucleotide synthesis and purification are streamlined by using standard solid-phase synthesis protocols and conventional purification methods. Computational mechanistic studies suggest that the unexpected cleavage pathway proceeds through a decarboxylative E2 elimination mechanism. This versatile methodology provides a general platform for the synthesis of amino-functionalized nucleic acids, enabling diverse applications in nucleic acid chemistry, chemical biology, and biotechnology.

papers.title: Access to 2H-Pyrrole-Based Skeletons via Cu-Catalyzed Asymmetric Alkylation of Ketoimino Ester
papers.abstract: The cross-coupling of alkyl halides with nucleophiles to construct chiral quaternary carbon centers represents a powerful strategy in the synthesis of three-dimensional molecular frameworks. Herein, we report a copper‑catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of ketoimino esters via in situ generation of chiral copper enolate intermediates, enabling efficient access to 2H-pyrrole derivatives bearing a chiral quaternary center. A catalyst system composed of Cu/(R,Rp)-phosferrox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation, furnishing chiral tetrasubstituted carbon stereocenters with excellent enantioselectivity. A variety of ketoimino esters and alkyl halides are nicely tolerated, allowing the rapid synthesis of enantioenriched 2H-pyrrole derivatives from readily available starting materials. The synthetic utility is further underscored by the antibacterial activity of several products against plant pathogens. Mechanistic studies reveal the potential dual pathways (SN2 substitution versus a latent radical pathway), providing new insights into the reaction mechanism.

papers.title: Porous Peptide Frameworks with Tertiary Structures
papers.abstract: Complex functions such as selective molecular recognition and catalysis arise from the precise three-dimensional arrangement of functional groups that are best exemplified in the protein tertiary structure. Reproducing this level of structural precision and chemical modularity in abiotic materials remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we show that peptide self-assembly into porous crystalline frameworks can result in tuneable tertiary structures composed of helix, loop, and β-strand motifs within a single chain that is only 15–19 amino acids in length, which is less than 6% the size of the average protein. These peptide frameworks were designed by hybridising a framework-forming 11-residue α-helix with variable sequence fragments, yielding extended lattices with channels lined by 8–10 distinct side chains, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD). As a proof-of-principle, these pores can be programmed to encode various constellations of functional groups capable of selective molecular recognition, including near quantitative discrimination of ATP over ADP and chain-length-dependent recognition of perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart programmable, protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.

papers.title: Probing the Quantum Nature of Intramolecular Vibrational Energy Redistribution in HCCH - H2CC Isomerization Using High-Resolution Photoelectron Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: High resolution photoelectron spectra of vinylidene anions (H 2 CC¯ and D 2 CC¯) are reported using variations on slow electron velocity-map imaging of cryogenically cooled anions (cryo-SEVI). This work builds on previous studies aimed at exploring the coupling between neutral H 2 CC and HCCH isomers. One-photon photodetachment (PD) spectra with improved cooling and signal levels probe very weak transitions to vibrational levels of H 2 CC in which the v 6 rocking mode is excited; this is the vibrational mode most strongly coupled to isomerization. In addition, vibrationally resonant two-photon detachment (VR2PD) experiments are carried out that probe PD from vibrationally excited anion levels to the same neutral v 6 states and other low-lying vibrational levels of neutral vinylidene. The experimental spectra show a clear boundary in spectral complexity near the predicted barrier height for H 2 CC->HCCH isomerization, indicating that vinylidene and acetylene states above the barrier are strongly mixed whereas states below the barrier are largely localized in their respective wells. This mixing is, however, largely absent in the cryo-SEVI spectra of D 2 CC¯. Comparison with quantum dynamics calculations based on an accurate full dimensional potential energy surface provides insight into the connection between the H 2 CC-HCCH isomerization reaction and the vibrational structure of vinylidene, revealing pathways of intramolecular vibrational energy flow in the quantum state space of this prototypical system.

papers.title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled with Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
papers.abstract: Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low‑emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H 2 O 2 production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural-decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces metal-free aqueous H 2 O 2 at concentrations above 1 g L -1 with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on‑site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water-treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H 2 O 2 .

papers.title: Toward a Low-Energy Direct-Air Capture Cycle by Reversible Proton-Intercalation Mediated Alkalization
papers.abstract: Mitigation strategies to avoid climate change impacts rely on direct air capture (DAC) of CO 2 . We demonstrate absorption of CO 2 at 400 ppm, and its desorption, by using solid proton-intercalation electrodes to swing the pH of an alkaline electrolyte. 1.76±0.16 GJ tonne -1 of electrical energy is used when enriching CO 2 two-fold, extrapolating to 25.3±0.16 GJ tonne -1 to include water condensation and compression energy. Twenty-fold enrichment requires 5.81±2.42 GJ tonne -1 of electrical energy, extrapolating to 7.81±2.42 GJ tonne -1 . Here, symmetric potassium-stabilized alpha-phase manganese dioxide electrodes are used to (de)intercalate protons from two separate electrolyte streams, thereby swinging dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) solubility in an asynchronous cycle wherein electrochemical steps occur in sequence with CO 2 transfer steps. Mixing among aqueous streams is shown by theory to reduce CO 2 transfer, where the retention of DIC concentration during alkalizing/dealkalizing steps is affected by mixing more so than alkali-ion concentration swing. Energy use further reduces by pre-mixing post-absorption and post-desorption electrolytes. Theory predicts that alkali-ion concentration swing increases with increasing electrode specific capacity and decreasing mixing volume, motivating the co-design of active materials and their electrode microstructures to enhance efficiency, productivity, and enrichment. The present DAC cycle may also be implemented using other electrochemical architectures.

papers.title: Selective Growth of (6,5)- and (9,8)- Enriched Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: The chirality-controlled growth of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) is important for the application of SWCNTs in high performance semiconductor devices. In this work, the chirality-selective growth of (6,5) and (9,8) SWCNTs was achieved in bulk phase, using cobalt-sulfur catalyst precursor system with MgO as the catalyst support. Under the optimal condition, characterized by UV-visible- near infrared absorption spectrum, SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) accounted for 28% and 30% of the total, respectively. TEM characterizations showed bimodal diameter distribution of the as-grown SWCNTs, which is consistent with the absorption spectrum. Due to the significant difference of tube diameter, SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) could be separated in aqueous two-phase system to obtain (9,8)-enriched SWCNT dispersion. Catalyst preparation condition, reduction temperature, growth temperature and carbon source affected the chirality distribution of the as-grown SWCNTs. We proposed that under the optimal condition, the diameter distribution of Co clusters presented bimodal distribution. In addition, the growth kinetics of (n,n-1)-SWCNTs is favorable against other chiralities. Therefore, the selective growth of SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) may be ascribed to the dual diameter distribution of Co nanoparticles and the higher growth rates of (n,n-1)-SWCNTs. This work shows the possibility to realize the chirality-selective growth of more than one chiralities whose diameters are different significantly.

papers.title: Real-Time Monitoring of Bulk Photopolymerization Reactions Using In Situ NMR
papers.abstract: A thorough understanding of photopolymerization reaction kinetics is paramount to enable the targeted control of material and curing properties of photopolymer systems. Recently, in situ NMR techniques have been developed to enable the investigation of complex bulk photopolymerization reactions difficult to monitor using conventional techniques. However, both lengthy acquisition parameters as well as the need for thermal equilibration periods have limited this method to discrete as opposed to real-time monitoring. In this work, instrumental parameters were systematically adjusted to examine their effects on experimental results and thereby maximize data acquisition speeds. While both the number of scans and recycle delay could be readily minimized to expedite data collection, excessive reduction in the acquisition time resulted in signal saturation and photo-chemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization (CIDNP), leading to peak amplification upon light exposure. Thus, optimizing instrumental parameters allowed for the real-time monitoring of a basic hexyl acylate photopolymerization showing exceptional reproducibility and sensitivity to subtle changes in reaction conditions including light intensity and film thickness. Additionally, application of the technique to a thermoset cure demonstrated the ability to monitor even rapid photopolymer reactions in real time. Coupled with the molecular specificity and high signal resolution inherent to NMR, the ability to rapidly and continuously collect data throughout the polymerization makes in situ NMR a powerful tool for the monitoring of complex bulk photopolymerization reaction kinetics in real time.

papers.title: A Dual–mode Sorption Model for Selective Ion Partitioning in Ligand-Functionalized Polymer Membranes
papers.abstract: Ion-selective ligand-functionalized polymer membranes (LFPMs) are promising materials for critical mineral (CM) industrial wastewater refining, but the effect of ligand identity on LFPM selectivity remains poorly described. We developed a dual–mode sorption (DMS) model for cation partitioning to quantitatively describe how ligand identity modulates cation selective partitioning in LFPMs. In this study, we trained a machine learning model to interpolate a sparse aqueous ion–ligand affinity (∆G Ion-Ligand ) literature dataset. We then parameterized LFPM-specific DMS models, modeling (1) hydrated free volume cation absorption a priori using the pore model with ion solvation and (2) cation adsorption at ligand sites with a competitive Langmuir model. We correlate Langmuir-type equilibrium coefficients with ∆G Ion-Ligand using linear free energy relationships. Once parameterized, the DMS model accurately predicts experimental partitioning selectivity for most cation pairs. Ultimately, this study elucidates connections between and LFPM selectivity to accelerate systematic LFPM design efforts for CM wastewater refining.

papers.title: Asymmetric duplex unzipping via truncation of surface-bound nucleic acids
papers.abstract: DNA microarrays are a powerful and versatile platform to perform the massively parallel synthesis and study of highly complex nucleic acid sequence libraries. Photolithography in particular outputs a very high number of essentially any type of nucleic acid oligomers, and hybridization with appropriate complementary probes tagged with a fluorescence label are standard assays performed on microarrays. The thermodynamics parameters involved in microarray hybridization have received a lot of theoretical and practical consideration but they remain difficult to predict based on classical descriptors such as T m or ΔG. In this study, we uncover some form of asymmetry when “unzipping” oligonucleotides duplexes using partially truncated surface-bound strands, and this asymmetry largely depends on the unzipping direction: we find that on average, truncations from the surface-bound 3ʹ-end cause greater destabilization than truncations from the solvent-facing 5ʹ-end. Beyond asymmetry, we identify consecutive GC tracts as responsible for significant drops in duplex affinity that deviate from Tm predictions. This dataset suggests that covalent tethering can also be used to control and manipulate duplex affinity on surfaces.

papers.title: The Disagreement Law: A Covariance Decomposition of Architectural Disagreement in Molecular Property Prediction and When It Fails
papers.abstract: The absolute predictive disagreement D(m) = |pred_A - pred_B| between two graph neural networks with different inductive biases is a strong empirical estimator of prediction error in molecular property prediction, outperforming Monte Carlo Dropout and deep ensembles on scaffold-split data (Merlini and Merlini, 2026). This paper asks why. Working in a controlled system where the ground-truth function f* is known, we show that disagreement obeys an exact decomposition, E[D^2] = MSE_A + MSE_B - 2E[e_A e_B], where e_X = pred_X - f* is the signed error of each model. The entire out-of-distribution (OOD) behaviour of the signal - including the documented failure of single-architecture uncertainty methods - is governed by the error-covariance term. We verify the identity to machine precision, recover it from data without supervision using symbolic regression (loss 6 x 10^-14, a 13-order-of-magnitude drop over simpler forms), and map its failure region: when the two models share an inductive bias (rho_AB approaches 1) the signal collapses, exactly as the decomposition predicts. We then confirm the identity on real chemistry by reloading published GIN+EGNN checkpoints on four kinase targets (EGFR, VEGFR2, JAK2, BRAF). Finally, we show that a single scalar derived from the law - the inter-architecture error correlation rho_AB - predicts the rank ordering of disagreement utility across the four targets (Spearman = -0.62, p = 0.013, across six protein families). This converts an empirical observation ("BRAF yields the strongest signal") into a quantity that can be estimated a priori, and yields a concrete design rule: the second model should be chosen for bias orthogonality, not accuracy. We are explicit about scope: the identity itself is elementary algebra; the scientific content is its interpretation and the decorrelation principle, the latter established here across 15 targets and six protein families (n = 15, Spearman = -0.62, p = 0.013).

papers.title: Detecting and isolating flare plumes from upstream oil and gas sites using aircraft sampling
papers.abstract: Aircraft flights have been used in multiple studies to attempt to isolate and measure the compositions of flare plumes. In this work, flare plumes from oil and gas facilities in the Permian Basin of west Texas were simulated, in combination with other plumes from the facilities, to predict concentrations along typical aircraft flight paths. Multiple types of flight paths were simulated. Aircraft spirals around sites with active flares, which transected flare plumes approximately 1000 m downwind of the flare encountered intersecting simulated plumes from multiple sources on the oil and gas sites, making unambiguous sampling of flare plumes very difficult under most conditions. Aircraft flight paths that followed flare plume centerlines toward active flares were typically able to isolate simulated flare plumes, but only within a few hundred meters of the flare and only if the flare plume centerline closely matched the flight path. Predicted concentration ratios in the simulations were qualitatively consistent with observed data from aircraft flights for the simulated facilities. These results demonstrate the need for very careful interpretation of flare combustion efficiencies derived from data collected by instrumented aircraft flying downwind of oil and gas sites.

papers.title: Photochemical efficiency of brown carbon decreases under concentrated organic aerosol conditions
papers.abstract: Under irradiation, brown carbon (BrC), largely produced by biomass burning, has been shown to undergo evolution in its light absorption and to form reactive intermediates, including singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ), in dilute aqueous solutions. However, no study to date has explored the potential link between the evolution of BrC light absorption and the efficiency of 1 O 2 production as concentration increases to approach values relevant to biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA). Here, we examine this link by determining both absorption enhancement and 1 O 2 production in illuminated BrC from laboratory-generated BBOA at concentrations as high as 2−4 g L −1 . Importantly, the total absorbance of solutions was maintained despite differing concentrations, by scaling the sample heights. All samples initially absorbed similar numbers of photons, but more concentrated samples exhibited less rapid relative absorption enhancement. Furthermore, more concentrated samples exhibited much lower apparent quantum yields of 1 O 2 . Between 2−4 g L −1 , when the 1 O 2 quantum yield was below 1%, absorption enhancement still occurred, with about the same initial rate, consistent with an increasing contribution from non- 1 O 2 -mediated pathways. Together, our results suggest that the photochemical efficiency of BrC is lower under concentrated BBOA conditions than would be extrapolated from dilute aqueous solutions.

papers.title: Elucidating the Mechanism of Electrocatalytic Halide Activation by Low-Coordinate Manganese and Iron Complexes through Voltammetric Analysis and Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Transition metal catalysis has undergone considerable development over the past few decades, with a growing shift toward earth-abundant first-row transition metals contributing to the advancement of more sustainable synthetic methodologies. Among these, Mn(pybox)Cl 2 and Fe(pyrox)OTf 2 have been proposed as electrocatalysts for reductive activation of organic halides and the generation of carbon-centered radicals for subsequent transformations. Here, we investigate the mechanisms of organic halide activation by these catalysts through a combination of cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, using benzyl bromide as a representative substrate. Cyclic voltammetry reveals distinct electrochemical behavior for the manganese and iron complexes, suggesting differences in both catalyst turnover and radical rebound pathways. Comparison of experimental and simulated voltammograms suggests benzyl radical rebound to Mn I and Fe II centers for Mn(pybox)Cl 2 and Fe(pyrox)OTf 2 , respectively. DFT calculations, however, indicate that while radical rebound to Mn I is thermodynamically favorable, rebound to either Fe I or Fe II centers is unfavorable. Mechanistic investigations of halide activation reveal that Mn(pybox)Cl 2 preferentially activates benzyl bromide through an outer-sphere electron transfer pathway, whereas Fe(pyrox)OTf 2 favors an inner-sphere S N 2-like mechanism, which effectively associates the benzyl radical with the iron center until dissociation occurs. Overall, this study reveals distinct mechanisms of electrochemical halide activation catalyzed by Mn(pybox)Cl 2 and Fe(pyrox)OTf 2 and provides mechanistic insights that can guide the future design of first-row transition-metal electrocatalysts for synthetic applications.

papers.title: Q-Chem/CP2K software interface for projection-based, pseudoperiodic wavefunction-in-DFT embedding
papers.abstract: We report an implementation of projection-based quantum embedding that combines periodic density functional theory in the CP2K code with correlated wavefunction calculations in the Q-Chem program. Using this interface, correlated wavefunction methods can be applied to a subset of the molecular orbitals, selected in an automated manner based on a user-defined list of nuclei, wth an embedding potential that provides electronic coupling to the remaining orbitals that comprise the environment. Our implementation uses exact projection, without the need for any level-shift operator, and is “pseudoperiodic” in the sense that periodic boundary effects are implicit in the orbitals used in the (non-periodic) wavefunction calculation. Convergence tests demonstrate that computed properties are faithful to the corresponding periodic quantities, provided that the high-level subsystem is spatially localized and small, relative to the periodic simulation cell. Spectroscopic examples for aqueous chromophores demonstrate converged results using a very limited subset of the water molecules in the simulation cell, decoupling the choice of excited-state method and basis set from the functional that is used to propagate ground-state ab initio molecular dynamics. Solvatochromic shifts for aqueous uracil are converged using equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory, without the need for solvent molecules in the wavefunction calculation, and the embedded calculation captures solvent effects that are absent in gas-phase “microhydration” studies.

papers.title: Simulation and Deconvolution of UV-vis Protein Charge Transfer Spectra
papers.abstract: We present a computational framework for simulating and analyzing non-aromatic UV–vis absorption in proteins arising from charged amino acids. Building on a prior scheme that combined time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) with Hirshfeld population analysis to deconvolute charge-transfer (CT) spectra, we introduce methodological improvements that enable a more accurate description and classification of deep-UV local and non-local CT transitions. The approach is first demonstrated on a lysine–glutamate (Lys–Glu) dimer and systematically extended to TDDFT spectra of charged amino acid clusters computed using both full quantum mechanical (QM) and hybrid QM/MM treatments. From these results, we establish and critically analyze a partitioning strategy that reconstructs CT spectra of entire proteins directly from molecular dynamics trajectories. Finally, we illustrate the framework by simulating and deconvoluting the 370–800 nm absorption profile of α3C, a model protein exhibiting CT spectra. This work provides a generalizable route to dissecting and interpreting both local and CT transitions in congested UV–vis spectra of proteins.

papers.title: Laser-Based Mode-Selective CO2 Splitting Toward Reverse Carbon Combustion
papers.abstract: We propose and computationally test a laserbased route for splitting CO2 by routing energy into selected vibrational modes rather than heating the molecule statistically. The concept targets the microscopic reverse of carbon combustion: storing external energy by converting CO2 back into reduced carbon and molecular oxygen. First-principles molecular dynamics with a hot-spot generalized Langevin equation thermostat provides an idealized representation of mode-selective vibrational pumping, analogous to narrow-band laser excitation but without an explicit radiation field. Pumping the 667 cm−1 bending mode prepares strongly bent CO2 but does not dissociate it. From this activated geometry, pumping the 2349 cm−1 asymmetric stretch opens a CO + O channel near one vibrational quantum, and subsequent COstretch excitation promotes the second cleavage step. These results reframe CO2 splitting as a problem of vibrational energy routing rather than brute-force heating.

papers.title: HueBase AI: an artificial intelligence-integrated cheminformatics pipeline for automated colorimetric sensor discovery
papers.abstract: Colorimetric sensor arrays offer a rapid, low-cost route to analyte detection across pharmaceuticals, agriculture, environmental monitoring, and food safety, classifying complex chemical mixtures through collective optical responses rather than specific molecular recognition. Their design, however, remains an empirical and time-intensive process that relies on iterative trial-and-error screening of dye-analyte combinations. Here we present HueBase AI, an end-to-end artificial-intelligence pipeline that unifies automated literature mining, cheminformatics, and machine learning to streamline colorimetric sensor discovery. A large-language-model agent, integrated with optical character recognition (OCR) and computer-vision modules, curated the first comprehensive open-source colorimetric sensing database (HueBase), comprising more than 14,000 experimentally validated dye-analyte-solvent interactions extracted from over 200 peer-reviewed publications. Each chemical entity is encoded as Morgan (2048-bit) and Molecular ACCess System (MACCS) (167-bit) molecular fingerprints, together with their concatenated representation, enabling systematic benchmarking of 16 classification algorithms across all three featurization (MACCS-only, Morgan-only, and concatenated MACCS + Morgan). An optimized XGBoost model, selected through a three-stage hyperparameter search, predicts dye-analyte responsiveness with 87.8% accuracy and was experimentally validated against two plant volatile organic compound (VOC) biomarkers, (E)-2-hexenal and methyl salicylate, using both existing reference dyes and novel candidate dyes identified from the Max A. Weaver Dye Library containing ~98,000 dyes. By transforming scattered, heterogeneous literature into a machine-actionable knowledge base, HueBase AI establishes a data-driven foundation for intelligent colorimetric sensing and charts a path toward rapid in silico dye screening and the automated design of next-generation sensor arrays.

papers.title: Glycolytic Pretreatment of Poly(ethylene terephthalate) for Enzymatic Hydrolysis
papers.abstract: Enzymatic recycling of PET offers a circular supply chain for poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) materials. Its commercial adoption has been slow due to cheaper virgin PET from global markets. To improve process economics, latest designs have eliminated cost-prohibitive cryogenic micronization pretreatment at the expense of slower enzymatic hydrolysis rates. To this end, we propose glycolytic pretreatment of PET feedstock as a cost-effective method to increase its hydrolysis rate. We hypothesize that reactive extrusion of PET with low amounts of ethylene glycol can enrich its oligomer content, which can partition into the solution-phase and undergo homogenous hydrolysis to increase enzymatic hydrolysis rates. Initial rate experiments at substrate and enzyme excess conditions using Humicola inoslens cutinase (HiC), combined with HiC dosing into glycolyzed PET leachates, verified our hypothesis. Solid-state NMR experiments showed chain mobilities and high chain disorder were preserved after glycolytic pretreatment. MW weight distributions confirmed oligomer enrichment. Notably, we discovered glycolyzed PET was very brittle, enabling micronization via ambient ball-milling in only 5 seconds. By enabling cheaper micronization of PET substrates, combined with the increased solution phase hydrolysis of oligomers, glycolytic pretreatment refines the state-of-the-art enzymatic recycling process.

papers.title: First-Principles Prediction of the Soave Temperature Function via Electron-Localization-Function Saturation: Analytical Derivation and Experimental Validation for 33 Pure Fluids
papers.abstract: The empirical polynomialmSRK(ω) = 0.480+1.574ω−0.176ω2 in the Soave–Redlich–Kwong (SRK) cubic equation of state has lacked a first-principles justification for five decades. We show that the sign pattern and coefficient structure of this polynomial arise from the Electron Localization Function (ELF) through a Pauli-exclusion saturation argument: the ELF anisotropy ∆ELF cannot grow unboundedly with molecular non-sphericity, yielding the bounded rational form mELF(ω) = m0 + λ

papers.title: Dynamic closure of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis InhA cofactor site reveals heterogeneous routes to isoniazid resistance
papers.abstract: Isoniazid remains a cornerstone of tuberculosis therapy, yet resistance-associated mutations in its target, InhA, are not fully explained by reduced NADH binding alone. Here, we combine X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, calorimetry, thermal stability profiling, and multi-scale molecular dynamics to dissect ten clinically observed InhA missense variants. The structures show that many substitutions preserve the canonical cofactor-bound architecture, but thermodynamic and simulation analyses reveal divergent routes to resistance. Active-site variants remodel water and hydrophobic networks to weaken NADH binding, whereas I95P and several interface-proximal variants populate a coenzyme closed-loop state that occludes the nicotinamide/adduct-binding pocket. A190S and Y259H instead appear to preserve NADH affinity while rigidifying the Phe149–Asp150 region required to accommodate the larger INH–NAD adduct. These findings establish InhA coding-region resistance as a spectrum of local, allosteric, and adduct-selective mechanisms, providing a framework for interpreting clinical variants and designing next-generation InhA inhibitors.

papers.title: Reactions of Bis(tert‑butylimino)bis(dimethylamino) Tungsten(VI) with molecular silanol, silica and silicon wafer : Analogy Between Molecular and Surface Chemistries relevant to ALD thin film growths from BTBMW
papers.abstract: We investigate the very first stages of tungsten film growth by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using the W(VI) precursor bis(t‑butylimino)bis(dimethylamino)tungsten BTBMW. Attention is given to the initial metal precursor pulse, probed on both model silica nanobeads support and SiO2-terminated silicon wafers. To achieve molecular-level precision in describing the surface chemistry, solution studies were performed using triphenylsilanol as a molecular analogue of surface silanols, thereby bridging surface and molecular reactivity. In particular, the mono-substituted complex, W(NtBu)2(NMe2)(OSiPh3) was isolated and fully characterized, serving as a molecular reference for the spectral signatures of W surface species. The convergence of data from molecular analogues, powder substrates, and 2D wafer surfaces, validated by XPS analyses, provides a consistent picture of the grafting process which is uniform. Collectively, our results show that BTBMW reacts efficiently and selectively with hydroxyl-terminated substrates, enabling controlled nucleation at the submonolayer-scale.

papers.title: A protein friction biosensor for screening binding-induced conformational changes
papers.abstract: Binding-induced modulation of protein structure is central to the therapeutic mechanism of many small-molecule drugs, yet most biophysical screening platforms rely on affinity-based readouts that do not directly report conformational changes. Here we introduce molecular friction sensing as a screening-compatible method for detecting ligand-induced changes in protein conformation with sub-Ångström resolution under physiological conditions. The method uses surface-tethered DNA origami nanolevers that are periodically drawn toward an electrode by attractive potentials and then released, allowing their upward diffusive motion to be tracked with microsecond resolution. Proteins attached to the distal end of the nanolever impose hydrodynamic drag, and ligand-induced structural rearrangements that alter protein friction are detected as changes in nanolever velocity. We validate the approach across multiple proteins and uncover subtle small-molecule dependent conformational changes. By resolving conformational changes independently of binding affinity or kinetics, molecular friction sensing adds an orthogonal readout to drug discovery.

papers.title: A Conformational Ensemble Picture of Melonic Carbon Nitride: Linking Polymorph Populations to Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction Activity
papers.abstract: Polymeric carbon nitride is widely treated as a single graphitic C3N4 phase, yet thermally condensed materials are better described as hydrogen-containing melon frameworks that can adopt several closely related structural states. How these metastable polymorphs form during synthesis, and how they govern photocatalytic CO2 reduction, remains poorly resolved. Here, a vibrational-mode-guided computational structure search is combined with temperature-controlled synthesis to identify and experimentally access metastable polymorphs of melonic carbon nitride. The structure search reveals seven low-energy conformers, all within 150 meV of the ground state, that span planar, corrugated and sheared geometries, indicating that condensed carbon nitride is more accurately viewed as an ensemble of polymorphs than as a single static phase. Carbon nitrides synthesized between 500 and 650 °C show that increasing thermal input compacts the interlayer stacking, sharpens vibrational signatures, raises the surface area (4.8 to 68 m2 g−1) and reorganizes nitrogen coordination, while lower-temperature materials retain more heterogeneous, corrugated configurations. Counter to conventional descriptors, the structurally heterogeneous, lowertemperature CN-500 delivers the highest CO and CH4 yields despite its lower surface area and less favorable charge-transfer behavior. To resolve this counterintuitive trend, a charge-carrier-explicit kinetic model that couples electron-hole generation, recombination, hole-mediated oxidation, CO2 activation and sequential proton-coupled electron transfer is developed and fitted to the time-resolved CO and CH4 evolution across all samples and electron-donor concentrations. The model resolves activity into two independent descriptors: an apparent CO2-activation constant that tracks the polymorph-dependent density of CO2binding sites, and an effective electron-flux parameter governed by the hole-mediated water-oxidation rate. Critically, the analysis identifies the oxidative half-reaction-not the reductive steps-as the rate-limiting process: because photogenerated electrons and holes are produced in stoichiometric pairs, the slow consumption of holes throttles the electron flux available for CO2 reduction, so that the oxidation kinetics indirectly govern the overall reduction rate. This assignment is confirmed by the systematic rise of the electron-flux parameter with hole-scavenger (TEOA) loading at nearly constant CO2-activation and COhydrogenation constants. These results establish melonic polymorphism as a key descriptor of CO2 photoreduction, identify hole-mediated oxidation as an under-appreciated rate-limiting control, and introduce structural-state engineering as a design strategy for carbon nitride photocatalysts.

papers.title: Aggregation-Enhanced Photocleavage for Time-resolved Multicolor
papers.abstract: Dynamic fluorescence systems capable of generating time-resolved multicolor optical outputs are highly desirable for advanced information encryption and optical storage. However, precise regulation of fluorescence evolution kinetics remains challenging, as most reported systems either exhibit intrinsically fixed photochemical kinetics or require complex multicomponent assemblies. Herein, we report an aggregationregulated photochemical system in which the photocleavage kinetics can be continuously programmed through aggregation-dependent excited-state engineering. A donor-acceptor luminogen TPEMN with a photocleavable central vinyl bridge was rationally designed. Upon photoirradiation, TPEMN undergoes a pronounced aggregation-enhanced photooxidative cleavage process in which photoreaction kinetics increase progressively with aggregation degree, accompanied by continuous multiple fluorescence evolutions from orange to blue. Systematic experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that aggregation suppresses excited-state structural relaxation, prolongs excited-state lifetime, facilitates intersystem crossing, and promotes reactive oxygen species generation, thereby markedly leading to accelerated photocleavage kinetics. This converts conventional binary photoresponses into well-resolved timedependent fluorescence states, allowing demonstration of time-gated information encryption with deceptive intermediates, multilevel anti-counterfeiting with “burnafter-read” functionality, and high-density quaternary optical storage. This work establishes aggregation-regulated excited-state engineering as a novel paradigm for manipulating photochemical reactivity, providing a conceptual framework for the development of high-efficiency photoreaction, adaptive stimulus-responsive materials and dynamic information application.

papers.title: G-NequIP: Data-Efficient Generalization of Equivariant Neural Network Potentials across Diverse Organic Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Neural network potentials (NNPs) have emerged as powerful tools for quantum-mechanical-level molecular simulation at substantially reduced computational cost; however, their generalization across diverse organic chemical space depends critically on both model architecture and training-set design. Here, we introduce G-NequIP, a generalized E(3)-equivariant NNP trained on approximately 150,000 DFT reference configurations at the ωB97X-D/6-311++G(3df,3pd) level for neutral and singly charged organic species containing H, C, N, O, F, S, Cl, and P atoms. Rather than exhaustive quantum-mechanical evaluation of large databases, the training workflow combined functional-group-guided sampling from GDB-derived and complementary datasets with progressive dataset expansion and force-sensitive active learning, exploiting the intrinsic data efficiency of E(3)-equivariant architectures to achieve broad chemical coverage from a compact training set. The final gas-phase model achieves an energy RMSE of 0.0053 eV atom-1 and a force RMSE of 0.0518 eV Å-1 on held-out test structures. Across potential energy surface (PES) scans, conformer generation, molecular dynamics (MD), vibrational density-of-states (VDOS) analysis, and charged-species collision cross-section (CCS) validation, G-NequIP consistently outperforms ANI-2x and approaches AIMNet2 accuracy in near-equilibrium regions, despite being trained on a substantially smaller dataset. A complementary G-NequIP-smdW model for SMD aqueous environments reproduces QM solvation free energies with RMSE = 0.99 kcal mol-1 on the FreeSolv dataset. Overall, G-NequIP demonstrates that equivariant NNPs, combined with chemically informed active learning, can generalize across diverse organic chemical space from compact training sets, providing a transferable framework for DFT-level conformational analysis, molecular dynamics, vibrational characterization, and solvation energetics.

papers.title: Antimony(V) Complexes of an N2O2-Type Tetradentate Azadipyrromethene Ligand and Their Near-Infrared Optical Properties
papers.abstract: Antimony(V) azadipyrromethene complexes featuring a tetradentate N2O2-type ligand were synthesized to investigate the impact of axial ligands on their photophysical properties. Reaction of the azadipyrromethene ligand with SbCl5 afforded the benchtop-stable dichloro complex aza-LSbCl2 in high yield. Axial ligand substitution enabled the conversion of aza-LSbCl2 to its dihydroxy, chloromethoxy, and dimethoxy derivatives aza-LSb(OH)2, aza-LSbCl(OMe), and aza-LSb(OMe)2, respectively. Photophysical studies revealed a ligand-dependent fluorescence turn-on effect; while the dichloro complex aza-LSbCl2 and the chloromethoxy complex aza-LSbCl(OMe) are nearly non-emissive, the aza-LSb(OH)2 and aza-LSb(OMe)2 exhibit near-infrared (NIR) emission with photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 8 and 6%, respectively. Time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations indicate that the fluorescence quenching in the dichloro and chloromethoxy complexes stems from a dissociative excited state characterized by Sb–Cl bond elongation, whereas oxygen-based ligands provide a structurally stable singlet excited state (S1) manifold. These findings demonstrate that axial-ligand engineering at the antimony center is an effective strategy for modulating the optical properties of antimony(V) azadipyrromethene complexes and highlight the potential of antimony as a central element for the development of NIR-emissive materials.

papers.title: Extending peptide ligation to acidic pH and junctions comprising glycosylated and phosphorylated amino acids
papers.abstract: The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine-containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β-branched amino acids, as well as O-glycosylated or O-phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2-mercapto-2-(4,5-dimethoxypyridin-2-yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca-phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain.
