In this work, we highlight a method for predicting relative rate coefficients (i.e. ratio of rates between two solvents) of bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reactions by using the COSMO-RS solvation model and a simple relationship derived from transition state theory. To benchmark this quantum-chemical method, we digitized a dataset of room-temperature rates for ionic reactions, comprised of 200 datapoints. Among these, 111 are SN2 rate data, spanning 55 different reactions across various solvents. We used these SN2 data to test a variety of different geometry optimization methods as inputs to the COSMO-RS method. The errors in relative rate constants at 298K are relatively low (RMSE ≈ 1 log10 unit) and are not very sensitive to geometry, demonstrating good accuracy and flexibility of this method across different workflows and solvent systems, with higher errors generally observed for systems with some halide nucleophiles. The data and calculations are available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260106.

papers.title: Molecular origins of ion mobility differences between the peptide standards GRGDS and SDGRG
papers.abstract: The reversed sequence pentapeptide pair GRGDS and SDGRG are widely used ion mobility spectrometry (IMS) standards as they exhibit distinct gas-phase mobilities despite identical mass and composition. Here, we investigate the molecular origins of their differing charge-state-dependent conformations using ion mobility mass spectrometry, cryogenic gas-phase infrared spectroscopy, NMR spectroscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations. In aqueous solution, both peptides populate highly flexible conformational ensembles with only minor differences in compactness. Upon desolvation, however, the peptides collapse into distinct gas-phase structures stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding. For the doubly protonated species, GRGDS adopts a compact cyclic “C-like” fold, whereas SDGRG forms a more extended “S-like” conformation driven by Coulombic repulsion between the protonated N-terminus and the arginine side chain. The singly charged ions show a more compact conformation for SDGRG compared to GRGDS, and a combination of different protomers and conformers appears to be present. Crown ether complexation and terminal glycine extensions of the doubly protonated species reduce the differences in IMS, supporting the importance of charge-charge interactions in defining the gas-phase folds. These findings provide molecular-level insight into a widely used IMS standard system and contribute to our fundamental understanding of structural rearrangements in peptides upon transfer to the gas phase.

papers.title: Biologically-driven generative chemistry: using biological data to guide de novo drug design
papers.abstract: Drug discovery is a dauntingly difficult process due to the enormous space of possible molecules and the complexity of biological systems. Traditional in silico drug design methods have focused primarily on optimising chemical properties, often overlooking or only implicitly handling key biological effects that determine whether or not a compound is a viable drug candidate. In recent years, deep generative models have emerged as a powerful class of machine learning methods capable of generating novel molecular structures tailored to specific design objectives. Increasingly, these models are being conditioned not only on chemical features but also on diverse categories of biological data, from bioassays and protein structures to gene expression signatures and cell morphology profiles. This biologically-guided paradigm holds the potential to improve both the relevance and clinical translatability of generated compounds. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and accessible overview of biologically-conditioned generative models for de novo drug design. We describe core generative modalities while critically examining current challenges in benchmarking and validation. Our goal is to orient researchers with a machine learning background to the data, design choices, and evaluation gaps that define biologically-conditioned molecular generation.

papers.title: Biologically-driven generative chemistry: using biological data to guide de novo drug design
papers.abstract: Drug discovery is a dauntingly difficult process due to the enormous space of possible molecules and the complexity of biological systems. Traditional in silico drug design methods have focused primarily on optimising chemical properties, often overlooking or only implicitly handling key biological effects that determine whether or not a compound is a viable drug candidate. In recent years, deep generative models have emerged as a powerful class of machine learning methods capable of generating novel molecular structures tailored to specific design objectives. Increasingly, these models are being conditioned not only on chemical features but also on diverse categories of biological data, from bioassays and protein structures to gene expression signatures and cell morphology profiles. We describe core generative modalities while critically examining current challenges in benchmarking and validation. Our goal is to orient researchers with a machine learning background to the data, design choices, and evaluation gaps that define biologically-conditioned molecular generation.

papers.title: PolyTrace: Grounded LLM Reasoning for Data-Efficient and Faithful Prediction of Polymer Glass Transition Temperatures
papers.abstract: The glass transition temperature (Tg) is a critical design property of polymers, yet structure-based prediction remains difficult for emerging polymer families with sparse measurements. Conventional machine learning models often lack enough training examples in this regime, while group contribution methods can miss scaffold-specific structure–property relationships. We introduce PolyTrace (Trustworthy Reasoning with Analogs, Contributions, and Evidence), an evidence-grounded framework that predicts polymer Tg through large language model (LLM) reasoning rather than statistical fitting alone. PolyTrace integrates group contribution estimates, nearest-neighbor analogs, and literature-derived structure–Tg rules, constraining the LLM to reason from the supplied evidence rather than recalled property values. Self-consistency sampling and split-conformal calibration quantify uncertainty. On a 77-polymer poly(aryl ether ketone) (PAEK) data set, PolyTrace achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 8.7K (R2 = 0.891) under random five-fold cross-validation (within-family interpolation), outperforming fingerprint-based regression by 31% and the strongest learned baseline (a pretrained TransPolymer regressor) by 29% (p < 0.001). Under scaffold-grouped cross-validation, the leakage-controlled extrapolation test, performance remains robust (MAE 9.1K, R2 = 0.902), matching the best group-contribution model in accuracy while showing greater consistency across scaffolds. On a 7,637-polymer homopolymer benchmark with 1,084 held-out test polymers, PolyTrace retains strong performance (MAE 28.4K, R2 = 0.874), a statistical tie with the best fingerprint baseline. Beyond accuracy, PolyTrace provides evidence attribution, automatically checked citations, calibrated intervals, and mechanistic explanations: citations are verifiable in 99.9% (large benchmark) to 100% (PAEK) of predictions, conformal intervals reach nearnominal coverage, and 89.9% (large benchmark) to 97.4% (PAEK) of explanations are rated mechanistically sound. These results support evidence-guided LLM reasoning as a complementary paradigm for molecular and materials property prediction when data are limited, heterogeneous, or distributed across weak sources of scientific knowledge.

papers.title: Rational Photocatalyst Selection for Efficient Radical–Polar Crossover Phosphonylation of N- Hydroxyphthalimide Ester–Containing Polymers
papers.abstract: The photoredox-catalyzed postfunctionalization of polymers bearing N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) ester moieties via radical–polar crossover (RPC) is a promising strategy for introducing phosphonate groups into polymer backbones, as we previously reported. However, the degree of functionalization (DOF) in the phosphonylation of methyl acrylate copolymers has been limited to 15% owing to competition between the RPC process and hydrogen atom transfer. In this study, we demonstrate that the rational selection of an organic photocatalyst on the basis of three key features, i.e., oxidation power, photostability, and excited-state lifetime, substantially improves the RPC efficiency in the phosphonylation of methyl acrylate copolymers containing NHPI ester moieties. Systematic screening of eight organic photocatalysts revealed that 2,4,5,6-tetrakis(3,6di-tert-butyl-9H-carbazol-9-yl)isophthalonitrile (4CzIPN-tBu), operating via a reductive quenching mechanism, affords a maximum DOF of 28%. The approach was extended to various phosphite nucleophiles and NHPI ester–containing polymer substrates, all of which afforded higher DOFs than those reported in our previous work. In addition, computational studies revealed for the first time the role of neighboring group participation in RPC-based polymer reactions: the ester groups of the methyl acrylate units form stable cyclic intermediates with the carbocation intermediates generated via RPC, effectively suppressing undesired back electron transfer and enabling efficient phosphonylation even from inherently unstable secondary carbocations. This study establishes rational design principles for enhancing RPC efficiency in postfunctionalization reactions, thereby contributing to the development of a broader range of functional polymer architectures.

papers.title: Monitoring In Crystallo Elementary Steps at Cationic, Site-Isolated, Pt-Sites using Solid-State NMR signatures.
papers.abstract: Understanding active sites and monitoring elementary steps in heterogeneous catalysis is central to establishing structure-activity relationships. In this context, solid-state molecular organometallic chemistry (SMOM) has emerged as an original approach in which reactive metal centres are site-isolated within a confined crystalline lattice. This enables in crystallo solid-gas transformations that are directly relevant to heterogeneous catalysis. However, experimentally-determined metal speciation of reaction products and tracking changes in the coordination environment of the metal sites upon in crystallo reactions can be challenging when samples are not suitable for analysis by single-crystal X-ray diffraction or threedimensional electron diffraction. Here, we report the development of SMOM approaches to generate isolated Pt sites in well-defined environments and demonstrate how 195Pt solid-state NMR spectroscopy enables reporting on the changes in the atomic-scale local structure of metal centres during in crystallo reactivity studies.

papers.title: Electrochemical oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes catalyzed by a water-soluble TEMPO mediator
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates the successful use of TMA-TEMPO as redox mediator for the electrochemical, halide-free oxidation of renewable alcohols, including carbohydrates and HMF, under galvanostatic conditions in an undivided cell. The reaction furnishes good to excellent yields of a variety of industrially relevant compounds, including glucaric acid and FDCA, using electricity as traceless oxidant in a fluoride-free, aqueous electrolyte.

papers.title: Extending SHARC to Periodic Systems: A SHARC–VASP Interface for First-Principles Nonadiabatic Dynamics
papers.abstract: Nonadiabatic effects arising from the breakdown of the Born–Oppenheimer approx- imation govern a wide range of photoinduced processes in molecules and materials. While trajectory surface hopping has become a standard tool for simulating excited-state dynamics in molecular systems, its extension to periodic solids remains comparatively underdeveloped. In this work, we present an interface between the trajectory surface hopping package Surface Hopping including Arbitrary Couplings (SHARC) and the plane-wave density-functional-theory code Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) that enables nonadiabatic dynamics simulations in periodic solids based on first-principles electronic-structure calculations. This development extends the applicability of SHARC from finite molecular systems to extended materials while retaining its modularity and support for arbitrary electronic couplings. Further, it provides a broadly applicable platform for investigating excited-state dynamics in solids using concepts and workflows familiar from the molecular nonadiabatic dynamics community, thereby establishing a unified theoretical and computational framework for both molecular and extended materials. As a first application, the interface is tested on bulk silicon, a prototypical semiconductor whose photoinduced carrier relaxation dynamics is strongly influenced by electron–phonon coupling and has therefore been extensively investigated both experimentally and theoretically.

papers.title: Reductive C-O bond cleavage and borylation of carboxylic esters
papers.abstract: Alcohols are abundant feedstocks in organic synthesis but remain underutilized as alkyl donors via C–O bond activation. In this work, the deoxygenative Markó–Lam reaction is studied computationally to probe how the reductive radical transformation may be tuned to efficiently furnish open shell intermediates. These results were experimentally illustrated with the formation of boronic esters from a series of carboxylic esters via an intermediate radical-polar crossover event.

papers.title: Environmentally sensitive fluorescent conjugates for assessing the local polarity of individual layers of the bacterial cell envelope
papers.abstract: The bacterial cell envelope is a multilayered structure critical for cell integrity, antibiotic resistance, and host-pathogen interactions. However, the biophysical properties of individual layers constituting the cell envelope remain poorly understood due to the lack of appropriate selective probes. To address this gap, we developed a toolbox of solvatochromic fluorescent probes by conjugating the environmentally sensitive dye Nile Red to selective biomolecular vectors targeting distinct layers of the bacterial cell envelope. Using ratiometric flow cytometry, we quantitatively assessed the polarity of individual envelope layers in live bacteria by calculating the generalized polarization (GP). Furthermore, we demonstrated the ability of these probes to monitor the impact of thermal and osmotic stress on the dynamics of individual envelope layers in real time. This work introduces a versatile platform for studying the spatiotemporal dynamics of bacterial cell envelopes under stress conditions. Additionally, it illustrates how Nile Red conjugation combined with ratiometric flow cytometry offers a powerful approach to probe the cellular microenvironment of antimicrobial compounds with unknown mechanisms of action.

papers.title: G-Quadruplex Hydrogels as Dynamic, Mechanically Tunable and Ion Conductive 3D Scaffolds for Cell Culture and Bioengineering Applications
papers.abstract: Hydrogels are widely used materials for biomedical applications. In particular, supramolecular hydrogels bioinspired on guanosine-quadruplexes (GQ) have been utilized in the last decade for drug delivery, biocatalysis and biosensing. However, when applied as scaffolds for cell and bioengineering applications, existing GQ hydrogels suffer from important limitations: i) scarcity of fabrication strategies under mild aqueous conditions, ii) quick disintegration within few hours under physiological conditions, iii) narrow tunability of their properties in relation to native tissues. These shortcomings hamper the broad use of GQ hydrogels in bioengineering. Herein, stable and versatile GQ hydrogels are developed as dynamic biomatrices for cell culture and tissue engineering applications. The GQ matrices are easily fabricated under mild aqueous conditions, present improved physical integrity and tunable mechanical properties within physiological ranges, besides fibrillar, porous microstructure, ion conductivity and cytocompatibility. Detailed characterization of GQ self-assembly process driving hydrogelation is presented through various spectroscopic, structural, rheological and microscopic techniques. For the first time, mechanistic insight on the ion conductivity of GQ hydrogels is revealed by electro-rheology. These matrices support the culture of diverse cell types in 2D and 3D, and showcase injectability and printability, making these scaffolds suitable for manufacturing soft medical devices. The results of this study expand the applicability potential of GQ hydrogel for advancing in vitro tissue models.

papers.title: Conformational Analysis, Intramolecular Interactions, and Anomalous Anharmonic Behavior in the 2-Chloroethyl Chalcogenol Triad (X = O, S, Se)
papers.abstract: We present a systematic computational study of the conformational landscape, intramolecular bonding, and anharmonic vibrational properties of 2-chloroethanol (ClCH2CH2OH), 2chloroethanethiol (ClCH2CH2SH), and 2-chloroethaneselenol (ClCH2CH2SeH). These molecules form a chalcogen triad (X = O, S, Se) that enables direct comparison of how the heteroatom modulates intramolecular X–H•••Cl hydrogen bonding and gauche stabilization. Conformational searches using the CREST/iMTD-GC algorithm followed by DFT optimization at the M06-2X-D3/aug-cc-pVTZ(-PP) level identify 5 distinct conformers for the 2-chloro isomers and 2–3 for the 1-chloro analogues. The gauche effect stabilizes the global minimum in all three 2-chloro compounds, with the conformational energy spread contracting from 2.69 (O) to 2.19 (S) to 1.90 (Se) kcal/mol. Boltzmann analysis at 298 K reveals that the global minimum dominates for the alcohol (83.4%) but distributes

papers.title: Ab Initio Investigation of Chemical Reaction Pathways in Ultracold NaBr and KBr Molecular Collisions: Diatomic Validation, Dissociation Energies, and the NaKBr2 Tetramer Intermediate
papers.abstract: Alkali bromides NaBr and KBr possess permanent electric dipole moments of approximately 9.1 and 10.5 D, among the largest of any diatomic molecule, making them exceptional candidates for dipolar quantum science and electric-field-controlled ultracold collisions. We report a systematic ab initio investigation of all two-body reaction channels for NaBr + NaBr, KBr + KBr, and NaBr + KBr collisions using CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVQZ potential-energy curves validated against experimental spectroscopic constants, supplemented by phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC) benchmarks. All bond-swap channels are endoergic by 38,000–43,000 cm−1 (109–122 kcal mol−1) and all atom-abstraction channels by 21,000–25,000 cm−1 (60–71 kcal mol−1), thermodynamically forbidding reactive product formation at ultracold collision energies. DLPNO-CCSD(T) approach potentials, validated against canonical CCSD(T), are purely attractive for all three collision pairs, with no entrance barriers. The NaBr + KBr system additionally supports a deep alternating NaKBr2 short-range complex (well depth −47.9 kcal mol−1 at the CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVQZ level, −42.8 counterpoise-corrected; −50.3 ± 0.3 kcal mol−1 at the ph-AFQMC level), a rectangular rock-salt intermediate analogous to the M2X2 minimum characterized for calcium monofluoride (CaF + CaF) collisions. Owing to the large permanent dipoles, the isotropic long-range interaction is dominated by the rotational dispersion term, giving total C6 ≈ 4×107–1.3×108 a.u. and universal s-wave loss rates of ≈6–8 × 10−10 cm3 s−1, at or above the KRb value. Suppressing these losses requires electric-field shielding with the molecules prepared in their first rotationally excited state; the resonant mechanism is predicted to be highly effective, with critical fields of ≈1.6–3.4 kV cm−1, comparable to those for strongly dipolar bialkali molecules such as RbCs and within an order of magnitude of KRb (∼12 kV cm−1). These results establish alkali bromides as thermodynamically stable against exchange chemistry while identifying complex-mediated (“sticky”) loss and resonant electric-field shielding as the dominant processes governing ultracold NaBr and KBr collisions.

papers.title: Characterizing Partially Unfolded States for the C-Terminal Domain in WT and 3PA moPrP under Acidic Conditions
papers.abstract: Misfolding and aggregation of the prion protein are central to prion disease, but the conformational states that precede aggregation remain incompletely defined. In particular, it is unclear how conserved proline residues influence the stability of the native fold and the accessibility of partially unfolded intermediates (PUF) under acidic conditions. Here, we combine multiple-walker well-tempered parallelbias metadynamics, clustering, hydration analysis, and residue-resolved hydrogen-deuterium exchange (HDX) protection factor calculations to examine the wild-type (WT) mouse prion protein and the triple-proline-to-alanine (3PA) mutant at pH 4.5. Reweighted free-energy surfaces reveal a native basin and multiple metastable PUF basins in both variants; however, the mutation substantially reshapes the folding-unfolding landscape. In WT moPrP, unfolding is initiated primarily in the H2-H3 subdomain, whereas in 3PA moPrP, the H1 helix becomes the main site of destabilization. The 3PA mutant also shows altered basin connectivity and higher barriers between nativelike and PUF states. Structural clustering, hydration maps, and short-range interaction energies indicate that the loss of protein-protein interactions in metastable states is compensated by increased protein-water interactions, with distinct patterns observed in WT and 3PA. Projections onto individual structural descriptors further show that conserved prolines contribute to local rigidity in H1 and the S2-H2 loop and help maintain coupling between the S1-H1-S2 and the H2-H3 subdomains. HDX protection factors derived from enhanced-sampling ensembles support these conclusions and reproduce mutation-dependent changes in local stability that are not captured by unbiased molecular dynamics (MD) simulations alone. Overall, the conserved prolines stabilize the mouse prion protein by restricting local flexibility and shaping the early unfolding pathways relevant to misfolding.

papers.title: NN-Dx: Chemically adaptive dispersion physics for density-functional theory
papers.abstract: London dispersion remains an error source in routine density-functional theory because common density-functional approximations lack the nonlocal response required for correlated charge fluctuations. We introduce NN-Dx, a density-free neural correction that learns chemically adaptive parameters inside a D4-like model rather than adding a black-box energy. Starting from element-specific isolated-atom dynamic polarizability spectra, an E(3)-equivariant network predicts environmental spectral corrections, adaptive charge-scaling parameters, and local corrections to Becke–Johnson damping, pair scaling and Axilrod–Teller–Muto three-body terms. Trained end-to-end on dispersion residuals, NN-Dx reduces default D4 errors by 66–90% across nine density functionals on the original D4 benchmark, giving sub-0.08 kcal mol -1 mean absolute errors (MAEs) for eight. On charged and neutral DES15K subsets, errors decrease by 85–93%. For PBE0 on a H/C/N/O subset of DES15K, NN-Dx reaches 0.037 kcal mol -1 MAE, about eighteenfold below ML-XDM, while preserving reference stationary-point structure in scanned binding curves.

papers.title: Catalytic Borylation of the High-Global-Warming-Potential Refrigerant HFC-143a
papers.abstract: Transition-metal complexes were identified that could catalyze the C-H borylations of the high global warming refrigerant HFC-143a. Reactions of gaseous HFC-143a with diboronic esters in the presence of select catalysts afforded the non-volatile C-H functionalized products [CF 3 CH 2 (B(OR) 2 )] and [CF 3 CH(B(OR) 2 ) 2 ]. The degree of monoborylation vs. diborylation depended on catalyst structure and nature of the boronic ester. The reactions were significantly affected by the rates of stirring, indicating mass transfer effects on the concentration of fluorinated refrigerant in hydrocarbon solvent.

papers.title: Multiscale View of Electrochemistry at 3D Printed Carbon-Polymer Composite Electrodes: Revealing How Nanoscale Features Contribute to Macroscopic Properties
papers.abstract: 3D printed electrodes – carbon composite electrodes - are growing in popularity but characterization studies are typically limited to voltammetric measurements, with peak to peak separation, for fast electron transfer redox couples, being used as a key metric of performance and properties. To fully understand voltammetric responses investigation of the nano- to microscale origins is critical. In this study, carbon black in poly lactic acid (PLA) electrodes, printed using fused deposition modeling and mechanically polished prior to use are investigated using cyclic voltammetry (CV), conducting atomic force microscopy (C-AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). Thermal gravimetric analysis shows the commercial filament contains ~23% by weight carbon black. The CV response for ferrocenylmethyl trimethylammonium (FcTMA+) oxidation in 0.1 M potassium nitrate shows peak shaped responses which increase in magnitude with scan rate up to 5 V s-1 where the current response becomes more sigmoidal. C-AFM reveals a RMS surface roughness of 68 nm after polishing, and localized conducting regions covering 11-15 % of the surface (n = 3). These sites vary in size, with mean and largest conductive site areas of 0.045 µm2 and 0.797 µm2 respectively. The active sites lie mostly in small recesses in the electrode surface, with the majority spaced less than 400 nm apart and a minority spaced at distances greater than a μm. Voltammetric SECCM maps of the surface, using a double-channel tip ~ 580 nm diameter, support the C-AFM data, showing a significant fraction of the surface has no electrochemical activity. For those sites with electrochemically-active regions, different CV characteristics are observed, as determined by the change in mass transport-limited current and waveshape (half-wave potential and inter-quartile potentials). Capacitance values obtained from the foot of each CV are used as a proxy for estimating active surface area in the SECCM footprint (not otherwise visible) and the limiting current provides a measure of the mass transport rate to the site. At 0.5 V s-1, SECCM CV responses range from slightly peak shaped, associated with the largest area active sites, to steady-state responses with different limiting current and interquartile potentials. These data are analyzed to reveal a greater than two orders of magnitude distribution in heterogeneous electron transfer kinetics at carbon black sites. Moreover the SECCM data help explain the macroscopic scan rate voltammetric data where widely spaced active sites become increasingly diffusionally-isolated and the wide distribution of local kinetics becomes more apparent as scan rate increase. Both are reflected in the observed change in CV waveshape.

papers.title: Site-specific lysine glycation decouples tau nucleation, uptake, and templated propagation
papers.abstract: Tau aggregation is a defining molecular feature of Alzheimer’s disease and related tauopathies, but how non-enzymatic chemical modifications tune tau assembly, cellular uptake, and templated propagation remains poorly understood. Lysine glycation is particularly difficult to dissect because reducing sugars and reactive carbonyl species generate heterogeneous mixtures of early and advanced glycation adducts, obscuring the effects of individual sites and chemotypes. Here, we overcome this limitation by preparing chemically defined tau proteoforms bearing single fructosyl-lysine or carboxyethyl-lysine modifications at selected lysine residues in K18 and full-length 2N4R tau. These homogeneous proteins reveal that lysine glycation is not a uniform pro-aggregation signal. Rather, individual glycation adducts produce site- and chemotype-dependent effects that suppress de novo fibrillization, remodel tau–polyanion binding, disrupt RNA-driven condensate formation, and alter cellular uptake and seeding in ways that are not predicted by bulk aggregation behavior. Together, these findings show that glycation can decouple tau nucleation, phase behavior, internalization, and templated recruitment, providing a molecular framework for understanding how metabolic and oxidative stress reshape tau biology without simply increasing aggregation propensity.

papers.title: Kinetically constrained ring-polymer molecular dynamics extended to electronically adiabatic reaction regimes
papers.abstract: Kinetically-constrained ring-polymer molecular dynamics (KC-RPMD) is an approximate quantum dynamical method for treating electronically non-adiabatic processes in condensed phase systems, predicting accurate electron transfer (ET) rate constants in the normal and inverted Marcus regimes through computationally efficient classical equations of motion. The favorable properties of KC-RPMD in the weak diabatic coupling regime have been well investigated. However, an in-depth study of its performance in the strong coupling regime has not been performed until now. In this work, we identify a breakdown of free energies and ET rates predicted by traditional KC-RPMD in the strong coupling regime. We extend KC-RPMD to allow for the direct simulation of systems spanning the full range of diabatic coupling strengths, maintaining all the favorable properties in the weak coupling regime while recovering the appropriate adiabatic description in the strong coupling regime. This is accomplished through a modification to the Gaussian restraint penalty function, which is made to gradually loosen and vanish at strong coupling. We demonstrate the accuracy of KC-RPMD on a variety of spin-boson model systems spanning a wide range of diabatic coupling strengths.

papers.title: Sulfonylative Pauson-Khand Reaction
papers.abstract: The Pauson-Khand reaction is a landmark transformation in organic synthesis, enabling the rapid assembly of cyclopentenone frameworks through a (2+2+1) cycloaddition of alkenes, alkynes, and carbon monoxide. Despite its long-standing impact, the conceptual framework of Pauson-Khand chemistry has remained largely restricted to carbon monoxide incorporation. Here we report a fundamentally distinct sulfonylative Pauson-Khand-type protocol enabled by interception of a photoinduced energy-transfer-mediated (2+2) cycloaddition pathway. The reaction proceeds under mild, energy-efficient conditions, exhibits broad substrate scope across diverse 1,6-enynes, and delivers products in good to excellent yields. A complementary photocatalyst-free variant relying on direct triplet excitation of alkynyl cyclohexadienones is also disclosed. Mechanistic studies, supported by Density Functional Theory calculations reveal the origin of reactivity and selectivity and establish this process as a mechanistically orthogonal alternative to classical Pauson–Khand chemistry.

papers.title: Cu(II) complexes with mixed pyridine-benzimidazole donors: LPMO-type activity and Copper-Oxygen Intermediates
papers.abstract: Copper-dependent lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs) are key enzymes in the oxidative depolymerization of recalcitrant polysaccharides and have inspired the development of biomimetic copper complexes capable of running the cleavage of O-glycosidic bonds. In this work, two mononuclear copper(II) complexes, bearing asymmetric pyridine–imidazole ligands containing either an imine or amine donors, were synthesized and investigated as structural and functional models of the LPMO active site. Electrochemical, UV-vis and EPR studies revealed the properties of both complexes fall in the range reported for the enzymes and previously reported synthetic systems. Density functional theory calculations supported the experimental redox and spectroscopic properties, providing insights into the coordination changes occurring upon reduction. The interaction of the complexes with hydrogen peroxide was studied by UV–vis and EPR spectroscopy at low temperature, revealing the transient formation of copper–oxygen intermediates consistent with Cu(II)-hydroperoxo species. The oxidative reactivity of the complexes was evaluated using p-nitrophenyl-β-D-glucopyranoside, coumarin-3-carboxylic acid, and cellobiose as model substrates. Kinetic analysis demonstrated a strong dependence of the catalytic activity on hydrogen peroxide concentration, indicating that oxidant activation constitutes a key step in the catalytic cycle. Reactive oxygen species generation studies further showed that peroxide activation proceeds mainly through metal-centered pathways rather than uncontrolled Fenton-type chemistry. The two complexes reported in this work thus reproduce several structural, electronic, and functional features of LPMOs and provide valuable insight into copper-mediated oxidative cleavage of carbohydrates.

papers.title: The Dielectric Dogma Paradox: Steric-Entropic Dominance and Anomalous Ion Pairing in Ternary Ionic Liquid–Carbonate Electrolytes
papers.abstract: The conventional design paradigm for lithium-ion battery electrolytes prioritizes high-dielectricconstant solvents to promote salt dissociation and enhance ionic conductivity. Here, we challenge this dielectric-centric dogma through systematic molecular dynamics simulations of ternary mixtures comprising 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([EMI][TFSI]), ethylene carbonate (EC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and LiTFSI. Contrary to the prevailing expectation that EC—possessing a static dielectric constant approximately thirtyfold greater than DMC—should dominate the lithium cation solvation shell, our simulations reveal a persistent preference for DMC coordination across all mixture compositions. We demonstrate that this anomalous behavior originates from competing steric and entropic factors that override purely dielectric considerations. Radial distribution function analysis shows Li+–O(DMC) first-shell distances of 2.17 Å with coordination numbers ranging from 1.37 to 3.34, while Li+–O(EC) distances extend to 2.32 Å with lower coordination numbers. Spatial distribution functions reveal that DMC molecules occupy geometrically favorable tetrahedral positions around Li+, whereas EC's bulkier structure imposes steric penalties. Increasing carbonate content paradoxically enhances cation–anion interactions: the [EMI]+–[TFSI]- coordination number increases from 12.37 to 7.89 as carbonate concentration rises, indicating that organic co-solvents do not simply dilute ionic associations but restructure them. Mean square displacement analysis shows ion dynamics decrease monotonically with carbonate content, with Li+ diffusion coefficients ranging from 0.079 × 10-12 m2/s (C1, pure carbonate) to 26.27 × 10-12 m2/s (G1, pure IL), revealing a nearly two-orders-of-magnitude dynamical range accessible through composition tuning. These findings establish a new conceptual framework wherein steric accessibility and entropic driving forces supersede dielectric constants in determining ion solvation and transport, providing design principles for next-generation hybrid electrolytes.

papers.title: Bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide anion decomposition initiated by the Solid Electrolyte Interphase
papers.abstract: Lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) is widely regarded as the leading salt for stabilizing lithium metal anodes, owing to the formation of an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and enabling Coulombic efficiencies (CE) >99.5%. Here, we identify sulfur–fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry as a previously unrecognized pathway governing the stability of FSI under cycling and aging conditions. We show that O-nucleophiles abundant at the lithium surface, including Li2O and lithium alkoxides, react with FSI to produce bis(sulfonato)imide derivatives, establishing a self-driven SEI degradation pathway. Through a detailed kinetic and crystallographic study, we isolate critical SuFEx intermediates and identify their chemical fingerprints in SEI layers. We demonstrate that methoxide-substituted FSI anions are particularly detrimental: being soluble and reduced at potentials less cathodic than FSI, they alter the SEI formation mechanism and decrease CE. These findings reframe electrolyte design strategies and suggest that suppressing SuFEx reactivity is essential for achieving sustained CE >99.9%.

papers.title: The Computational Horizon: Benchmarking AI-Driven Retrosynthesis Against a Topological Complexity Gradient.
papers.abstract: While Computer-Aided Synthesis Planning (CASP) excels at standard benchmarks, its operational limits regarding topological complexity remain undefined. This study evaluates three leading architectures Transformer-based (IBM RXN), Graph-based (ASKCOS), and Template-based (AiZynthFinder) against a curated "Complexity Gradient" of natural products ranging from industrial standards to supramolecular giants. Our results identify a deterministic "Complexity Cliff" at a Bertz Complexity Score of approximately 2,000. Below this threshold (e.g., Thymol), models achieved convergence. However, performance collapsed for stereochemically dense targets. Notably, template-based systems exhibited "Template Hallucination," generating high-confidence but chemically invalid routes for complex targets like Taxol. At the supramolecular limit (Maitotoxin, CT > 8000), all 2 architectures hit a "Zero-Shot Wall." We conclude that current AI paradigms excel at tactical pattern retrieval within a narrow window but lack the stereoelectronic reasoning required for complex de novo synthesis, necessitating a "Human-in-the-Loop" workflow.

papers.title: Manipulating diffusion energy barrier in graphene oxide subnanochannels for precise radionuclide separation and CsCl recovery
papers.abstract: Nuclear energy plays a crucial role as a low-carbon energy source. However, nuclear power generation produces large volumes of radioactive nuclear wastewater. The separation of nuclides from radioactive wastewater is essential for the safe disposal of nuclear wastes and the sustainable development of resources. Nevertheless, due to the similar properties of different radionuclide ions, achieving precise selective separation between them and recovering CsCl remains a significant challenge. Herein, a radiation-resistant graphene-based membrane with highly stable and well-ordered two-dimensional sub-nanoscale channels was constructed through ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) modification, which exhibits tunable ion diffusion energy barrier and ultra-high selectivity for radionuclide ions. The functional carboxylate groups within the GO-EDTA channel exhibit strong affinity for multivalent Sr 2+ and La 3+ . With selectivity ratios of up to 485 and 1,300 for mono/multivalent metal ions (Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /La 3+ , respectively), this membrane outperforms other previously reported membranes. Additionally, the CsCl with a purity of 99.5% was recovered using an electrodialysis discharge method. Besides, the channel maintains stable separation performance even under irradiation conditions. Furthermore, by using a quartz crystal microbalance, the contributions of partitioning at the pore entry and intrapore diffusion to the total energy barrier for salt transport were decomposed, demonstrating that precise ion separation can be achieved by modulating the diffusion energy barrier. This study provides a useful mechanism for designing membranes with high ion selectivity and highlights their potential applications in the field of nuclear resource recovery.

papers.title: RETRACTED: Alkyl Side-Chain and Ionic-Block Design of Mixed-Charge Polyurethane Copolymer Hydrogels: From Nanostructure and Viscoelasticity to Thermo-optical and Mechanical Properties
papers.abstract: Retracted by the authors because the author list is incorrect. Mixed-charge polyurethane (MCPU) copolymers with tunable alkyl side chains (C1, C6, C18) and ionic-block ratios (60%, 70%) are synthesized and assembled into single-network (SN) physical hydrogels. Three different nanostructures were identified by small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS): weakly segregated domains (C1), periodic microphase separation (C6), and microphase separation with interdigitated lamellar ordering (C18). Rheology studies provide a macroscopic relaxation timescale (τrelax) that quantifies the rate of noncovalent network rearrangement. The SN hydrogels with relatively short τrelax values (C1 and C6) exhibit thermo-optical switching, whereas C18 remains opaque. Blending the MCPU with a covalently crosslinked poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (PHEMA) network generates double-network (DN) hydrogels that preserve the thermo-optical switching performance. Monotonic tensile toughness peaks at the intermediate side chain (C6), whereas C18 maximizes modulus, strength, and per-cycle energy dissipation. However, the cyclic durability test shows that C1 survives 50,000 cycles, and C18, which dissipates the most energy per cycle, fails after only ~637 cycles. τrelax therefore tracks both the thermo-optical switchability and the cyclic durability, providing a single kinetic parameter that links them.

papers.title: Higher-order assembly enabled unconventional fluorescent hydrogel with multi-dimensional luminescent tunability
papers.abstract: Combining fluorescence and hydrogel material creates promising chemical and biological applications. Meanwhile, how to readily endue hydrogels with desired luminescent character remains challenging. Conventional methods rely on introducing alien synthetic fluorophores, which may face complicated preparation procedure, poor physiological adaptability and low optical tunability. Recently, clustering-triggered emission (CTE) demonstrates a potential alternative by enabling unconventional fluorescence of dye-free hydrogel itself. Despite the merit, most known CTE systems only absorb UV excitations and lack stimuli-responsiveness, which hinder their applications. Here, by bridging CTE with higher-order assembly (HOA), novel unconventional fluorescent hydrogels featuring multi-dimensional tunability can be created. Phase-separation constructs densely packed hierarchical structure in acrylic acid/1,2-diamine systems, rendering enhanced through-space interactions among flocks of π and n electron groups that lead to green and orange emissions under visible excitation. The controllable folding/unravel of HOA under diverse physical and chemical pathways offers such gel a variety of environmental responsiveness. Subsequently, functional devices towards sensing, dynamic display and information encryption have been fabricated. Undoubtedly, the great capability and versatility of HOA based CTE provide excellent tools for developing future soft luminescent materials.

papers.title: pH-responsive graphene oxide subnanochannels for sustainable lithium recovery from spent lithium ion battery
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of electric vehicles is expected to significantly increase the production volume of spent lithium-ion batteries. Separation of lithium from complex spent battery leaching solution is crucial for critical metal recovery and the sustainability of the circular economy. However, achieving precise separation between Li+ and competing multivalent ions remains a challenge due to their similar hydrated radii. In this study, an EDTA-functionalized graphene oxide membrane that exhibits pH-responsive properties and ultrahigh selectivity for monovalent and divalent ions was constructed. The EDTA ligands anchored within the nanochannels demonstrate pH-dependent coordination chemistry: under neutral or alkaline conditions, deprotonated EDTA binds strongly to multivalent cations, effectively gating the channels and facilitating preferential Li+ permeation. Conversely, under acidic conditions, the protonation of the carboxyl groups in EDTA weakens its binding to divalent ions. This results in a Li + /M 2+ selectivity of 300 under neutral or alkaline conditions, surpassing previously reported membranes. Additionally, through electrodialysis, a Li 2 CO 3 product with a purity of 98.5% was obtained. Furthermore, using quartz crystal microbalance, we decoupled the contributions of partitioning and diffusion energy barriers to the overall transport energy barrier, revealing that precise ion separation is achieved by modulating the diffusion barrier through pH-responsive coordination. This work provides mechanistic insights for the design of membranes with high ion selectivity and demonstrates the potential for sustainable lithium recovery from spent batteries.

papers.title: Q2Performance: Towards unbiased selection of machine learning regression models
papers.abstract: Selecting a single best machine learning regression model from a set of competing models can be challenging. While models selected based on cross-validation performance do not guarantee good predictions on external data, models selected solely on external validation performance do not ascertain precise predictions for other external sets. Therefore, we propose three quantitative metrics to guide modelers in selecting the best model. Three quantitative datasets of varying sizes and complexities were considered. Each dataset was randomly split into a modeling set and an independent external test set. The modeling set was further split thrice to generate training and validation sets. Various machine learning models were developed and validated against the validation sets. Our proposed metrics were computed for each model using only training and validation set performances. The novel metric values guided the selection of the best models, which also demonstrated expected performance on the independent external test set.

papers.title: Simultaneous selective recognition of two different anions within a hydrogen/halogen bonding cage
papers.abstract: The search for selective anion receptors that can function in water is a longstanding challenge in supramolecular chemistry, motivated by anions’ fundamental roles (and potential applications) in biological, environmental and industrial processes. Here we incorporate halogen and hydrogen bond donors into an easy-toprepare organic cage molecule and demonstrate that this can bind anions at either or both of a halogen bonding pocket and hydrogen bonding pockets depending on the nature of the anions and the solvent. The halogen bonding pocket comprised of six bromopyridinium donors is a potent host for iodide anions, and can selectively bind this guest in water as strongly as biological iodide binders (Ka = 43,000 M–1 measured by 1H NMR spectroscopy) with the exclusion of other halide anions. In DMSO/water mixtures, the hydrogen bonding pockets are able to recognise chloride anions, resulting in the formation of well-defined mixed anion iodide/chloride complexes with an iodide bound in the centre of the cage and chlorides in the peripheral binding sites. This demonstrates the exquisite selectivity afforded by halogen bonding systems and reveals a general route to a range of supramolecular anion hosts that bind multiple guests in different locations.

papers.title: Globally Antiaromatic Anthracene-Porphyrin Nanobelts
papers.abstract: Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented p-orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, displaying global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here, we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts exhibit global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96, or 120 π electrons, as revealed by 1 H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

papers.title: A phase field model for reactive liquid-solid systems
papers.abstract: Chemical precipitation is widely employed in industry, and improving the understanding of its underlying mechanisms is crucial for optimizing chemical engineering processes. The phase field method is frequently utilized to simulate multiphase processes; however, traditional phase field models encounter significant difficulties when simulating chemical precipitation, particularly in constructing multivariable free energy functions for complex, reactive liquid-solid transition systems. Here, a novel phase field framework is proposed to describe the microstructure evolution in reactive liquid-solid systems. In this model, an independent single-variable free energy function is constructed for each reaction in a multi-reaction system, replacing the complex multi-variable chemical free energy function shared by all reactions in the traditional phase field models, significantly reducing the difficulty of constructing the free energy functions. Inclusion growth during the steel refining process is employed as a benchmark case to demonstrate the capability of our new model. Simulation results show that the model successfully characterizes the shift in reaction equilibrium and the non-uniform spatiotemporal distribution of solutes and phases during the chemical precipitation process, unravelling a series of coupling effects arising from these phenomena.

papers.title: Computational studies on the enantioinversion of the molecular asymmetry of multiple chirality elements
papers.abstract: A series of quantum mechanical calculations and kinetic analysis was conducted on enantioinversion processes involving multiple chiral elements, with a particular focus on winding vine-shaped biaryls (bithiophene with/without methyl substituent and biphenyl types) exhibiting molecular asymmetry in both axial and planar chiralities. The inversions of the chiral elements were shown to take place in a stepwise manner, whereas the experimental racemization behavior appeared kinetically synchronized. Conformational analysis of the vine-shaped bithiophene revealed eight possible conformers for the pair of enantiomers using the CONFLEX method. Quantum mechanics calculations were carried out at the B3LYP/6-31G(d)//B3LYP/6-31G(d), B3LYP/6-311G++(d,p)+GD3//B3LYP/6-31G(d), MP2/cc-pVDZ//MP2/cc-pVDZ, and MP2/cc-pVTZ//MP2/cc-pVDZ levels of theory. Calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G(d) level were primarily used to search for each pathway, revealing that enantioinversion proceeded via three distinct steps. The first conformational transition leading to the second intermediate was calculated to occur with an activation energy of Δ E = 49.2 kJ/mol, without the inversion of chirality. Subsequently, an inversion of axial chirality was observed with a value of ΔE = 106.5 kJ/mol. This was followed by the final inversion of planar chirality, which also exhibited a value of Δ E = 70.3 kJ/mol. It was also established that the enantioinversion of the related biphenyl occurred in a manner analogous to that previously observed, whereas the inversion barrier of the axial chirality was found to be considerably higher (Δ E = 217.9 kJ/mol). The analytical solutions of the rate of racemization and pathway contributions under the quasi-equilibrium approximation were derived, which assumes rapid equilibration of low-barrier conformational changes while treating the kinetics of axial chirality inversion explicitly. DFT studies were conducted also on the enantioinversion of the vine-shaped bithiophene bearing a methyl substituent at the alkenyl moiety. This was because experimental evidence had shown that this process had hardly occurred. The DFT studies revealed that a much higher barrier existed at the initial inversion (Δ E = 205.9 kJ/mol). Conversely, a high barrier has not been identified in the calculation of the second transition state, where the dihedral angle of the axial chirality is estimated to be 0°.

papers.title: Operator Entanglement in Quantum Dynamics Simulations: Formalism and Analysis Tools
papers.abstract: We review the framework of operator Hilbert space and introduce the one-and two-particle super reduced density matrices (1-SRDMs and 2-SRDMs), as well as the super mutual information (SMI). The eigenvectors of the 1-SRDMs define what we term natural single particle operator bases, and provide a way to compress vibrational and vibronic Hamiltonians with controlled error. The SMI is defined from the operator entanglement entropy of the 1-SRDMs and 2-SRDMs, and captures the correlation between operators acting on different one-mode subspaces, which may be used to reveal and quantify both direct and indirect couplings that might otherwise be difficult to extract. Efficient numerical approaches for the calculation of SRDMs and the SMI are developed and applied to a set of prototypical vibrational and vibronic Hamiltonians, as well as approximations to the corresponding time-evolution operators. Through this, we demonstrate that: (i) commonly used vibronic Hamiltonians are amenable to extremely high levels of compression without compromising accuracy, and; (ii) SMI analysis can be used to systematically and quantitatively reveal both direct and indirect couplings that might otherwise be difficult to extract, including indirect couplings of vibrational modes via intermediary electronic-vibrational interactions.

papers.title: Sisyphus: A Topology-Compiled Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Platform with Structure-Only Input and Bayesian Parameter Refinement
Red-Light Tomographic Volumetric 3D Printing in Seconds for Fabrication of Colorless Structures
papers.abstract: Non-pulsed red light photopolymerization is attractive for volumetric additive manufacturing because longer wavelengths can improve light penetration, lower scattering, and reduce photodamage compared with ultra-violet or blue irradiation. In this work, we utilized methylene blue and triethanolamine as a sacrificial type II photoinitiating system for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel printing with a custom-made red-light tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing system. With the optimized formulation, PEGDA hydrogel structures were printed by red light within 30 s. The resulting constructs were colorless, extractable, and contained fully formed internal channels. This work establishes a type II photochemistry system as a promising route for extending tomographic volumetric 3D printing toward lower-energy visible-light irradiation and rapid fabrication of colorless hydrogel constructs.

papers.title: The Redox Array: Streamlined Ion-Electron Balancing
papers.abstract: The Redox Array (RA) is presented as a compact representation of the ion-electron method for balancing redox equations. The approach organises half-reaction-derived integers into a simple array structure, reducing intermediate transcription and repeated notation during balancing procedures. The RA is designed to consolidate intermediate simplification into a single stage, and provides a unified bookkeeping framework for both acidic and basic systems. The method is intended as a supplementary procedural tool for practitioners already familiar with conventional half-reaction balancing.

papers.title: Automated Active Space Selection with CASCI Dipole Moments
papers.abstract: Multireference calculations are well-suited for describing properties of highly correlated systems. In order to realize the full potential of multireference methods, it is necessary to judiciously choose the active space. It is possible to do this manually, but an automatic procedure for selecting the active space can benefit high-throughput applications and is not susceptible to human error. We previously developed two protocols, GDM-AS and EDM-AS, where the dipole moment calculated at the complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) level of theory is used to select the active space, and demonstrated the effectiveness of these protocols when the chosen active spaces are used to find low-lying excitation energies for molecules with non-zero dipole moments. In this work, we demonstrate that using complete active space configuration interaction (CASCI) dipole moments, with the orbitals from the second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory, instead of CASSCF dipole moments in our dipole moment active space selection (DM-AS) protocols can significantly improve the efficiency of active space selection compared to our previous methods while maintaining reasonable complete active space second-order perturbation theory (CASPT2) and complete active space pair-density functional theory (CAS-PDFT) vertical excitation energy. We also present new protocols, CASCI-D 2 DM-AS and its directional version, designed for charge transfer states. We discuss the performance of our new protocols in their ability to describe excitation energy of not only small organic molecules tested in our previous work, but also larger conjugated polar molecules, nonpolar molecules, and bimolecular complexes, to describe the ground-state spin state of transition metal oxides, and to describe bond dissociation curves of small molecules.

papers.title: Gas-Phase Fragmentation in Mass Spectrometry Informs the Shape and Topology of Thiolated Metal Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Thiolated metal nanoclusters (NCs), comprising a metal core protected by outer-layer staple motifs, have attracted widespread interest due to their promising applications in catalysis, biosensing, and biomedicine. While mass spectrometry (MS) is widely used to determine the chemical composition of metal NCs via intact mass measurement, its potential for in-depth structural analysis via gas-phase fragmentation in tandem MS (MS/MS) remains largely underexplored due to insufficient understanding of the fundamentals. Herein, we used collision-induced dissociation (CID), surface-induced dissociation (SID) and ion mobility (IM) to systematically investigate the dissociation pathways of model Au NCs featuring distinct symmetries and structural motifs. We demonstrate that gas-phase fragments in CID and SID overall shared the common fragmentation behavior of breaking the outer staples of Au NCs, but with different preferences in the location of bond cleavages. In addition, SID showed characteristic Au losses in ellipsoidal Au NCs with trimeric staples; and fragmentation efficiency in CID and SID varied differentially according to the shape of the NCs. Building on these findings, we applied the method to study non-crystallizable Au-Ag NCs with heterogeneous stoichiometry. The SID fragmentation data helped locate the Au and Ag atoms, providing valuable insights into the synthetic pathway of the NCs, which was otherwise inaccessible experimentally. Together, these results establish MS/MS as a structurally sensitive tool for metal NCs, with particular promise for heterogeneous systems that cannot be easily crystallized.

papers.title: Large-Scale Virtual Screening Prioritizes Candidate Allosteric Modulators of TIMP2: Computational Identification and Structural Characterization of a Cryptic Binding Site
papers.abstract: Background: Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-2 (TIMP2) has emerged as a critical regulator of synaptic plasticity and cognitive function through its role in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Recent evidence suggests that enhancing TIMP2 function, rather than inhibiting it, may offer therapeutic benefits for cognitive enhancement and neuroplasticity. However, TIMP2 has historically been considered "undruggable" due to its protein-protein interaction mechanism and lack of traditional binding pockets. Methods: We performed a large-scale virtual screening campaign using a CNS-filtered subset of the ZINC20 database. Starting from ~1 billion molecules, we applied strict CNS drug-likeness filters (MW: 250-430 Da, TPSA ≤70 Å², HBD ≤1, cLogP: 2.0-3.5), resulting in 13.6 million candidates distributed across 136 chunks. Using AutoDock Vina with an adaptive parallelization strategy, we screened six strategically selected representative chunks totaling ~600,000 molecules against TIMP2 (PDB: 1BR9), targeting both canonical and potential cryptic binding sites. Results: Virtual screening of six completed chunks (~600,000 molecules) identified a cryptic allosteric site involving residues Val6, Leu100, and Phe103 in TIMP2's N-terminal domain. From ~11,500 compounds meeting initial CNS and PAINS criteria, comprehensive ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI v2.1 revealed only 178 compounds (1.5%) achieving Tier 1 safety classification. Orthogonal toxicity validation using ProTox-III further refined this set to 154 highest-confidence candidates (Tier 1A, 86.5%), with 22 compounds (12.4%) requiring enhanced monitoring due to borderline acute toxicity (Tier 1B) and 2 compounds (1.1%) deprioritized due to extreme LD50 predictions (Tier 1C). Chunk-level survival rates varied dramatically from 0.3% (strict_0055) to 9.3% (strict_0028), with strict_0028 yielding the majority (52%) of all Tier 1 compounds. Notably, while halogenation is common (41.6% of Tier 1 compounds), it is not universal, with strict_0028 demonstrating that non-halogenated compounds can also achieve favorable ADMET profiles. The best overall compound (ZINC000870248439_1, -9.0 kcal/mol from strict_0120) and the largest chemical family (93 compounds from strict_0028, including both chlorinated and non-halogenated scaffolds) demonstrated excellent CNS penetration (BBB >0.9) and clean safety profiles. Conclusions : This work represents the first systematic computational prioritization of candidate small-molecule TIMP2 modulators and reveals a previously uncharacterized cryptic binding site that accommodates diverse chemical scaffolds. Integration of ADMET-AI and ProTox-III predictions enabled refined risk stratification, yielding 154 highest-confidence candidates validated across orthogonal computational toxicology platforms. The dramatic variation in ADMET survival rates across chunks (0.3-9.3%) highlights the importance of broad chemical space sampling. While halogenation enhances certain drug-like properties, our results demonstrate that both halogenated and non-halogenated compounds can achieve the demanding intersection of high affinity, CNS penetration, and drug safety. Structural validation using the AlphaFold v6 predicted structure confirmed the cryptic allosteric pocket with sub-angstrom accuracy (mean Cα deviation = 0.30 Å, triad pLDDT > 96), and cross-species conservation analysis revealed 100% pocket identity in mouse TIMP2, the primary translational model. Molecular dynamics simulation (100 ns apo) confirmed pocket stability under physiological conditions with 94% area preservation, sub-angstrom per-residue fluctuations (triad RMSF = 0.84 Å), and convergence of triad distances to within 0.14-0.43 Å of crystallographic values. Ligand-bound MD of seven representative compounds revealed compound-specific binding behavior ranging from complete dissociation (<7 ns) to persistent pocket occupancy over 100 ns. Two structurally distinct benzamide compounds maintained >96% heavy-atom contact over 100 ns: ZINC000583127796 (304 Da, spirocyclic thiolane, 98.7% contact, Phe103-anchored binding with pocket opening to 36.4 Å²) and ZINC001228612316 (268 Da, cyclopropane, 96.7% contact, balanced triad engagement with crystal-geometry preservation at 31.2 Å²). Across all seven compounds, persistent binding tracked with a primary benzamide that anchors at Phe103 plus a compact, conformationally restricted appendage rather than any single ring type: the two persistent binders carried different rings (a five-membered thiolane and a three-membered cyclopropane), and a benzamide compound bearing a larger, more flexible six-membered thioether dissociated. Ensemble re-docking across nine apo MD conformations spanning the 100 ns trajectory indicated that Site 1 remains ligand-compatible, with the lead accepted in every conformation, arguing against a single-conformation artifact. These results demonstrate that the cryptic pocket supports stable small-molecule binding through more than one persistent binding mode and point to a preliminary pharmacophore hypothesis—benzamide-mediated Phe103 anchoring together with geometric constraint in the appendage—for experimental optimization. These findings support TIMP2 as a potentially tractable drug target and provide 154 computationally validated chemical starting points across diverse scaffolds for experimental follow-up.

papers.title: Axial-ligand-induced spin-state modulation switching catalytic selectivity of single-atom nanozymes for bubble-propelled nanomotors
papers.abstract: Regulating the selectivity of single-atom nanozymes (SAzymes) is highly significant yet challenging, especially for heme-like M–N 4 structured SAzymes, which exhibit powerful enzyme-like catalytic efficiency and broad applicability. Inspired by the axial-ligand-regulated, Fe=O-axis-oriented local electric fields in natural heme metalloenzymes, which switches selectivity within a shared metal–oxo manifold, we synthesized FeNSC–O SAzymes featuring axial oxygen coordination stabilized by planar sulfur doping, achieving a catalase/peroxidase–like selectivity up to 7.4 times greater than that of planar oxygen-doped FeNC–O SAzymes. Low-temperature EPR, magnetic susceptibility measurements, and further DFT analyses revealed that axial oxygen coordination simultaneously withdraws electrons from Fe and stabilizes an intermediate-spin Fe center, thereby reducing spin polarization and weakening Fe–O orbital overlap with oxygen-containing intermediates, which suppresses the peroxide pathway and enhances catalase-like selectivity. Furthermore, encapsulating FeNSC–O within asymmetric hollow nanoreactors enabled the successful construction of H 2 O 2 -responsive, bubble-propelled nanomotors capable of efficient oxygen generation for active inflammatory-cell penetration and intracellular ROS scavenging, demonstrating promising potential for targeted therapy and precision medicine.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it is an unintentional duplication of 10.26434/chemrxiv.15007269/v1.

papers.title: Biocatalysts for peptide geranylation with linear and cyclic prenyl groups
papers.abstract: Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo- and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. In contrast, the prenyltransferase-terpene cyclase fusion enzyme NctPC installs a polycyclic isoprenoid moiety during biosynthesis of the ribosomal peptide natural product steromaze. However, the two characterized steromaze-like prenyltransferases require at least the presence of a macrocyclic (methyl) lanthionine ring as a prerequisite for prenylation. Here, we report the characterization of standalone NctPC homologs, the steromaze-like prenyltransferase NdnP and the terpene cyclase NdnC, further expanding the chemical space of ribosomal peptides with cyclic isoprenoid moieties. NdnP is highly promiscuous for the geranylation of peptides containing C-terminal tryptophan from ribosomal and synthetic origin without being leader- or modification-dependent. The terpene cyclase NdnC utilizes the geranylated tryptophan to yield a tetracyclic amino acid at the peptide C-terminus. The promiscuity of both enzymes for ribosomal and synthetic peptides makes them promising biocatalysts for lipopeptide drug development creating so far enzymatically inaccessible peptide terpenoid hybrids.

papers.title: Hyperbranched Networks that Mimic Experience-Dependent Synaptogenesis
papers.abstract: Neuromorphic systems that dynamically restructure their physical connectivity are essential for emulating adaptive behavior of biological neural networks. Here, we present a self-organizing conductive network based on electrodeposited copper dendrites guided by soft, self-assembled surfactant myelin structures. Under sustained electrical stimulation, conductive dendritic pathways emerge, extend, and stabilize, resembling experience-dependent synaptogenesis and dendritic spine formation in biological neurons. In contrast, weakly stimulated pathways progressively dissolve, exhibiting network pruning, analogous to synaptic elimination through disuse. The network displays Hebbian-like behavior, enabling direct correlation between persistent conductance changes associated with memory formation and the structural evolution of conductive pathways. By visualizing growth, reinforcement, and decay processes in real time, we directly observe how electrical input, local geometry, and electrochemical interactions cooperatively shape adaptive network connectivity. These findings establish a physically accessible platform for studying coupled structural and functional plasticity, and provide a route toward neuromorphic hardware with evolving topology and adaptive memory.

papers.title: Theoretical and computational chemistry in Brazil (1981-2023): a small language model (SLM) approach to analyzing scientific trends from the abstracts of the Brazilian Symposium of Theoretical
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are lightweight language models designed for efficient local deployment and task-specific adaptation. In this study, an SLM-based workflow was developed to analyze more than 5,000 one-page abstracts from the biannual Brazilian Symposium of Theoretical Chemistry from 1981 to 2023. We identified the main Brazilian states and universities contributing to the proceedings, most of which are in the wealthy Southeastern region. Brazilian theoretical and computational chemistry expanded strongly from the 1980s to the 2000s, followed by a decline and stabilization in the 2010s and early 2020s, likely influenced by changes in science funding. Although the number of abstracts and participants fluctuates with research funding over time, it has stabilized at around 300 since 1997. Research funding has been dominated by the federal agencies CNPq and Capes, but state foundations have made relevant contributions. The most popular theoretical methods over time include Configuration Interaction (CI), Molecular Dynamics (MD), and Density Functional Theory (DFT). CI calculations have been reported since the 1980s, whereas MD abstracts have focused on biomolecules. While the initial applications of DFT followed the rest of the world, investigations using the most advanced exchange-correlation functionals and dispersion corrections lag by 5-8 years. The local development of methods and software is very incipient, despite some successful cases. However, we identified serious delays in Brazilian theoretical and computational chemistry, relative to the rest of the world, in machine learning techniques, automated workflows, high-performance GPU architectures, and benchmarking. Given that most studies focus on molecular electronic structure calculations, the most widely used software is for this type of research. Open-source ORCA, which is increasingly used in Brazil, is one of the most important computational chemistry packages for molecular calculations and provides access to advanced electronic-structure methods, whereas solidstate DFT calculations with periodic boundary conditions remain relatively scarce. The most studied subjects are intra- and inter-proton, electron, and charge-transfer chemical phenomena. Hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions have also been widely studied, with water and benzene being the most studied molecules. Beyond reconstructing the development of theoretical and computational chemistry in Brazil, this study demonstrates that SLM-based semantic extraction can provide a scalable, low-cost, and reproducible strategy for analyzing long-term scientific trends in conference proceedings and other historical scientific archives.

papers.title: Kinetic Boundary between Autocatalysis and Diffusion in the Origin of Life
papers.abstract: A key characteristic of living systems is the ability to reproduce themselves using external chemical species. Autocatalysis is considered to be the core chemical mechanism underlying this function, and is under intense investigation regarding the origin of life. However, the presence of autocatalysis does not guarantee a sustainable chemical system, because the natural environment is an open system where chemical species diffuse away. Under such conditions, autocatalytic feedback must be above a certain kinetic threshold to maintain chemical concentrations. Here, we quantify the kinetic requirements for an autocatalytic network to be homeostatic in an open environment. In particular, we have obtained an analytical formula for the effective amplification rate, which characterizes the boundary between sustainable and unsustainable protometabolism. This equation shows stronger autocatalysis is required for larger protometabolic networks, because more species can be lost to diffusion. As diffusion occurs only at the boundary between interior and exterior environments, one possibility to suppress its influence relative to autocatalysis is to decrease the surface to volume ratio. Indeed, increasing the cell size from µm scale to cm scale relaxes the rate constants of autocatalysis by 8 orders of magnitude, suggesting that pores and channels within deep sea hydrothermal vents may have acted as the first cell walls for early life. We expect our approach of decomposing chemical reaction networks into components that either maintain or change the total amount of chemical species can be applied to other chemical systems where homeostasis is important.

papers.title: The Validation Split Defines the Discovery Claim in AI-Guided MOF Screening
papers.abstract: Machine learning is becoming a gatekeeper for metal–organic framework (MOF) discovery, but its credibility depends on whether validation matches the chemistry of deployment. Here, we show that the train/test split is not a technical choice, but the statement of what a model can legitimately support. In a controlled, database-scale adsorption benchmark, we hold targets, descriptors, models, hyperparameters, and metrics fixed while comparing random, geometry-, metal-cluster-, functional-group-, linker-, and topology-held-out splits for CO2 and CH4 uptake. Random, geometry-, functional-group-, and linker-held-out evaluations support broadly similar conclusions, whereas metal-cluster and especially topology holdouts reveal much harsher transfer regimes. For CO2 uptake at 0.15 bar, random-forest performance drops from R2 = 0.758 under random splitting to 0.267 under topology grouping, and top-5% recovery falls from 62.2% to 37.6%. We introduce split-aware, structurally auditable validation as a foundation for trustworthy AI-guided porous-material discovery. Significance statement. High-throughput MOF screening increasingly uses machine learning to decide which candidates should be simulated, synthesized, or inspected experimentally. This paper shows that such decisions cannot be judged by random-split accuracy alone. The same data, descriptors, models, and metrics can support a strong interpolation claim while weakening under a harder reticular-transfer claim. By treating the split as a chemistry-facing variable, we show that validation design changes not only regression scores, but also the identity of candidate shortlists. The resulting validation framework turns model evaluation into a traceable materials-screening argument: define the transfer problem, disclose elite-list survival, and route validation-fragile candidates to structural inspection, uncertainty analysis, additional simulation, or targeted data acquisition.

papers.title: Tuning Photochromism in Multivariate Zinc Dipyridyl-Naphthalenediimide Coordination Polymers
papers.abstract: Multivariate compositions of zinc halide dipyridyl-naphthalenediimide coordination polymers are shown to directly tune photochromic response through modification of halide lone pair-NDI LUMO overlap. Photochromic materials have attracted widespread attention for applications in data storage, sensing and catalysis among many others.1–7 Naphthalenediimides (NDIs) in particular are an extensively studied family of often photochromic compounds. This property arises from the NDI’s electron-poor aromatic core and a low-lying LUMO which makes them readily reduced to a radical anion (NDI˙−), a process which is usually accompanied by a change in colour of the NDI-containing material.8,9 In addition, NDIs are readily modified through synthetically facile substitution of functional motifs in their imide positions,10 or directly onto the naphthyl core.11 These qualities make NDIs a popular choice in constructing functional crystalline materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) and simple cocrystals.12–14 Crystalline NDI containing materials are attractive as the crystal engineering approach can be employed to tune electron-donor to electron-acceptor interfaces, while crystallography can inform the researcher on the precise inter- or intramolecular interactions which may give rise to the formation of the aforementioned NDI radical species, something which can be more challenging in the solution phase.15–17 In addition, crystal packing (particularly through π-stacking) can stabilise organic radicals, something which is attractive both for the investigation of radical species, but also in applications.18,19 Notably for crystalline materials such as coordination polymers (CPs) or MOFs, a multivariate-MOF (MTV-MOF) or multivariate-CP (MTV-CP) approach can be exploited wherein the composition of different metals or ligands can be systematically varied within a single polymer to tune the properties of the material.20-

papers.title: Adsorption of Molecular Nitrogen on Nickel-based Catalysts Studied by Infrared Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The performance of supported heterogeneous catalysts depends on their nanostructure and surface site distribution, in what is known as structure sensitivity. Molecular nitrogen (N2) adsorption on metal surfaces, which can be studied by infrared (IR) spectroscopy, was proposed as a method to probe for specific catalyst sites, such as the so-called B5 sites. However, discording evidence was presented in the literature, and spectral interpretation remains a point of discussion. In this work, we studied N2 adsorption on supported Ni/SiO2 catalysts using IR spectroscopy.
