papers.abstract: High-throughput and autonomous experimentation generate complex, heterogeneous datasets whose reuse, large-scale analysis, and linking to data from first-principles calculations remain challenging. Here, we report on an operational deployment of the open-source NOMAD Oasis data infrastructure as a digital backbone for daily high-throughput experimental work in a materials discovery group at DTU Nanolab. The customized platform supports the complete experimental workflow in a thin-film laboratory, linking physical inventory items, automated synthesis logs, high-throughput characterization data, and cloud-based analysis within a unified data model. The platform preserves full sample provenance across multi-step workflows and uses unified sample coordinates to enable direct cross-technique correlation. We demonstrate the capabilities of the platform on a combined experimental-computational project centered on phosphosulfide thin-film libraries. The data consists of 12,000 experimental samples acquired during routine operation over 18 months, complemented by more than 800 first-principles calculations - all managed in a unified data platform available at https://nomad.nanolab.dtu.dk/nomad-oasis/gui/search/combinatorial-samples . We show how an open, extensible data infrastructure system supports reproducible workflows, scalable analysis, and long-term data reuse.

papers.title: Unanticipated Enhancement to Phosphide Nucleophilicity in Dimethyl Sulfoxide for Advanced Catalytic P-C Bond Formation Reactions
papers.abstract: An exceptional nucleophilicity of phosphide (R2P-) was discovered for reactions conducted in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and leveraged for catalytic P-C bond formation. A range of simple bases affect this reactivity, and sodium hydroxide was chosen for deeper analysis due to its simplicity and abundance. This enhanced reactivity is not solely due to the high dielectric constant of DMSO or super base formation, rather aspects of phosphine association, proton management, and solubility drive the enhanced reactivity, based on comparison between solvents and spectroscopic analysis. The impact of this enhanced reactivity is substantial. Ring-opening reactions of epoxide and cyclopropane substrates are possible under catalytic conditions at ambient temperature. Likewise, hydrophosphination of a sweeping range of alkene and alkyne substrates is accessible at ambient temperature. To further demonstrate the utility of this simple, inexpensive, and water-tolerant catalysis, the catalytic preparation of phosphonium salts was also demonstrated. Despite tremendous advances in s-block catalysts, the hydroxide/DMSO combination provides the greatest combination of activation and versatility of any known P-C bond forming catalyst.

papers.title: Data-Driven Optimization of the Solid-Solution Ratio of Stannitetype CuxAg2-xZnGeySn1-yS4 photocatalysts Using Machine-Learning with Chemically Similar Out-of-Plane Data
Intracellular peptide nanofibers enhance T cell fitness and anti-cancer activity
papers.abstract: Cellular immunotherapies have transformed cancer treatment, yet their efficacy depends on the metabolic fitness and effector functions of therapeutic T cells. Here, we present synthetic peptides that self-assemble into nanofibrils within cytotoxic T cells, enhancing their anti-cancer activity. Correlative light and electron microscopy reveals intracellular nanofibrils that stiffen the cellular architecture and promote phosphorylation of key signaling proteins. Transcriptomic analysis shows upregulation of core metabolic pathways and stress responses, suggesting enhanced nutrient utilization and cellular fitness. Functionally, T cells containing synthetic nanostructures exhibit enhanced cytotoxicity in a bispecific engager model against breast cancer cells. By engineering non-disruptive synthetic nanostructures inside T cells, we can tune the immune cell phenotype and performance, offering a potential avenue to further advance cellular immunotherapies.

papers.title: Activity-cliff awareness enables robust graph learning for molecular property prediction
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting molecular activity is hindered by activity cliffs (ACs), which are sharp potency changes between highly similar compounds that distort the smoothness assumed by modern quantitative structure–activity relationship (SAR) models and graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we introduce AC awareness (ACA), an inductive bias that reshapes GNN latent spaces to account for these discontinuities. Implemented through an ACA loss combining regression with softmargin triplet contrastive learning, the method dynamically mines high-value activity-cliff triplets during training and corrects inconsistent neighbourhoods in latent space. This process yields progressively fewer cliff violations, more coherent activity gradients, and reduced label incoherence across diverse chemical spaces. Evaluated on 52 datasets spanning low-sample narrow-scaffold series, large mixed-scaffold benchmarks, matched-pair cliff classification, and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) property prediction, ACA consistently improves predictive accuracy over strong extended-connectivity fingerprint (ECFP) and GNN baselines. The approach generalizes across multiple GNN backbones and remains robust under fixed hyperparameters. These results suggest that ACA provides a principled strategy for enhancing molecular property prediction by aligning latent representations with the nonadditive behaviour underlying ACs.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Skeletal Editing of Furans to Pyridazines Using Hydrazine as Nitrogen Source
papers.abstract: We report a photocatalytic strategy for the direct skeletal editing of furans into pyridazines, achieving a formal oxygen-to-two-nitrogen (O-to-N2) ring-atom replacement in a single synthetic operation. By exploiting the polarity-inversion reactivity of acridinium-based photoredox catalysis, the hydrazine hydrate is oxidized to electrophilic radical cations that react with furan. DFT calculations reveal a mechanistically significant selectivity in one-electron oxidation: the acridinium photocatalyst preferentially oxidizes hydrazine over furan, generating an electrophilic hydrazinyl radical that initiates nucleophilic addition to the furan ring. The subsequent ring-opening and recyclization sequence furnishes substituted pyridazines in synthetically useful yields. This transformation bridges the electronic polarity gap between electron-rich furans and electron-deficient pyridazines, enabling rapid access to structurally diverse pyridazine scaffolds from readily available furan derivatives. A broad substrate scope encompassing alkyl-, aryl-, halo-, cyano-, ester-, and ether-substituted furans was demonstrated, along with late-stage diversification of complex molecules.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it is an incomplete duplicate of another preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv.15004715/v1).

papers.title: SabreSDN: A Complex-Valued 1D U-Net for Denoising SABRE-Hyperpolarized NMR Spectra at Low Concentration
papers.abstract: Signal Amplification By Reversible Exchange (SABRE) can enhance nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) signals by several thousand-fold through para-hydrogen-derived hyperpolarization. However, at low substrate concentrations (50~$\mu$M and below), the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) remains insufficient for reliable spectral analysis, particularly in time-resolved measurements where signal averaging is precluded by the finite hyperpolarization lifetime. Traditional denoising methods such as exponential windowing and Cadzow filtering rely on manually tuned parameters and fail to preserve fine spectral features. We introduce SabreSDN (SABRE Signal Denoising Network), a complex-valued 1D U-Net that operates directly on complex NMR spectra (8192~points, real and imaginary channels). The network incorporates four key architectural components: (1)~complex convolutions (CConv1d) that encode the absorption--dispersion Hilbert-transform relationship as a structural prior, halving parameter count relative to unconstrained real-valued convolutions; (2)~CBAM1d attention modules that jointly model channel-wise and frequency-axis feature importance; (3)~a MultiScaleBlock bottleneck with parallel dilated convolutions (dilation~1,~4,~8) to simultaneously capture narrow singlets, $J$-coupled multiplets, and broad spectral features; and (4)~gated skip connections that selectively suppress noisy encoder features during decoding. Training uses a three-component composite loss that allocates $4\times$ higher weight to peak-containing regions ($\sim$2.4\% of spectral points) together with frequency-domain amplitude matching and baseline smoothness regularization. Trained on 50~$\mu$M SABRE-hyperpolarized $^{19}$F NMR data (20,000 noisy--clean pairs, 80/20 train/val split across 50~epochs), the model reduces validation loss from 0.162 to 0.024. Denoised spectra show clear recovery of $J$-coupling multiplet fine structure with minimal baseline distortion. With 7.71~million parameters and $\sim$2~ms GPU inference per spectrum, SabreSDN is practical for integration into existing SABRE NMR acquisition pipelines. Code and model weights are available at \url{ https://github.com/kimariyb/SABRE-Denoise }.

papers.title: Ultra-small iridium oxide nanoparticles: from one-pot hydrothermal synthesis to oxygen evolution reaction catalyst
papers.abstract: Iridium oxide nanoparticles are efficient catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). We present a straightforward one-pot hydrothermal synthesis method to produce sub-1 nm Ir oxide nanoparticles in a single step, with size control achieved through post-synthesis annealing. By combining X-ray total scattering and pair distribution function (PDF) analysis with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), we find that the sub-nanometer-sized oxide has an increased number of edge-sharing [IrO6]-octahedra compared to the thermodynamically favorable rutile structure. PDF modelling using various cluster motifs reveals that a sheet-like cluster, derived from rutile and comprising seven [IrO6]-octahedra with a (110)-exposed surface, can describe the increased Ir-Ir edge-sharing connectivity. We further find that cluster growth leads to a decrease in the number of edge-sharing motifs, going towards the bulk rutile structure upon annealing. Operando X-ray total scattering and PDF analysis during OER reveal high structural stability of the ultrasmall (<3 nm) Ir oxides.

papers.title: Relative Stability of Metal Complexes with Various Diene Ligands: Experimental and Computational Study
papers.abstract: The binding strength of various dienes was established by NMR investigation of ligand exchange reactions in (diene)Rh(acac) complexes. The binding affinity decreases in the following order: tetraphenyl-cyclopentadienone > 1,5-cyclooctadiene > norbornadiene > tetrafluoro-benzobarrelene > dimethyl-tetrafluoro-benzobarrelene > bis(carboxymethyl)-norbornadiene >> bis(tert-butyl)-1,4-quinone > 1,5-hexadiene > bis(carboxymethyl)-2,2,2-bicyclooctadiene > carvone > 1,4-benzoquinone. The experimental data was used to confirm that B97-3c can serve as fast and robust computation method for predicting coordination strength (average deviation 1.1 kcal mol−1). Computational screening of metal-diene combinations demonstrated that the nature of the metal center is a more important factor than the structure of the diene. In accordance with Dewar-Chatt-Duncanson model electron-rich metal fragments form more stable diene complexes. Electron-withdrawing cyclopentadienones and benzoquinones were identified as strong ligands, which look promising for further investigation in catalysis.

papers.title: Outcome of Anodic Current Density Variation in Constant Cathodic Current under Bipolar Condition during the Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation (PEO) of AZ91D Mg Alloys
papers.abstract: Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation is a promising technique to form a protective ceramic layer over Mg and its alloys. However, the underlying mechanism behind the parameters is still unclear. Therefore, ceramic coatings have been fabricated on the AZ91D Mg alloys during the Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation (PEO) process by varying anodic current density. The formed coatings were characterized using SEM, XRD, and potentio-dynamic polarization (EIS). It has been found that optimized positive current density in bipolar condition improves the microstructure, and chemical stability of the coating.

papers.title: Iterative Constructing and Screening of DNA-Encoded Libraries Enable the Discovery and Structure Optimization of Macrocyclic Hit Compounds
papers.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides occupy a privileged "middle space" in drug discovery, offering the specificity of biologics combined with the synthetic tractability of small molecules. However, the rapid identification and structural optimization of macrocyclic leads for challenging targets remain formidable tasks. Here, we report a robust DNA-encoded library technology (DELT) platform designed for the synthesis, screening, and iterative optimization of novel dimeric macrocyclic peptides. Initially, a pooled library of approximately 1.2 billion unique members, cyclized via diverse thioether linkages or disulfide formation, was constructed and screened against the oncogenic target MDM2. This first-generation selection yielded compound Comp_1, which incorporates a highly enriched pharmacophoric fragment, F_1, and displays a 𝐾i value of 1.5 𝜇M. Leveraging the synthetic modularity of our platform, we established an iterative optimization campaign by incorporating F_1 into a second-generation asymmetric dimeric library (DEL_2) synthesized with enriched building blocks. A subsequent selection campaign against DEL_2 led to the discovery of highly potent macrocyclic candidates, exemplified by compound Comp_2 with a 𝐾i value of 18 nM—representing an approximate 100-fold affinity enhancement over the first-generation hit. This work not only highlights MDM2-targeting macrocyclic binders but also establishes a highly efficient, generalizable DELT-based iterative workflow for the rapid evolution of peptidic leads.

papers.title: ChemFusion: Hierarchical Knowledge Fusion with Functional Group-Aware Attention for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction plays a critical role in accelerating drug discovery and materials design, yet existing deep learning approaches often rely on a single modality of molecular representation and lack chemical interpretability. We propose ChemFusion, a hierarchical knowledge fusion framework that adaptively combines graphbased and sequence-based molecular representations through a functional group-aware attention mechanism. ChemFusion integrates three core modules: a multi-source molecular encoder that extracts complementary features from molecular graphs via graph neural networks and from SMILES strings via chemical language models; a functional group-aware attention module that identifies and differentially weights key functional groups to provide chemically interpretable representation enhancement; and an adaptive meta-learning fusion layer that dynamically adjusts the contribution of each representation source based on task-specific characteristics. Extensive experiments on eight MoleculeNet benchmarks demonstrate that ChemFusion consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving improvements of 1.1 to 2.3 percent in AUROC for classification tasks and 5.5 to 9.1 percent RMSE reduction for regression tasks over the strongest baseline. Moreover, the functional group attention weights provide chemically meaningful interpretations that align with established structure-property relationships, as validated by expert evaluation with average relevance scores above 4.0 on a 5-point scale.

papers.title: Mobility of Persistent Solvent-Rich Phases Governs Deposit Morphology in Electrospray Deposition
papers.abstract: In electrospray deposition (ESD), a high voltage atomizes a flowing solution into charged microdroplets. The self-repulsive droplets evaporate as they approach the target grounded substrate, depositing the solids and carried charge. In the self-limiting electrospray deposition (SLED) regime, manipulation of the electrostatic repulsion, hydrodynamic forces, and evaporation kinetics results in the accumulation of deposited charge and conformal coating complex 2D and 3D architectures. This is a useful property for a wide range of coatings; however, SLED has previously only been achieved for a narrow range of insulating materials. Here, we hypothesize that SLED is only possible when (1) the arriving charged solvent is rendered immobile either through absorption into the free volume of an amorphous solute or the open pores/surface of a dispersant, and (2) the solvent itself is not capable of ionic dissipation (e.g., water). In alternate regimes of ESD, the charge prevents solvent evaporation and there exists a resulting mobile phase capable of dissipating charge, which is either a supercooled liquid blend of solute and solvent or a solvent rich phase ejected from a drying crystal forming molecule or particle dispersion. Using in situ X-ray scattering measurements, optical microscopy, and electrostatic voltammetry, we related the electrospray behavior of a material to its crystallization throughout the course of the spray. We also demonstrate how combining supercooled liquids and particulate dispersions can also result in SLED sprays, which can occur intrinsically for semi-crystalline polymers. Our results provide a template for finding and achieving SLED over a wide range of particles and small molecules to create functional, conformal coatings.

papers.title: Green synthesis of Graphene Oxide and Polyaniline composite for the production of a Supercapacitor
papers.abstract: This research presents the synthesis and characterization of graphene oxide made from palm kernel shell using Hummer’s method and polyaniline nanoparticles from chemical oxidative polymerization of aniline monomer. By utilizing XRD to check the phase structure and purity of the produced nanoparticles, the crystallite size for graphene oxide and polyaniline, respectively, was determined to be 0.57 nm and 35.6 nm, respectively. By using a scanning electron microscope to examine the particles, we were able to determine their shape to be rod-like for polyaniline and sheet-like for graphene oxide, respectively. The EDS result from SEM gave us the elemental composition of the samples. The FTIR analysis was used to determine the functional group makeup of the samples. After printing the samples into conducting substrate, the electrochemical performance test was run and examined. Cyclic Voltammetry was used to calculate the electrode's electrochemical performance. The bow-like form of the cyclic voltammetry graph reveals that the sample is a composite. There was also a test done using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Further analysis of the Cyclic Voltammetry data revealed that the electrode's specific capacitance was 298.7F/g for a scan rate of 10mV/s. A 6.6mA galvanostatic charge discharge test was also used to estimate the energy density, which was determined to be 20.33Wh kg-1. The significance of this study lies in its potential to improve or increase electrochemical capacitor performance and making the precursor easily available.

papers.title: AutoPose: R-Group Decomposition Based Posing for RBFE
papers.abstract: Relative binding free energy (RBFE) calculations are widely applied in structure-based lead optimization but remain limited by ligand pose preparation and workflow scalability. We describe an automated structure-preparation strategy that combines RDKit-based R-group decomposition with Free-Wilson regression modeling to construct ligand poses from reference compounds, enabling prospective RBFE evaluation. Using four benchmark datasets (SHP2, CDK8, PFKFB3, and CDK2), we demonstrate that reconstructed poses are suitable for RBFE calculations performed with the high-throughput RBFE protocol in the TMD package. Prospective RBFE results correlate with Free-Wilson predictions across targets (R2 = 0.57–0.80). These findings indicate that R-group–based pose reconstruction provides a viable foundation for automated RBFE workflows in congeneric series, while Free-Wilson–based prescreening enables rapid triage of designs and can reduce or defer costly RBFE calculations during lead optimization.

papers.title: Microheterogeneity and Ion Clustering in Aqueous Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate Solutions
papers.abstract: The molecular-scale organization in concentrated aqueous potassium dihydrogen phosphate solutions may play a critical role in their behaviour, such as in the structural processes that precede crystal nucleation. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations are used to investigate the structure and dynamics of KDP solutions over a range of concentrations, where these solutions are analysed using a combination of structural correlation functions, Kirkwood–Buff analysis, cluster analysis, mobility measurements, and spatial density distribution functions. The results show that increasing concentration promotes hydrogen-bond-mediated association between dihydrogen phosphate ions, leading to the formation of extended ion clusters and ion-rich domains. The extent of clustering can depend on the water model used in the simulation, with weaker hydration environments promoting larger and more interconnected DP networks. Mobility analysis further indicates a significant reduction in ion diffusion as clustering increases, while water molecules remain comparatively mobile. Spatial density distributions around representative DP ions reveal distinct local environments associated with cluster interiors, cluster surfaces, and bulk-like solvent regions within the same solution. These findings provide clear evidence for micro-heterogeneity in concentrated KDP solutions arising from the competition between ion hydration and DP–DP hydrogen bonding. Such locally heterogeneous environments arising from ion association may promote the formation of pre-nucleation clusters, potentially influencing nucleation pathways as observed in experimental studies of KDP crystallization.

papers.title: Ultra-High Thermal Stability of a pyrroloquinoline quinone–Calcium Radical Persistent Above 1000 K
papers.abstract: The development of heat-resistant organic materials remains a major challenge. The coenzyme pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a two-electron redox cofactor that binds to proteins via Ca 2+ coordination. We isolated the one-electron-reduced PQQ radical generated by the reaction of Ca–PQQ with amines. Remarkably, this radical species remains stable for over 10 years in aqueous solution. In the solid state, it retains its radical character even after heat treatment at 700 °C (973 K) in air and 800 °C (1073 K) under nitrogen. These findings significantly extend the known thermal limits of stable organic radicals and provide a new design principle for heat-resistant organic materials.

papers.title: Balancing Localized and Charge-Transfer Excited States in Dithieno[3,2-b:2’,3’-d]pyrrole-Based NIR-II AIE Photosensitizers for Low Power Phototheranostics
papers.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is limited by the shallow tissue penetration of visible-light excitation and the hypoxic tumor microenvironment, while effective photothermal therapy (PTT) and PDT/PTT synergistic therapy remain difficult to achieve under clinically approved laser power. In this study, a molecular engineering strategy based on progressively strengthened donor-acceptor interactions is developed to construct near-infrared II (NIR-II) aggregation-induced emission photosensitizers (AIE-PSs). Dithieno[3,2-b:2’,3’-d]pyrrole (DTP) was employed as the donor due to its strong electron-donating capability and extended conjugated skeleton. Such structural features facilitate long-wavelength optical response while enabling effective excited-state regulation. By progressively changing the acceptors and strengthening donor-acceptor interactions, the excited-state nature is fine-tuned from a highly charge-transfer (CT)-dominated configuration toward a more balanced localized excitation (LE)/CT state. Such excited-state optimization simultaneously enables NIR-II emission, efficient Type-I PDT performance, and robust photothermal conversion (87.4%). Therefore, this work demonstrates DTP-based AIE PSs as a promising platform for safe and efficient NIR-II phototheranostics, achieving potent therapeutic efficacy under mild 808 nm laser irradiation without relying on excessive irradiation intensity.

papers.title: ent-Kaurene, ent-Kauran-16-ol, and Shunted Diterpenoids from an Engineered Strain of Aspergillus oryzae
papers.abstract: Aspergillus oryzae was engineered to produce high levels of geranylgeranyldiphosphate (GGPP) and ent -kaurene, via ent -copalyl diphosphate, as precursors for future metabolic engineering projects via the expression of ggs2 and cps/ks genes from Gibberella fujikuroi under the control of strong constitutive promoters. GGPP was shunted to three new metabolites that were fully identified by NMR and HRMS. ent -Copalyl diphosphate was shunted to a further seven new compounds that were also identified by NMR and HRMS. The titre of ent -kaurene was significantly increased by heterologous expression of a truncated hydroxymethylglutaryl CoA reductase gene from Avena strigosa (AstHMGR), while replacement of the dual terpene cyclase encoding gene cps/ks with the individual cyclase genes ptmT2 from Streptomyces platensis and Bjks from Bradyrhizobium japonicum resulted mainly in accumulation of ent -copalyl diphosphate-derived shunt products. Finally, ent -kauran-16-ol was biosynthesised by coexpression of ggs2 with the bacterial cyclases ptmT2 and ptmT3 .

papers.title: Visible Light Reactivity of Diazo Arylidene Succinimides with Carbon Tetrabromide: Monobromination and Thiolation via HAT Pathway
papers.abstract: Visible light induced highly regio- and chemo-selective monobromination of cyclic vinyl diazo compounds has been achieved for the very first time. This efficient and transition metal-free synthetic strategy relied on the commercially viable carbon tetrabromide and blue LED at room temperature under open atmosphere. Further, the method has been successfully explored for the direct construction of core scaffold of potential inhibitors of Rtt109 histone acetyltransferase thioheteroaryl tethered arylidene succinimides. The protocol proved to be highly regioselective as well as diastereoselective and enabled the controlled selective monobromination without any side products. The method also found to be scalable on gram quantity. An insight into the reaction mechanism has been explored by carrying out a series of control experiments, EPR studies, UV-absorption studies that unequivocally proved the radical pathway in this transformation.

papers.title: Versatile Mechanism-aware Yield Prediction Model of Ultrahigh-throughput Medicinal Chemistry Reactions
papers.abstract: High-throughput experimentation (HTE) has transformed chemical synthesis by enabling rapid, parallel reaction screening with substantially reduced experimental effort. Although integrating HTE data with machine learning (ML) models has been extensively explored over the past decade, most reported approaches target a single reaction class, limiting their broader applicability. Here, we introduce a mechanistically informed graph neural network (GNN) that predicts reaction yields across multiple reaction types by embedding sequential mechanistic steps directly into the network architecture via dynamic edge state updates. The effectiveness of our GNN model was demonstrated on three widely used medicinal chemistry reactions: Suzuki coupling, reductive amination, and amide coupling. Even with three different reaction types, the GNN model consistently maintained high predictive performance, achieving test R 2 values of up to 0.81. It generalized well to unseen substrates, significantly reducing the need for experimental efforts. Additionally, a newly designed classifier can successfully distinguish the zero-yield and non-zero-yield data points from the HTE datasets. Furthermore, we also highlight that a two-stage classification and regression approach can enhance predictive accuracy in the skewed yield data. These results demonstrate a versatile and interpretable framework for multi-reaction yield prediction that requires minimal tuning across reaction classes, offering a practical tool to accelerate experimental design and streamline drug discovery workflows.

papers.title: Water content and distribution in C-(A)-S-H as a function of Ca/Si ratio and relative humidity
papers.abstract: Calcium-(aluminum)-silicate-hydrate (C-(A)-S-H) phases are the primary binding components in cementitious materials, and their structure and water content depend on both composition and environmental conditions. This study examines the combined influence of Ca/Si ratio and relative humidity on the water content and structural evolution of synthetic C-(A)-S-H. First, the suitable curing and drying conditions of C-(A)-S-H were established. X-ray diffraction indicated that structural stabilization is achieved after extended curing, while low-temperature vacuum drying preserves the layered structure. These conditions were subsequently applied to all synthesized samples. XRD results show a systematic decrease in basal spacing with increasing Ca/Si ratio, accompanied by a significant reduction in specific surface area derived from water sorption measurements. Thermogravimetric and adsorption analyses reveal that the H₂O/Si ratio increases with both Ca/Si ratio and relative humidity, with capillary condensation becoming dominant at very high humidity levels. Overall, these results improve our understanding of how composition and humidity govern water retention and structural features in C-(A)-S-H, providing insights relevant for the design of more durable cementitious materials. Calcium-(aluminum)-silicate-hydrate (C-(A)-S-H) phases are the primary binding components in cementitious materials, and their structure and water content depend on both composition and environmental conditions. This study examines the combined influence of Ca/Si ratio and relative humidity on the water content and structural evolution of synthetic C-(A)-S-H. First, the suitable curing and drying conditions of C-(A)-S-H were established. X-ray diffraction indicated that structural stabilization is achieved after extended curing, while low-temperature vacuum drying preserves the layered structure. These conditions were subsequently applied to all synthesized samples. XRD results show a systematic decrease in basal spacing with increasing Ca/Si ratio, accompanied by a significant reduction in specific surface area derived from water sorption measurements. Thermogravimetric and adsorption analyses reveal that the H₂O/Si ratio increases with both Ca/Si ratio and relative humidity, with capillary condensation becoming dominant at very high humidity levels. Overall, these results improve our understanding of how composition and humidity govern water retention and structural features in C-(A)-S-H, providing insights relevant for the design of more durable cementitious materials.

papers.title: Harness Engineered LLM Agents for Material Science: A Case Study on Perovskite Materials with Machine Learning and Materials Project
papers.abstract: The integration of AI agents into materials science has gained noteworthy momentum in recent years. A fundamental challenge remains how to balance fully autonomous LLM-driven agent risking unpredictable or physically impossible results, against rigid and unadaptable standard operating procedures. This study applies Harness strategy as a feasible approach to designing agent interfaces for materials science, with a case study on perovskite materials using machine learning algorithms and crystal structure tools. The proposed agent framework with the harness concept replaces hard-coded operations with LLM-driven adaptive decisions across subclass assignment, feature selection, model selection, modelling scheduling, and result interpretation. Eleven machine learning regressors are evaluated under two conditions: without Harness (single pooled model) and with Harness (subclass-specific models with sample-count-weighted evaluation). Results demonstrate that Harness engineering improves machine learning model accuracies of these perovskite materials on across the machine learning model families based on retrieved perovskite data at the first-principles level in this specific case. This study provides a platform to transform AI agents into harnessed and reliable collaborators for materials science research.

papers.title: Architectural Disagreement as a Detector of Representation Ambiguity in Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: We present a six-notebook empirical study demonstrating that the absolute predictive disagreement D(m)=|pred GIN -pred ARCH2 | between two Graph Neural Networks with different inductive biases is a robust, generalizable, and mechanistically interpretable indicator of representation ambiguity in molecular property prediction — a phenomenon we operationalize as the Dark Chemical Space. Across Notebook 1 (ChEMBL33/QED, n=40,000, scaffold-split), we establish that D(m) correlates with prediction error at Spearman rho=+0.658 (p~0), exhibits intra-scaffold consistency above chance (ICC=0.536, z=7.16), and outperforms scalar chemical proxies by 4.3x. Notebook 2 (EGFR IC50, n=1,146) replicates on biological data (rho=+0.293, p=4.4e-24) and shows that D(m) outperforms MC Dropout (non-significant, p=0.29) by 9.4x and Deep Ensemble by 2.0x. Notebook 3 (6 biological targets: VEGFR2, JAK2, BRAF, CDK2, DRD2, EGFR) establishes generality: 6/6 targets significant (p<0.001), mean biological rho=0.326, signal consistent across kinases and GPCRs. Mechanistic analysis (NB3) localizes the signal primarily in the MLP prediction head (mean amplification gap +0.239 rho units), while message passing converges representations (rho decreases L1-to-L5 in the 2D setting). Notebook 4 introduces real 3D coordinates (ETKDGv3+MMFF94) and a true E(n)-equivariant model (EGNN, Satorras et al. 2021). The central finding of NB4 is that D(m) improves with 3D coordinates (EGFR: +0.274 vs +0.207; VEGFR2: +0.428 vs +0.414) despite EGNN being a worse predictor than GIN. Critically, layer-wise analysis reveals that on EGFR, 3D message passing grows rather than converges (rho peaks at L3=0.159 vs flat 0.055-0.063 in 2D), indicating that equivariant message passing actively processes geometric information rather than merely passing it through to the head. The central conceptual finding is that architectural diversity, rather than absolute model quality, drives the disagreement signal: explicit geometric information increases D(m) without improving predictive accuracy. We propose that the Dark Chemical Space identifies regions where two reasonable architectures, both correctly trained, arrive at different interpretations of the structure-activity relationship — a form of representation ambiguity that is more fundamental than simple predictive uncertainty. Notebooks 5 and 6 provide multi-seed robustness validation (3 seeds x GIN+EGNN on EGFR, VEGFR2, JAK2, BRAF with 3D coordinates): D(m) is stable across seeds (std 0.013-0.052); GIN outperforms EGNN 12/12 seed-target combinations; BRAF yields the strongest biological signal (rho=+0.514 +/- 0.052); the head amplification gap is consistently positive on 4/4 targets and all seeds; and the L3 layer-wise peak reported in NB4 is retracted (not seed-stable, std=0.056). Finally, NB6 converts D(m) into a practical candidate selection tool the Strange Molecule Hunter v2 — which identifies molecules where both architectures predict activity but disagree on confidence. On EGFR: 38 candidates, 89.5% truly active (2.09x enrichment over 42.8% baseline), 16 underestimated actives where the model underestimates true potency by more than 10x in IC50. On BRAF: Precision@50 = 94% (1.59x enrichment). Tanimoto scaffold distance correlates significantly with both D(m) and prediction error (p<0.001), but D(m) outperforms scaffold distance by 1.2-3.8x, confirming that it captures the architectural consequence of structural novelty rather than novelty per se.

papers.title: Engineering Near-Quantitative Bidirectional Switching and Zisomer Stability in Arylazopyrazoles through Cooperative Non-Covalent Interactions
papers.abstract: The limited thermal stability of Z-isomers in reversible E/Z photochromic systems deters their broader functional applications. Here we report a family of arylazo-1,3,5-triphenylpyrazole photoswitches that exhibit rapid E→Z, red-light-induced, and near-quantitative bidirectional switching with tunable Z-isomer thermal lifetimes. Notably, the nitro-substituted derivative enables bidirectional visible-light-mediated switching, exhibiting blue lightactivated forward isomerization and far-red (740 nm) light-induced reversal within the biological optical window. Single-crystal X-ray structures of both the E- and thermally metastable Z-isomers were resolved for all halogensubstituted derivatives, providing rare structural insight into T-type photochromic systems. The crystal structures reveal distinct "favourably twisted” conformations of the Z-isomer stabilized by cooperative noncovalent π···π stacking, C-X···π, and C-H···X interactions, establishing a general strategy for Z-isomer stabilization. Theoretical studies support that the thermal Z→E relaxation proceeds via a ground-state in-plane inversion mechanism.

papers.title: Exploring the Electrochemical Redox Properties of a Streptomyces-derived Indolocarbazole
papers.abstract: Indolocarbazoles are π-conjugated heterocycles with rich optoelectronic and redox properties, offering potential as sustainable redox active materials. Here, we report the electrochemical characterisation of arcyriaflavin A (Arc A), the simplest fully conjugated indolocarbazole scaffold derived by recombinant biosynthesis. Cyclic voltammetry in non-aqueous media revealed two irreversible one-electron reduction events at –1.90 and –2.42 V vs Fc/Fc+, consistent with an ECEC-type mechanism and a diffusion constant of 0.81 x 10-6 cm2 s-1. Kinetic studies of the first reduction step confirmed a second-order rate constant of 7.3 × 104 M-1 s-1, analogous to the phthalimide reduction mechanism. Half-cell charge/discharge experiments and complementary spectroelectrochemical UV–vis and ex situ NMR measurements suggested irreversible degradation of the electroactive species via proton-transfer steps and radical recombination reactions involving the phthalimide ring. TD-DFT simulations supported the proposed degradation mechanisms by qualitatively reproducing the observed electronic transitions and NMR shifts. Based on these results, N-alkylation of the phthalimide ring was proposed as a strategy to stabilise the reduced forms and enhance solubility, providing a molecular design route toward robust, biologically derived redox-active materials for sustainable energy storage.

papers.title: Stereocontrolled Synthesis of Rare L-Glycosyl-1-Phosphates for Probing Nucleotidyltransferases
papers.abstract: Glycosyl 1-phosphates are key precursors to nucleotide sugars that drive glycosyltransferasecatalysed glycan assembly, yet stereocontrolled access to L-configured variants found across nature remains limited. Here we report a Design-of-Experiments (DoE)-guided optimisation of L-glycosyl 1-phosphate synthesis, enabling high isolated yields of anomerically pure protected and unprotected β-L-glycosyl 1-phosphates. These donors support a robust chemoenzymatic route to natural and non-natural nucleotide sugars, expanding the repertoire of activated building blocks available for in vitro glycan synthesis. Using β-L-sugar 1-phosphates prepared in enabling quantities, we demonstrate that native and engineered microbial nucleotidyltransferases convert rare and canonical L-sugar donors into diverse dTDP-, UDP-, and GDP-β-L-sugar nucleotides, including previously unreported products. Tag-free nanoscale differential scanning fluorimetry (nano-DSF) reveals substrate-dependent stabilisation and destabilisation effects that illuminate cooperative binding behaviour and highlight opportunities for evolving improved nucleotidyltransferase stability and turnover. Collectively, this integrated synthetic–biocatalytic platform enhances access to rare nucleotide sugars and provides mechanistic insight into nucleotidyltransferase activity, enabling catalytic strategies for exploiting these enzymes in glycan synthesis.

papers.title: Thermal Oxidation Stability Investigation: Compositional Changes of Sulfur-Containing Compounds in Jet A Fuels when Subjected to Thermal Stress
papers.abstract: Thermal oxidation stability (TOS) is a useful metric to evaluate the resistance of fuel to degrade when it is exposed to elevated temperatures. Degradation is attributed to free radical reactions involving fuel molecules and dissolved oxygen (i.e., autoxidation), which may lead to insoluble deposits and fuel failure. Hence, investigating the oxidative degradation process is imperative as the reactions precede deposit formation. In this study, stable and unstable Jet A fuels were thermally stressed by using Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) measurements. Then, detailed qualitative characterization of the sulfur-containing compounds (SCCs) derived from the nonstressed, and thermally stressed Jet A fuels were determined and compared by using positive-ion mode atmospheric pressure chemical ionization coupled to an orbitrap mass spectrometer. The stable fuel showed slow, linear oxygen consumption and mass accumulation trends. Conversely, the unstable fuel demonstrated autocatalytic/autoaccelerative trends for oxygen consumption and mass accumulation. All detected non-oxidized classes of SCCs (e.g., alkyl thiols, thiophenes) exhibited oxidation in both fuels. Remarkably, significant compositional changes were noted in the unstable fuel. For example, the relative abundances of oxidized SCCs in non-stressed and stressed unstable fuel were 6.5 and 71.0%, respectively. Furthermore, the compositional data derived from high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) measurements supported a sequential addition of oxygen atoms to the SCCs during autoxidation, not dimer/trimer formation. Additional qualitative data of the SCCs was provided, including Kendrick Mass Defect plots. A detailed discussion using the HRMS data and additional composition information (e.g., total nitrogen) was used to further explain the QCM results. Overall, HRMS measurements provided novel qualitative data that implicated SCCs as having a direct role in the TOS of Jet A. The information from this study is germane for the development of future monitoring technologies as the oxidized SCCs may forewarn of adverse autoxidative reactions that ultimately lead to thermal stability failures.

papers.title: Protein Breathing Induces Non-Markovian Buried Ring-flip Dynamics in Cytochrome C
papers.abstract: Aromatic amino acids buried inside folded proteins play a critical role in stabilizing both the folded conformation and anchoring any incoming substrate molecules. Moreover, their ring flips serve as sensitive probes of protein breathing motions. In this work, we accurately estimate the ring-flipping rates of a phenylalanine residue in cytochrome C using metadynamics combined with reactive flux and Grote-Hynes theory. We show that the delayed response of cavity residues that provide steric hindrance to ring rotation manifests as memory-dependent friction. Increasing solvent viscosity slows the fluctuations of these cavity residues, reinforcing the delayed response and producing a fractional viscosity dependence of the flip rate, despite the ring being completely buried.

papers.title: Whole-Enzyme Reactive Free-Energy Simulations with a Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potential: Catalytic Mechanism and Mutational Effects of PETase
papers.abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) have emerged as powerful tools for atomistic simulations that achieve quantum mechanical accuracy at significantly reduced computational cost. Yet, their direct application to complex enzymatic reactions remains challenging owing to the immense size of solvated enzyme systems and the scarcity of transition-state structures in training data. In this study, we demonstrate that PFP (PreFerred Potential), a pretrained uMLIP across 96 elements in nature, simulates the complete hydrolytic cycle of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) catalyzed by PETase as a single reactive domain of approximately 20,000 atoms, without multiscale partitioning or system-specific fine-tuning. Umbrella-sampling simulations revealed stepwise mechanisms for both acylation and deacylation through distinct tetrahedral intermediates. The computed rate-limiting deacylation barrier of 20.5 ± 0.3 kcal/mol is in agreement with the range of 18.0–18.7 kcal/mol inferred from experimental turnover numbers. The PFP-based simulations further capture catalytic consequences of point mutations from loss of function (D177N, M132A) to predicted activity enhancement (D157N) and reveal that simultaneous neutralization of three distal acidic residues which are located more than 10 Å from the active site raises the activation barrier due to a collective long-range electrostatic effect that emerges naturally in the partition-free treatment. These findings demonstrate that the pretrained uMLIP, PFP, can provide physically plausible free-energy profiles for enzymatic reaction mechanisms and capture mutational effects, providing a powerful platform for rational enzyme design.

papers.title: A Hybrid Graph Neural Network for Temperature-Dependent Viscosity Prediction of Multi-Component Mixtures
papers.abstract: Viscosity is a critical physical property governing chemical processes and product handling, yet its accurate, temperature-dependent prediction for mixtures, and complex, polydisperse, oligomeric systems remains challenging. To tackle this, we present a hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework coupling a data-driven mixture embedding with an extended Arrhenius–Andrade equation, imposing a physically motivated inductive bias for temperature-dependent viscosity prediction, that also scales to industrially complex mixtures. The architecture predicts mixture viscosity at a reference temperature through a purely data-driven approach, while two learnable parameters of the semi-empirical equation enable physically consistent extrapolation to other temperatures. Trained on the publicly available binary mixture dataset, the hybrid model outperforms a conventional concatenation-based baseline on two distinct test benchmarks. Our approach is further successfully applied to industrially relevant, polydisperse oligomeric polyether polyol recipes achieving high predictive accuracy and illustrating that hybrid GNNs can bridge the gap between data-driven flexibility and physical interpretability.

papers.title: OmniInvent: Unified Generative Chemical Language Models through Blank Infilling
papers.abstract: Drug design requires navigating a vast and sparsely populated chemical space while balancing structural novelty with multiple property constraints. Most generative approaches to the problem remain specialized to individual tasks such as de novo design, scaffold decoration, or fragment linking. Here, we introduce OmniInvent, a chemical language model that operates directly on unmodified SMILES and supports both de novo and substructure-constrained molecular generation within a single framework. OmniInvent formulates molecular design as an autoregressive blank infilling problem over partially masked SMILES, combining prefix attention with two-dimensional positional embeddings, and is pretrained using an on-the-fly graph-based masking strategy that randomly selects connected molecular substructures and masks the corresponding SMILES segments without the need for task-specific fragmentation strategies. In direct sampling, OmniInvent generated highly valid, unique, and diverse molecules in de novo design, linker design, scaffold decoration, and motif extension. In goal-directed design, it was competitive on the Practical Molecular Optimization benchmark for de novo design and performed similarly to highly specialized state-of-the-art models in substructure-constrained design despite being trained as a general-purpose model. These results show that blank span infilling on SMILES provides an effective foundation for building unified molecular generative models across diverse drug design tasks.

papers.title: A Tailing Particle Migration and Coalescence Mechanism
papers.abstract: Sintering is a key factor governing the stability of heterogeneous catalysts and is commonly described by two mechanisms: Ostwald ripening (OR) through metal atom detachment and diffusion, and particle migration and coalescence (PMC) involving the motion of entire nanoparticles. Here, we investigate the structural evolution of Au nanoparticles (NPs) supported on ceria (CeO2) and identify an unconventional sintering mechanism. In this process, particle migration and coalescence of Au NPs occur simultaneously with the continuous formation of dispersed Au single atoms (SAs) along the migration pathway, generating a coupled particle–atom dynamics that we term tailing particle migration and coalescence (TPMC). We further show that the competition among OR, PMC, and TPMC can be quantitatively described by two energetic descriptors: metal-oxide binding and interfacial metal-metal binding. This framework enables construction of a mechanistic phase diagram that predicts dominant sintering pathways across different environments. Under CO atmospheres, stabilization of dispersed Au species drives a dynamic transition from TPMC to Ostwald ripening, highlighting the strong environmental dependence of catalyst sintering.

papers.title: AlphaFold3 and QM/MM for Determining Photophysical Properties of Fluorescent Proteins
papers.abstract: AlphaFold3 has been used extensively for protein design and produces accurate structures that computational chemists can use for understanding the biophysics of proteins including structure and function. Current research that uses AlphaFold focuses on protein structure and comparisons with available X-ray crystallographic data. Here, we present a comparison of AlphaFold3 structures of fluorescent proteins (FPs) with ones obtained from the Protein Data Bank, when available. Three experimentally characterized systems were explored i.e, blue fluorescent protein (BFP), mBlueberry2 (mBLB), and Dsred.M1 (RFP), to evaluate AlphaFold’s capability to generate reliable (or plausible) structures for FPs with existing crystal structures (BFP and RFP) as well as for systems without available crystallographic data (mBLB). Based on these results, where AlphaFold3 produces structures with similar resolution to the experimentally determined crystal structures, the impact on the protein structure can be investigated when substituting the natural chromophore with a non-canonical chromophore (nCC), i.e., one formed by incorporating a non-canonical amino acid. The results show that the single residue replacement needed to form the nCC does not strongly affect protein folding. Structures obtained from AlphaFold3 were subsequently optimized and vertical excitation energies were determined using quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical approaches (ωB97X-D/cc-pVDZ:AMBER and CAM-B3LYP/cc-pVDZ:AMBER, respectively). Overall, the results indicate that AlphaFold3 produces structures of sufficient quality to reproduce photophysical properties similar to those obtained using structures from the Protein Data Bank. Moreover, these findings suggest that fully computational design of FPs incorporating nCC is now feasible.

papers.title: Fast photochemical oxidation of nucleic acids maps protein- DNA interactions at sub-nucleotide resolution
papers.abstract: Transcription factor (TF) binding to DNA reshapes its backbone accessibility and modulate gene expression. However, protein–DNA interactions remain difficult to characterize with high resolution at the residue level. Here, we introduce Fast Photochemical Oxidation of Nucleic acids (FPON), a laser-driven hydroxyl-radical footprinting workflow coupled to liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis. FPON quantitatively maps DNA accessibility and damage at sub-nucleotide resolution, revealing structural and interaction patterns induced by TF binding. Using the Forkhead box O4 DNA‑binding domain (FOXO4-DBD) bound to a double-stranded insulin response element (IRE), FPON generated structurally informative DNA fragments resolved and assigned by LC-MSn in a single experiment. Quantitative analysis identified site-specific protection patterns within the FOXO4 recognition motif. In the absence of a high-resolution structure, these site-specific protection patterns guided the construction of an in silico FOXO4–IRE complex. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations revealed a strong agreement between experimentally observed cleavage suppression and reduced solvent accessibility of DNA backbone hydrogens. Furthermore, FPON resolved multiple chemically distinct cleavage products otherwise indistinguishable in conventional gel-based footprinting approaches. Together, these results establish FPON as an unbiased, high-resolution strategy for mapping protein-DNA contacts readily applicable to more complex chromatin systems and dynamic transcriptional processes.

papers.title: Randomness is All You Need – Studying the Effect of Molecular Conformation on Sigma Profiles as Machine Learning Features
papers.abstract: Sigma profiles (SPs) are powerful molecular descriptors that combine the size-independence and continuity of many machine-learned descriptors with the physical interpretability of structural descriptors like molecular graphs or SMILES. Though SPs have existed for a long time within the context of thermodynamic models like COSMO-RS and COSMO-SAC, there does not seem to be a consensus in the literature on the effect of molecular conformations on SPs or on their performance as inputs to thermodynamic or machine learning (ML) models. This work performs a systematic study on the effect of conformations on SPs as an input to ML models by developing three different conformer generation heuristics and using the resulting SP datasets to train Gaussian Process (GP) models as an inexpensive surrogate ML model. All SPs are generated using the open- source tool OpenSPGen following the suggested guidelines for level of theory, tessellation, and post-processing (averaging radius). The study shows that conformations have a small but statistically significant effect on the ML prediction of three out of six considered target properties. Additionally, it shows that the effect of conformations is more significant for smaller molecules, and that the number of conformations included is more important than the heuristic of conformer generation. The final recommendation of this work is to start by generating five random conformers, examine how the ML performance for the target property of interest changes with increasing the number of random conformers, then decide if the increase in performance from one to three to five conformers justifies generating more conformations and more SPs. Design, System, Application Sigma profiles (SPs) are a powerful molecular descriptor for physics-informed machine learning (ML) for molecular design applications because they uniquely combine physical significance and human-interpretability with continuity and size-independence. However, using SPs in ML applications requires guidelines for open-source SP generation at scale. This work develops guidelines for conformer generation and selection to yield the highest-performing SPs for ML applications. A systematic study on the effect of conformations on SPs and their performance as an ML descriptor was performed. The resulting guidelines were implemented as a default option in the open-source SP generation package OpenSPGen allowing consistent treatment of

papers.title: Surface Charge Reshapes Scaling Relationships: From Linear Descriptors to Nonlinear, Multi-Descriptor Models
papers.abstract: Scaling relationships (SRs) are widely used to accelerate catalyst design by relating adsorption energies and activation barriers through a small set of descriptors. However, these relationships are typically developed for neutral metal surfaces, despite that many catalytic environments—including electrocatalysis, plasma catalysis, and field-assisted systems—operate under nonzero surface charge. In this work, we systematically investigate how applied charge influences SRs using density functional theory calculations of intermediates and transition states in the water gas shift (WGS) reaction on five transition metal surfaces across multiple charge states. We show that surface charge perturbs adsorption and activation energetics in a species-dependent manner, challenging the transferability of conventional linear SRs and their associated descriptor sets. While adsorption energies can often still be approximated using linear scaling under charge, the underlying descriptors differ from those identified for neutral systems. In contrast, transition-state energetics exhibit significant deviations from linearity for both neutral and charged surfaces. Using symbolic regression, we demonstrate that non-linear, multi-descriptor models substantially improve predictive accuracy while remaining interpretable. These findings indicate that surface charge does not invalidate scaling relationships but rather reformulates them into charge-dependent, nonlinear forms requiring expanded descriptor sets. This work establishes a framework for developing predictive, chargeaware models for catalytic reaction networks.

papers.title: Phase-separating peptides identified from complex combinatorial mixtures
papers.abstract: Discovery of peptides that undergo liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is important for establishing sequence–property relationships but systematic approaches have remained elusive so far. Here, we report a tandem mass spectrometry platform to identify peptides prone to LLPS directly from combinatorial peptide libraries encompassing over 44,000 sequences and achieving an 86% true-positive rate across 38 validated candidates. This mixture-based strategy reveals that LLPS forming peptides stabilize aggregation-prone sequences, revealing emergent behavior undetectable in conventional single-peptide analysis. The resulting dataset establishes a foundation for machine learning applications to enable high-throughput prediction of peptide aggregation states.

papers.title: Benchmarking Pretrained Molecular Representations Against Classical Fingerprints for BACE-1 Inhibitor Prediction
papers.abstract: The identification of beta-secretase 1 (BACE-1) inhibitors capable of crossing the blood–brain barrier (BBB) remains a central challenge in Alzheimer's disease drug discovery. While pretrained molecular language models such as ChemBERTa have attracted considerable attention as general-purpose feature extractors, their advantage over classical descriptors for specific therapeutic targets has not been rigorously established. Here, we report a systematic comparison of four molecular representations for binary classification of 2,299 BBB-filtered BACE-1 compounds assembled from MoleculeNet and ChEMBL. The representations evaluated were ECFP4 Morgan fingerprints (2,048 bits), MACCS structural keys (167 bits), RDKit physicochemical descriptors (168 features), and pretrained ChemBERTa embeddings (768 dimensions). Using scaffold-based splitting, data-driven model selection across 27 classifiers, Bayesian optimization via Optuna, and validation through repeated cross-validation and Y-randomization, we found that classical ECFP4 fingerprints paired with the ExtraTreesClassifier achieved the highest test performance (ROC AUC = 0.894, MCC = 0.649), followed by RDKit descriptors (0.866), MACCS keys (0.863), and ChemBERTa (0.861). All pairwise differences were statistically significant (Wilcoxon p < 0.005), yet the total performance spread was only 0.033 ROC AUC units, suggesting that representation choice may be less decisive than often assumed. SHAP-based interpretability analysis revealed markedly different encoding strategies: MACCS keys concentrated predictive importance in a small number of structural fragments, whereas ECFP4 and ChemBERTa distributed it across hundreds of features. Applicability domain analysis confirmed that prediction accuracy scaled with chemical similarity to the training set. These results indicate that pretrained embeddings do not automatically outperform classical fingerprints for target-specific QSAR, and that careful pipeline design may warrant more attention than the choice of representation alone.

papers.title: Development and validation of a portable, fully automated prototype for microfluidic gas-liquid membrane contactor chips
papers.abstract: Microfluidic gas–liquid membrane contactors enable continuous, well-defined interactions between gas and liquid phases at the microscale, offering precise control over mass transfer conditions with minimal reagent consumption, making them valuable for applications ranging from gas sensing and solvent screening to organ-on-a-chip systems. However, most existing microfluidic implementations rely on bulky laboratory equipment operated manually, limiting their utility for data-intensive and field-deployable applications. Here, we present a portable, fully automated prototype integrating a microfluidic gas–liquid membrane contactor chip with a programmable fluidic platform, electrochemical workstation, a single board computer (Raspberry Pi) and a custom software stack for performing and monitoring gas dissolution and extraction experiments. The entire prototype is automated using open-source programming languages, Python and C++, in a Linux open-source operating system. The protocol or the working of the prototype was initially validated using gas dissolutions experiments performed on microfluidic chip containing bromothymol blue solution and using CO2 as the model gas. Further, validation was also performed using the microfluidic chip with an ionic liquid. Upon dissolution to CO2 in the ionic liquid, it’s characteristic resistance (recorded by the in-built portable electrochemical workstation) increases. Interestingly, it was also observed that, by significantly reducing the pressure in the gas microchannel using a DC vacuum pump, the ionic liquid can be regenerated. These results demonstrate that the prototype is a reliable, versatile, and field-deployable platform capable of supporting electrochemical characterization of gas dissolution and extraction processes at the microscale.

papers.title: Decoupling of σ–S in D-A Conjugated Polymer Thermoelectrics via Doping-Induced Microstructural Reconfiguration
papers.abstract: Achieving simultaneous enhancement of electrical conductivity (σ) and Seebeck coefficient (S) remains a central challenge in developing high-performance organic thermoelectric (OTE). Here, we demonstrate that decoupling of σ and S can be achieved in a novel donor-acceptor (D-A) conjugated polymer, PDPPEDOT, through the precise control of microstructural evolution induced by F4TCNQ doping. Spectroscopic analyses (UV-vis-NIR, Raman, and XPS) confirm efficient charge transfer between the PDPPEDOT backbone and F4TCNQ. Microstructural characterization via GIWAXS and AFM reveals that moderate doping (10 mg/mL) can act as a structural template to promote ordered molecular packing and uniform nanocrystalline domain formation, whereas excessive doping disrupts this structural integrity. Beneficial from optimized microstructural packing, PDPPEDOT thin film achieves a high electrical conductivity of 10.71 S/cm while maintaining a Seebeck coefficient of 76.75 μV/K, yielding a maximum power factor of 6.31 μW·m-1K-2 with a characteristic “volcano-shaped” trend. This study highlights doping-induced microstructural regulation as an efficient strategy for decoupling thermoelectric parameters and advancing next-generation highperformance D-A type organic thermoelectric materials.

papers.title: E(3)-VERDE: A 3D-Equivariant Neural Network for the Complete Ground and Excited- State Redox Landscape of Organic Photocatalysts
papers.abstract: Photoredox catalysis enables mild visible-light-driven chemical transformations; the rational design of organic photocatalysts is difficult because it requires ground- and excited-state redox potentials challenging to obtain by experiment or quantum chemistry. We introduce E(3)-VERDE, an E(3)-equivariant neural network trained on the Virtual Excited State Reference for the Discovery of Electronic materials database (VERDE materials DB) to predict ground- and excitedstate redox potentials together with zero-zero excitation energies for organic photocatalysts from a single low-cost ground-state geometry, without requiring excited-state geometry optimizations at inference. Its three-dimensional representation retains molecular shape and atomic arrangement as predictive information for these properties. On held-out DFT test data, the model reproduces reference values with R 2 of 0.97-0.99 and MAEs of 0.04-0.07 eV across the predicted redox potential and excitation-energy properties. On an experimental benchmark of 40 structurally diverse chromophores including dihydrophenazines, d ihydroacridines, cyanoarenes, N-phenyl carbazoles, N–N donors, acridinium salts, and Eosin Y derivatives, E(3)-VERDE achieves MAEs of 0.09-0.15 eV and lower errors than 2D-fingerprint, distance-only, and partially angular baselines on this benchmark. These results support E(3)-VERDE as a practical and efficient tool for high-throughput screening of organic photocatalysts from low-cost ground-state geometries.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Parallel Graph Reasoning and Chemical Constraint Refinement for Molecular Property Prediction and Reaction Analysis
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction analysis are critical tasks in computational chemistry and drug discovery, yet existing methods struggle to effectively leverage external chemical knowledge and enforce chemical validity constraints. We propose ChemRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework that integrates three novel modules for chemistry-specific reasoning. First, a Parallel Graph-Retrieval Reasoning module constructs a chemical knowledge graph and performs multi-chain parallel retrieval to capture complementary molecular knowledge from diverse reasoning paths. Second, a Chemical Constraint Refinement module progressively enforces atom conservation, valence rules, and reaction condition constraints through iterative refinement, ensuring the chemical validity of generated outputs. Third, a Multimodal Spectral Fusion module aligns molecular spectral data with graph structures via cross-modal attention, enabling comprehensive analysis that combines structural and spectral information. Extensive experiments on MoleculeNet, USPTO-50K, and the NIST spectral database demonstrate that ChemRAG achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a ROC-AUC of 0.893 for molecular property prediction, a Top-1 accuracy of 84.7 percent for reaction prediction, an F1 score of 0.796 for spectral analysis, and a synthesis pathway success rate of 76.4 percent, consistently outperforming existing baselines including specialized chemical vision-language models.

papers.title: Encapsulation and isomer discrimination of substituted pyrazines by an adaptable cofacial zinc porphyrin dimer
papers.abstract: Positional isomers of substituted pyrazines—important aroma compounds and pharmacophores—are notoriously difficult to distinguish because of their nearly identical physical properties, and hosts that could discriminate them through molecular recognition face a further obstacle: substituents adjacent to the coordinating nitrogen atoms severely impede metal coordination, limiting existing binuclear receptors to association constants below 1 M −1 . Here we show that a rigid cofacial zinc porphyrin dimer, in which two macrocycles are held face-to-face by covalent linkers, encapsulates a range of substituted pyrazines with binding constants of 10 5 –10 8 M −1 in solution. The host discriminates between positional isomers of identical molecular formula: 2,5-dimethylpyrazine is bound about tenfold more strongly than its 2,3-isomer, and whereas the 2,5-isomer is encapsulated with both nitrogen atoms coordinated to the two zinc centers, the 2,6-isomer is excluded from the cavity and instead coordinates only from outside. The host also encapsulates benzopyrazine (quinoxaline), which a previously reported self-assembled cofacial dimer cannot accommodate. Single-crystal X-ray structures and quantumchemical calculations reveal that the isomer discrimination arises not from the energetic cost of host deformation, but from how the substituent pattern weakens the axial coordination at the two metal centers. Combining a fixed metal–metal distance with deformable macrocycles thus provides a design principle for receptors that recognize and distinguish sterically demanding guests.

papers.title: O-Acylation of alcohol functional groups in neutral aqueous buffer directed by charge transfer interactions
papers.abstract: O-Acylation of alcohol functional groups (or ‘esterification’) in neutral aqueous buffer is typically achieved using polymer catalysts, such as enzymes. Here, we demonstrate the transformation by devising small molecular weight acylating reagents without the use of a catalyst. The key was to bring the substrate and acylating reagent into close proximity via charge-transfer interactions. The similarity in energy levels and orbital geometry between the highest occupied molecular orbital of azostilbene and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital of thioflavin-T (composed of N,N-dimethylaniline and benzothiazole) facilitated the charge-transfer interaction. The yields of charge-transfer interaction-based O-acylation were significantly varied, with slight differences in the structure of the substrate. The charge-transfer interaction strategy thus provides the unique result of exhibiting substrate selectivity, even when the substrate and acylating reagent are in close proximity. In addition, the acylating reagent was applicable to the reaction of the side chain of Ser residues in peptides. Ser residues present in peptides bearing various functional groups were chemo- and regio-selectively O-acylated both with aromatic and aliphatic acylation reagents. By combining them with biorelevant molecules (enzyme, amyloid), the scope of the reactions was further expanded (imparting reversibility, accelerating the reaction). The reaction systems based on the charge-transfer interaction are suggested by these results to be a promising method for life science research.

papers.title: A Germanium μ-Oxo Chloro Dimer en route to a Heavier Phosgene Analogue and 1,3-Digermadioxetane Dications
The synthesis of a stable [6]cumulene
papers.abstract: The synthetic evolution of even [n]cumulenes is presented, which culminates in the formation and study of the stable [6]cumulene [6]tBu. The instability of even [n]cumulenes is hypothesized to arise from the effects of the endgroups, in which bulky aryl endgroups are ineffective at protection, while bulky alkyl groups (tert-butyl) afford the ambiently stable [6]tBu. The lower molecular symmetry of [6]tBu, relative to the parent [6]cumulene ([6]H, H2C=(C4)=CH2], allows for experimental observation of the lowest excited singlet transition, which would otherwise be symmetry forbidden. X-ray crystallographic analysis reveals that [6]tBu has the lowest bondlength alternation of any [n]cumulene synthesized to date, making it an ideal starting point toward probing the properties of the unstable “cumulenic” carbyne, B-carbyne.

papers.title: Bis(styryl)benzene Probes for Targeting Early-Stage Amyloid-β Aggregates in Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.abstract: With the recent FDA approval of antibody-based therapeutics for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the need for diagnostic tools capable of detecting disease at the earliest stages has become increasingly urgent. Although small molecules offer advantages in terms of production, stability, and accessibility, no imaging agent currently enables reliable detection of early-stage aggregates of the amyloid-β (Aβ) peptide, among the earliest biomarkers in AD progression. Herein, we report a series of bis(styryl)benzene (BSB) probes derived from the Methoxy-X04 scaffold and a systematic structure–activity investigation examining how targeted molecular modifications, including hydroxyl positioning, (Me)HN or (Me)2N substitution, and incorporation of a 1,4dimethyl-1,4,7-triazacyclononane (tacn) moiety, modulate Aβ binding, cytotoxicity, and bloodbrain barrier (BBB) permeability. These Methoxy-X04 analogues retain Aβ affinity while exhibiting markedly improved cytotoxicity profiles and logD values consistent with in vivo applicability. Amyloid-β binding was evaluated using age-dependent in situ staining of 5xFAD mouse brain sections, supported by in vitro fluorescence-based oligomer and fibril assays and in silico analyses that reveal tunable selectivity toward early versus late Aβ aggregates. In vivo brain uptake studies of BSB5 and Me2tacnBSB5 further support the utility of these probes as modular Aβ-targeting fragments for the development of early-stage AD imaging agents.

papers.title: Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Protein–polymer bioconjugates represent a class of biomaterials that leverages the molecular specificity of proteins and the tunability of synthetic polymers. Strategic conjugation of polymers to protein surfaces can enhance key biomolecular properties such as structural stability and target affinity while preserving the biological functions of the native protein. The rational design of these hybrid biomolecules demands a detailed understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing protein–polymer interfacial behavior. Critically, strong interfacial interactions can impose substantial energetic barriers that hinder conformational sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) studies of this system. Enhanced sampling methods are highly effective for overcoming such limitations in the simulation of biomolecular interfaces. However, the opportunity to apply enhanced sampling methods toward navigating the complex interfacial landscapes of protein–polymer bioconjugates has yet to be realized by the field. In this study, we showcase the development of a molecular modeling framework that leverages enhanced sampling to extensively characterize protein–polymer bioconjugates. To validate this framework, we constructed two bioconjugate models of hen egg-white lysozyme grafted with activated methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) chains of varying lengths at multiple surface-exposed lysine sites. We then performed all-atom MD simulations of these PEGylated constructs, augmented with well-tempered metadynamics (WTM) to fully explore their conformational landscapes under multi-site polymer conjugation. This approach yielded converged free energy surfaces (FES) characterizing the thermodynamic favorability of grafted mPEG chain conformations at each conjugation site. We also identified key protein contact residues and site-specific non-bonded interactions responsible for bioconjugate stabilization. This study demonstrates a novel application of enhanced sampling methodologies in bioconjugate systems for characterizing site-specific conjugation effects on protein–polymer interfacial energetics and structural dynamics in the context of protein surface chemistry. More broadly, applying this methodological framework across diverse polymer chemistries and protein variants can elucidate molecular design rules for engineering bioconjugates with precise properties and functions for applications spanning biotechnology, energy, and health.

papers.title: Fueling carbodiimide chemistry: direct structural characterization of the O-acylisourea intermediate
papers.abstract: Carbodiimide-fueled molecular machines, catalytic reaction cycles, and a broad spectrum of synthetic transformations from peptide coupling to Steglich esterification depend on the fate of a single transient species: the O -acylisourea intermediate. Whether this intermediate engages in productive chemistry or diverts irreversibly to its inert N -acylurea isomer determines the outcome of every carbodiimide-mediated process. Yet direct structural characterization of the O -acylisourea generated from standard dialkylcarbodiimides has eluded the field for over four decades. Here we report the gas-phase separation and structural identification of both the O -acylisourea and the N -acylurea isomers, sampled directly from the reaction media by nanospray ionization (nESI), by coupling high-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry with tandem mass spectrometry (nESI-FAIMS–MS ⁿ ). Using N,N'-diisopropylcarbodiimide (DIC) and (S)-3,3,3-trifluoro-2-methoxy-2-phenylpropanoic acid (MTPA) as a model system, we achieve baseline FAIMS separation of the two isomers and stablish their assignments through three convergent lines of evidence: isomer-specific CID fragmentation patterns, real-time kinetic monitoring of the isomerization directly from solution and isomer-specific infrared multiple-photon dissociation (IRMPD) spectra supported by DFT calculations. These results constitute the first gas-phase separation and structural assignment of the O -acylisourea and N -acylurea isomers generated from a standard dialkylcarbodiimide and sampled directly from solution without chemical trapping or prior isolation, also providing a practical handle for tracking the O -acylisourea/ N -acylurea partition — and distinguishing both from downstream products — by standard tandem MS.

papers.title: Reinventing Density Functional Theory with Machine Learning on Integral Features
papers.abstract: Kohn–Sham density functional theory remains central to electronic structure modeling because of its efficiency and the steady gains in accuracy that has been achieved through improved density functionals. Here we introduce a conceptually new strategy in which a multilayer perceptron learns a nonlinear functional of integrated local descriptors (“integral features”). In contrast to grid-wise neural‑network approaches, the integral‑features formulation applies the nonlinear model only once per calculation, preserving the computational efficiency of standard density functionals while enabling a substantially richer functional dependence. Using this framework, we develop ML25@MN15, an integral-features functional trained on 185 databases spanning thermochemistry, kinetics, noncovalent interactions, spin-flip energies, and molecular structures.
