Enabled by its expanded representational flexibility, ML25@MN15 achieves a mean unsigned error of 1.05 kcal/mol over 7232 energetic data and consistently outperforms leading modern functionals across all major categories, including systems containing transition metals. Because the neural network operates on integrated descriptors rather than grid‑point values, the computational cost of ML25@MN15 remains comparable to MN15. These results demonstrate that introducing integral features and allowing the machine to determine the density functional’s dependence on them yields a high‑accuracy density functional without increasing computational cost.

papers.title: Strain-Induced Anisotropic Transport and Degeneracy Breaking in Monolayer and Bilayer Black Phosphorus: A DFT Based Analysis
papers.abstract: This study illustrates a DFT calculation of the electronic properties of unstrained monolayer and bilayer black phosphorus with 4% uniaxial strain. It uses the PBE functional theory on the GGA level, as well as optimized structure and band structures obtained from SCF calculations. The unstrained monolayer showed a direct bandgap of approximately 0.82 eV while the bilayer showed a reduced bandgap of 0.27 eV due to interlayer coupling. Under tensile strain (4%), the bilayer structure showed clear lifting of band degeneracy near the conduction band minimum, which was not observed for the monolayer. Modulation due to strain was more pronounced in the monolayer with the bandgap increased under tensile strain. Though the bilayer showed weaker tunability with stronger symmetry distortion effects. It is evident from the curvature analysis of the band that higher carrier mobility is preferred by monolayer BP, hence preferably balanced n-MOS and p-MOS active, while the bilayer is preferable for p-MOS operation under tensile strain. The observations confirm that strain and number of layers can be utilized to successfully engineer the black phosphorus's electronic properties towards nano-electronic and straintronic applications.

papers.title: Information entropy-based structural-functional chemintropic similarities for modeling binding reactions and design of antiviral molecules
papers.abstract: Chemical similarity is a fundamental concept in chemistry, materials science, and biology. The Tanimoto similarity measure is crucial in these areas; however, it has certain limitations, such as its inability to consider molecular function, lack of quantitative structural information, and sensitivity to molecular fingerprints. This study introduces chemintropic similarity (CS), an entropy-based metric that integrates both structural and functional molecular attributes within an entropic space using Shannon entropy theory. CS employs fractional Shannon entropy arrays derived from molecular representations (e.g., SMILES) and optimizes context parameters through machine learning. Incorporated into an entropic k-nearest neighbor (ekNN) model as a distance metric, CS surpasses conventional similarity measures, including Tanimoto, across multiple datasets, demonstrating reduced prediction errors and enhanced generalizability, particularly with small datasets. Variants utilizing Renyi entropy and entropy extracted from standard molecular fingerprints further improve model accuracy. The ekNN approach also exceeds baseline graph neural network (GNN) models in predictive performance. Applied to drug-virus interaction modeling, CS accurately predicts ligand binding to Dengue virus serotypes, facilitating pan-serotype modeling. By leveraging the "magic methyl" effect, a molecular design workflow was developed to generate novel drug candidates with significantly improved theoretical potency compared to GNN-based methods. This all-entropic framework offers a robust platform for molecular property prediction, activity cliff modeling, and drug design, integrating structural-functional information entropy to advance cheminformatics and drug discovery.

papers.title: Frequent Hitter Prediction Beyond Classification Models
Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
papers.abstract: Data-driven approaches are increasingly popular in catalysis, supplementing and even replacing traditional strategies that relied on empirical optimization. However, their application in the field of bio-inspired cage catalysis remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the limited chemical space of known catalytically active cages. As a result, mechanistic insights are often obtained using computationally intensive DFT calculations on a handful of structurally similar cages. As chemical systems grow in complexity, this approach becomes impractical. Herein, we report a framework that significantly expedites the exploration of a much wider structural landscape while offering computational insights. This is made possible by a novel in situ experimental procedure – which circumvents the traditional time-consuming process of prepare, isolate, characterize, and test – coupled with data-driven methods to identify molecular features that govern activity. Using this approach, we experimentally explore 30 unique PdnL2n cages (n = 2–4) that mediate a nitro-aldol reaction with activities spanning over four orders of magnitude. Using this dataset, a random forest model trained on molecular descriptors was developed to predict ΔG‡ (MAE of 0.4 kcal mol−1 and R² = 0.9). SHap-ley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted geometric preorganization and electrostatic interactions within the cage as key determinants of catalytic efficiency. Moreover, DFT calculations on a selection of cages further validated these insights, indicating that meaningful mechanistic understanding can be achieved at significantly reduced computational cost. We anticipate that this integrated screen / data-driven / mechanistic strategy will provide a blueprint workflow for understanding metal-organic cage reactivity and encourage the generation of more comprehensive structural datasets, ultimately enabling the rational design of improved catalytic architectures.

papers.title: Mechanism of Peroxides Activation by Atomic Hydrogen
papers.abstract: Atomic hydrogen (·H) has been intensively investigated owing to its potential role in a sustainable hydrogen-based economy for peroxides activation. However, the process of peroxides activation via ·H has not been systematically elucidated, and the mechanism of the complex reaction remains unrevealed up to this point. To gain mechanical insight into this redox reaction, theoretical calculations are conducted to study the activation of peroxides by ·H. Through quantum chemistry (QM) calculations and advanced ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we investigate how the O-O bonds are broken by ·H and reactive oxygen species (ROS) are produced. QM calculations show that O-O bonds are likely to gain electrons. AIMD simulations with advanced metadynamics sampling techniques are applied to compute detailed reaction processes and free energy files. One-electron transfer from ·H to peroxide is responsible for ROS generation. These findings may provide a theoretical mechanism for the peroxides activation with ·H to produce ROS, and much more sustainable catalytic peroxides systems can be rationally designed by appropriately utilizing ·H.

papers.title: Tetrahedral MII4L6 (M = Fe, Zn) cages equipped with walls featuring antiaromatic pentalene motifs
papers.abstract: Antiaromatic compounds are often difficult to work with due to their relative instability in comparison with aromatic analogues. As a consequence, their application in functional materials remains in its infancy. Here, we report the synthesis of porous M II 4 L 6 (M = Fe, Zn) coordination cages equipped with dibenzo[ a , e ]pentalene panels involving the antiaromatic motif of pentalene stabilized by benzannulation. Both cages encapsulate fullerene C 60 , with the more adaptable zinc(II) cage also binding C 70 , undergoing pronounced structural reconfiguration upon C 60 inclusion, and displaying broader affinity for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The cages selectively bind anthraquinone over its reduced form and interact with steroids such as testosterone and cholesterol. Remarkably, the chemical shifts of the guests are affected by the aromatic Clar sextets rather than the antiaromatic pentalene motif. These assemblies represent only the second reported example of a supramolecular cage with a cavity fully enclosed by antiaromatic walls and demonstrate that benzannulated antiaromatic motifs can be incorporated into cages without interrupting conventional host–guest behavior, while simultaneously allowing systematic tuning of magnetic shielding effects.

papers.title: Intermolecular Excitonic Coupling in Molecular Aggregates Facilitates Polariton Formation
papers.abstract: J-aggregates of cyanine dyes are optimal organic materials for polariton formation, enabling access to concentrated solution-processable thin films, extreme transition dipole strength due to superradiance, and ultranarrow linewidths. The polaritonic literature often neglects the microscopic intermolecular interactions responsible for these effects, condensing the supramolecular chemistry of J-aggregates into a source of large oscillator strength and ultranarrow linewidth. However, the underlying nature of the excitonic material drastically affects polariton properties. Here, we elucidate the effects of intermolecular dipolar coupling on polariton formation by comparing cavity coupling of a monomeric and J-aggregated cyanine dye at similar concentrations. The cavities display similar apparent Rabi splitting of 168 ± 4 meV (monomer) and 203 ± 1 meV (J-aggregate), yet possess distinctly different spectra, rendering the monomer intermediately coupled and the J-aggregate strongly coupled. Our results suggest that excitonic coupling facilitates polariton formation (even in highly disordered organic thin films), reinforcing J-aggregates as favorable molecular substrates for strong coupling.

papers.title: Accurate (n,m) Assignment of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes from Electron Diffraction Patterns via Local Candidate Search and Self-Consistency Correction
papers.abstract: The chirality ( n , m ) of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) strongly influences their properties and growth behavior, requiring accurate and reproducible evaluation methods. Nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) is a powerful approach for ( n , m ) assignment, but practical analysis is often affected by analyst-dependent steps, manual measurement errors, and the tilt of individual nanotubes relative to the incident electron beam. Here, building on the previously developed calibration-free diffraction analysis framework, we further developed a practical SWCNT chirality-assignment protocol that combines local candidate search with self-consistency-based cross-check correction while explicitly accounting for manual measurement errors and CNT tilt. Feature extraction and candidate screening were semi-automated using an ImageJ script and an Excel VBA macro, thereby improving efficiency and reproducibility. Using 2394 simulated NBED images covering CNT diameters of 0.4–2.3 nm, chiral angles of 0–30°, and tilt angles of 0.5–16.5°, the assignment accuracy improved from 71.6% for conventional TRUNC-based analysis to 97.7% with the proposed protocol. Errors in mean CNT diameter, mean chiral angle, and metallic CNT fraction were also significantly reduced. This improvement was primarily attributable to the newly introduced overlap ratio, which reduced ambiguity in initial candidate selection.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanism of the Catalytic Radical Termination in Fatty Acid Photodecarboxylase
papers.abstract: Fatty acid photodecarboxylase (FAP) is a photoenzyme that converts fatty acids into hydrocarbons through light-driven radical chemistry. Although the early photochemical steps have been elucidated, the molecular mechanism governing the catalytic termination remains unresolved. Here, we address this issue through a multiscale computational investigation based on explicit dynamic simulations of the reactive processes through a combination of classical and polarizable QM/MM strategies. Our results indicate that, following rapid decarboxylation, the resulting alkyl radical is predominantly quenched via a proton-coupled electron transfer mechanism mediated by the protonated arginine R451 and nearby water molecules. In contrast, water-assisted bicarbonate formation is found to be a rare event at that temperature, consistent with recent experimental observations. Furthermore, calculated absorption spectra demonstrate that distinct active-site configurations, either involving a neutral R451/water network or the presence of bicarbonate, can both account for the transient red-shifted flavin species FAD RS observed experimentally. Overall, these findings provide a coherent and unified molecular picture of the catalytic termination in FAP and emphasize the key roles played by active-site heterogeneity and water dynamics in controlling photoenzymatic reactivity.

papers.title: Hybrid HPC and quantum computing framework for multiscale modelling of chemical systems
papers.abstract: We present a multiscale workflow for coupling quantum computing algorithms for quantum chemical calculations with conventional High-Performance Computing (HPC) software. The resulting embedding framework, implemented in the multiscale computational chemistry environment ChemShell, combines a generic N-layer subtractive Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) scheme and selection of an active orbital space for the quantum algorithm region. We have benchmarked the embedding models for gas phase and solvated molecules to understand the performance, benefits and current limitations of embedding quantum computing algorithms within a QM/MM model. We compare the performance of simulated Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE) calculations on an HPC cluster using Graphical Processing Units (GPUs) and Central Processing Units (CPUs).

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Testing of Natural Products Against Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial drug resistance is a global concern driven by diverse bacterial mechanisms, many of which are exacerbated by human activities. Staphylococcus aureus resistant strains pose an immediate threat and a substantial health burden. Natural products (NPs), recognized for their structural diversity and antimicrobial properties, can inhibit enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (FabI), a rate-limiting enzyme of the type II fatty acid synthase (FAS-II) system, which is essential for the biosynthesis of fatty acids that form the bacterial lipid membrane. Herein, we present a general workflow that integrates structure- and ligand-based approaches, specifically, consensus molecular docking with predictions of machine learning models to prioritize NPs candidates for testing as FabI inhibitors of S. aureus . The overarching goal of the study was to ultimately identify bioactive molecules against S. aureus . Structural analysis of top-1000 NPs identified 472 scaffolds, with the predominant chemotypes corresponding to chalcones, flavanones, flavones, and phenylpropanoids. Experimental evaluation of selected compounds highlighted taxoquinone as a promising scaffold, exhibiting moderate activity against S. aureus strains tested (pMIC = 3.21). Structure similarity calculations further identified additional promising NPs within the analyzed LANaPDB and NatUV DB collections.

papers.title: Enhancing All-Solid-State Batteries Performance through Thickness Control and Surface Passivation of Thermally Evaporated Lithium Metal Anodes
papers.abstract: Thin lithium metal anodes are key to realizing high-energy-density and enhanced safety in allsolid-state batteries (ASSBs). However, extruded lithium foils thinner than 50 µm suffer from poor structural integrity, rough surfaces, and resistive native passivation layers which severely limit cycling stability. Here, we demonstrate that thermally evaporated, highly pure lithium with smooth, grain-boundaries surfaces morphology significantly improves interfacial contact and electrochemical performance. For a fixed lithium thickness, replacing extruded lithium with a 50 µm evaporated lithium anode increases the critical current density (CCD) from 1.6 to 2.1 mA cm-2 in Li|Li symmetric cells using Li6PS5Cl (LPSCl) as solid electrolyte separator. In LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811)|LPSCl|Li full cells, this configuration enables 161 stable cycles at 1.5 mA cm-2 and 1.6 mAh cm-2. A systematic thickness dependence study reveals that reducing the evaporated lithium metal to 25 µm severely limits full-cell performance (~20 cycles), underscoring the need for a sufficient electrochemically active lithium reservoir to mitigate void formation and to compensate for the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth. To address this limitation, an ultra-thin 65 nm LiF passivation layer was applied to 25 µm evaporated lithium. The LiF coating suppresses chemical degradation during storage, stabilizes the lithium/LPSCl interface, limits SEI growth, and mitigates dendrite formation, thereby increasing the CCD to 2.6 mA cm-2. In full cells, LiF-coated 25 µm lithium delivers over 500 and 300 cycles at current density of 1.5 mA cm-2 and 3 mA cm-2 respectively. These results establish LiF-passivated thermally evaporated lithium as a high-performance anode design for next-generation ASSBs.

papers.title: Activity-cliff awareness enables robust graph learning formolecular property prediction
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting molecular activity is hindered by activity cliffs (ACs), which are sharp potency changes between highly similar compounds that distort the smoothness assumed by modern quantitative structure–activity relationship (SAR) models and graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we introduce AC awareness (ACA), an inductive bias that reshapes GNN latent spaces to account for these discontinuities. Implemented through an ACA loss combining regression with softmargin triplet contrastive learning, the method dynamically mines high-value activity-cliff triplets during training and corrects inconsistent neighbourhoods in latent space. This process yields progressively fewer cliff violations, more coherent activity gradients, and reduced label incoherence across diverse chemical spaces. Evaluated on 52 datasets spanning low-sample narrow-scaffold series, large mixed-scaffold benchmarks, matched-pair cliff classification, and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) property prediction, ACA consistently improves predictive accuracy over strong extended-connectivity fingerprint (ECFP) and GNN baselines. The approach generalizes across multiple GNN backbones and remains robust under fixed hyperparameters. These results suggest that ACA provides a principled strategy for enhancing molecular property prediction by aligning latent representations with the nonadditive behaviour underlying ACs.

papers.title: Photon-Driven Catalytic Formic Acid Dehydrogenation Beyond the Sabatier Limit
papers.abstract: Sabatier scaling relationships impose fundamental limits on heterogeneous catalysis by coupling the energetics of reactant activation, intermediate stabilization, and product desorption. We show that visible photons circumvent this constraint by selectively removing a rate-limiting surface intermediate without changing the thermal catalytic energy landscape. Using formic acid decomposition on Pt, we demonstrated that 450 nm photon excitation reversibly promotes catalytic turnover by more than three orders of magnitude (4000x) beyond the thermal Sabatier-limited maximum while preserving 95% selectivity to dehydrogenation products, at an apparent quantum yield of 40%. Operando infrared spectroscopy showed that visible wavelength photons monotonically depleted linearly adsorbed CO*, the strongly bound intermediate accumulating to high steady-state coverage because thermal desorption is slow relative to its formation. Across excitation wavelengths, photon-driven rates collapse onto a single linear dependence on the extent of CO* depletion, identifying photon-promoted CO* desorption as the controlling event. Kinetic isotope experiments further separated the photon-driven and thermal pathways: thermal rates exhibited a primary formyl C–H isotope effect, while photon-driven rates did not, consistent with an isotope-insensitive CO* photodesorption step. With increasing photon flux, apparent formic acid reaction orders increased toward unity and apparent activation barriers decreased from 62 ± 3 kJ mol -1 toward zero, reflecting a photon-controlled shift from CO* coverage-dominated kinetics toward turnover governed by the intrinsic rate of formic acid activation. These findings demonstrate that photons break through Sabatier-imposed rate maxima not by modifying adsorption energies, but by shortening the lifetime of a strongly bound intermediate. This work establishes photon-regulated intermediate lifetimes as a strategy for catalytic performance beyond conventional thermochemical limits.

papers.title: All-Solid-State Mechanochemical CH4 Generation from La2(CO3)3·8H2O and La(OH)3 without External Heating or Gas Supply
papers.abstract: CH 4 generation is a promising route for CO 2 utilization. However, conventional CH 4 generation generally requires elevated temperatures and pressurized-gas infrastructure, raising challenges in terms of both energy consumption and operational safety. Here, we focus on lanthanum, which exhibits a high affinity for water and CO 2 , and demonstrate a gas-reactant-free mechanochemical route to CH 4 using La 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ·8H 2 O as the carbon source and La(OH) 3 as the H 2 source. Unlike conventional methods, CH4 generation was achieved without external heating or gaseous reactants by coupling H 2 evolution arising from the mechanochemical dehydration of La(OH) 3 with reactions involving La 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ·8H 2 O. Moreover, CH 4 generation and H 2 evolution were monitored in-situ by gas analysis using a quadrupole mass spectrometer(QMS) connected to the ball-milling system. Notably, whereas conventional thermal treatment of La(OH) 3 and La 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ·8H 2 O produces no detectable CH 4 , mechanochemical activation enabled CH 4 generation from carbonate with a yield of 91%.

papers.title: Hybrid Physics–Machine Learning Approaches for Distillation Column Startup Optimization: A Structured Review
papers.abstract: Distillation startup is among the most energy-intensive and poorly automated phases in chemical manufacturing, routinely involving extended periods of off-spec production before reaching steady-state operation. Existing machine-learning approaches for distillation control predominantly address steady-state operation, but hybrid physics–ML models specifically targeting startup transients remain underexplored. This review surveys hybrid grey-box modeling architectures with emphasis on the delta-ML (residual correction) paradigm, reviews model predictive control (MPC) strategies for distillation, and identifies three specific research gaps at their intersection. An ongoing implementation framework is described in which a simplified MESH-equation model is augmented by a neural network correction term and embedded within a receding-horizon MPC loop for startup trajectory optimization under feed composition uncertainty. The proposed approach is positioned to reduce time-to-on-spec product and reboiler energy consumption during startup, with relevance to petroleum refining, specialty chemical, and pharmaceutical manufacturing contexts where startup losses are disproportionately costly.

papers.title: Design of a Drug Delivery System for Controlled Release of Cinnamaldehyde with Potential Action in Neuroinflammatory Modulation
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle drug delivery systems are promising carriers for penetrating the blood-brain barrier (BBB) in the central nervous system (CNS), enabling the delivery of therapeutic agents to treat chronic neuroinflammatory conditions. In this study, elastic Span niosomes loaded with cinnamaldehyde were designed and characterized as a potential intranasal drug delivery system for neuroinflammatory modulation. Niosomes were synthesized via a low-energy emulsification method using Span 80, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and cinnamaldehyde, following a three-factor factorial design (18 formulations in triplicate). Particle size was characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), release kinetics were modeled using the Korsmeyer-Peppas equation, and response surface analysis (Statgraphics) was applied to optimize formulation parameters. The optimal formulation (BAB: 168.75 mg cinnamaldehyde, 25 mg/mL PVA, 0.945 mg/mL Span 80) yielded a mean particle size of 72.03 ± 20.23 nm. FT-IR spectroscopy confirmed the presence of all formulation components in the lyophilized systems. The Korsmeyer-Peppas model indicated Fickian diffusion-based release kinetics (n → 0). Response surface analysis showed that higher PVA:Span 80 ratios minimize particle size, while higher Span 80 concentrations maximize the release constant k. TEM images confirmed spherical vesicular morphology consistent with elastic Span niosomes. These results demonstrate the feasibility of cinnamaldehyde-loaded niosomes as a nanocarrier platform with potential for intranasal CNS drug delivery.

papers.title: Red Light-Responsive Bioorthogonal Chemistry Enabled On-Demand Prodrug Activation for Cancer Therapy
papers.abstract: Light-driven chemistry has revolutionized modern medicine, enabling precise disease detection and ondemand therapeutic interventions with high spatiotemporal accuracy. However, despite tremendous advances in bioorthogonal reactions have been achieved, photoclick chemistry-based therapeutics remain as a challenge in vivo. To address this limitation, we have developed a multifunctional BODIPYcaged glucamine dihydrotetrazine (BGdTz) that integrates cancer-targeting, fluorescence imaging, and photoactivable tetrazine bioorthogonal chemistry. By targeting the overexpressed glucose transporter 1 (Glut1) on cancer cells, BGdTz specifically accumulates at the tumor site, leading to high-contrast fluorescence imaging of tumor in murine models. Subsequent irradiation of BGdTz with red light results in a spatialtemporal formation of glucamine-tetrazine. Furthermore, we have demonstrated an imageguided bioorthogonal prodrug activation between BGdTz and trans-cyclooctene caged doxorubicin, revealing potent antitumor efficacy and minimal systemic toxicity in A375 xenograft mouse models. In summary, we present a red light-controllable tetrazine bioorthogonal platform operable in mammals, offering a powerful tool for dual cancer diagnosis and therapy. We anticipate that this photouncagingdriven tetrazine ligation will open new avenues for precision medicine.

papers.title: ()-Piyunneolignans A–F, Six Pairs of Neolignans Enantiomers from Piper yunnanense
papers.abstract: Phytochemical investigation of Piper yunnanense resulted in the isolation of seven neolignans, comprising six new compounds (1–6) and one analogue (7). Subsequent chiral resolution resolved these isolates into seven pairs of enantiomers. Their structures, including absolute configurations, were established by comprehensive spectroscopic data analysis and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) calculations. Piyunneolignans A–C (1–3) possessed the same C-9–C-2ʹ/C-8–O–C-3ʹ linkage as puberulin E (7), while piyunneolignans D–F (4–6) featured a unique C-9–C-3ʹ/C-8–O–C-4ʹ linkage.

papers.title: Photocatalyzed dehydrogenation of polyethylene
papers.abstract: Partial dehydrogenation has proven to be a key step in selective chemical upcycling of polyolefins. Existing methods for dehydrogenation of polyolefins are limited by the use of sacrificial hydrogen acceptors, high temperatures, precious metal catalysts or caustic reagents. We report a dual photocatalyst – nickel catalyst system for the dehydrogenation of polyethylene using inexpensive and commercially available reagents. This method allows for faster selective dehydrogenation of unprocessed postconsumer polyethylene at milder temperatures including functionalization of solid surfaces. Computational studies implicate a low barrier β-hydride elimination, an elementary step that is typically not facile from organonickel intermediates. An anionic nickel(II) species wherein a bromide anion modulates the metal center by distal hydrogen bonding with the ligand is proposed to account for this unusual behavior. The resulting dehydrogenated polymers were further hydrocarboxylated to generate poly(ethylene- co -acrylic acid) copolymers (EAA) and zinc-neutralized ionomers with promising physical properties. Due to their adhesive features, optical clarity, and mechanical toughness, these materials have numerous applications. The method further allows access to linear architectures of these materials, for which no commercial routes are available.

papers.title: Tuning Chiroptical Properties and Device Hyperfluorescence Efficiency via Acceptor Modification in an Intramolecularly Sensitised TADF Dendrimer
papers.abstract: Multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters offer an attractive solution for the fabrication of colour-saturated organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Still, their rigid frameworks often lead to slow reverse intersystem crossing and aggregation-caused quenching. To address these challenges and simultaneously introduce chiroptical properties in solution-processable materials, here we present the first examples of chiral intramolecular Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) MR-TADF dendrimers, CzPBN-CzBN and CzPBA-CzBN . These emitters combine an MRTADF core with chiral paracyclophane (CzP)-based donor dendrons linked to different acceptor units, benzonitrile for CzPBN-CzBN and benzoic acid for CzPBA-CzBN . While both dendrimers show narrowband TADF emission, the nature of the acceptor impacts their chiroptical properties. Specifically, CzPBA-CzBN exhibits circularly polarised luminescence (CPL), whereas CzPBN-CzBN does not due to a weaker circular dichroism signal. Conversely, in solution-processed hyperfluorescent (HF) OLEDs, the device with CzPBN-CzBN achieved a superior maximum external quantum efficiency ( EQE max ) of 19.7% and lower efficiency roll-off ( EQE of 18.9% at 1000 cd m -2 ) compared to the device with CzPBA-CzBN ( EQE max/1000 = 17.2/16.5%). These findings reveal an intrinsic trade-off between CPL response and HF device performance, demonstrating how precise modulation of the excited-state manifold via acceptor engineering can be used to tailor the properties of intramolecular sensitised TADF emitters.

papers.title: Simplifying Reactive Force Field Simulations
papers.abstract: Chemical reactivity modelling in large systems over extended timescales is computationally and theoretically challenging; ab initio methods are too expensive, while classical force fields cannot handle bond breaking/formation. Existing solutions like reactive force fields require extensive expertise to develop, and machine-learned approaches often need prohibitively large, high-quality datasets for training. These barriers have hindered the modelling of reactive chemical processes. Multi-state empirical valence bond (MSEVB) theory offers an alternative by enabling conventional unreactive force fields to be mixed in a controlled manner to selectively describe chemical reactions. However, existing MSEVB implementations are often field-specific, have license-restricted distribution, or rely on complex parameterisation schemes. This work presents a new open-source, general MSEVB implementation, specifically designed to make reactive modelling more accessible to non-experts by using simple energy-based coupling schemes. The implementation here focused on simple energy-based coupling, thereby eliminating the need for complex geometry-based coupling approaches, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for reactive force field development. This generalised approach is demonstrated to reproduce proton migration behaviour in Y-doped and undoped BaZrO 3 ; it is extended to model proton dynamics in bulk water; it incorporates Fermi smearing for electron migration in LiCoO 2 ; and it models proton transfer in liquid imidazole. We demonstrate that only two additional fitted parameters are needed to accurately model proton mobility across these chemically diverse systems.

papers.title: Computational studies on the enantioinversion of the molecular asymmetry of multiple chirality elements
papers.abstract: A series of quantum mechanical calculations and kinetic analysis was conducted on enantioinversion processes involving multiple chiral elements, with a particular focus on winding vine-shaped biaryls (bithiophene with/without methyl substituent and biphenyl types) exhibiting molecular asymmetry in both axial and planar chiralities. The inversions of the chiral elements were shown to take place in a stepwise manner, whereas the experimental racemization behavior appeared kinetically synchronized. Conformational analysis of the vine-shaped bithiophene revealed eight possible conformers for the pair of enantiomers using the CONFLEX method. Quantum mechanics calculations were carried out at the B3LYP/6-31G(d)//B3LYP/6-31G(d), B3LYP/6-311G++(d,p)+GD3//B3LYP/6-31G(d), MP2/cc-pVDZ//MP2/cc-pVDZ, and MP2/cc-pVTZ//MP2/cc-pVDZ levels of theory. Calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G(d) level were primarily used to search for each pathway, revealing that enantioinversion proceeded via three distinct steps. The first conformational transition leading to the second intermediate was calculated to occur with an activation energy of Δ E = 49.2 kJ/mol, without the inversion of chirality. Subsequently, an inversion of axial chirality was observed with a value of ΔE = 106.5 kJ/mol. This was followed by the final inversion of planar chirality, which also exhibited a value of Δ E = 70.3 kJ/mol. It was also established that the enantioinversion of the related biphenyl occurred in a manner analogous to that previously observed, whereas the inversion barrier of the axial chirality was found to be considerably higher (Δ E = 217.9 kJ/mol). The analytical solutions of the rate of racemization and pathway contributions under the quasi-equilibrium approximation were derived, which assumes rapid equilibration of low-barrier conformational changes while treating the kinetics of axial chirality inversion explicitly. DFT studies were conducted also on the enantioinversion of the vine-shaped bithiophene bearing a methyl substituent at the alkenyl moiety. This was because experimental evidence had shown that this process had hardly occurred. The DFT studies revealed that a much higher barrier existed at the initial inversion (Δ E = 205.9 kJ/mol). Conversely, a high barrier has not been identified in the calculation of the second transition state, where the dihedral angle of the axial chirality is estimated to be 0°.

papers.title: A High-Throughput ab initio Database of Harmonic Phonon Properties for Inorganic Crystals
papers.abstract: Phonons play an essential role in condensed matter physics, influencing key phenomena such as vibrational entropy, thermal conductivity, superconductivity, ferroelectricity, and photoluminescence spectra. Here, we present a comprehensive database of harmonic phonon properties, constructed using automated high-throughput (HT) density functional theory (DFT) calculations for 26,413 compounds. The database covers materials with all seven crystal systems and includes primitive cells with up to 60 atoms. In this work, phonons were computed using DFT-based (PBEsol level of theory) second-order interatomic force constants (IFCs), obtained from perturbed supercell calculations and fitted using either least-squares or LASSO-based regression depending on the number of required finite displacements. The phonon workflow is implemented in the HT software Atomate2, incorporating Pheasy, a compressive sensing lattice dynamics code. Within this framework, space group and point group symmetries, as well as the acoustic sum rule and rotational invariance constraints, are applied to the force constants to ensure physical accuracy and reduce numerical errors. This approach offers a substantial computational speedup compared to both the traditional finitedisplacement method and density functional perturbation theory, while maintaining accuracy comparable to both. The resulting phonon database includes phonon dispersions, phonon density of states (DOS), and derived thermodynamic properties such as Helmholtz free energy ( F ), entropy ( S ), and constant-volume heat capacity ( C V ). Our work not only establishes an HT methodology for phonon calculations, but also delivers a large-scale phonon database accessible to Materials Project (MP) users for a range of applications, including materials screening and follow-up computational studies.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Prediction of Corrosion Inhibition Efficiency via Electronegativity Equalisation, Conceptual DFT Descriptors, and PLS-Enhanced Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We present a highly accurate, physically interpretable QSPR model for corrosion inhibition efficiency (IE%) of organic compounds on carbon steel in 1 M HCl. Frontier orbital energies, dipole moment, and conceptual DFT indices (∆N , electrophilicity ω) were constructed without any quantum-chemistry software using the electronegativity equalisation theorem with a Mataga–Nishimoto hardness kernel (EE-HK). After adding 2D molecular descriptors and three latent variables extracted via partial least squares (PLS) from Morgan fingerprints, a nested 5fold cross-validated Ridge regression model with feature selection achieves a crossvalidated R2 of 0.890 ± 0.029 (RMSE 4.2%) across 314 chemically diverse inhibitors. The HOMO–LUMO gap and ∆N dominate the predictive power, confirming the electron-transfer mechanism of corrosion inhibition. The entire workflow is provided as a single open-source Colab notebook, requiring only atomic constants and molecular geometry, and can be used for rapid virtual screening of new inhibitor candidates.

papers.title: Effect of cross-sectional shape, channel tortuosity, and bend rounding on pressure drop in continuous-flow enzymatic microreactors: a Stokes regime CFD study
papers.abstract: The geometric selection of continuous-flow enzymatic microreactors is typically guided by productivity and immobilization criteria, without systematic consideration of energetic performance. This study presents a comprehensive hydraulic characterization of twenty-one microreactor geometries combining three cross-sections (circular, square, hexagonal) and seven channel configurations (straight, zigzag 150°, 120°, 90°, and rounded R3 variants) through CFD simulations in the Stokes regime (Re = 1 to 20). Results reveal a counter-intuitive hierarchy: straight channels consistently yield the highest pressure drop, while zigzag channels perform better at identical length. This behavior is attributed to local velocity redistribution at bends, confirmed by independent FEniCSx cross-validation. Rounding 90° bends (R3 = 3 mm) provides an additional ~6% reduction regardless of cross-section. The circular 90° R3 zigzag configuration achieves the optimal performance, with a 14.5% pressure drop reduction over the straight channel. These results consist in the first component of a multi-criteria selection framework integrating hydraulic performance, enzymatic productivity, and residence time distribution for rational microreactor design.

papers.title: Unraveling In-Situ Gas Capture Mechanisms in ZIF-8 Based Porous Liquids
papers.abstract: Porous liquids (PLs), a class of fluid phase materials exhibiting permanent porosity, have gained increasing attention as a transformative gas capture material due to exceptional sorption capacity and selectivity. To elucidate mechanisms of emergent gas capture, an exemplar ZIF-8 based PL was evaluated for CO 2 capture within a ternary solvent system containing ethylene glycol (EG), water, and 2-methylimidzole (HMIm). For the first time, in situ Attenuated Total Reflectance Infrared Spectroscopy (ATR-IR) was combined with CO 2 sorption testing and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to reveal the high sorption affinity and energetic feasibility of sorbent regeneration for this PL composition. CO 2 uptake in the ZIF-8 based PL was 1.5 mmol/g at 1 bar, 3x higher than that of neat ZIF-8, identifying enhanced CO 2 uptake at low pressures (< 3 bar). ATR-IR proved CO 2 uptake in the PL via formation of bicarbonate species and physisorption mechanisms. AIMD simulations identified ATR-IR band shifts that may be driven by interaction between the EG-H 2 O-HMIm system and CO 2 . Regeneration of the PL via CO2 desorption was achieved at a modest 70°C, lower than competing technologies and supporting the existence of mixed binding mechanisms and instability of the bicarbonate phase. As one of the first studies to evaluate dynamic in situ CO 2 binding within a PL, the existence of multiple binding mechanisms has presented an avenue for enhanced gas capture through design of multicomponent solvent mixtures. Through this investigation, we highlight the potential of tailored PLs for efficient and sustainable solutions in gas capture and storage.

papers.title: Self-Illuminating Nanocrystals Formed from Latent Therapeutic Precursors with Aggregation-Induced Emission
Accelerating Discovery of Glucose Binders via Machine Learning and Molecular Simulations
papers.abstract: Glucose recognition plays a central role in the development of glucose-responsive materials such as sensing platforms, and in therapeutic applications, such as drug delivery systems. This motivates a deeper understanding of the structural and chemical features that most strongly influence binding affinity between glucose and synthetic host molecules. We present a machine learning framework that integrates molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, chemical and structural feature extraction, principal component analysis (PCA), and Gaussian process (GP) regression to investigate glucose binding to synthetic host molecules. Structural and chemical descriptors were systematically assembled to capture geometric, electronic, and topological characteristics of each host, and subsequently reduced in dimensionality using PCA. The resulting principal components were used to train GP models that learn the relationship between feature variations and MD-derived free energy profiles. Representative potentials of mean force (PMFs) illustrate the diversity of binding stability across the host series, with the full dataset reported in the Supporting Information. Although the developed framework does not propose new host features, the combined PCA–GP analysis identifies significant design parameters—such as cavity size, heteroatom distribution, and hydrogen-bonding capacitythat most strongly govern glucose affinity, providing mechanistic insight and guiding the design of next-generation glucose binders.

papers.title: New BODIPY-Based Fluorescent Probes with Selective Sensing of Salts
papers.abstract: This study presents novel BODIPY-based probes for the selective detection of lithium, sodium, and magnesium hexafluorophosphate or antimonate salts, in the presence of other salts. Small cations bind to fluorines of dimethylamino-styryl BODIPY and its monobiotinylated hemicucurbit[8]uril macrocycle derivative causing change in probe electronic properties and conformation as evidenced by DFT calculations. Upon binding with target salts, the probes display a distinct visible color shift from blue to pink and fluorescence emission. These combined responses facilitate both rapid "naked-eye" recognition and fluorescence detection, demonstrating the potential of this macrocyclefunctionalized scaffold for practical electrolyte sensing applications.

papers.title: FLAMES – A flexible and extensible code for Monte Carlo simulations of nanoporous materials
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations are the cornerstone for computational studies of adsorption in nanoporous materials such as zeolites, Metal-Organic Frameworks, and Covalent Organic Frameworks. Currently, most of these simulations rely on classical force fields, which are often limited in their ability to describe specific interactions or the intrinsic flexibility of the host framework. Machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have emerged as a powerful alternative, offering near ab initio accuracy while remaining computationally feasible, potentially capturing framework flexibility and complex potential energy surfaces. Despite this promise, there is a significant gap, as current tools implementing MLIPs are often general-purpose codes adapted for adsorption or in-house solutions. Here, we introduce FLAMES (Flexible Lattice Adsorption by Monte Carlo Engine Simulation), a new software package designed to perform Monte Carlo-based simulations of nanoporous materials using MLIPs and other energy calculation methods, paving the way for more accurate and physically realistic molecular simulations. We detailed the implementation of different methodologies, including Widom insertion, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC), hybrid GCMC/MD, and Transition Matrix Monte Carlo simulations presenting validation examples for each method and evaluating the performance and accuracy of different energy calculation methodologies.

papers.title: Mechanoactivated Room Temperature Phosphorescence from Dynamic Regulation of Aggregate Structures
papers.abstract: Organic room‑temperature phosphorescence (RTP) typically requires a static, rigid environment to suppress non‑radiative decay of triplet excitons. This design principle creates a fundamental paradox for mechanically activated RTP: mechanical force usually disrupts crystalline order, leading to amorphisation and phosphorescence quenching rather than turn‑on. Here we resolve this paradox by exploiting a reversible crystal‑to‑crystal phase transition in a host–guest doped organic system. The as‑prepared material shows no RTP, yet mild mechanical stimulation (rubbing, scratching or pressing) triggers a domino‑like transformation that switches on intense, long‑lived phosphorescence. Structural and photophysical studies reveal that the stimulus drives a polymorphic transition while preserving long‑range order, with the guest playing a dual role in enabling RTP and kinetically controlling the phase transformation. The strategy is generalisable across multiple guests, and enables high‑contrast, spatially addressable phosphorescent patterning for advanced information encryption. Our work overcomes the long‑standing mechanoactivation paradox and establishes dynamic crystal phase transitions as a versatile platform for stimuli‑responsive RTP materials.

papers.title: Iterative representation learning organizes a vast catalytic chemical space for efficient catalyst discovery
papers.abstract: Data-driven catalyst discovery has remained largely confined to known or narrow search spaces because conventional active learning relies on descriptor spaces fixed before exploration. Here we show that active learning coupled with representation learning can explore a truly vast and largely unknown catalytic chemical space with minimal prior knowledge. We integrated highthroughput experimentation with automatic feature engineering and applied it to low-temperature dry reforming of methane, targeting a 61-dimensional elemental-composition space containing approximately 1012 multielement catalysts. Through the co-evolution of descriptor representation, predictive models, and data acquisition, the active-learning loop transformed the descriptor space so that chemically diverse high-performing catalysts were organized into a localized region. Sampling this region enabled the discovery of 91 catalysts with H2 yield ≥25%, spanning multiple chemically distinct elemental-combination families rather than a single dominant motif. These results establish iterative representation learning as a strategy for scaling catalyst exploration while efficiently discovering diverse high-performance catalysts.

papers.title: Triplet Exciton Manipulation in Hybrid Materials: Narrowband Emission with Persistent TADF, Dual-Color Afterglow, and Ultralong Phosphorescence
papers.abstract: The development of narrowband afterglow with small full width at half maximum (FWHM) is highly challenging due to inherent spectral broadening from triplet and solid-state emissions. Here, three hybrid materials with narrowband, long-lived, high quantum yield, and temperature-responsive dynamic afterglow are realized by doping the intrinsic narrowband thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) organic fluorophores into the in situ forming robust inorganic framework by a melt-cooling treatment. These hybrid materials exhibit a small FWHM of 33 nm, color purity of about 95%, and long persistent afterglow duration of over 20 s, which show a maximum photoluminescence quantum yield of 68.1% increased about 25 times compared with counterpart guests. Intriguingly, these three hybrid materials display three distinctive narrowband luminescence behaviors: persistent TADF (pTADF), ultralong room temperature phosphorescence (URTP), and dual-color afterglow of pTADF and URTP. Through structural characterization, photophysical studies, time-resolved ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical calculation, this work sheds light on the regulation of turning the luminescence mechanism of afterglow materials from pTADF to dual-color afterglow to URTP. Benefiting from their facile preparation, narrowband emission, long-lived afterglow, and temperature responsiveness, we showcased their great potential in an advanced application of temperature-dependent encryption. This study provides new insights into the development of high-colored purity and high-performance afterglow materials.

papers.title: Probabilistic Predictive Models as an Alternative to Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting: a CEST Test Case
papers.abstract: This paper evaluates probabilistic predictive models for CEST inverse analysis, and compares them to fingerprint matching on experimental spectra. Results published by Goren et al. (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 18972–18981, https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c03583) were used to train probabilistic regression and flow-matching models tailored for lanthanide identification based on exchange between the 19F signals of a free molecule and its organolanthanide complex. Both models demonstrated comparable accuracy to fingerprint-matching, additionally providing continuous-valued concentration and uncertainty estimates, reduced compute requirements, and generalization beyond the discrete fingerprint dictionary.

papers.title: Isolation and Structure Elucidation of Cytotoxic Compounds, Sukumolides A-C, derived from Deep Sea Marine Invertebrates Collected in Kochi
Computationally Guided Design of Isostructural Formamide Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: The rational design of novel hydrogen-bonded motifs for constructing robust molecular hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) is challenging, particularly for mesoporous solids. Here, we demonstrate that the integration of chemical insights and crystal structure prediction (CSP) enables the rational design of novel HOFs based on trigonal formamide-terminated linkers. The well-defined spikes of low-energy, isostructural HOFs on the predicted lattice-energy landscapes reveal a family of crystal packings with diverse hydrogen-bonded motifs that nonetheless all result in similar predicted pore topologies. These CSP results enabled the experimental discovery of isostructural HOFs with predetermined pore channel sizes and functionalities to be identified. For a linker with extended arms (TTBF), a hydrogen-bonded dimeric structure with cis -configured formamide groups was identified as a higher-energy ‘spike’ in a CSP landscape, corresponding to a mesoporous HOF with unprecedentedly large pores. This material was successfully synthesized and shown to be permanently mesoporous with the largest pore size exhibited by a HOF to date (4.2 nm). Our methodology illustrates the potential of a simple and scalable formylation reaction between formic acid and abundant amine precursors to generate porous HOFs, redefining the limit of pore sizes that can be achieved in molecular solids.

papers.title: Metal-Free CO2 Fixation: Conversion of Epoxides to Cyclic Carbonates by a Highly Efficient Bifunctional Boron-Tethered Nitrenium Catalyst
papers.abstract: The development of sustainable, metal-free catalytic platforms for the chemical fixation of carbon dioxide (CO2) into value-added products remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the rational design of a highly efficient bifunctional organoboron catalyst, featuring a Lewis acidic boron center tethered to an N-heterocyclic nitrenium ion, for the solvent-free cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides. This system exhibits enhanced catalytic activity and recyclability, delivering a broad range of cyclic carbonates in excellent yields under neat conditions. Thorough mechanistic studies reveal the key transient intermediates in the reaction pathway. Notably, our catalyst demonstrates the highest activity among the metal-free systems reported to date for the coupling of CO2 to propylene oxide under ambient conditions (TOF = 12.4 h-1, 25 °C, 1 bar), establishing this organoboron framework as a remarkably robust and sustainable catalyst.

papers.title: Physically Informed Population Initialization Improves Bonobo Optimizer Searches for Atomic Cluster Global Minima
papers.abstract: Reliable global optimization of atomic clusters is limited not only by the ruggedness of the potential energy surface but also by the quality of the starting population supplied to the search algorithm. We examine this issue for the Bonobo Optimizer (BO) using a workflow that combines external PyAR-style population initialization, local Lennard-Jones relaxation, geometry repair, and structural similarity filtering. The initializer generates physically reasonable and structurally diverse trial clusters before the BO loop begins, while the relaxation and filtering steps map candidates to local minima and reduce redundant population updates. On Lennard-Jones clusters, the unmodified BO framework becomes unreliable beyond LJ13, and local relaxation with similarity filtering alone remains insufficient for the double-funnel LJ38 benchmark, reaching the global minimum only 6 times in 20 runs. Adding the Tabu-style initializer changes this outcome: LJ38 is solved in all 20 independent runs, and the full LJ2–LJ100 benchmark reaches 949 successes in 1030 runs, corresponding to an overall success rate of 92.1%. The main remaining failures occur for LJ75–LJ77, consistent with the known difficulty of the Marks-decahedral exceptions. These results identify physically informed population construction as a practical route for improving BO-based cluster global optimization.

papers.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Carboxylate-Return Deoxygenative Cyclization of Propargylic Esters
papers.abstract: ：Transformations of easily accessible propargylic esters have emerged as a powerful synthetic tool for organic synthesis. A significant challenge lies in the transformation of propargylic ester is that the in-situ generated carboxylate is typically an unders utilized leaving group or a migrating acyloxy unit. The development of novel, robust methodologies to efficiently capture and edit the carboxylate moiety into the product would represent a meaningful advancement. Herein, we report a strategy that enables the carboxylate-return deoxygenative cyclization of propargylic esters with isocyanide, wherein the carboxylate anion serves as an active nucleophile to participate in downstream reactions. Under mild reaction conditions, all three C–O bonds (C=O & C–O bonds) of the carboxylate moiety in propargylic esters are concomitantly converted into C–C, C–N, and C–H bonds in a single step, thus affording α, β-unsaturated γ-lactams in an atom-economical manner.

papers.title: An emergent interfacial length scale governs hydrophobic attraction across all molecular scales, not a crossover
papers.abstract: Hydrophobic attraction is a water-mediated force between solutes (hydrophobes) whose origin remains controversial. A widely adopted organizing framework, due to Lum–Chandler–Weeks, posits a crossover in the free energy of solvation, from small-scale, fluctuation-dominated, volumetric behavior at small solute radii Rs to interfacial physics at Rs of the order 5–10 Å. If such a crossover were to reflect a genuine change in physical mechanism, this should be evident in the interaction between two hydrophobes. Using molecular simulation, we show that the range and depth of the potential of mean force between hydrophobes, together with local density and compressibility profiles around a single solute, exhibit no signature of crossover across this range of Rs. Rather, these quantities are governed by an emergent length scale ℓ present already at molecular dimensions. This length scale increases smoothly with increasing Rs and with proximity of water to liquid–vapor coexistence, ultimately leading to critical drying where ℓ diverges. Our analysis of cavity occupation statistics, which determine the free energy of hard sphere insertion, shows that density fluctuations do not exhibit the Gaussian scaling required for a distinct volumetric regime. The behavior commonly interpreted as a crossover therefore reflects the continuous growth of an interfacial, fluctuation-enhanced solvation layer, rather than the onset of a new microscopic mechanism.

papers.title: Topology-Informed Design Rules for Deconstructable Thermoset Copolymer Networks
papers.abstract: Existing models of thermoset deconstruction facilitated by incorporating cleavable comonomers rely on a mean-field reverse gel point paradigm, which predicts network dissolution once cleavable bonds reach a critical stoichiometric threshold, but does not account for where those bonds reside within the network architecture. Using reactive coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations coupled with graph-theoretic analysis, we extend this stoichiometric picture to show that deconstructability is governed by the curing-imprinted network topology rather than stoichiometry alone. This topological organization is hierarchical: at the local scale, the elastic effectiveness of crosslink junctions determines which crosslinks constitute the load-bearing scaffold; at the mesoscale, the crosslinking rate kinetically templates that scaffold into topologically modular communities—densely crosslinked clusters connected by sparse bridging strands that sustain network connectivity. Using betweenness centrality to identify nodes that disproportionately lie on inter-community shortest paths, we demonstrate that effective deconstruction of the network into macromolecular fragments requires cleavable comonomers to intercept these high-centrality bridging strands. We further find that under uniform, disassortative comonomer incorporation, this topological requirement provides a mechanistic basis for extending the reverse gel point to incorporate network topology. We also show that modularity imposes a fundamental limit on fragment uniformity that persists even when the centrality requirement is met. Finally, we demonstrate that chain stiffness provides a nearly independent lever to suppress mechanically redundant crosslinks and raise the glass transition temperature without significantly altering the deconstruction outcome. Together, these findings reframe the thermoset design space around network topology and provide actionable guidelines for engineering thermoset copolymers with predictable deconstructability and targeted thermomechanical performance.

papers.title: First Enantioselective Chalcogen Bonding Catalysis Controlled Solely by σ-Hole Interactions
papers.abstract: We report the first enantioselective organocatalysis governed solely by chalcogen bonding. A new class of chiral chalcogen-bond donors promotes the asymmetric aza-Henry reactio, governed solely by σ-hole interactions, to deliver drug-relevant β-nitroamines in high yields and enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er. Mechanistic studies and controlled experiments corroborate the essential role of σ-hole directionality during the enantioselective nucleophilic addition. Despite their perceived weakness, σ-hole interactions proved sufficiently strong to enable substrate binding in competition with the triflate anion bound in the catalyst’s σ-hole. Until now, chalcogen bonding has served only as a supporting interaction alongside more prominent stereodetermining tools; however, this work pioneers its use as an independent stereodetermining tool in asymmetric synthesis, offering a conceptual alternative to more established hydrogen-bonding or metal-based strategies.

papers.title: Biotin[6]uril-zinc tetraphenylporphyrin conjugate: a chiral multiporphyrin receptor with size-recognition properties
papers.abstract: A chiral multiporphyrin receptor was prepared by covalent attachment of six zinc tetraphenylporphyrin units to a biotin[6]uril sulfoxide scaffold through flexible amide-linked side chains. In non-coordinating solvents, the conjugate adopts a propeller-like, C3-symmetric conformation in which three π–π-stacked porphyrin pairs are arranged helically around the chiral macrocyclic core, producing a strong exciton-coupled circular dichroism (CD) response in the Soret region. Addition of methanol as a zinc-coordinating co-solvent disrupts porphyrinporphyrin interactions, sharpens the Soret absorption band, and reversibly quenches the CD signal. Binding studies showed that the receptor forms strong complexes with nitrogen-donor ligands, fullerenes, and hemicucurbituril macrocycles, with affinity governed primarily by the guest size and geometry. The highest affinities were observed for guests of approximately 7–8 Å, consistent with sandwich-type binding between adjacent porphyrin units. Although the receptor preferentially binds C70 over C60, it shows no significant enantiodiscrimination toward the chiral guests studied. Overall, this system represents a conformationally adaptive multiporphyrin receptor with reversible solvent- and guest-dependent UV-Vis and CD responses suitable for sensing coordinative and shape-complementary analytes in sub-micromolar concentration range.

papers.title: Multimolecular G-Quadruplexes as Structural Programmers of Responsive, Catalytically Active DNA Condensates
papers.abstract: Artificial DNA condensates built from nanostar motifs have emerged as a powerful platform for engineering membraneless compartments with material properties and phase behaviour encoded in the sequence of the construct. DNA nanostar designs have relied almost entirely on canonical double-stranded DNA to control and reconfigure condensates’ properties. Here, we move beyond canonical Watson-Crick-Franklin base pairing and introduce G-quadruplexes (G4s) as an interaction node that programs both phase boundaries and viscoelastic properties of DNA condensates. We exploit multimolecular G4s and their ion-dependent polymorphism to drive the multimerisation of nanostars into higher valency assemblies and control their material properties. Switching from bimolecular to tetramolecular G4 by simply changing the identity of the alkali metal in the buffer leads to a five-fold increase of viscosity for the same DNA construct. The G4 node endows the condensates with responsiveness to environmental changes, e.g. chelation of alkali metal, selective targeting, e.g. stabilisation/destabilisation by small molecules, and catalytic activity, e.g. peroxidase-like reactivity, when combined with suitable co-factors. This work introduces a new logic for controlling DNA condensation through non-canonical secondary structures. We anticipate that the tunable mechanics, environmental responsiveness, and catalytic activity presented in this work will make G4 nanostars a versatile platform for stimuli-responsive soft materials, microscopy-based screening of G4-targeting ligands, and addressable modules for synthetic cells.

papers.title: PeLED Agent: an evidence-grounded agentic workflow for additive discovery in perovskite light-emitting diodes
papers.abstract: Additive engineering has become the primary strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diode (PeLED) performance, but choosing the right molecule from a vast chemical space still relies on human intuition. Large language model (LLM) agents are well suited to this task, yet without external guidance they hallucinate structures and lose accuracy on niche material families. Here we report an LLM agent guided by three domain tools, a structured PeLED additive database, a heterogeneityaware Gaussian-process surrogate, and a band-matched GFN2-xTB physics screen. The agent treats each tool output as a separate signal, integrates the signals through a band-asymmetric arbitration layer, and returns an evidence-linked candidate shortlist. The database distils 150 papers into 72 entries. The surrogate reaches Spearman 0.69 on blue and 0.71 on green. The physics screen reaches LOOCV accuracy 100 % on blue and 78.9 % on green. The agent identified two PeLED additives unreported in prior literature. Trimethyl phosphonoacetate (TMPA) increased peak EQE from 13.84 % to 25.26 % for green emission. Aminotris(methylenephosphonic acid) (ATMP) increased peak EQE from 6.08 % to 17.20 % for blue emission. Device-level signatures matched the agent selection rationale. This tool-guided LLM agent framework demonstrates AI-era additive discovery for PeLEDs and generalises to other small-data, multi-physics materials problems.

papers.title: Designing Porous Boroaluminate Catalysts via Non-Hydrolytic Ether Elimination
papers.abstract: Boroaluminates are mixed oxides of boria and alumina that show promise for various catalytic applications due to their mild acidity. In this work, boroaluminate xerogels were successfully synthesized via alternative non-hydrolytic sol-gel (NHSG) ether elimination pathways, offering a controlled, template-free strategy for their design. We investigated the synthesis using four distinct alkoxide precursor combinations, utilizing aluminum isopropoxide and sec-butoxide as aluminum sources, alongside boron methoxide and isopropoxide as boron sources. This ether elimination approach provides an excellent alternative to traditional alkyl halide elimination routes, allowing the final porosity, coordination states, and surface acidity to be targeted more easily solely through precursor selection and precursor-to-solvent ratios. The synthesized boroaluminates exhibit a highly homogeneous bulk dispersion of aluminum and boron throughout the xerogel networks (as confirmed by XPS, ICP-OES, and EDS mapping), though calcination at 600 °C led to a surface depletion of boron species. Three of the four synthetic pathways yielded high-surface-area materials (590–772 m2 g–1) without the use of structure-directing agents. Analysis by 11B and 27Al MAS NMR, combined with NH3-TPD revealed that precursor choice directly affects the local atomic coordination, yielding unique catalytic centers—specifically 5-coordinated aluminum alongside 3- and 4-coordinated boron—and a heterogeneous distribution of weak and medium acid sites. Additionally, these materials were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the dehydration of ethanol. The boroaluminates exhibited highly temperature-dependent selectivity, favoring diethyl ether at lower temperatures and shifting predominantly to ethylene at higher temperatures. Four of the five prepared samples showed promising catalytic activity, consistently achieving ethanol conversions between 79 % and 93 % at 275 °C.

Although directional motion at the molecular scale has been widely demonstrated, its translation into controlled molecular architectures remains limited. Here, we show that a rotary molecular motor can actively direct the assembly of two polymer chains into a double-helical structure. Two poly(ethylene oxide) chains were covalently anchored to an overcrowded alkene-based motor, whose unidirectional rotation 20 is driven by UV-light. The resulting motor-induced entanglement was probed by single-molecule force spectroscopy, revealing distinct mechanical signatures, including force plateaus and twiststretch coupling behaviour, consistent with the formation of intertwined polymer chains in a doublehelical arrangement reminiscent of DNA. papers.title: CPL inversion via switching between prompt fluorescence and afterglow phosphorescence in chiral Al(III) and In(III) complexes
papers.abstract: Sign inversion of circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) was achieved through switching between prompt fluorescence and afterglow phosphorescence in chiral Al(III) and In(III) complexes at low temperatures. The afterglow properties could be tuned by altering both ligand substituents and central metal ions.

papers.title: Does Combination Occur Between Poly(methyl methacrylate) Radicals Under Atom Transfer Radical Reaction Conditions?
papers.abstract: The bimolecular termination of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) radicals has long been described as a mixed process of disproportionation and combination, a concept widely adopted in textbooks and kinetic models. However, direct structural evidence for the combination pathwaydefined by a head-to-head (H–H) linkage—remains scarce. In this work, we address this under atom transfer radical reaction (ATRR) conditions using well-defined PMMA macro-radicals. A model PMMA containing a diagnostic H–H linkage was synthesized and characterized by multidimensional NMR, establishing an unambiguous spectral fingerprint. Comparative NMR analysis of ATRR-derived polymers revealed no detectable H–H signals under conditions where the model exhibited a clear signature, indicating that combination termination is absent within detection limits. Quantitative NMR and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) further show that the observed molecular weight increase arises from addition of PMMA radicals to vinyl end-groups generated by disproportionation, followed by saturation via intermolecular hydrogen transfer. Orthogonal thermal stability tests corroborate this: the model polymer undergoes H–H bond cleavage and chain scission at 200 °C, whereas ATRR products remain structurally and molecularly unchanged. These findings demonstrate exclusive disproportionation-related termination under these ATRR conditions. These findings prompt a re-examination of termination assumptions in conventional radical polymerization systems.

papers.title: A Tensor-Based Approach for Identifying Slow Collective Variables in Biomolecular Dynamics with a Non-Markovian Framework
papers.abstract: Understanding conformational dynamics is essential for elucidating the mechanisms of many biological processes. A major challenge in analyzing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is identifying collective variables (CVs) that capture the slow dynamical modes governing long-timescale conformational changes. Existing approaches for CV discovery are largely based on Markovian dynamical models, which may be inadequate when the underlying dynamics exhibit memory effects. Here, we develop a framework that integrates nonlinear CV discovery with non-Markovian dynamical modeling. The method combines AMUSET-based time-lagged independent component analysis (AMUSET-TICA), which constructs nonlinear feature representations using tensor-based basis expansions, with the integrative generalized master equation (IGME) framework for modeling non-Markovian dynamics. To efficiently estimate the multiple Koopman matrices required for IGME fitting, we introduce a one-step multi-lag Koopman (OSMLK) fitting scheme. The resulting AMUSET-TICA-IGME framework identifies continuous nonlinear CVs directly from MD trajectories while incorporating memory effects through the IGME formalism. Applications to alanine dipeptide, the folding dynamics of the FIP35 WW domain, and the dimerization of 9-(diphenylmethylene)-9H-fluorene (9d9f) demonstrate that our framework accurately captures slow dynamical modes and provides stable kinetic models for systems with complex conformational dynamics. These results establish the AMUSET-TICA-IGME framework as a general strategy for integrating nonlinear feature representations with non-Markovian dynamical modeling, opening new opportunities for the analysis of long-timescale biomolecular dynamics.

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking with a Proper Approximate Density Functional: Exact Ground-State Energy as a Close Lower Bound on the Computed Energy
papers.abstract: In the widely-used Kohn-Sham density functional theory for the manyelectron ground state, only the density functional for the exchange-correlation energy is approximated. While the exact density functional minimizes at the exact ground-state energy for any system, widely used approximations can at best describe normally-correlated ground states. A “proper” approximation for a given problem is defined as one that well describes relevant normally-correlated states. Strong correlation, present in many quantum materials, can arise due to abnormally high degeneracy of the Kohn-Sham occupied and unoccupied one-electron energies near the Fermi level. In such situations, the approximate functional may lower its energy by spontaneously breaking symmetries that the ground-state density shares with the many-electron Hamiltonian, reducing the degeneracies that lead to strong correlation. Here the Levy constrained search is invoked to argue that the total energy of a “proper” functional with maximal spontaneous symmetry breaking is bounded from below by the exact total energy, and that the bound may be close to the extent that the abnormal degeneracies are removed. This is a consequence of a variational principle, and it may not hold in non-variational but more accurate approaches to normal correlation such as coupled cluster theory. Since the correlation energy of any one-electron state is zero, a widely “proper” approximate functional should be nearly or exactly self-interaction free, and progress toward a proper self-interaction correction is reviewed here. The time-centered physical interpretation of symmetry breaking is also discussed.

papers.title: Connecting key properties with potential antitumoral activity for a series of PtIV prodrugs carrying bioactive axial ligands
papers.abstract: Pt IV compounds are recognized as promising prodrug candidates due to their kinetic inertness and low intracellular toxicity until reduction activates the corresponding Pt II species. The axial ligands (L/L') critically modulate reactivity, reduction potential, and biological performance. We characterized 64 Pt IV compounds of general formula [Pt IV R 2 X 2 LL'], derived from cisplatin, oxaliplatin, satraplatin, and tetraplatin scaffolds, combined with 14 bioactive carboxylate ligands predominantly in axially symmetric anti arrangements, plus two additional cases: one axially unsymmetric anti and one symmetric syn . The bioactive ligands include inhibitors of histone deacetylase (HDACi), glutathione S-transferase (GSTi), and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2i), as well as mitochondrial stress inducers. DFT/IEF-PCM calculations in water and n-octanol yielded descriptors capturing electronic, redox, and lipophilic features, enabling PCA/HCPC classification and QSAR modeling of antiproliferative activity. Pt IV species define distinct chemical spaces from their Pt II congeners, clustering by equatorial leaving groups X (dichlorido vs. oxalato) and axial orientation, followed by the nature of R 1 /R 2 and then L/L'. In the cisplatin-derived series, syn/anti orientation and identity of the axial ligands govern reduction potential and correlate with cytotoxicity. These insights rationalize structure-activity relationships, deepen understanding of the mechanisms underlying cytotoxicity in ovarian and male colorectal cancer, and support new strategies and subfamilies to expand the search for improved Pt IV candidates.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Y2O3, ZnO, and CeO2 Additions to Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glasses: Composition–Structure–Property Relationships
papers.abstract: The development of high-modulus glasses is essential for advanced lightweight applications, requiring a fundamental understanding of how different oxide components dictate elastic performance. To maximize stiffness, oxides must be strategically introduced to enhance both network connectivity and volumetric packing density; hence, Y 2 O 3 , ZnO, and CeO 2 are investigated here due to their high single-bond dissociation energies and strong cationic field strengths. Magnesium aluminosilicate glasses (MAS) modified with Y 2 O 3 , ZnO, and CeO 2 were systematically investigated to establish composition–structure–property relationships. A constrained ternary mixture design (Y 2 O 3 –ZnO–CeO 2 = 14 wt.%) was used to span the compositional space efficiently. The measured Young’s modulus ranged from 97.5 to 113.8 GPa, while the specific modulus varied between 36.6 and 41.7 ×10 6 N·m/kg. The highest values were obtained for compositions adding Y 2 O 3 alone or Y 2 O 3 –ZnO. Raman spectroscopy revealed systematic changes in the Si–O stretching band, including shifts in band position and variations in band width depending on composition. These changes indicate structural reorganization of the glass network. A moderate correlation between Raman peak position and Young’s modulus confirms that structural connectivity effects contribute to stiffness, although additional factors such as packing density and cation field strength are also relevant. The results demonstrate that Y 2 O 3 is the most effective oxide for increasing stiffness, ZnO exhibits composition-dependent behaviour, and CeO 2 reduces the specific modulus. The combined analysis provides an experimental and structural basis to designing high-modulus glass systems.

papers.title: Mechanophotochemistry: Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
papers.abstract: Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis, a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed Electron Donor Acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2-4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C—S cross coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution-state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O 2 as a terminal oxidant, does not.
