In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless-steel milling ball directly 2 participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light-promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent-minimized and viable alternative to solution-state photochemical reactions.

papers.title: Solvation Thermodynamics Revisited
papers.abstract: Most chemical and biochemical reactions occur in solution; however, many details of the thermodynamics of solvation are not well understood, especially with regard to the role of energy and entropy in the solvation process. Currently, a prevailing view in the field is that the solvation free energy is fully determined by solute-solvent interactions acting through both energetic and entropic contributions. This rests on the claim, presented by Yu and Karplus [J. Chem. Phys. 89, 2366 (1988)], that the solvent-solvent energetic and entropic contributions to the solvation free energy exactly cancel. Here, we show that this result is not correct, but rather arises from an erroneous assignment of the solvent-solvent and solute-solvent entropic contributions. Namely, we demonstrate that the solvent-solvent and solute-solvent energetic contributions to the free energy, which have an unambiguous assignment, are not compatible with the Yu-Karplus decomposition of the solvation entropy. This indicates that, contrary to a now commonly held view, rearrangements of the solvent upon introduction of a solute may contribute both energetically and entropically to the solvation free energy.

papers.title: Directed attachment of catalysts into the extended environments of soft photoelectrodes for hydrogen evolution
papers.abstract: We present a detailed mechanistic investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticles (Pt-NPs) on (PEC) platforms for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction—formed from a blend of conjugated donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers—exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 x 101 to 2.5 x 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates vertical phase segregation, with acceptor-rich domains driving photoelectrochemical Pt-NP deposition heterogeneously via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the termini of “fast transport pathways.” X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and DFT modeling suggest that Pt-S interactions involving the bi-thiophene groups in (n-doped) P(NDI2OD-T2) dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters also demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O=C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings reveal that sub-micron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures where charge transport and catalytic sites operate in concert. The hierarchical assembly of these nanoenvironments will provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen evolution to more complex energy carriers, such as multielectron and proton redox reactions.

papers.title: Theoretical Insights into the Influence of Surface Charge Modulation on the Intrinsic Reactivity for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
papers.abstract: Ammonia is a foundational molecule important for manufacturing fertilizers, chemicals, and fuels. Its rates of synthesis and decomposition, however, are limited by the considerable barriers to activate the strong N2 bond and break the strong NHx-metal surface bonds. As a result, the maximum rates for these systems require an optimal balance of bonding to the catalyst surface which is controlled by the catalyst that is used. Dynamic modulation of the electronic structure of the catalyst under operating conditions offers a unique way to tune the reactivity without changing the metal catalyst or altering its composition. Catalytic condensers that use an electronic gating mechanism to control the charge have recently demonstrated the ability to rapidly alter the charge of supported catalytic particles between -0.17 |e-|/metal atom to +0.17 |e-|/metal atom and potentially control the kinetics for catalytic systems. Ab initio density functional theory calculations are carried out herein to examine the influence of such charge oscillations on the adsorption, reaction and activation energies for the key elementary steps in ammonia synthesis over a model Ru(0001) surface. The results show that surface charging significantly alters the bonding of NHx intermediates to the metal surface due to the influence of polarization and coulombic interactions. In the absence of charge N, H, NH and NH2 intermediates, which are unstable gas phase species, bind strongly to the metal surface whereas the stable gas phase N2 and H2 reactants and NH3 product bind more weakly. Increasing to positive charge significantly strengthens the binding of NH, NH2 and NH3 where the enhanced binding increases with increasing the number of protons on the nitrogen. This significant enhancement is the result of coulombic charge stabilization where the negatively charged N* atom is strongly stabilized by the positively charged surface to which its bonds and the positively charged proton ligands that sit above it thus forming a ‘charge sandwich’ that provides strong coulombic stabilization in addition to the covalent bonding. The adsorption of N2 is also strongly stabilized at increasing positive charge as a result of its significant polarization and charge stabilization. The N* and H* adatoms do not polarize with charge, as such there is little change in their binding energies with charge where the bonding interaction is dominantly covalent. The reaction energies for NHx hydrogenation show significant changes with surface charge as there is a significant increase in coulombic stabilization in moving from NHx-1* to NHx as the NHx*; more polarizable adsorbates are more strongly stabilized at positive charges. For NH2* hydrogenation, increasing to more positive charge decreased the activation barriers by more than 40 kJ∙mol-1 and shifted reaction energies from endothermic to exothermic. N* and NH* hydrogenation show smaller barrier changes but also become more favorable at more positive charges. In contrast, the reaction energies and activation barriers for N2 activation were increased with increasing positive charge. As a result, surface charging offers a mechanism to modulate the rates for these metal-ligand bond forming and breaking steps that can be used to significantly enhance catalytic activity.

papers.title: Improving ABFE Calculations for GPCRs by Addressing Errors in Apo-State Representation
papers.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) methods provide a robust computational framework for predicting protein–ligand binding affinities and have seen increased adoption in drug discovery workflows. Among these, absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations are especially valuable as they enable affinity prediction for novel compounds without prior experimental data. However, their broader adoption is limited by setup complexity, sampling challenges, and variable performance across systems. These challenges are particularly pronounced in therapeutically relevant complex membrane protein systems such as G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs). This underscores the need to evaluate ABFE performance in GPCR systems and to develop strategies to mitigate these errors. Here, we evaluate ABFE calculations across three GPCR systems: the adenosine A2A receptor (A2AR), dopamine D3 receptor (D3R), and the metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGlu5). We focus on three sources of systematic error in these systems: (i) inadequate resolvation of the binding pocket in apo-like alchemical states, (ii) inconsistent treatment of metal ions, and (iii) insufficient sampling of receptor conformational transitions between holo-like and apo-like ensembles. To address these issues, we introduce two methodological improvements: a biased grand-canonical-like water transport scheme to improve binding pocket resolvation, and a replica-exchange umbrella sampling (REUS)-based framework to quantify and correct the free energy associated with receptor relaxation to apo-like conformations. Together, these approaches reduce the systematic overestimation of binding affinities, improving agreement with experimental data while maintaining ranking performance. Overall, our results highlight the importance of accurately representing the apo state in ABFE calculations and provide a practical framework for applying high-accuracy free energy methods to membrane protein targets.

papers.title: Impact of Sterilization Techniques on the Physicochemical and Biological Properties, and 3D Printability of Thermoresponsive Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting offers transformative potential for functional disease modeling and tissue engineering. These applications demand effective sterilization of biomaterials to ensure reproducibility and clinical translation. This study evaluated pharmacopeia-standard disinfection and sterilization methods, including autoclaving, dry heat treatment (aerobic and anaerobic), ethanol washing (70%), UV irradiation, and filtration on three thermoresponsive hydrogels. The investigated hydrogels consist of Pluronic F127 (poloxamer 407) or two poly(2-oxazolines)/poly(2-oxazine) based block copolymers, namely poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline)- b -poly(2- n -propyl-2-oxazine) (pMeOx- b -p n PrOzi), or poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline)- b -poly(2-phenyl-2-oxazine)- b -poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) (pMeOx- b -pPheOzi- b -pMeOx). Results showed that ethanol washing and UV-irradiation sterilized inefficiently, while dry heat treatment caused partial thermal degradation (all polymers), compromised 3D-printability, and increased cell toxicity (Pluronic F127), likely due to the formation of oxidative degradation products. Filtration effectively sterilized both pMeOx-based block copolymers, while Pluronic F127 required a combined approach of autoclaving and triple filtration to achieve complete sterility. Overall, filtration and autoclaving emerged as the most suitable sterilization method, balancing chemical stability, mechanical integrity, printability, and cytocompatibility.

papers.title: Luminescent Solar Concentrators with Tailored Emission for Agrivoltaic Systems
papers.abstract: Luminescent solar concentrator (LSC) is one of the promising (semi-)transparent solar harvesting devices. In this work, we employ aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens), TPA-BT and TPA-NT, which retain high photoluminescence quantum yields in the aggregated state and efficiently convert ultraviolet and blue photons into red emission. This spectral conversion offers a dual advantage: it matches well with the spectral response range of silicon photovoltaic cells (600-900 nm) for efficient electricity generation, while simultaneously providing photosynthetically active radiation (400-700 nm) to promote plant growth. Large-area LSC devices (1600 cm2) were fabricated and evaluated under greenhouse conditions over a 14-day testing period. Among them, the TPA-BT LSC device demonstrated a daily electricity output of 1.75 Wh, corresponding to an estimated annual energy yield of approximately 2.7 kWh/m2. Importantly, this spectral conversion also delivered clear agricultural benefits, with plants grown under the LSC devices exhibiting significantly higher fresh weight (42.7%) than those grown under control conditions. By integrating these LSCs into greenhouse structures, we demonstrate a practical agrivoltaic platform that simultaneously generates renewable electricity and enhances crop productivity.

papers.title: Inner Sphere Allylic Substitution under Iridium Catalysis: Enantioselective Allylic Alkynylation with Unfunctionalized Alkynes
papers.abstract: Besides branched-selectivity, iridium-catalyzed allylic substitution is synonymous with outer sphere nucleophilic attack on the pi-allyl-Ir(III) intermediate. We now report the first inner sphere Ir-catalyzed asymmetric allylic substitution with unfunctionalized terminal alkynes as C(sp)–H nucleophile. This enantioselective allylic alkynylation relies on in situ generated zinc-acetylides as the nucleophile for reaction with branched allylic alcohols under Ir(I)/(phosphoramidite,olefin) catalyst and delivers 1,4-enynes, bearing an intervening stereocenter, generally with exclusive branched-selectivity and outstanding enantioselectivity (up to >99.9:0.1 er). The involvement of the inner sphere pathway in this allylic alkynylation reaction is confirmed through stereodifferentiating experiments using deuterium-labelled allylic alcohol.

papers.title: Red-shifting TADF emission with a bora-triptycene Lewis acid
papers.abstract: Binding of a Lewis acid to an emitter molecule is a versatile method to red-shift the emission. This approach is underexplored for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials. Herein we report that the addition of a Lewis acid can induce large (>100 nm) bathochromic shifts in the emission in sulfone-based donor-acceptor TADF (DA-TADF) emitters and for the first time in multi-resonant TADF (MR-TADF) emitters, whilst retaining TADF behaviour. This is achieved through the binding of a 9-sulfonium-10-bora-triptycene (BTripS) Lewis acid to the fluorophore carbonyl or sulfone moiety to form bench-stable Lewis adducts. In contrast, when using B(C6F5)3 as the Lewis acid, the generated adducts rapidly decompose on exposure to water to form H2O-B(C6F5)3. This work demonstrates that the formation of bench-stable Lewis adducts has significant potential as a method to red-shift the emission of two popular classes of TADF compounds. This provides a new approach to address the current challenge of accessing longer wavelength emitting MR-TADF materials.

papers.title: Regiochemical and Resisting Moment-Arm Effects Enable the Engineering of Atropisomeric Dithienylphenanthrene into a Mechanophore Scaffold
papers.abstract: Defining structure–mechanical activity relationships (SMARs) is essential for understanding how molecular structure controls force-coupled reactivity and for designing mechanophores with predictable mechanical responses. In this study, we conducted a systematic SMAR study to engineer dithienylphenanthrene derivatives into a functional mechanophore platform. These studies revealed that the mechanochemical reactivity of DTPs is governed by regiochemical control and by a previously unrecognized design principle that we term the “resisting moment-arm effect,” wherein distal steric congestion creates an opposing torque resisting the conformational adjustments required for the stereochemical conversion and thereby modulates mechanical activity. These SMARs guided the rational design of DTP5-p as a promising molecular force sensing probe and established dithienylphenanthrene as a new platform for atropisomer mechanochemistry, and revealed that structural modification remote from the force-transmission pathway can be leveraged to control mechanochemical reactivity.

papers.title: The patentability of intermediate chemical compounds
papers.abstract: The present study examines the protection of intermediate chemical compounds and analyses some landmark decisions of the EPO Boards of Appeal. The majority of the decisions under consideration focus on the inventive step requirement (Article 56 EPC). The role of an intermediate product in an innovative production process does not inherently render it inventive. However, it may be eligible for protection if its transformation into the final product requires an original inventive step. It is possible to claim both intermediate and final products in a single patent application, provided there is a strong technical and structural link between them. The rulings highlight the importance of demonstrating an unexpected technical effect—such as a substantial increase in yield—to justify the grant of the patent.

papers.title: Quantum Dot Bioconjugates Enable Order(s)-of-Magnitude Enhancement of Immunoglobulin E Detection Sensitivity
papers.abstract: Improving the sensitivity of immunoglobulin E (IgE) detection is crucial because the concentrations of allergen-specific IgE antibodies are often very low, particularly at early sensitization stages or in patients with weak immune responses. Bright, photostable detection labels are therefore essential for allergen microarrays designed for multiplexed IgE detection. However, conventional organic fluorophores suffer from low brightness and rapid photobleaching, thereby limiting microarray analytical performance. In contrast, fluorescent quantum dots (QDs) are exceptionally bright and photostable, enabling prolonged signal accumulation and offering new opportunities for ultrasensitive IgE detection. Here, we present a comprehensive comparative study of allergochips employing conventional conjugates of streptavidin with an organic dye (DyLight550–Str) or QDs (QD565–Str) for simultaneous detection of allergen-specific IgE antibodies covering a broad panel of allergens. In addition to microarray immunoassays, the optical properties and photobleaching behavior of both bioconjugates were investigated under conditions relevant to routine microarray diagnosis using a commercial laser scanner operating at excitation wavelengths of 398, 447, and 532 nm. Although the configuration of the commercial scanner was not optimized for QD detection, the QD565–Str bioconjugate enabled the detection of specific IgE antibodies in approximately 70% of samples identified using the DyLight550–Str reporter. Optical characterization showed that the shortest-wave visible spectral band (about 398 nm) was optimal for concentration-independent excitation of QD565–Str, with a fluorescence intensity approximately 2.2-fold higher than that of DyLight550–Str under its optimal excitation conditions (at 532 nm). The QD565–Str bioconjugates exhibited orders of magnitude greater photostability in the allergochip, enabling long-term fluorescence signal accumulation, whereas DyLight550–Str underwent pronounced photobleaching under the same conditions. Overall, the total fluorescence signal generated by QD565–Str on the allergochip was more than an order of magnitude stronger than that of the DyLight550–Str conjugate, providing a major advantage for detection of low-abundance IgE. These findings demonstrate strong potential for the use of QD bioconjugates in the development of a next-generation ultrasensitive IgE-detecting allergochip platform for multiplexed allergy diagnosis.

papers.title: Cyanamide-induced desulfhydration enables access to α,β-dehydropeptides
papers.abstract: Dehydroamino acids are found in natural products, disease-associated proteins, and are used for the diversification of proteins and peptides. The synthesis of peptide sequences containing dehydroamino acids remains non-trivial and only a few chemical methods allow for their incorporation. We report the conversion of amino acid residues bearing β-thiols into dehydroamino acids through the treatment of unprotected peptides and proteins with cyanamide under mild, fully aqueous conditions that are compatible with commonly used buffer salts.

papers.title: Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Protein–polymer bioconjugates represent a class of biomaterials that leverages the molecular specificity of proteins and the tunability of synthetic polymers. Strategic conjugation of polymers to protein surfaces can enhance key biomolecular properties such as structural stability and target affinity while preserving the biological functions of the native protein. The rational design of these hybrid biomolecules demands a detailed understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing protein–polymer interfacial behavior. Critically, strong interfacial interactions can impose substantial energetic barriers that hinder conformational sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) studies of this system. Enhanced sampling methods are highly effective for overcoming such limitations in the simulation of biomolecular interfaces. However, the opportunity to apply enhanced sampling methods toward navigating the complex interfacial landscapes of protein–polymer bioconjugates has yet to be realized by the field. In this study, we showcase the development of a molecular modeling framework that leverages enhanced sampling to extensively characterize protein–polymer bioconjugates. To validate this framework, we constructed two bioconjugate models of hen egg-white lysozyme grafted with activated methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) chains of varying lengths at multiple surface-exposed lysine sites. We then performed all-atom MD simulations of these PEGylated constructs, augmented with well-tempered metadynamics (WTM) to fully explore their conformational landscapes under multi-site polymer conjugation. This approach yielded converged free energy surfaces (FES) characterizing the thermodynamic favorability of grafted mPEG chain conformations at each conjugation site. We also identified key protein contact residues and site-specific non-bonded interactions responsible for bioconjugate stabilization. This study demonstrates a novel application of enhanced sampling methodologies in bioconjugate systems for characterizing site-specific conjugation effects on protein–polymer interfacial energetics and structural dynamics in the context of protein surface chemistry. More broadly, applying this methodological framework across diverse polymer chemistries and protein variants can elucidate molecular design rules for engineering bioconjugates with precise properties and functions for applications spanning biotechnology, energy, and health.

papers.title: PyQuiverHS: A Web Tool for Computing Isotope Effects
papers.abstract: Predicting isotope effects using electronic structure calculations is widely done, but current software options can present a barrier for some chemists, depending upon their needs and software/programming proficiency. Building upon existing code bases, we have developed PyQuiverHS as a free web tool (www.isotope-effects.com) to provide ready access to kinetic and equilibrium isotope effect calculations employing the Bigeleisen-Mayer (B-M) and enthalpy-entropy (H-S) partition functions. A graphical user interface assists in setting up a configuration file, which contains scaling factor and isotope substitution information. After uploading the configuration file and Gaussian frequency jobs for the unlabeled system, users execute a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) or equilibrium isotope effect (EIE) calculation at a particular temperature or range of temperatures with a defined increment. Wigner and Bell tunneling corrections are provided for KIE calculations. Overall KIEs or EIEs and their contributing B-M and H-S terms are compiled in auto-downloaded comma-separated values (*.csv) and plain text files. Automating the process with PyQuiverHS is a significant gain in efficiency, as previous methods for these types of calculations have relied on spreadsheets, which require time-intensive data manipulation. We demonstrate the utility of PyQuiverHS by calculating temperature-dependent conformational KIEs in 9,10-dihydro-4,5-dimethylphenanthrene (1), a doubly bridged biphenyl derivative (2), [2.2]-metaparacyclophane (3), a secondary KIE for the SN2 reaction of chloride with methyl bromide (4), and an EIE for the interconversion of chair conformations of 1,1,3,3-trimethylcyclohexane (6).

papers.title: Synthesis and modelling of chemically cross-linked hydrogels with a semi-self-driving lab.
papers.abstract: The high tunability of polymer networks makes hydrogels central to diverse applications spanning biomedicine, consumer products, and smart materials. The multifactorial nature of hydrogel synthesis, however, requires simultaneous optimization of monomer, crosslinker, initiator concentrations, solvent content, and initiation conditions, posing a significant challenge for traditional experimental approaches. Here, we report a semi-autonomous, human-in-the-loop self-driving laboratory that integrates liquid-handling robotics with active learning to model and optimize the synthesis of chemically cross-linked hydrogels. Using a Taguchi orthogonal array to seed initial experiments, the system iteratively refines predictive models for gelation, yield, optical clarity, and swelling degree across a five-dimensional formulation space. A Diverse Mini-batch Active Learning (DMAL) algorithm guides experimental selection to reduce model uncertainty efficiently. Model performance improved consistently over successive learning rounds. While gelation and yield were effectively predicted, optical clarity and swelling required more complex descriptors or modeling strategies. This work demonstrates the potential of hybrid automation to accelerate the rational design of multifunctional hydrogels through data-efficient, multi-objective modeling.

papers.title: Strong pore hydrophilicity and low confinement drive water permeability inside cage-like metal-
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with cage-like narrow openings and large internal cavities have shown potential for addressing outstanding challenges such as water harvesting and purification. However, a fundamental understanding of water structure and dynamics within these MOFs is essential to achieve high water flux. Here, we take a computational approach to determine the effects of pore confinement and chemical environment on water density, hydrogen bonding, diffusivity, and permeability in 78 pristine and functionalized cage-like MOFs that are predicted by literature-trained machine learning models to be stable in humid/wet conditions including under water submersion. Across this set, we observe significant variations in water density, hydrogen-bond network, dielectric environment, and diffusion, driven by confinement and hydrophilicity of the MOFs. We show that confinement exerts a stronger influence on water structure and diffusion, whereas hydrophilicity is more important for permeability. Finally, we establish design principles to achieve exceptional water permeability within cage-like MOFs without compromising ionic selectivity.

papers.title: Zn-crosslinked core-shell-corona micellar networks as functional and tunable gel electrolytes
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of a modular ABC triblock terpolymer platform via anionic ring-opening polymerization (AROP) for the construction of ion-conductive, supramolecular hydrogels. The terpolymer, comprising poly(allyl glycidyl ether)-block-poly(methoxyethoxy glycidyl ether)-block-poly(furfuryl glycidyl ether-co-tert-butyl glycidyl ether) (PAGE-b-PMEGE-b-P(FGE-co-tBGE)), was designed with orthogonal functionality: the PAGE block was quantitatively converted to a carboxylate-rich segment via thiol-ene click chemistry, the PMEGE block provides hydrophilicity and solubility, and the statistical P(FGE-co-tBGE) block forms a hydrophobic micellar core. In aqueous solution, this amphiphile self-assembles into well-defined core–shell–corona micelles with a pH-responsive carboxylate corona. Introducing Zn2+ ions triggers supramolecular gelation through dynamic metal–carboxylate coordination between micelles, forming a reversible network. The crosslink density, and thus the storage modulus (G’) and swelling degree, is tuneable by varying the carboxylate-to-Zn2+ stoichiometry. Critically, these metallo-supramolecular gels exhibit ion mobility, linking their dynamic mechanical properties to charge transport. This work establishes a versatile AROP-to-assembly strategy for creating functional block copolymer networks where structure and stimuli-responsive, conductive properties are governed by synthetic design.

papers.title: Solvent-Mediated Diffusion Enables Directed Functionalization of Polymer Semiconductor Interfaces
papers.abstract: The increasing interest in development of intrinsically stretchable electronic devices based on polymer semiconductors (PSCs) necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the interfacial chemistry of these PSC films, alongside facile processing methods to modify these properties which dictate layer compatibility. Solvent-mediated functionalization provides a scalable, controllable, and tunable method to target and modulate several key interfacial properties. Herein, we aim to understand the influence of solvent exposure on a blended polymer film. This is achieved through small molecule-modification of a poly-thieno[3,2b]thiophene-diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPPTT) and low molecular weight polybutadiene (BA) blended elastomer film. We investigated solvent-mediated film functionalization on blended films by incorporating 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorodecanethiol (PFDT), as the highly fluorinated small-molecule provided excellent measurement contrast throughout several characterization techniques. By comparing solvent environments which differentially swell the blended polymer films, we show programming of PFDT incorporation from uniform, through-thickness functionalization to surface-enriched gradients. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (QCM-D) measurements and further corroborated with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiles quantified the mass uptake of PFDT. In a non-swelling/compacting solvent environment, QCM-D reflected a diffusiongoverned uptake of PFDT with a distinct thickness-dependent concentration gradient. In contrast, swelling films with MPFB opened diffusion pathways that facilitates PFDT 3 penetration throughout the entire polymer network and resulted in more uniform functionalization across the entire film thickness. Collectively, these results establish a broader understanding of solvent-mediated film functionalization and furthers the understanding of molecular diffusion through PSC film systems.

papers.title: Distributed Polarization Enables Volumetric Electrochemical Promotion of Brønsted Acid Catalysis
papers.abstract: Temperature and pressure are conventional handles for promoting thermochemical reaction rates and are readily applied to catalytic active sites over the entire volume of a reactor. Electrical polarization has recently been recognized as a powerful complementary strategy for promoting thermochemical Brønsted acid catalysis, but is generally confined to the surface area of an electrode. Herein, we utilize collision-mediated electron transfer and design a reactor to polarize dispersed Brønsted acid catalysts across a reactor volume. This design increases polarizable active-site density 10,000-fold relative to 2D electrodes while preserving rate-potential scaling. While this enhanced volumetric scaling enables Brønsted acid catalyzed acylation reactions at room temperature, at 55°C, we drive acylation and olefin isomerization reactions to >50% conversion at >100 mM concentrations, improving upon open-circuit rates by up to 25-fold with pseudo-Faradaic efficiencies >1000%. Distributed polarization therefore provides a volumetrically-scalable complement to temperature and pressure to promote thermochemical Brønsted acid catalysis.

papers.title: Closing the H2S/NO Signaling Loop: Nitric Oxide Regeneration by a Synthetic Zn2+ Persulfide via Transnitrosation and Nitrite Reduction
papers.abstract: Cross-talk between reactive sulfur species (RSS) and reactive nitrogen species (RNS) is increasingly recognized as a central feature of biological redox signaling, yet the molecular basis for which persulfides (RSS – ) engage with nitrosative intermediates remains poorly defined. Motivated by the emerging roles of Zn 2+ persulfides in NO-mediated signaling, we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of a well-defined Zn2+ alkyl persulfide complex, [Zn 2+ (Mes 3 TPA)(SStBu)] + toward various nitrosating reagents. This Zn 2+ persulfide is inert toward NO• and tert-butyl nitrite (tBuONO) but reacts rapidly with Snitrosothiols (RSNOs) and NO + through formation of a transient S-nitrosopersulfide (tBuSSNO) intermediate. Subsequent homolytic S–N cleavage releases NO • and a perthiyl radical (tBuSS • ), which dimerizes to form the corresponding organic tetrasulfide, tBuSSSStBu. Although free nitrite (NO 2 – ) is unreactive toward the Zn-SSR complex, activation with either a Brønsted or Lewis acid enables efficient nitrite reduction to release NO • . Taken together, these results establish a molecular framework for Zn 2+ –persulfide mediated NO • regeneration and demonstrate how persulfidation can transform redox-inert Zn 2+ centers into dynamic redox sites that integrate RSS and RNS signaling.

papers.title: Computational Design of Functionalized Cyclodextrin Probes for Sensitive and Selective PFAS Detection
papers.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants that demand highly sensitive and selective molecular recognition strategies for field-deployable detection. Cyclodextrin-based field-effect transistor (FET) sensors demonstrate high sensitivity to perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), achieving sub-ppt detection limits, yet exhibit limited selectivity in the presence of structurally similar surfactants such as sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). In this work, we integrate molecular docking, all-atom molecular dynamics free energy calculations, and Bayesian optimization to computationally evaluate the competitive binding thermodynamics of a synthetic library of 1,629 functionalized α-, β-, and γ-cyclodextrins. Our screen identifies highly sensitive PFOS probes with predicted dissociation constants as low as K d PFOS = 2.8×10 −11 M and highly selective probes with PFOS selectivities over SDS of up to K d SDS /K d PFOS = 1.5×10 5 , corresponding to a 6,000× improvement in sensitivity and 2,500× improvement in selectivity over unfunctionalized β-cyclodextrin. Amine-functionalized cyclodextrins yield the highest discrimination ratios by selectively suppressing SDS binding under competitive conditions, while fluorinated groups further enhance PFOS selectivity through favorable host-guest interactions. Regression analysis reveals that PFOS affinity correlates with hydrophobic surface area, whereas high selectivity additionally depends on charge-resolved and electronic descriptors. These results establish quantitative structure-selectivity relationships for cyclodextrin-based PFOS recognition and provide design principles for next-generation PFAS molecular sensors.

papers.title: Hyperparameter Optimisation of Physics-Informed Neural Network using Particle Swarm Optimisation for predicting Lift and Drag Coefficient of NACA Airfoils.
papers.abstract: In the present research, the Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINNs) is applied alongside Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) to predict the aerodynamic coefficients of NACA airfoils. The base PINN is a solver that solves the steady state, incompressible, two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation in a meshless form that consists of the continuity equation, the x and y momentum equations, and appropriate boundary conditions as a constraint on the loss function. The PSO module is an automated selection of 9 significant hyperparameters, such as learning rate, 6 physicsloss weights, and 2 scaling factors for collocation density, based on a low-cost proxy network. Ten NACA airfoils from three geometric families (four-digit, five-digit and six-series) are tested at angles of attack 0° to 10°, and a Reynolds number of 100,000. The stages are optimised using a three-stage Reynolds number program (Re = 20,000 → 50,000 → 100,000) and a two-stage optimisation scheme (Adam followed by Limited-memory Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (L-BFGS)). The PINN model achieved an RMSE of 0.0342 and an R2 of 0.9925 for aerodynamiccoefficient prediction across multiple NACA airfoil profiles, with drag and lift predictions yielding R2 values of 0.9594 and 0.9891, respectively. Upon integrating PSO for hyperparameter tuning, the PINNs + PSO hybrid reduced the overall RMSE by approximately 48.7% for CL and 47.2% for CD relative to the baseline PINNs, achieving a final RMSE of 0.01754 for combined aerodynamic coefficients, while the R2 improved to 0.9980. The drag R2 increased from 0.9594 to 0.9887 (~2.93% gain) and the lift R2 from 0.9891 to 0.9971 (~0.80% gain). These results imply that PSO can yield substantial accuracy gains in PINNs that are systematically trained for aerodynamic prediction, even when the underlying network architecture is not altered.

papers.title: Numerical Investigation of Shock Impingement on a Supersonic Cavity Flow with Varying Shock Generator Height
papers.abstract: The interaction of external shock waves with cavity shear layers plays an important role in determining the aerodynamic behaviour of high-speed cavity flows. In this study, a numerical investigation is carried out to examine shock impingement on a supersonic open cavity, with focus on the effects of the vertical position of the shock generator and the freestream Mach number. An off-body shock generator is placed at different heights above the cavity opening to produce oblique shocks that interact with the cavity shear layer. Two-dimensional steady Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes simulations are performed using a density-based solver with an appropriate turbulence model. The flow fields are analysed using Mach contours, pressure contours, shock structures, and surface pressure distributions. The shock generator height is varied at three locations relative to the cavity depth, and simulations are carried out over a range of freestream Mach numbers. The results show that lower shock-generator positions cause stronger interaction with the cavity shear layer, leading to greater shear-layer deformation, stronger internal shock reflections, and higher surface pressures. As the generator height increases, the interaction weakens and the flow gradually approaches the baseline case without shock impingement. Increasing the freestream Mach number amplifies these trends, especially for lower generator positions.

papers.title: Deprotonation and Alkylation of Weakly Acidic C(sp3)–H Bonds through In Situ Generation of a Strong Hydride Base from 1,1,3,3-Tetramethyldisiloxane and Potassium tert-Butoxide
papers.abstract: The direct deprotonation of weakly acidic C(sp3)–H bonds remains a fundamental strategy for generating carbon nucleophiles, but typically requires strong bases, cryogenic conditions, and stepwise protocols. A general method enabling single-step deprotonation and alkylation of these substrates remains elusive. Herein, we report that a combination of 1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisiloxane (TMDSO) and potassium tert-butoxide (KOtBu) enables the direct alkylation of weakly acidic substrates in a single operational step using simple alkyl halide electrophiles. With a focus on alkylpyridines, a broad range of C–H alkylation products are obtained via in situ activation and alkylation, without the need for preformation of organometallic intermediates. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a pathway in which TMDSO and KOtBu cooperatively generate a transient, substrate-associated hydridic base with KH-like reactivity. Key substrate–potassium interactions, including N-coordination and cation–π binding, preorganize the system and enable rate-determining deprotonation with concurrent H2 evolution, followed by SN2 alkylation. These findings reveal a distinct mode of base activation that combines high basicity with unusual tolerance of alkyl halides, providing a practical approach to the alkylation of weakly acidic C–H bonds.

papers.title: Target-Adaptive Multichannel Molecular Similarity Complements Extended-Connectivity Fingerprints on Structurally Diverse Targets
papers.abstract: Molecular similarity search underpins virtual screening and lead discovery, and the Tanimoto coefficient over extended-connectivity fingerprints (ECFP) is its dominant tool. ECFP is, however, a two-dimensional topological representation: it is largely insensitive to stereochemistry, three-dimensional shape, and graded electronic effects. We introduce a physically grounded multichannel molecular representation that encodes per-atom electronic, steric, topological, and stereochemical/3D properties, and a target-adaptive procedure that selects, for each target, which channel family to fuse with Tanimoto. On a benchmark of 1,080 ChEMBL ligands spanning 18 protein targets, evaluated under leakage-free, compound-level, Bemis-Murcko scaffold-split nested cross-validation, the adaptive method improves macro same-target retrieval AUROC from 0.820 to 0.848 (+0.028; 95% CI +0.015 to +0.041), with statistically significant gains on 12 of 18 targets. Gains concentrate on the structurally diverse targets where Tanimoto is weakest, and the method defers to Tanimoto where it is already strong. Channel selections are mechanistically coherent: stereochemical/3D features dominate on targets with chiral or shape-sensitive binding (e.g. HMG-CoA reductase, CDK2, MAO-B), while electronic features dominate elsewhere. The approach complements rather than replaces ECFP/Tanimoto, adding orthogonal signal precisely in the scaffold-hopping regime.

papers.title: MERIT-ML: A Machine-Learning-Readiness Framework for Tabular Public Metabolomics Data
papers.abstract: Public metabolomics repositories contain thousands of deposited studies. However, deposition alone does not show whether a tabular matrix is suitable for supervised classification. We developed MERIT-ML (Metabolomics Evaluation of Readiness and Interoperability of Tabular Data for Machine Learning), an open-source, source-aware framework for extracting tabular data from the Metabolomics Workbench, building canonical per-analysis bundles, and assessing the readiness of each matrix for supervised classification. MERIT-ML provides each study with a design context and scores five core dimensions: structural integrity, analytical data quality, annotation and interoperability, label and class support, and ML task readiness. Metadata and FAIR reusability are reported separately. We also included feasibility gates so that critical constraints, such as missing matrices, insufficient samples, weak class support, and high missingness, are not masked by the overall readiness score. Of 6,696 analyses from 4,121 studies, 96.5% produced at least one valid tabular matrix. Still, readiness varied widely by source. Curated named-metabolite tables were generally cleaner and more interpretable. Untargeted m/z–RT tables were higher-dimensional, more sparsely annotated, and more prone to missing data. At the study level, 35.5% of studies were ML-ready, 34.5% were ML-ready with caveats, and 26.1% were limited by class support. The results suggest that supervised reuse is limited not only by table availability but also by sample size, class structure, source identity, and annotation state. MERIT-ML further demonstrates that many studies did not include paired m/z and retention-time metadata for named metabolites. This limits the reproducibility of annotations, transfer of methods, and reuse across instruments, even when tabular data are used. The web interface is available at https://merit-ml.in. MERIT-ML offers a practical solution for identifying studies suitable for supervised classification, benchmark construction, and repository curation.

papers.title: Connectivity, Rigidity, and Gelation in Linker-Mediated Colloidal Networks
papers.abstract: On the path to gelation, attractive colloids develop network connectivity, mechanical rigidity, and slow dynamics. Herein, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to quantitatively characterize these processes using a coarse-grained model of patchy colloidal particles that form equilibrium networks through linker-mediated, reversible binding interactions. We find that linker-mediated gelation proceeds through a cascade of coupled but distinct structural, mechanical, and dynamical changes. Ordinary connectivity percolation first produces a system-spanning network, while rigidity percolation is associated with the formation of a percolating backbone characterized by an average colloid coordination number of approximately 2.4 and a percolating subset of colloids with coordination number of three or more. The rheologically defined gel point occurs at larger bond strengths and higher global coordination, where linker-mediated colloid–colloid connections persist over the deformation time scale. This separation between topological rigidity and rheological gelation is accompanied by a pronounced increase in the bond persistence time as gelation is approached, indicating that persistent effective network connections are required for macroscopic gel-like response. Together, these results show that connectivity is central to equilibrium, linker-mediated colloidal gelation, but that different connectivity measures govern ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation. These observations reinforce the idea that gelation in homogeneous networks of linked colloids can be understood as a connectivity–controlled, dynamical—mechanical transition, distinct from heterogeneous, nonequilibrium gels, where rigidity often arises from irreversible aggregation and kinetic arrest.

papers.title: El Agente Seguro: An Agent for Chemical Safety
papers.abstract: Laboratory safety is becoming increasingly complex as chemical and materials research integrates automation, artificial intelligence, and data-driven experimentation. However, existing safety management approaches rely heavily on manual interpretation or on unconstrained language-model reasoning, which can lead to inconsistent and unreliable outcomes. In this work, we present El Agente Seguro, a graph-based multi-agent framework for safety planning and evaluation in chemical and materials laboratories. The system separates coordination and execution through a central safety director and a dependency-aware safety-solving graph, in which specialized subagents perform structured tasks with schema-constrained data exchange. This design enables controlled and data-driven safety reasoning across multiple layers, including chemical hazards, reaction risks, regulatory constraints, and opera-tional considerations. Benchmark evaluation across seven representative safety tasks demonstrates that El Agente Seguro achieves consistently strong performance relative to frontier general-purpose language models, while also providing more comprehensive and practically useful safety reasoning according to ranking-based evaluations. Beyond benchmark assessment, El Agente Seguro further demonstrates real-world safety capabilities including protocol-level hazard analysis, autonomous procedure modification, dual-use and prohibited chemical enforcement, multimodal SOP generation from laboratory images and experimental procedures, and computationally guided reaction safety prediction through integration with external scientific agents. These results show that structured, dependency-aware multi-agent workflows can improve context-sensitive safety reasoning beyond unconstrained language-model inference alone. Overall, El Agente Seguro establishes a scalable, extensible and practically deployable framework for intelligent laboratory safety into both human-operated and autonomous research environments.

papers.title: Red-Light Tomographic Volumetric 3D Printing in Seconds for Fabrication of Colorless Structures
papers.abstract: Non-pulsed red light photopolymerization is attractive for volumetric additive manufacturing because longer wavelengths can improve light penetration, lower scattering, and reduce photodamage compared with ultra-violet or blue irradiation. In this work, we utilized methylene blue and triethanolamine as a sacrificial type II photoinitiating system for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel printing with a custom-made red-light tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing system. With the optimized formulation, PEGDA hydrogel structures were printed by red light within 30 s. The resulting constructs were colorless, extractable, and contained fully formed internal channels. This work establishes a type II photochemistry system as a promising route for extending tomographic volumetric 3D printing toward lower-energy visible-light irradiation and rapid fabrication of colorless hydrogel constructs.

papers.title: Benchmark Maturity in MOF Adsorption Machine Learning: When Do Conclusions Become Scientifically Reliable?
papers.abstract: Benchmark tables increasingly determine how metal–organic framework (MOF) machinelearning studies justify descriptor choice, model complexity, and screening readiness, yet the reliability of those conclusions is rarely examined as a function of data volume. Here we recast MOF benchmarking as a maturity problem: when does a benchmark become large enough to support stable scientific conclusions rather than only competitive numerical scores? Using a fixed external test set, nested training subsets, and repeated retraining of 16 lightweight descriptor–model pipelines on a large ARC–MOF-derived tabular adsorption dataset, we quantify external-test error together with ranking reproducibility, pairwise probability of superiority, screening stability, and convergence of feature effects. For the main task, CO2 uptake at 0.15 bar, the best RMSE improves from 0.6347 at n = 500 to 0.4433 at full data. The more important transition is qualitative: a practically stable regime emerges near n ≈ 5 × 103–104, where method ranking, elite-candidate recovery, and feature-effect interpretation become substantially more reproducible even though absolute error continues to improve. Within this benchmark, geometry-plus-topology pipelines define the leading accuracy frontier, while topology-only models remain systematically weaker. These results show that strong benchmark accuracy alone is insufficient for defensible claims about descriptor value, model superiority, or screening readiness.

papers.title: Second-order kinetic analysis reveals origins of bifunctional enhancement on alloy electro-oxidation catalysts
papers.abstract: Multi-component electrocatalysts provide wide possibilities to tune reactivity, though the fundamental origins of modification, such as electronic perturbation or bifunctionality, are often ambiguous. Here we demonstrate methods to elucidate operative mechanisms on such materials with microkinetic analysis based on generalized degrees of rate control and second-order kinetic observables. CO electro-oxidation kinetics are analyzed on a series of carbon-supported Ag x Pd 100-x alloys to determine apparent CO and OH – reaction orders, and apparent transfer coefficients (inverse Tafel slopes). Each of these kinetic observables (derivatives of rate) varies across operating conditions, providing a rich dataset with second-order dependencies. The analysis reveals that OH – interacts with Ag sites through only partial charge transfer before coupling to Pd-bound CO. Maximum-likelihood fitting of binding energies, corroborated by grand-canonical density functional theory, also supports electronic effects favoring CO-OH coupling. The observation of non-integer charge transfer steps underscores a broader need for rigorous kinetic characterization beyond Tafel slope analysis.

papers.title: Bromine monoxide radical dominates dimethylsulfide oxidation before the springtime onset of Arctic ice melt
papers.abstract: To understand the atmospheric fate of dimethylsulfide (DMS) during the Arctic spring-to-summer transition and the onset of ice melt, we measured volatile methylated sulfur (VMS) species, including DMS and DMS-derived oxidation products, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and dimethyl sulfone (DMSO 2 ), in the Fram Strait during May and June of 2023. Elevated DMSO contributions to VMS, depleted O 3 , high surface albedo, and air temperatures < 0 ◦ C in air masses influenced by snow-covered sea-ice regions demonstrate that BrO • -initiated oxidation dominated DMS loss prior to the onset of sea-ice melt. GEOS-Chem simulations demonstrate that BrO • is an important oxidant for DMS, but modeled BrO • concentrations from sea salt debromination alone are too low to replicate observed O 3 , DMSO, and DMSO 2 , highlighting the importance of bromine activation in sunlit saline snow. BrO • -initiated oxidation reduces the DMS lifetime, and oxidizes DMS through methanesulfinic acid (MSIA) more quickly in the gas phase and in higher yields compared to • OH-initiated oxidation alone. Once melt onset begins and snowpack-driven halogen activation shuts off, • OH oxidation will dominate Arctic DMS oxidation. Our observations highlight the seasonal variability of halogen oxidation impacting sulfur species in the Arctic marine region, which are likely to change as sea ice extent decreases and the melt season in the Arctic lengthens.

papers.title: Fluorination of Alkoxide Ligands: Neither too much, Nor too little for Optimal Ligand Field Strength
papers.abstract: Fluorination is generally expected to act predictably in ligand design: each added fluorine atom withdraws electron density, weakens σ-donation, and steadily modulates reactivity. However, reported catalytic systems show activity instead peaking at intermediate fluorination—a non-monotonic trend that simple donor-strength arguments cannot explain. To disentangle this non-monotonicity, we prepared a series of homoleptic Mo(V) alkoxides bearing fluorinated tert-butoxide ligands via Mo(IV) → Mo(V/III) disproportionation. As oxo-free d¹ species with trigonalbipyramidal geometry, these complexes provide a direct EPR handle on ligand-field splitting, indicating strengthened axial fields at partial fluorination. Computations reveal enhanced donor–acceptor overlap and favorable electrostatics at intermediate F-content, rationalizing the fluorination sweet spot observed experimentally in catalysis. 17O NMR calculations pinpoint the physical origin of this effect towards C-CF3 σ* acceptor orbitals. Notably, computational exploration of Schrock-type catalysts, for which the influence of fluoroalkoxide ligand is well-known, shows that the specific alkoxide orientation can have a net influence of up to 6 kcal/mol on the ground and transition state energies for the metallacyclobutane formation during the olefin metathesis process. The findings provide understanding of fluorination and can be used to develop new alkoxide ligands and analogous promising synthons for alkoxide-containing catalysts.

papers.title: Selective Growth of (6,5)- and (9,8)- Enriched Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: The chirality-controlled growth of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) is important for the application of SWCNTs in high performance semiconductor devices. In this work, the chirality-selective growth of (6,5) and (9,8) SWCNTs was achieved in bulk phase, using cobalt-sulfur catalyst precursor system with MgO as the catalyst support. Under the optimal condition, characterized by UV-visible- near infrared absorption spectrum, SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) accounted for 28% and 30% of the total, respectively. TEM characterizations showed bimodal diameter distribution of the as-grown SWCNTs, which is consistent with the absorption spectrum. Due to the significant difference of tube diameter, SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) could be separated in aqueous two-phase system to obtain (9,8)-enriched SWCNT dispersion. Catalyst preparation condition, reduction temperature, growth temperature and carbon source affected the chirality distribution of the as-grown SWCNTs. We proposed that under the optimal condition, the diameter distribution of Co clusters presented bimodal distribution. In addition, the growth kinetics of (n,n-1)-SWCNTs is favorable against other chiralities. Therefore, the selective growth of SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) may be ascribed to the dual diameter distribution of Co nanoparticles and the higher growth rates of (n,n-1)-SWCNTs. This work shows the possibility to realize the chirality-selective growth of more than one chiralities whose diameters are different significantly.

papers.title: Cooperative Fe/Co Catalyzed Remote Desaturation for the Synthesis of Unsaturated Amide Derivatives
papers.abstract: Unsaturated amides represent common functional groups found in natural products and bioactive molecules, serving as versatile synthetic building blocks. Here, we report an iron(II)/cobalt(II) dual catalytic system for the syntheses of distally unsaturated amide derivatives. The transformation proceeds through an iron nitrenoid-mediated 1,5- hydrogen atom transfer (1,5-HAT) mechanism. Subsequently, the radical intermediate undergoes hydrogen atom abstraction from the vicinal methylene by a cobaloxime catalyst, efficiently yielding β,γ- or γ,δ -unsaturated amide derivatives under mild conditions. The efficiency of Co-mediated HAT can be tuned by varying different auxiliaries, highlighting the generality of this protocol. Remarkably, this desaturation protocol is also amenable to practical scalability, enabling the synthesis of unsaturated carbamates and ureas, which can be readily converted into various valuable molecules.

papers.title: MOLRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Graph Transformer for De Novo Molecular Generation and Property Optimization
papers.abstract: De novo molecular design, which aims to propose novel molecules with desired chemical and pharmacological properties, is a cornerstone challenge in modern chemistry and drug discovery. Although recent deep generative models have achieved impressive results on standard benchmarks, they still suffer from fragile string-based representations, the inability to incorporate chemical prior knowledge during generation, and ad hoc multiproperty optimization. In this paper, we propose MOLRAG, a unified end-to-end framework that integrates graph-structured attention, retrieval augmentation, and multi-task property prediction. The graph transformer encoder captures both local atomic environments and long-range chemical dependencies, the retrieval-augmented decoder conditions the generative process on chemically similar fragments extracted from an external molecular database, and the multi-task property head provides dense supervision signals and supports Paretooptimal candidate selection at inference. We evaluate MOLRAG on the ZINC250K, QM9, and a curated ChEMBL-DRD2 dataset, and we compare it against four representative baselines under identical data splits and compute budgets. Extensive experiments show that MOLRAG consistently outperforms the strongest baseline by a noticeable margin, achieving 99.2 Keywords: Molecular Generation, Graph Transformer, Retrieval-Augmented Learning, Multi-Objective Optimization, Drug Discovery.

papers.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Glaser-type Coupling for the Enantioselective Synthesis of Planar Chiral Pillar[5]arene Dimers
papers.abstract: As one of the most fundamental methods for constructing C(sp)–C(sp) bonds, the Glaser-type coupling has been extensively developed and widely applied across diverse fields since its discovery in 1869. Despite over 150 years of continuous refinement, a catalytic asymmetric version of this textbook reaction has remained conspicuously unreported, standing as a significant challenge in the field of asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report the first copper-catalyzed asymmetric Glaser-type coupling, achieved through a dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) strategy. Remote stereocontrol is enabled by a newly designed indane-fused Pyrox ligand with extended steric reach, allowing a broad range of racemic ethynyl-substituted pillar[5]arenes to be converted into planar chiral dimers under mild conditions with excellent enantioselectivities and good diastereoselectivities. This work not only delivers dual planar chiral macrocycles with abundant structural and functional diversity, offering key building blocks for practical applications, but also expanding the toolbox of asymmetric C–C bond formation in organic synthetic chemistry.

papers.title: Expanded Evaluation of a Robust On-Line Sample Cleanup-LC-MS Platform Suited for New Approach Methodologies (NAM)
papers.abstract: Sample preparation in bioanalysis can require significant numbers of (manual) steps and consumables. Such procedures can be bottlenecks regarding cost, throughput, and greenness. This is also the case for analysis of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) such as organoids and organ-on-a-chip systems. In this context, approaches tailored for measuring drugs in NAM-related cell culture media (CCM) are being developed. For mass spectrometry-based analysis, automated filtration/filter backflush solid-phase extraction liquid chromatography AFFL-SPE-LC is utilized. Case studies have shown that the “AFFL” platform allows for vast reductions in sample preparation efforts, as the “self-cleaning” filtration features and SPE conditions remove potentially clogging/contaminating materials from samples of biological origin, e.g. the salt- and protein content in CCM. Here, broader demonstrations of the AFFL platform’s traits for CCM analysis are provided, employing an extended panel of small-molecule drugs with varying polarity. The investigated AFFL platform shows reproducible chromatographic performance, as well as fit-for-purpose inter-matrix and inter-column robustness. Hundred-scale injections can be performed with satisfactory repeatability (e.g. retention time RSDs <1%), without interference from the various CCM matrices investigated. Practical NAM applications are also demonstrated. The approach has clear advantages in greenness, obtaining an AGREE prep score of 0.71, contrasting the <0.55 scores of more conventional/commercial approaches. The plastic consumable usage of our approach is 28 g/100 samples, a nearly 20-fold improvement over a previously established benchmark (500 g/100 samples). Taken together, these results demonstrate that AFFL provides a robust, low-waste, and scalable LC–MS based workflow for chemical analysis of NAM-derived samples.

papers.title: Bridging Generative AI and Synthesis-on-Demand Chemical Spaces for Structure-based De Novo Drug Design
papers.abstract: Generative AI offers a powerful alternative for de novo drug design but frequently produces molecules that lack viable synthetic routes. While synthesis-on-demand (SoD) chemical spaces provide access to trillions of readily synthesizable compounds, their rapid expansion has created a computational bottleneck for effective virtual screening (VS). This study proposes a bridging strategy to navigate these challenges by identifying structurally similar analogs of AI-generated leads within SoD chemical spaces. We evaluated five generative methods (AutoGrow4, LS-MolGen, MoLeR, MORLD, and REINVENT2.0) targeting the KEAP1-NRF2 protein-protein interaction. Using the Analog Hunter tool, we searched six SoD spaces, including the 7-trillion-molecule eXplore library, to find accessible analogs of the top AI-generated leads. Overall, the workflow identified 1701 synthesizable analogs, while being substantially less resource-intensive than VS and maintaining high chemical diversity, with the REINVENT2.0-eXplore pairing benefiting the most from this bridge strategy. Furthermore, 1037 of these analogs were predicted to be more potent than the reference inhibitor iKEAP1. These results show that bridging generative AI with chemical spaces can overcome the synthetic gap in de novo design, providing a scalable and efficient framework for discovering synthetically accessible and high-potency drug leads.

papers.title: TRPM8 Virtual Screening: The Essential Role of Target-Specific, Inactive-Enriched Machine-Learning Scoring Functions
papers.abstract: Motivation: The Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 8 (TRPM8) ion channel is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in pain, inflammation, and other disorders. While structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used in drug discovery, the effectiveness of generic and target-specific machine-learning (ML) scoring functions (SFs) for ion channels such as TRPM8 remains to be investigated. Results: We established the first comprehensive structure-based VS benchmark for TRPM8. This evaluates classical docking SFs, generic ML SFs and target-specific ML models retrospectively across multiple TRPM8 protein conformations and docking protocols. The evaluation revealed that generic ML rescoring at most provided modest and conformation-dependent improvements over classical docking on this target. Target-specific ML models based only on protein-ligand interaction fingerprints improved early enrichment on test sets when regression algorithms were employed. However, performance remained sensitive to protein conformation choice and chemical dissimilarity. Systematic evaluation of feature representations showed that combining structure-derived interaction features with ligand-based descriptors enhanced enrichment under selected docking tool-protein conformation combinations. Critically, presenting the learning algorithm with many more negative training instances, via inactive-enriched training, strongly reduced false positives. This also resulted in markedly improved generalization to chemically dissimilar test sets for structure-based models. By contrast, ligand-only QSAR models proved sensitive to more class-imbalanced training sets. Under inactive-enriched training, PLEC-based support vector regression (SVR) models achieved robust and strong VS performance, highlighting the critical role of learning the vast diversity of inactive molecules better during model training in developing reliable target-specific ML SFs for TRPM8. Availability: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18775467 Contact: p.ballester@imperial.ac.uk

papers.title: Operator Entanglement in Quantum Dynamics Simulations: Formalism and Analysis Tools
papers.abstract: We review the framework of operator Hilbert space and introduce the one-and two-particle super reduced density matrices (1-SRDMs and 2-SRDMs), as well as the super mutual information (SMI). The eigenvectors of the 1-SRDMs define what we term natural single particle operator bases, and provide a way to compress vibrational and vibronic Hamiltonians with controlled error. The SMI is defined from the operator entanglement entropy of the 1-SRDMs and 2-SRDMs, and captures the correlation between operators acting on different one-mode subspaces, which may be used to reveal and quantify both direct and indirect couplings that might otherwise be difficult to extract. Efficient numerical approaches for the calculation of SRDMs and the SMI are developed and applied to a set of prototypical vibrational and vibronic Hamiltonians, as well as approximations to the corresponding time-evolution operators. Through this, we demonstrate that: (i) commonly used vibronic Hamiltonians are amenable to extremely high levels of compression without compromising accuracy, and; (ii) SMI analysis can be used to systematically and quantitatively reveal both direct and indirect couplings that might otherwise be difficult to extract, including indirect couplings of vibrational modes via intermediary electronic-vibrational interactions.

papers.title: Free Energy Calculations Meet Generative Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Free energy differences govern the equilibrium properties of physical and chemical processes. Closely related quantities such as normalizing constants and model evidence appear throughout machine learning and Bayesian statistics. This broad relevance has motivated researchers across disciplines to develop methods for computing free energy differences. In this review, we survey methods for computing free energy differences between two states from sampled configurations, organized around the unifying concept of configuration space overlap between the two states. When the overlap is large, classical methods such as exponential averaging and the Bennett acceptance ratio can be applied directly, and we discuss their statistical properties. When the overlap is small, we consider three strategies: intermediate states, ensemble transformation, and reference states. The intermediate-state approach introduces a sequence of bridging states and is general and widely applicable, but it can be computationally expensive. The ensemble transformation approach instead learns a mapping that transforms one target state into a new state with significant overlap with the other, enabling direct estimation of the free energy difference without intermediate states. The reference-state approach computes the absolute free energy of each target state independently and obtains the free energy difference from the results. Both the ensemble transformation and reference-state approaches require learning a mapping between states such that the transformed state has substantial overlap with a target state. Learning such a mapping is a challenging problem, but recent advances in generative machine learning have provided powerful tools for this task. We review flowbased generative models trained via flow matching as scalable approaches to learning such mappings from sampled configurations, and show how they can be combined with classical free energy methods to compute free energy differences efficiently. We conclude by discussing practical guidance, challenges, and future directions.

papers.title: Development of a rapid LC–ICP-MS/MS method for screening structurally distinct PFAS and investigation of compound-dependent BaF+ responses
papers.abstract: Element-specific fluorine detection by ICP-MS/MS via BaF+ formation is a promising approach for the detection and quantification of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including species inaccessible by established ionisation techniques. In this work, we present a rapid (<7 min) LC–ICP-MS/MS method for separation and quantification of structurally distinct PFAS compounds, including carboxylic acids, sulfonates and fluorotelomer alcohols. While BaF+ detection is theoretically compound-independent, pronounced differences in signal response were observed depending on PFAS structure and solvent composition. Control experiments using inorganic fluoride added directly to the Ba solution revealed that increasing organic solvent content during gradient elution enhanced BaF+ formation. To further elucidate the origin of the compound-dependent response observed under LC conditions, direct nebulisation experiments were performed using different sample introduction systems. Using a conventional nebulisation system, BaF+ response factors varied by up to a factor of seven among representative PFAS, with longer-chain compounds yielding substantially lower responses. Replacing the sample introduction setup with a high-efficiency nebulisation system drastically reduced inter-class variability, demonstrating that differential aerosol formation and transport, rather than differences in intrinsic plasma chemistry, drive the compound-dependent response. Together, these findings define the critical operating constraints of BaF+-based fluorine detection and establish the conditions required for reliable and robust LC-ICP-MS/MS analysis of PFAS.

papers.title: Formulation Informatics (Nanomedicine): Deep Learning Workflows on HPC for the Predictive Design of Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs)
papers.abstract: The design and development of nanomedicines, with a critical emphasis on lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for the delivery of gene therapies and mRNA vaccines, has historically relied on empirical trial-and-error processes. This iterative approach imposes a substantial economic burden and severely restricts the exploration of the vast chemical space (> 106 possible combinations). In this research, we formalize and expand the paradigm of Formulation Informatics, a convergent discipline that merges the expertise of the Pharmacobiological Chemist (QFB) in experimental pharmaceutics and lipid physical chemistry, with next-generation Artificial Intelligence (AI) architectures. We present a massive computational pipeline based on Deep Learning implemented on PyTorch and TensorFlow, designed to run on High-Performance Computing (HPC) infrastructures and GPU clusters (Data Science and Supercomputing). Fed by massive physicochemical databases, the model extracts latent representations of molecular structures to predict optimal stoichiometries that maximize Encapsulation Efficiency (EE) and direct cellular specificity. The results show a predictive accuracy of 94.2% (R 2 = 0.94), accelerating the creation of targeted therapies and reducing R&D timelines from months to hours. This technological convergence catalyzes a revolution in the profiling of health technologies.

papers.title: Electrifying C–N Bond Formation: Inorganic Nitrogen Reduction as a Route to Sustainable Amino Acid Synthesis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical C–N bond formation driven by inorganic nitrogen reduction has recently emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable amino acid synthesis and remediation of nitrogen-containing pollutants. Beyond enabling greener access to α-functionalized organonitrogen compounds, these reactions provide a controllable platform for coupling reactive nitrogen intermediates with CO 2 - or biomass-derived carbonyl compounds. Despite rapid advances in this area, a comprehensive, mechanism-centered perspective encompassing the full spectrum of reductive inorganic nitrogen species, including nitrate, nitrite, nitrate, nitric oxide, hydroxylamine, ammonia, and dinitrogen, and their integration with carbonyl substrates for amino acid synthesis remains lacking. This Focus Review consolidates emerging mechanistic insights, highlights enabling catalyst design and reaction environments principles, and outlines actionable strategies toward selective, energy-efficient amino acid electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Enzymatic reaction directional feasibility prediction for computer-aided synthesis planning
papers.abstract: Enzyme reaction feasibility prediction is essential for the realization of computer aided synthesis planning and automated biocatalytic process scouting. Accurate prediction of enzymatic reaction feasibility can have a significant effect on the success or failure of an attempted transformation in the laboratory. However, reaction feasibility prediction remains a challenging problem and relies heavily on experts’ intuition and prior experience. In this work, we develop a chemical similaritybased algorithm to predict the feasibility of any proposed enzymatic reaction. This algorithm was developed using Rhea, SwissProt, MetaCyc, EcoCyc, Reactome, and GeneOntology databases of expertly curated, high-quality annotations of feasible direction of enzymatic reactions. For predicting the feasibility of a user input query reaction, our algorithm identifies a similar transformation with matching reaction chemistry from the database, and it uses the feasibility annotation associated with this precedent. Using 24,161 reactions from our database as a knowledgebase, this algorithm can predict the feasibility of enzymatic reactions with an accuracy of 92% in a leave-one-out-cross-validation study. The utility of the model is illustrated by identifying feasible biocatalytic routes towards active pharmaceutical ingredients and commodity chemicals while filtering out infeasible suggestions. We also demonstrate that the algorithm enables the automatic ideation of novel alternative feasible biocatalytic routes towards complex small molecules in addition to recovery of the published routes. This algorithm opens the door to harnessing the potential of computer-aided synthesis planning tools to ideate a diverse set of biocatalytic routes towards a user defined target molecule with minimal expert intervention.

papers.title: Ultrafast Spectroscopic Evidence for Adaptive Fluoride-Controlled Higher-State Emission through Excited-State Reorganization
papers.abstract: Controlling excited-state relaxation is central to modern photophysics. Anti-Kasha luminescence, involving radiative decay from higher excited states, remains particularly rare, and achieving such controllable higher-state emission offers a powerful route for sensing and photonic applications. In donor–substituted tetracyanobuta-1,3-dienes (TCBDs), strong charge-transfer properties are often overshadowed by nonradiative decay, suppressing emission. Here, we report an isatin-derived push–pull chromophore with E-configuration, IST–NH, synthesized via a [2+2] cycloaddition–retroelectrocyclization (CA–RE) reaction, that exhibits unprecedented fluoride-triggered dual anti-Kasha emission. In THF, addition of 1 equivalent of F- activates S3 emission at 398 nm, while higher concentrations (3 eq.) induce deprotonation, redirecting 2 relaxation to the S2 state with cyan fluorescence at 480 nm. Femtosecond transient absorption studies further support this concentration-dependent excited-state modulation, demonstrating precise control over higher excited-state dynamics using a single anionic stimulus. Spectroscopic, NMR, and TD-DFT studies reveal that F- binding via H-bonding, and subsequent deprotonation underlie this adaptive luminescence, with a benzyl-protected analogue IST–NBz reveal the crucial role of the N–H site. IST–NH achieves fluorescence-based fluoride detection with a detection limit of 27.2 nM and exceptional selectivity. These findings establish IST–NH as a rare, switchable anti-Kasha emitter that bridges fundamental excited-state photophysics with practical fluoride sensing, including colorimetric fiber-strip test.

papers.title: Semi-Quantitative Estimation of MDMA Tablet Dosage and Cocaine/Ketamine Purity Using a Simple to Operate Field-Portable Device
papers.abstract: High-dose MDMA tablets and variable-purity cocaine and ketamine samples are commonly encountered by drug checking services and police forces in the United Kingdom and Europe. At the time of writing, there are few simpleto-operate field-portable technologies that provide semi-quantitative information on MDMA tablet dosage or cocaine and ketamine purity at the point of sampling. We previously reported on the development of a low-cost, fieldportable device that can be used to rapidly screen illicit drug samples through Hybridized Spectral Fingerprinting (HSF); the combined measurement of fluorescence emission and diffuse LED reflectance. Here, we describe the development and testing of deep learning models for both MDMA tablet dosage and cocaine/ketamine purity that can be used in on this device in the field. We used 62 GC-EI-MS quantified MDMA tablet samples to train a convolutional neural network model to classify tablet samples in either 1–170 mg or 170–300 mg MDMA HCl dosage brackets. External testing on 195 positive and negative MDMA samples yielded a 98% device accuracy. We used 1H NMR quantified cocaine and ketamine samples to train a second convolutional neural network model for presumptive identification and semi-quantitative purity estimation of cocaine and ketamine samples, yielding an accuracy of 96% on an external test set of 47 samples.
