These findings demonstrate that Hybridized Spectral Fingerprinting paired with deep learning can be reliably used to alert on potentially harmful MDMA tablets and estimate the purity of cocaine and ketamine samples, supporting harm reduction activities and police screening or intelligence gathering workflows.

papers.title: The road to computationally designed artificial metalloenzymes
papers.abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) enable the introduction of organometallic cofactors into protein scaffolds for new-to-nature chemistry. Traditionally, these have been constructed from a handful of scaffolds capable of binding a range of cofactors and substrates. However, in comparison to natural enzymes, this can result in a lack of specificity, rate enhancement and stability. Recent advances in computational binder and enzyme design, and deeper insights into how natural (metallo)enzymes exploit their scaffolds to enhance active site performance, have greatly expanded the toolbox available to ArM designers. In this perspective, we outline some of these advances, and provide insight into how they can be leveraged to create more efficient and robust ArMs.

papers.title: DC electro-hydrodynamics of a surface-active, confined droplet system
papers.abstract: A theoretical and analytical investigation of the electrohydrodynamics (EHD) of a surfactantladen confined leaky dielectric droplet suspended in an immiscible liquid medium has been presented. The analysis considers the combined effects of confinement, surfactant transport, and Marangoni stresses within the creeping flow regime under the small deformation approximation. The governing equations for charge conservation, momentum transport, and surfactant transport are solved analytically based on the Taylor–Melcher leaky dielectric framework. The study systematically examines the influence of the confinement ratio α, Marangoni number Ma, and surface Péclet number Pes on the normal and tangential hydrodynamic stresses, deformation characteristics, and interfacial velocity distributions for two distinct electrical property systems. The results demonstrate that the electrical property contrast strongly governs the interfacial charge dynamics and surfactant redistribution, leading to significantly different sensitivities to surfactant-induced surface tension gradients in the two systems. System A exhibits strong dependence on Ma and Pes due to enhanced interfacial charge accumulation and vigorous recirculatory flow, whereas system B shows comparatively weak sensitivity owing to weaker interfacial forcing and limited surfactant convection. The analysis further reveals confinement-induced modifications in the stress distribution, deformation behavior, and interfacial transport characteristics. The present study provides physical insight into the coupled interplay between confinement, surfactant transport, and EHD interfacial dynamics in confined multiphase systems.

papers.title: Directed Heterodimerization: Total Synthesis of (–)-Folicangine, (–)-Voafolidine, (–)-Isovoafolidine, and (–)-Tabernaesine B
papers.abstract: We report the first total synthesis of heterodimeric aspidosperma–aspidosperma alkaloids (–)-folicangine, (–)voafolidine, (–)-isovoafolidine and (–)-tabernaesine B. Our biosynthesis-inspired stereoselective directed union of complex fragments derived from (–)-mehranine (northern half) and (–)-deoxoapodine (southern half) provided a methylene-bridged heterodimer, serving as a key precursor to these structurally related bisindole alkaloids. Methylenation of this versatile heterodimeric intermediate resulted in a stereodivergent ring closure to give (–)-tabernaesine B alongside its C7 diastereomer, enabling our stereochemical revision of this alkaloid. The corresponding C2'-hemiaminal alkaloids (–)-voafolidine and (–)-isovoafolidine were obtained via an analogous spirocyclization-reduction sequence from a hydrated derivative of the methylene-bridged heterodimeric precursor. Our biosynthesisinspired heterodimerization strategy allowed for the assembly of the intricate double hemiaminal alkaloid (–)-folicangine via C8iminium ion capture by the C2'-hemiaminal of an intermediate en route to (–)-isovoafolidine.

papers.title: Composition-Driven Degradation Pathways in Layered Sodium Cathodes
papers.abstract: Layered Na-Ni-Mn-O oxides are promising high-energy cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their development is limited by strong coupling between composition, structural ordering, airstability, and electrochemical reversibility. Herein, we resolve this complex material space by integrating high-throughput synthesis with uncertainty-aware machine learning and mechanism driven multi-modal characterizations. By synthesizing and characterizing over 300 materials across multiple temperatures, we construct a phase-structure-property map that captures phase stability, Na-loss-driven Ni segregation, transition-metal ordering, and moisture-induced degradation pathways. We show that Ni substation supresses Jahn-Teller distortion, drives Mn oxidation, and stabilizes a 2√3 × 2√3 R30° superstructure that governs both air stability and electrochemical response. High-throughput electrochemical mapping reveals non-monotonic capacity-retention relations and identifies performance regimes inaccessible to conventional approaches. Guided by uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling across ~105 compositions, we identify an optimized composition, Na0.55Ni0.287Mn0.713O2 achieving 96.1% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Operando diffraction and impedance spectroscopy show that degradation arises from coupled high-voltage P2→O2 slab gliding and low-voltage P2→P'2 distortion; restricting operation to 2.0-4.1V suppress both process and stabilizes long-term cycling. These results reveal design principles for controlling degradation pathways in layered oxides for durable sodium-ion cathodes.

papers.title: Revealed mechanisms of the suppression of the electrical conductivity by manganese doping in a lead-free BiFeO3-based piezoelectric system
papers.abstract: The bottleneck in the development of efficient BiFeO 3 -based lead-free piezoelectric ceramics is their high electrical conductivity, especially at elevated temperatures (>200°C). A significant reduction of several orders of magnitude in the conductivity is achieved by doping with multivalent transition metal cations, such as manganese. Despite this practical result, the underlying mechanisms leading to the conductivity reduction has not been clarified yet. Here, we elucidate the defect chemistry of BiFeO 3 (BFO)-based systems, focusing on the impact of Mn doping on their conductivity and functional properties through a combined experimental and modeling approach. In situ electric-conductivity and thermo-electric measurements under dynamic and equilibrium conditions in varying oxygen partial pressures were complemented by quantitative defect chemical modeling to clarify the underlying mechanisms. Our findings surprisingly reveal that the main effect of Mn in reducing the electrical conductivity in oxygen-rich conditions is to suppress bismuth (Bi) vacancy formation. Manganese doping also introduces additional hole and electron traps, which affect conductivity at low temperature and oxygen-poor conditions. This study provides new guidelines for controlling electrical conductivity in BFO-based systems, leading to an ultrahigh piezoelectric coefficient (d 33 ’) of ~1200 pm/V at ~300 °C and it demonstrates how quantitative knowledge of charge transition levels in multivalent species can support materials design strategies, paving the way for optimized lead-free piezoelectric materials.

papers.title: An Inverse Polarity Approach for Modular Synthesis of Heptamethine Dyes via Their Ketone Intermediates
papers.abstract: Heptamethine dyes has become a popular dye scaffold owing to its red-shifted absorption and emission wavelengths in the near-infrared (700−1000 nm) and shortwave infrared (SWIR, 1000−2000 nm, also known as NIR-II) region, enabling deeper penetration for in vivo imaging applications. Despite their widespread use, the synthesis of these complex fluorophores traditionally relies on a single synthetic stereotype involving the coupling between two nucleophilic heterocycles and an electrophilic methine precursor. These reactions often demand harsh conditions, leading to side products and limiting structural diversity. Herein, we report a versatile and modular synthetic strategy for heptamethine dyes based on an “inverse-polarity” approach. This route employs readily available building blocks, proceeding through a ketone intermediate that allows for the independent selection of heterocycles (symmetric or unsymmetric), the ring system on the methine bridge, and diverse 4'-substituents via organolithium addition. This method enables the synthesis of previously inaccessible fluorophores, including dyes with varied central ring systems and a unique scaffold bearing three terminal alkyne groups for multivalent bioconjugation. We demonstrate the synthesis of a series of heptamethine cyanine dyes spanning the NIR to SWIR regions, showcasing the wide applicability and broad compatibility of our method. This “inverse-polarity” approach thus unlocks a versatile synthetic platform, facilitating the development of future heptamethine dyes with tailored photophysical properties and targeting capabilities for advanced in vivo imaging.

papers.title: Negative Linear Compressibility of a One-dimensional Interpenetrated Metalorganic Framework
papers.abstract: A metal-organic framework (MOF) , UoB-200, with a necklace topology that exhibits rare 1D®1D parallel interpenetration is reported. UoB-200 exhibits significant negative linear compressibility (NLC) over a pressure range up to 3.44 GPa. When pressure is applied, elongation along the crystallographic c axis is observed via a wine-rack mechanism. The experimental results are modelled by simulations, which closely reproduce the mechanical response and suggest that the presence of solvent within the UoB-200 pores has minimal impact on the NLC behaviour at comparatively low pressures.

papers.title: Polyethyleneimine (PEI) molecular weight alters the photophysical and FRET properties of water dispersible NaYF4:Yb,Er upconversion nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) are optically active materials with near-infrared excitation and tuneable anti-Stokes emission, typically resulting in visible emission. A route to routine and reliable synthesis of water-dispersible UCNPs for biomedical imaging applications is the polyethyleneimine (PEI)- assisted solvothermal autoclave synthesis; however, the properties of the resulting UCNPs remain understudied. Herein, we report how PEI molecular weight alters properties of core-only, red-emitting, water-dispersible PEI-UCNPs. In terms of brightness, 1.2 kDa PEI-UCNPs exhibited 5 times more intense upconversion luminescence (UCL) than 25 kDa PEI-UCNPs and a 29% longer UCL lifetime (LT) for the red emission band (~640-690 nm, 4 F 9/2 → 4 I 15/2 Er 3+ transition) in DI H2O. Dispersal in D2O increased emission across wavebands, with green emission ( 2 H 11/2 , 4 S 3/2 → 4 I 15/2 Er 3+ transition) increasing by 248 - 365% whereas red emission only increased between 38-64%. From our results, we infer that PEI may quench the UCL via high-energy NH vibrations. We also examined Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) between PEI-UCNPs and an electrostatically adsorbed fluorescent model dye, AlexaFluor647® (AF647). 25 kDa PEI-UCNPs achieved highest LT-estimated FRET efficiencies of ~11% in H2O and 16% in D2O, respectively. These findings highlight that polymer MW should be considered when optimising UCNP synthesis.

papers.title: 25 Years of Cardiac Ion Channel QSAR: From hERG Dominance to Multi-Channel Modelling
papers.abstract: In 2013 the Comprehensive in vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) initiative proposed multi-channel assessment for proarrhythmic risk evaluation, yet ligand-based predictive modelling has remained largely single-channel. To quantify and explain this mismatch, we survey 146 QSAR and machine learning studies on cardiac ion channels published between 2001 and early 2026. Across this period, 90% of studies target hERG as their sole ion channel endpoint—a proportion reflecting regulatory incentives, data availability, and research inertia rather than scientific necessity. Although public data for Nav1.5 and Cav1.2 were sufficient for modelling years earlier, both channels received only isolated studies until 2022. Since then, multi-channel modelling has expanded substantially, with multiple groups now addressing hERG, Nav1.5, and Cav1.2 jointly. In contrast, two CiPA channels, Kv4.3 and Kir2.1, remain entirely unmodelled due to genuine data scarcity. Closing the remaining gaps will require coordinated data release (or federated learning) for neglected channels, methods suited to data-scarce targets, and standardised benchmarks enabling rigorous progress tracking—none of which individual research groups can establish alone.

papers.title: Breaking Dielectric Dogma: Steric-Entropic Dominance and Anomalous Ion Pairing in Ternary Ionic Liquid–Carbonate Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Conventional electrolyte design assumes that bulk dielectric constants (ε) govern ion solvation and that high-ε solvents necessarily dominate the first coordination shell of Li+ while promoting ion dissociation. Here we systematically challenge this electrostatic paradigm using charge-scaled classical molecular dynamics simulations of ternary 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([EMI][TFSI])–carbonate blends (EC/DMC) containing 1 M LiTFSI. Across five compositions from pure carbonate to neat IL, we uncover a striking, counterintuitive preference: Li+ coordinates preferentially with low-polarity dimethyl carbonate (DMC, ε≈3.1) over highly polar ethylene carbonate (EC, ε≈90). This anomalous behavior originates from local steric-entropic packing—the flexible, acyclic DMC allows an unconstrained tetrahedral geometry around Li+, whereas rigid cyclic EC imposes severe inter-ligand repulsion. Furthermore, carbonate addition paradoxically reinforces short-range Li+–[TFSI]- bidentate clustering and [EMI]+–[TFSI]- hydrogen bonding. This counterintuitive ion-pairing enhancement arises from a dielectric buffering effect: carbonate molecules screen long-range isotropic Coulombic repulsions, lowering kinetic barriers to close approach and deepening local interaction wells. Spatial distribution functions reveal that carbonate addition disrupts the native anisotropic order of neat [EMI][TFSI] (cations stacked above/below the ring plane, anions in-plane), driving isotropization while simultaneously strengthening specific H-bonds. Quantitative coordination numbers identify a structural ―sweet spot‖ at 40–60 % IL content, where balanced Li+–anion exchange and high vehicular transport coexist. These findings overthrow the simple ε-centric design rule, establishing steric-entropic constraints and dielectric mediation as primary variables for rationally designing non-flammable, high-conductivity post-lithium electrolytes.

papers.title: The Catalytic Asymmetric Alkylation of Olefins with Alcohol Derivatives
papers.abstract: Both olefins and arenes are abundant and versatile feedstock chemicals. Although the electrophilic alkylation of arenes constitutes an advanced technology, the corresponding alkylation of olefins is rather undeveloped. Here we report an asymmetric catalytic benzylation and allylation of unactivated olefins with acetates as electrophiles. The reaction is catalyzed by a single imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst operating as a silylium Lewis acid. Mechanistic experiments support an enantioconvergent S N 1 mechanism, featuring stereoablative ion pair formation, resulting in a dynamic kinetic resolution. The enantioenriched hydrocarbon products are readily derivatized to odorants and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in one or two steps. The developed method provides a metal-free alternative to cornerstone Tsuji–Trost -type allylations proceeding though π-allyl metal complexes.

papers.title: Data-Driven Circular Procurement of para-aramid using Handheld Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Reliable quality assessment of End-of-Life (EoL) materials remains a primary bottleneck in operationalizing the circular economy. The heterogeneity of EoL materials, limited traceability, and inadequate sensing technologies at collection points create inefficiencies that undermine the entire value chain. Handheld Near-infrared (NIR) and Raman spectroscopy offer a promising route toward real-time, non-destructive material analysis. Yet, their lower precision and high sensitivity to environmental variation hinder practical implementation. This study introduces a dual-perspective decision framework that integrates handheld spectroscopy with chemometrics to guide circular procurement. By linking material composition to both value (seller perspective) and acceptability thresholds (buyer perspective), the framework enables quantitative, evidence-based decision-making at the point of collection. Using para-aramid EoL materials as a proof of concept, four handheld spectrophotometers (Trinamix, Neospectra, Tellspec, and Mira) were benchmarked across multiple quality thresholds. Spectral data were used to develop classification (buyer) and regression (seller) models, while environmental and economic assessment quantified the broader impact of handheld screening. Trinamix emerged as the optimal device, achieving 100% balanced accuracy at the 92% para-aramid threshold and the lowest Root Mean Square Error of Prediction (RMSEP) of 0.56% with Support Vector Regression. By redefining EoL materials screening from a constraint into a data-driven analytical process, handheld spectroscopy delivers measurable environmental and financial benefits, advancing the transition toward low-carbon circular systems.

papers.title: Living Loop Network
papers.abstract: Cyclic topological defects—an inherent byproduct of polymer network formation—fundamentally constrain the mechanical performance of elastomers, hydrogels, and related functional materials. Herein, we introduce a living loop network (LON) constructed via an innovative self‑complementary cross-linking strategy of an A 2 B 2 -type [2]pseudorotaxane monomer. In this network, functional living loops are deliberately programmed into the polymer architecture during polymerization, directly replacing conventional static loop defects. Owing to the dynamic behaviors of living loops, the resulting LON exhibits substantially enhanced mechanical properties compared to conventional covalently cross-linked network containing static loops (control), demonstrating a fracture strain of 354% versus 144%, fracture stress of 4.6 MPa versus 3.7 MPa, and toughness of 7.9 MJ/m 3 versus 3.5 MJ/m 3 . More strikingly, following large-strain deformation, the LON achieves over 92% rapid elastic recovery without resting, enabled by the synergistic expansion-contraction of the living loops. This work introduces the novel concept of living loops, which not only provides a transformative approach to the long-standing challenge of loop defects but also endows polymer networks with a distinctive mechanical toughness and autonomous recovery mechanism.

papers.title: Seven is optimal: a K5 selection principle for photosynthetic energy transfer
papers.abstract: The Fenna–Matthews–Olson complex transfers excitation energy at ∼ 99% efficiency at physiological temperature—a performance no model derives from first principles. We show that a single combinatorial fact does: the complex has seven chromophores, and seven is the unique integer that decomposes as 5+5−3, allowing two complete pentachoric cells (K5) to share a triangular face (K3). This K3 junction minimises the number of inter-cell coupling edges to four—a combinatorial minimum among all 5+5−k decompositions. Applied to the measured Hamiltonian (Adolphs–Renger, 2006), the optimal decomposition places the shared face at {BChl1, BChl4, BChl6} with an intra/inter coupling ratio of 44.7, the four inter-cell edges being the four weakest in the Hamiltonian. The machinery of the companion paper P21—Ohm’s law as the stationary Dirichlet state, the edge dipole as stable carrier, face saturation as the resistance mechanism—places the complex deep in the ohmic regime (40% of face saturation), where transport is governed by a monotone density gradient from antenna to reaction centre with zero saturated faces. The absolute quantum yield (∼99%) is shown to be dominated by the ratio of trapping to recombination rates, not by the network topology; the K5 contribution is the separation ratio, the structural robustness, and the identification of the transport bottleneck as catalytic rather than topological. The PE545 complex (eight chromophores, 5 + 5 − 2, K2 junction) is tested as a falsification: its optimal ratio is 11.3, a factor 3.9× below the FMO, and none of its 280 decompositions matches the FMO value. All results are verified by a companion script (108 tests, 0 failures) with no free parameter beyond α∗ = 1/(4 ln 2) and the electron mass.

papers.title: In Silico study of Diosgenin - Serotonin receptor ligand interaction for neurotherapeutic potential using virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and ADMET assessments
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorder is an umbrella term that includes several diseases that are incurable and gradual, and there is lack of proven cures. Moreover, motor symptoms are the main focus for the current therapies. But non-motor symptoms (NMS) like depression, anxiety, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, and cognitive decline are also drastically affecting the daily lifestyle of patients suffering from neurodegenerative disorders. Evidently, serotonin receptors are a crucial protein of interest that plays a significant role in modulating NMS. Currently, daily dosages of corticosteroids are given to manage NMS in patients, but daily usage of those drugs includes distinct side effects. In this study, 50 phytocompounds are retrieved from several databases, and diosgenin is found to be the most potent candidate on the basis of its binding score. Moreover, to validate this, a computational biology approach has been utilized to study pharmacokinetic activity, molecular docking, along with molecular dynamic simulation (MD simulation) to validate the structural dynamic study of diosgenin and serotonin complex. Overall, diosgenin obtained from plants like Dioscorea species can be used as a safer alternative for the treatment of NMS affecting the daily lifestyle of patients in neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Fueling carbodiimide chemistry: direct structural characterization of the O-acylisourea intermediate by ion mobility–mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Carbodiimide-fueled molecular machines, catalytic reaction cycles, and a broad spectrum of synthetic transformations from peptide coupling to Steglich esterification depend on the fate of a single transient species: the O-acylisourea intermediate. Whether this intermediate engages in productive chemistry or diverts irreversibly to its inert N-acylurea isomer determines the outcome of every carbodiimide-mediated process. Yet direct structural characterization of the Oacylisourea generated from standard dialkylcarbodiimides has eluded the field for over four decades. Here we report the gas-phase separation and structural identification of both the Oacylisourea and the N-acylurea isomers, sampled directly from the reaction media by nanospray ionization (nESI), by coupling high-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry with tandem mass spectrometry (nESI-FAIMS–MSn). Using N,N'-diisopropylcarbodiimide (DIC) and (S)-3,3,3-trifluoro-2-methoxy-2-phenylpropanoic acid (MTPA) as a model system, we achieve baseline FAIMS separation of the two isomers and stablish their assignments through three convergent lines of evidence: isomer-specific CID fragmentation patterns, real-time kinetic monitoring of the isomerization directly from solution and isomer-specific infrared multiplephoton dissociation (IRMPD) spectra supported by DFT calculations. These results constitute the first gas-phase separation and structural assignment of the O-acylisourea and N-acylurea isomers generated from a standard dialkylcarbodiimide and sampled directly from solution without chemical trapping or prior isolation, also providing a practical handle for tracking the Oacylisourea/N-acylurea partition — and distinguishing both from downstream products — by standard tandem MS.

papers.title: pysorb: A Python Library and GUI for Adsorption Modelling
papers.abstract: pysorb is an open-source Python library for adsorption modelling that integrates isotherm fitting, multicomponent mixture prediction, dynamic fixed-bed breakthrough simulation, and kinetic studies within a single framework. The platform is designed to bridge scripted scientific computing and laboratory-facing workflows, exposing the same numerical routines through both Python interfaces and graphical applications. Equilibrium modelling supports flexible isotherm models, temperature-dependent parameters, nonlinear regression, and unary, Ideal Adsorbed Solution Theory (IAST), and extended mixture calculations. The mixture and breakthrough solvers support arbitrary components, sites, and site-level model combinations. The breakthrough solver supports non-isothermal and non-isobaric conditions, alongside kinetic solvers for dynamic uptake and zero-length column (ZLC) analysis. The code is written in pure Python using NumPy and SciPy. Numba JIT compilation can bring mixture and breakthrough kernels near compiled C/Fortran performance, although no benchmark is reported here. The Tkinter and Matplotlib GUI layer supports data import, model configuration, visualisation of fitted curves and breakthrough profiles, and session persistence. The current release provides an integrated adsorption-modelling framework; planned development will extend model coverage and introduce additional kinetic and process models.

papers.title: Cholesterol Lowering Medications and Brain Function Evaluating the Link Between Lipid Management and Cognitive Impairment: A Short Review
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are recognized as the leading cause of mortality worldwide, so lipid management is established as a cornerstone of preventive medicine. Because the brain is known as the most cholesterol-rich organ, a "Heart-Brain Paradox" is created when blood cholesterol is aggressively lowered. In 2012, a safety label change was mandated by the FDA due to reports of memory loss and confusion among statin users. In this review, the connection between medications like statins, PCSK9 inhibitors, and ezetimibe and cognitive function is evaluated. It is understood that lipophilic statins can pass through the blood-brain barrier, while hydrophilic statins are generally excluded. Additionally, the potential impacts of pharmaceutical excipients and environmental pollutants on the gut-brain axis are explored. It is concluded that the benefits of vascular protection are generally found to be much greater than the risks of cognitive impairment.

papers.title: System-Level Impacts of Reverse Water-Gas Shift Reactor Selectivity in Power-to-Liquid Fuel Production
papers.abstract: Power-to-liquid (PtL) production of drop-in hydrocarbons from captured CO 2 and electrolytic H 2 using reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) coupled with Fischer-Tropsch (FT) is a promising route for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify transport, but its performance is constrained by overall energy efficiency and hydrogen utilization across integrated units. Here, motivated by our development of highly selective, transition metal-free reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) catalysts, we quantify the system-level value of RWGS selectivity in an Aspen Plus model by comparing a CO-selective RWGS case against an unselective case that includes methanation at thermodynamic equilibrium, while keeping FT synthesis, recycle configuration, and plant boundary conditions consistent. For standalone syngas production, without downstream fuel production or syngas recycle, the selective case reaches a maximum energy efficiency of 81.6% at 650 ◦ C, 30 bar, compared to 79.3% at 800 ◦ C, 5 bar for the unselective case, and yields 5% lower syngas minimum selling price. In the integrated RWGS-FT plant, the energy efficiency optimum shifts from high-temperature/low-pressure operation in the unselective regime (57.4% near 900 ◦ C, 15 bar) to FT pressure-aligned, intermediate-temperature operation in the selective regime (59.5% at 650 ◦ C, 25 bar). The jet-fuel minimum selling price (MSP) is dominated by H 2 price, so the efficiency gains from improved RWGS selectivity translate into a MSP reduction of 3.3%. The relatively modest efficiency gain and cost reduction are augmented by operational advantages of running RWGS at less extreme temperatures, motivating the advancement of PtL systems utilizing selective RWGS as an alternative to conventional configurations.

papers.title: Multivariate Lanthanide Metal-organic Frameworks – Cationic Radius Biased Composition and Framework Structure Consistency
papers.abstract: The synthesis of a multivariate metal-organic framework (MTV-MOF) family, [Ln(DNNDI)1.5]n (UoB-116), is reported. UoB-116(Ln) is formed by 15 different metals (Ln = Y, La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu) all of which were shown to be isoreticular. The uniformity of the framework structure facilitated the synthesis of MTV-MOFs with 2, 4, 12, 15 or 16 (including In(III)) different metals. Single crystal structures of each unimetallic MOFs and MTV-MOFs with 12 or 16 metals were determined, confirming the isoreticular nature of this family of MOFs. Energy Dispersive X-Ray (EDX) analysis confirmed distribution of each metal throughout crystals of the MTV-MOFs and compositional analysis indicated increased concentration of lanthanides with smaller cationic radius. This observation allowed development of a protocol to control relative composition in a bimetallic system (UoB-116(LaxLuy). Subsequent studies demonstrated the introduction of Lu(III) to the surface of UoB-116(La) crystals, confirming the preferential incorporation of this smaller cation in the UoB-116 framework.

papers.title: From Benzene to [3]Radialene: Topological Engineering of Pure Hydrocarbons for Long-Wavelength Aggregation-Induced Emission Luminogens
papers.abstract: Due to the topological divergence between [3]radialene and benzene, hexaphenyl[3]radialene (HPR) exhibits a dramatic bathochromic-shift in emission (619 nm) with a Stokes shift >150 nm, which is distinct from its structural analogue hexaphenylbenzene (HPB). Our mechanism analyses revealed the localized bond rearrangement and moderate short-range charge transfer, which lead to its long-wavelength emission and enhanced aggregation-induced emission (AIE) character. Ring-locked derivatives, tridibenzocycloheptadiene[3]radialene (THR) and tridimethylanthrone[3]radialene (TAR), were synthesized, exhibiting tunable emission wavelength (507–685 nm) and high crystalline-state quantum yields (up to 49.2%). Our results establish the [3]radialene backbone as a robust hydrocarbon scaffold for high-performance, long-wavelength emitters by elucidating topology-dependent excited-state dynamics.

papers.title: Hydration-Gated Photoinduced Electron Transfer in O-BODIPY Dyes
papers.abstract: Fluorescent probes based on photoinduced electron transfer (PET) are widely used to image intracellular microenvironments, yet achieving a selective activation of PET by a single environmental parameter remains a challenge. Here we report donor–acceptor dyads based on the O-BODIPY chromophore in which PET is selectively activated by aqueous hydration rather than by generic solvent polarity. Replacing the fluorine groups at boron with triethylene glycol (TEG) chains confers aqueous solubility and modulates the electronic properties of the boron-coordinated core, suppressing PET in polar organic solvents while enabling efficient charge separation specifically in water. This switching arises from hydrogen bonding at the alkoxy oxygens, which strengthens the effective acceptor character of the BODIPY, as confirmed by electrochemical measurements, transient absorption spectroscopy, and DFT calculations. The mechanism is general across dyads incorporating various donors and can be extended to red-emitting chromophores by substitution of the BODIPY scaffold. The lead compound, 5-TEG, displays hydration-dependent fluorescence lifetimes spanning a 6 ns range. In fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of living cells, tumor spheroids, and intestinal organoids, 5-TEG provides exceptional brightness and spatially resolved lifetime contrast, enabling segmentation of subcellular compartments and reporting on microenvironmental differences. These results establish hydration-gated PET as a tunable photophysical mechanism for designing fluorescence probes with lifetime-encoded readouts in complex biological environments.

papers.title: Computational Prioritization of Chilean Papaya Compounds Against Human α-Glucosidase: A Docking and Rescoring Study
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus remains a major global health challenge, and α-glucosidase inhibition is a relevant strategy for reducing postprandial hyperglycemia. This study presents a reproducible computational pipeline for prioritizing Chilean papaya ( Vasconcellea pubescens ) compounds against the C-terminal subunit of human maltase-glucoamylase (CtMGAM; PDB 3TOP) using AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, native-ligand redocking, ligand-efficiency normalization, ProLIF interaction fingerprinting, expanded Vina/Vinardo rescoring, GNINA/CNN score-only rescoring, and exploratory chemical-space analysis. The integrated workflow combined primary CtMGAM docking, expanded Vina/Vinardo rescoring, and GNINA/CNN rescoring of selected poses. Procyanidin B1 produced the most favorable papaya CtMGAM Vina score (−6.856 kcal/mol; ligand efficiency = −0.1594), followed by kaempferol-3-glucoside (−6.290 kcal/mol) and quercetin-3-glucoside (−6.168 kcal/mol). Native acarbose redocking reproduced two AC1 crystallographic copies in 3TOP with RMSD values of 0.820 Å and 0.819 Å, supporting spatial consistency of the docking setup. Orthogonal rescoring indicated that procyanidin B1 should not be treated as a single dominant candidate: epicatechin, catechin, apigenin, epigallocatechin gallate, quercetin-3-glucoside, and kaempferol-3-glucoside also showed support across orthogonal scoring methods. These results support a hypothesis-generating follow-up panel for targeted α-glucosidase assays. They do not establish inhibitory potency, selectivity, or superiority over acarbose. The main contribution is a transparent workflow for conservative natural-product prioritization.

papers.title: Surface-initiated synthesis of sorbent polymers for waveguide-enhanced Raman spectroscopy-based detection of small molecules in aqueous solutions
papers.abstract: Small molecule detection in aqueous solution is critical to a broad range of applications. Chip-based spectroscopic methods, including Waveguide-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (WERS), are attractive approaches to small molecule detection and quantitation, but their use in aqueous applications is currently immature. Here, we demonstrate a surface-initiated polymerization (SIP) approach to the synthesis of covalently attached sorbent polymers grown from the surface of the WERS chip. Using poly-aminopropyl methacrylamide (P-APMA) as a model sorbent and lactate as a model analyte, we demonstrate that the covalently attached sorbent enhances lactate detection relative to a bare chip in a predictable manner that scales with the thickness of the film. Detection is selective, with no enhancement observed for a positively charged analyte (glycinamide). It is also reversible, suggesting the approach is suitable for long-term monitoring applications.

papers.title: Electrostatic gap fields enable inverse design of peptides controlling biomolecular condensates
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) organize many intracellular processes, yet there exist still open questions regarding the control on protein condensation. Here we introduce the electrostatic gap field (Δφ), a principle connecting electrostatic landscapes to phase behavior. Analogous to the energy gap stabilizing the native state in protein folding theory, Δφ quantifies the difference in charge distributions within the dilute and the condensed phases and defines a bias toward condensation. Using around 5 ms of molecular dynamics simulations of seven intrinsically disordered region (IDR)-containing proteins across diverse interaction environments, we show that independent of the force field and model construction, condensate formation consistently correlates with the emergence of a characteristic Δφ field. Guided by this principle, we design peptides that reproduce the gap field required to stabilize the condensed phase. Opposite-charge analogues perturb the target field. Machine-learning analysis confirms that Δφ encodes a statistically robust signal of condensation. These results establish electrostatic gap fields as a physically interpretable framework for describing, predicting, and engineering the behavior of biomolecular condensates.

papers.title: On the factors influencing electrode poisoning and recovery for isopropanol oxidation on platinum
papers.abstract: The isopropanol-acetone redox couple, consisting of two abundant and inexpensive chemicals, is a potential energy and hydrogen transport/storage vector. The selective electrooxidation of isopropanol (IPA) to acetone has primarily been explored on platinum group metals and their alloys. Given their high cost and relative scarcity, strategies are needed to ensure these catalysts are used efficaciously without sacrificing device performance (e.g., power densities, energy/faradaic efficiencies, and longevity). While 3-electrode experiments provide a means to estimate catalytic activity, metrics obtained from literature-sourced cyclic voltammetry (CV) are concerningly discrepant. To clarify reasons for such a range in observed behavior, we perform CV experiments in quiescent electrolyte and using a rotating disk electrode. We find that small amounts of impurities suppress IPA oxidation, especially under convection. Further, scan rate, convection, electrolyte purity, and IPA concentration individually can substantially influence the reaction rate explaining some of the breadth in the published literature. Because accumulation of impurities and reactive intermediates at the surface over time convolute understanding of CVs, we also perform chronoamperometry (CA) experiments to assess the timescales, extent, and persistence of performance decay. Finally, we show, through modeling and experiments, that potential pulsing offers a way to repeatedly recover catalyst performance and increase average reaction rates. Without a dynamic strategy to continue IPA oxidation, measures of performance from transient means (e.g., CV or CA) are challenging to contextualize.

papers.title: Large-Scale Virtual Screening Prioritizes Candidate Allosteric Modulators of TIMP2: Computational Identification and Structural Characterization of a Cryptic Binding Site
papers.abstract: Background: Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-2 (TIMP2) has emerged as a critical regulator of synaptic plasticity and cognitive function through its role in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Recent evidence suggests that enhancing TIMP2 function, rather than inhibiting it, may offer therapeutic benefits for cognitive enhancement and neuroplasticity. However, TIMP2 has historically been considered "undruggable" due to its protein-protein interaction mechanism and lack of traditional binding pockets. Methods: We performed a large-scale virtual screening campaign using a CNS-filtered subset of the ZINC20 database. Starting from ~1 billion molecules, we applied strict CNS drug-likeness filters (MW: 250-430 Da, TPSA ≤70 Å², HBD ≤1, cLogP: 2.0-3.5), resulting in 13.6 million candidates distributed across 136 chunks. Using AutoDock Vina with an adaptive parallelization strategy, we screened six strategically selected representative chunks totaling ~600,000 molecules against TIMP2 (PDB: 1BR9), targeting both canonical and potential cryptic binding sites. Results: Virtual screening of six completed chunks (~600,000 molecules) identified a cryptic allosteric site involving residues Val6, Leu100, and Phe103 in TIMP2's N-terminal domain. From ~11,500 compounds meeting initial CNS and PAINS criteria, comprehensive ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI v2.1 revealed only 178 compounds (1.5%) achieving Tier 1 safety classification. Orthogonal toxicity validation using ProTox-III further refined this set to 154 highest-confidence candidates (Tier 1A, 86.5%), with 22 compounds (12.4%) requiring enhanced monitoring due to borderline acute toxicity (Tier 1B) and 2 compounds (1.1%) deprioritized due to extreme LD50 predictions (Tier 1C). Chunk-level survival rates varied dramatically from 0.3% (strict_0055) to 9.3% (strict_0028), with strict_0028 yielding the majority (52%) of all Tier 1 compounds. Notably, while halogenation is common (41.6% of Tier 1 compounds), it is not universal, with strict_0028 demonstrating that non-halogenated compounds can also achieve favorable ADMET profiles. The best overall compound (ZINC000870248439_1, -9.0 kcal/mol from strict_0120) and the largest chemical family (93 compounds from strict_0028, including both chlorinated and non-halogenated scaffolds) demonstrated excellent CNS penetration (BBB >0.9) and clean safety profiles. Conclusions: This work represents the first systematic computational prioritization of candidate small-molecule TIMP2 modulators and reveals a previously uncharacterized cryptic binding site that accommodates diverse chemical scaffolds. Integration of ADMET-AI and ProTox-III predictions enabled refined risk stratification, yielding 154 highest-confidence candidates validated across orthogonal computational toxicology platforms. The dramatic variation in ADMET survival rates across chunks (0.3-9.3%) highlights the importance of broad chemical space sampling. While halogenation enhances certain drug-like properties, our results demonstrate that both halogenated and non-halogenated compounds can achieve the demanding intersection of high affinity, CNS penetration, and drug safety. Structural validation using the AlphaFold v6 predicted structure confirmed the cryptic allosteric pocket with sub-angstrom accuracy (mean Cα deviation = 0.30 Å, triad pLDDT > 96), and cross-species conservation analysis revealed 100% pocket identity in mouse TIMP2, the primary translational model. Molecular dynamics simulation (100 ns apo) confirmed pocket stability under physiological conditions with 94% area preservation, sub-angstrom per-residue fluctuations (triad RMSF = 0.84 Å), and convergence of triad distances to within 0.14-0.43 Å of crystallographic values. Ligand-bound MD of seven representative compounds revealed compound-specific binding behavior ranging from complete dissociation (<7 ns) to persistent pocket occupancy over 100 ns. Two structurally distinct benzamide compounds maintained >96% heavy-atom contact over 100 ns: ZINC000583127796 (304 Da, thiirane constraint, 98.7% contact, Phe103-anchored binding with pocket opening to 36.4 Å²) and ZINC001228612316 (268 Da, cyclopropane constraint, 96.7% contact, balanced triad engagement with crystal-geometry preservation at 31.2 Å²). Structure-activity analysis across all seven compounds identified a pharmacophore comprising a benzamide + aromatic ring + 3-membered ring constraint, in which ring strain at the piperidine junction—rather than specific heteroatom chemistry—determines binding persistence. These results demonstrate that the cryptic pocket supports stable small-molecule binding through multiple binding modes and establish a defined pharmacophore for experimental optimization. These findings support TIMP2 as a potentially tractable drug target and provide 154 computationally validated chemical starting points across diverse scaffolds for experimental follow-up.

papers.title: Depletion and Scale Degeneracy in Molecular Binding
papers.abstract: For a century, the significance of target depletion in finite-capacity binding has been systematically underestimated. The assumption that free and total target are interchangeable—reasonable under weak depletion—collapses catastrophically when depletion is strong. No existing theory describes binding across the full spectrum from zero to complete depletion. Here we present the Target–Capture Scaling (TCS) framework, a first-principles theory governed by two dimensionless numbers: ξ (the thermodynamic driving force) and κ (the depletion coefficient). TCS reveals a fundamental physical law—scale degeneracy—which states that absolute target, capture, and dissociation constant cannot be uniquely determined from a single equilibrium measurement. This law is broken only in the strong-depletion limit (κ→0), precisely where digital PCR operates, setting κ≤0.11 as the universal condition for absolute quantification. By restoring the long-neglected depletion term , TCS unifies the core equations of environmental adsorption, pharmacology, and enzyme kinetics, providing new predictions for each. TCS establishes an updated universal physical foundation for affinity binding across all disciplines.

papers.title: Hammett-driven secondary ligand effects control geometry and electronic structure of 5-substituted copper (II) cytosine complexes
papers.abstract: Metal-nucleobase interactions play central roles in biological chemistry and metal-based therapeutic design, yet the influence of nucleobase substitution on coordination geometry and thermodynamic stability remains underexplored. Herein, we report the systematic investigation of copper(II) complexes of 5-substituted cytosine ligands, specifically [Cu(XCyt)4](OTf)2 where X = H, F,Cl, or I designed to isolate the effect of a C5 halogen substitution on ligand-metal interactions. Characterization of these complexes was accomplished via solution-state UV-Vis, Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, 1H NMR spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction spectroscopy. Structural characterization by single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that C5 substitution has minimal impact on Cu···N bond distances, but induces pronounced, substituent-dependent changes in coordination geometry. Specifically, increasing substituent σpara Hammett constants generate stronger Cu···O interactions and a concomitant increase in the distortion of the CuN4 coordination environment. These structural perturbations correlate with systematic changes in electronic structure, as evidenced by linear shifts in UV-visible absorption and corresponding trends in paramagnetic relaxation behavior measured by 1H NMR spectroscopy. Collectively, these results demonstrate that distal substitution at the C5 position modulates metal-centered properties primarily through secondary-sphere interactions, rather than direct perturbation of metal-ligand bonding, which in turn drives linear perturbations of UV-Vis absorbance spectra and paramagnetic relaxation properties.

papers.title: Rational Design of Heteronuclear Dual-Atom Catalysts for Enhanced CO2 to Formate Conversion
papers.abstract: The development of efficient catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation is essential for sustainable hydrogen storage and carbon utilization. Herein, heteronuclear dual-atom catalysts (HDACs) were rationally designed on adenine-derived nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) supports with a high surface area of 3338 m2 g-1 and nitrogen content of 8.32 wt. %. Ruthenium was combined with transition metals (Fe, Co, and Ni) to investigate synergistic effects on catalytic performance. HRTEM-STEM and XPS analyses confirmed atomically dispersed metal species predominantly in the +3 oxidation state. Catalytic evaluation demonstrated that transition metal incorporation significantly enhanced CO2 hydrogenation to formate. Among the catalysts, RuFe/NC (1:2) exhibited the highest activity, achieving a specific activity of 268 mmolFA gcat-1 within 2 h, compared with 107 mmolFA gcat-1 for monometallic Ru. Enhanced performance was attributed to electronic interactions and dual-site catalytic effects that promote CO2 activation and intermediate stabilization. The catalysts also showed excellent stability over five reaction cycles.

papers.title: Hierarchical Dimensionality Escalation of Ionic Diffusion in Superionic Copper Iodide
papers.abstract: Superionic conductors are defined by the dynamical decoupling of sublattices, enabling liquid-like transport within a rigid solid framework. This state is fundamentally governed by the thermodynamic competition between ionic migration enthalpy and configurational entropy. In prototypical systems like copper iodide (CuI), superionicity emerges through a sequence of structural transitions that reshape the local potential energy landscape. While macroscopic transport is well-characterized, the microscopic topological evolution through which ions surmount coordination constraints to establish long-range connectivity remains elusive. Specifically, the evolution of diffusion topology across phase transitions and the role of lattice distortion in regulating migration barriers and transport dimensionality remain unresolved. Here we show, via machine learning-driven molecular dynamics, that the superionic transition in CuI manifests as a hierarchical dimensionality evolution, progressing from localized vibration to 1D, 2D, and ultimately 3D diffusion. This transition is driven by the softening of transverse acoustic phonons, which induces lattice reconstruction and establishes a triangulargate regulation mechanism that continuously reshapes the migration energy landscape through direction-selective geometric confinement. These findings provide a rigorous statistical physics framework for understanding partial melting and phase-transition kinetics, and for the rational design of high-performance solid electrolytes and semiconductors.

papers.title: Broadening the view of aryl diazonium ion reactivity with proteins and DNA
papers.abstract: Aryl diazonium ions (ADIs) are well established for their reaction with both proteins and DNA, and yet these reactions have been studied independently without systematic comparison. When electrophilic bioconjugation probes are introduced to environments containing multiple macromolecules, questions of selectivity and competitive reactivity become critical. Here, we establish a systematic method to evaluate the selectivity of a series of ADIs toward proteins, specifically tyrosine and histidine residues, across varying pH and solvent conditions, while also looking at the ADI reaction with DNA. Electron-deficient ADIs preferentially modified tyrosine over histidine, but all tested ADIs reacted with and degraded DNA. We also observed strong pH- and hydrophobicity-dependent effects on amino acid selectivity. These findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling ADI reactivity in complex biological environments, informing the design of selective bioconjugation strategies.

papers.title: Computing Optimal Programs for Programmable Catalysts using Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Programmable catalysts offer control flexibility to maximize performance by dynamically tuning the free energies of surface species. The performance of programmable catalysts is directly tied to the dynamic control program (protocol) used to modify surface reaction behavior through temperature, light, or electrical inputs. Due to the inherent complexity of such control programs and the limited understanding of their impact on individual reaction steps, identifying optimal settings remains challenging. In this work, we propose a computational framework for tuning complex control programs. Control programs are constructed by mixing ”basis” programs which enables the generation of complex protocols while keeping the number of tuning parameters low. Optimal programs are identified using Bayesian optimization; this approach builds a surrogate machine learning model to predict system performance as a function of the tuning parameters. Our framework also exploits the inherently periodic nature of control programs to accelerate system simulations and can be applied in a black-box manner (tied to a kinetic model or an actual experimental set-up). We apply this framework to explore the performance limits of reaction networks with different topologies. The results demonstrate that the framework can efficiently identify optimal programs and provide insights into the limiting behavior achievable through programmable catalysis and the factors that drive such behavior. When exploring the effects of combining additional basis functions for more complex programs, we find evidence that more complex programs can be beneficial in certain types of catalysts.

papers.title: Harnessing Bridge Resonance to Optimise Multiexciton Dynamics through Intramolecular Singlet Fission in Pentacene Dimers
papers.abstract: The central question in the study of singlet fission remains how to control the interchromophore couplings that govern the formation, spin evolution and decay of triplet pairs through molecular design. In intramolecular singlet fission materials, this control is achieved by tethering chromophores with a range of bridging units. These small bridges typically serve as inert structural scaffolds or provide pathways for conjugation between chromophores but usually are not directly involved in the fission pathway due to large orbital offsets. Here, we explore control of iSF rates by using a resonant bridge, in which the linker’s frontier orbitals are more closely aligned with those of the chromophore subunits. Through careful spectroscopic and computational comparison between analogous pentacene dimers bridged by strongly electron-withdrawing benzothiadiazole or passive phenyl bridges, we decouple the electronic contributions of bridge resonance from standard geometric and conjugative effects. Our investigations reveal that the benzothiadiazole moiety reconfigures the singlet potential energy surface of the covalently linked dimer, introducing significant orbital hybridisation between pentacenes and the bridge. This hybridisation can lead to new parasitic decay channels, but when the coupling is optimised it results in more rapid triplet-pair formation and suppressed triplet-pair decay in a manner that is remarkably robust against changes to the dielectric environment. Our findings thus demonstrate that resonant bridges rather than passive linkers is a powerful strategy for optimising multiexciton generation and utilisation in pi-conjugated chromophores.

papers.title: From Cannabinol (CBN) to Cannabiphenanthrene (CNP): A photochemical cascade reaction. A steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic investigation.
papers.abstract: The photochemical conversion of phytocannabinoids Cannabinol (CBN) into phenanthrene CNP was investigated in detail via a combined steady state/time resolved approach. The elucidated mechanism describes a two-photon cascade reaction where CBN is initially converted to cannabidinol (CBDN) via a C-O photoinduced cleavage, which in turn undergoes to 6π electron cyclization of the cannabinoid intermediate.

papers.title: Role of Alcohol Solvents in Glucose Isomerization and Etherification in Modulated UiO-66
papers.abstract: Solvent choice significantly affects the rates of glucose isomerization and the selectivity to form fructose. Methanol and 1-propanol were examined and assessed herein as solvents for the isomerization of glucose to fructose catalyzed by modulated UiO-66(Zr). Reactions carried out in 1-propanol favor the isomerization of glucose to fructose, whereas reactions in methanol favor side reactions where glucose reacts with methanol via etherification to form glucosides which lower 2 the selectivity to fructose. The fructose that forms subsequently reacts with both the propanol and the methanol solvents to form fructosides. Density functional theory quantum chemical calculations were carried out to examine the key steps of these reactions and explore the important role of the solvation media in affecting fructose selectivity. The higher hydrogen bonding acidity (which correlates with the propensity of donating a hydrogen for hydrogen bond formation) provided by the methanol solvation environment as compared to 1-propanol stabilizes transition states involving the attack of the alkoxide group on glucose in the etherification pathway. The methanol solvent molecules form a more intimate hydrogen bonding network thus stabilizing anionic intermediates that form during reaction and as such is a more acidic solvent than propanol. The higher acidity of methanol enhances base-catalyzed etherification reactivity over that of Lewis acid-catalyzed isomerization. Further evidence of the effect of solvation is provided experimentally by conducting reactions in mixtures of these alcohol solvents, which show that methanol-rich solvation environments favor glucose etherification (over isomerization) in contrast to 1-propanol-rich solvation environments which favor isomerization.

papers.title: Asymmetric Hydration Shell Reveals Interfacial TFSI Organization in Imidazolium Ionic Liquid Films
papers.abstract: Understanding how ionic liquids (ILs) organize and restructure solvent at aqueous interfaces is critical for developing molecular-level descriptions of ion transport and selectivity in separation systems. Here, we investigate interfacial organization of imidazolium based [BMIM], [HMIM], and [OMIM][TFSI] ILs at the air/aqueous interface using sum frequency generation (SFG) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Simultaneous measurements across the CH, OH, SO, and CF vibrational regions directly probe water and both cation and anion ordering. Increasing IL concentration suppresses the dangling free-OH peak while leading to a distinct 3600 cm ‑1 band. Subensemble analysis of MD simulations identifies this band as the asymmetric hydration shell of TFSI. This provides a unique opportunity to observe TFSI organization through both its direct vibrational signatures and its hydration shell. Global Frumkin isotherm analysis of all vibrational reporters yields systematic trends in adsorption free energy (−13 to −16 kJ/mol) and confirms attractive lateral interactions that strengthen with cation chain length. These results demonstrate that outer-sphere interactions and collective ion organization play central roles in interfacial IL film organization.

papers.title: Unified Mesoscale Framework Bridging Equilibrium Thermodynamics and Transport Properties of Ionic Liquids and Their Mixtures
papers.abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) have emerged as sustainable alternatives to molecular solvents due to their unique physicochemical properties. Although quantum chemical simulations provide fundamental insights into their intermolecular interactions, conventional all-atom and coarse-grained frameworks can hardly predict equilibrium thermodynamics and transport properties at the same time. This simulation challenge comes primarily from the high viscosity and low diffusivity of ILs due to strong ion-pairing, resulting in Schmidt numbers (Sc) that span multiple orders of magnitude. In this work, we present a unified mesoscale simulation framework that preserves thermodynamic consistency while quantitatively reproducing the transport properties of pure ILs and their mixtures. This framework integrates a bottom-up approach and an extended dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) formulation: equilibrium thermodynamics are derived from COSMO-RS analysis and fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations while DPD resolves coarse-grained dissipative forces into parallel and perpendicular components. A important contribution from this study is a novel algorithm grounded in micromechanical theory that systematically determines friction coefficients and cutoff radii. By incorporating the pair correlation function of the equilibrium structure, the algorithm establishes a functional dependency for the simulated viscosity and diffusivity and ensures they match experimental values across varying solvent compositions. We validate this framework using an imidazolium-based IL system, which demonstrates quantitative agreement with experimental transport properties and captures negative viscosity deviations from ideal mixing. Our framework bridges molecular chemistry and macroscopic rheology and will facilitate the screening, design, and implementation of IL-based processes for energy and separation systems.

papers.title: Coupled Molecular and Framework Descriptors for Band-Edge Spin Splitting in Chiral Hybrid Organic–Inorganic Perovskites
papers.abstract: Chiral hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites offer a chemically tunable platform in which inversion-asymmetric crystal fields and strong spin–orbit coupling generate spin-split band edges, yet the mechanisms through which the chiral molecules and the inorganic framework interact to produce spin splitting are not well understood. Here we use the electronic chirality measure—a wave-function-based metric—to quantify molecular chirality across three substitution series of chiral metal halides derived from methylbenzylammonium ligands. We find that halogen functionalization increases the valenceband spin splitting from 6.6 meV in the parent system to 64.8 meV in the benzylic-halogenated (S-MBA)X series and up to 110.0 meV in the side-chain-halogenated (S-MBA)CH2X series (X = H, F, Cl, Br). In contrast, for the pnictogen-substituted (S-MBA)Y series (Y = P, As, Sb, Bi), the splitting remains in the few-meV regime. The electronic chirality measure captures changes in the chiral electronic structure and provides a useful molecular descriptor for comparison with parityviolating energy differences, but it does not alone determine the band-edge splitting. The largest splittings emerge when electronic chirality, intrinsic cation dipoles, and inorganicframework distortion act cooperatively. Within each series, larger intrinsic cation dipoles are associated with smaller spin splitting energies. Large band-edge splitting occurs only when molecular chirality is efficiently converted into the induced chiral Pb/I framework mode, as parametrized by chirality transfer efficiency (CTE), and combined with a favorable cation electrostatic environment.

papers.title: Phase Transition in Crystalline Material Under Generation of Goldstone Modes
papers.abstract: Thermal fluctuations in Crystalline materials induce phase transitions where the symmetric energy landscape of a given state undergoes a transition to one of the final degenerate states with spontaneous symmetry breaking. A key characteristic of such a system is generation of low energy modes called Goldstone modes. In materials like pharmaceutical drug molecules, the onset of sudden polymorphic phase transition under certain conditions is not well understood. Here, we explore such phenomena from the perspective of an order parameter, while arguing that energy exchange in such systems generates Goldstone as well as massive Higgs like modes, which can reduce entropy during phase transitions. We specifically consider the role of conservative force fields and their interplay with thermal fluctuations defined by Langevin equation. The results imply that crystalline polymorphic transitions can be controlled by shielding crystals from thermal fluctuations through specific pattern of conservative force fields. It offers a novel pathway towards creating drug packaging technologies governed by electromagnetic force configurations. Key Words: Key Words: Ostwald’s rule, Polymorphism, Broken Symmetry, Phase Transition

papers.title: Length-Dependent Assembly and Chiral Emergence of Precise Donor-Acceptor Conjugated Oligomers
papers.abstract: Precise control over molecular length is essential for understanding how conjugated materials develop supramolecular chirality, liquid-crystalline order, and electronic function. Here, we synthesize a monodisperse series of pyridine-flanked diketopyrrolopyrrole-bithiophene (PyDPP-2T) oligomers (Monomer, Dimer, Trimer, Pentamer, and Heptamer) using a modular Stille/direct arylation polymerization (DArP) strategy. A sharp transition emerges between Trimer and Pentamer, beyond which chiral liquid-crystalline phases form in absence of molecular chirality. Pentamer, Heptamer, and Polymer exhibit distinct length-dependent chiral mesophases (helicoidal smectic, cholesteric, and nematic twist-bend) where positional order gives way to increasingly complex orientational order as the molecular contour length exceeds the persistence length. Electrical measurements show a monotonic increase in conductivity with backbone length, and Heptamer achieves polymer-level performance despite its discrete structure. These findings identify molecular length as a programmable design variable for engineering hierarchical order and function in π-conjugated materials.

papers.title: Integrated DFT, mean-field and experimental study of Cr-substituted Co–Zn spinel ferrite nanoparticles for magnetic hyperthermia
papers.abstract: Magnetic-hyperthermia therapy requires nanoparticles whose Curie temperature, coercivity and saturation magnetisation are tunable while remaining biocompatible in physiological media. Cr-substituted Co-Zn ferrite nanoparticles (Co0.6Zn0.4CrxFe2−xO4, x = 0,0.1,0.2,0.3) were synthesised by autocombustion and calcined at 500 ◦C for 2 h, yielding a pure cubic spinel phase confirmed by X-ray diffraction. Lattice constant and crystallite size decreased monotonically from 8.4039 Å and 34 nm to 8.3947 Å and 25 nm, consistent with the smaller ionic radius of Cr3+ relative to Fe3+. Saturation magnetisation, coercivity and effective anisotropy declined systematically with Cr content, driven by Fe3+ →Cr3+ replacement at the octahedral B-sites. DFT+U calculations placed Cr3+ at the B-site in a high-spin d3 configuration; Wannier90/TB2J Heisenberg exchanges (JBB : −3.82 → −2.90 meV; JAB : −3.00 →−2.40 meV) fed into a Néel two-sublattice mean-field theory reproduced the decrease of TC (996 → 736 K) and Ms(300K) (3.07 → 2.30 µB/f.u.; VSM: 2.49 → 1.53 µB/f.u.). Absolute TC is routinely overestimated by mean-field theory, so the comparison is made on the trend only. Induction heating (14.92 kA m−1, 337 kHz) reduced SAR and ILP correspondingly; the x = 0.3 sample at 0.5mg/mL attained 46.47 ◦C in 600s, confining heating to the therapeutic 42–47◦C window. In vitro hemolysis remained below 4% and MTT viability on human peripheral blood mononuclear cells exceeded 90% for x = 0.2 and x = 0.3. These findings establish Cr-substituted Co-Zn ferrite nanoparticles as biocompatible candidates for safe magnetic hyperthermia; the integrated DFT→MFT→experiment workflow is demonstrated for this system and is extensible to other AB2O4 substituted spinels.

papers.title: The Nanoscale Impact of Cyclopropane Fatty Acids and Hopanoids on Alcohol Tolerance in Clostridium acetobutylicum and Zymomonas mobilis
papers.abstract: Butanol and isobutanol are promising biofuel candidates produced natively by Clostridium acetobutylicum and Zymomonas mobilis. However, alcohol accumulation during fermentation disrupts membrane integrity and limits yields, increasing costs for industrial fermentation. These microbes have cyclopropane fatty acids (CFAs) and hopanoids in their native membranes in different ratios, which may contribute to observed alcohol tolerance differences in these organisms. To track the nanoscale origins of these alcohol phenotypes, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the effects of CFAs on membrane structure and dynamics in both species under butanol and isobutanol stress at concentrations up to 2.5 mol%. We simulate C. acetobutylicum membranes with varying CFA content and Z. mobilis membranes with varying CFA levels both with and without hopanoids. Key membrane properties including area per lipid, thickness, lipid order parameter, and lateral diffusion coefficient were analyzed across all conditions. In C. acetobutylicum, CFAs confer substantial protection against alcohol-induced perturbations. At high CFA content, changes in membrane properties remain minimal even at the highest alcohol concentrations. This protective effect is attributed to cyclopropane rings present in both acyl chains, which restrict conformational freedom in the membrane core. In contrast, Z. mobilis CFAs, which carry cyclopropane rings in only one tail, fail to stabilize the membrane on their own but produce a synergistic stabilization when paired with hopanoids, reducing alcohol permeability. These results establish that dual-ring CFAs provide significantly greater independent membrane stabilization than single-ring variants. We anticipate that future engineering efforts to produce robust biofuel-producing strains should thus prioritize dual-ring CFA pathways alongside increased active efflux to mitigate residual passive permeation.

papers.title: Mechanism and Reactivity Drivers of the Intramolecular Dearomative Didehydro-Diels–Alder Reaction
papers.abstract: Ring-fused heteroarenes are essential building blocks found in a wide range of compounds, including pharmaceuticals, natural products, and organic materials. While the intramolecular dearomative didehydro-Diels–Alder (IMDDDA) reaction of heteroarenes is a powerful method for synthesis of ring-fused heteroarenes, reaction outcome is highly sensitive to the precursor heteroarenes, tether, and alkyne. Using a combination of experimental reaction kinetics, DFT calculations, and data science tools, we transformed this complex challenge into a clear understanding of precursor reactivity. Our analysis revealed a comprehensive reactivity picture by examining key steric and electronic factors of the precursor, including aromaticity, diene conformation, and HOMO-LUMO gap energies. We developed a two-variable multivariate linear regression model using forward stepwise selection, which highlights the critical role of vibrational frequencies and heteroarene type in predicting these complex reactivity trends.

papers.title: Expanding the Scope of Mechanochromic Luminescence Through Mechanical Atropisomerization in Biaxial Atropisomer Molecular Solids
papers.abstract: Mechanoresponsive luminescent (MCL) materials hold promise for applications such as force sensing and lithography. This paper reports solid-state mechanical atropisomerization of biaxial atropisomers as a mechanism that enables mechanically activated photofluorochromic responses in molecular solids. A library of biaxial atropisomer small molecules are designed to undergo selective atropisomerization under mechanical stimulation and convert to their chemically inequivalent diastereomers. Mechanical activation converts a photoinactive solid of the parallel diarylethene atropisomer into an amorphous containing the photoswitchable antiparallel isomer, which subsequently undergo photocyclization under UV irradiation to exhibit photofluorochromism. Because this mechanical atropisomerization generates a distinct and thermally stable chemical species rather than a transient emissive state arising from lattice rearrangement or reversible bond scission, the resulting photofluorochromic response persists even after loss of the mechanically encoded supramolecular organization and is not erased by thermal reversion, distinguishing these mechanoactive biaxial atropisomers from conventional MCL solids. This persistence also enables a simple materials design strategy in which physical doping of small-molecule diarylethene atropisomers renders polymers mechanoresponsive, bypassing both covalent polymer modification required in conventional polymer mechanochemistry and the molecular-packing dependence of typical MCL solids. Importantly, solid-state mechanical atropisomerization was validated as a general mechanism within the tested subgroup of structurally diverse biaxial atropisomers and could guide the development of next-generation mechanoresponsive luminescent materials.

papers.title: Phosphaza-bicyclo[2.2.2]octane based diols as monomers for hybrid materials
papers.abstract: Most synthetic polymers are constructed from linear or monocyclic building blocks; the controlled use of bicyclic, three-dimensional organic monomers remains synthetically challenging. In contrast, incorporating unstrained inorganic cages like polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (POSS) and carboranes into polymer backbones is facile, and has been used to make materials with exceptional stability and mechanical properties. But inorganic cages besides these two are minimally explored in polymer chemistry. In this study, a phosphorus-nitrogen (PN) cage was converted via Staudinger reactions with azido alcohols to cage-containing aromatic (PNBP) and aliphatic (PNBH) diols, making monomers analogous to organic diols commonly used in polycondensation. Crystallographic analysis reveals how functional-group identity and conformational freedom influence intermolecular association and solubility. Attempted addition of these diols to diisocyanates does not yield polyurethanes, showing evidence of side-reactions involving an Aza-Wittig pathway instead. On the other hand, polycondensation with Me2SiCl2 yields PN–siloxane polymers featuring cages embedded directly within the main chain. The aromatic PN-siloxane polymer exhibits high rigidity, crystallinity, elevated melting and crystallization temperatures, and enhanced thermal robustness. Its aliphatic analogue exhibits high solubility, flexibility, and a low glass-transition temperature. Thermal and preliminary flame-retardant analyses demonstrate synergistic stabilization from phosphorus, nitrogen, and silicon. These results establish PN-based diols as versatile building blocks for cage-dense hybrid polymers and a platform for next-generation high-performance materials.

papers.title: Controlled Self-assembly of meso-Functionalized ABBA Zinc(II) Tetrabenzotriazaporphyrins into Supramolecular Systems
papers.abstract: Overcoming the preferred H-aggregation in phthalocyanine (Pc)-like molecules and formation of controlled, well-defined 3D-structures remains a challenging task that is necessary in order to fully realise their potential applications. In this work, we exploit complementary functionalization at the benzo (A or B) and meso (Ar) positions of tetrabenzotriazaporphyrins (Ar-ABBA TBTAPs). Key design features are the high-hindrance “B” fragments (distant from meso aryl), low-hindrance “A” fragments (adjacent to meso aryl), central zinc(II) cation and the coordinating meso- pyridyl groups aligned perpendicular to the macrocycle core, and with the nitrogen located at different positions to drive the assembly geometry. Through this approach, 3D architectures of slipped J-dimer, stair-like structure or box-like tetramer were formed and confirmed by X-ray crystallography on single crystals. These 3D structures persist in solution with dimerization constants ranging between K D ~ 10 5 – 10 8 M -1 , depending on the nitrogen position. The photophysical parameters (fluorescence and singlet oxygen quantum yield) of the supramolecular systems remained the same as those of monomers. These findings, together with straightforward synthetic availability of low-symmetrical ABBA-type TBTAPs derivatives, confirmed these molecules as a new platform for tunable 3D assemblies, with promising use for supramolecular applications.

papers.title: Glycosylated Diarylmethyloxy-Triazines: Facile Synthesis and Aqueous Self-Assembly for Supramolecular Hydrogel Formation
papers.abstract: Glycosylated self-assembling molecules enable the construction ofnanostructures whose surfaces are decorated with saccharides under aqueous conditions, reminiscent ofbiological systems at both the molecular and cellular levels. Such glyco-nanostructures thus hold great promise as soft materials for biological applications. Herein, we report the facile synthesis ofglycosylated diarylmethyloxy-triazines, which serve as new building blocks for fabricating self-assembled nanostructures in aqueous media and forming supramolecular hydrogels. The triazine scaffold enables the protecting-group-free synthesis ofglycosylated compounds with reasonable β-anomer selectivity. Notably, both the substituents on the aryl groups attached to the triazine core and the geometry of the glycosidic linkages in the disaccharides strongly influence the hydrogelation behavior and morphology ofthe self-assembled nanostructures.

papers.title: Towards High-Throughput Testing of Bipolar Plate Materials for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers: Correlative Contact Resistance and Stability Analysis
papers.abstract: Bipolar plates (BPP) are a major cost driver in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers for green hydrogen production that require replacement with more cost-effective materials. However, novel materials must combine high corrosion resistance and low dissolution rates with low interfacial contact resistance (ICR). Herein, we introduce a correlative workflow for determining electrochemical dissolution using a scanning flow cell coupled on-line to inductively coupled plasma spectrometer and ICR at the identical location utilizing a novel miniaturized ICR setup with a sample diameter of 2 mm. The applicability of the setup is demonstrated using titanium (Ti), for which the ICR is found to increase depending on the applied oxidation potential. Furthermore, automated ICR mapping across pristine Ti sheets with a platinum (Pt) coating featuring a thickness gradient reveal a pronounced ICR decrease when the Pt layer exceeds ~3.8 ± 1.4 nm Pt , while thicker Pt coatings (up to ~80 nm Pt ) do not provide further improvement. These results demonstrate that ultrathin Pt coatings can already substantially reduce the ICR of titanium-based BPP materials. Our setup enables high-throughput screening of material libraries and provides a powerful tool for developing optimized PEMWE components with low ICR and high electrochemical stability.

papers.title: NMR relaxation dispersion reveals an order of magnitude range of acid loop motions in protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B
papers.abstract: Motion of the active site acid loop is critical for the proper function of the enzyme, protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B). To investigate the motion of this loop we incorporated 7fluorotryptophan at residue 179 (7F-Trp) near the hinge of the acid loop – replacing the naturally occurring tryptophan at this position. Control experiments show identical kcat and Km values for for WT and 7F-Trp enzymes and 15N HSQC experiments show minimal chemical shift changes caused by the incorporation of fluorotryptophan into this enzyme. We then investigated the conformational motions of the acid loop by multifield 19F Carr-Purcell-Meiboom-Gill (CPMG) relaxation dispersion and R1ρ experiments.
