These experiments demonstrate that Trp179 has an exchange rate constant (kex) of 16,000 s–1 in the apo enzyme. This value contrasts with kex values for the amide backbone positions on the acid loop of 900 s–1 and sidechain methyl motions for V184 that occur with kex = 1800 s–1. These experiments demonstrate that the motion of the acid loop in PTP1B occurs on a rugged energy landscape governed by multiple processes. Furthermore, this work highlights the additional dynamical insight gained through the use of different spin-1/2 nuclei as motional probes.

papers.title: Experimental and Computational Analysis of Perovskite–Hole-Transport-Layer Interfaces: a Case Study in Carbazole-based Hole Transport Molecules
papers.abstract: Designing hole-transport molecules (HTMs) having strong interactions with the surface of organic lead halide perovskite is one route to enhancing the efficiency of this photovoltaic technology, although a lack of experimental methodologies for quantifying such interactions impedes progress in this direction. Here, using a series of structurally resolved carbazole-based HTMs with various functional groups differing in polarity/ionicity, we developed an analytical framework based on complementary spectroscopies to quantify the adsorption interactions between these HTMs and the perovskite surface. We demonstrated that increasing the polarity/cationicity of the functional group (i.e. –NH 2 /–NH 3 + ) appended to the HTM increased the amount adsorbed onto the perovskite surface, which is attributed to stronger HTM–perovskite interactions. Computational simulations by density functional theory not only yielded adsorption free energies consistent with these experimental results, but also revealed the intermolecular bonds formed between the polar/cationic moieties and the perovskite surface that conferred strong adsorptive interactions, which appear to benefit open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current in preliminary evaluations of solar cells fabricated with these carbazole-based HTMs. These results demonstrate that judicious functionalization for strong HTM-perovskite interactions, quantifiable by the analytical approach presented herein, could be a promising route towards enhancing the performance of perovskite solar cells.

papers.title: Electrochemical Alkyne Semihydrogenation and Carbonyl Reduction with a Bifunctional Cu Complex
papers.abstract: A (tBu,TolDHP)Cu complex is reported as an electrocatalyst for alkyne semihydrogenation and carbonyl reduction. Mechanistic investigations reveal the catalyst proceeds through intermediates where the storage of H2 across the ligand backbone enables substrate activation and reduction. This is the first reported homogeneous Cu catalyst for electrocatalytic semihydrogenation and carbonyl reduction.

papers.title: Element Interaction Manifolds for Systematic Analysis of Geometric Representations in Protein–Ligand Recognition
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of protein–ligand interactions requires representations that capture both molecular geometry and chemically specific interactions. Existing approaches encode molecular recognition through several geometric formalisms, including differential geometry and spherical harmonic surface descriptors such as three-dimensional Zernike descriptors (3DZD). However, the relative roles of local curvature, surface area, volume, global shape, and chemical partitioning in protein–ligand recognition remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we present a unified geometric study centered on the Element Interaction Manifold (EIM) framework. We integrate element-interactive curvature, surface-area, and volume descriptors into a common representation and systematically evaluate their roles in binding affinity prediction and ligand-aware binding-site similarity. To place differential geometry in context, we compare EIM against global 3DZD and a newly developed chemically partitioned extension termed element-pair 3DZD (EP-3DZD). Across PDBbind/CASF-2016 affinity prediction and unsupervised ligand-identity recognition tasks, chemically resolved local differential geometry consistently provides the strongest predictive performance and the best accuracy–complexity trade-off. Combining EIM with spherical harmonic descriptors yields only marginal improvements, suggesting limited complementarity between local interaction geometry and global shape representations. Overall, these results suggest that chemically resolved local differential geometry provides a compact, interpretable, and transferable foundation for protein–ligand recognition.

papers.title: Sisyphus: A Topology-Compiled Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Platform with Structure-Only Input and Bayesian Parameter Refinement
papers.abstract: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) platforms have achieved regulatory acceptance for drugdrug interaction and pediatric dose optimization, yet the dominant implementations require experimentally measured absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) parameters as input, limiting their utility in early drug discovery when only molecular structure is available. Machine learning approaches that predict pharmacokinetic endpoints directly from structure address this constraint but lack mechanistic interpretability and cannot extrapolate to untested scenarios such as drug–drug interactions or alternative dosing regimens. Sisyphus, an open-source PBPK platform that represents the human body as a typed directed multigraph, automatically compiles ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems from graph topology, and accepts a simplified molecular-input line-entry system (SMILES) string as the sole molecular input, is presented here. Five quantitative structure–activity relationship models predict ADME parameters from molecular structure; these are propagated through a whole-body PBPK model with native Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification, and a four-track meta-learner dynamically weights mechanistic-engine, direct machine-learning, clearance-regression, and volume-ofdistribution-based predictions on a per-compound basis. On a held-out set of 107 drugs (healthy volunteers, single oral dose, immediate-release, fasted state), the platform achieved a population-level geometric mean absolute fold error (AAFE) of 2.698 for maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), with 46.7% of predictions within 2-fold of observed values (bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] [2.32, 3.17]; in-domain subset AAFE 2.760 [2.30, 3.34], N = 79, excluding applicability-domain-flagged compounds). All reported benchmarks were generated from a fresh clone of the public repository with no proprietary or environment-specific data artifacts loaded, so the reported accuracy is structure-only and independently reproducible. Forty-one enumerated optimization attemptsspanning alternative molecular representations, training-data expansion, in vitro–in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) chain bypass, bond-dissociation-energy reactivity features, residual-correction models, post-hoc meta-learners, and orthogonal prediction sources—failed to improve downstream accuracy, while two strategies improved it and are retained in the pipeline. These results indicate that the accuracy ceiling originates from intrinsic clearance prediction quality (coefficient of determination R2 ≈ 0.24 on the Therapeutics Data Commons Hepatocyte_AZ dataset under scaffold-split cross-validation) rather than from model architecture or data scale. Substituting experimentally measured ADME parameters for predicted values in a 10-compound subset produced a modest, mixed improvement in engine AAFE (2.81 to 2.69; 6 of 10 compounds improved), indicating that ADME input quality is one contributor to prediction error rather than establishing that the engine is fully input-limited. The platform additionally supports multi-dose regimen simulation, Bayesian posterior parameter refinement that reduced prediction uncertainty by an average of 78% from a single observation across five compounds, drug–drug interaction prediction, and pharmacodynamic modeling. Prospective validation on 28 small-molecule new molecular entities (NMEs) approved in 2024–2025 yielded AAFE 3.21 (N = 28; in-domain 3.20, N = 16), modestly worse than the retrospective holdout; the gap was localized to systematic under-prediction of oral bioavailability for novel chemotypes rather than to clearance. Sisyphus addresses a capability not met by existing tools: a single platform spanning structure-only screening through observation-informed parameter refinement, in which mechanistic parameters retain physical meaning throughout the pipeline.

papers.title: Autonomous Discovery of Multi-Step Reaction Networks for Fe2O3 Reduction: Step-wise Kinetics and Reaction Model Identification from Isothermal TGA Data
papers.abstract: Three-step Fe2O3 reduction (Fe2O3 →Fe3O4 →FeO→Fe) governs solid inventory and residence time in chemical-looping hydrogen generation, yet existing kinetic characterisations assume a reaction model before fitting data, leaving open whether the assumed form is correct. This paper applies a coupled inverse physics-informed neural network (PINN) and sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) pipeline that treats the Avrami exponent n as a learnable parameter alongside A and Ea, so no reaction model is specified at any stage. Applied to deconvoluted differential thermogravimetric (DTG) data from Wang et al. [2] at five temperatures (750–950 ◦C), the pipeline converges within eight alternating iterations per step. Steps 1 and 2 independently recover n1 = n2 = 2.008, confirming Johnson–Mehl–Avrami (JMA) n ≈ 2 nucleation kinetics without that assumption being made anywhere in the formulation. Step 3 converges to the contracting-sphere model f(X) = (1−X)2/3, contradicting Wang et al.’s assumed JMA n = 3 and indicating interface-controlled rather than nucleation-growth kinetics at 750–950 ◦C.

papers.title: Reinventing Density Functional Theory with Machine-Learned Integral Features
papers.abstract: Kohn–Sham density functional theory remains central to electronic structure modeling because of its efficiency and the steady gains in accuracy that has been achieved through improved density functionals. Here we introduce a conceptually new strategy in which a multilayer perceptron learns a nonlinear functional of integrated local descriptors (“integral features”). In contrast to pointwise neural-network approaches, the integral-features formulation applies the nonlinear model only once per calculation, preserving the computational efficiency of standard density functionals while enabling a substantially richer functional dependence. Using this framework, we develop ML25@MN15, an integrated-features functional trained on 185 databases spanning thermochemistry, kinetics, noncovalent interactions, spin-flip energies, and molecular structures. Enabled by its expanded representational flexibility, ML25@MN15 achieves a mean unsigned error of 1.05 kcal/mol over 7232 energetic data and consistently outperforms leading modern functionals across all major categories, including systems containing transition metals. Because the neural network operates on integrated descriptors rather than grid-point values, the computational cost of ML25@MN15 remains comparable to MN15. These results demonstrate that introducing integral features and allowing the machine to determine the density functional’s dependence on them yields a high-accuracy density functional without increasing computational cost.

papers.title: Electron-Phonon Coupling Driven Self-Trapped Excitons: A Descriptor-Based Phase Diagram for Perovskites
papers.abstract: Self-trapped excitons (STEs) strongly influence the optical response of many perovskite materials, yet the microscopic factors governing their formation across different chemical families remain unclear. Here, we present a systematic firstprinciples investigation of STE formation in representative oxide, halide, and hydride perovskites to identify the key lattice and electronic descriptors controlling exciton localization. By combining lattice-dynamical analysis, mode-resolved electron-phonon coupling calculations, and excited-state structural relaxations, we show that STE formation is governed by the cooperative interplay between electronphonon coupling, lattice softness, and symmetry-allowed structural distortions. Strong self-trapping occurs when asymmetric octahedral distortions enable efficient exciton-phonon coupling and significant lattice relaxation, whereas stiff lattices with high phonon frequencies suppress exciton localization. Analysis of key descriptors—including the Huang-Rhys factor, phonon linewidth, and mass-weighted structural displacement—reveals clear correlations with STE stabilization energy and Stokes shifts. Based on these relationships, we introduce a generalized composite descriptor that integrates electron-phonon coupling strength, vibronic reorganization, and structural distortion, providing a predictive framework that separates materials into regimes of delocalized, intermediate, and strongly self-trapped excitons. This descriptor-based phase diagram establishes a transferable strategy for understanding and designing materials with strong STE emission and highlights the fundamental role of lattice dynamics in governing exciton localization and optical relaxation in complex perovskites.

papers.title: In-Water Construction of Azo-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks by Oxidative Coupling of Amines
papers.abstract: Azo-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) could be important alternatives to current imine-linked COFs owing to their robustness and extended π conjugation. However, their development has so far been limited by the lack of synthetic methods to crystallize them directly from their respective monomers, and reported examples have relied on linker-exchange strategies instead. Here, we introduced an in-water, single-step, oxone (KHSO 5 )-mediated oxidative coupling strategy of amines to synthesize crystalline azo-linked COFs based on tetraphenoxyethene (TPE) and N,N,N’,N’-tetraphenyl-1,4-phenylenediamine monomers, respectively. The reaction may proceed via oxidation of amine monomers with KHSO5 to generate aryl nitroso intermediates, followed by acid-catalyzed coupling to form azo-linked COFs. The new azo-linked COFs are thermo-chemically stable and explored as reusable photocatalyst to produce H 2 O 2 in water. The TPE based COF (NISER-1) yields H 2 O 2 production rate as high as ~6.5 mmolg -1 h -1 with excellent recyclability, when employing 10% benzyl alcohol (V/V) as a sacrificial agent. This proof-of-concept study not only offers a convenient, scalable, energy-efficient, and sustainable route for direct azo-linked COF synthesis but also shows azo-linked COFs as a promising platform for sustainable solar-driven chemical transformations and green oxidant production.

papers.title: In Situ GISANS Reveals Topology-Dependent Nanoconfined Radical Polymerization in Lipid Liquid-Crystalline Films
papers.abstract: Lipid liquid-crystalline mesophases provide nanostructured aqueous and hydrophobic domains that can direct chemical transformations under soft confinement. Here, we investigate how monomer polarity and mesophase topology govern free-radical polymerization within inverse lipid liquid-crystalline thin films using in situ grazing-incidence small-angle neutron scattering. Deuterated glycerol monooleate / lauric acid films forming bicontinuous cubic ( Pn3m type) and inverse hexagonal ( H 2 ) mesophases were used as nanoconfined reaction platforms for acrylate monomers spanning hydrophilic, cationic, and hydrophobic character. Selective deuteration and solvent contrast variation enabled in situ investigation of structural evolution during hydration, monomer incorporation, and photopolymerization under fully hydrated conditions. The observed structural responses were consistent with the partitioning of hydrophilic monomers into aqueous domains and butyl acrylate into lipid domains prior to polymerization. Photopolymerization within Pn3m type bicontinuous cubic films triggered pronounced topology-dependent restructuring into primitive Im3m cubic phases. In contrast, H 2 mesophases showed no detectable structural changes during photopolymerization in thin films, whereas corresponding bulk systems exhibited structural evolution after polymerization. This discrepancy suggests that confinement topology, hydration geometry, and local compositional changes collectively influence confined reaction pathways and structural responses. These findings establish that polymerization-induced structural remodeling in lipid nanoreactors is governed by monomer partitioning and mesophase connectivity. The work provides mechanistic design principles for engineering confinement-directed polymerization pathways and programmable polymer–lipid hybrid nanomaterials.

papers.title: Coordination-Mediated Nonlinear Catalytic Feedback in Enzyme-Like Copper-Tyrosine Self-Assembled Networks
papers.abstract: The cooperativity and nonlinear dynamics are among the most fundamental characteristics of life. Many molecular mechanisms, such as haemoglobin oxygen binding, actin polymerisation, microtubule dynamic assembly, and Ca2+ ion channels, are assembly-coupled cooperative phenomena in living systems. Natural enzymes are one such systems that rely heavily on the supramolecular environment and non-covalent interactions for their function. However, natural enzymes, their tuning, and their application under robust conditions are complex and challenging. Still, only a limited number of examples exist where minimal assemblies are coupled to enzyme-like functions. Inspired by such principles, we investigate enzyme-like catalysis in copper-tyrosine self-assembled networks (CuYs) as a model system for coordination-driven nonlinear catalytic regulation. The structural organisation of CuYs is comprehensively characterised, revealing the formation of well-defined supramolecular nanoassemblies in both the solid and solution phases. Finally, the Michaelis-Menten parameters and the nonlinear dynamics are studied using the o-phenylenediamine oxidation reaction, demonstrating peroxidase-like catalytic activity. The ordered assembly formation of CuYs and their EDTA-dependent reorganisation leading to a nonlinear effect in catalysis are simulated using molecular dynamics. This study reports the first example of a single tyrosine coordinated to copper, forming a self-assembled nanozyme. Enzyme-like regulation, supramolecular assembly, and nonlinear coordination-driven masking of catalytic activity are the unique features of the CuY self-assembled nanozyme. The enzyme-like activity emerging from minimal non-proteinaceous metal-ligand complexes represents a critical prebiotic bridge between inanimate matter and living chemical networks. Therefore, the present study opens avenues for understanding and generating minimal enzyme-like assemblies that exhibit characteristic life-like features.

papers.title: Can a Klots model-free analysis of kinetic energy release measurements for argon cluster ions, Arn+ provide new insight into the physical state of clusters?
papers.abstract: Experimental, high resolution kinetic energy peak profiles recorded following the unimolecular fragmentation of argon cluster ions, Arn+, where n = 5 – 60, have been fitted to a model-free functional form that yields accurate values for <εt>, the average kinetic energy release and T#, a microcanonical temperature. Through comparisons with molecular dynamics calculations, it is concluded from a plot of <εt>/kT# that a majority of the cluster ions, in these experiments, are liquid-like with comparatively low temperatures; however, one ion, Ar55+, appears to take the form of a solid-like cluster with a higher temperature. This conclusion regarding the latter ion matches many previous suggestions that the enhanced abundance of 55+ ions in the mass spectra of rare gas clusters is due to the presence of stable, closed shell icosahedra.

papers.title: A Practical and Scalable Green Allylic Hydroxylation
papers.abstract: Allylic alcohols are privileged moieties ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and natural products, and the straightforward approach to build these motifs is allylic hydroxylation. However, allylic hydroxylation has relied exclusively on the highly toxic SeO 2 oxidation for almost a century, which gives moderate-to-low yields and raises serious safety and environmental concerns. Here, we present a practical, scalable, and visible-light-mediated metal-free allylic hydroxylation that exhibits a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, and high site-selectivity as demonstrated by 50 diverse substrates. A parallel study on the representative substrates showed that this method is a more efficient alternative to SeO 2 oxidation. This approach, without PPh 3 addition, also affords allylic hydroperoxides accordingly. The cheap chemicals (O 2 as the oxidant) and mild conditions highlight the synthetic value and industrial potential of this method, which enables the late-stage modification of natural products and drugs.

papers.title: Templated On-DNA Synthesis Using PNA-Catalyst Conjugates: Improved Site Selectivity and Yields
papers.abstract: The development of efficient DNA-compatible synthetic methodologies that minimize DNA damage remains one of the most urgent challenges in the field of DNA-encoded libraries. In this work, we report a novel templated on-DNA synthesis platform that employs a PNA–catalyst conjugate capable of complementary hybridization with a DNA headpiece, thereby inducing close proximity between the catalyst and the reaction substrate. This strategy enables site-selective reactions at the warhead region, promoting on-DNA transformations while minimizing side reactions and DNA damage. The versatility of this platform was demonstrated across a range of photocatalytic transformations, including riboflavin tetraacetate (RFTA)-catalyzed benzyl alcohol oxidation and decarboxylative alkylation of α-amino acids, tris(2,2′-bipyridyl)ruthenium(II)-catalyzed azide reduction and decarboxylative coupling of α-amino acids for the synthesis of 1,2-amino alcohols, as well as Eosin Y-catalyzed β-keto sulfone formation. Collectively, the PNA-guided catalytic system afforded higher conversion yields than conventional catalytic systems for substrates on both standard (6-base-pair length) and extended (36-base-pair length) DNA headpieces and minimized DNA damage, as confirmed by qPCR analysis. The PNA used in the reactions was found to be completely removable through a standard ethanol precipitation process after the reaction. This approach is expected to significantly broaden the scope of catalysts compatible with on-DNA synthesis and serve as a practical and powerful tool for the construction of high-quality DNA-encoded libraries.

papers.title: A simple Cell Theory model of the energy surface within endohedral fullerenes
papers.abstract: Cell theory, as proposed by Lennard-Jones and Devonshire [Proc. R. Soc. A. 1937; 163: 53-70], has been adapted to describe the potential energy surface experienced by an atom or molecule within a spherical, endohedral fullerene. The intention being to: (i) remove the need to use multiple pair potentials within such structures, and therefore to allow the range of calculations on endohedral fullerenes to extend to very large carbon cages encapsulating large molecule; and (ii) simplify molecular dynamics calculations on collections of atoms and molecules contained within fullerene structures. Results are presented from calculations on atoms and molecules contained within C60, C180, and C540, and where comparisons with existing pair-potential and DFT calculations on the potential energy and geometry of endohedral C60 species are possible, the agreement is good.

papers.title: Silicon flavylium polymethine dyes for shortwave infrared imaging
papers.abstract: The shortwave infrared (SWIR, 1000–2000 nm) region offers significant advantages for in vivo fluorescence imaging, including reduced scattering, minimal autofluorescence, and deep tissue penetration. However, the development of small molecule fluorophores with high brightness and maximum emission above 1100 nm remains a key challenge. Here, we report a new class of silicon-containing flavylium (SiliFlav) polymethine dyes that address this limitation. By incorporating a silicon heteroatom into the established Flav scaffold, we achieve unprecedented bathochromic shifts in emission up to 200 nm, while maintaining respectable fluorescence quantum yields (up to 0.30%). A modular synthetic route enables diverse functionalization at the 1-, 2-, and 7-positions of the heterocycle, allowing for systematic tuning of photophysical properties and improved dye performance. The lead fluorophore, SiliFlav5, formulated into canola oil nanoemulsions, enables bright SWIR emission above 1300 nm. In vivo imaging in mice demonstrates high-resolution visualization of the vasculature and spleen, confirming the utility of SiliFlav polymethine dyes as a new platform for deep-tissue SWIR imaging.

papers.title: Four Distinct Surface Temperature Patterns Induced by Plasmonic Heating of U-shaped Cr2N nanostructures
papers.abstract: Chromium nitride (Cr 2 N) is a plasmonic material whose real part of the dielectric function becomes negative in the deep-ultraviolet region, enabling plasmon resonances to be tuned from the ultraviolet to the visible and near-infrared by structural design. Its relatively large imaginary part is also advantageous for thermoplasmonic applications. In addition, Cr 2 N exhibits a low thermal conductivity (12 W m -1 K -1 ) compared with that of noble metals. Here, we numerically demonstrate a U-shaped Cr2N nanostructure that generates four distinct surface temperature distributions, controlled solely by the polarization of monochromatic light at 1064 nm. Owing to its symmetry, the U-shaped structure supports different plasmon modes for horizontal and vertical linear polarizations, as well as for left- and right-handed circular polarizations. These mode differences lead to distinct Joule heating distributions that, due to the low thermal conductivity, are directly imprinted on the surface temperature patterns. As a result, the U-shaped nanostructure acts as a polarization-controlled nanoheater, exhibiting distinct temperature distributions for each polarization state. This result shows that surface temperature distributions can be controlled through plasmon mode design in nanostructures, analogous to the shaping of optical near fields by plasmon modes, which is important for thermoplasmonic applications.

papers.title: Interpretable and Robust Hammett Substituent Constant Prediction via Stacking Ensemble with Systematic Feature Engineering and Explainability Analysis
papers.abstract: The Hammett substituent constant σ is one of the most widely used empirical scales for quantifying the electron-withdrawing and electron-donating effects of aromatic substituents, yet its experimental determination remains resourceintensive. Although several machine-learning (ML) models—including graph neural networks such as GCN and Weave—have been proposed as predictive alternatives, existing approaches either rely on black-box architectures that offer no chemical interpretability or on constrained feature sets that limit generalisability. Here we present a systematic, multi-stage ML framework—designated σ-Stack—that addresses both shortcomings simultaneously. Starting from a cleaned dataset of 984 aromatic compounds described by 1,836 molecular descriptors computed with RDKit, Mordred, and PyBioMed, we applied correlation-based feature selection (F.S-2; 131 descriptors), Yeo-Johnson power transformation of the target, and Optuna-guided hyperparameter optimisation to build six base learners (Extra Trees, XGBoost, LightGBM, GradientBoosting, CatBoost, and a tuned MLP/ANN). These were integrated into a Ridge-meta stacking ensemble that achieved a cross-validated R2 of 0.866 ± 0.025 and a test-set R2 of 0.882 (RMSE = 0.112, MAE = 0.078, on the dimensionless σ 1 scale) on an independent 20% hold-out—values that substantially exceed those of all previously published single-model benchmarks on comparable data. Repeated 5 × 10-fold cross-validation confirmed the absence of split-dependent bias (mean R2 = 0.871 ± 0.025). Explainability was pursued at three complementary levels: global feature importance via SHAP beeswarm plots, local explanation of individual predictions via LIME, and multicollinearity auditing via variance inflation factors (VIF). The intersection of SHAP top-25% importance and VIF < 10 identified three chemically trustworthy descriptors that encode electronic polarisability, hydrogen-bond donor capacity, and molecular topology. An ablation study quantified the additive contribution of each methodological step, and AutoGluon multi-stacking was evaluated as an automated baseline. All training, evaluation, and visualisation scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/sevv007/bioformatic-sigma-Stack.

papers.title: Light-Gated Cargo Capture and Release Through Backbone-Functionalized DNA Amphiphiles
papers.abstract: Here we show that DNA strands densely functionalized with photoswitches reversibly assemble into cargo capture and release systems using orthogonal light triggers. Spherical micelles assemble upon exposure to green light (530 nm), capture hydrophobic cargo, and then release said cargo upon disassembly with 365 nm irradiation; this cycle can be repeated at least 10 times without fatigue. Conjugation chemistry at the DNA backbone enables this technology, achieving the location-specific, high-density attachment of light-responsive units without compromising the programmable properties of DNA. The resulting DNA amphiphiles are a robust platform for visible-light-controlled structural switching and cargo handling.

papers.title: Zero-Dimensional Ice Ring Topological Proton Glass: Gapless Texture Soft Modes, Anharmonic Wandering, and Three Conserved Invariants
papers.abstract: Traditional studies of confined ice have heavily relied on exogenous pore confinement such as carbon nanotubes and porous materials. Through a strategy of stepwise dimensionality reduction and geometric topological closure, and without any chemical doping or external substrate confinement, this work systematically constructs a full-curvature-gradient family of zerodimensional closed-loop ice rings, denoted PNH‑M‑Ring. Starting from two-dimensional intrinsic ice and one-dimensional free-standing multi-helix ice nanotubes (PNH‑INT, N = 3–7) and employing a self-developed topological curling program, we generate these structures. Using two first‑principles software packages (CASTEP, DMol3) and the semi‑empirical tight‑binding method DFTB+ in a hierarchical and complementary computational framework, together with stepwise convergence tests of phonons, supercell size evolution analyses, and multi‑temperature ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we demonstrate from four perspectives (atomic geometry, electronic structure, harmonic lattice vibrations, and finite‑temperature dynamics) that closing a one‑dimensional helical ice axially via two S1 ends to form a zero‑dimensional ice ring generates a new state of matter – the topological proton glass (TPG). Unlike KOH‑doped proton glasses where disorder is impurity‑induced, the present system relies solely on topological constraints to achieve a perfect satisfaction of the Bernal‑Fowler ice rules, yet becomes locked into a manifold of nearly degenerate ground states because of the closed‑loop topology (“perfect but trapped”). High‑precision harmonic phonon calculations consistently yield low‑frequency imaginary frequencies, which signal a cooperative, gapless texture soft mode throughout the ring and do not indicate structural mechanical instability. Finite‑temperature AIMD shows that at low temperatures the soft mode evolves into an anharmonic wandering dominated by global elliptical breathing and helical sliding; the oxygen skeleton remains fully connected, and any transient hydrogen‑bond breakage heals rapidly. We rigorously derive three topological invariants – enforced zero polarization flux, the Gauss linking number Lk, and the global ℤ2 chiral charge C0 – thereby establishing a quantitative criterion for TPG. Leveraging the complete research spectrum from 2D through 1D to 0D, we elucidate the evolutionary law of progressive stripping of translational degrees of freedom and the concomitant enhancement of topological frustration. We systematically clarify the role of nuclear quantum effects (NQE), propose two decisive experiments (deuteration and inelastic neutron scattering), and outline potential device applications. All configurations and input scripts are open‑source, and we invite the community to re‑examine our findings using PIMD or machine‑learning potentials.

papers.title: Estimating capture cross-sections for the uptake of molecules by nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Classical collision theory, together with a potential energy curve suitable for describing the interaction between a particle and an atom or molecule, has been used to derive an expression for the capture cross section of a nanoparticle. The expression consists of two components: a hard-sphere term that reflects the size of the particle and a term that arises from an attractive dispersion interaction (-1/R6) between the particle and the colliding species. Comparisons with experimental data on helium and ice nanoparticles show that the capture of molecules by the former to be dominated by the hard sphere term, whereas for the latter the form of the dispersion interaction provides good agreement with experiment.

papers.title: Carba-closo-dodecaborates as Superchaotropic Anions
papers.abstract: The host-guest chemistry of the 1-carba- closo -dodecaborate anion (CB 11 H 12 – ) and its 12-monosubstituted derivatives (R = I, Ph, Et, Bu, OH) with cyclodextrins has been studied, a class of weakly coordinating polyhedral boron cluster anions that have already found applications in catalysis, as ionic liquids, and oxidizing agents. These mono-anions bind surprisingly tightly (K a ⋍ 10 5 M –1 ) to the hydrophobic cavity of CDs, particularly the smallest α-CD and β-CD homologues. This binding propensity closely resembles the binding of larger boron clusters, decaborates and dodecaborates (B 10 X 10 2– and B 12 X 12 2– , with X = Cl, Br, I) as well as metallacarboranes (Co(C 2 B 9 H 11 ) 2 – ), which has been attributed to the superchaotropic properties of these large, charge-dispersed anions. The thermodynamic signature of the encapsulation of 1-carba- closo- dodecaborates by cyclodextrins is consistent with the chaotropic effect as dominant driving force, that is, the binding is strongly enthalpically driven (∆ H down to –19 kcal mol –1 ). The binding of the parent CB 11 H 12 – mono-anion exceeds the binding of the isosteric B 12 H 12 2– di-anion to the three CD homologues by 2-3 orders of magnitude, which indicates a higher chaotropicity, as expected when an ion has a lower charge density. The results position CB 11 H 12 – as the smallest superchaotropic ion known to date, an assignment that was confirmed through its strong effect on the cloud point of a non-ionic polymer (hydroxypropylcellulose). The CB 11 H 12 – ion was subsequently also tested as a chaotropic transmembrane carrier, and it was found to be active in delivering hydrophilic peptides (Arg 8 and phalloidin) through lipid bilayer membranes, in artificial liposomes as well as live CHO-K1 cells. The binding and transport activities of the different superchaotropic boron cluster anions correlate well with their volume and surface charge density, as descriptors of their chaotropicity.

papers.title: Unraveling the Role of Pendant Anionic Substituents in Tuning the Redox Properties of Ruthenium-Based Water Oxidation Catalysts
papers.abstract: Water oxidation catalysts based on ruthenium polypyridyl complexes provide highly tunable platforms for investigating how ligand structure influences redox behavior and catalytic performance. In this work, we employed density functional theory (DFT) to examine the effect of pendant anionic substituents on the redox properties of a series of ruthenium complexes of the form [Ru(terpy)(phenX)], where X = −SO 3 − , −COO − , and −PO 3 i Pr − . To quantify how through-space noncovalent interactions between these substituents and the ruthenium center affect redox properties, we first analyzed the Ru II/III oxidation in a series of MeCN-bound surrogate complexes, in which the coordinating acetonitrile spatially separates the anionic groups from the Ru center and eliminates complications associated with proton transfer and further oxidation beyond Ru III . The results show that introducing pendant anionic substituents consistently lowers the Ru II/III oxidation potential for the MeCN-bound complexes, indicating that these groups effectively modulate redox potentials through long-range electrostatic interactions, as further confirmed by energy decomposition analysis and electrostatic potential calculations. We then extended the computational investigation to the corresponding aqua complexes, focusing on the proton-coupled oxidation of [Ru II (terpy)(phenX)(H 2 O)] to form [Ru III (terpy)(phenX)(OH)], as well as the Ru IV/V oxidation in the corresponding oxo-bound complexes. In contrast to the MeCN-bound surrogate complexes, the substituent-dependent trends are not fully preserved, as the oxidation energetics are influenced by additional factors such as proton transfer and structural rearrangement across oxidation states. These findings provide molecular-level insights into how second-sphere anionic substituents influence the redox properties of ruthenium-based water oxidation catalysts, demonstrating both the effectiveness and limitations of electrostatic tuning strategies.

papers.title: Molecular Representation Learning by Integrating SMILES and Three-Dimensional Structures
papers.abstract: SMILES-based molecular language models are scalable but lack explicit threedimensional structural modeling, while existing 3D molecular pretraining methods usually do not use chemically informed SMILES tokens as an interface to atom-level geometry. Here, we propose AIS-RoChem3D, an Atom-in-SMILES-guided 3D denoising pretraining framework that aligns AIS token sequences with atom-level edge types, interatomic distances, and coordinates through an explicit token-to-atom mapping. AIS-RoChem3D uses a pair-bias Transformer encoder with ProbMix attention to jointly model sequence semantics, AIS-aware topology, and conformational geometry, and is pretrained with masked language modeling, coordinate recovery, and pairwise distance recovery. On MoleculeNet benchmarks, AISRoChem3D achieved competitive performance across classification and regression tasks, with strong improvements on ESOL and FreeSolv and task-dependent gains over the sequenceonlyAIS-RoChem reference model. On experimental ^13C NMR chemical shift prediction, AIS-RoChem3D also achieved strong atom-level regression performance using a simple feedforward readout, supporting the effectiveness of token-to-atom alignment for learning transferable atomic representations. These results show that AIS-guided 3D denoising pretraining provides a practical bridge between SMILES language modeling and atom-level structural representation learning.

papers.title: Reduced Flavins Catalyze the Redox-Neutral Cyclization towards Tetrahydronaphthalenes
papers.abstract: Flavin catalysis represents a powerful tool for constructing complex molecules both in enzymes and in the organic laboratory. Particularly intriguing reactivity is achieved by photochemical excitation of flavin cofactors, which results in strong oxidants or reductants depending on the catalyst redox state. While oxidations with the excited quinoid cofactor are well-studied, reductions with the excited semiquinoid or hydroquinoid catalysts remain scarce. Reductive catalytic activation of substrates holds great promise for synthetic organic chemistry since traditional strong reductants are typically stoichiometric metal reagents. We disclose the reductive activation of ketones via flavin catalysts and a subsequent intramolecular cyclization to tetrahydronaphthalenyl alcohols. A key advantage of our system is the use of hydrogen gas circumventing the necessity of organic reductants. From a synthetic standpoint, our method provides a streamlined route to electron deficient annulated products, while follow-up reactions inter alia result in dihydronaphthalenes. Mechanistically, the presence of flavin semiquinone species was clearly characterized by EPR spectroscopy in combination with control experiments. Our results highlight that reductive flavin catalysis benefits from hydrogen gas as a sustainable reductant, likely applicable to a broad range of reactions. Ketyl radical intermediates are common in catalysis - our strategy for their generation is envisioned to spawn an array of transformations with similar types of substrate activation.

papers.title: MERIT-ML: A Machine-Learning-Readiness Framework for Tabular Public Metabolomics Data
papers.abstract: Public metabolomics repositories contain thousands of deposited studies. However, deposition alone does not show whether a tabular matrix is suitable for supervised classification. We developed MERIT-ML (Metabolomics Evaluation of Readiness and Interoperability of Tabular Data for Machine Learning), an open-source, source-aware framework for extracting tabular data from the Metabolomics Workbench, building canonical per-analysis bundles, and assessing the readiness of each matrix for supervised classification. MERIT-ML provides each study with a design context and scores five core dimensions: structural integrity, analytical data quality, annotation and interoperability, label and class support, and ML task readiness. Metadata and FAIR reusability are reported separately. We also included feasibility gates so that critical constraints, such as missing matrices, insufficient samples, weak class support, and high missingness, are not masked by the overall readiness score. Of 6,696 analyses from 4,121 studies, 96.5% produced at least one valid tabular matrix. Still, readiness varied widely by source. Curated named-metabolite tables were generally cleaner and more interpretable. Untargeted m/z–RT tables were higher-dimensional, more sparsely annotated, and more prone to missing data. At the study level, 35.5% of studies were ML-ready, 34.5% were ML-ready with caveats, and 26.1% were limited by class support. The results suggest that supervised reuse is limited not only by table availability but also by sample size, class structure, source identity, and annotation state. MERIT-ML further demonstrates that many studies did not include paired m/z and retention-time metadata for named metabolites. This limits the reproducibility of annotations, transfer of methods, and reuse across instruments, even when tabular data are used. The web interface is available at https://merit-ml.in. MERIT-ML offers a practical solution for identifying studies suitable for supervised classification, benchmark construction, and repository curation.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Reveal Convergent PI3K/AKT and MMP9 Mechanisms of Ginkgo biloba Bioactive Compounds in Aging and Cancer
papers.abstract: Background : Aging and cancer share converging molecular drivers, including oxidative stress, dysregulated PI3K/AKT and MAPK signaling, ECM remodelling, and impaired apoptosis; however, most natural-product investigations have focused on these axes in isolation. Ginkgo biloba L. is a phytochemically rich source of flavonoids, biflavones, and terpenoid trilactones with documented pleiotropic bioactivities. However, no integrated study has mapped its bioactives across the convergent aging–cancer interface. Methods : We applied a unified network pharmacology and molecular docking pipeline to 14 G. biloba bioactives (anti-aging panels A1–A7; anticancer panels C1–C7), with ginkgolide A and bilobalide deliberately included in both panels for cross-panel benchmarking. ADME, drug-likeness, and computational toxicity (ProTox-3) were profiled. Targets were predicted using a tri-platform consensus (SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, NetInfer), yielding 1,496 unique human proteins. Sub-networks of the top 20 consensus targets were analyzed in Cytoscape v3.20.3 using 11 CytoHubba centrality algorithms. Sixteen hub proteins were docked using AutoDock Vina, and receptor stereochemistry was validated using Ramachandran analysis. Results : Network analysis identified GSK3β, XDH, ALOX5, AXL, and MCL1 as anti-aging hubs and TP53, VEGFA, MMP9, MAPK14, PI3Kα, EGFR, NR4A1, BRCA1, and NOX4 as anti-cancer hubs. Strikingly, XDH, GSK3β, NOX4, MAPK14, and AKT1 emerged in both networks, defining a convergent aging–cancer interface. Ginkgolide A achieved exceptional predicted PI3Kα affinity (ΔG = −10.18 kcal/mol), within a comparable predicted range to the FDA-approved inhibitor alpelisib (−10.3 kcal/mol, same methodology). Kaempferol bound to MMP9 at −9.008 kcal/mol, exceeding the reference inhibitor batimastat (−7.6 kcal/mol). Biflavones isoginkgetin and ginkgetin showed the highest predicted XDH and ALOX5 binding among aging targets. Cross-panel docking of identical molecules (A4/C4 and A5/C7) revealed target-class-specific selectivity profiles. All priority compounds fell within the WHO toxicity classes V–VI. Conclusions : This study provides the first integrated computational evidence that G. biloba bioactives may modulate convergent aging-cancer signaling through high-affinity engagement of the PI3K/AKT, MMP9, MAPK14, and XDH/MCL1 axes, prioritizing ginkgolide A, kaempferol, and biflavones for experimental validation.

papers.title: Red-Light Tomographic Volumetric 3D Printing in Seconds for Fabrication of Colorless Structures
papers.abstract: Non-pulsed red light photopolymerization is attractive for volumetric additive manufacturing because longer wavelengths can improve light penetration, lower scattering, and reduce photodamage compared with ultra-violet or blue irradiation. In this work, we utilized methylene blue and triethanolamine as a sacrificial type II photoinitiating system for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel printing with a custom-made red-light tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing system. With the optimized formulation, PEGDA hydrogel structures were printed by red light within 30 s. The resulting constructs were colorless, extractable, and contained fully formed internal channels. This work establishes a type II photochemistry system as a promising route for extending tomographic volumetric 3D printing toward lower-energy visible-light irradiation and rapid fabrication of colorless hydrogel constructs.

papers.title: Mapping Hierarchical Motifs in disorder-order transitions: learning the hierarchy of structural motifs in supercooled water and ice polymorphs
papers.abstract: Disorder-order transitions pass through structurally rich intermediates that conventional order parameters and classification cannot fully resolve. By extending the hierarchical motif framework previously demonstrated for low-dimensional materials, we learn a discrete vocabulary of structural motifs and a grammar of how they interact in space and time from homogeneous nucleation of supercooled water. By vector quantizing the latent representations of multimodal variational autoencoder (VAE) trained on the structures seen during the nucleation and crystallization of supercooled water, we establish the structural motif vocabulary comprising discrete labels (codebook) of liquid, transient, and ice motifs. Moreover, the variance component of the VAE quantifies the local disorder, decreasing from liquid to transient to ice motifs, which are inaccessible in conventional classifiers. Analysis of the motif grammar, including motif-motif transition, spatial co-occurrences, and primitive-ring occupancies, unifies the mechanistic descriptions of the spatiotemporal dynamics of the precursors of ice nucleation and growth. The transient motifs resolve two distinct structural roles: locally-ordered low-density (LD) environments that constitute precursors during supercooling, and disordered non-consolidating regions during crystallization. Furthermore, we observe that these precursors organize across a continuum of tetra-, penta-, and hexa-meric ring networks. This reveals two distinct processes during supercooling: closed pentamer/hexamer ring scaffolds form continuously (from trimers/tetramers) and persist, while motif identities relabel in bursts along an atomwise energy ladder. Extending the motif vocabulary to hypothetical ice polymorphs identifies approximately 252,000 candidates that are structurally similar to transient motifs; heterogeneous nucleation simulations with four selected candidates show that the ice/liquid interface controls selective Ih/Ic ice growth. Beyond characterizing structural motifs in disorder-order transitions, our framework provides a general methodology for understanding other systems of interest across distinct fields (e.g., microscopy experiments) and physical regimes (e.g., disordered materials).

papers.title: Fast training of bespoke SMIRNOFF-format molecular mechanics force fields using machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: Molecular mechanics force fields enable the thorough sampling required for applications such as alchemical binding free energy calculations for computer-aided drug design. However, parameters from transferable molecular mechanics force fields can be unreliable, and training accurate molecule-specific parameters against quantum mechanical (QM) reference data is slow. Here, we present presto (https://github.com/cole-group/presto), a Python package for fast training of bespoke SMIRKS-Native Open Force Field (SMIRNOFF) format force fields. presto generates training data using high-temperature molecular dynamics with well-tempered metadynamics. It iteratively fits all valence parameters to energies and forces from transferable machine learning potentials (MLPs). By leveraging fast MLP evaluations and training on the GPU using PyTorch (via the packages smee and descent), the fully-automated workflow completes in around 15 minutes for a 50-atom molecule on a single GPU. presto reduces torsion scan errors by a factor of three relative to Open Force Field Sage 2.3.0 on 400 molecules from TorsionNet500. It also achieves torsion scan performance comparable to direct QM fitting on a benchmark dataset of fragmented drug-like molecules, and relative conformer energies of 510 molecules from the set of Folmsbee and Hutchison are significantly improved compared to both Sage and espaloma. presto allows simultaneous fitting of congeneric series with partially shared parameters. It produces comparable relative binding free energy performance to OpenFF 1.3.1 (Parsley) on systems where Parsley already performs well, and may improve performance in cases where initial parameters are particularly poor.

papers.title: Carbocation-Based Proximity Labeling
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic proximity labeling platforms use localized release of reactive species to covalently label proteins near a photocatalyst, facilitating the identification of protein interactions. Singlet oxygen, Michael acceptors, radicals, nitrenes, and carbenes are currently used for labeling, with spatial resolution dictated by reactive intermediate lifetime and signal to noise limited by non-catalyzed reactivity. Here, we report a high-resolution proximity labeling platform based on photocatalytic generation of benzylic carbocations from coumarin precursors. Carbocations combine promiscuous crosslinking with limited diffusion in water (t 1/2 < 3 ns) and low non-catalyzed background labeling, properties that enable demanding applications such as small molecule target identification, binding affinity profiling, and proteinprotein interaction discovery on cell surfaces. We show that coumarin-based reagents can be used for improved identification of labeled proteins while maintaining compatibility with commonly used photocatalysts and light setups, allowing them to be used as drop-in replacements for diazirines in existing workflows.

papers.title: Near-Critical Supercritical-CO₂ Desiccation of Triple-Knockout Porcine Red Blood Cells: A Proposed Protocol with Haemolysis-Reduction Pathway Analysis (Revised v2)
papers.abstract: Genetically engineered triple-knockout (TKO) porcine red blood cells (pRBCs) — with the GGTA1, β4GalNT2, and CMAH carbohydrate-antigen genes inactivated and human complement-regulatory transgenes (e.g., CD47, CD55) expressed — are among the most genetically advanced xenogeneic red-cell concepts, but remain preclinical: there is no clinically deployed pig-red-cell transfusion product, and current handling assumes cold-chain storage identical to human RBCs (Yamamoto 2021; Ko 2022; Chornenkyy 2023). We propose a conceptual near-critical supercritical-CO₂ (scCO₂) desiccation protocol for ambient-temperature preservation of TKO pRBCs, operating at 74–80 bar and 31–35 °C (just above the CO₂ critical point, 31.1 °C and 73.8 bar), where near-zero surface tension is achieved while membrane perturbation is, by hypothesis, minimised relative to higher-pressure scCO₂. This revision (v2) states the central tension explicitly: scCO₂ is also a documented agent of microbial inactivation and cell-membrane disruption (Tamburini 2014), so its use here as a gentle drying medium is a hypothesis bounded by near-critical conditions, not a demonstrated capability. The principal barrier remains post-rehydration haemolysis — the best published red-cell desiccation results are of the order of several per cent, roughly an order of magnitude above the ≤0.8 % limit (Council of Europe/EDQM end-of-storage criterion). We analyse candidate haemolysis-reduction pathways (intracellular trehalose vitrification; controlled rehydration osmolarity; membrane complement-regulator retention) drawing on related freeze-drying and protein-transfer work (Chen Y 2006; Arav 2012; Sloand 1998). No experimental haemolysis, recovery, or potency data were generated; all values are cited literature anchors. Validation (XRPD/DSC of the dried matrix, in-vitro 24-hour recovery, haemolysis ≤0.8 %, and immunological characterisation) is required before any use. Public prior-art disclosure under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Three Pathogen-Reduction Strategies for Ambient-Temperature Dried Red Blood Cells: An Efficacy-Cost Decision Framework for Resource-Limited Settings
papers.abstract: Proposals to preserve red blood cells (RBCs) at ambient temperature by drying must address pathogen safety without a cold chain. Version 1 of this work over-stated the efficacy of riboflavin-ultraviolet (UV) treatment by quoting log-reduction values measured in plasma and platelet concentrates and applying them to red cells; this revision corrects that error. Riboflavin-UV light penetrates poorly through the haemoglobin of red-cell-containing units, so its measured efficacy in whole blood is materially lower than in plasma (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 ~3.3 log in whole blood vs ~4.8 log in plasma; Ragan et al. 2020), and it is weak against non-enveloped viruses and variable against bacteria. We therefore reframe the problem as a choice among three pathogen-reduction (PR) strategies applied to whole blood before drying: (A) riboflavin + UV (Mirasol, whole-blood format); (B) amustaline (S-303) + glutathione (the INTERCEPT red-cell system); and (C) a screening-led approach (two-stage point-of-care nucleic-acid and serological testing with minimal PR). We compile literature-derived log-reductions per pathogen class and documented cost estimates, compute a weighted composite safety score, and present an efficacy-cost decision matrix. Strategy A is the cost-effective sweet spot where adequate (composite ~84/100 at ~US$60/unit, no chemical residue) and is supported by a randomised clinical reduction of transfusion-transmitted malaria (AIMS; Allain et al. 2016) and by evidence that red cells from whole-blood Mirasol retain adequate quality for 21 days (Dimberg et al. 2019). Strategy B gives the broadest coverage including bacteria and non-enveloped viruses (>=4 log) and is the most clinically advanced for red cells (Phase 3 ReCePI; Cancelas et al. 2017; North et al. 2020), at higher cost and with a chemical-residue/immunogenicity profile to manage. Strategy C is the lowest-cost option but falls below a standalone safety threshold and is appropriate only as an adjunct screening layer. In all three, supercritical CO2 is used solely as the drying step, not as a pathogen-inactivation claim, and pathogen reduction is positioned as an adjunct to - not a replacement for - donor screening. No experimental potency, recovery, or inactivation data were generated; every value herein is a cited literature anchor or a labelled estimate. Validation is required before any use. This document is a public prior-art disclosure under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Ambient-Temperature Red Blood Cell Preservation by Intracellular Trehalose Vitrification and Supercritical-CO₂ Drying with Food-Grade Bacteriostatic Excipients: A Conceptual Framework (Revised v2)
papers.abstract: Red-cell transfusion in resource-limited and remote settings is constrained by cold-chain dependency (1–6 °C) and a 42-day shelf life. We describe a conceptual multi-component system for ambient-temperature dried red blood cells (RBCs): (i) intracellular trehalose loading as a vitrification agent (e.g., by transient electroporation; Chen Y 2006); (ii) supercritical-CO₂ (scCO₂) drying as a surface-tension-free dehydration step — not as a pathogen-inactivation or cell-disruption step; (iii) food-grade bacteriostatic excipients (ε-poly-L-lysine, rosmarinic acid, citric and ascorbic acids) for ambient microbial control; and (iv) an optional, unproven perfluorocarbon rehydration medium for supplemental oxygen. This revision (v2) makes three honesty corrections to v1: the inherent tension between scCO₂ as a gentle drying medium and scCO₂ as a microbicidal/cell-lysing agent is stated explicitly and resolved by restricting the process to near-critical, integrity-preserving conditions; the food-grade excipients are flagged as NOT intravenous-grade, requiring formal parenteral toxicology before any in-product use; and the perfluorocarbon rehydration element is downgraded to optional and unvalidated (consistent with the corrected oxygen-carrier analysis in the companion work). All citations have been verified and several v1 bibliographic errors corrected (see Disclosure). No experimental recovery, haemolysis, or stability data were generated; every quantitative statement is a cited literature anchor. Validation (in-vitro 24-hour recovery, haemolysis ≤0.8%, membrane-integrity and ATP/2,3-DPG panels, and parenteral toxicology of all excipients) is required before any use. Public prior-art disclosure under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Enteral, Intravenous, and Haemoglobin-Based Oxygen Carriers: A Capacity-Safety Decision Framework for Settings Without Compatible Blood
papers.abstract: Version 1 of this work proposed an oral perfluorocarbon (PFC) as a systemic, blood-group-independent oxygen supplement. That central claim is quantitatively implausible and is withdrawn here: resting oxygen consumption is ~250 mL O2/min, gastrointestinal absorption of an inert perfluoroalkane is minimal, and even intravenous PFC emulsions deliver only a limited, physically-dissolved oxygen payload that requires a high inspired-oxygen fraction (Riess 2001). v1 also misapplied a hydrocarbon-calibrated log-P estimate to a perfluoroalkane and over-stated a beta-cyclodextrin inclusion of a fluorophilic PFC; both are removed. This revision keeps the one defensible and genuinely novel element - enteral perfluorocarbon oxygenation - and reframes it honestly as one modality within a comparative landscape, not a blood substitute. We compare three oxygen-carrier modalities for the real clinical gap (oxygen delivery where compatible blood is unavailable: trauma, remote/military, mass-casualty, rare phenotypes): (A) enteral PFC oxygenation, for which oxygenated perfluorochemical delivered to the gut lumen has been shown to ameliorate respiratory failure in mammals (Okabe et al., Med 2021); (B) intravenous PFC emulsion (e.g., perflubron/Oxygent); and (C) a haemoglobin-based oxygen carrier (HBOC-201/Hemopure), which is approved in South Africa and Russia and offers near-blood oxygen capacity but carries a cardiovascular-safety signal (increased myocardial infarction and death in a meta-analysis; Natanson et al., JAMA 2008). Using relative, literature-informed scores for capacity, safety, non-invasiveness, and regulatory maturity, with documented-estimate costs, we present a capacity–safety–cost decision framework with hard clinical gates. No single modality reaches an “ideal” of high capacity and high safety; instead each is admissible in a distinct setting — A for pre-hospital/field use without intravenous access, B for elective peri-operative transfusion-sparing, and C as a last-resort, monitored option for life-threatening anaemia when no compatible blood exists. No experimental data were generated; all numeric inputs are relative literature-informed estimates or labelled cost estimates. This document is a public prior-art disclosure under CC BY 4.0; all methods and code are reproduced in full.

papers.title: Light-Promoted Synthesis of Glycosyl Bromides in Flow
papers.abstract: A new light-promoted method for the preparation of glycosyl bromides has been developed, exhibiting broad applicability to commonly used substrates. Upon irradiation with purple LEDs, bromine reacts with benzotrifluoride (PhCF3) to generate hydrogen bromide (HBr) in situ, which subsequently transforms the substrate into the glycosyl bromide in excellent yield. Unlike classical methods, the new strategy generates minimal acidic waste and features a simple work-up. Notably, its scalability was demonstrated under photo-flow conditions, enabling rapid, multigram-scale synthesis of glycosyl bromides. Furthermore, we show that the product bromides can be used directly as glycosyl donors in one-pot glycosylations.

papers.title: Autonomous computational catalysis through an agentic research system
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents are beginning to transform scientific research from tool-assisted workflows toward self-sustaining discovery processes. Computational catalysis provides a representative challenge, as catalyst discovery requires high-level questions to be translated into coordinated model construction, atomistic simulation, mechanistic analysis, and iterative design across multiple scales. Here we introduce CatMaster, a catalysis-native agentic research system that recasts computational catalysis as a low-barrier virtual ecosystem for autonomous research. CatMaster maintains an evolving research state and extends capabilities through self-feedback across model construction, calculation, critique and catalyst-design decisions within one extensible environment. Across progressively challenging tasks, CatMaster converts natural-language requests into concrete computational studies, from essential atomistic modelling and standard calculations to mechanism exploration and closed-loop catalyst design. It showed robust execution in representative computational-catalysis scenarios and near-leading performance across selected MatBench tasks, with phonons scenario demonstrating its modelling self-evolution capability. In the independent CO2-to-CO catalyst design case, CatMaster used iterative self-critique and evidence refinement to identify competitive B–CoN4 and NiN3B/N–NiN3B motifs. These results establish a virtual-ecosystem paradigm in which AI agents move beyond simulation execution toward end-to-end computational research, providing a foundation for autonomous discovery in catalysis and materials science.

papers.title: Quinones and tyrosines in the long-range donor-acceptor side interactions in photosystem II: Implications for proton-coupled electron transfer
papers.abstract: It has long been known that certain changes in the acceptor (reductive) side of the Photosystem II (PSII) reaction center result in alterations on the donor (oxidative) side. However, the nature of this long-range interaction remains unclear. In PSII, the proton-coupled electron transfer is carried out by plastoquinones, Q A and Q B , on the acceptor side and by the tyrosine residues, D1-Tyr161 (Tyr Z ) and D2-Tyr160 (Tyr D ), on the donor side. All four redox components share a similar head-group structure, are symmetrically located on the D1 and D2 core proteins and interact with histidine residues that serve as H-bonding partners. These histidine residues are D1-His215 (His B ), D1-His190 (His Z ), D2-His214 (His A ) and D2-His189 (His D ) respectively. The corresponding histidines of the Q B /Tyr Z pair and Q A /Tyr D pair are bound by the same transmembrane α-helix D of the corresponding D1 or D2 protein ~35 Å apart. It is hypothesized that changes in H-bonding accompanying reduction of acceptor side components are propagated along α-helix D, inducing corresponding alterations in the H-bonding of the donor side components, thereby facilitating their oxidation, and vice versa. Thus, the specific H-bond environment of the single electron acceptor Q A determines the oxidized state of Tyr D in active PSII. When Tyr D is oxidized, Q A is more favorably poised to accept an electron and to transfer it to Q B . On the other hand, the proton-coupled electron reduction and exchange of Q B governs Tyr Z oxidation and reduction during PSII turnover. The structural, functional and evolutionary implications of the proposed mechanism of long-range interactions in PSII are discussed in the context of possible computational and experimental methodologies that can be employed to test this hypothesis.

papers.title: Fast and Scalable Sample Preparation for Integrated Metabolome and Exposome-Wide Association Studies (MWAS/ExWAS)
Vanadium Doping of Anisotropic Cobalt Oxide Platelets: Effect of Increasing Laser Energy on Depth Penetration and Resulting Catalytic Activity
papers.abstract: Well-defined model systems are advantageous to study structure-activity correlations in catalysis, but particularly the preparation of differently doped nanostructures with identical shape and size can be challenging. This study employs Pulsed Laser Defect Engineering in Liquid (PUDEL) to dope vanadium into Co 3 O 4 while maintaining the size distribution, morphology and <111> orientation. The former is demonstrated via SEM-EDX, XPS, and Auger Electron Spectroscopy depth profiles. N 2 -adsorption profiles reveal a significant internal pore surface area and open sub-structure of the Co 3 O 4 platelets that undergo reconstruction due to the laser-induced heating and the related diffusion enhancement. Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) further confirm that the V-doped Co 3 O 4 is partially reduced and obtains increased concentrations of HS Co 2+ at O h -site. Additionally, the oxidative conversion of cinnamyl alcohol (CA) is enhanced while the electrocatalytic overpotential of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is reduced by 10 mV. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that vanadium dopants and high *OH coverage on the Co 3 O 4 surface both enhance the catalytic OER activity. The investigation opens a new avenue to systematically investigate the role of dopants in the formation of active sites in pre-designed oxide nanoparticle and thin-film model catalysts.

papers.title: Non-Covalent Luminescent Diradicals in Molecular Crystals for All-Optical Magnetic Field Sensing
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract. Luminescent solid-state materials with optically polarized electron spins are emerging platforms for nanoscale magnetic field sensing. In this work, magnetic-field-sensitive luminescent diradicals are engineered through isostructural doping of organic monoradicals into a diamagnetic host crystal. At moderate doping concentrations, non-covalent diradicals form through substitution of host molecules at adjacent lattice sites, enabling through-space exchange couplings with well-defined geometries. Optical pumping polarizes the resulting triplet diradicals through spin-selective intersystem crossing, mediated by excited-state charge separation and recombination between the radical subunits. Electronic structure calculations reveal that the associated spin-orbit couplings depend on the inter-radical geometry, identifying crystal design as a pathway to control the polarization mechanism. The unique excited-state spin selectivity gives rise to magnetoluminescence under weak magnetic fields through mixing of the triplet zero-field states, enabling an all-optical sensing protocol with a dynamic range governed by the zero-field splitting. A magnetic field sensitivity of 28 μT Hz-1/2 is achieved, which is competitive with alloptical sensing techniques based on NV centers. This work establishes a direct strategy to engineer optical spin polarization and magnetoluminescence contrast of diradical spins in the solid state.

papers.title: Programmable selection of tetrahedral crystal lattices from a single nanoscale scaffold
papers.abstract: Open tetrahedral lattices span diamond polymorphs, ice frameworks, zeolites and clathrates, and many are predicted to support complete photonic band gaps. Yet selectively assembling a chosen tetrahedral topology as a colloidal crystal remains difficult because distinct long-range structures share the same local fourfold coordination and compete during growth. Here we show that a single tetrahedron-shaped DNA origami can be programmed to self-assemble exclusively into diamond cubic, hexagonal diamond and ice0 by changing only the sticky-end sequences at its vertices. A competition-aware inverse-design workflow identifies interaction maps that encode each target topology while excluding competing crystals and finite off-pathway assemblies. Small-angle X-ray scattering and scanning electron microscopy support the selective formation of all three lattices. Photonic band-structure calculations on idealized high-index versions of these topologies show complete photonic band gaps under suitable refractive-index and fill-fraction conditions, linking the experimentally selected structures to ultraviolet-scale photonic design. These results establish a universal inverse design pipeline for programmable open-framework materials from a common nanoscale scaffold.

papers.title: Unravelling the opposing cumulenic effects of aryl group size and solvent polarity on the ground and excited states of symmetric 2,5-bis(arylethynyl)-1,3,4-thiadiazoles
papers.abstract: Linearly conjugated, rod-like bis(arylethynyl)arylene compounds have been widely employed as model systems with which to explore an array of molecular photophysical phenomena, and establish structure-property relationships underpinning the use of these compounds in electronic and optoelectronic applications. Whilst heterocyclic derivatives have proven to be important subsets of this family, examples featuring thiadiazoles, such as Ar‒C≡C‒ThD‒C≡C‒Ar (Ar = aryl; ThD = 1,3,4-thiadiazole) are rare, despite the high aromaticity of the ThD motif. Here, a spectroscopic and computational study of the optical properties of a series of 2,5-bis(arylethynyl)-1,3,4-thiadiazoles as a function of the steric and electronic properties of the aryl moieties (Ar = phenyl, 1-naphthyl and 9-anthracenyl) is presented. The evolving electronic structure as a function of the Ar group, represented by the contrasting degree of ‘cumulenic’ character in the molecular backbone in the ground (S 0 ) and excited (S 1 ) states, is shown to be the key feature influencing the photophysical properties of these compounds. In the ground state, the cumulenic character of the backbone increases with the nature of the aryl substituents (phenyl < naphthyl < anthracenyl) leading to higher rotational barriers around the Ar-C≡C-ThD (Ar=C=C=ThD) axis, decreased reorganization energy between the ground and excited states and greater vibrational structure in the electronic absorption spectra. A reverse trend was found in the S 1 excited state, where the cumulenic character decreases with the increasing size of the aryl-end group. The cumulenic character, reorganization energy and photophysics of the S 1 state of the anthracenyl derivative proved to be most sensitive to the solvent polarity, giving rise to unusual solvatochromic emissions.

papers.title: Scaffold-axis recurrence in a non-opioid ChEMBL subset associated with nociplastic-relevant biological targets: a chemoinformatic mapping with full-molecule structural-alert validation
papers.abstract: Background Nociplastic pain, defined by the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) as pain arising from altered nociception in the absence of clear tissue damage or somatosensory lesion, lacks a consolidated non-opioid medicinal-chemistry landscape. Public bioactivity databases such as ChEMBL contain large amounts of activity data against biological targets that have been associated with nociplastic-relevant biology (for example sodium channels, purinergic receptors, calcium channels, GPCR regulatory kinases and innate-immune signalling components), but this information is dispersed across many assays, units and activity relations. Aim To build a transparent, reproducible chemoinformatic map of recurrent molecular scaffolds across a manually curated non-opioid ChEMBL extraction associated with nociplastic-relevant biological targets, and to apply a full-molecule chemoinformatic validation layer (structural-alert, flatness, aggregation, assay-fragility and redundancy descriptors) to characterize which scaffolds survive standard chemoinformatic stress tests. The study is explicitly chemoinformatic and does not test therapeutic, efficacy or mechanism-of-action claims in vitro or in vivo. Methods Activity records were extracted from ChEMBL using activity-type and unit filters with a ≤10 µM potency cut-off; the standard_relation flag was retained at extraction so that records reported as "greater than" a value could be treated as censored lower-bound observations in downstream summaries. Records were merged with the molecule table, structurally standardized and deduplicated. A primary medicinal-chemistry filter combining Lipinski/RO5 + TPSA constraints, PAINS substructure alerts and instability filters was applied. Opioid-associated records were excluded by annotation. Recurrent Murcko scaffolds were tabulated across mechanistic axes. A separate full-molecule validation layer independent of the primary PAINS filter, computed BRENK-style structural alerts, flat-aromatic-risk, aggregation-stickiness-risk, assay-fragility and local-similarity-redundancy descriptors per compound, and aggregated them per scaffold. Results From 8,006 initial activity records (6,079 unique molecule IDs), 7,994 merged activity molecule rows yielded 6,058 standardized unique structures. After RO5/TPSA filtering 498 compounds remained; after primary PAINS filtering 483; after instability filtering 471 compounds (272 distinct Murcko scaffolds). Removing opioid-associated records left a non-opioid subset of 363 compounds, whose UMAP coordinates inherit the full-space embedding. Within this non-opioid subset, the scaffold-axis recurrence layer comprises 207 scaffold-axis rows, and a priority layer of 5 recurrent scaffolds was carried into mechanistic-axis and full-molecule validation analyses. All five priority scaffolds are classified as "Strong survival" in the chemoinformatic validation layer (mean stress-test score 0.225–0.533), with zero severe structural threats and at most two moderate threats per family. Across the eleven mechanistic axes annotated in this dataset, the GRK axis (n = 46 compounds), P2X7 (n = 22), Nav1.7 (n = 19), TRPA1 (n = 18) and Nav1.8 (n = 14) accumulate the largest number of unique non-opioid compounds. Exact activity records dominate over censored ">" records in the higher-occupancy axes. Interpretation The dataset delineates a small, internally consistent and chemoinformatically robust set of recurrent non-opioid scaffolds linked to nociplastic-relevant targets in ChEMBL. "Strong survival" is used here as a chemoinformatic label (low flatness, low aggregation, manageable assay fragility, no severe structural alerts, low redundancy) and not as a claim of biological efficacy, target engagement, selectivity, or therapeutic translatability. The deposited dataset is meant as a transparent starting point for follow-up experimental work and for further methodological scrutiny.

papers.title: ChemEvent-VLM: Multimodal Visual-Language Framework for Chemical Molecular Event Chain Reasoning
papers.abstract: Chemical reactions are fundamentally sequential processes in which reactants transform into products through causally linked molecular events, yet existing deep learning approaches predominantly treat reaction prediction as isolated single-step tasks, failing to capture the intrinsic event-chain structure of chemical transformations. In this paper, we propose ChemEvent-VLM, a multimodal visual-language framework that explicitly models chemical reactions as molecular event chains to enable causally grounded reasoning. ChemEvent-VLM integrates four synergistic modules: a Molecular Event Chain Modeling module that represents reactions as structured event sequences with chemical knowledge graph constraints, a Visual Dependency Decoupling strategy that dynamically balances visual and textual attention for long-context molecular reasoning, a Weak-to-Strong Generalization scheme that leverages supervisory signals from small chemical expert models to enhance large multimodal models without additional annotation cost, and an Anomaly-Aware Feedback mechanism that detects and corrects anomalous substructures in molecular images. We evaluate ChemEvent-VLM on three chemical benchmarks: USPTO-50k for reaction prediction, ChEBI-20 for molecular event reasoning, and PubChem-MolImg for molecular structure recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that ChemEvent-VLM achieves 84.5 percent accuracy on reaction prediction, 0.85 F1 on molecular event reasoning, and 0.189 BLEU-4 on molecular structure recognition, establishing new state-of-theart performance across all three tasks. Ablation studies confirm that each proposed module contributes meaningfully, with the event chain modeling module providing the largest improvement of 4.3 percent in reaction prediction accuracy.

papers.title: ‘One-Pot’ Kinetic Profiling of SNAr Reactions via Sequential Addition Kinetic Elucidation (SAKE)
papers.abstract: We introduce Sequential Addition Kinetic Elucidation (SAKE), a one-pot protocol for acquiring multiple kinetic datasets under synthetically relevant conditions. Using nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) reactions between aryl phenyl ethers and secondary amines as a case study, SAKE combines sequential reagent dosing with in situ monitoring and automated analysis.
