The methodology was applied to investigate competing uncatalysed and base-catalysed SNAr pathways, enabling the extraction of global rate laws using Auto-VTNA, with the amine order reflecting the pathway preference. Modelling reversible inhibition of the amine by phenol enabled reliable extraction of rate constants for both pathways via microkinetic modelling. The influence of temperature, electrophile electronics and amine basicity was studied using linear free energy relationships, and can be understood in light of the rate limiting proton transfer (RLPT) mechanism. A range of solvents were also trialled. Regression analysis uncovers quantitative correlations between solvent descriptors and the extracted kinetic parameters that may guide rational solvent selection. SAKE offers a streamlined and data-rich alternative to traditional kinetic methods, validated here on a mechanistically complex system featuring competing pathways and product inhibition.

papers.title: Rethinking How Band Gap Changes Enable Ferroelectricity in Wurtzite Nitride Alloys
papers.abstract: Wide-and ultrawide-band gap wurtzite III-nitrides are commonly alloyed with group-3 elements such as Sc, Y, and Gd to reduce the polarization switching coercive field ( E c ) for ferroelectrics. Because group-3 nitrides typically adopt the rocksalt structure with relatively small band gaps, alloying is generally expected to reduce both the band gap ( E g ) and dielectric breakdown field ( E b ). However, recent reports of band-gap widening in Ga 1−x Sc x N and In 1−x Sc x N challenge this assumption. Using DFT calculations, we show that band gaps in heterostructural III-nitride alloys is governed not only by the ground-state polymorph but also by structurally relevant polymorphs of the alloying end member. Extending the analysis to AlN-, GaN-, and InN-based alloys with Sc, Y, La, and B, we identify three distinct bandgap regimes that follow wurtzite-, hexagonal-BN-, or rocksalt-like trends. These behaviors are governed by bond ionicity and structural distortion, providing design guidelines for engineering E g and E b in wurtzite III-nitride alloys.

papers.title: Oxygen-vacancy-induced Ti 3d defect states and spin polarization in anatase TiO2: a GPU-accelerated DFT study
papers.abstract: While oxygen vacancies fundamentally dictate the electronic behavior of titanium dioxide, mapping their precise influence requires robust computational models. To investigate these vacancy-induced defect states in anatase TiO2, we employed density functional theory (DFT) within the PBE generalized-gradient approximation. Our baseline was a pristine Ti16O32 supercell, which we compared against a fully relaxed Ti16O31 model containing a single neutral oxygen vacancy. All self-consistent and non-self-consistent field calculations were executed using a GPU-accelerated build of Quantum ESPRESSO. In the pristine structure, we observed a standard PBE band gap of 2.159 eV, characterized by O 2p states in the valence band and Ti 3d states in the conduction band. However, introducing the vacancy fundamentally alters this electronic profile. The defect induces strongly spin-polarized states near the Fermi level, yielding a net magnetization of approximately 1 µB per cell. Projected density of states (PDOS) analysis confirms that these near-Fermi states are overwhelmingly Ti 3d in character, comprising over 90% of the orbital contributions within this energy window. Furthermore, atomresolved PDOS and geometric analyses directly link these dominant Ti 3d contributions to the titanium atoms immediately adjacent to the vacancy site. Finally, we evaluated the formation energetics across different chemical 1ORCID: 0009-0000-0795-4446 environments. The oxygen-vacancy formation energy reaches 4.804 eV in the O-rich molecular limit, whereas it drops significantly to 0.235 eV under Ti-rich/O-poor conditions (referenced to hcp Ti). Together, these findings offer a comprehensive, PBE-level mapping of how oxygen vacancies govern local atomic environments, spin polarization, and orbital behaviors in anatase TiO2.

papers.title: Globally Aromatic 10-Boratetraoxacorroles: Furan-Derived Chromophores with Intense Red to Near-Infrared Emission
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of a furan-based 10-bora-21,22,23,24-tetraoxacorrole ( 1 ) and an oxadiborepin-fused derivative thereof ( 2 ). Both macrocyclic boranes are globally aromatic, as supported by experiment and NICS and ACID calculations. The novel boracorroles exhibit intense absorption spanning the ultraviolet to near-infrared (NIR) regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. Notably, they display bright red ( 1 , Φ fl = 35%) and red-to-NIR ( 2 , Φ fl = 46%) fluorescence, achieving quantum yields up to three times that of conventional triphenylcorrole. DFT analysis reveals that the frontier orbital energies are strongly modulated by the meso -B atom, generating a large HOMO to HOMO−1 energy gap and, consequently, markedly enhanced Q-band extinction coefficients arising from the predominantly single-configurational character of the S 0 →S 1 transition (HOMO to LUMO). Incorporation of the BOB bridge in oxadiborepin-fused derivative 2 significantly stabilizes the LUMO, giving rise to red-shifted absorption and emission alongside distinct electrochemical behavior. In addition, the BOB unit further amplifies the global aromaticity of the corrole, underscoring efficient π-conjugation across the BOB bridge.

papers.title: Off-Stoichiometric Synthesis of Porphyrin-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Structural Modulation and Enhanced Chemiresistive NO2 Sensing
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with high porosity and tunable structures have emerged as promising materials for energy and environmental applications. Their synthetic versatility enables precise structural control, allowing tailored properties and functions. Herein, we report a green, aqueous synthesis of porphyrin-based COFs through stoichiometric tuning of amine and aldehyde monomers under ambient conditions. The resulting COFs display well- defined nanoscale morphologies with tunable porosity and crystallinity. Notably, off- stoichiometric conditions led to decreased crystallinity and surface area, indicating the formation of defect-rich structures. COFs synthesized under amine- and porphyrin-rich 2 conditions demonstrated exceptional chemiresistive NO2 sensing performance, with responses up to ~8000 at 100 ppm and a detection limit as low as ~12 ppb. The sensors also showed rapid response and recovery, excellent recyclability, and long-term stability. In situ DRIFTS measurements and DFT calculations revealed strong interactions between NO2 molecules and the imine and porphyrin units, along with charge transfer from nitrogen sites to NO2, accounting for the enhanced sensing behavior. This study establishes a facile, sustainable strategy for the structural modulation of COFs toward high-performance gas sensing applications.

papers.title: S-Aminodibenzo[b]thiophenium Salts as Versatile Precursors for the Photoredox-Catalyzed Generation of Sulfamoyl Radicals
papers.abstract: S -Aminodibenzo[ b ]thiophenium salts, accessible from S -methoxydibenzo[ b ]thiophenium tetrafluoroborate and the parent amines, are introduced as alternative precursors for the in situ generation of sulfamoyl radicals. Irradiation of S -aminodibenzo[ b ]thiophenium salts and the solid SO 2 surrogate DABSO with visible light in the presence of the organic photoredox catalyst Eosin Y affords sulfamoyl radicals as versatile reactive intermediates for the synthesis of sulfonamides. The utilization of this approach is demonstrated in the three-component synthesis of beta-ketosulfonamides.

papers.title: Rheological Signatures of Molecular Spin Crossover Switch in a Soft Polymer Composite
papers.abstract: Materials with on-demand switchable stiffness underpin soft robotics, adaptive damping and morphing devices. Leading strategies—magnetorheological elastomers, phase-change-particle composites and liquid-crystal elastomers—deliver large modulus changes but share two limitations: the switched state is volatile, decaying once the stimulus is removed, and the response is monotonic, lacking memory. Here, embedding a molecular spin-crossover (SCO) complex in poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) encodes a qualitatively different response: a hysteretic, room-temperature-bistable stiffness retained without a sustained stimulus and set by a tunable molecular transition. Two isostructural Hofmann-type clathrates, {Fe(pz)[Pd(CN)4]} (1) and {Fe(pz)[Ni(CN)4]} (2), are embedded at 3 wt% in PDMS; 1@PDMS retains a wide room-temperature transition while 2@PDMS is SCO-silent, providing a matched active/inactive control within one chemistry. Oscillatory shear reveals a hysteretic storage-modulus increase in 1@PDMS from ≈12 kPa (high-spin) to ≈29 kPa (low-spin)—up to 77%—coinciding with the magnetic and calorimetric transition, whereas 2@PDMS and neat PDMS show none. The loss factor tan δ likewise traces a hysteresis loop (≈0.20 to ≈0.35), so the elastic-to-dissipative balance, not only the stiffness, is bistable. Because 25 °C lies within the loop, the composite presents two retained mechanical states at one ambient temperature, identifying SCO composites as a molecularly programmable variable-stiffness material with chemically tunable bistability.

papers.title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled-Cluster Accurate Free-Energy Simulations
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of zeolite-catalyzed reactions requires a reliable description of reactive intermediates, which remains challenging for density functional theory (DFT) and often necessitates correlated wave function theory (cWFT). However, high-level methods such as coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)] are computationally prohibitive for periodic systems. Here, we develop a ∆-learning framework combined with a cluster-based QM/QM approach to enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with CCSD(T)-level accuracy at reduced cost. Starting from the MACE-MPA-0 foundation model, we perform data-efficient fine-tuning followed by a cluster-based ∆-learning to incorporate high-level corrections. This approach is applied to study the skeletal isomerisation of n-butene in zeolites using well-tempered metadynamics

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Cell-Cell Communication Inference, and Network Pharmacology Identify CXCR4 as a Therapeutic Target in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, fatal interstitial lung disease driven by dysregulated intercellular communication between fibroblasts, macrophages, and epithelial cells. Despite the approval of pirfenidone and nintedanib, disease-modifying therapy targeting upstream signaling networks remains an unmet clinical need. We present an integrated computational pipeline combining scRNA-seq re-analysis (GSE132771; n=3 IPF, n=3 normal donors), CellChat v2-based communication inference, and structure-based molecular docking of 105 bioactive natural compounds against CXCR4 (PDB: 3ODU; exhaustiveness=32). Single-cell analysis identified eight transcriptionally distinct populations, revealing a 65% increase in fibroblasts, a 67% reduction in epithelial cells, and exclusive emergence of CTHRC1+ pathological myofibroblasts in IPF. CellChat inferred 697 significant ligand-receptor interactions in IPF vs 502 in normal lung (+38.8%), with CXCL, SPP1, and MIF as the most prominently gained axes. Molecular docking identified Myricetin (CID 72322; -10.560 kcal/mol), Genistein (CID 65752; -9.973 kcal/mol), Glycyrrhetinic acid (CID 265237; -9.876 kcal/mol), and Licochalcone A (CID 5316743; -9.645 kcal/mol) as top CXCR4 binders, all surpassing AMD3100 (-9.471 kcal/mol). STRING network pharmacology confirmed CXCR4, CD44, MIF, SPP1, CXCL12, and ITGB1 as central hub proteins with universal extracellular accessibility. The convergence of transcriptomic, communicomic, and structural evidence on the CXCL/CXCR4 axis provides a mechanistically coherent, multi-layer computational rationale for CXCR4-targeted natural compound therapy in IPF.

papers.title: Halogen Identity Dictates Interphase Formation in Li Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: Designing a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) for Li metal batteries remains a major challenge. While LiF-rich interphases are widely considered optimal, alternative halide chemistries based on LiCl and LiBr remain largely unexplored. Here, we investigate how halogen identity (F, Cl, Br) in pyridinium-based additives governs interphase formation pathways in ether-based electrolytes. We observe that chlorinated and brominated additives result in minimal halide incorporation (~2.5%) despite targeting LiCl- and LiBr-rich SEIs. Instead, they undergo dimerization following initial reduction, forming redox-active dimers. Despite the release of LiCl and LiBr during electroreduction, their large solubility limits integration into the SEI. In contrast, fluorinated analogues undergo efficient defluorination without dimer formation, yielding LiF-rich, robust SEIs. This shift in reaction pathways, together with limited precipitation of LiCl and LiBr, leads to reduced interphase stability in systems containing chlorinated or brominated pyridinium additives, demonstrating that halogen identity dictates the dominant reaction pathways and resulting SEI stability.

papers.title: Visible light-controlled formation of G-quadruplexes
papers.abstract: Guanine (G)-quadruplexes are biologically relevant supramolecular assemblies formed by the π-stacking of hydrogen-bonded G-quartets around a coordinated metal cation. Their strong cooperativity affords exceptional stability but also limits dynamic control over their formation. Herein, we demonstrate visible-light regulation of G-quadruplex assembly through direct functionalization of guanosine with two state-of-the-art azo photoswitches: ortho-substituted azobenzene (osAZO) and arylazopyrazole (AAP). In the E configuration, both derivatives assemble into discrete D4-symmetric G-octamers, whereas photoisomerization to the Z state disrupts the quadruplex architecture. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal distinct switching efficiencies, with the AAP system exhibiting nearly quantitative reversible control. This study constitutes the first example of visible-light-controlled G-quadruplex formation via direct modification of the guanine scaffold and provides a foundation for cooperative, photoresponsive supramolecular materials.

papers.title: Well-Defined Molecular Potassium Catalysts for Mild and Selective Reduction of Carboxylic Acids by Hydrosilylation
papers.abstract: The selective transformation of carboxylic acids into alcohols remains a challenge, although many catalytic methods have been developed in recent years. Hydrosilylative reduction appeared as an attractive strategy in the presence of a metallic catalyst. In those processes, transition metals were usually employed for the catalyst design and the reactions often suffered from poor selectivity, limited functional group tolerance and requirement of elevated temperature. Here we report inexpensive and easy-to-make potassium-based catalysts that effectively promote the hydrosilylation of carboxylic acids to synthesize primary alcohols. The optimized catalyst could be produced in a gram scale in minutes from commercial potassium triethylborohydride and 18-crown-6. A broad range of aliphatic and aromatic carboxylic acids were employed and even challenging nitro and cyano groups could survive the hydrosilylation, although some limitations of the substrate scope were disclosed. Preliminary mechanistic studies proved a distinct mechanism of substrate activation from those reported in literature, through the isolation of a new adduct from the reaction of substrate and the potassium catalyst.

papers.title: Connectivity, Rigidity, and Gelation in Linker-Mediated Colloidal Networks
papers.abstract: On the path to gelation, attractive colloids develop network connectivity, mechanical rigidity, and slow dynamics. Herein, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to quantitatively characterize these processes using a coarse-grained model of patchy colloidal particles that form equilibrium networks through linker-mediated, reversible binding interactions. We find that linker-mediated gelation proceeds through a cascade of coupled but distinct structural, mechanical, and dynamical changes. Ordinary connectivity percolation first produces a system-spanning network, while rigidity percolation is associated with the formation of a percolating backbone characterized by an average colloid coordination number of approximately 2.4 and a percolating subset of colloids with coordination number of three or more. The rheologically defined gel point occurs at larger bond strengths and higher global coordination, where linker-mediated colloid–colloid connections persist over the deformation time scale. This separation between topological rigidity and rheological gelation is accompanied by a pronounced increase in the bond persistence time as gelation is approached, indicating that persistent effective network connections are required for macroscopic gel-like response. Together, these results show that connectivity is central to equilibrium, linker-mediated colloidal gelation, but that different connectivity measures govern ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation. These observations reinforce the idea that gelation in homogeneous networks of linked colloids can be understood as a connectivity–controlled, dynamical—mechanical transition, distinct from heterogeneous, nonequilibrium gels, where rigidity often arises from irreversible aggregation and kinetic arrest.

papers.title: World Models as a Diagnostic Framework for AI-Driven Scientific Design: Lessons from Molecular Generation
papers.abstract: Advances in machine intelligence for scientific design increasingly require systems that go beyond plausible generation to jointly represent, predict and plan within complex physical environments. We argue that the world-model concept from reinforcement learning provides a diagnostic lens for AIfor-science architectures and apply it to molecular generation as a detailed case study. A layered definition (strict, operational, broad) paired with a three-pillar decomposition (representation, dynamics, planning) reveals what each major family of generative methods captures about the molecular world and what it misses. Building on the Boltzmann-generators programme, we restate, in architectural terms, a familiar constraint on molecular learning—that the relevant target is an equilibrium distribution p(x) ∝ e−u(x)/kT rather than a single-state transition—and use it to motivate a dated, numerically bounded prediction: that scaling representation-only systems will not, on its own, close the dynamics gap, and that Boltzmann-aware primitives will be required.

papers.title: Insights into the micellar compartmentalization effect for photochemical synthesis
papers.abstract: Controlling which reaction components meet is a fundamental challenge in synthesis. Inspired by nature’s ability to compartmentalize, we use biomimetic micellar systems to control local concentrations and molecular encounters. By using simple, commercially available, selfassembling micelles, the localization of oxygen, photocatalyst and starting materials is controlled. On the contrary, no such control can be obtained in uniform, organic solvents. The preferred localizations of reaction components are revealed through MD simulations. Further, the size of the micellar system with all reaction components incorporated is investigated through diffusion NMR. A reduction in size of the micellar system is observed after reaction completion which is explained by major changes in the distribution of micelle loading. Time-resolved measurements confirmed the reduced encounters between molecular oxygen and photocatalyst (leading to quenching), with MD simulations further supporting a 75% decrease in encounters compared to a uniform distribution. These findings are investigated in the context of reaction design using the [2+2] photocycloaddition as a case study.

papers.title: Topology-Controlled Self-Assembly and Humidity-Adaptive Memristive Behaviour in Benzophosphole Nanohoops
papers.abstract: Controlling the condensed-state properties of p-conjugated macrocycles via molecular topology remains a fundamental challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Here, we report benzophosphole-embedded nanohoops as a heteroatom-doped platform where spatial configuration ( exo vs. endo ) directly governs molecular conformation, self-assembly, and electronic function. The endo -nanohoop adopts a unique outward-facing conformer that assembles into discrete tetrameric supramolecular cages stabilized by cooperative P=O···H 2 O interactions, which further evolve into hierarchical hollow nanobowl architectures exhibiting aggregation-induced emission enhancement (AIEE). More importantly, this topological differentiation generates distinct hydration microenvironments that dictate divergent memristive behaviours. The exo -analogues exhibit highly uniform volatile threshold switching arising from transient ion migration dynamics, enabling physical reservoir computing. In contrast, the endo -framework stabilizes a persistent bound-water network that facilitates proton-assisted ion transport and conductive filament stabilization, thereby supporting robust analog non-volatile memory operation. Leveraging the humidity-dependent switching characteristics of the exo system, we further demonstrate a bio-inspired neuromorphic sensor capable of real-time and noise-resistant respiratory monitoring. These findings establish a direct correlation between molecular topology, water confinement, and adaptive electronic functionality, providing a supramolecular strategy for designing intelligent organic memristive materials and sensing-memory integrated hardware.

papers.title: Atomic Environment Aware Lennard-Jones Parameterization for Electrostatic Embedding ML/MM Simulations
papers.abstract: Hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) methods have emerged as a powerful approach to multiscale modelling. Recent advances have focused on electrostatic embedding schemes, in which atoms in the ML region are polarized by the surrounding MM environment. Consequently, ML/MM electrostatics have been the subject of extensive study, whereas dispersion interactions remain comparatively underexplored. In analogy to established QM/MM practice, exchange-repulsion and dispersion interactions are commonly described using Lennard-Jones (LJ) 12-6 potentials with parameters transferred from existing force field libraries. However, such transferable parameters may be suboptimal for ML/MM interfaces, where consistency with the electrostatic embedding model is desirable. Here, we develop methodologies for deriving LJ parameters based on the exchange-hole dipole moment (XDM) model and the Fedorov polarizability scaling relation. Moreover, we propose a one-shot procedure for fine-tuning LJ parameters to experimental free energies. Focusing on the electrostatic machine learning embedding (EMLE) scheme, we show that these approaches yield EMLE models with competitive accuracy relative to conventional force fields and mechanical embedding schemes, while additionally providing chemically environmentaware LJ parameters. This capability offers a route to improved accuracy in demanding applications such as reactive modelling, where dispersion coefficients may depend strongly on the local chemical environment.

papers.title: Interplay between helical Δ/Λ chirality and the ligand-based asymmetric centre in cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes: Possibility for selective sensing of D-serine
papers.abstract: Cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes can possess Δ/Λ chirality and incorporate chiral ligands, enabling diverse photochemical applications, including sensing and asymmetric catalysis. Herein, two series of chiral iridium(III) complexes with or without a butyl group in their cyclometalated ligand framework were synthesised and characterised to clarify the role of the ligand framework in modulating the effects of Δ/Λ and ligand chirality on luminescence properties. The complexes were prepared by reacting enantiopure Δ- or Λ-[Ir( n BuBQ) 2 Cl] ( 1 ; n BuBQ = monodeprotonated 2-butyl-benzo[ h ]quinoline) and racemic [Ir(HBQ) 2 (CH 3 CN) 2 ]PF 6 ( 2 ; HBQ = monodeprotonated benzo[ h ]quinoline) with d - or l -serine. Precursor 1 exhibited higher substitutional lability than precursor 2 under comparable conditions because of its coordinatively unsaturated five-coordinate structure. Each precursor yielded four enantiomerically pure stereoisomers—Δ 1 - d , Λ 1 - d , Δ 1 - l , and Λ 1 - l ( 1 -series) and Δ 2 - d , Λ 2 - d , Δ 2 - l , and Λ 2 - l ( 2 -series)—enabling the systematic isolation and comparison of all possible stereoisomers in each series. Molecular structure analysis by single-crystal X-ray crystallography and theoretical calculations suggest intramolecular interactions between the serine ligand and n BuBQ framework in the 1 -series. In dichloromethane, the diastereomeric sets in the 1 -series ( i.e. , Δ 1 - d /Λ 1 - l and Λ 1 - d /Δ 1 - l ) showed much larger differences in emission intensity and radiative rate constant than those in the 2 -series. These results suggest that the butyl group in the ligand framework influences how differences arising from the combination of Δ/Λ chirality and d / l configuration of the coordinated serine ligand are manifested in the luminescence properties of the complexes. This work may provide a useful guideline for the ligand framework design toward selective luminescence sensing of d -serine.

papers.title: Strain-Induced Anisotropic Transport and Degeneracy Breaking in Monolayer and Bilayer Black Phosphorus: A DFT Based Analysis
papers.abstract: This study illustrates a DFT calculation of the electronic properties of unstrained monolayer and bilayer black phosphorus with 4% uniaxial strain. It uses the PBE functional theory on the GGA level, as well as optimized structure and band structures obtained from SCF calculations. The unstrained monolayer showed a direct bandgap of approximately 0.82 eV while the bilayer showed a reduced bandgap of 0.27 eV due to interlayer coupling. Under tensile strain (4%), the bilayer structure showed clear lifting of band degeneracy near the conduction band minimum, which was not observed for the monolayer. Modulation due to strain was more pronounced in the monolayer with the bandgap increased under tensile strain. Though the bilayer showed weaker tunability with stronger symmetry distortion effects. It is evident from the curvature analysis of the band that higher carrier mobility is preferred by monolayer BP, hence preferably balanced n-MOS and p-MOS active, while the bilayer is preferable for p-MOS operation under tensile strain. The observations confirm that strain and number of layers can be utilized to successfully engineer the black phosphorus's electronic properties towards nano-electronic and straintronic applications.

papers.title: A Hybrid Kinetic Monte Carlo Algorithm for ATRP: Coupling Deterministic Mean-Field Kinetics with Stochastic Chain Growth
papers.abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations of Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization (ATRP) suffer from severe computational stiffness due to the fast activation-deactivation equilibrium, which consumes the vast majority of computational resources and limits applicability to large-scale or complex architectures. In this work, we propose a Hybrid Mean-Field/kMC Algorithm designed to significantly enhance computational efficiency while maintaining microscopic accuracy. The core strategy involves decoupling the macroscopic concentration evolution from the microscopic chain growth. First, a stiff Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) solver is employed to pre-compute the macroscopic trajectories of radical and deactivator concentrations. Subsequently, within the Monte Carlo kernel, we introduce the concept of "Effective Activation Cycles." By sampling the number of monomer additions per activation event directly from a geometric distribution, the algorithm bypasses millions of null activation/deactivation loops. Furthermore, physical time is reconstructed from the macroscopic propagation rate, while termination events are stochastically re-coupled through a discrete Poisson counting process. This architecture restores microscopic event-level realizations that are inherently absent from the deterministic mean-field trajectory. Benchmarking against exact SSA demonstrates that the hybrid algorithm reproduces the time-resolved kinetic profiles, catalyst evolution, and molecular-weight distributions while achieving a computational speedup of at least 20-fold for sufficiently large simulated chain populations under standard kinetic conditions. To demonstrate its versatility, the framework is extended to computationally challenging regimes, including continuous catalyst regeneration and diffusion-controlled chain-length-dependent termination. A roadmap-robustness test further shows that a pseudo-linear ODE mapping can still synchronize the stochastic simulation even when microscopic kinetic corrections are imposed locally within the kMC kernel. These results establish the hybrid framework as an efficient and extensible simulation strategy for generating chain-resolved ATRP microstructural data.

papers.title: El Agente Seguro: An Agent for Chemical Safety
papers.abstract: Laboratory safety is becoming increasingly complex as chemical and materials research integrates automation, artificial intelligence, and data-driven experimentation. However, existing safety management approaches rely heavily on manual interpretation or on unconstrained language-model reasoning, which can lead to inconsistent and unreliable outcomes. In this work, we present El Agente Seguro, a graph-based multi-agent framework for safety planning and evaluation in chemical and materials laboratories. The system separates coordination and execution through a central safety director and a dependency-aware safety-solving graph, in which specialized subagents perform structured tasks with schema-constrained data exchange. This design enables controlled and data-driven safety reasoning across multiple layers, including chemical hazards, reaction risks, regulatory constraints, and opera-tional considerations. Benchmark evaluation across seven representative safety tasks demonstrates that El Agente Seguro achieves consistently strong performance relative to frontier general-purpose language models, while also providing more comprehensive and practically useful safety reasoning according to ranking-based evaluations. Beyond benchmark assessment, El Agente Seguro further demonstrates real-world safety capabilities including protocol-level hazard analysis, autonomous procedure modification, dual-use and prohibited chemical enforcement, multimodal SOP generation from laboratory images and experimental procedures, and computationally guided reaction safety prediction through integration with external scientific agents. These results show that structured, dependency-aware multi-agent workflows can improve context-sensitive safety reasoning beyond unconstrained language-model inference alone. Overall, El Agente Seguro establishes a scalable, extensible and practically deployable framework for intelligent laboratory safety into both human-operated and autonomous research environments.

papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for High-Rate Electrochemical Fingerprinting of a Model Fe2O3 Impurity in LiFePO4 Cathodes
papers.abstract: Rapid screening of impurity-related performance variation in LiFePO 4 (LFP) cathodes is challenging when low-to-moderate impurity levels are not readily resolved by structural characterization alone. Here, Fe 2 O 3 was introduced as an externally added model impurity, and 158 assembled Li half-cell records, including 156 valid high-rate traces spanning nine nominal addition levels, were evaluated under 10C cycling stress. Interpretable descriptors captured initial and end-of-test capacity, voltage hysteresis, polarization ratio, capacity-retention and energy-efficiency trends, and knee-cycle behavior. Because the model impurity is largely electrochemically inactive within the LFP cathode voltage window, first-cycle capacity was treated as an explicit shortcut rather than hidden within the machine-learning workflow. A naive inactive-dilution equation failed to recover the nominal addition level (R 2 = −2.044), whereas a nonlinear capacity-only model reached R 2 = 0.689. Long-term descriptors without initial capacity retained predictive power (R 2 = 0.608), and the full feature set achieved an out-of-fold R 2 of 0.865, RMSE of 2.873, and MAE of 1.889. Residual analysis further increased R 2 from 0.689 to 0.740 after long-term descriptors were added to the capacity baseline. Thus, initial capacity is the dominant information carrier but not a physically sufficient estimator. Polarization, efficiency decay, retention curvature, and knee behavior provide additional impurity-sensitive fingerprints. The resulting workflow offers a transparent, protocol-specific screening layer that complements XRD-based phase checks without claiming chemistry-agnostic impurity quantification.

papers.title: Virtual Library Generation, Drug-Likeness Filtering, and Docking of Taloside-Based Galectin-3 Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Galectin-3 (Gal-3) is a validated oncology target whose carbohydrate-recognition domain (CRD) is amenable to inhibition by taloside-based glycomimetics. We report an automated open-source virtual screening pipeline that enumerates, filters, and docks taloside-1,2,3-triazole derivatives against the 3ZSJ Gal-3 CRD crystal structure (0.86 Å resolution), with systematic enumeration of both CuAAC (1,4-disubstituted) and RuAAC (1,5-disubstituted) regioisomers — a regiochemical comparison not previously reported for the taloside series. Starting from one azide-functionalised taloside scaffold and eight aromatic alkyne building blocks, 16 geometrically verified products were generated (8 per regioisomer), of which 14 passed carbohydrate-adjusted Lipinski filters and were free of PAINS alerts. All 14 compounds were docked successfully (AutoDock Vina). The docking setup was validated by redocking the 57I taloside inhibitor (PDB 7RGX, bearing the same 2-nitrobenzoyl-O2 pharmacophore as the scaffold) against the cleaned 3ZSJ receptor: the top-ranked pose reproduced the crystal binding mode with a centroid distance of 1.39 Å. By combined docking–lead score, the 4-fluorophenyl CuAAC derivative (Vina −6.14 kcal/mol, combined score 0.922) and the unsubstituted phenyl CuAAC derivative (Vina −5.73 kcal/mol, lead score 0.905) emerge as co-equal priority candidates; the 0.41 kcal/mol Vina margin between them is within the scoring function’s expected error and should not be used to rank them experimentally. A scoring-sensitivity analysis confirms that the apparent 1,4-CuAAC preference in the combined ranking is partly an artifact of the binary synthetic-accessibility (SA) term: with the SA term removed or replaced by a standardised Ertl SA score, the two co-equal leads are unchanged but the top-three CuAAC sweep collapses (the 4-fluorophenyl RuAAC isomer rises to rank 3). An Asn164 closest-contact difference (3.11 Å in 4F_CuAAC vs 3.50 Å in Ph_CuAAC) is noted only as a hypothesis-generating observation; C–F is a weak H-bond acceptor and Vina does not explicitly score C–F···O contacts. Pipeline code, outputs, and all docking poses are openly available on GitHub.

papers.title: Towards libraries of different ultrasmall amorphous silica cage topologies
papers.abstract: Cage topology controlled at the nanometer length scale is expected to enable original functionalities, e.g., in catalysis and therapeutics. Cages are fundamental structural motifs of clathrates and their topological duals, Frank-Kasper phases, and are constituents of mesoporous silica frameworks. However, with one exception, they have not been synthesized as discrete particles. By varying reactant ratios of surfactant, oil, and silane, we report the discovery of 5(12)6(2) and 5(12)6(8) amorphous silica polyhedra, each coexisting with the previously identified 5(12) cage, using combined cryo-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) and single-particle reconstruction (SPR). Notably, the 5(12)6(8) polyhedron represents a topology not previously observed in mesoporous silica frameworks. Control over structural features is demonstrated, and insights into cage formation mechanisms are provided. Structural outcomes are summarized in a ternary morphology diagram alongside prior results, bridging serendipitous discovery and intentional design of silica cages displaying a level of control over silica polymerization rivaling nature.

papers.title: Single-Fluorophore FLIM Multiplexing and STED Nanoscopy in Live Cells with a Hydroxyl-Tunable Near-Infrared aza-BODIPY Platform
papers.abstract: Fluorophores that simultaneously enable stimulated emission depletion (STED) nanoscopy and fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) multiplexing within a single spectral channel remain scarce, particularly within a single, synthetically accessible scaffold. Here we report a family of hydroxyl-functionalised 3,5-tert-butyl BF2-azadipyrromethene fluorophores as a synthetically accessible platform for advanced live-cell imaging. We establish that hydroxyl content determines subcellular localisation, and that asymmetric derivatives distribute across organelles of distinct physicochemical character, generating two resolvable lifetime populations. This enables discrimination of lipid droplets and membrane-rich organelles using a single fluorophore, without genetic manipulation or multiple probes. All derivatives are compatible with 775 nm STED depletion, enabling super-resolved visualisation of membrane architectures. Further sulfonation of one derivative affords a water-soluble plasma membrane probe with robust photostability that retains STED and FLIM capabilities, demonstrating the post-synthetic versatility of this scaffold. This work introduces a single-fluorophore approach for targeting and resolving complex cellular environments via concurrent nanoscopy and intrinsic lifetime-based sensing.

papers.title: Sequence-guided engineering of a bacterial diterpene synthase induces further cyclization
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering serves as a powerful tool in biocatalysis, enabling the development of enzymes with improved stability, activity, and specificity for a range of academic, industrial, and pharmaceutical applications. However, a limited understanding of sequence–structure–function relationships in terpene synthases, the enzymes that form the complex polycyclic hydrocarbon skeletons of terpenoid natural products, presents a major challenge in predicting and engineering the products of terpene synthases. In this study, we investigated the product profiles of the first two bacterial variediene synthases, OdVS from Olivibacter domesticus and PsVS from Prauserella shujinwangii, and found that they share some products with the bacterial phomopsene synthase, PmS from Allokutzneria albata, despite low sequence similarity. Thirteen diterpenes were isolated and structurally elucidated including three previously unreported compounds. A series of variants of OdVS, PsVS, and PmS were constructed by targeting conserved residues around the active site and aided in the identification of key residues that help control the cyclization pathway. Ultimately, mutation of a single residue, PsVSY86L, was found to switch the major product of PsVS from the tricyclic variediene to the tetracyclic phomopsene.

papers.title: Enhanced Line Search Improves Robustness and Efficiency of Pose Sampling in Protein-Ligand Docking
papers.abstract: Physics-based protein–ligand docking critically depends on efficient pose sampling, yet established sampling and local refinement algorithms can be inefficient and unstable in the highly nonconvex energy landscapes characteristic of protein–ligand interactions. To address this limitation, we introduce an enhanced local optimization strategy based on curved line search (CLS) and integrate it into AutoDock Vina, resulting in Vina_CLS. The proposed method enables more flexible step-size selection during local refinement and improves convergence in challenging regions of the energy landscape. Across benchmarks on the PDBbind refined set and the LEADS-PEP dataset, Vina_CLS consistently outperforms the baseline, exhibiting greater robustness by solving more docking problems, as well as improved efficiency through reduced function and gradient evaluations and shorter runtimes. These gains translate into practical benefits, including more frequent identification of difficult-to-access local minima, enhanced redocking accuracy, and increased recovery of near-native poses. Together, these results demonstrate that improved local optimization can substantially enhance docking performance, highlighting an important, underexplored opportunity to advance structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Reveal Convergent PI3K/AKT and MMP9 Mechanisms of Ginkgo biloba Bioactive Compounds in Aging and Cancer
papers.abstract: Background : Aging and cancer share converging molecular drivers, oxidative stress, dysregulated PI3K/AKT and MAPK signaling, ECM remodelling, and impaired apoptosis, yet most natural-product investigations interrogate these axes in isolation. Ginkgo biloba L. is a phytochemically rich source of flavonoids, biflavones, and terpene trilactones with documented pleiotropic bioactivities, but no integrated study has mapped its bioactives across the convergent aging–cancer interface. Methods : We applied a unified network pharmacology and molecular docking pipeline to fourteen G. biloba bioactives (anti-aging panel A1–A7; anticancer panel C1–C7), with ginkgolide A and bilobalide deliberately included in both panels for cross-panel benchmarking. ADME, drug-likeness, and computational toxicity (ProTox-3) were profiled. Targets were predicted via tri-platform consensus (SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, NetInfer), yielding 1,496 unique human proteins. Sub-networks of the top 20 consensus targets were analyzed in Cytoscape v3.20.3 using eleven CytoHubba centrality algorithms. Sixteen hub proteins were docked using AutoDock Vina; receptor stereochemistry was validated by Ramachandran analysis. Results : Network analysis identified GSK3β, XDH, ALOX5, AXL, and MCL1 as anti-aging hubs and TP53, VEGFA, MMP9, MAPK14, PI3Kα, EGFR, NR4A1, BRCA1, and NOX4 as anticancer hubs. Strikingly, XDH, GSK3β, NOX4, MAPK14, and AKT1 emerged in both networks, defining a convergent aging–cancer interface. Ginkgolide A achieved exceptional predicted PI3Kα affinity (ΔG = −10.18 kcal/mol), within a comparable predicted range to the FDA-approved inhibitor alpelisib (−10.3 kcal/mol, same methodology). Kaempferol bound MMP9 at −9.008 kcal/mol, exceeding the reference inhibitor batimastat (−7.6 kcal/mol). Biflavones isoginkgetin and ginkgetin showed the highest predicted XDH and ALOX5 binding among aging targets. Cross-panel docking of identical molecules (A4/C4, A5/C7) revealed target-class specific selectivity profiles. All priority compounds fell within WHO toxicity classes V–VI. Conclusions : This study provides the first integrated computational evidence that G. biloba bioactives may modulate convergent aging-cancer signaling through high-affinity engagement of PI3K/AKT, MMP9, MAPK14, and XDH/MCL1 axes, prioritizing ginkgolide A, kaempferol, and biflavones for experimental validation.

papers.title: Modelling the Soil Dissipation Kinetics of Small Molecules
papers.abstract: Understanding the metabolic fate of small molecules is central to risk assessment and to rational design of plant protection products, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and food additives. In environmental systems, dissipation is governed by kinetic processes operating across soil, water, and other compartments. For chemicals released into the environment, especially active ingredients of plant protection products, assessing soil persistence is an essential regulatory requirement. The ability to predict soil persistence, ideally in advance of commissioning experiments, is highly valuable for identifying novel active ingredients for plant protection products. Here, we introduce machine‑learning models that predict the full time-course of small‑molecule dissipation in soil. These models are explicitly constrained by mechanistic assumptions encoded as ordinary differential equations (ODEs). By design, this physics‑constrained parameterisation enforces physical plausibility. To the best of our knowledge, our models are the first to predict soil dissipation kinetics from molecular structure using a constrained time-course framework. We found that this framework almost always outperformed a conventional QSAR approach in predicting pre-fitted kinetic parameters. We further investigated the incorporation of soil metadata, i.e., predefined and experimentally measured soil parameters, into the model, with mixed results. Our framework supports screening and design decisions by linking molecular properties and soil metadata to predicted environmental lifetimes and dissipation profiles.

papers.title: LLM-Assembled Multiscale Cascades for High-Throughput Screening: the case of Thermoelectric Materials
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening workflows often rank materials with a sequence of filters, but a single sequence can hide how strongly the final ranking depends on the chosen physical approximations. Here a multiscale cascade means an ordered workflow in which outputs from electronic, lattice, microstructural, uncertainty, and device-level models are passed from one layer to the next; the layers are theory or surrogate-model steps, not layers of LLMs. We use a large language model (LLM) as a workflowdesign assistant to assemble candidate model stacks from the literature, after which the equations, code, and physical handoffs are inspected and implemented by the author. The test case is thermoelectric screening, where the dimensionless figure of merit ZT = S2σT/(κe + κL) combines the Seebeck coefficient S, electrical conductivity σ, electronic thermal conductivity κe, and lattice thermal conductivity κL. Two independently assembled eight-layer cascades are applied to the same 314-compound vacancy-containing chalcogenide library. LLM1 uses Fan–Migdal band-gap renormalisation, a Kubo–DMFT transport surrogate, and a literature-trained Gaussian process for κL. LLM2 replaces those three early layers with Bose-Einstein band-gap renormalisation, acoustic-phonon Boltzmann transport, and a Debye–Callaway integral. The common four-stage screen sends 15 compounds to full evaluation in each cascade: LLM1 selects tellurides headed by CuAlTe2 (ZTpeak = 8.61), whereas LLM2 selects nonoverlapping sulfides headed by CuPb2S4 (ZTpeak = 0.325). The absolute LLM1 values are not claimed as validated performance forecasts: CuAlTe2 is literature-supported as a promising bulk thermoelectric, but reported and expected values are closer to ZT ≲ 2 than to 8.6. This study underscores the importance of transparently comparing multiple workflow designs to understand the sensitivity and reliability of high-throughput screening outcomes in materials discovery.

papers.title: pH-Dependent Free Energies of Insulin Fibrillation from Protonation Ensemble Statistics
papers.abstract: Protonation equilibria govern the pH-dependent stability of protein aggregates, yet their thermodynamic implications remain difficult to quantify. Here, we establish a direct connection between site-unresolved protonation statistics and pH-dependent free energy differences within a semi-grand canonical framework. Using constant-pH simulations of insulin assemblies from monomers to octamers, we show that the differential protonation response relative to the isolated monomer is directly related to fibril stability. Integration of this response reveals a non-monotonic free energy landscape with a crossover near pH ≈ 5.5–6 separating distinct electrostatic regimes. While the crossover is independent of fibril size, stabilization increases systematically with aggregate size, demonstrating cooperative proton-coupled interactions in the fibrillar state. These results show that pH-dependent stability is encoded in site-unresolved titration curves, while site-resolved analysis provides mechanistic interpretation. The present work demonstrates that the semi-grand canonical framework can determine the pH effects on equilibria in biomolecular systems from protonation statistics.

papers.title: OrbitChem: An Integrated Machine Learning and Physics-Based Platform for Space-Grade Molecular Design and Spacecraft Material Qualification
papers.abstract: The design of molecular absorbers for space-based photovoltaic applications demands simultaneous optimisation across quantum-chemical properties (bandgap, absorption efficiency), spacecraft material qualification standards (outgassing, radiation stability, thermal cycling fatigue), and mission-specific environmental constraints. No existing computational tool addresses these three domains in a single integrated pipeline. Here we present OrbitChem, a freely accessible platform that connects ExtraTrees-based machine learning molecular screening to physics-based spacecraft qualification, producing a unified Type II Civilization Score — a novel composite metric ranking organic photovoltaic (OPV) candidates for space solar energy harvesting at Kardashev Type II civilisation scale. Applied to 12 molecular candidates spanning acenes, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, perylene diimides, polyimides, and fluoropolymers, OrbitChem correctly identifies five candidates — Hexacene (Score 84.5), Coronene (85.5), Pentacene (86.0), Perylene (75.8), and PEEK ether monomer (82.6) — that simultaneously pass NASA MSFC-SPEC-1238 outgassing (TML < 0.11%, CVCM < 0.04%), achieve radiation stability ratings of Excellent at LEO (≥99% tensile retention over 50 kRad), and maintain thermal cycling safety factors ≥ 2.0×. The SpaceChem-AI sub-module achieves ExtraTrees R2 = 0.9959 for bandgap prediction, outperforming XGBoost (+0.0022 R2), LightGBM (+0.0147 R2), and linear models on an 8-model benchmark. OrbitChem is freely available at huggingface.co/spaces/chemenovausa/OrbitChem.

papers.title: Mo‑induced framework reorganization in ZSM‑5 nanopillars for stable oxidative methane coupling
papers.abstract: ZSM‑5 nanopillars (Si/Al = 36) were synthesized under hydrothermal conditions and post‑synthetically treated with Na2MoO4 to introduce atomically dispersed Mo species in the framework structure. Structural characterization (XRD, TEM, MAS NMR) reveals a framework reorganization upon Mo incorporation, including a space‑group transition (Pnma → P21/n), unit‑cell expansion, and a pronounced decrease in silanol defects. The results show about 75% reduction in silanol site density, consistent with silanol healing and partial dealumination while preserving the nanopillared morphology of the Mo-containing ZSM-5. Pyridine and low‑temperature CO‑probe FTIR indicate a redistribution and slight strengthening of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites. The Mo‑containing ZSM‑5 nanopillars compare to parent ZSM-5 nanopillars showed enhance performance in the oxidative coupling of methane (OCM), achieving higher CH4 conversion (15% vs. 11%), markedly improved C2+ selectivity (70% vs. 21%), and increased ethylene fraction at 775 °C, while maintaining stable activity and selectivity over 45 h on stream. The results demonstrate that combining morphology control with targeted Mo‑induced framework reorganization is an effective strategy to tune acidity and obtain structurally stable zeolite nanopillars for OCM application.

papers.title: Catalytic Allylation Coupling between Equimolar Aldehydes and Alkenes via sp3 C‒H Activation
papers.abstract: We here report a catalytic allylation of aldehydes with alkenes under equimolar conditions and visible-light irradiation. The reaction is enabled by an ion-pair electron donor–acceptor complex catalyst formed from a triphenylsilyl-substituted thiophosphoric imide (TPI) and 4-methylquinoline, in combination with a chromium chloride catalyst and a boroxine additive. This catalytic system accelerates the generation of a TPI-derived thiyl radical hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalyst, suppresses product-derived HAT, and enables equimolar coupling between diverse aldehydes and alkenes, including functionalized substrates. This strategy provides a preactivation-free platform for C–C bond formation from sp³ C–H-containing alkenes.

papers.title: Conformation and Coordination Mode Switching in Boron Complexes of trans-Vinylene Bridged [40]Tetrathiaoctaphyrin and [60]Hexathiadodecaphyrin
papers.abstract: Porphyrinoids constitute fascinating molecular platforms for exploration of concepts in coordination chemistry and electron delocalisation. Here, we report a diboron complex of a modified figure-eight octaphyrinoid with an unsual coordination motif, as well as the largest, fully characterised, BODIPY complex of a coremodified, trans-vinylene-bridged [60]dodecaphyrinoid, retaining its parent, open-form geometry.

papers.title: Axial dysprosium cyclopentadienyl-amide single-molecule magnets with hysteresis up to 92 kelvin
papers.abstract: Molecules showing magnetic memory effects at high temperatures could be used in high-density data storage devices. A magnetic hysteresis temperature ( T H ) of 100 K has been achieved for a near-linear dysprosium bis(amide)-alkene single-molecule magnet (SMM), and a bent dysprosium cyclopentadienyl-amide SMM has shown T H = 73 K. However, both these complexes exhibit fast magnetic relaxation at lower temperatures compared to dysprosium bis(cyclopentadienyl) SMMs. Here we report the synthesis of two highly axial dysprosium cyclopentadienyl-amide SMMs, [Dy{N(Si i Pr 3 ) 2 }(Cp R )][Al{OC(CF 3 ) 3 } 4 ] ( 1-Dy , Cp R = Cp ttt , C 5 H 2 t Bu 3 -1,2,4; 2-Dy , Cp R = Cpʹʹʹ, C 5 H 2 (SiMe 3 ) 3 -1,2,4). We find T H = 91 K for 1-Dy and 92 K for 2-Dy ; ab initio calculations on 1-Dy show that magnetic relaxation is controlled by a combination of short dysprosium-ligand distances, a near-linear N–Dy–Cpʹʹʹ centroid angle, and constrained vibrational modes. Together, this work demonstrates that dysprosium SMMs with large T H values can be achieved with a judicious combination of π-aromatic and σ-donor ligands.

papers.title: Ferrocene Meets Heterocycles: Modern Approaches to Direct C–C and C–X Bond Formation
papers.abstract: Ferrocene-derived heterocycles combine the unique redox and structural properties of the metallocene unit with the broad functionality of heterocyclic motifs, making them highly attractive for applications in catalysis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science. This review summarizes heterocyclization reactions of ferrocene derivatives leading to direct ferrocene–heterocycle bond formation without additional linkers. The discussed approaches are classified into two main groups: single-bond-linked systems and annulated ferrocenyl heterocycles. A wide range of synthetic methodologies is covered, including cyclocondensations, multicomponent reactions, aza-Wittig processes, “click”-type reactions, and transition-metal-catalyzed transformations, primarily based on readily available ferrocenyl precursors such as aldehydes, ketones, and chalcones. Particular attention is given to the construction of nitrogen-, oxygen-, and chalcogen-containing heterocycles. Overall, the reviewed strategies highlight the synthetic versatility of ferrocene and current trends toward more efficient and structurally diverse ferrocenyl heterocycles, providing a useful basis for the development of new functional molecules.

papers.title: Photolysis of Triclosan in the Presence of Polyethylene Plastic
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution represents one of the greatest anthropogenic threats to the environment. Plastic debris may absorb potentially toxic compounds of low water solubility in aqueous environments. Aquatic plastic pollution may transfer absorbed compounds to aquatic animals causing premature death. Here we examine how polyethylene (PE) plastic grocery bags affect the photolysis of triclosan (TCS, 5-chloro-2-(2,4-dichlorophenoxy) phenol) when it is absorbed on the surface of the PE in aqueous solution. The photolytic conversion of TCS to 2,8-dichlorodibenzodioxin (2,8-DCDD) is up to ten times faster on plastic than in solution when irradiated at 300 nm and 290 times faster when irradiated at 350 nm. Under these conditions, 2,8-DCDD is formed from the protonated form of TCS unlike in solution where 2,8-DCDD is formed from the deprotonated anion. Quantum mechanical calculations suggest the photolytic transformation of TCS to 2,8-DCDD is initiated by a decrease in phenol pka from 8.1 to -1.7 in the S1 excited state of TCS which initiates the cyclization reaction to form 2,8-DCDD on the surface of the PE. PE is the most abundant form of plastic found in the environment and the most common form of PE are grocery bags. TCS was chosen as a model compound for these studies given its widespread occurrence in the environment, its photolysis in solution has been studied extensively under a variety of conditions.

papers.title: Room-Temperature Luminescent Lanthanide Ionic Liquids for Optical Tagging and Anti-Counterfeiting
papers.abstract: The development of robust, scalable materials for next-generation anti-counterfeiting technologies requires the integration of unique optical signatures with practical processability. Here, we report a modular platform of room-temperature luminescent ionic liquids based on trihexyl(tetradecyl)phosphonium salts of lanthanide tris(dipicolinate) complexes (Ln = Eu, Tb, Dy, Sm). These materials combine the sharp, line-like f–f emission characteristics of lanthanides with the inherent advantages of ionic liquids, including negligible vapor pressure, high miscibility, and facile formulation. Crucially, the liquid nature enables direct volumetric mixing of discrete emitters, allowing rapid generation of binary, ternary, and quaternary systems with dense, information-rich emission spectra. The intrinsic emission signatures of each lanthanide are retained in the liquid state, while mixture systems exhibit enhanced spectral complexity without requiring additional synthetic steps. Thermal and calorimetric analyses confirm the preservation of stable room-temperature liquid behaviour, supporting compatibility with established processing and printing technologies. This approach decouples spectral complexity from synthetic complexity, establishing a scalable route to tailorable photonic security materials. The concept of “complexity through simplicity” introduced here offers significant potential for advanced optical tagging, secure identification, and functional soft-material design.

papers.title: PyChemTools: An Open-Source Workflow for Computational Chemistry, Spectral Analysis, and Reaction Modelling Huma Basheer, Imran A. Khan
papers.abstract: The growing integration of computational chemistry, spectroscopy, and cheminformatics in modern chemical research demands accessible, reproducible, and user-friendly analytical tools. Herein, we present PyChemTools, an open-source collection of Python-based repositories designed to support quantum-chemical output analysis, spectral annotation, scientific visualization, and cheminformatics workflows. The ecosystem comprises four principal modules: HI_ORCA_HI, for ORCA output parsing, thermochemical analysis, and reaction-energy profile generation; IR_spectra_annotator, for infrared spectral visualization and automated peak annotation; Universal Spectra Controller, for mass spectrometric (MS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR),QSAR_CT_HUMA, for descriptor-based quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) and cheminformatics investigations. Each repository was developed to reduce manual data-processing overhead through automated analysis, graphical rendering, and accessible graphical user interfaces (GUIs). Representative applications demonstrate utility in reaction-mechanism investigation, spectral interpretation, and computational chemistry workflows1. All repositories are openly available on GitHub, enabling the broader community to access, adapt, and extend these tools. This communication describes the functionality, design rationale, and scientific utility of the PyChemTools ecosystem with the aim of promoting wider adoption of open-source computational resources in the chemical sciences.

papers.title: Predicted cohesive properties of a TATB polymer-bonded insensitive high explosive
papers.abstract: Polymer-bonded explosives (PBXs) are composite materials whose structure-property relationships are poorly understood due to their complex microstructure. Microstructural adhesion between the energetic molecular crystals and the polymer binder in a PBX affects key properties including mechanical strength, safety, and aging characteristics, but is difficult to measure experimentally. To this end, we develop a molecular dynamics (MD) modeling framework to predict the cohesive properties of a prototypical PBX based on the insensitive high explosive TATB (1,3,5-triamino-2,4,6-trinitrobenzene) and a fluoropolymer binder. The MD framework rests on two key capabilities: (1) general protocols to construct MD simulations of crystal-polymer and crystal-crystal interfaces in low-symmetry materials, and (2) a numerically robust approach to compute the surface and interface energies. Formal analysis of the surface energy equation shows that its direct evaluation is poorly conditioned for systems involving polymers. In this respect, we adopt a regression-based approach for computing surface energies and extend it to interfaces. Application to a TATB-fluoropolymer PBX reveals several energetic drivers, including thermodynamic drivers for grain coarsening and a greater propensity for TATB crystallites to adhere to each other than to the polymer binder. These data indicate that the thermodynamic landscape governing formulation design and aging of PBXs is complex and involves additional variables besides crystal-polymer adhesion. While the present study focuses on explosives, the MD methodology is general and can be readily adapted to model other material systems involving low-symmetry crystals, including organic electronics, pharmaceuticals, and advanced polymer composites.

papers.title: Towards Sustainable Nitrogen-Containing Polymer Building Blocks: a New Pathway to Bio-Based Polyamide 8 and 9
papers.abstract: The synthesis of nitrogen-containing polymer building blocks from renewable resources remains a major challenge in polymer chemistry. Herein, we report an effective four-step synthetic route to linear amino acid monomers starting from the bio-based terminal fatty acid derivatives methyl 10-undecenoate and methyl 9-decenoate. The approach combines Wacker oxidation, oxime formation, Beckmann rearrangement, and final hydrolysis to afford AB-type monomers suitable for the synthesis of linear polyamides PA 8 and PA 9. Each transformation was individually optimized with respect to conversion, selectivity, and catalyst efficiency, enabling the Wacker oxidation to proceed with 93% conversion and 92% selectivity at a palladium loading of only 0.2 mol%, while the subsequent Lewis-acid-catalyzed Beckmann rearrangement afforded the desired amide with 96% selectivity. The final hydrolysis proceeded under basic conditions, avoiding side product formation. Importantly, the complete sequence was demonstrated on a 30 g scale for both substrates with only minor purification operations between steps, highlighting the robustness and scalability of the process. Overall, this work provides an efficient and adaptable pathway toward fully renewable, long-chain polyamide precursors, contributing to more sustainable strategies for nitrogen-containing polymer materials.

papers.title: Operando Visualisation of Cathode Water Management in Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysers Using Synchrotron X-ray Radiography
papers.abstract: Optimising water management in proton exchange membrane water electrolysers (PEMWEs) is essential for reducing the levelised cost of hydrogen and ensuring safe operation, as it influences both water vapour carryover and hydrogen crossover. In this study, we established an operando synchrotron X-ray radiography system to visualise the liquid water distribution and dynamics within the cathode gas diffusion layer. Quantitative analysis of the time-resolved radiographic data revealed that the cathode water behaviour is primarily governed by current density through its effect on electro-osmotic water supply and hydrogen-gas-driven water removal, together with cell temperature through liquid-vapour phase transitions. At lower temperatures, liquid water preferentially accumulates beneath the flow-field ribs owing to localised current density and limited evaporative drying. Increasing temperature enhanced evaporation, suppressed liquid water accumulation, and shifted the dominant transport mode from continuous to pulsating water transport. The results indicate that evaporation-condensation processes play a critical role in regulating cathode water dynamics. These findings provide mechanistic insight into cathode water management and its implications for water vapour carryover and hydrogen crossover in PEMWE systems.

papers.title: Catalytic Alkoxysilylation of (Hetero)Aryl Bromides with tert-Butyl Alkoxysilyldiazenes
papers.abstract: Aryl(alkoxy)silanes are valuable building blocks in organic synthesis and materials science, yet their preparation often relies on stoichiometric organometallic reagents or transition metal-catalyzed methods. Herein, we report a catalytic and transition metal-free alkoxysilylation of (hetero)aryl bromides using tert -butyl-substituted alkoxysilyldiazenes ( t Bu–N=N–SiMe 2 (OR)) as silylating reagents and t BuONa as catalytic initiator. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions and provides direct access to a broad range of functionalized aryl(alkoxy)silanes. Competition experiments and DFT calculations reveal that increasing the electrophilicity of silicon through alkoxy substitution accelerates the key C(sp 2 )–Si bond-forming step relative to SiMe 3 transfer. This enhanced reactivity significantly broadens the substrate scope, enabling the efficient alkoxysilylation of challenging hindered aryl bromides and those bearing electrophilic functional groups.

papers.title: Tricomponent α-Carbonyl Alkylation by a Cobalt-Catalyzed Polar–Radical and Radical–Polar Crossover Cascade
papers.abstract: Regioselective introduction of functional groups at distal positions of carbonyl compounds remains a significant challenge, often necessitating inefficient stepwise routes to access synthetically and medicinally important targets such as 1,6-aminocarbonyls. Direct radical α-functionalization of carbonyls can unlock broad scope strategies for position-specific installation of diverse functionalities and can address the inherent limitations of enolate-based approaches. However, the development of radical αfunctionalization has remained underexplored due to the scarcity of catalytic systems capable of effi-ciently promoting both the direct generation of α-carbonyl radicals and the regioselective construction of distally functionalized frameworks. We report herein the development of a tricomponent cobalt(salen)-catalyzed α-alkylation of carbonyl compounds, providing a direct approach to 1,6-aminocarbonyl frameworks from diverse unactivated carbonyls and aromatic amines. The reaction proceeds through a cobalt(salen)-catalyzed sequence involving polar–radical crossover (PRC), which enables direct for-mation of α-carbonyl radicals, and radical–polar crossover (RPC), which mediates regiospecific installa-tion of the distal amino group. The method tolerates a wide range of carbonyl substrates, including αsubstituted aldehydes that are typically prone to deleterious hydrogen atom transfer from the reactive carbonyl group. Mechanistic studies reveal the roles of cobalt(salen) O- and C-enolates in the PRC step and the involvement of α-carbonyl radicals in enabling the RPC process.

papers.title: Sulfur-anchored, high-loading L10-PtCo intermetallic catalysts for durable heavy-duty PEM fuel cells
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) for heavy-duty transport require cathode catalysts that combine high platinum utilization with exceptional resistance to electrochemical degradation, yet the failure mechanisms of intermetallic alloys under realistic operating conditions remain poorly resolved. In heavy-duty applications, high Pt loadings are further required to maintain thin catalyst layers, thereby enhancing mass transport and overall cell performance. Here we report a high-loaded (> 50 wt% Pt) L10-PtCo nanocatalyst on sulfurdoped carbon that couples strong metal-support interactions with an ordered intermetallic lattice to deliver both high oxygen reduction activity and outstanding stability under fuel-cellrelevant conditions. The catalyst reaches a mass activity of 1.28 A/mgPt at 0.9 V and, after 30,000 accelerated stress-test cycles, retains nearly its full electrochemically active surface area with only 2% loss, while substantially outperforming commercial PtCo/C and Pt/C benchmarks. In a 50 cm2 membrane electrode assembly, the catalyst translates this intrinsic reactivity into practical device performance. The sulfur-doped carbon-support also markedly suppresses carbon corrosion under start-up/shut-down-relevant conditions, limiting carbon mass loss to about 11%, versus 30% for PtCo/C. Operando small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering measurements in a working PEMFC, combined with online inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy, reveals the structural origin of this durability: suppressed Pt dissolution, delayed Co leaching, and mitigation of agglomeration. These measurements further uncover a coalescence-induced dealloying pathway and identify an anisotropic lattice evolution in the L10-core during potential cycling. These results provide mechanistic insight into degradation processes in intermetallic catalysts under operating conditions and establish design rules for durable PEMFC cathodes by stabilizing lattice structure and mitigating transition metal dissolution.

papers.title: Dissecting the Viral Large Terminase: Structural Evolution and Prospects for
papers.abstract: Some double-stranded DNA viruses utilize a powerful molecular motor to package DNA 13 into their capsids to liquid-crystalline density. The motor is composed of a portal complex and 14 large and small terminase subunits. The enzymatic component of the motor is the large terminase 15 that has two functional domains necessary for ATP hydrolysis and DNA cleavage. Large terminase 16 amino acid sequences are highly divergent, but their overall structural architecture and function 17 are conserved across tailed bacteriophages and herpesviruses. Because there are limited antiviral 18 drugs for herpesvirus infections, and these exclusively target the viral DNA polymerase, cross-19 resistance is of high concern. Therefore, the DNA packaging motor is being investigated as an 20 alternative drug target. In this review, we discuss the past and recent genetic, biochemical, and 21 structural research on large terminases that has illuminated their role in DNA packaging and 22 potential as a candidate for antiviral drug targeting. 23

papers.title: A hidden strain memory programs C2+ product branching in reconstructed copper electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: The lattice-scale structural basis of ethylene-to-C2+ alcohol branching in copper-catalyzed CO2 electroreduction remains difficult to quantify with conventional probes. Here, we show that weakly supervised, attention-based multiple-instance learning, trained on TEM image sets labeled by catalyst-state rather than product-selectivity or pixel-level annotations, reveals lattice features beyond manual inspection or ensemble-averaged characterization. The model decodes an electroreduction-imprinted strain memory, where diffuse εyy distortion contracts into localized islands, and its normalized attention-gated area fraction predicts ethylene-to-C2+ alcohol branching in out-of-sample validation (R2=0.93). Reciprocal-space analysis, operando spectroscopy, and DFT calculations link this memory to strain-bearing high-index step motifs that favor oxygen-retaining intermediates. Annealing erases the memory and shifts branching toward ethylene while largely preserving total geometric current density, whereas precursor and reduction protocols tune its retention to favor alcohol formation. These findings establish catalyst history as a programmable structural handle for C2+ product branching.

papers.title: Traffic Rather Than Land Use Influences Tire-Derived Organic Pollutants in Urban Soils
papers.abstract: Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly antioxidant N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-quinone), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. However, their distribution and controlling factors in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 TDOPs, including 6PPD and 6PPD-quinone, were quantified in 28 urban soil samples representing four land-use types in the highly urbanized Metro Detroit, Michigan, United States, where heavy traffic creates a strong potential for tire-derived contamination. TDOPs were widely detected in all soil samples, and 16 out of 19 compounds had a detection frequency ≥75%. Very low 6PPD/6PPD-quinone ratios, together with the relative enrichment of N,N'-diphenyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPPD) over 6PPD, suggest that substantial transformation of 6PPD had occurred in the investigated urban soils. Statistical analyses showed no significant differences among land-use types. In contrast, traffic-derived exposure metrics showed significant associations with a subset of TDOPs, with 6PPD exhibiting the strongest correlation. The Pearson correlation coefficient between log10-transformed 6PPD concentrations and log10-transformed traffic-derived exposure metrics reached a maximum of 0.730 at a decay length of 400 m ( p < 0.0001). These results show that soil contamination by TDOPs extends beyond the immediate roadside environment and suggest that traffic intensity (source strength), proximity, and environmental fate and transport processes jointly govern TDOP accumulation in urban soils.

papers.title: Diversification of heteroleptic assembly topologies through covalent bridging
papers.abstract: Expanding the structural and functional diversity of metallosupramolecular assemblies remains challenging for selective recognition, catalysis, and materials science. Existing synthetic strategies often impose constraints on the size, shape, and functionalization of building blocks, limiting access to assemblies of certain geometries or higher nuclearity. Here, we demonstrate a versatile approach for accessing a variety of heteroleptic, metal-mediated architectures based on the covalent bridging of identical or unlike ligands via flexible or rigid tethers, thus enabling synthetic routes to previously unattainable di- and tetranuclear multicomponent structures. Depending on the type of bridge and counter-ligand combination, we achieved the non-statistical assembly of Pd 2 (AB)CD cages, singly-bridged Pd 4 A 4 (B 2 )D 2 double-cavity systems and doubly-bridged Pd 4 (B 2 ) 2 D 2 structures. Dynamic cage-to-cage transformations enable triggered separation of C 60 from fullerene mixtures, while incorporation of photoswitchable ligands allows reversible modulation of cage geometry and properties. Remarkably, all assemblies arise from ligands that, in their untethered form, fail to yield clean integrative self-sorting. The robustness of this modular strategy is demonstrated through comprehensive NMR spectroscopic and mass spectrometric characterization and six single-crystal X-ray structures. Methodological progress in the synthetic access to nanostructures of increasing complexity promises to advance the functionality of soluble receptors, stimuli-responsive life-like systems and porous materials with intricate morphology.

papers.title: Choosing lower-end strategies in analytical measurement
papers.abstract: Lower-end analytical claims are often treated as formula-selection problems involving signal-to-noise ratios, σ/S calculations, blank-based estimates, regression residuals, intercept dispersion, or empirical lower-range validation. This framing is incomplete because these routes do not describe the same evidentiary object. This article develops a metrological framework for selecting lower-end strategies by distinguishing reagent blanks, method blanks, zero calibrators, and forced mathematical origins, and by separating baseline noise, blank variability, calibration scatter, intercept instability, heteroscedasticity, non-linearity, matrix effects, and full-method variability. The framework links analytical calibration practice with ICH Q2(R2), ICH M10, FDA bioanalytical validation, EPA method detection limit logic, CLSI EP17, ISO 11843, VIM-compatible terminology, Eurachem validation guidance, and GUM uncertainty propagation. It argues that a detection, quantification, reporting, or decision-facing lower-bound claim is fit for purpose only when the evidence source, variance model, calibration structure, uncertainty statement, and intended analytical use are aligned. Worked examples illustrate an intercept-based detection-limit estimate with uncertainty and an iteratively reweighted least-squares treatment of mixed additive/proportional variance. The proposed framework rejects universal low-end recipes and replaces them with an evidence map: baseline-controlled systems may justify signal-to-noise approaches; blank-dominated procedures require blank or method-blank evidence; heteroscedastic and non-linear systems require explicit variance or precision-profile modelling; and decision-facing reporting generally requires empirical full-method validation. The correct lower-end strategy is the one that matches the actual lower-end problem.

papers.title: Periodic Reassessment or Permanent Approval? A Critical Analysis of the EU Commission’s Proposal to Reform Pesticide and Biocide Authorisation in Europe
papers.abstract: On 16 December 2025, the European Commission published proposal COM(2025) 1030 within the Food and Feed Safety Simplification Omnibus, aiming to amend Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 on plant protection products and Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 on biocidal products.
