In this work, we investigate detection of these anions under pulsed current using the combined responses from three nonspecific electrodes made from common membrane support polymers: poly-vinyl acetate (PVA), poly-vinyl chloride (PVC), and poly-acrylonitrile (PAN). We measure the potential vs. time responses in solutions containing individual nitrate, phosphate, and chloride ions, and generate a synthetic dataset for ion mixtures from individual ion responses. We apply tree-based and neural-based machine learning (ML) algorithms to assess the feasibility of multi-ion detection using combined responses from multiple nonspecific electrodes. Our results demonstrate proof of concept for more robust and versatile multi-ion sensors without the need for membrane materials development. However, the approach remains constrained by factors such as manufacturing variability and the effort and cost required to generate sufficiently large training datasets. Under the assumptions of our synthetic dataset, we identify that >1,000 measurements are required to achieve a mean absolute percent error of ~10% from the combined response of three nonspecific electrodes for simultaneous detection of nitrate, phosphate, and chloride. This work establishes example datasets for individual ion sensing and mixed ion responses that can be used by the broader electrochemical sensing community, and highlights both the promise of applying pulsed-current sensing with ML for multi-ion monitoring, and the technological gap in high volume data needed to make this vision a reality.

papers.title: High-throughput, Picosecond Laser Interference-Patterned Doping of Thin Films for Spatially Resolved OER Screening
papers.abstract: The development of efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts requires a detailed understanding of how structural and compositional modifications influence the catalytic performance. Here, we present a high-throughput platform to induce structural and chemical modification in Co3O4 thin films by combining direct laser interference patterning (DLIP) with picosecond-pulsed laser defect engineering in liquids (PUDEL) and spatially resolved electrochemical screening via scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). This approach enables the generation of spatially varying surface modifications within a single experiment, including controlled film restructuring, defect formation, and compositional changes. Localized measurements reveal that the OER activity is maximized at moderate laser fluence, where film restructuring and compositional changes occur, while excessive fluence leads to ablation and reduced performance. Despite detectable Fe incorporation, activity trends are primarily governed by structural changes of the Co3O4 film. This work establishes DLIP-PUDEL combined with SECCM as a platform for rapid structure–activity correlation and accelerated electrocatalyst development.

papers.title: Identifying Critical Operating Constraints for Soluble Lead Redox Flow Battery Stability: A 25-Cycle Analysis of Charge-Discharge Asymmetry
papers.abstract: The soluble lead redox flow battery (SLRFB) offers a low-cost, membrane-free architecture for grid-scale energy storage, but its short cycle life remains a barrier to deployment. Prior work has shown that high charging current density and electrolyte agitation can extend cyclability to several hundred cycles, and in one report, to 2000 cycles. The relative roles of the charge and discharge half-cycles, however, are not known, leaving open the question of which step should be targeted for further improvement. In this work, we decouple the two by independently varying the applied current density during charging and discharging, with and without electrolyte stirring, using the standard PbMS/MSA electrolyte. Over 25 cycles, stable and reproducible operation is found to require a strict dual condition: stirring combined with high current density during both half-cycles. Symmetric highrate operation in unstirred cells holds charge efficiency near 90% for about 10 cycles before drifting; asymmetric high–low combinations degrade rapidly and lose reproducibility, indicating that deposit formation and dissolution are jointly sensitive to reaction rate and electrolyte transport. We also define the potential recovery capacity, WR, a scalar that relates cyclic discharge capacity to the twostep recharging potential profile and tracks the onset of degradation.

papers.title: β-Citronellol as a Sustainable Additive for Mechanochemical Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling Reactions
papers.abstract: Mechanochemistry has emerged as a more sustainable and facile synthetic platform for solvent-free transition metal-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions. Here, the discovery of β-citronellol as a sustainable additive for liquid assisted grinding is reported. It is found that β-citronellol enables the mechanochemical cross-coupling reactions of various aryl halides and aryl boronic acids in moderate to excellent yields under ambient conditions without phosphine ligands or the application of external heating. Additionally, the reaction is found to proceed with heteroaryl boronic acids on the gram-scale, and it is applicable towards the synthesis of functional organic compounds with extended π-conjugation.

papers.title: Identification of Metal-Organic Frameworks for CO2 Capture from Humid Flue Gas: Integrating Molecular Simulation, Machine Learning, and Experimental Synthesis
papers.abstract: Increasing global CO2 emissions are driving efforts to develop advanced carbon capture materials. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show great promise as CO2 adsorbents, yet maintaining performance under humid flue gas conditions remains a major challenge. Herein, we present an integrated computational high-throughput screening workflow that begins with a library of over 110,000 experimental MOF structures, explicitly includes the effects of water in adsorption simulations, and incorporates machine learning-based stability analysis to identify promising candidates from among existing MOFs. Guided by this workflow, we synthesized a top-performing MOF that demonstrates exceptional tolerance to humid conditions, maintaining high CO2 uptake at elevated relative humidity. We further revealed key structure-property relationships and structural motifs that offer valuable design principles for next-generation MOFs for CO2 capture in humid conditions.

papers.title: Evaluation of Binding and Cell Penetration of Imidazolium Amino Acids as Novel Isosteres for Trimethyllysine, Dimethylarginine, and Arginine
papers.abstract: Inhibition of histone trimethyllysine (Kme3) reader proteins is a promising therapeutic strategy due to their roles in gene regulation and disease, particularly cancer. However, developing effective inhibitors has proven challenging because of the extended, solvent-exposed binding interface and the cooperative reliance on interactions with multiple positively charged residues in the histone tail in addition to Kme3. While these cationic groups are often necessary for strong affinity binding, they reduce cell penetration of peptidic inhibitors, increasing the challenge of inhibitor development for this class of proteins. Herein we report the evaluation of three new imidazolium amino acids as novel lipophilic cationic isosteres for Kme3, dimethylarginine (Rme2), and Arg against a panel of histone reader proteins. We find that these isosteres can replace Kme3, Rme2, and Arg, with equivalent or even improved binding in some cases, while also providing unique selectivity patterns relative to the parent amino acid. Moreover, we find that these imidazolium amino acids promote improved cytosolic penetration due to their increased lipophilicity and lack of hydrogen bond donors. These new isosteres provide promising new chemotypes for inhibition of histone reader proteins, as well as other protein-protein interactions which rely on cationic residues.

papers.title: 1H NMR Metabolomics Reveals Differential Metabolic Signatures of Stress Hyperglycemia in Acute Ischemic Stroke Across Diabetic Status
papers.abstract: Stress hyperglycemia during acute ischemic stroke (SH-AIS) in patients with diabetic (DM) and non-diabetic (non-DM) poses challenges related to stroke pathophysiology, prognosis, and response to treatment, particularly in term of understanding the underlying metabolic changes. This study aimed to identify metabolomic differences in the plasma of SH-AIS patients, considering their preadmission diabetes status and focusing on sex-based variations. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy ( 1 H-NMR) was employed to investigate plasma samples from 43 patients with DM (n = 24) and non-DM (n = 19). The multivariate data analysis, including principal component analysis (PCA) and orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA), we identified significant metabolic segregation between the groups. Pathway analysis revealed a major divergence in the glycolysis or gluconeogenesis pathways between the DM and non-DM SH-AIS groups, highlighting the impact of premorbid glycemic status on acute stress responses. Furthermore, intra- and inter-group sex comparisons unveiled pronounced sexual dimorphism in the SH-AIS metabolic signature. Inter-group comparisons among the same sex identified N -acetylglucosamine as a key differential metabolite. Distinctively, the female group exhibited unique metabolic shifts characterized by significant alterations in 3-hydroxybutyrate (3HB), adipic acid, and acetone. These findings demonstrate that the metabolomic profile of SH-AIS is jointly modulated by diabetic status and biological sex. This study provides crucial molecular insights that could pave the way for more precise, sex-specific prognostic and therapeutic strategies with potential to guide individualized therapeutic strategies in SH-AIS.

papers.title: A Multi-Parameter Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship (QSPR) Model for Boiling Point Prediction of Organic Compounds
papers.abstract: This paper presents a group-wise Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship (QSPR) model for predicting the normal boiling points (NBP) of organic compounds using simple, structurally interpretable molecular descriptors. The model employs up to 14 descriptors per functional group class — including molecular weight (MW), hydrogen-bond donors (HBD), hydrogen-bond acceptors (HBA), ring count, aromaticity, individual halogen counts (F, Cl, Br, I), a non-linear Cl2 term, carboxyl count, nitro count, branching correction, and amide substitution type — all countable by direct inspection of the structural formula. A dataset of 732 compounds across 18 functional group classes was compiled from established chemical reference sources. Key design choices include: a quartic polynomial for straight-chain alkanes spanning MW = 16–563 g/mol (MAE = 3.20°C); a Cl2 descriptor capturing the non-linear saturation of successive chlorine substitution (CCl4 error = 4.0°C); a quadratic aromatic hydrocarbon equation accounting for accelerating π–π stacking with ring fusion (R2 = 0.9866, improving from 0.9531 with a linear equation); and separate primary, secondary, and tertiary amide sub-groups encoding N-substitution effects. The tertiary amide group is modelled by a linear equation (R2 = 0.5371) following rejection of a polynomial form that produced physically unreasonable external predictions. The model achieves overall R2 = 0.9547 and MAE = 11.58°C, representing a 74.5% MAE reduction versus a global MW-only baseline (MAE = 45.44°C). Preliminary external validation on 30 reliable-group unseen compounds yields MAE = 5.35°C, closely matching cross-validation estimates. The aromatic nitro group failure (R2 = 0.143) constitutes direct evidence that co-substituent electronic interactions dominate boiling point variation in that class beyond MW-based frameworks. The model is deployed as a freely accessible interactive web application.

papers.title: Analysis of Stress Evolution in Lithium Metal Anodes During Plating and Stripping Cycles
papers.abstract: Liquid cell batteries with lithium metal anodes may exhibit degraded Coulombic efficiency, due to plating of non-compact deposits consisting of whiskers. Experiments show that whisker growth is driven by compressive stress arising from metal-phase diffusion of deposited atoms. In situ wafer curvature measurements can reveal the dynamic stress response due to diffusion, but their interpretation is complicated by the unknown and changing deposit porosity. Here, a modeling approach is introduced that enables fitting of curvature transients during cycling to characterize the evolution of the diffusion and mechanical response of the lithium film. The analysis is based on metal-phase diffusion accommodated by elastic deformation and power-law creep, and circumvents the unknown microstructure of the film by focusing on open-circuit intervals during cycling. It is shown that curvature changes during plating cycles are caused by diffusion-induced compressive stress. Curvature increases during stripping periods are due to near-surface tensile stress in the metal, consistent with experimental observations of submicron near-surface voids.

papers.title: Synergy-Guided Molecular Editing for Synthetically Feasible Conversion of P-glycoprotein Substrates to Non-Substrates
papers.abstract: Drug efflux mediated by P-glycoprotein (P-gp) remains a major barrier to effective small-molecule therapeutics, limiting both bioavailability and central nervous system exposure. While machine learning models can predict P-gp substrates, translating these predictions into actionable molecular design remains largely unexplored, particularly in enabling the rational conversion of substrates into non-substrates to mitigate efflux liability. Here, we introduce the synergy-guided fragment genetic algorithm (SF-GA), a computational framework that transforms predictive insight into an interpretable molecular design strategy. By integrating fragment synergy analysis into the mutation stage of a genetic algorithm, SF-GA biases fragment replacement toward co-occurring substructures associated with non-substrate classification, thereby enabling chemically interpretable and property-directed molecular optimization. Compared to conventional genetic algorithms, SF-GA exhibits faster convergence, greater structural diversity, and improved synthetic accessibility, with ablation studies confirming the central role of synergy-guided mutation. The method enables molecular editing guided by synergy scores and structural similarity, facilitating the conversion of P-gp substrates into non-substrates within one to two generations. Docking simulations against human P-gp structures qualitatively support the predicted trends, providing additional validation for the proposed interpretable molecular editing framework.

papers.title: 63Cu NMR Study of Cu2MTtCh4 (M = Zn, Cd; Tt = Si, Ge, Sn; Ch = S, Se): A Tale of One or Two Sites
papers.abstract: Quaternary chalcogenides Cu 2 MTtCh 4 ( M = Zn, Cd; Tt = Si, Ge, Sn; Ch = S, Se) with diamond-like structures, derived from the cubic sphalerite and hexagonal wurtzite prototypes, have been extensively studied for their optoelectronic properties. The site distributions of the metal cations, which are often unclear, can be probed by 63 Cu solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. NMR parameters were extracted through a combination of multifield magic-angle spinning (MAS) and non-spinning experiments to establish structural trends within these compounds. Substitution of S with Se led to lower frequencies for the 63 Cu isotropic chemical shift. In contrast, substitution with heavier tetrels (Si to Ge to Sn) led to higher frequency chemical shifts, which correlate with narrower band gaps. Ambiguities in structural models were resolved by arguments about local symmetry of Cu sites, as examined by their quadrupole coupling parameters. The experimental results were compared with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, performed using r 2 SCAN and PBE functionals. The predicted electric field gradient (EFG) parameters were accurate, though the calculated magnetic shieldings exhibited limitations in these narrow-gap semiconductors. This work provides an analytical 63 Cu NMR spectroscopy method that can rapidly aid in assessing local structures in these diamond-like compounds and related chalcogenides.

papers.title: Interfacial Engineering of 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx Heterostructures for Enhanced Symmetric Supercapacitor Performance Across Various Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Engineering well-defined heterostructured composites is an effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage systems. In this study, a 2D/2D BiVO 4 /V 2 CT x heterostructure was synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method and, for the first time, systematically tested as a symmetric supercapacitor electrode in neutral (1 M Na 2 SO 4 ), alkaline (1 M KOH), and acidic (1 M H 2 SO 4 ) electrolytes. The composite showed better electrochemical performance compared to pristine V 2 CT x , with specific capacitances of 191.5 F g -1 , 107 F g -1 , and 239 F g -1 in Na 2 SO 4 , KOH, and H 2 SO 4 , respectively, at 0.016 A g -1 . A high energy density of 83.3 Wh kg -1 at 147.5 W kg -1 was achieved in the neutral electrolyte, along with excellent rate capability and Coulombic efficiency. These improvements arise from the synergistic interaction between BiVO 4 and V 2 CT x , which increases active site accessibility and promotes efficient ion and electron transport. Overall, the results show that the BiVO 4 /V 2 CT x heterostructure is a promising and versatile electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors.

papers.title: Molecular Structure and Toxicity Predictor (MSTP) V2: A Mobile-Developed Cheminformatics Web Application for 2D/3D Visualization and Machine Learning-Based Toxicity Prediction
papers.abstract: The Molecular Structure and Toxicity Predictor (MSTP) is an open-access cheminformatics web application built using RDKit, Streamlit, and scikit-learn. Version 2 (V2) represents a substantial advancement over the original release, introducing machine learning-based toxicity prediction, interactive three-dimensional molecular visualization, and a molecular descriptor computation module. The toxicity prediction pipeline employs a Random Forest classifier trained on the Tox21 benchmark dataset (7,831 molecules) using Morgan Fingerprints with a radius of 2 and 2048 bit vectors, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 73.23% on the held-out test set. The application accepts both SMILES strings and compound names via PubChem integration, renders two-dimensional and three-dimensional molecular structures, predicts binary toxicity classification with confidence scoring, and computes key physicochemical descriptors including molecular weight, LogP, topological polar surface area, and hydrogen bond donor and acceptor counts. The entire application, including the machine learning pipeline, was designed and implemented on a mobile phone without access to a laptop or desktop computer. The source code and trained model are publicly available. A V3 iteration integrating Graph Neural Networks for improved toxicity prediction is planned.

papers.title: Like-Charge Ion Pairing and Enhanced Interfacial Diffusion in Charged Aqueous Droplets
papers.abstract: Chemical reactivity in aqueous microdroplets has been widely reported to differ from that in bulk solution, yet the molecular-scale origins of these differences remain incompletely understood. Here we identify like-charge contact ion pairing as a mechanism for transient co-localization of reactive species. Using molecular dynamics simulations of charged water nanodroplets containing multiple OH - ions, we quantify the equilibrium constant, lifetime, and formation rate of contact ion pairs, with Cl - and Na + ions included for comparison. We find that OH - and Cl - exhibit a significantly higher propensity to form contact ion pairs than Na + ions. Hydroxide pairs are stabilized by hydrogen-bonded water bridges forming transient [OH - (H 2 O) n OH - ] structures ( n = 1 –3) with lifetimes of approx. 20 ps. These configurations are enriched in the droplet subsurface region, where ion density is elevated and water self-diffusion is up to twofold faster than in the bulk-like interior. Although diffusion enhancement alone does not account for reported rate accelerations, it increases ion–ion encounter frequencies in regions where pairing is most probable. Together, these results provide a molecular-level framework for understanding enhanced reactivity in microdroplets and suggest that the radial distribution of hydroxide ions may contribute to differences in negative-mode electrospray ionization efficiency.

papers.title: Natural Orbital Correlation Analysis of Cluster Bonding: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms with Quantum Topology Probes
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of electron correlation across molecular and cluster systems using the number of effectively unpaired electrons ND = P i ni(2 − ni), the Takatsuka–Head-Gordon index, computed from coupled-cluster natural orbital occupations over the complete correlated orbital space. Computed at the CCSD/def2-SVP level, all systems studied exhibit substantial total electron correlation when the full natural orbital space is retained: aromatic Al4 2 – (ND = 3.84), antiaromatic Al4 4 – (4.03), planar and icosahedral B12 clusters (4.42 and 4.99), heteroatomic B6N6 (5.11), and cesium–aluminum superatoms Cs3Al8 – and Cs3Al12 – (5.58 and 7.10, respectively). We show that ND is an extensive quantity dominated by the dynamic correlation tail over many weakly occupied virtual orbitals, and introduce the per-electron correlation density fe = ND/Ncorr as a complementary intensive measure. This intensive measure reveals a clear separation: small clusters (Al4, B12, B6N6) exhibit fe ≈ 0.07–0.14, while metallic superatoms show fe ≈ 0.04, reflecting the diluted nature of correlation in large delocalized systems. We demonstrate that truncation of the natural orbital space to a small active window dramatically underestimates ND, and that complete occupation data are essential for physically meaningful correlation diagnostics. In a separate study, we explore whether molecular bonding topology generates characteristic entanglement signatures on a neutral-atom quantum processor (Pasqal). Mapping atomic coordinates of nine molecular systems onto Rydberg atom registers, we find that different chemical topology classes—aromatic, antiaromatic, cage, and metallic—produce systematically distinct entanglement patterns, suggesting that molecular graphs encode topological information accessible to analog quantum hardware.

papers.title: Mixed Quantum-Classical Dynamics for Molecular Excited States: Reliability, Scalability, and Representation
papers.abstract: Mixed quantum–classical dynamics (MQCD) enables nonadiabatic simulations of molecular excited states by combining classical nuclear trajectories with quantum electronic-state population flow. The field is moving beyond benchmark small molecules toward nanoscopic systems, active environments, and long timescales—regimes where MQCD is stretched by three coupled demands: reliability, scalability, and flexibility in the electronic representation set by decoherence. Reliability means getting the controlling physics right: initial ensembles consistent with the experimental preparation, accurate potential energies and couplings driving the system’s evolution, and correct nonadiabatic branching and recombination. Scalability demands reducing time-to-converged observables by curbing repeated high-level electronic-structure calls. Surrogate excited-state models (including machine-learning potentials) can replace much of the on-the-fly electronic structure, while active learning, multi-fidelity strategies, and uncertainty quantification guide where new reference data and additional sampling are actually needed. Flexibility of representation is essential in dense excited-state manifolds, where the decoherence-selected pointer basis may differ from the adiabatic energy basis; localized representations and open-quantum-system tools (Lindblad dynamics, stochastic unraveling) provide practical routes to encode that choice. Together, these directions define an agenda for MQCD that targets larger, longer, and more environmentally complex excited-state dynamics while retaining a trajectory-based workflow.

papers.title: Beyond Single Structures: The Role of Structural Ensembles in Discrete-Continuum Modeling of Highly Charged Metal Ions
papers.abstract: Metal ions play critical roles in chemical, biochemical, and materials systems. The discrete-continuum model has been widely used for modeling metal ions in the aqueous phase due to its excellent balance of accuracy and efficiency. Previously, we demonstrated that a discrete-continuum model combining B3LYP-D3/Def2-QZVP for the first solvation shell with the SMD implicit solvent model for outer shells accurately predicts hydration free energies (HFEs) of divalent, trivalent, and tetravalent ions. However, those results relied on single optimized geometries. Here, we extend this approach by incorporating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to enhance conformational sampling for nine metal ions with charges from +2 to +4: the alkaline earth metals (Be2+, Mg2+ , Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+), Al3+, Ce3+, Zr4+, and Hf4+. MD trajectories were filtered through quantum mechanical geometry optimization to identify representative structures, from which Boltzmann-weighted HFE values were calculated. Our results reveal that larger alkaline earth metal ions access more local minima, with the number of representative structures increasing as surface charge density decreases. Remarkably, these local minima exhibit fundamentally different electronic structures and chemical bonding patterns, as revealed by ETS-NOCV analysis. For ions with surface charge densities below 0.1 e/ ̊A2, accounting for multiple minima through Boltzmann weighting substantially improves agreement between discrete-continuum predictions and experimental HFEs. We propose this threshold as a practical criterion for determining when enhanced sampling is necessary in discrete-continuum models. These findings establish that rigorous conformational sampling is essential for accurate HFE predictions of soft metal ions, while the single-frame protocol remains adequate for rigid ions with high surface charge densities.

papers.title: Direct evidence and quantification of homologous recognition between DNA duplexes
papers.abstract: Stretches of double-stranded DNA sharing the same sequence can recognise each other in cells. This phenomenon, known as homologous recognition, is essential for DNA recombination and repair. Yet, its mechanism remains debated, with purely physical interactions proposed as a contributing factor. Here, we use a minimal DNA nanosensor to quantify homologous pairwise interactions with exquisite precision. We find that homology enhances the duplex-duplex affinity induced by physiological divalent cations and measure the homology-driven recognition free energy as ~ −0.01 kcal/mol per base pair. This affinity substantially enhances co-alignment of homologous DNA in the confined geometry of the nanosensor, which mimics physical effects of concentrated biological environments. We introduce a quantitative electrostatic framework that attributes this emergent behaviour to coherent charge distributions unique to homologous DNA. Our findings provide compelling evidence in support of purely-physical sequence-specific interactions between intact double-stranded DNA, which may bear biological relevance for homologous recombination.

papers.title: Solid-Phase Synthesis of Orberryamides A–D and Their Derivatives Reveals PPARγ-Mediated Th17 Differentiation Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Orberryamides A–D ( 1 – 4 ) are a unique class of macrocyclic nonapeptides exhibiting significant inhibition of Th17 cell differentiation. Herein, we report a scalable total synthesis of these natural products and their derivatives using an integrated strategy that combines solid-phase peptide synthesis for macrocycle assembly with late-stage functionalization. Biological assays identified derivatives 27 and 29 as PPAR γ agonists that inhibit Th17 cell differentiation, providing insights into the immunomodulatory mechanisms this macrocyclic peptide family.

papers.title: Asymmetric Organocatalysis Enhanced by Nanohoop Confinement
papers.abstract: Chiral phosphoric acids are privileged organocatalysts for diverse asymmetric transformations. In BINOL-derived systems, high levels of enantioinduction are typically achieved through bulky aromatic substituents that create a confined and sterically well-defined environment around the Brønsted acid. Here we present an alternative design strategy based on ring closure around the catalytic center. We integrated a BINOL-derived phosphoric acid into the [9]cycloparaphenylene (CPP) scaffold and employed this “nanohoop” as an organocatalyst for the asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of 2-substituted quinolines. The chiral macrocycle exhibits excellent catalytic turnover and enantioselectivities up to 99% ee, substantially outperforming structurally comparable non-cyclic reference catalysts. Mechanistic studies combining kinetic monitoring, isotope labelling and DFT calculations reveal the importance of macrocycle structure adaptation together with attractive non-covalent interactions within the macrocycle-encapsulated ternary activated complexes. These insights enabled confinement-specific ee enhancements (e.g. from 7% to 77%) by biasing the reaction toward an in-cavity pathway using a bulkier hydride source. Our results highlight the untapped potential of macrocyclic confinement effects for efficient and selective catalysis.

papers.title: Humanoid robots with embedded intelligence: A comprehensive review on challenges, opportunities, and workplace applications
papers.abstract: Robots are increasingly transforming from industrial environments into the daily jobs of humans, assisting them at workplaces and in their homes. To develop such abilities, robots use AI (Artificial Intelligence) models trained on real-world datasets. Accurately trained models enable robots to perform essential functions such as task reminders, companionship, and assistance for elderly and differently abled people who rely on support with daily activities. This study presents a comprehensive review of the progress of a Smart Humanoid Personal Assistant Robot, integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI), computer vision, voice interaction, and motion control, to assist humans with everyday tasks. The purpose of this work is to motivate further research and development in personal robotics and to provide a practical, accessible solution for common daily challenges. The planned ‘Automated Robotic Guide for Operations & Support’ regulates how AI-powered robots can expressively improve quality of life by making human-technology communication more efficient, natural, and userfriendly. As a personal assistant, the robot can perform tasks such as voice-based reminders, object recognition, basic navigation, and interactive communication. This survey also highlights the potential for such robots to become everyday tools, similar to mobile phones, laptops, smart assistants such as Google Assistant and Amazon’s Alexa, and various digital platforms, especially for future generations.

papers.title: Lipid Tail Length Dictates Membrane Disruption by Carmofur Analogs and Reveals Noncanonical Modes of Action
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, with activity attributed to inhibition of acid ceramidase. It is also an established antiviral agent, due to its ability to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 main protease. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a hydrophilic nucleobase headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, suggests an additional membrane-directed mechanism orthogonal to canonical target engagement. Inspired by the unique observation that certain lipidated carmofur analogs induce potent disruption in model-membrane systems and enabled by modern computational giant unilamellar vesicle (GUV) quantification, we evaluated nine analogs with differing alkyl tail lengths in an effort to better understand the capacity of such lipidated compounds to directly engage with biological membranes. To efficiently quantify the membrane rupture capabilities of these analogs, we benchmarked the detection accuracy of transformer-based and CNN-based vision models, and YOLOv11 exhibited superior performance compared to RT-DETRv3.

papers.title: Scalable functionalization of azaindole derivatives for medicinal chemistry purposes
papers.abstract: A reliable protocol for the multigram synthesis of a series of functionalized azaindoles was developed. The challenges associated with the synthesis of certain fluorine-substituted azaindole starting materials were investigated. The starting compounds were synthesized via the Sonogashira reaction under optimized conditions. A series of functionalization protocols was subsequently applied, demonstrating access to a wide range of corresponding aldehydes, acids, halogenated derivatives, sulfonyl chlorides, as well as an azatryptamine derivative. The selective hydrogenation developed in this work enabled the synthesis of a series of novel azatryptamine derivatives and 2,3dihydroazaindoles. The developed azaindoles represents a useful class of building blocks for medicinal chemistry, offering diverse functional groups with significant potential for application in drug design.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of DSPC-Induced Structural Shifts in Lipid Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a leading platform for nucleic acid delivery, yet current formulations typically suffer from rapid in vivo clearance and limited extra-hepatic delivery. Recent experiments demonstrate that increasing the helper lipid content (e.g., to 40% DSPC, 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) can significantly improve mRNA stability, prolong circulation, and enhance transfection efficiency. In this study, we use coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to provide mechanistic insight into the structural changes driving these improvements. Our simulations confirm that elevated helper lipid content fundamentally alters 2 the internal morphology of the LNP. Consistent with experimental observations, at high DSPC levels the core transitions from a compact, disordered, predominantly lipid state to an extended structure with distinct lamellar-like elements encompassing lipid-rich and water-rich regions. This structural reorganization directly correlates with the enhanced stability and delivery properties reported in the experiment. These findings provide molecular-level understanding of the composition-morphology relationship and suggest that coarse-grained modeling can inform the design of novel LNP formulations.

papers.title: Starch-dominated, matrix-modulated gelation and structural recovery in air-classified protein-rich and starch-rich chickpea fractions
papers.abstract: Air classification of milled pulse flours produces protein-rich fine fractions and starch-rich coarse fractions, yet both remain composite matrices in which starch, protein and fibre collectively determine functionality. How milling severity governs starch redistribution and its consequences for gelation and structural recovery remains unclear. Here, desi (DCP) and kabuli (KCP) chickpea were jet-milled at 5k and 10k rotor speeds and air-classified. Fractions were characterised for composition, starch damage, pasting, gelatinisation, starch structure, and gel rheology, including three-interval thixotropy (3ITT). Milling severity altered starch partitioning in a variety-dependent manner: higher rotor speed reduced starch in DCP fines (21→17%) but increased it in KCP fines (8→12%). Coarse fractions concentrated starch to >50% with minimal damage (<2%) and showed the highest viscosities and moduli. KCP starch, with slightly higher crystallinity and longer amylopectin chains, formed stiffer gels than DCP starch, though both were weak gels. Under 3ITT, all matrices yielded (G′ decreased by ~1–1.5 log cycles) and partially recovered. Structural recovery increased with starch content (p < 0.001) and decreased with protein and fibre (p < 0.001). This reflects starch acting as the dominant phase undergoing gelatinisation to form a space-filling network, while protein and fibre act as discrete inclusions that dilute and disrupt network connectivity. The composition–recovery relationship was stronger in KCP (R2 = 0.76–0.81) than DCP (R2 = 0.25–0.42), consistent with behaviour near a percolation threshold. Fibre particle number further influenced recovery, suggesting a role in stress concentration and network disruption. These findings highlight the need to co-optimise protein enrichment, starch partitioning and matrix architecture in dry-fractionated pulse ingredients.

papers.title: Highly active Ni/(La, Ce)Ox catalysts for CO2 methanation: Effect of synthesis method on catalytic performance and structural dynamics
papers.abstract: Ni-based catalysts are widely used for CO 2 methanation due to their high activity comparable to noble metals and favorable cost. Herein, (La, Ce)Ox-supported Ni catalysts are prepared using incipient-wetness impregnation and sol-gel synthesis to investigate the effect of preparation method on catalyst properties, including basicity, crystallinity, electronic structure, and metal-support interactions. Compared to Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-IM prepared by impregnation, Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-SG prepared by sol-gel synthesis showed high activity with a CO2 conversion rate of 57.4 mmol CO2/molNi/s and 99.3% CH4 selectivity at 350 oC and 1 atm, and exhibited the lowest apparent activation energy among the catalysts studied. Comprehensive characterization pinpoints differences in domain size, Ni dispersion, as well as size and exposure of Ni(111) facets. Moreover, in-situ DRIFTS studies disclose a mechanistic difference in the CO2 methanation pathway, i.e., a dissociative pathway over the Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-SG, while an associative pathway prevails over Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-IM. In-situ time-resolved PDF measurements under reduction and methanation conditions with different H2/CO2 ratios revealed structural dynamics and Ni0 oxidation only over Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-SG at H2/CO2=1/1. In contrast, Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-IM remains unaffected. The reversible Ni0 oxidation in Ni/(La, Ce)Ox-SG is accompanied by an increased disorder in the La-doped ceria lattice, likely due to oxygen vacancy formation and oxygen migration from ceria to metallic Ni via the reverse oxygen spillover mechanism, indicating distinct differences in the metal-support interactions of the two catalysts.

papers.title: Substrate-dependent modulation of calf intestinal alkaline phosphatase by structurally-related vanillyl compounds
papers.abstract: Alkaline phosphatases are broadly distributed phosphomonoesterases that play important physiological and analytical roles, yet comparatively little is known about how structurally related vanillyl-derived aromatic compounds directly influence phosphatase activity. The present study examined the effects of a series of vanillyl-derived compounds and corresponding non-vanillyl analogues on calf intestinal alkaline phosphatase (CIAP) using both fixed-substrate and substrate-dependent kinetic assays. Under fixed-substrate conditions, vanillyl-derived compounds generally produced greater modulation of CIAP activity than corresponding non-vanillyl analogues, with vanillin exhibiting the strongest inhibitory effect among the compounds examined. Structure-activity relationships suggested that both the vanillyl aromatic scaffold and side-chain functionality contributed to the observed responses. Substrate-dependent analyses revealed that modulation was not limited to simple inhibition; several compounds produced apparent enhancement of activity under low-substrate conditions but progressively suppressed activity at higher substrate concentrations. These crossover behaviors occurred while substrate-velocity relationships retained broadly hyperbolic profiles, indicating perturbation of catalytic behavior without gross disruption of overall substrate dependence. Exploratory analyses of the capsaicinoid derivatives capsaicin and nonivamide yielded substantial variability, irregular concentration-response behavior, and signal loss at higher concentrations, precluding robust kinetic interpretation. Although detectable effects were generally confined to the millimolar concentration range, the findings demonstrate that comparatively simple vanillyl-derived aromatic compounds can produce reproducible, structure-dependent modulation of CIAP activity. More broadly, the results highlight the value of substrate-dependent kinetic analyses for identifying enzyme-small molecule interactions that may not be fully captured by endpoint inhibition measurements alone.

papers.title: Interfacial Transfer Theory for Hydrogen Spillover Driven by Chemical Potential Gradient
papers.abstract: Hydrogen spillover is an interfacial transport phenomenon widely present in heterogeneous catalysis, yet it has long lacked a first-principles macroscopic model. This study starts from the random walk of surface atoms, incorporates lattice gases model, bridges the tracer diffusion coefficient and the chemical diffusion coefficient via the Darken equation, and rigorously anchors the Onsager phenomenological coefficients within the non-equilibrium thermodynamic, thereby establishing a model for hydrogen spillover driven by the chemical potential gradient. The constitutive relationships between the transport characteristics of active hydrogen (Onsager phenomenological coefficient, characteristic length, characteristic diffusion rate and chemical potential gradient) and the support properties (reducibility, oxygen vacancies, and surface hydroxyl groups) are analyzed. The model is extended to the water phase and the subsurface of support, establishing a mathematical model that describes the cross-phase transport of active hydrogen. The theory of hydrogen spillover inherits and advances the classic surface diffusion equation and the Langmuir-Hinshelwood model, providing a paradigm theory for the active species spillover (hydrogen spillover, oxygen spillover, CO spillover, ammonia spillover, etc.).

papers.title: Electrochemistry Goes Mainstream: Applications in Modern Total Synthesis
papers.abstract: CONSPECTUS: For more than a century, synthetic organic electrochemistry has held out the promise of using electrons and holes—the universe’s cheapest and most tunable redox reagents—to orchestrate bond construction and functional-group interconversion with unparalleled precision and sustainability. Yet for decades its role in total synthesis remained peripheral, usually invoked when all else failed or as an alternative to reactions with a chemical counterpart. Why did a technique whose industrial pedigree includes multi-ton processes at BASF languish at the margins of academic complex molecule synthesis until the past ten years? The reasons are as familiar as they are frustrating: bespoke equipment, a steep learning curve, and the comforting (if often illusory) notion that “chemical reagents can do that, too.” Our laboratory’s entry into the field was pragmatically rather than philosophically driven. During the total synthesis of dixiamycin, exhaustive screening of chemical oxidants failed to forge the requisite N–N bond; constant-potential electrolysis succeeded cleanly. That single, necessitydriven success in 2014 marked the beginning of a deliberate campaign to move electrochemistry from workaround to strategic centerpiece. What followed was a convergence of two enabling developments: (1) the commercialization of standardized, user-friendly potentiostats that removed the engineering barrier, and (2) the invention of fundamentally novel reactivitymost notably electrochemical radical cross-couplings—that unlocked intermolecular C–C bond formations between latestage, densely functionalized fragments in manners hardly accessible using classic two-electron methods. In this Account we illustrate how these advances have rippled across every major natural-product class and bond type. Strategic functionalizations such as decarboxylative borylations (jawsamycin) and site-selective C–H oxidations (valencene, sclareolide, mitrephorone) now deliver gram-scale intermediates with minimal concession steps. Electrochemical C–N and C–O constructions have powered protecting-group-sparing routes to teleocidins, dragocins, and bipolarolides. The real paradigm shift, however, lies in intermolecular radical cross-couplings. C(sp2)–C(sp3) unions have enabled modular, scalable entries to polyene cores (progesterone, celastrol, isosteviol, vitamin D analogues) and complex macrocycles (bipinnatin J, micitide 982), while doubly decarboxylative C(sp3)–C(sp3) couplings have delivered fifteen natural products, including polyrhacitide A and PF1163A, both stemming from a single, inexpensive building block with ligand-controlled diastereoselectivity. Most strikingly, two sequential electrochemical couplings furnished over a gram of the intricate antibiotic nonthmicin, tolerating epoxides and free diols that would have derailed any conventional tactic. Electrochemistry has therefore ceased to be a niche curiosity and has become standard practice in our laboratory (64 syntheses to date)—and, increasingly, in the broader community. It offers an orthogonal retrosynthetic logic that maximizes convergence, minimizes redox fluctuations and protecting groups, and leverages inexpensive electricity rather than stoichiometric metals or pyrophoric reagents. The field now stands at an inflection point: practical paired electrolyses, direct reductive transformations, and mediator systems capable of engaging ever more complex substrates are within reach. For the synthetic chemist who has contemplated a stubborn redox problem or a chemoselectivity impasse, electrochemistry is no longer a last resort—it is an obvious tool to consider employing.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Descriptors Enable Machine Learning in Data-Sparse Chemical Systems
papers.abstract: Big-data approaches to chemistry falter when experimental data remain scarce, expensive, and noisy. Here we demonstrate that physics-informed descriptors overcome this limitation and enable accurate predictions from severely limited datasets. Taking capped diisocyanate deblocking as a test case, we introduce descriptors derived from the Bond Energies from Bond Orders and Populations (BEBOP) method that capture electronic structure and bonding at low computational cost. Trained on only 19 experimental compounds, BEBOP-informed LASSO regression predicts deblocking temperatures within an RMSE of ~11 °C over a 227–323 °C range, while conventional molecular descriptors fail to produce any meaningful correlation. We validate the resulting physically interpretable model on two new compounds, one within the training range and one outside of it. Embedding physical insight into descriptors rather than relying on algorithmic complexity reduces data requirements by an order of magnitude and offers a generalizable strategy for molecular design problems wherever large datasets are impractical.

papers.title: Comparative Assessment and Review of Hydrogen Storage Technologies: Materials, System Architectures, Performance Metrics, Challenges, Economics Analysis and Safety Considerations
papers.abstract: Hydrogen is widely recognized as a promising energy carrier for enabling the transition toward renewable and sustainable energy systems due to its high gravimetric energy density and zerocarbon emissions. However, the widespread deployment of hydrogen technologies remains constrained by challenges related to the safety, efficiency, economic feasibility, and scalability of hydrogen storage, motivating a comprehensive comparative assessment of storage materials, system architectures, performance metrics, economic factors, and safety considerations. The first part of the review examines the fundamental hydrogen storage mechanisms, including compressed gas storage, cryogenic storage, cryo-compressed storage, physical adsorption, and chemical absorption. Particular emphasis is placed on advanced storage materials such as fiberbased composites, carbon nanomaterials, nanostructured adsorbents, and functionalized hybrid systems. The influence of material morphology, porosity, surface chemistry, and functional groups on hydrogen adsorption capacity, storage kinetics, thermodynamic behavior, and overall system performance is critically evaluated. Comparative analyses of hybrid fiber–nanoparticle systems under varying pressure and temperature conditions are presented to identify key material characteristics governing hydrogen uptake. Design and analysis of emerging storage technologies are discussed for accelerating the development of nextgeneration hydrogen storage materials. The second part of the review focuses on hydrogen storage system architectures, particularly cylindrical pressure vessels ranging from Type I metallic cylinders to advanced Type V composite tanks. The associated failure mechanisms, including hydrogen embrittlement, matrix cracking, fiber fracture, delamination, and interlaminar failures are systematically reviewed. Modeling approaches based on Sievert’s law, Fickian diffusion, linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM), elastic-plastic fracture mechanics (EPFM), Tsai-Hill, Tsai-Wu, Hashin, Puck, cohesive zone modeling (CZM), smeared crack formulations and multi-physics coupled simulation techniques are comparatively assessed. Performance metrics of coupled modeling techniques are reported for enabling accurate prediction of damage initiation and progression of different storage architectures for safe operation. The third part addresses the safety considerations and operational challenges associated with hydrogen storage and utilization. Hydrogen’s high diffusivity, wide flammability range, low ignition energy, and rapid flame propagation characteristics can lead to leak-induced fire and explosion hazards. The review examines hydrogen dispersion, combustion, detonation phenomena, leak detection technologies, and mitigation strategies. Furthermore, the role of emerging digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital twins, predictive diagnostics, and real-time risk assessment frameworks, is explored for enhancing safety Review of Hydrogen Storage Systems 2 management and operational reliability. The review provides a comparative analysis of the technical, economic, and safety performance of current hydrogen storage technologies. Key challenges related to storage capacity, material durability, manufacturing cost, infrastructure requirements, lifecycle economics, and regulatory compliance are identified. The article highlights future research directions aimed at developing lightweight, high-capacity, costeffective, and inherently safe hydrogen storage systems capable of supporting large-scale deployment within a sustainable hydrogen economy.

papers.title: Cellulose-Based Composite for Sustainable Frost-Resistant Concrete
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the development of a sustainable cellulose-based composite material derived from banana peel and fungal biomass, modified with glycerin and reinforced with coal fly ash for use in durable and frost-resistant concrete. Cellulose was extracted from banana peel and fungal material through alkaline treatment using a 5–10% NaOH solution in a 400 ml medium at elevated temperature for 2 hours. This process effectively removed lignin and hemicellulose, yielding primary cellulose fibers. Before drying, the obtained cellulose was treated with 30 ml of glycerin for 15–20 minutes to enhance flexibility and prevent brittleness, thereby improving its mechanical performance in composite systems.

papers.title: Illuminating the Dark Kinome through Protein Language Models, Symbolic Regression, and Structure-Based Prioritisation
papers.abstract: Approximately 162 human protein kinases classified as Tdark by the Illuminating the Druggable Genome (IDG) initiative lack published pharmacological modulators. We report a computational prioritisation framework integrating protein language model embeddings (ESM-2), AlphaFold2 v6 predicted structures, the KIBA (Kinase Inhibitor Bioactivity) dataset, symbolic regression (PySR), and AutoDock Vina virtual screening. An ensemble of gradient boosting models trained on data pre-dating January 2018 and evaluated against ChEMBL activities deposited thereafter identified 20 high-priority candidates, of which 18 (90%) were subsequently de-orphanised by the scientific community (OR ≈ 19, p < 10 −10 , exact binomial test, conservative background rate 15%). Temporal leakage analysis confirms that no post-2018 bioactivity data contributed to any training feature or label. Symbolic regression established that global amino acid composition is an insufficient predictor of druggability (R 2 = −0.15, held-out test set), whereas the full ensemble incorporating ESM-2 embeddings achieved R 2 = 0.18, consistent with meaningful ranking performance. Among 37 kinases with no potent ChEMBL ligands, fpocket analysis of AlphaFold2 structures identified four structural intractability archetypes; blind virtual screening yielded binding hypotheses for SBK2 (A6NHR9) and NIM1K (Q8IYR2). All findings are prioritisation hypotheses subject to experimental confirmation.

papers.title: Differential Pressure Engineering as a Primary Strategy to Mitigate Carbonate Formation in CO2 Electrolysers
papers.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to fuels and chemicals is being constrained, in plain sight, by carbonate salt. Every AEM-based CO 2 electrolyser operating above 200 mA cm -2 is waging a losing battle against the spontaneous conversion of its own feedstock into electrochemically inert bicarbonate and carbonate ions that clog gas diffusion layers, poison membranes, and ultimately kill performance within hours. The field has explored catalyst redesign, electrolyte additives, periodic wash cycles, and acid anolytes, however, all of them palliative. Symmetric high-pressure operation has been shown to improve CO 2 utilisation, but it treats the cathode and anode compartments equivalently and neglects the most powerful degree of freedom available: the transmembrane pressure gradient. This perspectives article argues that differential pressure engineering, defined as the deliberate, controlled imposition of an asymmetric pressure difference between cathode and anode, is not merely one tool among many, but the primary, thermodynamically grounded strategy that the field has systematically neglected. We construct a comprehensive physical and engineering framework: from the coupled Nernst-Planck-Darcy transport equations that govern ion and solvent motion across the membrane under a pressure gradient, to the design rules for pressure-asymmetric membrane electrode assembly (MEA) architectures that enable continuous in-situ carbonate regeneration. We introduce the Differential Pressure Window (DPW) as a practical regime diagram that demarcates stable, carbonate-free operation from flooding and crossover failure, and provide a sensitivity analysis of the critical minimum pressure difference (Δp min ) parameter across realistic operating conditions. The perspective closes with a frank assessment of what membrane science, reactor engineering, and process systems optimisation must each deliver to make differential pressure CO 2 electrolysis the industrial standard it deserves to be.

papers.title: Echo-DESI mass spectrometry for automated nanolitre-scale ultrahigh-throughput reaction screening
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening underpins modern enzyme engineering, synthetic biology and reaction discovery, yet current workflows remain constrained by an analytical compromise between throughput and molecular specificity. Optical and labelled assays provide rapid screening but limited chemical information, whereas chromatography-coupled mass spectrometry (MS) offers molecular confidence at the expense of speed, sample consumption and solvent demand. Here we present Echo-DESI-MS, an automated nanolitre-scale MS workflow that enables label-free ultrahigh-throughput molecular screening by coupling acoustic liquid transfer with desorption electrospray ionisation MS imaging. Using contactless acoustic droplet ejection, the platform enables deposition in two minutes of up to 1536 discrete reaction aliquots onto a single microscope slide which can be analysed directly by ambient surface ionisation at approximately 3 s per sample. To support extraction of these high-density imaging datasets, we developed SpotExtractor, a dedicated software environment that converts a single MS imaging file into reaction-resolved quantitative outputs, integrating automated data extraction, sample labelling and visualisations. We validate the performance of this workflow using a 23-member cytochrome P450 BM3 hydroxylation library, achieving reaction conversion readouts with average standard deviations of 2.2%, negligible spot-to-spot carryover and approximately 120-fold faster analysis than equivalent LC-MS screening while using over three orders of magnitude less sample. The platform is compatible with repeat interrogation of deposited libraries by tandem MS and ion mobility and provides a generalisable route to sustainable high-throughput analytical screening across biocatalysis, directed evolution and high-density chemical assay workflows.

papers.title: Periodic Reassessment or Permanent Approval? A Critical Analysis of the EU Commission’s Proposal to Reform Pesticide and Biocide Authorisation in Europe
papers.abstract: On 16 December 2025, the European Commission published proposal COM(2025) 1030 within the Food and Feed Safety Simplification Omnibus, aiming to amend Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 on plant protection products and Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 on biocidal products. The proposal converts the current time-limited approvals of pesticide and biocide active substances (typically 10 to 15 years, followed by mandatory renewal) into time-unlimited approvals by default, replacing periodic reassessment with a reactive, case-triggered review mechanism initiated at the Commission's discretion. This paper sets out the proposed amendments, surveys the positions taken by the principal stakeholder groups (EU institutions, industry associations, farming organisations, civil society, and the scientific community), and finally presents our own analysis. The Commission justifies the suggested changes largely with the removal of administrative inefficiency. Industry and farming organisations broadly endorse this perspective, whereas civil society organisations oppose the proposal as a weakening of public safety and a disregard of environmental concerns. We find the Commission's justifications insufficient. The proposal was adopted without a full impact assessment and without a public consultation, and the Commission's claim that "no viable alternatives" exist disregards the obvious options of extending renewal periods, leveraging the One Substance, One Assessment framework, or reforming the Biocide Review Programme. Substantively, unlimited approval freezes the evidence base at the date of each substance's most recent evaluation, which for many active substances predates the 2018 endocrine disruption criteria, the 2023 EFSA bee guidance, and ongoing revisions of aquatic and terrestrial ecotoxicology guidance. It also removes the self-selection mechanism through which industry currently withdraws substances expected to fail renewal, which might hamper marked access for innovative solutions. Finally, the proposal introduces legal uncertainty through the deemed mutual recognition between Member States. The replacement of periodic review by Commission-triggered reassessment makes regulatory action dependent on political will and on the monitoring capacity of under-resourced agencies, neither of which past practice gives reason to consider sufficient. A further structural consequence, not assessed by the Commission, is the displacement of scientific disputes from administrative procedure to judicial review.

papers.title: Programmable and decodable synthetic polymer architectures through DNA-templated assembly
papers.abstract: The properties of synthetic polymers are encoded in their molecular architecture, yet no general framework exists to systematically control or decode that architecture. This gap has left vast regions of polymer design space unexplored, limiting the discovery of materials with tailored properties. Here, we establish DNA as a molecular programming language for synthetic polymers. Sequence-defined scaffolds direct diverse polymer blocks into programmable architectures including linear, star, and graft, decoupling spatial organization from chemical synthesis. In star architectures, programmed arm placement translates ionic strength into architecture-dependent shifts in spatial organization and rigidity. In graft architectures, DNA barcodes enable one-pot assembly and sequence-resolved decoding of arm placement in complex mixtures. These results establish a framework in which DNA programs, diversifies, and decodes the architecture of synthetic matter, accelerating discovery across materials science and medicine.

papers.title: Information entropy-based structural-functional chemintropic similarities for modeling binding reactions and design of antiviral molecules
papers.abstract: Chemical similarity is a fundamental concept in chemistry, materials science, and biology. The Tanimoto similarity measure is crucial in these areas; however, it has certain limitations, such as its inability to consider molecular function, lack of quantitative structural information, and sensitivity to molecular fingerprints. This study introduces chemintropic similarity (CS), an entropy-based metric that integrates both structural and functional molecular attributes within an entropic space using Shannon entropy theory. CS employs fractional Shannon entropy arrays derived from molecular representations (e.g., SMILES) and optimizes context parameters through machine learning. Incorporated into an entropic k-nearest neighbor (ekNN) model as a distance metric, CS surpasses conventional similarity measures, including Tanimoto, across multiple datasets, demonstrating reduced prediction errors and enhanced generalizability, particularly with small datasets. Variants utilizing Renyi entropy and entropy extracted from standard molecular fingerprints further improve model accuracy. The ekNN approach also exceeds baseline graph neural network (GNN) models in predictive performance. Applied to drug-virus interaction modeling, CS accurately predicts ligand binding to Dengue virus serotypes, facilitating pan-serotype modeling. By leveraging the "magic methyl" effect, a molecular design workflow was developed to generate novel drug candidates with significantly improved theoretical potency compared to GNN-based methods. This all-entropic framework offers a robust platform for molecular property prediction, activity cliff modeling, and drug design, integrating structural-functional information entropy to advance cheminformatics and drug discovery.

papers.title: Dual Fluorophore System for Direct Measurement of Acidity of Aerosol Particles
papers.abstract: Atmospheric aerosol particles exhibit diverse physical and chemical properties, depending on their composition and source, which are challenging to measure directly due to their chemical complexity. Aerosol acidity is a key chemical property that has significant implications for climate, heterogeneous chemistry, and human health. Here, we present a novel approach to measure aerosol acidity using carbon dots (CDs) as in situ fluorophores. The method uses a dual fluorophore system consisting of pH-sensitive CDs and pHinsensitive CDs incorporated into model aerosol particles, with the pH-insensitive CDs serving as an internal standard. Fluorescence microscopy was used to construct a calibration curve by plotting the ratio of fluorescence intensities of droplets of fluorophorecontaining standard solutions against pH. This calibration curve was used to determine the pH of model aerosol particles in the range of pH 1.5 – pH 3.5, demonstrating the e]icacy of this approach for real-time and direct measurement of the acidity. This approach holds significant potential to parameterize acidity in models, refine our understanding and predictions of aerosol properties such as heterogeneous chemistry, and aid in assessing the impact of aerosol particles on climate and health.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Crowdsourcing Initiative to Accelerate DEL-ML Hit Finding in Drug Discovery
authors: The First DREAM Target 2035 Challenge Consortium
papers.abstract: Rapid progress in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) is expected to dramatically accelerate the way therapeutic strategies and drugs are discovered. One of the first steps in a drug discovery campaign is to identify bioactive “hit” molecules that can be optimized into drugs. DNA-encoded libraries coupled with ML (DEL-ML) is a novel hit-finding technique where ML models are trained on ultra-large DEL screening data and used to predict hits from catalogs of readily available molecules. However, best strategies for data representation, model architecture, or hit selection are not yet clearly established. In this first open DEL-ML Target 2035 drug discovery challenge, AI experts combined their ML models with computational chemistry approaches to discover hits for the target protein WDR91, both retrospectively and prospectively. A great variety of computational strategies and tools were deployed, and novel WDR91 ligands were discovered. While a clear differentiating factor was the choice in data to train ML models, variations in fingerprint representation or model architecture had comparatively little impact on the outcome, emphasizing the need for impactful AI-driven technological improvement.

papers.title: Molecular engineering of chiral–polar one-dimensional helical perovskites for circularly polarized light detection and bulk photovoltaic effect
papers.abstract: One-dimensional (1D) helical perovskites have recently emerged as an attractive platform for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection owing to their intrinsically chiral electronic structures. However, many helical thin films remain effectively nonpolar at the macroscopic level despite their chiral crystal structures, limiting the emergence of polar optoelectronic phenomena such as the bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE). Here we show that molecular substituent engineering of chiral organic cations provides a direct route to lowering the crystal symmetry of 1D helical lead–halide perovskite thin films from a chiral nonpolar phase ( P 2 1 2 1 2 1 ) to a chiral–polar phase ( P 2 1 ) while preserving the strongly distorted helical inorganic framework. This symmetry reduction converts previously nonpolar helical films into polar ones, thereby activating BPVE without sacrificing the pronounced chiroptical response inherent to the helical structure. Chiral–polar 1D helical perovskite films exhibit highly selective CPL detection with large extinction ratios, together with a clear zero-bias photocurrent and finite photovoltage under solar illumination arising from BPVE. Importantly, the emergence of BPVE is not achieved by introducing a distinct structural motif, but rather by symmetry lowering within the same 1D helical architecture through targeted molecular design. These results demonstrate that 1D helical perovskites can simultaneously support chiral spin-selective optoelectronic responses and polar photovoltaic functionality within a single structural platform. By exploiting symmetry control through organic cation design, we establish 1D helical architectures as a unified materials platform for integrating chiral and polar optoelectronic functionalities in solution-processable hybrid materials.

papers.title: Observation of Covalent Adaptable Networks with Single-Particle Tracking Reveals Broad Spectrum of Diffusers
papers.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are materials with reversible bonds that give desirable properties not present in permanent networks, such as recyclability or self-healing. The introduction of the bond exchange process imparts complex dynamic behavior which is not yet fully understood. Analysis of CAN dynamics is difficult, since they are usually evaluated with techniques such as rheology or simulation, requiring assumptions of underlying models. Here, we solve this limitation by applying single-particle tracking (SPT) to analyze the motion of tracer polymers moving through CANs. This allows for direct visualization of chain rearrangement in-situ. We demonstrate that SPT is an effective technique for evaluating CAN dynamics by evaluating the self-diffusion of chains at several different crosslink densities. By synthesizing tracers either with or without crosslinkable groups, we quantify the effect of crosslinking on the movement of network strands. Interestingly, we find that the difference between these sets of tracers is significantly smaller than we expected. Further analysis reveals a broad spectrum of diffusers whose behavior is primarily affected by the behavior of the surrounding matrix. Diffusive timescales were found to be shorter than analogous rheological crossover timescales, suggesting that the crossover time is composed of several crosslink rearrangement steps

papers.title: Modulating Multicenter Bonding through Facile Addition of Diradical Precursors to a Bipyridine-Stabilized Borane
Atomically Precise Structures of Oleate-Capped CdSe Nanocrystals Determined by DNP-Enhanced Dipolar Dephasing Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are of interest due to their tunable electronic and optical properties. However, the characterization of surface structures of NCs remains an unresolved challenge. Here, we demonstrate that rotational-echo double-resonance (REDOR) experiments can be used to determine precise structural models of CdSe NC surfaces. An atom efficient ligandexchange scheme is demonstrated to introduce partially 13C-enriched oleate ligands onto CdSe NCs and enable 13C dephased REDOR experiments. DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd} and 111Cd{13C} REDOR NMR experiments were performed on the 13C-enriched oleate-capped CdSe zinc blende CdSe NCs. papers.title: Predictable hierarchical assembly of liquid-liquid phase separated carbon dot coacervates
papers.abstract: Hierarchical assembly of mesoscale components facilitates construction of complex organization of matter. Likewise, programmable assembly of cell-mimicking liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS)-mediated heterogeneous droplets would widen the design space of complex life-like materials. In this context, we introduce coacervates derived from a non-ionic, amphiphilic, and fluorescent polymer carbon dots (CDs) that spontaneously undergo LLPS, forming multiphase droplets with sharp internal interfaces and distinct compartmental morphologies. The difference in interfacial tension between dissimilar CD types primarily governs the hierarchical arrangement of phases, generating core-shell, Janus, and hybrid architectures. Even transition between core-shell to Janus morphology is achieved by modifying the surface tension of the assembling phases through simple adjustment of the solution pH. Leveraging the interfacial tensions of different CDs, we rationally designed and predictively constructed diverse multiphasic coacervate architectures, with controlled and reproducible outcomes. Compared to the archetypal random demixing, compartmentalization, and assembly of droplets, these designer mesoscopic assemblies of heterogenous coacervates allow bottom-up synthesis of predictable three-dimensional structures with adaptive and fluorescent compartments. Taken together, this work bridges a critical gap in understanding phase segregation in simple coacervate systems and establishes a robust, label-free platform for probing the physicochemical principles underlying hierarchical assemblies. These findings carry direct implications for the design of advanced soft materials that emulate biological complexity.

papers.title: Mapping Regioisomer-Dependent Buchwald-Hartwig C-N Coupling: Bromoimidazo[1,5-a]pyridines as a Model Electrophile Series
papers.abstract: Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling is a central method for constructing aryl- and heteroaryl-nitrogen bonds, yet condition translatability often fails for heteroaryl halides, even among closely related substrates. In this work, we examine the six available bromoimidazo[1,5-a]pyridine regioisomers using a representative nucleophile panel comprising benzamide, aniline, morpholine, and benzylamine. A limited-scale HTE campaign was conducted with an in-house ligand set, a fixed palladium source, and two bases. Reaction performance was assessed by LCMS with internal standard calibration, and selected hits were verified by preparative re-runs and NMR-confirmed product assignment. The resulting conversion and product yield maps reveal strong dependence on bromide position, nucleophile class, and ligand/base selection. The 6- and 8-bromo isomers show the broadest productive reactivity profiles, whereas the 5- and 7-isomers require narrow condition windows. The imidazole-ring 1- and 3-bromo isomers react readily but do not provide isolable, structurally confirmed target products. Methodologically, this work demonstrates that a compact HTE workflow can rapidly define useful ligand/base combinations for heteroaryl bromides while preventing misleading conclusions from conversion-only analysis. The same approach can be applied as an early-stage reactivity screen for other heteroaryl halide series.

papers.title: Samarium Catalyzed Hydrogenation of Unsaturated Compounds: A SmII or Sm0 Chemistry?
papers.abstract: Magnesium in combination with chlorotrimethylsilane (TMSCl) is commonly employed to develop SmI2 catalysis to perform reductions and reductive coupling reactions, where reductions were proposed to occur through electron transfer from SmI2. Present investigation demonstrated that under similar conditions, Mg turnings reduce higher valent samarium into its metallic state, which forms a coating on the surface of Mg turnings. This novel surface can act as an effective heterogeneous catalyst to perform hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes using TMSCl as an activator and tert-butanol as a hydrogen source. Detailed investigation using radical trapping, EPR spectroscopy and stoichiometric reactions with SmI2/additives completely ruled out the possibility of electron transfer and radical-based mechanism in these reactions. Mechanistic investigation is consistent with samarium in zero-oxidation state (Sm0) as the active catalyst enabling hydrogenation.

papers.title: A Review of the effect of wood species and chemical treatment on the optical properties of transparent wood
papers.abstract: Research on the topic of transparent wood (TW) has gained a lot of traction in recent years, with the largest uses as an energy-efficient building material, particularly as a replacement for glass and optical systems involving UV shielding and light management. However, there is no coherent or standardised framework in literature with regards to the best choice of wood species and treatment parameters to utilise to obtain the desired optical performance. This article compares the effectiveness of different treatments on various wood types and species to identify, which yield the best optical properties in TW and compiled results from the relevant literature of the past ten years. The findings show that hardwoods achieve better transmittance and haze and the optical properties improve with decreasing density. Wood species with low lignin and extractive content yield the best optical results. Alkaline treatment for delignification was the most effective to produce TW, even for thicker wood samples and softwoods generally require longer treatment times to obtain comparable delignification and transmittance as hardwoods.

papers.title: Hierarchical Flux Competition Governs Electrochemical-Chemical Coupling in Redox-Mediated Batteries
papers.abstract: Redox-mediated processes offer an effective strategy to accelerate sluggish kinetics and improve active-material utilization across diverse battery chemistries. However, rational optimization of redox-mediated systems remains challenging due to the lack of a quantitative framework describing the interplay among competing kinetic processes. Here, we establish a kinetic framework for electrochemical-chemical coupling by defining three effective flux descriptors corresponding to interfacial electron transfer, solid-state ion transport, and mediator diffusion. These descriptors, integrated with electrochemical parameters, reveal the hierarchy of competing fluxes and enable analytical determination of current-matching boundaries. The resulting framework provides a systematic approach to identify and manipulate rate-limiting steps, achieving flux-balanced operation with enhanced utilization and reduced polarization. Guided by this framework, a redox-targeting flow battery based on a [Fe(CN)6]3-/4-/Prussian blue catholyte delivers a volumetric capacity of 48 Ah/L at 100 mA/cm2 over 6,500 h, and achieves 27.6 Wh/L in a full-cell configuration. The demonstrated correspondence between kinetic descriptors, regime transitions, and device performance highlights the general applicability of the framework to redox-mediated electrochemical systems. This work reframes battery optimization as a problem of flux hierarchy and provides a generalizable pathway toward simultaneous enhancement of energy density and rate capability.

papers.title: Marcus Inverted Electron Transfer in Redox-Mediated Lithiation of Iron Phosphate
papers.abstract: Redox-mediated reactions enable charge transfer processes beyond conventional heterogeneous electrode interfaces and have emerged as versatile strategies in energy storage and conversion systems. However, the interfacial electron transfer mechanisms governing these reactions remain elusive. Here, ferrocene derivatives are employed as redox mediators to investigate interfacial electron transfer using the FePO4/LiFePO4 intercalation reaction as a model system, enabling independent control of thermodynamic driving force and electron transfer distance. This approach allows direct experimental observation of a Marcus-type inverted region. More importantly, the dependence of reaction kinetics on driving force can be fundamentally altered by interfacial electronic coupling, such that electron transfer distance becomes a dominant factor governing the overall reaction rate.
