Molecular stability further emerges as a key factor governing the effectiveness of redox-mediated processes under practical conditions and high utilization of FePO4 (up to 97%) is achieved through rational mediator selection. These results provide a general framework for understanding interfacial electron transfer in complex electrochemical environments and reveal the key factors governing redox-mediated reactions.

papers.title: Data-efficient protein language models craft ultrastable carbon-capture enzymes beyond evolution
papers.abstract: α-carbonic anhydrases (αCAs) underpin industrial carbon capture, yet natural enzymes are notoriously unstable under operational stresses. To overcome this limitation, a family-specific, fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) is developed and integrated with experimental validation to explore αCA sequence space beyond traditional protein design approaches. Although αCAs already operate near diffusion-limited rates (kcat ≈ 10 5 -10 6 s -1 ), the lead designed variant exhibited unprecedented robustness, remaining stable at 95 ºC and achieving a 1.8-fold increase in activity relative to the premier benchmark enzyme tdCA S82Y (stable up to 80 ºC; kcat ≈ 10 6 s -1 ). Despite sharing only 65.8% maximum sequence identity with the reference dataset, the engineered αCA enzyme outperforms all natural and ancestral counterparts. Computation-guided mutagenesis reveals distinct ligand-binding features absent in previously characterized αCAs, providing mechanistic insight into the enhanced performance. These findings demonstrate the utility of fine-tuned PLMs to access unexplored protein design space and establish a generalizable blueprint for engineering diverse protein families.

papers.title: Branched Kinetic Pathways Couple Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation to Supramolecular Polymerization
papers.abstract: Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) increasingly appears in supramolecular polymerization, yet whether dense liquid-like states are obligatory precursors, off-pathway aggregates, or alternative productive routes remains unresolved. Here we resolve this question for a naphthalene diimide-based boronic acid (NDBA) sticker–spacer monomer by directly simulating its spontaneous assembly from dispersed monomers into an ordered fibre at atomistic resolution without apriori structural bias. Unbiased multi-trajectory molecular dynamics, combined with structural order parameters, autoencoder-based dimensionality reduction, Markov state modeling, and transition-path analysis, reveals a metastable liquid-like condensed basin that is distinct from both transient oligomers and the final supramolecular polymer. Crucially, the kinetic network is branched rather than sequential. Most productive flux proceeds through a direct monomer-to-polymer pathway, whereas a substantial minority passes through an LLPS-mediated route before reaching the same ordered fibre. Seeded simulations further show that the condensed state is competent to support templated ordering. These results establish LLPS as a productive but nonobligate intermediate and provide a kinetic-network framework for quantifying pathway complexity in phase-separating supramolecular materials.

papers.title: Solvent and field effects on photoinduced ring-opening: dynamics of furan as a case study
papers.abstract: In this work, we approach the simulation of the light-induced ultrafast dynamics of furan from a new angle. We deeply investigate the impact of the explicit inclusion of the incident pulse and the description of protic and aprotic solvents on the photorelaxation. Upon excitation, furan is driven back to its electronic ground state via two deactivation channels, one characterized by a ring-puckering of the oxygen and one by a ring-opening via breaking of the carbon-oxygen bond. We found that explicitly including an 11 fs pulse in the simulation has a slight accelerating effect on the population dynamics; in addition, we could see an increase in the coherent motion of the puckering mode of furan. Interestingly, both solvents facilitate the ring-opening, an effect stronger observed in protic methanol thanks to the hydrogen-bonding of the solvent stabilizing the ring-open molecule. Overall, the study validates the general robustness of the routine approximation of simulating photodynamics in the gas phase using the sudden excitation approximation, but it also highlights differences that form the basis for future improvements of extending nonadiabatic dynamics simulations to an improved description of solvent and field effects.

papers.title: Towards C12 Polymer Precursors: Development of a Sustainable Value Chain Derived from Local Plant Oils
papers.abstract: The transition towards renewable carbon sources is essential for the sustainable production of polymer materials. Plant oil-derived oleochemicals represent promising feedstocks due to their wide availability and compatibility with existing industrial processes. In particular, renewable C12 building blocks are attractive intermediates for the synthesis of polyamides and polyesters, yet efficient and scalable routes from locally available plant oils remain limited. Herein, a complete value chain from plant oil-derived methyl oleate to a diverse portfolio of renewable C12 polymer precursors is demonstrated. Methyl 9-undecenoate was produced via cross-metathesis of methyl oleate with crude 2-butene using a ruthenium catalyst system tolerant towards impurities present in technical feedstocks. Reaction optimisation established robust conditions with conversions of up to 90% and selectivities of up to 93%. The process was successfully scaled from 20 mL to 300 mL without significant loss of performance, enabling the isolation of methyl 9-undecenoate with a purity of up to 99.4%. Subsequent isomerising functionalisation reactions, including methoxycarbonylation and hydroformylation, provided access to the key platform molecules 1,12-dimethyl dodecanedioate and methyl 12-oxododecanoate. These intermediates were further converted into a range of symmetric and asymmetric C12 polymer precursors such as diols, diamines, dicarboxylic acids as well as amino-, alcohol- and carboxylic acid functionalised esters. The presented approach establishes a scalable pathway from locally available plant oils to renewable C12 building blocks with high renewable carbon content, highlighting their potential for more sustainable polymer production.

papers.title: (Solid-)liquid-liquid equilibria in the ternary acetonitrile + n-heptane + palmitic acid system between 298K and 313K
papers.abstract: High-value, low-volume solutes are characteristic in the residues of bioprocessing wastes and are typically the focus of separation process design, with the equilibria of the waxy bulk components often being overlooked in the separation. In this work, a low-volume method for the measurement of (solid-)liquid-liquid equilibrium data is validated and applied for the generation of new (S)LLE data for the ternary system of acetonitrile + n-heptane + palmitic acid between 298 and 313 K. The results show that the fatty acid reports overwhelmingly to the alkane phase with temperature having a small effect on the distribution of palmitic acid between the phases, but a significant effect on the liquid operating region with rapidly decreasing solubility at lower temperatures. The data were modelled predictively using the new modified UNIFAC 2.0 model, and correlated with NRTL. The former was unable to capture quantitative details of the experimentally observed equilibria, while the latter showed excellent agreement with the data at all temperatures. The results reassert the importance of quantifying all equilibria present in a given system for the design of efficient and effective separation processes.

papers.title: Are Atoms Enough? An Explainable Graph Neural Network for Carbon Capture and Gas Separation in Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Are atoms enough to represent metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) in a graph neural network? Dominant crystal graph neural networks assume so, encoding each MOF entirely through its atoms and leaving pore space to emerge on its own. We introduce PoreGCN, a heterogeneous graph neural network in which Voronoi-derived pore vertices sit alongside atoms via dedicated atom-to-pore edges, giving the model a direct view of the cavities that govern adsorption and separation. Adding pore vertices produces large gains on the properties that matter most for screening. On the 2,737 real CoRE MOFs, the largest cavity diameter R2 rises from 0.07 under an atom-only baseline to 0.95 under PoreGCN. On the 51,163 hypothetical hMOF structures, PoreGCN reaches R2 between 0.91 and 0.99 across five geometric properties and R2 = 0.86 on log10(CO2/N2) selectivity. Retaining atoms alongside pores also unlocks two complementary attribution channels, the pore branch identifies which cavities drive a prediction, and the atom branch traces those cavities back to the metal nodes and linker chemistry responsible for them, something a pore-only model cannot do. Agreement between these two channels, combined with ensemble consensus, defines a four-scenario trust framework that separates individual predictions worth acting on from those requiring further validation, regardless of the model's population-level accuracy. Trustworthy selectivity predictions are 83.8% accurate at the 20% relative-error threshold against 8.3% for the untrustworthy subset, a roughly tenfold precision lift on the same model and test partition. The signal survives distribution shift, the condition that matters most in practice, maintaining a 1.3 to 2.0-fold enrichment on real CoRE MOFs as an independent external dataset, even where population-level calibration has been lost entirely. PoreGCN also recovers established chemistry independently, ranking fluorinated linkers and Zr-cluster secondary building units highest for CO 2 /N 2 selectivity. Predictions, trust labels, and per-atom attributions are available through a public web tool. https://huggingface.co/spaces/catenate/PoreGCN

papers.title: Do Frozen SMILES Foundation Embeddings Beat Fingerprints? A Split- and Low-Data Benchmark on ADMET and CNS Bioactivity Tasks
papers.abstract: In cheminformatics and molecular machine learning, frozen embeddings from pretrained SMILES encoders are an attractive low-cost feature source for property prediction, but their practical value depends on whether they improve over strong classical baselines. A common frozen-feature workflow is evaluated in which ChemBERTa or MoLFormer embeddings are cached once and then paired with inexpensive downstream classifiers for ADMET and CNS bioactivity classification. The comparators are Morgan fingerprints and RDKit descriptors, which remain strong practical cheminformatics baselines when combined with random forests, XGBoost, or logistic regression. To avoid conflating representation quality with downstream classifier choice, each representation family is paired with logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost classifiers where available. The revised benchmark contains 2580 completed fits across 8 curated binary tasks, 12 model configurations, random splits, scaffold splits, and low-data training budgets of 50, 100, 250, and 500 molecules. Frozen-vs-classical family comparisons are available for 43 dataset-regime rows; in this retrospective oracle comparison, the best classical baseline wins 36 rows and the best frozen embedding wins 7 rows. Across 215 paired seed-level comparisons, the mean AUROC difference for best frozen embedding minus best classical baseline is -0.026 with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [-0.032, -0.021]. A clustered bootstrap over dataset-regime rows gives a similar mean difference of -0.025 [-0.032, -0.018]. The average gap is modest but does not support default replacement of Morgan/RDKit baselines by frozen SMILES embeddings. These results provide a practical benchmarking recommendation for small-data cheminformatics and ADMET modeling workflows

papers.title: Long-range Metal-Metal Cooperative Nitrile Activation in 1,8-Diazaanthracene-supported Dicopper Complexes
papers.abstract: A 1,8-diazaanthracene based ligand (tBuPN-NP) is introduced as a platform that can combine metal-ligand cooperativity with long range metal-metal cooperativity. The scaffold enforces a welldefined large Cu···Cu separation while retaining sites capable of reversible dearomatization. This arrangement enables cooperative small-molecule activation across spatially separated metal centres, exemplified by formation of a nitrile-derived μ-bridged cyanomethyl fragment.

papers.title: Heat-Stable Oxytocin Formulations: A Review of Molecular Degradation, Cold-Chain Risk, and Stabilization Strategies
papers.abstract: Oxytocin is a cyclic nonapeptide used for labor induction, labor augmentation, and the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). It remains a first-line uterotonic for PPH prevention and treatment because of its low cost, rapid action, availability, and clinician familiarity. However, oxytocin has limited formulation stability and is highly sensitive to storage conditions. In aqueous solution, it is susceptible to heat-induced loss of potency and is therefore stored under refrigerated conditions at 2–8 °C. This requirement is difficult to maintain in lowresource supply chains, where inconsistent manufacturing, long transport routes, weak cold storage, and temperature fluctuations at the point of care can lead to poor-quality oxytocin. Heat accelerates deamidation, beta-elimination, disulfide exchange, oligosulfide formation, dimerization, oxidation, and aggregation. This review connects real-world evidence of oxytocin quality issues with the chemical processes behind its degradation, and discusses formulation approaches that can reduce or prevent specific breakdown pathways. The most defensible stabilization approaches are maintaining the formulation at approximately pH 4.5 , optimized buffer concentration, divalent metal-ion coordination, N-terminal amino-group modulation by 18-crown-6, chlorobutanol-assisted stabilization, and solid-state immobilization through inhalable dry powders or fast-dissolving tablets. Heat-stable carbetocin demonstrates that thermal stability of uterotonic peptides are feasible, but it does not eliminate the need for stable oxytocin as it is used across a wider range of obstetric indications. The review concludes with a framework and development plan that integrate supply-chain risk control, formulation design-space analysis, stability-indicating analytics, LC-MS degradation mapping, excipient screening, solid-state formulation, and predictive kinetic modeling.

papers.title: Facet Dependence for CeO2 as a Potential Ammonia Oxidation Electrocatalyst Studied by DFT
papers.abstract: The transition toward a carbon-free energy system requires energy carriers that are both sustainable and practical to scale. Ammonia is a promising candidate due to its high energy density, established infrastructure, and compatibility with renewable electricity. A key challenge in direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs) development is the lack of inexpensive, active, and poison-resistant anode catalysts capable of efficiently carrying out the ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR). Ceria (CeO 2 ) related materials have shown potential for AOR and adjacent reactions, however, a comprehensive mechanistic understanding of AOR on pristine ceria surfaces has not previously been established. This density functional theory (DFT) study examines CeO 2 (111), CeO 2 (110), and CeO 2 (100) for AOR. CeO 2 (100) was found to be the most active surface with the least positive limiting potential of 1.16 V and a potential determining step (PDS) of *NH 3 → *NH 2 . CeO 2 (111) and CeO 2 (110) possessed limiting potentials of 1.38 V and 1.33 V, respectively, with the same PDS as CeO 2 (100). Among oxide materials, the activity of CeO 2 (100) is improved over NiO. Introducing vacancies into CeO 2 may further improve its activity toward AOR.

papers.title: A Scalable Method for Quantitation of Per-and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Human Milk
Electrocatalytic Polarity Inversion of Azlactones: Access to α-Quaternary Amino Acids with Electron-Rich Coupling Partners
papers.abstract: The use of azlactones as nucleophiles is a well-established strategy to access α-quaternary amino acids. Herein, we present an electrocatalytic approach that reverses the natural polarity of azlactones. Indirect oxidation of the azlactone enolate, using triarylamine electrocatalysts, generates an electrophilic radical intermediate that couple with a variety of electron-rich SOMOphiles. This strategy enables Csp 3 –Csp 2 and Csp 3 –Csp 3 bond formation at the α-position of azlactone, providing access to arylated, β-oxoalkylated, alkenylated and allylated quaternary amino acid derivatives.

papers.title: No Pose Left Behind: Integrating Activity and Structural Data with Uncertainty-Aware Multi-objective Learning for Kinase Inhibitor Prediction
papers.abstract: Kinase inhibitors are central to targeted therapies, yet the disparity between large activity-focused databases (≈ 224, 000 unique kinase-ligand pairs in ChEMBL) and much smaller, structural datasets (≈ 6, 738 unique structures in KLIFS) limits the performance of structure-based machine learning (ML) for kinase-inhibitor binding affinity predictions. Although docking and other computational methods can generate large numbers of in silico structures, their use is typically restricted to poses within 2−4 Å of an experimental reference, discarding much of the simulated data. In this work, we introduce multi-objective Kinodata3D, a multi-objective E(3)invariant graph neural network (GNN) that leverages kinase–ligand structures across a broad range of structural quality. The model jointly predicts binding affinity, activity uncertainty, and structural quality, using the predicted reliability of each complex to weight its contribution to the activity loss. This allows the model to learn from a wide range of in silico structures without treating all of them as equally informative. Compared with an equivalent model without structure-quality prediction, multiobjective Kinodata3D reduces activity-prediction error and assigns lower uncertainty to structurally reliable complexes. Incorporating low-quality poses helps the model identify structurally unreliable complexes and assign them higher uncertainty, while prioritizing affinity learning from high-quality structures. By explicitly modeling structural quality, multi-objective Kinodata3D makes affinity predictions more interpretable by linking prediction confidence to the reliability of the input structure. These results show that in silico structures spanning a broad range of pose qualities can be used reliably for binding affinity prediction when structural uncertainty is modeled directly. Because the framework is agnostic to the structuregeneration method, it provides a general strategy for reducing structural data scarcity and delivering more accurate, better-calibrated, and more interpretable predictions for structure-based ML in drug discovery. multi-objective Kinodata3D is available at https://github.com/openkinome/multi-objective-kinodata-3D

papers.title: Mechanism of Aspartate 174-Regulated Activation of the Human Hv1 Proton Channel
papers.abstract: The allosteric activation and subsequent proton transport mechanisms of the human voltage-gated proton channel hHv1 remain elusive. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to investigate the role of highly conserved Asp174 in the work cycle of hHv1. Our simulations reveal that Asp174 protonation reduces the salt bridge-dominated activation barrier by one-third, thereby accelerating channel opening. Moreover, Asp174 neutralization triggers full opening of the hydrophobic gate in the active state, which is associated with the prolonged lifetime of proton transfer path that bypasses Asp112 at the central crevice of the pore, supporting the critical role of Asp112 as a proton shuttle. Finally, we propose a revised mechanism with atomic details that sheds light on the function of hHv1 and ion channels with Asp174-equivalent residues.

papers.title: Mapping Hierarchical Motifs in disorder-order transitions: learning the hierarchy of structural motifs in supercooled water and ice polymorphs
papers.abstract: Disorder-order transitions pass through structurally rich intermediates that conventional order parameters and classification cannot fully resolve. By extending the hierarchical motif framework previously demonstrated for static materials,1–3 we learn a discrete vocabulary of structural motifs and a grammar of how they interact in space and time from homogeneous nucleation of supercooled water simulated using the ML-BOP model. By leveraging vector quantization of the multimodal variational autoencoder (VAE) latent space, we establish the motif vocabulary comprising discrete labels (codebook) of liquid-like, transient and ice-like motifs. Moreover, the variance component of the VAE quantifies the local disorder, decreasing from liquid to transient to ice motifs, which are inaccessible in conventional classifiers. Analysis of the motif grammar, including motif-motif transition and primitivering co-occurrence, reveals a consistent picture of ice nucleation; in supercooled water, transient motifs comprising low-density-liquid precursors in pentamer/hexamer networks form metastable stacking-disordered ice nuclei, eventually growing into non-consolidating Ih/Ic domains. Crucially, our analysis uncovers role of LD liquid motifs forming pentamers and distorted hexamers as precursors to ice nucleation, which was previously unelucidated. Extending the motif vocabulary to hypothetical ice polymorphs identifies approximately 252,000 candidates that are structurally similar to transient motifs; heterogeneous nucleation simulations with four selected candidates evidence that ice/liquid interface controls selective Ic and Ih growth. Beyond identifying structural motifs and characterizing their relationships in supercooled water, our hierarchical framework provides a general methodology for understanding other systems of interest across distinct fields (microscopy experiments1–3) and physical regimes (disorder-order transitions).

papers.title: Single-Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: The crystallization of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) into single crystals remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three tripty cene-based single-crystalline COFs (COF-563, -564, and -565) under mild conditions within 24 hours. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH 2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of 3D COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp,

papers.title: Copper-Catalysed Arylation of Cyclic and Bridged Diamines for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Cyclic diamines are a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry, widely used to modulate physicochemical properties and as linker units in bifunctional molecules such as PROTACs (Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras). Existing approaches for aryl functionalisation of these motifs rely on SNAr or Buchwald–Hartwig amination, but methods for cyclic and bridged cyclic diamines remain underdeveloped. We report an operationally simple, ligand-free copper-catalysed Chan–Lam amination that couples arylboronic acids with a broad range of cyclic diamines under mild conditions. The protocol tolerates diverse functional groups, including halides and heteroaryl motifs, delivering pharmaceutically relevant building blocks in good yields. Notably, this strategy enables the first general access to bridged cyclic aryldiamines via Chan–Lam coupling, expanding the scope of this transformation. This method complements existing approaches and provides a practical route to complex diamine architectures for medicinal chemistry applications.

papers.title: Physics-Based vs AI-Based Free Energy Prediction for Protein-Ligand Potency: Public Benchmarks and Internal Project Evidence
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-ligand binding affinity remains a central challenge in computational drug discovery. Recent AI-based approaches can achieve strong performance on established public benchmarks; however, their robustness under distribution shift and in fully prospective settings remains unclear. In contrast, physics-based relative binding free energy (RBFE) calculations, exemplified by FEP+, have demonstrated consistently high accuracy across diverse perturbation classes, yet reproducing this performance with open and alternative implementations has proven difficult. Here, we study two questions: (i) which factors most strongly govern the accuracy and robustness of modern RBFE workflows, and (ii) to what extent current AI methods can complement or replace physics-based RBFE for potency prediction, particularly on previously unseen chemical matter. We introduce AnewFEP, a GROMACS-based RBFE workflow that combines a machine-learning-derived small-molecule force field with REST2 sampling and a set of numerical and protocol improvements targeting known failure modes. On a public benchmark suite comprising 1147 ligands across multiple perturbation categories, AnewFEP achieves an overall pairwise RMSE of 1.38 kcal/mol, comparable to FEP+ (1.26 kcal/mol). Through targeted case studies, we demonstrate how localized force field refinements, protein conformational control, and alchemical schedule design can substantially improve accuracy and stability. Finally, using internal fully prospective datasets consisting of de novo molecules, we show that a structure-predictive foundation model (Boltz-2) exhibits weak rank-ordering performance, whereas AnewFEP retains discriminatory power between weak and strong binders. Collectively, these results suggest that while AI methods are valuable on curated benchmarks, physics-based free energy calculations remain critical for prospective decision-making under distribution shift.

papers.title: Density-Corrected Density Functional Theory for Solids
papers.abstract: Density-corrected density functional theory (DC-DFT) considers whether self-consistent densities yield optimal energetics in Kohn-Sham calculations. With considerable success in molecular calculations, we here apply DC-DFT to solid-state calculations with Hartree-Fock (HF) densities. We resolve a known anomaly: that dispersion corrections can worsen results as one climbs Jacob’s ladder. This is illustrated for simple covalent solids, such as Si. The relative energetics of phases of ice are also much improved with HF densities, as is CO absorption on NaCl, while graphite interlayer binding is insensitive to its density.

papers.title: PDB Manipulation Suite (PDBMS): A browser-based toolkit for PDB file manipulation, molecule building and biophysical analysis, easily extendable via reasoning models
papers.abstract: We present here the PDB Manipulation Suite (PDBMS, https://pdbms.altervista.org/ ), a modular hub of web apps and platforms designed for the seamless creation, edition, and analysis of biomolecular coordinate files, all online and client-side i.e. without any user files even passing by any server. The suite is organized into specialized sub-platforms: (i) PDBMS-tools for rapid structure analysis and editing, supporting residue renumbering, sequence extraction, B-factor hacking, CIF/PDB conversion, basic calculations such as distances or solvent accessibility, and various means for mapping data; (ii) Web-PackMol for the assembly of complex molecular systems; and (iii) Web-MDA and the Conformational Ensemble Inspector for the deep analysis and inspection of single structures as well as ensembles coming from molecular dynamics trajectories, BioEmu predictions of conformational landscapes, docking poses, NMR models, etc., all assisted by a novel form of AI copilot that we introduce here. The various tools at the PDBMS facilitate inference of structural details, dynamics, and interactions across molecules and across time or ensemble indexes; others aid in the visualization of various kinds of data including AlphaFold 3 confidence scores and outputs from modern NMR spectroscopy pipelines. Since the source code for all tools at the PDBMS is inherently open and was developed largely with AI reasoning models at Google’s AI Studio, it is extremely easy to modify or add new functionalities at will. We demonstrate this by providing customized tools to assist the editing and visualization of outputs from NMR-specific software like NMRtist and Sparky; and we also demonstrate how the AI agent built into the Web-MDA app can provide new functionalities on request including modification of the app’s own GUI. By providing a “zero-footprint” environment available out of the box with no installs, no downloads, no registration, and trivially clonable code for custom local modifications and reuse, we hope the PDBMS will facilitate work in structural bioinformaticians, structural biology and molecular modeling online but preserving absolute data confidentiality, extreme portability across devices and operating systems, and maximal flexibility. We also hope these tools and ideas for in-software AI use will inspire others to develop further smart, client-only scientific software.

papers.title: Implementation and Validation of Titratable Cysteine in GROMACS-based Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Cysteine is a chemically versatile amino acid whose protonation state is central to catalysis, redox regulation, and covalent ligand recognition. Despite the growing availability of constant-pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) methods, cysteine is not included among the standard titratable residues of the GROMACS-based λ-dynamics implementation developed by Aho, Buslaev, and coworkers. Here, we introduce a titratable cysteine residue, CYST, for this framework and integrate it into the phbuilder workflow. The implementation describes the thiol/thiolate equilibrium of reduced cysteines within a fixed redox topology, while disulfide-linked cysteines are retained as non-titratable covalent states defined a priori. The new residue was calibrated on an ALA-CYS-ALA (ACA) tripeptide by refining the correction potential required to remove the intrinsic force-field bias along the λ coordinate. The resulting model reproduces the expected sigmoidal titration behavior of the peptide and yields a pKa of 8.33, matching the target value adopted in the calibration procedure. Transferability to proteins was then assessed using two complementary benchmarks. First, six engineered single-cysteine mutants of acyl-coenzyme A binding protein (ACBP) were used as a set of non-catalytic cysteines spanning different local environments. The calculations reproduce the overall high-pKa regime of these residues, while also showing that quantitative accuracy depends sensitively on the local conformational ensemble sampled around the introduced cysteine. Second, the implementation was applied to the reactive Cys106 of DJ-1, placing its titration in the correct acidic regime. Overall, this work establishes a practical cysteine extension of the GROMACS CpHMD framework for biomolecular simulations.

papers.title: Accessible hybrid DFT-quality NMR crystallography via gas-phase Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) crystallography is a robust method for structure determination, but its reliance on density functional theory (DFT) for geometry refinement limits its speed and accessibility. Recent machine‑learning predictors such as ShiftML3 can evaluate magnetic shieldings in seconds, but they still need high‑quality crystal geometries that are normally obtained from slow DFT optimisations. Here we demonstrate that machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can eliminate this bottleneck for organic crystals. Interestingly, models trained on gas-phase molecules at the hybrid ωB97M-V level (OMol25 dataset) — such as UMA- omol and MACE-Polar-1 — deliver structural quality rivaling hybrid periodic-DFT, without requiring large computational resources. The resulting MLIP–ShiftML3 workflow reduces computational cost by at least three orders of magnitude, making high-accuracy NMR crystallography accessible without HPC infrastructure, and opening the door to fast molecular dynamics simulations at the hybrid DFT level. Combined with sensitivity enhancement via dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP), we demonstrate the approach on L-histidine, extracting ¹³C and ¹⁵N chemical shift tensors and using ¹H chemical shifts at natural isotopic abundance and discriminating between its monoclinic and orthorhombic polymorphs.

papers.title: Differential Coats-Redfern Analysis for Thermolysis of Carbon-Relevant Polymers
papers.abstract: Thermolysis of plastic waste is increasingly explored both as an end-of-life route and as a precursor step for producing carbonaceous materials, but most thermogravimetric (TG) data for polymers are collected under single heating rates with limited data resolution and are not optimized for kinetic analysis. In this study, we use the recently developed differential Coats–Redfern (d-CR) framework to extract conversion-resolved kinetic information from open-source TG curves of eight technologically important polymers (PP, PS, PET, PMMA, PC, PA, PUR, PTFE) recorded at 10 °C·min⁻¹. Classical Coats–Redfern (CR) analysis of these single-rate datasets yields curved ln[g(α)/T²] versus 1/T plots and conversion-averaged activation parameters that can misrepresent the underlying degradation behavior. In contrast, d-CR converts the same thermogravimetry into conversion-resolved Eₐ(α) and ln A(α), while rate-parity and conversion-variant compensation tests for an effective mechanistic model selection. The resulting profiles reveal systematic differences in thermolysis energy demand between commodity and engineering polymers and provide a kinetic baseline for assessing whether catalytic routes genuinely reduce process severity in plastic recycling schemes from future works.

papers.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Formal [3+2+2] Cycloadditions of Bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone withDiynes: A Concise Approach to Functionalized Azulene Derivatives
papers.abstract: consequently, developing efficient methods for their preparation is important. Herein, we report the development of formal [3+2+2] cycloaddition chemistry involving 1,6-diynes and cis-2,3-bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone as a new synthetic approach to functionalized azulene derivatives. The azulene framework is efficiently constructed using the developed reaction, with synthetically versatile functional groups introduced in a single operation. An unusual rearrangement process consistent with a formal [1,7]-silyl migration from the C7 to C6 position of the azulene framework was observed during the course of the transformation. The synthetic utility of the method was demonstrated by further transforming the resulting silylated azulene derivatives into a variety of 1functionalized azulenes. This study provides a new strategy for constructing and functionalizing azulene skeletons as well as new insight into the reactivities of cyclopropanone-derived intermediates.

papers.title: Fusing Delta Learning and Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials for Efficient High Throughput Calculation of Surface Kinetic Parameters
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis is critical in most industrial chemical processes. Microkinetic models can be used to greatly facilitate optimization of catalyst design and process conditions, but require thermochemical and kinetic parameters for all relevant species 1 and reactions. Our software Pynta enables fully automated calculation of thermochemical and kinetic parameters, however, the computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations makes it difficult to calculate kinetic parameters at scale. In this work, we combine finetuning of the MACE multi-head v0 model with graph-based delta learning of stationary points using subgraph isomorphic decision trees (SIDT). We first generate a target chemical space on Pt111 by using the Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG) software to generate all possible surface reactions between a set of 153 chemically adsorbed species containing C,H,N, and O. Applying Pynta to this reaction set we are able to generate geometries for many gas phase species, adsorbates and transition states in this chemical space allowing us to efficiently sample near stationary points for finetuning and stationary points for delta learning. In particular, we adapt Pynta's harmonically force saddle point search (HFSP) algorithm to enable efficient and reliable sampling of near transition state points. With this training data we show that SIDT-driven delta learning of the foundation MLIP alone can achieve similar accuracies on enthalpies to foundation model finetuning approaches. However, we show that by combining the two approaches into one framework we are able to significantly improve our accuracies over either approach allowing us to achieve 0.07 eV MAE relative to DFT on test barrier heights. Applying this framework across all reactions in our chemical space, we are able to obtain near DFT accuracy rate coefficients for 3111 reactions on Pt(111).

papers.title: Mid-infrared photochemical reaction in confined space driven by resonant vibrational excitation
Length Scale Coordination between effective electron diffusion and light-Emitting Boosts Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency
papers.abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL), an emission of light excited by electrochemical reactions, which has drawn attention as a powerful tool for bioassays and environmental monitoring. Nonetheless, lack of understanding regarding bulk electron transport (ET) process in solid-state ECL emitters, particularly the mismatch between electron diffusion length ( L n ) at the photoelectrode and the light-emitting layer thickness ( d ), significantly limits ECL efficiency ( Φ ECL ) and hinders their widespread application. Herein, we report L n /d as a quantitative descriptor of bulk electron transport in solid-state ECL systems, and the general optimal L n /d range (0.9-1.2) for achieving high ECL efficiency is identified from the slope behavior of temporal ECL evolution curves. Meanwhile, the generality of this strategy is further validated across different ECL systems, including metal-organic framework (MOF), poly(heptazine imide) (PHI) and carbon nitride with tunable band structures (ACN and BCN). As a result, the optimal L n /d ratio range enables superior electron transport and mass transfer, yielding a record-high cathodic ECL efficiency for carbon nitride (CN) and enabling a visual tetracycline (TC) sensor with excellent detection range and limit.

papers.title: Low-temperature upcycling of polyvinyl chloride and polyolefins with AlCl3
papers.abstract: Plastic waste proliferation, particularly polyvinyl chloride (PVC), poses substantial environmental challenges. This study reports an innovative tandem dechlorination-cracking-alkylation process using aluminum chloride (AlCl3) as a cost-effective catalyst for efficient PVC upcycling. Under moderate thermal conditions (50-70 °C), this methodology yields substantial conversion rates of PVC into chlorine-free liquid alkanes while efficiently generating HCl as a byproduct. The process allows for co-upcycling of PVC with various polyolefins, including polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polyolefin elastomer powder (POE), with conversion rates exceeding 90% across multiple mass ratios. This eliminates the need for pre-sorting of mixed plastic waste streams. A tandem dechlorination-cracking-alkylation mechanism has been proposed. Practical applications demonstrate the effective conversion of post-consumer PVC products and their mixtures with other polyolefins. This research could advance PVC recycling capabilities and provide a scalable approach for industrial upcycling, supporting sustainable waste management initiatives.

papers.title: Feature Attribution in Graph Neural Networks and Its Connection to Chemical Group Contributions
papers.abstract: In recent years, explainable artificial intelligence has attracted considerable attention, particularly feature attribution methods that quantify the contribution of each input feature to model predictions. In chemistry, a concept similar to feature attribution has long been used to interpret molecular properties in terms of contributions from substituents or functional groups. A representative example is the group contribution method (GCM), in which molecular properties are estimated as the sum of contributions from predefined functional groups. In this study, we investigate the correspondence between feature attributions obtained from graph neural networks and those derived through classical GCMs. Models were constructed for boiling point and the octanol–water partition coefficient (logP ), with atom-wise contributions analyzed using integrated gradients (IG). The IG-based attributions were qualitatively consistent with established chemical knowledge. Furthermore, positive correlations were observed between the GCM contribution values and IG-based attributions for both properties, suggesting that the importance learned by machine learning models corresponds to conventional chemically interpretable trends.

papers.title: Self-oscillation of liquid droplets with excitable dynamics driven by dissipative self-assembly of surfactants
papers.abstract: Autonomous oscillations are fundamental nonequilibrium processes vital to life that contribute to homeostasis and robustness against noise from the external environment. Inspired by these biological systems, autonomously oscillating materials have been extensively developed to create lifelike objects. However, excitable dynamics, which are characteristic of threshold-triggered signaling in neurons, remain unexplored in the design of synthetic oscillatory materials despite their unique potential in signal processing to acquire adaptive functionalities. Herein, we report oil droplets on a water surface that exhibit autonomous oscillations with excitable dynamics driven by the assembly of two oppositely charged surfactants. The oscillation consists of a repetitive cycle of gradual expansion and rapid contraction of the interfacial areas of the oil droplets. Using AI-based image analysis, we quantified the dynamics and developed models to elucidate the underlying mechanism: the interfacial area gradually increased as surfactants accumulated at the oil–water interface and rapidly decreased upon threshold-triggered release of nanoemulsions, which effectively removed surfactants from the interface. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the oscillation is influenced by environmental fluctuations, introducing stochasticity into an otherwise deterministic excitable oscillator. This autonomous oscillatory system, analogous to the “integrate-and-fire” model of neural activity, provides a minimal physicochemical framework for designing adaptive liquid-like soft materials with complex excitable dynamics.

papers.title: Ultrafast RIXS Reveals Excited State Orbital and Spin Character of Solvated Organic Molecules
papers.abstract: The excited state photophysics of heteroatomic organic molecules are determined by the interplay between internal conversion and intersystem crossing. Experimental techniques which can access both orbital and spin character of the electronic excited states in detail are crucial for a mechanistic understanding of these processes. In this work, we demonstrate the required sensitivity to excited-state orbital and spin character with femtosecond time-resolved resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS). We apply the method to probe the excited state photophysics of pyrazine in aqueous solution at the nitrogen K-edge. We clearly separate the dynamics of two singlet and two triplet excited states and identify a new mechanism for the intersystem crossing of pyrazine involving the dark Au(nπ*) state.

papers.title: Harnessing amino‑acid chirality to control protein associations, solubility, and thermostability
papers.abstract: Chirality is a critical molecular‑level feature that can profoundly alter how proteins fold, aggregate, and function under stress, yet most stabilization strategies implicitly treat amino acids and osmolyte additives as if their chiral enantiomers were functionally interchangeable. Here we show that amino acid chirality provides a powerful handle to tune protein stabilization in crowded, formulation‑relevant environments using the prototypical osmolyte, proline. Focusing on bovine serum albumin (BSA) microspheres and egg white proteins, we systematically compare the D‑ and L‑enantiomers of proline and quantify their effects on protein aggregation, solubility, and thermal denaturation. D‑proline markedly enhances the solubilization of BSA microspheres relative to the 2 L‑form and significantly increases the time required for egg white proteins to denature at 60 °C. A combination of vapor‑pressure osmometry, dynamic light scattering, viscosity measurements, and vibrational sum‑frequency spectroscopy reveals that D‑proline strengthens and expands the protein hydration shell more than L‑proline. This leads to higher effective osmotic activity, increased thermodynamic and hydrodynamic radii, and lowered protein aggregation. These results establish amino acid chirality as a general design parameter for stereochemically tuning protein hydration, excluded volume, and phase behavior, suggesting that D‑proline and other unnatural amino acids could serve as superior excipients for stabilizing high‑concentration protein formulations in biomedical and biotechnological applications.

papers.title: Fast training of bespoke SMIRNOFF-format molecular mechanics force fields using machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: Molecular mechanics force fields enable the thorough sampling required for applications such as alchemical binding free energy calculations for computer-aided drug design. However, parameters from transferable molecular mechanics force fields can be unreliable, and training accurate molecule-specific parameters against quantum mechanical (QM) reference data is slow. Here, we present presto (https://github.com/colegroup/presto), a Python package for fast training of bespoke SMIRKS-Native Open Force Field (SMIRNOFF) format force fields. presto generates training data using high-temperature molecular dynamics with well-tempered metadynamics. It iteratively fits all valence parameters to energies and forces from transferable machine learning potentials (MLPs). By leveraging fast MLP evaluations and training on the GPU using PyTorch (via the packages smee and descent), the fully-automated workflow completes in around 15 minutes for a 50-atom molecule on a single GPU. presto reduces torsion scan errors by a factor of three relative to Open Force Field Sage 2.3.0 on 400 molecules from TorsionNet500. It also achieves torsion scan performance comparable to direct QM fitting on a benchmark dataset of fragmented drug-like molecules, and relative conformer energies of 510 molecules from the set of Folmsbee and Hutchison are significantly improved compared to both Sage and espaloma. presto allows simultaneous fitting of congeneric series with partially shared parameters. It produces comparable relative binding free energy performance to OpenFF 1.3.1 (Parsley) on systems where Parsley already performs well, and may improve performance in cases where initial parameters are particularly poor.

papers.title: Computational Screening of Chilean Natural Products Identifies Procyanidin B1 as a Promising α-Glucosidase Inhibitor
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus remains a major health burden, and natural products from endemic species continue to represent an underexplored source of bioactive leads. In this study, we computationally screened compounds from Chilean natural products against αglucosidase, a validated target for postprandial glycemic control. AutoDock Vina was used to dock 11 compounds against the C-terminal subunit of human maltase-glucoamylase (PDB: 3TOP), with binding sites defined from the co-crystallized ligand. Protocol reliability was supported by redocking of acarbose, which reproduced the expected binding mode with minimal deviation. Among the screened compounds, procyanidin B1 from Vasconcellea pubescens showed the most favorable binding affinity and ligand efficiency. Although its raw docking score was more favorable than that of acarbose, this comparison should be interpreted cautiously because flexible ligands may be penalized by the scoring function. Exploratory docking of sesquiterpene lactones from Leptocarpha rivularis against cruzipain suggested initial non-covalent recognition, but these compounds are expected to act as covalent Michael acceptors, and standard docking does not capture their full inhibitory mechanism. Overall, the results identify procyanidin B1 as the highest-priority candidate for experimental validation and support the potential of Chilean natural products as a source of enzymatic inhibitors.

papers.title: Surface Chemistry Guided Cellular Entry of Sub-
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are being explored as nanocarriers for theranostics. Surface functionalities are typically employed to modulate cargo loading and stimuli-responsiveness. Despite this progress, the role of COF functionalities in governing cellular trafficking remains largely overlooked. Pinpointing surface chemical effects becomes challenging due to concurrent variations in structural parameters. To address this, we designed a series of sub-100 nm isoreticular imine-linked nanoscale COFs (nCOFs) with comparable particle size, morphology, crystallinity, topology, and surface charge while systematically varying their surface functionalities. Using A549 lung cancer cells as model system, we could investigate how nCOF surface functionalities influence cellular uptake, internalization pathways, and subcellular localization by confocal microscopy, and flow cytometry. The results showed that surface functionality plays a decisive role in governing the cellular internalization efficiency of nCOF-R (R= -H, -OH, -OCH 3 , -OCH 2 CH 3 , and -OCH 2 CH 2 OCH 3 ) and internalization pathways. Together, these results establish surface functionality as a key determinant to regulate cellular trafficking behaviour and thus providing new insights that will guide the design of surface-engineered COF nanocarriers for improved performance in future biomedical applications.

papers.title: Nanoplastic Standards
papers.abstract: Open questions about the potential effects of nanoplastic particles have driven researchers to a frontier of measurement science, where they seek answers without the full support of metrological standards. Documentary and material standards improve the reliability of measurement results but are slow to develop, while researchers are eager to explore and publish. This mismatch motivates efforts to exploit any potential utility of existing standards and to elucidate emerging needs for new standards. Accordingly, we consider possible applications of microplastic and engineered nanomaterial standards to support nanoplastic analysis, and the many challenges of developing new nanoplastic standards. We study corresponding issues in four research activities—physicochemical measurements, reference materials, weathering methods, and toxicity assays. Our integrative perspective elucidates challenges and opportunities. We identify topics that can limit progress, such as measurement uncertainty propagation and process–product–purpose constraints. A focus review of recent literature shows uneven progress in addressing these issues. We suggest opportunities to expedite progress, such as feedback loops for measurand prioritization and uncertainty budgeting, timely development of imperfect standards, and metrological innovation to obviate current constraints. Our study informs the research, development, and application of nanoplastic standards to reliably answer open questions and to support other technological ventures.

papers.title: A Thermodynamically Consistent Approach to Molecular Simulations of Adsorption-Induced Deformation and Structural Transitions in MOFs
papers.abstract: Flexible metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) exhibit coupled adsorption-deformation behavior that cannot be captured in molecular detail by conventional rigid-framework simulations. We present an iterative hybrid GCMC/MD methodology that explicitly couples grand canonical Monte Carlo sampling of adsorbate configurations with isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics relaxation of the framework structure, using a Metropolis acceptance criterion in the osmotic ensemble to ensure thermodynamic consistency. Applied to argon adsorption on ZIF-8 at 87.3 K, the method quantitatively reproduces the experimental stepped isotherm characteristic of the gate-opening transition between low pressure (LP) and high pressure (HP) conformations and predicts non-monotonic strain isotherm with initial contraction (~0.5%) at low loadings followed by expansion (~0.7%) during gate-opening. The elastic modulus variation upon loading is calculated from the volume fluctuations. The simulations reveal and quantify the molecular mechanism of gate-opening through cooperative linker reorientation from a unimodal swing angle distribution centered at 0° to a bimodal distribution peaked at ±23°. The proposed approach is computationally efficient and provides a general framework for predicting adsorption-induced structural transitions in flexible porous materials without a priori knowledge of endpoint structures.

papers.title: Distributed Assembly Theory: Distinguishing Biological Causal Depth from Information Entropy via Recursive Fragmentation
papers.abstract: The search for a universal biosignature—a measurable property distinguishing living from abiotic systems—remains a central challenge in astrobiology. Two competing frameworks address this: Assembly Theory, which measures causal depth through the number of construction steps required to build an object, and Algorithmic Information Theory, which equates complexity with incompressibility as measured by compression algorithms such as LZW. A key criticism of Assembly Theory has been computational intractability—the claim that true Assembly Index calculation is impossible for complex molecules. Here we challenge that impasse. Using a 78-core heterogeneous distributed cluster and domainspecific chemical decomposition rules (BRICS), we computed a Modified Assembly Index (MA) for 395 molecules across four complexity classes in under 30 seconds. We find that LZW compression exhibits a negative correlation with biological complexity, assigning Methanol a higher score than Taxol. In contrast, MA correctly distinguishes all classes, with Complex Natural Products exhibiting a 3.14-fold increase over the Random Alkane abiotic baseline (MA = 1.00 ± 0.00, p < 0.001). A naive bond-shattering control experiment failed to reproduce this gradient, confirming that domain-specific fragmentation rules are essential. We release our complete open-source pipeline to democratize Assembly Index computation and establish a community benchmark for causal depth detection.

papers.title: Investigating Precursor Spatial Organization in Osteoclastogenesis Using DNA-Directed Cell Patterning
papers.abstract: Osteoclasts are large, multinucleated cells in bone marrow, which are of macrophage lineage and are responsible for bone resorption. Disruption of osteoclast differentiation or resorption activity can cause a broad spectrum of skeletal diseases ranging from osteoporosis to cancer-associated bone loss. Despite their key role in homeostasis, studying osteoclasts in vitro remains challenging largely because no commercially available cell line exists. Consequently, in vitro studies rely on 2 differentiation from precursor cells using osteoclastogenic factors. While prior studies have optimized various culture-based parameters, most in vitro models lack control over the spatial organization of precursors. This highlights the need for a platform offering such control to study inter-precursor proximity and local confinement in precursor fusion and multinucleation. Here, we employed a DNA-directed cell patterning system to immobilize THP-1-derived macrophages within defined seeding environments and evaluated how spatial organization regulates osteoclastogenesis. THP-1-derived macrophages were immobilized in defined polyacrylamide (PA)-confined circular seeding areas of varying diameter and inter-precursor spacing. Reducing macrophage spacing dramatically increased osteoclast formation, with close and medium configurations yielding 8.41 ± 0.82% and 8.03 ± 1.39% total osteoclast conversion, compared with 4.84 ± 0.27% in the far design. Decreasing the seeding area diameter further increased osteoclastogenesis: a microenvironment of 900 µm diameter yielded 12.55 ± 0.58% total osteoclasts, representing 1.49-, 2.25-, and 2.27-fold increases over 1200, 1400, and 1600 µm, respectively. Density-matched unpatterned controls failed to reach this conversion rate across all conditions, indicating that environmental confinement and precursor proximity affect osteoclast differentiation through mechanisms beyond initial seeding density alone. These findings reveal precursor spatial organization as an underappreciated regulator of osteoclast fusion and a practical strategy for improving osteoclast conversion in in vitro models. This platform is extensible to osteoblasts, stromal, immune, endothelial, and tumor cells, offering a foundation for in vitro recapitulation of human bone marrow disease.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Binding Affinity of Novel Modified BMP2 Knuckle Epitope Peptides with BMP Receptor Type II
papers.abstract: Recombinant human Bone Morphogenic Protein 2 (rhBMP2) is used clinically as a morphogen to induce osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in regeneration of skeletal defects and treat osteoporosis. Several limitations of rhBMP2 protein have shifted focus to the use of short 20-mer amino acid sequences inspired by the bioactive domain of rhBMP2, known as the knuckle epitope peptide (BMP2-KEP), which interacts with the Bone Morphogenic Protein Receptor Type II (BMPRII) on the surface of undifferentiated MSCs. However, due to the relatively collapsed configuration of the BMP2-KEP peptide in its free state compared to its native state as part of rhBMP2 protein, the peptide’s osteogenic activity is lowered by at least three orders of magnitude compared to rhBMP2. We previously used machine learning guided Quantitative Structure Activity Relationships (QSARs) to predict novel modified sequences of BMP2-KEP with open-arm configurations in the free state. The objective of this work was to compare the binding affinities of several modified 20-mer sequences of BMP2-KEP complexed with BMPRII receptor by Molecular Mechanics/Poisson Boltzmann Surface Area (MM/PBSA) to analyze peptide-receptor complex trajectories from molecular dynamics simulation. Contribution of different energy terms such as van der Waals, electrostatics, polar and non-polar solvation to the binding affinity of the peptides to the receptor were also determined. The calculations by MM/PBSA identified several sequences with higher binding affinity than the unmodified BMP2-KEP as well as a few sequences with lower binding affinity. Contact maps revealed that the modified BMP2-KEP sequence with highest binding affinity had multiple residues in close contact with residues in the binding pocket of BMPRII receptor whereas the sequence with lowest binding affinity as well as the unmodified BMP2-KEP had fewer contacts with the residues in the binding pocket of BMPRII receptor. The sequence with the highest binding affinity was KIKKASSVPTELSAISTLWL with a binding affinity of ~ -106 kcal mol-1 which was approximately an order of magnitude higher than the binding affinity of the unmodified BMP2-KEP (~ -14.66 kcal mol-1).

papers.title: Ketyl-Type Radical Generation via CN-Triggered Translocation Enables Coupling of Unactivated Dialkyl Ketones with Alkenes
papers.abstract: The direct coupling of aliphatic carbonyl compounds with alkenes remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a conceptually distinct strategy for intermolecular Heck-type coupling of alkenes with aliphatic carbonyl compounds enabled by CNtriggered photoinduced palladium catalysis. By exploiting in situ CN installation with trimethylsilyl cyanide (TMSCN), this transformation enables controlled generation of otherwise elusive dialkyl ketyl-type radicals under mild visible-light conditions. Central to the process is an alkyl/Pd hybrid radical manifold that undergoes intramolecular CN translocation, thereby generating ketyl-type radicals while preserving compatibility with Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling. The method furnishes allylic alcohol derivatives from simple alkenes and dialkyl ketones with high chemo- and regioselectivity and excellent E-selectivity, while suppressing the reductive pathways that typically dominate ketyl radical chemistry. Mechanistic studies support a CN-translocation-enabled ketyl radical generation pathway and establish a unified framework applicable to both ketones and aldehydes. In addition, preformed nitriles can directly engage in CN-migration-enabled alkyl Heck coupling, revealing nitriles as latent alkyl radical precursors under these conditions. This work expands the scope of photoinduced transition-metal catalysis and provides a general entry to carbonyl- and nitrilederived radicals for cross-coupling synthesis.

papers.title: Closed-loop LLM-guided molecular dynamics simulation for composition-strength optimisation of Co-Cr-Ni medium-entropy alloy
papers.abstract: Identifying high-performance alloy compositions through trial-and-error remains slow and resource-intensive. Here, we couple a large language model with iterative LAMMPS molecular dynamics to autonomously navigate the Co-Cr-Ni composition space without requiring pre-existing dataset. Across six independent search paths and 300 guided simulations, the framework progressively refined its decisions using live composition property feedback, converging on Co₇₂.₂Cr₁₈.₆Ni₉.₁ as the strongest candidate, with a peak tensile stress of 30.19 GPa. Validation in larger 2048-atom cells confirmed this result with low scatter (29.78 ± 0.06 GPa). Beyond this strength optimum, a separate high-Ni/low-Cr region emerged with a favorable toughness-stiffness balance, revealing that the loop also identified competing property regions. Polyhedral template matching traced deformation to FCC retention and localized non-FCC defect growth near failure, grounding the numerical trends in structural evidence.

papers.title: An interactive solvent selection guide inspired by the Safe and Sustainable by Design framework
Symmetry-Broken Biphasic WS2 Nano-whiskered Heterostructures Enable Field-Induced NO2 Sensing
papers.abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) materials have garnered ample interest as next-generation sensors and catalysts; owing to high surface-to-volume ratio, defect tunability, easy modulation of active sites and convenience in device fabrication. However, one major drawback delimiting surface activity of conventional vdW sensors is weak adsorption of target analyte on basal surface compared to the edge-sites, compromising their general applicability. This work categorically averts above limitations by introducing an inversion symmetry-broken biphasic-(hexagonalrhombohedral) ultralong WS2 heterostructure which harnesses its non-centrosymmetric features during field-induced room-temperature NO2 sensing. Under a +20 V bias, the heterostructure demonstrates an improvement in sensitivity from 75% → 90% alongside response/recovery of 35/80 sec. The band-modified energy channels enable in-situ modulation of Limit of Detection (LOD) down to 1 ppm. Surface-analyte interaction mechanisms were identified by the emergence of a giant 40% degree of circular polarization (DCP) in hybrid-static p-p surface quasi-states upon light-matter interaction, employing helicity-resolved circularly polarized operando Raman spectroscopy and polarity-resolved Stark-field of tuning rate 1.5 cm-1/(kV/cm). Operando UV-Vis spectroscopy alongside theoretical calculations indicates that NO2-mediated hole-injection redefines intrinsic A-B excitonic population via Fermi level pinning (FLP). Field effect-transistor 3 (FET)-based sensors harnessing perturbation-mediated band features have been introduced, holding potential towards transformative sensing devices.

papers.title: Speciation of Bulky Chiral Cyclopentadienyl Cobalt(III) Complexes: Isolation of Air-Stable 16-Electron Species
papers.abstract: Bulky pentasubstituted chiral cyclopentadienyl ligands (Cp V ) were shown to form distinct species upon cobalt(III) complexation, which differ in the nature and number of auxiliary ligands. Aside from the well-established coordinatively saturated Cp V Co(CO)I 2 architecture and its dimeric [Cp V CoI 2 ] 2 derivative, the formation of monomeric 16-electron species of type Cp V CoI 2 was confirmed as well, thus representing a rare example of air-stable chiral half-sandwich complexes with an unsaturated 3d-metal center. Herein, we report the isolation and structural characterization of these organometallic species, of which the dominant coordination mode depends on the steric encumbrance of the employed Cp V ligand. Addition of a two-electron donor ligand, such as carbon monoxide or an isocyanide, showed that the unsaturated complexes can be converted back to 18-electron adducts.

papers.title: Primary alkenes as a platform for orthogonal multi-isotope labelling
papers.abstract: The incorporation of stable isotopic tracers into drug-like molecules plays a central role in drug discovery and development, enabling accurate quantification, metabolic profiling, and pharmacokinetic studies. Despite significant advances in hydrogen and carbon isotope labelling methods, their controlled and orthogonal combination within a single molecular framework remains an unmet synthetic challenge. Primary alkenes represent an attractive yet underexploited structural motif in this context, offering readily accessible and versatile handles for isotope incorporation that have largely been overlooked as a platform for multi-isotope labelling. Herein, we report an operationally simple and gas cylinder-free strategy for the high-enrichment deuterioformylation of primary alkenes, establishing these motifs as a versatile platform for orthogonal hydrogen- and carbon-isotope labelling within a unified two-chamber reactor framework. By combining deuterioformylation with site-specific carbon-13 delivery from readily available labelling surrogates, independent control over orthogonal isotope incorporation is achieved. The utility of this labelling strategy is demonstrated across structurally diverse primary alkenes and pharmaceutically relevant targets, providing a practical and unified platform for multi-isotope labelling in drug discovery and development.

papers.title: Composition-driven phase separation and micellar ordering in PVPTetronic 908 hydrogels: structural insights by SANS and controlled release of sulfadiazine
papers.abstract: This study systematically investigates the phase behavior, nanoscale micellar structure, swelling capacity, and sulfadiazine (SDZ) release kinetics of aqueous poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP K90)–Tetronic 908 (T908) blends as a function of total polymer concentration and T908:PVP ratio. Phase diagrams over 20–80 °C at 5–30 wt% reveal a percolation threshold at ~25 wt%. Above this threshold, a body-centered cubic (BCC) micellar gel forms at physiological temperature across all compositions; however, near equimolar ratios induce gel-liquid phase coexistence driven by polymer demixing. Small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) confirms this macroscopic behavior at the nanoscale, demonstrating that PVP suppresses T908 self-assembly while reducing micellar size and aggregation number. Notably, at equimolar compositions, a low-q upturn evidences nanoscale microsegregation, where T908 micelles are expelled from PVP-rich domains. Within the gel state, the BCC paracrystalline lattice persists but exhibits increased distortion at high PVP content. T908 substantially enhances water uptake relative to pure PVP via sub-Fickian transport. Consequently, SDZ release is highly compositiondependent, with the equimolar blend achieving the highest cumulative release (90.2%), outperforming pure T908 (82.9%) and pure PVP (55.1%). These results establish a robust physicochemical foundation for tailoring PVP–T908 supramolecular hydrogels for advanced wound healing and transdermal delivery.

papers.title: Combining Electronic Structure Methods and Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials in Adsorption Studies
papers.abstract: Atomistic modelling methods can provide significant insights into the adsorption and drug delivery mechanisms of pharmaceuticals and related organic molecules in cation-exchanged zeolites, offering an atomic-level understanding of host–guest interactions and associated energetics. While density functional theory (DFT)-based methods are computationally expensive and force fields fail due to limited accuracy, machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are increasingly used, but their reliability for adsorption properties remains underexplored for such complex systems. We benchmarked over 20 universal MLIPs against DLPNO-CCSD(T) reference data for non-periodic systems, followed by an evaluation of the best performing subset of uMLIPs against DFT data. The eSEN-MP model was found to be the most reliable in reproducing the energetics and structural properties of the periodic host-guest systems studied here. We further applied eSEN-MP to 48 configurations of the drug molecule mercaptopurine in cationic FAU-type zeolites, considering different extra-framework cation species as well as models with and without co-adsorbed water molecules, and compared the results to DFT. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with eSEN-MP, benchmarked against ab initio MD, accurately reproduced structural parameters and dynamic behavior, while longer simulations provide detailed insights on the nanosecond timescale. These results suggest that MLIPs facilitate the reliable investigation of adsorption and drug delivery processes in cation-exchanged zeolites while significantly enhancing the efficiency of simulations, and that this machine learning–accelerated modeling strategy can be extended to other porous crystalline materials.

papers.title: Post-Synthetic Zn Modifications to Correct Speciation in Ti-MWW
papers.abstract: Ti-MWW is an important member of Ti-containing zeolites employed as heterogeneous catalyst in the ammoximation reaction. Despite the industrial prevalence of Ti-MWW catalysts, the development of more active variants is often hampered by the lack of characterization methods able to track transformations and interplay between a multitude of species. This challenge is exacerbated by the introduction of secondary metals, such as Zn, which allows to significantly enhance catalytic performance. Hence, we set out to employ an array of characterization methods, featuring microscopy and various spectroscopic techniques, enabling a more accurate handle on these changes. Thereby we find that the promotional role of Zn is closely linked to its healing of hydrophilic silanol nests, while simultaneously generating small TiOx clusters. These changes are accompanied by Ti weight loading dependent modifications of the extra-framework TiO2 and formation of Zn species. Overall, our study highlights the interplay between a plethora of species, enabling the assessment of different species, and a more rational development of post-modification of Ti-containing zeolites.

papers.title: Modular Platform for Directing-Group-Free Radical Dicarbofunctionalization of Unactivated Alkenes via Dual Nickel/Energy-Transfer Catalysis
papers.abstract: Multicomponent cross-coupling reactions of alkenes offer a powerful strategy for constructing three-dimensional, sp3-rich molecular architectures, a key objective in modern medicinal chemistry. However, the regioselective dicarbofunctionalization of unactivated alkenes without the use of directing groups remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced, Ni-catalyzed platform that enables the radical 1,2-dicarbofunctionalization of unactivated alkenes using diverse alkyl radical precursors and aryl, vinyl, acyl, alkenyl, and alkyl coupling partners. Mechanistic studies support a catalytic cycle in which multiple electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes mediate radical generation, atom-transfer radical addition (ATRA), and cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) or bimolecular homolytic substitution (SH2) processes. Additionally, preferential formation of an EDA complex between the Ni catalyst and the radical precursor suppresses undesired homo-coupling of the electrophilic partner. Notably, delivery of gaseous radical precursors such as trifluoromethyl iodide (TFMI) from the robust metal-organic framework (MOF) Al(OH)fum (fum2− = fumarate) or Al–fum offers advantages in terms of both operational safety and reaction efficiency, and the MOF further boosts the yields of reactions by modulating the concentration of amine (employed for radical generation) in solution. Collectively, this flexible, directing-group-free approach establishes a general platform for the rapid construction of structurally complex and pharmaceutically relevant molecules from readily available precursors.

papers.title: Substituent Effect Immunity and Oxygen Ferrying Electrons: A Complete Mechanism from Quantum Critical Window to Cascade Electron Transfer in High-Valent Manganese Oxide–Pyridine Systems
papers.abstract: Since 1937, the Hammett equation has been the cornerstone for quantifying substituent effects, yet its applicability to open-shell single electron transfer reactions involving high-valent metal oxides has never been tested. Here, through systematic density functional theory calculations of the SOMO–SUMO energy gaps between MnO42- and a series of para-substituted pyridines, we show that the Hammett linear free energy relationship completely fails in this prototypical open-shell d1 system, replaced by a nonlinear, nonmonotonic response—within the σp range of –0.66 to 0.00, the energy gap remains constant at 0.28 eV, forming a “quantum critical window”. Through systematic comparison with non-open-shell and non-metal analogues, it is confirmed that this immune window is specific to metal d orbitals. On this basis, we further investigate the mechanistic nature of single electron transfer in this system: the OAT epoxy configuration is identified by frequency analysis as a higher-order saddle point rather than a stable minimum. Electron transfer exhibits a continuous spin population spectrum from 0.85 to 0.002, rather than a simple on/off switch. The study shows that oxygen atom transfer and single electron transfer, traditionally viewed as competing pathways, are not independent channels but two stages of the same cascade reaction—oxygen first transfers from manganate to pyridine to form a transient epoxy saddle point, then electrons flow through this oxygen bridge to the pyridine, and finally oxygen returns to the metal center to complete net SET. Substituents modulate the stability of the epoxy saddle point through σ-inductive and π-conjugation effects, precisely controlling the on/off switching of this cascade process. This “oxygen ferrying electron” mechanism provides a unified kinetic framework for SET reactions of high-valent metal oxides.

papers.title: Hydration Changes are Essential for Efficient Breakdown of Faropenem by the L1 Metallo-β-Lactamase
papers.abstract: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL with that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Here we apply quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling to map the full reaction pathway and corresponding minimum free energy profile for hydrolysis of the penem antibiotic faropenem (whose reaction is complicated by the ability to form alternative enamine and imine products) by L1. We test different possible mechanisms, and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 lowering the free energy barrier for nucleophilic attack and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. Direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6-α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. The calculated free energy barriers for the formation of both products are consistent with the experimentally determined catalytic constant, and the calculated greater stability of the imine with its crystallographic observation. These simulations provide dynamic insight into L1 catalysis, highlighting features that can be exploited for inhibitor design.

papers.title: Impact of hydrophobic tail geometry and rigidity on amphiphile self-assembly
papers.abstract: The influence of hydrophobic tail geometry and rigidity on amphiphile self-assembly was investigated using a series of structurally related double-tailed amphiphiles. The molecules consist of a hydrophilic oligoglycerol dendritic head group coupled to hydrophobic tails of varying geometry, including a linear C10 chain, a decalin unit, an adamantane moiety, and a diamantane cage, the latter representing the next higher diamondoid homologue of adamantane. These systems provide a platform to study how increasing steric bulk and rigidity in the hydrophobic domain affects supramolecular organization. Self-assembly in aqueous solution was first investigated by dynamic light scattering (DLS), which revealed vesicular aggregates with varying degrees of polydispersity.
