papers.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DES) have emerged as promising green extraction media owing to their tuneable physicochemical properties and low environmental impact. However, the combinatorial space of possible DES formulations renders exhaustive experimental screening prohibitively resource-intensive. In this work, we report a high-throughput computational screening of 168 binary DES systems for the selective extraction of 12 primary and secondary metabolites from Sonneratia alba, a mangrove species of significant ethnopharmacological interest. These 12 evaluated metabolites, including quercetin, lignin, and cellobiose, structurally represent universal components of higher plant matrices, thereby establishing this predictive thermodynamic model as a translatable blueprint for diverse biomass upcycling applications. Thermodynamic descriptors, including infinite-dilution activity coefficients (ln γ∞), solubility capacities (C∞), and absolute selectivities (S∞), were computed across 9 molar ratios and 21 temperatures (0–100°C). Calculations utilized the COSMO-RS model parameterised via quantum chemical geometries (r2SCAN-3c) and surface charge distributions (BP86/def2-TZVP) generated within the ORCA framework, yielding an exhaustive dataset of 31,857 discrete thermodynamic state points. The opencosmorspy implementation facilitated this batch computation, proving that open-source COSMO-RS workflows represent a robust, cost-effective alternative to proprietary software. Screening identified the sodium propionate:1,3-butanediol system (3:1 molar ratio, 60°C) as the thermodynamic apex. It demonstrated a massive quercetin capacity (C∞=2.62×109) while functioning as a highly selective extraction medium, achieving absolute selectivities exceeding 1016 against lipophilic impurities. These findings provide a fundamental, physics-based blueprint for the sustainable, rational design of mangrove-derived nutraceuticals.

papers.title: Water-Soluble Luminescent Trityl Radical for Fluorescence/Magnetic Resonance Dual-Modal Imaging Probe
papers.abstract: Tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM) radicals are promising scaffolds for fluorescence imaging (FI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) owing to their long-wavelength emission and intrinsic paramagnetism. Incorporating donor-acceptor (D-A) architectures into TTM radicals has been an established strategy to enhance brightness and photostability of TTM radicals. However, conventional D-A type TTM radicals exhibit strong chargetransfer (CT)-dominated emission that is easily quenched in water due to accelerated non-radiative decay known as the energy-gap law. Here, we report water-soluble TTM radicals (TTM-trisTP3B and TTM-trisTP9B) which exhibit hybridized locally excited and CT character through rational modulation of the donor units and their substitution positions. New radicals exhibited high photostability and deep-red emission with photoluminescence quantum yields of 1.4% (TTM-trisTP3B, 690 nm), and 1.1% (TTM-trisTP9B, 685 nm) in water. Their dual functionality as both fluorescent probes and MRI contrast agents was demonstrated. TTM-trisTP3B was taken up by living cells, localized near the cell nucleus, and showed fluorescence. New radicals also provided a clear longitudinal relaxation time (T1)-weighted MRI contrast. This work represents the first demonstration of trityl radical functioning as practical FI/MRI dual-modal imaging probes, establishing a molecular platform without any surfactants or metals in which fluorophore and electron-spin source are unified.

papers.title: Unlocking Dormant Li⁺ Pathways Drives Fast Ion Transport in Li4Ti5O12 Oxide Spinels
papers.abstract: Li-rich lithium titanate (Li 4+ x Ti 5 O 12 , x > 0) is known for its superior ionic conductivity, yet we show that even stoichiometric Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO, x = 0), typically characterized by sluggish ion dynamics, can become a fast ion conductor without any change in Li content. Local defects, such as oxygen vacancies, introduced by vacuum treatment, without incorporating additional Li+ ions, activate a previously inaccessible 8 a -16 c -8 a diffusion pathway in non-lithiated LTO, markedly enhancing Li + mobility throughout the bulk. Using a synergistic combination of impedance spectroscopy, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), we elucidate the diffusion processes responsible for this transformation. Lithium-NMR unambiguously shows that the formerly localized Li + hopping process transforms into long-range ion transport upon vacuum treatment, evidencing the activation of extended diffusion pathways. Atomic-scale analysis reveals the structural and dynamic modifications that precondition the material for rapid Li + insertion, rendering zero-strain LTO one of the most promising anode materials for lithium-based batteries employing solid electrolytes. These findings resolve the long-standing conductivity puzzle of stoichiometric spinel LTO ( x = 0) by uncovering a previously unrecognized transport mechanism that may also operate in other spinel-type ion conductors with similar Li + distributions. This insight establishes a new route for controlling ion transport in spinel-based materials, relevant for next-generation energy storage technologies where precise control of ion dynamics is essential.

papers.title: A unifying framework for the calibration and characterization of dissolved organic matter fluorescence sensors
papers.abstract: Fluorescent dissolved organic matter (FDOM) sensors are widely used to monitor quantity and quality of dissolved organic matter (DOM). Yet, sensor calibration and characterization procedures remain inconsistent across platforms and manufacturers, hindering widespread use and interoperability of data collected. This study introduces a framework for sensor calibration that expands standardized benchtop fluorescence methodologies to in situ sensors. In contrast to factory calibration, this framework does not require comparisons with an arbitrary standard compound (quinine sulfate), rather it uses the fluorescence intensity of natural DOM expressed in Raman Units (RU). This removes the need for chemical standards, reduces the potential for laboratory errors, and avoids conceptual misunderstandings. Based on this framework, we designed and validated a calibration system enabling automated intensity gradients and temperature adjustments to quantify key performance metrics such as detector response, dark offset, detection limits, and temperature correction coefficients. In addition, the system allows the distinction between temperature effects on DOM fluorescence and sensor electronics. Several common sensor models were characterized and compared, revealing substantial differences in limits of detection, signal-to-noise ratios, and temperature sensitivity. During laboratory experiments and field-deployment, the high susceptibility of particular sensors to electromagnetic interference was a factor that significantly degraded their performance.

papers.title: Kinetic energy redistribution barriers in chemical reactions
papers.abstract: Crossing an activation energy barrier in a chemical reaction needs time because enough kinetic energy needs to redistribute into the barrier-crossing mode. Kinetic energy redistribution is also needed to get across regions with strong reaction path curvature. This latter fact is largely ignored, because barriers and curvature peaks often coincide, and curvature is invisible in the usual, pseudo-one-dimensional reaction energy profiles. Here we show examples for reactions without visible barriers in the critical bond-breaking / bond-forming region, with downhill energy profiles towards products. According to common wisdom, therefore their dynamics should proceed without any time delays, but actually there are curvature peaks that trap the dynamics for a long time in the downhill region. Besides reaction path curvature, further features are analyzed that contribute to dynamic delays, opening up unconventional reaction control possibilities.

papers.title: Meniscus-Driven Growth of Cobalt Hydroxide on Graphite: A Binder-Free Electrode Architecture for Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: Binder-free oxygen evolution electrodes with strong catalyst-support integration are important for practical alkaline water electrolysis. Here, a cobalt hydroxide catalytic layer was grown directly on graphite through a simple open-vessel aqueous deposition route exploiting the evolving air-liquid interface during solvent evaporation. As the solution level recedes, the moving meniscus establishes a localized growth front that confines nucleation along the waterline, producing a spatially defined cobalt hydroxide band without polymer binders, surfactants, or high-pressure processing. Scanning electron microscopy reveals a platelet-dominated nanosheet morphology characteristic of the brucite-type cobalt hydroxide framework, forming a mechanically integrated catalytic layer directly on the conductive graphite substrate. In 1.0 M KOH, the electrode reaches 10 mA cm-2 at an overpotential of 339.9 mV, with an onset potential of 1.459 V versus RHE and a Tafel slope of 75.55 mV dec-1. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy gives a charge-transfer resistance of 78.24 Ω, reflecting a functional electrode-electrolyte interface, and chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm-2 over 6 h confirms stable short-term operation. These results demonstrate that evaporation-front-mediated deposition is a viable, single-step strategy for fabricating directly integrated binder-free cobalt hydroxide electrodes with effective interfacial charge-transfer characteristics.

papers.title: Revisiting the Mechanism and Origin of Selectivity in Pd(II) Catalyzed Conjugate Additions of Arylboronic Acids
papers.abstract: Pd(II) catalyzed conjugate additions of arylboronic acids to α,β-unsaturated carbonyls using PyDHIQ or PyOx ligands are widely used for the enantioselective synthesis of quaternary centers. Building on previous computational studies of this reaction, the transmetalation step was revisited to locate several previously unknown but energetically competitive transition structures, specifically an alternative favorable pathway for the transmetalation through a 4-membered transition state with the PyOx ligand. Extensive conformational sampling of the transition structures provides into the effect of the conformation of the PyDHIQ ligand on the selectivity in the synthesis of β-aryl, β-quaternary δ-lactams. The ligand adopts the ‘closed’ conformation in the selectivity-determining transition state. Detailed analysis of noncovalent and electrostatic interactions in the different conformations provides physical insights into the origin of the experimentally observed stereoselectivity.

papers.title: Occurrence and Physicochemical Characterisation of Analgesic Pharmaceutical Residues in Leachate from a Municipal Solid Waste Dumpsite in Lagos, Nigeria: A Baseline Environmental Screening Study
papers.abstract: The occurrence of pharmaceutical residues in landfill leachate represents an increasingly recognised environmental concern, particularly in rapidly urbanising regions where pharmaceutical waste is co-disposed with general municipal solid waste. This study investigated the presence and concentrations of three widely consumed analgesic compounds — acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diclofenac — in leachate samples collected from the Solous Dumpsite, Igando, Lagos State, Nigeria, one of the largest active municipal solid waste disposal sites in West Africa. Three leachate samples were collected from distinct points within the dumpsite during the wet season and subjected to liquid-liquid extraction (LLE) prior to quantification by high-performance liquid chromatography with ultraviolet detection (HPLC-UV). Key physicochemical parameters — including pH, electrical conductivity, turbidity, total dissolved solids (TDS), and total suspended solids (TSS) — were simultaneously characterised. All three target analytes were detected in at least one sample. Acetaminophen recorded the highest mean concentration (5.62 ± 5.53 µg/L), followed by ibuprofen (0.89 ± 0.073 µg/L) and diclofenac (0.57 ± 0.406 µg/L), establishing a rank order of acetaminophen > ibuprofen > diclofenac. Turbidity values (mean 65.67 NTU) substantially exceeded the WHO guideline threshold of ≤5 NTU, indicating significant particulate and organic pollution loading. These findings provide the first reported baseline data on analgesic pharmaceutical residues in leachate specifically from the Solous Dumpsite and underscore the need for improved pharmaceutical waste management, leachate treatment infrastructure, and binding regulatory standards for pharmaceutical contaminants in Nigerian landfill leachate.

papers.title: A Smooth and Fully Differentiable Molecular Cavity Based on Discretization via Reference-Onto-Surface Projection
papers.abstract: We present a new molecular cavity for the use in continuum models that consists of two independent components: i.) a smooth van der Waals (SvdW) surface, which is fully differentiable and recovers the properties of a solvent-excluded-surface (SES) while remaining free of geometric singularities, and ii.) a Discretization scheme via Reference-Onto-surface Projection (DROP), a general approach to discretize arbitrary differentiable implicit surfaces that leads to fully consistent analytical derivatives. DROP can be used with any differentiable level set and can thus be generalized beyond molecular cavities, which we demonstrate here for a genus-2 surface. The integration consistency of DROP shows excellent agreement with conventional marching cubes meshing. We validate the SvdW-DROP cavity for applications with the Conductor-like Polarizable Continuum Model (CPCM) and the GOSTSHYP pressure model and compare the cavity with other state-of-the-art cavity construction schemes. Due to the smooth surface with no crevices, a more homogeneous CPCM surface charge distribution and lower outlying charges are obtained, compared with regular vdW cavities. Surface area and polarization energy scans show fully smooth energies and stable gradients, which are further validated using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and geometry optimizations. Due to its near linear scaling with system size, smooth potential energy surface, fully consistent derivatives, and avoidance of unfavorable kinks and crevices in its surface, the SvdW-DROP cavity outperforms conventional vdW-type cavity construction as well as state-of-the-art SES-type schemes.

papers.title: Redox-mediated electrified method for green and low-cost spent lithium-ion battery materials recycling
papers.abstract: After 30 years of commercialization and mass production, lithium-ion batteries have generated massive waste streams, especially with their expanding use in electric vehicles. Recycling spent batteries and valorizing useful components are therefore increasingly urgent for sustainable development. However, conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical methods are limited by high energy consumption or large chemical input, creating demand for greener and more efficient recycling technologies. Here, using LiCoO 2 as an example, we report a closed-loop electrified chemical process based on redox-targeting reactions to recover valuable species from spent battery materials using only electricity and water. Complimentary reductive leaching of LiCoO 2 and oxidative leaching of LiFePO 4 were performed with anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonate as a regenerative redox mediator to sequentially break down LiCoO 2 and achieve efficient separation of Co 2+ and Li + in the form of Co(OH) 2 and LiOH. This cost-effective and environmentally friendly method was also extended to the recycling of LiNi x Mn y Co z O 2 with a high recovery rate of Li+ and transition metal species. It is anticipated that the electrified chemical recycling method demonstrated here would provide a credible solution to the valorization of battery waste and contribute to the sustainable development of lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Catalysis by a metastable photoswitchable cage
papers.abstract: A visible-light-responsive ligand together with a non-switchable ligand can be assembled into a mixture of molecular cages with palladium(II) ions. When irradiated with 530 nm light, the system converges to form a single product, a metastable, mixed ligand molecular cage. This cage can be reversibly disassembled using 424 nm light, an example of integrative self-sorting controlled by light. The metastable assembly can catalyze both Michael addition and nitroaldol reactions. Importantly, visible light accesses a metastable catalytic state inaccessible under thermodynamic control. We demonstrate that the active assembled species can be switched on and off at will using visible irradiation. The metastable species is the most catalytically active assembly.

papers.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Hydro- and Deuteroacylation of Acrylates using Water as Hydrogen Source
papers.abstract: Acylation of activated alkenes provides useful and quick access to synthetically useful 1,4-difunctionalized compounds. In this work, an operationally simple mechanochemical protocol for the hydroacylation of acrylates and related activated alkenes is reported using thioesters as acyl donors and water as the hydrogen source. This approach selectively furnished linear coupling products, complementing previous nickel-catalyzed methodologies that predominantly yield branched 1,3-adducts. Substitution of water with D2O enables straightforward synthesis of deuterium-labeled products with high levels of selective isotopic incorporation. Detailed mechanistic investigations, including primary and secondary KIE studies, Hammett analysis, DFT computations and NMR spectroscopy, support a pathway involving migratory insertion at the nickel center, while providing no evidence for the involvement of radical intermediates.

papers.title: SitepKa: Site-Specific Acid and Base pKa Prediction Across Multiple Industrial Solvents
papers.abstract: The propensity of a molecule to donate or accept a proton fundamentally governs its reactivity, solubility, and biological activity across diverse chemical environments; however, accurately predicting the site and extent of protonation or deprotonation at scale remains an unresolved challenge. Existing deep-learning models are largely either limited to predicting pKa values only in aqueous media or unable to resolve site-specific pKa variations. Here we introduce SitepKa, a graph neural network that predicts sitespecific pKa values across water and 34 industrial organic solvents. The model identifies ionisable atoms, classifies each as acidic or basic, and produces site-level estimates through a dual-graph cross-attention architecture that explicitly models solute–solvent interactions, supplemented by Kamlet–Taft solvent descriptors. Trained on 33,269 experimental measurements from ten public sources, SitepKa achieves competitive accuracy on aqueous blind-challenge benchmarks (MAE 1.49–2.30 on SAMPL6–8) and transfers effectively to non-aqueous solvents including DMF and pyridine (MAE 0.87–0.99), a regime where deep-learning tools are largely absent. The model generalises to structurally complex macrolides and glycopeptides well outside its training size range without retraining, and correctly withholds prediction for non-ionisable atoms. These results establish that site-level, multi-solvent pKa prediction is achievable within a single workflow, with broad applicability across chemical and materials sciences, including pharmaceutical design, reaction development, and electrolyte engineering.

papers.title: The Canalised Cleavage of Glucosepane
papers.abstract: We report a strategy for chemical cleavage and de-clamping of glucosepane, the dominant protein–protein advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslink in aged human tissue. Glucosepane exceeds other AGE crosslinks in collagen and elastin by ~10–100-fold and accumulates in long-lived matrix, yet prior AGE-breaker attempts have relied on chemistries mismatched to its bicyclic aminal–amidine core. No peer-reviewed chemical cleavage method has been reported since glucosepane’s structural identification and total synthesis. The proposed cleavage sequence activates the lysine-side C–N bond, intercepts the opened/iminium intermediate with an aminooxy (α-effect) nucleophile before closure or re-crosslinking, and completes severance by second-site capture, hydrolysis, or post-capture redox chemistry of the trapped adduct. Lewis-acid activation, mild-acid and general-acid catalysis, and bifunctional preorganization increase neutral entry into the opened/iminium product pathway; targeted N1 oxidation adds redox entry through α-deprotonation followed by second oxidation, Bond-A β-scission, or photochemical priming; and matrix strain and water-activity effects further bias aged collagen toward the same chemistry. Direct β-scission remains the simplest projected redox route to the first Bond-A break in targeted mature-collagen treatment. In the bifunctional format, the activating group and aminooxy trap are held in one scaffold, making trapping effectively intramolecular (10³–10⁵ M effective molarity; ~2 × 10⁴–2 × 10⁶ above 50 mM bulk scavenger). The high-effective-molarity branch model favors second capture and complete severance (≈0.992) over recrosslinking (≈10⁻⁵), and rigid picolyl/aminooxy scaffolds place leading bifunctional opening barriers at ~13.0–13.4 kcal mol⁻¹, corresponding to projected opening rates of ~2.3–4.4 × 10³ s⁻¹. In the kinetic projection, substrate preselection plus accelerated opening and local capture raises the product-selectivity metric 295.5-fold (9.175 × 10⁻⁵ to 0.0271). Selectivity rests on lesion topology, local glucosepane burden, preorganized trap/scavenger capture, and physiological matrix strain; aromatic side reactions are tracked directly in the same product assay. Downstream MMP remodeling then amplifies the tissue response after chemical cleavage. The DFT/PCM descriptor panel places closed glucosepane at 5.68 eV; tryptophan/indole is the closest general side-chain comparator at 5.47–5.55 eV but is essentially absent from mature type I collagen; p-cresol/tyrosine and histidine lie higher at ~5.91 and 6.04 eV. After aminooxy trapping, the glucosepane-derived adduct lies at 2.80 eV, more than 2.6 eV below tryptophan/indole and more than 3.1 eV below the mature-collagen Tyr/p-cresol comparator (~5.91 eV). Constrained closed-state radical-cation scans bound direct redox access: the bare Bond-A surface peaks near 29.7 kcal mol⁻¹ and remains ~22.2 kcal mol⁻¹ uphill at 3.00 Å, with tested Zn geometries still high in energy. The α-deprotonation/second-oxidation branch is supported by a ~14.6 kcal mol⁻¹ transition-state diagnostic and is the strongest positive driver of projected trapped-product formation in sensitivity analysis (ρ = 0.615). Productive redox chemistry is therefore framed as targeted β-scission or iminium-forming entry into the trapped-product pathway, not nonspecific fragmentation. The anti-glucosepane Glu3 DNA aptamer supplies a validated glucosepane-binding handle for localization (K_D = 17.10 ± 0.96 nM; 10–15 kDa; below the ~40 kDa fibril size-exclusion threshold; Li et al., Nanoscale Horizons 2025 [74]), and ocular collagen provides the clearest first redox-access setting because corneal stroma and Bruch’s membrane are collagen-rich, avascular, and light-accessible. These results define a catalyst-trap/redox route for glucosepane crosslink cleavage and a chemically specific framework for addressing accumulated, turnover-resistant molecular lesions with suitable trappable or fragmentation-prone chemistry.

papers.title: Unconventional electron-rich and electron-deficient multicenter bonds in gold halide perovskites
papers.abstract: Cesium gold halides are prominent lead-free distorted double perovskites with potential as photovoltaic, photocatalytic, and photosensitive materials. They exhibit Cs2Au2X6 (X= Cl, Br, I) stoichiometry and crystallize in a tetragonal structure at room pressure due to the presence of mixed-valence gold states (AuI and AuIII). At moderate pressures, they tend to undergo a phase transition to the cubic perovskite with CsAuX3 stoichiometry, characterized by single-valence AuII. Here, we theoretically investigate the paradigmatic case of Cs2Au2Cl6 under compression and its transformation into CsAuCl3. Our results demonstrate that the tetragonal-to-cubic phase transition in this perovskite family is governed by a fundamental change in the chemical bonding. In Cs2Au2X6, bonding is dominated by 1D and 2D X‒Au‒X electron-rich multicenter bonds (ERMBs). In CsAuX3, bonding is characterized by 3D electrondeficient multicenter bonds (EDMBs) occurring as infinite linear ‒X‒Au‒X‒Au‒X‒ chains in the three directions. This transformation reflects the gradual pressure-induced polymerization of the [AuICl2]‒ and [AuIIICl4]‒ anions into a three dimensional network. The bonding change follows the stages recently proposed by the unified theory of multicenter bonding, which explains the origin of ERMBs and EDMBs in compounds involving electron-rich elements with valence s- and p-type electrons, such as halides. This study thus reveals that low-symmetry perovskites can feature ERMBs and that cubic perovskites, even those including elements with valence d-type electrons, such as gold, can exhibit EDMBs. These findings provide a bonding-based framework for understanding the unconventional properties of both distorted and ideal perovskites, which cannot be adequately described within the traditional classification of ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding.

papers.title: QENEX LAB: A Self-Contained Quantum Chemistry Platform with Reproducible Self-Assessed Compliance and Cryptographic Provenance Bundles
papers.abstract: QENEX LAB is a sovereign, air-gapped scientific computing platform for quantum chemistry and drug discovery, deployed on a single-server configuration with no external cloud or hardware dependencies. The platform provides 12 user-callable computational methods through a unified Molecule.compute() API (Hartree–Fock, MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), UCCSD, EOM-CCSD, CASSCF, DFT/LDA/B3LYP, TDDFT, DLPNO-CCSD, DMC) backed by 32 method-implementation modules and 6 basis sets (STO-3G, 6-31G*, cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ, aug-cc-pVDZ, aug-cc-pVTZ). Hartree–Fock energies agree with PySCF references to sub-nanohartree precision (drift < 1 × 10⁻⁹ Hartree) on 5 of 6 reference-validated (molecule, basis) tuples; the worst case is sub-millihartree (3.4 × 10⁻⁴ Hartree on H₂O / cc-pVDZ via the native Obara–Saika engine). Compliance posture is self-assessed against six published rubrics with full reproducibility: NASA TRL 6/9, DoD MRL 7/10, NASA NPR 7150.2D Rev D (40/42 PASS, 2 honest WARN), FAIR Principles for Research Software (20/20), ISO/IEC 25010:2011 (18/18), and WIPO PCT Rule 11 (8/8) — total 111/113. These are self-assessments, not external audits by NASA, DoD, ISO, IEC, or WIPO. The platform ships with a cryptographic provenance system: every computed energy emits a runnable .qlang verification program plus an atoms.json geometry sidecar that an external auditor can re-execute. The v2 preprint supersedes v1 (10.26434/chemrxiv.15001263/v1, March 2026); §V reconciles every v1 numeric claim against today's reproducer output and documents downward revisions where v1 was overstated. The companion open-source verifier subset (Apache 2.0, https://github.com/qenex-ai/qenex-verifier, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20083483) lets any reviewer independently reproduce every numeric claim in this abstract on a clean machine.

papers.title: Dimethyl Isosorbide: A Renewable Solvent for Sustainable Drug Discovery Chemistry
papers.abstract: As regulatory and environmental pressures intensify, the search for greener solvents in drug discovery is paramount. Dimethyl isosorbide (DMIso), derived from biomass, has emerged as a sustainable dipolar aprotic solvent alternative to traditional CMR solvents like DMF, DMAc and NMP. This work presents a comprehensive assessment of DMIso in key synthetic transformations relevant to medicinal chemistry like amide and ester couplings, nucleophilic aromatic substitutions, alkylations, and protection group chemistry. Our findings demonstrate that DMIso supports efficient reactions, tolerates strong bases such as NaH, and facilitates straightforward isolation of products. By sharing this work, we hope to contribute to a wider use of DMIso as a safe and versatile solvent for organic synthesis.

papers.title: Digital infrastructure to support and share daily high-throughput experimental materials research
papers.abstract: High-throughput and autonomous experimentation generate complex, heterogeneous datasets whose reuse, large-scale analysis, and linking to data from first-principles calculations remain challenging. Here, we report on an operational deployment of the open-source NOMAD Oasis data infrastructure as a digital backbone for daily high-throughput experimental work in a materials discovery group at DTU Nanolab. The customized platform supports the complete experimental workflow in a thin-film laboratory, linking physical inventory items, automated synthesis logs, high-throughput characterization data, and cloud-based analysis within a unified data model. The platform preserves full sample provenance across multi-step workflows and uses unified sample coordinates to enable direct cross-technique correlation. We demonstrate the capabilities of the platform on a combined experimental-computational project centered on phosphosulfide thin-film libraries. The data consists of 12,000 experimental samples acquired during routine operation over 18 months, complemented by more than 800 first-principles calculations - all managed in a unified data platform available at https://nomad.nanolab.dtu.dk/nomad-oasis/gui/search/combinatorial-samples . We show how an open, extensible data infrastructure system supports reproducible workflows, scalable analysis, and long-term data reuse.

papers.title: Multimodal Odor Perception Prediction Using Olfactory EEG and Physicochemical Features of Odorants
papers.abstract: Odor sensory evaluation is crucial in the food, textiles, and cosmetics industries. Traditional methods rely on expert human evaluators but suffer from poor repeatability, while modern electronic noses capture objective physicochemical characteristics of odorants but fail to account for human olfactory preferences. This study investigates the integration of human olfactory preferences encoded in electroencephalogram (EEG) signals with objective physicochemical properties captured by electronic noses. EEG data were recorded while subjects perceived mono-molecular odorants, and vibrational spectra (VS) and fingerprint features (FPF) were extracted for the same odorants. The fusion of EEG-derived features with VS and FPF significantly improved prediction performance compared to using individual feature modalities alone. To extract discriminative olfactory EEG representations, we propose a novel Topological Data Analysis-based Neural Olfactory Signal Extraction (TDA-NOSE) framework, which leverages phase space reconstruction and persistent homology to capture intrinsic topological structures in EEG signals. This work represents the first investigation of olfactory EEG analysis using TDA. Furthermore, we demonstrate that TDA-NOSE features outperform state-of-the-art deep learning models for odor perception prediction, even when using a single EEG channel, highlighting their strong representational capability and robustness. All experiments were conducted under cross-subject evaluation settings, where training and testing were performed on different subjects, demonstrating the ability of the proposed framework to generalize across individuals. Experimental results show that TDA-NOSE achieves 23.10% accuracy in ten-class classification and 67% accuracy in binary olfactory classification, significantly surpassing previously reported benchmarks. These findings underscore the effectiveness of multimodal fusion and the potential of topological representations for advancing olfactory perception modeling.

papers.title: Gas Phase Structures of Cationized Imidacloprid and Cationized Chlorpyrifos
papers.abstract: Neonicotinoids and organophosphates are important analytes due to their use as insecticides and environmental profiles. Cationized imidacloprid and chlorpyrifos as prototypical examples of these were analyzed with drift tube, traveling wave, trapped ion, and cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry, with experimental collision cross sections ( Exp CCS N2 ) derived for each to help understand their gas phase structures. The Exp CCS N2 of potassiated imidacloprid and chlorpyrifos are reported for the first time. The cross-platform Exp CCS N2 for [imidacloprid+K] + is 160−165 Å² and for [chlorpyrifos+K] + is 175–176 Å². Consistent assignment of [imidacloprid+H] + structure is achieved based on current work, literature interlaboratory CCS values, DFT energetics, predicted CCS ( Calc CCS N2 ) and literature IRMPD spectroscopy. Imidacloprid coordinates cations at the pyridinic N, with a varying degree of nitroguanidine interaction that depends on the cation. Sodiated and potassiated imidacloprid ions have a 10-membered ring structure where the overall size depends more on the non-covalent interactions than the incorporated cation size. Chlorpyrifos also coordinates cations at the N, but consistently forms 6-membered ring structures. Overall size trends for sodiated and potassiated species follow the cation size trends, revealing the change in size due to incorporated cation. The consistency of interlaboratory results and current results also support confident assignment for the protomer of [chlorpyrifos+H] + .

papers.title: Aggregation-induced emission luminogens based on restriction of intramolecular vibration
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, high-performance materials with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics have emerged as indispensable components in modern functional materials science. Among them, AIEgens based on the restriction of intramolecular rotation (RIR) mechanism have been thoroughly studied and developed. AIEgens operating via the restriction of intramolecular vibration (RIV) mechanism have emerged as a promising yet underexplored class; however, they remain constrained by a limited repertoire of molecular scaffolds and poorly defined design principles. This review categorizes reported RIV-type AIEgens into four types based on a geometry-oriented classification of molecular deformation modes: structural inversion driven by aromaticity, bending, twisting, and molecular bond vibration. The representative structures and underlying RIV mechanisms are elaborated in detail, aiming to establish a framework for the rational design and functional expansion of next-generation RIV-type AIEgens, with the ultimate goal of broadening their applications in optoelectronics and biomaterials.

papers.title: Phase-separated plantymers as high-strength adhesives
papers.abstract: Fossil-based adhesives are still a key reason everyday products remain unrecyclable and nondegradable. While the shift toward renewable biopolymer binders is accelerating, their industrial adoption remains hindered by poor bonding, moisture sensitivity, processing bottlenecks, and high costs. Here, we resolve these challenges by tuning the phase behavior of biopolymers. Using the agricultural byproduct zein as a scalable model, we engineer plant proteins into a coacervate via liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). This phase-separated system demonstrates versatility for common industrial application methods such as blade-and spray coating. We show that transitioning the system from a homogeneous solution to a coacervation regime significantly enhances its bonding performance. The adhesive delivers a bonding strength exceeding 12 MPa on wood substrates, surpassing most conventional fossil-and bio-based resins. Furthermore, it can be cured by simple drying and provides superior water resistance owing to the intrinsic hydrophobicity of the protein. A techno-economic analysis shows that recycling the volatile production solvent keeps costs competitive and makes the process market-ready. This phase-separation strategy establishes a versatile route for designing high-performance, sustainable bonding materials from a broad spectrum of biopolymers.

papers.title: Technical note: On the selection of precooling loops for low-temperature continuous flow chemistry.
papers.abstract: Precooling lines are often used in cryogenic flow chemistry but factors affecting their performance are not well characterised. We present a systematic study on the effects of: flow rate, residence time and internal diameter on the cooling performance of a selection of tubing commonly used in flow chemistry systems, using THF as the solvent. Based on our findings, guidelines for minimum residence times for effective precooling are suggested. The scope and limitations of precooling as a temperature management solution are explored in a series of lithiation reactions on aryl bromides in flow. We surmise that while precooling in flow is important, it is not the only factor relevant in stabilising extremely reactive organolithium species in isolation.

papers.title: PyFock: A Just-In-Time Compiled Gaussian Basis DFT Python Code for CPU and GPU Architectures
papers.abstract: Despite the robust ecosystem, ease of use, and flexibility offered by Python, most of the current popular quantum chemistry codes are still developed in Fortran, C, or C++ due to their speed advantage over Python. Furthermore, the tedious compilation process acts as a gatekeeping measure for a lot of aspiring beginners. PySCF and Psi4 have alleviated a lot of these problems, however, they still use C/C++ for the performance-critical parts of the code. This hinders community development or improvements/tweaks to the low-level algorithms used for molecular integral evaluations, especially when it comes to implementing GPU acceleration. In this work, we report PyFock, a Gaussian basis Kohn–Sham density functional theory code with the quantum chemistry specific algorithms such as molecular integrals and exchange–correlation term evaluation implemented entirely in Python that achieves high performance through Numba just-in-time compilation. PyFock employs the density fitting approximation with Cauchy–Schwarz screening to achieve approximately quadratic scaling with respect to system size (similar to PySCF), driven by the electron repulsion integral evaluations (Coulomb term), while the exchange–correlation contribution shows a subquadratic scaling. We demonstrate that the code achieves numerical accuracy consistent with PySCF and computational performance comparable to state-of-the-art C/C++ backends on multicore CPUs, with benchmarks carried out on systems of up to 450 atoms using the def2-SVP, def2-TZVP, and def2-QZVP basis sets. Furthermore, PyFock leverages GPU acceleration via Numba+CuPy, delivering speedups of up to 24× over PySCF (CPU) with 4-core CPU execution. The package is open-source with a flexible MIT license (available on GitHub) and easily installable via PyPI and supports all major operating systems, offering an accessible yet efficient platform for quantum chemistry education and prototyping.

papers.title: Balancing Diversity and Efficiency in Training Datasets for Robust Machine Learning Potentials
papers.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) enable atomistic simulations at near first-principles accuracy. As model architectures mature, their reliability is increasingly constrained by training data quality. Here, we introduce ATLAS (Automated Training with Latent-space Aware Sampling), a unified and multifunctional framework based on the reversibly compressed latent space and online reliability verification. By co-designing diversity and efficiency criteria with a diversity-aware database generator and a manifold-aware active learning workflow, we steer exploitation toward sparse configurational regions while preventing premature convergence. Validated on metals, alloys, and metal oxides, ATLAS produces compact datasets exceeding foundation model training chemical spaces by orders of magnitude with up to 317 times fewer structures. ATLAS-MLIPs outperform universal MLIPs by up to 425 K in melting point accuracy for CuZn, while surface energy errors for IrO x drop from 1.21 to 0.04 J/m 2 . ATLAS provides a principled and transferable strategy for building robust MLIPs across diverse material classes.

papers.title: Nano-Focusing of Fiber-Guided Vortex Beam using Plasmonic Nanoantennas
papers.abstract: Optical vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) and cylindrical vector beams (CVBs) offer unique functionalities in communication, sensing, and chiral light-matter interactions but are hindered by inefficient nanoscale coupling due to spatial mismatch. Here, we demonstrate a fiber-integrated plasmonic nanostructure platform for subwavelength confinement of a fiber-guided vortex mode using a radial plasmonic nanorod array on a polarization-maintaining ring-core vortex fiber facet. Simulations predict symmetry-selective electric-field enhancement at the nanoscale, preservation of polarization and OAM phase. Experimentally, the stable propagation of vortex modes with preserved polarization and helicity is verified in the far-field for both bare and nanostructure-fabricated fibers.

papers.title: β-gem-Difluorinated α-Spirocyclic Amines: a Thogny Way to Essential Medchem Relevant Building Blocks
papers.abstract: A set of previously unavailable β-gem-difluorinated a-spirocyclic amines is elaborated from ketones via fluorination with sulfur tetrafluoride. The reason for selecting the fluorinated agent over milder ones is clearly established. The impact of the ring size in both cycloamine and carbocyclic components is determined. Multigram synthesis of diverse difluorosubstituted amines is shown, owing to the development of a scalable procedure for starting spirocyclic ketones via the DOS approach at the building block level.

papers.title: Periodic GFN2-xTB in CP2K: Multipolar Ewald Electrostatics, k-Point Sampling, and Transferability Benchmarks for Molecular Solids
papers.abstract: Extended tight-binding methods are attractive for condensed-phase simulations because they retain an explicit electronic Hamiltonian at a cost far below conventional density functional theory. Their transferability to periodic materials, however, cannot be assessed reliably without a genuinely periodic Hamiltonian, Brillouin-zone sampling, and symmetry-aware crystal calculations. We present a periodic implementation of the second-generation geometry, frequency, and noncovalent interaction parametrization of extended tight binding (GFN2-xTB) in CP2K. The central theoretical ingredient is a multipolar Ewald formulation for the self-consistent shell charges, atomic dipoles, and quadrupoles of GFN2-xTB, together with analytical forces and stress contributions for geometry optimization, cell optimization, and molecular dynamics. Periodic GFN2-xTB is evaluated for molecular-crystal lattice energies and cell parameters using the X23b data set. Using Γ-point cell optimization, periodic GFN2-xTB gives a mean absolute lattice-energy error of 33.06 kJ mol−1 and a mean absolute relaxed cell-volume error of 7.76%. For the ranking of ice polymorphs in the DMC-ICE13 data set, periodic GFN2-xTB on a converged 33 k-point mesh improves the relative polymorph energies over GFN1-xTB, reducing the mean absolute error from 13.11 to 8.88 kJ mol−1, consistent with the improved description of hydrogen bonding enabled by anisotropic electrostatics. The benchmarks position periodic GFN2-xTB as an efficient electronic-structure level for screening, pre-optimization, and large exploratory simulations. This work creates the foundation for periodic anisotropic electrostatics in the extended tight-binding framework and their efficient application in CP2K.

papers.title: Transfer learning on universal interatomic potential embeddings improves generalization in structure-property defect models
papers.abstract: Oxygen vacancy formation energies govern the performance of metal oxides across energy conversion, catalysis, and electronics, yet predicting them accurately without density functional theory calculations for novel chemical systems remains challenging. Here, we show that frozen 256-dimensional embeddings extracted from a pretrained MACE universal machine-learning interatomic potential encode information sufficient to predict vacancy formation energies obtained from density functional theory without requiring supercell construction, vacancy creation, or geometry optimization. A lightweight multilayer perceptron trained on these embeddings (MACE-dGNN) achieves an element-wise cross-validation mean absolute error of 0.38 eV, halving the error of a baseline graph neural network trained from scratch (0.72 eV) and offering a modest advantage over direct MACE relaxation calculations (0.51 eV). Because the embedding approach decouples representation from the prediction task and generalizes well with limited data, it will (1) extend naturally to fine-tuning and prediction of properties (e.g., charged defects) that are inaccessible to generic energy-and force-output interatomic potentials and (2) be trainable on necessarily small datasets, potentially enabling the use of more expensive but accurate tools for generating training data (e.g., hybrid functional calculations) for which training or fine-tuning of interatomic potentials will be difficult. We demonstrate practical impact by revisiting a prior screening of thermochemical water-splitting materials, where improved generalization alters ∼45 % of candidate classifications.

papers.title: Graphite formation from CO2 electroreduction in a synergistic ionic-liquid–liquid metal system
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction at catalytic liquid metal surfaces offers a promising route for sustainable carbon conversion, yet suboptimal electrolyte formulations limit its practical implementation. We demonstrate CO2 reduction at a cerium-doped liquid metal (LM-Ce) using, for the first time, an ionic-liquid-based electrolyte that combines high CO2 solubility, electrochemical stability, and high solution conductivity. Using 1 M 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium trifluoromethanesulfonate (EMIM-TfO) with 2 M H2O in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), and under an applied potential of –1.44 V vs. standard hydrogen electrode (SHE), the system achieves a high current density while CO2 reduction to graphite proceeds with a Faradaic efficiency of approximately 80% and a high degree of graphitization (IG/ID ≈ 5). These results demonstrate that ionic liquids function not only as excellent supporting media but may also serve as active and potentially tunable components to improve CO2 reduction rates at LM-Ce interfaces.

papers.title: Understanding of individual chain and entanglement behaviors in polymers with molecular dynamics simulation
papers.abstract: This study aims to develop methods and a toolkit to build realistic polymer melt and network models and understand contributions from individual chains and entanglements to mechanical properties of the models during uniaxial tensile at different conditions. In the study, classical molecular dynamics simulations of united-atom models was primarily used to generate data of mechanical qualities of various polymer systems. The study found that during small and fast uniaxial tensile, polymer melts and networks show similar behaviors and the contributions from different types of entanglements are indistinguishable. The study also identified that contributions from individual chains are more important for performance of polymers at fast deformations. The results of the study laid basis for further research in mechanical properties of complex networks and roles of chain interactions at multiple scales.

papers.title: Carbon nucleophile-mediated pyridine ring-opening enables Polymethine-functionalized Cyanine 9
papers.abstract: Extension of polymethine cyanine dyes offers a direct route to fluorophores for near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence imaging. Despite favorable, red-shifted absorption (λmax ≈ 850 nm), enneamethine cyanines (Cy9) remain underdeveloped due to limited synthetic access. Herein, we report a general strategy to synthesize polymethinefunctionalized Cy9 dyes via a 7-carbon merocyanine-like intermediate (Mero-C7), generated through enolatemediated ring opening of pyridinium benzoxazole derivatives. Subsequent condensation with diverse indolenine donors enables rapid synthesis of a structurally diverse library of 21 Cy9 derivatives, the most extensive reported to date. Notably, this approach provides access to previously unattainable substitution patterns along the polymethine chain. A lead compound, SAT-NIR-853, was successfully formulated into PEGylated nanoliposomes, retaining its optical properties and demonstrating enhanced NIR-II imaging performance relative to Cy7 counterpart, indocyanine green (ICG) in tissue-mimicking models. Overall, this work establishes a scalable platform for long-wavelength Cy9 dyes and provides the foundation for next-generation NIR imaging agents.

papers.title: Intercalation-Modulated Electronic Regulation of Nitrogen Reduction on Doped MoS2
papers.abstract: Electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) is a promising alternative to the Haber–Bosch process but is fundamentally limited by sluggish kinetics, poor selectivity against the hydrogen evolution reaction, and the difficulty of balancing N2 activation with protonation energetics. Here, we report a reconstruction-aware computational study of NRR on intercalated and doped MoS2, integrating high-throughput density functional theory calculations with electronic-structure analysis and explainable machine learning. Screening 784 dopant–intercalant combinations reveals that NRR activity is primarily dictated by the doped atom, with Mo and W emerging as optimal active centers, while intercalation serves as an electronic regulator that modulates selectivity by redistributing Mo-projected d-states near the Fermi level, tuning the balance between σ-donation and π-back-donation at the active site without perturbing surface coordination geometry. Mechanistic analysis identifies NH → NH2 as the dominant potential-determining step for most active and selective systems, revising the long-standing emphasis on early or late hydrogenation steps. We further establish a transferable descriptor space defined by N2 adsorption free energy, N2 charge state, and N–N bond length that robustly captures both activity and selectivity across the full chemical space. Grand-canonical DFT validation identifies Hf-intercalated Mo-MoS2 as a priority experimental target. These results provide generalizable design principles for selective NRR catalysts on layered materials.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Reaction Kinetics for Fe2O3 Reduction: A Coupled Inverse PINN and SINDy Approach
papers.abstract: Kinetic models for Fe2O3 reduction by hydrogen determine fuel-reactor volume, solid inventory, and achievable hydrogen yield in chemical-looping hydrogen generation (CLHG) reactors. Conventional thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) workflows require an a priori choice of reaction model—shrinking-core, grain, or Johnson–Mehl–Avrami—before Arrhenius parameters can be fitted, and that assumption is restrictive when particle morphology or transport regime is uncertain. We present a coupled iterative framework combining an inverse physicsinformed neural network (PINN) with Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) to identify the pre-exponential factor A and activation energy Ea and to discover the conversion-dependence f(X) simultaneously, from 24 sparse baselinecorrected TGA observations digitised from Wang et al. (2023). The PINN reconstructs X(t) and its time derivative by automatic differentiation, removing the numerical-differentiation noise that limits direct SINDy application to sparse TGA data. SINDy then performs sparse regression over an eight-term library covering the canonical solid–gas reaction mechanisms. A modified Bayesian Information Criterion penalises both excess coefficient magnitude and physically invalid (negative) rate predictions. Starting from A(0) = 5 s−1 and E (0) a = 50 kJ/mol, the algorithm converged in eight outer iterations to A = 7.50× 10−2 s−1 and Ea = 27.75 kJ/mol, and identified f(X) = 0.990 (1 − X)1/3. Forward validation at unseen temperatures of 800 ◦C and 950 ◦C returned R2 = 0.951 and R2 = 0.940, respectively. The discovered model differs from the shrinking-core assumption of our prior inverse-PINN study and from the JMA nucleation model of Wang et al., and is consistent with the fine-grained morphology of the parent material. The framework removes the f(X) prior from the standard TGA kinetic analysis workflow and is applicable to other solid–gas oxygen-carrier systems where the reaction mechanism is uncertain.

papers.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Control of Benzo[a]phenoxazin Ligand Binding to Oncogenic c-MYC DNA G-Quadruplex
papers.abstract: G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures in oncogenic promoter regions play crucial roles in gene regulation and represent promising targets for anticancer therapeutics. Polyaromatic small molecule ligands, including benzo[a]phenoxazin-based derivatives, selectively bind G4 structures through π-π stacking or groove/loop binding, thereby mitigating transcriptional activity. However, the kinetic and thermodynamic parameters governing ligand-G4 interactions, particularly the ligand’s residence time within the G4 complex, have not been sufficiently characterized, although the residence time has been found to be a key parameter of drug efficacy and resistance in proteins. Here, we combine fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) with atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, including well-tempered metadynamics (WT-MetaD), and infrequent metadynamics (iMetaD), to characterize the binding thermodynamics and kinetics of a substituted cationic benzo[a]phenoxazin ligand with parallel G4 DNA formed by the c-MYC promoter Pu22 sequence. Steady-state fluorescence titration shows high binding affinity of the ligand to the parallel c-MYC G4 ( K = (2.9 ∓ 0.3) x 10 7 M -1 ), primarily driven by π-π stacking of benzo[a]phenoxazin aromatic core on the solvent-exposed 5’-terminal G-tetrad, along with stabilizing hydrogen-bond and salt-bridge interactions. FCS measurements reveal rapid reaction-coupled diffusion kinetics, yielding a ligand association rate of ݇ k on = (2.4 ∓ 0.2) x 10 9 M -1 s -1 and a ligand residence time ( τ res ) of ~10 ms in the G4-bound state, showing that ligand dissociation is the rate-limiting step. WT-MetaD simulations, employing contact-pair-based and hydration collective variables, enable reconstruction of a converged free-energy surface that provides binding free energy consistent with the experimental value and reveals multiple π-stacked binding orientations of the ligand on the G-tetrad, separated by barriers of ~30–35 kJ mol -1 . Extensive iMetaD simulations capture highly directional ligand-dissociation pathways through the loop region formed by T7, G8 and G9 of G4-DNA and recover a ligand residence time of ~9 ms, which closely matches the FCS result and directly validate iMetaD-derived kinetics. These findings establish a quantitative benchmark between enhanced-sampling simulations and experimentally measured kinetic and thermodynamic parameters for the interaction of benzo[a]phenoxazin with c-MYC G4 DNA. This work provides a generalizable multiscale framework for elucidating deeper molecular insight into ligand-G4 recognition across energy and time scales, identifying ligand residence time as a critical parameter that may be optimized through rational design of next-generation benzo[a]phenoxazin-based G4-targeted compounds with better efficacy.

papers.title: Acid Strength–Dependent Oligomerization Pathways in Furan Acylation
papers.abstract: 10 The acid-catalyzed acylation of furan with acetic anhydride to 2-acetylfuran (AF) offers a 11 promising route for biomass valorization, yet acid-induced oligomerization limits its practical 12 scalability. Herein, we systematically investigate the effect of acid strength on AF selectivity 13 and oligomer formation using five liquid Brønsted acids spanning a wide Hammett acidity 14 range (H0 ≈ −4.66 to −14.6). The AF yield exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on acid 15 strength, rising from 77.9% to 81.1% for moderately strong acids before dropping sharply to 16 52.5% under superacidic conditions. Gel-permeation chromatography (GPC) revealed that 17 oligomer molecular weight increases monotonically with acid strength, while the oligomer 18 fraction mirrors the non-monotonic AF yield trend. High-resolution LC–ESI–MS/MS 19 identified diacetylfuran (DAF) as the dominant side product and distinguishes two 20 mechanistically distinct oligomer families: those arising from nucleophilic substitution at the 21 carbonyl group (NSCO) and those from ring substitution (NSRO), the latter emerging 22 prominently only under strongly acidic conditions. Density functional theory (DFT) 23 calculations reveal that activation free-energy barriers for AF formation, DAF formation, and 24 oligomerization initiation scale linearly with catalyst deprotonation energy with statistically 25 indistinguishable slopes, indicating that increasing acid strength uniformly accelerates both 26 productive and unproductive pathways. These findings demonstrate that the observed 27 selectivity behavior originates from a coupled interplay of kinetic and thermodynamic factors, 28 and that acid-strength tuning alone is insufficient to suppress oligomerization. 29

papers.title: MolDiff-PEFT: Conditional Molecular Graph Diffusion with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Molecular Generation and Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Molecular generation and property prediction are fundamental tasks in computational chemistry and drug discovery. Existing approaches face two key challenges: generating molecules that simultaneously satisfy multiple chemical property constraints, and efficiently adapting pre-trained molecular models to downstream tasks without prohibitive computational costs. We propose MolDiff-PEFT, a unified framework that integrates conditional molecular graph diffusion with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. The framework comprises three components: a conditional discrete graph diffusion generator that progressively denoises molecular graphs guided by target properties through adaptive layer normalization, achieving 96% validity and 93% novelty on the MOSES benchmark; a hierarchical molecular encoder that captures multi-scale chemical information at atom, functional group, and molecule levels through graph attention and cross-attention mechanisms; and MolAdapter, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning module with dynamic routing that enables multi-task property prediction using only 2.6M trainable parameters. Extensive experiments on QM9, MOSES, and MoleculeNet benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both generation and prediction tasks. MolAdapter matches full fine-tuning with an average AUROC of 0.872 while reducing training time by 62.4%. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each hierarchical encoding level and the effectiveness of the dynamic routing mechanism.

papers.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission (AIE) Drug Nanocrystals: A New Paradigm from Molecular Design to Theranostics
papers.abstract: Drug nanocrystals have achieved remarkable clinical success as an effective strategy for enhancing the bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs. However, traditional drug nanocrystals still face fundamental obstacles in the visual tracking of their in vivo fate and real-time therapeutic evaluation. The discovery of the aggregation-induced emission (AIE) phenomenon offers a revolutionary opportunity to overcome this dilemma. This article systematically expounds the scientific connotation, design principles, fabrication strategies, and application prospects of a novel class of functional materials—AIE drug nanocrystals. AIE drug nanocrystals are nano-sized crystalline particles composed entirely of active pharmaceutical ingredients possessing AIE properties. They realize the ontological unification of “pharmacophore” and “fluorophore,” namely “Drug-Probe Unity” (DPU). This review first delineates the theoretical evolution from ACQ to AIE, from drug nanocrystal technology to AIE-pharmacology, and further to fluoropharmacology, proposing a drug classification framework based on four aggregation-state luminescent behaviors (ACQ, AIE, ARE, ARN). Subsequently, taking the AIE discovery of fenamates and the construction of high-performance DTPA-BT-F AIE nanocrystals as examples, the strategies for screening and de novo design of intrinsically AIE-active drug molecules are discussed. At the fabrication science level, the feasibility and polymorphic control challenges of preparing AIE drug nanocrystals using top-down, bottom-up, and combinatorial technologies are analyzed in depth. The unique photophysical properties, especially the polymorphism-, crystal habit-, and size-dependent fluorescence behaviors, and their advantages in high brightness, superior photostability, and super-resolution imaging are elaborated. In the application dimension, this review highlights breakthroughs in stimulated emission depletion (STED) super-resolution dynamic tracking, tumor-targeted theranostics, visualized drug release for oral/injectable delivery, and non-destructive evaluation of drug solid-state properties using AIE drug nanocrystals. Finally, the challenges in physical stability, scale-up production, and regulatory science are discussed, and a grand prospect is envisioned for AI-driven design, personalized nanomedicine, and clinical translation in the era of “fluoropharmacology.” This review aims to provide systematic theoretical guidance and a methodological framework for the development of next-generation intelligent nanomedicines integrating therapy with real-time self-reporting capabilities.

papers.title: MXenes: A Roadmap on Synthesis, Processing, and Applications
papers.abstract: MXenes, an emerging class of two-dimensional van der Waals materials, have become the focus of research, demonstrating exceptional potential in electrochemical, biochemical and electronic applications. This chapter provides a brief overview of MXenes, covering their fundamental characteristics, synthesis methods and current challenges, with particular attention on synthesis methods.

papers.title: Patent-Based Evidence on Sustainable Innovation in the Global Chemicals Industry
papers.abstract: This paper provides patent-based evidence on sustainability-oriented innovation in the global chemicals industry. Using priority patent data from 120 large chemical companies over the period 2012–2022, we examine trends in sustainability-related filings and their integration with digital technologies. We document an acceleration in sustainability-focused patenting during 2018–2022, alongside a rising share of such filings within total R&D activity. Innovation growth is concentrated in carbon management, recycling and bio-based materials, with particularly strong activity in feedstock and converter-industry segments of the value chain. We also find that digital technologies are becoming increasingly embedded in sustainability-related patenting, with digital-linked filings growing significantly faster than broader chemical patent activity. While sustainability-oriented patents remain a minority share of total filings, the results indicate a structural shift in innovation priorities within the sector.

papers.title: Development of a novel Proteolysis Targeting Chimera to degrade the NS5 Protein in the Zika Virus
papers.abstract: Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras (PROTACs) are bifunctional molecules that utilize the Ubiquitin-Proteasome System (UPS) to degrade proteins 1 . Most PROTACs thus far in development have target cancers; few have been developed for viruses 1, 2, 3 . One virus with a critical care gap is the Zika Virus 4 . Zika virus affects thousands worldwide 4 . When a pregnant woman is infected, the virus can be transmitted to the embryo, causing congenital malformations, stillbirth, and fetal loss 4 . This study aims to address this gap in healthcare by creating a computational PROTAC molecule to degrade essential Zika proteins. If combined with rapid testing following potential exposure by pregnant women, the PROTAC built could neutralize or lower the risk of birth defects. Molecules were built in Avagadro2 and tested against their targets in Swissdock 5, 6 . Docking data was analyzed in ChimeraX 7 . 14 iterations were produced, with the most successful one having binding affinity sufficient for degradation. The study shows a conceptual PROTAC is plausible for degrading essential Zika proteins. Future studies must focus on the optimization of the molecule, delivery systems, in vivo testing of degradation, ternary complex modeling, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration 4, 8 .

papers.title: PVmatAgent: A Large Language Model (LLM) Agent for Photovoltaic and Perovskite Material Design and Analysis
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has opened new opportunities for materials informatics. However, LLMs fall short in photovoltaic (PV) material design due to their lack of domain grounding, unreliable outputs, and inability to perform integrated computational tasks. To address these issues, this work presents PVmatAgent, an autonomous LLM-based computational agent designed specifically for PV materials design and analysis. PVmatAgent implements 13 domain-specific tools, falling into 9 functional modules or four categories at a higher level: knowledge acquisition, physics simulation, performance evaluation, and experimental guidance. The system integrates over a dozen domain-specific tools, including the machine learning force field CHGNet for geometric relaxation and formation energy calculation, the graph neural network MEGNet for bandgap prediction, the Goldschmidt tolerance factor and octahedral factor for perovskite stability screening, the photovoltaic performance evaluator including the Shockley–Queisser limit, SLME model and tandem current matching module, the material project agent for structure retrieval, the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) knowledge base. A hallucination truncation mechanism prevents the model from fabricating numerical outputs. The system was validated on four representative scenarios. Results demonstrate that PVmatAgent effectively executes computational tasks and provides corrective recommendations grounded in literature evidence for photovoltaic material design. This work offers a practical paradigm for LLM-based autonomous agents in AI-driven optoelectronic materials discovery.

papers.title: Systematic Under‐Characterization of Psychedelic Compound Classes in Published hERG QSAR Training Data: A Pre‐Registered Multi‐Family Analysis
papers.abstract: QSAR models for hERG cardiotoxicity are increasingly deployed in pre‑IND cardiac safety triage of psychedelic‑class therapeutics under accelerated regulatory review. We make two contributions. Empirical: across three structurally independent psychedelic compound families (22 tryptamines, 20 phenethylamines, 17 cathinones; 59 compounds spanning natural products to FDA‑approved medications), published primary hERG patch‑clamp literature with same‑preparation Ki + IC50 pairing yields one substantive datapoint (bupropion, IC50 = 69 µM). Six of 11 pre‑registered priors that anticipated marketed‑pharmaceutical compounds would have published patch‑clamp data were falsified in a tightly clustered pattern on the assumption “well‑known compound classes have published data.” A pre‑registered targeted full‑text retrieval protocol (PubMed bath‑salt toxicology, Drugs@FDA bupropion NDA filings, ergoline boundary spot‑check) surfaced zero additional pairs, resolving the central thesis to CONFIRMED at published‑literature level. Three‑architecture Sub‑analysis 2 on all 59 compounds (Pred‑hERG 5.0, ADMET‑AI 2.0.1, admetSAR 2.0) cleared the pre‑registered cross‑architecture positive‑call divergence (CAPD) threshold (effect‑size criterion S2.1) on three of three families at the surviving data scale under the (C) data‑landscape constraint; cathinones show 10× spread between ADMET‑AI Blocker rate (59%) and Pred‑hERG consensus (6%). Two suggestive (N = 2) cross‑family cases of the Paper I Pred‑hERG consensus‑rule override are observed (psilocin and a 4‑hydroxy‑N‑methyl‑N‑ethyl tryptamine analog: binary correctly calls Blocker, consensus overrides to Non‑blocker); systematic characterization of the asymmetric‑failure‑mode hypothesis requires larger‑scale evaluation (§4.5). The pre‑registered bidirectional scaffold‑vs‑bit‑level hypothesis resolved PARTIAL CONFIRMATION on the scaffold‑aware half: combined ADMET‑AI + admetSAR positive‑call rate on scaffold‑in‑training‑but‑bit‑level‑distant compounds is 47.8% of the rate on scaffold‑novel‑bit‑distant compounds, confirming scaffold‑context recognition by graph‑encoded and descriptor‑encoded architectures. Methodological: we adapt the PRISMA‑S search‑protocol‑asload‑bearing‑methodology pattern (Rethlefsen et al. 2021) to chemoinformatics QSAR‑validity work and offer the data‑landscape‑primary template as a worked example for chemoinformatics adopters; the template pre‑registers a search protocol as load‑bearing methodology, ties central‑thesis disposition to retrieval outcome, and frames secondary contributions as evidence‑for the primary finding. The empirical finding implies pre‑IND cardiac safety triage of psychedelic‑class compounds operates against a data infrastructure that QSAR architectures cannot bridge from training to query distribution; the methodological contribution generalizes as a reusable template for meta‑empirical literature‑state claims in QSAR‑validity work.

papers.title: Iron Complexes Supported by a Rigid Macrocyclic PNPN Ligand
papers.abstract: Seesaw ligands enforce a coordination geometry of the two co-ligands being in a cis configuration in an octahedral environment. While nitrogen-based weak field seesaw ligands are often employed, strong field ligands with mixed nitrogen- and phosphine-donors are rarely encountered. Herein we report the synthesis of iron(II) dihalide complexes 1 supported by a rigid seesaw PNPN ligand, yielding C 2v -symmetric compounds. Halide abstraction results in formation of five-fold coordinated cationic complexes 2 . Uptake of π-acidic ligands give cationic 3 . Dicationic complex 4 , containing two acetonitrile monodentate ligands, is prepared from Fe(OTf) 2 . The structure of 1 and 3 is studied in solid-state and in solution, including 15 N-NMR spectroscopy. Furthermore, the application as catalysts in sp 2 -sp 3 Kumada cross-coupling is demonstrated, showing high reactivity with a catalyst loading of 1 mol% in one hour reaction time at room temperature.

papers.title: Predicting solubility curves in solvent mixtures using thermodynamic cycles and machine learning
papers.abstract: Predicting solubility limits of neutral organic compounds in solvent mixtures is crucial across chemical engineering, pharmaceuticals, environmental science, and biomedical research. Understanding solute interactions with solvent combinations at varying temperatures enables flexible solvent tailoring in drug development. Machine learning has shown great potential for solvent screening, offering alternatives to costly experimental measurements, yet existing approaches remain limited to single-solvent systems. In this work, we extend two previously developed machine learning models, SolProp and FusionCycle, to handle mixed-solvent systems, evaluating them against conventional machine learning models similarly adapted for mixtures. These methodologies are broadly categorized as Thermo-ML, trained on solubility-related properties via thermodynamic cycles, and Direct-ML, trained directly on solubility data. Models are benchmarked on a dataset of approximately 126,831 experimental solubility measurements in binary solvents, with FusionCycle-mix achieving a root-mean-square error below 1 log unit, demonstrating strong predictive performance in complex multi component systems.

papers.title: ActiveFusion: Fused representations improve active learning for molecular property prediction
papers.abstract: Active learning provides an efficient strategy for molecular property prediction by iteratively prioritizing compounds for experimental evaluation. However, the effectiveness of active learning pipelines depends strongly on the choice of molecular representation, and systematic understanding of how representation families affect the active learning process in uncertainty and predictive performance remain limited. In this work, we introduce ActiveFusion, a framework for integrating heterogeneous molecular representations within active learning workflows for molecular property prediction. The framework enables systematic evaluation of physicochemical descriptors, molecular fingerprints, learned graph neural network (GNN) representations, and pretrained Transformer-based representations, as well as feature-level fusion strategies that combine complementary chemical information sources. ActiveFusion evaluates models across four molecular property prediction regression tasks. Across datasets, we demonstrate that feature fusion between learned graph representations and physicochemical descriptors consistently improves prediction performance and discovery (average final iteration R 2 of 0.62, 0.57 and 0.47 for our overall best representations Chemprop+RDKit, Chemprop, and RDKit respectively). We show that exploration-driven acquisition strategies enhance scaffold coverage and promote sampling of structurally novel regions of chemical space, and that model-agnostic acquisition of new compounds based on diversity has strong performance. Notably, pretrained Transformer-based embeddings do not consistently outperform physicochemical features or GNN-learned representations in our setting, highlighting the continued relevance of chemically interpretable features and learned features from supervised, task-specific models for active learning application in molecular property prediction. Overall, ActiveFusion provides a systematic framework for studying representation–acquisition interactions in molecular discovery with representation fusion capabilities. Our study offers practical guidance for designing active learning pipelines that balance prediction accuracy with chemical space exploration.

papers.title: Revisiting Deep Learning DTA Methods from the Dataset Viewpoint
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a study revisiting deep learning drug-target affinity models, which are otherwise used as benchmark methods in the literature to compare more complex and heavy-weighted architectures. We focus on training and testing these models using pKd values from BindingDB, a dataset that presents binding affinity information of a high variety of ligans and proteins. These activity data need a proper pre-treatment and curation prior to actually using them for production tasks, a factor that is often overlooked in the literature. We show that a combination of a thorough curation of the dataset and a proper hyperparameter tuning of slight modifications of the revisited models (e.g, by using pretrained protein embeddings to describe the proteins) provides beyond state of the art performances at a much lower computational cost, with respect to more demanding deep learning models. We study the distributions of the protein and ligand learned (or eventually, pre-trained) embeddings, to observe how they classify the proteins depending on the (super)families they belong to (for the former), and how they distribute in the embedding space depending on the values of their binding affinities, with respect to a given protein (for the latter). We take advantage of the graph representations of the ligands to further approach explainability at an atom-wise level, by computing the directional derivative of the model with respect to each of the atoms of a ligand. This method, unlike other derivative-based approaches such as Grad-CAM and variants, turns out to be extremely useful for regression tasks of binding affinities, as this provides direct means of assessing which atoms contribute to an increase/decrease of the binding affinity, depending on both the sign of the directional derivative, and on its absolute value-an indication of how steep the function is with respect to each atom.

papers.title: Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials and Nuclear Quantum Effects
papers.abstract: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer is a prototypical ultrafast process that forms the foundation for many chemical and biological phenomena and is highly sensitive to changes in the underlying potential energy landscape. Here, we develop neural network potentials for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline that describe ground- and excited-state dynamics with near ab initio accuracy. These neural network potentials enable efficient sampling of the proton transfer coordinate and incorporation of nuclear quantum effects through path-integral molecular dynamics. The free energy profiles show that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer proceeds on a largely barrierless excited-state surface, with nuclear quantum effects reducing and smoothing the residual barrier. Non-equilibrium simulations yield an average proton transfer time of ∼11.4 fs for quantum hydrogen, consistent with experiment, and reveal a clear isotope effect, with slower dynamics for deuterium and classical nuclei. Mechanistic analysis identifies transient proton donor–acceptor contraction as the key enabling coordinate, while the proton crosses the midpoint prior to reaching the minimum of this coordinate, indicating a dynamically driven transfer. Subtle changes in the conjugated backbone precede proton transfer and evolve on a slower timescale, reflecting early electronic reorganization and coherent coupling between proton motion and backbone vibrations. Bond-length alternation and vibrational coherence analysis reveal isotope-dependent coherence loss, with deuteration producing stronger damping and more localized proton/backbone dynamics relative to hydrogen. These results establish neural network potential-based approaches as an effective framework for simulating excited-state proton transfer with explicit nuclear quantum effects.

papers.title: A covariance-response diagnostic for pH-dependent state-weighted observables
papers.abstract: Many pH-dependent measurements are interpreted by fitting a state-weighted observable, such as an NMR chemical shift, absorbance, partition coefficient, binding fraction, or kinetic rate. The fitted curve reports the average value, but it does not directly separate whether a local pH response is limited by acid-base activity or by the ability of the observable to distinguish between the states.
