papers.abstract: Existing peptide models saturate natural-sequence proteomics benchmarks, but whether they capture the underlying physicochemical dynamics or merely pattern-match on sequence statistics remains unclear. Public peptide datasets offer no axis along which to test this: non-canonical residues and stereochemical variation are essentially absent. We introduce StereoPep, a benchmark of 48,788 chemically synthesized peptides spanning 11 libraries, produced in the laboratory via high-throughput flow synthesis and characterized experimentally by reversephase liquid chromatography retention time. Unlike model-generated synthetic data, every peptide in StereoPep is a real molecule paired with a chromatographic measurement. The dataset is constructed around matched diastereomeric pairs (sequences identical in primary structure but differing at a single stereocenter), providing a direct test of whether models capture three-dimensional stereochemical information. StereoPep enables progress across multiple fields: it serves as a benchmark for stereochemistry-aware molecular representations and geometric deep learning, supports adapting protein language models to non-canonical residues, and underpins emerging proteomics multiplexing strategies that encode samples through retention-time shifts. Across specialized retention-time models, graph-based architectures, and protein language models, all approaches predict overall retention reasonably well (Pearson r ≈ 0.80) but collapse on diastereomer pair discrimination (AUC ≈ 0.55), revealing that current representations encode atomic composition far better than 3D structure.

papers.title: Tunable multimetallic nanoparticle exsolution from high-entropy spinel oxides
papers.abstract: Metal nanoparticle exsolution from oxides is a powerful route to generate stable metal-oxide interfaces relevant for catalysis, but controlling the process remains challenging. High-entropy oxides (HEOs) serve as compositionally complex and defect-tolerant host lattices that broaden the scope of this process beyond conventional oxides. Here, we use several in situ X-ray and microscopic techniques to track the structural, chemical, and electronic evolution of spinel-type HEOs during thermally induced exsolution under reducing conditions. We show that exsolution proceeds through composition-dependent pathways dictated by the ability of the host lattice to undergo local structural rearrangements. By varying the nominal B-site composition, we control whether exsolution occurs directly from the spinel lattice or through transient rock salt intermediates. These findings establish metal nanoparticle exsolution from high-entropy spinels as a structure- and composition-governed process and identify local rearrangements as the basis for tuning the exsolved phase composition and extent.

papers.title: A Label-Free Si-BioFET with Linearly Assembled Gold Nanoparticles for the Detection of miR-141
papers.abstract: Sensitivity of field-effect transistor biosensors (BioFETs) for nucleic acid detection is often limited by weak electrostatic control and low probe density at the sensing interface. Here, we present a BioFET platform with improved sensitivity based on lightly p-doped Schottky-barrier silicon nanobelt transistors, exhibiting reproducible ambipolar behavior in a back-gated configuration. These devices are encapsulated with an Al2O3/ZrO2 nanolaminate to prevent device performance degradation and facilitate stable biofunctionalization. Dry-state measurements demonstrate selective detection of prostate cancer biomarker, miR-141, after immobilization of complementary capture DNA, achieving detection down to the ~100 pM range, and discrimination against the non-complementary sequence, miR-155. To enhance sensitivity, template-assisted self-assembly of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) is used to form ordered linear structures directly on the sensing region. The supracolloidal assembly of AuNPs at the sensing interface tunes the receptor spacing and orientation and amplifies the influence of target hybridization on transistor response. Compared to planar devices, the hybrid AuNPBioFET exhibits improved signal modulation while preserving the label-free detection mechanism. This approach bridges scalable top-down semiconductor technology and bottomup self-assembled nanostructures, providing an innovative pathway for developing biosensing platforms with high sensitivity and multiplexing capabilities for detecting nucleic acids.

papers.title: Local Acidity as a Corrosiveness Descriptor of Fluorinated Ether Solvents in Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: Electrolyte engineering based on solvent fluorination has proven effective for stabilizing lithium (Li) metal batteries by weakening the Li+-solvent interaction. However, the influence of fluorination on the chemical reactivity of an electrolyte toward Li metal remains poorly understood. Here, the effects of fluorination are systematically investigated by increasing the degree of fluorination (from 2 to 5 substituents) of the terminal carbon atom of the 1-ethoxy-2-methoxyethane (EME) and 1-(2-methoxyethoxy)propane (MEP) backbones (denoted F2EME, F4MEP, and F5MEP). Fluorination-induced corrosion deviates from that suggested by conventionally calculated LUMO-based rationales; instead, it is quantitatively described by the local pKa associated with cleavage of the ether C–O bond. Among the three derivatives, F4MEP is identified as the optimal solvent; it is sufficiently fluorinated to promote the formation of an anion-rich solvation structure for an inorganic-rich, protective Li metal interphase, yet it is not severely corrosive as it is not over-fluorinated. Consequently, an F4MEP-based 20 μm-Li||NCM811 full-cell retains 80% of its capacity over 368 cycles. This study establishes the local pKa as a descriptor for evaluating the solvent corrosiveness and highlights the necessity of optimizing the degree of fluorination for high-performance Li metal battery electrolytes.

papers.title: Enantioselective Hydrogenation of Hydroxyacetone on Intrinsically Chiral Pt(643) Surfaces
papers.abstract: Asymmetric catalysis underpins pharmaceutical synthesis but is dominated by homogeneous molecular catalysts that complicate product separation and recycling. Heterogeneous alternatives, including hybrid systems in which molecular catalysts are immobilised on solid supports, often suffer from diminished activity and poor stability. Here, we use density functional theory and microkinetic modelling to evaluate intrinsically chiral platinum surfaces as a heterogeneous alternative, taking the hydrogenation of hydroxyacetone to 1,2-propanediol (1,2-PD) as a model reaction. On the mirror-image Pt(643)S and Pt(643)ᴿ surfaces, hydroxyacetone chemisorbs at the undercoordinated chiral kink, and the effective transitionstate barriers for the two reaction pathways differ by 0.21 eV, favouring S-1,2-PD on Pt(643)S and R-1,2-PD on Pt(643)ᴿ. By contrast, hydroxyacetone is only physisorbed on the achiral Pt(111) terrace and is hydrogenated to a racemic product with a lower effective barrier of 0.75 eV. Microkinetic modelling that accounts for the realistic coexistence of kink and terrace sites identifies an operational window near 500 K and 10-2 bar in which strong substrate binding at the chiral kink outcompetes the racemic terrace pathway, yielding enantiomeric excesses approaching 99 %. These results establish chiral Pt(643) surfaces as a viable platform for fully heterogeneous asymmetric hydrogenation and motivate experimental verification.

papers.title: Synthesis of Ni(II) CNC-Pincer Catalysts with Electronic Donor or Acceptor Groups for Visible Light Driven Carbon Dioxide Reduction
papers.abstract: A durable catalytic system is necessary to reduce CO 2 and transform it into useful products. Our catalysts contain Ni(II) bound to CCN pincer ligands composed of N-heterocyclic carbene and pyridine donors. These CNC pincers have electron-donating or -withdrawing substituents on the pyridine ring giving three complexes: Ni R wherein R = NMe 2 , NPh 2 , or CF 3 . These three compounds are also compared with our previously reported Ni H complex (R = H) to examine a compound that is electronically intermediate. A combination of spectroscopic and crystallographic techniques were used to characterize these complexes. A p K a value of -2.7 was determined for protonation of the NMe 2 substituent within Ni NMe2 by 1 H-NMR studies in DMSO-d 6 , and this value aligned well with DFT studies and electrostatic potential surface maps before and after protonation. The study of photocatalytic CO 2 reduction was performed for three complexes in both the presence and absence of an external photosensitizer (PS). Formate (HCO 2 - ) is the major product in the presence of external PS for all these complexes. With a PS, complex Ni NMe2 is the most active photocatalyst for CO formation (TON = 60), where catalysts Ni CF3 and Ni NMe2 are the most active catalysts for formate production (TON = 780 and 750, respectively). The catalysts also perform well as self-sensitized catalysts without external photosensitizer present and produce only formate (TON as high as 220 for Ni NMe2 ). Cyclic voltammetry was used to study the electrochemical properties of each complex under N 2 and CO 2 atmospheres and have revealed that two electrons must be transferred before catalysis ensues. The excited state lifetimes of the complexes were determined by transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) measurements. This data suggests that all of the new catalysts have excited states that persist for 26-59 ps and that these excited states are likely responsible for diffusional photochemistry involved in CO 2 reduction.

papers.title: Steering Diluted-NO Electroreduction Selectivity via Molecular Substituent Engineering
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the deliberate control over the hydrogenated products in electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction (ENOR) between NH 3 and NH 2 OH by varying the substituents of iron phthalocyanines grafted on multi-walled carbon nanotubes. While the methoxy-featured catalyst exhibits dominant NH 3 selectivity, another one with carboxyl groups favors efficient NH 2 OH formation which is endowed not only by its electron-deficient Fe center to facilitate the NH 2 OH desorption, but also the carboxyl-strengthened interfacial hydrogen-bonded water network to avoid deep hydrogenation. More intriguingly, this ENOR-to-NH 2 OH electrocatalyst exhibits Faradaic efficiencies up to 90%, a maximum turnover frequency of 12.0 s -1 and yield rates reaching 4330 μmol h -1 mg -1 from diluted NO (0.5% ~ 10%), all of which surpass most reported ones. It is even applicable to a simulated flue gas source with interfering CO 2 and SO 2 to afford single-pass NO conversion efficiencies up to 30%.

papers.title: ClickChem: Automated Conjugation Chemistry Planning for Antibody–Drug Conjugates
papers.abstract: Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) require precise conjugation chemistry to covalently attach cytotoxic payloads to monoclonal antibodies while preserving antigen-binding function and pharmacokinetic stability. The selection of an appropriate conjugation strategyencompassing the reaction family, the conjugation site on the antibody, and the linker architecture—remains largely empirical, relying on iterative experimental screens that are costly and time-consuming. We present ClickChem, a computational pipeline that auto-mates conjugation chemistry selection for ADC design. The pipeline operates in six sequential stages: functional-group detection on the payload, multi-conformer solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) scoring of antibody conjugation sites, chemistry family planning across seven reaction families, linker selection from a curated library, in silico bond formation via SMIRKSbased reaction execution, and product validation through a six-layer quality-control protocol incorporating Maximum Common Substructure (MCS) analysis. A distinguishing feature of the site-scoring module is an ensemble-averaged SASA calculation that generates multiple antibody conformations through an Anisotropic Network Model (ANM) and aggregates solvent-exposure statistics across the ensemble, yielding a confidence metric that penalises residues whose accessibility fluctuates between conformations. We evaluate the pipeline on three fronts. First, we verify concordance with established clinical precedent by exercising the pipeline on the payloads and conjugation-site annotations of ten FDA-approved ADCsincluding Adcetris, Kadcyla, Enhertu, and Trodelvy—and show that the pipeline selects the conventionally employed reaction family in all ten cases (10/10 concordance). Second, we present two end-to-end case studies—MMAF and Doxorubicin conjugated to a full-length IgG surrogate (PDB: 1IGT) via heterobifunctional SPAAC–IEDDA dual-click chemistrydemonstrating handle installation, site-specific conjugation at three distinct residue types

papers.title: Precursor-programmed ionic organization governs electrostatic polarization for selective photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide synthesis
papers.abstract: Controlling ionic organization in polymeric photocatalysts remains a fundamental barrier to efficient solar-driven hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis. In conventional poly(heptazine imide) (PHI) systems, cation incorporation is directed by equilibrium in molten salts, yielding statistically distributed and weakly correlated ionic environments. Here, we demonstrate that organic-inorganic ionic cocrystals (ICCs) act as molecularly preorganized precursors that encode spatially correlated cation arrangements during framework formation, enabling deterministic placement of Li+ at imide-bridged N sites. This precursor-programmed architecture decouples composition from function, establishing that photocatalytic performance is governed by ionic arrangement rather than cation identity or content. The resulting dual-cation material (CALiK) delivers an apparent quantum yield of 58% at 410 nm, among the highest reported for metal-free carbon nitride photocatalysts. Operando-relevant spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal directional charge migration driven by internal electrostatic gradients and enhanced accumulation of long-lived electrons. Complementary density functional theory calculations attribute this behavior to electrostatically polarized charge landscapes arising from spatial correlation between Li-N coordination sites and cyano-derived electron-accepting domains, which lower the energetic barrier for the two-electron oxygen reduction pathway. These findings establish that precursor programming of ionic configurations as a general strategy for controlling charge dynamics and catalytic selectivity in polymeric semiconductors.

papers.title: Artificial Coater: A Self-Driving Lab Maps Thin Film Processing Windows and Reveals Failure Mechanisms in Hybrid Perovskites
papers.abstract: Solution-processing of metal halide perovskites remains highly sensitive to subtle variations in environment, formulation, and human technique, often leading to unpredictable outcomes and limited mechanistic understanding. Despite rapid advances in materials and device performance, researchers continue to rely heavily on manual and intuition-driven optimization, inconsistent fabrication protocols, and subjective film quality evaluation. These challenges persist across diverse coating methods, including but not limited to antisolvent dripping, which is especially sensitive to ambient manufacturing. In this work, we present the Artificial Coater , a self-driving laboratory that integrates automated experimentation, Bayesian optimization, in situ UV-Vis and photoluminescence spectroscopy, and machine vision to evaluate and optimize thin film fabrication autonomously, reveal film formation mechanisms, and underlying causes of failed fabrication. To enable scalable and unbiased interpretation of in situ spectral evolution, we apply non-negative matrix factorization across thousands of spectra, revealing latent spectral features associated with successful versus failed coatings. Using the benchmark composition FA 0.83 Cs 0.17 Pb(I 0.83 Br 0.17 ) 3 , we identify critical processing parameters governing crust formation, nucleation uniformity, and phase evolution. Our approach uncovers mechanistic insights into the formation of compact and uniformly converted perovskite thin films versus films exhibiting visibly rough morphologies across the coated area, links variations in morphology to solvent extraction-mediated crystallization and reveals antisolvent drip design rules. This study establishes a data-intensive in situ framework with materials processing transparency, providing reusable and interpretable data for broader applications, including for potential transferability to other fabrication platforms and materials prepared using antisolvent drip.

papers.title: Direct Growth of BODIPY-based Conjugated Porous Polymer shell on Upconversion Nanoparticles for NIR-driven Photocatalysis
authors: Víctor A. de la Peña O´Shea
papers.abstract: The great applications of upconversion nanoparticles (UCNP) can be further extended by their encapsulation within conjugated porous polymers (CPPs). However, the synthesis of monodisperse core@shell based CPPs upconversion nanohybrids remains a challenge. Herein, we report a simple, general strategy that combines (i) prefunctionalization of UCNPs with polymerizable units, (ii) monomer‑feed control, and (iii) a centrifugation‑based work‑up to ensure anchoring to the inorganic core to provide covalent binding to grow CPP with tunable shell thickness, and low polydispersity. Thus, BODIPY-based CPP was grown over both core (NaYF 4 : Yb 3+ (20%), Er 3+ (2%)) and core-shell (NaYF 4 : Yb 3+ (20%), Er 3+ (2%)@NaYF 4 ) UCNPs, yielding UC C @CPP and UC CS @CPP. Under near infrared (NIR) excitation, UCNP upconvert light to activate the surrounding CPP shell leading to photocatalytic activity. UC CS @CPP exhibits a two-fold higher photocatalytic activity than UC C @CPP highlighting the critical role of the NaYF 4 passivation shell in preserving upconversion efficiency. Our approach addresses critical limitation of the previous designs achieving improvements photooxidation yields (i.e. 42%) and excellent recyclability. This modular approach addresses key limitations in the synthesis of UC@CPP hybrids and provides a robust platform for designing ROS-generating, NIR-driven photocatalysts.

papers.title: Efficient Microwave-Enhanced Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis of Secretin Hormones Amenable for Rapid Library Design and Lead Optimization
papers.abstract: Microwave-enhanced solid phase peptide synthesis of complex, therapeutically relevant, aspartimide-prone secretin hormones was achieved under optimized conditions with economical and commercially available protected amino acids. In order to determine robust and general methods, standard Fmoc SPPS conditions, Oxyma-buffered deprotection solution, Fmoc-(Dmb)Gly-OH, Fmoc-Asp(OMpe)-OH, and combinations thereof were systematically evaluated for crude purity using LC-MS. Aspartimide formation was significantly reduced, and syntheses were completed in a single run without the need for expensive, commercially inaccessible, or diversity-limiting peptide fragments or pseudoprolines, supplying methods amenable for rapid library generation, hit-to-lead endeavors, and lead optimization.

papers.title: Reconfigurable DNA-surfactant coatings for tunable oil and water barriers
papers.abstract: Commercial coatings for paper often rely on non-renewable, non-biodegradable polymers, thereby restricting the end-of-life options of the composite to non-circular pathways. The application of biopolyelectrolyte-surfactant complexes composed of DNA and cationic lipids as barrier coatings resolves these issues. The coatings are recoverable and closed-loop recyclable via multiple methods (e.g., dissolution or salt-triggered dissociation) by leveraging the solubility of the complexes and the reversibility of their non-covalent interactions, enabling the reuse of the base material (i.e., paper), coating (i.e., complex), and components (i.e., DNA and cationic lipid). Performance of the coating is tunable by selection of the cationic lipid structure and self-assembly behavior, yielding a range of hydrophobic/hydrophilic and oleophobic/oleophilic properties that can exceed industry requirements (e.g., Kit rating >6), as measured by standardized, industry-accepted methods. Moreover, the circular, reconfigurable design of the coating during reassembly by swapping the original cationic lipid component for another, yields fit-for-purpose coatings. The synthesis and purification of this material system follow numerous principles of green chemistry (e.g., non-hazardous synthesis, no derivatization, energy efficiency, high atom economy, and easy separation). Ultimately, mix-and-match selection of components and their reversible non-covalent interactions for assembly, disassembly, and reconfigurability presents a framework for constructing functional, sustainable, and circular platform materials.

papers.title: A Terminal Carbazole Fused Ladder Type B, N-doped Multiresonant TADF Emitter: A Strategy for Deep-Blue OLEDs
papers.abstract: Attaining precise control of emission within the blue spectral region remains inherently challenging for ladder-type π-extended multiresonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR-TADF) compounds, despite their many advantageous design features. Here, we aim to address the undesired red-shifting of the emission in ladder-type MR-TADF compounds by incorporating terminal fused carbazoles. We report two MR-TADF compounds, B2N3 and B3N3, the latter of which is a p- and n-doped heptacene polycyclic aromatic π-hydrocarbon (PAH), both of which contain fused carbazoles at both ends of the molecule. Relative to the previously reported MR-TADF compound α-3BNMes, the emission of B3N3 is blue-shifted and narrower, emitting at lPL of 427 nm and having a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 25 nm in toluene. In contrast, B2N3, which is more conformationally flexible, emits at λ PL of 441 nm and has a FWHM of 32 nm in toluene. Sensitized organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) using B2N3 and B3N3 as terminal emitters showed EQE max of 12.8 and 10.7% emitting with CIE coordinates of (0.15, 0.10) and (0.16, 0.09), respectively.

papers.title: VizChemoton: Visualization of Quantum Chemical Reaction Networks and Their Cheminformatics Features
papers.abstract: Automated explorations of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) guided by quantum chemistry (QC) calculations are undergoing rapid development that enables numerous applications. However, CRNs are accessible primarily through specialized quantum chemistry software without interface for cheminformatic exploitation of the generated data. Here, we present VizChemoton, an open-source module within the reaction exploration framework Software for Chemical Interaction Networks. VizChemoton enables visualization of CRNs and serves as an interface for cheminformatics applications based on conversion of molecular structures that accounts for radicals, zwitterions, and molecular complexes into string-based representations via RDKit mol objects. The conversion performance exceeded 90% of QC-generated compounds based on the evaluation of four CRNs constructed with density functional theory and extended tight-binding methods. We find that compounds absent from public structural databases correspond primarily to molecular complexes and unstable reaction intermediates. All essential QC and associated cheminformatics data are distributed in interoperable CSV and JSON formats to support downstream machine learning applications whereas reaction networks are readily visualized through a browser-based standalone HTML interface.

papers.title: Optimizing Three-Dimensional, π-Orbital Accessibility for Molecular Diffusion-based Photon Upconversion
papers.abstract: Achieving high-efficiency, solution-state triplet–triplet annihilation-based photon upconversion (TTA-UC) at solar equivalent intensities is fundamentally dictated by π-orbital overlap that modulates triplet dynamics during collision. However, it has been difficult to identify the optimal intermolecular geometry of planar chromophores that maximize TTA-UC performance, as this requires non-planar, three-dimensional side group engineering. Here, we systematically introduced linear alkyl chains onto sp 3 carbons of the 5,10-dihydroindeno[2,1-a]indene (DHI) skeleton to control steric hindrance in the out-of-π-plane direction and to optimize π-orbital accessibility for efficient TTA-UC. The length-dependent, solution-state study revealed that methyl groups can maximize the TTA-UC quantum yield, whereas longer n-butyl groups are required to sufficiently suppress triplet quenching. These experimental results are supported by molecular dynamics simulations showing that the alkyl chains limit parallel intermolecular geometries at proximity. Furthermore, by using a heavy-metal-free organic sensitizer with a higher absorption coefficient, the DHI system achieves an external upconversion quantum yield of over 9% under solar-equivalent 445 nm laser excitation (1.4 mW cm −2 ). These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for designing steric environments that modulate singlet and triplet dynamics, advancing the development of low-power, sunlight or indoor-light-driven upconversion applications.

papers.title: Late-stage carbonyl removal via sequential double carbon–carbon cleavage
papers.abstract: The direct removal of carbonyl groups from cyclic ketones offers a non-intuitive but rapid route to access multi-substituted saturated structural motifs via late-stage modification. However, such transformations have been challenging to achieve, especially in a chemoselective manner. Here we report reductive and annulative carbonyl removal methods, enabled by N′-alkyl hydrazonamide (NAHA) reagents, via sequential double C–C bond cleavage. These transformations efficiently convert diverse cyclic ketones to the corresponding ring-opened and ring-contracted analogues with broad functional group tolerance. Besides late-stage modification of complex bioactive compounds, this carbonyl-removal strategy can also be applied to the synthesis of all-carbon quaternary centers lacking polar functional groups, terminal deuteration, and iterative ring contraction.

papers.title: Flexi-GIST: Solvation Thermodynamic Decomposition and Mapping for Flexible Molecules
papers.abstract: Solvation mapping methods provide spatially resolved estimates of solvent thermodynamic quantities but are formally restricted to rigid representations of molecular systems. This restriction limits their applicability to biologically relevant molecules, for which conformational flexibility can significantly influence both solvation free energies and the spatial distribution of solvent thermodynamics. Although the underlying statistical mechanical formalism has been defined for flexible systems, its direct evaluation requires an ensemble average over solute configurations and is computationally intractable for all but the simplest systems. As a result, solvation mapping is typically applied to only a single rigid solute conformation. To address this limitation, we present Flexi-GIST, an extension of Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory (GIST) that enables spatially decomposed solvation thermodynamics estimates for flexible molecules. Flexi-GIST approximates the formally exact ensemble average over solute configurations by clustering them and evaluating GIST on representative conformations for each cluster. The representative solvation thermodynamic estimates are then combined to approximate the thermodynamics of solvating the flexible molecule. Solute configurational entropy contributions are accounted for using a nearest-neighbor entropy estimator with a truncated mutual information expansion. We validated the Flexi-GIST methodology on a set of flexible small molecules in explicit solvent. Solvation free energies obtained by spatial integration of solvation maps are compared to values computed using thermodynamic integration of flexible solutes, demonstrating agreement between the two methods. This framework extends solvation mapping to flexible molecular systems and provides a basis for estimating spatially resolved solvation thermodynamics in cases where rigid representations are insufficient.

papers.title: Photoexcited-nitroarene/nickel-dual catalysis for scalable and direct C(sp3)-C cross-coupling in flow
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) offers a sustainable avenue for unlocking the synthetic potential of native C(sp3)-H bonds. However, the highly regioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) linkages from ubiquitous hydrocarbon feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we introduce a metallaphotoredox platform that leverages simple, commercially available nitroarenes as unique HAT photocatalysts, exploiting their highly electrophilic oxygen-centered diradical excited states for selective C(sp3)-H cleavage. Merged with nickel catalysis, this approach enables the direct and efficient construction of C(sp3)-C(sp2) and challenging C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds from unactivated hydrocarbons. The practicality of this protocol is highlighted by rapid reaction kinetics, a broad substrate scope and excellent scalability to achieve 100-mmol synthesis by its implementation in continuous-flow mode. Detailed mechanistic and computational investigations reveal that the triplet nitroarene functions as a potent oxygen-centered diradical, facilitating a regioselective C(sp3)-H abstraction that seamlessly intercepts the nickel catalytic cycle to accomplish the crosscoupling.

papers.title: Reactions of Terminal Olefins with Iron Carbenes
papers.abstract: The application of sustainable, earth-abundant iron complexes to the olefin metathesis of terminal olefins remains a formidable challenge due to competitive, metathesis-divergent deactivation pathways. Herein, we investigate the reactivity of a pincer-supported iron carbene complex and its derivatives toward various linear and terminal olefins. Reactions with styrene, ethylene, or 2vinylanisole under ambient conditions proceed through 2π+2π cycloadditions to generate transient metallacyclobutane intermediates that rapidly undergo metathesis-divergent b-hydride elimination to yield stable iron allyl hydride complexes. The addition of benzonitrile to iron allyl hydride complexes demonstrates a unique hydride transfer from the iron center to the nitrile carbon, yielding a paramagnetic terminal imide complex. Conversely, reactions with the sterically demanding 1,1-disubstituted olefin, a-methylstyrene, successfully suppress b-hydride elimination. Heating this mixture induces a 2π+2π cycloaddition followed by cycloreversion and a subsequent 1,2-hydride shift rearrangement, resulting in productive, albeit low-yield, metathesis to generate a paramagnetic side-bound iron olefin complex.

papers.title: Breaking Good: a curriculum-aligned citizen science approach to developing new treatments for mycetoma
papers.abstract: Participation in open source and citizen science projects provides students with the opportunity to be involved in solving real world problems. These approaches provide authentic learning experiences which help develop students' understanding of the role that science plays in society, deepen engagement, and increase motivation. Open Source Mycetoma is a project that enables open, community participation in the search for novel medicines for mycetoma, a neglected tropical disease. In this article, we share a two-day curriculum-aligned program, developed as part of The Breaking Good Initiative, in which high school students (Year 11 and 12) synthesize and analyze (IR, NMR, MS, and HPLC) new drug candidates for a structure/activity relationship (SAR) study, as part of Open Source Mycetoma. The program develops students’ scientific understanding in synthetic chemistry, and explores fundamental questions concerning the nature of science and scientific inquiry, across two facilitated workshops. The workshops can also be adapted for other contexts, including undergraduate laboratory programs; delivering learning outcomes that include practical laboratory skills, organic synthesis, and compound characterization.

papers.title: Modeling the Effects of Fermi Resonances in the CH Stretching Region of the Spectra for Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Anions
papers.abstract: A strategy is developed for evaluating spectra of anions of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) molecules. The high symmetry of these systems and the similarity of the frequencies of the CH wagging and ring distortion vibrations result in normal modes that are highly mixed in character. This results in extensive mixing among the nearly degenerate states with energies in the 2600 to 3200 cm -1 region of the spectrum. When we generate vibrational modes that resemble localized CH stretching, CH wagging or ring distortion vibrations from linear combinations of the normal modes we find that the 2:1 Fermi resonances that couple the states with two quanta of excitation in the CH wagging vibration and one quantum of excitation in the corresponding CH stretching vibration are an order of magnitude or more larger than all of the other terms that couple these nearly degenerate states. The Fermi resonance coupling terms are evaluated for polar and Cartesian representations of the displacements of the hydrogen atom in the plane molecule for the anions of anthracene, pyrene, perylene and fluroanthene. We find the Fermi coupling constants to be nearly constant across all of the the CH bonds in these four ions, with values of 125 and 62 cm -1 for the Cartesian and polar representations of the Hamiltonian, respectively. When the polar coordinate representation of the displacements of the hydrogen atoms is used, the leading contribution to the Fermi coupling constant can be traced to the kinetic term in the Hamiltonian that involves the momentum of the wagging vibration, where the leading contribution to the effective mass is the moment of inertia of the CH bond. Using a Fermi coupling constant 62 cm1, along with a transferrable model for the anharmonicity of the states in this energy range with one ar two quanta of excitation, we can reproduce the recently reported spectra of these anions.

papers.title: Near-Critical Supercritical CO2 Desiccation of TKO Porcine Red Blood Cells: A Proposed Protocol with Hemolysis Reduction Pathway Analysis for Ambient-Temperature Xenogeneic Blood Preservation
papers.abstract: Genetically engineered triple-knockout (TKO) porcine red blood cells (pRBCs) — with GGTA1, beta4GalNT2, and CMAH antigens eliminated and human CD47 and CD55 transgenes expressed under erythroid-specific promoters— represent the most clinically advanced xenogeneic RBC candidate to date. However, no ambient-temperature preservation method exists for TKO pRBCs, and all current protocols require cold-chain storage identical to donated human RBC. The principal barrier to desiccation-based preservation is post-rehydration hemolysis: the best published lyophilization result achieves approximately 8% hemolysis — tenfold above the WHO transfusion limit of 0.8%. Here we propose a near-critical supercritical CO2 (scCO2) desiccation protocol operating at 74–80 bar and 31–35°C — conditions approaching the CO2 critical point (Tc = 31.1°C, Pc = 73.8 bar) — where near-zero surface tension is achieved while membrane permeabilization is minimised relative to conventional high-pressure scCO2. We identify a five-component add-process stack — antioxidant coating (rosmarinic acid and ascorbic acid), N2 inert atmosphere, mixed CO2/N2 atmosphere (70:30), controlled rehydration, and Dextran-40 rehydration medium — predicted to multiplicatively reduce hemolysis toward the WHO threshold. Additionally, a GPI-anchored protein reinsertion step via lipid vesicle carrier at rehydration is proposed to restore CD47 and CD55 surface expression lost during desiccation. A structured validation roadmap is provided. This document constitutes a public prior art disclosure under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Antibody-Mediated Recognition of Chiral Poly(2-oxazoline) Nanorods Driven by Enantioselectivity
papers.abstract: Chirality critically governs the pharmacodynamics and clinical performance of small molecule drugs, yet its role in governing bio-nano interactions of synthetic polymeric nanocarriers has remained largely unexplored. Surface grafting with hydrophilic, biocompatible “stealth” polymers such as poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) is a critical design strategy for nanomedicines intended to reduce nonspecific biological interactions and achieve prolonged circulation. However, the rising prevalence of anti‑PEG antibodies has driven the search for fundamentally new design principles, mostly focused on substituting PEG with an entirely different polymer type. Poly(2-oxazoline)s (POx) constitute a versatile class of biocompatible synthetic polymers that uniquely enable access to numerous water-soluble macromolecules that can be rendered chiral, an attribute rarely accessible in synthetic stealth polymers. Here, we report the fabrication of crystalline-core nanorods bearing a chiral poly(2,4-dimethyl-2-oxazoline) (PdMeOx) corona via crystallisation-driven self-assembly (CDSA), and examine the influence of polymer chirality on biodistribution and antibody recognition in vivo. Well-defined enantiopure and racemic PdMeOx‑b‑poly(2‑(isopropyl)‑2‑oxazoline) block copolymers were synthesised and assembled into short nanorods with distinct optical activities, enabling a detailed investigation of chirality-dependent bio–nano interactions. We demonstrate that polymer chirality induces the generation of enantiomer-specific antibodies, an effect that has not previously been reported for synthetic macromolecular nanomaterials. These findings reveal stereochemistry as an orthogonal design parameter for modulating immune interactions and suggest a future strategy in which alternating polymer chirality, rather than changing polymer type, can be exploited to mitigate antibody-mediated clearance through structured dosing regimens.

papers.title: A Semi-Empirical Quantum-Mechanical Evaluation of Matrix Hamiltonian Perturbations in Fungal Cell Wall Degradation
papers.abstract: This short communication provides a rigorous numerical instantiation of a previously formulated quantum-mechanical framework modeling the biocide activity against Venturia inaequalis. By integrating empirical spectral parameters into a localized secular determinant, we quantify the groundstate energies of vital host matrices and map their transition-state destabilization. The catalytic action of biocontrol agents is modeled through an effective, shielded Yukawa-like interaction Hamiltonian, showing how electronic delocalization drives the macroscopic collapse of the pathogen’s cell wall.

papers.title: Programmable Access to α-Quaternary Ketones and Aldehydes via Stereodefined β-Oxy Vinylbenziodoxoles
papers.abstract: Fully substituted acyclic enolates are valuable intermediates for the enantioselective construction of α-quaternary carbonyl compounds, yet reliable control of enolate geometry—particularly for aldehydes—remains difficult under conventional deprotonation conditions. β-Oxy vinylbenziodoxoles (VBXs), accessible through two complementary pathways, provide stereodefined acyclic enolate precursors that retain alkene geometry through subsequent cross-coupling and carbonate formation. These VBXs undergo configuration-retentive Sonogashira coupling, enabling modular installation of alkynyl substituents. Subsequent conversion to allyl enol carbonates furnishes ketone- and aldehydetype enolate surrogates with defined E / Z configuration. Under Pd/Trost-ligand conditions, these carbonates participate in enantioselective decarboxylative allylic alkylation to deliver αquaternary ketones and aldehydes in high yield and enantioselectivity. The decisive role of enolate geometry is demonstrated by the opposite sense of asymmetric induction for E - and Z -isomers of the carbonate precursor. The resulting alkynyl-substituted products are readily diversified through manipulation of the allyl, alkynyl, and carbonyl groups.

papers.title: Wafer-scale heteroepitaxy of Sn-alloyed ε-Ga2O3 on sapphire via low-pressure Mist-CVD
papers.abstract: The industrial deployment of metastable ε-Ga 2 O 3 on sapphire is currently impeded by intrinsic crystallographic incompatibility and the difficulty of achieving macroscopic homogeneity via solution-based growth techniques. Here, we present a Sn-mediated lattice engineering approach to resolve these limitations using a scalable low-pressure Mist-CVD system. Beyond its conventional role as a dopant, we demonstrate that heavy Sn alloying effectively modulates the cation sublattice, promoting the randomization within the Pna2 1 rotational domains and reducing the overall symmetry of the orthorhombic framework. This symmetry regulation significantly mitigates the lattice misfit with the substrate reducing the (004) X-ray rocking curve FWHM to 0.045° (162 arcsec). TEM investigations indicate a rapid lattice recovery mechanism, where initial interfacial disorder is effectively suppressed within a few nanometers. Furthermore, we demonstrated highly consistent wafer-level growth, realizing a thickness deviation of merely ~2 nm across a 2-inch wafer for a ~60 nm thick epitaxial film. This work identifies Sn-alloyed ε-Ga 2 O 3 as a versatile and high-fidelity template, offering a simplified single-source route for the scalable manufacturing of next-generation power electronics.

papers.title: Analysis of Stress Evolution in Lithium Metal Anodes During Plating and Stripping Cycles
papers.abstract: Liquid cell batteries with lithium metal anodes may exhibit degraded Coulombic efficiency, due to plating of non-compact deposits consisting of whiskers. Experiments show that whisker growth is driven by compressive stress arising from metal-phase diffusion of deposited atoms. In situ wafer curvature measurements can reveal the dynamic stress response due to diffusion, but their interpretation is complicated by the unknown and changing deposit porosity. Here, a modeling approach is introduced that enables fitting of curvature transients during cycling to characterize the evolution of the diffusion and mechanical response of the lithium film. The analysis is based on metal-phase diffusion accommodated by elastic deformation and power-law creep, and circumvents the unknown microstructure of the film by focusing on open-circuit intervals during cycling. It is shown that curvature changes during plating cycles are caused by diffusion-induced compressive stress. Curvature increases during stripping periods are due to near-surface tensile stress in the metal, consistent with experimental observations of submicron near-surface voids.

papers.title: Millisecond-resolved X-ray spectroscopy observation of transient ligand-coordinated Pd0 complex for Pd nucleation
papers.abstract: The role of metal-ligand intermediates in nanoparticle synthesis remains largely unexplored, yet it is invaluable for the synthesis of high-performance functional nanomaterials. Understanding these complex systems requires highly time-resolved, in situ experimental observations. In this study, we investigate cetyltrimethylammonium chloride-capped Pd reduction as a model for ligand-mediated nanoparticle formation, using 500-millisecond resolution in situ X-ray spectroscopy. The reduction rates of Pd 2+ are determined to be (1.8–3.9) × 10 -5 M s -1 across temperatures ranging from 30 to 60°C, with an activation energy of 22.59 kJ mol -1 . We identify a transient chlorine-coordinated Pd 0 complex (Pd 0 -Cl) as the nucleation and growth-determining species, which fits well with a population-balanced precipitation growth model. By adjusting the reaction conditions, we demonstrate the ability to speed up or even bypass specific growth stages, providing experimental kinetic control over the process. These high-resolution measurements of growth rates are essential for advancing the rational design and synthesis of nanomaterials, offering valuable insights into controlling nanoparticle formation through metal-ligand interactions.

papers.title: Barrel aging gins: A chemical and kinetic analysis of flavor and color development
papers.abstract: Barrel-aging has long been used to alter the flavors of spirits. For gins, however, barrel-aging is a relatively new process. While spirit aging has been studied in detail, the effect of barrels on the delicate flavors of gin, and the balance of these flavors with those extracted from a barrel, has yet to be studied. In this manuscript we evaluate several, relevant, chemical processes that occur when aging gin in new, charred, American oak barrels. We observe phenolic compounds being extracted with kinetics that can be described by a modified intraparticle diffusion model. We observe much more complex dynamics for both gin and barrel derived aroma compounds, suggesting the presence of multiple chemical processes for these molecules within the barrel. We generate a flavor wheel for barrel aged gin and use this, along with GC-MS data, to give context to flavor development over the course of aging. This study elucidates some of the key chemical mechanisms that control flavor development in barrel aged gins. Because of the nuance required by the craft of producing gin, we expect more detailed studies will follow ours.

papers.title: Synergy-Guided Molecular Editing for Synthetically Feasible Conversion of P-glycoprotein Substrates to Non-Substrates
papers.abstract: Drug efflux mediated by P-glycoprotein (P-gp) remains a major barrier to effective small-molecule therapeutics, limiting both bioavailability and central nervous system exposure. While machine learning models can predict P-gp substrates, translating these predictions into actionable molecular design remains largely unexplored, particularly in enabling the rational conversion of substrates into non-substrates to mitigate efflux liability. Here, we introduce the synergistic fragment genetic algorithm (SF-GA), a computational framework that transforms predictive insight into an interpretable molecular design strategy. By integrating fragment synergy analysis into the mutation stage of a genetic algorithm, SF-GA biases fragment replacement toward co-occurring substructures associated with non-substrate classification, thereby enabling chemically interpretable and property-directed molecular optimization. Compared to conventional genetic algorithms, SF-GA exhibits faster convergence, greater structural diversity, and improved synthetic accessibility, with ablation studies confirming the central role of synergy-guided mutation. The method supports both scaffold-preserving peripheral editing and skeletal editing, converting P-gp substrates into non-substrates within one to two generations while maintaining a traceable rationale for each transformation.

papers.title: Chemically Auditable Failure Atlases for Trustworthy MOF Adsorption Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models are now widely used to rank metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for gas adsorption, but an attractive global error does not reveal whether a specific pore regime, topology family or chemistry class can be trusted during screening. Here we introduce an interpretable failure-atlas workflow that converts standard tabular adsorption predictions into chemically auditable maps of local error, rank instability, model disagreement and descriptor-space novelty. Using a strict common cohort of 263,735 computation-ready MOF structures from the merged adsorption–descriptor table, we analyse CO2 uptake at 0.015 and 0.15 bar and CH4 uptake at 5.8 and 65 bar with ridge regression, random forests and histogram gradient boosting. Random forests give the best global accuracy for all four targets, with MAE values of 0.057, 0.256, 0.444 and 0.628 mmol g−1, respectively, and high-pressure methane reaches R2 = 0.984 and Spearman ρ = 0.992. The failure atlases show why those averages are insufficient. For the primary dilute-capture target, CO2 at 0.15 bar, HGB has a global MAE of 0.286 mmol g−1, yet local error rises to 0.670 mmol g−1 in high-density frameworks, 0.796 mmol g−1 in ultramicroporous/high-constriction pores and 1.233 mmol g−1 in the small-pore subset, where 45.5% of elite candidates are misclassified. Trust maps further identify unstable regions, including moc topologies and constricted ultramicropores, where model choice materially changes the prediction. The resulting atlases provide a reproducible diagnostic layer between model benchmarking and materials decision-making: they identify where fast ML ranking is defensible and where richer descriptors, targeted simulation or experimental validation are required.

papers.title: Increased Secondary Coordination Sphere Acidity Lowers the Barrier to Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction and Suppresses H2 Evolution
papers.abstract: A limited number of reports have investigated how protic secondary coordination sphere (SCS) groups alter the selectivity of electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction catalysed by iron tetraphenylporphyrin (FeTPP) derivatives. We previously reported a series of FeTPP‐based isomers bearing SCS amides at varying positions around the porphyrin core and showed that CO:H 2 selectivity depends on SCS amide positioning. The present work builds on this precedent by evaluating the influence of SCS amide p K a (p K a = 23.8–26.2 in MeCN) on CO:H 2 selectivity in the presence of exogenous 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl) phenol (p K a = 23.8). The most acidic SCS groups enable a high faradaic efficiency (FE) towards CO (FE CO ≥ 81%) while inhibiting H 2 evolution (FE H2 ≤ 7%), while the least acidic SCS affords poor CO selectivity (FE CO = 45 ± 3%) and increased H 2 evolution (FE H2 = 35 ± 10%). Fast scan rate cyclic voltammetry experiments and catalytic plateau currents were used to extract kinetic parameters and equilibrium constants for the competing CO and H 2 evolution pathways. A Brønsted analysis shows that increasing SCS acidity lowers the kinetic barrier for CO 2 reduction (Brønsted α = 0.4 ± 0.1), but the barriers to H 2 evolution are insensitive to changes in SCS acidity (α ≈ 0). Accordingly, our kinetic and thermochemical data suggest that CO:H 2 selectivity is governed by the relative barrier heights of the rate-limiting steps for each pathway. Collectively, these results demonstrate how tuning SCS p K a can improve CO 2 reduction selectivity and mitigate undesirable H 2 evolution.

papers.title: Synthesis of poly(a-aminoketones) through Pdcatalyzed Csp3–Csp3 cleavage of azetidinol monomers
papers.abstract: Herein we describe a synthetic route to poly(aminoketones) based on the Pd-catalyzed C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bond cleavage of N -protected 3-azetidinol monomers containing a haloaryl group. The reactivity of the azetidinols was sensitive to the nature of the N -protecting 2 group. Thus, substrates with N -tert-butyloxycarbonyl or -phenyl polymerized in the presence of catalytic amounts of Pd(OAc) 2 and PPh 3 to give the corresponding poly(aminoketones) in moderate to good yields, whereas the N -tosyl, -benzoyl or -acetyl substrates were unproductive. Azetidinols containing the linkers 1,4- or 1,3-phenylene, 9,9-dimethyl-2,7fluorenylene or 4,4'-biphenylene between the two reactive sites of the monomer (azetidinol and halogen) gave polymers containing these moieties in the polymeric chain. Furthermore, the organometallic nature of the mechanism was confirmed by the isolation and characterization of an aryl–Pd(II) catalytic intermediate. This methodology represents a complementary strategy to classic polyamine synthesis via cationic or anionic ring-opening polymerization of azaheterocycles, which allows the inclusion of different arylene linkers in the polymer main chain. Among the groups evaluated, the Boc group provides the most favorable reactivity while also allowing facile deprotection to afford polyammonium salts of potential biotechnological interest.

papers.title: Impact of Chronic Micro-Particulate Exposure on Enamel Microhardness: an in vitro Simulation of Dust-Induced Enamel Fatigue
papers.abstract: Objectives: Heavy-industry workers are chronically exposed to airborne micro-particulate dust generated by drilling, excavation, and mineral fragmentation. While respiratory consequences are well documented, the long-term effects of repeated dust exposure on dental enamel remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether chronic exposure to industry-derived micro-particulates reduces enamel microhardness under simulated occupational conditions. Methods: Commercial hydroxyapatite-enamel analog discs (n = 60) were exposed to cyclic suspensions of standardized industrial dust particles composed primarily of silica, iron oxide, graphite, and aluminosilicates. Samples were divided into four groups: Control, Low Exposure, Moderate Exposure, and High Exposure. Exposure cycles simulated 1 year, 5 years, and 10 years of occupational particulate accumulation using repeated abrasive sedimentation and dehydration-rehydration phases. Surface microhardness was assessed using Vickers microindentation. Surface morphology and microcrack formation were evaluated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Results: Progressive reductions in enamel microhardness were observed with increasing particulate exposure intensity and duration. High Exposure samples demonstrated a 31.8% reduction in Vickers hardness compared to controls (p < 0.001). SEM analysis revealed increasing surface pitting, erosive grooves, and microfracture propagation correlated with particle concentration. Clinical Significance: Chronic exposure to airborne industrial micro-particulates may contribute to progressive enamel weakening through cumulative abrasive and dehydration-mediated mechanisms. These findings suggest occupational dust exposure could represent an underrecognized risk factor for accelerated enamel fatigue in industrial workers.

papers.title: Entropy in materials design: Modelling entropic stabilisation of crystalline materials
papers.abstract: Computational materials design promises to accelerate discovery of new materials with tailored properties. Besides predicting their properties, it is paramount to assess whether candidate materials are stable and possible to synthesise. However, most high-throughput computational studies predict stability based on internal energies calculated from density functional theory, neglecting the effects of entropy. This has recently led to disappointments as materials predicted to be stable in ordered, crystalline structures were found to be disordered when synthesised. Methods for modelling entropic stabilisation of materials have been known for decades, but until recently only feasible for the simplest materials. Developments in computational hardware, materials databases and machine learning methods are now pushing this frontier, making materials modelling at finite temperature accessible for increasingly complex materials at the scales needed for materials design. Here, we highlight the fundamental theories for modelling entropic stabilisation, their realisation as computational methods, as well as recent applications of entropic modelling in complex materials and efforts towards its integration in high-throughput computational materials design. We conclude that time is ripe for a tighter integration of finite temperature modelling in computational materials design, and propose near term developments needed to realise its full potential.

papers.title: Chirality-induced spin polarization: Some fundamental ingredients
papers.abstract: This paper examines some fundamental ingredients that produce enantiomerspecific spin-polarization in chiral systems, leading to chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). In particular, it examines parity and time-reversal symmetries of the key quantities, such as linear and angular momenta and spin. Enantiomer-specific spinpolarization emerges because of the symmetry relationship between the two mirror images that results in different transformation properties for axial and polar vectors. It is best described by pseudoscalars. The analysis of the structure of the spin–orbit coupling (SOC) operator shows that the chirality of the system enters the picture via the shapes of molecular orbitals, which are determined by (electrostatic) molecular field. The spin–orbit operator detects the handedness of the orbitals and reports on it by the phase of the individual matrix elements. This explains how a local operator can sense the effect of a distant molecular field. Symmetry of the SOC also explains different electronic population dynamics observed in chiral and non-chiral molecules. Drawing from the field of molecular magnetism, we connect spin-polarization with magnetic anisotropy and show that the latter is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for the former. The anisotropy requires a non-zero expectation value of the angular momentum operator in the spin–orbit-perturbed states and lifting electronic degeneracy within the multiplet. Formal theoretical analysis is supplemented by numerical examples.

papers.title: Modulated Catalyst Reactivity Precludes Slow Carbene Addition in Azetidine-to-Pyrrolidine Ring Expansions
papers.abstract: Nitrogen heterocycles are frequently found in pharmaceuticals, natural products, pesticides, and other bioactive molecules. Among these, five-membered Nheterocycles appear in 39% of FDA-approved drugs, with pyrrolidines specifically accounting for nearly 15%. Reliable methods to access stereochemical- and functional group-diverse high-Fsp3 pyrrolidines without the need for extensive pre-functionalization or harsh reaction conditions are attractive. The reaction of azetidines with donor-acceptor carbene precursors in the presence of a Rh catalyst generates azetidinium ylides, reactive intermediates which undergo selective ring expansion to furnish high Fsp3 pyrrolidine scaffolds. The method is mild, operationally simple, requires no slow addition of the carbene precursor, displays good functional group tolerance and provides rapid access to functional group-rich N-arylpyrrolidines. These products can be further diversified to construct complex, drug-like pyrrolidines. Mechanistic studies were conducted to understand the role of N-substitution and inconsequential slow addition of the carbene precursor, insights that will inform future method development.

papers.title: Red-Light-Driven Photo(electro)catalysis in Perovskite Nanocrystal@Donor-Chromophore-Acceptor Hybrids through Trap-Mediated Exciton Generation and Surface Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: Harvesting low energy photons to drive chemical transformations remains a key challenge in light-to-chemical energy conversion. Herein, we report CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals functionalized with a donor-chromophore-acceptor (DCA) Cu(I)-bisdiimine complex that facilitates directional interfacial charge transfer. Under low power density (5 mW cm -2 ) red light photoexcitation (λ ex = 650-670 nm), well below the bandgap energy, pristine CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals exhibit photoluminescence arising from trap-mediated sequential multiphoton excitation, as supported by a nonlinear power dependence (n = 2.5), effectively generating band edge excitons under subbandgap continuous wave illumination. Upon functionalization with the DCA, this emission is quenched while the structural characteristics of the nanocrystals are maintained, suggesting that that surface attached DCA induces exciton extraction. This interfacial charge transfer was partially confirmed through photoelectrochemistry where DCA-functionalized nanocrystals adsorbed onto TiO 2 yielded photoelectrodes that show measurable photocurrent (0.5 μA cm -2 ) under red light photoirradiation. Furthermore, this hybrid material was successfully used as a photocatalyst for styrene photopolymerization (29% isolated yield after 48 hours) under the same low power density red light. These findings open the door for the use of metal halide perovskite nanocrystals as low energy, red light photocatalysts.

papers.title: Hydrogen-Bond Scalar Couplings as Covalency-Sensitive NMR Fingerprints of Amorphous Ice
papers.abstract: Through-hydrogen-bond scalar couplings are attractive NMR observables because they connect high-precision spectroscopy with local hydrogen-bond structure. It is less clear whether they can also report hydrogen-bond covalency in amorphous ice and other frozen or heterogeneous aqueous environments. Here we combine ab initio molecular dynamics configurations of water, density-functional response calculations of indirect nuclear spin–spin couplings, and absolutely localized molecular orbital (ALMO) energydecomposition analysis. Benchmark calculations against SOPPA(CCSD) water-dimer references validate BLYP/pcJ-1 for the through-hydrogen-bond 1hJO−H coupling. The coupling is dominated by the Fermi-contact term and therefore follows an approximately exponential distance dependence, but ensemble and vibrational averaging prevent a transferable one-dimensional distance ruler. Extending earlier NMR/ALMO work on liquid water, 1hJO−H correlates with ALMO charge-transfer stabilization and charge-transfer amount. Thus 1hJO−H is an experimentally accessible, covalencysensitive fingerprint of hydrogen bonds, provided that geometry and ensemble effects are included explicitly.

papers.title: Ordered interfacial assembly of rough microellipsoids
papers.abstract: Dense, orientationally and translationally ordered, two-dimensional (2D) monolayers of colloidal ellipsoids are fabricated at air-water interfaces. Kinetic arrest and disordered structures from long-range quadrupolar capillary attraction are overcome by synthesizing polystyrene microellipsoids with surface roughness, specifically nanoscale concavities, which attenuate capillary attraction. With increasing area fraction, the particle assembly shows a disorder-order transition from isotropic to plastic crystal at low ellipsoid aspect ratio (AR) and an isotropic to nematic transition at high AR, agreeing qualitatively with simulated hard ellipse close-packing in 2D. The ordered particle assembly is successfully transferred to solid substrates via Langmuir-Blodgett deposition, demonstrating the potential of surface roughness to create anisotropically ordered 2D patterns via interfacial templating.

papers.title: The water-soluble [60]fullerene derivatives as binders of SARS-CoV-2 proteins
papers.abstract: Water-soluble fullerene derivatives represent emerging molecular nanomaterials for antiviral drug discovery, yet their target selectivity against SARS-CoV-2 proteins remains insufficiently defined. Here, four functionalized [60]fullerenes, C60(OH)24, C60ser, C60ALA, and C60Trp, were evaluated as binders of key SARS-CoV-2 targets involved in viral entry and replication: spike glycoprotein, papain-like protease, 3CL main protease, and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Microscale thermophoresis revealed distinct target-dependent binding profiles governed by fullerene functionalization. The C60Trp fullerene was the most active derivative, binding Spike with nanomolar affinity (Kd = 94.8 nM) and showing micromolar affinity toward papain-like protease and 3CL main protease. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported the preferential interaction of C60Trp with the spike protein cavity through combined fullerene cage complementarity and polar interactions with lysine and arginine residues. The tested derivatives showed low cytotoxicity in A549 cells, and C60Trp was efficiently internalized. These findings identify tryptophan-functionalized [60]fullerene as a promising multivalent scaffold for SARS-CoV-2 protein targeting.

papers.title: Redox tuning and protonation control of peroxidase catalytic regimes in engineered heme protein active sites
papers.abstract: Designer metalloenzymes emerge as versatile catalysts capable of expanding the scope of natural catalytic reactions. The first- and second-coordination sphere of a metal active site are known to modulate catalytic activity, yet models connecting structural properties to physical parameters governing catalysis are scarce. Here, we examine to which extent tuning of the heme redox potential and protonation of residues within the enzymatic pocket govern peroxidase activity. To this end, we employ the Hexameric Tyrosine-coordinated heme protein (HTHP) as a model in which the native Tyr axial coordination is replaced by His, Cys or Met, as confirmed by resonance Raman spectroscopy and crystallography for selected variants. These modifications alter the Fe3+/Fe2+ redox potential by a span of ca. 290 mV, as determined by UV-Vis spectro-electrochemistry, corresponding to ca. 40 % of the accessible range for globular α-helical heme b cytochromes. Analysis of peroxidase activity across a broad pH range reveals two distinct catalytic regimes. At alkaline pH, increasing the driving force for proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) from Compound I to Compound II leads to decreased catalytic activity, qualitatively consistent with the Marcus inverted region. In contrast, at lower pH values, catalytic turnover is dominated by protonation events within the distal heme pocket, indicating a shift from driving-force controlled to protonationcontrolled reactivity.

papers.title: Nickel K-edge XANES studies on Pyridinophane-supported Coordination Complexes
papers.abstract: * mirica@illinois.edu Keywords: Nickel, oxidation state, multidentate ligands, XAS, XANES, K-edge ABSTRACT: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a powerful technique to identify the electronic and geometric structure surrounding a specific element and is of growing interest for the characterization of homogeneous organometallic compounds, especially for sensitive and highly reactive in-situ species. In this study, we performed a systematic, quantitative analysis of the rising Ni K-edge for a series of 25 pyridinophane-supported compounds by fitting the K-edge to the relevant 1s to 4p transitions. We observe how ligand substitution, oxidation state, and variable binding modes have a direct effect on the energy and shape of the Ni K-edge as they affect Ni bond distances and p-orbital symmetry. By leveraging the flexible denticity of pyridinophane ligands, we quantify the variable solution-phase binding mode of previously ambiguous structures. This study helps establish using the intense, rising Ni K-edge to monitor in-situ reactivity and to characterize coordination environments of Ni catalysts using only 1-2 scans.

papers.title: Synthesis of siccanin by computational subtarget selection
papers.abstract: The species-selective SDH inhibitor siccanin presents unique opportunities for therapeutic development but suffers from poor physiochemical properties and challenging chemical problems. Here we report an approach to its synthesis that quickly intercepts its unusually hindered cis- syn -cis drimane core, i.e. its local chemical space. Computation helps rationalize and predict reactivity, especially conformational preferences, configurational outcomes and the reactivity of a key O -centered radical.

papers.title: H-Phosphonate-Promoted Activation of Alcohols to give 1°, 2° and 3° Iodides; Utilisation of Both Atoms in I2
papers.abstract: Herein we report an atom economic route to alkyl iodide synthesis via H-phosphonate promoted alcohol activation. The methodology can be applied broadly to 1°, 2°, 3°, benzylic and other alcohols in very good yields. A less wasteful route from raw materials is utilised and both atoms of I2 are incorporated in the halogenation process. A mechanism is proposed, evidenced by NMR studies. Finally, green metric calculations show the methodology exceeds benchmark procedures.

papers.title: Giant Band Gap Renormalization Dictates Current–Voltage Behavior of 2D Semiconductor Electrodes
papers.abstract: Electrochemical and electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors rely on current flow across atomically thin interfaces. Existing models used to describe current–voltage (J-V) behavior were developed for bulk semiconductors and generally neglect giant band gap renormalization (BGR), 1–3 a defining property of 2D semiconductors in which the electronic band gap (E g ) changes strongly (>0.5 eV) with carrier concentration (n). 4–6 Because E g determines the energy-level alignment at semiconductor interfaces, BGR should fundamentally alter interfacial current flow. However, directly measuring BGR under operating device conditions has remained experimentally challenging, leaving its impact on 2 electrochemical and solid-state device behavior unknown. Here we show that giant BGR governs the J–V behavior of monolayer (ML) MoS ₂ electrodes at electrochemical interfaces by reducing the energy-level overlap between semiconductor and molecular acceptor states, suppressing the interfacial electron-transfer rate constant (kₑₜ) by an order of magnitude. Using in situ spectroelectrochemistry and many-body theory, we find that E g changes by >0.2 eV with n over a 400 mV electrochemical potential window. Across independently prepared ML-MoS ₂ electrodes, variations in n produce a continuum of electrochemical responses ranging from reversible to irreversible behavior. These results establish BGR as a governing parameter in 2D semiconductor electrochemistry, provide a framework for accessing the Marcus inverted regime in (photo)electrocatalytic and voltage-tunable sensing applications, 7–10 and suggest that BGR may contribute more broadly to device-to-device variability in 2D electronics, including threshold-voltage variations in field-effect transistors. 11–15

papers.title: HiMac: High-Throughput Initialization of Multidentate Adsorption Configurations for Geometry Relaxation and Transition-State Searches
papers.abstract: High-throughput computation is essential for the rational design of heterogeneous catalysts, and the quality of initial adsorption configurations directly determines the efficiency and success rate of subsequent geometry optimization. Existing heuristic methods are constrained by rigid-body approximations, which makes them difficult to handle complex multidentate adsorption, and the low-precision force-field correction schemes they rely on lack generality. To address this issue, this work proposes a general algorithm, High-Throughput Initialization of Multidentate Adsorption Configurations (HiMac). The algorithm reformulates configuration generation as a multi-objective optimization problem. It employs forward kinematics to model molecular flexibility and combines it with a loss function based on parent molecule similarity, thereby unifying site selection with pose adjustment. A statistical learning module is further integrated to prioritize the exploration of chemically favorable sites and reduce computational cost. Experiments show that HiMac generates high quality initial configurations for geometry relaxation and transition-state searches, applies to arbitrary adsorbate-surface systems, and provides a general and efficient method to accelerate the rational design of heterogeneous catalysts.

papers.title: Binding Affinity Determines the Success of Endogenous CuII–NTA Spin Labelling for In-Cell EPR Distance Measurements
papers.abstract: In-cell electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy requires robust spin-labelling strategies compatible with cellular conditions. Cu II -NTA coordination to genetically engineered double-histidine (dHis) motifs has shown promise for endogenous labelling in E. coli . Here, we evaluated the effect of varying Cu II -NTA affinity on the success of these experiments. Relaxation induced dipolar modulation enhancement (RIDME)-based titrations revealed dissociation constants ( K d ) in the 10 -6 and 10 -8 range for two different β-sheet i and i+2 dHis sites. In-cell EPR spectra demonstrated that the persistence of the Cu II EPR signal correlates with these binding affinities. The success of in-cell pulsed electron-electron double resonance (PELDOR) involving both β-sheet sites and a high-affinity α-helical site depended on the site; the higher-affinity site yielded analyzable results, the lower-affinity site did not. These results highlight the critical importance of low K d binding sites for reliable in-cell distance measurements with endogenous Cu II -NTA labelling and the substantial sensitivity gain offered by RIDME experiments.

papers.title: Charge-Selective Adsorption of Organic Molecules in Microfluidic Mg(OH)2 Precipitate Membranes
papers.abstract: The porous mineral structures of alkaline hydrothermal vent chimneys have been proposed as natural concentrators of dissolved organic molecules, potentially addressing the longstanding dilution problem in deep-sea origin-of-life hypotheses. Here, we use microfluidic chemical garden precipitates composed of a primary mineral phase in white smoker chimneys, Mg(OH) 2 , to evaluate the adsorption and diffusion behavior of organic dye molecules as a function of their charge state. Pre-grown precipitate membranes are exposed to anionic (methyl orange, fluorescein), zwitterionic (rhodamine B), and cationic (crystal violet, malachite green) dye solutions under controlled flow conditions. UV-Visible spectroscopy of digested membranes reveals millimolar loading concentrations for anionic dyes after 20 h, limited uptake of the zwitterionic dye over the same period, and negligible adsorption of cationic species. Light intensity analyses of timelapse microscopy confirm that anionic dyes permeate the full membrane width within 4 h, while zwitterionic and cationic dyes remain confined near the injection interface. Steady-state and time-resolved emission measurements indicate increased environmental heterogeneity for membrane-bound fluorophores, consistent with adsorption across a distribution of pore sites. Raman and ATR-IR spectroscopy corroborate dye-mineral interactions. These results demonstrate that monomineral Mg(OH) 2 precipitates have pronounced charge-selective permeability, favoring anion transport in a manner analogous to the preferential hydroxide diffusion observed during membrane growth. This selectivity implies that negatively charged prebiotic molecules may have been preferentially concentrated within alkaline vent chimney walls, offering a mineral-mediated mechanism to locally elevate reactant concentrations in an otherwise dilute deep-sea environment.

papers.title: Magnetic fields from microscopic sources: a new quantum-based discrete interaction approach
papers.abstract: At nanometer scales, the Ørsted magnetic field generated by electrical current no longer strictly follows continuum magnetostatics. A nitrogen–vacancy magnetometry experiment reported suppressed and spatially reshaped magnetic fields in metallic nanowires, and these deviations are not captured by the Biot–Savart law. We introduce a microscopic current–magnetisation (CMH) framework that reconstructs magnetic induction directly from electron–ion correlations within atomically resolved conductors. Each carrier generates a locally screened axial source determined by its motion relative to nearby ions, yielding an exactly divergence-free magnetic field through a compact vector-potential formulation. The Biot–Savart kernel emerges only as a long-distance coarse-grained limit. When device dimensions approach the screening length, CMH predicts intrinsic field suppression and spatial smoothing. Crucially, the framework enables direct prediction of molecular orbital ring-current fields, revealing near-field structures that differ qualitatively from continuum loop models while preserving correct long-range behavior. CMH reframes current-induced magnetism at the atomic scale, where classical approaches fail, and opens a new and predictive pathway for engineering magnetic responses to enable design of next-generation nanomagnetic devices with improved performance.

papers.title: Absolutely localized molecular orbital energy decomposition analysis reconciles experimental evidence for on-water catalysis
papers.abstract: On-water catalysis denotes the acceleration of organic reactions at aqueous interfaces. Two mechanistic pictures have dominated the discussion: stabilization of the transition state by hydrogen bonds to interfacial water molecules, and proton transfer from the water surface to the reacting species. Neither picture alone explains the full set of experimental observations, in particular the different isotope effects reported for related cycloaddition reactions. Here, absolutely localized molecular orbital energy decomposition analysis is used to resolve this apparent conflict at the level of molecular interaction energies. For the cycloaddition of quadricyclane with dialkyl azodicarboxylate and related dienophiles, interfacial hydrogen bonds polarize the hydrated transition-state cluster and strengthen charge transfer between the organic reactants. In more strongly accelerated cases, proton transfer from interfacial water further amplifies this charge-transfer stabilization. These findings reconcile the hydrogenbond and proton-transfer models as limiting regimes of a common interfacial polarization mechanism and provide a quantitative molecular interpretation of the available experimental evidence.

papers.title: ApprOxiMate: A Lightweight Composition-Only Framework for Mixed Oxidation State Estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate assignment of oxidation states in multicomponent inorganic systems remains a significant challenge for high-throughput materials discovery, where existing methods are computationally intensive. Here we introduce ApprOxiMate, a deterministic, composition-only algorithm that estimates mixed and fractional oxidation states by iteratively satisfying global charge neutrality using standard reduction potentials (SRPs). The framework resolves exact stoichiometric fractions of each valence species, enabling rapid screening without structural input. We demonstrate its utility in two settings: first, in simulating alkali deintercalation in layered cathode materials, where ApprOxiMate correctly identifies the sequence of active redox couples and predicts practical capacity limits consistent with experimental observations; and second, in generating oxidation-state-aware composition-based feature vectors (CBFVs) for machine learning. Applied to crystal system classification in a dataset of 2,283 Mn–O-based inorganic compounds, the ApprOxiMate feature set achieves a weighted F1 score of 0.862 with an Extra Trees classifier, outperforming established neutral-atom descriptors (Magpie, Oliynyk), particularly for linear models, where improvements of up to 9.6% in F1 score were observed. SHAP analysis confirms that oxidation-state-dependent descriptors such as local covalent radius deviation and localised electronegativity capture known physical distortion mechanisms, including Jahn–Teller effects in Mn3+, that are invisible to composition-only neutral-atom features. ApprOxiMate thus offers a physically grounded yet computationally efficient route to incorporating redox chemistry into large-scale materials screening workflows.
