papers.title: Intrinsic Catalyst Reactivity—not Matched Surfactant Polarity—Drives Yield Differences in Aqueous Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Micelles in aqueous–organic syntheses are commonly assumed to serve as the primary reaction sites that colocalize and transform reactants. However, under synthetically relevant high-concentration conditions, phase separation may alter this simplified picture. Here, we investigate an aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction producing a fluorescent product, with triethylamine as the base and Kolliphor EL as the surfactant. Fluorescent lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) and microspectroscopy reveal that micrometer-scale triethylamine-rich organic droplets, rather than surfactant micelles, function as the predominant reaction sites and reservoirs for organic species. Direct measurements of droplet and micelle molecular composition disprove a previously proposed product–surfactant polarity “matching” mechanism in which micellar saturation inhibits catalytic turnover. Instead, the observed yield differences originate primarily from intrinsic catalyst reactivity. Consistent with this interpretation, surfactant-free “on-water” conditions still afforded quantitative conversion, albeit more slowly, indicating that the surfactant mainly enhances homogenization rather than creating selective reaction environments. These findings challenge prevailing assumptions regarding micellar catalysis and demonstrate how microscale imaging can directly identify the physical reactivity locations in heterogeneous aqueous reaction systems.

papers.title: FAVES V4: A Production-Deployed Compliance and Liability Screening System for Drug Discovery at 122M-Compound Scale, Aligned to HHS/ONC FAVES and NIST AI 600-1
papers.abstract: FAVES V4 is a compliance and liability screening system for drug discovery, aligned to two complementary federal frameworks: the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services / Office of the National Coordinator FAVES rubric for trustworthy AI in healthcare and life sciences,31 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1),38 which names chemical and biological design tools as a distinct chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) risk class (Section 2.1). The five letters; Fair, Appropriate, Valid, Effective, Safe; are not principles asserted in this paper; they are operational properties demonstrated against published evidence in production, with named action-ID anchors drawn from NIST AI 600-1 throughout Section 4. A single-API screening call returns regulatory status (DEA / FDA / CWC / EPA / EU REACH), structural alerts (1,585 SMARTS across PAINS, Brenk, NIH, ZINC, and 7 ChEMBL sub-catalogs via RDKit FilterCatalog), pharmacokinetic classification (BOILED-Egg), and prior-art disclosure (InChIKey identity resolution against PubChem and a local 122M-compound database), with per-field provenance metadata. The system is deployed in production with both live RDKit computation (~5 ms per molecule) and a precomputed database cache (122,407,635 documents). The five FAVES properties are operationalized through a complete governance bundle: an Intended Use Statement (Appropriate), risk-based component classification mapped to GAMP and CSA (Valid), end-to-end validation protocol with predetermined acceptance criteria (Valid), three-layer audit trail with two non-skippable layers (Safe), and change-control SOP with a worked rollback example (Safe). Validation across five tests against predetermined acceptance criteria; V3 regulatory benchmark, V4 field completeness, BOILED-Egg implementation, prior-art resolution, and external cross-RDKit-version reproducibility; yields 362/362 compounds passing post-fix at the time of submission. The initial 341/342 pre-fix execution identified a single defect; an incorrect cortisol SMILES in the deployed FDA whitelist that omitted the 11β-hydroxyl; which was root-caused, corrected, deployed, and re-validated through the documented change-control SOP. We report both numbers transparently: the defect was surfaced because the validation was honestly scoped to the full 102-compound regulatory benchmark rather than an undersized fixture, and the change-control loop functioning visibly in production is itself a stronger claim than a never-exercised one. To our knowledge, this is the first cheminformatics screening system whose full HHS/ONC-and NIST AI 600-1-aligned governance scaffolding is described in operational detail, with each of the five FAVES properties demonstrated against public evidence. The benchmark dataset, validation reports, and latency measurements are released for reproducibility; the seven NMCP-FAVES governance documents are summarized in Section 4 with NIST action-ID anchors and worked examples, and full operational versions are available from the corresponding author.

papers.title: Synthesis of Homochiral Metal-Organic Framework CFA-1 from Achiral Building Blocks via Chiral Induction
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) assembled from achiral building blocks that nonetheless crystallize in Sohncke space groups represent an underexplored route to chiral porous materials. However, accessing such materials requires enantioselective crystallization strategies, which remain a fundamental challenge. Here, we employ a chiral induction approach to produce enantiomorphically enriched CFA-1 (Zn5(OAc)4(bibta)3; H2bibta = 1H,1’H-5,5’bibenzo[d][1,2,3]triazole), a MOF constructed from achiral linker that crystallizes in the P321 chiral space group. Using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and 3D electron diffraction (3DED) for absolute structure determination, we establish that (R)-ibuprofen induces a left-handed (M) crystal morphology alongside a right-handed (P) absolute crystal structure, designated P-CFA-1, while (S)-ibuprofen affords the opposite enantiomorph. Enantiomorphically enriched CFA-1 promotes catalytic asymmetric transformations, highlighting the potential of intrinsically chiral frameworks for asymmetric catalysis.

papers.title: System Pharmacology-Driven Tri-Modal Leads Discovery of Anti-Mpox Therapeutics: Integrating Quantum Mechanics, Molecular Dynamics, and Network Topology
papers.abstract: The re-emergence of the Mpox virus (MPXV) as a global public health threat highlights the critical limitations of existing antivirals, which predominantly target viral replication while neglecting host-mediated immunopathology and severe clinical symptomatology. To address this therapeutic gap, we developed a system pharmacology-mediated trimodal framework from a comprehensive cheminformatics and medicinal chemistry workflow integrating quantum mechanics, molecular dynamics, network topology, and AI-driven retrosynthetic analysis. Here, we report the discovery of three unique functional leads selected via ligand-based virtual screening (LBVS) targeting the highly conserved viral VP39 methyltransferase (PDB: 8B07), a pivotal enzyme in viral mRNA cap formation and replication from a focused library enriched for structural analogs of validated inhibitors. Following viral target preparation and ligand library construction, candidates underwent molecular docking and ADMET profiling, which predicted favorable oral bioavailability and high safety margins. Electronic stability and chemical reactivity were validated via DFT frontierorbital analysis, while 200-ns MD simulations confirmed dynamic stability. Crucially, following simulation, thermodynamic efficacy for the top lead complexes was substantiated by MM-GBSA binding free energies (ΔG bind) ranging from –23.44 to –25.49 kcal mol–1, significantly outperforming the reference inhibitor. Pivotally, biological activity spectra and network pharmacology analysis revealed alongside direct viral VP39 blockade, these scaffolds exhibit a synergistic, host-directed effect polypharmacological division of labor, Lead 1 act as a potent viral egress inhibitor targeting host kinases (ABL1/SRC), Lead 2 functions as an immunomodulator via Toll-like receptor (TLR9) and GPCR pathways and Lead 3 offers a novel symptomatic management strategy by targeting voltage-gated sodium channels (SCN9A). Finally, the synthetic route prediction confirmed the translational feasibility of these candidates from commercially available precursors. This study establishes a rational, multi-scale computational strategy for discovering next-generation Mpox therapeutics that simultaneously arrest viral spread, potentiate host immunity, and alleviate debilitating symptoms.

papers.title: DOPING GRADIENT DIRECTION IN SEMICONDUCTOR PHOTOANODES CONTROLS SPACE CHARGE WIDTH, BAND ALIGNMENT AND WATER SPLITTING PERFORMANCE
papers.abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting relies on semiconductors capable of absorbing sunlight promoting the generation of excited electrons/holes, which are then used to catalyze the water splitting reaction. Despite extensive research, the efficiency of PEC devices in practice remains far from the theoretical limit. One of the main reasons for this issue is linked to semiconductor doping. Aliovalent doping is often required to enhance the electrical conductivity of the light-absorbing material, however by doing so, it reduces the space charge width, limiting the charge separation efficiency of the device. In this work, using hematite (α-Fe2O3) as a case study, we demonstrate the use of doping gradient as a viable strategy to improve the water splitting performance compared to conventional homogeneous doping. We discovered that the direction of doping gradient matters, with one gradient direction enabling to extend the space charge width and to align the conduction and valence band favorably; conversely, the other doping direction was found to provide unfavorable properties and consequently reduce the PEC performance. Through a combined experimental and computational analysis, our study provides a deeper understanding of the influence of doping gradient on space charge width and band alignment of semiconductors, which is applicable not just to hematite but to any n-type semiconductor in general.

papers.title: Graphene Oxide-anchored Ru-dmso Catalyst for Sustainable Nitrile Hydration in Aqueous medium
papers.abstract: A Ruthenium-dmso catalyst has been successfully heterogenized on graphene oxide GO@cis,fac-2c (GO@2c) for the first time, creating a sustainable system for nitrile hydration in water. We report the synthesis and characterization of three isomers of [RuCl2(bpea-pyrene)(dmso)] complex: trans,mer-2a (2a), trans,fac-2b (2b) and cis,fac-2c (2c). Isomerization studies and DFT calculations confirm that 2c is the most thermodynamically stable isomer. DFT calculations further elucidate the isomerization mechanisms, revealing the energetically accessible pathways connecting 2a, 2b, and 2c. Photo- and thermochemically induced processes were investigated in various solvents, elucidating distinct ligand substitution and oxidation pathways. Isomer 2c was heterogenized on GO via π interactions between the ligand's pyrene moiety and the support. This represents the first example of a molecular Ru-dmso complex non-covalently anchored on GO. Both homogeneous 2c and heterogeneous GO@2c efficiently catalyze the transformation of nitriles to amides with high selectivity. Notably, the GO-supported catalyst showed enhanced activity for acrylonitrile compared to its homogeneous counterpart. GO@2c exhibited excellent reusability over five cycles with negligible Ru leaching and high structural stability. These results highlight the system as a robust, reusable, and sustainable catalyst for aqueous nitrile hydration. Finally, a plausible mechanism is proposed to account for the observed reactivity.

papers.title: One Emitter, Many Lifetimes: Formulation-Encoded TADF Organic Dots for Multiplexed Imaging of Cancer-Immune Cell Co-Cultures
papers.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF)-based organic dots (Odots) are an attractive class of luminescent probes for multiplexed fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) as they can provide an unprecedented degree of tunability of their photoluminescence (PL) lifetimes. In this work, we demonstrate how formulation control of the Odot composition can be used to modulate the PL lifetime, which was then exploited in multiplexed FLIM studies. We synthesized and evaluated 48 TADF-Odots composed of eight structurally related derivatives of the multiresonant TADF (MR-TADF) emitter DiKTa , differing in number, strength, and steric demand of donor substituents, and six different formulations that modulated the degree of emitter aggregation. Controlled decrease in emitter aggregation as a function of doping concentration in the Odots produced a progressive blue-shift in the 1 emission, an increase in PL quantum yield up to 53%, and a lengthening of the PL lifetime, ultimately producing a family of Odots with PL lifetimes ranging from 4 to 35 ns. In vitro FLIM experiments in cancer cells validated the strategy for tuning the photophysics as a function of formulation, with PL lifetimes ranging from 3 to 16 ns. Finally, using different Odot formulations, each with the same emitter, we demonstrated signal resolution in multiplexed imaging experiments of co-cultures of human cancer and immune cells.

papers.title: Local SEI formation on Graphite Anodes Probed by Alternating-Current Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy
papers.abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) governs the electrochemical performance, stability, and lifetime of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Despite extensive studies, the local evolution of the SEI on graphite anodes during lithiation remains poorly understood. Here, alternating-current scanning electrochemical microscopy (AC-SECM) was applied to investigate localized impedance and interfacial heterogeneity on graphite electrodes in 1 M LiPF 6 in EC:EMC (3:7 wt%). Spatially resolved AC-SECM impedance, and phase maps obtained at different potentials applied to electrode revealed significant potential-dependent changes associated with SEI growth. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) confirmed increasing interfacial resistance and suppressed charge-transfer kinetics at lower potentials. These preliminary results demonstrate that AC-SECM is a promising approach for resolving local SEI formation and interfacial electrochemical behavior on graphite anodes and has the potential to extend this technique for other battery systems.

papers.title: The Synthetic Role of PFAS in Drug Substance Manufacturing: An IQ Consortium Working Group Review on the Potential Impact of PFAS Restrictions on Patient Access to Medicines
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been widely used in consumer and industrial applications including the pharmaceutical industry. This widespread adoption throughout society has recently come under scrutiny due to human health and environmental concerns associated with the toxicity and environmental persistence of certain PFAS. Within the IQ Consortium, a Working Group (WG) focusing on drug substance manufacturing has been established to assess the prevalence of PFAS in commercial drug substance manufacturing and the potential impact of PFAS regulations on patient access to medicines. To address gaps in current definitions, we introduce a functional classification—visible, contributing, and invisible PFAS—to distinguish PFAS present in marketed active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), those essential for installing PFAS moieties into APIs, and reagents or solvents enabling synthesis without remaining in the final product. Survey data from IQ Consortium member companies and literature analysis confirm extensive PFAS use and presence across the drug substance supply chain. These findings highlight that broad PFAS restrictions could disrupt manufacturing, necessitate significant process redevelopment and regulatory revalidation, and jeopardize continuity of supply. Proactive engagement and risk mitigation strategies are critical to balance environmental objectives with uninterrupted patient access to essential medicines.

papers.title: From PBE Band Gap Predictions to Experiments: Calibration, Transferability, and Failure Boundaries
papers.abstract: PBE remains the workhorse of high-throughput electronic-structure screening despite ~30% errors on sp semiconductors and qualitative failures on Mott insulators. The standard response (regression, scissor operators, or ML surrogates calibrating PBE to experiment) rests on a category error: the PBE-to-experiment discrepancy stacks three independent failure modes. Theoretical error (the missing derivative discontinuity in semi-local exchange-correlation) sets an irreducible floor. Missing-physics error (spin-orbit coupling, self-interaction in localized 3d/4f states, dynamic disorder) is system-dependent and only sometimes calibratable. Metrological error (optical vs quasiparticle vs transport gaps) is a definitional mismatch data cannot repair. Scalar calibration conflates these three sources and yields models that look accurate on random splits and fail on novel chemistry. We quantify: switching from random 80/20 to B-site GroupKFold inflates ML calibration MAE on a 1,117-compound lead-free halide perovskite benchmark by 44%, independently reproduced here at 21-31% inflation on matbench_expt_gap (n=4,604, range reflects whether metals are included) under general element-leave-out. A decision framework diagnoses which error category dominates and prescribes the minimum-cost remedy (group-wise calibration, then mBJ, HSE06+SOC, or GW+BSE in sequence). The framework is tested on a 544-compound multi-functional benchmark (Borlido 2019, Das 2022, Mohn 2026), where decision-tree routing recovers within 4% of uniform-HSE06 accuracy at roughly 57% of the compute cost; per-chemistry analysis identifies wide-gap strongly ionic systems as a regime where HSE06 over-corrects and calibrated PBE wins. In contrast to functional benchmarks (Borlido JCTC 2019; npj Comput. Mater. 2020), our focus is the validation architecture and the orbital-resolved diagnostic signals that should trigger escalation.

papers.title: Counterion-Controlled Magnetization from Polaron–Bipolaron Crossover at Elevated Carrier Densities
papers.abstract: The optoelectronic and thermoelectric properties of organic semiconductors at ultrahigh charge densities critically depend on the relative abundance of paramagnetic polarons and magnetically silent singlet bipolarons. In this study, we employ a modified Hubbard–Ising framework that incorporates the key physical interactions governing polarons, bipolarons, and counterions in the presence of an external magnetic field to uncover the microscopic origin of spin-density evolution across different doping regimes. Our results reveal that counterion-induced electrostatics play a dominant role in driving spin pairing and the polaron-to-bipolaron crossover, outweighing the effects of electron–phonon coupling. By systematically exploring the interplay between polymer electronic structure, counterion size, counterion proximity to the backbone, spatial distribution, and inter-counterion spacing, we identify key design principles governing the non-monotonic evolution of spin density in highly doped organic semiconductors. The theory rationalizes recent experimental measurements of unpaired spin concentrations and, in doing so, establishes predictive guidelines for controlling magnetic response in purely π-conjugated carbon-based materials. More broadly, a fundamental understanding of the quantum-mechanical and structural factors governing the crossover from polarons to bipolarons provides a blueprint for the rational design of organic spintronic devices, metal-free magnets, and molecular quantum sensing technologies.

papers.title: One-step polymerization of a long-chain metal-backboned polymer
papers.abstract: Metal-backboned polymers, featuring backbones composed exclusively of metal atoms interconnected by consecutive metal–metal bonds, have been proposed as a new class of materials for promising applications in optics, electronics and magnetics, but it remains unavailable to synthesize them. Leveraging the high bond strength and long-range tunability of Au–Au interactions, we report a straightforward one-step polymerization to make metal-backboned polymers for the first time. This strategy achieves a degree of polymerization exceeding 50 and stable chain integrity in solution, providing a concise and efficient route to produce them. Systematically structural characterizations reveal a one-dimensional linear Au backbone, in which gold atoms are interconnected by continuous Au–Au bonds and alternately stabilized by peripheral ligands. The resulting gold-backboned polymer (GBP) exhibits typical polymer behaviors including glass transition temperature and film-forming ability. In addition, Au backbone enables effective electron delocalization and long-wavelength phosphorescence. This work establishes a general and efficient route towards the synthesis of GBPs.

papers.title: Steering Diluted-NO Electroreduction Selectivity via Molecular Substituent Engineering
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the deliberate control over the hydrogenated products in electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction (ENOR) between NH3 and NH2OH by varying the substituents of iron phthalocyanines grafted on multi-walled carbon nanotubes. While the methoxy-featured catalyst exhibits dominant NH3 selectivity, another one with carboxyl groups possesses not only an electron-deficient Fe center to facilitate the NH2OH desorption, but also a strongly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water layer to avoid deep hydrogenation, both steering its ENOR toward selective NH2OH formation. Consequently, the carboxyl-derived catalyst exhibits high Faradaic efficiencies (FE; up to 90%), turnover frequency (12.0 s-1) and yield rate (4326 μmol h-1 mg-1) for NH2OH production from diluted NO (0.5% ~ 10%), surpassing most pioneering electrocatalysts, which is even applicable to a simulated flue gas source with interfering CO2 and SO2 to afford single-pass NO conversion efficiencies up to 30%.

papers.title: Stacked borophene-analogue sheets enable molecular catalyst–electrode integration
papers.abstract: Developing highly active and designable electrode catalysts through simple methods remains a key challenge. Here, we report a facile strategy to construct efficient electrocatalysts by integrating a molecular catalyst with a conductive two-dimensional material. Anionic stacked borophene-analogue sheets (sBS) were combined with a cationic pentanuclear iron complex (Fe5), a water oxidation catalyst composed of earthabundant metal, via simple solution mixing to form the composite sBS·Fe5. Spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal that the composite formation induces electronic interactions between sBS and Fe5. The composite exhibits high conductivity derived from sBS while preserving the intrinsic catalytic activity of Fe5 on the electrode surface, leading to state-of-the-art performance. In addition, mechanistic investigation at the molecular level, enabled by the excellent dispersibility of the composite, suggests that interfacial electronic interactions contribute to the formation of key intermediates that determine the reaction pathway. This work provides a new design principle for highperformance electrode catalysts.

papers.title: Divergent Synthesis and Storage of SF5X from a Single Bench-Stable Reagent
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a novel concept to promote formation of the mixed sulfur fluorides SF 5 Br and SF 5 Cl, nitro sulfur pentafluoride SF 5 NO 2 as well as disulfur decafluoride S 2 F 10 divergently from one single bench-stable, liquid and commercially available organic reagent. Upon the photoreaction with bromine liberation of SF 5 Br in up to 87% is observed. The reported method does not rely on any other additives or reagents but the halogen and exploits a chromoselectivity approach to purify the sulfur fluoride in the reaction mixture containing residual halogen. Consequently, SF 5 Br could be trapped by alkynes to grant access to SF 5 Br adducts in good to excellent yields in up to 81% yield over two steps. Furthermore, this concept could be expanded to the release of SF 5 Cl by reaction with BrCl to obtain SF 5 Cl in up to 82%. This reaction features an unprecedented, halogenide catalysed conversion of SF 5 Br into SF 5 Cl. At the same time the reagent can act as a storage for SF 5 X with an improved safety profile and can release the molecule on demand. The storage of SF 5 X on industrial level is a critical safety hazard, which can be addressed by the described method. This report is the first example of an addition and extrusion sequence of SF 5 Br or SF 5 Cl in very good yields from an air-stable organic precursor molecule. Furthermore, the power of this concept is underlined by a proof-ofprinciple study on the release of SF 5 NO 2 or S 2 F 10 from the same reagent. Therefore, we propose this reagent as a general platform for the liberation of various SF 5 X derivatives with improved safety profile.

papers.title: Mechanism of Peroxides Activation by Atomic Hydrogen
papers.abstract: Atomic hydrogen (·H) has been intensively investigated owing to its potential role in a sustainable hydrogen-based economy for peroxides activation. However, the process of peroxides activation via ·H has not been systematically elucidated, and the mechanism of the complex reaction remains unrevealed up to this point. To gain mechanical insight into this redox reaction, theoretical calculations are conducted to study the activation of peroxides by ·H. Through quantum chemistry (QM) calculations and advanced ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we investigate how the O-O bonds are broken by ·H and reactive oxygen species (ROS) are produced. QM calculations show that O-O bonds are likely to gain electrons. AIMD simulations with advanced metadynamics sampling techniques are applied to compute detailed reaction processes and free energy files. One-electron transfer from ·H to peroxide is responsible for ROS generation. These findings may provide a theoretical mechanism for the peroxides activation with ·H to produce ROS, and much more sustainable catalytic peroxides systems can be rationally designed by appropriately utilizing ·H.

papers.title: Light-Controlled Qubit Coupling in Organic Diradicals Linked by an MR-TADF Emitter
papers.abstract: Photoexcited high-spin states in organic systems represent an attractive platform for the optical control of magnetic interactions in molecular spin-qubit architectures. Here, we theoretically study two multiresonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF)-bridged organic diradicals incorporating stable 1,2,3,5-dithiadiazolyl (DTDA) radical units as molecular candidates for generating long-lived quintet excited states. Using high-level multireference ab initio electronic structure methods, namely CASSCF/QD-NEVPT2 and CASSCF/XMS-PDFT, we show that both systems preserve a disjoint ground state electronic structure with nearly degenerate singlet and triplet manifolds arising from weakly interacting radical spins. Upon photoexcitation of the MR-TADF bridge, population of the bridge-centered LUMO activates exchange interactions between the two DTDA radicals, stabilizing a low-lying metastable quintet state through coupling between the bridge-centered triplet excitation and the radical spins. The calculated spin-orbit couplings reveal that thermally activated torsional distortions around the bonds connecting the MR-TADF bridge to the radical units efficiently enable intersystem crossing between singlet, triplet, and quintet excited-state manifolds. In particular, intersystem crossing from the low-lying triplet states to the quintet manifold reaches rates on the order of 10 7 s −1 . Overall, these results establish MR-TADF emitter-linked organic diradicals as promising molecular platforms for accessing long-lived photoexcited quintet states and suggest a viable route toward the light-controlled activation of magnetic interactions between molecular qubits.

papers.title: Mechanistic Diversity of Mg(I)-Mediated 2–6 CO Coupling Revealed through Computational Reaction Path Exploration
papers.abstract: Reductive coupling of CO in homogeneous systems has long been used to model the Fischer-Tropsch reaction to produce hydrocarbon fuels. Mg(I) complexes have enabled multiple CO coupling reactions; however, their mechanisms are challenging to characterize due to strong ionic interactions and multiple competing pathways. Here, we performed automated reaction path network exploration for 2-, 3-, 4-, and 6-CO coupling reactions mediated by Mg(I) complexes using the single-component artificial force induced reaction (SC-AFIR) and the Δ-learning neural network potential methodologies. These unbiased explorations reveal pathways for all experimentally observed products while uncovering a rich mechanistic landscape comprising multiple competing and previously inaccessible pathways. While CO coupling steps for 2- and 3-CO coupling reactions are similar to earlier reports, the reaction path network uncovers new pathways for C–H activation in the 2-CO coupling reaction. SC-AFIR exploration of the 4-CO coupling reaction highlights competing reaction pathways, leading to both kinetically and thermodynamically controlled products. A key resting state obtained for Mg-complex provides rationale for related CO coupling observed in Al complexes with similar ligand environments. Intrinsic bond orbital (IBO) analysis shows that strong ionic Mg–O interactions facilitate the rare event of C–O cleavage in the 4-CO coupling reaction. The 6-CO coupling proceeds stepwise, in contrast to earlier reports, with the Mo center acting as an organizing nucleus that facilitates sequential CO coupling. The reaction path network also identifies several accessible channels for previously unidentified products. Overall, this study reveals pronounced mechanistic diversity in Mg(I)-mediated CO coupling and demonstrates how reaction path network exploration can resolve complex, multichannel reactivity in low-valent main-group systems.

papers.title: XNA Sequencing by Chemical Ligation of DNA Fragments on an Acyclic Artificial Nucleic Acid (L-aTNA)
papers.abstract: Xeno nucleic acids (XNAs) have attracted interest in nucleic acid therapeutics and origin-of-life studies. Sequencing of XNAs is imperative for studying the molecular evolution of functional XNAs, such as aptamers and XNAzymes, but enzyme-based approaches are often not suitable for sequencing of acyclic XNAs. In this study, we demonstrate the nonenzymatic information transfer from an acyclic L-threoninol nucleic acid, L- a TNA, to DNA by chemical ligation of 5-mer DNA fragments on an L- a TNA template. The resulting DNA can then be subjected to next-generation sequencing (NGS). A 20-mer region of L-aTNA was accurately transcribed into DNA, and the resulting DNA sequences reflected the complementarity between the DNA fragments and the L-aTNA template. Notably, this strategy was also successful for a 30-mer L- a TNA transcription region. This method enables the identification of variable positions and their base composition within populations of L- a TNA strands containing randomized positions. Moreover, a 2′- O -methyl RNA template was successfully sequenced, suggesting that this method will be suitable for sequencing of XNAs that can cross-pair with DNA. This method will be useful during selection of XNA aptamers and XNAzymes.

papers.title: New insights on PFAS inputs to the Great Lakes based on sediments from Lakes Superior and Huron
papers.abstract: This study presents the first comprehensive survey of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in sediments from Great Lakes Superior and Huron since 2010. Six cores and surface sediments were collected from Superior and Huron in 2021 and 2022, respectively. Superior surface sediments contained primarily perfluorocarboxylic acids (PFCAs), reflecting atmospheric deposition as Superior’s primary PFAS input. Frequent detections of perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctane sulfonamide (PFOSA) across both lakes suggest atmospheric input of PFOSA as an important contributor of PFOS to sediments. PFAS in Superior were strongly correlated with sediment organic matter (SOM), indicating strong influence of sediment transport and partitioning processes on spatial distributions, while correlations were weaker for Huron. Average surface sediment concentrations were comparable between Superior and Huron except for PFOS, which was >2x more concentrated in Huron sediments, suggesting possible influence of legacy aqueous film-forming foams (AFFF) to PFAS contamination in Huron. Huron spatial patterns were consistent with AFFF contamination originating from southern Georgian Bay spreading to the Huron main body. Temporal profiles for Superior showed gradually increasing PFAS fluxes from the 1960s through 2020. In contrast, PFAS fluxes in Huron near the Main Channel began to rapidly increase in 2007, suggesting that AFFF contamination may have been spreading within the Huron main body for nearly two decades. These results warrant continued efforts to reduce PFAS inputs to the Great Lakes.

papers.title: ClickChem: Automated Conjugation Chemistry Planning for Antibody–Drug Conjugates
papers.abstract: Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) require precise conjugation chemistry to covalently attach cytotoxic payloads to monoclonal antibodies while preserving antigen-binding function and pharmacokinetic stability. The selection of an appropriate conjugation strategyencompassing the reaction family, the conjugation site on the antibody, and the linker architecture—remains largely empirical, relying on iterative experimental screens that are costly and time-consuming. We present ClickChem, a computational pipeline that auto-mates conjugation chemistry selection for ADC design. The pipeline operates in six sequential stages: functional-group detection on the payload, multi-conformer solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) scoring of antibody conjugation sites, chemistry family planning across seven reaction families, linker selection from a curated library, in silico bond formation via SMIRKSbased reaction execution, and product validation through a six-layer quality-control protocol incorporating Maximum Common Substructure (MCS) analysis. A distinguishing feature of the site-scoring module is an ensemble-averaged SASA calculation that generates multiple antibody conformations through an Anisotropic Network Model (ANM) and aggregates solvent-exposure statistics across the ensemble, yielding a confidence metric that penalises residues whose accessibility fluctuates between conformations. We evaluate the pipeline on three fronts. First, we verify concordance with established clinical precedent by exercising the pipeline on the payloads and conjugation-site annotations of ten FDA-approved ADCsincluding Adcetris, Kadcyla, Enhertu, and Trodelvy—and show that the pipeline selects the conventionally employed reaction family in all ten cases (10/10 concordance). Second, we present two end-to-end case studies—MMAF and Doxorubicin conjugated to a full-length IgG surrogate (PDB: 1IGT) via heterobifunctional SPAAC–IEDDA dual-click chemistrydemonstrating handle installation, site-specific conjugation at three distinct residue types

papers.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Hydro- and Deuteroacylation of Acrylates using Water as Hydrogen Source
papers.abstract: Acylation of activated alkenes provides useful and quick access to synthetically useful 1,4-difunctionalized compounds. In this work, an operationally simple mechanochemical protocol for the hydroacylation of acrylates and related activated alkenes is reported using thioesters as acyl donors and water as the hydrogen source. This approach selectively furnished linear coupling products, complementing previous nickel-catalyzed methodologies that predominantly yield branched 1,3-adducts. Substitution of water with D2O enables straightforward synthesis of deuterium-labeled products with high levels of selective isotopic incorporation. Detailed mechanistic investigations, including primary and secondary KIE studies, Hammett analysis, DFT computations and NMR spectroscopy, support a pathway involving migratory insertion at the nickel center, while providing no evidence for the involvement of radical intermediates.

papers.title: Detonation Nanodiamond-Supported Ru(II) Poly(pyridine) Complexes as Efficient and Recyclable Photoredox Catalysts
papers.abstract: The immobilization of ruthenium based photocatalysts onto functionalized detonation nanodiamond (DND) particles is reported, providing recyclable heterogeneous systems for visible-light photoredox catalysis. The resulting nanoparticle-supported colloidal catalysts were evaluated in the αfunctionalization of carbamates and in three-component trifluoromethylation reactions of alkenes under visible light irradiation. In all cases, the heterogeneous systems display catalytic performances comparable to, or exceeding, those of their homogeneous counterparts. This enhanced activity is attributed to the electronic interaction between the Ru complex and the DND surface, which may facilitate interfacial charge transfer through favorable alignment of frontier orbitals. Additionally, the supported photocatalysts can be readily recovered and reused for more than 10 cycles without any significant loss of activity, demonstrating their robustness and stability. These results highlight the potential of nanodiamond-supported photocatalysts as efficient and sustainable alternatives for photoredox transformations involving noble metals.

papers.title: Storage and retrieval of electronic spin coherence using nuclear spins in a vanadyl paddlewheel
papers.abstract: Electronic and nuclear spins are complementary carriers of quantum information: whereas nuclear spins exhibit long coherence times suitable for its storage, electronic spins ensure rapid addressing and readout. A key challenge is harvesting the benefits of both spin degrees of freedom by transferring coherence between them. In this work, we achieved this goal by working on a molecular architecture that affords precise control over electronuclear properties by chemical design. As a model system, we used heterobimetallic paddlewheel complex [VOPt(SOCPh) 4 ] diluted in [TiOPt(SOCPh) 4 ]*2THF diamagnetic crystalline host matrix (nominal molar concentrations of 1 and 10%). In [VOPt(SOCPh) 4 ], vanadyl electronic spin S = 1/2 is hyperfinely-coupled to the nuclear spin I = 7/2 of 51 V. These electronic and nuclear spins were simultaneously manipulated using sequences of Radiofrequency (RF) and Microwave (MW) pulses generated by a multifrequency on-chip setup operating at cryogenic temperatures. First, Electron Nuclear DOuble Resonance (ENDOR) experiments were performed to show the readout of the 51 V nuclear spin transitions through the electronic spin echo. Further experiments with a dedicated RF-MW pulse sequence demonstrated that electronic phase coherence can be stored in the nuclear spins and retrieved (Storage and Retrieval, SR) after a total free precession time that greatly exceeds the electronic phase memory time. This key result establishes a route for encoding quantum information on the electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom of a chemically tunable platform.

papers.title: “AI-Driven QSAR Modelling and Virtual Screening For Anti-Cancer Scaffold Discovery”
papers.abstract: Advances in drug discovery increasingly depend on computational approaches that enable the efficient prioritization of therapeutic candidates. In this study, cheminformatics and computational learning framework was integrated to evaluate the potential modulators of cancer-associated proteins Caspase-9, BCL-2 and Veg-F. A dataset comprising 100 compounds with experimentally reported IC50 values was curated and standardized in canonical SMILES format. Compounds with IC50 < 5 µM were classified as active. Molecular descriptors were calculated using RDKit and employed as features for multiple ML models. Regression models, including Random Forest Regressor, HistGradientBoosting Regressor, and a Feedforward Neural Network, were developed to predict bioactivity, whereas Random Forest Classifier was trained for toxicity prediction, with SMOTE applied exclusively across the training phase to handle class imbalance. ADMET properties were evaluated using ADMETlab 2.0, and compounds satisfying Lipinski’s Rule of Five along with favourable activity and safety profiles were retained, yielding 40 active and non-toxic candidates. Due to computational power limitations and project duration constraints, molecular docking simulations were conducted using AutoDock Vina on five representative compounds selected from the active and non-toxic subset. Molecular Docking studies suggested favourable binding interactions for compounds such as Citral and Thiophene with the target proteins, while Benzothiazole exhibited promising scaffold characteristics for further optimization. The Random Forest Regressor demonstrated highest predictive performance (R2 = 0.929), while the HistGradientBoosting Regressor achieved moderate accuracy (R2 = 0.7531). A sequential neural network model produced a mean absolute error of approximately 0.84 with minor overfitting recognized during training. Toxicity prediction models further demonstrated reliable classification performance (Accuracy = 0.85, AUC-ROC = 0.959), highlighting the relevance of physicochemical descriptors in determining compound safety profiles. Overall, this work demonstrates an integrated computational pipeline for molecular feature prediction, QSAR modelling, toxicity assessment, offering a rational strategy for prioritizing and optimizing potential scaffolds for anti-cancer drug development.

papers.title: Precursor-programmed ionic organization governs electrostatic polarization for selective photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide synthesis
papers.abstract: Controlling ionic organization in polymeric photocatalysts remains a fundamental barrier to efficient solar-driven hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis. In conventional poly(heptazine imide) (PHI) systems, cation incorporation is directed by equilibrium in molten salts, yielding statistically distributed and weakly correlated ionic environments. Here, we demonstrate that organic-inorganic ionic cocrystals (ICCs) act as molecularly preorganized precursors that encode spatially correlated cation arrangements during framework formation, enabling deterministic placement of Li+ at imide-bridged N sites. This precursor-programmed architecture decouples composition from function, establishing that photocatalytic performance is governed by ionic arrangement rather than cation identity or content. The resulting dual-cation material (CALiK) delivers an apparent quantum yield of 58% at 410 nm, among the highest reported for metal-free carbon nitride photocatalysts. Operando-relevant spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal directional charge migration driven by internal electrostatic gradients and enhanced accumulation of long-lived electrons. Complementary density functional theory calculations attribute this behavior to electrostatically polarized charge landscapes arising from spatial correlation between Li-N coordination sites and cyano-derived electron-accepting domains, which lower the energetic barrier for the two-electron oxygen reduction pathway. These findings establish that precursor programming of ionic configurations as a general strategy for controlling charge dynamics and catalytic selectivity in polymeric semiconductors.

papers.title: Electrochemical Control of Tunable Infrared Nanocrystal Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Dynamic control of photonic materials at mid-infrared wavelengths is essential for applications spanning thermal management, active imaging, and optical signal processing, yet achieving strong modulation within small material volumes remains a central challenge. Conventional approaches rely on lithographically patterned metasurfaces with limited scalability, or on ultrathin materials with weak light–matter interaction. Here we show that cavity-coupled assemblies of sub-10 nm plasmonic tin-doped indium oxide nanocrystals function as dynamic metasurfaces with electrochemically switchable linear and nonlinear optical responses. By integrating colloidal nanocrystals into a photonic architecture, we co-locate permittivity modulation and electromagnetic field confinement within the same nanoscale volume, achieving 77% absolute reflection modulation. Synthetic control of tin doping provides spectral selectivity across 2.5–4 µm, while solution processing yields centimeter-scale device uniformity. Beyond linear modulation, voltage-controlled near-field enhancement enables electrically switchable ultrafast nonlinear response with 100% relative reflection modulation and 0.25 ps recovery time, enabling dual-timescale optical control.

papers.title: Structural Constraint of Overcrowded Alkenes: Macrocyclization of 9,9'-Bifluorenylidene
papers.abstract: We report the successful synthesis of Cyclic BF and Cyclic Bis-BF, in which alkyl bridges installed at the 2-position serve as a precise structural handle for constructing macrocyclic architectures with fine-tuned molecular strain. Enabled by a modified Barton–Kellogg reaction, this strategy overcomes the significant steric barriers typically associated with functionalizing 9,9′-bifluorenylidene. Comprehensive characterization, including NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, DFT calculations, UV–Vis spectroscopy, and electrochemical measurements, reveals that strain-induced conformational locking governs the molecular structure - mechanical expansion – electronic property relationship. Notably, the macrocyclic frameworks exhibit electronic invariance despite increased molecular complexity, highlighting the dominant role of molecular strain induced by structural constraint. This work establishes a versatile strategy for designing highly strained macrocycles with predictable and tunable properties, providing new insights into the interplay between molecular architecture, geometry, molecular strain, and electronic properties.

papers.title: Iterative LLM-driven de novo drug design with multi-method consensus scoring: a case study on EGFR T790M/L858R
papers.abstract: We present a closed-loop de novo drug-design pipeline in which a large language model (Claude Opus 4.7) acts as the reasoning generator inside an iterative loop with classical physics-based filters (RDKit drug-likeness, PAINS, SA), AutoDock Vina docking, MM-GBSA rescoring (amber14 + SMIRNOFF + OBC2), and short implicit-solvent molecular dynamics for pose-stability triage. Unlike generative neural networks, the LLM emits a structured rationale per proposal — making the chemistry behind every design auditable. Applied to EGFR T790M/L858R (PDB 4ZAU) over three feedback rounds with 60 proposals, the pipeline produced 27 unique candidates with docking scores ranging from −8.0 to −9.91 kcal/mol. A re-dock against wild-type EGFR (PDB 1M17) followed by single-trajectory MM-GBSA on the top five hits identified a single triple-confirmed lead, EGFRm-009 (a 3-(2-trifluoromethyl-4-fluorobenzyl) pyridopyrimidinone), with a Vina ΔΔG (wt − mut) of +1.24 kcal/mol, MM-GBSA ΔΔG of +23.86 kcal/mol, and a stable docked pose over 2 ns of OBC2 MD (heavy-atom RMSD ≤ 2.75 Å). Vina ΔΔG and MM-GBSA ΔΔG correlate with Pearson r = 0.60 across the top-5 set. The full pipeline runs on a single workstation without commercial software (no Schrödinger Suite, no GPU cluster) and is open-sourced as SchrodingerLite.

papers.title: Plasmonic nanorods form reconfigurable liquid crystalline assemblies
papers.abstract: Self-assembly of plasmonic nanoparticles typically involves attractive interactions or out-of-equilibrium processes, impeding the dynamic structural tunability required for applications. Anisotropic nanoparticles, however, spontaneously assemble at equilibrium into responsive liquid-crystalline phases, driven primarily by repulsive interactions. Here, assemblies of plasmonic silver nanorods combining long-range order with fluidity over macroscopic scales, and organized in isotropic, nematic and smectic phases, were designed by balancing electrostatic and depletion interactions. These assemblies respond to multiple external stimuli, including electric and magnetic fields, temperature, and light, enabling both quick alignment and reversible phase transitions. Control over interparticle spacing and orientational order allows for collective plasmonic coupling and tunable polarization-dependent optical properties, establishing a simple and scalable route to reconfigurable plasmonic materials with dynamic optical functionalities.

papers.title: Microplastics alter the fate of inland-derived microbial contaminants transported into coastal environments by tropical cyclones
papers.abstract: Tropical cyclones transport diverse contaminants, including microbial contaminants and microplastics, from inland to coastal environments. However, the fate of these inland-derived contaminants after transport remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the mechanisms by which microplastics affect the fate of inland-derived microbial contaminants in coastal waters. Field observations following Hurricane Milton revealed substantial transport of microplastics from inland areas to Florida’s Gulf Coast, where antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) associated with particles larger than 25 µm accounted for approximately 25% of the total ARG abundance introduced during the hurricane event. We confirmed that biofilm formation on microplastics reduced the decay rates of inland-derived bacteria to about half under simulated coastal conditions. We also confirmed that inland-derived bacteria coexisted with indigenous marine bacteria in coastal environments, facilitated by microplastics, for extended periods (weeks to months), posing a potential risk of horizontal gene transfer of ARGs from inland to coastal environments. Consequently, microplastics may extend the impact of storm-introduced microbial threats beyond what is captured by conventional fecal indicator bacteria-based assessments. This study highlights the need to reconsider microbial water quality recovery in coastal environments by accounting for particle-associated processes following extreme events.

papers.title: Encoding Spatially Resolved Optical Function in Single Crystals via Homochiral Crystal-on-Crystal Growth
papers.abstract: How can distinct functionalities be spatially encoded within a single crystalline material while preserving structural coherence? Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) provide tunable architectures, but controlling chirality and interfaces in heterostructures remains challenging. We demonstrate homochiral crystal-on-crystal growth, yielding dumbbell-shaped 30 MOF heterostructures with predictable morphology. Epitaxial growth of terminal caps on a central bar occurs across a shared crystallographic interface, preserving the intrinsic habits of each domain. X-ray diffraction and interface modeling reveal chirality transfer across the junction, forming a continuous homochiral architecture with aligned nanosized channels. Distinct pore environments enable region-specific dye uptake, producing sharply defined spatial 35 segregation of chromophores. The alignment of dyes within anisotropic channels further gives rise to segment-specific, polarization-dependent optical responses. These results establish a strategy for encoding multiple optical functions within a single crystal through controlled heteroepitaxial growth.

papers.title: Computational Prediction of Substrate Scope of a Homogeneous Catalyst: The Case of Metal-free C-H Borylation by a Frustrated Lewis Pair Catalyst
papers.abstract: Predicting substrate scope in catalytic reactions from first principles requires evaluating not only the lowest-energy productive pathway, but also competing processes that can suppress turnover. Here we present FRUST, an automated computational workflow for substratescope prediction, and apply it to metal-free C–H borylation mediated by the boron-based frustrated Lewis pair catalyst developed by Fontaine and co-workers (Science 2015, 349, 513–516). FRUST generates intermediates and transition-state guesses for each unique aromatic C–H position, performs conformational sampling, and estimates barriers using constrained xTB geometries refined by DFT single-point calculations. Benchmarking against literature substrates shows that the workflow captures the dominant mechanistic trends of the FLP catalytic cycle and identifies TS1 as the principal barrier-defining step across both benchmark and screening sets. Application to 69 aromatic substrates identified a small number of lowbarrier candidates, including phenols, N-aryl amides, and selected aprotic arenes. However, targeted DFT validation showed that even the most promising aprotic candidates lie near or beyond the empirical reactivity window, suggesting that the current FLP catalyst is unlikely to exhibit broad substrate scope beyond known activated heteroarenes. Analysis of protic substrates further revealed important off-cycle limitations: O–H borylation of phenols is predicted to deactivate neighbouring C–H sites, while N-aryl amides are likely to undergo N–H borylation without subsequent productive C–H borylation. These results demonstrate that efficient computational screening can retain mechanistic resolution, but also highlight the need to include side-reaction prediction when assessing catalyst scope and designing next-generation metal-free borylation catalysts.

papers.title: Molecular Engineering of Conjugated Polyelectrolyte-Enzyme Biohybrid Sheets for Solar CO2 Conversion
papers.abstract: Bridging synthetic light-harvesting materials with enzymatic CO2 fixation offers a compelling strategy for semi-artificial photosynthesis, yet molecular design principles governing semiconductor–biocatalyst interfaces remain underdeveloped. Conjugated polyelectrolytes (CPEs) are biocompatible, metal-free photosensitizers with optoelectronic and surface properties that can be programmed at the molecular level, providing a versatile platform to engineer biohybrid function. Here, we establish a molecular design framework for organic semiconductor–enzyme assemblies using a systematic series of seven CPEs that spontaneously self-assemble with formate dehydrogenase (FDH) into photocatalytic biohybrid sheets. Precise variation of sidechain functionality and conjugated backbone structure reveals clear structure–property–activity relationships that dictate direct electron transfer at the abiotic-biotic interface. Molecular control over surface charge density, hydration environment, solution-processability, and long-range charge separation enhances CO2-to-formate reduction rates by more than two orders of magnitude. The optimized biohybrid sheet achieves a turnover frequency of 27,488 h‒1 with stable operation over 48 h, establishing a benchmark for FDH-based systems. These findings define actionable design principles for co-optimizing soft electronic structure and biointerfacial chemistry to construct high-performance biohybrid platforms incorporating metal-free light harvesters for solar chemical production.

papers.title: In Silico Top-Down Fourier Transform Mass Spectra to Advance Proteoform Analysis Methods
papers.abstract: Top-down (TD) Fourier transform mass spectrometry (FTMS) of proteins generates highly information-rich mass spectra. However, the resulting spectral complexity can hinder data interpretation and method development. Here, we apply transient-mediated, instrument-specific simulations of protein TD mass spectra with defined product ion-level ground truth. The workflow integrates sequence-based product ion generation, empirically-informed fragmentation statistics, charge location modeling, and user-defined FT processing. The simulations capture key FTMS characteristics, including m/z-dependent resolution, peak interference, and realistic peak shapes. As a proof of concept, we simulated intact carbonic anhydrase II TDMS datasets under conditions reported for corresponding 21 T FT-ICR MS electron transfer dissociation experiments. The simulated mass spectra reproduced key experimental descriptors of spectral complexity, including peak density, spectral dynamic range, and isotopic structures. Using datasets with increasing complexity, we evaluated TDMS annotation performance and observed a substantial decrease in product ion annotation rates from c-ion-only mass spectra to the most complex datasets containing a-, c-, y-, and z-type product ions, reflecting the impact of spectral congestion on confident assignment. These results show that transient-based FTMS simulation can reveal conditions when spectral congestion becomes the main limitation to interpretation. The initial dataset of simulated mass spectra and transients is available through ProteomeXchange under identifier PXD075270.

papers.title: Dynamic Self-Assembly Mediated by Stored and Released Electrons in Pimer Supramolecular Polymers of Chromophore Amphiphiles
papers.abstract: Summary Reversible self-assembly of supramolecular polymers plays a critical role in living systems, exemplified by the cell cytoskeleton. Analogous synthetic systems could be functional in the spatiotemporal control of chemical reactions, design of active matter, and energy storage for use on demand. We report here on an energy-storing supramolecular system that reversibly converts from small aggregates of molecules to supramolecular polymers. The aminonaphthalimide chromophore amphiphile monomer is conjugated to a methyl viologen moiety, that converts energy from visible light, chemical fuels, an electrochemical bias, or X-rays to store electrons and trigger formation of a polymeric pimer, accompanied by conversion from a solution to hydrogel. Supramolecular polymerization is synergistically triggered by p-p stacking and p-radical pimerization that stores electrons in the assembly. These electrons can be released, generating reactive oxygen species which proceed to oxidize an organic substrate in the absence of visible light thus providing a model system for dark photocatalysis.

papers.title: Prediction of triplet geometries across chemical space with flow-matching based machine learning
papers.abstract: Obtaining accurate triplet excited-state geometries is critical for diverse applications with spin-based properties, including photocatalysis, optoelectronics, and photodynamic therapy where triplet energy and structural relaxation govern process efficiency and device performance. Yet, it remains computationally prohibitive for large-scale screening. In this work, we present GoFlow-T1 by adapting a machine learning framework based on flow matching, GoFlow, for the direct prediction of minimum-energy triplet-state geometries across chemically diverse organic molecules. The model is trained on quantum-chemically optimized triplet structures for approximately 11,000 compounds, encompassing chromophores, pharmaceuticals, natural products, and functional dyes. By learning the structural relaxation patterns associated with intersystem crossing and triplet-state stabilization, GoFlow-T1 generates equilibrium, that is minimum-energy, triplet geometries without the need of explicit excited-state geometry optimization, which in turn enables the rapid computation of triplet energies and singlet-triplet energy gaps. A benchmark against time-dependent density functional theory demonstrates near-quantum-chemical accuracy for both structural and energetic observables, while reducing computational cost by several orders of magnitude. Integrating GoFlow into photophysical screening pipelines enables the scalable identification of molecules with optimal triplet state properties for diverse photochemical applications. This work demonstrates that machine learning-driven prediction of excited-state equilibrium geometries is a practical, efficient strategy for high-throughput modeling and the data-driven discovery of functional photoactive candidates.

papers.title: First-Principles Microkinetic Model for Ammonia Synthesis on Fe(110) under Non-Equilibrium Programmable Heating and Quenching Operation
papers.abstract: Traditional thermochemical processes typically operate under relatively static conditions, where conventional reactors restrict the time scales over which key reaction parameters (such as temperature) can be varied. Electrification via Joule heating offers a way to overcome this limitation by producing pulsed temperature profiles with millisecond time resolution via programmable electric currents through a lightweight resistive catalyst support. The programmable heating and quenching (PHQ) approach enables access to nontraditional reaction dynamics and may significantly enhance product yield and selectivity with improved energy efficiency. Ammonia (NH 3 ), produced by the Haber-Bosch (HB) process, plays a critical role in fertilizer production and is gaining attention as a potential hydrogen carrier. The conventional HB process requires high temperatures and pressures, limiting energy efficiency and decentralized production. Dong et al. demonstrated NH 3 synthesis from H 2 and N 2 at ambient pressures using a PHQ reactor and an Fe catalyst, with yields higher than under isothermal conditions and stable output (Dong et al. Nature, 605, 470-476 (2022)). Here, we used density-functional-theory-based microkinetic modeling under both steady-state (isothermal) and dynamic (PHQ) conditions to understand the effect of controlled thermal fluctuations on heterogeneous catalysis of NH 3 synthesis on the most stable facet of Fe, namely (110). We demonstrate how PHQ can alter reaction rates and surface species, specifically, we predict fluctuations in concentrations of adsorbed N vs. NH; we also investigate how variations in temperature pulsing, e.g., the maximum temperature allowed and cycle time, influence yield. We find that PHQ enhances NH 3 yield only when the average of the fluctuating temperature deviates from the optimal isothermal temperature (especially when lower). Furthermore, increasing the time between high-temperature pulses could dramatically improve energy efficiency due to the slow temperature decay between pulses.

papers.title: Crustal distribution of rare earth elements modulated by hydrocarbon migration
papers.abstract: Rare earth elements (REE) are critical to technological advancements, yet elevated concentrations as seen in the few known conventional deposits are uncommon. Understanding the distribution of REE in sedimentary systems is important to securing REE resources from unconventional deposits. Studies addressing the mobilization of REE in sedimentary basins focus on a single fluid phase rather than multiphase fluid, oil-water systems. We strategically chose the Phosphoria Total Petroleum System (PTPS) in the Intermountain West of the United States to investigate mobilization and partitioning of REE between oil, water, source rock, and reservoir rock. The PTPS has REE-enriched source rock from which hydrocarbons have undergone large-volume, long-distance migration. Our data show REE concentrations are five orders-of-magnitude higher in source rock than in oil and are an average of six times greater in oil than in water. We report a near 100:1 ratio of lighter mass REE in oil relative to water decreasing to ~1:1 for the heavier mass REE, suggesting mobilization, preferential partitioning, and redistribution of REE by hydrocarbons. Such redistribution of critical minerals by hydrocarbons may represent an underrecognized link between carbon and metal cycling in sedimentary basins, with implications for metal fate and transport, unconventional critical mineral resources, and sustainable subsurface energy systems globally.

papers.title: Naphthalene-Attached Luminescent Radicals : Investigation of Position-Dependent Photophysical Properties
papers.abstract: Tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM) radicals substituted at the C1 and C2 positions of naphthalene were synthesized. The C1 substitution led to a broader photoluminescence (PL) spectrum and a significantly lower PL quantum yield (PLQY) compared to the C2 substitution. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations suggested that these differences arise from variations in steric effects and the associated molecular conformation in the excited states. Our results emphasize that the bonding position is crucial for controlling the photophysical properties of acene-substituted TTM radicals.

papers.title: Probing first-cycle electrochemical kinetics and discontinuities in NMC cathodes using single-particle electrochemistry
papers.abstract: Polycrystalline NMC particles undergo intergranular cracking during cycling due to anisotropic volume expansion. These cracks facilitate electrolyte penetration into the particles, improving electrochemical kinetics. While cracking and electrolyte penetration are well established, their frequency and extent are poorly understood. Here, we use single-particle electrochemistry to study electrochemical kinetics during the first and second charge cycles of individual NMC622 cathode particles. We identified an average of 65 electrochemical discontinuities during the first charge, each corresponding to an abrupt increase in electrochemical surface area from intergranular cracking. Moreover, by quantifying the exchange current between the first and second cycle, we show that the surface area increases by a factor of 10-20 within individual battery particles. These findings highlight the distinct electrochemistry of NMC particles during the first cycle and, more broadly, enable the study of discrete, discontinuous events within individual battery particles.

papers.title: AQ-GNoME: an Aqueous Stability Augmentation of the GNoME Database
papers.abstract: Aqueous stability is a fundamental requirement for materials used in electrochemical energy technologies, yet no systematic Pourbaix stability screening has been performed for Google DeepMind’s GNoME database of more than 520,000 novel inorganic crystals. Here, we introduce AQ-GNoME, an aqueous-stability augmentation of the GNoME database, enabling systematic shortlisting of GNoME candidates for electrochemical applications. The database additionally includes machine-learning-based substitutional-disorder predictions and Herfindahl–Hirschman Index supply-risk metrics, thereby supporting structural-order and supply-risk based filtering. User-defined criteria across electrochemical potential and pH, elemental composition, structural order, and supply concentration reduce the database to a manageable, project-specific shortlist. We apply AQ-GNoME to identify GNoME materials relevant for further investigation in electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) and acidic oxygen evolution (OER), focusing on candidates absent from the Materials Project and ICSD. For eCO2RR, combining aqueous stability criteria with a compositional heuristic intended to mimic copper’s selectivity, we identify 8 ordered multimetallic candidates. For acidic OER, combining stability and supply-concentration criteria, we identify 39 Ir-lean oxides, of which 26 are metallic under HSE06 DFT. AQ-GNoME therefore provides a practical framework for electrochemical materials discovery within GNoME, reducing the search space from more than half a million compounds to experimentally tractable candidate sets.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Microsolvation via Free Energy–Based Solvation Site Identification
papers.abstract: In quantum chemical descriptions of solutions, solvents are treated either implicitly, accounting only for bulk properties, or explicitly by including solvent molecules in the calculations. Although explicit treatments are more accurate, they are often computationally prohibitive. As a cost-effective alternative, microsolvation models have emerged that include only a limited number of solvent molecules to capture the most relevant solute–solvent interactions. However, determining their optimal number, positions, and orientations remains a challenge. Here, we introduce the Free Energy Based Identification of Solvation Sites (FEBISS) 2, a revised microsolvation protocol based on Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory (GIST) applied to molecular dynamics trajectories. The method identifies thermodynamically favorable solvation sites from Free Energy contributions. It automatically places, orients, and ranks solvent molecules by interaction strength. This approach provides a physically grounded criterion for selecting the number of solvent molecules in microsolvated clusters. We demonstrate the applicability of the approach across a range of systems, from small organic molecules to transition-metal catalysts, and for various solvents.

papers.title: Internal conversion in functionalized poly-chlorinated trityl radicals can be tuned by a characteristic high-frequency mode
papers.abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of radiative losses by internal conversion (IC) in a series of doublet radical emitters and diradicals derived from the poly-chlorinated trityl moiety. Minimizing radiative losses of these systems by molecular design is of current interest to opto-electronics and quantum technological approaches. Our results clearly indicate that IC in the doublet emitters as well as in different diradical architectures is governed by a characteristic high-frequency mode, which is associated with a quinoidal stretch. For the doublet emitters, we can establish that deliberate design allows to deactivate this mode as decay channel, resulting in a significantly reduced IC rate and an improved internal luminescence quantum yield. We propose an analogous design principle for highly luminescent diradicals, and discuss the role of a high radiative efficiency in the context of quantum applications.

papers.title: Nitrogen in supramolecular chemistry: Understanding the pervasive role as acceptor of halogen, chalcogen, pnictogen and tetrel bonds
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-centred Lewis bases are well established as nucleophiles in synthetic chemistry, as ligands in coordination chemistry and as pervasive components in hydrogen bonding in chemistry and structural biology. Their role as acceptors of halogen bonds, chalcogen bonds, pnictogen bond and tetrel bonds, collectively described as sigma-hole interactions, is also well established experimentally, but only selectively investigated through exploration of geometric and energetic trends. Here we report a comprehensive study, in which we identify the prevalence of this class of interactions and analyse experimental geometric trends from crystallographic data. These analyses are supported by high-accuracy coupled-cluster quantum chemical calculations of interaction energies and use of symmetry-adapted perturbation theory to examine the underlying energetic contributions. Our focus is on comparison, across the four families of sigma-hole interactions, of the behaviour for Nsp 3 vs. Nsp 2 vs. Nsp hybridisation at the nitrogen atom bearing the lone-pair. Halogen bonds and chalcogen bonds are more abundant than their pnictogen and tetrel bond analogues, whereas interaction prevalence, defined as a proportion of crystal structures containing the necessary interacting groups that then form the corresponding as sigma-hole interaction, tends to be greatest for the heavier congener in each sigma-hole donor group (i.e. I, Te, Sb/Bi, Sn/Pb). The relative prevalence of tetrel bond interactions compared to halogen bond interactions increases from Nsp 3 to Nsp 2 to Nsp acceptors, highlighting the importance of steric demands. The heavier congeners among the sigma-hole donor groups generally form interactions with shorter normalised interaction distances, although this is mitigated by steric interactions, most prominently for tetrel bonds and for Nsp 3 Lewis bases. Preference for linearity with respect to the sigma-hole angle and the angle at the nitrogen lone pair follow the trend Nsp 3 > Nsp 2 > Nsp also as a consequence of steric demands. The broader implications of these comprehensive results in areas such as supramolecular, materials and medicinal chemistry are considered.

papers.title: Tailoring B, N-embedded Helicenes towards Narrowband Circularly Polarized Organic Light-Emitting Diodes
papers.abstract: Owing to their inherently helical π-conjugated frameworks, helicenes are considered promising candidates for circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Nonetheless, their implementation in circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes (CP-OLEDs) remains limited due to difficulties in achieving both high color purity and external quantum efficiency (EQE). Recent advancements incorporate multi-resonance properties with boron-nitrogen units, which have shown significant improvements in this regard. Herein, a chiral emitter ( C 1 ) consisting of 1,4-B,N-embedded helical configuration is studied. C 1 exhibits narrowband fluorescence emission at 510 nm with a full width at half maxima (FWHM) of 23 nm in toluene and 26 nm in thin film. The resolved enantiomers show symmetric CPL, with a dissymmetry factor ( g lum ) of 1.0 × 10 –3 . The solution-processed CP-OLED based on C 1 exhibits external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 5.3%, delivering bright green emission centred at 514 nm with a FWHM of 28 nm. To further enhance the performance of the device, hyperfluorescent (HF) OLEDs are fabricated with C 1 acting as a terminal emitter and BPy-DTC as the TADF sensitizer. The maximum EQE of 13.5% is achieved, with a narrow FWHM of 39 nm. This work highlights the strong potential of helicene-based emitters for application in narrowband CP-OLEDs.

papers.title: A Degradation-Aware Machine Learning/Computational Fluid Dynamics Framework for Spatiotemporal Assessment of Membrane Aging in Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Durability of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a major challenge, as progressive membrane aging alters proton transport and amplifies performance losses at the cell level. Existing computational studies often rely on empirical property correlations and lack direct connection to material-level degradation mechanisms, limiting their ability to capture how membrane aging propagates to system-level behavior. In this work, a degradation-aware machine learning-Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) coupled framework is developed to explicitly link membrane aging with PEMFC performance. Leveraging a dataset derived from coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of Nafion® membranes, proton conductivity is parameterized as a function of temperature, water content, and degradation-induced loss of sulfonic acid groups. A symbolic regression surrogate is embedded into a 3D PEMFC CFD solver, enabling spatially and temporally resolved updates of membrane ionic conductivity under local operating conditions. The coupled framework captures heterogeneous conductivity evolution, reproduces polarization and overpotential behavior, and quantifies power retention under varied operating conditions. By projecting these degradation-aware responses onto operating maps, the model reveals performance-durability trade-offs and identifies conditions under which degradation effects are amplified or mitigated at the cell level. This framework provides a robust tool for designing and optimizing PEMFC operating strategies.

papers.title: Design, synthesis and biological characterization of dual-targeting PROTACs for ataxia telangiectasia and RAD3-related (ATR) and aurora kinase A as chemo-sensitizers for leukemia cells
papers.abstract: The ataxia telangiectasia and RAD3-related (ATR) kinase is a central regulator of DNA damage responses. Its pharmacological degradation by proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represents a promising strategy to sensitize cancer cells to DNA-damaging chemotherapy. It is currently unknown if ATR PROTACs can be pharmacologically designed to target a second cancer-relevant kinase. In this study, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel cereblon (CRBN)-based PROTACs for ATR. Structure-guided design and chemical synthesis enabled the development of a focused library of degraders based on selective ATR inhibitors and optimized CRBN ligands. Among the synthesized compounds, Abd141 turns out as the most promising degrader, showing robust ATR degradation in human leukemia cells, without affecting ATM, WEE1 or DNA-PKcs. Consistently, the developed PROTACs prove activity in an in vitro ATR/ATRIP binding assay. Abd141 exhibits high chemical, microsomal, and plasma stability, and no cytotoxicity in non-cancerous HEK293 cells. Proteomic studies and experiments identify aurora kinase A (AURKA) as additional target of CRBN-induced proteasomal degradation by Abd141. These findings disclose Abd141 as innovative chemo-sensitizer that encourages preclinical development.

papers.title: 2-Triazolylphenols as potent and versatile clicksalicylamide protonophores
papers.abstract: Protonophores are small molecules that facilitate proton transport across lipid bilayers leading to a wide range of therapeutic and research applications. We report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a new class of clickaccessible protonophores based on the 2-triazolylphenol scaffold. The 1,2,3-triazolyl motif acts as an amide isostere and promotes intramolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions that facilitate transmembrane transport of both protonated and deprotonated species. A focused library of derivatives was prepared through copper-catalysed azide–alkyne cycloaddition and characterised by spectroscopic, solution, and solid-state methods. Transmembrane proton transport assays in synthetic vesicles identified several highly active compounds, with the most potent derivatives displaying activities comparable to well-established salicylamide protonophores, including niclosamide. Biological evaluation across a panel of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cell lines confirmed cellular activity and demonstrated mitochondrial uncoupling in respiratory ASPC1 cells. 19 and 24, the most active derivatives identified, induced cytotoxicity across all explored cell lines with distinct cooperativity in respiratory phenotypes under normoxic conditions. The scaffold was further adapted to generate orthonitrobenzyl photocaged protonophores that were inactive in the dark but reactivated efficiently upon blue-light irradiation in liposomal membranes. These results establish 2-triazolylphenols as a synthetically versatile platform for the development of tunable protonophores with potential applications in mitochondrial chemical biology and anticancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Structure Activity Relationship and Antimycobacterial Evaluation of Bromotyrosine 1 Derivative Compounds Produced by Pseudoceratina Sp. Collected from Morotai 2
papers.abstract: 13 14 15 16 Abstract 17 The investigation of anti-tubercular compounds derived from marine organisms has become a 18 priority topic since the global rise in tuberculosis (TB) cases. Marine sponges remain a leading 19 source of bioactive secondary metabolites.
