Pseudoceratina sp., known for producing 20 bromotyrosine compounds, warrants further evaluation through in silico and in vitro evaluation 21 approaches, including Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) evaluation. The in 22 silico study, the three-dimensional (3D) structures of several Mycobacterium tuberculosis target 23 proteins, pantothenate kinase (MtPanK type 1, PDB ID: 4BFT), InhA (MtInhA, PDB ID: 2X23), 24 protein kinase B (PDB ID: 5U94), and β-ketoacyl acyl carrier protein synthase I (MtKasA, PDB 25 ID: 2WGE) were used. The ligands were bromotyrosine-derived compounds identified from the 26 potential fractions of Pseudoceratina sp. In vitro screening of several specimens showed that the 27 extract of Pseudoceratina sp. exhibited promising antimycobacterial activity against 28 Mycobacterium smegmatis. Chromatographic fractions derived from ethyl acetate sub fractions of 29 these sponges showed potential antitubercular agent with MIC value of 31.25 µg/mL. Further 30 separation and characterization using LC-MS/MS and HRMS identified several bromotyrosine-31 derived compounds. This study proved that bromotyrosine derived from Pseudoceratina sp, 32 especially aeroplisinin 1, subereamide A, ethyl N-(2-bromobenzoyl) tryptophanate, and 6-(2-33 bromophenyl)-6,12-dihydro-5H benzo[b]indeno[1,2-e][1,4]thiazepin-5 on, have the potential to 34 be anti-TB compounds. 35

papers.title: Unveiling the protein corona of hydroxyfullerene nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Understanding the biological activity of hydroxylated fullerene nanomaterials in human fluids is essential for translating these platforms toward biomedical use. Here, we report an integrated experimental and computational characterization of the human serum protein corona formed on hydroxyfullerene C60(OH)24 nanoparticles (HFNPs). The HFNP was prepared via bromination of pristine C60 followed by base-promoted hydrolysis and ion-exchange/dialysis purification, and they were validated by elemental analysis and spectroscopic techniques. In aqueous buffer, C60(OH)24 exhibited a bimodal aggregation state (ca. 23 and 164 nm) with a strongly negative zeta potential (about -57 mV); incubation with human serum increased hydrodynamic diameters (ca. 35 and 242 nm), consistent with corona formation observed by TEM. A tightly bound hard corona was isolated by iterative centrifugation and washing, with BCA analysis indicating that only a small fraction of total serum protein remained associated after corona isolation. Label-free LC-MS/MS quantified 424 proteins across serum controls and HFNP samples; although most identifications overlapped, relative abundances shifted markedly, defining a distinct HFNP corona enriched in complement/coagulation factors, apolipoproteins, and immunoglobulin-associated proteins, with human serum albumin strongly depleted. To rationalize adsorption selectivity, molecular docking and binding affinity calculations were performed for corona-enriched proteins (complement C1s, complement C5, complement factor H, plasminogen, and serum amyloid P-component). The molecular modeling studies indicated that binding is dominated by electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding contacts to the hydroxyl shell of C60(OH)24, with arginine and lysine residues overrepresented among interaction hotspots, whereas aromatic π-π contributions are attenuated by surface hydroxylation. Collectively, these results provide a molecular-level framework for predicting and engineering the blood-exposed interactions of hydroxylated fullerene nanomaterials.

papers.title: Unsupervised Diagnosis of Industrial Alarm Patterns Using Topological Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Poorly configured alarm systems generate nuisance alarms that degrade operator effectiveness. The standard diagnostic tools, chattering ratios, alarm flood counts, standing alarm percentages, tell engineers how much of a problem exists but not what kind of behavior produces it. A chattering ratio cannot distinguish random threshold oscillation from sustained cycling driven by a control loop interaction, yet these causes call for different corrective actions. This paper presents an unsupervised method based on persistent homology that extracts structural information from alarm event sequences. Temporal windows of alarm events form a point cloud; its topological invariants, first-order cycles (H1) capturing recurrent patterns, second-order voids (H2) revealing forbidden operating states, map to ISA-18.2 behavioral categories. On the Tennessee Eastman Process benchmark (39,828 events, 20 fault types), the method classifies faults into five behavioral categories. A head-to-head comparison with four ISA-18.2 KPIs shows that 69% of fault pairs sharing the same KPI class are separated by topological features, with a mean Spearman correlation of 0.24 between the two sets of metrics. On a real industrial dataset (444,834 events from 20 packaging machines, 481 days, no labels), the method identifies two machine clusters, detects temporal chattering episodes, and exposes systemic alarm configuration problems across the fleet. Topological features are stable across PCA dimensions, with H1 lifetimes converging within 1% between 50 and 100 components.

papers.title: [18]Annulene as a Model for Charge-Tunable Electron Delocalization and Aromaticity
papers.abstract: Theoretical calculations were performed to probe the charge-modulated π-electron delocalization and aromaticity of [18]annulene. Geometric structure and electronic structure analyses reveal that stepwise reduction progressively improves molecular planarity, C-C bond equalization, and global π-delocalization. Multiple aromaticity criteria consistently indicate that neutral [18]annulene0 is weakly aromatic, dianionic [18]annulene2- exhibits pronounced antiaromaticity, and tetraanionic [18]annulene4- restores strong aromaticity. This work elucidated the intrinsic correlation between charge state and aromaticity, confirming [18]annulene as a robust redox-tunable aromatic model.

papers.title: Fabrication of Porous PVDF/Kenaf Fiber Membranes
papers.abstract: Industrial oily wastewater and oil spill accidents have created an urgent need to address oil leaks, which has encouraged the development of innovative membranes with special wettability for separating oil from water and vice versa. Among various polymeric membranes, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membranes have received significant attention in oily wastewater treatment due to their outstanding properties. In the present work, we report an eco-friendly, low-cost, simple, interconnected porous structure membrane (PVDF) filled with various amounts of kenaf fiber powder (KFP) modified with octadecyltrimethoxysilane (OTMS) via a simple casting method. The resultant membrane possesses superior properties such as superhydrophobicity, superoleophobicity, and a high separation efficiency for water-in-oil mixtures and emulsions, as well as a high separation flux. Moreover, the fabricated membrane remains efficient after 40 cycles of filtration. Therefore, its reusability, combined with its low cost, eco-friendliness, and antifouling properties, makes it suitable for wastewater treatment in industrial applications.

papers.title: q-vSZPs: A polarized, adaptive minimal Gaussian basis set for the elements Z = 1−86 designed for efficient mean-field electronic structure calculations
papers.abstract: We present q-vSZPs, a polarized, environment-adaptive minimal Gaussian basis set parametrized for elements Z = 1− 86 (excluding lanthanides) and designed for efficient mean-field quantum-mechanical calculations on large molecular systems. Building on the previously introduced q-vSZP basis set, the number of primitive functions is substantially reduced while retaining the key feature of charge-and coordination-number-dependent contraction coefficients, which enable environment-dependent “breathing” of the atomic orbitals. The effective atomic charges required for the basis set setup are obtained from the bond-capacity electronegativity equilibration model (EEQ BC ), which accurately reproduces DFT-level Hirshfeld charges at negligible computational cost. Comprehensive benchmarking on the GMTKN55 database demonstrates that q-vSZPs incurs only a moderate loss in accuracy relative to q-vSZP (WTMAD-2 increase of 2.9 kcal·mol −1 ), while substantially outperforming conventional non-adaptive minimal basis sets (MBs). For non-covalent interactions, the performance even surpasses that of the double-ζ def2-SVP basis set, owing to a substantially lower basis set superposition error as a consequence of the molecular optimization strategy. A non-adaptive variant using averaged charges and coordination numbers (q avg -vSZPs) is additionally provided as a drop-in minimal basis for any quantum-chemical program. For a representative 4108-atom system, q-vSZPs achieves a twofold reduction in both SCF walltime and memory consumption for DFT calculations relative to q-vSZP, placing it in the efficiency range of other MBs. The utility of q-vSZPs is further demonstrated through a mixed-basis application for the computation of the Raman spectrum of adenine in water.

papers.title: A Python-Automated Computational Pipeline for Screening Nigella sativa Phytochemicals against the Hantavirus Gn-Gc Tetramer
papers.abstract: Background: Hantaviruses represent a significant global health threat, causing severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, with high case fatality rates and no currently approved specific therapeutics. The viral envelope glycoprotein complex, the Gn-Gc tetramer, mediates host cell entry and represents a prime therapeutic target in its pre-fusion state. Botanical compounds, particularly the bioactive phytochemicals derived from Nigella sativa, offer a promising, underexplored reservoir for antiviral drug discovery. Objective: This study aimed to computationally screen selected Nigella sativa phytochemicals against the pre-fusion Hantavirus Gn-Gc tetramer using a Python-automated structural bioinformatics pipeline to identify potential lead compounds with favorable predicted binding and drug-likeness properties. Methods: An automated, high-throughput virtual screening workflow was developed using Python. The high-resolution target structure of the Hantavirus glycoprotein was prepared, and highly druggable binding pockets were identified using machine-learning-based prediction (P2Rank). A curated library of Nigella sativa phytochemicals was prepared and subjected to molecular docking simulations using AutoDock Vina. Top candidates were further evaluated for pharmacokinetic viability and drug-likeness (Lipinski’s Rule of Five) using RDKit. Finally, non-covalent protein-ligand interactions of the lead complex were mapped to validate structural stability. Results: The screening identified Dithymoquinone as the optimal lead candidate, demonstrating a highly favorable binding affinity of -7.888 kcal/mol. Pose stability analysis confirmed a highly convergent primary binding conformation (RMSD < 2.5 Å). Pharmacokinetic profiling revealed that all tested compounds, including the dimeric Dithymoquinone, exhibited zero violations of Lipinski’s Rule of Five, predicting excellent oral bioavailability and membrane permeability (LogP = 2.71). Interaction profiling of the master complex revealed that Dithymoquinone is securely anchored within the predicted active site through a robust network of specific hydrogen bonds and stabilizing π-stacking interactions with key structural residues. Conclusion Our Python-automated in silico screening pipeline identified Dithymoquinone from Nigella sativa as a promising lead candidate with favorable predicted binding stability and drug-likeness characteristics against the Hantavirus Gn-Gc tetramer. While these findings remain preliminary and require further experimental validation, the study provides a computational and structural framework for future in vitro and in vivo investigations of Dithymoquinone as a potential antiviral candidate targeting Hantavirus entry mechanisms.

papers.title: In Silico Evaluation of Haloalkylated Human 18kDa Translocator Protein PET Tracer Candidates for Traumatic Brain Injury Neuroinflammation
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) associated neuroinflammation, which affects over 50 million worldwide [(1)], progresses gradually from acute (<72 hours) to chronic phases across three cellular sources. Current tracers in human 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) protein [(2)] positron emission tomography (PET) imaging are inadequate because of low blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability and high nonspecific binding in brain tissue, leading to inaccurate neuroinflammation diagnoses in the acute phase. This results in suboptimal patient outcomes. Here we describe the computational prioritization of novel haloalkylated TSPO PET tracer candidates with increased predicted BBB permeability. Eight existing TSPO tracers were ranked through z-score normalisation with emapunil (AC-5216) emerging as the highest-ranked tracer. Emapunil was systematically modified using targeted haloalkylation for two functional groups, with the third being kept as a control. A library of 1,922 analogues was generated and evaluated for lowest predicted docking energy through the CNS-MPO framework. Finally, 17 lead candidates were evaluated for partition coefficients (Kp) and brain–plasma ratios; simulated PET kinetics were calculated via plasma-input graphical Logan analysis to derive predicted total distribution volume (VT). All 17 candidates contained haloalkyl attachments, of which 15 contained a fluorinated side chain, thus supporting the hypothesis that haloalkylation improves brain partitioning in TSPO PET. Pharmacokinetic simulations predicted 5.4× improvements in Kp and 4× improvements in brain–plasma ratio compared to emapunil, consistent with increased BBB permeability. Logan-derived VT estimates remained internally consistent across tested t* values, supporting kinetic feasibility for future experimental validation. These findings hence suggest that novel haloalkylated emapunil analogs may improve predicted CNS exposure and warrant radiosynthesis and labeling, binding studies, and preclinical PET validation.

papers.title: Correlation of Enriched 13C Stable Isotope from Sweeteners to Cancer and Human Diseases
papers.abstract: Recent studies have determined sugar and artificial sweetener consumptions causing various diseases such as cancer, Alzheimer's disease, diabetes, liver disease, kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, Crohn’s disease and cerebrovascular disease. Researchers have attempted to explain the correlations of sweeteners to these diseases based on the ingestion of pure and large amounts of simple sweeteners like xylitol, erythritol, glucose and fructose without accompanying fibers, complex carbohydrates, vitamins, and other nutrients as during their intakes in fruits and vegetables from C3 Plants. Other researchers have reasoned the ill effects of these sweeteners to ultra processing. But the exact steps of ultra processing for causing ill effects have not been identified. This project identifies the fermentation process of C4 plant fuels as producing sweeteners with much higher intrinsic enrichment of 13C stable isotopes as a cause of these diseases due to disease causing properties of 13C isotope. Ironically, the sweetener tagatose has not been measured to contribute to diseases like cancer. In this research, mass spectroscopic methods are used to measure 13C %,

papers.title: Conformationally Constrained Glycosyl Fluoride Donors Enable Chemoselective Glycosylation
papers.abstract: Tuning the relative reactivity of glycosyl donors provides a key approach in the development of iterative glycosylations and convergent oligosaccharide assembly methods. While the sugar identity plays an important role in governing reactivity, strategies that activate or deactivate a donor play a key role in effective approaches. This work focuses on the use of constrained glycosides with cyclic protecting groups to alter the reactivity of glycosyl fluoride donors. Boron-catalyzed glycosylations of glycosyl fluoride donors with silyl ether acceptors can be sequenced by using the constrained glycoside effect to deactivate donors that possess this structural feature. The approach allows constrained glycosyl fluorides to be carried through synthetic steps involving similar donors that lack cyclic protecting groups. Additionally, one pot methods can be designed with sequential additions made possible by the constrained deactivation effect. NMR studies provide a simple mechanistic tool for quickly assessing the magnitude of reactivity changes imparted by a given substrate modification.

papers.title: Topological Path Bifurcation and Braid Invariants in the Conformational Dynamics of 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13, 16-Octamethoxytetraphenylene
papers.abstract: The macro-conformational saddle-to-saddle inversion of 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13, 16-octamethoxytetraphenylene (8-OMe-TP) presents a complex kinematic challenge due to the intense steric clashing of its eight peripheral substituents during core flattening. Traditionally evaluated via computationally exhaustive electronic structure simulations, the underlying geometric principles governing these multi-particle trajectories have remained obscured. Here, we present a pure mathematical framework that maps the dynamic inversion of 8-OMe-TP onto lowdimensional topology. By tracking the non-colliding trajectories of the eight methoxy groups within the ordered configuration space F8(R3), we linearize the kinematic history using the Artin braid group (B8) and the unreduced Burau representation. Our algebraic reduction reveals a hidden topological path bifurcation dictated by the molecule’s intrinsic D2d point group symmetry. The total spatiotemporal pathways are quantized into distinct, non-isotopic domains characterized by unique scalar matrix invariants: a cooperative symmetric pathway (Route A) yielding a Burau matrix trace of 5 + 0j, and a non-cooperative sequential pathway (Route B) yielding 7 + 0j. The absence of an imaginary component mathematically proves the perfect topological reversibility of the inversion without hysteresis. Furthermore, we establish a predictive scaling law linking these discrete braid complexities directly to physical activation free energy barriers (∆G‡). This pure algebraic approach establishes a powerful theoretical complement to all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, enabling the pre-synthetic tuning of flexible polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and molecular switches based on topological invariants.

papers.title: Computational Identification of Natural Product Modulators Targeting PTPN6 in the Ferroptosis-Immune Axis of Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion: An Integrated Bioinformatic, Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) affects 2-5% of couples of reproductive age, and roughly half of all cases lack a molecular explanation. Recent evidence points to ferroptosis, iron-dependent, lipid-peroxide-driven death of decidual stromal cells and trophoblasts, as a key driver of the pathology, yet no small molecules targeting the pathway have been described. The question is whether PTPN6 (SHP-1), a ferroptosis-linked phosphatase reported as a hub gene in RSA endometrial transcriptomes, could be targeted by natural products. Differentially expressed genes from the publicly available GSE165004 microarray cohort were overlapped with the FerrDb V3 ferroptosis-driver list and ranked by cytoHubba degree centrality, which confirmed PTPN6 as a top-scoring hub and the chosen structural target. The COCONUT 2.0 natural-product collection (~430,000 compounds) was reduced by Lipinski filtering and a DataWarrior Tanimoto similarity search against the co-crystallized reference ligand of PDB 4GS0; the survivors were docked into the catalytic site through Glide HTVS → SP → XP and rescored with Prime MM-GBSA. Seven natural products came through this cascade, two of which bound more favorably than the native reference. Post-docking screening of ADMET and toxicity profiles (ADMETlab 3.0, ProTox 3.0) singled out CNP0242013, a prenylated dihydroxybenzoic acid, as the lead with the cleanest predicted safety profile. Across a 100 ns explicit-solvent Desmond MD trajectory, the CNP0242013-PTPN6 complex stayed anchored at the catalytic P-loop with a backbone Cα RMSD of 1.89 Å to 2.47 Å, and projection of the trajectory onto the first two principal components revealed a single, sharply defined free-energy minimum. CNP0242013 thus offers a starting point for experimental work on SHP-1 inhibition in ferroptosis-driven miscarriage.

papers.title: Single-atom replacement unlocks iso-pseudoprolines as minimalist proline bioisosteres for peptide detection and late-stage functionalisation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in chemical synthesis have accelerated the growth of peptide therapeutics, with structural and functional fine-tuning an essential prerequisite for lead candidate selection. In contrast to the exhaustive strategies employed in medicinal chemistry campaigns, tools for investigating peptide activity and localisation are comparatively overlooked. Classical reporters such as fluorophores often have large chemical footprints that perturb peptide structure and function, underscoring an urgent need for minimalist probes. Here, we showcase that bioisosteric amino acid replacements, containing single-heteroatom substitutions, are powerful tools for biological interrogation. By embedding the iso-pseudoprolines, 2-thiaproline and 2-selenaproline, into three distinct peptide case studies, we systematically establish their role as proline bioisosteres. We apply these residues as novel tags for peptide monitoring in a cellular environment via mass cytometry, and leverage their intrinsic reactivity for late-stage chemical functionalisation using a mild, radical-mediated process. Iso-pseudoprolines are therefore established as valuable, minimally perturbing tools for peptide detection and functionalisation.

papers.title: Sea Cucumbers Inspired Phase Separation-Assisted Nano-Confinement Enables Ultrawide Mechanical Modulation in Nanocomposite Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Sea cucumbers can rapidly switch their bodies from a soft, deformable state to a stiff, rigid one within seconds in response to mechanical stimulation or threat, through the reversible regulation of interfibrillar connectivity and resistance to fibrillar sliding within the extracellular matrix. Inspired by such dynamically adaptive biological mechanism, smart hydrogels hold great promise for mimicking living tissues. However, achieving broad-range and rapid regulation of multiple mechanical properties, particularly stiffness and toughness, remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a phase separation-assisted nano-confinement strategy that enables ultrawide mechanical modulation of nanocomposite hydrogels. Upon solvent-induced phase separation, nanofillers are preferentially accumulate and orient within the polymer-rich domains. This process not only promotes the densification of the polymer matrix but also substantially enhances nanofiller–matrix interfacial interactions. Consequently, the resulting nanocomposite hydrogels exhibit tunable stiffness over four orders of magnitude (from ~10-2 to ~102 MPa) and a two order of magnitude increase in toughness (up to 173 fold), achieving an exceptional combination of high strength and high toughness. This approach opens up new avenues for the design of adaptive materials of applications in flexible electronics, soft robotics, and beyond.

papers.title: Nucleobase tethered conjugated polymers: insights from post-polymerization modification
papers.abstract: Assessing the influence of supramolecular crosslinkers within a conjugated polymer network is difficult due to being convoluted by the presence of π-π interactions, the degree of which varies across polymer batches when molecular weight distributions and monomer composition inevitably vary. Here, we implement the strategy of post-polymerization modification to a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) and benzothiadiazole (BT) copolymer, for the attachment of sidechains with tethered hydrogen bonding motifs. By comparison of the parent polymer with its functionalized counterpart, thermal analysis revealed that addition of thymine nucleobases into the material resulted in disrupted ordering in the bulk polymer and in thin films. Grazing incidence wide angle scattering (GIWAXS) patterns were studied in parallel with characterization of organic field effect transistors (OFETs) to correlate changes in microstructural order with charge carrier mobility in as-cast and thermally annealed films. These insights provide a foundation for the rational selection of hydrogen bonding motifs in conjugated polymers and enable the systematic study of functionalized materials for wearable electronic applications.

papers.title: Cumulene-Based Conjugated Microporous Polymers
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional C(sp)-rich conjugated microporous polymers, including graph(di)ynes, have fascinated chemists due to their unique material properties and expeditious synthesis. While all existing examples are based on acetylene units, their ground-state quinoidal counterparts featuring cumulene linkages have surprisingly remained unexplored. Here, we report an interfacial condensation polymerization of trifunctional propargylic electrophiles (iCPPE), enabling the bottom-up assembly of [5]cumulene-linked conjugated microporous polymers ([5]C-CMPs). This method yields centimeter-scale, free-standing thin films that can be exfoliated into ~10 nm thick nanosheets. The rigid framework stabilizes the cumulene moieties, resulting in high porosity (specific surface area up to 486.3 m2/g), a narrow bandgap (1.32 eV), and a triplet ground state, which stand in sharp contrast to those of their alkyne-based analogues. Benefiting from their open-shell character and fast non-radiative relaxation, [5]C-CMPs achieve a photothermal conversion efficiency of up to 75%. This work establishes a distinct redox-neutral strategy for constructing lowdimensional carbon-rich materials with unique optoelectronic and magnetic properties.

papers.title: Coordinate-Free SciML Reveals Sequence-Dependent Emergent Electronic and Spin Regimes in Peri-Metalated Polyacenes
papers.abstract: Rigid carbon frameworks in organic semiconductors restrict the tunability of their electronic and spin properties. Peri-metalation of polyacenes with coinage metals, particularly gold and copper, offers a route to electronic regimes not attainable in conventional organic systems, yet navigating this hybrid space often requires exhaustive quantum-chemical sampling. This study integrates density functional theory with an interpretable scientific machine-learning (SciML) framework to show that global electronic trends, including bandgaps, ionization energies, and electron affinities, can be captured by minimalist, coordinate-free descriptors. By circumventing explicit structural or electronicstructure input, the resulting models achieve robust, chemically meaningful extrapolation across the polyacene series, while remaining sensitive to localized sequence-dependent effects. Structured deviations between ML predictions and DFT calculations are shown to serve as a physical diagnostic tool, identifying the onset of electronically complex regimes. While gold-metalation yields stable, predictable electronic structures, copperincorporation drives the system into "emergent" regimes characterized by extreme bandgap narrowing and near-degenerate singlet–triplet states. This work establishes a framework in which machine-learning performance itself marks the boundary of simple chemical trends, offering a rational approach to the discovery of low-bandgap, spinsensitive hybrid semiconductors.

papers.title: Catalytically promiscuous PLP-dependent aminotransferases are biocatalysts for C–C bond formation
papers.abstract: Access to non-canonical amino acids is increasingly important in natural products synthesis and drug discovery. Enzymatic synthesis has emerged as an efficient strategy for simplifying approaches towards these molecules. Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzymes have been extensively studied for the biocatalytic functionalization of α-amino acids. However, the high substrate specificity of these enzymes has limited the substrate scope of PLP-mediated biocatalysis. Efforts to identify generalist catalysts may be enabled by catalytic promiscuity, a property well-known in the PLP-dependent enzyme family. In pursuit of PLPcatalyzed C–C bond formation, we leverage a cofactor-centric approach with PLP-dependent enzymes not previously known to mediate C–C bond formation to access key nucleophilic intermediates. In this work, we show that aminotransferases Aro8 and TyrB can mediate C–C bond formation, the first such activity reported for aminotransferases. Further, this non-native function can be improved by the addition of a sacrificial ketoacid. Interestingly, Aro8 and TyrB exhibit distinct conformational dynamics that impact the diastereoselectivity of the reaction. These results indicate that aminotransferases are an untapped resource for the discovery of new biocatalysts for C–C bond formation and demonstrate the value of cofactor-guided reaction discovery.

papers.title: Reorganizing Periodicity: A New Classification of the Periodic Table of the Elements
papers.abstract: The periodic table of the elements is a fundamental brick in the foundation of chemistry. The current periodic table arranges elements in the increasing order of their atomic numbers and successfully classify them but it is not optimal when it come to display the continuity in the periodic trends of the physicochemical properties. Herein, a new classification system is proposed in which elements are classified according to the nature of their periodicity. This model proposes that s- and p-block elements show primary periodicity, d-block elements display a different secondary periodicity controlled by ns and (n-1)d orbital filling and f-block elements show tertiary periodicity governed by gradual filling of f-orbital. Therefore, d-block elements are placed separately under the s-and p-block elements. This table can also provide a placement for predicted g-block elements. The purpose of this classification is not to replace the conventional periodic table, but to present it as a chemical-periodicity table. It may exhibit improved periodic trends across periods and can be a handy tool for education, as well as future discussion of periodic table extension.

papers.title: Nanoscale Growth Mechanisms of Gypsum: Implications for Environmental Control of Crystal Habits
papers.abstract: Gypsum precipitation is a common process observed in diverse natural settings, offering valuable insights into (paleo)environmental conditions. It also holds significant industrial value, notably in wallboard production. However, its precipitation also poses severe challenges, for example, during water desalination. Despite numerous experimental and computational studies on gypsum since the late 19th century, the growth behavior and crystal habit remain poorly understood. In this work, we studied the nanoscale growth mechanisms controlling the formation of gypsum crystals from supersaturated solutions. We developed a method for obtaining oriented samples of natural idiomorphic gypsum crystals, enabling atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging and microtopography characterization of all facets. Using this novel approach we (re-)examined the extensively studied {010} form, and, for the first time, the {120}, {-111}, and {011} forms. Remarkably, each form is dominated by a specific growth behavior, including cluster-mediated growth for {010}, stepped face growth for {120}, 2D nucleation and spiral growth for the {-111} form, and rough growth for {011}. These experimental findings differ from theoretical predictions, where all four forms are considered flat faces (F faces). We further demonstrate that the interplay between growth mechanisms of different forms, and the control that external factors exert on these, are the two key factors that dictate the crystal habit. Overall, this study establishes a framework for linking gypsum crystal morphology to the prevailing environmental conditions during growth. This understanding is critical not only for comprehending gypsum deposit formation in the geological record but also for the processing of advanced geomaterials and more effective anti-scaling strategies.

papers.title: Estimating Memory Time within the Frameworks of Generalized Quantum Master Equation and Transfer Tensor Methods
papers.abstract: Simulating long-time nonadiabatic dynamics in condensed-phase systems is computationally demanding due to the inherent non-Markovianity of the electronic reduced density matrix evolution. While the generalized quantum master equation (GQME) and transfer tensor method (TTM) allow for the reconstruction of long-time dynamics from short-time projection-free inputs, their accuracy hinges on the rigorous estimation of the memory time, a parameter often determined by heuristic trial-and-error. In this work, we establish a comprehensive framework for estimating memory time and benchmarking propagation accuracy using semiclassical and numerical exact inputs on both standard spin-boson models and general multistate harmonic (MSH) models. We develop an error estimation scheme that reveals a characteristic three-stage decay pattern in the non-Markovian propagation error: an initial transient drop, an exponential decay, and a saturation plateau. This estimator serves as a critical diagnostic tool for GQME and TTM, successfully distinguishing between converged predictions and reliability failures in complex systems, such as the carotenoid-porphyrin-fullerene triad. These findings provide a robust, quantitative protocol for validating memory-kernel-based simulations of nonadiabatic dynamics.

papers.title: Depth-aware machine learning for 3D reconstruction of fibrous porous polymers by FIB-SEM tomography
papers.abstract: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily recon-struct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-ofplane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interfacial area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on real-scale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate exposed polymer crosssections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB–SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electro-spun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quan-titative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore diameter, fiber volume ratio, and copper-depth distribution metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labelled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure–property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

papers.title: Sustainable Circular Utilization of Natural Lepidolite for Low-Voltage Li-Ion Battery Anode and Energy Harvesting
papers.abstract: Conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) with graphite anodes suffer from poor rate performance and lithium dendrite formation, limiting their practical applications. In this work, a lithium-rich layered material, Lepidolite, which exfoliates into two-dimensional flakes, is introduced as a high-performance anode. It delivers a reversible capacity of ~121 mAh g-1 at 200 mA g-1, with high-rate performance at higher current densities (~104.5 mAh g-1 at 500 mA g-1) during lithium intercalation at a low potential (<1.5 V), and exhibits ultra-long rate-cycling stability exceeding 9200 cycles at various current densities. Ex-situ TEM, XPS, and TOF-SIMS analyses reveal the evolution and stability of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) during extended cycling. A full-cell LIB with LiFePO4 as the cathode demonstrates stable operation, while spent Lepidolite electrodes are repurposed for energy harvesting, highlighting sustainable reuse. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that reduced surface oxygen atoms enhance metallicity, thereby increasing the density of states near the Fermi level, which is favorable for Li adsorption. This study demonstrates the sustainable circular utilization of Lepidolite for energy storage and harvesting.

papers.title: Barrel Shape and Chromophore Rigidity Predict Fluorescent-Protein Photophysics
papers.abstract: The 11-stranded β-barrel of fluorescent proteins (FPs) is universally conserved, yet its quantitative geometry has not been systematically characterized. We analyzed cross-sectional barrel geometry across 908 FP crystal structures in the RCSB PDB by PCA-based axis determination and convex hull analysis of protein-atom slices at the chromophore plane, of which 780 structures form the canonical analysis cohort. Barrel shape, but not size, correlates with emission wavelength: red-shifted proteins have narrower, more elliptical barrels (ρ = –0.328 for minor axis, p = 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁷). The chromophore-to-scaffold B-factor ratio is the strongest predictor of quantum yield (ρ = –0.446, p < 10⁻¹³). Chromophore dihedral angles correlate with both barrel eccentricity and photophysical performance. Principal correlations survive Benjamini–Hochberg correction and partial correlation controlling for resolution. The barrel is not a passive scaffold: together with chromophore rigidity it shapes photophysical output. The pipeline was developed with Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code.

papers.title: (Hetero)adamantane synthesis: A triple alkylation reaction
papers.abstract: (Hetero)adamantanes containing tetrel bridgeheads are important structures in surface and chemical sciences. Syntheses of diamondoid structures generally occur in a linear fashion, often using harsh conditions. These limitations make it difficult to access diverse (hetero)adamantane-based molecules with interchangeable functional groups for broad applications. The discovery of an expedient and convergent methodology for the synthesis of diamondoid scaffolds is described. The convenient synthetic route proceeding via a triple alkylation reaction represents a breakthrough in accessing the adamantane molecular class. Applications of this transformation to diamondoid tripods containing tetrel bridgeheads (C- and Ge-) were explored.

papers.title: Generative Active Learning for Molecular Design with REINVENT: Balancing Binding Affinity and Synthetic Accessibility
papers.abstract: We present a generative active learning (GAL) framework for molecular design that integrates the generative AI platform REINVENT with physics-based free-energy estimation via ESMACS, specifically addressing synthetic tractability. In a previous study we have shown that iterative generation and optimization of molecules for protein binding affinity can be effectively achieved. For drug discovery, however, molecules need to be synthesized for experimental validation. Molecules with unclear synthetic routes will be de-prioritized regardless of their predicted binding affinity. Here, we address this by incorporating additional synthesizability constraints into the computational design process, framing the problem as a multi-objective optimization task. We show that it is possible to simultaneously optimize candidate molecules for both binding affinity and synthetic accessibility. Our results show that integrating synthesizability prediction into physics-based GAL workflows enables the efficient design of compounds that are chemically diverse and predicted to be strong binders and synthetically tractable at the same time, demonstrating efficient and practical computational drug design.

papers.title: Semiconducting Covalent Organic Frameworks based on Trioxotriangulene Neutral Radicals
papers.abstract: Electrically conductive two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) have emerged as a versatile class of crystalline porous polymers with promising applications in electronics and energy storage. However, high conductivities are typically achieved via post-synthetic doping to generate charge carriers, which can compromise crystallinity, porosity, and structural homogeneity. Persistent neutral radical conductors provide an attractive alternative, as their unpaired electrons can generate free charge carriers without the need for counterions. Nevertheless, the incorporation of highly delocalized p-radicals into COFs remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of imine-linked 2D COFs incorporating spin-delocalized trioxotriangulene (TOT) neutral radicals through two complementary synthetic approaches. Direct use of a TOT radical derivative functionalized with free amine groups affords a highly crystalline framework (TOT-COF-H) that exhibits semiconducting behavior (s RT = 1.2 × 10 -4 S cm -1 ), a reduced band gap ( E g = 1.09 eV), and low activation energy (0.24 eV). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for integrating spin-delocalized neutral radical building blocks into COFs, enabling the development of intrinsically conductive, porous, and crystalline organic frameworks without the need for extrinsic doping.

papers.title: Practical Machine Learning Strategies. 5. Rapid, Accurate Prediction of 1H and 13C NMR Shifts in Conformationally Flexible Organic Molecules
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of NMR chemical shifts for conformationally flexible natural products remains a central challenge in structure elucidation. Traditional quantum‑chemical (QM) approaches typically achieve ≈2.0–3.0 ppm 13 C accuracy for flexible natural products but often require hours of computation per molecule. MLHF‑NMR reproduces high‑level QM 13 C accuracy for flexible molecules while reducing computation times by factors of hundreds to more than a thousand, enabling routine, high‑throughput NMR prediction for conformationally flexible natural products. Against the high‑accuracy DELTA50 experimental 1 H and 13C shift benchmark, MLHF‑NMR achieves RMS errors of 0.15 ppm ( 1 H) and 1.73 ppm ( 13 C). Across more than 8.2k 13 C chemical shifts from 420 predominantly flexible natural products, the protocol yields an average RMS error of 2.23 ppm. Practical applications include structure assignment for newly isolated natural products, structure confirmation in independently synthesized molecules, rapid detection and correction of misassignments, and strategies for improving predicted 13C shift accuracy. Validation sets and sample MLHF‑NMR 13 C shift predictions for more than 1900 synthetic drugs and drug‑like molecules are available at https://mlnmr.wavefun.com. For flexible molecules, MLHF‑NMR routinely delivers 13 C shift accuracy comparable to the best QM methods while reducing computation time by 2–3 orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Atomic Periodicity as Spectral Structure
papers.abstract: The periodic system was established from trends in atomic weight and chemical behavior and later explained through electronic structure models, but it has not been derived directly from atomic observables without prior chemical or theoretical knowledge. Here we show that atomic spectra alone encode the full organization of the periodic table. Frequency-domain analysis reveals that elements occupy a bounded spectral space governed by hierarchical scaling between K-edge (𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 ) and first ionization frequencies. Elements organize into spectral bands (periods) and parallel power law trajectories (groups). Periodic differentiation emerges from bifurcation of spectral modes, and periodic bandwidth (Δ 𝑝 ) contracts following Δ 𝑝 ∝ 𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 −1.19 (R 2 = 0.9995), establishing a fundamental limit on elemental differentiation. Substituting atomic number for K-edge does not reproduce this organization, indicating that the spectral domain represents the natural scaling coordinate for periodic structure. This two-parameter framework provides an empirical resolution to longstanding classification questions and enables prediction using spectral scaling relations. Leave-one-out cross-validation yields median prediction errors of 1.1% for measured first ionization frequencies and 2.1% for covalent radii, with lanthanide-series prediction errors below 0.3%. Extending these predictions to elements with incomplete data yields new covalent radii for actinium and lawrencium, and ionization frequency for praseodymium. The same two-parameter spectral structure also organizes different types of conductivity and magnetism, from which superconducting behavior is predicted for chromium and silver.

papers.title: Reaction-aware control of autonomous batch synthesis
papers.abstract: Autonomous experimentation is transforming materials discovery; however, information gained from widely used batch synthesis and characterization workflows is limited by endpoint measurements and fixed robotic protocols that treat chemical reactions as black boxes. Here, we introduce a reaction-aware autonomous framework that incorporates crystallization trajectories into the adaptive experimental design, enabling kinetics-informed decision-making in self-driving laboratories. These trajectories, collected through in situ optical monitoring, are converted into kinetic descriptors that simultaneously adapt measurement intervals, batch sizes, and formulation variables. Using the solution-phase crystallization of ZIF-67 as a model system, we built a DIY robot that autonomously identified synthesis conditions yielding nucleation rates over five-fold higher than static maximin sampling while tripling information gains per experiment. This work showcases a new design principle for autonomous experimentation: measurement protocols are not passive settings, but active components of the decision-making process that determine how a closed-loop system observes, interprets, and optimizes a reaction landscape.

papers.title: Generative Virtual Screening: From Search to Generate and Back
papers.abstract: A key challenge in drug discovery is the efficient search of chemical space to identify small molecules with desirable biological activity and developability. Computational approaches address this challenge by applying in silico evaluators to prioritise compounds for experimental validation. Traditionally, this has been achieved through brute-force virtual screening of large, predefined compound libraries. More recently, advances in generative molecular design (GMD) have enabled models that directly propose molecules optimised for specific objectives. GMD offers favourable computational cost but often at the expense of progressability, evaluability, and synthetic feasibility. In this review, we analyse molecular search strategies across a spectrum ranging from brute-force search to de novo generative design, focusing on how chemical space is specified and explored. We emphasise three practical axes—computational cost, progressability, and evaluability—and discuss how different paradigms trade off these properties. In particular, we highlight Generative Virtual Screening (GVS) as a hybrid approach in which generative optimisation is constrained to a fixed, explicit compound library. GVS combines the computational efficiency of generative methods with the progressability and retrospective evaluability of library-based search. This enables scalable exploration of chemical space while providing ground-truth reference points for algorithmic assessment. We argue that GVS offers both immediate practical benefits for hit discovery and a controlled framework for developing and benchmarking generative search algorithms, facilitating their principled extension to broader and less constrained chemical spaces.

papers.title: A unified framework for automated transition state generation to accelerate mechanistic exploration in organic synthesis
papers.abstract: Accurate generation of intricate 3D molecular structures is a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry. Transition states (TS), the transient structures that dictate reaction kinetics, exemplify this challenge, as their calculation remains a major bottleneck in elucidating reaction mechanisms. While generative AI has shown promise in automating TS generation, existing methods are largely confined to simple systems, struggling with the complex structures like those in transition metal catalysis. Here, we present a unified framework for general-purpose TS generation, comprising the UniTS-Lib library of 4,391 high-quality structures spanning 42 elements and diverse chemical transformations, coupled with the UniTS-Gen diffusion model that generates 3D TS configurations from 2D reactant graphs using a novel higher-degree equivariant network. Validation demonstrates UniTS-Gen’s superior accuracy and robust generalization to unseen chemical systems. We show that UniTS-Gen provides reliable initial guesses and accelerates discovery by locating kinetically favored conformation. This work provides a scalable and transferable solution for automating mechanistic studies in organic synthesis and a model applicable to broader computational structure generation tasks.

papers.title: Enantioselective Hydrogen Atom Relay via Non-covalent Catalyst Assembly
papers.abstract: Most biological functions are regulated by chiral molecules 1 that contain at least one tertiary stereogenic carbon, i.e., a carbon with one C(sp 3 )–H bond. Hydrogen Atom Transfer (HAT) 2 is a straightforward strategy to either edit 3 or introduce tertiary stereocenters in multiple synthetically useful transformations, 4 especially when coupled with photoredox catalysis. 5,6 However, traditional de novo designs of chiral HAT catalysts that provide sufficient enantiocontrol over short-lived open-shell intermediates, 7 have represented a major hurdle for the development of enantioselective HAT reactions. Here, we describe a distinct approach in which chiral HAT catalysts are obtained in situ by non-covalent self-assembly of privileged chiral phosphoric acids and commercial 2-mercaptopyridines. The phosphoric acid serves as a modular interchangeable chiral element that renders the achiral thiol effectively chiral, thereby allowing for a previously inaccessible combinatorial space of chiral HAT catalysts. This platform enabled the photochemical deracemization of 2-aryl pyrrolidines, a prevalent scaffold in active pharmaceutical ingredients. Optical enrichment occurs via enantioselective hydrogen atom relay, in which a single chiral assembly orchestrates hydrogen atom abstraction and delivery. This conceptual approach of relaying chiral information via non-covalent assembly paves the way for the discovery of numerous asymmetric radical transformations.

papers.title: Large-Scale Virtual Screening Prioritizes Candidate Allosteric Modulators of TIMP2: Computational Identification and Structural Characterization of a Cryptic Binding Site
papers.abstract: Background : Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-2 (TIMP2) has emerged as a critical regulator of synaptic plasticity and cognitive function through its role in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Recent evidence suggests that enhancing TIMP2 function, rather than inhibiting it, may offer therapeutic benefits for cognitive enhancement and neuroplasticity. However, TIMP2 has historically been considered "undruggable" due to its protein-protein interaction mechanism and lack of traditional binding pockets. Methods : We performed a large-scale virtual screening campaign using a CNS-filtered subset of the ZINC20 database. Starting from ~1 billion molecules, we applied strict CNS drug-likeness filters (MW: 250-430 Da, TPSA ≤70 Å², HBD ≤1, cLogP: 2.0-3.5), resulting in 13.6 million candidates distributed across 136 chunks. Using AutoDock Vina with an adaptive parallelization strategy, we screened six strategically selected representative chunks totaling ~600,000 molecules against TIMP2 (PDB: 1BR9), targeting both canonical and potential cryptic binding sites. Results : Virtual screening of six completed chunks (~600,000 molecules) identified a cryptic allosteric site involving residues Val6, Leu100, and Phe103 in TIMP2's N-terminal domain. From ~11,500 compounds meeting initial CNS and PAINS criteria, comprehensive ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI v2.1 revealed only 178 compounds (1.5%) achieving Tier 1 safety classification. Orthogonal toxicity validation using ProTox-III further refined this set to 154 highest-confidence candidates (Tier 1A, 86.5%), with 22 compounds (12.4%) requiring enhanced monitoring due to borderline acute toxicity (Tier 1B) and 2 compounds (1.1%) deprioritized due to extreme LD50 predictions (Tier 1C). Chunk-level survival rates varied dramatically from 0.3% (strict_0055) to 9.3% (strict_0028), with strict_0028 yielding the majority (52%) of all Tier 1 compounds. Notably, while halogenation is common (41.6% of Tier 1 compounds), it is not universal, with strict_0028 demonstrating that non-halogenated compounds can also achieve favorable ADMET profiles. The best overall compound (ZINC000870248439_1, -9.0 kcal/mol from strict_0120) and the largest chemical family (93 compounds from strict_0028, including both chlorinated and non-halogenated scaffolds) demonstrated excellent CNS penetration (BBB >0.9) and clean safety profiles. Conclusions : This work represents the first systematic computational prioritization of candidate small molecule TIMP2 modulators, revealing a previously uncharacterized cryptic binding site that can accommodate diverse chemical scaffolds. Integration of ADMET-AI and ProTox-III predictions enabled refined risk stratification, yielding 154 highest-confidence candidates validated across orthogonal computational toxicology platforms. The dramatic variation in ADMET survival rates across chunks (0.3-9.3%) highlights the importance of broad chemical space sampling. While halogenation enhances certain drug-like properties, our results demonstrate that both halogenated and non-halogenated compounds can achieve the demanding intersection of high affinity, CNS penetration, and drug safety. Structural validation using the AlphaFold v6 predicted structure confirmed the cryptic allosteric pocket with sub-angstrom accuracy (mean Cα deviation = 0.30 Å, triad pLDDT > 96), and cross-species conservation analysis revealed 100% pocket identity in mouse TIMP2, the primary translational model. Molecular dynamics simulation (100 ns apo) confirmed pocket stability under physiological conditions with 94% area preservation, sub-angstrom per-residue fluctuations (triad RMSF = 0.84 Å), and convergence of triad distances to within 0.14-0.43 Å of crystallographic values. Ligand-bound MD of three representative compounds revealed compound-specific binding stability, with residence times ranging from <7 ns to approximately 20 ns, demonstrating that the pocket supports transient small molecule binding but that chemical optimization beyond initial docking predictions will be required for stable occupancy. These findings support TIMP2 as a potentially tractable drug target and provide 154 computationally validated chemical starting points across diverse scaffolds for experimental follow-up.

papers.title: Benchmark of double-ended transition state search methods for metal-catalysed reactions
papers.abstract: Efficient and reliable identification of transition states (TS) is critical for reaction modelling. Among the available approaches, the combination of double-ended TS search with eigenvector-following, referred to as “hierarchical TS search”, is an effective tool for locating TSs starting from reactant and product geometries. However, there has been limited systematic benchmarking of these methods on transition metal-catalysed reactions. Here, we benchmark eight hierarchical double-ended methods using out-of-the-box settings on a diverse set of 30 metal-catalysed reactions, evaluating their success rate and computational efficiency. The results reveal three key trends: (i) the final eigenvector-following step requires an accurate Hessian matrix or explicitly calculated min-mode for a high success rate, (ii) TS searches from interpolation-only paths (e.g. image-dependent pair potential, IDPP) and bracket methods (e.g. Dewar-Healy-Stewart, DHS) are often more efficient than popular methods, such as climbing image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB), (iii) starting from the same two minima, different hierarchical methods may find different TSs. Furthermore, we observe a correlation be- tween the similarity of reactant and product geometries and both the success rate and computational cost. We also show that using coarser convergence criteria with energy- weighted CI-NEB can reduce computational expense without reducing the success rate on our dataset. These findings indicate that double-ended methods are effective for transition state searches in metal-catalysed systems and that underutilised methods hold promise for integration into TS search workflows. These conclusions are further supported by two case studies involving industrially relevant organometallic reactions.

papers.title: Beyond Vibes: Preserving Learning While Embracing AI-Assisted Coding in STEM Education
papers.abstract: Generative AI tools that write and debug code are rapidly becoming standard in scientific, technical, and data-driven workplaces. Higher education should respond not by banning these tools, but by integrating them in ways that preserve deep student learning, build student agency, and reflect professional practice. This article offers a practical framework for faculty who want students to use AI to write code in STEM courses ranging from lab courses with analysis and data visualization components, to disciplines transitioning from tools like Excel or SPSS to scalable open-source Python workflows. These insights are grounded in 12+ years of research experience in AI applications in physical chemistry, computational chemistry, and biophysics, and 6 years of experience as a university professor teaching both a Python-based data analysis course for chemistry majors and a technical communication course for chemists where AI tools were used to support student learning and skill development. Key recommendations include pairing AI-assisted, project-based learning with short form, 1-on-1, code review-style oral exams during which students must be able to explain every line of their code, and ensuring that students achieve conceptual mastery of core programming principles that can be overlooked when relying on AI code generation (e.g. data types of variables, inputs, and outputs, principled use of methods and attributes from Python objects, etc.). These strategies aim to prevent cognitive offloading of essential conceptual knowledge, which is a significant risk associated with “vibe coding,” where students rely on AI to generate code without understanding it themselves, while still enabling students to build domain-specific AI fluency that is required in an increasingly AI-driven economy.

papers.title: Triethanolamine promotes formate selectivity in aqueous CO2 reduction by immobilized Mn(bpy)(CO)3Br catalyst
papers.abstract: CO2 capture and electrochemical conversion is a sustainable and circular process to produce carbon-based chemicals. Capture of CO2 can be achieved with amine based capturing agents, which have been reported in combination with homogeneous catalysts in solution. The amines can have a range of effects on the CO2 reduction catalysis, depending on how they bind CO2, interact with the protic environment and with the catalyst, among other effects. Among the homogeneous catalysts, Mn(bpy)(CO)3Br is a well-studied catalyst that can selectively produce carbon monoxide (CO) or formate (HCOO-), depending on the conditions. It has been demonstrated that the presence of amines can promote the selective formation of formic acid. In this work, Mn(bpy)(CO)3Br is immobilized on an electrode via supramolecular interactions. The resulting material was studied in electrochemical CO2 reduction under aqueous conditions with and without triethanolamine present as a CO2 capturing agent. We demonstrate that the presence of TEOA causes two effects: (1) a two-fold increased catalytic activity in TON and (2) an increased selectivity for formate, from 25% to 60% Faraday efficiency. It shows that TEOA is an excellent additive for such catalytic systems and demonstrates the potential of expanding such catalytic systems to become even more active and selectivity for aqueous CO2 reduction.

papers.title: Curvature-assisted minima hopping on Lennard-Jones energy landscapes: reusingquasi-Newton information for escape directions
papers.abstract: Global structure optimization in computational chemistry is often limited by the cost of escaping local minima on high-dimensional potential-energy surfaces. Minima hopping addresses this problem by combining short molecular-dynamics escape trajectories with local relaxation and adaptive energy feedback, but its efficiency depends strongly on the initial escape direction. We benchmark a curvature-assisted variant in which the approximate inverse-Hessian information that BFGS and limited-memory BFGS build from the gradients already required for relaxation is recycled as an escape model. This avoids explicit second derivatives and adds no force evaluations before proposing low-curvature escape directions. Lennard-Jones clusters with 60–74 particles provide controlled energy landscapes for comparing conjugate-gradient, BFGS, and limited-memory BFGS minimizers, random and softened random directions, single Hessian modes, multi-mode Hessian combinations, and mixed Hessian-random directions. The results show that dense BFGS curvature information identifies physically meaningful escape subspaces and can reduce repeated local exploration. Single deterministic modes, however, oversample local funnels, and limited-memory curvature information is not reliable enough for direct mode selection. Combining several BFGS modes improves robustness, but the conventional softened random direction with L-BFGS remains 1 the lowest-cost baseline in total force evaluations. The study clarifies when curvature reuse is algorithmically useful: it must provide an inexpensive soft-mode subspace while preserving stochastic diversity.

papers.title: Contrastive representation learning for polymer informatics
papers.abstract: Modeling polymer structure–property relationships remains challenging due to structural complexity and data scarcity. Self-supervised learning offers a promising strategy to learn transferable polymer representations from unlabeled data, but existing approaches primarily capture local context and may overlook higher-level structural characteristics in polymer chains. Here we present PoCo, a contrastive framework that learns polymer representations by encoding polymer-specific invariances across augmented sequence views. PoCo achieves state-of-the-art performance across five benchmark datasets, spanning 67 property prediction tasks. It outperforms multimodal baselines with 90% fewer parameters. The learned representations spontaneously organize into chemically meaningful substructures, enabling direct and intuitive fragment-level interpretation. These results highlight contrastive learning as an efficient and interpretable paradigm for polymer informatics.

papers.title: In silico Design of a Miniaturized [Fe-Mn] Pocket Inspired by Natural R2lox and RNR Active Sites: A Topological Hypothesis via Protein Minimization
papers.abstract: Inspired by the active sites of natural heteronuclear [Fe-Mn] enzymes such as R2lox and Class Ic ribonucleotide reductases (RNRs), this design present an in silico protein minimization strategy to construct a miniaturized binuclear coordination pocket within a 15-mer peptide (Ac-HEHGH-GPGP-HGDAH-C-NH2). Structural topology modeling via PEP-FOLD 4.0 demonstrates that the rigid GPGP β-turn drives spontaneous peptide folding, assembling the Histidine clusters and Aspartate side chains into a high-density, compartmentalized cavity. AlphaFold 3 simulations further confirm strict steric exclusivity against bulky heme cofactors, verifying the pocket’s specificity for free transition metal ions. This work establishes a robust topological hypothesis that natural-like non-heme heteronuclear centers can be rationally condensed into minimal sequence spaces, providing a structural platform for de novo metalloenzyme design.

papers.title: Molecular Modeling of Triethyl Phosphate: Extension and Validation of the TraPPE Force Field
papers.abstract: The study of physical properties of organophosphorus chemical warfare agents (CWAs) is essential for detection, protection, decontamination and destruction. Due to the extreme toxicity of CWAs, other organophosphorus molecules with similar chemical structures are employed in experimental studies as simulants, such as dimethyl methylphosphonate (DMMP) and diisopropyl methylphosphonate (DIMP). Triethyl phosphate (TEP) can also be considered as an alternative simulant, especially that it is more accessible due to its several industrial applications. Classical molecular simulations complement experimental research on organophosphates. Here, we present the extension of the transferable potentials for phase equilibria (TraPPE) force field to TEP. Using this model, TEP can be parameterized based on interaction parameters from similar organophosphates in conjunction with ab initio calculations. The model was validated by performing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to predict liquid densities and Gibbs ensemble Monte Carlo simulations to model vapor-liquid equilibrium to predict vapor pressures which were compared with literature data. MD simulations were performed to predict the enthalpy of vaporization, surface tension, viscosity and diffusivity. Additionally, we parameterized and tested trimethyl phosphate (TMP) due to its structural similarity to TEP. Our study helps assess TEP and TMP as alternative CWA simulants, and provides predictions of their physical properties, over a wide range of temperatures, complementing the scarce experimental data. The presented force field can be further utilized for predicting other properties based on molecular simulations, such as adsorption of TEP or TMP.

papers.title: RETRACTED: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies Candidate COX-2 Inhibitors: A Computational Prioritization Study
papers.abstract: Retracted by the author because incorrect underlying data was used. A corrected version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15005946/v1.

papers.title: Industrial Large Models for Safety and Quality Control in the Chemical Process Industry
papers.abstract: Chemical manufacturing is entering a new stage of digitalization as large, general-purpose artificial intelligence systems are adapted for industrial use. Conventional machine-learning tools in chemical engineering have usually been designed for narrow tasks, such as detecting abnormal sensor patterns or estimating difficult-to-measure process variables. Industrial Large Models (ILMs), by contrast, can combine numerical plant data, engineering documents, oper-ating procedures, safety studies, and laboratory records in a single reasoning workflow. This article discusses how such models can support process safety and product-quality assurance in the chemical process industry. It explains the main architectural elements of ILMs, including domain adaptation, retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, physics-based validation, and local deployment. It then describes applications in dynamic hazard analysis, operator support, soft sensing, and grade-transition optimization. The article also highlights limitations that must be addressed before ILMs can be trusted in safety-critical settings, especially hallucination, cybersecurity, regulatory accountability, and the need for deterministic verification.

papers.title: MitoGatekeeper Systems Studio: A Molecular-to-Systems Framework for NADHSensitive AIFM1-AK2 Control of ATP Synthase Substrate Supply and Mitochondrial Energy Adaptation
papers.abstract: ATP synthesis by oxidative phosphorylation is commonly explained through the respiratory chain and the rotary mechanism of ATP synthase. However, a complete systems-level understanding of mitochondrial energy conversion also requires attention to substrate logistics. ADP must be regenerated and delivered, inorganic phosphate must be imported, ATP must be exported, and cellular redox state must be translated into local molecular organisation. Recent work identified an NADH-dependent interaction between apoptosis-inducing factor mitochondriaassociated 1, AIFM1, and adenylate kinase 2, AK2, placing AK2 near oxidative phosphorylation complexes, adenine nucleotide transporters, and ATP synthase. This finding provides a mechanistic link between metabolic state, local ADP regeneration, and ATP synthase substrate supply. Here, we expand this concept into a molecular-to-systems framework and present MitoGatekeeper Systems Studio, an aAidea scientific software platform that integrates NAD+/NADH redox state, AIFM1-AK2 recruitment, ANT-mediated nucleotide exchange, phosphate supply, ATP synthase function, calcium signalling, IF1-associated ATP-conservation logic, ROS pressure, mitochondrial quality control, tissue vulnerability, and assay recommendation. The framework is designed for education, hypothesis generation, experimental planning, and scientific communication, not for clinical diagnosis or therapeutic decision-making. At the molecular level, the app models AIFM1 as an NADHsensitive regulator that recruits AK2 through C-terminal binding determinants to support ATP + AMP ⇌ 2 ADP buffering near ATP synthase. At the systems level, the app represents mitochondrial bioenergetics as a dynamic state space in which fuel supply, redox pressure, membrane architecture, stress responses, and maintenance capacity jointly influence ATP output and resilience.

papers.title: PIGNet V2: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for High-Throughput Crystalline Material Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the electronic and thermodynamic properties of crystalline solids from atomic structure is a central problem in computational materials science. Density Functional Theory (DFT) provides first-principles accuracy but scales as O(N3) with system size, rendering it computationally intractable for the highthroughput screening of large compositional spaces. Here we present PIGNet V2, a Physics-Informed Graph Network that combines attention-gated message passing, 56-dimensional 3-body angular edge features, and a physics-constrained multi-task prediction head to simultaneously infer band gap, formation energy, and thermodynamic stability from unrelaxed crystal structures. By embedding physical constraints directly into the model architecture— Softplus-bounded non-negative properties, thermodynamic penalty terms in the loss function, and post-prediction conformal calibration—PIGNet V2 guarantees zero physically impossible predictions across all test configurations. Trained on 125,000 structures from the Materials Project, the model achieves a band gap MAE of 1.24 eV after epoch 1 (converging toward the production target of <0.22 eV) and a formation energy MAE of 0.314 eV/atom (targeting <0.055 eV/atom at convergence), with a stable validation loss of 0.601 and no gradient instabilities. The companion BatteryFormer module extends infer-ence to unrelaxed crystal structures, eliminating the DFT geometry optimisation bottleneck and enabling the screening of 104,934 high-entropy cathode configurations for the Na6CoS4 system—identifying an Ir/Ru co-doping strategy that theoretically elevates energy density from 752.4 to 1104.5 Wh/kg. Keywords: graph neural networks; physics-informed machine learning; materials property prediction; density functional theory surrogates; crystal structure; uncertainty quantification; battery cathode design

papers.title: Sustainable production of Carbon Black pigment from waste Tire Pyrolysis for Printing Ink Applications
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and cost-effective materials has intensified interest in alternative sources of carbon black derived from waste resources and environmentally friendly processes. This study investigates the production of recovered carbon black (rCB) from the pyrolysis of scrap rubber tires and its application in nitrocellulose-based flexographic printing inks. The rCB was obtained through pyrolysis of waste tires at temperatures ranging from 350–600°C and subsequently processed into pigment concentrates using optimized dispersion techniques. The performance of the developed rCB pigment was benchmarked against commercial PRINTEX®35 carbon black manufactured by Orion Engineered Carbons GmbH. The pigment concentrates were prepared using a controlled formulation and dispersed through bead milling to achieve a uniform particle size distribution. The developed inks were evaluated in terms of shade, rheological behavior, gloss, pH stability, tint strength, opacity, tonal value, and adhesion performance. Experimental results demonstrated that the recovered carbon black exhibited performance comparable to commercial carbon black while offering significant cost and sustainability advantages. The findings highlight the potential of waste tire-derived carbon black as an environmentally sustainable, economically viable, and circular alternative for industrial flexographic printing ink applications.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operator Learning for Fe2O3 Reduction Kinetics Identification from Sparse Thermogravimetric Data
papers.abstract: Reduction kinetics of iron-oxide oxygen carriers govern the design of fuel reactors in chemical looping hydrogen generation, yet conventional identification of Arrhenius parameters relies on dense thermogravimetric datasets and non-linear curve fitting that does not generalise beyond the measured temperature window. This work applies physics-informed machine learning to the reduction of Fe2O3 by hydrogen using only sparse thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) data. Two contributions are reported. First, an inverse physics-informed neural network (PINN) recovers the apparent activation energy Ea and the pre-exponential factor A of a lumped contracting-volume kinetic model from 24 sparse isothermal conversion observations sampled across three temperatures (750, 850, and 900 °C). The recovered apparent activation energy is 24.07 kJ mol−1, consistent with the step-resolved values reported by Wang et al. [11]. Second, a physics-informed deep operator network (PI-DeepONet) learns the solution operator G : T 7→ X(t) that maps reduction temperature to the full conversion trajectory. Against held-out TGA data the PI-DeepONet reproduces an unseen extrapolation temperature of 950 °C with a coefficient of determination R2=0.978, compared with 0.524 for a data-only operator of identical architecture and 0.271 for the single-condition inverse PINN. Once trained, the operator predicts a conversion trajectory in milliseconds, removing the per-temperature retraining cost of a standard PINN. All code is available at https://github.com/Kiran-1318/Fe2O3_redox_PINN.

papers.title: Beyond Weight-Based Pricing: CL5D Digital Fingerprinting of Mahua (Madhuca longifolia), Kendu (Diospyros melanoxylon) and Sal (Shorea robusta) for Pharmaceutical and Nutraceutical Value Chain Development
papers.abstract: Minor Forest Produce (MFP) — principally Mahua (Madhuca longifolia), Kendu leaf (Diospyros melanoxylon), Sal leaf and Sal seed (Shorea robusta) — sustains the livelihoods of millions of tribal gatherers across eastern India, yet is traded exclusively on a weight-basis at prices ranging from Rs. 5–15 per kilogram. This pricing model systematically ignores the rich phytochemical architecture embeddedineachspecies,effectivelytransferringsubstantialvaluefromtribalproducersto downstream intermediaries and manufacturers. The present study introduces and applies the CL5D Non-Binary Algorithm — a novel analytical framework that characterises plant materials through three orthogonal parameters: Concentration Energy (C_energy), Diversity Score (D), and Phase Stability (Phi) — to generate a Digital Fingerprint for each MFP. CL5D analysis reveals that Mahua flowers carry a C_energy signature of 208,744, positioning them as high-grade bio-fuel and caloric superfood ingredients; Kendu leaf exhibits a Diversity Score of 9.0 with high coherence, comparable to pharmaceutical-grade antioxidants; Sal leaf demonstrates potent anti-inflammatory and woundhealing phytochemical profiles; and Sal seed exhibits Phase Stability values rivalling cocoa butter, confirming premium cosmetic and food-binding applications. A proof-of-concept functional food the Sal-Ragi Endurance Brick, engineered from Sal fat, Ragi and Kendu extract — validates the CL5D model in a marketable product with glycaemic control and zero synthetic preservatives. The study further characterises downstream applications of all process residues: fermented Mahua press cake as aquaculture feed, Sal seed cake as ruminant supplement, and Sal and Kendu residues as organic soil amendments. The CL5D framework is proposed as a deterministic replacement for commodity-weight pricing within the Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK) programme, offering a scalable pathway to certified, value-based tribal entrepreneurship.

papers.title: Effect of solvent, pH and thermal annealing on carbon nanotube functionalization
papers.abstract: Quantum well defect-modified single-walled carbon nanotubes are environmentally responsive nanomaterials with broad potential in biosensing, imaging, and quantum computing. The most widely used approach for their covalent functionalization relies on aryl diazonium chemistry, which introduces sp 3 -hybridized aryl defect sites onto the nanotube lattice. Here we investigate how solvent, pH, substituent electronics, and thermal annealing influence the functionalization of SWCNTs with aryl diazonium salts. This approach involves ‘over-functionalization’ with aryl groups resulting in loss of optical properties, followed by thermal annealing to reduce defect density. We find that solvent choice changes both the Raman D:G ratio and the relative intensity of E 11 , E 11 -, and, in some cases, E 11 *- emission. Thermal annealing at 200 °C under ambient atmosphere typically restores fluorescence from initially quenched samples, consistent with partial recovery from an overfunctionalized state.
