Finally, pH-dependent experiments suggest that electron-poor NO 2 PhN 2 -BF 4 reacts most effectively under acidic conditions, whereas electron-rich OMePhN 2 -BF 4 is more strongly activated under basic conditions. Overall, solvent and pH control the degree and optical outcome of aryl diazonium functionalization, while thermal annealing provides a practical post-reaction route for recovering useful defect emission from over-functionalized nanotubes. To our knowledge, this work provides the first systematic analysis of how solvent and pH govern quantum-well defect formation in aryl-functionalized SWCNTs.

papers.title: Energy Dissipation in CNT-Reinforced Hydrogels Governed by Deformation Anisotropy
papers.abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT)-reinforced polyacrylamide (PAAm) nanocomposite hydrogels are promising materials for wearable human-machine interfaces, flexible electronics, and soft robotics owing to their combined mechanical robustness and electrical functionality. Here, we report an unusual mechanical energy dissipation mechanism under cyclic loading-unloading in CNT-reinforced PAAm hydrogels. At a given stretch or input energy, the dissipation factor (defined by the ratio of dissipation to input mechanical work) is significantly higher under uniaxial stretching than under equibiaxial stretching, in contrast to conventional stress-softening materials. This counterintuitive behavior reveals that deformation anisotropy plays a decisive role in governing internal damage. Under uniaxial stretching, strong anisotropy promotes CNT alignment, facilitating interfacial sliding and detachment of non-covalent interactions, thereby maximizing energy dissipation. In contrast, biaxial deformation suppresses CNT reorientation, limiting dissipative processes despite a larger mechanical work input. In-situ small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) measurements confirm the more pronounced CNT alignment under uniaxial stretching. Combined mechanical and SAXS analyses further reveal the compatibilizing role of gelatin between the PAAm matrix and CNTs: hydrogen bonding of gelatin with both components enables cooperative alignment with CNTs under deformation. These findings uncover a fundamental decoupling between stiffness and energy dissipation in CNT-based soft composites, highlighting the critical role of the compatibilizer, and contribute to the establishment of a general design principle for anisotropy-driven hydrogels with enhanced durability under complex loading conditions.

papers.title: The synthesis of four new gemini-type hydroxy derivatives of cholesterol with potential biological activity as ligands of RORs
papers.abstract: This work presents the synthesis of the firsts Gemini-type derivatives of cholesterol with a triple bond in the second sidechain. The rigidity of this new chain, which can be observed in analogues 1 and 2, could be the key to the create new interactions in the receptor allowing these compounds to act as agonist or inverse agonist of RORs. The introduction of a double side chain allows the formation of more interactions with the receptor and increases the activity of these new compounds. Furthermore, the presence of a hydroxyl group in C-25 helps to stabilize the ligand in the LBD of RORs.

papers.title: Bench-Stable Solid Organozinc Reagents: Synthesis and Application
papers.abstract: Organozinc reagents transformed organic synthesis due to their compatibility with functional groups. Nonetheless, organozinc reagents are susceptible to air and moisture and are often produced in solution form, which restricts their industrial application. Solid organozinc pivalates (RZnX·Mg(OPiv)2·nLiCl) were developed by the reaction of RMgX with Zn(OPiv)2·2LiCl. (CF3)2Zn·TMEDA was synthesized from air-stable (DMPU)2Zn(perfluoroalkyl)2, which was derived from ZnEt2 and perfluoroalkyl iodide. A method that generates stable monomeric organozinc species in a single step, eliminates solvents such as DMA, uses commercial Zn, and eliminates stoichiometric additives like LiCl is very desirable. We demonstrate the direct synthesis of stable solid organozinc reagents (15 examples), including sterically demanding tBuZnBr, from commercial zinc. They exhibit high stability at room temperature and offer excellent yields in open-air palladium catalysis. These reagents are monomeric, devoid of complex mixtures. Single-crystal XRD, and especially the NMR spectrum, were obtained for these reagents.

papers.title: Sparse Linear Surrogates Match Neural-Network Potentials on the SPICE Biomolecular Benchmark with Three Orders of Magnitude Smaller Training Sets
papers.abstract: We introduce the orbital cluster expansion (OCE), a linear regression on physics-motivated local features derived from atomic orbital eigenenergies, and benchmark it against the SPICE 2.0 biomolecular dataset at the ωB97M-D3BJ/def2-TZVPPD level. On 677 dipeptides spanning the natural amino acids, ridge regression on 414 OCE features attains a parent-stratified test root-mean-square error of 27meV per atom and Spearman ρ = 0.9999, matching MACE-OFF and ANI-2x trained with 10 4 to 10 6 conformations. Comparable accuracy holds on 500 PubChem drug-like molecules and 500 DES370K dimers, demonstrating chemical generality. We characterise a fundamental dual regime: while inter-molecular ranking is preserved across chemistries, intra-conformer ranking is random because the basis cannot resolve geometry-only variation within a fixed connectivity. OCE provides an interpretable, data-efficient alternative for biomolecular screening.

papers.title: Direct Conversion of Aryl Iodides to Trialkylamines via Aminomethylation: Reaction Scope, Mechanistic Studies, and Applications
papers.abstract: Despite the high utility and value of trialkylamines and their derivatives, their synthesis is hindered by a limited substrate availability and non-reusable transition-metal catalysts. To that end, this study develops an aminomethylation strategy using aryl iodides and formamides while examining the substrate scope and underlying mechanism for synthesizing trialkylamines under parts-per-million-level (65 ppm) reusable palladium catalysis. This method can accommodate a wide range of substrates, including electron-rich and electrondeficient aryl, polyaryl, and heteroaryl iodides. Similarly, various formamide derivatives yield aminomethylated products. This aminomethylation strategy is used to directly synthesize biologically active molecules, such as a rivastigmine analog, and natural products, e.g., gramine. In addition, tryptamine, a serotonin receptor, and diindolylmethane, a metabolite, are successfully produced by derivatizing the aminomethylated products. Isotopelabeling experiments indicate that formamide derivatives were precursors for the reducing agent, in addition to providing both amines and carbon. A plausible catalytic pathway is proposed based on isotope-labeling experiments and density functional theory calculations, providing insights for future research and new applications in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.

papers.title: Charge Storage and Dark Photocatalysis in Multivariate Ti-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Dark photocatalysis, which decouples electron storage from photoconversion, offers a promising route to buffer solar intermittency, however requires precise control of light-matter interactions. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a platform to tailor these interactions at the molecular level through judicious selection of organic linkers and interconnected metal nodes. This study advances design principles for dark photocatalysis by integrating two linkers with complementary light-interaction roles in a multivariate (MTV) COK‑47 (COK= Centrum voor Oppervlaktechemie en Katalyse) series. Varying the ratio between biphenyl dicarboxylic linker (biph) and bipyridine dicarboxylate linker (bipy) shows that under continuous irradiation (365 nm), the photocatalytic activity of COK‑47biph is the most active member of the solid solution series and surpasses COK‑47bipy by threefold. COK‑47bipy in contrary, exhibits an eightfold increase in photocharging capacity, revealed by a multispectroscopic approach, evidencing the formation of Ti3+ and reduced linker species as storage unit, compared to COK‑47biph. The stored charges drive methyl viologen (MV) reduction and H2 evolution in the dark. Notably, the mixed linker material COK‑4750‑50 combines both advantages, delivering near-maximal H2 production under illumination while retaining substantial charge storage capability, resulting in the highest MV reduction activity and second highest dark H2 evolution in the series. These findings connect framework composition to light/matter interaction, charge storage capacity, activity, and establish a design strategy for multifunctional dark photocatalytic materials.

papers.title: Evaluation of Structure-Aware Machine Learning methods for the Discovery of Protein–Protein Interaction Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are increasingly recognised as therapeutically actionable targets, yet the discovery of small-molecule PPI inhibitors remains challenging because PPI interfaces are often large, shallow, dynamic and structurally heterogeneous. Machine learning (ML) approaches have shown promise for PPI inhibitor prediction, but most models rely on ligand-centred descriptors and may therefore capture scaffold similarity rather than compatibility with a specific protein–protein interface. In this study, we evaluated a structure-aware ML framework for the prediction of small-molecule PPI inhibitors by comparing ligand-only Extended Connectivity Fingerprints (ECFPs) with Protein–Ligand Extended Connectivity (PLEC) fingerprints. ECFP-based models showed high sensitivity on the external labelled prediction set, while PLEC-based models behaved more conservatively, recovering fewer positives but showing stronger rejection of ChEMBL-derived negatives. Family-specific ECFP models further demonstrated that PPI inhibitors could often be assigned to the correct PPI family, particularly when additional negative examples were included during training. Leave-one-family-out analyses revealed that extrapolation to unseen PPI families was strongly family-dependent: ECFP descriptors provided broader generalisation across several families, whereas PLEC descriptors improved recovery in selected cases. Overall, these results indicate that ligand-only and structure-aware descriptors provide complementary information for PPI inhibitor prediction.

papers.title: Direct Observation and Unambiguous Assignment of 15N–13C Correlations Using SLIC-SABRE Hyperpolarization
papers.abstract: We demonstrate direct access to heteronuclear 15 N– 13 C correlations in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) using complementary 15 N-and 13 C-detected experiments with dramatic sensitivity enhancement. This is enabled by signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE) polarization transfer driven by spin-lock induced crossing (SLIC) pulses applied at low magnetic field. Notably, SLIC-SABRE operates under near-Earth field conditions using a compact coil-based setup, making the method readily accessible. We show that conventional one-dimensional (1D) SABRE experiments do not allow unambiguous assignment of 15 N– 13 C correlations due to severe spectral overlap, which we overcome using two-dimensional (2D) heteronuclear detection resolving individual 15 N– 13 C pairs. Combining 13 C and 15 N SLIC-SABRE experiments enables rapid and precise determination of 15 N– 13 C coupling constants and 13 C-induced isotopic effects on 15 N chemical shifts. The general applicability of the approach is demonstrated for 15 N-3-methyl-[1,2,4]-selenadiazolo[4,5-a]pyridin-4-ium bromide (24 mM) and 15 N 2 metronidazole (87 mM), both at natural 13 C abundance (1.1%). The measured 15 N– 13 C couplings further reveal sensitivity to molecular state, including coordination to the SABRE organometallic Ir complex. Overall, the method provides a practical route for rapid characterization of heteronuclear connectivity and local structure in nitrogen- containing systems.

papers.title: Sanity and Decomposition Pipeline for Metal-Organic Frameworks in Generative AI
papers.abstract: Generative models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) demand automated validation and decomposition tools that scale to large datasets while preserving chemical realism. Here we present a unified sanity framework that combines two newly developed tools — LibCIF for ultrafast MOF decomposition and validation, and OxiChecker, an oxidation-state anomaly detector — complemented by external geometry based sanity filters (PLATON, MOFChecker). We benchmark OxiChecker against MOSAEC across major MOF databases (ARCMOF, BWDB, CoRE-MOF, QMOF), compare the full Sanity Pipeline against standalone methods on CoRE-MOF, QMOF, and approximately 25,000 structures from an in-house LLaMA-3-based generative model (1B parameters), and summarize PLATON alerts over the 300k-scale BWDB collection. The Sanity Pipeline is shown to effectively subsume the charge-balance diagnostics of MOSAEC while providing complementary geometric checks. The C++ implementation of LibCif achieves sub-second per-structure runtimes one to two orders of magnitude faster than Python-based alternatives, making it uniquely suited as a real-time reward signal in reinforcement-learning generative pipelines, while the full validation cascade serves as an offline post-filter. LibCif further provides O(N) supercell-aware decomposition into chemically meaningful nodes and linkers, enabling scalable extraction of building blocks for downstream modeling and generative design.

papers.title: Photoredox Nickel-Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Alkoxycarbonylation of Benzylic C-H Bonds
papers.abstract: Radical-mediated transition-metal-catalyzed C-H carbonylation represents a direct and powerful approach for the synthesis of carbonyl compounds; however, the stoichiometric oxidants typically required for hydrogen atom abstraction hamper the extensive application of these protocols and raise environmental concerns. Herein, we report a photoredox/Ni-catalyzed acceptorless dehydrogenative alkoxycarbonyation of alkylarenes with alcohols. A variety of benzylic carboxylates, benzofuranones, and lactones were obtained from readily available feedstocks. Notably, the use of biphosphine ligand promotes the reductive elimination of acylnickel(II) intermediate with alcohols while suppressing undesired single-electron oxidative addition. Furthermore, the reaction is distinguished by broad functional-group compatibility, high selectivity, and ambient conditions with 1 atm CO.

papers.title: Boronic Acids as Radical Precursors for Carbon Nanotube Functionalization
papers.abstract: Covalent sp 3 quantum defects in single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) unlock powerful capabilities for quantum nanosensors, bioimaging, and optoelectronic devices. However, the chemical diversity of accessible quantum defects has been constrained by dependence on aryl diazonium salts, which are inherently unstable, prone to side reactions, and of which only a few dozen are commercially available, limiting color center/quantum well defect engineering to a narrow slice of chemical space. A recently developed handle-free Fenton-based approach expanded defect diversity across over 200 small molecules but is limited to small, polar, and aliphatic substrates, leaving aryl rings and extended alkyl chains largely inaccessible. Here, we report a boronic acid deboronation strategy that directly addresses this gap. Under Fenton oxidative conditions, both aryl and alkyl boronic acids undergo homolytic C-B cleavage to generate carbon-centered radicals that add covalently to the SWCNT sidewall under mild, aqueous conditions. With thousands of structurally diverse boronic acids commercially available as bench-stable solids, this chemistry opens access to a quantum defect library orders of magnitude larger than previously achievable using aryl diazonium salts. We observed this generality across more than 50 substrates spanning electron-donating, electron-withdrawing, and heteroaromatic structures, and establish a linear Hammett correlation between substituent electronics and defect-state emission wavelength that enables predictive control over defect photophysics. Furthermore, by employing meta and para positional isomers of representative substrates, this work provides the first systematic investigation of mesomeric versus inductive substituent effects on both the extent of SWCNT covalent functionalization and the resulting quantum well depth. To demonstrate the utility of this expanded defect library, we rationally designed four NIR-fluorescent SWCNT pH nanosensors spanning a pK a range of 5.2 to 7.2. This work establishes boronic acid deboronation as a practical and scalable route to SWCNT quantum defects for sensing, bioimaging, optoelectronic, and quantum photonic applications.

papers.title: From building blocks to complex molecules: a practical and general route towards deuterated compounds
papers.abstract: Molecules containing deuterium are powerful tools with diverse applications across chemical and biomedical research. However, deuterated molecules are often challenging or expensive to make, limiting their application in non-specialist labs. Herein, we report a practical, simple, and general route towards deuterated molecules using commercially available palladium pre-catalysts and sodium borodeuteride. Simply by mixing the components in open flasks at room temperature, we achieve selective deuteration with high labelling efficiency within minutes. Remarkably, we uncovered an unexpected selectivity for deuterium over hydrogen installation in protonated solvents, such as water and methanol. These unique features enable the selective and straightforward deuteration of diverse substrate classes, including complex molecules with labile protons such as unprotected peptides. The versatility, ease, and efficiency of our method will make deuterated molecules more accessible to non-specialist labs, accelerating and diversifying their adoption.

papers.title: MPID Polarizable Force Field: GPU Implementation and Biomolecular Simulations
papers.abstract: The multipole and induced dipole (MPID) model provides a sophisticated description of electrostatics through permanent atomic multipoles up to the octopole level and point induced dipoles, but its high computational cost has limited its routine application to biomolecular simulations. Here, we present a GPU-accelerated implementation of the MPID model in OpenMM. The implementation produces energies and forces fully consistent with those obtained from CHARMM and enables routine microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations of explicitly solvated protein systems. Moreover, force field parameters were transferred directly from the Drude oscillator model to the MPID framework without reparameterization, yielding the MPID-2019 protein force field. Tests on five proteins show that MPID-2019 reproduces a range of NMR observables, including scalar couplings and relaxation order parameters. These results demonstrate that MPID-2019 is a valid polarizable force field readily applicable to protein simulations and that the effective equivalence of the induced dipole and Drude oscillator formalisms can be established at the biomolecular level.

papers.title: Sparse Dynamic and Dense Immobile States of Li-ions in Graphite Staging as Seen by 7Li NMR Relaxation
papers.abstract: Even though the staging mechanism of graphite has been studied extensively by, primarily, diffraction methods, the nature of dilute stages with stoichiometries lower than LiC 12 remains an open question. Here we reconsider the stages from the perspective of Li ion dynamics as observed by 7 Li NMR spin relaxation. We find that in stage-1 (LiC 6 ) and 2 (LiC 12 ), the Li ions are quite immobile which is consistent with dense Li-filled interlayers. In stage-2L (LiC 18 ), Li ion motion is fast with low activation energy indicating the presence of easily accessible vacancies. The data supported by confocal Raman spectroscopy also suggest that the coexisting stage-2 and stage-2L 2 domains are in the order to micrometers, close to the grains size. We propose that the split Raman G-band observed in stage-2L is connected to in-plane inhomogeneity of electron distribution induced by locally occupied and vacant Li + sites. The phase equilibrium of stage-2 and stage-2L domains is temperature-dependent, with low temperature favoring the low-entropy stage-2 phase.

papers.title: Generation of carbon particles from sucrose in a programmable aerosol reactor
papers.abstract: Carbonization of biomass-derived precursors is a key route toward sustainable carbon materials. However, conventional hydrothermal and pyrolytic approaches are typically conducted under bulk heating conditions in batch or furnace-based reactors, offering limited flexibility for dynamic adjustment of reaction parameters during operation. Here, we report a programmable aerosol microdroplet reactor that enables controlled carbonization of sucrose as a model biomass precursor. The system employs an upward-spray configuration with precisely adjustable flow rate, heating conditions, and precursor composition, providing a versatile platform for investigating carbon formation within droplet-confined environments. Under optimized thermal conditions, the reactor consistently produced uniform carbon microspheres with negligible residual sulfur, indicating efficient carbonization within the aerosol phase. Systematic variation of precursor concentration, acid ratio, and injection parameters enabled reproducible synthesis of spherical carbon microparticles.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Cross-Modal Molecular Reasoning Network for Property Prediction and Reaction Analysis
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction analysis are fundamental tasks in computational chemistry that underpin applications in drug discovery and materials science. While deep learning methods, particularly graph neural networks and transformers, have shown remarkable progress in molecular representation learning, existing approaches suffer from three key limitations: reliance on single-modal representations, inability to incorporate external chemical knowledge during inference, and lack of symbolic reasoning for chemical validity. In this paper, we propose RACM-MRN, a Retrieval-Augmented Cross-Modal Molecular Reasoning Network that systematically addresses these challenges. Our framework integrates four synergistic components: a Molecular Knowledge Graph Retrieval Module that retrieves structurally similar molecules as contextual knowledge, a Cross-Modal Attention Fusion Module that integrates molecular graphs, spectral signals, and textual descriptions through hierarchical cross-modal attention, a Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Module that enforces chemical validity constraints on neural predictions, and a Federated Training framework with a dissimilarity measure for privacy-preserving collaborative learning. Extensive experiments on the MoleculeNet benchmark suite demonstrate that RACM-MRN achieves state-of-the-art performance, obtaining ROC-AUC scores of 0.912 on BBBP, 0.869 on Tox21, 0.685 on SIDER, and 0.771 on MUV for molecular property prediction, as well as top-1 accuracy of 0.935 on USPTO-50k and 0.869 on USPTO-MIT for chemical reaction prediction. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each module, with the cross-modal fusion improving BBBP by 2.3 points and the neuro-symbolic constraints increasing chemical validity from 87.3 percent to 96.8 percent.

papers.title: Bridging batch and flow: a universal, scalable platform for automated multistep synthesis employing high-speed circulating flow reactors
papers.abstract: Automated multistep synthesis of small organic molecules remains a formidable challenge, as conventional batch platforms are often limited by scalability, while continuous-flow systems face difficulties in handling solids, slow reactions, and compatibility across multiple steps. Here, we introduce a modular automated multistep synthesis platform built around high-speed circulating flow (HSCF) reactors that integrate the strengths of both batch and flow approaches. This architecture enables the rapid adoption of literature-reported protocols across homogeneous, heterogeneous, and photochemical transformations for scalable multistep synthesis. Two platform configurations were demonstrated: an “all-in-one” setup enabling fully automated synthesis of brexpiprazole (>25 g) within a compact footprint, and an “integrated flow” platform facilitating the semi-continuous production of esonarimod and two benzoxazinone derivatives at rates exceeding 10 g/day. This work establishes a universal, scalable, and reconfigurable architecture that significantly advances automated multistep synthesis, offering a practical solution for the on-demand production of functional small organic molecules.

papers.title: p-Type Organic Semiconductors with an Annulated Thiazole: Photochemical Synthesis and Theoretically High Hole Mobility Predicted from Crystal Structure
papers.abstract: Two dithienonaphthothiazole derivatives, b -DNT and l -DNT , were synthesized via photoinduced 6π-electrocyclization–dehydrogenation of the bithiophene-substituted benzothiazole 1 . The direct photoirradiation reaction of 1 in the presence of molecular iodine (I 2 ) and propylene oxide preferentially forms b -DNT , but under photoinduced electron-transfer conditions using p-chloranil as the photosensitizer, b -DNT is generated exclusively. Investigations using nanosecond absorption spectroscopy in conjunction with laser flash photolysis, along with density-functional theory calculations led to the identification of potential intermediates in these photochemical processes. X-ray crystallographic analysis showed that both b -DNT and l -DNT crystallize in a slipped π-stacking packing motif. PBEPBE/6-31G* level calculations suggest that crystals of these substances have large charge-transfer integrals (t) between neighboring molecules that are π-stacked along the b-axis. The t value for l -DNT (101 meV) is nearly twofold larger than that for b -DNT (54 meV), which is attributed to the existence of more extensive π-overlap in the former. Based on the Marcus hopping model, theoretical hole mobility along the π-stacking direction in l -DNT is predicted to be as high as 4.0 cm 2 V –1 s –1 . These results suggest that, owing to their excellent charge transport properties, crystals of b -DNT and l -DNT have the potential of serving as p-type organic semiconductors.

papers.title: Near-Infrared (NIR) -Triggered Debonding of EVA Adhesives: Linking Absorber Properties to Thermomechanical Failure
papers.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR)-triggered debonding is a promising strategy for on-demand disassembly of adhesive systems, but the relationship between absorber properties, heating conditions, and macroscopic debonding behaviour remains poorly understood. Here, NIR-triggered debonding of EVA-based adhesive films containing carbon black (CB) or cesium tungsten oxide (CTO) was systematically investigated as representative broadband and spectrally selective absorbers (0–4 wt%). Optical spectroscopy, temperature-dependent adhesion, oscillatory rheology, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and controlled NIR irradiation experiments show that debonding consistently occurs within a 70–80 °C window determined primarily by the EVA matrix, while absorber identity and loading mainly influence how rapidly this threshold is reached. CB exhibits loading-dependent, absorber-mediated debonding (~4–7 s), whereas CTO shows weak loading dependence (~9–11 s), indicating that environmental heating dominates under the present conditions. These findings establish a physically motivated framework linking absorber optics, thermal coupling, and matrix failure in NIR-triggered debondable adhesives. More broadly, they show that spectral selectivity alone does not necessarily translate into improved macroscopic debonding performance, providing guidance for the design of future NIR-responsive debond-on-demand systems.

papers.title: Cationic fullerenes for efficient siRNA delivery to pancreatic cancer. From synthesis to protein corona differences and toxicological studies on the zebrafish model
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal solid tumors, owing to its aggressive physiology, late diagnosis, dense stromal barriers, and limited responsiveness to currently available therapies. In this setting, RNA interference offers an attractive strategy to suppress oncogenic drivers at the post-transcriptional level, including targets that are difficult to modulate with conventional small molecules. Fullerenes are especially compelling in this context because their well-defined carbon cages can be extensively functionalized. Here, we report the development of two water-soluble cationic fullerene nanomaterials based on C60 and C70 scaffolds, each functionalized with branched polyethyleneimine and polyethylene glycol, as nonviral carriers for siRNA delivery to pancreatic cancer cells. We further examine how scaffold identity influences physicochemical properties, gene-silencing performance, and protein-corona composition. Using PANC-1 model, we show that both nanomaterials efficiently complex siRNA and mediate silencing, whereas the C60-based platform displays superior functional performance. We then extend this system to therapeutically relevant cargoes targeting EGFR and KRAS-associated signaling and evaluate its safety in a zebrafish embryo model. Together, these studies identify cationic fullerenes as a promising class of siRNA delivery agents for PDAC and underscore the importance of protein-corona composition as a mechanistic variable in the design of carbon-based nanomedicines.

papers.title: Understanding In-liquid Sample Environments for Infrared Nano-spectroscopy of Soft Materials
papers.abstract: Recent advances in infrared (IR) scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) have enabled label-free IR spectroscopy of biomolecules and cells in native aqueous environments with nanoscale spatial resolution. This is achieved using an ultrathin membrane that prevents direct mechanical interaction between the AFM probe and the liquid while permitting the evanescent optical field to detect the underlying sample. In this configuration, the membrane influences the far- and near-field response of the microscope, requiring the multilayered 2 sample system to be considered when interpreting near-field interactions. Here, we present a systematic study of ultrathin silicon nitride (SiNx) and silicon carbide (SiC) membranes, investigating their near-field optical response both in a dry condition and in contact with aqueous solutions of bovine serum albumin and DNA molecules. In addition, we demonstrate nanoscale IR (nano-IR) imaging and spectroscopy of individual aggregates of α-synuclein protein in the form of fibrils, in a liquid environment under a SiNx membrane. Results indicate that the membrane material not only influences the available transparency window but also introduces spectral changes determined by the optical properties of the membranes and the adhesion of the sample to the substrate. Furthermore, we show that finite dipole modeling can reproduce the near-field spectra of membrane-biomolecule stacked samples, providing a consistent framework for interpreting experimental nano-IR results. This comparative study provides insights relevant for selecting membrane materials for mid-IR s-SNOM experiments in liquid, highlighting the advantages and limitations of SiNx and SiC materials, while identifying potential sources of artifacts and deviations from the idealized model.

papers.title: First Structural Determination of an Isolable and Planar Tropyl Radical
papers.abstract: Planar hydrocarbon-based tropyl radicals remain elusive because seven-membered open-shell systems readily undergo structural deformation and intermolecular reactions. Herein, we report the design, isolation, and structural characterization of dibenzotropyl radicals bearing anthryl-based π-systems. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations predicted that bianthryl and teranthryl substituents stabilize orthogonally twisted conformations containing a planar dibenzotropyl radical unit while suppressing the formation of reactive folded structures. One-electron reduction of the corresponding dibenzotropyliums afforded persistent neutral radicals for both the bianthryl and teranthryl derivatives, which are stable under ambient conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis of the bianthryl-substituted radical revealed a sterically unperturbed planar dibenzotropyl structure, providing the first crystallographic evidence for a planar hydrocarbon-based tropyl radical. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical studies revealed reversible redox interconversion between the cationic and radical states while retaining the planar seven-membered framework. These findings provide insight into redox-active seven-membered π-systems and establish a design strategy for stable open-shell hydrocarbons.

papers.title: Symmetric versus asymmetric electron transfer in symmetric molecules
papers.abstract: Photoinduced electron transfer (ET) in symmetric donor-acceptor-donor (D-A-D) or (A-D-A) molecules attracts attention due to applications in advanced materials. It is normally assumed that ET occurs asymmetrically, from one donor to acceptor, thus breaking molecular symmetry and resulting in a dipole moment in the excited state. However, the symmetry can be preserved with symmetric ET from both donors leading to a nondipolar state with a high quadrupole moment. Here we report on the symmetric ET in a D-A-D probe, 5,5'-di(9H-carbazol-9-yl)-2,2'-bipyridine. This probe is negligibly solvatochromic in absorption, but highly solvatochromic in emission, and shows a strong decay of the emission oscillator strength in solvents of increasing polarity. We develop a 3-excited-state model that catches the experimental observations quantitatively, much better than the previously proposed 2-state model. Both the symmetric and asymmetric ET are analyzed; the conclusion is in favor of the symmetric ET as it fits well the experimental data, while the asymmetric ET cannot.

papers.title: Real-Space Imaging of Valence-Electron Bonding Dynamics with Ultrafast Hard X-Ray Scattering
papers.abstract: Chemical reactivity is governed by the time-dependent redistribution of valence electron density, yet ultrafast diffractive imaging probes are typically dominated by scattering from the atoms and/or core electrons and therefore primarily report nuclear motion. Building on recent hard x-ray time-resolved scattering measurements of photoexcited deuterated ammonia, we extend ultrafast x-ray scattering off the evolving valence electron density into a real-space framework by retrieving the time-dependent electron pair density (PD). Using scattering difference signals, we reconstruct transient real-space ∆PDs that directly recover (i) the prompt redistribution of valence electron density following excitation into a diffuse Rydberg orbital, (ii) the subsequent localization of the electron density on the fragments following N–D bond fission, and (iii) distinct electronic-structure fingerprints of ballistic dissociation channels. These ∆PDs provide an intuitive, chemically interpretable measure of bond breaking and rearrangement by tracking the emergence, displacement, and loss of electron density between atomic centers while retaining femtosecond time resolution. Comparison with ab initio simulations guides the interpretation of the recovered ∆PDs and supports the inferred pathway assignments.

papers.title: Comparing numerical treatments for drug classification using IR spectra
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate the numerical relationships between illicit drugs based on IR spectra from a publicly available library. Classification models were trained to test how well single component drugs can be classified using their IR spectra alone. Two challenges were considered: classifying spectra representing various amphetamine, fentanyl, and cocaine compounds, and classifying spectra specifically of fentanyl analogs. All spectra were sourced from the most recent version of the SWGDRUG IR library (Version 3.1). Multiple classification models with varied parameters were created for each task. The models for challenge 1 performed very well, with several models having a median reported accuracy of 100% The models did not perform well with the appreciably more difficult challenge 2, with median classification accuracies ranging between 50% and 75%. Our results demonstrate the appropriateness of classifying drugs based on IR spectra at the major class level, while confirming the limitation of trying to use IR spectroscopy for analog level discrimination. Efforts to determine the “bounds” of drug classification using IR spectra is on-going in our lab. All source code used to generate the results presented in this article are available at https://github.com/Brandon12G/GiotisNumericalTreatments.

papers.title: Electric Field-Dependent Excited-State Twisting in Donor-Acceptor Thiazolothiazole Dyes Establishes a New Class of Cell Membrane Voltage Sensors
papers.abstract: Voltage sensitive dyes (VSDs) are versatile and powerful reporters of the membrane potential across cell membranes. Thiazolothiazole (TTz) dyes are a promising new class of VSDs with high photostability and low cytotoxicity. However, the mechanistic basis of their voltage sensitivity is unknown. To address this, we developed a new generation of asymmetrically substituted TTz dyes (asym-TTz). They exhibit strong solvatofluorochromism with large Stokes shifts and exceptionally high transition dipole moments of 23-29 D, representing an 80% increase from previous TTz VSDs. An asym-TTz derivative, TwistTz-P, bearing a carboxyphenyl acceptor group, shows sustained cellular membrane localization and a voltage sensitivity of ~10% DF/F per 100 mV. Computational analysis of TwistTz-P under varying electric fields revealed a pronounced twist on both sides of the TTz bridging unit in the excited-state. The degree of twisting was voltage-dependent, exhibiting increase upon depolarization, consistent with the experimentally observed fluorescence decrease at an identical voltage. In another asym-TTz dye (FlatTz-P), where a carboxypyrazinyl acceptor group was incorporated, excited-state twisting under varying electric fields was negligible and demonstrated no voltage sensitivity. These observations establish electric field-dependent excited-state twisting as a new voltage sensing mechanism, and additionally, represent a new strategy with which to create highly sensitive VSDs.

papers.title: Multiplexed Interdigitated Ultramicroelectrode arrays for in-Soil health monitoring
papers.abstract: Real-time monitoring of nitrate (NO3-), pH, and dissolved oxygen (DO) is essential for optimizing nutrient management for both soil and water health which are closely interlinked. Conventional analytical methods, while accurate, lack portability and are unsuitable for continuous field deployment. This work presents a compact electrochemical sensor system based on silicon interdigitated platinum ultramicroelectrode arrays (IDE-UMEs) capable of simultaneous, in situ measurement of NO3-, pH, and DO. Nitrate sensing was achieved by modifying one IDE comb with a CuO/Co3O4/rGO nanocomposite, enabling high sensitivity and stability across environmentally relevant concentrations (10–1000 µM; LOD 0.82 µM). A second IDE functionalized with gold nanoparticles accurately measured pH over the range 3–7, while the modular architecture also accommodated additional DO sensors. To support long-term operation in soil, the system incorporated an on-chip reference electrode stabilization layer, humidity-regulating membranes, and in-situ pH-control strategies to improve signal reproducibility. Laboratory tests, soil leachate measurements, and pot trials confirmed reliable performance and effective analyte detection under variable conditions. Field deployment during a full growing season demonstrated strong agreement with laboratory reference methods and successfully captured nutrient fluctuations linked to fertilization and irrigation. Integration with a data platform enabled real-time visualization and calibration, supporting site-specific fertilizer management and reducing nitrogen application by ~500 kg with an associated environmental risk reduction without compromising crop yield.

papers.title: A model to derive Langmuir-Hinshelwood parameters from heterogeneous uptake experiments in a fast flow reactor
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous interactions between reactive trace gases and aerosol particles alter both the atmospheric trace gas composition and the chemical properties of the participating particles. Incorporating these interactions into aerosol models requires kinetic parameters, which are often derived from uptake experiments in flow reactors and are typically limited to uptake coefficients. We present a framework that enables the extraction of a more fundamental set of kinetic parameters, including adsorption, desorption, and reaction rate constants, as well as the concentrations of adsorptive and reactive sites, directly from such uptake data. The framework is currently formulated for the Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism, but can be readily extended to other mechanisms. The model for time-dependent gas-phase mass transfer and surface chemistry that this framework is based on was developed procedurally, starting from the most rigorous implementation and undergoing two major simplifications, enabling computationally effective fitting to experimental data. Application of the framework was demonstrated by fitting the model to experimental uptake curves, deriving uptake coefficients and partitioning constants from fitted parameters, and making predictions under atmospheric conditions. Finally, an analytical approach for predicting partitioning through reactive Langmuir-Hinshelwood uptake was derived that can improve the accuracy of treating partitioning in aerosol models at no additional computational cost.

papers.title: The Role of Intermolecular Interactions on the Optical Rotation of Chiral Systems in the Condensed Phase from Periodic Coupled Cluster Simulations
papers.abstract: In this study, we present an analysis of intermolecular interactions on the optical rotation (OR) of condensed phase systems. We investigate periodic 1D chains of H2O2 molecules and of a geometrically equivalent H4 model, and we determine the change in OR as a function of the intermolecular distance along well defined molecular axes: the O–O bond axis, the C2 rotational axis, and a third axis perpendicular to the O–O bond and C2 axis. The simulations rely on the first implementation of the linear response function for the OR tensor at coupled cluster level with single and double excitations with periodic boundary conditions (LR-CCSD-PBC), using the modified velocity gauge (MVG) and the origin-independent length gauge [LG(OI)] formalisms. We validate the methods against reference calculations on finite cluster chains aligned along the O–O bond axis, which allow us to explore the role of basis set size and k-point sampling of the first Brillouin zone in reciprocal space. Our results show that the effect of intermolecular interactions is significant even up to 8-10 Å between cells, which is likely an underestimation due to the compact basis set used in the simulations. Furthermore, simulations with point-charge embedding fail to reproduce both the quantitative and qualitative trends of the

papers.title: User-Friendly Urine Collection for High-Throughput Gut Metabolomics
papers.abstract: The rapid migration toward telemedicine, personalized health, and large-scale epidemiological research demands diagnostic testing at a fundamentally different scale. Urine is an excellent matrix for testing at scale: it can be collected non-invasively, cheaply and often. Urine is rich in endogenous metabolites, dietary compounds, and gut-derived microbial products at concentrations that often exceed plasma’s. However, two compounding problems limit its use. There are groups that require caution with collection, such as non-toilet-trained infants, older adults with incontinence, and children on the autism spectrum, where contamination rates above 60 % are routine. Also, when a sample is obtained, cold chain shipping, ultra-low temperature biobanking, and strict freeze-thaw management are required. These are costly and difficult to sustain across homes, long-term care facilities, and multi-site studies. Sample handling remains the single largest source of variability in untargeted urine metabolomics. To address this, we tested and validated a user-friendly dried urine spot (DUS) card platform that tackles both problems simultaneously. The card supports self-collection from a diaper, potty, specimen cup, or incontinence product and removes refrigeration from every pre-analytical step. The DUS card has been evaluated for targeted and untargeted metabolomics. A cold methanol extraction from fully dried cards gave the most consistent recovery across sulfonamide internal standards, theobromine, and indole-3-lactic acid in three matrices. Benchmarking against conventional tube-based collection for creatinine, sulfamethizole, prolyl-isoleucine, and cholic acid confirmed analytical equivalence, and a 30-day storage study showed that drying alone preserves metabolite integrity at ambient temperature. We also used DUS to sample 120 urine specimens from a blackcurrant anthocyanin supplementation trial. The samples were analyzed by LC-MS/MS and the metabolome explored with Molecular Community Networking. The DUS workflow matched the conventional method in network topology while consistently yielding broader annotation coverage, including an expanded bile acid panel. The DUS method provides a scalable, cost-effective solution for high-throughput metabolomics that is particularly convenient for sampling in the populations and settings where conventional urine collection has historically presented challenges.

papers.title: A quantum chemical dataset of electrostatic and electronic properties of drug-like molecules
papers.abstract: We present a quantum chemical dataset of electrostatic and electronic properties for 149,074 drug-like molecules from the MOSES benchmark, a curated subset of the ZINC database. All calculations are performed at the B3LYP/6-31G* level using ORCA 6.0.0, with molecular geometries generated using RDKit ETKDGv3 and MMFF94 optimization. Each molecule is annotated with per-atom CHELPG and Mulliken partial charges, molecular dipole and quadrupole tensors, polarizability tensor, HOMO and LUMO energies, and electrostatic potential extrema. Functional sensitivity of per-atom partial charges is evaluated by comparing B3LYP and ωB97X-D3 calculations for a subset of molecules, while geometry sensitivity is assessed by comparing density functional theory optimized and MMFF94 optimized structures. A SchNet graph neural network baseline is included to predict CHELPG charges from molecular structure. The dataset is intended to support machine learning of molecular electrostatics, development of force fields, and quantitative structure-activity modeling in drug-like chemical space. All data and associated code are publicly available.

papers.title: Bridging Johnstone’s Triangle with Generative AI
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers unprecedented potential for personalized Socratic tutoring in science education, yet unconstrained Large Language Models (LLMs) present profound epistemological risks. Chemistry requires students to navigate Johnstone’s Triangle—translating between macroscopic observations, submicroscopic particle kinetics, and symbolic representations. Novice learners frequently conflate these domains, assuming, for example, that physical phase changes break intramolecular bonds. Because LLMs are autoregressive engines trained on generalized, anthropocentric language, they naturally default to macroscopic analogies (e.g., suggesting the use of a "microscope" to observe molecules) when prompted to explain particulate behavior. This deterministic hallucination inadvertently reinforces students’ foundational alternative conceptions. To mitigate this risk, this paper introduces the Pedagogical Evaluation, Design, and Analysis Lab (PEDAL) framework. PEDAL is a theoretical prompt architecture that engineers strict epistemological guardrails and cognitive pacing constraints within zero-shot LLM environments. By enforcing sequential domaingating—mandating that students correctly articulate submicroscopic kinetics before attempting symbolic translation—the framework minimizes extraneous cognitive load, lowers the affective filter, and aligns conversational AI with constructivist inquiry. Furthermore, the strategic application of negative constraints explicitly prohibits the generation of macroscopic visual analogies. This framework details the theoretical necessity of structural prompting, analyzes semantic failure modes within generative examples, and discusses critical implications for science teacher education, Universal Design for Learning (UDL), Social-Emotional Learning (SEL), and the advancement of pedagogical AI literacy.

papers.title: Salt Formation and Crystal Forms of Pyronaridine Phosphate salts: Single Crystal X-Ray Structures of New Triphosphate crystalline forms and Structural Proof of a Hemiheptaphosphate salt
papers.abstract: Pyronaridine is an antimalarial API first developed in the 1970s and is sold as a material historically described as the tetraphosphate salt, which is said not to exhibit polymorphism. Our study indicates that there are multiple salt forms of pyronaridine phosphate and that no structurally confirmed true tetraphosphate has yet been reported. Single-crystal X-ray structures of crystalline forms reveal several triphosphate forms (including hydrated and solvate forms) and one hemiheptaphosphate salt (with 3.5 phosphate units per molecule of pyronaridine). Other crystalline forms have been obtained but have not yet been fully characterized by single-crystal X-ray crystallography and are therefore tentatively assigned as probable hydrated hemiheptaphosphate-related forms. The relevance of these different forms to API manufacturing and stability is discussed.

papers.title: A dual-targeting nitrogen mustard-class I HDAC inhibitor hybrid molecule is superior to the combination of an HDAC inhibitor plus chlorambucil in glioblastoma cells
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are key epigenetic regulators of gene expression and often dysregulated in cancers. In particular class I HDACs are frequently overexpressed in solid cancers including glioblastomas. Whereas HDAC inhibitors mostly show limited effectiveness in monotherapy, they often act synergistic in combination with anticancer agents, particularly DNA damaging agents. One approach to make use of this synergy is to combine two pharmacophores in one hybrid molecule. The aim of this study was to combine a class I selective HDAC inhibitor with an alkylating agent in a dual-targeting hybrid molecule to improve efficacy of alkylating agents in glioblastomas. Structural variations in the cap region of the class I selective HDAC inhibitor VK1 were introduced to accommodate the nitrogen mustard chlorambucil into the HDAC inhibitor. This resulted in a chlorambucil-type series and a truncated series lacking the propyl linker of chlorambucil. Biological evaluation revealed that the truncated series acted primarily as HDAC inhibitor, whereas the chlorambucil-HDAC inhibitor hybrid compounds induce strong DNA damage estimated as γH2AX immunostaining. Notably, the most potent hybrid compound induced stronger DNA damage, caspase activation, and cytotoxicity due to synergistic interaction than the combination of chlorambucil plus the HDAC inhibitor. In conclusion, the synergy of the two pharmacophores, HDAC inhibitor and nitrogen mustard group, combined in one hybrid compound highlights the superior efficacy and potency of the dual-targeting approach over the combination of two single warhead inhibitors which may be of particular interest in glioblastomas.

papers.title: Solvation-Mediated Ammonia Synthesis in a Nanoheterogeneous Liquid Alloy
papers.abstract: Liquid catalysts challenge the conventional notion of active site, because reactivity can arise from transient solvation environments formed within dynamically structured liquids. Here, we investigate this effect for ammonia synthesis in a liquid Li−Na alloy using machine learning accelerated molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations. We show that Li0.64Na0.36, close to its consolute point, forms nanoscale Li-rich and Na-rich domains separated by fluctuating interfaces. These transient environments play distinct and cooperative roles along the reaction pathway. Molecular nitrogen is preferentially activated in Li-rich coordination environments, where strong electron donation weakens the N−N bond and promotes dissociation. In contrast, progressive hydrogenation of nitrogen intermediates is accompanied by increasing stabilization in Na-rich regions. Ammonia formation therefore proceeds through a solvation-mediated mechanism in which chemical transformations are coupled to the redistribution of reactive species across dynamically evolving liquid domains. These findings suggest that liquid alloy catalysts can be designed by controlling nanoscale heterogeneity, allowing dynamic solvation environments to orchestrate the sequence of catalytic steps.

papers.title: Synergistic Self-Driven Nanoconfinement and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Deeply Supercooled ”No Man’s Land” Water
papers.abstract: The 150–235 K ”no man’s land” (NML) of deeply supercooled water is a debated regime where rapid crystallization complicates experimental observation of a hypothesized liquid-liquid phase transition (LLPT). Using TIP4P/2005 molecular dynamics simulations at ambient pressure, we identify two density-differentiated, structurally and dynamically heterogeneous quasi-liquid states (QLS) within this region. Our analysis reveals that the low-and high-density NML phases represent a novel form of supercooled liquid that is neither strictly glassy nor spinodal. Specifically, a lowdensity QLS (ρ ≈ 0.925 g/cm 3 ) emerges as a stable, structurally arrested phase featuring a selfgenerated soft skeleton of nanoclusters. This network acts as an intrinsic nanoporous structure that imposes nanoconfinement on the remaining liquid, demonstrating that NML confinement can be a self-driven phenomenon. Furthermore, a high-density phase (ρ ≈ 0.98 g/cm 3 ), captured via biased methods, provides insights into prenucleation mechanisms. Finally, we establish the temperaturedependent, nonlinear behavior of density and compressibility, highlighting a structurally driven anomaly that bridges our understanding of deep supercooling. This work provides a new, structural framework for understanding deep supercooling within the NML.

papers.title: Multisite Anion Receptors: Interplay of OH and CH Binding Sites in Sulfate-Bridged Resorcinarenes
papers.abstract: We report sulfate‑bridged resorcin[4]arenes as hetero‑multisite anion receptors that combine OH and CH‑binding sites within a single macrocyclic framework. Density functional theory calculations (B3LYP/6‑31+G(d,p)/SMD(THF)) show that –SO2– bridges strongly increase the electrostatic surface potential at lower‑rim CH sites. Receptors selectively bridged with two –SO2– groups at opposite corners of the macrocycle, bearing upper‑rim substituents (H, Br, NO2) and retaining OH groups for binding, were synthesized. NMR spectroscopy and single‑crystal X‑ray diffraction confirm cone conformations with inward‑oriented –SO2– bridges. Anion binding studies with chloride in THF, THF:water, and chloroform reveal that replacing two –CH2– bridges with –SO2– bridges enhances CH binding by up to two orders of magnitude. CH and OH sites, when present within the same receptor, act as effective anion‑binding motifs, with their contributions controlled by substituents and solvent. Experiments show complementary, solvent‑dependent behavior of OH and CH binding sites and demonstrate that chlorinated solvents selectively weaken CH binding while leaving OH binding largely intact, enabling the design of multisite receptors that remain effective in diverse environments.

papers.title: Workshop on Materials for Space
papers.abstract: The U.S. National Science Foundation sponsored a Workshop on materials for use on spacecraft in low Earth orbit and beyond. A virtual workshop, chaired by Timothy K. Minton and organized by a small Steering Committee (including the Chair), was facilitiated by a professional workshop and support company, Knowinnovation (KI). The Workshop gathered approximately 50 experts from materials science, space environments effects, spacecraft engineering, and mission planning communities with the goals of identifying current and future needs for materials that can perform their functions in various space environments and defining materials research areas where investment is likely to have the greatest impact on future missions. The "Workshop on Materials for Space" was held on July 17 & 23-27, 2023. During this time, the KI facilitators guided the participants through a process of generating approximately 300 ideas for potential stewarding, combining ideas and down selecting to 25 ideas for further consideration, and ultimately preparing 16 distinct white papers. The white papers could be grouped into six themes: (1) Materials development, discovery, and maturation; (2) Manufacturing in space and for space; (3) Testing, performance prediction, and certification; (4) Definitions of space environments; (5) Curated space materials center; (6) Workforce development. The main areas of recommended research are in the materials-agnostic methodology for taking new materials from the laboratory and testing them, predicting (with uncertainty limits) their performance in a well-defined space environment, and certifying the materials for flight. The recommended research would speed the process of placing new materials on spacecraft and would lead to more accurate predictions of their functional properties for the duration of the relevant space mission. Such research would naturally impact the whole of society, bringing new knowledge and economic benefits. These benefits require a talented and innovative workforce in interdisciplinary science and engineering as related to materials for space, and recommendations were also made for strategies to attract a larger body of students to related fields and educate them for careers where their talents can push back the frontiers of space utilization and exploration.

papers.title: Redox tuning and protonation control of peroxidase catalytic regimes in engineered heme protein active sites
papers.abstract: Designer metalloenzymes emerge as versatile catalysts capable of expanding the scope of natural catalytic reactions. The first and second-coordination sphere of a metal active site are known to modulate catalytic activity, yet models connecting structural properties to physical parameters governing catalysis are scarce. Here, we examine to which extent tuning of the heme redox potential and protonation of residues within the enzymatic pocket govern peroxidase activity. To this end, we employ the Hexameric Tyrosine-coordinated heme protein (HTHP) as a model in which the native Tyr axial coordination is replaced by His, Cys or Met, as confirmed by resonance Raman spectroscopy and crystallography for selected variants. These modifications alter the Fe3+/Fe2+ redox potential by a span of ca. 290 mV, as determined by UV-Vis spectro-electrochemistry, corresponding to ca. 40 % of the accessible range for globular α-helical heme b cytochromes. Analysis of peroxidase activity across a broad pH range reveals two distinct catalytic regimes. At alkaline pH, increasing the driving force for proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) from Compound I to Compound II leads to decreased catalytic activity, qualitatively consistent with the Marcus inverted region. In contrast, at lower pH values, catalytic turnover is dominated by protonation events within the distal heme pocket, indicating a shift from driving-force controlled to protonationcontrolled reactivity.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Regression Digital Twin for Continuous Inference of Encoded Mechanical Heterogeneity in Architected Materials
papers.abstract: Architected materials achieve programmable mechanical behavior through spatially encoded compositional heterogeneity, yet inferring encoded stiffness fractions from structural appearance alone remains unreliable when mechanically distinct configurations are visually indistinguishable prior to loading. Here we show that deformation sequences acquired during tensile loading constitute a physically meaningful information channel for continuous design-space inference, and introduce a design-space digital twin, a single learned model spanning a continuous material design space. A spatiotemporal framework integrating convolutional feature extraction, long short-term memory temporal learning, and regression-constrained representation is trained on six discrete stiffness fractions (G0–G50) at strains up to 60%. An intermediate condition (G25), withheld entirely from training, is predicted with a mean value of 25.3 and a mean absolute error of 1.47, more than three times lower than the minimum error achievable by discrete classification, confirming genuine interpolation within a continuous and navigable design space. Systematic variation of sequence starting frames reveals a deformation-dependent learnability regime, wherein mechanically informative morphology emerges progressively during loading and an optimal onset balances morphological contrast against temporal evolution. These findings reframe digital twinning for architected materials as a design-space inference problem, establishing deformation evolution as the information channel and regression-constrained temporal learning as the enabling strategy.

papers.title: Secondary Active Ion Transport Driven by a Lipophilicity Gated Compartmentalised Chemical Reaction
papers.abstract: Active ion transport sustains cellular homeostasis by coupling chemical reactions to ion pumping across membranes. In nature, this coupling is achieved by complex protein pumps and transporters that convert chemical energy into transmembrane electrochemical gradients. Replicating such complex behaviour using synthetic systems remains a major challenge. Here we show that a compartmentalised chemical reaction can drive secondary active ion transport across lipid bilayers. The efficiency and lifetime of gradient formation are programmed by compound lipophilicity, revealing a precursor/product permeability asymmetry that converts reactivity into directional chemical work. Coupling this reactiongenerated proton gradient to synthetic ionophores enables uphill transport of chloride, sodium and calcium ions. Finally, incorporation of a photo-switchable molecular machine-like ion relay allows repeated cycles of chemical gradient generation and light-triggered ion pumping. These results establish reaction-driven, gated active transport in synthetic vesicles and provide design principles for chemically fuelled membrane systems that emulate key features of living cells.

papers.title: A Practical Approach to Ultrathick Lithium-Ion Battery Cathodes by Cold-Welding of Aluminum Microfiber Fleeces
papers.abstract: Increasing the areal capacity of lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrodes beyond the commercial standard of 3 – 4 mAh/cm² is a promising strategy to improve cell-level energy density and simplify manufacturing. Three-dimensional (3D) metallic microfiber nonwovens have previously been demonstrated as effective current collectors for ultrathick LIB electrodes, enabling efficient electron and Li+ transport deep into thick active material layers. Here, we present a facile and scalable cold-welding-based consolidation route for aluminum microfiber (AlMF) fleeces as an alternative to thermal sintering, which is a fragile process due to the regrowth of insulating Al 2 O 3 at inter-fiber contacts. Polyisobutylene (PIB) is identified as a suitable temporary binder that stabilizes the unconsolidated nonwoven mechanically, allowing impregnation with active material slurry while preserving the open 3D structure of the fleece. Under cold welding conditions, PIB depolymerizes quantitatively and without residue. Using this approach, NMC622-based electrodes up to 240 µm in thickness with an average areal capacity of 8 mAh/cm² were produced and evaluated in half and full cell configurations vs. lithium foils and 3D graphite anodes with copper fleece current collectors. Near-complete active material utilization is achieved at low current densities. Capacity losses at elevated rates were found to be mostly transport-limited and reversible upon returning to lower current densities. The small standard deviation values of all investigated cold-welded electrodes show the high reproducibility and predictability of electrodes prepared by the cold-welding process. The presented approach offers a practical platform for high energy density LIB cathodes.

papers.title: Nickel K-edge XANES studies on Pyridinophane-supported Coordination Complexes
papers.abstract: * mirica@illinois.edu Keywords: Nickel, oxidation state, multidentate ligands, XAS, XANES, K-edge ABSTRACT: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a powerful technique to identify the electronic and geometric structure surrounding a specific element and is of growing interest for the characterization of homogeneous organometallic compounds, especially for sensitive and highly reactive in-situ species. In this study, we performed a systematic, quantitative analysis of the rising Ni K-edge for a series of 25 pyridinophane-supported compounds by fitting the K-edge to the relevant 1s to 4p transitions. We observe how ligand substitution, oxidation state, and variable binding modes have a direct effect on the energy and shape of the Ni K-edge as they affect Ni bond distances and p-orbital symmetry. By leveraging the flexible denticity of pyridinophane ligands, we quantify the variable solution-phase binding mode of previously ambiguous structures. This study helps establish using the intense, rising Ni K-edge to monitor in-situ reactivity and to characterize coordination environments of Ni catalysts using only 1-2 scans.

papers.title: Synthesis of siccanin by computational subtarget selection
papers.abstract: The species-selective SDH inhibitor siccanin presents unique opportunities for therapeutic development but suffers from poor physicochemical properties and challenging chemical problems. Here we report an approach to its synthesis that quickly intercepts its unusually hindered cis-syn-cis drimane core, i.e. its local chemical space. Computation helps rationalize and predict reactivity, especially conformational preferences, configurational outcomes and the reactivity of a key O-centered radical.

papers.title: Highly Charged Porphyrin Molecular Wires
papers.abstract: Successive oxidations, or reductions, of an extended molecular ω-system can give rise to significant changes in the electronic structure compared to the neutral or singlycharged counterparts. In this work, we investigated highly reduced states of butadiyne-linked porphyrin oligomers with up to nine porphyrin units and one negative charge per porphyrin. CW-EPR and 1 H Mims ENDOR spectroscopy were used to probe the proton hyperfine interactions in these polyanions. Both techniques show a continuous narrowing of the spectra with simultaneously increasing charge and oligomer length corresponding to a decrease in the magnitudes of the largest hyperfine interactions. This is consistent with density functional theory calculations that support delocalization of spin density over the entire lengths of the molecules with high degrees of spin polarization and non-uniform spin density distributions. These spin distributions can also be described by a Hubbard model with anti-ferromagnetic spin coupling between electrons on adjacent sites. Finding systems with coherent wavefunctions that span the entire length of ω-conjugated molecules, up to a length of more than 10 nm, will help identifying suitable candidates capable of coherent electron tunneling through molecular junctions.

papers.title: Hardening effects and high-power electromechanical properties in Ag-doped 0.93(Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-0.07BaTiO3 lead-free piezoceramics
papers.abstract: Although (Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 )TiO 3 -based lead-free ceramics are promising candidates for resonance piezoelectric applications, the influence of acceptor doping and defect chemistry remains unclear. This study investigates the effects of A -site Ag + acceptor dopant on the structural, ferroelectric, and electromechanical properties of 0.93(Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 )TiO 3 -0.07BaTiO 3 ceramics. Increasing Ag + content induced typical acceptor doping effects, including grain growth and reductions in resistivity, activation energy, and piezoelectric coefficient ( d 33 ). A distinct crossover in piezoelectric behavior was observed: low doping levels led to decreased coercive field ( E c ) and increased dielectric loss ( tanδ ) and permittivity ( ε r ), whereas higher doping levels caused pronounced piezoelectric hardening, as evidenced by increased E c and decreased P r , tanδ , ε r , and d 33 . Moreover, a 440% increase in planar mechanical quality factor ( Q m,p ), with excellent stability over a broad range of vibration velocities, was achieved. These findings help clarify the role of A -site acceptor doping, which can aid the adaptation of these materials for real-world applications.

papers.title: Axial Ligand Effects on Electronic Structures and H-Atom Abstraction by Oxidoiron(IV) Complexes Featuring Triplet-Only Reactivity
papers.abstract: Oxidoiron(IV) species are crucial intermediates for the functionalization of C–H bonds by biological oxidases and oxygenases, and understanding the relations between ligation, electronic structure and reactivity of the FeIV=O unit is key to the rational design of bioinspired catalysts. Here, a series of FeIV=O complexes based on a macrocyclic tetracarbene ligand and with different anionic trans-axial ligands (Lax = CF3COO−, tBuS−, AdaS−) has been comprehensively characterized, including X-ray crystallography in two cases as well as zero-field and applied-field 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy, magnetic susceptibility measurements, magnetic circular dichroism (MCD), and helium tagging infrared photodissociation (IRPD). This establishes a detailed picture of the electronic structures of these ferryl complexes featuring a well separated S = 1 ground state, and the influence of the trans-ligand. The confinement to triplet-only pathways in C−H bond activations and comparison with the parent FeIV=O complex (Lax = MeCN) allows to uncover trends in hydrogen atom abstraction (HAA) ability without perturbations from different extents of two-state reactivity (TSR). Kinetic studies on HAA for C‒H substrates with BDEs up to 78 kcal mol−1 show relatively minor effects of the axial ligands, with rates following an electrophilc trend in the order Lax= MeCN > CF3COO–  RS–. This contrasts the anti-electrophilic trend found for a related series of tetramethylcyclam (TMC) based FeIV=O complexes for which TSR is dominant. For the present systems, temperature-dependent KIEs in combination with computations at the DFT and ab initio level of theories suggest a semiclassical model with modest tunneling contributions that are most pronounced in case of a strongly donating trans-thiolate. This study thus provides a combined experimental and computational basis for understanding intrinsic axial ligand effects and the effect of a trans-axial thiolate in S = 1 ferryl intermediates.

papers.title: Cubane Isomerization: Transformations Overlooked for Half a Century Uncovered by an Algorithmic, First-Principles Catalyst Discovery Framework
papers.abstract: The discovery of new chemical reactions remains a central challenge in chemistry, as it still relies heavily on trial-and-error experimentation guided by human intuition. Among such longstanding targets, cubane isomerization has been studied extensively for decades. Here we investigate this reaction using an algorithmic, first-principles strategy for reaction discovery and catalyst optimization. The method integrates automated reaction path exploration, kinetic prediction of product distributions, and virtual ligand-based optimization of catalyst properties to identify catalyst features that favor a target product. Applied to cubane isomerization, the framework revealed overlooked rearrangement pathways and the catalyst characteristics required to realize them. Using these predicted catalyst characteristics as experimental design principles, we confirmed two reactions that had remained hidden for more than five decades without prior empirical optimization.

papers.title: pdb2reaction: End-to-End Reaction-Path Elucidation from PDB Structures Using Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Elucidating enzymatic reaction mechanisms requires a sequence of computational tasks comprising active-site extraction, minimum-energy path (MEP) search, transition-state (TS) refinement, intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) validation, and quasi-rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (QRRHO) thermochemistry—stages typically connected by ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning. We present pdb2reaction, an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates this entire pipeline directly from a user-curated PDB using a single machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) backend. A GPU-accelerated pysisyphus fork is bundled to perform all Hessian-based heavy computations on the same CUDA device as the MLIP, minimizing data transfer overhead. This toolkit also implements a bond-change-driven recursive path-search algorithm, which successfully recovered the two-step reaction mechanism of the geranyl pyrophosphate (GPP) C6-methyltransferase BezA from a single reactant PDB and a minimal scan list. The identified mechanism comprises an S N 2-like methyl transfer followed by glutamate-mediated deprotonation via a cationic intermediate. A benchmark comprising 23 reaction steps across six different enzymes demonstrated that pdb2reaction recovered the literature mechanisms for 16 out of 23 steps using two of the five tested MLIP backends, with each successfully yielding transition states characterized by a single imaginary frequency. pdb2reaction enables rapid PDB-tomechanism elucidation on a single GPU, providing a high-throughput complement to higher-cost DFT or QM/MM calculations.

papers.title: H-Phosphonate-Promoted Activation of Alcohols to give 1°, 2° and 3° Iodides; Utilisation of Both Atoms in I2
papers.abstract: Herein we report an atom economic route to alkyl iodide synthesis via H-phosphonate promoted alcohol activation. The methodology can be applied broadly to 1°, 2°, 3°, benzylic and other alcohols in very good yields. A less wasteful route from raw materials is utilised and both atoms of I2 are incorporated in the halogenation process. A mechanism is proposed, evidenced by NMR studies. Finally, green metric calculations show the methodology exceeds benchmark procedures.

papers.title: Analysis Tool for Rapid SAXS Data Set Interpretations: Comparative Study of Backbone Influence on Internal Morphology of Anion-Exchange Membranes
papers.abstract: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs) are key components in electrochemical energy devices, where nanoscale morphology governs water and ionic transport and overall performance. In the growing interest toward radiation‑grafted AEMs, the influence of polymer backbones on properties remains insufficiently explored. Here, we investigate how differences in backbone chemistry between ethylene tetrafluoroethylene (ETFE) and low‑density polyethylene (LDPE) affect the AEMs bearing identical functional groups. Small‑angle X‑ray scattering (SAXS) is combined with ex‑situ characterization to provide an overview of bulk properties. LDPE‑based membranes show ~30% higher water uptake and swelling compared to ETFE films, attributed to the greater chain mobility of the more amorphous polyethylene matrix. The d‑spacing values extracted from SAXS profiles (22-35 nm) do not always mirror bulk hydration behavior: higher degrees of functionalization of LDPE membranes show greater swelling yet reduced spacing, demonstrating that bulk and nanoscale structural responses are decoupled. Additionally, to reduce the barrier to adopting SAXS in the membrane community, we developed TRAMA. This Jupyter Notebook-based platform guides researchers through the data analysis workflow without prior expertise. This work highlights the critical role of the polymer backbone in determining AEM morphology and the value of SAXS as a characterization tool, providing an accessible means of processing scattering data.

papers.title: Arylboron TPE-analog AIEgens Enabling Reversible Closed-Shell/Open-Shell Switching
papers.abstract: Achieving the synergistic integration of emission regulation and reversible electronic-state switching in aggregation-induced emission (AIE) systems remains challenging, as it requires balancing restriction of intramolecular motion (RIM) with spin delocalization. Here, we construct a class of arylboron-functionalized TPE-analog molecules and systematically elucidate an RIM-governed AIE mechanism via a rotor-locking strategy. Structure-property correlations reveal that rotor positioning decisively dictates conformational freedom and emission behavior, endowing the system with pronounced AIE activity and reversible mechano-/piezochromic responses. Upon electrochemical reduction, stable boron-olefin radicals are generated, exhibiting broadband absorption spanning the visible to the NIR-II region. Leveraging the reversible redox activity of the boron center, electrochemical switching between closed- and open-shell states is achieved, enabling electrochromic devices with high optical contrast and fast response. These systems are further extended to applications in smart displays, large-area smart windows, and light-adaptive electrochromic canopy system.

papers.title: Occupancy-Weighted Global Instability Index: A Pragmatic Metric for Disordered Crystal Structures
papers.abstract: The Global Instability Index was developed to aggregate bond valence sum deviations into a single structural quality metric, but its standard formulation weights all species at all crystallographic sites equally regardless of fractional occupancy. For disordered structures, minority species at mixed-occupancy sites contribute disproportionately, systematically inflating apparent instability in well-refined phases.
